SOURCES SOUGHT SYNOPSIS

Notice Type: Sources Sought / Request for Information (RFI)

Title: Wing Conference Room Audio/Visual (A/V) Modernization

Location: Will Rogers Air National Guard Base (WRANGB), Oklahoma

Potential NAICS Code(s): i.e., 541512 - Computer Systems Design Services or 334310 - Audio and Video Equipment Manufacturing

1.0 INTRODUCTION AND DISCLAIMER

This is a Sources Sought Synopsis conducted for market research purposes in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 10. This is NOT a solicitation for proposals, proposal abstracts, or quotations.

The purpose of this notice is to identify potential sources and solutions to include small businesses, capable of providing a comprehensive A/V modernization solution for the Wing Conference Room (WCR) at Will Rogers Air National Guard Base for logical and physical switching between secure and unsecure systems to include respective Video Teleconferencing (VTC) systems. The Government will not reimburse any costs associated with the preparation or submission of information in response to this notice.

2.0 BACKGROUND & STATEMENT OF OBJECTIVES (SOO)

The Government is seeking a fully integrated, functional, and secure A/V solution that can instantly transition between Classified (RED) and Unclassified (BLACK) VTC and briefing modes.

Potential vendors must be capable of meeting the following Statement of Objectives:

I. Scope: Provide a solution that primarily utilizes existing Government Furnished Equipment (GFE), identifying and proposing any "minimum essential hardware/software upgrades" required.

II. Period and Place of Performance: Base Year plus two (2) Option Years at WRANGB, Oklahoma City, OK.

III. Performance Objectives:

Master Control & Seamless Transition: Centralized master controller allowing seamless transition between "Classified Mode" and "Unclassified Mode" without manual cable swapping for all devices to include VTC systems, all peripherals, and workstations contained in the WCR.

Secure State Transitions (Red/Black Separation): Maintain strict physical/logical separation of data streams per AFSSI 4212 and DISA STIGs. Verifiable disconnection of unclassified components during classified sessions, and vice versa.

Visual Situational Awareness: Automated, unambiguous visual indicators (e.g., signs, GUI banners) displaying the current operating mode (SECRET or UNCLASSIFIED).

System Functionality: Restore all displays, ensure 1-to-1 mapping of physical assets to the UI, and maximize equipment uptime.

Service Level Agreement: Must have ability to provide remote support within 30 minutes and on-site support within 24 hours.

IV. Operating Constraints:

Clearance: On-site personnel will require a minimum SECRET security clearance for classified network integration and Real ID to access WRANGB.

Compliance: All new hardware will be in compliance with DISA STIGs

3.0 REQUESTED INFORMATION (CAPABILITY STATEMENT)

Interested parties are requested to submit a Capability Statement demonstrating their ability to meet the objectives outlined above. Responses should be concise (no more than 5 pages) and include the following:

Required Information	Description

Company Profile- Company Name, Address, CAGE Code, Unique Entity ID (UEI), and Point of Contact (Name, Phone, Email).

Business Size/Status- Specify business size and socio-economic status under the designated NAICS code (e.g., Large, Small, 8(a), SDVOSB, WOSB, HUBZone).

Technical Capability-	A brief narrative demonstrating the vendor's technical approach and capability to achieve the SOO, particularly regarding RED/BLACK separation, DISA STIG compliance, and master control integration.

Past Performance- Examples of up to three (3) similar projects completed within the last five years, ideally within DoD/secure environments.

Contract Vehicles- List of any applicable Government-wide Acquisition Contracts (GWACs) or GSA Schedules the company currently holds.

Feedback on SOO- Any feedback, questions, or recommendations regarding the clarity or feasibility of the stated objectives.

4.0 SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS

All responses must be submitted via email to the Contracting Office points of contact listed below:

Contracting Officer: Ryan Moehle, Maj    ryan.moehle@us.af.mil    405-686-5442

In email messages please use the subject line: "Sources Sought Response - WRANGB A/V Modernization - [Your Company Name]".

NOTICE of SOURCES SOUGHT 
 
Defense Finance and Accounting Service (DFAS), Contract Services Directorate, is seeking sources for the 
Technical Services Office (TSO) Combined Support. Responses from all qualified and experienced sources 
including small businesses, are encouraged to respond to the Notice. 
 
The ideal provider will have approximately nine (9) full-time staff capable of providing Automated Disbursing 
System (ADS-COBOL), Intra-Governmental Payments and Collections (IPAC), Centralized Disbursing System 
(CDS) and Mechanization of Contract Administration Services (MOCAS) analysis support for the Defense Finance 
and Accounting Service (DFAS) in Cleveland, Ohio local commuting area. The scope of this contract is to provide 
the personnel, management, and technical services required to perform tasks in the following areas: 
 
Category Services Included 
Software 
Lifecycle & 
Development 
Requirements Definition, Design & Analysis, 
Development, Engineering, Programming, Debugging, 
Maintenance, Migration, and Reuse Support. 
Implementation 
& Migration 
Software & Hardware Installation/Implementation, 
Hardware Migration, and Document Conversion. 
Analysis & 
Improvement 
Functional & Business Process Improvement, Software 
Process Improvement, and Economic/Business Case 
Analysis. 
Support Services Customer Support and Operations Support. 
Oversight & 
Management 
Quality Assurance, Risk Management, Configuration 
Management, and full System Life Cycle Management. 
Security Information Assurance. 
 
 
The contractor shall support Agency I&T in achieving the following primary goals: 
 Production Support: 
Provide robust, uninterrupted support for all AIS in the production environment. This includes proactive 
maintenance, debugging, and technical support to ensure system availability, stability, and operational 
readiness in support of the Agency's mission. 
 
 Customer Support: 
Deliver responsive and effective support to end-users and stakeholders. These objective covers resolving 
issues, responding to inquiries, and providing guidance to ensure user productivity and satisfaction. 

 
 System Development Lifecycle (SDLC) Support: 
Manage and execute all phases of the SDLC for new and existing systems. This includes expert support 
for requirements analysis, design, development, modification, technology infusion, and conversion to 
enhance system capabilities and adapt to new requirements.

I.  Agency and Contracting Activity (RFO 6.104-1(a)(1)):
Agency: AFGSC 
Contracting Activity: 509th Contracting Squadron, 660 Tenth Street Suite 222, Whiteman AFB MO 65305 
 
II.  Nature and/or description of the action being approved (RFO 6.104-1(a)(2)): 
The action to be processed is justification for the use of other than full and open competition due to the availability of only 
one responsible source. In this particular acquisition, HSQ Tech, Inc. is the sole manufacture and proprietor of their software 
and systems. This software and system monitors and controls the Waste Water Treatment Plant, Water Plant, Electrical 
Generators, Transfer Switches, Electrical Systems, and Fire Suppression System to ensure that all of the services are running 
within the correct parameters. In order to solicit this requirement under Full and Open Competition, the entire infrastructure 
in which this system utilizes would need to be reconstructed including the upgrade of 69 remote  
field RTU/PLC panels as well as all existing monitors, laptops, network switches, routers, radio, Oracle Dell Server, UPS's, and 
modems. Doing so would cost up to an estimated $7M.
III.  Description of supplies/services required to meet agency needs (RFO 6.104-1(a)(3)): 
This requirement is to provide service and maintenance for the Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) System 
which is currently installed at Whiteman AFB in accordance with the Statement of Work. The SCADA system monitors and 
controls the Waste Water Treatment Plant, Water Plant, Electrical Generators, Transfer Switches, Electrical Systems, and Fire 
Suppression System. This is a service for a base year and four (4) option years. 
IV.  Statutory Authority Permitting Other Than Full and Open Competition (RFO 6.104-1(a)(4)): 
10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements.
V.  Rationale for Use of Authority (RFO 6.104-1(a)(5)): 
This system must be serviced by HSQ Tech, Inc. due to its proprietary nature. HSQ Tech, Inc. is the only company trained to 
service and install their proprietary software and associated hardware. All of the software and a majority of the internal 
hardware for the current SCADA system is created by HSQ Tech, Inc. and can only be maintained by this contractor. HSQ 
Tech, Inc. has been selected for this service for several reasons: Whiteman AFB has a full complement of HSQ Tech, Inc. 
systems and HSQ Tech, Inc. has proprietary rights to all software and associated hardware. Purchasing services through HSQ 
Tech, Inc. will guarantee system performance, reliability, and security. Purchasing this service under Full and Open 
Competition would cause significant hardship to the Government and the internal systems that utilize the current SCADA 
system. 
VI.  Integrated Market Analysis and Efforts to Solicit Competition (RFO 6.104-1(a)(6), (8), and (10)): 
Our agency contacted HSQ Tech, Inc. to verify if any other entities are certified to work on the company's software. Gus 
Jimenez, Vice President and Chief Operations Officer for HSQ Tech, Inc., responded to our agency on 19 February 2026 by 
stating, "No there is not." See "Email-Proprietary System."  
  
HSQ Tech, Inc. also provided a sole source letter in August 2025 stating that HSQ Tech, Inc. as the manufacturer, is the only 
authorized company that supports the hardware and software for both MISER SCADA System and the RTUs along with MISER 
SCADA Client Software and XView for Windows." See "HSQ_Whiteman AFB Sole Source_082025".

REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) 
 
PROJECT TITLE: Selective Service System (SSS) Readiness Simulation 
(Requirements & Acquisition Baseline) 
 
PROJECT SUMMARY 
SSS is seeking additional information for market research and future procurement 
purposes for the design, development, and delivery of a government-owned 
predictive Discrete Event Simulation (DES) model.  This simulation model will 
support the Agency by enabling the analysis and visualization of staffing, 
resource needs, manpower delivery, and operations. 
Put simply, the model will help SSS explore how manpower delivery, routing, 
and resource considerations interact under a range of mobilization conditions. 
This capability is intended to support planning, decision-support, and 
organizational readiness. 
 
Background 
The Selective Service System’s mission is to register men and maintain a 
system that, when authorized by the President and Congress, rapidly provides 
manpower in a fair and just manner, while managing civilian work for 
conscientious objectors (COs).  The Agency carries out its statutory 
responsibilities through six mission essential functions (MEFs).  These functions 
are described at a high level to help industry understand the operational areas 
that the proposed simulation model may represent. 
a. Registration:
 
Maintaining complete and accurate registration information for individuals required to 
be registered. 
b. Selection: 
Conducting an impartial process to determine which eligible individuals would be 


2  
selected for induction into military service. 
c. Notification: 
Providing timely, reliable communication to individuals who have been selected, 
including instructions on required next steps. 
d. Delivery: 
Coordinating the movement of selected individuals to Military Entrance Processing 
Stations. 
e. Classification:
 
Administering a process to evaluate claims submitted by selected individuals and 
assigning classifications (e.g. exemption, deferment, postponement, conscientious 
objection, etc.). 
f. Alternative Service Program:
 
Managing a program that assigns individuals classified as COs to approved civilian 
work contributing to national health, safety, or welfare. 
 
General Capability Areas of Interest 
SSS seeks industry input regarding the following capabilities: 
• Ability to design and build a DES model representing SSS MEFs.  
• Ability to simulate staffing, resource needs, and operational flows under 
varying conditions.  
• Ability to support multiple scenarios reflecting differing operational demands.  
• Ability to support user-modifiable parameters, assumptions, and 
configurations.  
 
• Ability to provide analytical outputs, dashboards, sensitivity analysis, 
statistical analysis, and reporting features that support decision-making based 
on simulation results. 
• Ability to provide training, documentation, and knowledge transfer enabling 
SSS personnel to operate, maintain, and update the model after delivery. 
 
Schedule 
SSS anticipates that delivery of a simulation capability would occur between 
December 2026 and May 2027, subject to the results of this market research and 
subsequent acquisition planning. 
 
 
 

3  
 
Note to Vendors 
This RFI is issued solely for conducting market research and does not constitute a 
Request for Proposal or a Request for Quote and does not obligate the Government 
to any current or future commitments. The Government will not pay/reimburse any 
costs or charges resulting from contractors’ responses to this RFI.  
 
The Government greatly appreciates your response, which will be used for planning 
purposes in enhancing our specifications and further acquisition development for this 
critical requirement. Once a solicitation is released, we will forward your point of 
contact with a link to the site.  
 
The requesting organization address is: Selective Service System (National 
Headquarters), 1501 Wilson Blvd, Arlington, VA 22209-2461. 
 
Instructions to Respond to the RFI 
If your firm is interested, capable, and qualified to provide the Government’s 
requirements described herein, please submit the following: 
 
1) Y our company’s capability statement including relevant past performance, 
2) A projected timeline for completing the work, 
3) Estimated costs associated with delivering the requirement, and 
4) A ny other relative information supporting this requirement.   
 
The Government will allow for questions on this RFI.  The suspense date for 
vendor questions to this RFI is 2:00 PM Eastern Standard Time (EST), Monday, 
11 MAY 2026.  Please email your questions to the Contract Specialist contact 
indicated below.  
 
The RFI closes at 2:00 PM EST, on Thursday, 21 MAY 2026.  Please e-mail your 
submission and vendor information to: Mr. Cane Toussaint, Contract Specialist, 
ctoussaint@sss.gov by the closing date and time or sooner. The vendor’s e-mail 
subject line shall state: SSS Readiness Simulation.  Telephone calls regarding this 
RFI will not be accepted.

REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI)

 Risk Management Framework (RMF) Process Efficiencies

Issuing Organization: 764 ESS

RFI Number: 

Posting Date: 1 May 2026

Response Due Date: 27 May 2026

Considered NAICS Code: 541512 – Computer Systems Design Services 

Considered PSC Code: DA01 – IT and Telecom – Business Application/Application Development Support Services

Classification: UNCLASSIFIED

1.0 PURPOSE

This Request for Information (RFI) is issued by the 764th ESS Contracting Squadron on behalf of USAFE-AFAFRICA/A6 for planning and market research purposes only. This RFI is NOT a Request for Proposal (RFP), Request for Quote (RFQ), or an Invitation for Bid (IFB), and does not commit the Government to issue a solicitation, award a contract, or pay any costs incurred in the preparation of a response. All information submitted in response to this RFI is voluntary.

The Government seeks information from industry on potential solutions to address the requirements identified within this RFI. Of particular interest are commercial solutions, particularly automation and AI solutions that drive both process improvements and mature technologies to deliver efficiencies in the Risk Management Framework (RMF) process while maintaining full compliance with NIST SP 800-53 Revision 5 and DoDI 8510.01. 

2.0 BACKGROUND

Without question, Europe has been a crucible of innovatively dynamic and deadly adversarial threats, a fact that was driven home by Russia’s invasion of Ukraine in 2022, an evolution of warfare on that has been on display for the whole world to see. North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) countries race to rapidly respond to these threats with technology underpinning countermeasures. Technology has inherent cybersecurity risk, which the Department of War (DoW) mitigates via the Risk Management Framework (RMF) process (NIST SP 800-53 Revision 5; DoDI 8510.01).

DoW Problem

The RMF's multi-step process, with its numerous tasks, roles, and documentation requirements, can be highly complex and perceived as overly bureaucratic. This complexity can lead to a lengthy and cumbersome process, making it difficult for organizations to navigate and implement effectively. Additionally, the detailed nature of each step, while thorough, can create a significant administrative burden, exacerbated by the transition from NIST SP 800-53 Rev 4 to Rev 5, as well as the US Air Force mandating 720 baseline controls for every system seeking a new or renewed authority to operate (ATO). However, those are just baseline controls, and the reality is that NIST SP 800-53 has over 1,100 controls that could apply to a system.

The diagram below is a notional 12-month timeline to secure an ATO. Information Systems Owners (ISOs), as well as the AODR/SCA team collaborate and work together on the Plan step (Step 0). ISOs and their teams are primarily responsible for Steps 1-3 (orange) but receive significant assistance from the AODR/SCA team throughout the steps. The AODR/SCA Team are almost solely responsible for Step 4 but can engage the ISO and security team as needed. Step 5 is mostly preparing the decision brief and documents, while Step 6 is a whole-team effort. 

The RMF's detailed and often lengthy process portrayed above is not always well-suited for today's fast-paced and dynamic environments, particularly those that embrace agile development methodologies and fielding technology at the speed of need. The time required to complete the full RMF cycle for a new system, for an authorized system to make a significant change, or for an authorized system to connect to another system--the latter two situations resulting in more analyses and paperwork--can be a major drawback, hindering innovation and rapid deployment of new technologies.

Specific to USAFE-AFAFRICA (U-A), the war in Ukraine, kinetic and non-kinetic weapon development of adversaries, and developmental testing of Air Force Research Lab capabilities, demanded that U-A have its own Authorizing Official (AO) boundary. Operation EPIC FURY only further drove home the need for U-A to expedite its own capability development and implementation. As a result, U-A’s AO boundary is growing at a rate unsustainable by the current way U-A manages the RMF process. Since August 2024, U-A’s AO Boundary grew from 8 approved systems to 17 approved systems, with another three systems that are working toward approval (one of which still isn’t approved after 17 months). This rate of growth coupled with the Rev 4 to Rev 5 transition milestones set by SAF/CN, required the AODR/SCA team to nearly completely focus on the status quo, and hindered U-A’s cybersecurity program to dedicate the manpower needed to scrutinize existing processes, develop efficiencies, and pilot new automation and/or AI technologies organically.

3.0 NEED STATEMENT

USAFE-AFAFRICA/A6 seeks commercial solutions to prototype and operationally demonstrate efficiencies in all steps of the RMF process while adhering to NIST SP 800-53 Revision 5 and DoDI 8510.01. This includes both process improvements (non-technological), and technological innovations that can speed up the RMF process without sacrificing quality of work. The end goal is for the Authorizing Official Designated Representative (AODR) to provide an accurate cybersecurity risk that the AO can weigh against operational risk. Based on the operational urgency, prototype/pathfinder nature, and 12-month implementation window, the Government is considering a layered acquisition approach to utilize Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO). However, the Government will consider Industry input in its market research on how to address this requirement.

4.0 SCOPE & GOVERNMENT EXPECTATIONS

This multi-phased approach seeks to identify efficient process improvements, as well as mature commercial technologies that will demonstrate end-to-end objectives within no more than 12 months. This is an operational pathfinder in concert with U-A’s AODR, the Security Control Assessment team, system owners and their support teams (e.g. PgMs, ISSOs, ISSMs), and requirement owners.

Contingent on the quality and completeness of the white papers the Government receives, and should the government choose to execute a contract supporting this effort, the Government expects the vendor to fully implement process improvements and technical capabilities within 12 months from contract award. In turn, the Government is willing to dedicate reasonable time to provide vendors with access to U-A personnel involved in navigating RMF to help vendors better understand the local processes. The Government expects the vendor to examine and analyze each step of the RMF process and deliver process improvements and a functional technology/tool that streamlines each step. Doing so allows both the system owner’s team and the AODR/SCA team to benefit from gained efficiencies, rather than limiting benefits to a single entity by focusing on just one RMF step. The Government expects the vendors to address systems that are unclassified, SECRET, and SECRET//REL (TOP SECRET systems are authorized by a different AO). The Government expects vendors to propose technology that either already meets NIST standards via an ATO or interim authority to test (IATT), a technology that currently possesses a Common Criteria for Information Technology Security Evaluation, or technology that is in the process of being evaluated by a competent and independent Common Criteria licensed laboratory. Technology that does not possess an ATO or Common Criteria certificate will be addressed on a case-by-case basis. While vendors may utilize consultants for process mapping, as mentioned earlier in this paragraph, the primary deliverables must be fully implemented within 12 months of contract award.

5.0 COMPELLING SOLUTION CHARACTERISTICS

Required Attributes

- Address all steps of the RMF process

- Include an analysis of all 720 baseline controls and what can be standardized by a template

- Be novel in capability, responsiveness, and delivery accuracy

- Be capable of reducing Step 4 from 90 days to no more than 45 days

- Be mature and ready to demonstrate to key stakeholders, to include U-A’s AO

- Be ready to fully implement within no more than 12 months

- Be adaptable to various types of systems (kinetic, non-kinetic, COTS, GOTS, etc.)

- Incorporate automation and/or AI

- Be cost-effective and friendly to supply chains

Desired Attributes

- A system and/or processes that thoroughly reviews RMF artifacts submitted by the program owners

- A system and/or process that can output results with applicable references (e.g. explain why a control was partially satisfied or failed)

- A system and/or process that can output results in a way the SCAR can easily review the results and make recommendations to the SCA

- A system and/or process that can handle increased load and surge without degraded performance

- A system that is simple to operate and can evolve over time without major cost implications and training requirements

- A system that guarantees confidentiality, integrity, and availability of its data

- A system that offers a consistent user experience and provides a consistent output.

6.0 INFORMATION REQUESTED FROM INDUSTRY

Responses should be limited to 12 pages (excluding cover page and capability statements) and address the following:

Company Information: 

- Company name, CAGE code, UEI, address, POC (name, phone, email)

- Business size and applicable socioeconomic certifications

- Contract vehicles currently held (GSA MAS, GWAC, IDIQ, OTA consortia memberships, etc.)

Technical Solution Overview 

- Description of proposed solution (process, technology, or hybrid)

- Mapping of solution capability to each of the six RMF steps

- Approach to standardizing/templating the 720 USAF baseline controls

- Description of automation/AI components and underlying models/architecture

- Approach for reducing Step 4 from 90 to ≤45 days

Maturity & Compliance

- Technology Readiness Level (TRL)

- Existing ATO status (Issuing AO, boundary, classification, expiration) OR

- Common Criteria certification status (EAL level, Protection Profile, lab)

- FedRAMP status (if cloud-based)

- DoD IL level (IL2/4/5/6) supported

- Past performance on similar DoD/Federal RMF efforts

Implementation Approach

- A brief description of how the vendor would conduct a live technical demonstration or pitch (using synthetic/dummy data)

- A proposed milestone schedule that shows how the vendor would achieve full implementation in 12 months (e.g. ## days for analyses, ## days for prototype delivery, ## to pilot prototype, etc.)

- Personnel/access required from the Government

- Use of consultants/subcontractors (if any)

- Risks and mitigation strategies

Pricing Construct (ROM)

- Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) cost estimate

- Pricing model (FFP, T&M, subscription/SaaS, hybrid)

- Identification of any contract vehicles through which the solution can be procured

Recommended Acquisition Approach

-Vendor recommendation on acquisition pathway (FAR-based contract, OTA, CSO, SBIR/STTR, etc.)

- Recommended contract type and rationale

7.0 SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS

Interested parties are requested to respond to this RFI with a white paper. White papers are due no later than 27 May 2026, 1400 CEST. Responses shall be submitted via e-mail to Mr. Corey Chopko at corey.chopko@us.af.mil, Ms. Ina Hemmer at ina.hemmer.de@us.af.mil, and Capt Kevin Sheedy at kevin.sheedy.3@us.af.mil as described for the below sections. Proprietary information, if any, should be minimized and MUST BE CLEARLY MARKED. To aid the Government, please segregate proprietary information. Please be advised that all submissions become Government property and will not be returned.

U-A representatives may or may not choose to meet with potential Offerors. Such discussions would only be intended to get further clarification of potential capability to meet the requirements, especially any development and certification risks.

Questions regarding this announcement shall be submitted in writing via e-mail to Mr. Corey Chopko at corey.chopko@us.af.mil, Ms. Ina Hemmer at ina.hemmer.de@us.af.mil, and Capt Kevin Sheedy at kevin.sheedy.3@us.af.mil by 13 May 2026, 1400 CEST. Verbal questions will NOT be accepted. Questions will be answered by posting answers in response to this RFI; accordingly, questions shall NOT contain proprietary or classified information. The Government does not guarantee that questions received after 13 May 2026, 1400 CEST, will be answered.

The information provided in the RFI is subject to change and is not binding the Government. The Government has not made a commitment to procure any of the items discussed, and release of this RFI should not be construed as such a commitment or as authorization to incur cost for which reimbursement would be required or sought. All submissions become Government property and will not be returned.

Facilitator 
Statement of Objectives (SOO) 
Part D Transaction Facilitator 
 
1. Background 
 
The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) administers the Medicare Part D 
prescription drug benefit program. A critical component of Part D administration is the 
coordination of benefits (COB) between Medicare Part D plans and other payers, including non-
Part D plans providing prescription drug coverage. CMS requires a Part D transaction facilitation 
contractor to support the accurate tracking of True Out-of-Pocket (TrOOP) costs, facilitate 
eligibility queries, and ensure secure and compliant exchange of protected health information 
(PHI) in accordance with Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) and 
applicable federal regulations. 
 
CMS seeks a contractor to provide transaction facilitation services that support the Medicare 
Part D COB program. The contractor shall bring innovative, efficient, and compliant solutions to 
meet the objectives described herein. 
 
2. Scope 
 
This Statement of Objectives (SOO) describes the high-level outcomes and objectives CMS 
seeks to achieve through this acquisition. Offerors are required to submit, as part of their 
technical proposal, a Performance Work Statement (PWS) and a Quality Assurance 
Surveillance Plan (QASP) that describe how they will meet these objectives and how 
performance will be measured and monitored. 
 
The appendices referenced herein (Appendices A through I) define technical specifications, 
data formats, matching criteria, and transaction standards that shall remain unchanged and 
must be incorporated into the offeror's proposed PWS. 
 
 

Part D Transaction Facilitator —  Statement of Objectives (SOO) 
CMS —  For Official Use Only | Page 2 
 
Referenced Appendices (unchanged and incorporated by reference): 
 
• Appendix A – HHS Contractor Non-Disclosure Agreement 
• Appendix B – Baseline Deliverables 
• Appendix C – Medicare Part D Eligibility Index  
• Appendix D – Medicare Part D Eligibility Verification Transactions (E1), Financial 
Information Reporting Transactions (FIR), Supplemental Payment Information Transactions 
(Nx), and Hospice Nx. 
• Appendix E – Transaction Payer Sheets 
• Appendix F – FIR Mass Retrigger Dates 
• Appendix G – Real-time Nx Process 
• Appendix H – E1 Matching Logic 
• Appendix I – BIN/PCN Routing Supplemental Transaction 
 
3. Contract Type 
 
This is a Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contract with a Time-and-Materials (T&M) Order-level 
materials (OLMs) Contract Line Item Number (CLIN) for each period. 
 
4. Offeror Submission Requirements 
 
In response to this SOO, offerors shall submit the following as part of their technical proposal: 
 
1. Performance Work Statement (PWS): A detailed PWS describing the offeror's approach to 
achieving each objective stated in Section 5 of this SOO. The PWS shall describe the 
specific tasks, methods, processes, staffing, tools, and technologies the offeror will employ. 
The PWS must incorporate all technical requirements contained in Appendices A through I. 
2. Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan (QASP): A QASP that identifies measurable 
performance standards, Acceptable Quality Levels (AQLs), surveillance methods, and 
remedies for each performance objective in the PWS. The QASP shall align to the 
performance objectives and framework described in Section 6 of this SOO. 
 
  

Part D Transaction Facilitator —  Statement of Objectives (SOO) 
CMS —  For Official Use Only | Page 3 
 
5. Performance Objectives 
 
Objective 1: Part D Transaction Facilitation 
 
CMS seeks accurate, timely, and compliant processing of Part D Coordination of Benefits 
(COB) related transactions between Medicare Part D plans and other payers. The  tasks listed 
below require require a 24/7 real-time, on-line switching network and connectivity with 
pharmacies, other pharmacy switches, Part D plan sponsors, and other payers, providers, and 
other entities as designated by CMS  
The Contractor shall: 
• Maintain the Medicare Part D Eligibility Index (Appendix C) provided by CMS; 
• Use the Medicare Part D Eligibility Index (Appendix C) to accept and respond to 
pharmacy-initiated or from CMS approved entities eligibility queries; 
• Build a database of primary Part D and supplemental payer BIN/PCNs; 
•  Accept from pharmacies, payers and other switches Part D related transactions and 
route these transactions to the appropriate entity; 
• Identify and accept supplemental claims transactions from pharmacies, payers and 
switches, and create and route transactions reporting supplemental claims data to the 
Part D plans; 
• Create and route automated TrOOP balance transfer transactions to Part D plans and 
accept responses to these transactions. 
• Create and route coordination of benefits, other coverage enrollment information and 
other data as defined by CMS. 
• Utilize existing commercial IT system(s) to support this objective. 
  

Part D Transaction Facilitator —  Statement of Objectives (SOO) 
CMS —  For Official Use Only | Page 4 
 
Objective 2: HIPAA-Compliant Business Associate Agreement (BAA) Execution 
 
CMS seeks full compliance with the HIPAA Privacy Rule (45 CFR Parts 160 and 164) in the 
exchange of Protected Health Information (PHI) between the Part D Transaction Facilitator and 
Medicare Part D plan sponsors. The contractor shall achieve outcomes including, but not limited 
to: 
 
• Execution of a signed BAA with each Medicare Part D prescription drug plan sponsor prior 
to the exchange of TrOOP information. 
• Maintenance of BAA execution rates such that no more than 10% of plan sponsors require 
amendment to the standard language agreement; the Contracting Officer's Representative 
(COR)/Project Officer (PO) shall be notified if this threshold is exceeded. 
• Timely notification to CMS of any plan sponsor that has not executed a BAA by December 
31 of each year. 
• Execution of BAAs with newly identified Part D sponsors prior to the beginning of each new 
Part D contract year, based on a list provided by CMS no later than October 1. 
• Publication of the CMS-provided standard language BAA on the contractor's website for 
plan sponsor access. 
  

Part D Transaction Facilitator —  Statement of Objectives (SOO) 
CMS —  For Official Use Only | Page 5 
 
Objective 3: Pharmacy Eligibility Query (E1) Support 
 
CMS seeks reliable, accurate, and secure responses to pharmacy eligibility queries to support 
beneficiary access to Part D benefits at the point of sale. The contractor shall achieve outcomes 
including, but not limited to: 
 
• Provision of timely and accurate responses to E1 eligibility queries using the current 
National Council for Prescription Drug Programs (NCPDP) standard E1 transaction, per 
specifications in Appendix D and Appendix E. 
• Use of all official (non-audited off) records in the "Part D Contract Data" field of the Medicare 
Eligibility Index to determine historical, current, and future coverage, including contract 
information, coverage dates, and 4Rx data. 
• Application of minimum matching criteria as defined in Appendix H.Compliance with CMS 
security and privacy standards for all E1 query responses. 
• Maintenance and ongoing support of the E1 environment, including requirements analysis, 
design, development, quality assurance (QA), and project management. 
• Implementation and management of pharmacy exclusion tables as directed by CMS. 
• Publication of E1 specifications, RxBIN/PCN information, and matching criteria as defined in 
Appendices E, H, and I on the contractor’s website. 
  

Part D Transaction Facilitator —  Statement of Objectives (SOO) 
CMS —  For Official Use Only | Page 6 
 
Objective 4: Disaster Recovery (DR) and System Architecture Compliance 
 
CMS seeks a resilient, modern, and compliant system architecture that meets federal continuity 
of operations and security requirements. The contractor shall achieve outcomes including, but 
not limited to: 
 
• Design and re-architecture of the current DR environment to comply with applicable CMS 
and federal guidelines. 
• Maintenance of system availability, integrity, and confidentiality at a Moderate risk level in 
accordance with FIPS 199 and NIST SP 800-60. 
• Alignment with the CMS Technical Reference Architecture (TRA), which will be provided 
upon request. 
  

Part D Transaction Facilitator —  Statement of Objectives (SOO) 
CMS —  For Official Use Only | Page 7 
 
Objective 5: Information Security and Privacy Compliance 
 
CMS seeks full compliance with all applicable federal information security and privacy 
requirements. The contractor shall achieve outcomes including, but not limited to: 
 
• Protection of government information and systems in accordance with the HHS Information 
Security and Privacy Policy (IS2P) and CMS Information Systems Security and Privacy 
Policy (IS2P2). 
• Safeguarding of Personally Identifiable Information (PII) at a Moderate confidentiality impact 
level per OMB Circular A-130. 
• Handling of Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) in accordance with Executive Order 
13556 and NIST SP 800-171 Rev 3. 
• Immediate notification (within one (1) hour) to CMS of any new or unanticipated threats, 
hazards, or safeguard failures. 
• Destruction of information and data in accordance with NIST SP 800-88 Rev 1 when no 
longer needed. 
• Compliance with the Privacy Act and applicable FAR clauses. 
  

Part D Transaction Facilitator —  Statement of Objectives (SOO) 
CMS —  For Official Use Only | Page 8 
 
Objective 6: Program and Technical Management 
 
CMS seeks transparent, accurate, and timely project management and reporting to support 
CMS oversight. The contractor shall achieve outcomes including, but not limited to: 
 
• Development and maintenance of a Project Management Plan (PMP) when requested by 
the COR. 
• Provision and maintenance of a baseline integrated project schedule using the current CMS 
version of Microsoft Project, or an alternative format acceptable to the COR. 
• Active participation in joint management reviews with CMS (Bi-weekly or as needed), 
attended by persons with authority to make cost and schedule decisions. 
• Active participation in MA & Part D system workgroups and meetings as directed by CMS, 
including preparation of materials, agendas, meeting minutes, and presentations upon 
request. 
• Participation in status conference calls as directed by the COR. 
• Preparation and submission of Monthly Status Reports as requested by the COR, including 
the CMS Financial Status Report Spreadsheet. 
• Preparation and submission of meeting minutes documenting meeting date(s), participants, 
purpose, decisions reached, and action items (including responsible party and due date). 
• Preparation and submission of meeting agendas for meetings where the contractor is the 
primary presenter, including meeting date, purpose, intended audience, and specific agenda 
items. 
• Submission of all proposed key personnel substitutions or additions in writing to CMS at 
least thirty (30) days prior to the proposed substitution, including a detailed explanation and 
complete resume; all substitutions must have qualifications equal to or greater than the 
person being replaced. 
  

Part D Transaction Facilitator —  Statement of Objectives (SOO) 
CMS —  For Official Use Only | Page 9 
 
Objective 7: Transition-In Support (Optional) 
 
CMS seeks a seamless transition of duties, responsibilities, activities, and functions from the 
incumbent contractor. The contractor shall achieve outcomes including, but not limited to: 
 
• Collaboration with the previous contractor to ensure an orderly and seamless transition over 
approximately 3 months (or as otherwise specified by CMS). 
• Transfer of all tools, data, documentation, and institutional knowledge necessary to maintain 
continuity of operations. 
  

Part D Transaction Facilitator —  Statement of Objectives (SOO) 
CMS —  For Official Use Only | Page 10 
 
Objective 8: Section 508 Compliance 
 
CMS seeks full compliance with Section 508 of the Rehabilitation Act for all Information and 
Communication Technology (ICT) developed or delivered under this contract, in accordance 
with E205 Electronic Content requirements. 
 
  

Part D Transaction Facilitator —  Statement of Objectives (SOO) 
CMS —  For Official Use Only | Page 11 
 
6. QASP Framework 
 
Offerors shall propose a QASP that addresses, at a minimum, the performance objectives, 
standards, AQLs, surveillance methods, and remedies described in this section. The 
Government will use the offeror's proposed QASP as the basis for performance monitoring 
throughout the contract. CMS reserves the right to modify the QASP by mutual agreement 
during the period of performance. 
 
The QASP shall include, at a minimum, the following elements for each performance standard: 
 
• Performance Objective — The outcome or result to be achieved. 
• Performance Standard — The measurable threshold defining acceptable performance. 
• Acceptable Quality Level (AQL) —  The minimum level of performance the Government 
will accept before initiating remedies. 
• Surveillance Method —  How CMS will monitor and verify contractor performance. 
• Remedy —  The action CMS will take if performance falls below the AQL. 
The table below provides the minimum QASP framework that offerors must address. Offerors 
are encouraged to propose additional performance standards that demonstrate their 
commitment to quality and innovation.

Performance Work Statement (PWS) 
Cat6A LAN Drop/Fiber Installation, Bldg. 15177 
 
 
Organization: AFLCMC/EBR 
Address: Bldg. 15177 
Eglin AFB, FL 32542 
 
1. Purpose: 
The contractor shall Engineer, Furnish, Install and Test (EFI&T) the installation of (48) CAT6A network 
drops, and (2) 24-strand Multi-Mode (MM) cables in Bldg. 15177. 
 
2. Speciﬁc Task Objectives: 
2.1.  Cat6A Drop Installation Tasks: 
• In comm room 006, install a new 48-port modular patch panel in Rack C utilizing Rack Units 
(RU) 18/19.  
 
• Install 40-total Plenum UTP Green CAT6A data cables and jacks from comm room 006 to room 
002. Reference drawing T-101. 
 
•  In room 002, install a 48-port modular patch panel on a wall mount bracket as a consolidation 
point using Green CAT6A jacks. 
 
•  Install 8-total Plenum UTP Green CAT6A data cables and jacks from comm room 006 to room 
005. Reference drawing T-101 
 
•  In room 005, install White LD10 Panduit and White deep device boxes for the Green CAT6A 
jacks. Downward sloped 4-port face plates shall be used. 
 
• Contractor shall create a 4.5-inch wall penetration and install a 4-inch sleeve from the hallway 
into comm room 006 above the drop ceiling, and a 4.5-inch wall penetration and 4-inch sleeve 
from the hallway into room 002. Reference drawing T-101.  
 
• Contractor shall create a 2.5-inch wall penetration and install a 2-inch sleeve from the hallway 
into room 005. Reference drawing T-101.  
 
• Install approx. 65-feet of J-hooks with retaining clips as illustrated in drawing T-101. 
 

  
• Sleeves or slots shall not be left open except during cable installation and shall be properly ﬁre 
stopped. All new work area outlets shall have a j-hook placed either above the ceiling or with in 
close proximity to, and a minimum of 12-inches of slack provided on the j-hook. 
 
2.2. Fiber Optic Tasks: 
• In comm room 006, Rack A (FODP 1), install (2) 24-strand MM cables, Aqua color, 1-each 
24MM to comm room 202, and comm room 120. Provide/install LC cassettes and terminate 
the 24MM cables in existing FODP 1.  Reference drawing T-201. 
 
• In comm room 120, utilize existing pathways the Green NIPR cables use from comm room 006. 
Fiber will then be terminated on a NEW wall mounted FODP in the back corner of the room. 
FODP shall be mounted at a height of 6’ from the ﬂoor to the bottom of the mount. 
 
• In comm room 202, utilize the existing pathway that Green NIPR cabling takes from comm 
room 006. The 24-strand ﬁber will terminate into rack O, installing a NEW FODP on RU 1/2.  
 
• Perform 100% veriﬁcation acceptance test and provide a test report for multi-mode optical 
ﬁbers, (all strands) end-to-end and bi-directional attenuation tests IAW OFSTP-14, OFSTP-7, 
TIA-568-C.3 and TIA-526-7. Installer shall use Tier One Testing using an Optical Power Meter 
and Light Source for all Inside Plant (ISP) multi-mode optical ﬁbers.  
 
3.  General Requirements: 
3.1. The contractor shall follow all technical requirements, deliverables, parts and materials, 
speciﬁcations, practices, product speciﬁcations, methods and procedures, and guidance 
contained within the 96
th Communications Squadron Cyber Infrastructure Standards and 
Installation Speciﬁcations (CISIS).  This includes, but is not limited to; 
• Patch Panels: IAW CISIS 2.2.9.1 
• Work Area Outlets (WAO): IAW CISIS 2.2.9.2 
• Horizontal Cable: IAW CISIS 2.2.9.3 
• Fiber Patch Panels: IAW CISIS 2.2.10 
• Grounding/Bonding: IAW CISIS 2.2.11Infrastructure shall be grounded/bonded and labeled 
IAW TIA 607 and the CISIS.  
• Labeling: IAW CISIS 2.2.16 Work Area Outlets (WAO), Racks, Cabinets, Cabling, etc shall be 
labeled IAW TIA-606 and the CISIS. 
• Testing: Cat6A/Fiber cable shall be tested IAW the CISIS Chapter 3. 
• Test Equipment Calibration: Test Equipment and Test Reports shall document a calibrations 
date within 1 year of test date and be IAW the CISIS 3.1.4. 
• Parts and Materials: IAW CISIS Chapter 4 
• Rack Elevations: The contractor shall mount equipment (i.e. Patch Panels) IAW the locations 
speciﬁed in the CISIS Attachment D. 

  
3.2. Product Submittal: The contractor shall provide with their proposal, a complete list of the 
products the contractor will provide to satisfy this PWS, to be reviewed by the government as part 
of the technical evaluation. Provide catalog cuts, illustrations, schedules, diagrams, and/or 
brochures illustrating the manufacturer, part number, size, physical appearance, and other 
characteristics of the materials, systems, or equipment to be installed. This shall include, but not 
be limited to, conduit, duct, innerduct, couplers, handholes, cable, splices, tracers, enclosures, 
cabinets, connectors, patch panels, etc.  Material/Products submitted must be IAW the CISIS 
Chapter 4. 
3.3. The contractor shall provide all tools, installation materials, and test equipment and labor 
required to perform installation as called for by the PWS. 
3.4. Any damage caused by the contractor to existing facilities or equipment during site performance 
of the PWS will be repaired at the expense of the contractor, unless otherwise directed by the 
government. 
3.5. The contractor shall restore the site to the original condition which existed prior to the install, 
unless otherwise directed by the government. 
 
4. Deliverables:  
4.1. The contractor shall provide ISP/OSP copper/ﬁber test report(s) and As-Built drawings prior to 
scheduling a ﬁnal QC inspection IAW CISIS Chapter 3. 
• Test Results: The contractor shall provide test reports IAW the CISIS. 
• As-Built Documentation: The contractor shall provide As-Built documentation IAW the CISIS. 
Provide soft-copy drawings in .PDF format. 
 
5. Acceptance Testing and Veriﬁcation: 
• Witness Test: Following the contractor’s completion of the installation, Test Result and As-
Built review/acceptance by the government, the contractor shall demonstrate acceptable 
performance of the installed infrastructure in the presence of government representatives. The 
government will witness the testing of a government selected sample of ten percent (10%) of 
all installed Cat6A drops and/or ﬁber optic strands to verify compliance with the required 
performance speciﬁcations. In the event that any tested drop or strand fails to meet the 
required performance speciﬁcations during this witness test, the testing event shall 
immediately expand from a 10% random sample to a one hundred percent (100%) test of all 
installed drops and/or strands.  The contractor shall correct all discrepancies found during 
testing. 
• Final QC: The government will conduct a quality control (QC) inspection of the physical 
installation and provide the contractor with a list of any noted discrepancies. The contractor 
shall be responsible for correcting all identiﬁed discrepancies within ﬁve (5) duty days of 
notiﬁcation. A ﬁnal QC inspection will be conducted by the government to verify that all punch 
list items have been successfully resolved prior to ﬁnal acceptance of the work. 
 
6. Applicable Speciﬁcation and Reference Documents: 

  
6.1.   96th Communications Squadron Cyber Infrastructure Standards and Installation Speciﬁcations, 
to include Applicable Publications and Standards referenced within, dated May 2025.

1 
 
 
STATEMENT OF WORK 
for 
Online Writing Tool 
 
 
I. INTRODUCTION 
The Indian Health Service (IHS) is responsible for providing federal health services 
to American Indians and Alaska Natives. The provision of health services to 
members of federally recognized tribes grew out of the special government-to-
government relationship between the federal government and Indian tribes. This 
relationship, established in 1787, is based on Article I, Section 8 of the 
Constitution, and has been given form and substance by numerous treaties, laws, 
Supreme Court decisions, and Executive Orders. The IHS is the principal federal 
health care provider and health advocate for Indian people, and its goal is to raise 
their health status to the highest possible level. The IHS provides a comprehensive 
health service  
 
II. SCOPE & PURPOSE 
The Indian Health Service (IHS) Division of Program Management and Budget 
wishes to purchase an online English writing assistance tool for approximately 600 
IHS employees. An online writing assistance software tool will provide 
improvements to articulate in a clear, high-quality, and efficient manner. This tool's 
features allow paragraph rewrites and proofreading to alleviate grammatical errors, 
typos, and incorrect punctuation. An integrated workflow allows us to connect all 
applications and websites on desktops and laptops to assist with narration, improve 
team communication and collaboration with custom styles, support knowledge 
sharing, and define team acronyms. Software also provides security protection for 
data and information when using the tool.  
 
III. TASK OBJECTIVE STATEMENT 
The Indian Health Service (IHS) seeks to procure an online English writing 
assistance software tool to enhance the professional writing capabilities of 
approximately 600 IHS employees. The primary objective of this software is to 
enable users to produce clear, concise, accurate, and high-quality written 
communications. Specifically, the software must include advanced functionalities 
such as paragraph rewriting to improve readability and coherence; comprehensive 
proofreading to identify and correct grammatical errors, typographical mistakes, and 
punctuation inaccuracies; and seamless integration across multiple desktop and 
laptop applications and websites utilized by IHS employees. 
 
Additionally, the software must support enhanced team collaboration and 
communication by enabling customization of writing styles, facilitating consistent 
organizational language, and allowing for knowledge sharing, including the ability to 

 
2 
 
 
define and manage team-specific acronyms and terminology. Given the sensitive 
nature of the information managed by the IHS, the software solution must provide 
robust security features designed to protect user data and maintain confidentiality 
during use. 
 
IV. REQUIREMENTS 
Requirement Description: Brand Name Specific: Grammarly: GRMLYENT-200 
Grammarly Business Enterprise. The Potential Contractor is required to be an 
authorized reseller of the proposed brand name, specifically GRMLYENT-200 
Grammarly Business Enterprise. 
 
The proposed software tool shall provide comprehensive online English language 
writing assistance, inclusive of but not limited to: 
 
• Real-time grammar checking and proofreading to identify grammatical errors, 
spelling mistakes, punctuation inaccuracies, and stylistic inconsistencies. 
 
• Functionality to rewrite paragraphs or sentences to enhance readability, clarity, 
and overall quality of written communication. 
 
• Seamless integration capability with various desktop and laptop-based 
applications (e.g., Microsoft Office Suite, web browsers, email clients) utilized 
by IHS employees. 
 
• Customized style guide functionality that enables defining, sharing, and 
enforcing writing styles, standards, and team-specific terminology, including 
acronyms unique to IHS. 
 
• Advanced collaboration features to facilitate efficient team communication and 
consistency in documentation across teams. 
 
• Robust data security and privacy protections compliant with federal standards 
to secure sensitive IHS information at rest and in transit. 
 
• The solution must be either hosted on-premises or provided as SaaS. If the 
solution is SaaS, it is essential that it complies with FedRAMP at the moderate 
level. 
  

 
3 
 
 
• Security features: 
o SCIM: Automate the provisioning process 
o Managed Mode: Ensure users sign in only from their organizations’ 
email addresses. 
o User Groups: Create separate groups within one subscription to easily 
customize features and manage users.  
o Custom Roles: Manage admin permissions based on the level of access 
needed with flexibility 
o Client Control: Control which apps (e.g., Extension, Desktop app, etc) 
can be used. 
o Confidential Mode: Prevent processing content labeled with 
“Confidential.”  
o Data Loss Prevention: Prevent the intake and transmission of sensitive 
data types.  
o Enterprise Key Management (BYOK): Exercise control over encryption 
key access, rotation, and revocation, and view access logs.  
• Cost center visibility: Gain visibility into license usage across all cost centers.  
• Style guide: create style guides to help write consistently and on brand in real-
time 
• Brand tones: use of brand voice in a tone profile that is adopted or avoid 
specific tones in corresponding 
• Knowledge Share: keep aligned internal information like acronyms, project 
names, term descriptions, and key contracts.  
• Snippets: create and insert reusable phrases, sentences or paragraphs to help 
save time. 
• Analytics dashboard: measures and drives progress with actionable insights.  
• Customer Support: Priority Support: expedited response times from the support 
team 
 
Critical Requirement: For cloud services, the Federal Risk and Authorization 
Management Program (FedRAMP) is a mandatory government-wide program for 
Federal Agency cloud deployments. The FedRAMP program provides a standardized 
approach to security assessment, authorization, and continuous monitoring for cloud 
products & services.   
• If the potential contractor is not FedRAMP authorized, NIST SP 800-53 
controls may be considered, but they do not guarantee approval of the proposed 
approach. The Indian Health Service (IHS) is required to maintain a secure 
public health infrastructure, and it is crucial that all applications and services 
comply with federal cybersecurity policies and regulations.   
• Offeror shall acknowledge each bullet below. IHS reserves the right to address 
additional concerns during the review of proposals.  
• The offeror shall demonstrate the services of an “agency-hosted private 
government cloud,” a cloud computing infrastructure dedicated to the Indian 
Health Service. Within this contract, the term “private cloud computing 
infrastructure” refers to computing infrastructure that is provisioned for 
exclusive use by the Indian Health Service and does not have interconnectivity 

 
4 
 
 
to other cloud computing infrastructure.  
• Limit Sensitive Data Input – No Sensitive Data: IHS users shall not enter non-
public or sensitive data into the online writing tool.  
• Data Retrieval and Monitoring: If an IHS user inputs sensitive data by mistake, 
the offeror shall make demonstrative efforts to help IHS retrieve or expunge 
sensitive data from the systems.  
• Privacy Addendum (DPA) and Acceptable Use Policy: How the policy aligns 
with IHS Federal Privacy requirements. Note: Public privacy policies evolve; 
they cannot reduce protections for IHS data. 
• Security Controls and Audits: Offeror shall maintain robust security controls, 
including annual SOC 2 Type II audits and industry-standard practices. A SOC 
2 Type II report evaluates the vendor's controls over security, availability, 
confidentiality, and privacy. Offeror shall list any additional security controls 
IHS needs for compliance with FISMA for this proposal. Security control that 
may not be available at the time of the award but may be available during the 
duration of the contract shall be offered to IHS for consideration. The offeror 
may continue to offer additional security controls once the award has been 
made. IHS recommends that the offeror pursue FedRAMP Moderate 
authorization within 18 months of the award. 
• Data Ownership and Liability: IHS retains sole ownership of its content and 
data; the offeror bears no liability for the content itself. IHS shall remain the 
owner of all text or data entered, and the offeror may not use IHS data for any 
purpose except to provide the service (no secondary use, such as marketing or 
AI model training, unless expressly permitted in writing). No ownership rights 
are conferred to the offeror over any patient information or clinical content 
processed, and such content must be treated as IHS confidential data.  
• No Unilateral Changes to Terms: The offeror shall not change the terms and 
conditions without written authorization from a warranted contracting officer.  
Inquiries regarding the terms and conditions of the contract shall be written and 
sent electronically via email to the contracting officer representative. In the 
subject line, list the award number and the name of the inquiry.  
• Execution of a Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) 
and Business Associate Agreement (BAA) between the contractor and IHS: 
IHS is a covered entity; any vendor handling Protected Health Information 
(PHI) on IHS's behalf should sign a BAA. A BAA contractually obligates the 
vendor to safeguard PHI in accordance with HIPAA's Security Rule. 
• Prohibit PHI Input Without Authorization: IHS users are forbidden from 
inputting PHI unless explicitly allowed. IHS users shall not submit any 
individually identifiable health information into the online writing database 
unless such use is explicitly authorized in writing by IHS's Privacy Office and 
covered by HIPAA BAA. Furthermore, IHS data should not be used as a 
repository of medical records or sensitive patient details in the normal course 
of work. If there are specific use cases where IHS wants to analyze clinical text 
with the contractor, those should be reviewed on a case-by-case basis and 
covered by the BAA and a proper risk assessment. 
• Protecting PII and Privacy: IHS handles various Personally Identifiable 

 
5 
 
 
Information (PII). The contractor shall demonstrate the privacy protection for 
any PII that might be processed.  
• Data Use and Purpose Limitation: IHS data is only to provide writing 
assistance services and for no other purpose. IHS explicitly forbids the offeror 
from using IHS content for product development or marketing without consent, 
ensuring compliance with the Privacy Act and other federal privacy laws.  
• Data Minimization and Retention: Offeror shall store IHS data only transiently 
and delete IHS-specific data after a defined retention period (e.g., after the text 
analysis is returned or within X days). Any logs or stored text containing IHS 
user content must be purged regularly to reduce the risk of long-term exposure. 
If the offeror maintains some user text for audit or troubleshooting, the contract 
should define limits and require secure storage. IHS could negotiate the right to 
request deletion of its content from the offeror's systems at any time. 
• Sub-processor Transparency: The offeror shall notify IHS within five days of 
any sub-processors (third-party services) that might handle IHS data (cloud 
hosting providers) and obtain IHS approval for any new sub-processor.  
• Compliance with Privacy Standards: IHS requires the offeror to maintain 
certifications, ISO 27018, and comply with NIST privacy controls as outlined 
in NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5's Appendix J for privacy. The contractor may 
identify additional privacy standards within their organization that safeguard 
sensitive data and provide strong privacy controls that would benefit IHS data.  
• FISMA Moderate Controls and FedRamp Alignment: As a federal healthcare 
provider, IHS must comply with FISMA, meaning any system or service it 
uses should implement security controls commensurate with the sensitivity of 
the data (often Moderate impact level for PII/PHI). 
• Security Control Baseline: The offeror shall enumerate specific controls or 
families of controls that the offeror will maintain. For example, access controls 
(NIST AC family) to ensure only authorized personnel can access IHS data; 
encryption of data in transit and at rest (NIST SC controls) for any stored 
content; audit logging (AU controls) of administrative access to IHS data; 
incident response processes (IR controls) that align with IHS's requirements for 
reporting and mitigation, etc. Rather than listing all 300+ controls, IHS can 
require that the internal security program meet the general NIST SP 800-53 
Moderate baseline. The DHS clause on additional security measures for 
FISMA is a starting point – IHS should formalize it by requiring annual 
attestation that the offeror meets NIST 800-53 controls for moderate systems. 
If the offeror has a security assessment report mapping its SOC 2 or ISO 
controls to NIST controls, it should be shared with IHS. This ties the vendor's 
obligations directly to federal cybersecurity standards. 
• FedRAMP or Equivalent Assessment: Vendor shall, within 18 months, provide 
the necessary documentation (e.g., security package) to IHS to assess the 
service against FedRAMP Moderate requirements, and shall work in good faith 
toward obtaining a FedRAMP Moderate authorization." IHS requires the 
contractor to submit an annual SOC 2 Type II report and/or an ISO 27001 
certificate to verify controls, as well as the summary results of any penetration 
tests or vulnerability assessments conducted by the contractor. In the interim, 

 
6 
 
 
IHS requires the contractor to submit an annual SOC 2 Type II report and/or an 
ISO 27001 certificate to verify controls, as well as the summary results of any 
penetration tests or vulnerability assessments conducted by the contractor. 
Regular security check-ins or audits can be written into the oversight plan.  
• Data Breach Notification and Incident Handling: Per OMB and FISMA 
guidelines for federal agencies, IHS must be promptly informed of breaches in 
cloud services. The contractor shall notify the contracting officer representative 
by voice call and via email within 24 hours of discovering any Security 
Incident involving IHS data. A security Incident is any breach of security that 
leads to accidental or unlawful access to or loss of customer data. The 
contractor shall include written details of the incident, the affected data, and 
the mitigation steps in that notification. Furthermore, IHS requires the 
contractor to cooperate with incident response efforts – e.g., allowing IHS to

C.1 OVERVIEW / BACKGROUND  
The Library of Congress (Library) requires contract support for maintenance of its Empress Media Asset Management 
(eMAM) system.  The Office of the Librarian’s Design Office, Office of Communications and Multimedia Group (MMG) 
currently use the eMAM tracking all its produced media assets in a centralized system.  The eMAM system was procured 
in FY24 and implemented during summer 2025.  The first year of maintenance for the system was included as part of the 
initial procurement.  On-going manufacturer support is required for the licensed users, and to ensure active support on 
the custom implementation of the system. Included with the annual maintenance will also be two business unit licenses 
which are being added to the system.
C.2 SCOPE  
The contractor shall provide maintenance and business licenses for the Library’s eMAM media asset management 
system. 
C.3 REQUIREMENTS. 
The contractor shall provide two (2) business unit licenses and maintenance support for the eMAM system. The Library 
currently uses the following interfaces: Director, Ingest, Archive and Delivery; for 25 concurrent system users.
 
C.3.1 Maintenance Support
Maintenance support must include the following services:
 All software batch updates

 Maximum response time of 12 hours per incident (excluding weekends)
 Access to online support web portal (Monday – Friday, 24 hours a day)
 Email support (Monday – Friday, 24 hours a day)
 Web chat support (Monday – Friday, 24 hours a day)
 Maintenance support shall last for one calendar year, from the period of performance start date.
C.3.2 Business Units
The contractor shall provide two (2) Business Unit licenses.  The Business Unit licenses will expand the system from its 
current state of one (1) Business Unit (used by MMG) to three (3) Business Units, with the same level of maintenance 
support as the current system. The Business units shall enable each user to work in partitioned environment areas of the 
system with customized layouts within each of the interfaces. The business units must enable a new instance of 
Director, Ingest, Archive, and Delivery interfaces for use by the Library’s Design Office and the Office of 
Communications.

RFI Virtualization Enterprise Software Solutions (Final)
For: Virtualization Enterprise Software Solutions for the Department of War (DoW)
RFI Number: 842674441
Issuing Agency: Defense Information Systems Agency (DISA)
Date of Issuance: April 24, 2026
Response Due Date: 15 Days Post-Release

1.0 INTRODUCTION & PURPOSE

The Defense Information Systems Agency (DISA), on behalf of the Department of War (DoW), is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) to conduct market research. The purpose of this RFI is to identify qualified sources capable of providing a standardized, enterprise-scalable virtualization software solution, to include all associated software sustainment, upgrades, and technical support services under an enterprise-wide agreement within the next 12 months.

The objective is to establish a centralized, efficient, and cost-effective procurement vehicle. The Government intends to establish a Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) with a five-year ordering period (one-year base period and four one-year options) to procure products and services for the DoW, including 4th Estate Agencies, Combatant Commands (COCOMs), and Military Departments (MILDEPs), against the GSA Multiple Award Schedule (MAS) Information Technology category.

This is an RFI only. This is not a solicitation or Request for Quote (RFQ) and does not commit the Government to award a contract. The Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this RFI. All costs associated with responding to this RFI are solely at the interested party's expense.

2.0 BACKGROUND AND CURRENT VIRTUALIZATION ENVIRONMENT

The Department of War (DoW) is committed to leveraging advanced technologies to enhance the security and effectiveness of its IT operations. DISA is collaborating with DoW components to create an enterprise-wide solution for procuring commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) virtualization software. This initiative aims to consolidate numerous existing contracts and streamline vendor management for critical Virtualization products supporting server virtualization, cybersecurity, endpoint protection, and network management across the DoW's IT infrastructure.

The DoW’s virtualization environment is a critical component of its global IT infrastructure, providing enterprise compute capabilities supporting approximately 700,000 cores. This environment is characterized by its significant scale, geographic diversity, and complex security requirements, with resources deployed across CONUS and OCONUS locations. These include DoW data centers, enterprise computing facilities, and tactical/forward-deployed environments, spanning multiple security domains and classification levels.

All solutions must align with DoW enterprise architecture, cybersecurity (e.g., STIGs, Impact Levels), and lifecycle sustainment requirements. The platform primarily supports the following use cases:

Mission Application Hosting: Serving as the foundation for critical warfighting and business systems.

Development & Testing: Providing sandboxed environments for developing and testing new capabilities.

End-User Computing (EUC): Supporting Virtual Desktop Infrastructure (VDI) and other virtualized user-facing services.

3.0 SCOPE OF REQUIREMENTS

The Government requires a comprehensive virtualization portfolio to support an estimated 700,000 subscriptions. The proposed solution must be structured to accommodate diverse client needs through offerings like tiered bundles, individual licenses, and hybrid models. A comprehensive migration plan with a detailed timeline is mandatory. This plan must detail the strategy for transitioning from the current VMware framework to the proposed solution with minimal disruption to mission-critical operations.

The plan must also explicitly describe how Artificial Intelligence (AI) will be leveraged to drive automation, reduce administrative overhead, and simplify the deployment, management, and security of the platform. Furthermore, all proposed capabilities must be designed to integrate with DoW regulations and frameworks, and must minimally address the following core areas:

3.1. Core Platform Capabilities

Virtualization: Provide a solution that supports both full virtualization and paravirtualization to consolidate applications and establish cloud or VDI environments. It must include live VM migration, storage migration, and seamless import/export functionality, including cross-migration, all managed from a unified administration plane.

Disaster Recovery & Backup: Deliver robust business continuity through VM-centric snapshots, clones, and replication. The solution must support enterprise-grade backup and recovery via modern APIs (e.g., VSS) and allow for granular recovery (file/folder, full VM, disk-level) across data centers.

Application & Data Virtualization: Provide capabilities to decouple applications from the underlying OS (application virtualization) and to abstract and integrate disparate data sources without requiring data movement (data virtualization).

Remote & Automated Management: Enable remote management and monitoring of all infrastructure, including direct remote console access. A comprehensive REST API for programmatic automation and third-party integration is mandatory.

3.2. Management, Analytics, and Security

Cybersecurity: Deliver advanced threat detection and incident response. This must include Secure Boot, shielded VMs, and native micro-segmentation for application-centric security policies. The system must use AI-driven insights for self-healing security configurations to maintain compliance.

Asset Management: Provide a centralized dashboard to discover, track, monitor, and manage all physical and virtual IT assets. Crucially, this tool must operate across the DoW's globally distributed and logically partitioned network boundaries, providing a unified view of real-time asset utilization. 

Network Management & Security: Offer solutions for network monitoring, management, and security, including capabilities for SD-WAN, web/email security, and virtual networking.

Logging, Analytics, and Reporting:

Log Management: Ingest syslog and custom logs from all platform components (hypervisors, hosts) and retain them for at least one year.

Analytics & Search: Provide real-time search and analytics to correlate events across all layers (hosts, clusters, VMs, applications, storage).

Performance & Capacity: Offer real-time and historical analytics (CPU, memory, storage, network) with one-year data retention. The platform must provide forecasting, capacity planning, and "what-if" modeling for workload placement.

Alerting & Notifications: Support threshold-based and dynamic anomaly detection alerts, with routing to multiple platforms via email, webhooks, and REST API integrations.

3.3. Security, Compliance, and Workforce Enablement

Security and Compliance:

DoW Impact Level: Products must meet a minimum of DoW Impact Level 5 (IL5) certification, with a clearly defined roadmap to achieve IL6.

Authentication: The solution must support two-factor authentication via SAML 2.0 or OIDC to ensure integration with the DoW Enterprise Identity, Credential, and Access Management (E-ICAM) solution.

Training and Continuous Learning:

Foundational Awareness: Introductory training for all technical staff to build a baseline understanding of the new platform's architecture, terminology, and core concepts.

Deep Technical Training: An intensive, hands-on curriculum for senior engineers and the core migration team covering platform administration, advanced networking, security configuration, and migration-specific tooling.

Operational Enablement: Role-based training for day-to-day operations teams focused on new Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), common administrative tasks, and basic troubleshooting.

Continuous Learning: A strategy for ongoing education, including hands-on labs, to keep staff skills current on new features, performance optimization, and advanced security practices.

3.4. Operational Use Cases
The following use cases represent critical operational scenarios that the proposed virtualization solution must support. Vendors must address the specific technical challenges and provide detailed responses to the requirements outlined in each scenario.

Use Case 1: Hypervisor-Native Hybrid Cloud and Workload Mobility

Operational Scenario: During a large-scale joint training exercise, a wargaming simulation application exhausts the compute resources of the local Department of War (DoW) cluster and requires immediate expansion into a commercial cloud.

Technical Challenge: The virtualization platform must seamlessly extend its software-defined data center (SDDC) to a DoD-approved Impact Level 5 (IL5) commercial cloud. This must be accomplished without application refactoring by leveraging bare-metal cloud instances to maintain a single, unified management plane.

Required Vendor Response:

Detail the platform's ability to deploy its native hypervisor stack onto bare-metal IL5 cloud infrastructure, creating a single, stretched logical cluster.

Explain the storage replication protocols and memory-state synchronization algorithms that enable live virtual machine (VM) and container migration across the WAN.

Describe how the software-defined networking (SDN) controller uses overlay protocols (e.g., GENEVE, VXLAN) at the hypervisor kernel level to stretch Layer 2 networks to the cloud provider.

Use Case 2: Zero Trust Architecture with Hypervisor-Level Micro-Segmentation

Operational Scenario: A hyper-converged DoW environment hosts hundreds of transient VMs and containers, mixing workloads that process Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) with unclassified tasks on the same physical servers.

Technical Challenge: Security boundaries must be enforced at the VM level. The virtualization software must natively block unauthorized East-West traffic at the virtual network interface before it reaches the physical network, using hypervisor-level controls.

Required Vendor Response:

Describe the platform's distributed firewall (DFW) architecture and how it operates within the hypervisor kernel, independent of the guest operating system.

Detail how the platform uses Guest Introspection APIs to enable agentless anti-malware scans and file integrity monitoring for CUI workloads.

Explain the cryptographic mechanisms built into the software-defined storage (SDS) and SDN layers that provide native encryption for data-at-rest and data-in-transit.

Use Case 3: High-Fidelity Secure Virtual Desktops with GPU Virtualization

Operational Scenario: Geographically dispersed intelligence analysts require real-time, interactive access to 3D geospatial rendering applications (e.g., ArcGIS) and CUI databases from thin clients.

Technical Challenge: The virtualization platform must deliver a high-performance graphical experience comparable to a local workstation while ensuring all compute, memory, and data remain physically secured within the IL5 data center.

Required Vendor Response:

Outline the Virtual Desktop Infrastructure (VDI) connection broker architecture and how its display protocol (e.g., Blast Extreme, PCoIP, HDX) dynamically adapts encoding based on real-time network conditions.

Detail the platform's ability to abstract physical GPUs into virtual GPU (vGPU) profiles and algorithmically schedule frame buffer allocation to individual desktop VMs.

Explain how the connection broker enforces DoD CAC/PIV cryptographic authentication and applies granular policy restrictions (e.g., blocking USB drives, clipboard access, and local printing) to prevent data exfiltration.

4.0 INFORMATION REQUESTED

Interested parties are requested to provide a response that addresses the following areas:

4.1. Company Information

Company Name, Address, and Website.

Point of Contact (Name, Title, Email, and Phone Number).

CAGE Code and Unique Entity ID (UEI).

4.2. Capability Statement
