STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW) 
April 27, 2026 
xEMU Liquid Cooling and Ventilation Garment (LCVG) Thermal Control Loop 
Development 
Vendor SOW 
1. Background 
Significant investment by NASA has recently occurred, within the context of the xEMU 
program, to develop the Liquid Cooling and Ventilation Garment, used to control 
crewmember heat storage during extra-vehicular activity, or EVA. This investment 
culminated in the delivery of multiple xEMU LCVG garments to NASA.  The xEMU Liquid 
Cooling and Ventilation Garment Thermal control loop is a very complicated assembly, 
consisting of molded and extruded parts, custom-irradiated to achieve a specific melting 
behavior under increased temperatures, and very specific and directed application of heat 
using custom tooling in order to thermally bond the various parts of the assembly together.  
Development of the materials, tooling and processes for assembly of the LCVG thermal 
control loop required a significant investment by NASA in multiple vendors during the 
xEMU program.  This Statement of Work (SOW) aims to finalize the xEMU LCVG thermal 
control loop tooling design and processes, to enable repair of the existing xEMU LCVG fleet, 
as well as fabrication of additional LCVGs, as needed. 
2. Scope of Work 
The Contractor shall work to mature the xEMU LCVG thermal control loop, including 
manifold-to-manifold, manifold-to-tubing, and tubing co-bonding. This effort includes 
development of the necessary heating elements, heat clamps, and detailed procedure to 
enable NASA to finalize the LCVG thermal control loop fabrication. 
 
All work shall be performed in close coordination with NASA to ensure alignment with 
project objectives and lessons learned from prior development phases. Due to the 
challenges associated with meeting requirements associated with this complicated 
assembly, this contract will be considered a single iteration best-effort, and therefore 
technical requirements are considered “shoulds”; meeting requirements for proof pressure 
and tubing pull-out are not considered a requisite for acceptance.  
3. Period of Performance 
The Period of Performance (POP) for this effort shall be five (5) months following Approved 
to Proceed (ATP). All milestones shall be scheduled relative to ATP. 

4. Milestones and Deliverables Schedule 
Milestone Timing Description Deliverables 
M1 – Kickoff ATP + 2 weeks Project kickoff 
meeting and 
alignment on scope, 
schedule, and 
technical approach. 
Kickoff 
presentation; 
finalized schedule 
M2 – Final Delivery ATP + 5 months Completion of 
optimized thermal 
bonding process 
Delivery of samples, 
applicable drawings 
and testing reports. 
    
5. Technical Goals and Objectives 
The contractor shall design, fabricate, and test xEMU thermal loop assembly components, 
including development of supporting tooling, processes, and documentation to meet NASA 
requirements, which are: 
(1) Proof testing to 52.5 psid for five minutes with no leakage. 
(2) Pull-out testing of all tubing thermal bonds to permanent deformation of 1” length; 
post-prooftesting to 52.5 psid for five minutes with no leakage. 
Below is an itemization of the thermal bonds which need to be developed as part of this 
effort: 
 
Fabrication 
• Primary Thermal Loops: 
• QTY (2) subscale xEMU primary thermal loops, each consisting of: 
• Splitter hose clamp (SDN13103905, QTY 1) thermally bonded to 
Splitter socket (SDN13103906, QTY 1) 
• Splitter socket (SDN13103906, QTY 1) thermally bonded to 
Tubing, paratubing (SDN13103921-002, QTY 4) 
• Tubing, paratubing (SDN13103921-002, QTY 4) thermally 
bonded to Primary manifold tee (SDN13103903, QTY 4) 
• Primary manifold tee (SDN13103903, QTY 4) thermally bonded 
to Tubing, capillary (SDN13103921-001, QTY 24) in deadhead 
configuration 
• Auxiliary Thermal Loops: 
• QTY (4) subscale xEMU auxiliary thermal loops, each consisting of: 
▪ Tubing, auxiliary (SDN13103921-003, QTY 1) thermally bonded 
to Auxiliary manifold tee (SDN13103904, QTY 1) 

▪ Auxiliary manifold tee (SDN13103904, QTY 1) thermally bonded 
to Tubing, capillary (SDN13103921-001, QTY 10) in deadhead 
configuration 
Tooling and Equipment Development 
• Design and fabrication of 6 clamshell molds supporting heating elements and 
thermocouples, unique to each bond area: 
• Splitter hose clamp to splitter socket 
• Splitter socket to paratubing 
• Paratubing to primary and capillary manifold 
• Primary manifold to tubing 
• Capillary manifold to tubing 
• Paratube co-bonding 
• Procurement and wiring of heating drivers, thermocouple data loggers, and 
harnessing for convenient operations 
• Evaluation and iteration of clamshell geometry based on preliminary bond 
evaluations. 
• Any equipment required to test and evaluate against NASA requirements. 
6. Deliverables 
The Contractor shall provide the following deliverables: 
 
-Project kickoff meeting and weekly technical status updates. 
-Drawings and assembly instructions for tooling/custom equipment (thermal bonding rigs) 
-Detailed work instructions for thermal bonding processes, including itemization of 
tools/supplies with supplier sources. 
-Delivery of test results against NASA requirements  
-Updated documentation of production processes and CAD revisions. 
 
7. Assumptions 
1. NASA provides all Elvax parts, drawings, and CAD. 
2. All SDN part numbers provided as GFE by NASA. 
3. No new NASA part numbers issued for thermal loop samples 
4. Best Effort, single iteration tooling and deliverable fabrication; acceptance of 
deliverables not contingent on passing proof pressure leakage tests 
8. Contract Type 
The services described in this Statement of Work shall be provided on a Firm Fixed Price 
(FFP) basis. The Contractor shall perform the services using commercially reasonable best 
efforts and in accordance with the terms and conditions of the governing Agreement. The 
fixed price is not subject to adjustment based on the Contractor’s actual costs incurred in 
performing the services.

APPENDIX A: PROGRAM AND TECHNICAL DESCRIPTION  
   
 
1. BACKGROUND  
The lack of continuous, molecular -level insight into the body — for example real-time 
tracking of hormones, cytokines, and drug levels — leads to preventable disease progression 
and missed chances for early intervention. Wearable technologies could change this by 
providing timely data to inform a speciﬁc course of action or modify behavior in real time . 
Unfortunately, current devices are often cumbersome, inaccurate, or too costly because 
each biosensor is engineered as a bespoke system with expensive, non -reusable 
components.  
Delphi will improve the biosensor development ecosystem , enabling low-cost but high-
performance sensing by shifting to  a chiplet-based architecture. With chiplets, components  
of what would typically be an Application Speciﬁc Integrated Circuit (ASIC) can be reused 
and remixed  into new devices that share the same high performance . Yields and scaling 
tend to be easier, and the approach inherently enables heterogeneous integration , which is 
ideal due to the diverse material set often needed for biosensing. De lphi aims to leverage 
existing advances in chiplets to focus on the components speciﬁc to biosensing. First, " dry," 
hermetically sealed chiplets must provide ultra -low power management, overcoming the 
limitations of  current power-hungry standards and the constraints of low duty cycle 
operation and RF or internal power harvesting.  Additionally, chiplets that ensure secure 
communication  of medical data from these  body-worn devices must be developed.  Second, 
“wet” biosensor chiplets that directly interface with biology are needed . Delphi aims to 
extend the state of art from biophysical measurements  or high-concentration metabolites  to 
the continuous measure ment of low concentration biochemical markers , such as hormones 
and cytokines, over extended periods. Third, these chiplets must be integrated into 
biocompatible packages that are fully encapsulated except at the sensing interface. 
Existing encapsulation methods either lack the selectivity and reliability required at the 
chiplet scale or depend on rigid, complex, non -modular solutions. New packaging strategies 
must protect delicate electronics, preserve sensor surface chemistry, and support durable, 
long-term operation in biological environments.  
By the end, Delphi will quickly and cheaply develop modular wearable or ingestible 
sensors for monitoring a broad range of biological markers.   
2. PROGRAM OVERVIEW  
Today, the lack of deep biological insight — such as continuous monitoring of hormones, 
cytokines, and drug levels — contributes to preventable disease progression, missed 
opportunities for early intervention, and limited personal health agency. Emerging weara ble 
technologies could close this gap by providing real -time physiological data, enabling 
individuals and clinicians to recognize early warning signs, tailor treatments, and adjust 
behaviors in the moment rather than after damage has occurred. Consequently , Delphi seeks 
to empower all Americans to fully understand their bod ies by providing this information. This 
will require a revolution in the cost and performance of biosensors. The program will leverage 
chiplets, a new system architecture in microelectronics, to greatly decrease cost ; reduce size, 

APPENDIX A: PROGRAM AND TECHNICAL DESCRIPTION  
   
 
weight, and power (SWaP) ; and enable all developers to access cutting edge capabilities. By 
the end, Delphi will quickly and cheaply develop modular wearable or ingestible sensors for 
monitoring of a broad range of biological markers. The beneﬁts include early detection to 
prevent disease progression, continuous monitoring for safe home recovery, and precis e, 
closed-loop therapy for superior health outcomes.  
PROGRAM DESCRIPTION   
The Delphi program is soliciting proposals to create an open, extensible platform to support 
wearable and ingestible  biosensors. Current bioelectronic devices are largely built from 
scratch for each application, using discrete components on printed circuit boards and, only 
later, costly custom ASICs. Because each ASIC must integrate multiple functions onto a 
single die, every desi gn becomes its own expensive, time -consuming project, slowing 
progress and limiting performance. Delphi performers will create a standard format of 
packaging and interconnections that will enable integration of chiplets from multiple 
manufacturers. Proposers should identify preferred packaging and interconnect 
solutions; however, a series of meetings in the ﬁrst 2 months of the program will establish 
a consensus packaging approach, thus ensuring interoperability . Given the needs of 
biosensing, ultra -high-density  interconnects are unlikely to be needed. Approaches that 
integrate power, such as a battery or an RF antenna, into the substrate are encouraged.  
Teams will likely need to develop Delphi speciﬁc “dry” chiplets for capabilities unique to 
biosensing (e.g. power management and highly secure communications) but are expected to 
leverage commercially available chiplets or IP for more generic device funct ions, thereby 
leveraging the cost savings due to production scales. While development and testing of 
implantable devices is out scope for the Delphi program, platforms that could ﬁt within the 
size, weight, and power limitations of an implantable device o r serve as wearable or 
ingestible would be viewed favorably.  
Delphi teams will develop “wet” biosensing chiplets capable of real -time measurement of 
deep biological information. Except for continuous glucose monitors, most commercial 
sensors measure only biophysical signals. Routine, continuous detection of low 
concentration biochemical analytes, such as hormones (0.1 — 100 µg/L) and cytokines (≈10 
ng/L), has been demonstrated by only a few groups, and typically for just a few days in 
wearable formats. New sensing modalities demonstrate  the potential for longer term, 
regenerative measurements that could be adapted to hormones, cytokines, or other 
markers. However, each new biomarker currently demands a dedicated discovery and 
optimization process along with device re -engineering, limiting scalability and slowing the 
development of the multiplexed sensor panels needed for comprehensive health proﬁling. 
Delphi is seeking a pproaches that are generalizable to multiple analytes to increase the 
extensibility sensor systems  and platforms. Additionally, the development of surface 
chemistries that prevent sensor fouling is typically arduous. Delphi is open to new concepts 
that can rapidly improve the passivation of sensor surfaces to deliver  methods that are 
compatible with clean rooms. Performing sensor functionalization within the fab , likely in a 
separate post-processing hood,  would minimize  the surface contamination that hinders the 
formation of high -quality passivation. To meet these challenges, teams must develop 
design, optimization, and manufacturing processes that support rapid retargeting of new 

APPENDIX A: PROGRAM AND TECHNICAL DESCRIPTION  
   
 
analytes and scalable production, including chiplet printing and processing, device 
packaging, and sterilization.  
Delphi teams will need to develop robust biocompatible materials and encapsulation 
processes for protecting electronics, while providing biosensors access to their target 
environment. Conventional materials and fabrication methods often fall short when app lied 
to small electronic components. These conventional approaches frequently result in leaks or 
failures, as they are not designed to accommodate the unique challenges posed by 
miniaturized devices. Moreover, there is currently no solution that can simult aneously 
protect delicate electronics, permit selective exposure where needed, and preserve the 
surface chemistry essential for sensor function. Approaches must be made compatible with 
the underlying biochemistry of the biosensor chips while meeting the ex tremely tight 
tolerances and critical materials properties associated with chiplet fabrication to prevent, 
for instance, warping of the small system.  
NATIONAL HEALTH IMPACT 
A national ARPA-H program to enable small, low -cost, high-performance biosensors would 
address key gaps: the lack of scalable platforms for deep molecular monitoring outside 
specialty centers; the need for minimally invasive, high -frequency data on inﬂamm ation and 
metabolic status; and technical barriers in miniaturization, power, and multimodal sensing. 
Emerging technologies — such as self-powered ingestible metabolite sensors, integrated GI 
smart capsules, interstitial ﬂuid -sampling microneedles, and swea t-based biosensors —
demonstrate that battery -free or low-power operation, multi -marker detection, and wireless 
telemetry are feasible in preclinical and early clinical settings. If these platforms can be 
engineered for low -cost, robust manufacturing and des igned for usability and connectivity 
in resource -limited environments, they could expand access to high -frequency molecular 
data beyond infrequent lab testing, enabling earlier detection of disease activity and more 
adaptive management.  
Delphi seeks to lower the cost of all biosensors and is agnostic to the targeted disease. 
However, proposers must identify their targeted disease or health or wellness indications 
and justify their choice, as described below.  Examples of beneﬁts to patients could include 
earlier detection of ﬂares in inﬂammatory bowel disease and rheumatoid arthritis, pre -
symptomatic recognition of sepsis or pulmonary hypertension progression, and dynamic 
monitoring of treatment response, p articularly in rural and low -resource settings. By 
bending the cost curve, Delphi hopes to vastly increase the market for biosensors, enabling 
individuals to better understand and improve their own health , thereby reducing expensive 
and avoidable hospitalizations and emergency department visits.  
PROGRAM SCOPE 
Delphi will unite the scalable production of commercial microelectronics with advances in 
biosensor  detection and biocompatibility coming out of academia and other research 
institutions. Multidisciplinary teams must include at least three key roles: (1) a  “dry” chiplet 
group (interposer/substrate, interconnects, power management, secure communication), (2) 
a “wet” biosensor group for detecting diverse humoral biomarkers, and (3) an encapsulation

Proposers should choose one of  two tracks: (1) Minimally invasive devices that either

will culminate in formal human clinical trials to validate safety and efﬁcacy. (2) Non -invasive 
wearables that do not break the skin’s surface which aim to promote healthy lifestyle

supports both advanced medical devices and wellness -focused wearables.  
3. DELPHI  TECHNICAL AREAS  
Delphi will quickly advance the development of modular, chiplet -based wearables and

custom-built for each application, relying on discrete components in relatively  large PCB

TA3 ≡ Biocompatible Encapsulation: Develop hermetic encapsulation to seal integrated

REQUEST FOR INFORMATION

3DX Data Migration

April 24, 2026

1.0 Description 

1.1 The United States Air Force, Air Force Life Cycle Management Center, AFLCMC/WVSS is seeking information from interested companies with the capability to deliver a data migration solution for the 3DEXPERIENCE (3DX) platform. Previous efforts configured the application code to serve as a collaboration and approval platform to support the Government's migration to a digital-based acquisition program. The application integrates data from other supporting applications including Cameo and Teamwork Cloud (TWC) and CATIA.

1.2 THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) ONLY. This RFI is issued solely for information and planning purposes; it does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFP in the future. This RFI does not commit the Government to contract for any supply or service whatsoever. Further, the Air Force is not at this time seeking proposals and will not accept unsolicited proposals. Responders are advised that the U.S. Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this RFI; all costs associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the interested party’s expense. Not responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future RFP, if any is issued. If a solicitation is released, it will be synopsized on the www.sam.gov website. It is the responsibility of the potential offerors to monitor these sites for additional information pertaining to this requirement.

2.0 Background

The United States Air Force (“Government” or “Customer”) is executing a digital engineering approach to program execution guided by the “e-Program” Digital Engineering criteria set forth in the Digital Building Code published by SAF/AQ on 3 May 2021.  This approach is consistent with the five goals identified in the 2018 DoD Digital Engineering Strategy and the guidance provided in the Digital Engineering DODI 5000.97 (Dec 2023). 

3.0 Work Description 

3.1 The contractor will deploy or develop and deploy a solution that exports data on a recurring basis from one air-gapped on-premises Windows hosted 2025x 3DX instance and imports that data into another air-gapped on-premises Windows hosted 2025x 3DX instance in a traceable manner while maintaining data integrity, digital threads, and all metadata.

3.1.1	Data types in use include all objects ingestible and all objects created by 3DX, including but not limited to PDFs, Word, CATIA, 3DXML, and Enovia business objects with the ability to add new objects/types desired.  3DSwym data is desired but not required.

3.1.2	Work will continuously be occurring in each 3DX instance so solution must add/merge and not just overwrite/delete existing data to the imported instance.  Data from exported instance cannot be deleted in this process.

3.1.3	Solution will need to move all data to start but ability to move only new and updated data for all subsequent runs is desired.  

3.1.4	Ability to make all transferred data read-only but linkable in the second 3DX instance is desired.  Updated data is desired to be flagged/marked to indicate changes occurred.

3.1.5	Data movement only occurs from one 3DX instance to the other instance in one direction, with no ability for the second instance to communicate back to the first.  

3.1.6	Data and digital threads will need to be validated in the new instance without reaching back to original instance.

3.1.7	For any solution that requires it, the Contractor will assist with the Authority to Use (ATU) and/or the Authority to Operate (ATO) certifications at the IL5, IL6, and IL6+ levels. 

3.1.8	The contractor will not be responsible for the Cross Domain Solution and will not be hosting any data.

4.0 Requested Information 

4.1 Interested parties are requested to respond to this RFI with a white paper addressing the following questions:

4.1.1. Please include a brief description of how you would develop a data migration solution. Alternatively, if you plan on utilizing an existing application, please provide additional specifications. 

4.1.2 If developing a solution, what team configuration do you feel would be needed to complete the solution in a timely manner? Please provide your suggested FTE and labor mix, along with the estimated timeframe. 

4.1.3 Do you have any additional questions or suggestions that you believe would be helpful for this data migration effort? 

5.0 Responses 

5.1 Interested parties are requested to respond to this RFI with a white paper. 

5.2 White papers in Microsoft Word compatible format are due no later than May 10, 2026 at 4:00 PM and shall be submitted via e-mail only to the Contracting Officer; Capt. Landon Smith, landon.smith.13@us.af.mil. 

5.3 Proprietary information, if any, should be minimized and MUST BE CLEARLY MARKED. To aid the Government, please segregate proprietary information. Please be advised that all submissions become Government property and will not be returned. Results will be reviewed and retained by the government and Government support contractors. Solicitation does not obligate the government to issue an RFP or award a contract. Responses must be at responders expense.

5.4 Section 1 of the white paper shall provide administrative information, and shall include the following as a minimum: 

5.4.1 Name, mailing address, overnight delivery address (if different from mailing address), phone number, fax number, and e-mail of designated point of contact. 

5.4.2 Recommended contracting strategy. 

5.4.3 Business type (large business, small business, small disadvantaged business, 8(a)- certified small disadvantaged business, HUBZone small business, woman-owned small business, very small business, veteran-owned small business, service-disabled veteran-owned small business) based upon North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code 541512, Computer Systems Design Services. “Small business concern” means a concern, including its affiliates, which is independently owned and operated, not dominant in the field of operation in which it is bidding on Government contracts, and qualified as a small business under the criteria and size standards in 13 CFR part 121. 

Please refer to Federal Acquisition Regulation FAR 19 for detailed information on Small Business Size Standards. The FAR is available at https://www.acquisition.gov/browse/index/far

5.4.4 The facility security clearance of the offeror.

5.5 The number of pages in Section 1 of the white paper shall not be included in the 8-page limitation, which applies only to Section 2 of the white paper. 

5.6 Section 2 of the white paper shall answer the issues addressed in Sections 3 and 4 of this RFI and shall be limited to 8 pages of text (excluding pictures and graphs).

6.0 Questions 

Questions regarding this announcement shall be submitted in writing by e-mail to the Contracting Officer, Capt. Landon Smith, landon.smith.13@us.af.mil.  Verbal questions will NOT be accepted. Questions will be answered by posting answers to the www.sam.gov website; accordingly, questions shall NOT contain proprietary or classified information. The Government does not guarantee that questions received after 26 April 2026 will be answered. To access the website, go to www.sam.gov. Interested parties are invited to subscribe to the website to ensure they receive any important information updates connected with this RFI. 

7.0 Summary 

THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) ONLY to identify sources that can provide a data migration solution within 3DX. The information provided in the RFI is subject to change and is not binding on the Government. The Air Force has not made a commitment to procure any services discussed, and release of this RFI should not be construed as such a commitment or as authorization to incur cost for which reimbursement would be required or sought. All submissions become Government property and will not be returned.

SALIENT CHARACTERISTICS

Northern Arizona VA Health Care System—Vocera

450 communication devices and supported software with the following:

Badge

Badge must be lightweight. Badge may not exceed 4 ounces.

Badge must be hands-free to give hospital staff increased mobility and greater practicality to complete multiple tasks at the same time.

Badge must have a button to push to talk to contact other hospital staff without knowing what number to call.

Dedicated panic button to request immediate assistance for rapid response such as code blue.

Badge must have a universal clip to attach badge to clothing for optimal speech recognition which is no more than six inches under the chin.

Badge battery must last a minimum of 35 hours without being charged.

Badge must be an antimicrobial material to inhibit the growth of bacteria for hospital Safety.

Badge must have the ability to interrupt a busy signal to call a Code Blue or a Rapid Response call.

Badge must have the ability to leave a voice message for staff or group of users that can be retrieved when staff or users log back into the system.

Badge must be staff centered so that when staff log in to the system, it pulls up staff’s profile and privileges because this information is maintained on the server, and limits sharing of the devices among staff.

Badge must be FIPS compliant to operate in VA wireless system.

Capability to align with one integrated system throughout NAVAHCS.

Network/Server compatibility with hosting at NAVAHCS.

Picture is to provide guidance to the vendor only

Battery

Battery must be durable to be worn throughout various shifts.

Battery must have approximately a minimum of 4 hours talk time. 

Must have a minimum of 40 hours standby time.

Under care and usage, batteries should be replaced at a minimum of 18 months.

8-Bay Chargers

8-Bay charger must have a minimum of 8 connected bays to charge 8 batteries at the same time. 

8-Bay charge must charge all 8 charges at once and this should take up to 6 hours or less.

	

Clips

Must provide clips that attach the badge to clothing. 

The clips can be adjusted, and length cannot exceed 6 inches from the chin for speech recognition.

Standard Warranty for all equipment 

Must replace or repair all broken equipment.

Badge comes with a minimum 1 year warranty from the shipment date to the original end user.

Extended Warranty for Badges

Must be a minimum of 2-year warranty for the badges beyond the initial year included with device purchase.

Must replace or repair broken badges damaged by normal use.

Extended Warranty for 8-Bay Chargers

Must be a minimum 2-year warranty for 8-bay chargers

Must replace broken 8-bay chargers.

LICENSE 

Badges must be FIPS compliant.

Badge must be validated for effective hardware-based encryption in the VA wireless network.

OTHER REQUIRED DOCUMENTATION

Vendor must provide approved VA Directive 6550 for the Vocera Supplies.

Vendor must be in compliance with VA Directive 6500.

Vendor must provide a letter that they are the approved Original Equipment Manufacturer and/or distributor.

Vendor must demonstrate that their product will have compatibility with existing services and equipment currently in use within NAVAHCS.

B.2  STATEMENT OF WORK


Smart Badge Communication System and Service Agreement
Northern Arizona VA Health Care System (NAVAHCS)
500 N. Hwy 89, Prescott, AZ 86313

1. Background

The Northern Arizona VA Health Care System (NAVAHCS) operates an enterprise Vocera communication platform that provides hands-free, real-time voice and messaging communication across inpatient, outpatient, and ancillary departments to support timely response to Veterans’ care needs, including rapid escalation in emergent situations and fall-reduction workflows. Existing Vocera B3000N badge devices and associated peripheral hardware have reached end-of-life and require replacement to maintain continuity of operations, reliability, and security posture. NAVAHCS also requires continued software maintenance and premier support for the Vocera platform, messaging, telephony, and analytics components to ensure ongoing availability, performance, and cybersecurity compliance.

NAVAHCS intends to procure and deploy the Vocera V5000 Smartbadge system, associated licensing, peripherals, and extended warranty, together with implementation, workflow optimization, training, go-live, and post-deployment services to integrate seamlessly with the existing Vocera environment and underlying VA network and telephony infrastructure. This acquisition will support a standardized, FIPS-validated, enterprise smart-badge solution across NAVAHCS that aligns with VA data security requirements and VHA Handbook 6500.6.​

2. Scope

The contractor shall furnish all labor, materials, equipment, software, licensing, configuration, integration, training, documentation, and support necessary to provide a fully functional Vocera V5000 Smartbadge communication solution and associated services for NAVAHCS. The scope includes:

Provision of V5000 Smartbadge devices, FIPS 140-2 device licenses, batteries, 8-bay chargers, clips, and training kits as specified herein.

Provision of Vocera premier level support for Voice, SIP Telephony, Platform, Messaging, and Per-Device Messaging over a base year plus four option years.

Implementation and configuration of the V5000 Smartbadge system, including database updates, SIP integration, messaging integration, and analytics, in alignment with the existing Vocera platform and VA infrastructure.​

Workflow design, call-flow and messaging design, deployment optimization, and clinical workflow integration services for up to 35 units/ancillary departments.​

Training, go-live support, and post-deployment assessment for Vocera Voice, Messaging, and Analytics.​

Compliance with all applicable VA, VHA, and VAAR security, privacy, and information system requirements, including VA Handbook 6500 and VA Handbook 6500.6.​​

3. Objectives

The objectives of this SOW are to:

Replace end-of-life Vocera badges with V5000 Smartbadges that meet NAVAHCS functional, clinical, and security requirements.​

Maintain uninterrupted Vocera platform operations with premier software support and upgrades throughout the period of performance.

Optimize clinical workflows and communication patterns using the Vocera system to support timely Veteran care, rapid escalation (e.g., code blue, rapid response), and staff safety.​

Ensure that all systems and services comply with VA information security and privacy policies, including FIPS-validated encryption and adherence to VA Handbook 6500.6.​

4. Period of Performance

The period of performance shall be a base year with four (4) option years. Exercise of option years shall be at the sole discretion of the Government in accordance with the contract.

5. Place of Performance

All on-site work shall be performed at:

Northern Arizona VA Health Care System
500 N. Hwy 89
Prescott, AZ 86313​

Remote services (e.g., some design sessions, remote training, support) may be performed at the contractor’s facilities, subject to VA telework, security, and access controls.​

6. System Requirements

6.1 Smartbadge Devices

The contractor shall provide 450 Vocera V5000 Smartbadges (SKU 220-02100) with 1-year warranty and 2-year extended warranty. Smartbadge functionality shall meet or exceed the following NAVAHCS requirements:

Form factor and ergonomics:

Lightweight badge not exceeding approximately 4 ounces; V5000 is approximately 3.1 oz (89 g).

Dimensions: 4.0 × 2.0 × 0.7 in (10 × 5.2 × 1.7 cm)

Display: 2.4-inch touchscreen

Hands-free operation with push-to-talk capability and a universal clip enabling placement within six inches below the user’s chin for optimal speech recognition.​

Controls and user interface:

Dedicated call button, volume control, Do-Not-Disturb/hold function, and emergency call button.

Color touchscreen display for call control and status indications.​

Battery performance:

Minimum battery life of 4 hours talk time and 40 hours standby; the V5000 battery meets these specifications.

Clinical and safety features:

Dedicated panic/emergency button to request immediate assistance for rapid response and code blue events.​

Ability to interrupt a busy signal to place critical code calls (e.g., Code Blue, Rapid Response).​

Ability to leave and retrieve voice messages for individuals or groups.​

Staff-centered login profile stored on the server with role-based privileges to support shared device use while maintaining access control.​

Voice commands (over 100 supported), touchscreen keyboard for contacts and text messages, broadcast and rapid-response messaging, dedicated panic button

Security and compliance:

FIPS-validated device license (V5000 FIPS 140-2 Device License, SKU 261-01950) compatible with the VA wireless network.

Support for WPA2/AES encryption and enterprise authentication (e.g., EAP-TLS, PEAP) per Vocera V-Series network specifications.​

Environmental:

Operating temperature 32–104°F (0–40°C), humidity 5–95% non-condensing, ingress protection at IP54 or better, and drop survivability of at least 1.2 m to linoleum.​

6.2 Batteries

The contractor shall provide 1,000 V5000 batteries (SKU 230-02150) meeting NAVAHCS requirements:

Durable batteries suitable for multiple shifts with approximately 4 hours talk time and 40 hours standby.

Replacement life under normal use of approximately 18 months.​

6.3 Chargers

The contractor shall provide 75 V5000 8-Bay universal chargers (SKU 230-02158) with extended warranty. Chargers shall:

Provide a minimum of eight simultaneous charging bays with the capability to charge all inserted batteries concurrently within approximately six hours or less.​

Include a two-year extended warranty beyond the base warranty for 8-bay chargers (SKU 920-05082).

6.4 Clips and Training Kits

The contractor shall supply:

36 packs of V5000 Clips (Grip, 25-Pack, SKU 230-02155) to attach badges to clothing and maintain placement within six inches of the chin.

Four V5000 Training Kits (100 Users, SKU 230-02200) to support training and orientation activities.

6.5 Licenses and Software

The contractor shall provide and maintain all required licenses, including:

450 V5000 FIPS 140-2 Device Licenses, Version 1.0 (SKU 261-01950).​

Vocera Premier Support, Enterprise License – Voice, 450 users (SKU 920-01338).​

Vocera Premier Support, SIP Telephony, 6 ports (SKU 920-01111).​

Vocera Platform Premier Support – Instance and Virtual Appliance (SKU 920-01965, 920-04137).​

Vocera Premier Support, Messaging, 50 users (SKU 920-02050).​

Per-Device Messaging licenses and associated premier support for devices above 450 (SKU 910-05020 and 920-05212).​

Licensing shall support up to 450 Voice users, associated Messaging users, and integration with existing NAVAHCS Vocera Platform, Engage, SIP Telephony, and Analytics services.​

7. Service and Support Requirements

7.1 Premier Support

The contractor shall provide premier level support services for the Vocera solution for the base year and all exercised option years, including:

Perpetual term license software updates and upgrades for supported components.​

Unlimited technical support incidents with Severity-1 support available 24x7x365.​

Designated support contacts (2–5) and one Return Merchandise Authorization (RMA) contact per site.​

Support for all Vocera servers in scope, including:

Vocera Platform Server Cluster (2-server array)

Vocera SIP Telephony Service

Vocera Messaging Service

Vocera Engage

Vocera Staging Server

Vocera Analytics Server​

7.2 Warranty

Standard warranty: minimum one-year warranty from shipment date for all V5000 Smartbadges.​

Extended warranty for badges: minimum two-year extension (SKU 920-05002) providing repair or replacement for badges damaged by normal use.

Extended warranty for 8-bay chargers: minimum two-year extension (SKU 920-05082).

8. Contractor Responsibilities

8.1 Deployment and Integration

The contractor shall replace existing B3000N badges with V5000 Smartbadges using a phased deployment approach while maintaining continuous clinical operations. Responsibilities include:​

Validating NAVAHCS servers and infrastructure to ensure they meet Vocera Infrastructure Planning Guide requirements and VA standards.

Installing and configuring the latest generally available Vocera software on the Vocera Application, Messaging, Engage, SIP Telephony, and Analytics servers in a high-availability configuration.​

Configuring up to 450 V5000 badges and reviewing configuration with the NAVAHCS System Administrator.​

Assisting NAVAHCS IT staff with integration to the existing PBX via SIP and validating telephony operation in the NAVAHCS environment.​

Conducting end-to-end testing of Voice, Messaging, Engage, and Analytics solutions, including calls between badges and phones and validation of alert workflows.​

Providing implementation reports documenting system configuration at completion of installation.​

8.2 Wireless Performance Assessment

The contractor shall perform an on-site readiness assessment of NAVAHCS’s wireless network covering up to 700,000 square feet and 35 units/ancillary dep

The Department of Veterans Affairs, Veterans Integrated Service Network (VISN 22), Phoenix VA Healthcare System (PVAHS) located at 650 E Indian School Road, Phoenix, AZ, 85012-1839 is issuing this Notice of Intent (NOI) to inform industry contractors of the Government’s intent to execute a Sole Source award IAW RFO FAR 12.102(a) and RFO FAR 6.103-1 - Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements per 41 USC §3304(a)(1) as implemented by FAR 6.302-1. 

This requirement is to procure a Carl Zeiss FORUM Data Management Software for Phoenix VA Healthcare System. PVAHS already uses this  software and is connected to VA system. Zeiss FORUM is manufactured by Carl Zeiss, which provided confidence in the interoperability of FORUM with the existing system. In addition, utilizing a Zeiss system for the Zeiss instrument provided benefits for storing and accessing raw data. 

The data management system shall include all necessary software, licensing, and labor to fully set up and integrate the system with the existing equipment. The system must be able to connect with the VA’s current electronic health record, VistA. The system shall be approved by the Electronic Health Record Modernization Integration Office Healthcare Technology Management (EHRM-IO HTM) team to ensure compatibility with the incoming EHRM. The viewing software must be VA Technical Reference Manual (TRM) approved for use on standard VA information and technology issued computers.

Request for Information (RFI)

The Department of Veterans Information Technology Service Management Platform (ITSMP)

Introduction

This RFI is for planning purposes only and shall not be considered an Invitation for Bid, Request for Task Execution Plan, Request for Quotation or a Request for Proposal.  Additionally, there is no obligation on the part of the Government to acquire any products or services described in this RFI.  Your response to this RFI will be treated only as information for the Government to consider.  You will not be entitled to payment for direct or indirect costs that you incur in responding to this RFI.  This request does not constitute a solicitation for proposals or the authority to enter into negotiations to award a contract.  No funds have been authorized, appropriated or received for this effort.  Interested parties are responsible for adequately marking proprietary, restricted or competition sensitive information contained in their response.  The Government does not intend to pay for the information submitted in response to this RFI.

The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) for this requirement is 541519.  

Please reference previous RFI 36C10B25Q0222.

2. Submittal Information:

All responsible sources may submit a response in accordance with the below information.  

There is a page limitation for this RFI of 20 pages (not including Attachment 1).  The Government will not review any other information or attachments included in excess of the 20-page limit. NO MARKETING MATERIALS ARE ALLOWED AS PART OF THIS RFI.  Generic capability statements will not be accepted or reviewed.  Your response must include the following:

Interested Vendors shall at a minimum, provide the following information in the initial paragraph of the submission:

Name of Company

Address

Point of Contact

Phone Number

Fax Number

Email address

Company Business Size and Status

For VOSB and SDVOSBs, proof of verification in VetCert.	

NAICS code(s)

Socioeconomic data

Data Universal Numbering System (DUNS) Number or Unique Entity ID 

Existing Contractual Vehicles (GWAC, FSS, or MAC)

Provide a summary of your capability to meet the requirements and questions described in section c and answer all questions in Attachment 1 – ITSM Question and Capabilities

Ability to meet solution requirements identified below and in Attachments 1.

For each product identified, submit technical documentation demonstrating the products capability to meet the functional requirement.  

Describe the terms of your SaaS agreement.

Provide your Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program (FedRAMP high) certification status and risk level.

Provide a list of your available license packages/suites.

Your company’s intent and ability to meet the set aside requirement in accordance with VAAR 852.219-73 VA Notice of Total Set-Aside for Verified Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses and 13 CFR §125.6, which states the contractor will not pay more than 50 percent of the amount paid by the Government to it to firms that are not SDVOSBs. 

1. Unified Platform for IT + Enterprise Workflows

a. Does your platform support IT Service Management (ITSM), IT Operations Management (ITOM), Human Resources Service Delivery (HRSD), Customer Service Management (CSM), Security Operations (SecOps), and Governance, Risk & Compliance (GRC) natively within one platform?

b. How are these modules integrated, and can they share data seamlessly without requiring third-party tools?" 

		2. AI + Workflow Automation

a. What AI or machine learning capabilities are embedded in your platform to support ITSM and enterprise workflows (e.g., predictive intelligence, virtual agents, generative AI assistants)?

b. Are these AI features native to the platform or do they require third-party integration?

		3. Low-Code / App & Workflow Builders

a. Does your platform provide low-code and / or no-code development tools to build applications, workflows, and automations?

b. How does your tool ensure that low-code development aligns with enterprise governance and security requirements?

c. Can applications built on your platform integrate natively with the ITSM modules, or are they siloed?

		4. IT Service Management (ITSM) Depth

a. Describe your platform’s capabilities for incident, change, problem, and configuration management.

b. Does your platform include a Configuration Management Database (CMDB)? If so, how is it maintained and integrated with IT operations?

c. How does your platform support asset management and lifecycle tracking (hardware, software, and cloud resources)?

		5. Integration & Interoperability

a. What integration options does your platform support (e.g., APIs, plug-ins, Integration Hub, connectors)?

b. Can your platform connect to federal systems and third-party tools securely while remaining compliant with FedRAMP and VA-specific requirements?

		6. Transition, Migration, and Adoption

a. Describe your approach to transitioning and migrating your platform into a new enterprise environment while maintaining continuity of critical operations.

b. How will your company ensure that existing enterprise functions and capabilities are preserved or enhanced during migration?

c. What strategies, tools, and methodologies do you use to minimize downtime and risk during a migration of this scale?

d. What training approach will you provide to personnel, system administrators, and business stakeholders to ensure successful adoption and operational readiness?

e. Provide an estimated timeline (e.g., phased rollout, pilot to full production) for transition to full production, including training, testing, and deployment.

		7. General Questions

a. How does your platform ensure scalability across a federal enterprise of VA’s size and complexity?

b. Describe your licensing model and how it supports enterprise agreements (ELA).

c. Provide details on security certifications (FedRAMP High, FISMA, HIPAA, etc.).

Responses are due no later than 4PM EST, October 14, 2025 via email to John A Adamitis, Contract Specialist at john.adamitis1@va.gov and Heather Utt, Contracting Officer at heather.utt@va.gov.  Please note “ITSMP” in the subject line of your response.  Mark your response as “Proprietary Information” if the information is considered business sensitive. Introduction: 
This is a Request for Information (RFI) only issued for conducting market research.  Accordingly, this RFI constitutes 
neither a Request for Quote (RFQ)/Request for Proposal (RFP), nor a guarantee that one will be issued by the 
Government in the future; furthermore, it does not commit the Government to contract for any services described 
herein.  The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) is not, at this time, seeking proposals or quotes, and therefore, 
will not accept, review, or evaluate unsolicited proposals or quotes received in response hereto. This notice is not 
to be construed as a commitment on the part of the Government to award a contract, nor does the Government 
intend to pay for any information submitted because of this request.  The Government does not reimburse 
respondents for any costs associated with submission of the information being requested or reimburse expenses 
incurred for responses to this RFI.   
The information provided may be used by VA in developing its acquisition strategy and Performance Work 
Statement (PWS) or Product Description (PD).  Any information submitted by respondents to this RFI is strictly 
voluntary; however, any information received shall become the property of the Government and will not be 
returned to the respondent.  Interested parties are responsible for adequately marking proprietary, restricted, or 
competition sensitive information contained in their response. This is a request for information and does not 
obligate the Government in any way, nor does it commit the Government to any specific course of action. Product 
information, brochures, part numbers, and/or other description information may be included with the submission.   
Requirement: 
This requirement will be for brand name or equal commercial software subscriptions for license entitlements, with 
a focus on reducing overall costs.  VA, Office of Information and Technology (OIT), Infrastructure Operations (IO) IT 
Service Management (ITSM) currently leverages ServiceNow as the OIT Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) tool.  
The following information outlines the current state of the ITSM solution utilized by VA. In an effort to reduce costs, 
we are requesting that industry partners review our existing modules and the utilization of our current tool. We are 
open to the identification and evaluation of alternative tools that can meet our requirements and support the 
mission of the VA. VA requires enterprise licenses that will accommodate the VA userbase of up to 600,000.  
Please see RFI submission instructions below. The Government is also seeking recommendations on the best user 
model, either ala carte and/or unlimited license, to meet the VA’s requirements.  
Today, VA uses ServiceNow in the following mission-critical manners:  ServiceNow is configured to support VA 
service desk operations across the entire enterprise and provide event and incident management for early warning 
and detection of system degradations and service interruptions to prevent outages to critical VA business systems.  
As VA adds clinicians, support staff, and volunteers to meet the needs of increased patient care, the ITSM Tool is 
used to provision all new devices and provide immediate clinical application access for staff.  Veterans Health 
Information Systems and Technology Architecture (VISTA) is the VA’s Electronic Health Record Management 
(EHRM) system.  The ITSM Tool ensures system availability which monitors potential deficiencies in over 30 VISTA 
applications, including those that will be subsequently migrating to the new EHRM platform, called Cerner.  The 
ITSM Tool triages IT-related issues that surface in VA medical devices used by clinicians.  To support burgeoning 
telehealth needs, VA uses the ITSM Tool for clinician credentialing and for immediate system password reset across 
the enterprise for all VA applications, including performing specific application capacity monitoring in support of 
telehealth.  The ITSM Tool monitors the VA network health for the entire workforce.  Its capability can report and 

 
 
triage issues that could disable telehealth workers or otherwise negatively impact all other IT services provided to 
Veterans and their families. 
The OIT ERP tool provides VA with a single service management console to support key stakeholders across the VA 
enterprise including OIT, Veterans Benefits Administration, Veterans Health Administration, and National Cemetery 
Administration. 
Currently, the majority of the existing contract operates under a bundled unlimited license agreement, a user 
model based on a top limit of 750,000 VA users controlling the contract not to exceed.   . We are seeking a more 
structured approach to limit the number of licenses to a maximum of 600,000. VA wants to focus less on growing 
the footprint of the current ITSM tool at the VA and focus more on fully utilizing what we have deployed today. 
The ITSM tool must meet the following requirements: 
 The ITSM Tool must have Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program (FedRAMP) High approval  at 
time of proposal submission. The vendor must provide documentation verifying current FedRAMP authorization, 
including an Authorization to Operate (ATO). For cloud-hosted solutions, the ITSM Tool must be deployed on a 
FedRAMP-authorized cloud service provider. The vender must also demonstrate ongoing compliance with 
FedRAMP continuous monitoring requirements to ensure the security and integrity of federal data.  
 The current tool guarantees a minimum uptime of 99.8%, measured monthly, excluding scheduled 
maintenance. The vendor must provide a Service Level Agreement (SLA) outlining uptime commitments equal to or 
greater (99.8%), incident response times and penalties for non-compliance.  
 The ITSM Tool must allow the VA to track license utilization in real time vis dashboard or other means.  
 Hosting solutions should be provided to include Cloud and On-Premises.  
 The cloud hosting solution must offer secure, scalable cloud=based deployment on a FedRAMP-authorized 
cloud service provider. 
 The current solution is hosted by the license provider, however if an on-premises solution is available resulting 
in cost savings to the VA but as part of the RFI response vendors must provide requirements for deployment on CA 
managed infrastructure.  
 See Attachment A for all currently in production modules in green (owned) that would be required to meet 
capabilities. As mentioned above focus more on fully utilizing what we have deployed today. 
 
Current license utilization is as follows:  
 
The VA currently utilizes the license types listed in the Part Table, with the following license utilization 
requirements. The ITSM tool for this request must match both the license utilization and capabilities. The VA uses a 
total of 25 ServiceNow environments, with seven designated for specific purposes: 2 for Production and 5 for Sub 
Production. The remaining environments are dynamic and used as needed.

Secure Software Attestation: 
The contractor shall comply with M-22-18 when using third-party software on VA information systems or otherwise 
affecting the VA information. M-22-18 requires software producers to self-attest that secure software development 
practices are utilized as outlined by EO 14028 and NIST Guidance. The contractor must provide a self-attestation of 
compliance with these requirements. A third-party assessment provided by either a certified FedRAMP Third Party 
Assessor Organization (3PAO) or one approved by the agency shall be acceptable in lieu of a software producer's 
self-attestation.   This requirement is applicable to new purchases, software renewals, and major version changes. 
Although no documentation is required in response to this RFI, contractors are encouraged to upload attestations 
in advance of the actual solicitation to the CISA RSAA portal available at: https://softwaresecurity.CISA.gov 
 
Section 508 Requirements: 
The Federal Accessibility Law affecting all Information and Communications Technology (ICT) Procurements 
(Section 508) is part of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, which was amended in 1998. It requires that all federal 
agencies ensure their electronic and information technology is accessible to people with disabilities. This means 
that employees and members of the public with disabilities must have access to ICT that is comparable to the 
access available to those without disabilities. 
Please ensure that the provided software solution complies with “508 Chapter 2: Scoping Requirements”. 
Information about these Section 508 standards can be found at Revised 508 Standards and 255 Guidelines (access-
board.gov).

1.0  BACKGROUND 
The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Office of Information and Technology (OIT), 
Infrastructure Operations (IO) Enterprise Service Management (ESM) requires the 
acquisition of cloud-based Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) solution delivered via a 
multi-instance Platform-as-a-Service (PaaS) and Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) 
subscription model. 
 
This requirement supports the VA mission to enhance IT service delivery, strengthen 
operational efficiency, and advance digital transformation across the enterprise. The 
required solution must provide enterprise-wide integration and functionality consistent 
with leading ERP in the marketplace 
 
VA OIT currently leverages a SaaS platform to manage critical enterprise operational 
practices, including enterprise service desk operations, incident and event triage, 
request fulfillment, change enablement, and problem resolution. Additionally, the 
platform supports application provisioning, clinician support, and telehealth availability. 
The SaaS platform is central to maintaining uptime for essential systems, including 
Veterans Health Information Systems and Technology Architecture (VistA) and the new 
Oralce/Cerner Electronic Health Record Management (EHRM) platform. 
 
As demand increases for real-time support, automation, cybersecurity compliance, and 
adaptability to evolving legislative and policy requirements, VA requires acquisition of a 
next-generation ERP solution with capabilities that meet or exceed industry standards 
for federal environments. This solution must span across IT Service Management 
(ITSM), IT Asset Management (ITAM), IT Operations Management (ITOM), IT Business 
Management (ITBM), Human Resource Service Delivery (HRSD), and other service 
domains.

7. Question #7: 
 
“Please confirm whether the requirement for experience supporting earth and 
atmospheric science laboratories is strictly mandatory, or if experience in other scientific 
laboratory environments (e.g., physics, chemistry, or biology labs) demonstrating 
equivalent expertise in instrument integration and scientific software development will be 
considered acceptable. If acceptable, please clarify how equivalency will be evaluated.” 
 
USGS’s Response: Experience supporting earth and atmospheric science 
laboratories is essential to ensure the Contractor is familiar with the type of 
instrumentation and its applications. The U.S. Geological Survey’s Denver Argon 
Geochronology Lab (DAGL) involves highly specialized scientific instruments, 
unique data-acquisition workflows, rigorous environmental controls, and custom 
software ecosystems that are not reasonably comparable to other laboratory 
environments. 
 
8. Question #8: 
 
“Please confirm whether all development activities must be performed onsite at the 
Denver Federal Center, or if a hybrid model (remote development with periodic onsite 
integration/testing) is permissible. If hybrid is allowed, please specify the expected onsite 
frequency and any tasks that must be strictly performed onsite.” 
 
USGS’s Response: The lead developer is expected to be onsite throughout the 
development of the product. The computer system connected to the 
instrumentation is not accessible remotely. 
 
9. Question #9: 
 
“Does the Government have any preferred or existing software architecture frameworks, 
design patterns, or reusable code bases (e.g., from other USGS labs) that the contractor is 
required or encouraged to leverage?” 
 
USGS’s Response: The Contractor will be granted access to a comparable 
LabVIEW package from a similar laboratory for their use.

interface documentation availability for required hardware components (e.g., Argus VI

“Will the contractor have continuous access to all required hardware systems during 
development, or will access be limited or scheduled?”

to Government computer systems.

UNITED STATES DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION (USDOT) 
NATIONAL HIGHWAY TRAFFIC SAFETY ADMINISTRATION (NHTSA) 
  
Synopsis for Solicitation 693JJ926R000032 
 
Crash Investigation Sampling System (CISS) – PSU Operations Center 
Synopsis 
This synopsis is issued in accordance with FAR 5.203(a) to provide a minimum 30-day public 
notice prior to issuance of a solicitation. 
The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) intends to issue a solicitation for 
a Full and Open Competition in support of the National Center for Statistics and Analysis. 
Introduction and Background 
The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) requires contractor support to 
operate and maintain the Primary Sampling Units (PSUs) and the PSU Operations Center for the 
Crash Investigation Sampling System (CISS), a core component of the Agency’s crash data 
collection program.  
CISS provides nationally representative, real-world crash data to support vehicle safety research, 
policy development, rulemaking, and evaluation of safety technologies and programs.  
This requirement supports the continued collection, processing, and quality assurance of crash 
investigation data across the national PSU network.  
Contract Type and NAICS 
NHTSA intends to award a Cost-Plus-Fixed-Fee contract. 
The applicable NAICS code is: 
541990 – All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services 
 
Period of Performance 
The anticipated period of performance is 66 months from date of award, consisting of: 
• One (1) three-year base period 
• Two (2) one-year option periods 
• One (1) six-month option to extend services 
 
The anticipated effective date of the contract is September 27, 2026. 
 
Solicitation Release 
The solicitation is anticipated to be released on or about May 2026. 

2 
 
 
 
 
Objective / Scope of Work 
The objective of this contract is to provide support for the for the PSU Operations Center 
(PSUOC) for NHTSA’s Crash Investigation Sampling System (CISS). This includes operational 
oversight of personnel at the seventy-three (73) CISS PSUs, administrative management of work 
locations, and execution of the standardized crash data collection activities using CISS Data 
Systems.  
The seventy-three (73) PSUs include   sixty-five (65) currently operational and eight (8) 
additional units anticipated to be added in 2027 
System for Award Management (SAM) 
Offerors must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) at www.SAM.gov to 
be eligible for award. 
 
Notice 
THIS NOTICE IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS. This synopsis is for informational 
purposes only and does not constitute a commitment by the Government. 
The solicitation will be posted electronically via http://www.sam.gov. No requests for advance 
copies will be honored. 
Interested parties are responsible for monitoring SAM.gov for updates, amendments, and 
additional information. 
 
Anticipated Award Timing 
The Government anticipates making the award in advance of September 27, 2026, effective date 
to ensure continuity of operations.

1. INTRODUCTION
This Request for Qualifications (RFQ) is for non-personal construction  inspection 
services for all phases of road and bridge projects administered by Central Federal Lands 
Highway Division (CFLHD) of the Federal Highway Administration (FHWA) for 
various Federal Land Management Agencies (FLMA).  CFLHD provides engineering 
and construction services for road and bridge projects for FLMAs and other entities on 
projects in the states of Arizona, California, Colorado, Hawaii, Kansas, Nebraska, 
Nevada, New Mexico, North Dakota, Oklahoma, South Dakota, Texas, Utah, and 
Wyoming. These projects include work on roadways, bridges, and trails which 
encompasses a wide range of work from new projects to rehabilitation of existing 
environments.  
To ensure adequate oversight of ongoing and future projects, and to support the mission 
of the FHWA, the CFLHD intends to procure multiple-award Indefinite Delivery 
Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contracts for construction inspection services.  CFLHD 
anticipates awarding up to five (5) IDIQ contracts for Construction Inspection (CI) 
services.  Projects will primarily involve improvements to rural low-volume roadways in 
environmentally sensitive areas. This RFQ is being issued as an unrestricted competitive 
acquisition in accordance with Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation Overhaul 
(RFO) 6.101, Full and Open Competition with at least one (1) award reserved for a Small 
Business Concern. The NAICS code for this procurement is 541330, Engineering 
Services. All firms responding to this RFQ are required to be licensed to practice 
architect-engineer services (A&E) within one (1) or more of the States served by 
CFLHD, with the capacity to perform CI in all fourteen (14) States  (States are listed 
under Section 4. General Information & Requirements of this RFQ).  
Firm  when used 
in connection with architect-engineer services as defined in 40 U.S.C. 1102, means any 
individual, partnership, corporation, association, or other legal entity permitted by law to 
practice the professions of architecture or engineering and that submits a response to this 
RFQ. 
The Government intends to award the IDIQ contracts with a five-year (i.e. 60 month) 
period of performance, with an option to extend for an additional six (6) months. Each 
task order issued under these contracts will include a defined Statement of Work and will 
be negotiated on an individual basis. The Government does not guarantee the issuance of 
any specific number of task orders or a particular volume of work beyond the stated 
minimum guarantee. 
1.1. Summary of Work 
Firms shall provide construction inspection services that encompass comprehensive 
oversight and quality assurance for highway, road, and bridge projects. These services are 
essential to ensuring that all construction activities adhere to contract specifications, 
engineering standards, and applicable regulatory requirements. Key responsibilities 
include, but are not limited to:

with approved plans, specifications, and safety standards. 
1.1.2. Contract Inspection Support: Assist with documentation, progress tracking, and

1.1.3. Materials Testing Oversight: Observe and report on field and laboratory testing of

These services are performed by experienced personnel who are assigned to project sites 
for short and long-term durations, based on the complexity and schedule of each project. 
Inspectors are required to possess a thorough understanding of federal highway 
construction standards and procedures, particularly those established by the Federal

2. PERSONNEL REQUIREMENTS
2.1. Personnel Classification Overview 
2.1.1. .  The COTA provides on-site 
construction contract oversight and construction inspection within limited 
delegations and delivers day-to-day project engineering and management services 
for the duration of a construction project. The COTA manages and administers all 
assigned work through all phases of the construction project. They serve as the 
principal contact and technical liaison between CFLHD, client agencies, the 
construction contractor, and other project stakeholders, such as landowners and 
resource agencies. The COTA works closely and cooperatively with the 
Contracting Officer (CO), Construction Operations Engineer (COE), Contracting 
Officer's Representative (COR), and the Government Project Engineer to monitor, 
document, and advise on contract actions. Additionally, they oversee project 
inspection staff and prepare final project closeout documentation. The COTA 
performs this work primarily at the project location. 
2.1.2. On-Site Construction Inspector.  The Construction Inspector performs 
construction inspection and technical support duties on construction projects. The 
CI monitors daily construction activities, materials, and workmanship for 
compliance with contract provisions, drawings, and specifications. They conduct 
quality assurance activities, including materials sampling or witnessing, verifying 
construction surveys, and monitoring safety and environmental controls. 
Additionally, they provide administrative and engineering support by maintaining 
detailed daily logs, assisting with progress estimates, assisting with contract 
modifications, and ensuring project records are accurate and complete.  
There are two classification levels for Construction Inspectors
responsibility and requires more advanced experience. Construction Inspectors 
perform their duties primarily at the project site.  
2.1.3. Additional Services. Additional Services encompass specialized consultant 
engineering, inspection, and project management tasks required to support the 
core project team. Personnel in these roles provide targeted expertise for specific 
assignments, including constructability reviews, complex schedule development 
and analysis, contract dispute and claims review, and post-construction records 
inspection. Duties may also include specialized inspection such as 
precast/prestressed concrete inspection at off-site facilities, resource monitoring 
and inspection, forensic engineering, and non-destructive testing.  Because these 
roles address unique project needs, the Government negotiates all such services 
individually based on the specific scope of each assignment. Personnel 
performing these specialized functions may perform this work either on-site or 
off-site as dictated by the task order.

Introduction   
The U.S. Government Publishing Office (GPO), through its Library Services & Content Management 
division (Superintendent of Documents), is gathering information on acquiring, implementing, 
maintaining, and supporting a high-performance integrated library system. The existing ExLibris 
Aleph Integrated Library System (ILS) is essential for GPO’s Library Services & Content 
Management to achieve their mission of improving services for Federal Depository Libraries and 
the public. To enhance these efforts, we are aiming to modernize and upgrade our library system, 
which supports the Catalog of U.S. Government Publications (CGP).
 
 
This information overview outlines the fundamental functional requirements for a replacement 
system designed to meet both current and future workflow needs. It also ensures continued 
support for the mission of Library Services & Content Management. 
 
Background 
Library Services & Content Management (LSCM) aims to inform the American public by managing 
four mandated programs that support federal information lifecycle management across various 
formats: 


U.S. Government Publishing Office Integrated Library System Functional Requirements                                
02/02/26  
 
3 
 
 Federal Depository Library Program 
 Cataloging and Indexing Program 
 International Exchange Service 
 By-Law distribution services 
To improve access to federal information, the Government Publishing Office (GPO) is seeking a 
modern Integrated Library System (ILS) or Library Platform Service (LPS). The current ILS supports 
online services for federal libraries and the public, enabling distribution and preservation of 
government publications for all federal branches. GPO centralizes production and provides 
publications free through the Federal Depository Library Program. 
The ILS enhances public access with features like a web-based catalog, timely publication updates, 
replacement of manual catalog production, and MARC record creation in partnership with OCLC. 
The system is built on Ex-Libris software and hosted on a FedRAMP-certified platform, supporting 
about 500 simultaneous users and maintained via Cloudflare security. 
Aleph software integrates with Oracle database servers across test, production, and disaster 
recovery environments on Red Hat Enterprise Linux. GPO staff manage data using a Windows-
based client; current Aleph tools lack browser-based access for metadata staff. The ILS holds over 
one million records updated daily. 
The Catalog of U.S. Government Publications (CGP) serves as the main tool for finding electronic 
and print publications from all government branches, hosting descriptive records dating back to 
the late 1800s and providing direct links to online materials. 
 
CGP Scope: 
- Bibliographic information for new and historic Government Publications dating back to the 
late 1800s  
- Over one million bibliographic records generated since July 1976 
- Over 275,000 links to official full-text electronic titles 
- Updated daily 
 
CGP Features: 
The staff at GPO are committed to providing access to government documents while ensuring the 
intellectual integrity of the materials. Some of the features provided by the CGP are:  
 Direct links to the official digital version of a publication when available via PURLs 
(Persistent Uniform Resource Locators) 
 A robust search engine with extensive search features including:  
o Multiple search types: Basic, Advanced, Browse, or Expert 
 Boolean 
 Quoted  
 Truncated 
 Parenthetical  
 Common Command Language (CCL) 

U.S. Government Publishing Office Integrated Library System Functional Requirements                                
02/02/26  
 
4 
 
o Instructions for maximizing the effectiveness of each search type 
 Catalogs to Search: curated subsets such as the Congressional Serial Set and Electronic 
Titles 
 New Titles with dedicated Dynamic Searches and Monthly Archive Reports 
 An integrated email feature that enables sending up to 20 records at a time for future use 
 Federal Depository Library Coordinators have access to Z39.50, CGP logged in features such 
as special views, special services such Selective Dissemination of Information (SDI), saving 
and managing records, as well as others. 
 
GPO PURLs: 
Since March 1998, the U.S. Government Publishing Office (GPO) has used Persistent Uniform 
Resource Locators (PURLs) to provide stable links to online Federal resources. If a user clicks on a 
PURL, the request will be routed to the Federal publication. GPO staff modify PURL entries as the 
location of the Federal information changes, and GPO’s PURL server will route traffic to the 
appropriate Web site. GPO staff in our Office of Archival Management (OAM) and Library Technical 
Services (LTS) performs routine maintenance on PURLs and their bibliographic records.  
 
GPO Metadata Standards: 
GPO is the authoritative source for descriptive and subject cataloging for Federal Government 
documents. GPO’s Library Technical Services (LTS) creates bibliographic records that adhere to the 
national and international standards, as well as local GPO guidelines and practices: 
- Resource Description and Access (RDA) 
- Library of Congress-Program for Cooperative Cataloging Policy Statements (LC-PCC PS) 
- Library of Congress Su bject Headings Manual 
- MARC 21 Format for Bibliographic Data 
- MARC 21 Format for Authority Data 
- ANSI/NISO Z39.71-2006 (R2011) Holdings St atements for Bibliographic Items  
- MARC 21 Format for Holdings Data 
- OCLC Bibliographic Formats and Standards 
- Program for Cooperative Cataloging (PCC) gu idelines (including BIBCO, CONSER, NACO, 
and SACO) 
- GPO Cataloging Guidelines 
- Other standards as appropriate 
- Also working towards using BIBFRAME 
 
In October 2017, GPO started posting cataloging records on its GitHub repository. The CGP on 
GitHub is a location where users may freely download record sets extracted from the CGP. MARC 
record files are offered in UTF-8, MARC-8, and MARCXML formats.  
 
Through 2021, the ILS integrated with our Federal Depository Library Directory (FDLD), which was 
managed as a service of the CGP as an independent MySQL database that interfaces with the CGP to 
create and maintain accounts for the over 1,000 FDLs.  It also, provided the ability to Locate 
Libraries via an integrated link contained within the bibliographic record which opens a search 
interface that imports the title and GPO Item Number from the bibliographic record allowing the 

U.S. Government Publishing Office Integrated Library System Functional Requirements                                
02/02/26  
 
5 
 
user to search by City or State to locate their nearest FDL.  The "Locate a Library" feature within 
each record allowed users to find a nearby Federal depository where a particular publication or 
expert assistance could be found. 
 
Objective 
This procurement seeks a modern, sustainable technical solution to upgrade the library system, 
supporting GPO’s goals of improved processes, enhanced security, and legacy system elimination 
in a cost-effective way. 
The required system is an online, real-time platform with a graphical interface for catalog access to 
all print and digital materials, including external electronic databases. It Should be interoperable 
with other systems, hosted on a FedRAMP-certified platform or SaaS, offer geographically 
separated backups, and support Test, Development, Production, and Disaster Recovery 
environments.

6. Rationale Justifying Use of Cited Statutory Authority: This acquisition must be limited to 
Camunda Enterprise because it is essential to our operations. We have a significant investment in the 
Camunda platform, which currently runs . These systems were built 
using Camunda's proprietary software, so they cannot be moved to another platform. Switching would 
force a complete and costly redevelopment of , essentially wasting prior investments. 
This process would also cause unacceptable delays and disrupt vital support to our mission. Therefore, 
to save money, maintain efficiency, and avoid mission disruption, sticking with the Camunda brand is 
the only practical solution to meet DFAS needs. 
 
 
7. Description of Efforts Made to Solicit Offers from as Many Offerors as Practicable: An RFI was 
posted to determine the interested vendor base on January 26, 2026, and closed on February 4, 2026, 
which resulted in a response from  interested vendors. None of the responses had a current 
agreement with Camunda.  
 
 
8. A Short Description of the Results of RFI Posting, Or Market Research Conducted, or a 
Statement of the Reason Non of the Above Actions Were Conducted.  
Market research was initiated through two Requests for Information (RFIs) to identify potential 
vendors for Camunda software licenses. The first, GSA RFI, received  responses but ultimately 
confirmed that no 8(a) companies held a current reseller agreement with Camunda. A separate RFI on 
NASA SEWP yielded  response from  
. Following the RFIs, direct contact with Camunda revealed that only  
vendors are authorized to resell Camunda licenses to the government:  
  Because 
 of the  authorized resellers are SDVOSBs, the decision was made to set this contract aside 
specifically for SDVOSB competition. 
 
 
9. List of the Sources that Expressed a Written Interest in the Acquisition.  
 
 
 
10. Any Other Facts Supporting the Use of Other Than Full and Open Competition: N/A 
 
 
11. A Statement of the Actions, if any, the Agency May Take to Remove or Overcome any Barriers 
to Competition Before any Subsequent Acquisition for the Supplies Required.  
In order to remove or overcome barriers to competition in future acquisitions for this requirement, the 
agency will work with the program office to conduct market research to ascertain if there are changes 
in the marketplace that would enable future actions to be competed on other than a brand name basis. 
 
 
12.  DETERMINATION OF FAIR AND REASONABLE COST: The contracting officer will 
determine that the anticipated cost to the Government of the service/supplies covered by this 
justification will be fair and reasonable.
