Description/Specifications/Statement of Work
A.1        SCOPE
This Description of Need (DON) defines the requirement for the procurement of brand-name Camunda Enterprise 
Edition software licenses and associated annual maintenance and technical success services. The purpose of this 
acquisition is to ensure the continuity of service for the agency's standardized Business Process Management 
(BPM) platform. In 2021, the agency selected and invested in the Camunda platform to automate and manage 
critical business processes. This procurement is a direct follow-on action to maintain the operational status of these 
existing systems and leverage the significant prior investment in technology, development, and personnel training.
 
The scope of this requirement includes the following: 
Software Licensing:
Procurement of Camunda Enterprise Edition software licenses is sufficient to support the agency's 
production, staging, and development environments.
Software Maintenance:
Access to all new versions, releases, security patches, and software updates for the Camunda 
platform to ensure it remains secure and up to date.
Technical Success Support:
Access to enterprise-level technical support from Camunda's subject matter experts to assist with 
troubleshooting, configuration, and best practices.
 
A.2       BACKGROUND 
The DFAS Portal Workflows team plays a critical role in driving efficiency and automation across the organization, 
supporting 29 distinct workflows that encompass a potential user base of up to 30,000 individuals. To further 
enhance its process automation capabilities, DFAS strategically selected Camunda Enterprise as its enterprise-wide 
solution in 2021. This acquisition will ensure continued support, modernization, and scalability of the Camunda 
Enterprise environment, including migration to Azure Government Cloud.
 
A.3      REQUIREMENTS
The Contractor shall provide the following brand-name Camunda Enterprise Edition software licenses, software 
maintenance, and technical success support.

FLAG SECRETARY OFFICE AND OFFICIAL FUNCTION SUPPORT SERVICES 
 
1.0 INTRODUCTION 
 
This performance work statement (PWS) identifies and defines the service requirements for the Flag 
Secretary Office and Official Function support services requirements for the Commander Naval Air 
Force U. S. Pacific Fleet (COMNAVAIRPAC/CNAP) San Diego, CA. 
 
2.0 BACKGROUND 
 
The Flag Secretary Office coordinates the administrative activities of the CNAP Staff as well as the 
management and oversight of CNAP headquarters facilities. This office is the primary focal 
point/liaison with Navy Public Works in the maintenance and upkeep of CNAP buildings. The office 
is also responsible for staff engraving and graphic design requests, and for the oversight, planning 
and coordination of official CNAP Command events.  
 
The Flag Mess prepares and serves over 1,000 meals per month to the CNAP staff, and provides 
mess support services for a minimum twelve (12) Official Flag Functions/Events each year. The Flag 
Mess is staffed by five to six Culinary Specialists (CS’s), E-6 and below, and falls under the 
oversight of the Flag Secretary. The number of personnel assigned to work CNAP Official 
events/functions varies, depending on the event. This work statement encompasses tasks necessary to 
provide official functions and events menu planning, and ceremonial and reception material 
warehouse management support services. 
 
3.0 SCOPE 
 
The objective of this order is to obtain the requisite level of expertise for performance of the tasks 
defined in the Section 4 of this work statement. The Contractor shall provide qualified and 
experienced personnel capable of providing the services described herein. 
 
4.0 PERFORMANCE REQUIREMENTS 
 
The contractor shall perform the following tasks in accomplishing the requirements of this contract. 
The contractor shall provide the necessary timely assistance to meet emergent requirements as 
requested by properly designated authority. 
 
4.1 CNAP FLAG SECRETARY OFFICE SUPPORT SERVICES – FACILITIES 
LIASION/ENGRAVING/GRAPHIC DESIGN 
 
4.1.1 Coordinate and/or perform minor general maintenance to include but not be limited to the 
repair and/or replacement and hanging and/or installation of light bulbs and fixtures. 
 
4.1.2 Submit trouble calls through the Public Works Department for all 13 buildings that are under 
the cognizance of the CNAP Flag Secretary. These trouble calls will include, but are not limited to, 
locksmith, landscaping, electrical, plumbing, carpentry, pest control, sanitation problems, recycling, 

 
 
and hazardous material and waste disposal. A list of buildings and map of their location is provided 
as Attachment A. 
 
4.1.3 Maintain safety requirements in accordance with Naval Base Coronado Fire Marshall directives 
by performing quarterly and semi-annual review/inspections of fire extinguishers, and heat producing 
devices; ensure requisite permits are obtained and properly displayed. 
 
4.1.4 Maintain custodial control of 13 Government Vehicles used by CNAP staff personnel. The 
contractor shall maintain a database identifying tag number of vehicles assigned to the Command, the 
responsible department, and the mileage. 
 
4.1.5 Prepare complete sets of drawings, which include multiple views, detail drawings, and 
assembly drawings. Drawings are required for CNAP official ceremonies and programs such as 
Change of Command Programs, Battle of Midway Ceremony, Retirement Programs, Retired 
Aviation Flag Officers Symposium, Prospective Commanding Officer and Executive Officer 
Conferences, Commanders Conferences, Award Ceremonies, Heritage Months Flyers, CFC/Navy 
Relief Campaigns Posters and other events as required by the Flag Secretary or Protocol offices. The 
contractor will work from sketches, models, and verbal information supplied by designer to 
determine the most appropriate views, detail drawings, and supplementary information needed to 
complete assignments. The contractor selects required information from precedents, manufacturers' 
catalogs, and technical guides. 
 
4.1.6 Expedite engraving requests exclusively for CNAP staff. 
 
4.1.7 Provide setup/breakdown services of equipment and facilities used for CNAP official events 
held at Quarters A, Sea Cabin or CNAP Headquarters Building 8; reserve vehicles through Public 
Works Department as requested by Flag Secretary Office. Schedule of anticipated CNAP Official 
Functions/Events for each year is provided in Table 4.5 of this work statement. 
 
4.1.8 Issue, setup and break-down ceremonial gear in support of all official formal CNAP staff 
functions and ceremonies as required by the Flag Secretary or Protocol Officers. The contractor shall 
obtain and coordinate approval for use of ceremonial gear with CNAP N412 prior to issue and setup. 
 
4.2 OFFICIAL FUNCTIONS AND EVENTS MENU PLANNING 
 
4.2.1 For each official function/event listed in 4.5, the contractor shall create a menu, budget, and 
table and seating layout. All documents are to be submitted to N41 representative for review, who 
will then forward drafts to CNAP Protocol Office to be submitted to Chief of Staff (COS) and the 
Admiral for approval. The planning process begins 30-120 days prior to the official function/event 
and involves the following: 
 
4.2.1.1 Pre-planning meeting with Protocol Office, Flag Secretary, and Code N41 representative to 
determine estimated number of guests, budget, and vision for the vent, such as theme and type of 
dinner/reception (i.e. formal, stand-up, buffet). 
 
4.2.2 Conduct a final review of menu, budget, and table and seating layout with Protocol Office 14 
days prior to the official function/event. Adjustments will be made based on number of RSVP’s, and 
a final budget will be approved by the Protocol Office. The number of guests will vary from 12 to 
1,500 depending on the official function/event. 

 
 
4.2.2.1 Prepare grocery lists based on the final approved menu, budget, and table and seating layout, 
to include recommended sources of supply for review and purchase by CNAP N41. 
 
4.2.2.2 Standard preparation of formal meals consists of five courses plus a minimum of two 
appetizers. 
 
4.2.2.3 Standard preparation for stand-up or buffet receptions consists of two protein dishes, two 
vegetable/fruit dishes, two starch side dishes to complement the protein dishes, two-to-three choices 
for deserts, and beverage selection (the contractor will not be responsible for providing 
meals/beverages as part of this requirement). 
 
4.2.3 Complete the “AIRPAC Event Checklist” spreadsheet for each official function/event, 
identifying event name, date, time, place, number of guests, food, equipment (e.g. tables, tents, 
chairs, lighting, heaters, grills, service ware, serving dishes, etc.), linens, manpower, and 
consumables (e.g. towels, soap, trash bags, etc.) needed for the event and commensurate with the 
number of guests. Above listed items will be provided by the Government. 
 
4.2.4 Ten to fifteen days (10-15) prior to smaller events with fewer than 100 guests, the contractor 
shall create recipes for the approved menu items and demonstrate proper food handling, sanitation, 
preparation, presentation, set-up, and service to CNAP staff Culinary Specialists (CS’s) and assigned 
working personnel. Historically, there are five to six CS’s and five to ten non-CS working party 
personnel. The referenced CSs and non-CSs personnel will be provided by the Government. 
 
4.2.5 Twenty-one to forty-five (21-45) days prior to larger events with more than 100 guests, the 
contractor shall create recipes for the approved menu items and demonstrate proper food handling, 
sanitation, preparation, presentation, set-up, and service to CNAP staff Culinary Specialists (CS’s) 
and assigned working personnel. Historically, maximum 20 CS’s and 50 non-CS working party 
personnel. The referenced CSs and non-CSs personnel will be provided by the Government. 
 
4.2.6 Breakout ceremonial/reception equipment, linens, and consumables stowed in building 273 
needed for the event, and transport to location on day of function/event. 
 
4.2.6.1 Assist with the breakdown, cleaning, and re-stowing of equipment at the end of each event. 
 
4.2.7 Provide table layout to lead military representative designated by CNAP Protocol Office to 
oversee the event; assist in the set-up and break-down of tables, chairs, tents, equipment, etc. 
 
4.2.8 Check for compliance with NAVMED P5010: Food Service Sanitation, and make 
recommendations for corrections to the designated military representative to ensure safety and 
sanitation standards in kitchens, dining room, food preparation, and storage areas are being met. 
 
4.3 CEREMONIAL AND RECEPTION MATERIAL WAREHOUSE MANAGEMENT 
 
4.3.1 Conduct initial wall-to-wall inventory upon assumption of duties, and provide a written report 
of inventory results to CNAP N41. Initial CDRL deadline is within 30 days of contract award then 
semi-annually thereafter. 
 

 
 
4.3.2 Issue ceremonial and reception material to CNAP Aircraft Carriers, Air Wings, and squadrons 
located at NAS North Island upon receipt of CNAP N41 approved request. (Approximately one 
approved request per week). 
 
4.3.3 Inventory items, inspect, and evaluate reception and ceremonial gear for serviceability upon 
return of material from subordinate CNAP commands and official function/events, and make 
recommendations for repair or replacement to CNAP N41. (Approximately once a week). 
 
4.3.3.1 Identify and recommend sources of supply for new and replacement ceremonial and reception

Scope of Work: Structural Evaluation and Installation of Pharmacy Carousels

Project Overview

This scope outlines the structural evaluation and installation of two new pharmacy carousels (approx. 13,300 lbs. each) at the VA Medical Center. The evaluation will determine the adequacy of the existing structural system to support the equipment, and the installation will be performed in compliance with VA TIL specifications, including applicable design, safety, and construction standards.

1. Objectives

Evaluate the structural capacity of existing elevated slabs, beams, columns, and foundations at the designated location.

Install two pharmacy carousels in accordance with VA TIL specifications, ensuring proper anchorage, alignment, and integration with existing infrastructure.

Ensure compliance with VA PG 18-10 Structural Design Manual (July 1, 2023) and other applicable codes and standards.

2. Scope of Services

2.1 Kick-Off Meeting

Conduct an initial meeting with the Client to: 

Confirm project scope and objectives.

Review equipment specifications and location plans.

Define analysis and installation requirements.

2.2 Structural Evaluation

Review available record drawings and documentation.

Analyze the structural adequacy of: 

Elevated slabs.

Supporting beams.

Vertical columns.

Foundation system.

Evaluate load paths, bearing capacities, and deflection limits.

Identify any required structural reinforcements.

2.3 Installation of Pharmacy Carousels

Coordinate delivery and staging of carousel equipment.

Install carousels at designated location per VA TIL specifications, including: 

PG 18-3 Design and Construction Procedures.

PG 18-4 Standard Details and Specifications.

VA Master Construction Specifications (e.g., Division 11 – Equipment).

Ensure proper anchorage, leveling, and alignment.

Verify installation meets safety, accessibility, and operational requirements.

Coordinate with VA facility staff to minimize disruption to operations.

2.4 Standards and Codes

All work will comply with: 

PG-18-10: VA Structural Design Manual (July 1, 2023)

Purpose: Provides structural design criteria for VA facilities.

Relevant Sections: 

Live Load Requirements: Ensure the slab and supporting structure can handle the 13,300 lb. equipment load.

Deflection Limits: Must meet serviceability criteria for vibration and deflection.

Anchorage Requirements: Guidelines for anchoring heavy equipment to concrete slabs.

Seismic Considerations: If applicable, anchorage must meet seismic design criteria.

VA TIL specifications.

IBC, ACI, ASCE, and NFPA standards.

2.5 Reporting

Submit an electronic report summarizing: 

Structural analysis and findings.

Installation procedures and verification.

Recommendations and compliance documentation.

3. Assumptions

Equipment specifications and location will be provided by the Client.

Evaluation and installation are limited to a single location and specific equipment model.

Additional models or locations may be added via contract modification.

4. Exclusions

The following services are excluded from this scope and fee:

Development of full construction documents (drawings/specifications).

Evaluation of building areas outside the designated location.

Site investigations to verify record drawing accuracy.

Selection of alternative equipment.

Material testing (e.g., concrete sampling).

Design of structural reinforcements, if required (may be added via modification).

5. Deliverables

One (1) electronic structural evaluation and installation report in PDF format.

Summary of findings, installation verification, and compliance documentation.

Supporting calculations and references to applicable codes.

6. Schedule

Kick-off meeting: Within 5 business days of NTP.

Structural evaluation: Within 15 business days of receiving all required information.

Installation: To be scheduled upon completion of evaluation and approval by VA.

  (a) Inspection/Acceptance. The Contractor shall only tender for acceptance those items that conform to the requirements of this contract. The Government reserves the right to inspect or test any supplies or services that have been tendered for acceptance. The Government may require repair or replacement of nonconforming supplies or reperformance of nonconforming services at no increase in contract price. If repair/replacement or reperformance will not correct the defects or is not possible, the Government may seek an equitable price reduction or adequate consideration for acceptance of nonconforming supplies or services.  The Government must exercise its post-acceptance rights—

    (1) Within a reasonable time after the defect was discovered or should have been discovered; and

    (2) Before any substantial change occurs in the condition of the item, unless the change is due to the defect in the item.

  (b) Assignment. The Contractor or its assignee may assign its rights to receive payment due as a result of performance of this contract to a bank, trust company, or other financing institution, including any Federal lending agency in accordance with the Assignment of Claims Act (31 U.S.C. 3727). However, when a third party makes payment (e.g., use of the Governmentwide commercial purchase card), the Contractor may not assign its rights to receive payment under this contract.

  (d) Disputes. This contract is subject to 41 U.S.C. chapter 71, Contract Disputes. The Contractor shall proceed diligently with performance of this contract, pending final resolution of any dispute arising under the contract.

  (e) Definitions. The clause at FAR 52.202-1, Definitions, is incorporated herein by reference.

  (f) Excusable delays. The Contractor shall be liable for default unless nonperformance is caused by an occurrence beyond the reasonable control of the Contractor and without its fault or negligence such as, acts of God or the public enemy, acts of the Government in either its sovereign or contractual capacity, fires, floods, epidemics, quarantine restrictions, strikes, unusually severe weather, and delays of common carriers. The Contractor shall notify the Contracting Officer in writing as soon as it is reasonably possible after the commencement of any excusable delay, setting forth the full particulars in connection therewith, shall remedy such occurrence with all reasonable dispatch, and shall promptly give written notice to the Contracting Officer of the cessation of such occurrence.

  (g) Invoice.

    (1) The Contractor shall submit an original invoice and three copies (or electronic invoice, if authorized) to the address designated in the contract to receive invoices. An invoice must include—

      (i) Name and address of the Contractor;

      (ii) Invoice date and number;

      (iii) Contract number, line item number and, if applicable, the order number;

      (iv) Description, quantity, unit of measure, unit price and extended price of the items delivered;

      (v) Shipping number and date of shipment, including the bill of lading number and weight of shipment if shipped on Government bill of lading;

      (vi) Terms of any discount for prompt payment offered;

      (vii) Name and address of official to whom payment is to be sent;

      (viii) Name, title, and phone number of person to notify in event of defective invoice; and

      (ix) Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN). The Contractor shall include its TIN on the invoice only if required elsewhere in this contract.

      (x) Electronic funds transfer (EFT) banking information.

        (A) The Contractor shall include EFT banking information on the invoice only if required elsewhere in this contract.

        (B) If EFT banking information is not required to be on the invoice, in order for the invoice to be a proper invoice, the Contractor shall have submitted correct EFT banking information in accordance with the applicable solicitation provision, contract clause (e.g., 52.232-33, Payment by Electronic Funds Transfer—System for Award Management, or 52.232-34, Payment by Electronic Funds Transfer—Other Than System for Award Management), or applicable agency procedures.

        (C) EFT banking information is not required if the Government waived the requirement to pay by EFT.

    (2) Invoices will be handled in accordance with the Prompt Payment Act (31 U.S.C. 3903) and Office of Management and Budget (OMB) prompt payment regulations at 5 CFR part 1315.

  (h) Patent indemnity. The Contractor shall indemnify the Government and its officers, employees and agents against liability, including costs, for actual or alleged direct or contributory infringement of, or inducement to infringe, any United States or foreign patent, trademark or copyright, arising out of the performance of this contract, provided the Contractor is reasonably notified of such claims and proceedings.

  (i) Payment.—

    (1) Items accepted. Payment shall be made for items accepted by the Government that have been delivered to the delivery destinations set forth in this contract.

    (2) Prompt payment. The Government will make payment in accordance with the Prompt Payment Act (31 U.S.C. 3903) and prompt payment regulations at 5 CFR part 1315.

    (3) Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT). If the Government makes payment by EFT, see 52.212-5(b) for the appropriate EFT clause.

    (4) Discount. In connection with any discount offered for early payment, time shall be computed from the date of the invoice. For the purpose of computing the discount earned, payment shall be considered to have been made on the date which appears on the payment check or the specified payment date if an electronic funds transfer payment is made.

    (5) Overpayments. If the Contractor becomes aware of a duplicate contract financing or invoice payment or that the Government has otherwise overpaid on a contract financing or invoice payment, the Contractor shall—

      (i) Remit the overpayment amount to the payment office cited in the contract along with a description of the overpayment including the—

        (A) Circumstances of the overpayment (e.g., duplicate payment, erroneous payment, liquidation errors, date(s) of overpayment);

        (B) Affected contract number and delivery order number, if applicable;

        (C) Affected line item or subline item, if applicable; and

        (D) Contractor point of contact.

      (ii) Provide a copy of the remittance and supporting documentation to the Contracting Officer.

    (6) Interest.

      (i) All amounts that become payable by the Contractor to the Government under this contract shall bear simple interest from the date due until paid unless paid within 30 days of becoming due. The interest rate shall be the interest rate established by the Secretary of the Treasury as provided in 41 U.S.C. 7109, which is applicable to the period in which the amount becomes due, as provided in (i)(6)(v) of this clause, and then at the rate applicable for each six-month period as fixed by the Secretary until the amount is paid.

      (ii) The Government may issue a demand for payment to the Contractor upon finding a debt is due under the contract.

      (iii) Final decisions. The Contracting Officer will issue a final decision as required by 33.211 if—

        (A) The Contracting Officer and the Contractor are unable to reach agreement on the existence or amount of a debt within 30 days;

        (B) The Contractor fails to liquidate a debt previously demanded by the Contracting Officer within the timeline specified in the demand for payment unless the amounts were not repaid because the Contractor has requested an installment payment agreement; or

        (C) The Contractor requests a deferment of collection on a debt previously demanded by the Contracting Officer (see 32.607-2).

      (v) Amounts shall be due at the earliest of the following dates:

        (A) The date fixed under this contract.

        (B) The date of the first written demand for payment, including any demand for payment resulting from a default termination.

      (vi) The interest charge shall be computed for the actual number of calendar days involved beginning on the due date and ending on—

        (A) The date on which the designated office receives payment from the Contractor;

        (B) The date of issuance of a Government check to the Contractor from which an amount otherwise payable has been withheld as a credit against the contract debt; or

GENERAL INFORMATION

CONTACT INFORMATION

DESCRIPTION

PRESOLICITATION NOTICE

Request for Architectural and Engineer (A/E) 330 submission

Solicitation:  

Replace Roofs of Bldg 1, Project No. 589-26-133

CONTRACT INFORMATION

This A-E Services requirement is being procured in accordance with the Brooks Act (Public Law (PL0582) and implemented in accordance with the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Subpart 36.  Firms will be selected based on demonstrated competence and qualifications for the required work.  

This procurement is restricted to Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) firms. This requirement is being procured in accordance with FAR Subpart 36.6.

This is not a Request for Proposal and an award will not be made with this announcement. This announcement is a request for SF 330’s from qualified Architectural and Engineer (A&E) contractors that meet the professional requirements.  

The selection criteria for this acquisition will be in accordance with FAR 36.602-1 and are listed below. All factors are listed in descending order of importance. The completed SF 330 will be evaluated by the Kansas City VA Medical Center Evaluation Board in accordance with FAR 36.602-3 and the selection report shall serve as the final selection list, which will be provided directly to the Contracting Officer.  The Government will not pay nor reimburse any costs associated with responding to this request. The Government is under no obligation to award a contract as a result of this announcement. 

Award of any resultant contract is contingent upon the availability of funds.

No solicitation document is available and no other information pertaining to project scope, etc. is available at this time. Any request for assistance with submission or other procedural matters shall be submitted to Matt Finley via e-mail to: matthew.finley@va.gov. Personal visits to discuss this announcement will not be allowed.

The NAICS Code for this procurement is 541330 Engineering Services and small business size standard of $25.5 M.  

Award of a Firm Fixed Price contract is anticipated. Anticipated time for completion of design is approximately 297 calendar days including time for VA reviews. The A/E firm shall also be required to perform construction services if award of a construction project contract is made.

In accordance with FAR 36.204, the estimated magnitude of the construction project being designed is anticipated to be between $1,000,000, and $5,000,000. 

DATABASE REGISTRATION INFORMATION:

VERIFICATION OF STATUS OF APPARENTLY SUCCESSFUL OFFEROR. THIS ACQUISITION IS 100% SET-ASIDE FOR QUALIFIED SERVICE-DISABLED VETERAN OWNED SMALL BUSINESS AE FIRMS IN COMPLIANCE WITH VAAR 852.219-73 ONLY BUSINESSES VERIFIED AND LISTED AS  CERTIFIED IN THE SBA CERTIFICATION DATABASE AT https://veterans.certify.sba.gov, SHALL BE CONSIDERED.

SYSTEM FOR AWARD MANAGEMENT (SAM):

Federal Acquisition Registrations require that federal contractors register in the System for Award Management (SAM) database at www.sam.gov and enter all mandatory information into the system. Award cannot be made until the contractor has registered. Offerors are encouraged to ensure that they are registered in SAM prior to submitting their qualifications package.

THE EXCLUDED PARTIES LIST SYSTEM (EPLS):

To ensure that the individuals providing services under the contract have not engaged in fraud or abuse regarding Sections 1128 and 1128A of the Social Security Act regarding federal health care programs, the contractor is required to check the Excluded Parties List System (EPLS) located at www.sam.gov for each person providing services under this contract. Further the contractor is required to certify that all persons listed in the qualifications package have been compared against the EPLS list and are NOT listed. During the performance of this contract the Contractor is prohibited from using any individual or business listed on the List of Excluded Individuals/Entities.

PROJECT INFORMATION

The mission of the Veterans Affairs Kansas City VA Medical Center is to provide the highest quality health care to our nation’s veterans. In order to accomplish this mission Kansas City Facility Engineering Service (FES) intends to partner with an Architect/Engineer (A/E) or Engineer Firm for a design completion for Project 589-26-133, Replace Roofs for Building 1.

General Statement: 

The U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) is seeking Architectural and Engineering (A/E) services to develop comprehensive, stand-alone Construction Documents, Reports, and Specifications for Project 589-26-133: Roof Replacement for Building 1, at the Kansas City VA Medical Center.

This project specifically involves replacing the roofing system on the 11th floor of Building 1. The scope of work includes, but is not limited to:

Removal and reinstallation of rooftop units, conduits, piping, and solar panels

Removal, reinstallation, and certification of the lightning protection system

Potential installation of fall protection railings to meet current design and code requirements

Possible removal of non-operational or abandoned equipment located on the roof

PAST PERFORMANCE 

Submitters will be evaluated on past performance on recent and relevant contracts with Government agencies (emphasis on VA work) and private industry in terms of construction cost estimating, cost control, quality of work, compliance with performance schedules and a record of significant claims against the firm due to improper or incomplete engineering services (references required).  Project past performances that are older than 10 years will receive a lesser rating than those references for projects accomplished within the past 10 years. ESTIMATING EFFECTIVENESS

Provide information on the five (5) most recently awarded construction projects that were designed by this A/E team.  Provide the project title, brief scope of work, A/E team’s construction estimate total and actual construction award price.

If the team does not have any recent projects, provide the same information on projects that the prime A/E for this team was the prime A/E for the past projects.  Provide the names, titles and experience of the persons that will perform the design for each discipline; and then has oversight of the entire estimate.

CLAIMS, TERMINATIONS, AND LITIGATION

Claims and Terminations: record of significant claims against the firm or terminated contracts because of improper or incomplete architectural and engineering services will be examined.  Provide information on any litigation involvement of the past five (5) years and the outcome or confirm no claims or terminations exist.

STATEMENT OF WORK  
 
 
1. Objective/Requirements 
The NASA Goddard Space Flight Center (GSFC) requires the purchase of Battelle 
NEON Research Support Services (NRSS) to support mission-critical atmospheric 
and ecological research activities. 
 
 
2. Characteristics, Scope, and Specs 
 
Requirement is for Battelle NEON Research Support Services (NRSS). 
 
The vendor, Battelle Memorial Institute, shall provide the Battelle NEON Research 
Support Services (NRSS) with the following requirements: 
 
Scope of Work 
 
Battelle shall provide full operations and maintenance support for AERONET sun 
photometers (CIMEL CE-318N) deployed at 36 NEON-operated field sites and two 
NEON facilities. The purpose of this effort is to ensure uninterrupted data collection and 
near real-time data transfer to the AERONET data system during the Period of 
Performance specified herein. Services include routine preventive and corrective 
maintenance, minor repairs, instrument calibrations, and associated data handling in 
accordance with established NEON operational processes and standard procedures. 
 
 Operations and monitoring: Support continuous operation of CIMEL CE-318N 
instruments at 36 NEON-operated field sites and two NEON facilities, including 
routine monitoring of instrument status and data flow. 
 Preventive maintenance: Perform scheduled inspections, cleaning, and routine 
upkeep in accordance with established NEON operational processes and standard 
operating procedures. 
 Corrective maintenance and minor repairs: Troubleshoot operational issues, 
replace consumables and minor components as needed, and restore instruments to 
nominal operation. 
 Calibration support: Coordinate CIMEL calibrations with AERONET in 
accordance with approved workflows, including instrument handling and 
shipping/receiving coordination, transfer of standard calibrations, and required 
documentation. 
 Data handling and transfer: Ensure CIMEL raw observation data are transmitted 
from field systems to the NEON cyberinfrastructure and subsequently transferred 
to AERONET in near real-time, subject to network and communications 
availability. 
 Incident and outage response: Respond to data transfer interruptions, instrument 
outages, and configuration changes affecting data continuity or quality, and 
coordinate resolution with AERONET within mutually agreed timeframes.

SOURCES SOUGHT/REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) 
 
DEPARTMENT OF HOMELAND SECURITY/UNITED STATES SECRET SERVICE 
OFFICE OF TRAINING/JAMES J. ROWLEY TRAINING CENTER/ 
SPECIALTY PROGRAM BRANCH 
 
This notice constitutes a Request for Information (RFI) Pursuant to Federal Acquisition 
Regulation (FAR) Part 15.201 for the purpose of determining the capability of sources in the 
marketplace for a contemplated effort for an Autonomous Robotic Training System tailored for 
law enforcement shooting and tactical response training applications. This RFI is for 
procurement planning purposes only and shall not be construed as a request for proposal/quote, 
solicitation, or commitment on the part of the Government to issue any future solicitation or 
award. The Government will not reimburse any costs associated with the development and 
submission of materials in response to this request. 
 
The contemplated effort would be a firm fixed price with a one-year base period and four one-
year option periods. The estimate of ($9.9 million total contract value). The North American 
Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this requirement is NAICS: 541330 
 
Responses must show demonstrated, recent, and relevant experience in the areas of defining the 
capabilities and support requirements necessary for a comprehensive autonomous robotic 
training solution by providing technical, logistical, and cost information to inform the future 
acquisition actions. 
 
• One (1) Autonomous Robotic System, including: 
• Eight (8) All-Terrain Autonomous Robot Infantry Targets  
• One (1) Autonomous Robotic Vehicle Target   
• Four (4) CQB Autonomous Robotic Infantry Targets 
 
All targets listed above should have the following features: real time response in live fire 
scenarios to include flinching, audio response when hit, ease of use for indoor and outdoor 
environments, ability to perform tasks such as patrolling information, scattering to cover, chasing 
other fleeing targets, attacking a position using bounding techniques, or be programmed to act as 
a single robotic opposing force, with hit detection & hit indication. The targets should also have 
ballistic protection from various ammunition calibers.  
 
Command and Control: 
Three (3) Command and Control Stations - capable of managing multiple robotic assets 
simultaneously 
 
Communication and Range Extension 
Two (2) Communication Range Extension Kits, to ensure reliable communication across varied 
operational environments 
 
Support Equipment: 
 One (1) Smart Range Trailer for mobile training operations 

 One (1) T100-Hundred Transportation Trailer for transportation and deployment of robotic 
assets 
 
Support Services 
  - Vendor operators for robotic targets based on the James J. Rowley Training Center 
  - Comprehensive training for personnel 
  - Maintenance and technical support as needed 
  - System integration and customization services 
  - Spare parts and consumables 
  - Maintenance logs (routine and emergency) and remediations for robotic targets 
 
The Contractor must also demonstrate/describe recent (within the last 5 years) and relevant 
experience in the following areas in addition to the supply of the physical target system noted 
above: 
 
Full-time support at the location for all operational requirements. 
Ongoing warranty, software upgrades, and spares 
Operation and maintenance of the robots and associated equipment 
All software upgrades, 
All spares and maintenance, 
Ongoing warranty, and on-premises support 
 
For the contemplated effort, the Contractor will be required to provide: 
 
- Technical specifications and capabilities 
- System interoperability features 
- Deployment and operational considerations 
- Estimated costs and pricing structure 
- Lead times and delivery schedules 
- Past performance and references 
- Support and maintenance plans 
 
If demonstrating any of the aforementioned requires reference to specific contracts, indicate 
those contract numbers respective to each capability example described, to include a point of 
contact for each referenced contract.  Should there be teaming or subcontracting arrangements 
referenced, identification of specific contract numbers will be required for those arrangements as 
well. If the services demonstrated were performed for a private vendor, please also provide for 
such requirements a verifying reference. 
 
All interested parties are invited to submit a capabilities statement, which shall not exceed three 
(3) total pages and no smaller than 12 point Times New Roman font.  
 
The capability statement should demonstrate understanding, capability, approach, qualification, 
and past experience in meeting the work requirements identified in Attachment # 1, Draft 
Performance Work Statement. Finally, interested firms should identify challenges and risks 
associated with meeting the requirements of the Summary Scope of Work and how the 

organization would minimize those risks. The Government will review the capability statement 
to determine if the interested firm is capable of satisfying the requirements based on its 
demonstrated understanding, capability, approach, qualification, and past experience in each of 
the areas included in the Draft Performance Work Statement (Attachment #1). Please note that a 
small business concern may submit a capability statement that includes the expertise of a large 
business partner under a teaming arrangement. If a teaming arrangement is contemplated, then 
the response to this notice must clearly discuss the areas of the Draft Performance Work 
Statement that the small business firm intends to perform and the specific areas that the large 
business teaming partner intends to perform. Please note that the prime contractor must perform 
at least 50% of the cost of manufacturing the supplies (excluding the cost of materials), pursuant 
to the FAR clause at 52.219-14 entitled “Limitations on Subcontracting (OCT 2025) 
(DEVIATION 26-03)(effective November 28, 2025)”.  
 
In furnishing the requested information, please include the following as part of the submission:  
1. Name of the Organization  
2. Address of the Organization  
3. CAGE Code and UEI Number for the Organization  
4. Small business standing (i.e. large or small business) under NAICS Code 541330 – 
Engineering Services ($5.5 million) 
5. If a Small Business, indicate Small Business Type(s) (e.g., Small Business, Woman-Owned 
Small Business, Economically Disadvantaged Woman-Owned Small Business, Small 
Disadvantaged Business, 8(a) Certified, HUBZone Certified, Veteran Owned Small Business, 
and/or Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business)  
6. Telephone/Fax Number, Address, and Email address for the primary point of contact for 
Capabilities Statement  
7. A description of your organization’s capability to meet the requirements stated above  
8. A summary of your organization’s history relative to similar requirements 
 
As much as possible, it is preferred that capability statements be nonproprietary. However, 
capability statements with company-sensitive data and concepts will be accepted, and the 
Government will respect restricted data markings. Responders are expected to appropriately 
mark their submissions that contain proprietary information; receipt of classified materials is not 
anticipated. 
 
All responses shall be submitted electronically, via email, no later than 4:00 PM Eastern Time 
(ET) on May 11, 2026, to the points of contact listed below. Only attach MS Word/Excel 
compatible files or Adobe Acrobat PDF files in electronic correspondence.  
 
Points of Contact 
 
Contract Specialist: Casey Cauffman, Casey.Cauffman-Davis@usss.dhs.gov  
 
Contracting Officer: Erik Syfert, Erik.Syfert@usss.dhs.gov

1.0 Introduction: The United States Secret Service (USSS), James J. Rowley Training Center

other personnel.  The mission is to provide the USSS with trained assets to conduct the USSS 
Mission. This is a non-personal services contract to provide an Autonomous Robotic Training

simulation munition training. The ARTS will be comprised of mobilization of the system to 
accommodate various off-site training venues for law enforcement personnel, improving 
operational readiness and tactical decision-making. The Government will not exercise any 
supervision or control over the contract service providers performing the services herein.

operation, scenario customization, data collection, and performance assessment in various  
training environments.

ARTICLE 1:  SCOPE OF THE AGREEMENT

A.  Background

THIS PARAGRAPH(S) DESCRIBES THE VISION OF THE PROGRAM AND SHOULD ANSWER THE FOLLOWING QUESTIONS:  

WHAT IS THE PURPOSE OF THE AGREEMENT?  

WHAT IS THE CURRENT TECHNOLOGICAL SITUATION?  

WHAT MAKES THIS PROGRAM A “CRITICAL TECHNOLOGY” EFFORT?  

WHY IS THE CURRENT TECHNOLOGY NOT SUFFICIENT?  

WHY IS IT NECESSARY FOR THE GOVERNMENT TO SUPPORT INDUSTRY IN ADDRESSING THIS SITUATION?  

WHAT ARE THE ISSUES OF PARTICULAR IMPORTANCE TO DARPA? 

WHAT ARE THE DUAL-USE (MILITARY AND COMMERCIAL) APPLICATIONS?  

WHAT IS THE MARKET POTENTIAL?  

WHAT ARE THE COMMERCIALIZATION GOALS?  

IF THE PROGRAM IS SUCCESSFUL, THEN WHAT?  WHERE DO WE GO FROM HERE?  

IF THIS COLLABORATION IS SUCCESSFUL, WHAT WILL WE HAVE ACCOMPLISHED?

B.  Definitions

In this Agreement, the following definitions apply:

Agreement:  The body of this Agreement and Attachments 1-X, which are expressly incorporated in and made a part of the Agreement.

Data:  Recorded information, regardless of form or method of recording, which includes but is not limited to, technical data, software, and trade secrets. The term does not include financial, administrative, cost, pricing or management information and does not include subject inventions, included in Article 7.

Foreign Firm or Institution:  A firm or institution organized or existing under the laws of a country other than the United States, its territories, or possessions. The term includes, for purposes of this Agreement, any agency or instrumentality of a foreign government; and firms, institutions or business organizations which are owned or substantially controlled by foreign governments, firms, institutions, or individuals.

Government:  The United States of America, as represented by DARPA.

Government Purpose Rights:  The rights to use, duplicate, or disclose Data, in whole or in part and in any manner, for Government purposes only, and to have or permit others to do so for Government purposes only.

Invention:  Any invention or discovery which is or may be patentable or otherwise protectable under Title 35 of the United States Code.

Know-How:  All information including, but not limited to discoveries, formulas, materials, inventions, processes, ideas, approaches, concepts, techniques, methods, software, programs, documentation, procedures, firmware, hardware, technical data, specifications, devices, apparatus and machines.

Limited Rights:  Rights to use, modify, reproduce, release, perform, display, or disclose Data, in whole or in part, within the Government.

Made:  Any invention means the conception or first actual reduction to practice of such invention.

Party:  Includes the Government (represented by DARPA), or the Performer, or both.

Performer:  COMPANYPERFORMER NAME

Practical application:  To manufacture, in the case of a composition of product; to practice, in the case of a process or method, or to operate, in the case of a machine or system; and, in each case, under such conditions as to establish that the invention is capable of being utilized and that its benefits are, to the extent permitted by law or Government regulations, available to the public on reasonable terms.

Program:  Research and development being conducted by the Performer, as set forth in Article 1, Paragraph C. 

Property:  Any tangible personal property other than property actually consumed during the execution of work under this agreement.  

Subject invention:  Any invention conceived or first actually reduced to practice in the performance of work under this Agreement.

Technology:  Discoveries, innovations, Know-How and inventions, whether patentable or not, including computer software, recognized under U.S. law as intellectual creations to which rights of ownership accrue, including, but not limited to, patents, trade secrets, and copyrights developed under this Agreement.

Unlimited Rights:  Rights to use, duplicate, release, or disclose, Data in whole or in part, in any manner and for any purposes whatsoever, and to have or permit others to do so.

C.  Scope

The Performer shall perform a coordinated research and development program (Program) designed to develop (INSERT RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT EFFORT). The research shall be carried out in accordance with Attachment 1, the Task Description Document (TDD). The Performer shall submit or otherwise provide all documentation required by Attachment 2, Report Requirements.

The Performer shall be paid a fixed amount for each milestone accomplished in accordance with Attachment 3, Schedule of Milestones and Payments and the procedures of Article 5. The Schedule of Milestones and Payments may be revised or updated in accordance with Article 3. 

D.  Goals/Objectives

The goal of this Agreement is (INSERT GOAL(S) OF AGREEMENT).

The Government will have continuous involvement with the Performer. The Government will also obtain access to research results and certain rights in patents and data pursuant to Articles 7 and 8. DARPA and the Performer are bound to each other by a duty of good faith and best research effort in achieving the goals of the Program. 

This Agreement is an “other transaction” pursuant to 10 U.S.C. § 4021. The Parties agree that the principal purpose of this Agreement is for the Government and the Performer to provide for a coordinated effort to advance research and technology goals of the program and not primarily for the acquisition of property or services for the direct benefit or use of the Government. This Agreement is not intended to be, nor shall it be construed as, by implication or otherwise, a partnership, a corporation, or other business organization.

ARTICLE 2:  TERM

A.  Term of this Agreement

The Program commences upon the date of the last signature hereon and continues for (INSERT NUMBER OF MONTHS) (xx) months. Provisions of this Agreement, which, by their express terms or by necessary implication, apply for periods of time other than specified herein, shall be given effect, notwithstanding this Article.

B.  Termination Provisions 

(Use if the performers are providing cost (resource) share

Subject to a reasonable determination that the program will not produce beneficial results, either Party may terminate this Agreement by written notice to the other Party, provided that such written notice is preceded by consultation between the Parties. In the event of a termination of the Agreement, it is agreed that disposition of Data developed under this Agreement, shall be in accordance with the provisions set forth in Article 8, Data Rights. The Government and the Performer will negotiate in good faith a reasonable and timely adjustment of all outstanding issues between the Parties as a result of termination. Failure of the Parties to agree to a reasonable adjustment will be resolved pursuant to Article 7, Disputes. The Government has no obligation to pay the Performer beyond the last completed and paid milestone if the Performer decides to terminate.

OR

(Use if the performers are NOT providing cost (resource) share)

The Government may terminate this Agreement by written notice to the Performer, provided that such written notice is preceded by consultation between the Parties. The Performer may request Agreement termination by giving the Government sixty (60) days written notification of their intent to do so. If the Performer decides to request termination of this Agreement, the Government may, at its discretion, agree to terminate. The Government and the Performer should negotiate in good faith a reasonable and timely adjustment of all outstanding issues between the Parties as a result of termination, which may include non-cancelable commitments. In the event of a termination of the Agreement, the Government shall have paid-up rights in Data as described in Article 8, Data Rights. Failure of the Parties to agree to an equitable adjustment shall be resolved pursuant to Article 6, Disputes.

C.  Extending the Term

The Parties may extend by mutual written agreement the term of this Agreement if research opportunities within the vision statement set forth in Article 1 reasonably warrant. Any extension shall be formalized through modification of the Agreement by the Agreements Officer (AO) and the Performer’s Administrator.   

ARTICLE 3:  MANAGEMENT OF THE PROJECT  

A.  Management and Program Structure

The Performer shall be responsible for the overall technical and program management of the Program, and technical planning and execution shall remain with the Performer. The DARPA Agreements Officer’s Representative (AOR) shall provide recommendations to Program developments and technical collaboration and be responsible for the review and verification of milestones.

B.  Program Management Planning Process

Program planning will consist of an Annual Program Plan with inputs and reviews from the Performer and DARPA management, containing a detailed schedule of research activities and milestones.

Initial Program Plan:  The Performer will follow the initial program plan that is contained in Attachment 1, TDD and Attachment 3, the Schedule of Milestones and Payments.

Overall Program Plan Annual Review

The Performer, with DARPA PM participation and review, will prepare an overall Annual Program Plan in the first quarter of each Agreement year (for this purpose, each consecutive twelve (12) month period from (and including) the month of execution of this Agreement during which this Agreement shall remain in effect shall be considered an “Agreement Year”).  The Annual Program Plan may be presented and reviewed at an annual site review, at the discretion of the DARPA PM, which will be attended by the Performer’s Management, the DARPA AOR, Senior DARPA management or other DARPA program managers and personnel as appropriate. The Performer, with DARPA participation and review, will prepare a final Annual Program Plan.

The Annual Program Plan provides a detailed schedule of research activities, commits the Performer to meet specific performance objectives and describes the milestones. The Annual Program Plan will consolidate all prior adjustments in the research schedule, including revisions/modifications to prospective milestones. Recommendations for changes and technical revisions or modifications to the Agreement which result from the Annual Review shall be made in accordance with the provisions of Article 3, Paragraph C.

C.  Modifications

As a result of meetings, annual reviews, or at any time during the term of the Agreement, research progress or results may indicate that a change in the TDD would be beneficial to program objectives. Recommendations for modifications, including justifications to support any changes to the TDD and prospective milestones, will be documented and submitted by the Performer to the DARPA PM and AOR with a copy to the DARPA AO. 1 OVERVIEW 
The Air Force Research Laboratory (AFRL) Enterprise Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO)   
serves as the overarching enterprise announcement providing the framework for the 
issuance of competitive solicitations (i.e. Spirals), which will seek innovative, commercial 
solutions to meet the mission of the AFRL enterprise. Innovative products and/or services 
competitively selected by peer review of proposals resulting from a general solicitation are 
considered commercial notwithstanding the deﬁnition under Revolutionary FAR Overhaul 
(RFO) Subpart 2.101.  
 
2 AUTHORITY 
This CSO is issued in accordance with R-DFARS Subpart 212.70, for the acquisition of 
innovative commercial products or commercial services. The use of a CSO is permanently 
authorized by section 803 of the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) for Fiscal Year 
(FY) 2022 (Pub. L. 117-81) codiﬁed at 10 USC 3458. 
 
3 SCOPE  
The scope of this CSO encompasses the Areas of Interest (AOI) identiﬁed in Attachment 1 
Areas of Interest (AOI). The Government seeks to obtain innovative solutions or new 
capabilities that fulﬁll requirements, close capability gaps, and/or provide potential 
technological advancements. Meaningful proposals with varying technical or scientiﬁc 
approaches are anticipated.  
 
The Government reserves the right to amend the requirements of this CSO and each 
subsequent Spiral. 
 
Potential offerors are advised that awards resulting from this announcement may be 
modiﬁed during performance to effect within-scope changes including, but not limited to, 
increase in value and/or level of effort as the Government explores the innovative solution.  
 
4 INNOVATIVE SOLUTIONS  
Resulting solutions awarded under the CSO shall meet the deﬁnition of “innovative” in 
accordance with10 USC 3458 and implemented by R-DFARS 212.7001:  
Innovative means—  
(1) Any technology, process, or method, including research and development, that is 
new as of the date of submission of a proposal; or 
(2) Any application that is new as of the date of submission of a proposal of a 
technology, process, or method existing as of such date. 
 

FA8652-26-S-C003 
AFRL Enterprise CSO 
Page 5 of 13 
 
A note on innovative studies and analysis (S&A) that may be funded with Operations and 
Maintenance (O&M) appropriations: The effort must also meet the deﬁnition of S&A; the 
working deﬁnition of which is “short term (preferably 1 year), non-developmental, 
investigative work that addresses urgent and the near-term needs, issues, and consultative 
questions. ” 
 
5 CSO WITH SPIRALS 
Both enterprise-wide (i.e. centralized) and decentralized Spirals may be issued by either 
AFRL/PK or an issuing Mission Organization, respectively. This CSO will be active 
indeﬁnitely for the issuance of the Spirals and will be updated annually, until terminated. It 
is the responsibility of prospective offerors to monitor the Governmentwide Point of Entry 
(GPE), SAM.gov (https://sam.gov), for additional information pertaining to this CSO as well 
as for future Spirals issued hereunder.  
 
Prospective offerors shall adhere to this enterprise CSO as well as the information 
contained within the Spiral. Spirals will identify the areas of interest and period of 
performance requirements to which prospective offerors shall focus their solutions, as well 
as speciﬁc submission instructions/dates/times, and evaluation criteria. Each Spiral will be 
announced on the GPE.  
 
6 TYPES OF AWARDS 
The Government intends to award RFO Part 12 ﬁxed-price type contracts, including ﬁxed-
price incentive; however, it reserves the right to award Other Transactions for Prototype 
(OTP) pursuant to 10 USC 4022 (to include follow-on production agreements).  
Prospective offerors are encouraged to review 10 USC 4022, including 10 USC 4022(f).   
The Government reserves the right to incrementally fund any or all awards under this CSO. 
 
The Government reserves the right to make no award as a result of the CSO Spirals and 
may award one or more contracts and/or OTPs for all, or part of, any submission. All awards 
are subject to the availability of funds and successful negotiations. The Government is not 
responsible for any monies expended by the offeror prior to the issuance of any award, to 
include, but not limited to, bid and proposal preparation costs.  
 
7 ONE-STEP AND TWO-STEP SPIRALS 
Spirals issued under this CSO may utilize either a One-Step or a Two-Step process as 
outlined below and may be Open or Closed.  
 

FA8652-26-S-C003 
AFRL Enterprise CSO 
Page 6 of 13 
 
 
 
Open Spirals provide an avenue for Industry to submit innovative solutions in alignment 
with the AOIs at any given time; Open Spirals may be issued by AFRL/PK (enterprise) or an 
issuing Mission Organization (decentralized).  
 
Closed Spirals will be issued by a Mission Organization (decentralized) and narrow the 
area of interest for speciﬁc requirements and require submission by a speciﬁed time. Late 
bid and proposal provisions in accordance with RFO 52.212-1(c) apply. Proposals that the 
Government determines to fall within a Closed Decentralized Spiral but are submitted 
under an Open Spiral will not be considered for award.   
 
One-Step Spiral for Commercial Solutions Proposal (CSP):  
This process requires the prospective offeror to submit a CSP in response to a One-Step 
Spiral. 
 
Contents: The CSP shall include a technical proposal, price proposal, and Statement of 
Work (SOW) in accordance with Attachment 3: CSP Template, or as otherwise directed in 
the Spiral. The Government reserves the right to require a Pitch in conjunction with, and as 
part of, the CSP. 
 
Evaluation: The CSP will be evaluated in accordance with Section 8 of this CSO unless 
varying criteria is established at the Spiral level. At the conclusion of the evaluation, the 
offeror will be notiﬁed of the CSP categorization as deﬁned in Section 9. 
 


FA8652-26-S-C003 
AFRL Enterprise CSO 
Page 7 of 13 
 
Two-Step Spiral for Commercial Solutions Brief (CSB) and CSP:  
This process requires the prospective offeror to submit a CSB in response to a Two-Step 
Spiral. 
 
Step-One Contents: The CSB shall include a PowerPoint Brieﬁng and White Paper in 
accordance with Attachment 2: CSB Template, or as otherwise directed in the Spiral. The 
Government reserves the right to require a Pitch in lieu of the CSB. 
 
Evaluation: The CSB will be evaluated in accordance with Section 8 of this CSO unless 
varying criteria is established at the Spiral level. A CSB that does not meet the compliance 
or evaluation criteria will not be considered further. At the conclusion of the CSB 
evaluation, the offeror will be notiﬁed of the CSB categorization as deﬁned in Section 9. An 
offeror whose CSB is categorized as Selectable will be invited to move forward to Step-Two.  
 
Step-Two Request for CSP: The designated Contracting Officer (CO) will issue a Request for 
CSP to the offeror(s) selected to move forward. Contents: The offeror shall submit a CSP 
that includes a technical proposal, price proposal, SOW and additional documentation as 
outlined in Attachment 3: CSP Template, or as otherwise directed in the Spiral. The 
submission due date will be included in the Step-Two Request for CSP .  
 
Evaluation: The CSP will be evaluated in accordance with Section 8 of this CSO unless 
varying criteria is established at the Spiral level. The Government reserves the right to 
select all, some, or none of the submissions. 
 
8 EVALUATION 
General CSO Compliance: The CSB and/or CSP will be reviewed for compliance and to 
determine whether the commercial solution is "innovative" pursuant to R-DFARS Subpart 
212.7001. 
 
Method of Evaluation: The method of evaluation for CSB and CSP will include scientiﬁc, 
technological, or other subject-matter expert peer review process. 
 
CSB Evaluation Factors: The Government will evaluate using the factors below unless 
otherwise speciﬁed at the Spiral level. The evaluation factors are of equal importance.  
a. Technical Merit and Applicability 
b. Funding Availability 
 

FA8652-26-S-C003 
AFRL Enterprise CSO 
Page 8 of 13 
 
CSP Evaluation Factors: The Government will evaluate using the factors below unless 
otherwise speciﬁed at the Spiral level. The evaluation factors are of equal importance. 
a. Technical Merit and Applicability 
b. Importance to Agency Programs 
c. Price 
i. Price shall be considered to the extent appropriate, but at a minimum price will 
be determined fair and reasonable using the procedures at R-DFARS Subpart 
212.204   
d.  Funding Availability 
 
9 CATEGORIZATION 
CSB and CSP submissions will be categorized as either Selectable, Selectable/Insufficient 
Funding, or Not Selectable as deﬁned below: 
 
Selectable: Based upon the evaluation criteria, the CSB/CSP is selectable and sufficient 
funding is available.  
 
Selectable/Insufficient Funding: Based upon the evaluation criteria, the CSB/CSP is 
selectable; however, insufficient funding is available.  
 
Not Selectable: Based upon the evaluation criteria, the CSB/CSP is not selectable based. 
Even if there is sufficient funding, the submission should not be funded.  
 
The Government reserves the right to award all, some, or none of a proposal. When the 
Government elects to award only part of a proposal, the selected part may be categorized 
as Selectable, though the proposal, as a whole, may not merit such a categorization.  
 
10 SELECTION 
CSB Selection: If a CSB is categorized as Selectable, the offeror will be notiﬁed that it has 
been selected to move to the Step-Two Request for a CSP .  
 
CSP Selection: Award(s) will be made once a CSP is categorized as Selectable. The CO 
reserves the right to negotiate proposed scope of work, price, and other terms and 
conditions as may be required.  
 
If a CSB or CSP has Technical Merit and Applicability, but there is insufficient funding, the 
CO may issue a formal notiﬁcation to the offeoror requesting authorization to maintain the 

FA8652-26-S-C003 
AFRL Enterprise CSO 
Page 9 of 13 
 
submission electronically for consideration and subsequent funding for a period of time, 
not to exceed one year. 
 
11 OTHER AWARD CONSIDERATIONS 
Eligibility. To be considered for award, offerors must be registered in the System for Award 
Management (SAM) at https://sam.gov, be considered responsible within the meaning of 
RFO Subpart 9.1, “Responsible Prospective Contractors,” have a satisfactory performance 
record, and otherwise be eligible for award based on federal law and regulation.  
 
Safeguarding Covered Defense Information (CDI). Awards shall include either R-DFARS 
252.240-7997, NIST SP 800-171 DoD Assessment Requirements (Deviation 2026-O0025), 
(FAR-based contracts), or equivalent (OTP), and the awardee shall be required to 
implement the NIST Special Publication (SP) 800-171 in effect at the time of the Spiral 
solicitation, or as otherwise authorized.  
 
Additional Compliance Criteria for 10 USC 4022 OTPs. If the Government decides to

GENERAL INFORMATION: 
The Air Force Research Laboratory (AFRL) Rocket Lab at Edwards AFB, CA is conducting 
market research to define the acquisition strategy for the Aerospace System’s Technical Research 
and Operation Services (ASTROS) II contract. This is the follow-on effort to the current 
ASTROS contract (FA9300-16-C-0001). A Draft Performance Work Statement (PWS) for 
ASTROS II is provided as Attachment 03. It details the revised and expanded scope of work for 
this effort. 
T
he primary work location is the Edwards Rocket Lab, CA, which is a secure site located within 
a controlled and restricted area. All required travel to other government or contractor facilities 
will be specified in the PWS or an approved Work Plan (WP). 
T
he Government is considering all contracting strategies and types, including the potential for a 
small business set-aside. The anticipated North American Industry Classification (NAICS) code 
for this procurement is 541715 - Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and 
Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology). The corresponding small business 
size standard is 1,300 employees, with Exception 3 - Guided Missiles and Space Vehicles, Their 
Propulsion Units and Propulsion Parts. 
T
he Government anticipates that the successful offeror will be required to maintain a 
comprehensive security program in accordance with (IAW) the draft Department of War Contract 
Security Classification Specification, DD Form 254 (provided as Attachment 05). At a minimum, 
all contractor personnel supporting this effort must possess a favorable National Agency Check 
with Inquiries (NACI). Respondents should note that performance may require personnel to 
obtain and maintain Top Secret/Sensitive Compartmented Information (TS/SCI) clearances 
during the contract lifecycle. Additionally, to comply with R-DFARS 252.204-7021 and 252.204-
7025, the Government expects that both the prime contractor and any subcontractors will be 
required to achieve and maintain the appropriate Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification 
(CMMC). General information regarding this CMMC requirement is outlined in Attachment 07. 
T
he anticipated period of performance is 10 years, which may include performance incentives. 
The target date for contract award is June 2027, with performance scheduled to begin in 
September 2027. 
TH
ERE IS NO SOLICITATION AT THIS TIME 
This is a Request for Information (RFI) posting ONLY . This RFI does not constitute a request for 
proposals and is not to be construed as a commitment by the Government - no contract will be 
awarded by this RFI. Submission of any information in response to this RFI is purely voluntary - 
the Government assumes no financial responsibility for any costs incurred. The Government is 
under no obligation to acknowledge receipt of any information received or provide feedback to 
respondents with respect to any information submitted. Telephone inquiries will not be accepted 
or acknowledged. 
T
he Government may revise or cancel this RFI at any time. The information contained herein is 
subject to change before a formal Request for Proposal (RFP) is issued. 
ASTROS II RFI
Page 3 of 137

PURPOSE STATEMENT: 
This RFI is structured as a three-part series, detailed in Attachments 01 through 02 and Series 03 
noted below. The insights gathered during this initial phase are critical in helping the 
Government evaluate the industry capabilities and experience available to execute the required 
work. Series Two will focus on gathering feedback to shape the Proposal Evaluation Approach. 
Finally, Series 03 will be an upcoming Industry Day, designed to acquaint prospective offerors 
with the AFRL Rocket Lab's unique mission, specialized infrastructure, and remote operational 
environment. 
Industry feedback is a critical component in finalizing the acquisition strategy for the ASTROS 
follow-on contract. We respectfully request and encourage potential offerors to submit detailed 
responses across all three series to help ensure a well-structured and effective procurement. 
SERIES 03 – INDUSTRY DAY NOTICE: 
The Government intends to host an Industry Day at Edwards AFB, CA to provide interested 
contractors with further insight into the mission requirements, unique location, and the security 
protocols outlined in this RFI. This event will serve as an opportunity for industry partners to 
engage with program stakeholders and clarify expectations. Specific details, including the date, 
location, and registration instructions, will be posted to the System for Award Management 
(SAM.gov) at a later date.

Solicitation Request : Air Force Research Laboratory, Aerospace Systems Directorate 
(AFRL/RQ-West) is establishing this open two -step ARA to solicit technology demonstration  
white papers of interest to the Air Force Research Laboratory research as described below. 
Potential offerors issuing white papers may be requested to provide a full proposal after white paper 
reviews. In addition to the white paper process, AFRL may issue calls under this ARA for specific 
research objectives. Calls issued under this ARA will include instructions to potential offerors, 
evaluation criteria, and include a common due date for proposals received in response to the call. 
The ARA will allow for submission of white papers during the open period of the ARA and will 
provide for specific proposal preparation times and due dates on individual calls identified during 
the open period of the ARA . White papers should be addressed to the Contracting White Paper 
Focal Point identified below. This is an unrestricted solicitation. Small businesses are encouraged 
to respond on all or any part of this solicitation. The NAICS Code for this acquisition is 541715, and 
the small business size standard is 1,000 employees. White papers/proposals submitted shall be in 
accordance with this announcement or with any specific calls issued as a part of this announcement. 
Offerors should remain vigilant for any specific calls or updates related to this ARA. 
 
Communication related to this ARA, including submission of white papers and feedback on this 
solicitation shall be submitted to the following email address: 
White Paper Focal Point*: AFTC.PZRA.BAAs@us.af.mil     
Please CC the CPOC listed in VII-2 in all submissions. The Government CPOC will provide a 
confirmation of receipt for each white paper submitted. Offerors are advised only contracting 
officers are legally authorized to contractually bind or otherwise commit the Government.

UNDER ANY CIRCUMSTANCE. IV-1.1.8. lists steps to be taken prior to the submission or

Open Period: The AFRL Rocket Lab ARA has an open period of 10 years. For ease of reference, 
this ARA may be republished at a minimum of yearly intervals within the open period but may be 
updated more frequently dependent on mission requirements. 
 
Type of Contract/Instrument : The Air Force reserves the right to award the instrument best 
suited to the nature of research proposed. Awards for efforts as a result of this announcement will 
be in the form of contracts, purchase orders, grants, cooperative agreements or other transactions 
depending upon the nature of the work proposed. Accordingly, the Government may award any 
appropriate contract type. 
 
Brief Program Summary: AFRL Rocket Lab ARA  is a two-step open ARA with the ability of 
issuing future calls that enable study efforts on novel concepts, as well as research and 
development contracts to mature specific technologies to appropriate technology readiness levels 
(TRL) depending on end use. Specific award details are described below, but the Government 
anticipates awarding multiple contracts of varying duration and value. However, the maximum 
single award value issued against this ARA  will not exce ed $500M. This ARA allows 
consideration of white papers as well as calls issued by the Government when specific 
requirements are identified. 
 
Proposals Due Date and Time:  White papers must be submitted as described below. Multiple 
awards are anticipated. The number of resources made available under this ARA will depend on 
the quality of the white papers and any subsequent proposals received and the availability of funds. 
White papers may be submitted anytime during the open period. Calls issued by the Government 
against this ARA will specify a due date when proposals specific to each call are due. 
 
I. RESEARCH TOPIC DESCRIPTION 
 
 
I-1. Statement of Needs 
 
• Topic 1 - Ground and Flight Experiments: Establish, enhance, upgrade, and sustain 
ground and flight experimental equipment to provide increased reliability, data quality, 
throughput, and/or to lower overall sustainment and personnel requirements to safely 
conduct ground and flight experiments. The government is interested in test processes, test 
equipment/systems, studies & analytical methods, and physical and digital tools used to 
plan, prepare, configure, verify & validate, rocket test facility and supporting functions. 
This includes, but is not limited to, a broad range of technologies, advanced tooling, 
measurement systems, sensors & inspection techniques, improved methods for generating 
vacuum & altitude environment, including steam generation, modeling & simulation, digital 
engineering / digital transformation. Proposals should seek to develop innovative 
technologies for rocket testing and rocket test systems to enhance national defense 
capabilities through accelerated fielding of tactical missile systems, strategic missile 
systems, space launch systems, and in-space systems. 
 
• Topic 2 - Missile System Technologies: Create and demonstrate innovative technologies 
or solutions for increasing the effectiveness of missile systems of all sizes and types and at

Contracting Officer: Ms. Amber Taylor 
Contracting Officer / Agreements Officer 
AFRL Enterprise Strategies and Initiatives Division 
 
CSO Type: This is a Centralized, Open Two-Step Spiral issued in accordance with R-DFARS 
212.70, Defense Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO). 
 
Overview: The Government is currently accepting Commercial Solutions Brief (CSB) 
submissions for innovative solutions, ranging from advanced component development 
through operational systems development, that are within the scope of the Areas of 
Interest (AOI) identiﬁed in Attachment 1 of the above-referenced AFRL Enterprise CSO. 
CSB submissions that are categorized Selectable will be invited to proceed to Step Two – 
Request for Commercial Solutions Proposal (CSP). Only CSB submissions are requested 
at this time. An offeror submitting a CSP without ﬁrst submitting a CSB will not be 
eligible for award.  
 
Step One CSB DUE DATE AND TIME: CSBs may be submitted, and will be accepted, until 
5:00 PM Eastern, 30 April 2027. Submissions received after this date and time will be 
considered late in accordance with RFO 52.212-1(c).  
 
Step Two CSP DUE DATE AND TIME: Will be speciﬁed in the Request for Step-Two CSP. 
Proposals received after the speciﬁed date and time will be considered late in accordance 
with RFO 52.212-1(c). 
 
Step One Submission Instructions: 
Attachments referenced herein are located in the above-referenced AFRL Enterprise CSO 
announcement posting in SAM.gov.   
 
Follow the Two-Step Spiral submission and formatting instructions described in AFRL 
Enterprise CSO Section 7 and CSO Attachment 2, respectively.  
 

FA8652-26-S-C003 / SPIRAL 26-S-C005 
2 
 
CSB submissions shall be submitted to afrl.cso.mailbox@us.af.mil with subject line: “CSB 
Submission under Centralized Open Two-Step Spiral” . Submissions containing Controlled 
Unclassiﬁed Information (CUI) are required to be transmitted through the Department of 
Defense Secure File Access Exchange (DoD SAFE). In those instances, offerors shall 
contact the Contracting Officer via afrl.cso.mailbox@us.af.mil to request a Drop-off link. 
An email response conﬁrming receipt will be sent to offerors for either submission method.  
 
There is no limit to the number of CSBs any one offeror may submit. If an offeror submits 
multiple CSBs, each must provide a unique approach.  
 
This Centralized, Open Two-Step Spiral shall not be used to circumvent a Decentralized 
Spiral issued by a Mission Organization. A CSB submission that the Contracting Officer 
determines to be duplicative with, or submitted in lieu of, a Decentralized Spiral 
submission will not be considered for award. 
 
Step One Evaluation and Selection:  
CSB submissions under this Spiral will be evaluated in accordance with the evaluation 
criteria identiﬁed within Section 8 of the AFRL Enterprise CSO. At the conclusion of the CSB 
evaluation, the offeror will be notiﬁed of the CSB categorization. An offeror whose CSB is 
categorized as Selectable will be invited to move forward to Step-Two. 
 
Step Two Submission Instructions: 
Follow the Two-Step Spiral submission and formatting instructions described in AFRL 
Enterprise CSO Section 7 and the CSP template. Any deviation from this instruction will be 
identiﬁed in the Step-Two Request for CSP .  
 
Step Two Evaluation and Selection:  
CSB submissions under this Spiral will be evaluated in accordance with the evaluation 
criteria identiﬁed within Section 8 of the AFRL Enterprise CSO. Any deviations from the 
Enterprise CSO will be identiﬁed in the Step-Two Request for CSP .  
 
A CSP categorized Selectable will be reviewed as described in Section 11 of the AFRL 
Enterprise CSO. The offeror will be notiﬁed and informed of the outcome.  
 
Award Type(s): See AFRL Enterprise CSO Section 6.  
 

FA8652-26-S-C003 / SPIRAL 26-S-C005 
3 
 
Anticipated Number of Awards: Not speciﬁed. The Government reserves the right to make 
no award as a result of this Spiral and may award one or more contracts and/or Other 
Transactions for Prototype (OTP) for all, or part of, any proposal received.  
 
Estimated Program Cost: Not speciﬁed; dependent upon proposed approaches and 
funding availability. The Government reserves the right to fund all, some, or none of the 
proposals submitted; may elect to fund only part of a submitted proposal; and may 
incrementally fund any or all awards. All awards are subject to the availability of funds. 
 
Notiﬁcation: 180 days is a notional timeframe for a CSB to be reviewed; it could be longer 
based on the white paper review cycle.  
 
General: 
Offerors are responsible for monitoring SAM.gov for any amendments to the Enterprise 
CSO and/or this Spiral.  
 
General questions regarding this Open Enterprise Spiral shall be directed to 
afrl.cso.mailbox@us.af.mil. Utilize the following in the email subject line: “AFRL CSO 
General Question(s)”.

The purpose of this Request for Information (RFI) is to identify qualified contractors and identify brands of nursecall systems with a code blue communication system capable of integrating with existing Hill-Rom hospital beds to relay all the required bed data back to the nurse stations without the use of middleware.

Introduction

SALIENT CHARACTERISTICS 

The following are salient characteristics of a brand name or equal Hillrom Voalte nurse call system:

The brand name or equal Hillrom Voalte nurse call system shall not use middleware to interface bed data. 

A brand name or equal Hillrom Voalte nurse call system shall be approved on the Medical Device Risk Assessment (MDERA).  

A brand name or equal Hillrom Voalte nurse call systems with code blue communication system shall provide all information required below in a visual dashboard accessed via the workstations located at the nurse stations. The dashboard shall list the following required information:

Patient room number

Patient name or corresponding Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPPA) compliant naming convention.

Patient notes (ex. Hard of hearing, NPO (nothing by mouth), etc.)

Risk Status: based on electronic medical records assessment (Fall Risk, Skin, Pulmonary) or manual entry

Assigned staff

Active calls

Call wait times

Rounding reminders that automatically reset based on caregiver presence

PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT (PWS)
