Page 2 of 16 
 
1.0  BACKGROUND 
The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Office of Information & Technology (OIT), IT 
Budget and Finance (ITBF) provides leadership, resources, and financial expertise to 
deliver world-class IT products and services and improve end-user experience for 
Veterans, their families, caregivers, and survivors. Specifically, ITBF links the full IT 
budget process with the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Secretary and Chief 
Information Officer’s (CIO) priorities, ensuring that budgets reflect the organization’s 
values and support innovation and modernization. ITBF also provides budgetary 
expertise for IT systems and operations for VA Administrations/Staff Offices, to optimize 
the reach and impact of investment dollars. 
 
The Technology Business Management (TBM) Branch, the IT Financial Management 
and Oversight Service (ITFMOS), and the Financial Data Management (FDM) Branch 
each play crucial roles within VA OIT ITBF, focusing on data integration, IT cost 
transparency, informed decision-making, and compliance with funding and procurement 
law, regulation, and policy. 
 
Through the implementation of financial data management and data governance 
practices, advanced analytical models, and ensuring compliance with regulatory 
frameworks, these branches contribute to the following initiatives: 
1. Efficiency and Accountability: By maintaining precise data management systems 
and robust financial models, these branches ensure that resources are allocated 
efficiently, and accountability is maintained at all levels of operation. 
2. Increase Transparency: The TBM Model and comprehensive reporting 
mechanisms provide clear visibility into IT costs and resource utilization, promoting 
transparency in government spending. 
3. Enable Data-Driven Decision Making: The analytical frameworks and data sets 
utilized by these branches enable informed decision-making at tactical, operational, 
and strategic levels, aligning with the goal of fostering a culture of data-driven 
governance. 
 
The TBM Branch's responsibilities include maintaining and enhancing the TBM Cost 
Transparency Model, a sophisticated analytical framework that provides detailed views 
of IT costs through a multi-layered approach encompassing resources, functions, 
products, and services. This model employs standard TBM taxonomy and activity-based 
costing, both of which are technical methodologies requiring expertise in financial 
modeling, data analytics, and IT cost management. By fostering IT cost transparency 
and improving decision-making through data-driven insights, the TBM Branch supports 
the priority of promoting efficient and accountable government operations. Additionally, 
the integration of TBM into existing business processes and its alignment with federal 
frameworks further demonstrates the technical nature and strategic importance of these 
activities. 
 

ITBF TBM and Accounting Technical Enablement 
VA-26-00004314 
 
Page 3 of 16 
The Travel, Purchase Cards, and Conferences (TPC) Branch within ITFMOS provides 
critical oversight for the proper funding of VA IT-related acquisitions, conducting 
technical reviews and audits to maintain compliance with Federal Travel Regulations, 
Federal Acquisition Regulations, and VA Financial Policies. It communicates necessary 
revisions of Travel, Charge Card, and Conferences policies for VA and OIT, and works 
actively to reduce fraud, waste, and abuse of government funds by monitoring these 
programs. The branch also ensures the accurate and timely updates to the charge card 
program bank’s system to reflect the current hierarchy of cardholders and their status. 
These activities require technical skills in financial systems, compliance auditing, and 
policy implementation.  
 
The core functions of the FDM Branch involve the unification and analysis of budget and 
finance data across the VA Office of Information and Technology (OIT). This unification 
aims to provide an authoritative enterprise data source that enhances business 
decisions at tactical, operational, and strategic levels. The utilization of these platforms 
for data aggregation, analysis, and reporting requires a strong technical foundation in 
data science, data analytics, and database management. These technical efforts enable 
accurate and efficient financial planning, resource allocation, and decision-making 
processes.

The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Veterans Health Administration (VHA) mission is to ensure that all enrolled Veterans receive the health care they have earned through their service. The VHA is the largest integrated health care system in the United States, providing care at 1,380 health care facilities, including 170 VA Medical Centers and 1,193 outpatient sites of care of varying complexity (VHA outpatient clinics) to over 9.1 million Veterans enrolled in the VA health care program.

The Institute for Learning, Education and Development (ILEAD), which resides within the Office of Human Capital Management (HCM), is responsible for an employee’s learning journey within VHA, providing virtual and in-person training, products, services and cohort-based experiential development opportunities for employees in all phases of their career, from entry-level, through mid-career, to aspiring and new supervisors and managers, and for budding, future and current senior leaders at the executive level.

ILEAD’s Strategy and Learning Services (SLS) service line includes the Informatics section, which delivers data services and support for all ILEAD’s efforts.

In 2025, ILEAD became part of the Access Choices and Excellence initiative pursuant to Executive Order 14296, Section 5(a) dated May 9, 2025, Keeping Promises to Veterans and Establishing a National Center for Warrior Independence. Reducing administrative work such as training for clinical teams is an essential element in increasing access to care and decreasing employee burnout. Accurately assessing and reporting on training burden at both the national and local levels necessitated ILEAD compiling and regularly updating extremely large datasets that aren’t part of VHA’s existing data warehouse. This data is combined into models and dashboards that accurately provide the comprehensive information required both to inform senior leaders and to guide the reduction in training burden at all levels. ILEAD has been tasked with updating and maintaining these data sets as part of ongoing monitoring of training burden. ILEAD is also regularly tasked with managing and analyzing disparate sets of training data to support emergent VHA senior leadership efforts such as the recent Secretary of Veterans Affairs request for options on supporting continuing medical education (CME). This contract provides the additional data analytics capacity and capabilities that are required for ILEAD SLS Informatics to support all of these efforts. 

ILEAD SLS requires insight into Human-Systems Integration (HSI) factors and Human-Centered Design (HCD) methodologies to provide information for rapid prototyping and deployment; workflow and process automation; and dynamic visualization for decision-making. The goal is to ensure that design of future-state models, dashboards, processes, systems, and governance are scalable and focused on the human element to support workforce development and improve learning outcomes while optimizing performance and affordability.

HSI is the relationship between humans and their environment and how systems are designed and used relative to that relationship. HSI includes humans in their different roles in the system. Systems include people, processes, policies, structures, hardware, software, architectures, interfaces, ecosystems, and strategy. Execution is concerned with the integration of these elements to optimize the performance of the whole.

ILEAD SLS requirements should be structured using HSI techniques such as (1) Human Centered Design (HCD) which aims to make systems usable and useful by focusing on the users, their needs, and requirements, and by applying human factors/ergonomics, usability knowledge, and techniques (ISO 9241-210:2010(E)); (2) Designing for User Experience (UX) which involves the design of the entire process of acquiring and integrating the product with insight into meaningful and valuable aspects of human-computer interaction and product ownership to deliver products that are intuitive, easy, and enjoyable to use, and solve the problem(s) they are designed to solve in the most user-friendly manner possible and (3) Customer Experience (CX) design which focuses on the complete design of the customer lifecycle bringing a focus on the customer to every touch point VA has with its customers.

NOTICE OF INTENT 842673947 
 
 
The Defense Information Systems Agency (DISA)/Defense Information Technology Contracting 
Organization (DITCO) intends to negotiate a sole source contract with Akamai Technologies, 
Inc., a large business, for the Global Content Delivery Service (GCDS) III requirement.  A sole 
source Justification & Approval document is being coordinated and, upon approval, a copy of it 
will be posted here on SAM.gov to comply with the public display requirements of FAR 6.103-1 
and FAR 5.101. 
 
The proposed contract action is for the Global Content Delivery Service (GCDS) III requirement. 
GCDS is DISA’s enterprise-class, managed content delivery network (CDN) for accelerating, 
securing, and monitoring web content, applications, and data transfers. GCDS operates on both 
NIPRNet and SIPRNet, delivering services through globally distributed edge locations to reduce 
latency, improve performance, and ensure resilient access to information for Department of 
Defense (DoD) missions worldwide. The objective of this requirement is to obtain a reliable, 
responsive, and cost-effective GCDS that leverages commercial best practices and Zero Trust 
security principles. 
 
DISA delivers information technology (IT) solutions for the DoD and requires processing, 
storage, communications, identity management, and content delivery services for diverse 
customer applications across the DISN and other DoD networks. This acquisition provides state-
of-the-art global content delivery capacity, including globally distributed network optimizing 
content delivery speed and security, to meet current and future DoD customer requirements. 
GCDS, as a DISN zero trust enterprise-level service, is designed to secure, accelerate, and 
improve the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of mission-critical applications globally. 
By strategically deploying content delivery capabilities at DISA-owned and DISA-approved 
processing locations, GCDS enables DISA to enhance communication effectiveness through 
improved information interoperability. 
 
GCDS provides the Government with a secure and reliable system for the rapid global delivery 
of digital content, including websites, videos, files, and online applications, to military users and 
systems around the world. GCDS ensures that warfighters, analysts, and other defense personnel 
can instantly access the information they need, wherever they are, without delays or failures. 
GCDS protects this content with high-level cybersecurity tools to ensure that sensitive data stays 
secure. This service is especially critical for missions that operate across different time zones and 
geographic regions, where real-time access to web applications and secure data is essential for 
success. Without GCDS, digital content would take longer to load, be more vulnerable to 
cyberattacks, and risk becoming unavailable during key operations. GCDS ensures that vital 
military content is fast, secure, and always available, anywhere in the world it is needed. 
 
This follow-on effort will deliver the current GCDS services and bring parity to the vendor’s 
commercial offerings. This effort, referred to as Defense Edge, intends to enhance content 
delivery, identity management, and security services for DISA by unifying existing public and 
private service offerings into a single, elevated platform. 

The incumbent subcontractor Akamai Technologies, Inc., is the only source capable of providing 
all necessary services. 
 
The statutory authority for other than full and open competition is 10 USC 3204 (a) (1), as 
implemented by FAR 6.103-1(c)(2), only one responsible source and no other supplies or 
services will satisfy agency requirements.  Companies who believe they can provide this service 
must indicate their interest in writing within 15 days of this notification and include a detailed 
capability statement.  No reimbursement for any cost connected with providing capability 
information will be provided.  All responsible sources will be considered in evaluating the 
determination to issue a sole-source contract.  Quotations or proposals received in response to 
this notice cannot be accepted since this synopsis cannot be considered a request for quote or a 
request for proposal.  A solicitation will NOT be posted to SAM.gov due to the sole source 
nature of the requirement.  
 
This acquisition is justified under the authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204 (a) (1), “only one responsible 
source,” because Akamai Technologies, Inc. is the only known source capable of meeting 
DISA’s requirements without unacceptable delays or increased costs to the Government. Akamai 
has been deeply integrated into DISA for over a decade, providing highly available, low-latency 
content delivery and security services across both classified and unclassified networks. As such, 
transitioning to an alternate provider would require significant system re-architecting, 
recertification, and re-accreditation, resulting in unacceptable delays, increased costs, and 
significant disruption to mission-critical services across the DoD enterprise. 
 
This approach aligns with the Secretary of Defense Memorandum titled, “Implementation of 
Executive Order 14222 – Department of Government Efficiency and Cost Efficiency Initiative,” 
dated May 27, 2025, DoD Components are now directed to avoid the use of IT integrators and 
consultants, defined as firms providing IT system design, implementation, or advisory services, 
unless it is clearly justified that: 
 
 - The work cannot be performed by existing DoD personnel or agencies; and 
 - The required service cannot be procured directly from the service provider. 
 
Following a thorough market research effort in accordance with FAR Part 10, DISA has 
determined that Akamai Technologies is the only responsible source capable of meeting the 
DoD's requirements for secure, reliable, and globally distributed content delivery services. 
Akamai’s proprietary infrastructure, integrated security features, and operational capabilities 
have been customized to meet GCDS III requirements, and no other vendor possesses the 
technical capacity, cleared operations, or proven performance to deliver these services without 
significant disruption to ongoing DoD missions. 
 
Awarding the contract directly to Akamai eliminates unnecessary reliance on intermediaries, 
reduces costs, and mitigates the risks associated with transitioning to an unproven alternative. 
Akamai’s established global footprint, prior investments in DoD-specific requirements, and 
ability to provide assured performance and continuity are critical to maintaining the security, 
speed, and reliability of the GCDS platform. 
 

Given the urgency of maintaining uninterrupted content delivery and credential management, 
Akamai is the only vendor capable of fulfilling these requirements to the standards demanded by 
DISA and its mission partners. This sole-source acquisition is deemed essential to sustain the 
DoD’s global content delivery mission and ensure alignment with DoD efficiency goals. 
  
The North American Industry Classification System Code (NAICS) for this requirement is 
541519 with the corresponding size standard of $34M. 
 
CONTRACT/PROGRAM BACKGROUND:  
 
Contract Number: HC108421D0002 
Contract Vehicle: Open Market 
Incumbent and their size and CAGE: Peraton Enterprise Solutions LLC (at award Perspecta 
Enterprise Solutions LLC, Change of Name Agreement on Mod P00007), Large Business, 
CAGE: 1U305 
Subcontractor: Akamai Technologies, Inc., Large Business, CAGE: 1YEZ5  
Method of previous acquisition: Full and Open Competition 
Period of performance: February 9, 2021 – February 8, 2027 
 
SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS: The contractor must have a final Secret Facility Clearance from 
the Defense Counterintelligence Security Agency. Personnel performing work under this 
contract must be U.S. citizens possess an interim or final Secret security clearance when contract 
performance starts.

Sara Vogelgesang 
sara.a.vogelgesang.civ@mail.mil 
  
Tricia Singler 
tricia.l.singler.civ@mail.mil

additional publicly available information. Please continue to review www.disa.mil.

NATO UNCLASSIFIED 
NATO UNCLASSIFIED 
2 
Introduction 
NATO is advancing toward data- centric operations, AI -enabled decision superiority, and multi -
domain operational integration. The delivery of a secure, off-premises cloud infrastructure capable 
of handling information up to NATO Secret is a critical enabler of this transition and of the NATO 
Digital Transformation programme. 
To de- risk and accelerate cloud deployment , NATO Allied Command Transformation (ACT) 
intends to contract for a Secure Cloud Service (SCS). SCS will serve as a pre- accreditation 
validation environment, enabling iterative security testing, architecture refinement, and the 
generation of auditable evidence aligned with NATO Security Policy and NIST SP 800-53 Rev.5, 
while delivering a first level of operational cloud capability to priority Communities of Interest 
(COIs). Two prototypes will be delivered to address two different technologies. 
The ACT hereby notifies the following Procurement Opportunity in accordance with the Procedure 
for NATO Competitive Procurement. This notification is issued to foster open and fair competition 
among eligible vendors from participating nations.  
This notification does not constitute a commitment to award a contract. This Procurement 
Opportunity is still pending validation of funding and approvals. 
 
To award the contract(s), the ACT will apply a Sealed Bidding Procedure in accordance with the 
Procurement Policy for NATO Common Funding.  
The RFP (Request for Proposal) will contain two (2) lots, one lot per type of cloud architecture:  
• Lot # 1: a Physical Air-Gap Cloud (fully isolated infrastructure, maximum assurance) 
• Lot # 2: a Hybrid Secure Cloud (cryptographically isolated commercial cloud leveraging 
Confidential Computing) 
 
The contract will be awarded to one or two vendor(s) as a fixed-price contract with the following 
estimated period of performance per Lot:  
• a base period of performance from the award date (estimated 15 July 2026) through 15  
July 2027,  
• one (1) option period may be added: 15 July 2027 – 15 July 2028  
 
The estimated total contract value, inclusive of options, is approximately EUR 20,000,000.00 for 
the two Lots (estimated EUR 5,000,000 per lot per year).  
The cloud architecture (prototype)  prioritize representative capability validation over full 
operational scale.  
 
Vendors are invited to review the requirements described herein and to register for participation 
through the appropriate national authority of the prime vendor's nation of origin. Vendors may 
form partnerships or sub-contractor relationships; however, all vendors, whether prime, partner, 
or sub-contractor, shall meet all identified eligibility requirements for participation.  
Declarations of Eligibility shall be sent to hqsact.contracting@nato.int by 18 May 2026,   0900 
hours, Eastern Standard Time, Norfolk, Virginia. E -mail subject shall include the Procurement 

NATO UNCLASSIFIED 
NATO UNCLASSIFIED 
 
Opportunity information along with company name (for example:  RFP-ACT-SACT-26-54 
Company XYZ). 
This opportunity reflects NATO's commitment to transparency, equal treatment of suppliers, and 
the efficient delivery of goods, works, and services in support of NATO missions and participating 
nations. All eligible and responsible sources may submit a proposal, if and once RFP is published, 
which shall be considered by the ACT. 
1. Title of Procurement Opportunity 
Secure Cloud Service (SCS). 
2. Description of Requirement 
2.1. Background 
Secure cloud capability delivery is on the critical path to NATO Digital Transformation and to 
enabling advancements in Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Multi -Domain Operations (MDO). 
Following decision at NAC (North Alliance Council) level, the alliance  is accelerating its 
programmatic schedule to deploy cloud capabilities. 
These milestones remain vulnerable to delays driven by two principal risk areas: security 
accreditation timeliness for off-premises NATO Secret cloud services, and the complexity of 
migrating Community of Interest (COI) applications into a cloud environment. Several priority 
COIs also require a first level of cloud capability. 
The SCS is designed to de- risk cloud deployment and accelerate the overall roadmap by 
producing a comprehensive security audit report and accreditation evidence package to 
inform a future NATO Secret accreditation decision by December 2026, together with a cloud 
migration sandbox available to COIs through July 2027, or up to July 2028 with options. 
2.2. Project Context & Objective 
The SCS prototype s are contractor-operated service under NATO governance and data 
sovereignty controls supporting approximately 100 concurrent (scalable to 150 for testing 
conditions) users across at least four Communities of Interest. The capability will be deployed 
as a distributed off -premises cloud architecture across at least four sites (government or 
privately owned) in three NATO countries, validating two complementary architectural 
configurations and delivering operational services to priority COIs.  The prototype prioritizes 
representative capability validation over full operational scale The primary objectives are: 
2.2.1. Develop and validate two types of cloud architecture: a Physical Air -Gap Cloud (fully 
isolated infrastructure, maximum assurance) and a Hybrid Secure Cloud (cryptographically 
isolated commercial cloud leveraging Confidential Computing), demonstrating NATO's 
balance of security and operational flexibility. 
2.2.2. Demonstrate and validate a federated, distributed, zero-trust-aligned cloud architecture 
across at least four sites (government or privately owned) in three NATO countries, grounded 
in NIST SP 800-207 and NATO Security Policy. 
2.2.3. Generate accreditation artefacts and audit-ready evidence — including System Security 
Plan, Zero Trust Maturity Report, Vulnerability Assessment Report, and Data Flow Diagrams 
— to enable informed accreditation and implementation decisions. 
2.2.4. Establish a direct, dedicated secure connection between the User Headquarters and 
the Cloud Service Provider (CSP), with minimum target throughput of up to 10 Gbps (or 

NATO UNCLASSIFIED 
NATO UNCLASSIFIED 
 
equivalent performance supporting AI and multi -domain workloads) and network -layer 
encryption. 
2.2.5. Migrate and validate up to four priority COI application workflows — Secure Digital 
Workspace, Secure Generative AI, Modeling & Simulation, and C2 Operations demonstrating 
both refactor/rebuild and lift-and-shift migration approaches. 
2.2.6. Deliver a Confidentiality, Integrity, and Availability (CIA) cloud environment, leveraging 
Cross-Domain Solutions (CDS) and Cross -Transfer Services (CTS) to enable controlled, 
automated data transfer and the secure delivery of updates and patches in to air -gapped 
environments. 
2.2.7. Provide a migration sandbox through July 2027, or up to July 2028 with options, to allow 
additional Communities of Interest to de-risk their transition to the cloud. 
3. Scope of Work [subject to change, pending solicitation to be published] 
The scope is focused on validating representative capabilities required for future operational 
scale, rather than delivering full enterprise deployment. The technical expertise and services 
required to be performed by the Contractor consist of the following lines of effort: 
3.1. Security Architecture and Zero Trust Implementation.  
3.2. Data-Centric Security and Cryptographic Key Management. 
3.3. Secure Direct Connection and Headquarters Infrastructure. 
3.4. Development of Two Cloud Architecture Configurations.  
3.5. Delivery of Four Priority Communities of Interest (COIs).  
3.6. Application Migration Testing.  
3.7. Security Audit, Documentation, and Accreditation Support.  
3.8. Continuous Monitoring, Operations, and Sustainment. 
 
The estimated key milestones for delivery are summarized in the following table: 
Milestone Key Deliverables 
Contract Award Finalised Project Management Plan; Initial Security 
Architecture Design. 
Secure Connectivity 
Established Direct secure connection setup and 100 user onboarding. 
Secure Clouds Developed Two types of prototype cloud architectures and configurations 
on two sites. 
COI Deployment Deployment of COI capabilities across two operational sites 
with consistent functionality and availability. 
Additional Site Deployment Expansion to a total of four fully functional operational sites 
across three NATO countries. 
Security Audit Execution Comprehensive security audit to assess system compliance, 
identify vulnerabilities, and validate implemented controls. 

NATO UNCLASSIFIED 
NATO UNCLASSIFIED 
 
Milestone Key Deliverables 
Final Audit & Accreditation Delivery of final security audit report and, if achieved, system 
accreditation. 
COI Migration Sandbox Sandbox environment for Communities of Interest to de-risk 
cloud migration. 
4. Vendor Eligibility 
4.1. Participation in this Procurement Opportunity is restricted to vendors from NATO 
member nations.  
4.2. Vendors (partners and subcontractors) must hold a NATO or National Facility 
Security Clearance (FSC). The Proposed team must hold NATO or National 
SECRET clearance, at the time of proposal submission.  
4.3. Vendors must demonstrate the financial, technical, and professional capacity to 
deliver a secure cloud service at NATO Secret level, including demonstrable 
experience with Zero Trust architectures, Confidential Computing, Cross-Domain 
Solutions, and operation of dedicated private cloud connectivity. 
5. Access to Solicitation Documentation 
Interested vendors, officially registered by national authorities with a Declaration of Eligibility, 
may participate in and receive the link to the solicitation documentation for this Procurement 
Opportunity by email when the solicitation is released on 
https://www.act.nato.int/opportunities/contracting/

5X52.232-9003, Electronic Invoicing and Payment Requirements and Instructions to Implement Usage of the Invoice Processing Platform (IPP) (MAR 2026)

(a) Definitions. As used in these instructions, "Payment request" means a bill, voucher, invoice, or request for contract financing payment with associated supporting documentation. The payment request must comply with the requirements identified in FAR 32.905(b), "Payment documentation and process" and the applicable Payment clause included in this contract.

(b) Effective 23 Mar 26, the Contractor shall submit payment requests electronically using the Invoice Processing Platform (IPP) at www.ipp.gov. Information regarding IPP is available on the Internet at www.ipp.gov. Assistance with the IPP application can be obtained by contacting the IPP Production Helpdesk via email IPPCustomerSupport@fiscal.treasury.gov or phone (866)973-3131. The Contractor shall ensure that its supporting documentation includes a copy of the contractor’s internal invoice and conforms to IPP requirements. IPP accommodates up to 25 supporting attachments per invoice. Individual attachment file size may not exceed ten megabytes (10mb). If the Contractor assesses that their supporting documentation will not reasonably conform to IPP requirements, the Contractor shall contact the Contracting Officer to explore possible alternatives. In addition, the IPP only allows certain characters to be used as the invoice number. The invoice number shall conform to the IPP convention, and the attachments (if used) shall match exactly the invoice number allowed. The allowed characters in the IPP are "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789-_"

(c) Properly certified invoices shall be entered into the Internet Payment Platform (www.ipp.gov). To assist (Agency) in making timely payments, the Contractor is required to provide/verify all required fields in the IPP including: (1) Contract number; (2) Name, address and Taxpayer I.D. number of Contractor; (3) Invoice Date; (4) Unique invoice number for that particular invoice; (5) Period the payment covers; and (6) Cost amount by each line item including quantity and unit price

(d) Contractors wishing to check the payment status of their vouchers are able to do so within the IPP application. In addition, questions may be directed to the Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR). In the absence of a COR, contact the Contracting Officer whose name and contact information appears on the face page of this contract/order.

(End of clause)

5X252.204-7000-90, PUBLIC RELEASE OF INFORMATION (MAR 2023)

(a) Except as provided in paragraph (b) of this clause, information pertaining to this contract shall not be released to the public unless authorized by the Contracting Officer in accordance with DFARS 252.204-7000, Disclosure of Information. Requests for approval to release information pertaining to this contract shall be submitted to the Contracting Officer by means of NGA Form 5230-1, National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency Request for Clearance for Public Release. 

(b) The contractor may provide past performance information regarding this contract, without completing an NGA Form 5230-1 and without Contracting Officer approval, when submission of such information is to the Office of the Director of National Intelligence (ODNI), the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA), the National Reconnaissance Office (NRO), the National Security Agency (NSA), the Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA), and NGA to support source selections at those agencies. The contractor is responsible for the proper classification and handling of such information, and shall provide a copy of the information provided to the Contracting Officer.

(End of Clause)

PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT 
MUTLIMODAL AI INVESTIGATIVE PLATFORM  
SCANWRITER AI OR EQUIVALENT 
 
C.1 Introduction/Overview 
In support of its law enforcement investigative mission the Internal Revenue 
Service (IRS) Criminal Investigation (CI) Division has a need to purchase 
ScanWriter AI and support or equivalent meeting the identified salient 
characteristics. This requirement is for an investigative data automation, analysis, 
and evidentiary traceability platform, to support IRS Criminal Investigation (CI) 
operations involving high-volume financial records, large multimedia evidence, 
multilingual transcription and translation, and court-defensible analysis conducted in 
on-premises and air-gapped investigative environments.  
 
The platform shall support integration with CI’s existing hyper-converged 
infrastructure (HCI), including its composable HCI architecture and GPU-
accelerated AI/ML compute services. Integration with the Government’s AI 
acceleration framework shall be achieved during the base period of performance 
and may be phased in at Government direction, rather than required as a Day-One 
condition.   
 
C.2 Objective 
The objective for this requirement is for an investigative data automation and analysis 
platform capable of processing large-scale financial records and multimedia evidence 
while maintaining deterministic evidentiary traceability, court-defensible analytics, and 
operational independence in on-premises and air-gapped environments. 
 
C.3 Scope 
The required solution shall: 
• Operate fully on-premises and in disconnected environments with no reliance on 
contractor-hosted services. 
• Convert unstructured financial documents and large multimedia evidence (>4GB) 
into structured, auditable datasets. 
• Provide multilingual transcription and translation while preserving timestamps, 
metadata, and evidentiary integrity. 
• Maintain deterministic, immutable linkage between every derived data element 
and its originating source artifact. 
• Enable one-click validation from analytic outputs back to original evidence 
without reprocessing. 
• Support human-in-the-loop decision support, explainability, and override for 
investigative triage functions. 
• Avoid proprietary ontologies, data lock-in, or contractor-dependent sustainment 
models. 
• Meet or exceed all salient characteristics identified in C.2.1. 
 
This requirement is for court-defensible automation, not general analytics. The 
contractor shall provide a solution that natively preserve source-to-insight traceability, 
explainability, and government control.  

 
 
 
C.2.1 Salient Characteristics 
The salient characteristics set forth below define the IRS CI’s minimum functional, 
performance, security, evidentiary, multilingual, and enterprise scalability requirements 
for the investigative data automation and analysis platform described in the Scope. The 
contractor shall provide a solution that provides:  
 
• Court-defensible analytics and evidentiary traceability 
• Compliance with chain-of-custody and oversight requirements 
• Enterprise-scale multilingual investigative capability 
• Reduced contractor lock-in and long-term sustainment risk 
• Operational readiness for high-volume, complex financial investigations 
• AI-enabled decision support with explainability and governance controls

deployment environments. 
• Be operable, configurable, and extensible by government personnel or 
government-designated integrators without permanent contractor-embedded 
staff. 
• Support deployment within CI-2 hyper-converged and composable GPU-enabled

governance sequencing.1 
• Scale via government-approved compute resources without external data

GENERAL INFORMATION

DESCRIPTION

Introduction

This Request for Information (RFI) is issued for information and planning purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation nor does it restrict the Government as to the ultimate acquisition approach. In accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 15.201(e), responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. 

The purpose of this RFI is to identify qualified vendors, who are able to meet Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) requirements for System Integration and Device Testing Support. Any contract/order that might be awarded based on information received or derived from this market research will be the outcome of the competitive process. The purpose of this RFI is to obtain market information on capable sources of supply, industry’s best practices, and input specific to the information provided. The Government is not responsible for any cost incurred by industry in furnishing this information. All costs associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the interested vendor's expense. Not responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future Request for Quote (RFQ), if any is issued. Any information submitted by respondents to this RFI is strictly voluntary. All submissions will become Government property and will not be returned. Interested vendors are responsible for adequately marking proprietary, restricted or competition sensitive information contained in their response.

Scope

The Contractor shall provide a digital health system that fully supports VA National Center for Collaborative Healthcare Innovation (NCCHI) needs to enhance protocols for diagnosis, stratification, referrals, treatment, and post-treatment care of venous disease and comply with Federal Law and VA requirements capable of supporting up to 2000 patients in the VA Palo Alto Healthcare System (VAPAHCS) and Minneapolis VA Health Care System (MVAHCS).

The Contractor shall fully implement the system in both VAPAHCS and MVAHCS, including software installation, data migration, testing, deployment and technical support. The Contractor shall also provide training to the VA staff, system maintenance and technical support.

This effort aims to standardize care protocols for vascular ulcers, and implement a digital platform for Veterans, care providers, and hospital executives. The platform will provide improved protocols, evidence-based guidance, and enhanced educational resources to ensure effective management and treatment of lower extremity vascular ulcers.

RFI Response Instructions

NOTE: The capability package must be clear, concise, and complete. VA is under no obligation to provide feedback to the company or to contact the company for clarification of any information submitted in response to this RFI.

Provide the following information: 

Company Information:

1. Company Name

2. CAGE/Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) under which the company is registered in SAM.gov and SBA Veteran Certification (VetCert)

3. Company Address

4. Point of contact 

5. Telephone number

6. Email address

7. For small business concerns, indicate whether at least 50 percent of the total amount paid by the Government will be paid to firms that are similarly situated.

Brief summary describing your company’s technical approach to meeting the requirements, to include:

1. Describe your approach to meeting the scope stated in this RFI.

2. Does the draft PWS overall provide sufficient detail to describe the technical and functional requirements that encompass the requirement? If “NO”, please provide your technical and functional comments, recommendations and questions on elements of the draft PWS that may contribute to a more accurate proposal submission and efficient, cost-effective effort. 

3. Does Section 5.0 Specific Task and Deliverables accurately describe what services are to be provided? If “NO”, please provide your technical and functional comments, recommendations and questions.

4. Please include a Rough Order Magnitude (ROM) in your response.

5. If your company is a Small Business, also include the following:

The intent and ability to meet set-aside requirements for performance of this effort. 

Information as to proposed team members, the percentage of work each is to perform and which PWS requirements would be subcontracted.

All proprietary/company confidential material shall be clearly marked on every page that contains such.

Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSB) and Veteran Owned Small Businesses (VOSB) must indicate whether at least 50% of the cost incurred would be expended for prime employees or employees of other eligible SDVOSB/VOSB firms. BACKGROUND

The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Veterans Health Administration (VHA), National Center for Collaborative Healthcare Innovation (NCCHI) is dedicated to advancing healthcare outcomes for Veterans through innovative technologies and practices. By fostering collaboration among healthcare professionals, researchers, technologists, and key stakeholders, the NCCHI aims to implement cutting-edge solutions to address Veterans' unique healthcare challenges. 

To support this mission, NCCHI seeks to enhance the management of complex diseases among Veterans through a digital platform. Venous diseases, such as Post-Thrombotic Syndrome (PTS), Pelvic Congestion Syndrome (PCS), Superficial Venous Insufficiency (SVI), Chronic Venous Disease (CVD), Pulmonary Embolism (PE) and Venous Leg Ulcers (VLU), pose significant global health challenges. Veterans with these conditions often experience a reduced quality of life, difficulties navigating the healthcare system, and an increased risk of social isolation, substance abuse, and suicide. 

The current management pathways for venous diseases are inadequate, fragmented, and contribute to substantial healthcare costs, estimated at approximately $15 billion annually in the United States for VLU alone. A lack of focused training on venous disease in medical education leads to inconsistent diagnosis, variable referrals to specialists, and diverse treatment approaches that fail to address the root cause of the disease or consider long-term care implications. There is a deficiency in practical evidence-based guidance available for clinicians to inform proper management and treatment strategies. This gap underscores the necessity for improved educational resources and enhanced evidence-based protocols in the care of patients with venous disorders.

This effort aims to standardize care protocols for vascular ulcers, and implement a digital platform for Veterans, care providers, and hospital executives. The platform will provide improved protocols, evidence-based guidance, and enhanced educational resources to ensure effective management and treatment of lower extremity vascular ulcers.

A. The purpose of this amendment is to provide the Government’s official responses to 
the questions submitted by interested vendors on April 19, 2026.  
 
The questions and the Government’s corresponding responses are set forth below. 
 
Question 1: Patient Lay Summary Letters (PWS Section 5.2.8.B): Section 5.2.8.B 
requires the system to "allow for some nationally standardized portions of the 
Results letters that cannot be changed locally, while still allowing some aspects of 
the results letter to be customized by the facility." Patient Hub currently 
supports results letter customization by facility (including by state), but does not 
enforce nationally standardized, non-editable letter components.  
 
Can VA clarify what specific portions of the results letters are intended to be 
nationally standardized, and whether facility-level customization (which would allow 
facilities to adopt a common standard voluntarily) meets this requirement?  
 
Response: The VA wants to nationally standardize and require the lay summary 
letters utilize FDA breast density statements. The goal is to standardize as much as 
possible.  
 
Question 2: Disaster Recovery and Backup Responsibilities (PWS Section 5.3, 
Technical Functionality, Item 2): Section 5.3 requires the Contractor to provide a 
comprehensive disaster recovery plan, including a process for performing automated 
system backups, a process for restoring system backups, and a summary of third-
party enterprise backup solutions/agents that the MTRS system supports. Because 
Patient Hub will be hosted on VA infrastructure, backup and restore operations will 
be performed by VA IT using VA enterprise tools.  
 
Can the VA confirm that (a) responsibility for executing, scheduling, and monitoring 
system backups and restorations rests with VA IT, and (b) a vendor’s obligation 
under Section 5.3(2) is limited to documenting Patient Hub's compatibility with VA's 
enterprise backup solutions and providing technical guidance to support VA's 
backup and recovery processes? 
 
Response: VA confirms that it is a VA responsibility to execute system back-ups and 
restorations. The expectation is that the contractor would provide a comprehensive 
plan for VA to execute based on the technical compatibility and capability of the 
MTRS system backup features and processes. The contractor shall also provide 
technical guidance as required for the backup and recovery process. 
 
Question 3: Patching Responsibilities (PWS Section 5.12.F and Addendum B, 
Section B6.n): Section 5.12.F requires the Contractor to provide technical expertise 
regarding system patching and updates, including operating system (OS) patches, 
application updates, database updates, and system vulnerabilities. Section B6.n 
further requires the Contractor to apply security fixes within specified timeframes

when the Contractor is responsible for operations or maintenance of the systems. 
Because Patient Hub will be hosted on VA infrastructure, OS patching is performed 
by VA IT.  
 
Can the VA confirm that (a) responsibility for OS-level patching rests with VA IT, (b) 
a vendor’s patching obligations under Sections 5.12.F and B6.n are limited to 
application-layer and database updates for the Patient Hub software, and (c) A 
vendor’s role with respect to OS patches is limited to providing technical guidance,

Question 4: Security Incident Reporting Timeline (PWS Addendum B, Section B5.a 
and Addendum A, Section A1.0): Section B5.a requires reporting of suspected 
security/privacy incidents to the VA Enterprise Service Desk within one hour, and 
Section A1.0 similarly requires notice to the COR/CO within one hour of disclosure

incident response procedures, provide for customer notification within 24 hours, 
which allows time for initial triage and confirmation of whether an event constitutes a

Can the VA (a) extend the notification window to 24 hours for suspected incidents,

REQUEST FOR QUOTE

RFQ DJA-26-ASOD-PR-0088

BACKGROUND

ATF requires BLN 8.13 and BLN 10.01: Vehicle Forensics Collection: Commercial vehicle forensics and vehicle-resident data sanitization capability, consisting of portable hardware and associated software licenses, training, and support. The capability enables authorized ATF personnel to lawfully acquire, analyze, report, and, when authorized, sanitize electronic data stored within vehicle infotainment, telematics, and control modules. for the Reliability and Maintainability Information System (REMIS) Program in support of the 
United States Air Force (USAF). This action is required to prevent a break in service caused by a 
stay of performance on a competitive follow-on contract. 
 
Solicitation Number: FA877026RB005 
 
Agency/Office: Department of War / Business Enterprise Systems (BES) 
 
Location: Wright-Patterson Air Force Base 
 
Description: 
The Department of War, BES AFLCMC/GBK4M, intends to negotiate and award a firm-fixed-
price contract on a sole source basis to Innovative Management Concepts, INC., located at 428 
Honaker Road, Blairsville, GA 30512-1205. 
 
The purpose of this acquisition is to obtain REMIS support during a period of performance from 
01 June 2026 to 31 August 2027. Under this requirement, the Contractor shall provide all 
technical and operational support for the REMIS program. This includes full software 
development life-cycle activities, systems engineering, development, integration, and operational 
processes to preserve and enhance REMIS service capabilities. The contract type is a mix of 
Firm-Fixed Price (FFP), Labor Hour (LH), and Cost Reimbursement (CR). The contract will 
include a 3-month base and two (2) 6-month options.  
 
Justification: 
This acquisition is being conducted under the authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), as implemented 
by FAR 6.302-1, "Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy 
agency requirements." This action is critical to ensure the uninterrupted continuation of 
enhancement and sustainment services for the REMIS contract. The contractor is the only 
responsible source capable of continuing these critical services without a disruption. The 
contractor possesses an unmatched and immediate understanding of the complex requirements, 
architecture, and operational dependencies of the REMIS system. 
 
Response Instructions: 
This notice of intent is NOT a request for competitive proposals. However, all responsible 
sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation, which shall be considered by 
the agency. Capability statements must be received by 08 May 2026 before 1700 EST and must 
clearly demonstrate the vendor's ability to meet the requirements described herein. A 
determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to 
this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. 
 

Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether 
to conduct a competitive procurement. 
 
Point of Contact: 
Antonio Ayubi, Contracting Officer 
Email: antonio.ayubi@us.af.mil

REQUEST FOR INFORMATION 
U.S. Special Operations Command 
AI Based Protections on Commercial Internet  
 
 
27 April 2026 
 
 
 
 
 
 


2 
 
The United States Special Operations Command (USSOCOM), J6 is requesting 
information regarding AI driven cybersecurity solutions for use on its commercial internet 
service that can perform the following capabilities: 
Real-time threat detection, behavioral analytics, automated incident response, and 
continuous learning are necessary to counter increasingly sophisticated threats  to 
enhance the defensive posture of HQs USSOCOM commercial internet.   
This Request for I nformation (RFI) is for planning purposes only and shall not be 
considered as an invitation for bid, request for proposal, or as an obligation on the part of 
the Government to acquire any products or services. Your response to this RFI will be 
treated as i nformation only. No entitlement to payment of direct or indirect costs or 
charges by the Government will arise as a result of contractor submission of responses 
to this announcement of the Government use of such information. Interested parties are 
responsible for adequately marking proprietary or competition sensitive information 
contained in their response. The Government does not intend to award a contract on the 
basis of this RFI or to otherwise pay for the information submitted in response to this RFI. 
There are no guarantees of a follow-on contract for this requirement.   
The intent of the RFI is to: 
1) Identify artificial intelligence (AI) driven cybersecurity solutions that meet the 
minimum technical requirements identified below.  
The minimum technical requirements are as follows:  
• On-prem or hybrid deployment model and integration with existing security 
stacks and tools (e.g. MDE) 
• Protection of Windows, Linux, and Mac operating systems 
• Policy enforcement capabilities (blocking, prompting, step-up verification, session 
restriction) 
• Logging and auditing 
• Enhanced detection for exfiltration attempts, unauthorized access, and 
anomalous file activity 
• Zero Trust cybersecurity principles 
• Real-Time Web Filtering: Ability to analyze and block access to malicious 
websites, including phishing sites, and malware distribution points in real-time.  
• Predictive Threat Intelligence: Identify and block new and emerging (zero-day) 
malicious domains and URLs based on behavioral analysis, rather than relying 
solely on known threat feeds.  
• Encrypted Traffic Analysis: Capability to inspect encrypted traffic (e.g., TLS 1.3) 
for threats without compromising data privacy.  
• Anti-Phishing and Social Engineering Prevention: Advanced detection of 
sophisticated phishing, spear-phishing, and social engineering attempts by 
analyzing content, context, and sender behavior.  

3 
 
• Behavioral Baselining:  Establish and dynamically update a baseline of normal 
behavior for each user and entity (e.g., servers, devices, applications) on the 
network.  
• Anomaly Detection:  Identify and flag statistically significant deviations from 
established baselines that may indicate an insider threat, compromised 
credentials, or account takeover.  This includes detecting unusual login 
times/locations, abnormal data access patterns, and atypical system interactions.  
• Risk Scoring:  Assign risk scores to anomalous activities to help security teams 
prioritize alerts and focus on the most critical threats, reducing alert fatigue and 
false positives.  
• Data Discovery and Classification:  Automatically discover and classify sensitive 
data, such as CUI, across the domain   
• Data Loss Prevention (DLP):  Monitor and prevent the unauthorized exfiltration of 
sensitive data across various channels (e.g., email, web uploads, removable 
media). The system should understand the content and context of data to prevent 
leaks. 
• AI Governance: Provide visibility and control over the use of internal and external 
AI tools by employees to prevent the leakage of sensitive data into generative AI 
platforms. 
Responses to the RFI must include: 
i. Indicate if purchase can be made through NASA SEWP, GSA, FedBizOpps, or on 
some other Government Contract or Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) 
Responses should be no greater than a five page info paper or 15 slide PowerPoint 
presentation. Do not provide price quotes.  
Please provide the name of the firm, address, POC, phone/fax number, and email 
address. 
Responses will be viewed by both Government and non- Government employees.   If a 
Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA) is required, submit the NDA with your response.  
E-mail responses only . All communication must be conducted via e- mail to 
Kristen.colyer@socom.mil.

Request for Information (RFI) for Enterprise Governance, Data Tagging, and Records Management Solution for Microsoft 365

1. GENERAL INFORMATION

Notice Type: Request for Information (RFI) / Sources Sought

RFI Number: RFI-ARMY-DTSPO-2026-0420

Issuing Office: Army Contracting Command – Aberdeen Proving Ground, Huachuca Division, Bravo Branch

NAICS Code: 541512 - Computer Systems Design Services

Date Issued: 20 April 2026

Response Due Date: 28 April 2026, 4:00 PM Arizona Time

DISCLAIMER: This Request for Information (RFI) is issued solely for information and planning purposes. It does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFP in the future. This RFI does not commit the Government to contract for any supply or service whatsoever. The Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this RFI. All information received in response to this RFI that is marked “Proprietary” will be handled accordingly.

2. BACKGROUND

The U.S. Army operates one of the largest and most complex Microsoft 365 (M365) environments in the world, presenting significant challenges for governance, security, and compliance. The Government requires a technical solution to enforce policy, automate administrative and records management tasks, provide hierarchical visibility and control, and empower a delegated administration model across Major Commands (MACOMs) and subordinate organizations. The solution must seamlessly integrate with and enhance the native capabilities of the M365 platform while scaling to meet the Army's performance demands.

3. SCOPE OF REQUIREMENT

The Government is seeking a mature, scalable Commercial-Off-The-Shelf (COTS) solution to meet requirements across several key functional areas, including Enterprise Governance, Data Sensitivity and Security (Data Tagging), Automated Records Management, SharePoint & Teams Management, and Storage Optimization. The solution must be a configurable, vendor-supported platform, not a custom software development effort.

4. INFORMATION REQUESTED

Interested parties are requested to provide a response that addresses the following sections.

PART I: CORPORATE INFORMATION

1.1 Company Name & Address:

1.2 Point of Contact: (Name, Title, Email, Phone Number)

1.3 CAGE Code & Unique Entity Identifier (UEI):

1.4 Business Size & Socio-Economic Status: (e.g., Large Business, Small Business, 8(a), WOSB, SDVOSB, etc.)

1.5 Federal Contract Experience: Briefly describe your experience providing IT solutions to DoD or other Federal agencies. Include relevant contract vehicles you currently hold (e.g., GSA MAS, SEWP, ITES-SW2).

1.6 Subcontracting: Does your approach for this requirement require subcontracting?

PART II: SOLUTION OVERVIEW

2.1 Solution Name & Description: Provide the name of your potential proposed COTS solution and a brief, high-level overview of its architecture (e.g., Software as a Service (SaaS), on-premises virtual appliance, hybrid).

2.2 Federal Security Compliance: Describe your potential solution's current security posture. Is it FedRAMP authorized? At what level (Low, Moderate, High)? Does the solution operate in Azure Government Cloud at DoD Impact Level 5 (IL5)?

2.3 Maturity: How long has the potentially proposed solution been commercially available?

PART III: CAPABILITY & TECHNICAL QUESTIONS

Please provide a direct response to each of the following questions regarding your potentially proposed solution.

How do you integrate with other capabilities? Particularly MS Purview and SharePoint Online.

What Admin permissions or API permissions required for the software to function?

How are admin permissions managed within the software?

How are logs handled?

How are reports and alerts managed? Are they customizable?

What administrative roles or service accounts from your solution require permissions within the Army’s Microsoft 365 (A365) tenant?

Do any components require tenant-wide administrative permissions (e.g., Global Admin, SharePoint Admin, Compliance Admin)? If so, how are these used?

Does the product use Azure Entra ID app registrations, and what Application Programming Interface (API) permissions are required?

Does the solution require any vendor access to Army M365 data or your solution’s supporting infrastructure during normal operations or troubleshooting?

Describe which functions of your solution run inside the Army M365 tenant versus within your hosted environment.

Does any processing leverage vendor-managed Artificial Intelligence/Machine Learning (AI/ML) models, and can AI/ML analytics be performed without exporting sensitive content or metadata?

What is the expected volume of API calls per day, and does the solution require elevated throttling limits?

Does your solution support Common Access Card/Personal Identity Verification (CAC/PIV), conditional access, and Entra ID-based identity?

What access (if any) do your personnel or systems require to Army M365 data or to your solution’s supporting infrastructure (e.g., SaaS back end, support tools, logs), including during troubleshooting, and what authentication/authorization controls govern that access?

Can the solution operate with zero vendor access after deployment, and can all vendor access be disabled or audited by Army Network Enterprise Technology Command (NETCOM)?

Identify whether any Army data (including metadata, logs, labels, or content) is copied, stored, or processed outside the M365 boundary. Include any dependencies on vendor-managed infrastructure, hosting outside Department of Defense (DoD) IL5, or use of non-U.S. regions or subcontractors.

If your solution includes SaaS or vendor-hosted components, identify the compliance level of those environments (e.g., FedRAMP High, DoD IL5) and status of any relevant authorizations (e.g., DISA Provisional Authorization for IL5). 

How does your solution enforce Army-aligned delegated administrative scoping, and are all administrative actions fully audit-logged with the ability to export logs to Army Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) tools in near real time?

Where are audit logs, telemetry, and analytics data stored, and can all such data remain entirely within the Army’s M365 tenant? If any logs reside in vendor systems, identify what data elements are stored, for how long, and in what regions or environments.

How does the solution ensure compliance with National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) retention rules when performing:

Redundant, Obsolete, and Trivial (ROT) cleanup

lifecycle actions

metadata remediation

bulk operations

Does any processing leverage vendor-managed AI/ML models outside the Army environment?

Does your backup capability require extraction of data outside Microsoft’s boundary, and (if so) are backups stored in environments certified at IL5?

Can data restores be performed without violating retention or legal hold constraints?

Provide a complete list of all administrative actions your system can take on Army content or configuration, including:

Where the logic runs (tenant / vendor / hybrid)

Required permissions

How actions are validated and logged

Whether actions can be restricted by MACOM or command

What guardrails exist to prevent accidental or malicious bulk changes?

5. SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS

Format: Responses shall be submitted in PDF format. 

Submission: All responses must be submitted electronically to the points of contact below no later than the Response Due Date.

Name: Contracting Officer, Walter L. Carbajal 

Email: walter.l.carbajal.civ@army.mil 

Subject Line: "Response to RFI RFI-ARMY-DTSPO-2026-0420

Questions: Any questions regarding this RFI shall be submitted via email to the same points of contact no later than 23 April 2026, 4:00 PM Arizona Time.

SBEM IDIQ Task Order 1 (TO-1) 
Statement of Work 
Introduction 
In this Task Order, NOAA intends to acquire near-real-time global navigation satellite 
system (GNSS) radio occultation (RO) satellite data satisfying the requirements set forth in 
the NOAA Commercial Data Program Space Based Environmental Monitoring (SBEM) 
IDIQ contract Statement of Work (SOW). NOAA intends to use these data in operational 
numerical weather prediction models, space weather models, and other systems. NOAA 
reserves the right to issue subsequent, simultaneous, and additional Task Orders for RO 
data during this period of performance.  
Scope 
NOAA is soliciting commercial near-real-time satellite-based GNSS RO and ionospheric 
measurements that will be processed into neutral atmosphere and space weather products. 
These derived products will be fed into NOAA’s operational data systems, including weather 
and space weather analysis and prediction systems, and used for weather, climate, and 
atmospheric research purposes. All data and products will be archived by NOAA. NOAA 
seeks the following requirements: 
Requirements 
Part I - Data Preparation 
I. Requirements for New GNSS-RO Data Providers 
A. For Contractors who have not previously delivered GNSS-RO data to NOAA, the 
Contractor shall provide all necessary information needed to support NOAA 
implementation and testing of the Contractor’s data. The Contractor shall provide 
technical documentation (SBEM IDIQ SOW Section C.4.5.3: Data Delivery and 
Documentation), including but not limited to data format specifications, sample data, 
and other information required for data ingestion and processing (SBEM IDIQ SOW 
Sections C.3.1: Test Data, C.3.1.1: Limited Test Data Deliveries, C.4.5.4: GNSS-RO 
Test Data). Delivery mechanisms and data handling procedures will be communicated 
to the Contractor. 
B. The Contractor shall provide engineering support as needed to enable Government 
acquisition and processing of the supplied datasets to include supporting technical 
exchanges. The Contractor shall deliver sample data for secure ingest, configuration 
and testing. Additionally, the Contractor shall deliver up to 48 hours of contiguous 
near-real-time data for testing of delivery and data flow processes (SBEM IDIQ SOW

Government agencies, International Partners, including but not limited to 
those responsible for national meteorological, space weather, or

D. Spatial distribution is an important aspect of the data delivery requirements. The 
Government seeks delivery of all global data (all latitudes and longitudes) to meet or 
exceed the requirements specified in SBEM IDIQ SOW Section C.4.3.2: Specific 
Geospatial Distributions, paragraphs 1 and 2 only (paragraph 3 does 
      not apply to 
this task order).  
E. This SOW includes Desired Capabilities.  Desired Capabilities are features of Offeror 
provided data that are requested by the Government but are not mandatory.  Desired 
Capabilities are requested in order to improve the utility of delivered data and are 
considered to add value to the Offeror proposals.   
II. Requirement - Neutral Atmosphere Data 
A. The Government seeks a total of 10,000 to 26     ,000 compliant radio occultation 
(RO) profiles per day as specified in SBEM IDIQ SOW Sections C.4.3.3: Neutral 
Atmosphere Data Requirements (Category 1), and C.4.5: Delivery Requirements.  
III. Desired Capability - Total Electron Content (TEC) Data  
A. The Government seeks a total of 500 to 1,000 compliant Total Electron Content 
(TEC) ionospheric tracks per day as specified in SBEM IDIQ SOW Sections C.4.3.5     
: Space Weather Data Requirements, C.4.3.5.1     : Requirements for Total Electron 
Content (TEC), and C.4.5: Delivery Requirements.  
IV. Desired Capability - Temporal Resolution Enhancements 
A. To increase temporal resolution of the Government’s GNSS-RO data collections, the 

 
4 
Government seeks RO observations from Sun-Synchronous Orbits (SSO) other than 
only within the 0800-1200 and 2000-2400 equatorial crossing time ranges and/or 
from lower-inclination orbits (non-SSO).  The equatorial crossing time is defined as 
when the space vehicle crosses the Earth’s equatorial plane.  This Temporal 
Resolution Enhancement data will be included as part of the total number of profiles 
in Part II, Section II of this SOW. The Contractor is requested to provide the number 
of compliant temporal resolution enhancement RO profiles they can deliver within 
each proposed local time window and/or from each lower-inclined orbit (for satellites 
not in SSO). 
B. While currently a desired capability, NOAA views the diversification of equatorial 
orbital crossings and increased temporal sampling over the tropics and subtropics as 
a high-priority strategic objective. The Government intends to use this data to validate 
requirements for anticipated mandatory coverage in future Task Orders. 
V. Requirement Deliverables - Operational Status Reporting 
A. The Contractor shall deliver information reports as specified in the SBEM IDIQ SOW 
Section C.3.3
     : Notifications.      . The Contractor shall deliver the i     nformation 
reports to NOAA      no later than seven (7) calendar days following the conclusion of 
each three-month reporting period (e.g., the December, January, and February report 
is due by March 7th; the March, April, May report is due by June 7th; etc.). 
B. The Contractor shall inform the Government within 24 hours of any anomalies that 
adversely affect contractual data delivery requirements and provide an estimated 
time of repair.

REQUEST FOR INFORMATION - Next Generation 
Command and Control (NGC2) Software 
Application Storefront, Pipeline and Tailorable 
Warfighting Applications 
Synopsis 
The following Request for Information (RFI) is to gain an understanding from Industry on the 
capabilities offered to support Project Manager for Command and Control Applications (PM 
C2 Apps) entire portfolio. The Government is considering an acquisition strategy that uses a 
"teaming" model to consolidate the PM C2 Apps portfolio under a singular lead, tasked with 
managing a unified development pipeline and application storefront. This approach mirrors 
the Next Generation Command and Control (NGC2) "clean-slate" methodology, which 
emphasizes Agile and Development, Security and Operations (DevSecOps) environments to 
rapidly deliver and iterate on mission-focused software. By partnering with a lead entity to 
integrate a mix of Government-Off-The-Shelf (GOTS), Commercial-Off-The-Shelf (COTS), and 
tactical solutions, the strategy aims to provide the Warfighter with a flexible, modular, and 
interoperable suite of applications that can be updated at the "speed of relevance". The 
Government is particularly interested in solutions offered by entities with direct control over 
the capability's development and innovation. Respondents should clearly describe whether 
they are the original capability provider or an intermediary (reseller/integrator), and 
demonstrate their ability to drive innovation, influence product roadmaps, and provide direct 
technical support. The government envisions mission success by establishing group 
collaboration among all industry partners for the overall success of the program to include 
the application development/oversight from various partners (GOTS/COTS/etc) through 
pipeline/DSO to the storefront for User Access. The government intends to conduct an 
industry day to provide an overview to further support and enhance market research. 
Understanding this is a new concept, the Government welcomes feedback on the feasibility of 
this approach from Industry as well as the specific questions detailed in later sections of this 
RFI.
 
Description 
1. Description  
1.1 PM C2 Apps seeks industry interest regarding the availability of a software application 
storefront, pipeline and tailorable warfighting application solutions. This Request For 
Information (RFI) is being issued to conduct market research for solutions using an Agile and 

DevSecOps environment. Furthermore, this advanced notice is being issued to obtain insight 
and responses from Industry regarding some or all of the questions and requests listed in 
Table 1. These responses will help PM C2 Apps shape requirements, understand capability 
gaps, and/or understand Industry provided solutions that PM C2 Apps may pursue through 
the Army Open Solicitation (AOS) during 3rd quarter (Q3) Fiscal Year (FY) 2026.  
 
1.2 THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION: The Government is not obligated to pursue any 
procurement as a result of this request. This RFI is for informational purposes only; this is not 
an Invitation for Bid (IFB), Request for Proposal (RFP), or Request for Quotation (RFQ). All 
information contained in this RFI is preliminary as well as subject to modification and is in no 
way binding on the Government. The Government will not pay for information received and is 
in no way obligated by the information received in response to this RFI. Responders to this 
invitation are solely responsible for all expenses associated with responding to this RFI and 
will NOT be reimbursed. The information provided will be used by the Government for the 
purpose of conducting market research and this RFI will be the basis for collecting 
information on capabilities available. Interested parties are responsible for adequately 
marking proprietary or competition sensitive information contained in their response. It is 
the responsibility of the interested parties to monitor SAM.gov for additional information 
pertaining to this RFI.  
 
1.3 The information provided may be used by the Army in developing its acquisition strategy 
or developing system Performance Specification.  The applicable North American Industry 
Classification System (NAICS) code for this requirement is 541511 with a Small Business Size 
Standard of 1250 employees. 
 
2. Background 
The expected operational mission of PM C2 Apps is to deliver and continuously update the 
foundational platform that enables rapid, secure, and continuous software delivery for the 
Army's Next Generation Command and Control (NGC2) ecosystem. While navigating the 
requirements below, the initial set of features will focus on establishing an end-to-end "thin 
thread" of capability: a basic Continuous Integration/Continuous Delivery (CI/CD) pipeline for 
onboarding software applications and a rudimentary storefront interface to display it. This 
established the foundation for PM C2 Apps to support their primary mission to provide 
warfighting function applications.  
 
 
 

3. Responses 
3.1 Responses: Interested parties are asked to respond to this RFI with the enclosed 
Attachment 1 – Response Form.  The Attachment 1 Response Form shall be submitted as one 
(1) document in Microsoft Word for Office 2000 compatible format. Respondents are asked to 
use the template “Attachment 1 Response Form” to identify their solution(s) that could 
answer the requests and inquiries in section 3.3, , 3.41 (table 1), and section 3.4.2.  The 
Government will not consider inserted textboxes/pop-ups or internet links to additional 
information as part of the response.  Responses shall be limited to no more than twenty-five 
(25) pages using 11-point font for the entire submission (including company information, 
answers to technical questions, supporting documentation, ROM, notional schedule, etc.).  
Respondents are permitted to replace the cover page in the template with their own but it 
must be one (1) page and shall only include what is outlined in Section 3.2 and 3.3.   
Responses are due NLT 27 MAY 2026, 1200, Eastern Time (ET) and must be submitted via e-
mail to the following email address: PM_C2_Apps_RFI@army.mil with the email subject 
line “PM_C2_Apps_RFI_Response_Form ”  
 
3.2 Proprietary information, if any, should be minimized and MUST BE CLEARLY MARKED. To 
aid the Government, please segregate proprietary information. Please be advised that all 
submissions become Government property and will not be returned. In addition to 
Government civilians, Government support contractors may review and evaluate the 
whitepaper submission.  As of now, PM C2 Apps has not identified the need for contractor 
support personnel to review RFI response(s). Should a need be identified, the RFI will be 
updated to include Proprietary Data Protection Agreement (PDPA) instructions. 
 
 
3.3 Company Information. The response should provide the following information: 
i. Contact Information: Company name, mailing address, overnight delivery address (if 
different from mailing address), phone number, fax number, and e-mail of designated point 
of contact. 
 
ii. Availability of your proposed solution for purchasing through an existing multiple award 
IDIQ contract vehicle, such as Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) and Common Hardware 
Solutions (CHS).  
 
iii. Business size and socioeconomic status for NAICS Code 541511. 
 
iv. Status as a Traditional Defense Contractor or Non-Traditional Defense Contractor.

below.  As a reminder from the synopsis, respondents should also clearly describe whether 
they are the original capability provider or an intermediary (reseller/integrator), and 
demonstrate their ability to drive innovation, influence product roadmaps, and provide direct 
technical support.
