CONTROLLED UNCLASSIFIED INFORMATION 
 
 FA8307-26-R-CW02 
Request for Information (RFI) 
For 
 
Offensive Cyber Depot 
Operations & Sustainment 
 
 
1. Introduction 
 
(U) This Request for Information (RFI) is in accordance with the Revolutionary Far Overhaul 
(RFO) clause 52.215-3 (Request for Information or Solicitation for Planning Purposes - Oct 
1997) and is published only to obtain information for use by the Air Force Life Cycle 
Management Center(AFLCMC), Joint Base San Antonio - Lackland, Texas, for planning 
purposes only. 
 
(U) This RFI does not constitute an invitation for bids, a request for proposal, a solicitation, a 
request for quote or an indication that the Government will contract for the items provided by 
submitter. The Government will not reimburse respondents for any costs associated with the 
preparation or submission of the information requested. Response to this RFI is strictly voluntary 
and will not affect any potential offeror's ability to submit an offer if a solicitation is released. 
Any requests for a solicitation package will be disregarded. The Government does not intend to 
award a contract based on this RFI or otherwise pay for the information solicited. No entitlement 
to payment of direct or indirect costs or charges by the Government will arise as a result of 
preparing submissions in response to this RFI and the Government's use of such information. 
 
(U) Submittals will not be returned to the sender. Respondents of this RFI may be requested to 
provide additional information/details based on their initial submittals. 
 
2. Background 
 
(CUI) AFLCMC/HNCK Cryptologic and Cyber Systems Division, Contracting Branch Joint 
Base San Antonio - Lackland TX, is seeking a Depot Support contract from vendors who have 
the capability to perform Cost Plus operations and sustainment activities for cyber weapon 
systems within the AFLCMC/HNCO (Offensive Cyber Systems) portfolio.  Ideally, vendors will 
recommend use of an existing Indefinite Delivery / Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract to which 
they are a party, and which is accessible by DoD Agencies. 
 
3. Objective 
 
Potential vendors will be required to perform the following:  
 
(CUI) 
 Provide Tier 1, 2, and 3 level support for complex information systems. 
 

CONTROLLED UNCLASSIFIED INFORMATION 
 
(U) Repair, update, and return complex information systems to service. 
 
(CUI) Create virtual machines, networks, and infrastructures in an air-gapped environment. 
 
(U) Update and maintain hardware and software configuration baselines for these systems. 
 
(CUI) Software expected to be relevant to this effort includes (but is not limited to) 
 - Microsoft Server 2022 and beyond 
 - Red Hat Enterprise Linux 
 - VMWare / vSphere / ESXi 
 - Microsoft Windows 11 Enterprise 
 - SecureView 
 - Etc. 
 
(CUI) Hardware expected to be relevant to this effort includes (but is not limited to) 
 - Servers 
 - Switches 
 - Firewalls 
 - Workstations 
 - Keyboard / Video / Mouse (KVM) devices 
 - Etc. 
 
(U) Install and maintain services under a service-oriented architecture. 
 
(CUI) Work within the government’s Risk Management Framework (RMF) to obtain and retain system 
Interim Approval to Test (IATT), Authority to Connect (ATC), and Authority to Operate (ATO) 
approvals. 
 
(U) Perform system scans in compliance with Security Technical Implementation Guides (STIG). 
 
(U) Perform continuous system monitoring to maintain RMF ATO including, but not limited to, 
performing system ACAS scans in compliance with DISA Security Technical Implementation Guides 
(STIG), performing weekly security posture reviews, and monitor Information Assurance Vulnerability 
Alerts (IAVMs) 
 
(U) Write, update and provide System User Manuals, System Description/Design Documents, System 
Installation Guides, and other types of technical reports and data. 
 
(CUI) Provide and operate a contractor Sensitive Compartmented Information Facility (SCIF) in the San 
Antonio Metropolitan Area.  The SCIF must have connected AFSCI terminals and provide sufficient 
space for the contractor workforce (estimated 8 - 10 positions) 
 
(CUI) Provide and operate an unclassified server space to host Test and Integration (T&I) system offsite. 
Space must have an internet connection to allow contractor team to download system updates that can be 
tested on the T&I before being brought on site. 
 
(CUI) Provide Help Desk services to our customers.  Help Desk ‘tickets’ will be maintained on the 
AFSCI system.  Help Desk will be available on a 24/7 basis via an ‘on call’ point of contact at all times. 
 
(CUI) The workforce will require TS/SCI eligibility and is anticipated to consist of a mix of the following 

CONTROLLED UNCLASSIFIED INFORMATION 
 
(or similar) labor categories: 
 - Network Specialists 
 - System Engineers 
 - System Administrators 
 - Help Desk Support 
 - Configuration Manager 
- Test Engineer 
 - Information System Security Manager (ISSM) 
 - Other, as deemed necessary by the contractor 
 
(CUI) Some members of the workforce will require Special Access eligibility. 
 
(U) Work with the incumbent contractor to ensure a smooth transition, if applicable. 
 
4. Requested Information. 
 
(U) This is not a request for competitive proposals.   If a vendor believes it can meet the 
Government's requirement, it may identify its interest and capability to Capt Charles Craig 
(Contracting Officer) at charles.craig.2@us.af.mil within ten (10) business days of this 
publication. Interested vendors are requested to submit a capability statement/white paper (no 
more than 5 pages, not inclusive of title page) and a ROM.  Hard copies will not be accepted. 
Respondents shall ensure submissions are sent at the appropriate security level. It is preferred 
that only non-proprietary information be submitted. However, proprietary information, if 
submitted, should be kept to a minimum and MUST BE CLEARLY MARKED. Respondents are 
advised that information submitted in response to this RFI may be released to non-Government 
advisors for review and analysis. 
 
5. Questions. 
 
(U) If you have any specific questions (relating to the above information only) please submit 
them in written format to the Contracting Officer listed above no later than April 20, 2026.  
Telephonic questions will not be entertained, and responses to this RFI will not be returned.

The Defense Health Agency and the Defense Health Agency Contracting Activity (DHACA) located at Fort Detrick, MD, intends to negotiate solely (as prescribed in FAR 13.106-1(b)(1)(i) with Accenture Federal Services LLC, 800 North Glebe RD # 300, Arlington, VA, 22203-1807.

The required services entail an annual maintenance agreement, which includes technical support and product updates for the “Accenture StartingPoint” CTD templates. The Defense Health Agency, Office of Regulated Activities (ORA) purchased proprietary, macro-based, Microsoft Word electronic Common Technical Document (CTD) "StartingPoint" templates from Octagon Research Solutions, Inc., now Accenture, in February 2009.

Accenture Federal Services LLC “StartingPoint” CTD Templates enable rapid deployment of regulatory authoring standards across functional areas to facilitate efficient authoring of all components of the CTD along with submissions to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. This requirement will allow for continuation of product updates, and support for use of the existing templates. Templates include instructional text from the International Council for Harmonization (ICH) guidance documents as well as automation of frequently used authoring functions. The content templates and the associated administration files that govern their automation require updates frequently. Updates consist of new or updated content templates, and issue resolutions. In addition, new functions may require additional technical support regarding how the templates work and how to use the templates, beyond that which can be read in a user guide.

The anticipated period of performance of this contract is five (5) years (base plus four (4) option years).

The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) for this requirement is 518210 Data Processing, Hosting, and Related Services and the size standard of $40,000,000.00.

PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT (PWS)

FOR

Saber Net Broadband & Wi-Fi

Spangdahlem Air Base

March 2026

TABLE OF CONTENTS

1.0. BACKGROUND & SCOPE

2.0. PERFORMANCE REQUIREMENTS

3.0. SYSTEM AVAILABILITY AND CUSTOMER SUPPORT

4.0. SERVICE & TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS

5.0. DELIVERABLES

6.0. SAFETY REQUIREMENTS

7.0. SECURITY REQUIREMENTS

8.0. APPENDICES

1.0. BACKGROUND & SCOPE

1.1. Background: The 52d Fighter Wing (52d FW) at Spangdahlem Air Base requires a high-speed wireless Wide Area Network (WAN), hereafter referred to as “Saber Net.” This network will provide wireless internet access to residents in unaccompanied housing dormitories across the installation.

1.2. Scope: The contractor shall provide, install, and maintain a comprehensive, turnkey wireless internet solution. This service will support all buildings listed in Appendix 1 and any future buildings added via contract modification following scope determination. The service must allow residents to connect stand-alone computers and personal media devices to the internet via a wireless access point (AP) or hard-wired LAN connection. The contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, tools, maintenance, and technical support necessary for uninterrupted, 24/7 high-speed internet service.

2.0. PERFORMANCE REQUIREMENTS

The contractor's performance shall be evaluated based on the following objectives. Failure to meet these thresholds may result in corrective actions as determined by the Contracting Officer.

3.0. SYSTEM AVAILABILITY AND CUSTOMER SUPPORT

3.1. Hours of Operation: The Saber Net network shall meet an operational availability of ninety-five percent (95%) or higher each month, 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. This includes maintenance response time and bandwidth degradation.

3.2. Maintenance & Repair: The contractor shall provide all necessary maintenance, repair, and/or replacement of equipment to ensure uninterrupted service.

3.3. Help Desk: The contractor shall operate a help desk from 0800 to 1700, 7 days a week, to support users.

3.4. On-site Support: The contractor must be available for on-site support between 0730 and 1630, Monday through Saturday, to resolve hardware or software issues that cannot be fixed remotely.

3.5. Service Call Log: The contractor will maintain a control log for all service calls. Except for U.S. and German holidays, calls must be completed within 24 hours if no replacement parts are required. Repairs requiring parts shall be completed within 24 hours after parts become available.

4.0. SERVICE & TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS

4.1. Network Speed & Equipment: The contractor shall install and maintain a commercial TCP/IP-capable network that meets the bandwidth requirements specified in Section 2.0. Each dormitory room requires sufficient wireless APs to ensure complete Wi-Fi saturation.

4.2. Data Usage: The contractor shall provide broadband service with unlimited data. There shall be no data caps, usage-based throttling, or overage charges.

4.3. Data Retention for Investigative Support: The contractor shall implement a system to log and securely retain user activity data for a minimum of 180 days. This data must be sufficient to associate a user with a specific IP address at a given date and time and must be provided in a timely manner in response to lawful requests.

4.4. Login & Content Filtering: A captive portal (login landing page) must be presented to each user, clearly describing the terms of use. The contractor shall apply appropriate web content filters to block inappropriate material in accordance with Component-level policy. Prohibited content includes, but is not limited to:

4.4.1. Pornography and other sexually explicit materials

4.4.2. Websites promoting hate speech, extremism, or violence

4.4.3. Illegal gambling sites

4.4.4. Peer-to-peer file sharing sites known for copyright infringement

4.4.5. Malicious websites, including those associated with phishing, malware, and spam

4.4.6. Anonymizing services or proxies that obscure user identity or location (VPN)

4.4.7. Unauthorized or illegal activities

4.5. Compliance: The contractor shall comply with all U.S. and German government regulations, including obtaining a valid internet service provider license from the Bundesnetzagentur (BNetzA) and meeting all requirements detailed by German law.

4.6. Technician Qualifications: Any installation or repair team must include at least one technician fluent in English.

5.0. DELIVERABLES

The contractor shall submit the following deliverables to the government for approval and acceptance:

6.0. SAFETY REQUIREMENTS

6.1. The contractor shall conform to all standardized safety practices required by U.S. and German government guidelines. The contractor must immediately notify the Contracting Officer of any safety mishaps.

7.0. SECURITY REQUIREMENTS

7.1. Physical Security & Base Access: The contractor is responsible for safeguarding all government property. All contractor personnel shall obtain appropriate base access credentials and comply with all installation security measures, including traffic regulations, vehicle searches, and personal identification requirements.

7.2. Prohibited Items: Weapons, firearms, and ammunition are prohibited on the installation.

7.3. Reporting: Contractor personnel shall report any information that may pose a threat to the security of DoD personnel, resources, or information.

STATEMENT OF Requirement

Maxwell_42CS_NIPR Virtual CORE Storage Hardware Upgrade

Introduction and Background. The 42nd Communications Squadron at Maxwell AFB, AL has 

a requirement to upgrade its HPE, 3PAR 8400 2N NIPR Core (File, Print, Web & Application) Storage Hardware, with a Modular Smart Array (MSA) and add a Fourth Node. After equipment installation and the data migration to the new MSA, the vendor will need to move the (4) Hosts to a Direct Connect and remove the (2) current HPE SN6000B 16GB 48/24 FC Switches from the data path.

Equipment Specifications:

      2.0.1.  Please see below and Excel Spreadsheet.

Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) MSA 2070

Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) DL360 Gen 11 8SFF Server

3 Years of Initial Licensing (If Required) and Sustainment Support (Warranty)

   3.0.1. The contractor shall provide all Project Management Services, Design, Draft, Engineer,  

   Fabricate, Modify, Furnish, Install, Program, Configure, Join to the Network, Migration   

   Services, Transitions, Test and make Operational, a complete Turnkey Solution for the   

   42nd Communications Squadron’s NIPR Virtual CORE Storage Hardware Upgrade Project.

   3.0.2. All bidding contractors are highly encouraged to conduct their own independent configuration   

   survey PRIOR to submitting a bid.  Government project information is deemed reliable but not  

   guaranteed on interface, interconnect, configurations, versioning, licensing and hardware 

   connections. It is the vendor’s responsibility to ensure the project will be a successful turnkey 

   project as bid with no outstanding issues on the government.

   3.0.3. The contractor will provide a Project Completion Test Plan 30 days before the contract 

   start date, detailing all applicable tests to be performed, that will show all applicable   

   equipment, software, circuits, trunks and dial plans are in 100% correct working order.

   3.0.4. Contractor is to provide a submittal sheet for approval on all material, hardware and   

    software to be used for government acceptance NLT 10 prior to start of the project. 

      3.4.1. Submittal data includes Make, model, operating system (OS), software, technical 

      specification sheets and connections of items be deployed.

      3.4.2. Any required Authority To Operate (ATO) documentation with expiration dates.

   3.0.5. Provide final documentation to include as-built documents that describe the final   

   deployed solution.

   3.0.6. Provide knowledge transfer describing the final configurations and architecture.

   3.0.7. Provide basic training on administration, management and troubleshooting the installed 

   equipment.

   3.0.8. Configure Security Technical Implementation Guide (STIG) hardening and/or other  

   additional Information Assurance (IA) scans as required.

   3.0.9. The contractor shall provide the customer with all manufacturer warranties as needed   

   for any component incorporated into this project, along with equipment manuals, literature,  

   CDs and DVDs and other documentation on all equipment.

   3.0.10. All new Information Technology Services (ITS) equipment and cabling supplied must be     

   ITS standard products and supplied from a reputable manufacturer. No refurbished, recertified,  

   reconditioned, remanufactured or ‘gray’ items will be accepted.

   3.0.11. No refurbished, re-manufactured or counterfeit parts will be accepted, nor will they be  

   installed on the Air Force Network (AFNET). 

   3.0.12. All Work must be performed by Authorized Technicians.

   3.0.13. Support: 24x7 Telephone with Next Business Day Onsite.

   3.0.14. Perform Remote Diagnostics.

   3.0.15. Perform On-Site Maintenance if Required.

   3.0.16. Cover All Parts, Labor and Materials needed to Repair or Replace.

   3.0.17. All new equipment must be Forward/Upward Compatible to growing technology.

   3.0.18. All equipment and parts must be Trade Agreement Act (TAA) Compliant and JELA 

   eligible.

   3.0.19. When complete, all attached and/or associated equipment must be returned to a 100%  

   fully operational state.

   3.0.20. Keep Your Hard Drive: 42 CS will keep all old hard drives for sanitization purposes.

   3.0.21. All replaced parts and any work generated residue must be removed, completely    

   transported off Maxwel AFB and/or Gunter Annex and properly disposed. Use of base  

   dumpsters IS NOT  ALLOWED.

 7.0. Security

7.0.1. Security Requirements For Unclassified Services Only, No CAC Required

1. Contractor Notification Responsibilities:  The contractor shall notify the contracting officer within 30 days before on-base performance of the service. The notification shall include:  

a. Name, address, and telephone number of contractor employees working on the contract.

b. The contract number and contracting agency.

c. The location(s) of service performance and future performance, if known.

d. The date service performance begins.

e. Any change to information previously provided under this paragraph.

2.  Installation Access Requirements:  As prescribed by the DAFFARS 5352.242-9000, Contractor access to Air Force installations, AFI 31-218, Motor Vehicle Traffic Supervision, and DoDM5200.08v3_AFMAN31-101v3, Installation Perimeter Access Control.  

The contractor shall obtain base identification and vehicle passes, if required, for all contractor personnel who make frequent visits to or perform work on the Department of the Air Force installation(s) cited in the contract. Contractor personnel are required to wear or prominently display installation identification badges or contractor-furnished contractor identification badges while visiting or performing work on the installation.

The contractor shall submit a written request on company letterhead to the Contracting Officer (CO) listing the following: contract number, location of work site, start and stop dates, and names of employees and subcontractor employees needing access to the base. The letter will also specify the individual(s) authorized to sign a request for base identification credentials or vehicle passes. The contracting officer will endorse the request and forward it to the issuing base pass and registration office or Security Forces for processing. When reporting to the registration office, the authorized contractor individual(s) should provide a valid driver’s license, current vehicle registration, and valid vehicle insurance certificate to obtain a vehicle pass.  

During performance of the service, the contractor shall be responsible for obtaining the required identification for newly assigned personnel and for prompt return of credentials for any employee who no longer requires access to the work site.

Upon completion or termination of the contract or expiration of the identification passes, the prime contractor shall ensure that all base identification passes issued to employees and subcontractor employees are returned to the issuing office.

Failure to comply with these requirements may result in the withholding of final payment.

Vehicle Inspections.  All commercial vehicles will be directed to Gate 3 (Kelly St) or Gate 4 (Congressman Dickenson for Gunter) for processing through the Commercial Vehicle Inspection (CVI) Area, when operational.  During non-duty hours and holidays, commercial vehicle inspections will be conducted at Gate 1 (Maxwell Blvd) or Gate 4 (Congressman Dickinson Drive) only. Inspection members will conduct thorough inspections of the interior and exterior of the vehicle for items prohibited from the installation such as explosive devices, weapons and ammunition, drugs, and open or closed alcohol containers.

 REAL ID Act:  All Maxwell Air Force Base and Gunter Annex visitors must present a REAL ID-compliant credential to be issued a pass.

REAL ID-compliant cards have a star marking ⭐️on the upper portion of the card. If the card does not have a star marking, it is not REAL ID-compliant and won’t be accepted as proof of identity to board commercial aircraft or access military installations like Maxwell or Gunter.

Those without a REAL ID-compliant driver’s license may also use a U.S. passport or passport card, a Transportation Worker Identification Card (TWIC), a Veteran Health Identification Card (VHIC), or a combination of the following documents to be issued a pass:

An original or certified true copy of a birth certificate with a raised seal

A social security card

A driver’s license issued by a state, territory, or the District of Columbia that is not REAL ID-compliant.

All three documents must reflect the same name (or a documented former name through legal name change documents such as a court order, marriage certificate, or divorce decree).

More information about accessing Maxwell can be found here:  https://www.maxwell.af.mil/About-Us/Fact-Sheets/Display/Article/4024201/base-access-information/

Controlled/Restricted Areas:  If work under this contract requires unescorted entry to controlled or restricted areas, the contractor shall comply with DAFI 31-101, Integrated Defense, and DoDM5200.02_DAFMAN 16-1405, Air Force Personnel Security Program. 

If unescorted access is not authorized and the contractor requires access to controlled/restricted areas, they must be escorted by appropriately cleared government personnel at all times. 

If work is required in a classified environment, the area must be sanitized, and the contractor will be escorted at all times by appropriately cleared government personnel.  

5.  Reporting Requirements:  The contractor shall comply with DAFI 71-101, Volume-1, Criminal Investigations, and AFI 71-101, Volume-2, Protective Service Matters, requirements.  Contractor personnel shall report to 42d Air Base Wing Information Protection Office, any information or circumstances of which they are aware may pose a threat to the security of DoD personnel, contractor personnel, resources, and classified or unclassified defense information.  Contractor employees shall be briefed by their immediate supervisor upon initial on-base assignment and as required thereafter.  

6.  Traffic Laws:  The contractor and their employees shall comply with base traffic regulations set forth in AFI 31-218, Motor Vehicle Traffic Supervision and DoDM5200.08v3_AFMAN31-101v3, Installation Perimeter Access Control.  Personnel in violation may be issued a Central Violations Bureau Form 1805 traffic ticket.  

7.  Random Installation Entry/Exit Checks: Entry/exit vehicle checks are conducted by order of the 42 ABW Commander.  These checks are conducted for the purpose of safeguarding the base and protecting government property by discovering and seizing stolen property, classified information, and contraband. Refusal to submit to an installation (entry/exit) vehicle check may result in the loss of base driving privileges, revocation of base registration, or debarment action.

8.  Cellular Phone Operation Policy:  The use of cellular phones while operating a motorized vehicle is prohibited on Maxwell-Gunter.  Although discouraged, drivers are authorized to use devices, i.e. ear bud or ear boom, which allows their cellular phone to be operated hands-free.  The device must not cover both ears. This policy applies to everyone driving on Maxwell AFB and Gunter Annex.  Personnel in violation may be issued a Central Violations Bureau Form 1805 traffic ticket.  

9.  Wireless Electronic Devices: The contractor will not establish their own Information Technology (IT) systems or networks (Local Area Networks [LAN], Wide Area Network [WAN], Cellular phone/USB Modem as WAN, Wi-Fi as WAN, etc.), or camera system without the direct permission of the Program Manager and governing communications and responsible information systems office (42 CS).

10.  Firearms and Ammunition: Transporting weapons or ammunition, concealed or otherwise, IS NOT permitted by any non-law enforcement personnel on Maxwell AFB/Gunter Annex at any time regardless of state issued concealed weapons/LEOSA permits.  Violations may result in criminal prosecution under applicable federal laws.

11. Illegal Weapons. The weapons below are considered illegal, unless

specifically authorized by competent authority and are prohibited on Maxwell AFB/Gunter Annex. Violations may result in criminal prosecution under applicable federal laws.

a. Switchblade knives or knives with any type of automatic blade release.

b. An incendiary/explosive weapon (e.g., grenades, flash bangs).

c. Fireworks

d. Homemade mortars, aka "tennis ball launchers" or similar devices.

Hewlett Packard Multi -Jet Fusion  4200 3D Printer Maintenance Services

1.0  Scope & Requirement Background  
The Fleet Readiness Centers Southeast (FRCSE) is an industrial facility that provides a wide variety of aircraft services 
including maintenance, repair and overhaul, as well as components manufacturing.  FRCSE currently utilizes two Hewlett 
Packard (HP) Multi Jet Fusion (MJF) 4200 3D printers to manufacture aircraft components.  This Statement of Work 
(SOW) defines the requirements for the Contractor to provide continuous preventive and corrective maintenance 
services to ensure these systems remain fully operational.   
 
1.1 Objectives 
The Contractor shall perform Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) certified maintenance and repair services for two 
(2) HP MJF 4200 3D printers, including build units and processing stations. 
 
2.0 Applicable Documents 
2.1 Fleet Readiness Center Southeast Work Restrictions (Enclosure 1). 
 
3.0 Requirements-   
3.1 The Contractor shall perform the following specific tasks:   
 
3.1.1     Freight and Shipping:  All items requiring shipping shall be included in the cost to maintain the systems and shall 
not be billed separately.   
 
3.1.2 Personnel Qualifications:  All services shall be performed by an OEM certified HP MJF Field Service 
Representative (FSR).   
 
3.1.3 Response Time:  All services requiring onsite support shall be accomplished within three (3) business days of 
notification unless otherwise noted in this SOW.  The Contractor shall document the date/time of notification 
and the date/time of arrival in the Maintenance Service Report (See attached CDRLs A001-AD01). 
 
3.2 Maintenance Tasks 
3.2.1 The Contractor shall provide all labor, equipment, tools, material, transportation and qualified personnel necessary 
to perform annual comprehensive system maintenance and technical support services for the FRCSE HP MJF 4200 3D 
printers.    
 
3.2.2 Annual Comprehensive Maintenance Agreement

Destruction Cart Salient Characteristics 
1. The organization has a critical need for a self-contained, mobile system to ensure the complete 
and verifiable destruction of sensitive and classified data on various storage media, including 
hard disk drives and solid-state drives. The primary goal is to achieve irreversible data 
elimination that meets the highest security standards, such as those set by the NSA for Top Secret 
data, while maintaining a strict, auditable chain-of-custody from start to finish. The impact of not 
fulfilling this need is severe, potentially leading to catastrophic data breaches, failure to pass 
mandatory security audits, and non-compliance with government regulations. This would 
fundamentally compromise the organization's mission execution and overall security posture. 
Therefore, this acquisition is of paramount significance. 
To meet mission requirements, any proposed solution must, at a minimum, be certified to NSA 
standards for data destruction. It must be capable of both degaussing magnetic media and 
physically destroying solid-state media. A critical requirement is an integrated verification 
system that automatically documents the entire process, generating an unalterable certificate of 
destruction—including photographic evidence of the media —for each item destroyed. This 
system must be isolated, with no network connectivity like Wi-Fi or Bluetooth, to ensure its 
integrity in secure environments.  
Performance targets should focus on achieving complete and verified data sanitization, with 
specifications such as erasure field strength and physical destruction force serving as benchmarks 
to ensure the end result—verifiable data elimination —is met or ex ceeded. 
2. Cart 
3. TS-1XT Gauss Degausser or equal 
4. PD-5 NSA Listed Hard Drive Destroyer or equal

1.0  BACKGROUND 
The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Veterans Health Administration (VHA), Office 
of Mental Health and Suicide Prevention (OMHSP), in coordination with the Office of 
Information & Technology (OIT) Health Data Management portfolio is pursuing 
enhanced capabilities to support care coordination and suicide prevention efforts for 
Veterans receiving care in community settings.  This effort aligns with legislative 
priorities including Elizabeth Dole 21st Century Veterans Healthcare and Benefits 
Improvement Act, which emphasizes improved care coordination, timely access to 
information, and enhanced support for Veterans at risk.   
 
VHA has identified a gap in timely visibility into care events occurring outside of VA 
facilities, particularly for Veterans receiving treatment in community hospitals, 
emergency departments, and post-acute care settings.  Without timely notification of 
these events, VA care teams may be delayed in coordinating follow-up care, which is 
especially critical for Veterans identified as high-risk.  Improving awareness of these 
events is essential to enabling proactive outreach and prevention. 
 
To address this gap, VA is exploring the use of electronic notification (eNotification) 
services that provide near real-time alerts for Admission, Discharge, and Transfer (ADT) 
events occurring in community settings.  Market research conducted by VA indicates 
that no single vendor provides sufficient national coverage across all relevant care 
settings.  As a result, a solution that leverages multiple notification networks is 
necessary to achieve targeted/adequate coverage and ensure comprehensive visibility 
into Veteran care events. 
 
This pilot will support up to six (6) VA Medical Centers (VAMCs) and a defined 
population of Veterans identified as high-risk.  VA will provide a Veteran attribution list, 
that will be updated periodically, to enable targeted notification delivery.  Notifications 
will be transmitted via Direct Secure Messaging (DSM) infrastructure, through the 
Oracle Health’s Health Information Service Provider (HISP), into VA Direct Secure 
Messaging (DSM) inboxes, leveraging existing infrastructure without requiring direct 
integration with VA clinical systems.  The objective of the pilot is to assess the 
effectiveness, timeliness, and operational impact of eNotification services in improving 
care coordination and supporting suicide prevention efforts.

3.0  SCOPE OF WORK 
The Contractor shall provide and implement an Admissions, Discharge, and Transfer 
(ADT) eNotifications Software as a Service (SaaS) utilizing multiple existing provider 
networks already in place to support a VA-defined population of Veterans identified as 
at-risk across up to six (6) VA Medical Center (VAMCs).  The Contractor shall support a 
VA-defined population of up to approximately 82,000 patients, with attribution data 
provided and maintained by VA and updated on a quarterly basis.  The Contractor shall 
provide implementation support including configuration, testing, and deployment of the 
SaaS solution and enable filtering of notifications based on VA-defined criteria, including 
Veteran/patient association with a home VAMC.   
 
The Contractor shall support the ingestion, processing, and delivery of real-time ADT 
eNotifications associated with the VA-defined patient population and relevant treatment-
related events.  The Contractor shall support the secure transmission of eNotifications, 
using Direct Secure Messaging through VA-approved Health Information Service 
Provider (HISP) or other VA-approved mechanisms to securely exchange 
Veteran/patient attribution data with VA.  The Contractor shall support coordination

1. Introduction  
 
This Request for Information (RFI) is issued for conducting market research and 
planning purposes only. Accordingly, this RFI constitutes neither a Request for Quote, 
Request for Proposal, nor a guarantee that one will be issued by the Government in the 
future; furthermore, it does not commit the Government to contract for any services 
described herein. Additionally, this RFI does not restrict the Government as to the 
ultimate acquisition approach. In accordance with Revolutionary Federal Acquisition 
Regulation Overhaul 15.101(c), responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be 
accepted by the Government to form a binding contract.  
The purpose of this RFI is to identify qualified vendors, who can meet Department of 
Veterans Affairs (VA) requirements for
 Capital Assets Facilities Management System 
Software and Support. The purpose of this RFI is to obtain market information on 
capable sources. Your response to this RFI will be treated only as information for the 
Government to consider. The Government is not responsible for any cost incurred by 
industry in furnishing this information. All costs associated with responding to this RFI 
will be solely at the interested vendor's expense. Not responding to this RFI does not 
preclude participation in any future solicitation if any is issued. Any information 
submitted by respondents to this RFI is strictly voluntary. All submissions will become 
Government property and will not be returned. Interested vendors are responsible for 
adequately marking proprietary, restricted or competition sensitive information 
contained in their response.
 VA is under no obligation to provide feedback to the 
company, or to contact the company for clarification of any information submitted in 
response to this RFI. 
Be advised that set-aside decisions may be made based on the information provided in 
response to this RFI.  Responses should be as complete and informative as possible. 
 
2. Background: 
The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), VA Pacific Islands Health Care System 
(VAPIHCS)  located in Kapolei, HI has a requirement for services and management of 
its Capital Assets and Facilities Management System (CAFM). This system must 
contain a Drawing / Space / Capital Asset Inventory (CAI) database and a certain set of 
infrastructure drawings with graphical tools to store and share engineering drawings, 
assign space, and report usage among organizational groups. In addition, the system 
must provide tools for book and share rooms and desks. It shall be a multi-user, multi-
tasking system supporting multiple users in organizations spanning many buildings and 
sites. Cloud-based access shall be required.

1.0  PRODUCT REQUIREMENTS 
The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA),  VA Pacific Islands Health Care System  (VAPIHCS)  
located in Kapolei, HI has a requirement for services and management of its Capital Assets and 
Facilities Management System  (CAFM). This system must contain a Drawing / Space / Capital 
Asset Inventory (CAI) database and a certain set of infrastructure drawings with graphical tools 
to store and share engineering drawings, assign space, and report usage among organizational 
groups. In addition, the system must provide tools for book and share rooms and desks. It shall 
be a multi-user, multi-tasking system supporting multiple users in organizations spanning many 
buildings and sites. Cloud-based access shall be required. The software solution  shall be 
FedRAMP approved and authorized for operation within the VA environment. Maintain continuous 
monitoring and compliance throughout the period of performance.   
 
The Contractor Shall Provide the Following:

• Requirement 1: Access 
 
The software and associated drawings and data shall be hosted on a server maintained 
by the vendor. VA users shall access the system through the internet in an encrypted and 
protected environment. The vendor shall maintain the server and provide technical support 
on an on-going basis to VAPIHCS users.

Facilities Maintenance Software    TAC Number:  VA-26-00023047  
 
Page 4 of 32 
 
 
The vendor shall maintain the system without interruption on a 24/7 basis and provide 
unlimited technical support. Technical support may be limited to normal operating hours. 
Technical support shall include telephone calls and email messages. 
 
• Requirement 2: Training  
 
The Vendor shall conduct on-line training for users. This shall be an interactive session 
where users shall be able to gain hands-on experience. This training course shall last 
approximately four (4) hours. In addition to formal training, VAPIHCS may set up an 
unlimited number of brief training sessions as and when needed. 
 
• Requirement 3: Database Maintenance 
 
Ongoing additions or renovations as well as operational changes may cause changes to 
drawings and the database. Periodically, the VAPIHCS shall send to the vendor drawings 
and other documentation that detail the alterations. Typically, these changes shall  be 
forwarded as AutoCAD files. The vendor shall, upon receipt of such documents, consult 
with VAMC staff and clarify the changes as necessary. The vendor shall then incorporate 
the changes in the drawings and update the databases. The vendor shall make the  
changes in less than ten (10) business days. The vendor shall send at least once a quarter 
a notification to the medical center reminding the medical center and asking for data and 
drawing changes that may have taken place since the previous update. 
 
 
• Requirement 4. Implement As-Builts Module  
 
o The contractor shall host a CAFM program on a server on the cloud accessible 
through the internet, in an encrypted and protected environment.  
o VAPIHCS will supply the vendor  with PDF drawings for Akaka clinic. VAPIHCS 
shall get an AutoCAD version of this drawing.  
o The drawing being supplied is dated December 2021 and VAPIHCS will mark up 
and send to the vendor any changes between this drawing and as-built conditions.  
o The vendor shall update the drawing so that it will truly be as built. Once the data 
is inside the system, the vendor  shall review the data and make any necessary 
corrections.  
o There will be assigned System coordinators to provide monthly updates to the 
vendor service technicians to update/Maintain the database for VAPIHCS. 
 
• Requirement 5. Implement Space Module 
 
o The space assignment database consists of the following items for each space:  
 
 Room number  
 Service Line  
 Space function (Patient room, Exam room, Office room etc.)  
 Gross and Net square footages

The 42d Contracting Squadron, Maxwell AFB, AL, is conducting market research to identify potential sources capable of providing a turnkey solution to replace the 42d Communications Squadron’s End-of-Life (EOL) Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) Commvault CommServe and Media Agent Servers. The Government requires brand name HPE ProLiant DL360 Gen12 servers, or equal, to ensure 100% compatibility with the existing, standardized HPE Storage Area Network (SAN) and core server infrastructure.

This requirement includes not only the delivery of the servers but also all associated migration services, installation, configuration, testing, and training. Information gathered from this notice will be used to finalize the acquisition strategy for the requirement detailed in the attached draft Statement of Requirements (SOR).

NOTES OF IMPORTANCE:

A solicitation does not exist for this requirement. This is only a sources sought synopsis, so please do not submit proposals. The Government does not intend to award a contract based on this sources sought.

If the Government decides to pursue a solicitation, portions of your responses to this sources sought may be incorporated into the final solicitation. Respondents are discouraged from submitting any information deemed competition-sensitive or proprietary.

Respondents will not be reimbursed for any costs incurred in responding to this sources sought. Information submitted will not be returned to the respective respondents.

Oral submissions of information will not be considered in response to this sources sought.

To assist the Government in developing a potential acquisition strategy, please provide the following information:

1. GENERAL INFORMATION:

Company name, address, point of contact, voice and fax telephone numbers and email address. 

Type of business, (i.e., small, small disadvantaged, woman-owned, Hub Zone, serviced-disabled veteran-owned small business, large business, etc.), under North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) 541519 which contains a size standard of 135 EMP., CAGE Code and Unique Entity Identifier (UEI). 

Under which NAICS code does your company usually provide the requirements described above. Please provide rationale for your answer if different from NAICS 541519.

Please describe any customary commercial contract terms or conditions that you feel would make any resulting contract more effective if applicable.

2. CAPABILITIES: The Government is only seeking qualified, experienced providers interested in satisfying this potential requirement. Please address the following regarding your capabilities in meeting the requirements detailed in Attachment 1:

Is your company capable of meeting the requirement with the brand name equipment? Please respond “Yes” or “No.”

Is your company capable of meeting the requirement with an alternative (non-HPE) solution? If so, you must provide a detailed technical narrative and supporting data to substantiate the claim of 100% seamless integration with the existing HPE-exclusive environment without causing mission degradation or requiring significant re-engineering and retraining for government technicians.

3. RESPONSES: Interested vendors must e-mail responses to this sources sought to the point of contact identified below. The due date and time for responses to this sources sought is at 12:00 p.m. Central Daylight Time on 05 May 2026.

1st Lt John Putnam (Contract Specialist) @john.putnam.8@us.af.mil (334)953-8083

Mr. Jeremy Kersey (Contracting Officer) @jeremy.kersey.1@us.af.mil (334)953-3526

STATEMENT OF Requirement

42CS_Commvault CommServe Servers

Introduction and Background. The 42nd Communications Squadron at Maxwell AFB, AL has a requirement to replace its Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) Commvault CommServe and Media Agent Servers due to them reaching End of Life and End of Service and perform Migrations Services. These Servers support the Primary Base Data Backups for the Base Storage Area Network (SAN) and other Core Network Servers. 

Equipment Specifications:

      2.0.1.  Please see below and Excel Spreadsheet.

(5 EA) Hewlett Packard Enterprise HPE ProLiant Compute DL360 Gen12 8SFF NC Configure-to-order Servers 

3 Years of Initial Licensing (If Required) and Sustainment Support (Warranty)

                

3.0 Contractor Responsibilities: 

   3.1 The contractor shall provide all migration services for the  42nd Communications Squadron’s (2)  

   CommServe and Media Agent Servers.

   3.0.2. All bidding contractors are highly encouraged to conduct their own independent configuration   

   survey PRIOR to submitting a bid.  Government project information is deemed reliable but not  

   guaranteed on interface, interconnect, configurations, versioning, licensing and hardware 

   connections. It is the vendor’s responsibility to ensure the project will be a successful turnkey 

   project as bid with no outstanding issues on the government.

   3.0.3. The contractor will provide a Project Completion Test Plan 30 days before the contract 

   start date, detailing all applicable tests to be performed, that will show all applicable   

   equipment, software, circuits, trunks and dial plans are in 100% correct working order.

   3.0.4. Contractor is to provide a submittal sheet for approval on all material, hardware and   

    software to be used for government acceptance NLT 10 prior to start of the project. 

      3.4.1. Submittal data includes Make, model, operating system (OS), software, technical 

      specification sheets and connections of items be deployed.

      3.4.2. Any required Authority To Operate (ATO) documentation with expiration dates.

   3.0.5. Provide final documentation to include as-built documents that describe the final   

   deployed solution.

   3.0.6. Provide knowledge transfer describing the final configurations and architecture.

   3.0.7. Provide basic training on administration, management and troubleshooting the installed 

   equipment.

   3.0.8. Configure Security Technical Implementation Guide (STIG) hardening and/or other  

   additional Information Assurance (IA) scans as required.

   3.0.9. The contractor shall provide the customer with all manufacturer warranties as needed   

   for any component incorporated into this project, along with equipment manuals, literature,  

   CDs and DVDs and other documentation on all equipment.

   3.0.10. All new Information Technology Services (ITS) equipment and cabling supplied must be     

   ITS standard products and supplied from a reputable manufacturer. No refurbished, recertified,  

   reconditioned, remanufactured or ‘gray’ items will be accepted.

   3.0.11. No refurbished, re-manufactured or counterfeit parts will be accepted, nor will they be  

   installed on the Air Force Network (AFNET). 

   3.0.12. All Work must be performed by Authorized Technicians.

   3.0.13. Support: 24x7 Telephone with Next Business Day Onsite.

   3.0.14. Perform Remote Diagnostics.

   3.0.15. Perform On-Site Maintenance if Required.

   3.0.16. Cover All Parts, Labor and Materials needed to Repair or Replace.

   3.0.17. All new equipment must be Forward/Upward Compatible to growing technology.

   3.0.18. All equipment and parts must be Trade Agreement Act (TAA) Compliant and JELA 

   eligible.

   3.0.19. When complete, all attached and/or associated equipment must be returned to a 100%  

   fully operational state.

   3.0.20. Keep Your Hard Drive: 42 CS will keep all old hard drives for sanitization purposes.

   3.0.21. All replaced parts and any work generated residue must be removed, completely    

   transported off Maxwel AFB and/or Gunter Annex and properly disposed. Use of base  

   dumpsters IS NOT  ALLOWED.

5.0 Technical POCs: 

      5.0.1. Johnny Batton, 42CS/SCXP, (334) 953-3461

      5.0.2. Mike Jamison, 42CS/SCOO, (334) 953-9733

6.0. Shipping Information: The contractor shall provide and deliver the new equipment to 42CS/SCXE Attn: Johnny Batton Bldg. 1154, IT Warehouse 455 S. Kelly Street Maxwell AFB, AL 36112. 

6.0.1. Delivery of the product will be F.O.B. Destination.

 7.0. Security

7.0.1. Security Requirements For Unclassified Services Only, No CAC Required

1. Contractor Notification Responsibilities:  The contractor shall notify the contracting officer within 30 days before on-base performance of the service. The notification shall include:  

a. Name, address, and telephone number of contractor employees working on the contract.

b. The contract number and contracting agency.

c. The location(s) of service performance and future performance, if known.

d. The date service performance begins.

e. Any change to information previously provided under this paragraph.

2.  Installation Access Requirements:  As prescribed by the DAFFARS 5352.242-9000, Contractor access to Air Force installations, AFI 31-218, Motor Vehicle Traffic Supervision, and DoDM5200.08v3_AFMAN31-101v3, Installation Perimeter Access Control.  

The contractor shall obtain base identification and vehicle passes, if required, for all contractor personnel who make frequent visits to or perform work on the Department of the Air Force installation(s) cited in the contract. Contractor personnel are required to wear or prominently display installation identification badges or contractor-furnished contractor identification badges while visiting or performing work on the installation.

The contractor shall submit a written request on company letterhead to the Contracting Officer (CO) listing the following: contract number, location of work site, start and stop dates, and names of employees and subcontractor employees needing access to the base. The letter will also specify the individual(s) authorized to sign a request for base identification credentials or vehicle passes. The contracting officer will endorse the request and forward it to the issuing base pass and registration office or Security Forces for processing. When reporting to the registration office, the authorized contractor individual(s) should provide a valid driver’s license, current vehicle registration, and valid vehicle insurance certificate to obtain a vehicle pass.  

During performance of the service, the contractor shall be responsible for obtaining the required identification for newly assigned personnel and for prompt return of credentials for any employee who no longer requires access to the work site.

Upon completion or termination of the contract or expiration of the identification passes, the prime contractor shall ensure that all base identification passes issued to employees and subcontractor employees are returned to the issuing office.

Failure to comply with these requirements may result in the withholding of final payment.

Vehicle Inspections.  All commercial vehicles will be directed to Gate 3 (Kelly St) or Gate 4 (Congressman Dickenson for Gunter) for processing through the Commercial Vehicle Inspection (CVI) Area, when operational.  During non-duty hours and holidays, commercial vehicle inspections will be conducted at Gate 1 (Maxwell Blvd) or Gate 4 (Congressman Dickinson Drive) only. Inspection members will conduct thorough inspections of the interior and exterior of the vehicle for items prohibited from the installation such as explosive devices, weapons and ammunition, drugs, and open or closed alcohol containers.

 REAL ID Act:  All Maxwell Air Force Base and Gunter Annex visitors must present a REAL ID-compliant credential to be issued a pass.

REAL ID-compliant cards have a star marking ⭐️on the upper portion of the card. If the card does not have a star marking, it is not REAL ID-compliant and won’t be accepted as proof of identity to board commercial aircraft or access military installations like Maxwell or Gunter.

Those without a REAL ID-compliant driver’s license may also use a U.S. passport or passport card, a Transportation Worker Identification Card (TWIC), a Veteran Health Identification Card (VHIC), or a combination of the following documents to be issued a pass:

An original or certified true copy of a birth certificate with a raised seal

A social security card

A driver’s license issued by a state, territory, or the District of Columbia that is not REAL ID-compliant.

All three documents must reflect the same name (or a documented former name through legal name change documents such as a court order, marriage certificate, or divorce decree).

More information about accessing Maxwell can be found here:  https://www.maxwell.af.mil/About-Us/Fact-Sheets/Display/Article/4024201/base-access-information/

Controlled/Restricted Areas:  If work under this contract requires unescorted entry to controlled or restricted areas, the contractor shall comply with DAFI 31-101, Integrated Defense, and DoDM5200.02_DAFMAN 16-1405, Air Force Personnel Security Program. 

If unescorted access is not authorized and the contractor requires access to controlled/restricted areas, they must be escorted by appropriately cleared government personnel at all times. 

If work is required in a classified environment, the area must be sanitized, and the contractor will be escorted at all times by appropriately cleared government personnel.  

5.  Reporting Requirements:  The contractor shall comply with DAFI 71-101, Volume-1, Criminal Investigations, and AFI 71-101, Volume-2, Protective Service Matters, requirements.  Contractor personnel shall report to 42d Air Base Wing Information Protection Office, any information or circumstances of which they are aware may pose a threat to the security of DoD personnel, contractor personnel, resources, and classified or unclassified defense information.  Contractor employees shall be briefed by their immediate supervisor upon initial on-base assignment and as required thereafter.  

6.  Traffic Laws:  The contractor and their employees shall comply with base traffic regulations set forth in AFI 31-218, Motor Vehicle Traffic Supervision and DoDM5200.08v3_AFMAN31-101v3, Installation Perimeter Access Control.  Personnel in violation may be issued a Central Violations Bureau Form 1805 traffic ticket.  

7.  Random Installation Entry/Exit Checks: Entry/exit vehicle checks are conducted by order of the 42 ABW Commander.  These checks are conducted for the purpose of safeguarding the base and protecting government property by discovering and seizing stolen property, classified information, and contraband. Refusal to submit to an installation (entry/exit) vehicle check may result in the loss of base driving privileges, revocation of base registration, or debarment action.

SBU - CONTRACTING AND ACQUISITIONS 
 
1. Introduction 
The U.S. Department of State (DOS) is conducting market research in accordance 
with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 10 to identify commercially 
available solutions capable of supporting a centralized survey and evaluation 
system across the Department. 
The Department currently utilizes Qualtrics and seeks information on comparable 
or alternative solutions available in the marketplace, including the extent to which 
small businesses can independently provide such capabilities. 
This RFI is issued for information and planning purposes only and does not 
constitute a solicitation. Responses will not be considered as proposals or offers. 
The Government does not intend to award a contract based on this RFI or 
reimburse any costs associated with the preparation of responses. 
 
2. Objectives 
The Department seeks to: 
• Identify commercially available solutions with capabilities similar to or 
exceeding Qualtrics FedRamp Authorized Moderate (SaaS) 
• Assess the availability of solutions from small businesses 
• Understand implementation timelines, cost structures, and deployment 
models 
• Review technical, security, and integration capabilities 
 
3. Scope  
The U.S. Department of State (DoS) is seeking a contractor to provide 
comprehensive services for the continued utilization of the Centralized Evaluation 
System (CES). This includes providing access to a FedRAMP authorized at the 
Moderate level SaaS platform powered by Qualtrics and delivering the necessary 

 
SBU - CONTRACTING AND ACQUISITIONS 
support services to plan, validate, deploy, integrate, configure, and maintain the 
platform to meet the Department’s enterprise-wide requirements. 
The contractor will provide ongoing subject matter expert support services 
required to operate, maintain, and safeguard the CES, while also training 
Department of State staff on its effective use. The contractor will ensure the CES 
continues to meet the Department’s operational needs across its bureaus, while 
supporting future enhancements and innovations to align with evolving 
requirements and strategic goals.  
The Centralized Evaluation System (CES) operated by the U.S. Department of 
State requires custom integrations with enterprise systems such as the Student 
Information System (SIS), Learning Management Systems (LMS), other HR 
Systems, and data visualization tools such as Power BI. These integrations are 
essential for seamless data exchange, automated workflows, and real-time insights 
to support the Department’s mission and strategic goals. The contractor must 
design, develop, and implement secure APIs and workflows that comply with 
FedRAMP standards and Department of State technical and security requirements, 
ensuring the CES remains a robust and interoperable enterprise-wide solution. 
The Department is interested in solutions that provide: 
• Enterprise-wide 360-degree feedback assessments, evaluating training and 
development programs, survey design, distribution, and management 
• Advanced analytics and reporting capabilities 
• Role-based access control and data segmentation 
• Maintain Integration with existing enterprise systems 
• Compliance with federal security and privacy requirements

and include additional details where indicated.

Performance Work Statement 
1.0 INTRODUCTION 
The Naval Postgraduate Dental School (NPDS) is the premier institution for postgraduate dental education and training for dental officers of the 
United States Navy. The mission of NPDS is to provide advanced, specialized training in dentistry to ensure the operational readiness and 
professional development of the Navy Dental Corps. 
To support this critical mission in an evolving educational landscape, NPDS requires the implementation of a modern, robust, and secure Learning 
Management System (LMS). This PWS outlines the requirements for a comprehensive, cloud-based, commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) LMS solution 
to be provided by a contractor. 
2.0 BACKGROUND 
NPDS is committed to modernizing its educational delivery, enhancing curriculum management, and providing verifiable credentialing for its 
trainees. The current educational framework relies on disparate systems and manual processes, which limit the ability to deliver standardized, 
interactive, and trackable training across the enterprise. This creates administrative inefficiencies and hinders the adoption of modern pedagogical 
approaches. 
To close this capability gap, the Government has identified a need to procure a fully managed Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) LMS solution. This 
platform will serve as the central hub for all academic and training activities, from course content delivery and student assessment to the issuance of 
digital credentials. Based on extensive market research and a review of Government requirements, Canvas LMS by Instructure, Inc., has been 
identified as the only brand-name solution that meets the Government's minimum needs. Its proprietary features, integrated credentialing module, and 
established Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program (FedRAMP) authorization make it uniquely suited for this requirement. This 
performance work statement (PWS) defines the specific tasks the contractor shall perform to deliver and sustain this capability for NPDS. 
3.0 SCOPE 
The scope of this PWS is to acquire the Canvas Learning Management System, a FedRAMP Moderate-authorized SaaS platform, and all associated 
implementation, licensing, training, and support services. The contractor shall provide a turnkey solution that enables NPDS to deliver, manage, and 
track all aspects of its postgraduate dental education programs. 
This includes providing the core Canvas LMS, the Canvas Credentials module for digital badging, and all necessary professional services to ensure a 
successful and timely implementation. The contractor shall provide a scalable and secure platform that supports both instructors and learners, 
enhances the educational experience, and provides robust administrative and reporting capabilities. The solution must be capable of expanding to 
include additional users or modules as the needs of NPDS evolve. 
4.0 TASKS 
The contractor shall perform the following tasks to meet the requirements of this PWS 
4.1. Task 1: Program Management 
The contractor shall provide effective program management throughout the period of performance. 
4.1.1. Kick-Off Meeting: Within fourteen (14) days after contract award, the contractor shall conduct a post-award kick-off meeting with the 
Government's Contracting Officer's Representative (COR) and other designated stakeholders. The contractor shall present a draft Project Management 
Plan (PMP) and an overview of the implementation timeline. 
4.1.2. Project Management Plan (PMP): Within thirty (30) days after award, the contractor shall deliver a final PMP that details the project schedule, 
key milestones, risk management approach, and communication plan. 
4.1.3. Monthly Status Reports: The contractor shall provide a monthly status report to the COR, detailing progress, risks, and performance against the 
established plan. 
4.2. Task 2: Platform Provisioning and Licensing 
The contractor shall provide and maintain the cloud-based LMS platform. 
4.2.1. Canvas LMS Instance: The contractor shall provision one (1) production instance of the Canvas LMS hosted within a FedRAMP Moderate-
authorized cloud environment. 
4.2.2. User Licensing: The contractor shall provide: 
Canvas Cloud Subscription licenses for up to 500 Users. 
Canvas Credentials Subscription licenses for up to 500 Users. 

N0018926QB054 
Page 5 of 22 
 
 
4.2.3. Platform Scalability: The contractor shall provide a mechanism for the Government to procure additional user licenses or add-on modules (e.g., 
Canvas Studio, Canvas Catalog) at any time during the period of performance. Additions will be incorporated via contract modification in accordance 
with FAR 52.217-9, Option to Extend the Term of the Contract. 
 
 
4.3. Task 3: Implementation and Configuration 
The contractor shall provide all necessary professional services to implement and configure the LMS. 
4.3.1. Canvas LMS Essential Implementation: The contractor shall provide the "Canvas LMS Essential Implementation Bundle," which includes 
virtual consulting sessions covering technical scoping, authentication configuration, data provisioning and validation, and project closeout. 
4.3.2. Canvas Credentials Implementation: The contractor shall provide the "Canvas Credentials Implementation Bundle" to fully configure the digital 
badging and micro-credentialing functionality in coordination with NPDS stakeholders. 
4.3.3. Instructional Design Template: The contractor shall provide one (1) "Instructional Design - Ready Made Template" to accelerate the 
development of standardized and professionally designed course content 
4.4. Task 4: Training and Technical Support 
The contractor shall provide comprehensive training and support services. 
4.4.1. Technical Support: The contractor shall provide "Basic Support," which includes 24/7/365 access to Tier 1 technical support for all licensed 
users via phone, email, and live chat. 
4.4.2. On-Demand Training: The contractor shall provide access to the "Training Portal Essential - Core On-Demand Content" for all NPDS 
instructors and administrators, offering self-paced training on the features and use of the Canvas platform

5.2. Period of Performance 
The period of performance shall be one 12-month base period and four (4) 12-month option periods, if exercised by the Government. 

N0018926QB054 
Page 6 of 22 
 
 
Base Period: 1 May 2026 - 30 April 2027 
Option Period 1: 1 May 2027 - 30 April 2028 
Option Period 2: 1 May 2028 - 30 April 2029 
Option Period 3: 1 May 2029 - 30 April 2030 
Option Period 4: 1 May 2030 - 30 April 2031 
5.3. Place of Performance 
All services required under this contract shall be performed at the contractor's facility. The Learning Management System (LMS) provided by the 
contractor must be accessible to authorized Government personnel worldwide via the internet. This includes personnel located at the Navy 
Postgraduate Dental School in Bethesda, MD, as well as other authorized locations. 
5.4. Level of Effort 
The level of effort is considered inherent to the firm-fixed-price of the COTS subscriptions and services required to meet the performance standards 
outlined in this PWS. No specific labor hours are mandated. 
5.5. Minimum Contractor Qualifications 
The contractor shall be the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM), licensor, and sole provider of the Canvas LMS, holding all proprietary data 
rights. The contractor must possess and maintain a FedRAMP Moderate (or higher) Authority to Operate (ATO) for the proposed solution for the 
entire period of performance. 
5.6. Government Furnished Equipment/Property/Information (GFE/P/I) 
No GFE/P/I will be provided. The Government will provide the contractor with points of contact and access to stakeholders as needed to fulfill the 
tasks of this PWS. 
5.7. Security Requirements 
The Canvas LMS platform must be compliant with all federal security requirements for a SaaS platform at the FedRAMP Moderate level. The 
contractor shall be responsible for the security of the system and the data contained within it. Although this is an unclassified system, it will contain 
Personally Identifiable Information (PII). All PII and any potential Protected Health Information (PHI) shall be handled in accordance with the Health 
Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 (HIPAA) Security and Privacy Rules, the Privacy Act of 1974, and DFARS 252.204-7012. 
5.8. Travel 
No travel is anticipated or authorized under this contract. 
5.9. Other Direct Costs (ODCs) 
No ODCs are anticipated or authorized under this contract.

The Department of Homeland Security, Immigration and Customs (ICE) Office of Acquisition 
Management (OAQ) Irving, TX 75063, hereby gives notice of their intent to solicit and award a 
sole source contract under the statutory authority of 41 U.S.C 3304 permitting other than full and 
open competition to Edge Ops LLC., 3222 Sunrise Drive, Jefferson, MD 21755. Edge Ops 
LLC’s Unique Entity Identification (UEI) number is EZEEYT9FDDD5.  The contracting officer 
has determined in accordance with the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR), RFO 6.103-1, 
only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. 
The Department of Homeland Security (DHS), Homeland Security Investigations (HSI),

Statement of Work 
 Department of Homeland Security (DHS)  
Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) 
National Coordination Center (NCC) 
Project SAFEHAVEN 
April 7, 2026 
 
 
1. BACKGROUND 
 
1.1 Purpose. 
The purpose of this contract is to establish Project SAFEHAVEN analytic support 
services to the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF). The Homeland Security Task 
Force (HSTF) National Coordination Center (NCC) requires dedicated analytic support to 
sustain ongoing homeland security operations, including support to ICE Homeland 
Security Investigations (HSI) and broader mission partners. The Government requires an 
analytic cell capable of deploying against active mission requirements with real-time 
targeting, threat network analysis, and operational reporting. The Project SAFEHAVEN 
requires a mission-engineered, commercially available analytic support solution. 
Unlike traditional subscriptions that deliver raw data and leave the analytic burden to 
Government personnel, Project SAFEHAVEN shall deliver operationally relevant 
analytic output—targeting packages, threat group associations, geolocation products, and 
pattern-of-life assessments—through an integrated support environment. This analytic 
support capability presents the Government with the ability to eliminate reliance on 
fragmented tools and disparate analytic efforts, achieving significant cost savings and 
operational efficiency. 
 
1.2 Requirement Areas Overview 
The scope of work is organized around seven (7) requirement areas.  Each area 
represents a distinct deliverable within the Project SAFEHAVEN analytic cell and is 
defined in detail in Section 2.0 of this statement of work. 
• Track and Geolocate.  The analytic cell shall deploy real-time geolocation 
capability against mission targets, providing operators with current and 
historical location intelligence, pattern-of-life analysis, and positional 
awareness across domestic and international areas of interest. 
• Threat Group Analysis. The analytic cell shall categorize individuals and 
networks into operationally relevant threat groupings—including 
transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), foreign terrorist organizations 
(FTOs), drug trafficking networks, human trafficking organizations, gang 
affiliates, extremists, fugitives, sex offenders, and illegal re-entrants—and 
produce actionable analytical products for mission leadership. 
• Multi-Hardware Observation.  The analytic cell shall correlate observations 
across multiple device types and signal sources to maintain continuity of 
observation on mission targets, ensuring subjects cannot evade analytic 
coverage by changing devices or networks. 
• Training.  The Contractor shall provide educational briefings—including 

on-site, virtual, and vendor-hosted sessions—to ensure Government 
personnel can effectively task, receive, and act on SAFEHAVEN analytic 
output. 
• Reporting.  The Contractor shall provide analytic products based on 
individual customer requirements for product delivery based on priorities 
determined by the PM. Structured monthly usage reports, analytical 
summaries, and ad hoc mission reporting will be proved upon request. 
• User Support.  The Contractor shall provide dedicated mission support 
specialists, and escalation pathways for urgent operational requirements. 
• Information Security.  The Contractor shall ensure all analytic operations 
comply with FedRAMP High, IL-5, Privacy Act, and DHS 4300A 
requirements, with zero-query-retention protections, end-to-end encryption, 
and hosting on a secure Cloud infrastructure meeting all applicable DHS 
security standards. 
 
 
2.0 SCOPE OF WORK/TASK REQUIREMENTS 
The following subsections define the seven (7) requirement areas comprising the 
Project SAFEHAVEN scope of this requirement for the HSTF NCC.  The contractor 
shall deliver all capabilities described herein through the SAFEHAVEN analytic cell, 
deploying directing against Government mission requirements.    
 
2.1 Track and Geolocate. 
The Contractor shall deploy real-time track-and-geolocate analytic capability 
against HSTF NCC mission requirements. The SAFEHAVEN analytic cell shall 
produce geolocation intelligence products in support of active targeting 
operations, including but not limited to: 
• Real-time location of mission targets across domestic and international areas 
of interest. 
• Historical pattern-of-life analysis identifying habitual locations, routes, and 
behavioral patterns. 
• Geolocation resolution leveraging multiple collection sources to establish and 
maintain positional awareness. 
• Maritime positional intelligence in support of coastal, port, and open-ocean 
mission requirements. 
• International and U.S. domestic location intelligence fusion to support cross-
border targeting. 
• Rapid-response geolocation tasking to support time-sensitive operational 
requirements. 
Track-and-geolocate output shall be delivered through SIGNAL and /or a secure, 
web-based interface accessible to authorized HSTF NCC personnel. The analytic 
cell shall provide geolocation products in response to specific mission taskings 
and standing analytic coverage of priority targets. Frontline operators shall be able 
to task, receive, and act on geolocation intelligence without requiring manual data 
processing or external support. 
 

2.2 Threat Group Analysis. 
The Contractor shall provide dedicated threat group analysis in support of HSTF 
NCC targeting and intelligence operations. The SAFEHAVEN analytic cell shall 
identify, categorize, and map individuals and networks into operationally relevant 
threat groups, producing analytical products that enable mission leadership to 
understand and act against organized threat structures. Threat categories shall 
include but not be limited to: Transnational Criminal Organizations (TCOs), 
Foreign Terrorist Organizations (FTOs), Drug Trafficking Networks, Gang 
Members, International Extremists, and Fugitives etc. 
The analytic cell shall produce threat group products that identify associations 
between subjects, map patterns of movement and communication, reveal network 
structures, and highlight operational vulnerabilities within targeted organizations. 
Threat group analysis shall be integrated directly into SAFEHAVEN’s targeting 
workflow, enabling analysts to move from identification to actionable intelligence 
within relevant operational timelines. 
 
2.3 Multi-Hardware Observation. 
The Contractor shall analytic capability to maintain continuity of observation on 
mission targets across multiple device types, networks, and operational 
environments. Multi-hardware observation capabilities shall include: 
• Correlation of target activity across mobile IoT devices to maintain unified 
target profiles. 
• Association mapping across Wi-Fi access points and network identifiers. 
• Correlation of target activity across multiple networks and geographic 
locations. 
• Fusion of observations from multiple collection sources to build 
comprehensive operational pictures of target behavior. 
• Temporal analysis correlating multi-source observations to establish and 
refine pattern-of-life assessments. 
The analytic cell shall produce unified target profiles that aggregate available 
observations. This ensures that HSTF NCC analysts receive a robust operational 
picture rather than fragmentary reporting from individual collection sources. 
 
2.4 Training. 
The Contractor shall comprehensive, mission-tailored briefings to ensure HSTF 
NCC personnel can effectively task the SAFEHAVEN analytic cell, interpret 
analytic output, and integrate SAFEHAVEN products into operational workflows.  
 
2.5 Reporting. 
The Contractor shall deliver project reports to help the Government maintain 
visibility into analytic activity, mission output, and operational impact. Reporting 
requirements include: 
• Monthly usage reports include analyst activity, tasking volume, and analytic 
output summaries. 
• Analytical summary reports aggregating SAFEHAVEN mission output for 
leadership review. 

• Ad hoc mission reporting as requested by the Contracting Officer’s 
Representative (COR). 
All reports shall be designed to support both program oversight and operational 
decision-making at the mission leadership level. 
 
2.6 User Support. 
The Contractor shall dedicated support to ensure uninterrupted access to the 
SAFEHAVEN analytic cell for all authorized HSTF NCC personnel. User support 
shall include: 
• Dedicated mission support specialists who understand the HSTF NCC 
operational environment and can assist with analytic tasking. 
• Escalation pathways for urgent operational requirements to ensure the analytic 
cell remains responsive to time-sensitive mission needs. 
• Compliance with applicable DHS security policies in relation to OPSEC and 
reporting.  
User support shall be designed to minimize unplanned downtime for operational 
users. The Contractor shall maintain dedicated personnel familiar with the HSTF 
NCC mission environment to provide responsive, context-aware support 
throughout the period of performance. 
 
2.7 Information Security. 
The Contractor shall ensure that SAFEHAVEN analytic operations meet or 
exceed information security requirements applicable to DHS operations. The 
security posture of the analytic cell shall protect both Government operational 
activity and the integrity of analytic products. Information security requirements 
include: 
• FedRAMP High authorization, ensuring compliance with the federal cloud 
security baseline. 
• Impact Level 5 (IL-5) compliance for controlled unclassified information 
(CUI). 
• Zero-query-retention architecture. The analytic cell shall not retain user search 
parameters, tasking details, or sensitive operational metadata beyond what is 
required to produce the requested analytic output. 
• Compliance with the Privacy Act and DHS 4300A security policy. 
• Hosted on secure Cloud infrastructure that meets applicable DHS security 
standards. 
The information security posture shall ensure that HSTF NCC operations are 
protected against unauthorized access and compromise of analyst activities. The 
zero-query-retention design protects operational security—ensuring that the 
analytic cell does not become a repository of sensitive Government tasking 
information. 
 
3.0 OTHER APPLICABLE REQUIREMENTS 
 
3.1 Period of Performance.  
The period of performance will consist of one (1) base year, May 1, 2026 through 

April 30, 2027. 
 
3.2 Place of Performance. 
The primary place of performance will be the Contractor’s facilities with frequent 
visits to the Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) headquarters facilities in 
the Washington Metro Area. 
 
3.3 Travel. 
The Contractor travel is not required for this requirement. Local meetings 
or activities planned outside  of the defined place of performance are 
permitted, but all expenses incurred are the responsibility of the contractor
