The United States Senate (hereinafter referred to as the “Senate”) Office of the Sergeant at Arms 
(“SAA”) is responsible for the delivery of Senate Office web presences on the Senate’s public internet 
network, www.senate.gov.  In order to provide Senate Offices with services and software that meet their 
technical and functional requirements, the SAA will enter into contracts with web developers to design, 
develop, and/or maintain the Senate Offices’ public websites in part or in whole for United States 
Senator and Committee Offices (“Senate Office” or “Office”). The web developer(s) shall hereinafter 
be referred to as the “Contractor”.  
 
B.2 DESCRIPTION OF SERVICES  
 
The Contractor shall assist Senate Offices with the requested website services, as listed in Section B.7.1, 
for their public senate.gov websites.  Any products or services to be furnished under this Contract shall 
be ordered by issuance of Task Order(s) by the Contracting Officer (see Section G.1).  The Contractor 
will be provided with a base build that is configured with tools, features, content types, and plugins for 
use by Senate Office websites.  The Senate reserves the right to further define and/or change 
requirements through contract or task order modifications.  
 
Management rights to the site and its content, in whatever stage of completion, shall be the sole property 
of the Senate Office.

The SAA anticipates award of hybrid Multiple Award Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (“IDIQ”) 
contracts utilizing both Firm-Fixed-Price and Labor-Hour Task Orders.  Under  a Labor-Hour Task 
Order, the Contractor shall not exceed the existing funding and originally proposed labor hours on the 
Task Order without written approval from the Contracting Officer.  In addition, under a Labor-Hour 
Task Order, if the actual number of hours required to complete the task is lower than the number 
proposed, the Contractor shall invoice for the actual number of hours to complete the work.  All services 
shall be provided at fixed labor rates that will comprise either a Firm-Fixed-Price or Labor-Hour 
estimate per Task Order.   
 
The SAA may elect to award multiple IDIQ contracts for the same or similar services should it be 
determined it is in the best interest of the Senate.  In addition, the Senate reserves the right to resolicit 
and award additional IDIQ Contracts later, as the SAA determines necessary at its sole discretion.   
 
B.4 PRICING  
 
The schedule at Section B.7.1 shall provide the firm-fixed labor-hour and monthly rates for the services 
offered herein under this Contract.  All pricing shall be fully burdened with all administrative costs and 
other direct costs unless specifically otherwise identified or agreed upon by the SAA.  Travel costs are 
not expected under this Contract, however in the event that travel outside of the Metropolitan 
Washington Area is required, the Contractor shall provide a Firm-Fixed-Price for the required long-
distance travel and the SAA shall approve the travel by issuance of a written Task Order or Task Order 
modification prior to the Contractor incurring any such costs. 

Page 3 of 57  
  
The Contractor shall provide website design and development, website maintenance and end-user 
support, training, and content migration services on an hourly basis.  Alternately, Website maintenance 
and end-user support may also be provided monthly at a firm-fixed price (FFP).  All pricing submissions 
shall be rounded to the nearest whole dollar, i.e., $250.46 is $250.00, $250.73 is $251.00.  
 
The Contractor’s goal shall be to deliver all services within the task order value and period of 
performance, in accordance with industry best practices.   
 
B.5 TERM  
 
This Contract is effective for a one-year base period, which shall commence on or about January 1, 
2027.  The Contract will have five (5) one-year option periods.  The SAA may exercise option(s) in 
accordance with Section H.9, Exercise of Options.   
 
B.6 PRICE RE-DETERMINATION AND ADJUSTMENT  
 
The Contractor may offer a price reduction at any time effective upon the date offered by the Contractor 
and shall apply to all services performed on or after the effective date of price change.  Price increases 
shall be mutually agreed.  Any pricing changes shall be incorporated into the Contract through a 
modification hereto.

SECTION C - TASK ORDERS/STATEMENT OF WORK

Contract term.   
 
C.1.3 The Contractor shall use SAA-provided resources solely and exclusively for providing and

The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC),  National Center for Immunization and 
Respiratory Diseases (NCIRD), Office of Director (OD), Office of Laboratory Systems and Response 
(OLSR), intends to award a sole source firm fixed price purchase order to Key Solutions, Inc., 2803 
Lakeview Ct, Fremont, CA, 94538 for the purchase of the eProtocol software license for the Institutional 
Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC) and for the purchase of Lab Animal Resource System (LARS) 
software license. 
The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) utilizes the Key Solutions’  eProtocol modules to 
manage their animal care program. It currently supports the entire agency in the area of animal 
procurement and ordering; animal record keeping; data collection; reporting tools; and billing 
information. The Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC) protocol compliance module 
ensures consistent protocol review, maintains full traceability, simplifies role -based access, and 
strengthens compliance oversight. The Lab Animal Resource System (LARS) module streamlines end -
to-end activities, from animal requisition to daily management. Both software licenses will include up to 
50 active IACUC users, 16 hours of web-based training, an annual maintenance agreement, custom 
services, and data migration services. 
This contract action is for supplies or services for which the Government intends to solicit and negotiate 
with only one source under the authority of FAR 6.103-1(b) and 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1) or 41 U.S.C. 
3304(a)(1). The NAICS code for this acquisition is 541511, Custom Computer Software Programming 
Services. 
Interested entities may identify their interest and capability to respond to the requirement. This notice of 
intent is not a request for competitive quotations; however, all responses received within fifteen (15) days 
of the issuance of this notice will be considered by the government. A determination by the government 
not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of 
the government. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining 
whether to conduct competitive procurement. Any quotation/response should be emailed to contract 
specialist Felipe Cardenas at tpp5@cdc.gov by 4:00pm EST on May 12, 2026.

EV ALUATION CRITERIA 
(a) Basis for Award 
The Government will award a contract to the responsible quoter whose quote, conforming to the 
solicitation, is determined to be the most advantageous to the Government, price and other 
factors considered (best value).  
(b) Evaluation Process 
The evaluation will be conducted in two steps. 
Step 1 – Evaluation of Technical Capability (Pass/Fail)  
The Government will first evaluate each quote's Technical Capability (Go/No-Go) requirements 
listed in Section L. A quote will receive a "Pass" for meeting or exceeding all requirements stated 
in the Technical Capability (Go/No-Go) Requirement and move into Step 2 – Best Value 
Evaluation. A quote will receive a “Fail” for not meeting one or more of the requirements stated 
in the Technical Capability (Go/No-Go) and will not move onto Step 2 – Best Value Evaluation.  
Step 2 – Best Value Evaluation 
Only quotes that receive a "Pass" rating in Step 1 will be further evaluated. To determine the best 
value, the Government will perform a comparative analysis of the “Pass” rating quotes against

2. Factor 2: Past Performance

providing access to equivalent or superior GPUs than the ones outlined in Section L, will 
receive a higher rating.

requirements of the contract; and (2) reduce the contract price to reflect the reduced value of the services
performed.  In the event Contractor fails promptly to reperform the services or redeliver the goods, or to take
necessary steps to ensure future performance of the services or delivery of the goods in conformity with the
requirements of the Award, the FDIC shall have the right to either (1) by contract or otherwise, have the services
performed or the goods delivered in conformity with the contract requirements and charge to Contractor any cost
occasioned to the FDIC that is directly related to the performance of such services or the delivery of such goods; or
(2) terminate this Award for default as provided in 7.6.6-02, Termination for Default.
 
(c) Contractor shall provide and maintain an inspection system acceptable to the FDIC covering the goods or
services to be delivered or performed hereunder.  Records of all inspection work by Contractor shall be kept
complete and available to the FDIC during the term of this Award and for such longer period as may be specified
elsewhere in this Award.

GENERAL INFORMATION

CONTACT INFORMATION

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

DESCRIPTION

THIS REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) – SOURCES SOUGHT IS ISSUED SOLELY FOR MARKET RESEARCH AND PLANNING PURPOSES ONLY AND DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION

1.  Responses to this Sources Sought must be in writing.  The purpose of this Sources Sought Announcement is for market research only to make appropriate acquisition decisions and to gain knowledge of Small Business Capability, including Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses and Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSB/VOSB) interested and capable of performing the work.  

2.  The NAICS for this requirement is 541519 - Other Computer Related Services  

 

The contractor shall provide a commercial, cloud-based scheduling solution for the Northern Arizona VA Healthcare System (NAVAHCS) Emergency Department, including software subscription or licensing, implementation, configuration, testing, training, go-live support, and ongoing technical support for the period of performance.

The solution shall provide a centralized platform to create, publish, maintain, and review schedules in real time and shall support schedule automation, user self-service, reporting, and, if included in the awarded package, time and attendance and workforce analytics capabilities. Any interfaces or integrations shall be limited to those approved by the Government.

The Contractor shall provide all supervision, coordination, staffing, software, licenses, website access, training, redundancy and other related services as necessary to provide and maintain VASDHS building records and files and make them readily accessible to VA staff through the Contractor’s website. The Contractor shall perform all these services as defined by this Statement of Work (SOW) and by the COR or other CO designated representative. See attached DRAFT SOW and Salient Characteristics Sheet.

3.. Interested and capable Contractors should respond to this notice not later than Tuesday, May 05, 2026, at 12:00 PM Pacific Time, by providing the following via email only to Israel.Garcia2@va.gov.

 	(a) company name

 

(b) address  

(c) point of contact  

(d) phone, fax, and email of primary point of contact

(e) Contractor’s Unique Entity ID (SAM) number

(f) Type of small business, if applicable, (e.g. Services-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB), Veteran-owned Small Business (VOSB), 8(a), HUB-Zone, Women Owned Small Business, Small disadvantaged business, or Small Business).  

(g) A statement that addresses whether you believe that your performance under this contract should be exempted from the Service Contract Act or not. Please name any applicable exemption, if any.

(h) Statement indicating if you have a current contract to provide the required services that you intend to provide for this procurement under either the General Services Administration (GSA) Federal Supply Schedule (FSS), or any other federal contract.  If yes, provide the contract type and contract number, as well as the identity of the federal agency with whom you hold that contract.

(i) General pricing for your patient lift product. This information will be used for VA internal market research purposes and pricing information received in response to this RFI will not be shared by the Contract Specialist.  

(j) Statement indicating whether your company is considered small under the size standard for the NAICS code identified under this RFI. Responses are welcome to specify a different NAICS in which they could meet this requirement.

(k) A capability statement that addresses the organization’s qualifications and ability to perform as a contractor specifically for the work described above and in the attached Draft SOW. Respondents are also encouraged to provide specific examples (e.g. contract number, point of contact information) of the Contractor’s experience providing the same or similar services. Failure to provide sufficient information may result in the Government’s inability to determine that the respondent is capable. GENERAL STATEMENTS OF CAPABILITY ARE NOT ACCEPTABLE. Respondents must provide the following information for each reference contract the respondent identifies as evidence of the respondent’s capability to perform the work required by this procurement.  Respondents must provide the following information for each reference contract:

(1) the legal name of entity with whom the respondent held the contract;

(2) the contract number;

(3) a description providing details of the specific tasks the respondent performed under 	that contract;

(4) the dates during which the respondent performed the contract;

(5) the name, phone number, and email address of a person at the entity with whom the

 respondent held the contract who can verify the information the respondent provides 

regarding this reference contract.

If a respondent offers to demonstrate experience through the proposed use of subcontractors, the respondent must provide all of the information required above for one or more reference contracts performed by each subcontractor the respondent intends to use.

NOTE: The information requested above is required for the Government to evaluate whether there are sufficient small business concerns of a particular type who are capable of performing the work required by this procurement to determine if this procurement should be set aside for a given type of small business concern.  failure to submit all of the information requested above to support a respondent’s claimed experience may be viewed by the government as evidence that the respondent lacks the ability to provide the required service described in the DRAFT SOW.  this, in turn, may affect the government’s determination about whether the requirements for a set-aside procurement have been met.


4. SDVOSB/VOSB respondents.

(a) If respondent is VOSB or SDVOSB, respondent is encouraged to provide proof of SDVOSB/VOSB certification.  In addition, SDVOSB/VOSB Contractors are asked to acknowledge that they understand the limitations on sub-contracting pursuant to FAR 52.219-14, Limitations on Sub-Contracting, which will be included in the impending solicitation.  Further SDVOSB/VOSB contractors are asked to respond that they are capable of providing the requested services keeping within the parameters of this clause.

(b) Small businesses, including SDVOSB/VOSBS are also advised that per 13 CFR, § 125.6 the prime contractor's limitations on subcontracting are as follows:

     	(1) General. In order to be awarded a full or partial small business set-aside contract with a value greater than $250,000, an 8(a) contract, an SDVO SBC contract, a HUBZone contract, a WOSB or EDWOSB contract pursuant to part 127 of this chapter, a small business concern must agree that: 

   	(2) In the case of a contract for services (except construction), it will not pay more than 50% of the amount paid by the government to it to firms that are not similarly situated. Any work that a similarly situated subcontractor further subcontracts will count towards the 50% subcontract amount that cannot be exceeded. 

5. Please note that if VA’s pending market research establishes that two or more verified VOSB or SDVOSB can provide the services required, VA will set aside the underlying solicitation per 38 U.S.C. §8127. 

6. All Offerors who provide goods or services to the United States Federal Government must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) database found at https://www.sam.gov.  Registration must include Representations and Certifications.  

--End of Sources Sought Announcement--

  This RFI is issued solely for information and planning purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation.  All information received in response to this RFI that is marked as proprietary will be handled accordingly.  In accordance with FAR 15.201(e), responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract.  Responders are solely responsible for all expenses associated with responding to this RFI.

Essential/significant physical, functional, or performance characteristics:
• Must be able to create schedules as far out in the future as desired (monthly, quarterly, annually, etc.).
• Must be 100% web-based, accessible by a web browser both inside the VA hospital and outside, and not locally hosted 
and/or require additional hardware/software at the facility.
• Must be accessible via native iPhone and Android mobile applications and provide full end-user functionality (schedule 
viewing, requesting, swapping, etc.), with FedRAMP approved use from both military and personal smart phones.
• Must offer multiple ways of creating the schedule including the ability to have software automations create the 
schedule. The automations should use a rules-based engine, powered by a configurable algorithm.
• Must be a solution with interactive/intuitive logic to prevent scheduling gaps if the algorithm is unable to reach "100%" 
during the automated build process, which presents data related to conflicts and suggestions on provider availability.
• Must be a solution that can take into account various preferences/rules for consecutive shifts and allows for more 
variable numbers of consecutive, time-based shifts.
• Must be a solution with the ability to track provider targets in "real time" as it relates to the number of shifts or hours as 
well as consider this information in future automated schedule builds.
• Must be able to incorporate individual provider scheduling preferences.
• Must provide user-friendly decision support tools to aid in the efficient creation of schedules.
• Must support the ability for providers to submit requests for open shifts, specific roles, or time off electronically. It 
should also enforce any limits that a facility would like to put in place.
• Must be able to support functionality which allows administrators and providers to put shifts up for pickup (QGenda's 
"available shifts" board) and ability to request to pick shifts up.
• Must be able to support a multi-tier approval process.
• Must be able to track time worked via a mobile application and/or web solution. The mobile application should also be 
able to geo-verify and flag exceptions to all time punches. Finally, the time tracking capabilities should enable users to 
identify and report on overtime.
• Must support the ability to pull reports on-demand and be exportable to Excel, PDF, and CSV including number of shifts 
worked, call fairness, weekdays vs weekends, PTO reports, etc.
• Must be able to filter schedule data in any format (by region, by site, by provider type, etc.).
• Must be able to support the request process through the mobile application. It should also let providers submit shifts to 
a "swap market" for time they are looking to take off and also allow them to pick up shifts from other providers looking 
to change their schedule.
• Must have the ability to configure various levels of user permissions and associated functionality at the enterprise, 
departmental and user level.

Department of Veterans Affairs

STATEMENT OF WORK

1. Contract Title:

QGenda Scheduling Automation for the Northern Arizona VA Health Care System (NAVAHCS) Emergency Department.

2. Background.

The NAVAHCS Emergency Department operates in a dynamic clinical environment that requires accurate, timely, and accessible scheduling for physicians, nurses, and other designated clinical team members. Manual or fragmented scheduling processes can limit real-time visibility, delay communication of schedule changes, and reduce administrative efficiency in a 24/7 setting.

NAVAHCS is seeking a secure, healthcare-specific scheduling solution that improves schedule transparency, flexibility, and fairness when operationally feasible; increases access to the most current schedule information from any location or device; and strengthens time and attendance accuracy and workforce planning. The sample QGenda federal Statement of Work provided to the Government indicates that QGenda is already being used within the Department of Veterans Affairs and is positioned to support secure federal healthcare scheduling needs.

3. Scope.

The contractor shall provide a commercial, cloud-based QGenda scheduling solution for the NAVAHCS Emergency Department, including software subscription or licensing, implementation, configuration, testing, training, go-live support, and ongoing technical support for the period of performance.

The solution shall provide a centralized platform to create, publish, maintain, and review schedules in real time and shall support schedule automation, user self-service, reporting, and, if included in the awarded package, time and attendance and workforce analytics capabilities. Any interfaces or integrations shall be limited to those approved by the Government.

4. Specific Tasks.

4.1 Project Planning and Discovery.

The contractor shall conduct project kickoff and discovery activities with the Government to identify scheduling groups, staffing roles, shift types, duty locations, coverage requirements, leave and request rules, reporting needs, implementation milestones, and system administrator responsibilities.

Department of Veterans Affairs  
Request for Information  
36C10B26Q0380 
Inventory Management Modernization 
April 27, 2026 
 
 
This is a Request for Information (RFI) only.  Do not submit a quote. This RFI is for planning 
purposes only and shall not be considered a Request for Quotation.  Additionally, there is no 
obligation on the part of the Government to acquire any products or services described in this 
RFI.  Your response to this RFI will be treated only as information for the Government to 
consider.  You will not be entitled to payment for direct or indirect costs that you incur in 
responding to this RFI.  This request does not constitute a solicitation for quotes or the authority 
to enter negotiations to award a task order/contract.  No funds have been authorized, 
appropriated or received for this effort.  The information provided may be used by the 
Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) in developing its acquisition strategy.  Interested parties 
are responsible for adequately marking proprietary, restricted or competition sensitive 
information contained in their response.  The Government does not intend to pay for the 
information submitted in response to this RFI. 
 
Introduction:  
The Department of Veterans Affairs anticipates either a single or multiple award Indefinite 
Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) for a supply chain enterprise inventory management system 
to include procurement and receiving services contract in Fiscal Year 2027.  As such, VA is 
seeking industry feedback on the draft Performance Work Statement (PWS) to provide a 
modernized Inventory Management and ordering solution.  It is acknowledged that the VA 
Supply Chain is antiquated and complex.  As such, there may not be one single technology 
solution from a single vendor, and some desired objectives may not be readily achievable.  
Utilizing a system of systems approach is acceptable and teaming is encouraged. Additionally, it 
is acknowledged that there are several existing technology solutions already in operation 
throughout VA which could be included in potential solutions. 
 
VA is a large and complex civilian Agency within the Federal Government providing care to 
Veterans and their dependents.  VA spends billions of dollars on goods and services across 
several organizations including the Veterans Health Administration (VHA), Veterans Benefits 
Administration (VBA), National Cemeteries Administration (NCA), VA Central Office 
(VACO), and the Office of Information and Technology (OIT), each responsible for logistics and 
asset management activities and functions specific to its mission.  In support of these activities, 
and surge capabilities in response to the 4th Mission, VA requires an integrated and 
comprehensive supply chain capability that can sustain operations under all conditions, rapidly 
scale to meet emergent needs, and maintain uninterrupted delivery of critical goods and services. 
 
VHA, VBA, NCA, VACO, and OIT are each responsible for logistics and asset management 
activities and functions specific to their mission. VA requires an easy to use, integrated, 
intelligent supply chain modernization and management solution that is cloud based.  The VA 
Supply Chain manages the flow of goods, services, and information between all stakeholders, 

RFI - Inventory Management Modernization 
2 
 
including within VA, external suppliers and service providers, and the ultimate customer – the 
Veteran. This includes, but is not limited to, Prosthetics; Pharmacy and Pharmacy Bio‑response; 
Information Technology; Supplies; and Burial and Benefit supplies, as well as the administration 
of these functions. The objective of this effort is to align VA’s supply chain to enhance mission 
efficiency by reducing process and system complexity, standardizing data and business practices, 
and improving integration with other VA enterprise systems. 
 
Capability Statement 
Submit a capability statement and proposed business process flows describing your company’s 
ability to meet the objectives in the attached draft PWS. The capability statement shall be limited 
to 15 pages.  
 
The capability statement shall address the following: 
 
1. Include the following identification information 
 
a. Company Name 
b. Unique Entity ID Number under which the company is registered in 
SAM/vetbiz.va.gov/ 
c. Small Business Status and applicable NAICS code (it is intended the solicitation will 
be related to 541512). Please also indicate whether you will be able to comply with 
VAAR 852.219-10, VA Notice of Total Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small 
Business Set-Aside and with subcontracting limitations in 13 CFR 125.6 in execution 
of this effort? 
d. Company Address 
e. Point of contact name 
f. Telephone number 
g. Email address 
h. Please provide any available contract vehicles the proposed solution would be 
available on (i.e. SEWP, GSA, etc.). 
i. Please provide a Rough Order of Magnitude needed in order to meet the requirements 
detailed in the PWS 
 
2. Demonstrate your expertise and capability in implementing a nationwide supply chain 
modernization/optimization for an organization of similar size, scope and complexity as VA. 
Have you done this type of work with the Federal Government? Provide supporting details to 
indicate whether you were the prime contractor or subcontractor. Please state whether you 
intend to propose on this effort as a Prime contractor or subcontractor.   
 
3. In addition, please include responses to the following questions in your capabilities statement:
 
 
a) Please provide any feedback on whether a single or multiple award IDIQ is better suited 
for this effort?  
b) Does your firm have a system compliant with the Electronic Industries Alliance Standard 
748 (EIA-748) per Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul (RFO) 

RFI - Inventory Management Modernization 
3 
 
Deviation Part 34.2? Does your firm have any contracts utilizing Earned Value 
Management in an Agile environment?   
c) If you are proposing cloud-based products/services/platforms and it will be hosted 
outside of VA enterprise cloud, is it currently Federal Risk and Authorization 
Management Program (FedRAMP) compliant/authorized?  If so, at what level? 
d) Does your solution have the capability to interface with, but not limited to, any of the 
following VA systems: The Integrated Financial and Acquisition Management System 
(iFAMS); the current Financial Management System (FMS), VA electronic health record 
system established under the Electronic Health Record Modernization Program; and the 
Veterans Health Information Systems and Technology Architecture (VistA) and 
Computerized Patient Record System (CPRS). 
e) Please describe your systems’ current and past use in major healthcare facilities with the 
ability to support real‑time, enterprise‑wide inventory visibility across multiple supply 
chain functional areas. Provide examples of where this capability is currently deployed.  
f) Define the scalability and performance characteristics of your solution, to include use 
during surge operations associated with VA’s 4th Mission. How would you scale the 
system for maximum volume of transactions, users, and data your system can support via 
reliability, availability (99.99%,) and maintainability (RAM). Provide examples and 
describe what you do currently to maintain adequate RAM score for other 
implementations of your system(s). 
g) Describe your system and whether it is a single solution or if it will be comprised of 
multiple systems to meet the requirements of the PWS.  
h) Describe your approach to data governance, including support for data cleansing, data 
standardization, data enrichment, data quality, interoperability, metadata/lineage tracking, 
and compliance with VA and federal data standards. 
i) Please describe how your solution supports integration with emerging technologies such 
as predictive analytics, AI/ML, demand planning tools, and inventory optimization 
engines. 
j) What is your typical deployment approach and timeline (e.g., phased rollout, pilot-first, 
big-bang, progressive wave deployment)?  
k) What is your software license schema/type (enterprise, individual, subscription, SaaS, 
monthly, annual, etc.)?  Describe the level of support that comes with the license price. 
Does your solution require any third-party licensing? 
l) Describe your Organizational Change Management (OCM) approach and support for 
business process reengineering and experience in large‑scale federal logistics or 
healthcare transformation efforts. Include training methods, end‑user adoption strategies, 
and post‑go‑live stabilization support. 
m) Please describe your solution’s capabilities to perform the following functions and any 
specific devices utilized for the purposes below: 
                    - Barcode/RFID scanning/Barcode Printing 
                    - Serial and lot tracking 
        - Expiration tracking 
                    - Recall management 
                    - Perpetual inventory 
n) Describe your solution’s ability to support the full medical supply chain beyond typical 
Medical Surgical consumables, accommodating commodity‑specific workflows and 

RFI - Inventory Management Modernization 
4 
 
special considerations for Pharmacy, Prosthetics, DME, Consignment, and Biologics. 
Provide an assessment of how significantly your workflows would need to be altered to 
meet unique federal and VA requirements—such as minimal, moderate, or extensive 
changes; include rationale across regulatory compliance, data standards and item master 
governance, integration approach, security and privacy, accessibility (Section 508), and 
acquisition/financial processes; and cite comparable large‑scale healthcare deployments 
where available. 
o) How much of your system adaptability is configuration rather than customization? 
p) Describe your cybersecurity and identity‑management capabilities, including support for 
multi-factor authentication, single sign‑on, audit logging, encryption at rest/in transit, and 
compliance with NIST SP 800‑53 and VA cybersecurity policies. 
q) Explain your solution’s ability to operate during network outages or degraded conditions. 
Does your system offer offline mode, local caching, queuing, or other continuity-of-
operations capabilities? 
r) Provide a business process flow, in flow‑diagram format, that depicts both manual and 
automated processes and assumes VA’s VALIP as the middleware between systems. This 
submission shall be provided in addition to the 15‑page capability statement. 
 
3. Please provide any questions or comments you may have on the draft PWS included with this 
RFI as well as the intended Contract/Order type.  Please state whether the draft PWS includes 
enough information for your firm to provide a proposal?  If not, please provide what specific 
definition or information you need from VA to ensure you can provide an accurate and 
reasonable proposal. 
 
 
Responses to this Request for Information shall ONLY be submitted electronically via 
email to Jason King at 
jason.king6@va.gov and Michelle Prinston at michelle.prinston@va.gov 
no later than 12:00PM Eastern Time on May 11, 2026.

Sources Sought Notice 
Department of the Interior 
U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) 
Alaska Science Center (ASC) 
 
The U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) is conducting market research to determine the availability of 
qualified businesses capable of providing maintenance and support services for an existing StarWind 
HyperConverged Appliance (HCA) environment, as described below. 
 
This Sources Sought Notice is for information and planning purposes only and does not constitute a 
solicitation. This is not a Request for Quote (RFQ). The Government is not obligated to issue a 
solicitation or award a contract as a result of this notice. The Government will not reimburse any costs 
associated with responding. 
 
The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 541519 Other Computer 
Related Services, with a size standard of $34.0 million. The applicable Product Service Code (PSC) is DF01 
IT and Telecom IT Management Support Services (Labor). 
 
All responsible sources may submit a capability statement demonstrating their ability to meet the 
requirement. Responses shall be submitted via email to Joel Berberena at joel_berberena@ios.doi.gov 
and must be received before the close date of this notice. Late responses or responses submitted by 
other than email will not be considered. 
 
Capability Statement Requirements 
Interested vendors shall provide the following: 
1. Description of capability to provide maintenance and support for hyperconverged infrastructure 
environments 
2. Experience supporting StarWind HyperConverged Appliance (HCA) or similar hyperconverged or 
virtualized storage/compute systems 
3. Description of ability to support Dell OEMR R740xd2 server hardware or equivalent enterprise 
server platforms 
4. Description of ability to provide hardware support for end-of-life or legacy systems, including 
access to replacement components 
5. Description of ability to provide software support, including updates, patches, and 
troubleshooting for hyperconverged platforms 
6. Description of access to proprietary software support or equivalent capability to support 
StarWind environments 
7. Examples of similar work performed supporting enterprise IT infrastructure, particularly aging or 
legacy systems 
8. Company information, including business size, UEI, and SAM registration status 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

140G0326Q0103 PR0044043274 StarWind HCA Support Renewal 
Statement of Work 
StarWind HyperConverged Appliance (HCA) Support Renewal 
Requisition: PR0044042927 
 
I. GENERAL INFORMATION 
A. Introduction 
The U.S. Geological Survey (USGS), Alaska Science Center (ASC), requires continued maintenance and 
support for an existing StarWind HyperConverged Appliance (HCA) environment. 
 
B. Background 
The existing system consists of two Dell OEMR R740xd2 servers configured as a hyperconverged 
appliance. The hardware is approaching seven years of service life and is nearing the end of its 
supported lifecycle. Continued support is required to maintain operational capability until a planned 
transition to a cloud-based environment is completed. 
 
C. Scope 
The Contractor shall provide maintenance and support services necessary to sustain the existing 
StarWind HCA environment, including compatibility with existing hardware and software configurations. 
 
II. WORK REQUIREMENTS 
A. Technical Requirements 
1. Provide maintenance renewal for StarWind HCA hardware and software 
2. Provide remote technical support for troubleshooting system issues 
3. Provide access to software updates, patches, and system fixes as applicable 
4. Provide hardware support, including diagnosis and coordination of replacement components for 
aging systems 
5. Provide access to support resources, including ticketing and technical documentation 
 
III. DELIVERABLES 
1. Active support coverage for the StarWind HCA environment 
2. Documentation verifying support coverage period 
3. Access to support services, including contact information and support portal access (if 
applicable) 
 
IV. SUPPORTING INFORMATION 
A. Place of Performance 
USGS Alaska Science Center 
 
B. Government Furnished Property (GFP) 
Existing StarWind HCA hardware and software 
The Government is seeking information on vendors capable of meeting these requirements. Responses 
will be used to determine the appropriate acquisition strategy.

SOURCES SOUGHT SYNOPSIS (Not a Notice of Solicitation) 
99 CONS Sources Sought – 805 CTS Offsec Learn Enterprise Subscription 
 
The United States Air Force, 99 CONS, Nellis AFB, NV is seeking capabilities packages of 
potential sources, including small business (SB), 8(a), HUBZone, and Service-Disabled Veteran-
Owned (SDVO) small businesses that are capable of providing an Offensive Security Enterprise 
Training platform and Penetration Testing with Kali Linux course (PEN-200) for six users for 
one year. 
 
All interested firms shall submit a response demonstrating their capability to provide these items 
to the Primary Point of Contact listed below. Responses to this notice are not considered offers 
and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. No solicitation (Request 
for Quotes) exists; therefore, do not request a copy of the solicitation. The decision to solicit for 
a contract shall be solely within the Government's discretion.  
 
The NAICS Code assigned to this acquisition is 541519 – Other Computer Related Services with 
a size standard of $34.0M. Firms responding should indicate their size in relation to this size 
standard, and indicate socio-economic status (SB, 8(a), SDVO, or HUBZone). Respondents are 
further requested to indicate their status as a Foreign-owned/foreign-controlled firm and any 
contemplated use of foreign national employees on this effort. The Government reserves the 
right to consider a small business set-aside based upon responses hereto for any subsequent 
action. All prospective contractors must be registered in the System for Award Management 
(SAM) database to be awarded a DoD contract.  No set-aside decision has been made.  Note that 
a key factor in determining an acquisition to be a Small Business Set Aside is that small business 
prime contractors must perform at least 50% of the effort, as defined in Federal Acquisition 
Regulation (FAR) clause 52.219-14.   
 
Any information submitted by respondents to this sources sought synopsis is voluntary. This 
sources sought notice is not to be construed as a commitment by the Government, nor will the 
Government reimburse any costs associated with the submission of information in response to 
this notice. Respondents will not be individually notified of the results of any Government 
assessments. The Government's assessment of the capability statements received will factor into 
whether any forthcoming solicitation will be conducted as a full and open competition or as a 
set-aside for small businesses, or any particular small business program.  To ensure your 
response along with any and all attachments are received, attachment(s) must be less than 
10 MB [in total].  It is the responsibility of the respondent to contact the government to 
confirm receipt prior to the offer due date and time. 
 
 
 
 
 
CAPABILITIES PACKAGE: All interested firms shall submit a capabilities package that 
explicitly demonstrates their capability to provide the required commodities. The capabilities 
package should be brief and concise, yet clearly demonstrate an ability to meet the stated 
requirements. 

 
Responses may be submitted electronically to the following e-mail address: 
sencere.gilbert@us.af.mil  
 
All correspondence sent via email shall contain a subject line that reads “99 CONS Sources 
Sought – 805 CTS Offsec Learn Enterprise Subscription” If this subject line is not included, the 
email may not get through email filters at Nellis AFB. Filters are designed to delete emails 
without a subject or with a suspicious subject or attachments. Attachments with files ending in 
.zip or .exe are not allowable and will be deleted. Ensure only .pdf, .doc, .docx, .xsls or .xls 
documents are attached to your email. All other attachments may be deleted. Responses shall be 
emailed to: 
 
99 CONS,  
POC – SSgt Sencere Gilbert   
Email: sencere.gilbert@us.af.mil 
 
RESPONSES ARE DUE NOT LATER THAN 30 April 2026 BY 4:00 PM Pacific Time. 
Direct all questions concerning this acquisition to SSgt Sencere Gilbert at 
sencere.gilbert@us.af.mil

SECTION I-CONTRACT REQUIREMENTS 
1. CONTRACT T
YPE AND CEILING
The purpose of this Statement of Work (SOW) is to establish a single-award contract for
the procurement of commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) tax preparation software and
associated support services. Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) Contract Line-Item Numbers
(CLINs) will be used for the acquisition of software licenses and related services, as
required by volunteer sites.
This acquisition will be conducted in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation 
(FAR) Part 15, Contracting by Negotiation. 
This contract does not obligate any funds at the time of award. Funds will be obligated 
through the issuance of orders or modifications in accordance with applicable funding 
procedures. The Government does not guarantee that the total quantity of supplies or 
services ordered will equal the maximum contract ceiling. 
The contractor is guaranteed a minimum order of 8,500 software licenses during the 
base period and, if exercised, during each of the four (4) option periods. 
The maximum contract ceiling amount the Government may award under this contract 
is (To Be Completed at Time of Award). 
2. PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE
The base ordering period is a 12-month base period, with four (4)
consecutive 12-month option ordering periods as stated below:
• Base Period: August 17, 2026 – August 16, 2027
• Option Period 1: August 17, 2027 – August 16, 2028
• Option Period 2: August 17, 2028 – August 16, 2029
• Option Period 3: August 17, 2029 – August 16, 2030
• Option Period 4: August 17, 2030 – August 16, 2031
Transition-in activities are required for the first (90) days of contract performance. 
During the initial contract period, transition activities such as knowledge 
transfer, system setup, data migration, help desk stand-up, training 
material development, live web-based training sessions, and system testing 
and acceptance, will be started in August 2026. 
In option years, training material development and live web-based training 
will be started in August and be completed before January each year. 
Software shall operate at its full capacity by the beginning of the 2027 
filing season (Tax Year 2026). 
Software licenses are valid one year of each contract period.

3. PLACE OF PERFORMANCE
The place of performance will primarily be the Contractor’s site. Ta
sk orders may be
issued for performance to be at VITA sites, TCE site, Internal Revenue Service (IRS)
facilities, or Treasury facilities. The specific place of performance shall be identified in
the award.
4. ORDERING PROCEDURES
A Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) single-award contract will be awarded to the Contractor based
on the pricing submitted for each deliverable under the applicable Contract Line-Item
Numbers (CLINs). The Contractor shall provide software licenses and associated
support services in accordance with the requirements set forth in this contract.
Performance shall be authorized through the contract award and any subsequent 
contract modifications, as applicable. Work shall be performed upon direction of the 
Contracting Officer, based on requirements identified by the Contracting Officer’s 
Representative (COR) or Program Office and supported by a valid, fully funded 
requisition. 
5. SHIP TO LOCATIONS
Unless otherwise specified, all deliverables/ work products shall be provided to the IRS
COR and shipping to approximately 12,000 domestic and 70 international shipping
addresses which could include multiple deployments.
6. DELIVERABLES
Unless otherwise requested in writing by the COR, work products shall be produced
using Microsoft Office 2010 or later Professional products and delivered in accordance
with the deliverable schedule under Attachment 2. If it is required that deliverable(s) be
submitted in media storage form, all devices must be scanned and certified as virus
free.
7. RAMP-UP PERIOD
Work under this statement of work may require a ramp-up period at the initial start of
this contract. Under the Ramp-up Period the Contractor will recruit and hire personnel
specifically for this contract.
Note: Refer to 4.6 TASK 6 in the SOW: RAMP-UP KNOWLEDGE TRANSFER-IN.
8. ORDER ADMINISTRATIVE DATA

season, normal help desk hours are required Mon-Fri: 8 AM ET – 5 PM ET. In the case

8.3 Personnel Removal and Replacement 
The applicable contractor employees are subject to investigation by the government. 
Applicable contractor employees who undergo contractor clearances that reveal, but are

felony, a crime of violence or a serious misdemeanor, a record of arrests for continuing

to determine if a contractor employee assigned to a task shall continue with the task. 
The contractor shall agree to remove the person assigned within one day of official 
notification by the government and provide a replacement within five days. New hires or 
substitutions of personnel are subject to the contractor clearance requirement.  
8.4 Deliverables/ Work Products 
All contractor deliverables or work products shall remain categorized as "Official Use 
Only.” The release of any portion must be authorized in writing by the government. 
The contractor shall adhere to Section 508 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, which 
requires access to the Federal Government electronic and information technology. The 
law applies to all Federal agencies when they develop, procure, maintain, or use 
electronic and information technology. Federal agencies must ensure that this 
technology is accessible to employees and members of the public with disabilities. 
http://www.section508.gov/. 
Each Electronic and Information technology product or service furnished under this 
statement of work shall comply with the Electronic and Information Technology (EIT) 
Accessibility Standards (29 U.S.C. 87794(d)).  
For every EIT product or service accepted under this contract by the Government that

Government, make every effort to replace or upgrade it with a compliant equivalent

The contractor will be working with sensitive taxpayer data under this contract and must

SECTION II-STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW) 
1. Background:
The Stakeholder Partnerships, Education and Communication (SPEC) organization within
Customer Assistance, Relationships and Education (CARE), provides free elec
tronic tax
preparation for taxpayers who are generally low-income, elderly, disabled or have limited
English proficiency. This service is provided nationwide in approximately 12,000 volunteer
sites. Most of the return preparation is performed by certified volunteers.
Over each of the last three years, approximately 3.6 million Federal returns and 2.7 million state 
returns were processed at these sites by over 96,000 volunteers, partners and employees. 
Generally, sites operate from January (beginning of e-file) through April 15. Some sites remain 
open year around. 
1.1 Volunteer Income Tax Assistance (VITA): 
SPEC partners with Community Based Coalitions, Non-profit Organizations, and local City and 
State Governmental Agencies to provide free tax preparation services. These agencies support 
the Volunteer Income Tax Assistance (VITA) program. VITA partners and volunteers prepare 
basic tax returns for low-income taxpayers, who are U.S. citizens, residents and non-resident 
aliens. All tax preparation is performed by a certified volunteer with the taxpayer present or by a 
taxpayer with the assistance of a certified volunteer. These returns generally include income 
from wages. 
VITA sites are located at neighborhood community centers, libraries, churches, shopping malls 
and other locations that are convenient to the taxpayer, including a supplemental program for 
taxpayers living abroad or near U.S. embassies overseas. Internet accessibility is to be 
determined by location. 
SPEC also partners with the Armed Forces Tax Council to provide free return preparation for 
active and retired military personnel at military bases and ships across the nation and 
internationally. These returns can be more complex and include a wide- variety of forms and 
schedules. These sites have Internet access but operate in a secure environment which tends to 
impede communication speeds. 
1.2 Tax Counseling for the Elderly (TCE): 
Tax Counseling for the Elderly (TCE) offers tax assistance services similar to those provided 
by VITA, as well as free tax counseling for elderly taxpayers, who are restricted to retirement 
homes, neighborhood sites, or private care homes. These returns are generally more complex 
than those prepared through VITA and may include income from pensions, annuities, and 
social security benefits. 
2. Objectives:
The objectives of this single award contract are the following:
• provide secure, commercial off the shelf (COTS) Tax Preparation Software supporting
VITA/TCE operations

• provide reliable user support and training to ensure successful filing season operations
• deliver timely and accurate reporting to support IRS program oversight

reporting, and system capabilities necessary to support IRS VITA and TCE programs across
approximately 12,000 sites globally.

expect the contractor to expend significant resources in preparation for this briefing. Rather, the 
intent of the briefing is to initiate the communication process between the Government and 
Contractor by introducing key participants, explaining their roles, reviewing communication 
ground rules, and assuring a common understanding of the requirements and objectives.

PERSONAL PROPERTY ACTIVITY 
1 SOLDIER WAY 
SCOTT AIR FORCE BASE, ILLINOIS 62225-5357 
 
 
24 April 2026 
 
SUBJECT: Personal Property Activity Information Technology Software Solutions Industry Day 
Synopsis and Registration 
 
1. Purpose.  The Personal Property Activity (PPA) is hosting a focused Industry Day to engage 
with commercial partners regarding Information Technology (IT) software solutions to 
modernize and increase the efficiency of processing military household goods moves.  The 
primary objectives of this event are: 
 
a. To conduct market research on available commercial software capabilities that support all 
aspects of IT software solutions specifically related to military household goods relocation 
services.  
i. Software solutions include full platforms or IT software capabilities, 
capable of integrating with a government owned system.  
 
ii. Specific items of interest include In Transit Visibility, counseling services, 
claims processing and adjudication, and mobile applications. 
 
b. To provide an equal and fair opportunity for registered participants to engage with a cross 
functional team of PPA subject matter experts regarding military household goods related IT 
software solutions.  
 
c. To conduct interactive demonstrations of relevant IT software solutions via individual 
meetings between the PPA cross functional team and individual registered attendees.   
 
d. To provide an equal and fair opportunity for registered participants to provide a written 
response of military household goods related IT software solutions, following the guidance 
below.  
 
2.  Event Details.  Interested attendees must register with the Contracting Officer according to 
the Registration Deadline and Instructions (see Section 3 below).  The PPA will NOT allow 
registration after the registration window closes.  After registration closes, all registered 
participants will receive the event time, date, and schedule of the industry day.  Registered 
participants can withdraw from attendance if circumstances prevent attendance.  On the day of 
the event, the PPA will provide an overview of the event details along with detailed instructions 
for demonstrations.  
 
     a.  Written Responses:  All registered participants are welcome to submit an IT software 
solution overview, which highlights the company’s IT capabilities related to the military 
household good relocation services.  Written submissions must be no more than 10 pages with 11 
point font and provided to the Contracting Officer.  
 

2 
     b.  Demonstrations:  All registered participants may request the opportunity to demonstrate 
their military household goods related IT software solution to the PPA.  Participants must request 
to conduct a demonstration in their registration submission.  All demonstrations will be subject 
to a strict time limit based on the number of demonstrations requested.  The PPA will share the 
time limit and schedule with attendees after registration closes.  
 
3.  Registration Deadlines and Instructions.  All participants must register to participate in 
this industry day.  Interested parties must submit their registration via email, within the 
registration window for attendance.  
 
• Registration Window:  April 24, 2026 through May 8, 2026 
• Registration Email:  christopher.t.frost4.civ@mail.mil  
• Required Information: 
o Company name, attendee names and titles 
o Contact information for each attendee 
o A brief capability statement highlighting relevant IT software solutions. 
o If you request to demonstrate your IT software solution capability to the PPA. 
 
4.  Disclaimer. 
 
     a.  This notice is issued solely for information and planning purposes and does not constitute a 
Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFP in the future.  
 
     b.  The Government will not pay for any information received or for any costs incurred by 
attendees participating in this Industry Day.  
 
     c.  The Government reserves the right to adjust the event details (to include cancellation) as 
necessary.  
 
 
 
CHRISTOPHER FROST 
Contracting Officer

PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT (PWS)

FOR

Nutanix IT Equipment Maintenance & Support

PART I: GENERAL INFORMATION

1.0  General: This is a non-personal services contract to provide maintenance & support for the Nutanix IT equipment located at the located at the Corpus Christi Army Depot (CCAD), Corpus Christi, Texas.  The Government will not exercise any supervision or control over the contract service providers performing the services herein.  Such contract service providers shall be accountable solely to the Contractor who, in turn is responsible to the Government.

Description of Services: The contractor shall furnish all labor, tools, material, equipment, and supervision necessary to perform the IT equipment maintenance and support accordance with the performance work statement (PWS).    

1.2  Background This procurement is for maintenance and support for the depot’s Nutanix IT equipment, utilized for the purpose of providing maintenance, troubleshooting, repairs, replacement parts and telephone support.

1.3.Scope: The Contractor shall provide comprehensive maintenance and support on all depot owned Nutanix IT equipment.  Support includes telephone/remote support, technical support, designated response times, hardware support and software support.

1.4  Objectives: The purpose of this Performance Work Statement (PWS) is to list the requirements and response times, including equipment to be covered, which will be identified on a separate equipment list with serial numbers provided.  Specific response times are in section 5 of this PWS.

1.5  General Information:

1.5.1 Quality Control Plan (QCP):  The Contractor’s existing quality assurance system shall be utilized in accordance with FAR 12.208.

1.5.2  Quality Assurance (QA): The Government will evaluate the contractor's performance under this contract in accordance with the requirements as defined in this PWS.  This quality requirement is focused on what the Contractor must do to ensure that the maintenance and support services are completed within the required time frame and within the standards as set forth in the contract.

1.5.3  Recognized Holidays. The following are recognized US holidays. The Contractor shall ensure the necessary support is available on these days if required:

	New Year’s Day				Labor Day

	Martin Luther King Jr.’s Birthday		Columbus Day

	President’s Day				Veteran’s Day

	Memorial Day				Thanksgiving Day

	Independence Day			Christmas Day

	Juneteenth

1.8  Post Award Conference/Periodic Progress Meetings:  The Contractor shall attend any post award conference convened by the contracting activity or contract administration office in accordance with FAR Subpart 42.5. The Contracting Officer, COR, and other Government personnel, as appropriate, may meet periodically with the Contractor to review the Contractor's performance. At these meetings the Contracting Officer will apprise the Contractor of how the Government views the Contractor's performance and the Contractor shall apprise the Government of problems, if any, being experienced. Appropriate action shall be taken to resolve outstanding issues. These meetings shall be at no additional cost to the Government.

1.8.1  The Contractor shall attend, participate in, and furnish input to scheduled and unscheduled meetings, conferences, and briefings that relate to the functions and services herein as required by the Government to provide effective communication and impart necessary information. The Contract Manager or designated representative shall attend meetings as requested by the Government. Meeting attendees shall at times include Contractor managerial, supervisory, and other personnel knowledgeable of the subject matter. Meetings may start or end outside of regular duty hours.

1.9  Contracting Officer’s Representative:  Contracting Officer Representative (COR):   The COR will be identified by a separate letter.  The COR monitors all technical aspects of the contract and assists in contract administration.  A letter of designation is sued to the COR, a copy of which is sent to the Contractor, states the responsibilities and limitations of the COR, especially with regard to changes in cost or price, estimates or changes in delivery dates. The COR is not authorized to change any of the terms and conditions of the resulting order.

1.10  Key Personnel:  The following personnel are considered key personnel by the Government:  Program Manager and Alternate Program Manager.  The Contractor shall provide a Program/Contract Manager who shall be responsible for the performance of the work. The name of this person and an Alternate Program/Contract Manager, who shall act for the Contractor when the Program/Contract Manager is absent, along with a Curriculum Vitae (CV) for each of these individuals, shall be provided in writing to the Contracting Officer no later than 5 days after contract award.

1.11  Identification of Contractor Employees:  All Contractor personnel attending meetings, answering Government telephones, and working in other situations where their Contractor status is not obvious to third parties must identify themselves, to include proper marking of signature blocks in correspondence, to avoid creating an impression in the minds of members of the public that they are Government officials. The Contractor shall ensure that all documents or reports, produced by Contractors are suitably marked as Contractor products or that Contractor participation is appropriately disclosed.

The Contractor shall not divulge or release data or information developed, or obtained under performance of this PWS, except to authorized Government personnel or upon written approval of the Contracting Officer. The Contractor shall not use, disclose, or reproduce proprietary data, which bears a restrictive legend, other than as specified in this PWS. All documentation showing individual names or other personal information shall be controlled and protected under the provisions of the Privacy Act of 1974, Public Law 93-579, 5 United States Code (U.S.C.) Section 552a.

1.17  Protection of Government and Contract Information: Per Public Use Notice of Limitations stated by Defense imagery Management operations Center and contained at  www.dimoc.mil/resources/limitations/, the Contractor shall not cite any information (e.g., contract information, pictures, locations, etc.) obtained through this contract on any hard copy or digital marketing tools to include its company website.

1.18  Non-Disclosure Statements:  The Contractor shall provide signed non-disclosure agreements to the Government no later than ten (10) business days prior to commencement of work under the contract. Disclosure of information by Contractor personnel may result in removal of Contractor personnel from performance under this contract.

1.21   Safety: The following provides information pertaining to Safety and Accident Prevention:

1.21.1 The Contractor shall conduct all work in a safe manner and in compliance with Federal, State, Local, Department of Defense, Army, and Depot regulations and national consensus standards.

1.21.2 The Contractor will provide a Site-Specific Safety and Occupational Health Accident Prevention Plan (APP) and Activity Hazard Analysis (AHA).

1.21.2.1 Site-Specific Safety and Occupation Health Accident Prevention Plan (APP).  The Contractor will develop, promulgate, and enforce a written site-specific safety and occupational health accident prevention plan (Herein referred to as safety plan).  The safety plan shall identify protocols and procedures to ensure a safe and healthy workplace.  The safety plan will be reviewed and deemed acceptable by the COR before beginning any on-site activities.

1.21.2.2 Activity Hazard Analysis (AHA).  The Contractor will identify in sequence the activities being performed, the specific anticipated hazard, equipment, materials, and the control measures to implemented to eliminate or minimize each hazard to an acceptable level of risk. The contractor will use the more stringent standard when standards are different. The names of the competent and qualified person required for a particular activity (e.g., excavation, scaffolding, fall protection, or other activities as specified by OSHA) shall be identified and included in the activity hazard analysis, as well as proof of their competency and qualification. The analysis will be reviewed and deemed acceptable by the COR before beginning any on-site activities.  

1.21.3 Service Condition.  No part of the services covered by the McNamara-O’Hara Service Contract Act of 1965 will be performed in buildings or surroundings or under working conditions, provided by or under the control or supervision of the Contractor or any Subcontractor, which are unsanitary or hazardous or dangerous to the health or safety of service employees engaged to furnish the services.1.23  Required Training:  The following provides information on training requirements.

This training shall be completed within ten (10) calendar days after the contract is awarded and prior to work commencement, with the results reported to the COR within five (5) business days after the contract is awarded and within ten (10) calendar days after new employees commence contract performance. PART 2: DEFINITIONS & ACRONYMS

2.0  DEFINITIONS AND  ACRONYMS:

2.1  Definitions:  Although not inclusive of every term used within this PWS, the following provides a list of definitions used throughout this PWS and commonly used in the acquisition field.

CONTRACTOR. A supplier or vendor awarded a contract to provide specific supplies to the Government. The term used in this contract refers to the prime.

CONTRACTING OFFICER (KO). A person with authority to enter into, administer, and/or terminate contracts, and make related determinations and findings on behalf of the Government. Note: The only individual who can legally bind the Government.

CONTRACTING OFFICER'S REPRESENTATIVE (COR). As defined in DFARS 202.101, means an individual designated and authorized in writing by the Contracting Officer to perform specific technical or administrative functions. DoD Instruction (DoDI) 5000.72, Part II Definitions states the following when defining a COR: “Defined in subpart 202.101 of Reference (f). Any individual delegated responsibilities pursuant to subpart 1.602-2 of Reference (e), regardless of local terminology, must be certified in accordance with this instruction. For example, local terminology can be COR, Contracting Officer’s technical representative, technical point of contact, technical representative, alternate COR, administrative COR, assistant COR, line item manager, task order manager, quality assurance personnel, quality assurance evaluator, or COR management.” In addition, Army Regulation 70-13, Chapter 2, paragraph 2-2g, states, in part, the following when providing other surveillance support personnel to assist the COR when needed, “…These other surveillance support personnel may serve as on-site representatives of the COR in performance of actual contract surveillance if they meet all COR requirements and have been appointed by the Contracting Officer as alternate CORs.”

DELIVERABLE. Anything that can be physically delivered and includes non-manufactured items such as meeting minutes or reports.

PHYSICAL SECURITY.  means that part of security concerned with physical measures designed to safeguard personnel; to prevent unauthorized access to equipment, installations, material, and documents; and to safeguard against espionage, sabotage, damage, and theft.

QUALITY ASSURANCE. The Government procedures to verify that products being provided by the Contractor meet acceptable standards.

QUALITY CONTROL. All necessary measures taken by the Contractor to assure that the quality of an end product shall meet contract requirements.

SUBCONTRACTOR. One that enters into a contract with a prime contractor. The Government does not have privity of contract with the subcontractor.

WORKDAY.  The number of hours per day the Contractor provides support in accordance with the contract.

WORK WEEK.  Monday through Friday , unless specified otherwise.

Lenel HSPD-1 2 / FIPS 201 -3 Compliant Physical Access Control System Upgrade 
INTRODUCTION 
The mission of the Indian Health Service (IHS) is to raise the physical, mental, social, and 
spiritual health of American Indians and Alaska Natives to the highest level. As part of this 
mission, the IHS is committed to ensuring the safety and security of its patients, staff, and 
facilities while providing high-quality healthcare services across its regions. 
To support this mission, the purpose of this contract is to upgrade existing Homeland 
Security Presidential Directive 1 2 (HSPD-1 2) compliant Physical Access Control Systems 
(PACS) in Indian Health Service facilities located throughout the Great Plains Area. These 
upgrades will enhance the protection of federal facilities, patients, staff, and property 
through compliance with HSPD-1 2, Federal Information Processing Standard (FIPS) 201 -3 
, and all applicable federal security and privacy regulations. 
The implementation of these system upgrades will ensure standardized, secure, and 
efficient access control for all IHS facilities, promote accountability, and safeguard critical 
federal healthcare infrastructure. By modernizing physical security technologies and 
eliminating obsolete PAM modules, the IHS will continue to uphold its mission of providing 
safe and secure environments where quality healthcare can be delivered to the Native 
communities it serves. 
OBJECTIVES 
o Ensure compliance with HSPD-1 2 and FIPS 201 -3 requirements 
o Replace outdated Lenel hardware with current-generation controllers 
o Modernize PIV reader infrastructure with HID Signo readers 
o Enable direct Federal Bridge connectivity through Lenel PIV licenses 
o Eliminate dependency on Physical Access Modules (PAM) 
o Maintain fully functional access control systems throughout the upgrade 
process 
SCOPE OF WORK 
The Contractor shall perform the following work across ﬁfteen (15 ) designated IHS 
facilities in the Great Plains Area: 
• Hardware Replacement 
• Lenel Controller Upgrades  
 

o Replace existing Lenel 4420 controllers with Lenel X4420 controllers (20 total 
units) 
o Replace existing Lenel 1 320-S 1 and 1 320-S 2 controllers with Lenel 1 320-S 
3 controllers (3 6 total units) 
HID Reader Replacement  
o Remove all existing HID PIV readers 
o Install new HID Signo PIV readers with Card + PIN and Prox antenna, OSDP 
and Bluetooth enabled (1 34 total readers) 
Software Licensing 
o Provide and install Lenel PIV authentication licenses (LNL-SWG-AUTH-002) 
for all installed readers (1 34 licenses total, enabling 268 authenticating 
readers) 
o Conﬁgure PIV licenses to enable direct Federal Bridge connectivity 
o Eliminate the need for separate Physical Access Modules (PAM) 
Installation Requirements 
The Contractor Shall 
o Provide all cabling, conduit, junction boxes, and associated materials 
required for installations 
o Install cabling in accordance with IHS Cabling standards and Levington 
certiﬁcation standards 
o Label all cables at both ends with permanent, clearly legible labels 
o Perform all work in a professional and workmanlike manner 
o Protect government property and repair any damage caused by installation 
activities 
o Coordinate work schedules with facility personnel to minimize operational 
disruptions 
o Ensure emergency access procedures remain functional at all times 
Conﬁguration and Testing

o Conﬁgure all new hardware within the existing Lenel OnGuard system 
o Migrate existing cardholder data and access permissions to new controllers 
o Test PIV card authentication at each reader location 
o Verify certiﬁcate chain validation through Federal Bridge

Request for Information (RFI): National Guard Bureau (NGB) Enterprise Data and 
Artificial (AI) Program 
 
1. General Information 
 
Issuing Agency: National Guard Bureau 
 
Purpose: 
This RFI is issued for market research purposes to inform the development of an NGB 
Enterprise Data and AI Program. The intent is to identify industry capabilities, innovative 
approaches, and potential solution architectures that can enable NGB to establish an 
enterprise-wide data environment and AI-enabled decision advantage. 
 
This RFI is not a solicitation for proposals and does not obligate the Government to 
issue a future procurement. Information received will be used to shape requirements, 
refine acquisition strategy, and assess the feasibility of available technologies and 
implementation approaches. 
 
NAICS Code: 518210 (Data Processing, Hosting, and Related Services) – Please 
suggest an alternative NAICS if you identify a more appropriate one. 
 
Product Service Code (PSC):  
D399 (IT and Telecom – Other IT and Telecommunications) 
D302 (Systems Development) 
D308 (Programming) 
D307 (IT Strategy and Architecture) 
D310 (Cybersecurity and Data Protection) 
Please suggest an alternative PSC if you identify a more appropriate one. 
 
2. Classification 
The capability must support both unclassified and classified data environments, Impact 
Levels 2-6 (Public up to SECRET). The solution is expected to operate within or 
integrate with a FedRAMP High-authorized cloud service provider and align with DoD-
approved cloud environments where applicable. 
 
The architecture must implement Zero Trust principles in accordance with Department 
of War and National Guard Bureau policies. This includes end-to-end encryption, strong 
identity and access management, continuous monitoring, and the ability to maintain a 
comprehensive and immutable audit trail of all data access, movement, and 
modification. 
 
Solutions must account for cross-domain considerations and enable secure data 
sharing across classification and impact levels where mission requirements dictate, in 
compliance with applicable security controls and policies. 

 
 
3. Description of Requirement 
The National Guard Bureau is seeking information on capabilities to design, develop, 
and implement a modern NGB Enterprise Data and AI Program that enables the 
organization to operate as a data-driven force. 
 
The objective is to establish a scalable, interoperable, and secure data ecosystem that 
integrates disparate data sources across the Army National Guard, Air National Guard, 
NGB Joint Staff, and the 54 states, territories, and the District of Columbia Joint Force 
Headquarters. 
 
This program is intended to improve situational awareness, enhance decision-making at 
all echelons, reduce redundancy across systems, and enable advanced analytics and 
artificial intelligence capabilities in support of domestic operations, federal missions, and 
Combined Joint All Domain Command and Control (CJADC2). 
 
NGB recognizes that data environments across states and components vary in maturity, 
architecture, and adoption. As such, the enterprise solution must be capable of 
integrating with existing systems while providing a path toward greater standardization, 
interoperability, and reduced operational burden on the states. 
4. Core Capability Areas 
Data Ingestion and Integration 
The solution must support ingestion of structured, semi-structured, and unstructured 
data from multiple sources, including legacy systems, service-level platforms, and state-
managed environments. 
 
Both batch and real-time data ingestion capabilities are required. The architecture 
should support API-based integration, data streaming, and secure data exchange 
mechanisms to enable near real-time data availability. 
 
The solution should accommodate integration with existing DoD and service data 
platforms and enable federation where full centralization is not feasible. 
 
Data Storage and Management 
The platform should provide a scalable, multi-tiered data architecture, such as a 
combination of data lake, data warehouse, and data fabric or mesh approaches where 
appropriate. 
 
Capabilities must include data normalization, transformation, tagging, and 
standardization to enable consistent data use across the enterprise. 
 

The architecture should support metadata management, data cataloging, and 
discoverability to ensure users can identify and access relevant data efficiently. 
 
 
Analytics and AI Enablement 
The solution must provide advanced analytics capabilities, including self-service 
analytics, ad hoc querying, and data visualization. 
 
The platform should enable the development, deployment, and governance of AI and 
machine learning models to support predictive analytics, automation, and decision 
support. 
 
Support for low-code or no-code analytics tools is desired to empower non-technical 
users while maintaining governance and security controls. 
 
Governance and Data Management 
A comprehensive data governance framework is required, including data ownership, 
stewardship, quality management, and lifecycle management. 
 
The solution should provide capabilities for data lineage tracking, ensuring traceability of 
data from source to consumption. 
 
Data quality tools should enable validation, monitoring, and remediation to maintain 
trust in enterprise data assets. 
 
Security and Zero Trust Architecture 
The solution must be designed with Zero Trust principles, enforcing continuous 
verification of users, devices, and data access requests. 
 
Capabilities must include robust identity, credential, and access management, role-
based and attribute-based access controls, and enforcement of least privilege. 
 
Micro-segmentation and data-level security controls should be implemented to protect 
sensitive information and limit lateral movement within the environment. 
 
Continuous monitoring, threat detection, and automated response capabilities are 
required to protect data and ensure compliance with DoD cybersecurity requirements. 
5. Strategic Considerations 
The NGB Enterprise Data and AI Program must account for the distributed nature of the 
National Guard and the need to balance enterprise capabilities with state-level flexibility. 
 
Solutions should reduce duplication of effort, minimize cost burdens on states, and 
enable shared services where appropriate. 
 

Interoperability is a key requirement. The solution must enable seamless data exchange 
across components, services, and mission partners while maintaining security and 
compliance. 
 
The program should provide a foundation for future AI capabilities, automation 
initiatives, and advanced decision support tools aligned with DoD digital modernization 
priorities. 
6. Industry Engagement Objectives 
Through this RFI, NGB seeks to understand: 
 
1. Available technologies and platforms that can support a federated yet 
interoperable enterprise data environment 
 
2. Approaches to integrating disparate data sources across multiple organizations 
with varying levels of maturity 
 
3. Best practices for implementing Zero Trust within enterprise data platforms 
 
4. Strategies for enabling AI and advanced analytics at scale within a secure 
environment 
 
5. Recommended implementation approaches, including phased delivery, pilot 
efforts, and scaling strategies 
 
6. Potential risks, challenges, and mitigation strategies associated with deploying 
an NGB Enterprise Data and AI Program within a complex, distributed 
organization 
 
Please provide your response – to include information and/or questions – via email to 
Jeannie Botteri, jeannie.m.botteri.civ@army.mil and LaKia Johnson, 
lakia.l.johnson.ctr@army.mil.
