Library of Congress

United States Copyright Office (USCO) Index Data

2026-COP-0018

OVERVIEW / BACKGROUND 

Index Data LLC custom built, developed and successfully implemented two software applications, eCO Receipts Public Interface and AD MetaSearch and a custom Z39.50 gateway to access the underlying Oracle Siebel database for the Library of Congress’ United States Copyright Office in 2009. These applications provide access and search functionality for Library patrons, Copyright staff and LC Recommending Officers to Copyright bibliographic data.  

The MasterKey platform, which is the underlying tool in the Metasearch software, was in production in Library Services as a federated search capability serving staff and meeting the needs of the general public searching Library databases.  

SCOPE

The contractor shall provide ongoing support for Copyright’s maintenance of its

customized software installation of two applications and one gateway: eCO Receipts Public Interface and Masterkey Metasearch Federated Search and the Z39.50 gateway.

REQUIREMENTS

The contractor shall provide maintenance that includes the following:

•	Review and analysis of defects reported, and changes required, scope and level of effort 	

•  Modify existing software to correct bug errors.

• Provide answers to specific technical how-to questions/concerns and bug fixes. 

Update the interface to add new database targets as needed

The core application was developed by Index Data for searching Library bibliographic and Copyright registration data through a customized materialized view Oracle database, The search user interface can be used for multiple search targets. The main searching is done by the Pazpar2 engine that was created and developed by Index Data. The following are tools and software that were used to develop and maintain these core applications: 

zSQLgate program 

Z39.50 SRU and SRW

Pazpar2 (Metasearch Engine)

YAZ Toolkit

C/C++

Perl

HTML/JavaScript

XML

SCHEDULE OF EVENTS/DELIVERABLES 

SERVICE LEVEL AGREEMENTS

Support under this contract covers answers to specific technical how-to questions/concerns with bug fixes only. Note: It does not cover extended instruction beyond 15 minutes on how to use the software or perform various administrator functions, analytical help determining the best way to use the software, or enhancements or configuration changes that are considered new functionality.

Support hours are from 8:30 AM – 5:00 PM EST Monday – Friday (excluding Federal holidays)

Response Time – within 24 business hours

Resolve Time – Software maintenance as a product includes the publishing of bug/defect fixes that could be routine or emergency types via patches and updates/upgrades in function and technology to maintain the operability and usability of the software product. Furthermore, the contractor shall provide the greatest amount of lead time as reasonable to minimize the impact to usability and accessibility of the systems. 

The number of Library Technical Points of Contact (POC) shall not exceed three (3) LOC staff. 

 TESTING AND QUALITY ASSURANCE

Quality assurance will be achieved through establishing and agreeing upon scope for each bug deliverable, adhering to LOC SDLC complying with internal contractor review and stakeholder, USCCO, and COR review.     

KEY PERSONNEL

All technical staff assigned to this effort shall be considered key personnel.  In the event of key personnel reassignment, removal, or resignation, the Contractor shall provide written notification at least 30 calendar days in advance to the designated CO and COR.  This notification, at a minimum, shall include a justification statement (including proposed replacements/substitutions) in sufficient detail to permit evaluation of the impact of the proposed change on the program and its schedule.  The Contractor shall make no replacement of key personnel without prior written consent by the CO. The list of personnel (specified in an attachment to the Schedule of this contract) may, with the consent of both parties to this contract, be amended from time to time during the course of the contract to add or delete personnel, as appropriate.

	The Contractor shall identify individuals who will support the agreement. The contractor shall notify the COR one week prior to non-availability. Contractor’s away-time should not negatively impact the timely completion of a bug fix especially in the event of an emergency fix. 

	To simplify communication, all contact related to the Agreement between Index Data and the Customer must be facilitated by the COR.

NUMBER 8955.6 
1 October 2019 
Administrative Update 1, 13 May 2020 
 
CIO-T 
 
SUBJECT: NGA Web Property Standards and Guidelines 
 
References: See Enclosure 1.  
 
1. PURPOSE. This Instruction: 
 
a. Establishes policy, assigns responsibilities, and designates authorities for NGA 
web property standards and guidelines on enterprise domains in accordance with (IAW) 
Reference (d). 
 
b. Rescinds NGA Instruction (NI) 8955.5, “NGA Instruction for Preparing NGA Web 
Pages,” 23 May 2009. 
 
2. APPLICABILITY. This Instruction applies to all NGA civilian employees, military 
service members, other Government agency personnel assigned to NGA, and 
contractors, hereinafter referred to as personnel. 
 
3. DEFINITIONS. See Glossary. 
 
4. POLICY. It is NGA policy to: 
 
a. Establish web property standards and guidelines to manage compliance, style, 
and content for NGA web properties on enterprise domains. 
 
b. Disseminate information electronically on multiple security domains IAW relevant 
US Government laws and policies, DoD policies, IC policies, and NGA policies.   
 
c. Establish uniform style and mandatory content elements for NGA web properties 
on enterprise domains IAW Reference (d). 
 
5. RESPONSIBILITIES. See Enclosure 2.

6. EFFECTIVE DATE. This Instruction is effective on the date of signature.

(b) Office of Management and Budget (OMB) Memorandum M-11-15, “Final Guidance

(c) OMB Memorandum M-15-13, “Policy to Require Secure Connections across 
Federal Websites and Web Services,” 08 June 2015 
(d) OMB Memorandum M-17-06, “Policies for Federal Agency Public Websites and

(e) Electronic Code of Federal Regulations, Title 36, Chapter XII, Subchapter B, §

(f) Title 17, United States Code (USC), “Copyrights,” 30 June 2017 
(g) Committee on National Security Systems Instruction No. 4009, “Committee on

(i) ICD 710, “Classification Management and Control Markings System,” 21 June 2013 
(j) Department of Defense Instruction (DoDI) 5025.13, “DoD Plain Language 
Program,” 11 April 2013, Incorporating Change 4, 31 May 2018 23 January 2020 
(k) DoDI 8520.02, “Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) and Public Key (PK) Enabling,” 
24 May 2011 
(l) NGA Directive (NGAD) 8000, “Information Management and the Chief Information 
Officer,” 12 June 2013, Administrative Update 2, 28 October 2015 
(m) NGA Instruction (NGAI) 5500.7, “Handling of Personally Identifiable Information,” 
15 February 2013 5401.1, “Privacy and Civil Liberties Program,” 26 January 2020 
(n) NGAI 5720.1, “Clearance for Public Release,” 12 May 2015 
(o) NGAI 8040.2, Volume 1, “Records and Information Lifecycle Management: Records 
Management Program,” 30 March 2016 
(p) NGAI 8220.1, “Identity Authentication and Authorization,” 11 April 2018 
(q) NGAI 8400.4, “Implementation of Electronic and Information Technology 
Accessibility/Section 508 Program,” 05 July 2017, Admin Update 1, 24 January

ENCLOSURE 2 
 
RESPONSIBILITIES 
 
1. Chief Information Officer (CIO). 
 
a. Establishes and oversees web standards for enterprise domains including 
administration, security, and sustainment of web infrastructure, services, tools, and 
Domain Name Service (DNS) directory development IAW Reference (l). 
 
b. Designates the Director, CIO and Information Technology Services (D/CIO-T), as 
the authority to manage the enterprise domain web property framework. 
 
2. D/CIO-T. 
 
a. Manages web properties residing on the enterprise domains. 
 
b. Assigns Director, Future Experience Office (D/TF), to develop NGA web property 
standards and guidelines for enterprise domains. 
 
3. D/TF. 
 
a. Establishes, assigns, and maintains DNS guidelines and standards. 
 
b. Maintains NGA web style guidance to ensure a consistent user experience across 
enterprise domains. 
 
c. Reviews, assumes control of, and removes NGA web properties that are not 
compliant with the standards and guidelines of this Instruction. 
 
d. Promotes usage of best practices to mitigate privacy risks and effectively protect 
personally identifiable information (PII) collected, stored, or transmitted on NGA web 
properties. (Reference (m)) 
 
e. Maintains the NGA Web Guidance and Resources website (hereinafter referred to 
as the Online Resources), located at https://www.intranet.nga.ic.gov/web/. 
 
4. Director, Office of Corporate Communications. 
 
a. Manages the review of all NGA products and information that are publicly 
released (where applicable), all external marketing (e.g., social media, correspondence 
with the press, and promotional products), and all writing for public release for 
adherence to NGA messaging standards on public-facing web properties available over 
the World Wide Web IAW Reference (n). 
 
b. Ensures that information released to the public is unclassified IAW Reference (n). 

UNCLASSIFIED 
 
NGAI 8955.6 
7 
 
UNCLASSIFIED 
 
c. Coordinates and interacts with media and external sources regarding NGA web 
properties IAW Reference (n). 
 
5. Senior Component Official for Privacy collaborates with the D/CIO-T Chief 
Information Officer to ensure that protections and disclaimers are in place for web 
properties that collect, store, or transmit PII IAW Reference (m). 
 
6. Information Developers and Designers. 
 
a. Comply with web standards and guidance provided in the Online Resources when 
developing, modifying, and maintaining NGA web properties on enterprise domains. 
 
b. Comply with all header and footer guidance provided at the Online Resources, 
Content Delivery Network for all NGA web properties. 
 
c. Format and publish NGA web properties that enable all users to retrieve and use 
information, including Section 508 compliance, IAW References (d), (l), and (q). 
  

UNCLASSIFIED 
 
NGAI 8955.6 
8 
 
UNCLASSIFIED 
ENCLOSURE 3 
 
NGA WEB PROPERTIES GUIDANCE 
 
1. Workflow processes for requesting and developing NGA web properties are provided 
in the Web Governance Concept of Operations (CONOPS), the relevant Standard 
Operating Procedures (SOPs), and this Instruction.  
 
2. The CONOPS, SOPs, and links to style guides, design elements, and best practices 
are provided in the Online Resources. 
 
3. Web Design Style Guidance. 
 
a. NGA web properties meet and maintain high standards of effectiveness and 
usability to provide quality information that is readily discoverable and accessible to 
authorized users. (References (d) and (q)) 
 
b. The UXD Web Style Guide is a resource to help developers and software 
engineers overcome common design problems when creating a new web property. A 
core function of the Online Resources is to provide assistance in the creation of a more 
consistent “look and feel” across NGA web properties. The Online Resources UXD Web 
Style Guide is located on the following networks: 
 
NGANet/Joint Worldwide Intelligence 
Communications System (JWICS) 
https://www.intranet.nga.ic.gov/web/ 
http://design.nga.ic.gov 
Secret Internet Protocol Router 
Network (SIPRNet) https://design.nga.smil.mil 
Sensitive But Unclassified (SBU) https://designsystem.digital.gov/ 
http://design.nga.mil 
 
c. The efficient, effective, and consistent use of NGA web properties and web 
services standards promotes a more citizen-centered Government and user-friendly 
experience. 
 
4. Writing in Plain Language. 
 
a. Plain language and communication have many benefits. Avoiding vagueness and 
unnecessary complexity makes it easier for users to understand information and use 
services. Plain writing assists the user in complying with applicable requirements to 
better understand the NGA web property. (References (b) and (j)) 
 

UNCLASSIFIED 
 
NGAI 8955.6 
9 
 
UNCLASSIFIED 
b. NGA web properties on enterprise domains must conform to the plain writing 
memorandums and referenced materials identified in the content guidance provided in 
the Online Resources. 
 
5. Copyright Protections. 
 
a. Copyright is a form of legal protection grounded in the US Constitution and 
granted by law for original works created in any medium. 
 
b. NGA web properties on enterprise domains must comply with the US Copyright 
laws and referenced materials IAW Reference (f). Copyright guidance is provided in the 
Online Resources. 
 
6. Accessibility Guidance. 
 
a. Accessibility is one of the most important aspects of web development. 
Accessibility allows the greatest number of users to view content more completely. 
Users have a better experience if accessibility is built into web properties from the 
beginning. 
 
b. US Code and Public Laws require Federal Agencies to ensure electronic and 
information technology (EIT) is accessible to people with disabilities. Section 508 of the 
Workforce Investment Act of 1998 applies to all Federal agencies when developing, 
procuring, maintaining, or using EIT. (References (a) and (q)) 
 
c. NGA web properties on enterprise domains comply with Section 508 
requirements. Accessibility guidance and tools are located on networks identified in 
paragraph 3.b. of this Enclosure. 
 
d. For overall questions regarding Section 508 compliance, contact the Section 508 
coordinator at NGASection508Coordinator@coe.ic.gov. (References (a) and (q)) 
 
7. Analytics, Performance Metrics, and Feedback Guidance. 
 
a. Web analytics are the collection, analysis, and communication of web data for 
purposes of understanding and optimizing web usage. Web analytics measure web 
traffic and assess the effectiveness of a web property. The resulting analysis helps the 
organization determine the value of its content or an application, and provides insight to 
improve its offerings and the user experience. 
 
b. NGA web properties on enterprise domains should have a web analytics 
collection capability. (Reference (d)) Web analytic solutions are provided in the Online 
Resources. 
 
8. Security Guidance. 
 

UNCLASSIFIED 
 
NGAI 8955.6 
10 
 
UNCLASSIFIED 
a. NGA web properties provide Government information and services to support the 
performance of NGA’s mission. Security and risk management are essential functions 
incorporated into the lifecycle of NGA web properties, including classification markings, 
public key infrastructure (PKI) certificates, and hypertext transfer protocol secure 
(HTTPS) IAW References (c), (k) and (p). 
 
b. Intelligence sources, methods, and activities are safeguarded IAW Reference (i). 
Additional information for classification marking requirements is provided in the Online 
Resources. 
 
c. Websites, services, and online resources available over the public internet that 
are maintained and operated in whole or in part by NGA are provided through HTTPS. 
(References (c) and (k)) Additional information for HTTPS implementation is provided in 
the Online Resources. 
 
9. Search and Discovery Guidance. 
 
a. Search functions are universal and an expected website feature commonly used 
to find information. Search engine optimization (SEO) is critical to reaching users who 
primarily rely on commercial search engines. 
 
b. NGA web properties on enterprise domains must provide search capabilities IAW 
References (d) and (h). D/TF provides search solutions, how to incorporate a search 
capability into an NGA web property, and how to maximize discovery of web assets via 
SEO and NGA search tools. Additional information is provided in the Online Resources. 
 
 
c. NGA web properties on enterprise domains are published to a registry to assist 
search and discovery of content and services. Search and Discovery Guides are 
available in the Online Resources. 
 
d. NGA web properties on enterprise domains contain metadata tags to assist 
search and discovery. Search and Discovery Guides are located on networks identified 
in paragraph 3.b. within this Enclosure provided in the Online Resources. 
 
10. NGA Dissemination on Domain Networks Guidance. 
 
a. IC computer domain networks disseminate intelligence information. NGA has 
multiple IC domain networks based on classification. Web properties are stored on 
servers that are connected to the domain networks and are reachable using DNS. 
When the DNS is translated into an Internet Protocol (IP) address, an information 
system (IS) can pinpoint the location of another IS/server where the web property is 
stored. 
 
b.

(a) All goods and services shall be subject to inspection and test by the FDIC Oversight Manager, to the extent

(b) The FDIC shall have 15 business days from the date of Contractor''s delivery to determine if such goods and
services are in compliance with the requirements of the contract.  If any services performed or goods delivered
hereunder are not in conformity with the requirements of this Award, the FDIC shall have the right to require
Contractor to reperform the services or redeliver the goods in conformity with the requirements of the Award, at no
additional increase in total contract amount.  When the services to be performed are of such a nature that the defect
cannot be corrected by reperformance of the services, the FDIC shall have the right to (1) require Contractor
immediately to take all necessary steps to ensure future performance of the services in conformity with the
requirements of the contract; and (2) reduce the contract price to reflect the reduced value of the services
performed.  In the event Contractor fails promptly to reperform the services or redeliver the goods, or to take
necessary steps to ensure future performance of the services or delivery of the goods in conformity with the
requirements of the Award, the FDIC shall have the right to either (1) by contract or otherwise, have the services
performed or the goods delivered in conformity with the contract requirements and charge to Contractor any cost
occasioned to the FDIC that is directly related to the performance of such services or the delivery of such goods; or
(2) terminate this Award for default as provided in 7.6.6-02, Termination for Default.
 
(c) Contractor shall provide and maintain an inspection system acceptable to the FDIC covering the goods or
services to be delivered or performed hereunder.  Records of all inspection work by Contractor shall be kept
complete and available to the FDIC during the term of this Award and for such longer period as may be specified
elsewhere in this Award.

1.0  PRODUCT REQUIREMENTS 
The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Veterans Health Administration (VHA), has a 
requirement for brand name Medicopia software licenses and Brand name Zebra 
Printers, and accessories. The Lattice Medicopia software application is used for 
positive patient identification (PPID) during specimen collecting. The Lattice Medicopia 
runs a Microsoft Windows Server 2019 operating system(s) and Microsoft SQL Server 
2019 database on the VA Enterprise network. Medicopia is a software solution provided 
by Lattice / DCS to allow positive patient identification (PPI) at the patient bedside with 
barcode scanning of the wristband before specimen collection. Medicopia is VA TRM 
approved, requires no modifications to VISTA or CPRS, and satisfies the Joint 
commission recommendation for PPID and printing labels at the bedside. A barcode 
scanner is used at the patients' bedside to scan their wristband, ensuring they are the 
correct patient. The mobile printer will only generate the specimen labels after positive 
patient identification. Medicopia can receive and display VISTA/CPRS lab orders and 
provides a method to print specimen labels in the presence of the patient with bar-
coded stickers. Medicopia tracks accurate data regarding collection date/time, collector, 
specimens, etc. Additional workflow assistance and data auditing services are also 
included, for supervisor and hospital informatics use. 
 
The proposed action will require the purchase of 40 Zebra printers, model ZQ610, 40-
each Zebra AC adapter, 40-each USB cables, one each Zebra wi-fi display android 
processor, one each communication cable, one each communication cable, one each 
USB power supply, 40-each ONECARE battery maintenance plan, 40-each POCC 
staging mobile ZQ61, 40-each combination mounting of ZQ610 customer supplied 
antenna bracket and monitor inset adapters. 
 
The Contractor shall provide installation services to perform the following; Zebra printer 
ZQ610 mounted on the Howard Medical Cart which connects to the VA computer via 
USB cable. Lattice Medicopia client software is installed on the VA computer to access 
Medicopia middleware to print specimen labels on the ZD610 Zebra printers.   
 
The Period of Performance shall be one 12-month base period plus four 12-month 
option periods for licenses and maintenance as described above. The delivery of 
hardware shall be within 45 days after receipt and processing of the delivery order.

1.1  SPECIFIC TASKS AND DELIVERABLES  
 
The Contractor shall provide the following: 
 
o HL7 ADT (Admit, Discharge, Transfer) messages. These messages 
are standardized, high-volume electronic messages used to communicate patient 
demographic and visit status changes between hospital information systems 
(HIS), Electronic Medical Records (EMR), and ancillary systems. They act as 
real-time updates ensuring all care systems share consistent data on patient 
movement, location, and registration. The server uses it to connect to VISTA and 
send/translate data back and forth from VISTA and the Zebra printers. If the 
interface goes down, the staff will implement their back-up plan, which they will 
devise, while HTM and OIT work with VISTA teams to bring the interface up. 
o LDAP (Lightweight Directory Access Protocol) in Active Directory (AD) is the 
core, open-standard protocol used to query, read, and modify information stored 
within the Microsoft AD database. While Active Directory is the database itself, 
LDAP acts as the language applications use to authenticate users and locate 
network resources. 
o A Laboratory Information System (LIS) interface is a software connection that 
allows laboratory instruments and computer systems to exchange data 
automatically. It connects the LIS with Electronic Health Records (EHRs), 
Hospital Information Systems (HIS), and analytical instruments, eliminating 
manual data entry, accelerating reporting, and reducing errors. 
o The Contractor shall provide Implementation schedule and provide project 
management to ensure the project is on schedule and all software is functional 
and working, printers are installed and specimen labels are able to be printed in 
the various wards.  
o The Contractor shall hold weekly status meetings from project start through go-
live. 
 
1.2       TRAINING  
 
The contractor shall provide both classroom and on-site training for “super-users’ at the 
facility. Training sessions shall be for up to 16 trainees for one hour in duration. Training 
documentation will be provided electronically. The Contractor shall provide 
comprehensive training plan to include how to operate the equipment, what happens if 
equipment experiences work stoppages, how to print bar code labels and provide 
training materials which may include brochures, website information, manuals and any 
combination of these to ensure an immersive learning experience.

chain, logistics, expendables, assets, inventory, facilities, prosthetics, and 
environmental compliance HELM provides the enterprise capabilities needed to support 
a unified, efficient, and data driven supply chain and logistics environment across VA. 
VA does not currently operate with standardized, enterprise-wide supply chain business 
processes or technical systems. Numerous functional and capability gaps have been 
identified through Government Accountability Office (GAO) and Office of Inspector

strengthening cybersecurity and resilience, improving data quality, enhancing user 
experience for logisticians, and establishing consistent, interoperable processes across 
VHA, VACO, VBA, and NCA. 
 
VA currently relies on approximately 63 disparate legacy systems across 174 sites, 
resulting in fragmented operations, limited enterprise visibility, and inefficiencies. 
Standardization and modernization are required to transform Supply Chain systems into 
integrated, enterprise-wide system of systems that supports responsive, efficient clinical 
and nonclinical supply operations.

Questions & Answers Form
# RFP Reference Page No. Question/Comment NOAA Response
1
Solicitation, Section 
003 Addendum to 
FAR 52.212-2, 
Paragraph (e)(1) 40 & 42
How will objective requirements be evaluated (full credit vs partial 
credit vs binary)?
The Government will employ a Technical Evaluation Team (TET) to evaluate the proposed data 
capabilities, including the ability to exceed the Threshold requirements and meet or exceed 
objective requirements.   TET evaluators will identify related strengths and weaknesses in the 
offer and evalute for the following: 
- Strengths: aspects of the offer that exceed Threshold Requirements, enhance value to the 
Government, or that would increase the likelihood of successful contract performance.  
- Weaknesses: failures to address Threshold Requirements of the technical proposal, aspects 
of the proposal that decrease value to the Government, or aspects of the proposal that 
decrease the likelihood of successful contract performance.
After identifying all applicable strengths and weaknesses, evaluators will assign appropriate 
confidence ratings to Technical Capabilities and Overall Technical Proposal.  The TET will utilize 
confidence ratings to provide evaluators the ability to look holistically at the strengths and 
weaknesses of each offer. 
2
Solicitation, Section 
4, RFP 52.212-1 
(2)(c) and Section 
003 Addendum to 
FAR 52.212-2, 
Paragraph (e)(1) 39 & 42
How will risk be evaluated within the Technical Volume (standalone 
factor or embedded in technical capability)?
TET evaluators will identify and rate specific risks associated with technical capabilities in the 
offer; each TET member will identify risks as part of the overall evaluation and assign risks as 
weaknesses.  Risks will be included in the development of confidence ratings for Technical 
Capabilities and Overall Technical Proposal.
3
Solicitation, Section 
4, RFP 52.212-1 
(2)(b) 39-40
Are appendices (e.g., technical tables, compliance summaries) 
evaluated or excluded from scoring since they are excluded from the 
page count?
Appendices are included in scoring as they are a part of the submitted proposal.  However, 
appendices are intended to be used as reference material for the main proposal; a good guide 
for Offerors is to consider that the proposal should be able to completely respond to the RFP 
requirements in the main body.  The examples of technical tables and compliance summaries 
mentioned are appropriate uses of appendices.
4
Solicitation, Section 
2, SOW Section VI 
Security 
Requirements and 
Section 4, RFP 
52.212-1
12-13 & 
38-39
Are there specific security artifacts expected in the proposal (e.g., 
SSP, POA&M, accreditation approach)?
Please see VI SECURITY REQUIREMENTS for details on security compliance requirements 
expected in the contract.   
5
Solicitation, Section 
2, SOW Section II, 
Table 3 9
How will data latency be evaluated -- Average latency, Maximum 
latency, Percentile thresholds?
Latency will be evaluated along all of these methods.  As this is a Pilot Project, the Government 
is interested in collecting latency data on the piloted datasets during the delivery period and in 
working with vendors to determine latency characteristics, causes, and methods to improve 
system latency in future operational data purchases.
6
Solicitation, Section 
2, SOW Section 
IIIA. Operational 
Delivery 
Requirements 11
How will optional capabilities (e.g., Level 2 products) be evaluated? 
How will additional value-added capabilities be evaluated? Scored 
positively, neutral, or ignored? Please see response to questions 1 and 2.
7
Solicitation, Section 
2, SOW Section II.B 9
How will NOAA weigh the trade-off between higher revisit rates 
(quantity) and superior spectral or spatial resolution (quality) in the 
technical evaluation? Specifically, will data that exceeds the 200m 
spatial resolution threshold be given additional technical merit? Will 
data with more relavent spectral bands be given additional technical 
merit?
Every observational capability involves tradeoffs implemented in order to deliver data with the 
highest utility.  For fire imagery, the Government has indicated its Threshold and Objective 
requirements in the SOW which indicate its understanding of system characteristics that could 
provide high utility.  However, Applicants are invited to explain how their proposed solution 
tradeoffs provide high utility for the needs expressed in the SOW. 
This Solicitation is for a Pilot Project and the Government understands that Applicants may not 
yet have a mature satellite constellation that can provide the revisit rates that their  operational 
constellation will offer.  
8
Solicitation, Section 
2, SOW Section II.B 9
When will the specific coordinates defining the Regions of Interest 
(ROI) be finalized? Will there be a lead time for offerors to optimize 
tasking schedules?
Upon award, the Government will begin working with the Contractor to define ROIs and develop 
an effective tasking schedule.  The Pilot includes a one-month Preparation Phase before Data 
Delivery, which will include time for optimizing tasking schedules.  

9
Solicitation, Section 
2, SOW Section II.B 9
How many Regions of Interest (ROI) are anticipated to be active at 
once? Please refer to II.B. OBSERVATION CAPABILITY AND REQUIREMENTS.
10
Solicitation, Section 
2, SOW Section III, 
Delivery 
Requirements 9
How should the contractor handle Geographic Exclusion Areas that 
may fall within a predefined region of interest?
The Contractor is required to adhere to all GEAs as defined in Government data license 
agreements and security directives. It is noted that the risk of incidental capture of sensitive 
features is significantly mitigated by the coarse spatial resolution of the environmental datasets 
intended for geophysical characterization rather than high-resolution imaging. In the event that a 
GEA overlaps with a scientific Region of Interest, the following protocols may apply and shall be 
reviewed by the COR: Data Masking: The Contractor shall implement automated filtering to 
ensure no prohibited data is processed. Methodological Adjustment: Should a security exclusion 
overlap with a planned validation site, the Contractor shall notify the COR and recommend an 
alternative, non-excluded location that provides similar scientific value for the comparison.
11
Solicitation, Section 
2, SOW Section III, 
Delivery 
Requirements and 
Section VII, Data 
Rights 9 & 13
To meet the latency requirements of this RFP, will NOAA provide the 
necessary authorization to operate or license modifications to allow for 
data delivery faster than current standard NOAA commercial license 
constraints (e.g. NOAA-dictated 24-hour imagery hold)?
License modifications provided by the Office of Space Commerce Commercial Remote Sensing 
Regulatory Affairs (CRSRA) office are beyond the scope of this Solicitation and resulting Pilot. 
NOAA will consider modifications to the data licensing indicated in the SOW which help the Pilot 
exceed Threshold Requirements, enhance value to the Government, or increase the likelihood 
of successful contract performance.

PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT 
21 April 2026 
 
AIRFIELD AUTOMATION SYSTEM (AFAS) SUPPORT 
AIR FORCE FLIGHT STANDARDS AGENCY 
TINKER AFB OKLAHOMA CITY, OKLAHOMA 
 
 
1.0 SCOPE 
 
This task will require the contractor to provide the support necessary to perform support and 
engineering services to accomplish technical software support for the maintenance of the Airfield 
Automation System (AFAS) software system.  
 
1.1 GENERAL 
 
The Air Force Flight Standards Agency (AFFSA)/Airfield Automation Directorate requires Information 
Technology technical support with regards to Airfield Automation System (AFAS), a product of Systems 
Atlanta, Inc (SAI), software suite.   
The system is designed to meet the information needs of air traffic control (ATC) and airfield 
management (AM) personnel, both military and civilian. The AFAS resources in each Radar Approach 
Control (RAPCON) and/or Air Traffic Control Tower (ATCT) are a collection of Commercial Off The Shelf 
(COTS) general purpose systems that provide a centralized repository of information used to provide 
decision support tools, aid in planning purposes and maintain situational awareness for air traffic 
controllers. AFAS provides rapid access to a wide array of information from multiple sources, integrated 
for display and distribution via a single system.  
 
1.2 TASK EXECUTION PLAN 
 
1.2.1 Task 1:  Telephone Support 
 
The contractor shall provide telephone software support (both engineering and product technical 
support) direct to HQ AFFSA AFAS Program Manager and all AFAS customers.  
 
Contractor Help Desk personnel shall diagnose and resolve system and maintenance issues related to 
AFAS software configuration, SAI database building, AFAS network infrastructure, SAI software and 
associated AFAS support tools.   
 
Engineering support shall be provided by the contractor’s engineering staff to resolve AFAS software 
issues including those involving changes in operating system and security changes required for 
continued Air Force network operations. The contractor shall also provide reconfigurations of AFAS 
license files, as necessitated by changes in local network operations.  The contractor shall provide 
original and replacement configuration disks and software documentation, as needed.  
 
Product technical support shall be provided by the contractor’s training staff to resolve issues involving 
utilization of AFAS, using software features, creating and managing the database, configuring profiles, 
organizing data most efficiently for rapid access, and other product use knowledge areas. 

 
 
 
Contractor Help Desk personnel shall receive and log calls, fill out a Customer Service Request (CSR) 
form, and forward the CSR to the appropriate SAI resource for resolution.  Response time to each 
support request that is logged within the hours of support coverage shall be within two hours not to 
exceed twelve hours.  A monthly electronic CSR report identifying problems, date opened/closed and 
solution shall be provided to the AFAS Program Manager as well as notifying AFAS Program Manager by 
email each time a CSR is opened. Contractor format is acceptable.    
 
The contractor shall be available to provide telephone support for 8-continuous hours (eg., 0800-1600, 
0900-1700, Eastern Time), Monday through Friday, except contractor observed holidays. If support 
requires the direct involvement of Air Force personnel at overseas locations, telephone support shall be 
provided on a pre-scheduled basis to cover normal duty hours of the Air Force Location. 
 
1.2.2 Task 2:  Site Configuration/Reconfiguration  
 
AFAS location site configuration and reconfigurations generated as defined below: 
 
• What’s Up Gold (WUG) Remote Maintenance Monitor (RMM) reconfiguration(s) due to 
geographic moves of AFAS equipment 
• Global Naming Table (GNT) changes and updates 
• AFAS Workstation name changes 
• Proxy Server changes 
• DNS Server changes 
• IP Address changes 
 
Configuration changes will not be made until approved by AFAS Program Manager.  Configuration files 
to be delivered to applicable site and AFAS Program Manager.   
 
1.2.3 Task 3:  Engineering Services 
 
The contractor shall provide engineering services for AFAS as identified by AFAS Program Manager. 
These services may include activities such as: 
• Technical Interchange Meetings (TIMs)  
• Catastrophic System Failure that exceed telephone support Technicians 
• IDS data page template designs 
• Remediation of system deficiencies of the core software 
• Software maintenance patching services 
• On-site technical support when needed 
 
Engineering services will not be provided until approved by AFAS Program Manager.   
 
1.2.4 Task 4: Image Creation 
 

 
 
One SDC/AFAS Image (Kiosk) based on Win 11 Operating System utilizing the current AF SDC that will 
include AFAS software and adaptations to make the AFAS workstation suitable for an operational air traffic 
environment and Win 11 patches available at the time of image creation.   
1.2.5 Continuation of Essential Department of Defense (DoD) Contractor Services During Crisis:  This 
requirement has been determined not to be essential and does not require continued support during a 
crisis as defined in DFARS 252.237-7023.  
 
1.3 PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE/PLACE OF PERFORMANCE 
 
The period of performance is twelve months beginning May 23, 2026 and ending May 22, 2027 plus 4 
option years.  Therefore, the total period of performance with options will run from May 23, 2026 
through May 22, 2031.       
 
1.4 GOVERNMENT FURNISHED EQUIPMENT/MATERIALS/FACILITIES 
 
N/A 
 
1.5 INSPECTION AND ACCEPTANCE 
 
Acceptance of invoice will be made by HQ AFFSA/AFAS COR (Contracting Officer Representative). 
 
2.0 APPLICABLE DOCUMENTS 
 
None 
 
3.0 REQUIREMENTS 
 
This task shall require the contractor to provide the support necessary to perform the following 
functions: 
• Provide first level support to all current AFAS systems and locations to include the following: 
• Resolve AFAS software issues including those involving issues caused by changes in 
operating system and security changes required for continued Air Force network operations. 
• Issues involving utilization of the AFAS, using software features, creating and managing the 
database, configuring profiles, organizing data most efficiently for rapid access in air traffic 
control environment, and other contractor product use knowledge areas. 
• Maintain current AFAS interfaces. 
• Generate new AFAS software configurations/license files approved by AFAS Program Manager 
and deliver to the applicable field unit and AFAS Program Manager. 
 
4.0 DELIVERABLE 
 
The contractor shall be aware that in the absence of any contract requirement from the Service 
Summary does not detract from its enforceability nor limit the rights or remedies of the Government 
under any other provision of the contract.  The contractor shall ensure the following service methods 
are achieved as follows:   
 
Service Summary (SS) Requirement 

 
 
The contractor shall ensure the performance objectives, performance thresholds, and support for 
surveillance methods are achieved as follows: 
 
Performance Objectives and Thresholds 
The contractor shall achieve performance thresholds identified in Table 2.1 of this PWS. 
 
NOTE 1:  The performance thresholds are designed to: 
 a. Align contractor performance objectives.  
 b. Focus on critical success factors in meeting performance objectives. 
 c. Reflect performance goals. 
 d. Promote continuous improvement in performance.  
NOTE 2:  The AFAS Program Manager will exercise surveillance over the performance thresholds. 
 
Surveillance Methods 
The contractor shall support the AFAS Program Manager’s surveillance methods as identified below: 
 a. Random sampling of recurring service outputs. 
 b. One hundred percent inspection of the output. 
 c. Periodic inspection of the process or output. 
 d. Customer complaints. 
 
NOTE:  The AFAS Program Manager may use a combination of surveillance methods, as defined above, 
to monitor contractor’s performance even though the specific surveillance method is not called out in 
Table 2.1.  
 
Contractor Performance Evaluation 
The contractor shall be aware that the evaluation of performance will occur when AFAS Program

NOTE:  In the event the performance measure is not met, the Contracting Officer Representative (COR)

Contractor employees shall identify themselves as contractor personnel by introducing themselves or

5.1.2 Contractor Manpower Reporting (CMR):  The Contractor shall report ALL Contractor labor hours, to

Subject: ATR Data Analytics Solution RFI QA document

…had one question regarding this statement: Assess the ability to integrate with the Agency’s existing cloud infrastructure (Azure-based environment).​Would the government also entertain vendors who are deployed in AWS Government hosting platforms?  Yes

Is ATR open to a multi-product platform response, or are they seeking a single-vendor analytics suite (e.g., pure Databricks/Snowflake)? Yes Open (they must be in Gov. Cloud with FedRAMP High Authorization)

What existing data sources does ATR need to ingest from — case management systems, litigation databases, court records, financial filings, third-party data providers? Any additional detail is appreciated. Initial data ingestion comes from many sources, including data produced by parties during investigations and second requests. This will include structured, unstructured and semi-structured data.

What is the current Azure environment (Azure Government or Azure Commercial)? Will the solution require FedRAMP High or Moderate authorization? Currently Government Cloud requiring FedRAMP High Authorization

Is there an existing ATO (Authority to Operate) process in place at ATR, and what is the expected timeline? This process is initiated as part of an Authority to Test and will be required to meet all Authority to Operate controls prior to being production ready

Will structured and unstructured data be stored in the government environment, or can it data be processed in a FedRAMP-authorized cloud? The data must be processed within government cloud boundaries. No data can leave government environment.

What is the expected data volume range (TBs of data, number of concurrent users)? 5kbs to as much as 400TBs can be produced at any one time. Volume depends on data use type. Economic data comes in much larger sizes.

How many users will be using the tool? Will the users primarily be Data Scientists, Economists and/or Lawyers? Any breakdown related to user demographics would be appreciated. Please provide peak concurrent users expected to access the Data Analytics Solution as well. Current needs: >30, System Admins, Data Scientists and Economists mainly, 10 users peak. It is possible that other types of users could be involved, but that is unknown at this time. They are likely to be Attorneys, Paralegals or Data Processing specialists that help with the loading and validation of production data.

Is the Government open to layered or component solutions in which a specialized vendor addresses a defined capability bundle (for example, investigative analytics over structured and unstructured litigation data, with native entity extraction, relationship graphing, and source-traceable AI), as a complement to a separate enterprise platform addressing data warehousing, MLOps, and broad analytics infrastructure? Or does ATR intend a single-prime platform award covering the full Appendix A scope? (sidenote from vendor: We ask because our platform delivers a set of capabilities the named reference vendors do not — specifically around investigative entity analysis, relationship discovery across disparate sources, and AI-generated answers with structural source citations preserved by the data architecture rather than reconstructed by the model. We are not, however, an end-to-end data warehousing or model lifecycle management platform, and we would not want to consume ATR’s evaluation time submitting against requirements that lie outside our intended scope.) Open to discussion, but all requirements for Appendix A must be met.

Can you confirm if this is related to a recompete or if it's new work? New

NFR 1.18 requires FedRAMP compliance. Does the Agency require FedRAMP Moderate or FedRAMP High authorization? Please confirm the minimum required impact level. Yes FedRAMP High Authorization

What is the highest data classification level the DAS must handle? (e.g., Unclassified, Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI), For Official Use Only (FOUO), Personally Identifiable Information (PII)) CUI

BR 1.02 states that the solution must be flexible to work with other cloud platforms. Does the Agency anticipate the DAS operating solely within its existing Azure infrastructure, or is a multi-cloud or hybrid-cloud deployment (where some components operate in a separate FedRAMP-authorized cloud environment) within scope for the resulting procurement? We are willing to explore other possible architecture options, including multi-cloud or hybrid-cloud environments because our data currently exists within multiple cloud environments, and there may be a need to connect to those data sources. All environments must support FedRAMP High Authorization

NFR 1.17 specifies RTO <= 1 hour, RPO <= 5 minutes, and 99.95% uptime. Is the disaster recovery site expected to be within the same cloud provider and region, or must it be geographically separated (e.g., East/West US)? DR should be in same cloud provider, but we will accept a recovery site within the same region, but different availability zones.

NFR 1.17 specifies RTO <= 1 hour, RPO <= 5 minutes, and 99.95% uptime. Is an active-active or active-passive failover architecture acceptable to satisfy this requirement? Both are acceptable, but are application dependent

Approximately how many total named users will require access to the DAS platform? >30 initially. We do not have an estimate for future needs.

Can the Agency provide an approximate breakdown of DAS users by role type (e.g., system administrators, data scientists/engineers, economists/analysts, read-only/business users)? Yes. Please provide tiered licensing structure if that is the intent here. Users may include: >30, System Admins, Data Scientists, Economists, Attorneys, Paralegals and Data Processing specialists.

What is the approximate total data volume currently under management at ATR that would be ingested or migrated into the DAS? > 450 TB already in Azure Cloud. This information does not include the size of any production data which can range from 500TB to 1PB.

What is ATR's estimated annual data growth rate? At least 10% based off the last 3 years and the current rate of ingestion for this year of economic data. However, when we include the data produced during investigations and litigation, that amount grows at approximately 20-30% per year.

FR 1.01 requires support for unstructured data ingestion. Approximately what percentage of ATR's total data assets are unstructured (e.g., legal documents, deposition transcripts, contracts, correspondence, multimedia files)? > 90%

What is the approximate total volume of unstructured data currently managed by ATR? 
Approximately 450 TB of economic data and between 500TB to 1PB of production data.

FR 1.02 requires support for MPEG and MP3 formats, and FR 1.15 requires automated ingestion and classification. Approximately what volume of audio or video files (e.g., recorded depositions, wiretaps, hearing recordings) does ATR currently manage?  The volume of video and audio files varies significantly by case and is not fixed. If your solution has any limitations processing or storing this type of data, please include that in the comments section of the evaluation criteria.

What are the typical file sizes and formats of ATR's audio and video evidence files? Varies extensively, can be in any audio or video format type, but most common is MP4.

BR 1.18 specifies a streaming throughput requirement of at least 50,000 records per second. What are the anticipated streaming data sources that drive this requirement (e.g., financial data feeds, regulatory filing APIs, internal system event logs, real-time monitoring data)? Typically, data is ingested via physical media or from a staged NAS, developing an automated ingestion pipeline is desired as part of another project related to this request

Approximately how many automated data pipelines, ETL workflows, or scheduled jobs currently exist in ATR's environment that would need to be migrated, replicated, or rebuilt in the new DAS? Currently we have about 5 pipelines and about 200 jobs per week, but they’re not automated and will have to be created as part of the new solution. No need to migrate anything

Will ETL pipeline development, configuration, and ongoing maintenance be performed by contractor staff, government staff, or a combination of both? Combination

Will AI/ML model training, development, and deployment be performed by contractor data scientists or government economists/analysts? Possibly all of the above

Is there an existing data analytics platform, data warehouse, or incumbent contractor currently supporting ATR's data analytics needs? Yes

What data currently resides in the existing system, and will the incumbent contractor be expected to cooperate with transition activities? Case data, there is no incumbent contract currently supporting this work as part of the product implementation. All resources are both federal employees and onsite contract support from other Division contracts. We do not expect support beyond tier 2 or 3 maintenance support to be required as part of any RFP. 

Does the Agency currently hold active enterprise licenses for PowerBI, Tableau, and/or IBM Cognos? Yes, we own PowerBI licenses. We do not own Tableau or IBM Cognos.

Will the existing BI visualization tools (PowerBI, Tableau, IBM Cognos) continue to operate alongside the new DAS, or is the DAS expected to replace any of these tools? Continue to use existing visualization tools

FR 1.10 requires Git-based source control integration. What specific Git platform does ATR currently use (e.g., GitHub Enterprise, Azure DevOps, GitLab)? We do not have one standard.

Does ATR have a preferred or existing CI/CD automation platform?  No preferred  /Yes we have existing CI/CD platforms (BitBucket, Nexus, Ansible Tower, Jenkins, Terraform)

Does ATR currently have AI or ML models in production that must be migrated to or supported by the new DAS? We are exploring OpenAI RAG models but have not created any AI models in production.

What frameworks were used to build ATR's existing AI/ML models (e.g., scikit-learn, TensorFlow, PyTorch, R statistical models)? We do not have any active models in production. 

Is a parallel operation period required during transition from the existing environment to the new DAS? Yes If a parallel operation period is required, what is the minimum acceptable duration before the legacy system can be decommissioned? Approximately 90 days

What contract type is anticipated for the DAS acquisition (e.g., Firm Fixed Price, Time and Materials, Cost Plus Fixed Fee)? ATR has not made of decision on contract type. 

What period of performance is anticipated for the DAS acquisition (e.g., base year plus option years)? Base, plus 4 options

What is the anticipated timeline from RFI response (May 1, 2026) to RFP release? Does ATR anticipate releasing the RFP within FY2026? Yes, we expect to release the RFP within this FY.

What enterprise productivity, cost management and analytics tools are currently being utilized by ATR? Cloud based Dashboard and Tools

Will it be necessary to integrate current solutions into the new solution, or will the existing data need to be migrated to the new solution? TBD, depending on solution selection

Can the government elaborate on the currently deployed visualization tools (such as PowerBI, Tableau, or others), any preferred or mandated tools, the specific Azure services in use (e.g., Azure Data Lake Gen2, Azure SQL, Azure Synapse, Azure Databricks), and the immediate versus future support requirements for other cloud platforms (like AWS or GCP) to understand integration touchpoints? We have data visualization through PowerBI. As for tools and Cloud platforms the purpose of this RFI is to find out the industry tools available. Propose the tool you think is best based on the RFI information and your industry experience. 

Does ATR require existing ETL workflows to be migrated, or will this be a completely new ETL implementation? TBD, depending on solution. We have tested some solutions.

Is the government's objective to provide analytic services or to establish an analytic support system for ATR users? Both

Can the government provide details about ATR's current training infrastructure? Specifically, do you have a Learning Management System (LMS) in place? Yes

What kind of access and functionalities are available to non-technical users? Does their access include things like self-service query builders, pre-built dashboards, natural language interfaces, and other similar features? Pre-built Dashboards

Does ATR require support for specific data classification levels, such as Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) or For Official Use Only? Yes, CUI

Does ATR have specific data retention policies for different data types? Additionally, what is the established process for data disposal? Yes.  Data disposal is dependent upon record schedules, litigation holds, and case disposition.

What are ATR's specific requirements for cross-matter information barriers in litigation contexts? Criminal data is subject to Grand Jury secrecy requirements. Conflicts of interest may also be relevant, so RBAC roles are important. Data security should allow for flexibility based on roles and groups.

What specific ROI metrics does ATR leadership currently track? Are there established baselines for time-to-decision or TCO? We currently have no tracking mechanisms but would be interested in metrics that would provide valuable insights to senior leadership, including CIO, about the speed to review and system responsiveness.

What are the current wait times for compute resource availability that need to be improved? Ability to analyze >1TB of data per day 

Are there specific DOJ, ATR or federal AI transparency requirements we should be aware of beyond general explainability? Systems must meet all requirements as listed in EOs and OMB Directives on AI such as EO 14147, EO 14179, EO 14283, EO 14275, EO 14319, M-25-21, M-25,22, and M-26-04 as well as any new EO and OMB Directives on the subject.

How many active litigation matters or investigations does ATR typically manage concurrently? The RFI is intended for high-level capability assessment, we are unable to provide additional details beyond what is included in the RFI materials. If your solution has any limitations, please include it into the comments section of the evaluation criteria. 

Does the "US-based companies" requirement for AI models apply to open-source models, or only proprietary/commercial models? Yes to all. It must not have any foreign source within its supply chain pursuant to EO 13873.

Please specify the main external data sources that ATR should connect to? The RFI is intended for high-level capability assessment, we are unable to provide additional details beyond what is included in the RFI materials.

Statement of Work 1 
 
Introduction 
The mission of the Indian Health Service (IHS) is to raise the physical, mental, social, and 
spiritual health of American Indians and Alaska Natives to the highest level. As part of this 
mission, the IHS is committed to providing a reliable and efficient health information 
system, modernizing IT infrastructure, improving access to care, and reducing medical 
errors through technology. 
Statement of Work (SOW) 
Enterprise Cisco UC/Collaboration & RPMS Systems Support 
The Indian Health Service (IHS) Great Plains Area (GPA) seeks a single contractor to provide 
comprehensive support services that encompass the full scope of work contained in both 
the Enterprise Cisco Unified Communications (UC) and Collaboration Support requirements 
and the Resource Patient Management System (RPMS) Systems Support requirements. The 
selected contractor will deliver unified communications engineering, system 
administration, maintenance, troubleshooting, modernization, and Tier 2/Tier 3 support for 
both the Cisco collaboration ecosystem and RPMS/EHR platform environments across all 
GPA facilities. These services will be consolidated under one contract to ensure coordinated 
oversight, streamlined support, and high system reliability for mission-critical 
communication and clinical information systems. 
Section C —  Statement of Work 
C-1. Overview 
The Great Plains Area requires comprehensive, integrated IT support services across two 
major operational domains: 
• Enterprise Cisco UC and Collaboration Systems supporting voice, video, telehealth, 
conferencing, and communication. 
• Engineering Services to migrate Billings into the GPA Calling Cluster 
• RPMS/EHR Systems supporting clinical operations at nineteen facilities, including 
four 24/7 hospitals. 
The contractor shall ensure the stability, performance, compliance, and modernization of 
both environments. 
C-2. Place of Performance 
Support will be provided primarily remotely using IHS-approved secure connectivity. On-
site work will occur only when authorized in writing by the COR. All RPMS and Cisco UC 
support may involve phone or VPN access. All travel must be pre-approved and reimbursed 
under relevant policies. 

Statement of Work 2 
 
C-3. Period of Performance 
Base Period: One (1) year 
Option Periods: Four (4) one-year option periods 
C-4. Background 
The GPA Cisco environment includes UCM, Unity, Expressway, IM&P, Webex, and related 
systems. RPMS systems run on Windows or AIX and support 19 locations including four 
hospitals. Both environments support mission-critical healthcare and administrative 
operations. 
C-5. Objectives 
Cisco UC Objectives: 
- Ensure stable and optimized Cisco UC operations. 
- Provide Tier 3 engineering support. i.e. Networking issue resolution, infrastructure 
equipment support, ISP escalations, last mile carrier / local Telco POC, cloud configurations, 
SME for related projects. 
 
RPMS Objectives: 
- Maintain continuous RPMS/EHR operations. 
- Provide Tier 2 support and coordinate Tier 3 escalations. i.e. Restart RPMS services and 
interfaces for RPMS servers, disaster recovery and restore functions, beta testing and  
installing patches and RPMS updates, Server maintenance; physical and virtual. 
C-6.1 Scope of Work – Cisco UC Support 
Tier 3 Engineering and Escalation Support 
• Serve as the senior technical resource for Cisco UCM, Webex, and associated 
collaboration technologies. 
• Troubleshoot and resolve complex call flow, SIP trunking, voice gateway, 
Expressway-C/E traversal, and media resource issues. 
• Manage cluster-level operations and interoperability between on-premises and 
cloud-based platforms. 
• Interface with Cisco TAC for major incidents, software defects, and root cause 
analysis. 
System Optimization and Performance Management 
• Monitor system performance, call quality, and resource utilization. 
• Perform scheduled backups of Cisco Unified Communications applications, 
Expressway-C/E clusters, and related collaboration components, and validate 
restore integrity per IHS configuration and continuity requirements 
• Conduct QoS audits and implement configuration adjustments to enhance service 
reliability. 

Statement of Work 3 
 
• Optimize integration between Cisco UCM and Webex for seamless collaboration and 
conferencing. 
• Provide quarterly reports summarizing performance trends and improvement 
recommendations. 
Configuration and Lifecycle Management 
• Plan and execute upgrades, patches, and system refreshes for UCM clusters, Unity, 
and Expressway. 
• Maintain standard configuration baselines and ensure consistent call routing and 
dial plan policies. 
• Support onboarding of new sites, users, and call flows within the enterprise 
environment. 
• Document configurations, workflows, and system dependencies in accordance with 
IHS change management. 
Security and Compliance 
• Ensure systems adhere to IHS and HHS security baselines and hardening standards. 
• Coordinate vulnerability mitigation and patch management activities. 
• Support required compliance standards through documentation and evidence 
gathering. 
• Collaborate with IHS cybersecurity and ISSO teams for remediation and audit 
support. 
Reporting and Knowledge Transfer 
• Deliver monthly reports detailing incidents, system performance, and optimization 
activities. 
• Provide updated documentation following significant changes or upgrades. 
• Participate in technical reviews and meetings with IHS leadership as requested. 
C-6.2 IHS Billings Migration to GPA UC Cluster: 
Migrate up to 1600 phones and 6 sites from two (2) separate Communications and Unity 
Connection clusters into the existing IHS Great Plains Area (GPA) Communications Manager and 
Unity Connection clusters 
• Configure up to six (6) new sites in the GPA cluster 
• Configure up to six (6) gateway routers with SRST in the GPA cluster 
• Migrate existing PSTN and analog gateway routers to register with the GPA CUCM 
cluster 
• Activate PRI for Little Shell site with new DIDs for users/phones 
• Modify existing dial plan to fit into GPA’s 10-digit dial plan 
• Configure up to ten (10) paging groups into GPA’s existing InformaCast Advanced (ICVA) 
cluster with up to ten (10) legacy paging interfaces (LPI/analog overhead speakers) 

Statement of Work 4 
 
• Duplicate/Import all Auto-Attendant features into new Unity Connection cluster 
• Configure up to ten (10) E911 locations into GPA’s existing CER based on IP subnet – 
Required for E911 support 
• E911 locations based on dedicated DID availability 
• Migrate sites/users in seven (7) separate migration events 
• Perform testing, troubleshooting and support post site migration 
Assumptions: 
• All devices (phones and gateways) will be migrated in a like-for-like manner.   It is 
assumed that all devices are currently Cisco supported. 
• Current paging gateways are of a hardware version that will support a firmware upgrade 
to version 2.X 
• Utilize existing IHS/GPA UC and ICVA licensing 
C-6.3 Scope of Work – RPMS Systems Support 
The Subcontractor is responsible for ensuring that the Resource and Patient Management 
System/Electronic Health Record (RPMS/EHR) operates reliably across the Great Plains Area 
(GPA). To meet Indian Health Service (IHS) standards, the Subcontractor must maintain 99% 
system uptime and ensure all RPMS systems follow standard configuration guidelines across 
both IRIS and Windows environments. This includes providing continuous monitoring, timely 
maintenance, technical expertise, and coordination with federal staff. 
The Great Plains Area’s Office of Information Technology (GPA OIT) requires both Tier 2 and 
assistance with Tier 3 engineering-level support. Approximately 400–600 tickets per year are 
handled through Tier 2 services, making the subcontracted support a critical operational 
function. 
Support is provided to nineteen facilities (four of which are 24/7 hospitals) and is conducted 
remotely via phone or VPN. 
 
Core Technical Responsibilities 
1. RPMS Platform & Operating System Support 
The Subcontractor must provide full support for: 
• Server hardware and OS environments: This includes IBM AIX servers and Windows-
based systems. 
• RPMS patching and updates: Ensuring systems remain synchronized with IHS National 
Release cycles. 
• IRIS database environments: Installation, upgrades, configuration, and ongoing 
maintenance of IRIS databases, journaling, and mirroring. 

Statement of Work 5 
 
• Backup management: Ensuring consistent and reliable site backups. 
• General RPMS issue resolution: Troubleshooting system failures, data issues, and 
performance concerns. 
• OS and application patching: Applying updates to operating systems, RPMS applications, 
IRIS, and any related RPMS/EHR tools. 
2. System Monitoring & Reliability Assurance 
To maintain the required 99% uptime, the Subcontractor must: 
• Perform proactive monitoring of all systems to detect potential issues early. 
• Notify GPA OIT about emerging issues before they become operational problems. 
• Ensure system performance remains optimal through tuning, testing, and analysis. 
• Provide technical guidance to improve reliability, stability, and security. 
 
Tier 2 Support Responsibilities (Detailed) 
Tier 2 support includes direct issue resolution, troubleshooting, and technical intervention 
across all 19 facilities. 
Key responsibilities include: 
• Patch Management & Break-Fix 
Applying patches and resolving failures affecting Windows and AIX systems, including 
real-time operational disruptions. 
• Help Desk Support 
Offering help desk services for federal, tribal, and urban RPMS systems. 
• Transmission and Connectivity Issue Resolution 
Fixing failures in system communication between AIX and Windows environments. 
• Coordination with On-Site Admins 
Scheduling maintenance with local system administrators to minimize operational 
impact. 
• Documentation Requirements 
All steps taken to resolve issues must be documented in the centralized repository 
within 2 hours of ticket closure. 
• Rapid Downtime Response 
Subcontractor personnel must respond “as soon as possible” for any downtime events 
and must be reachable 24/7 for emergencies. 
Specialized Technical Responsibilities: 
• Providing qualified specialists for IBM AIX High Availability administration. 
• Supplying experienced personnel skilled in IRIS/Caché environments for Windows and 
AIX. 
• Assisting with RPMS server conversions from AIX to Windows. 

Statement of Work 6 
 
• Providing remote user support, including RPMS password resets and server 
troubleshooting. 
• Troubleshooting:  
o Vista Capture and Display client issues 
o ACHS Web Printing Module setup 
o RPMS-Dentrix dental integration 
o IRIS Management Portal errors 
o Great Plains Area DI server issues 
o BMW application problems 
o RPMS Error Trap investigation and resolution 
 
Tier 3 Support Responsibilities 
Though Tier 3 engineering support is provided by IHS headquarters, the Subcontractor must: 
• Identify issues requiring Tier 3 assistance, track them, and coordinate the escalation 
process. 
• Provide monthly status reports documenting:  
o All support calls handled 
o Risks identified and their mitigation 
o Final resolutions 
• Recommend improvements to enhance RPMS reliability based on proactive monitoring. 
• Maintain full tracking of escalated tickets through their final resolution. 
• Prepare and organize training materials, presentations, and documentation 
(PowerPoints, meeting notes, reports). 
 
Staffing Requirements 
• Provide the equivalent of one full-time employee, which may be composed of multiple 
specialists (AIX expert, IRIS specialist, Windows engineer, etc.). 
• A single dedicated Project Manager/Point of Contact must oversee all activities, ensure 
communication, and enforce best practices. 
• Staff must be able to provide:  
o Business-hours support for standard maintenance windows 
o After-hours emergency support without additional overtime costs 
o Adjusted work schedules to meet facility needs 
C-7. Personnel Qualifications 
• Cisco UC Engineer: Senior-level Tier 3 engineer with expertise in UCM, Unity, 
Expressway, Webex, SIP, and QoS. 
• RPMS/IRIS Team: 4–5 personnel experienced in AIX, IRIS, and RPMS administration, 
coordinated by a Project Manager.  
• All staff must hold required IHS credentials. 

Statement of Work 7 
 
C-8. Government-Furnished Resources 
IHS will provide system access, administrative permissions, documentation, network 
diagrams, and maintenance coordination. 
C-9. Security, Privacy & Access Requirements 
All personnel must pass background checks and comply with IHS/HHS security 
requirements. All work must safeguard PII and PHI and follow site-specific security 
processes. 
C-10. Accessibility Requirements 
All services procured under this contract must conform to 36 CFR Part 1194 accessibility 
standards unless exempt. 
C-11. Deliverables 
- Monthly performance and activity reports. 
- Quarterly optimization reports. 
- Preventive maintenance schedule. 
- Updated documentation after major changes. 
- Quality control plan.

Judge Advocate General's Corps (JAGC) Online Collegiate Recruiting Network – Salient Characteristics

The contractor shall provide a subscription service to its proprietary network that meets the following requirements:

 Platform Access and Functionality

The contractor shall grant and maintain access to the 12twenty platform for 1 authorized USAF JAGC user. 

The platform shall, at a minimum, provide the ability to:

Search and filter a national database of law student resumes and profiles.

Post and manage job announcements for military and civilian opportunities to the contractor's full network or a selection thereof.

Directly message and communicate with student candidates.

Create a branded employer profile for the USAF JAGC with access to additional branding and messaging avenues for each partnered school.

Network Reach


The contractor's database must provide access to 187 or more collegiate institutions.

Candidate Identification and Engagement


The platform shall provide features to enhance candidate engagement:

Identify students who may be high-quality applicants using the contractor’s proprietary metrics and algorithms. These students may then be invited to apply or be highlighted to the JAGC.

Track engagement and response rates of JAGC direct messaging to students.
Schedule and promote interviews and recruiting events via the contractor’s network.

Service Availability and Support

The contractor shall notify the Government Technical Point of Contact (TPOC) and the Contracting Officer (CO) in writing of any scheduled maintenance that will impact software availability.

The contractor shall notify the TPOC and CO in writing of any unscheduled outages, issues, or potential issues that may affect performance.

The contractor shall make a representative reasonably available for meetings, tutorials, or other discussions at the request of the TPOC.

DELIVERABLES

1.	The Contractor shall provide 1 seat software access to their network service upon contract award.

2.	The Contractor will make a representative reasonably available for meetings, tutorials, or other discussions at the request of GPOC
