DEPARTMENT OF TREASURY

BUREAU OF ENGRAVING AND PRINTING

BEP Warehouse SOG Evaluation

Landover, MD

ENGINEERING EVALUATION 

PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT 

						

                                 

DISTRICT OF COLUMBIA FACILITY

WASHINGTON, DC 20228

02/27/2026

BACKGROUND:

The Department of Treasury’s Bureau of Engraving and Printing (BEP), Washington DC Facility (DCF) is comprised of the Main Building, the Annex Building, and the Landover Warehouse. The mission of the BEP is to manufacture and produce United States currency.

The Landover Warehouse is located at 3201 Pennsy Dr, Landover, MD 20785.  The structure’s substructure consists of concrete footings, piers, and Slab On Grade (SOG).  The superstructure consists of Pre-cast double tees and CMU walls, steel columns, roof joists and steel beams, and light gauge metal deck.  The warehouse is mainly used as a storage location for BEP’s shipped equipment crates.

PURPOSE:

Project Objective:  

The purpose of this solicitation is to obtain an engineering evaluation of the existing warehouse concrete SOG. The evaluation is to include maximum load capacity, loading patterns, types, and criteria to the existing concrete slab on grade for this warehouse, as well as engineering recommendations and approaches to enhance the determined capacity.  

2.2 Scope of the Product, Service, or Outcome:

This project is a Structural Analysis / Evaluation task.  The contractor shall submit a proposal that includes the total cost and price breakdown for each item to this Scope of Work (SOW) as delineated herein:

2.2.1. Structural Evaluation:

The contractor shall conduct site survey, review available drawings and existing conditions of the SOG, and perform any necessary analysis and testing that shall be required to fulfill the requirements of this SOW.  Original shell building drawings are not available; therefore the contractor is expected to perform technical aspects and approaches that can be, but not limited to, site visits for measurements, provide tools and equipment, perform technical testing as needed, and any other applicable approaches that can achieve the purpose of this SOW. 

2.2.2. Documents:

The contractor shall provide signed and sealed technical report that shall include analysis data and drawings that serves and achieve the purpose of this SOW as indicated.  Technical report shall be submitted to BEP for review and approval.

The contractor shall provide a preliminary schedule one week after contract is awarded and at the kickoff meeting.  BEP can provide the available and historical documents for the area of work, however, the accuracy of these drawings cannot be guaranteed.  Archived and available documents shall be provided upon request and shall be used for “Informational Purposes Only”.  It is the Contractor’s responsibility to gather all information necessary for the successful outcome and completion of this project, including but not limited to a thorough understanding of the existing conditions under which the work will be performed.

2.2.3. Safety:

The Contractor shall be responsible for all means and methods required to perform this evaluation, and shall adhere and comply with all the requirements of BEP-EMS document 75D-07.0-04 EHS Contractor Requirements.

CODES, STANDARDS AND REFERENCES

The Contractor shall comply with the current edition of all applicable practices, codes, methods, and industry standards as prepared by technical societies and associations. In the event of conflict between codes and standards of the organizations, the more stringent regulations shall govern. 

GENERAL REQUIREMENTS:

4.1	Place/ Location of Performance/ Delivery:

The service shall be performed at the Landover Warehouse located at 3201 Pennsy Dr, Landover, MD 20785.

4.2	Travel Requirements:

None.

4.3	Special Requirements:

4.3.1 Contracting Officer Representative (COR):  

The (COR) will be identified by separate letter issued by the CO.  The COR monitors all technical aspects of the Contract and assists in Contract administration.  The COR is authorized to perform the following functions: assure that the Contractor performs the technical requirements of the contract; perform inspections necessary in connection with contract performance; maintain written and oral communications with the Contractor concerning technical aspects of the contract; issue written interpretations of technical requirements, including Government drawings, designs, specifications; monitor Contractor's performance and notifies both the CO and Contractor of any deficiencies; coordinate availability of government furnished property, and provide site entry of Contractor personnel.  A letter of designation issued to the COR, a copy of which is sent to the Contractor, states the responsibilities and limitations of the COR, especially with regard to changes in cost or price, estimates or changes in delivery dates.  The COR is not authorized to change any of the terms and conditions of the Contract. 

4.3.2 Physical Security:  

The Contractor shall be responsible for safeguarding all government equipment, information and property provided for Contractor use under this Contract.  This Contract requires access into the Controlled Industrial Area of the BEP.  The Contractor personnel shall recognize that BEP deals with sensitive information and other proprietary information, which are valuable, special, and unique assets. All information pertinent to BEP’s information technology resources is highly sensitive and may not be released to third parties without the express, written consent of BEP.  This information requires strict control procedures to preclude unauthorized disclosure or dissemination.  Information pertinent to personnel is protected from unauthorized disclosure under the provisions of the Privacy Act of 1974 (5 U.S.C. 552a).  Contractor personnel shall not divulge, disclose, or communicate in any manner, any information to any third party without prior written consent of the BEP. Contractor personnel shall protect information and treat it as strictly confidential and will abide by the security requirements of BEP. A violation of this paragraph shall be a material violation of this Contract.  Should the Contractor receive or suspect they have learned of sensitive or classified information, the Contractor shall identify and report suspicions to the COR.  Contractor personnel performing work under this Contract shall be subjects of background investigations, conducted by BEP’s Office of Personnel Security, prior to start of work under this Contract.  Each Contractor employee performing under this Contract must successfully complete the Government required background check form at time of the proposal submission; and must maintain the level of security required for the life of the Contract.

4.3.3 Identification of Contractor Employees:   

All contract personnel attending meetings, answering Government telephones, and working in other situations where their contractor status is not obvious to third parties are required to identify themselves as such to avoid creating an impression in the minds of members of the public that they are Government officials.  They must also ensure that all documents or reports produced by Contractors are suitably marked as Contractor products or that Contractor participation is appropriately disclosed.  All Contractor personnel shall clearly identify themselves as a Contractor and shall be required to wear identification (ID) badges in a visible location on the front of exterior clothing, above the waist, (except when safety or health reasons prevent such placement). ID badges shall be worn at all times when performing work.  ID badges shall have an identification picture; and shall state the name of the individual and the company they represent.  Contractor personnel are prohibited from possessing weapons, firearms or ammunition, on themselves or within their Contractor-owned or privately owned vehicle while on BEP premises.

4.3.4 Organizational Conflict of Interest:  

Contractor and subcontractor personnel performing work under this Contract may receive, have access to or participate in the development of proprietary or source selection information (e.g., cost or pricing information, budget information or analyses, specifications, or work statements, etc.) or perform evaluation services which may create a current or subsequent Organizational Conflict of Interests (OCI) as defined in FAR Subpart 9.5.  The Contractor shall notify the CO immediately whenever it becomes aware that such access or participation may result in any actual or potential OCI and shall promptly submit a plan to the CO to avoid or mitigate any such OCI.  The Contractor’s mitigation plan will be determined to be acceptable solely at the discretion of the CO and in the event the CO unilaterally determines that any such OCI cannot be satisfactorily avoided or mitigated, the CO may affect other remedies as he or she deems necessary, including prohibiting the Contractor from participation in subsequent contracted requirements which may be affected by the OCI.

4.3.5 Non personal service statement: 

Contractor employees performing services under this Contract will be controlled, directed, and supervised at all times by management personnel of the Contractor. Contractor management will ensure that employees properly comply with the statement of work. Contractor employees will perform their duties independent of, and without the supervision of, any Government official or other Government Contractor.  The tasks, duties, and responsibilities set forth in this Contract may not be interpreted or implemented in any manner that results in any Contractor employee creating or modifying Federal policy, obligating the appropriated funds of the United States Government, overseeing the work of Federal employees, providing direct personal services to any Federal employee, or otherwise violating the prohibitions set forth in Parts 7.5 and 37.1 of the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR).  The Government will control access to its facility and will perform the inspection and acceptance of the completed work.

V.       ACCEPTANCE OF WORK

SUBSTANTIAL COMPLETION - Substantial completion of the work is defined herein as the point at which the work is complete in all respects except for a few minor items which are to be listed on the Contractor’s punch list. Substantial Completion is inclusive of all accepted systems being fully operational. The Contractor shall demonstrate that all newly installed systems are fully operational. With the issuance of a substantial completion certificate, executed by the Contracting Officer (CO) and the Contractor, the BEP will take possession of the work and operate the installed systems/equipment. Prior to the issuance of an executed substantial completion certificate the Contractor shall have had all tests completed, witnessed, and approved by the BEP’s authorized representative. The provision of all required training, operating and maintenance manuals, and other such requirements in this SOW shall be a prerequisite to the Contractor’s notification requesting a substantial completion walk-through.

The Contractor shall notify the CO and/or COR in writing at least ten (10) calendar days prior to the estimated date of substantial completion and request a substantial completion walk-thru. The letter shall include a dated punch list as developed by the Contractor. The purpose of the walk-through is to review the Contractor’s list for accuracy and to identify any additional items needing completion prior to final acceptance. The Contractor, shall, upon receipt of a partial or substantial completion punch list, correct his or her work as required within seven (7) calendar days. The substantial completion walk-through shall be performed by the BEP COR and/or CC.

The date of the BEP’s acknowledgement of substantial completion shall establish the Contractor’s one year guarantee of workmanship and the manufacturer’s product warranties. In the instance of a Partial Substantial Completion Certificate, the previous sentence shall apply to the work identified in the partial substantial completion certificate only. The Contractor shall ensure all warranty requirements, including manufacturers’ warranties, in an electronic spreadsheet format that will be provided to the CO and COR.

FINAL COMPLETION - The Contractor shall inform the CO and/or COR in writing at least seven (7) calendar days prior to the estimated date of the completion of the work and request a final acceptance inspection.

Status-

REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL No. 74330226R0039 
Fallen Servicemembers Religious Heritage Restoration Program 
 
OVERVIEW 
The American Battle Monuments Commission (ABMC) is soliciting proposals for commercial 
research services to identify American Jewish servicemembers buried under grave markers that 
incorrectly represent religion or heritage, and to identify surviving next o f kin (NOK), as described 
in the attached Statement of Work, Attachment 1. 
 
CONTRACT TYPE 
ABMC anticipates award of a Firm Fixed Price (FFP) contract. Travel expenses, if required, should 
be proposed as a separate CLIN.  
 
PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE 
The period of performance is anticipated for  12 months for the base year , beginning upon contract 
award. 
 
EVALUATION CRITERA 
ABMC intends to award one contract to the vendor whose proposal represents the best value to the 
Government. ABMC will evaluate offerors based on the below factors on a best -value approach, in 
order of importance. Non-price factors, when combined, are more important than price. Price remains 
an important consideration. 
 
Factors 
1. Demonstrated Capability and Expertise: Experience and past performance in work similar to the 
Statement of Work, including research, evidence based documentation, and NOK identification. 
2. Technical Approach: Soundness and feasibility of the proposed methodology, including 
handling of records, case file development, and NOK research. 
3. Management, Schedule, and Deliverables: Ability to manage the work and deliver required 
products in a timely and reliable manner 
4. Quality Control and Data Protection: Adequacy of QC procedures and safeguards for sensitive 
information and PII. 
5. Price: Price will be evaluated for reasonableness and consistency with the proposed approach. 
 
PROPOSAL FORMAT 
Proposals shall be submitted in three volumes in pdf format. 
Volume I – Technical Approach 
Describe how the offeror will perform the Statement of Work, including: 
• Research methodology and source verification 
• Case file development with citations and confidence assessment 

 
• Approach to identifying and documenting NOK 
• Deliverables and schedule 
• Quality control procedures 
• Data protection and privacy safeguards 
• Staffing and key personnel 
 
Volume II – Experience   
Provide evidence of demonstrated capability and expertise, including: 
• Up to three relevant past projects 
• Past performance references (at least two) 
• Experience of key personnel 
 
Volume III – Price   
Provide a Firm -Fixed-Price for the base period and a price breakdown aligned to the Statement of 
Work. Include a brief narrative explaining key pricing assumptions. 
 
QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS 
Questions shall be submitted in writing to the Contracting Officer and Contracting Specialist no later 
than 14 April 2026 at 5PM (Eastern Time). Responses will be issued by written amendment or 
posting. 
 
PROPOSAL SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS 
Proposals shall be submitted via email to the Contracting Officer and Contracting Specialist with the 
subject line “Proposal – 74330226R0039 – Offeror Name” no later than 5PM (Eastern Time) on 
28 April 2026 to the following: 
 
Michael Bachofen     Michael G. Knapp 
Contracting Officer     Contracting Officer’s Representative 
bachofenm@abmc.gov     knappm@abmc.gov   
 
Jessica Young 
Contracting Specialist 
youngj.ctr@abmc.gov    
 
 
ATTACHMENTS: 
1. Statement of Work, dated April 3, 2026 
2. Questions and Answers Template 
 
Solicitation Compliance 
Failure to comply with the material requirements  of this solicitation, including the restriction on 
unauthorized NOK contact, may render a proposal unacceptable.

Contractor expected to independently identify all potential candidate cases across ABMC

This is part of the core deliverable.

actual conditions may vary? 
Yes, assumptions shall be clearly stated in submissions with acknowledgement that actual 
conditions may vary.

STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW) 
 
Fallen Servicemembers Religious Heritage Restoration Program  
 
April 3, 2026 
 
1. Background and Purpose 
 
The American Battle Monuments Commission (ABMC) maintains American military cemeteries and 
memorials around the world and is committed to honoring United States servicemembers with 
accurate commemoration. In support of the Fallen Servicemembers Religious Heritage Restoration 
Program, ABMC seeks contractor support to research and identify American-Jewish servicemembers 
interred in American military cemeteries whose headstones or grave markers incorrectly represent 
their religion and heritage, and to identify surviving next of kin to support potential corrective actions 
and outreach. 
 
2. Scope and Objectives 
 
Scope 
The Contractor shall conduct historical, genealogical, and documentary research to: 
(1) identify American -Jewish servicemembers buried at American military cemeteries with 
grave markers that incorrectly reflect their religion and heritage, and  
(2) identify and locate surviving next of kin for those servicemembers, consistent with 
applicable law, regulation, and ABMC policies. 
 
Important limitations and boundaries (consistent with this SOW): 
 
• The Contractor shall not contact next of kin unless explicitly authorized in writing by the 
Contracting Officer (CO) or Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR). 
• The Contractor’s role is limited to research, documentation, and reporting. Any decisions 
regarding marker corrections and any engagement with families or stakeholders remain with 
ABMC. 
• The Contractor shall not issue public statements, respond to media inquiries, or represent 
ABMC with respect to matters relating to the contract without prior written authorization 
from the CO. 
 

Page 2 of 7 
 
Objectives 
 
• Develop and execute a research methodology to identify likely and confirmed cases of 
misidentified religion/heritage on grave markers. 
• Produce evidence-based case files for each recommended correction, including source 
citations and confidence assessment. 
• Identify, verify, and document surviving next of kin or appropriate family representatives, 
with contact information obtained through lawful means. 
• Provide ABMC with completed case files to support change of headstone suitable for 
ABMC review, decision-making, and potential engagement with families and stakeholders. 
• Ensure sensitive handling of personal data and respectful treatment of the deceased and their 
families. 
 
3. Period of Performance 
 
The contract is anticipated to be a Firm -Fixed-Price (FFP) contract.  The period of performance is 
anticipated to be one (1) base year, with (4) option years (as shown in proposed CLIN structure below) 
that may be exercised at the Government’s discretion and subject to the availability of funds.

4. Definitions and Abbreviations 
• ABMC: American Battle Monuments Commission. 
• American military cemetery: A cemetery administered by ABMC or otherwise identified 
by ABMC in this contract as within scope. 
• Case: A servicemember record for which the Contractor has developed evidence indicating 
the decedent was American-Jewish and the marker religion/heritage is inconsistent with 
available records. 
• Next of kin (NOK): Surviving family member(s) or legally recognized representative(s) as 
defined by ABMC for purposes of outreach and potential marker correction consideration. 
• Source: A primary or secondary document used to support findings (e.g., military personnel 

Page 3 of 7 
 
records, casualty records, burial records, cemetery interment records, vital records, 
synagogue/community records, published rosters, newspaper obituaries, naturalization 
records). 
 
5. Requirements (Tasks) 
5.1 Task 1: Project Initiation and Research Plan 
 
Within 30 calendar days after award, the Contractor shall submit a research plan for ABMC approval 
that describes the methodology, sources, tools, staffing, quality controls, schedule, and risk 
management approach for the work. The plan shall include proposed criteria for identifying likely or 
confirmed American-Jewish servicemembers and for determining that a grave marker is inconsistent 
with the evidence. 
 
5.2 Task 2: Data Collection and Source Research 
 
The Contractor shall collect and analyze relevant source materials to establish identity, service, burial 
location, and religion/heritage indicators. Research may include, as appropriate, Federal records (e.g., 
National Archives holdings), ABMC cemetery/in terment records, Department of Defense casualty 
systems where accessible, state and local vital records, genealogical repositories, community and 
religious archives, and reputable published sources. The Contractor shall maintain full citations and 
copies/record references sufficient for ABMC to independently verify findings. 
 
5.3 Task 3: Case Identification, Analysis, and Evidence Packages 
 
The Contractor shall identify candidate cases and develop an evidence package (“Case File”) for each. 
Each Case File shall, at minimum, include: 
 
• Servicemember identification: full name, service branch, service number (if known), dates 
of birth/death, unit (if known), conflict/era. 
• Burial information: cemetery name, plot/row/grave (or equivalent), current marker 
inscription details relevant to religion/heritage. 
• Summary of evidence supporting American-Jewish identity (primary sources preferred), 
with citations. 
• Summary of evidence supporting that the current marker is inconsistent with the evidence 
(e.g., incorrect religious emblem/wording), with citations. 
• Confidence assessment (e.g., High/Medium/Low) and rationale. 
• Known sensitivities/flags (e.g., conflicting records, ambiguous indicators, name changes), 
and recommended ABMC review steps. 
 
5.4 Task 4: Identification of Surviving Next of Kin 
 
For each Case File, the Contractor shall perform genealogical research to identify surviving next of 
kin and/or legally recognized family representatives and provide ABMC with a documented kinship 

Page 4 of 7 
 
pathway (family tree narrative or equivalent) supported by source citations. The Contractor shall use 
lawful, ethical means for locating contact information. The Contractor shall not contact next of kin 
unless explicitly authorized in writing by the CO or COR. 
 
5.5 Task 5: Coordination, Status Reporting, and Stakeholder Sensitivity 
 
The Contractor shall participate in recurring status meetings (virtual unless otherwise directed) and 
provide updates on progress, issues, and risks. The Contractor shall coordinate with ABMC -
designated points of contact regarding access to ABMC records, cemetery information, and 
prioritization. All work products and communications shall be prepared with appropriate respect and 
sensitivity given the nature of the subject matter.

Notice of Industry Day event for the upcoming Unclassified IT Service Contract 
 
The F-35 Lightning II Joint Program Office (JPO), Arlington, Virginia, will host an industry day May 21, 
2026, to discuss the program’s upcoming requirement for Information Technology (IT) and 
Information Assurance (IA)/Cybersecurity Services (CS).  During this vital forum, the Government 
will share its upcoming procurement needs with our industry partners. This event is intended to be 
a place of transparent communication and collaboration between the public and private sectors; it 
offers a prime opportunity for vendors to understand the Government’s requirements, ask clarifying 
questions, and network with both Government officials and potential partners.  The F-35 JPO will 
use feedback and information about industry capability to refine its requirements. 
 
The F-35 JPO requires comprehensive IT and IA/CS support for its Joint Virtual Enterprise (JVE) 
network and standalone workstations. This support, crucial to the JPO’s mission effectiveness and 
the successful fielding of F-35 mission capabilities, will be provided across all directorates, 
functional areas, and integrated product teams. This includes, but is not limited to, program 
management, enterprise performance management, enterprise architecture, emerging capabilities 
and requirements implementation, life cycle management, operations & maintenance, enterprise 
data management, service desk support, IT training, and CS support. This includes managing the 
JVE network to support both unclassified communications, ensuring seamless connectivity and 
service across the network, and coordinating with contractors responsible for classified systems 
and external trusted networks.  The Contractor shall be responsible for a full range of services as 
outlined in the Draft PWS, Attachment 1. 
 
The Government anticipates the RFP will be released under the North American Industry 
Classification System (NAICS) 541512, Computer System Design Services, with a size standard of 
$34.0 Mil. The resultant contract is expected to be base plus four years. We encourage any and all 
interested parties to attend the industry day to discuss this requirement in further detail. 
 
Please refer to this link for more information and RSVP to the event. Please submit all questions 
through the form on this link: https://www.jsf.mil/industry-day.  
 
Please feel free to reach out to Contract Specialist Sanjana Garg Sanjana.Garg@jsf.mil or 
Contracting Officer, John Meyers at John.Meyers@jsf.mil.

F-35 JOINT PROGRAM OFFICE  
DIRECTORATE OF ENTERPRISE SERVICES ACQUISITION 
 
 
 
 
Unclassified IT Follow-On 
Performance Work Statement  
(PWS) 
 
 
1.0 INTRODUCTION. 
The F-35 Lightning II Joint Program Office (JPO) leads the life-cycle program management of 
the F-35A, F-35B, and F-35C: the fifth-generation joint strike fighter air system of choice for the 
U.S. Air Force, U.S. Navy, U.S. Marine Corps, international partners, and foreign military sales 
customers.  The mandate of the JPO is to deliver a capable, available, and cost-efficient air 
system to the warfighter - outpacing key competitors to win tomorrow's high-end fight as we 
develop, deliver, and sustain war-winning fifth-generation capabilities at high-end fourth-
generation costs. The JPO mission is to ensure the F-35 is: 
• lethal, scalable, and adaptable while safeguarding warfighters and outpacing aggressors. 
• operationally sustainable by delivering parts when needed and leveraging predictive 
maintenance technologies to keep parts on wing longer while enhancing repair velocity. 
• cost efficient for the U.S. services and international partners by optimizing procedures 
across the acquisition life cycle.  
 
Scope. 
The purpose of this effort is to obtain Contractor support to provide Information Technology (IT) 
and Information Assurance (IA)/Cybersecurity Services (CS) to the F-35 Lighting II Joint 
Program Office (F-35 JPO) Virtual Enterprise (JVE) network and standalone workstations as 
well as SSE, cyber systems engineering and risk management (e.g., RMF). The IT Services 
support the F-35 JPO mission and enhance its effectiveness, efficiency, and productivity by 
providing the Government with a full range of IT and CS services.  
The service requirements consist of program management, enterprise performance management, 
enterprise architecture, emerging capabilities and requirements implementation, life cycle 
management, operations & maintenance, enterprise data management and storage, service desk 
support, IT training, end-user capabilities and support, and cybersecurity incident response. 
These services are critical to the successful fielding of F-35 mission capabilities.  


2 
 
The Contractor shall provide resources, materials, and services as necessary to perform the tasks 
defined in this PWS, except as specified in the Government-Furnished Resources and Property 
list. Operating, maintaining, and properly managing the life cycle of hardware, software, and 
services is the crucial, primary service provided by this contract. Auxiliary IT engineer support 
will be provided to the F-35 Autonomic Logistics Information System (ALIS) team, as well as 
CS support to the Air Systems team.  
The F-35’s classified communications also traverse the JVE backbone. The Contractor shall 
provide networking services in support of the classified networks requirements by maintaining 
the JVE network and coordinating connections, changes, outages, etc. with the Contractor 
responsible for the classified systems. The Contractor shall ensure that service is maintained 
across the JVE network up to the switch port feeding the Tactical Local Area Network 
Encryption (TACLANE) or other encryption device where support falls to the Contractor 
responsible for the classified system(s). 
In addition to F-35 JPO-controlled networks, Government and Contractor personnel may require 
access to services provided on other networks. The F-35 JPO has established several trusted 
connections to include:  af.mil, navy.mil, Lockheed Martin (LM) Autonomic Logistics 
Information System (ALIS), and LM Failure Reporting, Analysis and Corrective Action System 
(FRACAS). The Contractor shall maintain the JVE connections to the aforementioned systems 
and will work with those managing those systems to trouble-shoot issues when required.

3.0 TASKS/PERFORMANCE REQUIREMENTS.  
The Contractor shall provide all services and project supervision, as required in accordance with 
the Performance Work Statement (PWS). 
 
The Contractor’s team shall be responsible for performance of the tasks and activities, as 
specified within this PWS, to support the following: the Government’s day-to-day IT operations 
management processes pertaining to IT service operations; IT engineering activities; continual 
service improvement across the Government’s enterprise; and managing and maintaining CS 
integrity of all servers, devices, storage, or cloud-based computing resources from external and 
internal security threats. 
TECHNICAL OBJECTIVES  
3.1 Operations Management Services  
Operations Management Services is the maintenance and management of IT services to the F-35 
JPO including, but not limited to, telephony services (1,300+ Voice over Internet Protocol 
[VoIP] devices), video audio teleconference services (2,500+ video teleconferences [VTCs] 
annually), Network Operations Security Center (NOSC, 12 critical and 23 less critical service 
checks), network services (355 network devices, at Continental United States (CONUS), Japan, 
and Republic of Korea sites), application services and management (18+ custom applications and 
370+ software titles), and infrastructure management services (338 servers). 
3.2 Telephony Services  
Contractor shall manage Government devices, including but not limited to, laptops, desktops, 
mobile phones, tablets, and mobile hotspot devices. Support covers licensing, throughout the F-
35 JPO community within the confines of DoD and F-35 JPO cybersecurity policies and 
procedures. Contractor shall include the following services:

• Ensure seamless and uninterrupted communication through the implementation and 
continuous support of both voice and data telecommunications infrastructure. 
• Continue to explore innovative ways for improvement in Optimizing the performance, 
reliability, and scalability of telecommunication services, including VoIP, mobile 
communication systems (laptops, mobile phones, iPads, and other like-type devices,) and 
integrated networks. 
• Perform routine audits and troubleshooting to address any service degradation or failures 
within telecommunications systems. 
• Provide recommendations for technology and software refreshes that leverage other DoD 
or commercial technologies that enhance capabilities. 
• Maintain records in accordance with DoD policies, support 100 percent accountability of 
GFD (government furnished devices).  
• Conduct initial user training and assistance for use as necessary to end users upon the 
issuance or assignment of any type of phone.  
 
3.3 Video/Audio Teleconference (VTC) Services  
Contractor shall manage Non-classified Internet Protocol (IP) Router Network (NIPRNet) 
audiovisual (A/V) services for standard conference rooms, VTC rooms, and the Conferencing 
Center in addressing the following requirements:

conference rooms during core hours from 0600-1800 in Arlington, VA. 
• Provide high-quality, secure, and scalable video conferencing services to meet 
organization communication and collaboration needs, supporting both internal and 
external stakeholders. 
• Monitor and maintain the video teleconferencing infrastructure, ensuring seamless 
operation of video, audio, and screen-sharing functionality. 
• Implement and manage regular upgrades and maintenance to ensure compatibility with 
latest software versions, security protocols, and end-user devices. 
• Provide written end-user audiovisual instructions specific to each integrated audiovisual 
conference room configuration. 
• Provide end-user training on the audiovisual and collaboration applications in established 
conference rooms, VTC rooms, and the Conferencing Center upon request.  
• Daily monitoring of equipment for functional and operational readiness . Maintain 
equipment replacements on-hand to quickly repair commonly failed or recommended 
spares by sponsored system agency. 
• Coordinate with internal and external counterparts, to include Government personnel, 
contractors providing services or support for other contracts, or requirements, for 
troubleshooting or implementation of new equipment as necessary, (break/fix or new 
capability).  
• Perform patch and firmware upgrades, break/fix support, daily operations, and 
management support, including onsite assistance for special events.  
3.4 Network Operations Security Center (NOSC) 
Contractor shall manage, monitor, and report on the state of confidentiality, integrity, and 
availability of Joint Virtual Environment (JVE) critical and less critical services, including, but 
not limited to what is contained in Table 1. Critical and Less Critical Services.

PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT (PWS)

Defense Civilian Pay System

Part 1

General Information

General:

1.1 Introduction. The contractor shall provide all personnel and items necessary to perform the functional and technical support for the Defense Civilian Pay System (DCPS) as defined in this Performance Work Statement (PWS) except for those items specified as Government furnished property and services. 

1.2 Background. The primary purpose of this contract is to obtain information and technology (I&T) support for the Defense Civilian Pay System (DCPS) located at the Defense Finance and Accounting Service (DFAS), Indianapolis, IN. DCPS was selected as the standard Department of War (DoW) formally Department of Defense (DoD), civilian pay system in 1991. The system maintains pay and leave entitlement records, deductions and withholdings, time and attendance data and other pertinent employee personnel data. Through the use of DCPS, DFAS is standardizing civilian payroll policies, processes, systems and procedures throughout the Department.

Multiple accounting systems interface with DCPS by receiving one or a combination of several standard accounting interface files. These files are created on a daily, weekly or biweekly basis and are electronically transmitted to the appropriate installation level or departmental accounting system. Each disbursing officer that services a DCPS payroll office is responsible for the disbursement of funds, as vouchers and certified by the payroll office. 

The DCPS Automated Information System (AIS) is developed and maintained by a single Central Design Activity (CDA), I&T Payroll Services - Indianapolis. The CDA provides functional requirements analysis; database design and maintenance; identification of system hardware and telecommunications requirements; technical design; programming; documentation; and implementation support and training materials for customers. The CDA also monitors operation of pay processing and receipt of interfacing files between trading partners and resolves problems for customers and payroll offices. Customers of DCPS include the DoW, Health and Human Services, Department of Energy, Veterans Affairs, Executive Office of the President, and the United States Agency for Global Media.

1.3 Objectives. The overall objective of this PWS is to define the tasks necessary to obtain the full software life cycle support in the development and maintenance of DCPS.

1.4 Scope. The contractor shall provide all necessary personnel, management, materials, administrative and technical services required to meet the requirements and/or tasks outlined in this PWS. The software and non-software support services to be acquired fall within the general areas of implementing change requests to the system and performing routine system maintenance. The software and non-software support services to be acquired fall within the general areas of:

	Software Design

	Software Development

	Database Development

	Software Maintenance

	Database Maintenance

	System Change Request Requirements Analysis

Software Testing

	Software Implementation

	Configuration Management

	Release Management

	Systems Interfaces

	Customer Inquiries

	Performance Measurements

	Production Support

	Audit Readiness

	Information Assurance

1.6 Quality Assurance Plan (QAP). The contractor shall develop, maintain, and manage an effective QAP to ensure services are performed in accordance with this Performance Work Statement (PWS) and the performance standards set forth in the Performance Requirements Summary (PRS) at Technical Exhibit 1. The contractor’s QAP is the means by which it assures compliance with the work requirements and shall include procedures to identify, prevent, and ensure the non-recurrence of defective services. The plan should consider the directions provided in Section 7.1 of this PWS and will be used to collect and monitor performance data for reporting to the Contracting Officer Representative (COR). The contractor shall deliver their proposed QAP with their quote. After the initial QAP is accepted, the contractor must receive the Contracting Officer's (CO) acceptance in writing for any proposed changes, and a revised plan must be submitted within 5 business days of any changes. Unless otherwise indicated, the rating period for performance will be quarterly, with formal monthly status reports on progress.

 

1.7 Recognized Holidays.

President’s Day				Veteran’s Day

Memorial Day					Thanksgiving Day

Juneteenth National Independence Day	Christmas Day

Independence Day				

If the holiday occurs on a Saturday the holiday will be observed on Friday. If the holiday occurs on Sunday the holiday will be observed on Monday.

1.8 Hours of Operation. The contractor shall conduct business between the hours of 6:00am and 6:00pm, Monday - Friday except for federal holidays or when the Government facility is closed due to local or national emergencies, administrative closings, or similar Government directed facility closings. The contractor must at all times maintain an adequate workforce for the uninterrupted performance of all tasks defined within this PWS when the Government facility is not closed for any of the above reasons. Production Support personnel are required 24/7 to perform operations and help desk support.

1.8.1 Extended/Emergency Hours. When mission needs dictate, contractor staff shall be available to support the work described within this PWS outside of standard facility duty hours, including nights and weekends. The Contracting Officer Representative (COR), Contracting Officer (CO), or management will provide reasonable advance notice for such requirements. Except in cases of a bona fide emergency, "reasonable notice" is defined as a minimum of 48 hours. For emergency situations, the COR, CO, or management will provide notice as soon as is practicable, and the contractor shall be required to respond accordingly.

1.9 Place of Performance. The work will be performed at the DFAS Indianapolis Center or at other locations agreed to by the COR or Contracting Officer and the contractor. Travel may be required to CONUS locations to support DCPS customers. CONUS sites are predominantly military bases or other Government installations. See paragraph 1.24 for further travel information.

GENERAL INFORMATION

PLACE OF PERFORMANCE

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

DESCRIPTION

Request for Information

Enterprise Service Desk Managed Contact Center Infrastructure 

TAC RFI Number: 36C10B26Q0368

1. Introduction 

The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Enterprise Command Operations (ECO) is issuing a Request for Information (RFI) in support of a planned future solicitation for its Enterprise Service Desk Managed Contact Center Infrastructure (CCI) solution. ECO is seeking feedback and engagement from interested parties. 

See Section 3 for CCI Solution capabilities and anticipated future capabilities.

This RFI is issued for information and planning purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation nor does it restrict the Government as to the ultimate acquisition approach. In accordance with (IAW) Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 15.101(c), responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. The purpose of this RFI is to obtain market information on capable sources of supply, industry practices, and input specific to the information provided. The Government is not responsible for any cost incurred by industry in furnishing this information. All costs associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the interested party’s expense. Not responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future Request for Proposals, if any is issued. Any information submitted by respondents to this RFI is strictly voluntary. All submissions become Government property and will not be returned. Any proprietary/sensitive information must be clearly marked by the vendor. 

2. Disclaimer

The Government will not reimburse any costs incurred in responding to this market research request. Participation is voluntary, and non-response will not preclude participation in any future solicitation. The Government may use the information received to refine requirements, 

acquisition strategy, and solicitation structure

3. CCI Solution Capabilities

The current CCI solution utilizes the NICE CXOne platform. Additional features and enhancements leverage Medallia and fill integration with VA’s IT Service Management (ITSM) tool, currently ServiceNow.

3.1 Current Capabilities

The VA operates in a multi‑vendor environment in which contractors must work collaboratively, using non‑proprietary materials and coordinated processes to ensure seamless, consistent service delivery. The CCI Contractor must fully cooperate with all stakeholders, participate in required joint activities, align with VA governance, share deliverables, and support coordinated handoffs and continuous service improvements across vendors.

The CCI Contractor will provide and maintain a fully integrated up-to-date CCI solution that interoperates with VA systems, supports multi-channel contact handling, delivers intelligent routing, real-time reporting, and secure access for both onsite and remote agents. They are responsible for designing and updating call flows and automated messages, ensuring compatibility with VA firewalls and change-management processes, addressing security vulnerabilities, and staying current with OEM releases. The solution must include complete call management capabilities, service observation, required Site Reliability Engineering (SRE), and support for operational disruptions, while also supplying all associated documentation and reports.

The Contractor must deliver comprehensive performance analysis and reporting across the CCI solution, ITSM, and ESD vendor operations, using automated monitoring tools, defined metrics, surveys, and trend analyses to assess service quality, Service Level Agreement (SLA)adherence, and customer satisfaction. The Contractor must also maintain robust data management practices, provide dashboards and reporting interfaces, support quality assurance reviews, and ensure continuity through coordinated disaster recovery, contingency, and escalation plans aligned with VA standards.

The CCI Solution has the following core capabilities:

Intelligent Routing & Queuing

Intelligent, skills‑based routing across modalities (voice, chat, web)

Universal queue; dynamic prioritization; overflow and default routing

Multi‑vendor routing and support for Moves, Adds, Changes, and Deletes (MACD) on queues and routing configs

Real‑time, rules‑driven routing (skills, availability, SLA, language, presence)

Warm/cold transfers; conferencing; multi‑channel transfer capability

Ability to use Interactive Voice Response (IVR)‑captured data for routing; omni‑channel context passing

Simulation/testing tools for routing; emergency routing controls

Expansion of ports and routing resiliency

Interactive Voice Response (IVR)

Visual IVR and speech/Natural Language Understanding (NLU)‑driven automated interactions

Elastic IVR ports for surges; configurable greetings and announcements

Database integration for data retrieval, verification, and self‑service

Dual-Tone Multi-Frequency (DTMF)/speech capture; transcription and reporting in English & Spanish

Natural speech recognition (English & Spanish) with high accuracy

Survey capability; accessibility support (Teletypewriter (TTY)/ American Standard Code for Information Interchange (ASCII))

Comprehensive reporting, real‑time caller activity visibility

Ability to update messages rapidly; integrate with backend databases

Caller authentication; self‑service transactions; multi‑language support

Quality Management

Real‑time monitoring of interactions, queues, agents

100% or selective voice/screen recording; remote playback

Quality Management forms, scorecards, evaluators; multiple scoring systems

Call search, tagging, flagging; trend analysis across channels

Speech analytics; archive retrieval; Federal Information Processing Standards (FIPS)‑compliant encryption

Supervisor monitoring, targeted recording, and evaluation tools

Integration of metadata, attachments, transcripts (including Spanish translation)

Recording & Monitoring

Full multimedia recording (voice, chat) with metadata capture

Archive, playback, selective or random recording

FIPS‑compliant encryption; configurable business‑rule recording

Synchronization of audio + chat transcript; search across metadata

Export and movement of archived data; masking of sensitive information

Ability to pause/stop live recording; apply speech analytics

Storage Requirements

Capacity for 100% call recording + 20% screen capture

National Archives and Records Administration (NARA)‑compliant retention: 6 months online, 18‑month archive

Elastic storage; ability to move data between archive and online

Agent Features

Softphone/desk phone support with full call controls

Screen pops with customer/IVR data; toll‑free/local dialing

Real‑time visibility into blocked calls

Agent state management (ready/not ready, reason codes)

Local/global phone books; voicemail; customizable buttons

Free seating with preserved metrics

Remote & End‑User Training

Train‑the‑trainer model; comprehensive system training

Government‑approved curriculum; reusable training materials (videos, docs)

Virtual interactive training; semi‑annual updates

Data analysis to identify training needs

Supervisor Tools

Real‑time team/agent status; silent monitoring; barge‑in/intercept

Alerts on agent events; escalation handling; assistance tools

Real‑time skill assignment changes; reason code management

Custom dashboards; reporting across all channels

Broadcast messaging; whisper coaching; filtering and alerts

Extensive reporting, drill‑down, and permission‑based access

Agent & Supervisor Desktop Tools

Softphone with call control, agent state changes, reason codes

Performance statistics; multi‑line appearance

Manager views: team status, forced state changes, reassignments

Web Chat – Core Capabilities

Secure chat integrated with ITSM; multi‑session handling

Transcripts, history, attachments, pre‑defined responses

Routing by business rules/skills; supervisor monitoring/coaching

Surveys; chat bot escalation; KM integration

Queueing, after‑hours messaging, browser compatibility

Workforce Management (WFM)

Forecasting (long/short‑term), scheduling, and “what‑if” modeling

Real‑time and historical adherence monitoring

Multi‑site, multi‑skill planning; scheduling templates

Intra‑day management (reassign, overflow, call‑flow changes)

Reporting on adherence, staffing, agent activities

Virtual Call Queue

Automatic callback with estimated wait times and retries

Maintain queue place when caller opts for callback

Configurable triggers (queue depth, wait time, time of day)

Voicemail message capability; multi‑timezone support

Reporting: successful/failed callbacks, usage, wait‑time accuracy

Automated Call Survey

Post‑call and delayed call‑back surveys (DTMF/voice)

Recording of comments; scoring, weighting, configuration

Reporting (15‑minute segments to yearly); trend and statistics

Linking results to interactions and agents; export tools

Text (SMS)

SMS chat with live agent; attachments; automated replies

Routing by business rules, keywords, and phone number

Ability to shift from automated to live agent without losing context

Confirmation texts; integration with VA Knowledge Base

Computer Telephony Integration (CTI)

Screen pops with caller and history data

Integration with third‑party systems via standard APIs

Support for intelligent routing, call control, reporting, blending

Screen Capture

Capture agent activity across multimedia interactions

Secure, FIPS‑compliant capture, storage, search, playback, export, and archival of interactions with full metadata

Configurable business rules controlling when and how interactions and screens are recorded

Real‑time authorized monitoring of agent screens

Enhanced Features

Web Callback functionality with agent‑availability–based routing and full VA operating‑hours integration

AI‑driven features including AutoPilot (voice assistant), Agent Co‑Pilot, and Supervisor Co‑Pilot

Full integration with ServiceNow, Medallia, reporting tools, and major‑incident IVR workflows

Advanced authentication and security enhancements including one‑time passcodes (SMS/IVR) and voice biometrics

3.2 Future Capabilities

The CCI solution requires integration, testing, and implementation of VA approved Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning (ML), Robotic Process Automation (RPA), Speech/Sentiment Analytics or third-party applications into the CCI solution using industry standard APIs and repeatable, agile software and system engineering processes. In addition the CCI solution is anticipated to expand into the following future capabilities:

Conversational AI (Voice & Chat)	

Natural language voice bots and chatbots

Multilingual conversational AI

Intent recognition with contextual memory

Dynamic conversation flow generation

Voice AI with natural prosody and interruption handling

AI Intent-Based Routing	

Routes contacts based on detected intent, sentiment, customer value and/or agent expertise

Predictive Routing	

Optimizes for CSAT, FCR and AHT

Journey-Aware Routing	

Considers prior interactions, unresolved tickets, open incidents and channel switching

Proactive and Predictive Service	

Proactive outreach notifying customers of outages, proactive service alerts and AI-triggered outreach when behavior indicates trouble

Predictive issue resolution when detecting potential service failures and automatically opening tickets or contacting customers

Workforce Engagement Management	

AI forecasting of contact volumes

Automated scheduling

Skill-based workforce planning

Real-time adherence monitoring

Agent coaching recommendations

Hyper-Personalized Customer Experience	

Customer identity resolution

Interaction history

Behavioral signals

Real-time personalization

Intelligent Process Automation	

Auto ticket creation

Backend task automation

System integration workflows

Automated service fulfillment

Knowledge Intelligence	

AI-generated Knowledge Articles

Knowledge GAP detection

Auto-recommendation during calls (within IVR and for agents)

Knowledge effectiveness scoring

Automatic knowledge creation from resolved cases

Real-Time Operational Intelligence	

Real-time service dashboards

Anomaly detection

Predictive workload forecasting

Customer journey analytics

Root cause identification

Integrated Service Management	

Ticket creation from calls

IVR context passed into tickets

Automated updates between systems

Incident correlation

Service status awareness

Simulation-Based Agent Training	

AI-generated training scenarios

Simulated customer interactions

Automated feedback

Experience Orchestration 	

Customer journey orchestration

Cross-system workflow execution

Real-time decision engines

Adaptive service workflows

4.0 Submittal Instructions

All responsible sources may submit a capability statement in accordance with the information below. Interested parties shall provide a maximum of five-pages briefly addressing their recommended solution and approach. All responses should at minimum provide: 

Recommended approach to maintaining, enhancing, and/or replacing ECO’s current CCI solution and associated benefits/risks to this approach

Flexible cost-effective Firm-Fixed-Price licensing models for the CCI solution to support fluctuating helpdesk agents and other users

Strategic opportunities for future capabilities and enhancements

Recommended contract vehicle, 

In addition, all responses should list your company business size and status.

Responses are due no later than 10:00AM ET Monday, May 4, 2026  via email to Dan DiNocera, Contract Specialist, at Daniel.dinocera@va.gov; Andrea Caltabilota, Contract Specialist, at Andrea.Caltabilota@va.gov; and Evan Schlisserman, Contracting Officer, at Evan.Schlisserman@va.gov. Performance Work Statement - Maintenance and Calibration of Clemex MMT-X7 Automated Microhardness Tester 
1.0  Background and Objectives: 
The Clemex MMT-X7 Dual Automated Microhardness Tester with CMT and Vision Lite V8.1 is a testing apparatus that 
automates the process of creating and measuring indentations to determine material hardness. The objective of this 
contract is to procure an on-site service agreement for maintenance and calibration for the Clemex MMT-X7 consisting of 
one (1) base and two (2) option years. These services are necessary to maintain the machine's capabilities and support 
ongoing testing programs. 
2.0 Scope of Work: 
The contractor shall provide a service and calibration agreement for the Clemex ID 5470 - MMT-X7 Dual Automated  
Microhardness Tester (System ID: 05470). The service agreement shall include, at a minimum, one (1) On-site Dual CMT 
Calibration service visit scheduled within the contract period of performance (including Engineer labor and travel), parts 
and their installation during the visit, and telephone/remote support for the duration of the contract. 
The service plan is composed of the following components from the manufacturer: 
ClemexCare CMT 12-month plan: Technical support, remote hardware problem diagnostics, and free software 
updates containing the latest features. 
On-site Dual CMT Calibration: Includes labor and travel for the calibration visit. 
ClemexCare Vision Lite 12-month plan: Technical support, remote hardware problem diagnostics, and 
free software updates containing the latest features.

• Task orders issued under this item are primarily for the production of a Life Safety and Fire Risk Assessment per DO/RM 58:

complete evaluation of each park structure’s construction, function, operational support systems, and occupancy as they impact fire

required in the performance of specific task order requirements. Engineering or technical support documents that address the

3.0 Professional Licenses and Registrations for “Required Disciplines” 
 
At a minimum, the contractor must be able to provide fire protection engineers with experience in condition assessments, work in 
government buildings, and work involving historic buildings, collections, and archives. Assessments will require a thorough 
knowledge of the most recent edition of the International Code Council (ICC) codes to include the International Fire Code (IFC) and 
the International Wildland-Urban Interface Code (IWUIC), and the National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) codes and standards 
referenced therein, including NFPA 70: National Electrical Code (NEC). Specific policy related requirements that differ from code, 
such as those in DO/RM 58: Structural Fire Management or the Structural Fire Design Guide, will be provided when needed. All work 
where a fire protection engineer is required is to be accomplished by a registered professional fire protection engineer in the United 
States. All task orders will require the contractor to appoint a senior fire protection engineer as the project manager who will be 
responsible for review of all submittals prior to submission to the NPS. Particular tasks may require specific skills and certifications, 
which will be listed in the task orders when issued.

1 Program Description  
The Advanced Research Projects Agency for Health (ARPA-H) invites small businesses 
to submit research proposals under this Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) 
and Small Business Technology Transfer (STTR) solicitation. All eligible organizations 
with relevant expertise are encouraged to apply (See section 2 for eligibility 
requirements). The topics are described in Section 8 Research Topics, and new topics 
may be added periodically. 
The mission of ARPA-H is to accelerate better health outcomes by supporting the 
development of high-impact solutions to society’s most challenging health problems. 
Innovative small businesses can contribute to this mission through the ARPA-H Small 
Business Program (SBP). ARPA-H holds small business performers to the same 
rigorous technical standards as other ARPA-H performers. Commercialization and 
transition are key elements of the ARPA-H SBP, and ARPA-H provides tailored support 
to help performers overcome a range of challenges. 
This solicitation contains specific topic areas where ARPA-H is seeking proposals from 
small businesses for high-impact solutions. Proposals are expected to use novel 
approaches to achieve revolutionary advances in science, technology, or systems. 
Specifically excluded are proposals for open-ended research projects or that 
represent an incremental advance in the current state of the art. Additionally, 
proposals directed towards policy changes, traditional education and training, or 
construction of physical infrastructure are outside the scope of the ARPA-H mission 
and will not be considered. 
 
 
SHORTCUT TO TECHNICAL TOPICS 
 
  

 
 5 
1.1 Program Phases 
The SBIR/STTR program organizes projects into three phases: 
• Phase I: Feasibility 
• Phase II: Full Research / Research & Development (R&D) Effort 
• Phase III: Commercialization (Not part of this solicitation) 
These phases build on each other, with each subsequent phase the maturity of the 
technology should advance so that the ﬁnal output is ready for commercialization. 
Once a performer has successfully completed a Phase I, ARPA-H (or any other 
agency) can invite them to submit a Phase II proposal to continue development. 
Note: This solicitation does not accept Phase III proposals. 
1.1.1 Phase I: Feasibility 
The objective of Phase I is to determine the scientiﬁc or technical and commercial 
feasibility of the proposed solution. Typically, a Phase I proposer has a solution 
concept but has not yet built a prototype to test technical feasibility.  
This phase is intended to de-risk the effort and is substantially smaller in scope and 
cost than subsequent phases. At ARPA-H, a typical Phase I lasts 6-12 months but may 
last longer in rare circumstances. The result of a Phase I is a proof-of-concept or early-
stage prototype. 
NOTE: Performers with a Phase I award from ARPA-H may submit a Phase II proposal 
to ARPA-H to continue the development of their technology. This usually occurs in the 
last quarter of the period of performance or shortly after contract completion. The 
performer should notify the ARPA-H SBP of their intention to submit a proposal, and 
ARPA-H will provide submission instructions. While all Phase I participants are 
welcome to submit a Phase II proposal, not all will be selected for a Phase II award. 
ARPA-H may also invite performers to submit a Phase II proposal outside of specified 
solicitation timeframes. 
1.1.2 Phase II: Full Research/Research & Development (R&D) Effort 
The objective of Phase II is to further develop a technology or R&D effort initiated in 
Phase I. During Phase II, performers advance from a proof-of-concept into a 
commercially viable prototype. Phase II awards are larger in scope and cost than 
Phase I efforts and typically last 12-24 months, although they can be longer or shorter. 
Individual topics may include estimates regarding the anticipated project duration 
which are meant to guide proposers rather than be hard requirements. 
While the speciﬁc Phase II activities in a project are case-speciﬁc, they usually include 
continued improvement of the technology along with evidence generation. This may 

 
 6 
include completing pre-clinical work, conducting enabling studies for an 
Investigational New Drug (IND), or even ﬁrst-in-human trials. At ARPA-H, it is common 
for a Phase II to conclude with an FDA submission (when applicable). 
Additional emphasis is placed on commercialization during Phase II. Performers must 
submit a detailed Commercialization Plan and provide regular updates. This is a key 
activity of Phase II efforts at ARPA-H and necessary to prepare for a successful 
transition. During Phase II, performers often develop or initiate strategic partnerships, 
manufacturing plans, regulatory engagements, go-to-market strategies, and user-
testing (these examples are meant to be illustrative rather than exhaustive or 
prescriptive).   
A Phase II may be awarded as (a) a follow-on to a Phase I award, (b) a Direct-to-Phase 
II, or (c) integrated into a Fast Track project.  
1.2 Award Types 
In some instances, ARPA-H will consider Fast Track proposals that combine Phases I 
and II, or Direct-to-Phase II proposals that skip Phase I. Not all phases or award types

PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT (PWS) 
 
Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) Cemetery Enterprise Application Support 
(CEAS) 
 
PART 1 
GENERAL INFORMATION 
 
1.  General:  This is a non-personnel service contract to provide Cemetery Enterprise Application 
Support (CEAS) to the Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) for Army National 
Military Cemeteries (ANMC) and the Office of Army Cemeteries (OAC).  The OCIO CEAS is 
responsible for support for the following areas, project management, change management and 
governance, and Enterprise Architecture (EA) and OCIO strategic planning support.  This is not 
a software development contract. 
 
1.1  Description of Services/Introduction:  The Contractor shall provide all personnel, 
equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and other items and 
non-personnel services necessary to perform the tasks as defined in this PWS except, for those 
items specified as government furnished property and services.  Contractor shall perform to the 
standards defined in this contract. 
 
1.2  Background: The Office of Army Cemeteries (OAC) is defined by Public Law as the 
statutory authority to manage and oversee operations at Arlington National Cemetery, the United 
States Soldiers’ and Airmen’s Home National Cemetery.  The Department of the Army created a 
special staff Principal, the Executive Director for Army Cemeteries and a policy oversight 
directorate and compliance for all Army cemeteries, both post cemeteries and national 
cemeteries.  In accordance with this law, this PWS outlines the contractor responsibilities in 
providing program management support, defining and establishing business processes, 
developing, implementing and sustaining plans for operations and maintenance for ANMC/OAC 
business systems which contain Department of War Cemetery data.  Additionally, the contractor 
shall provide enterprise architecture support in accordance with the DOW Architecture 
Framework.  Based on the special significance and the attention that national and post cemeteries 
receive, strict adherences to these specifications are essential. 
 
1.3  Objectives: The objective of this effort is to provide program management support across the 
evolving Cemetery Management suite of cloud applications.  The basic services in this PWS 
shall enable the Project Management Office to manage the development and operations of IT 
based systems to conduct cemetery operations and oversee the Change Control Board (CCB) and 
Enterprise Architecture Governance Board (EAGB).  These services shall be leveraged to align 
IT investments with ANMC/OAC strategic goals and objectives outlined in the ANMC Goals 
and Objectives and OAC Strategic Plan. 
 
1.4  Scope: The Contractor shall provide specialized professional expertise and program 
management support to implement the goals of the Government and OCIO operations and 
management.  The Government intends to acquire contract support to all activities outlined in 
this Performance Work Statement in support of the Army’s current and future goals and 

 
 2 
objectives for program level planning, operations and maintenance, and migrations.  The scope 
and project shall contain tasks and milestones to allow for efficient planning and budgeting for 
IT solutions. Scope will include inter-agency coordination with external cemetery stakeholders to 
include but not limited to Depmant of War Mortuaty and Casulaity Affairs, American Battle 
Monuments Commission (ABMC) and National Cemetery Administration (NCA) Veterans 
Affairs (VA).  
 
1.5 Period of Performance:  The period of performance shall be a base twelve (12) months with  
three (3) twelve (12) month options from date of award.  Option periods may be exercised in 
accordance with FAR Clause 52.217-9 entitled, “Option to Extend the Term of the Contract”. 
The period of performance reads as follows: 
 
Base Year:   19 Novmeber 2026 – 18 November 2027    
Option Year I:  19 Novmeber 2027 – 18 November 2028   
Option Year II: 19 Novmeber 2028 – 18 November 2029 
Option Year III:  19 Novmeber 2029 – 18 November 2030   
 
1.6  General Information 
1.6.1  Quality Control: Quality control is the responsibility of the contractor.  The contractor is 
responsible for the delivery of quality services/supplies to the government (see FAR 52.246-1, 
Contractor Inspection Requirements). 
The contractor shall develop, implement and maintain an effective quality control system that 
includes a written quality control plan (QCP).  The QCP shall implement standardized 
procedure/methodology for monitoring and documenting contract performance to ensure all 
contract requirements are met.  The contractors’ QCP must contain a systematic approach to 
monitor operations to ensure acceptable services/products are provided to the government.   The 
QCP, as a minimum, shall address continuous process improvement; procedures for scheduling, 
conducting and documentation of inspection; discrepancy identification and correction; 
corrective action procedures to include procedures for addressing government discovered non-
conformances; procedures for root cause analysis to identify the root cause and root cause 
corrective action to prevent re-occurrence of discrepancies; procedures for trend analysis; and 
procedures for collecting and addressing customer feedback/complaints.  The contractor shall 
upon request provide to the government its quality control documentation The Contractor shall 
deliver the QCP within thirty (30) days after contract award.  QCP must address test plan 
development, release coordination with ANMC and its stakeholders, and code promotion 
documentation. After acceptance of the quality control plan the contractor shall receive the 
contracting officer’s acceptance in writing of any proposed change to its QC system.   
 
1.6.2  Quality Assurance:  The Government shall evaluate the contractor’s performance under 
this contract in accordance with the Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan (QASP).  This plan is 
primarily focused on what the Government must do to ensure that the contractor has performed 
in accordance with the performance standards.  It defines how the performance standards will be 
applied, the frequency of surveillance, and the minimum acceptable defect rate(s). 
 
 
 
 

 
 3 
1.6.3  Federal Government Holidays: ANMC and OAC observe the following Federal holidays: 
 
            New Year’s Day   1st day of January 
 Martin Luther King Jr. Day   3rd Monday of January 
 Presidents Day   3rd Monday of February 
 Memorial Day    Last Monday of May 
 Juneteenth Day   19th day of June 
 Independence Day    4th day of July 
 Labor Day    1st Monday of September 
 Columbus Day   2nd Monday of October 
 Veterans Day    11th day of November 
 Thanksgiving Day   4th Thursday of November 
 Christmas Day               25th day of December 
 
1.6.4  Hours of Operation: The Contractor is responsible for conducting business to best align 
with ANMC’s operating hours between 0600-1800 Eastern Standard Time, Monday through 
Friday, except federal holidays or when the Government facility is closed due to local or national 
emergencies, administrative closings, occupational safety or health hazards, or similar 
Government directed facility closings.  The Contractor shall maintain an adequate work force at 
all times for the uninterrupted performance of the tasks defined within this PWS when the 
Government facility is not closed for these reasons.  When hiring personnel, the Contractor shall 
keep in mind the stability and continuity of the workforce are essential. 
 
1.6.5  Place of Performance:  The primary place of performance shall be Arlington National 
Cemetery and Contractor facility. 
 
1.6.6  Type of Contract:  The Government anticipates award of a firm fixed price contract. 
 
1.6.7  Security Requirements: This is an Unclassified contract.  There are no requirements for 
Contractor personnel to have route access to classified Government information in the 
performance of this contract; however, Contractors with elevated privileges shall be required to 
have/maintain a SECRET clearance in order to access any environment(s) connecting or crossing 
Army or DOW Information systems.  If Contractor personnel are required to attend meetings, 
briefings or work on a full time basis on site at a secure Government facilities, a valid, current 
final SECRET eligibility and access must be granted and posted in the Joint Personnel 
Adjudication System (JPAS) to gain access. 
 
1.6.7.1  P hysical Security:  The contractor shall be responsible for safeguarding all government 
equipment, information and property provided for contractor use. At the close of each work period, 
government facilities, equipment, and materials shall be secured. 
1.6.7.2  Key, Key Code.  All references to keys include key cards or fobs (and also  implies any 
other government issued means of access to allow the contractor to enter any ANMC secured area 
or facility. AN MC shall issue key cards/codes to the Contractor (and subcontractor). The 
Contractor shall be responsible for keys and key codes provided by the Government.  Keys shall 
not be lost, misplaced, or duplicated by Contractor personnel, nor used by unauthorized Contractor 
personnel. The Contractor shall develop and implement procedures to ensure that keys issued to 

 
 4 
the Contractor by the Government are safeguarded. The Contractor developed procedures covering 
key control shall be included in the Quality Control Plan. Such procedures shall include turn-in of 
any issued keys by personnel who no longer require access to locked areas.  
The Contractor shall prohibit the use of Government issued keys/key cards by any persons other 
than the Contractor’s employees. The Contractor shall prohibit the opening of locked areas by 
Contractor employees to permit entrance of persons other than Contr actor employees engaged in 
the performance of assigned work in those areas, or personnel authorized entrance by the 
Contracting Officer. 
The Contractor shall report any occurrence of duplicated, misplaced, or lost keys to the Contracting 
Officer and COR within twenty-four (24) hours after discovery of occurrence and submit a written 
report to the Contracting Officer by close of business the  next workday. The written report shall 
provide complete details relating to duplication, misplacement, and/or loss. 
1.6.7.2.1. In the event keys, other than master keys, are lost or duplicated, the c ontractor shall, 
upon direction of the contracting officer, re-key or replace the affected lock or locks; however, the 
government, at its option, may replace the affected lock or locks or perform re-keying.  When the 
replacement of locks or re -keying is performed by the government, the total cost of re -keying or 
the replacement of the lock or locks shall be deducted from the monthly payment due the 
contractor.  In the event a master key is lost or duplicated, all locks and keys for that system shall 
be replaced by the government and the total cost deducted from the monthly payment due the 
contractor. 
 
1.6.7.2.2. The contractor shall prohibit the use of government issued keys/key cards by any 
persons other than the contractor’s employees.  The contractor shall prohibit the opening of 
locked areas by contractor employees to permit entrance of persons other than contractor 
employees engaged in the performance of assigned work in those areas, or personnel authorized 
entrance by the contracting officer. 
 
1.6.7.3 Lock Combinations  The contractor shall establish and implement methods of ensuring that 
all lock combinations are not revealed to unauthorized persons.  The c ontractor shall ensure that 
lock combinations are changed when personnel having access to the combinations no longer have 
a need to know such combinations.  These procedures shall be included in the Contractor’s Quality 
Control Plan. 
 
1.6.8 Federal Facility Access, General Protection, Security Policies and Procedures. Contractor 
personnel (including subcontractors’ employees) entering government properties shall abide by 
the applicable installation, facility and area commander’s access and local policies and 
procedures.  The contractor shall provide required information for background checks to meet 
installation access requirements.  Contractor workforce shall also comply with all personal 
identity verification requirements as directed by DOW, HQDA, and/or local policy.  In addition 
to the changes clause otherwise authorized by this contract, should the Force Protection 
Condition Level (FPCON) or Health Protection Condition Level (HPCON) at any individual 
facility or installation change, the government may require changes in contractor security matters 
or processes.  Contractor employees, including sub-contractors, shall immediately report 
suspicious activity to the ANMC G2/3 - Directorate of Security and Operations at 703-614-4303 

 
 5 
during business hours, and 703-588-2800 during after-hours. Emergencies should be reported 
immediately by calling 911. 
 
ANMC/OAC Contractor personnel will be issued vehicle passes (hangtag/placards) that must be 
displayed when entering the Cemetery (regardless of whether the vehicle is privately or company 
owned, or as designated by ANMC G2/3 - Directorate of Security and Operations. The 
contractor shall maintain a current list of all vehicles and individuals issued such passes. The 
contractor shall provide a list of these vehicles to include make, model, color and associated 
license plate information to the COR within five (5) days of contract award and within one (1) 
day of any changes to the list through contract period of performance.   Additionally, contractors 
shall park in designated parking locations, as directed by ANMC, and if required, access/key 
cards shall be issued to Key Personnel to enter secured parking areas (see Section 1.6.7.2 Key 
and Key Control). 
 
1.6.9 Visit Notification.  Contractors visiting ANC shall provide 24 hour notice for all site-visits, 
provide vehicle information, and proper contractor identification may be required. Contractor 
employees whose duties require on site work at ANMC or OAC will be issued a photo ID badge 
and must be presented or visible to ANMC/OAC staff. 
 
1.6.10   Key Personnel and Special Qualifications:  The Government considers the Senior Project

INFORMATION TERMS OF USE AGREEMENT (N00024-26-R-5510) 
 
As part of Request For Information N00024-26-R-5510 and any 
subsequent synopsis and/or solicitation issued under the same 
notice, you may receive AN/SPY-6(V) radar technical data and 
other Government Furnished Information (GFI) upon Government 
receipt and verification of your DD Form 2345 Military Critical 
Technical Data Agreement and receipt of the executed Terms of 
Use Agreement herein. These documents shall only be used in 
connection with the above referenced notice. 
 
AN/SPY-6(V) GFI is controlled in accordance with the following: 
 
DISTRIBUTION STATEMENT D:  Distribution authorized to 
Department of Defense (DoD) and U.S. DoD contractors only 
(Critical Technology). Other requests shall be referred to 
the Program Executive Office, Integrated Warfare Systems 
(PEO IWS 2.0), Washington Navy Yard, 1333 Isaac Hull Ave 
SE, Washington, DC 20376. 
 
WARNING: This document contains technical data whose export 
is restricted by the Arms Export Control Act (Title 22, 
U.S.C. Sec. 2751 et seq.) or the Export Administration Act 
of 1979 (Title 50, U.S.C., App 2401, et seq.), as amended.  
Violations of these export laws are subject to severe 
criminal penalties. Disseminate in accordance with 
provisions of DoD Directive 5230.25. 
 
DESTRUCTION NOTICE: For Unclassified or Limited 
Dissemination Documents destroy by any method that will 
prevent disclosure of contents or reconstruction of the 
document. 
 
In order to facilitate your review, you are granted authority to 
make copies for distribution internal to your company. All 
copies are property of the U.S. Government and must be 
controlled in accordance with DoD 5220.22-M, National Industrial 
Security Program Operating Manual (NISPOM) and the terms of your 
Company’s Defense Security Service (DSS) approved document 
handling procedures.
