CLASSIFICATION CODE: D - IT and Telecom - Information Technology and Telecommunications 
 
TITLE: Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) Performance Measurement Support Services 
 
SOLICITATION NUMBER: 1333ND26QNB670135 
 
RESPONSE DATE: 05/05/2026 
   
CONTACT POINTS: Robert Cowins, Contract Specialist, (301) 975-8335 
        Hing Pan Wong, Contracting Officer, (301) 975-6289 
 
The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) has a requirement for the procurement V2X 
Performance Measurement Support Services to be utilized by the Communication Technology 
Laboratory (CTL) at NIST, Gaithersburg, MD campus.  
 
(I) This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products or commercial services prepared 
in accordance with the format in part 12 - Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial 
Services as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement 
constitutes the only solicitation; quotations are being requested and a written solicitation will not be 
issued. 
 
(II) The solicitation number is 1333ND26QNB670135 and this solicitation is a Request for Quotation 
(RFQ). This acquisition is being solicited as 100% small business set-aside. 
 
(III) The solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through 
Federal Acquisition Circular (FAC) 2025-06 Published August 27, 2025 and Effective October 1, 2025 
and the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO), supplemented by Department of Commerce Acquisition 
Policy.   
 
(IV) The associated North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this procurement 
is 541690 - Other Scientific and Technical Consulting Services, with a small business size standard of 
19 million in annual revenue. 
 
(V)  All offerors shall provide a firm-fixed-price quotation for the following line item(s):

(VI) The requirements for the line items to be acquired above are in the attached Statement of Work

Attachment 1: Statement of Work: 5G Open Radio Access Network Time-Sensitive Networking Support

Attachment 2: Applicable Provisions and Clauses 
 
(VII) Date(s) and place(s) of delivery and acceptance and FOB point are required in accordance with 
the attached Statement of Work document. 
 
(VIII) Interested parties must possess an ACTIVE registration in the System for Award Management 
system, www.SAM.gov, when submitting a quotation and shall continue to be registered until time of 
award, during performance, and through final payment of any contract resulting from this solicitation. 
The Contracting Officer shall confirm that quoters have an “active” registration at the www.sam.gov 
website upon receipt of the quotation. If the SAM.gov registration is not active, the quotation will not be 
considered for award  
 
(IX) The provision at FAR 52.212-1, Instructions to Offerors— Commercial Products and Commercial 
Services (DEVIATION Jan 2026), applies to this acquisition. See Addendum to FAR 52.212-1 below. 
 
Addendum to FAR 52.212-1, Instructions to Offerors – Commercial Products and Commercial 
Services (DEVIATION Jan 2026): 
DUE DATE FOR QUOTATIONS 
Offerors shall submit their electronic quotations, via email, so that NIST receives them not later than 
12:00pm Eastern Time, 05/05/2026. E-mail quotations shall be submitted directly to the Contract 
Specialist at robert.cowins@nist.gov. 
 
Please reference the RFQ number in the subject line of all email communications. Quotations shall not 
be deemed received by the Government until the quotation is received in the e-mail inbox set forth 
above. 
 
INQUIRIES: 
Offerors must submit all questions concerning this solicitation in writing to both the Contract Specialist 
robert.cowins@nist.gov. Questions should be received no later than 04/28/2026. All responses to 
timely submitted questions, will be made in writing, without identification of the questioner, and will be 
included in an amendment to the solicitation. Even if provided in other form, only the responses 
included in the amendment to the solicitation will be deemed as the Government’s formal response 
and govern performance of the contract.  
 
QUOTATION PREPARATION INSTRUCTIONS:  
 
All quotations shall conform to solicitation provisions/clauses and be prepared in accordance with this 
section. The quotation shall be clearly and concisely written as well as be neat and logically 
assembled. All pages of the quotation shall be appropriately numbered.  
  

 
 
The Offeror’s quotation shall be clearly divided into the following distinct volumes: 
 
Volume I – Technical Quotation 
Volume II – Price Quotation  
Volume III – Terms and Conditions 
 
 
Volume I - Technical Quotation: 
 
The Offeror shall submit one (1) copy of their technical quotation, electronically, via E-mail to the 
Contract Specialist identified above. The technical quotation shall address the following:  
 
Technical Capability:  
The offeror shall submit technical approach and capability documentation which may include a 
narrative, charts, graphs, tables, drawings, product / service literature, and as applicable, 
demonstrated authority to provide the necessary items and perform the required services identified 
in the Statement of Work/Specifications document (Attachment 1). The documentation shall 
clearly describe, in sufficient detail, the vendor's authority, proposed items, resources and 
methods to successfully fulfill the requirements including specifications, performance capability 
requirements, delivery schedules, warranties, and all service requirements. The submission shall 
clearly identify each line item above. The submission must demonstrate that the proposed system 
meets or exceeds each minimum requirement described within the attached statement of work 
document by providing a citation between the statement of work paragraph and the relevant 
section of the technical description or product literature.  The offeror must not simply state they 
will meet or exceed the requirement; evidence must be provided. If applicable, evidence that the 
quoter is authorized by the manufacturer to provide the item(s) in the quotation shall be included.  
 
Past Performance: 
The offeror shall submit up to 3 examples of relevant past performance performed within the last 3 
to 5 years. Examples should be of work similar in scope, size and complexity to this requirement.  
The description of each reference described in this section shall not exceed one single-sided page. 
For each of the contracts, the quoter shall provide the following information:  
• Contract number 
• Client’s name and address 
• Total contract value 
• Period of performance 
• Identification of role played by quoter (i.e., Prime Contractor, Subcontractor, etc.) 
• Narrative describing the requirement and its relevance to the current requirement 
• Name of contracting officer or point of contact, telephone number and e-mail address 
 
The quoter is encouraged to focus on prior projects encompassing the same RFQ requirements and 
describe how these requirements were specifically supported by the quoter. The quoter may use 
prior experiences in which they served as a prime contractor or subcontractor; however, past 
performance as a prime contractor may instill higher confidence. 
 
 
 

 
Volume II - Price Quotation: 
 
The offeror shall submit one (1) copy of their entire quotation, electronically, via E-mail to the 
Contract Specialist identified above. The price quotation shall address, at minimum, the following 
information.  
 
a) The solicitation number  
b) The name, phone number, and email address of the quoter's/contractor’s point of contact; 
c) Unique Entity Identifier # for quoter's/contractor’s active SAM.Gov registration. 
d) A firm fixed price for each required line item, including a unit price and total amount where 
applicable, and the aggregate quoted firm fixed price for the requirement. Where the 
Government has identified a line item as requiring a Not to Exceed price, quoters shall comply 
with this. 
e) If applicable, Shipping and Delivery costs must be included in the quotation either as a 
separate line item or contained in the total price of the quote. The quotation shall include a 
total firm fixed price for the requirement that includes all shipping/delivery costs 
f) Any applicable discount terms.  
 
Volume III – Terms and Conditions: 
 
The offeror shall review the provision and clauses attachment and complete any required 
information as record via a separate volume response to this solicitation.   
 
Note: System updates may lag policy updates. The System for Award Management (SAM) may 
continue to require entities to complete representations based on provisions that are not included 
in this solicitation. Contracting officers will rely on representations from offers based on provisions 
in the solicitation. Entities are not required to, nor are they able to, update their entity registration to 
remove these representations in SAM. 
 
Acceptance of Terms and Conditions: 
If the contractor objects to any of the terms and conditions contained in this solicitation, the contractor 
shall state "The terms and conditions in the solicitation are acceptable to be included in the award 
document with the exception, deletion, or addition of the following:" [Contractor shall list exception(s) 
and rationale for the exception(s)]. It is the sole responsibility of the contractor to identify in their 
quotation any exceptions to the terms and conditions of the solicitation. If the contractor does not 
include such a statement, the submission of a quotation in response to this solicitation will be regarded 
as the Contractor's acceptance of the Government's terms and conditions for inclusion into the 
resultant purchase order (PO).  
  
Note: This procurement is not being conducted under the GSA Federal Supply Schedule (FSS) program 
or another Government-Wide Area Contract (GWAC). If a quoter submits a quotation based upon an 
FSS or GWAC contract, the Government will accept the proposed price. However, the terms and 
conditions stated herein will be included in any resultant purchase order, not the terms and conditions 
of the Quoter’s FSS or GWAC contract, and the statement required above shall be included in the 
quotation.    
 

 
 
 
Basis of Award 
 
Evaluation Factors 
  
Award shall be made to the offeror whose quotation offers the best value to the Government price and 
other factors considered. The Government will evaluate quotations based on the following evaluation 
criteria listed in descending order of importance: 1) Technical Capability 2) Technical Key Personnel, 3) 
Past Performance, and 4) Price. All non-price factors, individually and when combined, are more 
important than price.  
  
Technical Capability: The government will evaluate the extent to which the offeror has demonstrated 
the technical capability to successfully perform these services, and demonstrated a feasible technical 
approach to successfully perform and manage the required tasks while ensuring that all deliverable 
schedule requirements are met.  
 
Technical Key Personnel:  
The Government will evaluate the key personnel proposed by the offeror for the extent to which they 
are qualified to efficiently and effectively address the requirements in the Statement of Work. The 
Government will consider the extent to which the proposed key personnel meets or exceeds the 
minimum qualifications identified in the Statement of Work, as well as the qualifications “preference” 
identified in the Statement of Work. Greater consideration will be given to key personnel that exceed 
the specific minimum qualification requirements and/or meet the key personnel preference identified 
in the Statement of Work. 
  
Past Performance: The Government will evaluate the Offeror's past performance information and, if 
appropriate, its proposed subcontractors' past performance to determine its relevance to the current 
requirement and the extent to which it demonstrates that the offeror has successfully completed 
relevant contracts in the past three years.  In assessing the offeror's past performance information, 
NIST will evaluate, as appropriate, successful performance of contract requirements, quality and 
timeliness of delivery of goods and services, cost management, communications between contracting 
parties, proactive management and customer satisfaction. Evaluation of this factor will be based on 
information contained in the technical portion of the quotation and information provided by 
references.  The Government will evaluate past performance information by contacting appropriate 
references, including NIST references, if applicable.  The Government may also consider other 
available information in evaluating the Offeror’s past performance.  The Government will assign a 
neutral rating if the offeror has no relevant past performance information.   
  
NOTE -- If an offeror does not have a history of relevant contract experience, or if past performance 
information is not available, the offeror will receive a neutral past performance rating; however, an 
offeror without a history of relevant experience may receive a lowered rating for the Experience Factor. 
  
Price: The Government will evaluate price for reasonableness. 
  
Past Performance, Experience, and Price shall not be evaluated on quotations that are 
determined technically unacceptable under the Technical Capability evaluation factor.  

 
FAR 52.212-2 Evaluation- Commercial Products and Commercial Services (DEVIATION Jan 2026) 
 
(a) Evaluation factors. The Government will award a contract resulting from this solicitation to the 
responsible Offeror whose offer conforming to the solicitation will be most advantageous to the 
Government, price and other factors considered. The following factors will be used to evaluate 
offers: 
 
The Government intends to award a single firm fixed price purchase order (PO) from this solicitation 
utilizing simplified acquisitions procedures in accordance with FAR part 12 of the Revolutionary FAR 
Overhaul. The Government reserves the right not to award a PO and to make an award without 
discussions based solely upon initial quotes. 
 
(b) Options (if applicable). The Government will evaluate offers for award purposes by adding the total 
price for all options to the total price for the basic requirement. The Government may determine that an 
offer is unacceptable if the option prices are significantly unbalanced. The evaluation of options does 
not obligate the Government to exercise the option(s).

STATEMENT OF WORK/PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT
United States Naval Academy - Information Technology Services Division
1. Background.
The United States Naval Academy (USNA) Information Technology Services Division (ITSD) is responsible for developing, managing and 
integrating information systems and providing information technology products, services and capabilities for approximately 7,000 midshipmen, 
faculty and staff across the academy's 630 acre campus and for the approximately 300 midshipmen candidates, faculty and staff at the Naval Academy 
Preparatory School (NAPS) located in Newport R.I.
The ITSD Finance Department is responsible for all information technology (IT) and other major equipment including integrated planning, 
programming, budgeting, procurement, licensing, receipt, payment, accounting, maintenance, support, and inventory management of all hardware and 
software and associated services in conjunction with other educational support equipment to meet documented organizational needs. It is responsible 
for maintaining liaison with external entities including tenant commands and oversight authorities and
managing special enterprise projects by representing USNA IT interests and coordinating execution across multiple internal and external entities 
including but not limited to GSA/WITS,
NAVSUP/FLC, NAVFAC/PWD, CINC/NSAA, USNA Architect and commercial vendors. The Finance Department also provides general business 
support including travel, training, payroll,
supply, and similar services.
2. Objectives.
The objective of this task is for the USNA to renew the licensing and maintenance for the Momentus venue and event management software (f/k/a 
Ungerboeck) that has been supporting this business process for over 5 years. This system supports the USNA venue managers across the yard that 
maintain the schedules for over 300 spaces available for
being reserved for academic, athletic, religious, or any other type of public or private events. It allows for end-users to request venue reservations 
through a self-service portal, coaches and athletics staff to reserve fields and courts on a recurring basis for team practices, and venue managers to 
coordinate, approve, and deconflict the schedules of the venues that they have under their Management.
3. Scope of Services
The Vendor will provide the following services for the renewal period of Base year PoP is 01 May 2026 - 30 APR 2027
Software Upgrades, Security Patches & Maintenance:
Delivery and implementation of all available software upgrades and security patches throughout the 
renewal period on manual schedule until such time as USNA can align
with wave format of upgrade scheduling.
Ensuring the software remains current and secure against known vulnerabilities.
Notification to the Client of any critical updates or security patches requiring immediate
action.
Software Access:
The software that USNA currently uses has been repackaged into Momentus Enterprise Core Software. USNA must retain all current features as part 
of this new packaging to include:
Continued access to the Momentus platform (110 & OSB) for all authorized users throughout the renewal 
period.
Maintenance of software functionality and availability.
Event Management
OSB
Crystal Reports/Report Builder
U4VE - Online Calendar of Events (iEBMS COE) (Enterprise)
iEBMS - Calendar of Events (Perpetual)
PRIVATE BETA - Ungerboeck Phone (Perpetual)

Customer Success Team Check-ins:
Scheduled check-in meetings with the Vendor's Customer Success Team [Frequency -
not less than quarterly].
Support:
Technical support during vendor's standard business hours.
Support will be provided for all software related issues, including, but not limited to, access problems, 
error messages, and functionality issues.
Custom Crystal Reports Support:
Remote support for existing custom Crystal Reports.
Assistance with troubleshooting issues related to custom reports.
Guidance on maintaining compatibility of custom reports with software upgrades.
4. Deliverables
Renewed software licenses and access credentials.
Delivery and implementation of all software upgrades and security patches.
Scheduled customer success team check-in meetings.
Ongoing technical support.
Support for custom Crystal Reports.
5. Term and Renewal
This SOW is effective for the renewal period beginning on 01 May 2026 and ending on 30 APR 2027.
Two option year renewals have been included.
Requirements
Renew the licensing and maintenance for the Momentus venue and event management software.

Solicitation Pg 57, Para 2.4 (Past 
Performance) 
Please clarify whether Past Performance will be evaluated at the company level, 
individual instructor/personnel level, or a combination of both. If both, what 
weighting or consideration is given to each? 
Past performance will be evaluated at the company level. The 
weight will be seen as either acceptable or unacceptable. 
Company’s with no past performance will not be negatively 
affected and seen as acceptable. 
Solicitation Pg 57, Para 2 (Evaluation 
Factors) 
The solicitation states award will be based on price and other factors; however, it 
also states quotes will be evaluated for technical acceptability and not ranked. 
Please confirm whether this procurement is Lowest Price Technically Acceptable 
(LPTA) or a Best Value Tradeoff. 
Award will be made based on price and other non-price factors. 
Meaning award will be made to the offeror with the lowest price 
who receives an acceptable rating in all other non-price factors. 
Solicitation Pg 57, Para 2 (Evaluation 
Factors)

Pass/Fail

support, or strictly by CLIN as written, and whether offerors may provide supporting

CLIN as written

 All training will be completed on ft. Benning but spread across 5 
or more ranges

(Operating Hours) 
Please clarify the expected number of courses per year and whether this varies 
annually. 
 3 annual courses with the possibility to conduct a 4th course. The

submitted for the 4th course specifically.

 Training schedules will not be the same annually and may adjust

Training calendars are not shareable due to their classification

PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT
1. SPECIFICATION:
1.1. This requirement is in support of the USS BLUE RIDGE (LCC-19), which requires Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM)-authorized 
Technician(s) to provide system programming, testing, and maintenance of the Government furnished and installed King Fisher Temporary Fire 
Detection system. This assistance includes visual and operational inspection of the Government installed Fire Detection Systems. After installation 
Contractor must provide a detailed installation diagram and training on alarm conditions and how to interpret them to U.S. Naval Ship Repair Facility 
and Japan Regional Maintenance Center (SRF-JRMC) Yokosuka Fire Safety Council Representative (FSC) and The Ship Force Watch Standers.
1.2. Technician must be on-site during installation phase and available to provide distance support and occasional "as needed" onsite support during 
normal and evening working hours to facilitate Fire Detection System component monitoring, each modification, and each repair to support work 
upon request from the FSC at SRF-JRMC Yokosuka.
1.3. OEM to provide support from the Japan based technician to accommodate the periodic and sporadic need for Temporary Fire Detection support 
to SRF-JRMC Yokosuka.
2. REFERENCES:
2.1. NAVSEA Technical Manual S0570-AC-CCM-010/8010 Industrial Ship Safety Manual for Fire Prevention and Response
3. ENCLOSURES:
3.1. None.
4. GENERAL SCOPE OF WORK:
4.1. The Contractor will provide OEM-authorized Technical Representative(s) and equipment to provide system programming, testing, maintenance 
of the Government installed King Fisher temporary detection system in accordance with Reference 2.1.
4.1.1. The Contractor must accomplish the requirements of paragraph 4, for up to a total of 335 EA Temporary Fire Detector and associated 
equipment, to include equipment installation and removal assistance "as needed" by SRF-JRMC.
4.1.2. The Contractor must accomplish the requirements of paragraph 4, for up to a total of 35 EA Temporary Flood Sensors and associated 
equipment, to include equipment installation and removal assistance when directed by the SUPERVISOR.
4.1.3. Activation of a temporary detector must be indicated on the centrally manned control panel at Central Control Station (CCS)/Damage Control 
Central (DCC) and the remotely located annunciator panel at either the ship's primary Quarterdeck or the secondary Quarterdeck. An alarm specific 
space location must be provided by the Contractor and available on the control panel and annunciator panel to enable the Ship's watch stander to 
quickly identify which space the alarm was activated in. This will facilitate immediate dispatching of Ship fire response personnel to the affected 
space.
4.1.4. The Contractor must provide an Alarm indicator index or similar to satisfy paragraph 4.1.2. Index must be provided at each control panel and 
annunciator immediately after satisfactory completion of installation programming and testing. Provide electronic copy of the Alarm indicator index 
to the SRF-JRMC FSC. This document must be updated immediately after each new detector is installed under paragraph 4.1.1.
4.2. SYSTEM INSPECTION: The Contractor must inspect each installed system component, including each independent back-up power supply, to 
ensure proper function and operation with SRF-JRMC Yokosuka Shop 99 representatives.
4.2.1. The contractor must provide bi-monthly (two-week interval) inspections of the installed temporary system.
4.2.2. The contractor must verify functionality of each equipment component used to replace each defective equipment component.
4.2.3. The Contractor must repair each nonfunctional part as needed to maintain functionality. The Contractor must notify SRF-JRMC Yokosuka 
Shop 99 of each equipment component requiring replacement. SRF-JRMC Yokosuka Shop 99 will install each replaced equipment component. The 
Contractor must provide a report of each defective equipment component requiring immediate replacement, and each equipment component that may 
require replacement in the future.
4.2.4. The contractor must provide a report of each defective equipment component replaced and/or repaired. This report should include each 
equipment component that may require future replacement and/or repair.
4.2.5. The contractor must provide onsite or remote technical assistance troubleshooting each fire detection system fault within 24 hours from 
notification by the Government. The expected duration of this assistance when exercised is three (3) days. The government may exercise this option 
up to 12 times during the period of performance.
5. ISSUES AND CONDITION REPORTING:
5.1. The Contractor must bring their own tools to support 4.1 and 4.2.
N6264926QB029
Page 4 of 31

5.2. The Contractor must provide the following training:
5.2.1. Provide One each training session on temporary fire detection system functionality and fault identification for approximately 12 each Ship's 
Force personnel in the following electronic/electrical ratings (GSE/EM, ET/IC). These personnel will be responsible for providing notification to the 
Project Team within 10 minutes on each system fault that cannot be reset during and outside of normal working hours.
5.2.2. Provide One each training session for 9 each SRF-JRMC Fire Safety Officers, 2 each Project Supervisors, and approximately 10 each Zone 
Managers/Work Integration Managers on temporary fire detection system installation and operation.
5.2.3. Provide training session for approximately 90 Ship's Force personnel qualified as Command Duty Officer, Engineering Duty Officer, Officer of 
the Deck, Central Control Station Supervisor, Fire Safety Watch and Sounding & Security on temporary fire detection system functionality and 
operation. Training may be held in between One each and 3 each session depending on mission requirements.
5.2.4. Contractor must provide electronic media of the training material provided to meet paragraph 5.2.1 through 5.2.3 for reference material.
6. PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE:
6.1. Base Period of Performance: 05 AUG 2026 - 04 AUG 2027 (365 days)
6.2. Option 1 Period of Performance: 05 AUG 2027 - 19 JAN 2028 (168 days)
6.3. Option 2 Period of Performance: 20 JAN 2028 - 02 FEB 2028 (14 days)
6.4. Option 3 Period of Performance: 03 FEB 2028 - 16 FEB 2028 (14 days)
7. GOVERNMENT FURNISHED PROPERTY/MATERIALS:
7.1. The Government will furnish and install each King Fisher Fire Detection System component, and each required replacement component. 
Computer and other computer accessories are not provided under this contract.
8. GOVERNMENT SUPPORT:
8.1. If the Contractor requires additional support, this support must be requested through Project Sup. This request does not constitute approval.
9. CONTRACTOR FURNISHED PROPERTY/MATERIALS:
9.1. Contractor must provide all tools, equipment, and material need to complete the contract requirements of this PWS.
10. ESTIMATED WORK HOURS:
10.1. Normally, all work is performed between the hours of 8:00am and 4:45pm Monday through Saturday.
11. PLACE OF PERFORMANCE:
11.1. Onboard the SHIP per 1.1 at SRF-JRMC, Yokosuka Japan

Spaceport and Launch Assessment Study (SPLAS) 
Statement of Work (SOW)   
Page 1 of 7 
 
DISTRIBUTION STATEMENT C. Distribution authorized to U.S. Government  
agencies and their contractors To protect and limit distribution in accordance with the 
desires of and agreements with the foreign government that furnished the technical 
information. 
 
Assigned pursuant to Chapter 15 of Title 50, U.S.C.(Reference (v)) and Executive Order 
13526 (Reference (w))(date of determination). Other requests for this document shall be 
referred to (USSF , PAW, Space Access).  
 
1. Introduction 
This Statement of Work (SOW) outlines the requirements for a Technical Services Case 
between Portfolio Acquisition Executive (PAE) for Space Access (SA) and a Partner Nation 
(PN) to support the establishment of a PN National Security Space Launch (NSSL) 
capability at a sovereign spaceport, utilizing a Commercial Launch Vehicle (CLV) . This 
SOW is based on the signed Letter of Request (LOR) for Letter of OƯer and Acceptance 
(LOA) between the USG and the PN. 
 
2. Project Objectives 
The objective of this Technical Services Case is to provide the PN with the necessary 
engineering, logistical, and technical assistance to successfully establish an NSSL service 
from a sovereign spaceport utilizing a US commercial launch vehicle (CLV), with a priority 
focus on tailoring USSF best practices for National Security launch operations and mission 
assurance from the spaceport. This includes: 
• Developing a familiarization with the launch vehicle capability and support systems 
• Tailoring US Space Force spaceport development and operations best practices, for 
launch of national payloads from the spaceport to the PN context 
• Identifying potential mission risks and mitigation strategies associated with using the 
CLV for PN NSSL 
• Providing technical documentation and support to enable PN to eƯectively monitor 
and control the CLV launch pad as it relates to PN NSSL service 
• Assessing the requirements and interfaces of the CLV launch system and the 
spaceport 
• Providing launch mission assurance assessment expertise 
 
  

Spaceport and Launch Assessment Study (SPLAS) 
Statement of Work (SOW)   
Page 2 of 7 
 
3. Scope of Work 
3.1  Commercial Launch Service Provider Familiarization: Assess launch vehicle 
capability to meet the mission requirements of PN National Security Space Launch 
using U.S. Space Force evaluation criteria (tailored as needed). This assessment may 
be accomplished through a combination of site and facility visits and document review, 
and shall include: 
o Vehicle capability overview 
o Assessment of the launch service provider’s (LSP) mission execution processes 
and procedures (including but not limited to: manufacturing, vehicle mating, pad 
roll-out, pre-launch, launch,) 
o Ability to accommodate PN national security satellites and meet mass and orbit 
performance requirements 
o Identiﬁcation of technical, cost, and schedule risks 
Deliverable (CDRL A01): General Launch Vehicle familiarization  
3.2  Assessment of Spaceport Operator’s plan to support NSSL: Conduct site surveys at 
spaceport facilities that will support operation of CLV at the spaceport and summarize 
ﬁndings. Assess the spaceport and spaceport operator’s ability to meet the mission 
requirements of the PN National Security Space Launch through use of CLV using U.S. 
Space Force evaluation criteria (tailored as needed). This includes: 
o Ability of payload processing facilities to accommodate PN satellites  
o Identiﬁcation of technical, cost, and schedule risks 
o Assessment of spaceport ability to meet physical and cyber security requirements 
o Identiﬁcation of additional requirements that need to be leveraged on the 
spaceport operator and the CLV launch complex for NSSL that do not apply to 
commercial launch 
The report should include a detailed assessment of the following: 
Launch Site Systems: Assess launch site systems including CLV launch complex sensors, 
interfaces, and infrastructure, spaceport infrastructure, payload processing facilities,  
ground support equipment, sensors, Telemetry, Tracking, and Control (TT&C) systems (this 
may include, but not limited to, launch vehicle telemetry collection, ﬂight safety control (if 
autonomous ﬂight safety is not used), and space vehicle separation (if required)), and 
ground handling processes and procedures to determine whether all equipment meets 
requirements, are capable of being certiﬁed, and have proper interfaces. The assessment 
should also consider launch vehicle and expected space vehicle commodity requirements 
such as liquid nitrogen, hydrazine, kerosene, liquid oxygen, etc. Report will include 

Spaceport and Launch Assessment Study (SPLAS) 
Statement of Work (SOW)   
Page 3 of 7 
 
recommendations of additional sensors or equipment requirements that apply to NSSL 
operations. 
Deliverable:  Spaceport assessment and NSSL requirements documents (CDRL 
A02)   
 
3.3  National Security Launch Requirements:  Work with PN to understand their 
objectives and risk tolerance for National Security Space assets. Based on this 
understanding, and the capability of the launch provider and their launch solution, provide 
general technical assistance and support in deﬁning requirements, and recommend and 
prioritize requirements to ensure the launch solution will meet PN’s mission objectives. 
Recommend a mission assurance approach, such as accepting a launch provider’s 
baseline system and responding to mission unique requirements as needed, or other 
solutions. 
The report should include the following: 
Launch Site Speciﬁcations: requirements based on general CLV launch vehicle 
speciﬁcations to be imposed on the spaceport operator for use of CLV for NSS 
operations. The document shall include NSSL mission assurance requirements for 
the CLV launch complex that may be more stringent than the commercial 
requirements for commercial payload launches. 
Launch Readiness Veriﬁcation (LRV) Process: Develop an LRV process for use 
of CLV , based on USSF mission assurance processes tailored to PN requirements 
to ensure CLV and launch complex systems are capable of achieving PN NSSL 
mission success when operating from the spaceport. 
Test, Evaluation, and System Safety Assessment: Assess spaceport operator’s 
approach to ground and ﬂight safety requirements that meets PN’s launch 
licensing authority requirements and recommend areas for tailoring to reduce 
new/additional qualiﬁcation. This may include identiﬁcation of the U.S. 
Government / U.S. Space Force test, evaluation, and system safety 
documentation that would be applicable to CLV and spaceport operator’s launch 
operations at the spaceport. This may also include recommending tailored 
approaches to said documents. 
Deliverable: National Security Launch Requirements (CDRL A03) 
3.4   Suggested Training: Assess spaceport operator and PN personnel current 
knowledge base and suggest courses for personnel to participate in to gain a better 
understanding space launch operations, safety, mission assurance, regulations, and other 
mission areas as applicable based on their desired level of competence.  This shall be 
assessed through discussions with relevant PN and PAE/SA personnel. 

Spaceport and Launch Assessment Study (SPLAS) 
Statement of Work (SOW)   
Page 4 of 7 
 
Deliverable: List of recommended education & training (CDRL A04) 
 
3.5  Comprehensive Analysis and Recommendations:  At the conclusion of the study 
or period of performance, deliver a consolidated report and brieﬁng with a summary of all 
assessments and recommendations for PN to successfully establish a National Security 
Launch capability using the CLV at the PN spaceport.  This report shall include elements 
of the previously outlined deliverables as well as recommendations for further studies as 
needed to address any identiﬁed gaps in capability. 
Deliverable: Comprehensive National Security Launch Assessment and 
Recommendations Report and Brieﬁng (CDRL A05) 
 
3.6  Technical Interchange Meetings (TIMs): Conduct Technical Interchange Meetings 
(TIMs), planning conferences, review meetings, and other relevant meetings and deliver 
meeting agendas, minutes, and action items for each exchange with the partner, 
spaceport operator, and launch service provider. Target is 12 meetings per year, with 2 in-
person and 10 virtual with PN and spaceport operator.  Additional progress review and 
kickoƯ/closeout meetings with the PAE/SA case team will be required with at least 2 in-
person.  Each virtual engagement will be scheduled not later than 7 calendar days in 
advance, with each engagement not being more than 8 hours in length.  The contractor 
shall provide read ahead materials not less than 24 hours prior to each engagement and 
publish action items not more than 24 hours after each engagement.  In-person 
engagements will be held at a Government or contractor facility most advantageous to the 
study team. OCONUS in-person meetings shall be scheduled not less than 1 calendar 
month in advance to allow suƯicient time for USG personnel to process international 
travel request documentation. 
Deliverable: Meeting Agendas, Meeting invitations, Minutes and Action Items 
(CDRL A06) 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

Spaceport and Launch Assessment Study (SPLAS) 
Statement of Work (SOW)   
Page 5 of 7 
 
4. Deliverables 
At the conclusion of the case the contractor shall return all data, information, reports, and 
other documents gathered or generated during the course of the case to the Space Access 
Project Manager The deliverables for this Technical Services Case are listed within the 
Scope of Work section. All deliverables will be provided in English. 
 
 
Contract Data Requirements List (CDRL) Deliverables 
CRDL No. CDRL Title 
A01 General Launch Vehicle assessment  
A02 Spaceport assessment and NSSL requirements document 
A03 National Security Launch Requirements 
A04 List of recommended education & training 
A05 Comprehensive National Security Launch Assessment and 
Recommendations Report and Brieﬁng 
A06 Meeting Agendas, Meeting invitations, Minutes and Action Items 
 
5.0 Acceptance Criteria 
Deliverables will be considered acceptable upon written conﬁrmation from the PN and 
Space Access Project Manager that the deliverable meets the requirements outlined in this 
SOW. 
All work and deliverables submitted under this Statement of Work will be formally accepted 
by the designated Space Access Project Manager or their representative. Acceptance will 
be contingent upon the fulﬁllment of the following general criteria: 
• Completeness: The deliverable must be complete and address all requirements 
outlined for that speciﬁc item in the SOW. 
• Accuracy: Information presented must be factually accurate, well-researched, and 
supported by data where applicable. 
• Clarity: All documents must be written in clear, concise, and unambiguous English. 
Technical concepts should be explained in a manner understandable to the 
intended audience. 
• Timeliness: All deliverables must be submitted on or before the agreed-upon 
deadlines 
 
5. Schedule and Milestones 
The period of performance for this Technical Services Case is 12 months from the date of 
award.  The contractor’s local team members shall meet in person, with others supporting 
virtually, with the Space Access case team within 10 calendar days of contract award at the 

Spaceport and Launch Assessment Study (SPLAS) 
Statement of Work (SOW)   
Page 6 of 7 
 
Government site to deﬁnitize a study plan and schedule.  The study plan and schedule will 
outline the lines of inquiry, sources of information, and roles and responsibilities of each 
member of the study team (both Government and contractor).  The contractor will identify 
all members of their study team, areas of expertise, availability and percent commitment 
to the study, and work location.  The contractor shall provide a written summary of the joint 
study plan within 2 calendar days of the conclusion of the study plan meeting. 
 
6. Roles and Responsibilities 
• PAE Space Access (SA): Responsible for providing the technical expertise, 
documentation, and support outlined in this SOW including facilitating sharing of 
information on the CLV system. PAE/SA will assign a Project Manager to oversee the 
execution of the work. 
• Partner Nation: Responsible for providing access to relevant information, facilities, and 
personnel. PN will assign a Project Manager to coordinate with PAE/SA. 
• Spaceport Operator: Will be involved in providing access to relevant information, 
facilities, and personnel related to assessments of the sovereign spaceport. 
• US Contractor: Will be responsible for the performance of the work outlined in this 
SOW and in accordance with the terms and conditions of the contract. The contractor 
shall establish and maintain on-line for the duration of the contract a secure workspace 
accessible to each Government and contractor members of the project team, and only 
these members with the exception of PN members as appropriate.   All data, work 
products, and status, interim, and ﬁnal reports will be saved in a project-relevant ﬁle 
structure to facilitate rapid access by the study team.   Data protection for up to CUI is 
required and the contractors system shall meet the requirements of NIST SP 800-171 
Rev 3. 
• Space Access Contracting OƯicer: Only authorized individual able to direct the 
contractor to perform or make authorized changes to the SOW or terms and conditions 
of the contract. Works closely with the Space Access Project Manager to ensure 
contract performance is acceptable. 
 
7. Standards and Requirements 
• All contractor personnel shall be U.S. citizens and authorized access to Controlled 
Unclassiﬁed Information, proprietary information of the LSPs, and U.S. Export 
Controlled data covered by the U.S. Munitions List (USML) and International TraƯic 
in Arms Regulations (ITAR), 22 CFR Parts 120-130 
• All contractor personnel shall enter into non-disclosure agreements as needed with 
the LSP or other contractors and fulﬁl the non-disclosure requirements. 

Spaceport and Launch Assessment Study (SPLAS) 
Statement of Work (SOW)   
Page 7 of 7 
 
The contractor shall return all data, information, reports, and other documents gathered or 
generated during the course of the study to the Government Project Manager and will not 
employ any of the data or information gathered during this study for any other purposes 
during the course of the study without the approval of the Government Project Manager. 
 
9. Project Management and Reporting 
• The contractor shall supply the Space Access PM with relevant details and products 
to enable SA to provide monthly progress reports to PN summarizing the work 
completed, any issues encountered, and planned activities for the next month.

STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW) 
Scientific Evidence Evaluation and Knowledge Integration for 
Translational Toxicology 
 
April 13, 2026 
1 General Information 
1.1 General 
This is a non-personal service(s) contract under which the personnel rendering the service(s) 
are not subject, either by the contract’s terms or by the manner of its administration, to the 
supervision and control usually prevailing in relationships between the Government and its 
employees. The purpose of this contract is to provide all services and supplies necessary to 
conduct scientific evidence evaluation and knowledge integration for translational toxicology in 
support of the National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences (NIEHS), Division of 
Translational Toxicology (DTT).  
1.2 
Description of Services 
Independently, and not as an agent of the Government, the Contractor shall furnish all the 
necessary services, qualified personnel, procedures, materials, equipment, and facilities not 
otherwise provided by the Government as needed to perform the objectives set forth below. In 
general, activities shall be conducted according to the requirements described in a research 
outline (see Section 3.1), which includes project-specific activities, milestones, and deliverables. 
1.3 Background and Scope 
DTT is an intramural division of NIEHS, National Institutes of Health, that uses traditional and 
cutting-edge research approaches to better understand how factors in our environment may 
impact human health. Such approaches include using scientific expertise to identify, collect, 
analyze, and interpret diverse types of information relevant to the effects of environmental 
exposures on human health. Information from the fields of toxicology, epidemiology, chemistry, 
data science, informatics, pathology, and other disciplines is used in the design of research 
programs; in literature-based health assessments; and in the development of novel tools and 
informatics approaches.  
The objective of this contract is to provide scientific and technical expertise and support for 
scientific evidence evaluation and knowledge integration for translational toxicology related to 
the evaluation and reporting of effects of environmental substances and other issues that may 
impact public health. Nine specific requirement areas under this contract to support DTT within 
NIEHS include: (1) systematic evidence mapping and scoping reviews of environmental health 
literature, (2) systematic review and evidence synthesis, (3) report development and scientific 
writing, (4) document preparation and publication, (5) coordination and management of 
external peer review, (6) logistical management for advisory group meetings and workshops, 
(7) provision of scientific or technical consultants with expertise in relevant scientific disciplines, 
(8) development and implementation of novel tools and informatics approaches, and (9) 

   
 
 2 
program management. These requirement areas are managed by several offices and branches 
within DTT. Additional information about the DTT organizational structure is available on the 
NIEHS website. 
The National Toxicology Program (NTP) is an interagency partnership comprised of NIEHS (part 
of the National Institutes of Health), the National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health 
(NIOSH; part of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention), and the U.S. Food and Drug 
Administration (FDA; primarily at the National Center for Toxicological Research). NTP is 
headquartered administratively at NIEHS, and many of the activities performed under this 
contract will support NTP projects and research programs. 
The activities carried out by this contract will address the aforementioned requirements for 
scientific evidence evaluation and knowledge integration for translational toxicology. 
1.4 Overview of Required Capabilities 
The Contractor shall conduct activities supported by the following Capability Areas described in 
more detail in Section 2 – Required Capability Areas:  
• Systematic Evidence Mapping and Scoping Reviews of Environmental Health 
Literature 
• Systematic Review and Evidence Synthesis 
• Report Development and Scientific Writing 
• Document Preparation and Publication 
• Coordination and Management of External Peer Review 
• Logistical Management for Advisory Group Meetings and Workshops 
• Provision of Scientific or Technical Consultants with Expertise in Relevant Scientific 
Disciplines  
• Development and Implementation of Novel Tools and Informatics Approaches 
• Program Management 
1.5 Policies and Procedures 
For scientific evidence evaluation and knowledge integration for translational toxicology, the 
Contractor and applicable subcontractor(s) shall comply with the below guidelines: 
a. Handbook for Conducting Systematic Reviews for Health Effects Evaluations 
• Available at: https://ntp.niehs.nih.gov/go/ohathandbook.  
b. Handbook for Preparing Report on Carcinogens Monographs 
• Available at: https://ntp.niehs.nih.gov/go/rochandbook.  
1.6 Reports and Deliverables 
Information on specific reporting requirements is presented below. All deliverables shall be 
electronic and PC and MAC compatible unless otherwise specified by the Contracting Officer’s 
Representative (COR). Each final document or report shall be submitted electronically in MS 
Word and/or PDF formats to the COR for review. Unless otherwise directed, all submitted final 
electronic deliverables shall be compliant with Section 508 regarding accessibility (see Section 
1.6.4). In some cases, there may be accommodations for which the Government will provide 
information annually. Unless otherwise instructed, all reports submitted under this contract 

   
 
 3 
shall reference the contract number, the title and type of report, and the submission date on 
the first page of the report. 
In addition to the reports mentioned herein, any incidence or unforeseeable occurrence not 
listed here, including personnel changes which may impact activities under the contract, shall 
be immediately reported to the Government. 
DELIVERABLE  REFERENCE  DUE/FREQUENCY  SUBMIT TO  
Quality Management 
Plan Section 1.6.1.1 Revise as needed or when major changes 
occur COR, CO, and CS 
Monthly  
Progress Report  Section 1.6.1.2 Due once per month  COR, CO, and CS 
Monthly Budget 
Summary Report Section 1.6.1.3 Due once per month as an attachment 
with the monthly invoices COR, CO, and CS 
Annual Report Section 1.6.1.4 Due 4 weeks from the last day of each 
contract year COR, CO, and CS 
COR = Contracting Officer’s Representative; CO = Contracting Officer; CS = Contract Specialist. 
 
1.6.1 Periodic Reports 
1.6.1.1 Quality Management Plan 
A Quality Management Plan (QMP) shall be submitted before performance of work under the 
contract and updated versions submitted at regular intervals (e.g., biannually). 
1.6.1.2 Monthly Progress Report 
Once per month, the COR shall receive a summary of the work currently in progress. This report 
shall include details on the status of all active work, current costs for active work, cumulative 
costs for the contract (including direct and administrative costs), any problems encountered, 
and remedial actions taken to resolve those problems. The monthly progress report shall also 
include a summary of the work performed by any subcontractor and/or ad hoc consultant, 
including their deliverables, hours spent, and cost. This summary shall also include a description 
of how the subcontractor/consultant work aided the Contractor in completing or nearing 
completion of a specific project. 
1.6.1.3 Monthly Budget Summary Report 
A summary report shall be submitted monthly that includes budget information for each 
activity separately undertaken and for the contract as a whole. The report must include each 
activity’s budget, total expenditures on the activity for the month, summaries of current 
contract year and cumulative expenditures, and projected expenses to complete each activity. 
Budget summary reports shall be submitted monthly to the COR as MS Excel spreadsheets (or 
in other spreadsheet software by agreement) and shall be sortable as required by the COR. 
Budget summary reports shall be included as an attachment with the monthly invoices. 

   
 
 4 
1.6.1.4 Annual Report 
An annual report shall be submitted within 4 weeks of the last day of each contract year. Each 
annual report shall detail all significant outcomes resulting from the requirements as described 
within the SOW and contract, including a breakdown of costs by research activity incurred to 
date, any problems encountered and remedial actions taken to resolve the problem, and any 
deviations from the SOW and/or contract. 
1.6.2 Research Products 
For each activity performed under the contract, research products shall be generated by the 
Contractor and submitted to the COR according to the milestones and deliverables schedule 
included in the research outline. The type and number of product(s) may vary depending on the 
nature of the activity.  
1.6.3 IT Security Plan and Other IT Deliverables 
Refer to Appendix A for specific requirements related to information technology (IT) security. 
1.6.4 HHS Section 508 and Accessibility Standards 
Section 508 of the Rehabilitation Act, as amended by the Workforce Investment Act of 1998 
(P.L. 105-220) requires that when Federal agencies develop, procure, maintain, or use 
information and communication technology (ICT), it shall be accessible to people with 
disabilities. Federal employees and members of the public who have disabilities must have 
access to, and use of, information and data that is comparable to people without disabilities. 
All products, platforms and services delivered as part of this work statement that are ICT, or 
contain ICT, must conform to the Revised 508 Standards, which are located at 36 C.F.R. § 
1194.1 & Apps. A, B, & C, and available at https://www.access-board.gov/ict/. 
All requirements are applicable to support services and documentation deliverables. All 
functional performance criteria apply when using an alternative design or technology that 
achieves substantially equivalent or greater accessibility and usability by individuals with 
disabilities, than would be provided by conformance to one or more of the requirements in 
Chapters 4-6 of the Revised 508 Standards, or when Chapters 4-6 do not address one or more 
functions of ICT. 
For each proposed product or platform, a fully completed Accessibility Conformance Report 
(ACR) using the Voluntary Product Accessibility Template (VPAT) 
(https://www.itic.org/policy/accessibility/vpat) or HHS conformance checklist(s) 
(https://www.hhs.gov/web/section-508/accessibility-checklists/index.html) must be 
submitted. 
Prior to acceptance of deliverables, the offeror must demonstrate conformance to the HHS 
Section 508 requirements via HHS Section 508 checklist(s) (https://www.hhs.gov/web/section-
508/accessibility-checklists/index.html). The Government reserves the right to perform testing 
on required ICT items to validate the offeror’s Section 508 conformance claims. If the 
Government determines that Section 508 conformance does not meet the HHS Section 508 
requirements, the Government shall, at its option, require the offeror to remediate the item, at 
no additional cost to the Government, to align with the HHS Section 508 conformance 
requirements prior to acceptance. 

   
 
 5 
References: 
• Section 508 Standards: https://www.access-board.gov/ict/ 
• HHS Policy on Section 508 Compliance and Accessibility of Information and 
Communications Technology (ICT): https://www.hhs.gov/web/governance/digital-
strategy/it-policy-archive/hhs-policy-section-508-compliance-accessibility-information-
communications-technology.html 
• HHS Accessibility and Section 508 Conformance Checklists: 
https://www.hhs.gov/web/section-508/accessibility-checklists/index.html  
1.7 Post Award Conference/Periodic Progress Meetings 
The Contractor shall attend any post award conferences convened by the contracting activity or 
contract administration office in accordance with FAR Subpart 42.5. The Contracting Officer 
(CO), COR, and other Government personnel, as appropriate, may meet periodically with the 
Contractor to review the Contractor's performance. At these meetings the CO will apprise the 
Contractor of how the Government views the Contractor's performance and the Contractor 
shall apprise the Government of problems, if any, being experienced. Appropriate action shall 
be taken to resolve outstanding issues. These meetings shall be at no additional cost to the 
Government. 
1.7.1 Progress Meetings 
The Contractor shall attend, participate in, and furnish input to scheduled and unscheduled 
meetings, conferences, and briefings that relate to the functions and services herein as 
required by the Government to provide effective communication and impart necessary 
information. The Principal Investigator (PI), Program Manager (PM), and/or designated 
representative shall attend meetings as requested by the Government. Meeting attendees shall 
at times include Contractor managerial, supervisory, and other personnel knowledgeable of the 
subject matter. Meetings may start or end outside of regular duty hours.  
1.8 Contracting Officer’s Representative 
As determined by the CO, a COR will be appointed and identified by letter of designation, a 
copy of which will be provided to the Contractor by the CO. The designation letter states the 
responsibilities and limitations of the COR. The COR has the responsibility and authority to 
monitor all aspects of the day-to-day administration of the contract. Responsibilities include 
ensuring the timeliness and delivery of quality products and services to meet the requirements 
of the contract. 
1.9 Personnel 
This contract requires a high degree of collaboration among (or by) Contractor staff. Each 
requirement described in this SOW shall be performed by an appropriate mix of professional 
and technical staff. The Contractor shall employ and/or have access to staff with broad 
professional and technical expertise in environmental health sciences necessary to conduct 
evaluations of complex scientific literature and fulfill the activities of the SOW. Contract 
personnel shall have the expertise to contribute to problem formulation and research design as 
required. Contractor staff may need to be available after normal working hours and on 
weekends. 

   
 
 6 
Personnel assigned to this contract, including subcontractors and/or consultants, shall 
demonstrate to the COR that there are no conflicts of interest relative to the work to be 
conducted prior to performing work under the contract. Personnel assigned to this contract 
with access to federal IT resources may be required to pass a security investigation (see 
Section 4).

PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT (PWS) 
                          SAFEGUARDS IT COMPUTER SECURITY SUPPORT 
 
 1 
 
1.0 OVERVIEW 
 
1.1   INTRODUCTION AND BACKGROUND 
 
The Office of Safeguards (Safeguards) within Governmental Liaison, Disclosure and Safeguards 
(GLDS) function of Privacy, Governmental Liaison and Disclosure (PGLD) is responsible for 
ensuring that Federal Tax Information (FTI) provided outside of the IRS is secured and used 
appropriately. Safeguards assess approximately 300 federal, state and local agencies, as well as 
their authorized contractors receiving FTI under various sub-sections of Internal Revenue Code 
(IRC) §6103 and other IRC provisions. Agencies must implement appropriate safeguards to 
protect confidentiality and prevent unauthorized access or use of FTI. Safeguards works in 
partnership with the recipient agencies to identify and mitigate risks to FTI. The specific 
safeguard requirements are outlined in IRC §6103(p)(4) and detailed in Publication 1075, Tax 
Information Security Guidelines for Federal, State, and Local Agencies. 
 
Publication 1075 is primarily based upon National Institute of Standards & Technology (NIST) 
Special Publication (SP) 800-53, Assessing Security and Privacy Controls for Information 
Systems and Organizations for moderate risk systems, IRC §6103 statutory requirements and IRS 
policy and procedure. All automated information systems and networks which receive, process, 
store, transmit, or protect FTI must meet these information protection requirements. 
 
Current Contract Number 2032H5-23-F-00312  
Incumbent:  Sky Solutions, LLC. 
Approximate contract value:  $15,864,000.00 
 
2.0 OBJECTIVE  
 
The objective of this requirement is to increase security of FTI and to ensure consistent 
application of information security standards across all partner agency information systems. 
 
3.0   REQUIREMENT TASKS 
 
The mission of Safeguards is to promote taxpayer confidence in the integrity of the tax system by 
ensuring the confidentiality of IRS information provided to federal, state, and local agencies.  
Safeguards verifies compliance with IRC §6103(p)(4) safeguard requirements through the 
identification and mitigation of any risk of loss, breach, or misuse of FTI held by external 
government agencies. 
 
The Contractor shall provide cybersecurity and information technology (IT) expertise. The 
Contractor shall optimize its processes, to reduce costs and minimize risk to FTI in possession of 
agency partners, while continuing to meet all regulatory and agency documented standards and 
guidance; and obtain information technology expertise and ancillary support to enable Safeguards 
to meet on-going and new regulatory objectives having an impact on the Safeguards Program. 
 
The Contractor shall collaborate with IRS leadership, staff, and other contractors in support of 
agency computer security reviews. Support shall include the following: conducting preparatory 
agency outreach; conducting pre-review research and analysis to determine scope and potential 
areas of concern; executing automated and manual computer security compliance scans of partner 
agency systems during the review; preparing reports, documenting scan results and other 

PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT (PWS) 
                          SAFEGUARDS IT COMPUTER SECURITY SUPPORT 
 
 2 
computer security findings; and analyzing and responding to various partner agency computer 
security information submissions. Other computer security review-related support includes 
stakeholder outreach, risk-based modeling for agency review selection, computer security review 
methodology updates, and general IT expertise. The Contractor shall provide ad hoc support for 
the assessment of other projects, pilots, and new legislation that include provisions falling within 
the purview of Safeguards. 
 
In accordance with Executive Order (EO) 14179, the contractor is permitted to use Artificial 
Intelligence (AI) to assist in this task.  
 
The Contractor shall adhere to IRS Publication 1075 (Tax Information Security Guidelines for 
Federal, State, and Local Agencies), Federal Security Modernization Act (FISMA), Privacy Act 
of 1974, Internal Revenue Code  §6103, NIST Risk Management Framework and IRS Safeguards 
Program requirements when utilizing artificial intelligence tools to enhance technical support 
capabilities assisting in the management and updates of Safeguards Computer Security 
Evaluation Matrices (SCSEM’s) and associated automated evaluation files.  
 
Contractors shall not process, store, or have access to FTI, PII, SSI, Classified or controlled 
unclassified information and any agency specific confidential data.  
 
The Contractor shall utilize only publicly available information from approved sources including 
IRS Publication 1075, NIST Special Publications and Standards, IRS Safeguard Program public 
website materials, Federal regulations and guidance documents and publicly available industry 
best practice standards to include Center for Internet Security (CIS) Benchmarks and Defense 
Information Systems Agency (DISA) Secure Technical Implementation Guides (STIG). All 
queries submitted must contain no FTI or PII; referenced only publicly available information, 
comply with informational handling classifications and be reviewed for compliance prior to 
submission. 
 
3.1   TASK 1- ORIENTATION BRIEFING  
 
The contractor shall facilitate an orientation briefing via a video conference call (Microsoft (MS) 
Teams, Zoom, etc.) with its representatives, ensuring all parties have a common understanding of 
the task order tasks and requirements. The contractor shall bring, at a minimum, its key personnel 
to this meeting. 
 
3.2   TASK 2, RAMP-UP KNOWLEDGE TRANSFER/TRANSITION-IN  
  
3.2.1 RAMP-UP KNOWLEDGE 
 
Ramp-Up Knowledge Transfer is defined as the contractor acquiring and understanding the 
necessary documentation, information, and processes related to any work in progress. The 
Government anticipates this task will be performed in conjunction with the Transition-In 
activities after the award of this task order.  
 
The contractor shall appoint a knowledge transfer manager serving as key personnel to oversee all 
areas of information that are accounted for and all knowledge of information is transferred from 
the current incumbent. This can be the Project Manager (PM) or other approved key personnel.

The project schedule shall identify tasks, dependencies, deliverables, and milestones. The project

complete and accurate status reports for the KTP. 
 
3.2.2 TRANSITION- IN  
 
The Transition-In task permits an effective transition from the incumbent Contractor to the new 
Contractor. The Government estimates this task will take approximately 120 calendar days to 
complete from date of award of the task order. Successful transition can be defined by its capacity 
to maintain full continuity of operations. To ensure a successful, low-risk transition, the 
contractor shall follow the approved Transition-In Plan and keep the government fully informed 
of status throughout the transition-in period. During the transition-in period, the incumbent is 
responsible for performance. This Task would be worked concurrently with Task 2, Ramp-Up 
Knowledge Transfer.

 4 
In addition to the transition activities in the approved KTP, the contractor shall ensure the 
following activities have been successfully completed within 75 days of the transition-in period to 
ensure timely commencement of services after the 120-Day Transition-In period: 
 
1. Obtain final access to tools and documentation 
2. Comprehend and successfully perform all the technical and process documentation. 
3. Comprehend and successfully apply the existing data and system security policies in

The Transition-in Checklist provides a vehicle to verify completion of the necessary transition-in

3.3   TASK 3, TASK MANAGEMENT  
 
3.3.1 General Requirements 
The Contractor shall provide personnel, including an equivalent contractor Subject Matter Expert 
(SME), to perform the requirements set forth herein. 
3.3.2 Monthly Status Report (MSR) Call 
The Contractor shall facilitate a Monthly Status Report (MSR) Call that includes presentation 
materials, such as a slide deck and supporting documentation, outlining expenditures, billings, 
progress, status, and any problems or issues encountered during task performance. The MSR shall 
include financial projections and an overview of support provided during the previous invoice 
period, including a list of all deliverables accepted and those in progress. All MSR materials and 
activities are subject to review and acceptance by the Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR) 
and the Technical Point of Contact (TPOC). 
3.3.3 Task Order Program Management Plan (PMP) 
The Contractor shall develop, implement, and maintain a Task Order Program Management Plan 
(PMP), subject to Government review and approval, manage, track, and evaluate performance 
throughout the period of performance. The PMP shall include control policies and procedures 
consistent with standard industry practices for project administration, execution, and tracking. 
The PMP may consist of multiple components, including, a project plan and performance status 
dashboards. The PMP shall include a consolidated roll-up of performance data for all active 
subtasks and shall be structured to support reuse for MSR Calls and other reporting requirements. 
The Contractor shall maintain the PMP in accordance with agreed-upon project management best 
practices. The PMP is subject to review and acceptance by the COR and TPOC. 
 
3.3.4 Administrative Touchpoint 
The Contractor shall attend and facilitate a weekly Administrative Touchpoint meeting, not to 
exceed one (1) hour in duration, as scheduled by the COR. The purpose of this meeting shall be to 
address onboarding activities, Government Furnished Equipment (GFE), and other administrative

Professional services in support of Commander Navy Installations Command (CNIC) Shore Operations 
Training Delivery Branch, N36T specifically instructors to facilitate virtual training, Mobile Training 
Teams (MTTs) and formal course delivery to CNIC Region and Installation and Region Category 5 First 
. CNIC N36T, the Shore Responders including leadership and emergency operations watch team personnel
Operations Training Group (SOTG), is responsible for delivering efficient and effective operations-
focused training to 10 regions and 70 installations worldwide. Under this statement of work, SOTG  
MTTs and Virtual Training Teams (VTTs) will ensure and improve the Navy's operational shore 
readiness via professional training to prepare Region and Installation personnel on proper procedures to 
design, develop, and implement training processes to enhance readiness throughout the CNIC enterprise; 
Conduct command, control and communication (C3) pre-training benchmark assessments for emergency 
management teams; Deliver formal SOTG-led mobile and virtual courses including: Emergency
Management for Senior Leaders Course (EMSLC), Regional Operation Center Crisis Action Team (ROC

/CAT Member Course, Emergency Manager Course (EM), Installation Training Officer (ITO) Course,

(CDO) Course, , Homeland Security Exercise Evaluation Program (HSEEP)  Course, Incident Command 
System 191 & ICS 449 (ICS 300/400 Train-the-Trainer) Courses, and emerging training solutions.
 
Contractor will support curricula management, exercise coordination, execution, and other administrative 
support efforts related to MTT and VTT training efforts. The contractor shall provide experienced full- 
time personnel who meet the specific skill sets as defined in para 3, and who are willing to travel up to 
40% of the time and who possess exceptional oral and written communication skills. These individuals  
must also possess expertise in Navy Region and Installation integrated training, Emergency Management 
processes, and training/exercise assessments as well as a minimum of five years' experience developing 
and providing training both in person and virtually.

This revised RFC removes all Help Desk related scope and terminology. References to incidents,

Purpose of This Follow-up Request for CollaboraƟon 
The U.S. Census Bureau (USCB) is issuing this Request for CollaboraƟon (RFC) to follow on the 
insights gained from the iniƟal Decennial-as-a-Service (D-X) Request for InformaƟon (RFI)  SAM 
noƟce #13PDRD25Q00000007 on 8/14/25, to gather addiƟonal industry input on areas not fully 
addressed in the original RFI responses. As we conƟnue reﬁning our acquisiƟon strategy, the 
USCB remains commiƩed to transparency, open communicaƟon, and meaningful collaboraƟon 
with industry partners. Accordingly, this RFC is designed to: 
 Address capability areas not fully addressed in the original RFI 
 Validate assumpƟons and operaƟonal models held by the government 
 Encourage industry to share best pracƟces, risks, and integraƟon strategies 
 Strengthen alignment between government expectaƟons and commercial capabiliƟes 
 Support a more informed, evidence-based acquisiƟon approach 
The detailed scope and operaƟonal descripƟons provided in the iniƟal D-X RFI conƟnue to serve as the baseline for 
this RFC. Please consider that informaƟon when assessing capability gaps or dependencies. 
The Census Bureau values industry experƟse and seeks to ensure that the D-X soluƟon is shaped 
through open dialogue, shared understanding, and collaboraƟve problem-solving. 
This RFC seeks industry partners capable of delivering a single fully integrated, naƟonwide 
equipment and endpoint lifecycle management ecosystem, operaƟng under a single-integrator 
model, to support logisƟcs, equipment handling, cellular services, site deployments, and 
operaƟonal support funcƟons necessary for the 2028 Dress Rehearsal and 2030 Decennial 
Census operaƟonal readiness across all states and U.S. territories. 
BACKGROUND  
The objecƟve of the D-X program is to deliver a complete, as-a-service soluƟon for centralized 
management of standard equipment and mobile devices that ensures cybersecurity 
compliance, operaƟonal eﬃciency, cost transparency, and end-to-end lifecycle accountability, 
while meeƟng all schedule milestones for the 2028 Dress Rehearsal and 2030 Decennial Census, 
including site deployment and teardown Ɵmelines, mobile device deployment cycles, ATO 
approvals, and system go-live dates.  The D-X soluƟon must be a turnkey, FedRAMP-authorized, 
NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5-compliant, ATO-authorized, as-a-service operaƟonal ecosystem, 
coordinated under a single-integrator model, and including but not limited to the following 
capabiliƟes: 
 
 Devices, equipment and asset management services

o End-to-end management of all standard equipment and devices provided as-a-
service, including but not limited to mobile devices, peripherals, networking gear, 
printers/MFPs, and paper data capture equipment 
o Mobile device provisioning, conﬁguraƟon, and deployment 
o Equipment maintenance, repair, replacement and compliant disposiƟon 
o Inventory accuracy, chain-of-custody tracking, and real-Ɵme asset visibility

o Support for site deployments across all states and U.S. territories, including 
remote and island locaƟons, including installaƟon of vendor supplied equipment, 
peripherals, and other site-based infrastructure required to establish fully 
operaƟonal ﬁeld oﬃces. 
 Mobility, Uniﬁed Endpoint Management (UEM), and Cellular Services 
o UEM for device conﬁguraƟon, compliance, patching, and security baselines, and 
cross-plaƞorm governance to ensure that all mobile devices, regardless of 
operaƟng system or management plaƞorm, follow the same security baselines,

 Mobile Device Management (MDM) for device enrollment, policy

o FedRAMP-authorized, NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5-compliant hosƟng and security

Transparency and CollaboraƟon 
 This noƟce is part of our broader eﬀort to build a collaboraƟve, transparent, and 
industry-informed acquisiƟon environment for D-X. The Census Bureau may work to 
support a fair, informed, and well-aligned acquisiƟon process through the following: 
Publishing relevant operaƟonal plans, schedules, milestones, and mission constraints, as

 Engaging in two-way, iteraƟve communicaƟon, including follow-up quesƟons, reverse
