 InviƟng industry feedback on feasibility, risks, and alternaƟves, and ensuring vendors 
have equal access to the informaƟon needed to develop well-informed responses. 
AddiƟonal InformaƟon for Industry 
The following areas were not fully addressed in the original RFI and require input to support 
planning, integraƟon, and acquisiƟon strategy development. 
For the purposes of this RFC, “Everything-as-a-Service (XaaS)” refers to a fully managed, subscripƟon-based service 
model in which vendors deliver the tools, technology, processes, people, and outcomes required to support Census 
operaƟons. This includes OEM-agnosƟc soluƟons, integrated service delivery, predictable pricing, and end-to-end 
lifecycle management across mulƟple service domains. The Census Bureau uses XaaS to describe a uniﬁed 
ecosystem of managed services that collecƟvely supports the 2028 Dress Rehearsal and 2030 Census. 
Managed Service Integrator (MSI) Model 
The USCB is considering a single-integrator model in which one Managed Service Integrator 
(MSI) provides end-to-end orchestraƟon across all D-X service domains. This MSI would 
coordinate mulƟple XaaS providers and ensure uniﬁed governance, interoperability, and 
accountability across logisƟcs, mobility, devices, warehousing, asset management, cellular 
services, site deployments, and support operaƟons. The USCB is seeking industry insight into 
MSI models, governance structures, and best pracƟces for managing a large, mulƟ-vendor 
ecosystem under a single-integrator construct. 
AssumpƟons: 
 Demonstrated experience coordinaƟng many diﬀerent operaƟonal areas, such as 
logisƟcs, devices, mobility, cellular services, site deployments, and support, so they 
funcƟon as one integrated service. 
 Proven tools and processes to keep all systems and vendors aligned, sharing accurate 
data, and working together smoothly across the enƟre operaƟon. 
 Can manage and support Decennial Census operaƟons across all states and U.S. 
territories, including remote and island locaƟons, making sure equipment, deployments, 
logisƟcs, cellular services, and support all work together smoothly at naƟonwide scale. 
 Takes responsibility for delivering consistent, end-to-end service outcomes across all 
operaƟonal areas, not just managing individual vendors 

 
6 
 
Command Center AssumpƟons 
The D-X vision includes a Command Center that provides a real-Ɵme operaƟonal cross-domain 
layer that provides conƟnuous visibility, coordinated response, and cross-domain decision 
support across the D-X ecosystem. It uniﬁes data from logisƟcs, asset management, endpoint 
management, cellular services, and help desk other XaaS-domain workﬂows into a single 
operaƟonal view, enabling leadership and operaƟons teams to monitor service health, track 
incidents and requests across departments track cross-domain condiƟons and workﬂow acƟvity, 
and take acƟon without switching between systems. 
AssumpƟons: 
 Provides a uniﬁed operaƟonal picture that enables real-Ɵme monitoring of service 
health, incident trendsservice-tower condiƟons, and cross-domain workﬂow status 
across all D-X service areas XaaS domains. 
 Enables proacƟve operaƟonsmanagement, including endpoint health monitoring, 
vulnerability tracking, and ﬁeld service coordinaƟon, by leveraging integrated data and 
automated alerƟng across all Ɵers XaaS towers. 
 Supports coordinated incident response and case rouƟng acrossresponse and workﬂow 
rouƟng across IT, HR, Safety, LogisƟcs, and ﬁeld operaƟonsother D-X service domains, 
ensuring that leadership and operaƟonal teams can track progress and take acƟon from 
a single environment. 
 Operates on a common data foundaƟon that may support AI-driven automaƟon, 
allowing the system to autonomously resolve requests, execute mulƟ-step workﬂows, 
and complete end-to-end acƟons within established policies. 
Data Interoperability and IntegraƟon 
D-X will rely on a combinaƟon of mulƟple commercial and government systems working 
together seamlessly. To achieve this, the USCB must understand how vendors approach data 
integraƟon, API frameworks, synchronizaƟon, and real-Ɵme visibility across disparate plaƞorms, 
including those operated by federal partners. We are seeking industry insight into best 
pracƟces, integraƟon paƩerns, and potenƟal challenges associated with building a uniﬁed 
operaƟonal ecosystem that spans both commercial and government environments. 
AssumpƟons: 
 Integrates commercial and government systems into a uniﬁed operaƟonal ecosystem 
that supports seamless data exchange and coordinated service delivery. 
 Applies federal and commercial best pracƟces to ensure data quality, synchronizaƟon, 
and real-Ɵme visibility across diverse plaƞorms and partner environments. 
 Provides end-to-end integraƟon across logisƟcs, UEM, cellular, and asset management 
systems to enable consistent, mission-ready operaƟons. 

 
7 
 
OEM-AgnosƟc Device and Equipment As-a-Service Models 
The USCB is evaluaƟng OEM-agnosƟc as-a-service models for mobile devices (smartphones, 
tablets, laptops), oﬃce equipment (printers, mulƟfuncƟon devices), paper data-capture 
equipment (scanners, leƩer openers, guilloƟnes), and oﬃce networking equipment (access 
points, servers, and related infrastructure). These models may include brand-speciﬁc or 
equivalent conﬁguraƟons where required. The USCB seeks industry input on how such 
as-a-service oﬀerings are typically structured commercially, including provisioning approaches, 
service levels, lifecycle services, refresh strategies, and performance management. The USCB 
also requests informaƟon on risks, dependencies, and constraints that should be considered 
when implemenƟng an enterprise-scale, mulƟ-vendor as-a-service model. 
AssumpƟons: 
 Bundles diverse equipment categories, including mobile devices, oﬃce and paper data 
capture equipment, scanners, and networking hardware, into a uniﬁed, scalable, 
OEM-agnosƟc program that delivers provisioning, kiƫ ng, and lifecycle services. 
 Predictable pricing, refresh cycles, and service-level commitments that are in alignment 
with other large-scale as-a-service programs, including break/ﬁx services, rapid 
replacement SLAs, inventory pooling, buﬀer stock strategies, and secure end-of-life 
disposiƟon. 
 Supports enterprise-scale device volumes, including approximately 360,000 
smartphones, 20,000 tablets, and 20,000 laptops, with the ability to surge or de-surge 
inventory and services based on operaƟonal tempo and ﬁeld deployment needs. 
 Provide cellular service for all mobile devices naƟonwide across all states and U.S. 
territories by leveraging the best-performing local carriers in each area, supported by 
performance monitoring, availability metrics, and rapid carrier remediaƟon path

(b) Nature of Work: Corporal Michael J Crecenz VA Medical Center (CMCVAMC) in 
Philadelphia, PA, is seeking Architect-Engineering (A/E) services to develop working 
drawings, phasing plans, infection control plans, contract specifications, and cost 
estimates for full and complete construction of Project No. 642-25-125, A/E – Remove 
and Replace Building 2 Grease Trap.  
II.  PROJECT INFORMATION (Scope of Work):
A/E – Remove and Replace Building 2 Grease Trap:
The A/E shall provide design and engineering services for this design project, including all 
applicable site visits, laser and video scanning, field investigation, studies, and user interviews 
to prepare construction drawings, specifications, narratives, cost estimates and schedules 
associated with the following work:
(a) Perform field investigative services, including underground and video scanning, of all 
surrounding utility lines and piping associated with the grease trap, including inlet piping 
from kitchen to outlet piping to sanitary system. Determine integrity of piping, whether 
complete removal and replacement of existing piping is required or an alternate solution 
such as pipe jetting and lining. Complete removal and replacement of piping shall 
require additional engineering services, such as civil and structural engineering.
(b) Design a new grease entrapment system for the Building 2 kitchen. Entrapment system 
shall provide similar or increased grease capacity.
(c) Design phasing. Temporary grease entrapment system for the duration of the 
construction project. A Traffic control plan. Demolition and construction plan, including 
removal of manhole and associated concrete, trenching and shoring work.

DISTRIBUTION STATEMENT A. Approved for public released; distribution unlimited 
 
Approved for Public Release 
26-MDA-12338 
REQUEST FOR INFORMATION  
 
Missile Defense System - Next (MDS-Next) 
 Capability Solutions for Strategic Architecture Thrust Areas  
 
Notice Number: 26-MDA-12338 
 
NAICS Code: 541715 - Research and development in the physical, engineering, and life 
sciences, except nanotechnology and biotechnology 
 
 
1.0 BACKGROUND 
 
The Missile Defense Agency (MDA) is executing a strategic planning effort to inform future 
capability development and investment opportunities in response to the 2035+ projected threat 
environment. As part of this effort, the Agency has identified Strategic Architecture Thrust 
Areas representing priority focus areas for advancing missile defense capabilities in the 2035+ 
timeframe. These thrust areas reflect where the Agency is seeking new or alternative 
approaches to address future mission challenges and achieve improved mission outcomes. 
 
This RFI represents the transition from identifying and prioritizing strategic focus areas to 
evaluating solution approaches that can advance those areas. Responses will inform 
prioritization of capability areas and potential POM investment decisions.  
 
Detailed descriptions of the Strategic Architecture Thrust Areas will be available to 
respondents with the appropriate clearance level. Additional context on future capability 
attributes is provided in the MDS-Next Characteristics briefing that will be available to 
respondents at the Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) level. See Section 9.0 for 
instructions on requesting access to these resources.   
 
2.0 OBJECTIVE 
 
The objective of this RFI is to obtain solution-oriented information describing specific capability 
approaches and architectural concepts that advance one or more of the identified Strategic 
Architecture Thrust Areas. Responses should clearly describe what capability is being proposed, 
how it addresses the thrust area, and how it improves mission outcomes. 
Information received will be used to: 
• Identify solution approaches that measurably address validated Strategic Architecture 
Thrust Areas 
• Assess the technical feasibility, maturity, and integration considerations of proposed 
approaches 
• Enable focused technical dialogue and evaluation at the 1:1 technical exchange  
• Inform prioritization of potential capability areas and support POM-28 investment 
decisions 
 
This effort is intended to produce decision-relevant insights to further long-range planning 
efforts. 
 
3.0 STRATEGIC FRAMING 

 
DISTRIBUTION STATEMENT A. Approved for public released; distribution unlimited 
 
Approved for Public Release 
26-MDA-12338 
 
The Agency is not solely seeking incremental improvements to existing systems or approaches. 
Respondents are encouraged to consider whether fundamentally different capability constructs, 
architectures, or operational concepts are required to advance the identified Strategic 
Architecture Thrust Areas. 
 
In particular, respondents should consider: 
• Whether current approaches represent the most effective and efficient path forward, or if 
alternative paradigms may provide greater mission advantage 
• What new capabilities or concepts, including those developed outside traditional missile 
defense applications, could be adapted to significantly improve outcomes 
• Preference will be given emerging technologies, cross-domain solutions, or non-
traditional approaches that could change how the mission is executed or approached 
 
The intent is to identify both evolutionary improvements and non-traditional or disruptive 
approaches that provide meaningful operational advantage. 
 
4.0 SCOPE 
 
Responses should focus on capability-level approaches and architectural concepts that: 
• Directly align to one or more Strategic Architecture Thrust Areas  
• Address challenges posed by the 2035+ projected threat environment 
• Demonstrate the potential to improve operational effectiveness at the system or mission 
level 
 
Respondents should consider: 
• How the proposed approach changes outcomes relative to the identified Strategic 
Architecture Thrust(s), and if applicable, the Key Area(s) where the architecture would 
particularly benefit from additional science and technology (S&T)  
• Applicability across multiple mission areas or threat sets, where relevant 
• Integration with existing and planned missile defense architectures 
 
5.0 SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS 
 
Respondents shall use the Strategic Architecture Thrust Areas to ensure clear alignment of 
proposed solutions. The MDS-Next Characteristics briefing is provided as additional context to 
inform how proposed approaches align to desired future mission attributes. The characteristics 
briefing is not an exhaustive list and is provided as reference. Characteristics provided in the 
briefing should not be interpreted as limiting or constraining potential solutions.   
 
Submissions must clearly align to one or more Strategic Architecture Thrust Areas. Responses 
should be specific, structured, and focused on capability outcomes. Respondents should avoid 
general descriptions, marketing material, or platform-centric responses. Responses that do not 
demonstrate clear alignment or sufficient detail may be assessed as less relevant. 
 
Responses shall be submitted as concise pitch papers and must address the following elements: 
 
• Strategic Architecture Thrust Area Alignment 

 
DISTRIBUTION STATEMENT A. Approved for public released; distribution unlimited 
 
Approved for Public Release 
26-MDA-12338 
o Identify the specific Strategic Architecture Thrust(s) and Key Area(s) addressed 
and describe how the proposed approach advances that intent  
o Maintain clear traceability to the Strategic Architecture Thrust(s) and Key Area(s) 
throughout the response 
 
• Capability Approach 
o Provide a clear description of the proposed capability or architectural concept 
o Describe: 
 The function of the capability 
 How it operates within the broader system 
o Responses should address: 
 Whether the approach represents a new or alternative way to achieve the 
mission outcome 
 How it differs from or improves upon current or planned capabilities 
 Estimated timeline to achieve initial operational fielding of the proposed 
capability, including key milestones for development, prototyping, testing, 
and deployment 
o Where applicable, identify: 
 Approaches derived from other domains, missions, or industries 
 Capabilities not traditionally associated with missile defense that could be 
adapted to this mission 
 
• Operational Impact 
o Describe how the approach improves mission outcomes in relation to the thrust 
area 
o Address: 
 What operational limitations are mitigated or eliminated 
 Whether the approach enables new operational concepts or reduces 
reliance on existing constructs 
o Clearly articulate whether the approach: 
 Enhances current capabilities, or 
 Fundamentally changes how the mission is performed 
 
• Technical Feasibility and Maturity 
o Describe the current level of maturity (concept, prototype, demonstration, etc.) 
o Technology Readiness Level  
o Identify key technical challenges, risks, or dependencies 
 
• Cost Considerations 
o Provide the estimated Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) cost for the proposed 
solution, including development, prototyping, integration, production, and 
fielding, as applicable 
o Identify: 
 Major cost drivers and underlying assumptions 
 Any dependencies on Government-furnished resources, infrastructure, or 
enabling capabilities 
 Areas of cost uncertainty or variables that could materially affect the 
estimate 
 

 
DISTRIBUTION STATEMENT A. Approved for public released; distribution unlimited 
 
Approved for Public Release 
26-MDA-12338 
• Integration Considerations 
o Describe how the approach would integrate with: 
 Existing systems 
 Planned architectures 
o Identify required interfaces, dependencies, and enabling capabilities 
 
• Small Business Considerations 
o The Government is seeking to understand the capability of small businesses to 
contribute to the Strategic Architecture Thrust Areas and to inform potential 
future acquisition strategies. 
o Small business respondents are requested to address the following: 
 Describe relevant capabilities, technologies, or solution approaches the 
small business can provide that align to the Strategic Architecture Thrust 
Areas 
 Identify any unique or innovative contributions the small business brings, 
including capabilities derived from non-traditional or commercial 
applications 
o If proposing a teaming arrangement, describe: 
 The role of the small business in the overall solution 
 Any teaming partners or subcontractors, as applicable 
 How the small business contributes to the overall capability approach 
 
• Additional Considerations 
o Respondents are strongly encouraged to identify solutions that: 
 Leverage capabilities from other Services, Agencies, or Departments 
 Adapt technologies or concepts from the commercial sector or other 
mission areas 
 Reduce costs per missile defense kill or sustainment costs of fielded 
system 
 Represent cross-domain or non-traditional applications relevant to missile 
defense 
 
6.0 USE OF SUBMISSIONS  
 
Responses will be reviewed by the Agency to identify Technology Areas for further examination 
and will inform prioritization of capability areas and potential POM investment decisions. The 
submissions will be discussed as part of the respondent’s requested 1:1 technical exchange. 
Submission does not constitute a commitment by the Agency to pursue any specific approach or 
activity.

B.2  ORDER LIMITATIONS, CONTRACT CEILING, AND ORDERING PROCEDURES

This Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract has a base ordering period of sixty (60) months from the date of award. The effective period of the contract shall include this ordering period and shall continue until completion of the final Task Order (TO) issued under the contract. The period of performance of any TO is independent of the base ordering period, and TO performance may extend beyond the expiration of the ordering period, provided the TO was issued prior to the end of the ordering period. The Government is under no obligation to issue any TOs against this contract beyond satisfaction of the minimum ordering guarantee. TOs may be issued at any time during the base ordering period. Any duly warranted Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Contracting Officer is authorized to place orders under this IDIQ contract.

The TOTAL MAXIMUM CONTRACT VALUE, defined as the cumulative sum of all contractor payment obligations associated with all TOs issued under this IDIQ contract, shall not exceed $6,400,176. The MINIMUM GUARANTEE ORDER(S) VALUE for this IDIQ contract award is $2,000.00, provided that the Contractor demonstrates it has exercised due diligence and made its best efforts to secure one or more TOs under this contract.

Ordering under this IDIQ contract will be conducted in accordance with applicable laws and regulations governing placement of orders under multiple award IDIQ contracts. The Government reserves the right to use written or oral communications, including but not limited to written proposals, oral presentations, or a combination thereof, as appropriate to the nature and complexity of each requirement. For new projects (i.e., requirements that are not follow on or continuation efforts where an incumbent on this IDIQ is the primary facilitator (PF)), the Government will provide fair opportunity to all eligible IDIQ awardees in accordance with applicable regulation. Selection criteria for new project TO awards may include any combination of the following factors, listed in no particular order of importance unless otherwise specified in the TO request: technical approach and capability, price/cost, and past performance. The relative importance of these factors and the specific evaluation method (Best Value, LPTA, or price only) will be stated in the TO request, and the Government reserves the right to tailor the evaluation factors and their relative importance for each individual TO.

For existing projects where a contractor under this IDIQ is already performing as the primary facilitator (PF) on the requirement (even on a separate contract unrelated to the IDIQ), the Government may place follow on or continuation TOs directly with that contractor on a non-competitive basis. In such cases, fair opportunity procedures will not apply and the Government may make a direct award to the incumbent PF when justified and in the Government’s best interest.

The minimum ordering guarantee under this IDIQ will be satisfied through TOs associated with the ESPC projects at VISN 16 (Locations TBD) and Dayton. The Government intends to non-competitively issue one TO for VISN 16 (Locations TBD) and one TO for Dayton, OH to IDIQ awardees, at the Government’s discretion. Continuity of Operations Plan – Abbreviated Performance Work Statement (PWS)   
 
Introduction and Background 
The United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) is the federal agency for granting U.S. 
patents and registering trademarks. The strength and vitality of the U.S. economy depends 
directly on effective mechanisms that protect new ideas and investments in innovation and 
creativity. The continued demand for patents and trademarks underscores the ingenuity of 
American inventors and entrepreneurs.  
The Office of the Chief Administrative Officer (OCAO), Office of Administrative Services, 
Security and Emergency Management Division oversees implementation and compliance with 
all federal laws and regulations pertaining to COOP and OEP programs including developing 
plans, procedures, training materials and educational programs for designated COOP; Pandemic, 
Emergency Communications, and OEP (such as printed material, articles, Power Point, 
classroom and computer-based training). 
The Office of Procurement (OP) within OCFO awards and administers a wide variety of 
contracts and simplified purchases for the acquisition of goods and services in support of the 
agency’s mission. It seeks to obtain immediate program support to help perform day-to-day 
activities as the office continues to grow and expand to meet demand. 
 
Purpose and Scope 
 
Purpose  
The purpose of the COR contract is to acquire support services by securing a company that will 
provide four Emergency Management Specialists and one supervisor to assist the Security and 
Emergency Management Division with assessing USPTO’s COOP program and revising the 
COOP plan to adhere to the recently updated Federal Continuity Directives (FCD). Focus areas 
include; gap analysis; Mission Essential Function (MEF) Validation; Business Process Analysis 
(requirement) / Business Impact Analysis (BIA); COOP Plan update and documentation; and 
developing a Training, Testing, and Exercise (TT&E) Program. All work must conform with 
applicable federal government regulations and policies, as well as other agency supplemental 
regulations and policies as appropriate.  
 
Scope / Performance Elements  
The Contractor shall perform to the requirements and performance objectives listed in this 
contract.  
 
Continuity of Operations (COOP) - Performance Elements  
• Objective 1 - Gather COOP and Emergency Management documentation, conduct 
interviews, analyze operations and needs to develop a gap analysis based on current 
Continuity Directives. 
• Objective 2 - Review MEF’s, validate or revise then prioritize MEF(s), conduct a MEF 
validation report. 
• Objective 3 - Conduct a full Business Process Analysis / Business Process Analysis 
through workshops and interviews with Business Units. 
• Objective 4 - Update the COOP plan structure and framework to align with the newly 
updated Federal Continuity Directives, to include Primary, Alternate, Contingency, 

Abbreviated PWS for RFI Number: ACQ-26-0982 EMS/COOP Support Services Page 2 of 8 
 
and Emergency (PACE) communications strategies and procedures. Provide a final 
documentation package. 
• Objective 5 - Develop TT&E program and requirements based on the updated plan 
and develop an AAR/IP. 
 
Planning 
 
Continuity of Operations Support - Major Activities 
1. Conduct a gap analysis on USPTO’s COOP Program utilizing the most recently 
updated Federal Continuity Guidance. 
2. Validate or conduct a MEF identification to solidify USPTO’s essential function(s). 
3. Conduct a risk-based requirement/BIA based off of the MEF identification process.   
4. Assist in the revision and modernization of USPTO COOP Plan and annexes by 
defining mission owners, building an effective structure, ensure plans are integrated 
into daily activities, and incorporate PACE communication requirements in 
accordance with the most recent FCD’s. 
5. Assist appropriate Business Units in developing and maintaining COOP plans, 
procedures, and rosters. 
6. Support actions needed to maintain agency continuity assets, including devolution, 
alternate operating facilities, essential records, and continuity communications 
systems.  
7. Ensures that the MEF ID/ requirement-BIA / COOP plans and procedures / Alternate

Statement of Work (SOW) for Main Reduction Gears Engineering Services

1.0 INTRODUCTION

1.0.1  The Naval Surface Warfare Center Philadelphia Division (NSWCPD) is a Department of Defense entity responsible for research and development, test and evaluation, engineering and fleet support organization for the Navy’s ships, submarines, military watercraft and unmanned vehicles. This requirement is for NSWCPD Code 426, which has responsibility for Lifecycle Management (LCM) and In-Service Engineering (ISE) for US Navy Main Reduction Gears (MRG). The LCM and ISE mission involves maintaining adequate and effective operational readiness, safety and mission effectiveness of US Navy MRGs and their associated auxiliary systems. In support of this mission, NSWCPD provides engineered solutions to fleet MRG problems.

MRG Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) design, construct, install, service, support and provide repair and replacement parts for the gearboxes under their purview. They possess certain unique knowledge, experience and expertise, and access to technical information that is not available elsewhere. 

In support of its MRG LCM and ISEA mission, NSWCPD intends to leverage off the contractor’s unique knowledge, experience and expertise, and access to technical information related to the RENK BUSL 261, RENK ASL 2/160, RENK BOS 156, and RENK ASL 95 reduction gear models, for the purpose of improving in-service and lifecycle support initiatives. The contractor will assist NSWCPD in developing, delivering and executing engineered solutions to fleet MRG problems.

1.0.2  This contract is for non-personal services.  It does not create employment rights with the U.S. Government whether actual, inherent, or implied

1.0.3  Government/Contractor Relationship

1.0.3.1  The services to be delivered under this Contract are non-personal services and the parties recognize and agree that no employer-employee relationship exists or will exist under the Contract between the Government and the Contractor's personnel.  Therefore, it is in the best interest of the Government to provide both parties a full understanding of their respective obligations. 

1.0.3.2  The Contractor employees shall identify themselves as Contractor personnel by introducing themselves or being introduced as Contractor personnel and displaying distinguishable badges or other visible identification for meetings with Government personnel. In addition, Contractor personnel shall appropriately identify themselves as Contractor employees in telephone conversations and in formal and informal written correspondence.

1.0.3.3   Contractor personnel under this Contract shall not engage in any of the inherently Governmental functions listed at FAR Subpart 7.5 or DFARS Subpart 207.5. 

1.0.4  Employee Relationship: 

1.0.4.1  The services to be performed under this Contract do not require the Contractor or its personnel to exercise personal judgment and discretion on behalf of the Government.  Rather the Contractor's personnel will act and exercise personal judgment and discretion on behalf of the Contractor.  

1.0.4.2  Rules, regulations, directives, and requirements that are issued by the U. S. Navy and NSWCPD under its responsibility for good order, administration, and security are applicable to all personnel who enter a Government installation or who travel on Government transportation.  This is not to be construed or interpreted to establish any degree of Government control that is inconsistent with a non-personal services contract. 

1.0.4.3  Inapplicability of Employee Benefits: This Contract does not create an employer-employee relationship.  Accordingly, entitlements and benefits applicable to such relationships do not apply.   

1.0.4.4  It is the Contractor's, as well as the Government's, responsibility to monitor Contract activities and notify the Contracting Officer if the Contractor believes that the intent of this Section has been or may be violated.  

1.0.4.4.1  The Contractor shall notify the Contracting Officer in writing via letter or email within three (3) calendar days from the date of any incident that the Contractor considers to constitute a violation of this Section.  The notice should include the date, nature, and circumstances of the conduct; the name, function, and activity of each Government employee or Contractor official or employee involved or knowledgeable about such conduct; identify any documents or substance of any oral communication involved in the conduct; and the Contractor's estimated date when, absent a response, cost, schedule or performance will be impacted.

1.0.4.4.2  The Contracting Officer will, within five (5) calendar days after receipt of notice, respond to the notice in writing.  In responding, the Contracting Officer will either:

(i)	Confirm the conduct is in violation and when necessary direct the mode of further performance,

(ii)	Countermand any communication regarded as a violation,

(iii)	Deny that the conduct constitutes a violation and when necessary direct the mode of further performance, or

(iv)	In the event the notice is inadequate to make a decision, advise the Contractor what additional information is required, and establish the date by which it should be furnished by the Contractor.  

BACKGROUND 

Virtually all mechanical equipment needs continuing engineering support to solve operational problems. Military systems require a higher level of engineering support than commercial equivalent systems. The military systems normally push the leading edge of technology and are subjected to ever-changing and demanding environments and mission cycles. New problems are continually experienced after approval for operational use. The new problems are a result of greater exposure, changes in mission, changes in system weight or configuration, variations in manufacture or repair, aging of the hardware, maintenance concept changes, critical materials availability, and changing component coating and fuel compounds. (i.e.: Bio-Fuel technologies and similar advances). These changes in engine usage can be dramatic and can have a dramatic impact on safety, readiness, and mission effectiveness. Therefore, a direct contract relationship with MRG OEMs is essential to maintain these systems at full operational capability.

SCOPE OF WORK 

This Statement of Work (SOW) describes services to be applied via Task Orders (TOs) detailing specific support requirements within the scope of this contract SOW. The overall scope of this SOW is to provide lifecycle, modernization and in-service support for the RENK BUSL 261, ASL 2/160, BOS 156, and ASL 95 reduction gear models and their related shipboard auxiliary systems. The support required will involve technical, logistics, training, administrative and program management efforts related to reduction gear lifecycle and in-service concerns.

3.4 Product improvements (design, development, testing & evaluation, and deployment) - The contractor shall provide materials, engineering personnel, and the manufacturing and testing facilities to design parts, components, or systems to meet the program objectives and support new technology development and integration. The contractor shall validate the designs by bench tests, MRG system tests, and support of fleet evaluations. Engineering Change Proposals (ECP) and associated technical data shall be developed and submitted. The purpose of this Request for Information (RFI) is to gather market research information for

Verification/Validation (IV&V) for the Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) hardware/
software integration for the Sentinel Weapon System. NSCCA/NSATE is defined in AFMAN

Verification/Validation options for Nuclear Surety for FPGA hardware/software integration for 
the Sentinel Weapon System.

PRE-SOLICITATION NON-COMPETITIVE –  
Notice of Intent to Sole Source 
1. SOLICITATION NUMBER: 75N98026Q00234 
 
2. TITLE: External Institutional Review Board (IRB) Services for Multi-Site 
Studies 
3. RESPONSE DATE: May 5, 2026, at 9:00 am EDT.  
 
4. PRIMARY POINT OF CONTACT: 
Nicholas Capobianco 
nicholas.capobianco@nih.gov  
 
I. INTRODUCTION: 
THIS IS A PRE-SOLICITATION NON-COMPETITIVE (NOTICE OF INTENT) 
SYNOPSIS TO AWARD A CONTRACT WITHOUT PROVIDING FOR FULL OR 
OPEN COMPETITION (INCLUDING BRAND-NAME).  
 
The National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NHLBI), Division of Intramural 
Research (DIR), requires continued Institutional Review Board (IRB) services to 
support ongoing multi-site clinical research studies conducted under Investigational 
Device Exemption (IDE) and Investigational New Drug (IND) protocols. These studies 
involve multiple participating sites and require centralized IRB oversight in accordance 
with NIH policy. 
The NIH Intramural IRB is currently unable to serve as the IRB of record for certain 
NHLBI multi-site studies, including those with existing reliance on a commercial IRB 
and those requiring continuity through study closeout. As a result, NHLBI requires the 
services of an external IRB to ensure uninterrupted regulatory oversight, subject safety, 
and data integrity. 
 
 
II. NORTH AMERICAN INDUSTRY CLASSIFICATION SYSTEM (NAICS) 
CODE and SET ASIDE STATUS 
NAICS Code: 541990 – All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services 
Size Standard: $19.5 million 
This acquisition is not set aside for small business. 
 
 
III. REGULATORY AUTHORITY  
The resultant contract will include all applicable provisions and clauses in effect through 
the Federal Acquisition Circular (FAC) 2024-07 dated 08-29-2024. 

This acquisition is conducted under the procedures as prescribed in FAR Part 12—
Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services and FAR Part 13—
Simplified Acquisition Procedures. 
 
IV. STATUTORY AUTHORITY 
This acquisition is for a commercial service and is conducted under the authority of FAR 
13.106-1(b)(1)—Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will 
Satisfy Agency Requirements. 
 
V. DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENT: 
Purchase Description: 
The Contractor shall provide IRB services on an as-needed basis, including but not 
limited to: 
• Initial and continuing review of multi-site study protocols 
• Review of investigators and sub-investigators 
• Review of informed consent forms (ICFs), including site-specific language 
• Review of recruitment materials and subject-facing documents 
• Review of protocol amendments and modifications 
• Review of reportable events requiring full board review 
• Site closeout activities 
• Administrative reviews and changes 
• Emergency use reviews, as required 
Salient Characteristics: 
The required services must meet the following minimum characteristics: 
• Ability to serve as the IRB of record for ongoing multi-site FDA-regulated 
clinical studies (IDE/IND) 
• Capability to maintain continuity of IRB oversight for active protocols without 
disruption 
• Existing infrastructure to support reliance agreements across multiple study sites 
• Compliance with all applicable federal regulations, including 45 CFR 46 and 21 
CFR 56 
• Ability to support ongoing reporting, amendments, and closeout activities for 
studies currently under review 
• Secure handling of sensitive human subjects research information 
 
PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE: 
June 1, 2026 – May 31, 2027 
 
PLACE OF PERFORMANCE: 
Services will be performed remotely via electronic communication between the 
Contractor and NHLBI personnel. 

VI. CONTRACTING WITHOUT PROVIDING FOR FULL OR OPEN 
COMPETITION (INCLUDING BRAND-NAME) DETERMINATION 
The Government intends to award a sole source contract to: 
Advarra, Inc. 
6100 Merriweather Drive, Suite 600 
Columbia, Maryland 21044 
This determination is based on the need for continuity of IRB oversight for ongoing 
multi-site clinical studies currently under review by Advarra. Transitioning to a different 
IRB provider at this stage would introduce unacceptable risks, including disruption to 
regulatory oversight, potential impacts to subject safety, and compromise of data 
integrity. 
Existing reliance agreements and the history of oversight associated with these studies 
further necessitate continued use of the current IRB of record through study completion. 
 
VII. CLOSING STATEMENT 
THIS SYNOPSIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS. However, 
interested parties may identify their interest and capability to respond to this notice. 
A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon 
responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. All responsible 
sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation which shall be 
considered by the agency. 
Responses must include sufficient detail to demonstrate the capability to meet the 
requirement and must include pricing information, delivery timelines, business size 
status, and proof of active SAM registration. 
All responses must be received by the closing date and time of this announcement and 
must reference the solicitation number, 75N98026Q00234. Responses must be submitted 
electronically to Nicholas Capobianco, Contract Specialist at 
nicholas.capobianco@nih.gov.

Introduction: 
Mobile Command and Control Systems (MC2S) Branch has the responsibility of acquiring 
and sustaining mobile C2 systems in support of the U.S. Air Force and Department of 
Defense. The MC2S Branch is conducting market research through this Sources Sought 
Request for Information (RFI) for the intended competition of the MC2S requirement. A 
Classiﬁed Industry Day to include one-on-one sessions is notionally planned for the mid-
July timeframe, but subject to change.  Conﬁrmation of dates and attendance instructions 
for Industry Day will be determined and announced separately after responses to this RFI 
are reviewed.  
This is a request for information only and does not constitute a request for quote (RFQ) or 
request for proposal (RFP), or a promise to issue an RFQ or RFP in the future.  
General Information: 
Please provide the following information in response to this RFI: 
- Company Name 
- Company Address 
- Company Point of Contact (POC) 
- CAGE Code 
- NAICS Code(s) 
- Company Status as Large or Small Business 
- Company Facility Clearance Level 
To the maximum extent possible, please submit non-proprietary information. Any 
proprietary information submitted shall be identiﬁed as such and handled/protected in 
accordance with applicable Government regulations. The Government requests responses 
to the questions below. Respondents are welcome to provide additional information not 
speciﬁcally requested below. 
The Government will accept unclassiﬁed and classiﬁed responses. The Government will 
provide email addresses where classiﬁed information can be sent upon request.  Please do 
not submit responses greater than 20 pages of original text responses, and no more than 
20 pages of general organizational description materials (brochures or other marketing 
materials). 
Request for Information: 
1. Please provide responses to the following questions that summarize your 
organization’s ability to meet mission-speciﬁc capabilities, ability to sustain 
capabilities, facility capabilities and your ability to meet security requirements. 

2. Mission-speciﬁc capability questions: 
a. What is your organization’s ability to design, integrate, produce, and sustain 
mobile command and control systems-of-systems?  Please provide 
examples of experience in this mission area. 
b. Please provide additional details and experience in the following areas: 
i. System engineering of mobile C2 systems, in particular experience 
with system-of-systems integration.  
ii. Integrating, testing, managing, and sustaining classiﬁed systems.  
iii. Electromagnetic Pulse (EMP). Please detail experience hardening and 
testing systems (IT/comm systems, power systems, HVAC systems, 
etc.), vehicles/transportation capabilities IAW MIL-STD-188-125. 
iv. Mobile, transportable, or ﬁxed power generation systems. 
v. HVAC systems, in particular designing mobile or transportable HVAC 
systems with sizing and space limitations 
vi. Water puriﬁcation systems 
vii. Satellite communications systems, both commercial and military 
viii. Radio systems (RF/HF/UHF etc.), both commercial and military 
ix. Other secure communications capabilities. 
c. Please detail experience partnering, coordinating, and/or working with other 
capability providers (companies or other organizations) to integrate 
capabilities into system-of-system platforms.  
3. System Sustainment questions: 
a. What is your organization’s ability and experience to provide on-going 
sustainment of the systems described in the mission-speciﬁc questions?  
i. Experience conducting periodic depot maintenance (PDM), depot 
level repairs, ﬁeld level repairs (both emergency and routine), or 
equivalent actions.  
ii. Experience developing and/or providing training for delivered systems.  
b. Experience with documentation. Detail experience developing technical 
manuals, network interface documentation, system speciﬁcation 
documentation, engineering drawings, engineering models (MBSE), or other 
relevant data. 
4. Facility and Security questions: 
a. Does the company have cleared facilities? If so, to what level(s) is the facility 
cleared? What networks and/or secure communications capabilities are in 
the facility? Does the company have cleared production and/or maintenance 
spaces within the facility? 

b. Does the company have experience with Government Owned Contractor 
Operated (GOCO) facilities? If so, please provide details on management of a 
GOCO facility. 
c. Please provide examples of current or recent performance of classiﬁed 
requirements or contracts to the best of your ability while providing this 
information at the unclassiﬁed level.  
5. Industry Day attendance: 
a. Please provide whether your company plans to attend the MC2S Industry 
Day. 
b. Please provide whether your company requests a one-on-one session with 
the MC2S Branch for questions.  
i. Industry Day location and dates will be determined after responses to 
this RFI have been reviewed. Details will be provided in a separate 
announcement to industry. For planning purposes, the notional 
Industry Day timeframe is mid-July at Hanscom AFB, Bedford, MA.

Consolidated Performance Work Statement (PWS) 
PROJECT TITLE: Application Arsenal (AA) Enterprise Engineering and Lifecycle Support 
1.0 TASK ORDER PURPOSE 
The purpose of this Task Order is to procure engineering, software development, technical 
services, and program management for the continued design, implementation, security, 
and sustainment of the Application Arsenal (AA) enterprise service. The primary objective is 
to deliver comprehensive lifecycle support to ensure the system operates securely and 
effectively, meeting the evolving needs of the warfighter and government personnel. 
2.0 SCOPE 
The scope of this effort includes the full lifecycle of systems engineering and software 
sustainment for the AA platform. The contractor shall provide all necessary personnel, 
materials, and services to perform the tasks outlined in this PWS. The primary technical 
environment for this effort is the Overmatch Software Armory (OSA); however, work may be 
directed to other government-mandated DevSecOps pipelines (e.g., ORION) as required. 
This contract is intended to be the primary support vehicle for the Application Arsenal 
platform. The performance requirements described below may be initiated and funded by 
diverse DoD Components. The contractor shall support all tasks as directed by the 
Contracting Officer's Representative (COR), provided the work is within the scope of this 
PWS. 
3.0 BACKGROUND 
The Naval Information Warfare Center Pacific (NIWC-PAC) established the Application 
Arsenal (AA) to provide critical software delivery capabilities to the fleet. 
Application Arsenal (AA) is the enterprise distribution, update, and installation service for 
software at the tactical edge. It enables software developed in a software factory to be sent 
Over-The-Air (OTA) to the edge across many different environments. AA currently deploys 
software to Agile Core Services (ACS), the USMC Common Hosting Environment (CHE), the 
Overmatch Production Environment (OPE), Five Eyes (FVEY) partners, and autonomous 
vehicles, with more systems projected to come online. 
This PWS defines the requirements for contractor-provided services essential to enable the 
design, implementation, and sustainment of the AA enterprise service for a diverse set of 
DoD-wide stakeholders, including the Rapid Capabilities Office (RCO), the Portfolio 
Acquisition Executive for Robotic and Autonomous Systems (PAE RAS), the Portfolio 
Acquisition Executive Mission Systems (PAE MS), the U.S. Marine Corps (USMC), and Naval 
Sea Systems Command (NAVSEA). 

4.0 APPLICABLE DOCUMENTS 
The contractor shall comply with all documents referenced in the performance 
requirements that the contractor will have to use or comply with in performance of this 
PWS tasking. This list is not exhaustive, and other documents may be specified in 
individual Task Orders. 
• NIST SP 800-53, "Security and Privacy Controls for Information Systems and 
Organizations" 
• Applicable Department of Defense (DoD) and Department of the Navy (DoN) 
regulations, directives, and instructions. 
5.0 PERFORMANCE REQUIREMENTS 
5.1 Engineering & Integration Requirements 
• 5.1.1 AA Development: The contractor shall provide the planning, development, 
testing, and integration required for all new AA releases and enhancements. 
o 5.1.1.1 Capability Development: Efforts shall include modernizing existing 
deployment architectures by leveraging and integrating with the Overmatch 
Software Armory (OSA) DevSecOps pipeline, deploying with Agile Core 
Services (ACS), and ensuring alignment with the Common Hosting 
Environment (CHE) and other shared government platforms. The contractor 
shall design and implement scalable, secure integration pathways for Navy 
programs of strategic importance, ensuring compliance with mandated 
DevSecOps tooling, security guardrails, and enterprise release practices, 
including interoperability with Five Eyes (FVEY) partners. 
o 5.1.1.2 Cybersecurity Engineering: The contractor shall engineer and 
integrate required cybersecurity controls into new AA releases in alignment 
with Risk Management Framework (RMF) standards. Deliverables shall 
include Security Control Traceability Matrices (SCTMs), Plans of Action and 
Milestones (POAMs), and other documentation required for the Authority to 
Operate (ATO). 
o 5.1.1.3 Fielding: The contractor shall perform the installation, configuration, 
and testing necessary to field new releases across all authorized operational 
environments for CONUS and OCONUS locations, ashore and afloat. This 
effort shall include robust system validation through Factory Acceptance 
Testing (FAT), Site Acceptance Testing (SAT), and System Operational 
Verification Testing (SOVT). 

• 5.1.2 Software Delivery Pipeline Integration and Replication 
o 5.1.2.1 DevSecOps Engineering Services: The contractor shall provide 
engineering services to design, implement, and integrate secure DevSecOps 
pipeline capabilities within the Government-designated DevSecOps 
environment (e.g., OSA, ACS). 
o 5.1.2.2 Secure Software Distribution: The contractor shall develop and 
validate secure methods for efficient transfer and replication of software 
artifacts to remote and distributed environments, including ashore, afloat, 
autonomous, and cloud-hosted domains. 
• 5.1.3 Infrastructure, Command and Control (C2), Autonomous Systems, and 
Cross-Domain Solution (CDS) Integration 
o 5.1.3.1 CDS Engineering and Integration: The contractor shall integrate with 
existing infrastructure and established Cross-Domain Solutions (CDS) to 
provide the secure, bi-directional data transfer capabilities necessary to 
support distributed autonomous operations across disparate security 
domains. 
o 5.1.3.2 Integration Support for Autonomous Systems: The contractor shall 
support the integration of edge servers, autonomous vehicle platforms, and 
related mission systems with currently fielded and emerging technologies. 
This includes the integration of payloads and sensors common to unmanned 
and autonomous systems. 
o 5.1.3.3 Support for Autonomous Operations and Data Exchange: The 
contractor shall leverage and enhance existing infrastructure to support 
Command and Control (C2) data exchange for real-time operational 
scenarios, exercises, and mission requirements. This includes data to and 
from autonomous systems, such as mission tasking, telemetry, and sensor 
data. 
 
• 5.1.4 Rapid Agile Development & Integration Support (RADIS) (RDT&E): The 
contractor shall provide a rapid technical response to issues employing engineering 
techniques to solve problems using an agile software approach to develop, test, and 
integrate new C4I capabilities to meet identified Science & Technology (S&T) gaps 
for the warfighter. 
5.2 Support Requirements 
• 5.2.1 Application Arsenal (AA) Sustainment: The contractor shall provide 
comprehensive support to sustain the functionality, security, and operational 
availability of all fielded AA releases. 

o 5.2.1.1 Operations & Maintenance (O&M): The contractor shall operate, 
maintain, and sustain all fielded releases, including proactive monitoring, 
repairs, and routine updates. 
o 5.2.1.2 System Administration: CSWF-qualified personnel shall perform 
routine system administration on Linux and Windows servers. 
o 5.2.1.3 Cyber & Information Assurance (IA): The contractor shall provide 
operational IA support, including managing security patches, conducting 
vulnerability scanning and remediation, and preparing all required artifacts 
for cybersecurity compliance. The contractor is not responsible for managing 
the eMASS ATO record. 
o 5.2.1.4 Help Desk: The contractor shall provide help desk support, including 
remote and on-site assistance. 
• 5.2.2 Sustainment of Fielded Capabilities: The contractor shall provide 
engineering and technical support for the sustainment of previously fielded 
software, infrastructure, and cross-domain capabilities, including support for 
exercises and operational events. 
• 5.2.3 RADIS (O&M): The contractor shall provide a rapid technical response to 
enhance, upgrade, test, and integrate C4I capabilities to meet identified S&T gaps 
for the warfighter, developing user stories in OSA or other Government-mandated 
environments. 
• 5.2.4 Training and Logistics Support: 
o 5.2.4.1 Training Support: The contractor shall provide user and 
administrator training for sustained systems. 
o 5.2.4.2 Logistics Support: The contractor shall provide logistics support to 
maintain operational readiness, including tracking software licenses and 
managing version releases. 
• 5.2.5 Technical Data and Reporting: The contractor shall generate, update, and 
maintain a complete and accurate Technical Data Package (TDP) for all supported 
systems and report regularly to government stakeholders. 
6.0 TRAVEL 
No travel is anticipated on this Task Order. Should travel be required, it will be authorized 
separately by the Contracting Officer's Representative (COR). The following long distance 
travel is estimated: 

The Contractor shall attend support meetings, conferences, workshops, and fieldings at 
CONUS and OCONUS locations in support of the SOW requirements. Travel to locations 
within United States Africa Command (USAFRICOM), United States Central Command 
(USCENTCOM), United States European Command (USEUCOM), United States Indo-
Pacific Command (USINDOPACOM), United States Northern Command (USNORTHCOM), 
United States Southern Command (USSOUTHCOM) may be required. All travel 
requirements (including plans, agenda, itinerary, or dates) shall be pre-approved by the 
Government, and is on a strictly cost reimbursable basis. All travel is expected to originate 
from San Diego, CA. 
Contractor personnel must adhere to all current DoD, SECNAV , OPNAV , and NIWC Pacific 
instructions related to foreign travel. 
7.0 PROPERTY REQUIREMENTS 
No Government Furnished Property (GFP) is anticipated for this Task Order. 
8.0 SECURITY 
The work performed under this effort is anticipated to be up to the SECRET level, with 
potential for personnel to provide services within laboratories and vessels classified up to 
TOP SECRET. The contractor personnel will require access to classified data, information, 
meetings, and spaces. The contractor shall adhere to all security requirements outlined in 
the DD Form 254, Contract Security Classification Specification. 
9.0 DELIVERABLES 
The contractor shall provide the data deliverables specified in the Contract Data 
Requirements List (CDRL), DD Form 1423, attached to the Task Order. This includes, but is 
not limited to, a Software Development Plan (SDP), Monthly Status Reports, and Technical 
Data Packages (TDP). 
10.0 PERFORMANCE REQUIREMENTS SUMMARY

Question # | PWS Section to which the question or comment applies to: | Question / Comment | Answer
1 | 1.3.3 | Consider program-wide Unified Communications.  Link admin, instructors, trainees, classrooms, labs...anyone anywhere, interconnected. All devices supported, panel/desktop/laptop/tablet/cellphone/walkie-talkie/'motorola'/radios, all linked. Connect within (or among) MSTCs to facilitate learning, administration, collaboration, problem solving, contingency response.  Comms Logger - Record and playback any/all-channel audio and speech-to-text converted text, by user/room/timestamp etc. for AAR, admin etc.  Display speech-to-text during instruction for efficiency, clarity, notes/reference recording, ESL assist and visual learning.  Optional remote live radio control to reach live outstations/ranges/excercises/ training.  Simulated radio or communications bridges into and out of simulations. | Each MSTC is a closed system.  The ATO does not allow for connectivity between MSTCs.
2 | 1.3.3 | Consider use of Phraseology Trainers to allow trainees to learn and practice any types of phrases/sentences/conversations required for efficient communication.  Phraseology Trainers enable individual engagement, personalized skil level based practice and repetition, reduces instructor and classroom time.  Can be installed on any device, takehome/issued or not.  Speeds training/throughput, reduces net cost, increases confidence fluency and clarity.  Reduces risk of mis-communication or under-communication. | Phraseology Trainers are not a requirement and will not be funded.
3 | 1.2 Background | " Cadavers may also be utilized for training." What role will the contractors play in cadaver training and how will it be funded? | Instructor/Operators may use cadavers in place of manikins. Cadavers are provided by the installation at no cost to the contract.
4 | 1.2 Background page 1 | PWS states "single patient" injuries.  Will there be a new requirement that replicates the LSCO medical environment for multiple patient scenarios with new Joint Triage adherence? | No.
5 | 1.2 Background page 1 | Will the Distance Learning be on Joint Knowledge Online or another platform?  Will there be any contractor requirements to develop this or be responsible for this? Will there be a requirement to add this to course catalog and scheduling procedures in ATRRS? | The contractor is not required to develop distance learning, nor will there be a requirement for the contractor to add this to the course catalog. The MSTCs currently have no distance learning.
6 | 1.3 Scope page 4 | What are the other miscellaneous courses to be instructed. Will there be associated cost to the contractor for additional certifications, travel or specialized training? | No additional certifications, travel or specialized training will be required for other courses.
7 | 1.3 Scope page 5 | What is Tier I and II? Is that TCCC Tiers I and II? If so will it be replacing CLS or be taught in addition to CLS? | Deployed Medicine Tier I (All Service Members) and Tier II (Combat Lifesaver)
8 | 1.3 Scope page 4 | Also, what are the requirements for CLS training?  Is this only a Train the Trainer or students at MSTC locations?  Suggest discovery of true demand signal for this and provide detailed direction on requirements to avoid mission creep and accurate manning for each site. | CLS is provided to U.S. Army Medics and as a train the trainer for Units who use the TC3X systems.
9 | 1.3 Scope page 5 | Recommend adding language to the PWS stating "non DOD, state or local agency training such as local fire departments is prohibited"  Some of the current locations experience mission creep without this guardrail. | Recommendation noted.
10 | 1.3.3 Scope page 5 | Will the scenario development be virtual or for live training environment?  Will there be additional FTEs allowable for this requirement? | Scenario development would be for live training. No additional FTEs are allowable.
11 | 1.3.1 (Training/Education Services) | The PWS states: "the Contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision and other items necessary to satisfy the performance-based requirements." Given that MSTCs are already established at 25 locations with existing infrastructure, could the Government please clarify what specific additional facilities, equipment, tools, and materials the contractor is expected to provide beyond the assets currently available at these 25 sites? | No.
12 | 1.3.1, 1.3.3, 2.2 | 1.3.1 & 1.3.3 state "Unless otherwise specified herein, the Contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision and other items necessary to satisfy the performance-based requirements contained herein" Should offerers include high fedility mankins, Moulage kits, AAR Tools, Class IV supplies and all other equipment necessary to facilitate training IAW TC8-800, DHA, and other MEDCoE guidelines? 
Or is all the required equipment and materials furnished for all MSTC site under a seperate contract as stated in section 2.2? "All simulators and equipment that is used for the training are being provided, serviced, and inventoried under a separate contract that has already been established." | All required equipment and materials are currently provided at each MSTC. Simulators/equipment are provided/serviced under an existing, separate contract.
13 | 1.3.1 (Training/Education Services) | The PWS states the contractor shall provide "all personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and other items necessary." Is there a government-furnished property list available that details exactly which items will be provided by the government versus those the contractor must provide? | All required equipment and materials are currently provided at each MSTC.
14 | PWS 1.3 Scope; 2.7 Location and Hours of Work; 3.1–3.2 Performance Requirements; 2.3.4.1–2.3.4.5 OCONUS Requirements | Is there a minimum number of I/Os that must be physically present at an MSTC at all times, regardless of training demand or scheduled events? | There is no requirement to maintain a minimum number of physically present I/Os at a MSTC.
15 |  |  | 
16 |  | Are OCONUS MSTCs historically (or expected to be) staffed similiarly as CONUS sites? | Yes.
17 |  | Is there a typical or maximum number of concurrent training operations that are expected to be supported at an MSTC? | As a general rule, each MSTC has 2-3 classroom spaces and would not exceed the space limitations for concurrent classes.
18 |  |  | 
19 | PWS 2.7.2 Surge Support Requirements | During surge events, what is the typical increase in personnel required, and what is the expected duration and frequency of surge periods? | Surge events are all unique and would be negotiated on an as-needed basis.
20 | PWS 2.6 Contractor Personnel, Disciplines, and Specialties; 3.4.2 MSTC Team Lead Qualification Requirements; 2.13 Security; 3.4.1 Medical Certification Standards | Is an MSTC Team Lead required at each site, and does this role differ from a Site Lead, if applicable? If not required at each site, can the Government please clarify which sites a Team Lead is required for and the distiguishing reasons why? | Each MSTC requires a Team Lead (this term replaces Site Lead).
21 |  | Are all I/Os considered the same level, or does the Government distinguish between I/Os based on qualifications, certifications, or years of experience? | I/Os are distinguished by Medically Credentialled Certification level. For example, NREMT, Paramedic, etc.
22 |  | Can the Government provide baseline certification, security clearance, and minimum years-of-experience requirements applicable to all labor categories, and clarify differences in requirements between CONUS and OCONUS personnel? | Certificaitons are based on American Red Cross requirements. No security clearance is required. The only specified minimum years of experience is for the Team Lead. There is no difference between CONUS and OCONUS personnel / requirements.
23 |  | Can the Government provide historical staffing levels or anticipated staffing levels by MSTC site – while still continuing offerors to propose alternative solutions? | Anticipated staffing levels are provided in Attachment 2 as recently updated.  Historical data will not be provided.
24 | 2.3.4 Personnel Administration page 7 | Please clarify what certifications must be managed and refreshed by the contractor (NREMT, BLS, ALS, PALS, PHTLS etc and if the contractor should include the cost of this in its pricing proposal.  This keeps a low bidder from ignoring those costs in the pricing volume and asking for a contract modification after award, and the associated protests when that happens. | MEDIC Tables I–VIII; MEDIC Table VIII Validation​; Combat Lifesaver (CLS)TCCC Tier 3); All Service Member (ASM / TCCC Tier 1); Basic Life Support (BLS)​; Heartsaver / AED; TC-3X Train the Trainer; Delayed Evacuation Causality Management (DECM); Advanced Life Support (ALS); Pediatric Advanced Life Support (PALS); Individual First Aid Kit (IFAK); TCCC All Tiers; Comprehensive Medic Training (CMT); Pre-Hospital Trauma Life Support (PHTLS) - Not all inclusive as individual sites may have requirements based on MOS population.
25 | 2.7 Location and Hours of Work page 13 | Will the surge request be issued as a task order that allows for pricing and travel pay, or is that to be considered in the initial pricing? If so, what percentage should the contractor calculate for surge support annually? | Surge events are all unique and would be negotiated on an as-needed basis.
26 | 2.15.8 (EO, EEO, Fraternization, and SHARP) | The PWS requires annual training for all contractor employees. Will the government provide this training, or is the contractor expected to develop and deliver this training? | Annual training identified in Paragraphs 2.14.1 - 2.15.8 are standard training available through JKO or a similar training platform.  TC 8-800 training is provided at the MSTCs at no cost to the Government. All other annual/bi-annual training for medical credentials is at cost to the contractor and shall not be provided by the MSTCs.
27 | 2.17 (Quality Assurance Surveillance Plans) | Will the government provide the QASP prior to proposal submission to ensure our Quality Control Plan properly aligns with government oversight expectations? | Yes.  The QASP is provided via an update as Attachment 36.
28 | 2.2 (Business Relations) | Is the current W-TRS contractor precluded from competing for this MIOSS contract, or are they eligible to submit a proposal? | If the current W-TRS contractor type aligns with the requirements of the Combined Acquisition Plan/Service Acquisition Strategy, they are allowed to bid.
29 | 2.3.4 (Personnel Administration) | Are there documented instances under the current contract where personnel must travel off-installation to obtain refresher training for required certifications? If so, how is this handled administratively and financially, and will similar arrangements be necessary under the future MIOSS contract? | Yes. The contractor is financially responsible for the certificaiton/recertificaiton. It is the responsibility of the contractor to handle this administratively. The training cannot interfere with any other requirement of the PWS.
30 | 2.3.4.1 (OCONUS Requirements) | For OCONUS locations, are quarters currently provided by host installations for MSTC support personnel? Will this accommodation arrangement continue under the MIOSS contract, or will contractors need to make alternative housing arrangements? | Housing is not provded.
31 | 2.7.1 (Government Installation Work Schedule) | For accurate planning and pricing purposes, should contractors calculate a man-year as 1,920 hours or 1,912 hours? | A man-year is 1,920 hours.
32 | 2.7.3 (Instructor Operator vacancies) | Considering the unique challenges of OCONUS positions, would the Government consider extending the two-week vacancy filling requirement for OCONUS locations due to country-specific clearance and visa processing timelines? Additionally, would the Government permit temporary assignments of Instructor/Operators from MSTCs with lower operational requirements as an interim solution until permanent replacements can be properly vetted and hired? | Relief from requirement for OCONUS positions will need to be requested from the APM and evaluated on a case-by-case basis.  Consideration may be given to a temporary lower qualifying instructor, however, this too will be on a case-by-case basis.
33 | 2.8.1 (Reimbursement of Travel, Per Diem, and Special Material Costs) | To ensure accurate pricing and resource allocation, could the Government provide an estimated frequency and duration of TDY assignments and travel days anticipated during contract execution? Will travel expenses be captured as a separate Contract Line Item Number (CLIN)? What specific documentation requirements (travel requests, expense reports, receipts) will be required to authorize travel and substantiate reimbursement claims? | No TDY is anticipated however, if incurred, would be captured as a separate CLIN and proposed to prior to authorization to travel.
34 | 2.9 (Tools and Equipment) | Please clarify the responsibility matrix for maintenance and lifecycle support of computer equipment at the MSTCs. Will this responsibility continue under the MIOSS contract or remain elsewhere? Additionally, which entity (MIOSS contractor or Government) will be responsible for replacement of expendable supplies used during operations? Is the WTRS contract maintaining management of logistical support and sustainment to the MSTCs, or is that logistical requirement incorporated into this PWS with W-TRS oversight? | Computers for the classrooms and MT-C2 system, and expendable training supplies used by the Contractors are provided by the Government. The W-TRS Contract maintains TADSS and procures expendable (non-Class VII) suppiles used for training at the MSTC.  Class VIII supplies are provided by the Government.
35 | 2.3.4.1 | How are staffing gaps that are host-driven going to be treated? | Relief from requirement will need to be requested from the APM and evaluated on a case-by-case basis.
36 | 2.3.4.1 | Do penalties apply when the Host Nation holds up staffing? | No.
37 | 2.3.4.1 | Can local nationals be subbed? | No.
38 | 2.7 | Do surge timelines account for accreditation lag? | No.

PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT (PWS) 
 
FOR 
 
SUPPORT SERVICES FOR HEWLETT PACKARD ENTERPRISE HIGH PERFORMANCE COMPUTE NODE 
 
 
PART 1 
GENERAL INFORMATION 
 
 
1.1
 General: This is a non-personnel services contract to provide on-site Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) High-
Performance Compute (HPC) system administration support services to be provided to the Naval Oceanographic Office 
(NAVOCEANO or NAVO) for a period of one year and is similar to the system administration support services provided 
on contract N0018925P0496. The Government shall not exercise any supervision or control over the contract service 
providers performing the services herein  
 
 
1.2 Background 
1.2.1 The Naval Oceanographic Office (NAVOCEANO) collects, processes, and disseminates complex oceanographic 
data, forecasts, and products to Fleet users using HPC technologies including Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine 
Learning (ML) algorithms.  NAVOCEANO requires specialized services for the system administration, operational 
support, and cybersecurity compliance of a new Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) High-Performance Compute (HPC) 
cluster. This system is a strategic asset designed to run advanced Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) 
algorithms. The architecture consists of cutting-edge technologies, including GPU-accelerated compute nodes, an HPE 
Slingshot high-speed interconnect, a Lustre-based parallel file system, and an image-based operating system deployment 
infrastructure. Due to the new technology and complexity of these components, expert contractor support is necessary to 
ensure the system's stability, security, and optimal performance to meet mission-critical objectives 
 
 
1.3 Description of Requirement 
The contractor shall provide specialized support services for system administration,
 operational support, and cybersecurity 
compliance of the HPE HPC system.  The contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, tools, materials, supervision, 
and other items necessary to perform the services. 
 
 
1.4 Period of Performance, Place of Performance and Hours of Operation  
 
1.4.1 The period of performance shall be 12 months after award.  
1.4.2 The contractor shall perform services at NAVOCEANO. NAVOCEANO is located at Stennis Space Center, 
Mississippi. 
1.4.3 Recognized Holidays/Government Closure:  Federal law (5 U.S.C. 6103) establishes the public holidays for 
Federal employees.  Any other day designated by federal statute, executive order, presidential proclamation and/or local 
determinations relating to adverse weather conditions, national emergencies, administrative closings, or similar 
Government directed facility closings may require office closure.  During such periods of closure, contractor employees 
will not be allowed to work, nor will the contractor be compensated, however, offsite work is allowed, with Contracting 
Officer's (KO) approval, on a case-by-case basis when mutually agreed upon by the Government and the contractor. 
 
  
 
1.4.4 Hours of Operation 

 
Page 2 of 9 
 
SUPPORT SERVICES FOR HEWLETT PACKARD ENTERPRISE HIGH PERFORMANCE COMPUTE NODE 
 
The contractor is responsible for performing support services during an 8-hour workday between the hours of 0700 and 
1630, Monday through Friday, except when the government facility is closed or government personnel are not in the 
designated office location. The contractor must maintain an adequate workforce for the uninterrupted performance of all 
tasks defined within this performance work statement when the Government facility is not closed.  The stability and 
continuity of the contractor workforce are essential. 
 
1.5 Post Award Conference/Periodic Progress Meetings 
1.5.1 The Contractor shall attend any post award conference convened by the contracting activity. The contracting 
officer and the Contracting Officers Representative (COR) may meet periodically with the contractor to review the 
contractor's performance. At these meetings, the contracting officer will apprise the contractor of how the Government 
views the contractor's performance and the contractor will inform the Government of problems experiencing, if any. The 
Government or the contractor, as applicable, shall take appropriate action to resolve outstanding issues. These meetings 
shall be at no additional cost to the Government.  
 
1.6 Program Management 
1.6.1 The contractor shall assign a Program Manager (PM)/Contract Manager (CM) to act as the single primary point of 
contact with the NAVOCEANO COR. The PM/CM specifically has the responsibility of communicating with the COR on 
all matters pertaining to this Performance Work Statement (PWS). The PM/CM shall direct the individual contractor 
employee’s effort through the company’s internal management system; this management system shall provide project 
progress visibility to assure on-time completion of all requirements. 
1.6.2 The contractor shall utilize standard processes based on industry best practices wherever applicable. 
1.6.3 The contractor shall sponsor quarterly program management reviews to monitor contractor performance and 
discuss any issues that the contractor and/or NAVOCEANO are experiencing with the project referenced herein with the 
COR and/or Contracting Office. NAVOCEANO COR will schedule this review; submit a suggested agenda to the 
contractor who shall be responsible for all briefing slides and materials. 
16.4 The contractor shall support other NAVOCEANO briefings and meetings as applicable by providing feedback 
and documentation/numbers concerning any efforts. 
 
1.7 Identification of Contractor Employees: All contract personnel are required to identify themselves as such while 
attending meetings, answering Government telephones, answering emails and working in other situations where their 
contractor status is not obvious to third parties. Identification of contractor status is required to avoid creating an 
impression in the minds of members of the public or other Government personnel that they are Government officials. 
They must also mark all documents or reports produced by contractors as contractor products or that contractor 
participation is appropriately disclosed. All contractor personnel shall obtain and wear badges in the performance of this 
service 
 
5 Personnel Education / Experience Requirements 
5.1 Education: 
5.1.1 All contractor personnel conducting system administration services, at a minimum, the combination of education 
and experience required to qualify for the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) General Schedule Qualifications 
Standard, IT Specialist Series 2210 or Computer Scientist series 1550.  The IT Specialist Series 2210 qualifications build 
upon the general requirements of the 2210 series with a specific focus on the technical skills needed to manage and 
maintain network infrastructures, operating systems, and applications.   The Computer Scientist Series 1550 qualifications  
Requires one of the following basic education requirements: 
Bachelor’s Degree in Computer Science: A bachelor's degree in computer science from an accredited institution.  
Bachelor's Degree with Specific Coursework: A bachelor's degree with 30 semester hours in a combination of 
mathematics, statistics, and computer science. Of these 30 semester hours, at least 15 must have included a combination 
of statistics and mathematics, including differential and integral calculus. 
All academic degrees and coursework must be from accredited or pre-accredited institutions 
  
 

 
Page 3 of 9

5.1.2 All contractor personnel conducting system administration shall have, at minimum, the combination of education 
and training required to qualify for the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) General Schedule Qualifications 
Standard, IT Specialist 2210 series at or above the GS12 level which is equivalent to four (4) years of specialized 
experience in the fields of IT system administration and IT network administration of HPC systems used for scientific 
data processing using AI/ML. More specifically LINUX based operating systems, parallel file systems, GPU-accelerated 
compute nodes, and high-speed network interconnects. 
 
5.2 All contractor personnel shall have specialized knowledge of HPC systems used for scientific data processing using 
AI/ML. More specifically LINUX based operating systems, parallel file systems, GPU-accelerated compute nodes, and 
high-speed network interconnects.  
 
 
 
PART 2 
DEFINITIONS & ACRONYMS 
 
 
 
 
2.1.  CONTRACTOR. A supplier or vendor awarded a contract to provide specific supplies or service to the Government. 
The term used in this contract refers to the Prime Contractor. 
 
2.2  CONTRACTING OFFICER.  A person with authority to enter into, administer, and or terminate contracts, and make 
related determinations and findings on behalf of the Government. Note: The only individual who can legally bind the 
Government. 
 
2.3   CONTRACTING OFFICER'S REPRESENTATIVE (COR).  An employee of the U.S.Government designated and 
authorized in writing by the contracting officer to perform specific technical or administrative functions. Such 
appointment shall be in writing and shall state the scope of authority and limitations. This individual has authority to 
provide technical direction to the Contractor if that direction is within the scope of the contract, does not constitute a 
change, and has no funding implications. This individual does NOT have authority to change the terms and 
conditions of the contract.  
 
2.4  DEFECTIVE SERVICE. A service output that does not meet the standard of performance associated with the 
Performance Work Statement. 
 
2..5  QUALITY ASSURANCE. The Government procedures to verify the services performed by the Contractor are within 
acceptable standards. 
 
2.6   QUALITY CONTROL. All necessary measures taken by the Contractor to assure that the quality of a product or 
service shall meet contract requirements. 
 
 
 
PART 3 
SPECIFIC TASKS 
 
 
3.1 Task 1: System and Network Administration 
The contractor shall provide expert system administration for the entire HPC ecosystem.
