The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Alaska District is conducting market research to facilitate 
determination of acquisition strategy. The determination of acquisition strategy for this 
acquisition lies solely with the government and will be based on this market research and 
information available to the government from other sources. This market research is being 
conducted in order to identify A-E Services Contractors with the capabilities to perform the 
following requirement: 
The Alaska District is contemplating an Indefinite Delivery multi-discipline contract(s) to be 
procured in accordance with the Brooks A-E Act as implemented in FAR Part 36 and the 
supplements thereto.  Anticipate award of three (3) to (5) multiple award task order contracts 
with a shared capacity of $40 million.  The contract type shall be indefinite delivery, firm fixed 
price over a term of 5 years.  Anticipated average task order range will be from $150K - 
$2M.  The maximum task order limit will be $20M.  When the conditions in Revolutionary FAR 
Overhaul (RFO) 19.104-1 are met at the time of order set-aside, and the specific program 
eligibility requirements, as appliable are also met, Task order set-asides for small businesses 
(totally or partially) will be discretionary. 
The anticipated NAICS is 541330, Engineering Services, PSC is C219 A-E: General – Other and 
Size Standard is $25.5M. 
PROJECT INFORMATION: The AEs selected would be required to have sufficient staff, 
flexibility, and capability to be available on an as-needed basis.  Typical types of services to be 
provided are related to the study and design of new, renovations, repair, and modernization of 
mechanical and electrical systems to include: studies and designs of electrical power, 
communication, grounding, lighting and control systems; study and design of heating, 
ventilation, air conditioning and refrigeration with DDC controls, utilidors and enclosed utility 
systems; performance of commissioning services (LEED both Fundamental and Enhanced); 
study and design of fire protection and detection systems (including aircraft hangar aqueous film 
forming foam (AFFF) fire suppression systems as well as standard wet, dry, and pre-action 
sprinkler systems); general building designs; the design of POL systems is incidental to facility 
design.  The AE may also perform construction phase services, inspection and investigations or 
may development Design/Build RFPs. The AE and their subcontractors must have experience in 
cold regions design. Cold regions design is not considered to be a separate discipline that can be 
subcontracted. Rather, knowledge and experience in the design, construction and operation of 
facilities in arctic, subarctic, and cold region environments must be integral to all design 

disciplines.  The AE may be required to participate in programming, value engineering studies, 
design Charrettes and project review conferences; participation may include facilitation, VE 
Study team, etc.  The Government may require that designs be in metric and/or English systems 
of units. The firm must demonstrate the ability to; provide drawings in AutoCAD (version as 
required by the project); Have the capability to provide designs using building information 
modeling (BIM) software; use the latest version of M2 (cost estimating software furnished by the 
Government); provide a cost estimate in work breakdown structure (WBS); provide draft DD 
Form 1354, Transfer and Acceptance of Military Real Property; provide electronic bid set (EBS) 
documents; use SPECSINTACT, for all projects unless otherwise directed in the Task Order. 
The AE will be required to use Dr. Check’s programs (permissions and passwords will be 
distributed on a project-by-project basis).  Systems information required for Dr. Checks: Internet 
Explorer (Microsoft); the web site is: http:\\www.buildersnet.org\drchecks.  The Government 
may require the AE provide engineering, testing, and design services during construction.  The 
Government may require the AE to provide the Government Construction Management and 
Design Staff with Fundamental and Enhanced Commissioning Services for various projects. The 
Commissioning Services shall include individuals to serve as the Commissioning Authority on 
the project as described in the USGBC LEED Reference Guide 2025 Edition, Energy and 
Atmosphere Prerequsite 1 and Credit 3. These persons will support the Government in verifying 
contract compliance regarding the design, construction and initial post-occupancy phase of the 
project delivery as it relates to enhanced commissioning.   The Government may require the AE 
to prepare and review energy models prepared by others using DOE approved modeling software 
in accordance ASHRAE 90.1 Appendix G and UFC 3-400-01. 
LOCATION: Primarily Various Locations, Alaska, but may be utilized outside Alaska on an 
exception basis.  Facilities will generally be located in arctic or subarctic environments.

EVALUATION CRITERIA 
FACA Panel Support Services: Verbatim FACA Panel Transcripts, Meeting Reports, and 
Recommendations Summary Preparation Services 
 
 
The offeror shall demonstrate the technical approach chosen for this task order covering all aspects 
of the Statement of Work (SOW).   
 
The offeror shall provide sufficient detail to demonstrate their technical understanding of and 
capability of performing the requirements of the SOW.   
 
Quotes that restate the requirements in the SOW without providing substantive descriptions 
of the planned work will be considered technically unacceptable.   
 
Offerors shall demonstrate experience in all phases of verbatim transcription and meeting reports, 
and will address the following: 
 
• The contractor shall demonstrate their end to end workflow capturing and producing verbatim 
transcripts, including contingency plans should there be instances where audio quality, 
overlapping speech, or unclear terminology prevent confident verbatim capture; 
 
• The contractor shall demonstrate how they will incorporate human transcriptionists and 
reviewers with any automated or AI -assisted transcription tools, including the specific role 
each plays at each stage of production;  
 
• The contractor shall demonstrate how they will incorporate pre- and post- meeting 
materials — including the agenda, Panel roster, HCPCS/CPT code lists, and meeting- specific 
reference documents — into its preparation workflow to improve transcription accura cy; 
 
• The contractor shall  demonstrate how it will accomplish regurgitation requests ( restated 
recommendations) within a committed maximum response time , in a manner that supports 
rapid, reliable retrieval during an active meeting . The contractor must include the anticipated 
response time for these on-demand requests; 
 
• The contractor shall demonstrate how it will handle edge cases, including requests involving 
multiple recommendations made in rapid succession, ambiguous keyword queries, or 
recommendations referencing multiple HCPCS codes; and management of post-delivery 
error correction, including the process for identifying, reporting, and correcting inaccuracies 
discovered after a deliverable has been submitted to CMS; 
 
• The contractor shall demonstrate its production workflow for 508 compliant meeting reports, 
including how it will capture and accurately summarize each matter discussed and each 
conclusion reached; compile the required attendee lists, public presenter lists, and estimated 
public attendance figures; and assemble the required appendix materials (agenda, Panel 
roster, attendance sheet);  
 

  
 
 2 
• The contractor shall demonstrate how all deliverables are quality checked.  This is to include 
identifying and accurately rendering alpha -numeric terminology spoken conversationally, 
including HCPCS/CPT codes, APC numbers and titles, long descriptors, medical terminology, 
legal language, and government acronyms.  Its committed minimum accuracy rate for verbatim 
transcripts —  Offerors shall state a specific minimum accuracy rate as a percentage for each 
transcript; 
 
• The contractor shall demonstrate the management of personnel preparation for each meeting, 
including the process for briefing assigned staff on meeting-specific materials — such as the 
agenda, Panel roster, and pre-meeting code lists — at least one week prior to each meeting, 
consistent with the requirement to provide staff names and contact information to CMS at 
that time; 
 
 
Experience of Personnel 
 
The quote shall describe the educational background, professional experience, and special 
qualifications of all professional personnel to be involved in this task order.  When consultants or 
subcontractors are to be used, their special qualifications, educational background, and experience 
shall be included.  
 
The quote shall specify how the personnel proposed under this task order will be integrated 
organizationally and what their responsibilities and their percentage of time under the purchase  
order. 
 
The offeror shall include a list of names and proposed duties of the personnel, consultants and 
subcontractor employees assigned to the project. The government is not requesting, nor reviewing 
any resumes submitted. 
 
Prior Experience 
 
The technical proposal shall provide the general background experience and qualifications of the 
offerors’ organization. The offeror shall demonstrate relevant capabilities that it can bring to this 
project and any other advantages it offers based upon its experiences.  
 
Ideally, prior experiences should involve producing verbatim transcripts. 
 
The Offeror shall include summaries of recent contracts, subcontracts and task or purchase 
orders with the CMS, other Department of Health and Human Services agencies, other U.S. 
Government organizations and/or commercial firms for the same or similar services required by 
this solicitation.   
 
The list of directly related projects shall cover at least the last 6 months, but not more than the 
most recent 3 years.

36C26226Q0506 Question and Answers

1) Can you provide photographs of the installation locations?

ANSWER: We can mark the locations on the plan drawing. 

2) Can you describe the types of walls the screens will be mounted to? I.E. CMU, drywall with metal studs, drywall with wood studs, brick?

ANSWER: Mostly dry walls and some locations with tiled walls. 

3) Will the screens be mounted in Landscape or Portrait format?

ANSWER:  The VA San Diego Healthcare System will rely on the contractors' expertise to assess and provide professional recommendations to determine the optimal orientation. As noted in the Statement of Work (SOW), the design must comply with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) requirements. 

4) You mention a range for screen size of 47"-65". Will you require different sized screens for different locations? Should screen size be standardized for all 16 installation locations?

ANSWER: The VA San Diego Healthcare System will rely on the contractors' expertise to assess the space and provide professional recommendation to help the facility make an informed decision. 65” are most likely going near the main entrances and 47” for other locations.

5) Is there any branding, color pallet, or logo placement that should be incorporated into the design of the screens? 

ANSWER: Yes. Similar navy blue color and logo as seen on the main VA website: https://www.va.gov/ shall be used as a starting point for design. 

The contractor shall have design discussion sessions with VASD for interface design. VASD will be relying on the contractor's design expertise. 

6) Will power and data connections be available at each installation location?

ANSWER: Power will be VASD’s responsibility. Cabling and network set up will be the contractor’s responsibility. 

7) Will the installer be able to utilize the dumpster, compactors, or recycling facilities at each installation location? Or will they be responsible for hauling away all packaging material? 

ANSWER: No. Contractors are responsible for their housekeeping. Note that at the main La Jolla Medical Center contractors shall only use the service elevators. 

8) Can the screens be received at each facility prior to installation? Or can they be received at a central location? Or will the installer be responsible for bringing the screens to each installation location? 

ANSWER: The contractor is responsible for safely storing their materials and tools. No materials, screens, or tools shall be left or stored on-site unsupervised at any time. VASDHS is not responsible for the storage, damage, or loss of any items left at VASDHS's medical center or clinics.

9) Can you clarify the expected time frame for issuing a PO and the desired installation date for the 16 screens? 

ANSWER: The PO will be issued once the contract has an award.  Dates for the installation will be June 30-July 31.

1. Combined Synopsis/Solicitation  
1.1. This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products or commercial 
services prepared in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulations (FAR) part 12. 
This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Offers are being requested and a 
separate written solicitation will not be issued. 
 
Solicitation number 140D0426Q0324 is issued as a request for quotation (RFQ) for 
Artificial Intelligence (AI) Chatbot Services to enhance agency Recruitment Efforts. 
 
This acquisition is a total small business set-aside. This solicitation incorporates 
provisions and clauses by reference. The full text of provisions and clauses may be 
accessed electronically at www.acquisition.gov.  
 
1.2. The period of performance for this Purchase Order will consist of a one-year Base 
Period estimated to begin on June 1, 2026, followed by four (4) one-year Option 
Periods, as outlined in the table below. If all options are exercised, the total period of 
performance will not exceed five (5) years. Continued performance under this 
Purchase Order is contingent upon the availability of funds and the Contractor’s 
acceptable level of performance. 
 
 Base Period: June 01, 2026, to May 31, 2027 
 Option Period 1: June 01, 2027, to May 31, 2028 
 Option Period 2: June 01, 2028, to May 31, 2029 
 Option Period 3: June 01, 2029, to May 31, 2030 
 Option Period 4: June 01, 2030, to May 31, 2031 
 
1.3. The U.S. Department of the Interior (DOI), Interior Business Center (IBC), 
Acquisition Services Directorate (AQD), is issuing this RFQ on behalf of the Peace 
Corps (PC), Office of Volunteer Recruitment and Service (VRS), for Artificial 
Intelligence (AI) Chatbot Services to enhance agency Recruitment Efforts. 
 
The Peace Corps seeks a FedRAMP High authorized, commercially available SaaS 
conversational AI solution (“Chatbot”) to enhance recruitment, outreach, and public 
engagement across peacecorps.gov. The solution must deliver high-quality, secure, 
and scalable interactions with the public while integrating seamlessly with existing 
systems. 
 
Through the implementation of the integrated conversational AI chatbot service, the 
Peace Corps expects to:

applicants with recruiters and the marketing team.

 Decrease the time and effort Peace Corps staff spend responding to commonly 
asked questions and requests for guidance from the public that can be

Statement of work – Sports Streaming Services 
 
Background 
 
The purchase of a sports streaming service for varsity sports statistics and online viewing services as 
required by NFHS.  
Objectives 
 
The objective of this service is to have digital records of all varsity sport activities and to be able to 
accurately track sports statistics, in compliance with NFHS.  
 
Scope 
 
The scope of this project is to obtain access to online streaming services to track varsity games. 
 
Tasks 
 
The task will be to deliver a compatible streaming service similar to the ones used in our region, 
southwest 1-A, to stream and record all varsity games.

BIE – St. Stephens Indian School

SECTION L - INSTRUCTIONS, CONDITIONS, AND NOTICES TO QUOTERS 
L.1. OVERVIEW  
The USCB is issuing this competitive Request for Quotation (RFQ) under the General Services 
Administration (GSA) Multiple Award Schedule (MAS) for its CenTAM Acquisition 
Framework requirements. Through this effort, USCB intends to establish four (4) blanket 
purchase agreements (BPAs) under the MAS to acquire application development, 
modernization, data engineering, geospatial, and related technical services in support of its 
mission.  
All four BPAs under this RFQ are being competed as total small business set-asides.  
Only small businesses holding the applicable GSA MAS IT Category SIN 54151S are 
eligible to submit quotes.  
The Government will accept only quotes submitted by small businesses under GSA MAS SIN 
54151S. Any quote submitted by a Quoter that is not a small business will not be accepted and, 
therefore, not considered for evaluation or award.  
For the purposes of this RFQ “quoter” means a small business concern. Contractors that submit a 
proposal will be referred to as quoters.  
The Government intends to execute and award the initial orders for the single award BPAs based 
on initial quotes. Therefore, quoters are highly encouraged to propose their best technical and 
pricing quotes in their initial submissions. 
L.2. AUTHORITY (GSAR 538.71 – FSS ORDERING PROCEDURES) 
This RFQ is issued under GSAR Subpart 538.71 – Federal Supply Schedule (FSS) Ordering 
Procedures, as implemented via GSA’s Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) class deviation. 
Ordering will be conducted using RFQs and evaluation of quotations under FSS procedures. 
Unless otherwise prescribed, FAR Parts 5, 6, 13, 14, 15, 16, and 19 do not apply to these 
ordering procedures.  
These procedures constitute “competitive procedures” under 41 U.S.C §152, including 152(4) 
for procurements conducted under the Small Business Act. They enable the Government to 
conduct best-value evaluations consistent with GSAR 538.71 - FSS ordering procedures.  
L.3. COMMUNICATING INNOVATIVE TECHNIQUES WITH INDUSTRY 
This solicitation encompasses several innovative procurement techniques (see GSAR 538.7102-2 
for more coverage of streamlined processes and innovative procurement techniques). To increase 
transparency of them with industry, they are listed below. The Periodic Table of Acquisition 
innovations (PTAI), https://acquisitiongateway.gsa.gov/periodic-table, includes a full tile sharing 
the description, problems solved, benefits of use, small business benefit, and real sample 
documents (including training aids) for each:  
• Communicating Innovative Techniques with Industry (CITI)  

 
2 
 
• Confidence Ratings  
• Down-Selects 
• Fusion Procurements  
• Highest Technically Rated Vendors  
• On-the-Spot Consensus Evaluation  
• Streamlined Documentation  
L.4. CENTAM BPA STRUCTURE 
The CenTAM Acquisition Framework will consist of four BPAs to support the full spectrum of 
USCB application modernization, data engineering, analytics, geospatial, and related IT services 
needs. The Enterprise BPA is intended to support large-scale, more complex efforts across all 
USCB programs requiring broad technical depth and integration. The Systems and Program 
Support (SPS) BPA is intended to support smaller-scale, narrowly scoped efforts across all 
USCB programs. The Decennial BPA is dedicated to supporting the Decennial Program only, 
while the Geospatial BPA supports Geospatial initiatives across USCB.

L.5. QUOTER ELIGIBILITY AND TEAM PARTICIPATION LIMITATIONS 
L.5.1 QUOTER ELIGIBILITY  
To be eligible to submit a quote under this RFQ, Quoters must hold the applicable MAS SIN for 
the BPA(s). 
Participation as a Joint Venture (JV) or SBA-approved Mentor-Protégé JV (MPJV) is 
permitted, subject to the following conditions: 
• The JV or MPJV entity itself must hold the required MAS SIN at the time of the 
quotation submission.  
MAS Certified Teaming Arrangements (CTAs) are not permitted under this RFQ.  
L.5.2 TEAM PARTICIPATION LIMITATIONS 
A Quoter may participate in this acquisition either as a prime contractor or a subcontractor, 
but only on one team.  
Participation on multiple teams, whether across BPAs or within a single BPA, is prohibited.  
Enterprise, Decennial, and Geospatial BPAs: 
• A Quoter may submit a quote for one or more of the following BPAs:  Enterprise, 
Decennial, or Geospatial BPAs. 
SPS BPA: 
• Submitting a quote for Enterprise, Decennial, and/ or Geospatial BPAs  precludes 
participation in the  SPS BPA in any capacity  (Prime or subcontractor).  
• Quoters submitting a quote for the SPS BPA may participate only in the SPS BPA and 
may not participate (as a Prime or subcontractor) in Enterprise, Decennial, or 
Geospatial BPAs. 
L.5.3 PERMITTED PARTICIPATION PATHS 
Each Quoter must choose one of the following participation paths: 
• Enterprise BPA only; or 
• Decennial BPA only; or 
• Geospatial BPA only; or 

 
4 
 
• Any combination of Enterprise + Decennial + Geospatial; or 
• SPS BPA only 
Participation (Prime or subcontractor) in the SPS BPA mutually excludes participation (Prime 
or subcontractor) in the Enterprise, Decennial, or Geospatial BPAs.  
L.5.4 RESPONSIBILITY FOR TEAM COMPLIANCE 
It is the Quoter’s responsibility to ensure that all proposed subcontractors fully understand and 
comply with the solicitation’s BPA quoting restrictions. If any proposed subcontractor is found 
to be in violation of these restrictions, either at submission or at any point during evaluation: 
• The non-compliant subcontractor will be removed from the Quoter’s team ; and 
• If the Quoter relied upon that subcontractor for Demonstrated Prior Experience or 
Key Personnel, those portions of the submission will also be removed from 
consideration.  
Removal of such required information may result in the quote being deemed incomplete and 
non-compliant, and therefore ineligible for award for the affected BPA(s). 
L.6. GENERAL  
Quoters are instructed to read the entire RFQ document, including all attachments, prior to 
preparing your quote. Omission of any information from the quotation submission requirements 
may result in the quote being deemed “Noncompliant” and disqualified from further evaluation.  
To aid in the evaluations, quotes shall be clearly and concisely written, neatly prepared, properly 
indexed, and logically assembled. Quoters are asked to bear in mind that all material submitted 
should be directly pertinent to the solicitation requirements. Extraneous narratives, elaborate 
brochures, marketing materials, and so forth, shall not be submitted. All pages of each part shall 
be appropriately numbered, identified with the name of the Quoter, the date, and the solicitation 
number to the extent practicable.  
Quoter’s submissions shall address all requirements identified in Section L and the evaluation 
factors set forth in Section M of the solicitation. 
In responding to this RFQ, it is the Quoter’s responsibility to provide current, complete, and 
accurate information in their quotes. If in reviewing the quotes, the Government identifies or 
otherwise learns that the provided information is not accurate or misrepresents the Quoter’s 
status or capabilities, that information may be used by the contracting officer to determine the 
Quoter not being eligible for award.  
Quotes must be received on or before the due dates and times specified in the RFQ, and any 
subsequent amendments. Only information received on or before the due date and time shall be 
considered for award. Any submission, modification, or revision received after the time specified 
for receipt of quotes is “late” and will not be considered unless it is received before award is 
made AND the Contracting Officer determines that accepting the late quote would not unduly 
delay the acquisition. Facsimile quotes and hard copy quotes via portal mail will not be accepted.  
Quotes shall be submitted via email to Matthew Gore at matthew.s.gore@census.gov and Bryan 

 
5 
 
Shearer at bryan.allan.shearer@census.gov and the submission email shall be entitled “Quoter 
Name – (BPA(s))”)) 
The quotes shall be valid for no less than 210 calendar days from the quote due date. The Quoter 
shall make a clear statement that the quote is valid for the specified number of calendar dates in 
the Business & Price Volumes of the quote. The Government reserves the right to request 
additional information after receipt of the Quoter’s response to the solicitation.  
This RFQ does not commit the Government to pay any cost for the preparation and submission 
of a quote.  
Penalty for False Statements: Quoters are advised that 18 U.S.C. 1001 prohibits the knowing 
and willful submissions of false, fictitious, or fraudulent statements, representations, or 
certifications to the Government. Any such submission may result in criminal penalties, 
administrative remedies, elimination from this competition, or other actions as permitted by law. 
L.6.1 COMMUNICATIONS  
Prior to releasing the Draft RFQ, the Government will issue drafts of Sections C, J, L, and M. 
The intent will be to receive questions and comments solely during the pre-solicitation period to 
identify discrepancies and clarify requirements for the final solicitation. 
The Government does not intend to conduct a formal questions & answers (Q&A) period after 
the final RFQ is issued. However, the Government reserves the right to open an additional round 
of questions if deemed necessary and in the Government’s best interest.  
All correspondence in conjunction with this solicitation must be directed to the Government 
Contracting Officer and Contract Specialist identified below: 
Contracting Officer: Matthew Gore 
E-mail address: matthew.s.gore@census.gov 
Contracting Specialist: Bryan Shearer 
E-mail address: bryan.allan.shearer@census.gov 
L.6.2 ANTICIPATED SOLICITATION SCHEDULE 
The dates included in the table below are intended to be helpful with planning purposes and 
reflect the Government’s anticipated solicitation schedule. It is the Government’s intent to 
adhere to this schedule. However, these dates are subject to change. Any changes will be clearly 
communicated to the Quoters.

L.6.3 QUOTATION PREPARATION INSTRUCTIONS 
The instructions below establish the required format and content so quotes can be

Two-Phase Process  
This solicitation uses a two-phase approach to streamline submissions for each of the 4 BPAs: 
• Phase 1 – Demonstrated Prior Experience  (Written) 
o Mandatory. Quoters must submit a Phase 1 response for each BPA they intend 
to pursue. 
• Advisory Notifications: after Phase 1, the Government will advise, per BPA, whether 
the quoter should proceed to Phase 2.  
o Each BPA is evaluated separately and independently  and will receive its own

o A Quoter may be advised to proceed for one BPA (e.g., Decennial) but not for

NOTE (SPS independence): The SPS BPA is independent of the Enterprise, Decennial, and

Autonomy Technologies for Complex Advanced Teaming Operations (CATO) 
 
Introduction 
 
Description: The Government seeks technology offers that enable autonomy and collaborative teaming capability for 
uncrewed aviation systems (UAS), operating at high levels of supervised autonomy in tactical Army operations in complex 
air-ground-littoral environments.  Complex environments in this context include littoral, maritime, and urban settings, and 
terrain with varying elevation, obscuration, and concealment opportunities.  Assumptions for operating conditions in these 
environments will include denied and degraded communication and positioning conditi ons as well as active and dense hostile 
presence.  Autonomy technologies of interest are software solutions for autonomous mission planning and execution, 
knowledge representation and sensemaking, mission oversight and decision-making, human-autonomy interface, and network 
management.  These technologies are to be applied in the context of heterogeneous, multi-UAS operations integrated into 
small unit Soldier formations.  Of specific interest are solutions based on Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning 
(ML) technologies such as large and small language models and agentic AI or other novel approaches.  The intent is to lay the 
foundation for AI-based next generation “learning” enabled autonomy capabilities. The Government will use selected offeror 
solutions to inform and evaluate modifications and upgrades to Program of Record requirements .  The AI-enabled 
technologies to be demonstrated in CATO are anticipated to be candidates for insertion into the Launched Effects (LE) 
Family of Systems (FoS) aircraft, the new Future Long Range Assault Aircraft (FLRAA), Future Tactical Unmanned Aircraft 
System (FTUAS), the existing aviation fleet and existing and planned Ground Systems.  
 
Topic Audience:  
Small Business, Large Business, Non-traditional Companies, Venture-Capital-funded startups, Academia, and Historically 
Black Colleges and Universities/ Minority Institutions (HBCU/MI).  
 
Department of the Army research, Development, Test, & Evaluation (RDT&E) Budget Activity (BA):  
Department of the Army Research, Development, Test, & Evaluation (RDT&E) Budget Activities (BA): 
 
BA 2, Applied Research; and 
BA 3, Advanced Technology Development 
 
Program Element(s): 
PE 0602345A / Unmanned Aerial Systems Launched Effects Applied Research 
PE 0603465A / Future Vertical Lift Advanced Technology 
PE 0603345A / Unmanned Aerial Systems Launched Effects Advanced Technology Development 
 
Project:   
A41 - Adv Teaming for Tactical Aviation Operations Tech 
AL1: Adv Teaming for Tactical Aviation Oper Adv Tech 
A45 / Air Launched Effects Advanced Technology   
 
Keywords:  
Collaborative Autonomy, UAS, AI/ML, Agentic AI, Knowledge Abstraction, Mission Planning, User Interface, User 
Experience 
 
Budget:  
 
FY26 FY27 FY28 FY29 Total 
$5M $8M $11M $5M $29M 
 
Program Schedule: 
 
Multiple awards are anticipated each year, based upon availability of funds.  Offers in the form of summary offers (see Step 1 
below for description of a ‘summary offer’) may be submitted at any time prior to the closing date of this funding opportunity 
which ends 36 months after the date this funding opportunity is published in SAM.gov.  Due to the iterative nature and 

pace of advancement of autonomy technologies, the Government may refine its requirements through amendments to this 
funding opportunity.  Offerors selected for award will mature and test their software solutions through phases of 
development.  An industry product may be integrated for assessment at a partner facility hosted by a University Affiliated 
Research Center (UARC); followed by integration at an industry partner’s Systems Integration Lab (SIL); and, if selected, at 
the Government’s human-in-the-loop Modeling and Simulation (M&S) facility and/or in Live-Virtual-Constructive (LVC) 
flight test activities.  Industry solutions will be assessed using entry and exit criteria to proceed through each of these phases.  
Assessments will use operational scenarios as each Offeror’s products progress through phases of development.  Operational 
scenarios could start simple, such as a single UAS conducting a search or rendezvous task and  increase in complexity to 
involve multiple teams of heterogeneous UAS conducting complex autonomous functions, such as collaborative mission 
planning and execution, scene understanding from multimodal information, and tactical decision making / decision aiding in 
coordination with human team members in a representative tactical Army scenario.  Specific entry and exit criteria will be 
established by mutual agreement between the Government and the Offeror at the start of each phase , such as: 
 
1. Demonstrate behavior required for scenario used in phase. 
2. Perform consistently without failures. 
3. Allow the Government to integrate and use the product with other third party products with ease.  This includes the 
impact of restricted rights, if any, and cooperation with other industry partners.   
 
The ideal duration of a phase is six months or less.  
Alterations from Standard BAA Process.   
 
This funding opportunity adds an additional process consisting of three step s, further described below:  
 
Step One: Summary Offer 
 
Instead of a concept paper, interested Offerors will submit a summary of their proposed solution, hereinafter referred 
to as a ‘summary offer’. The summary offer may include no more than one page of text/graphics and/or five minutes of 
video.  The file size limit for the summary offer is 500MB.  Submission instructions are as provided in the Master BAA 
for the concept paper.  The Government will review the summary offers and select offers of interest who will be invited 
to provide an oral presentation (see Step Two).  
 
Step Two: Oral Presentation 
  
Offerors invited to provide an oral presentation will be contacted by the Government to schedule a time for a virtual 
oral presentation using the Government’s Microsoft Teams application.  The Offeror will submit its presentation 
materials (pdf, mp3/mp4, or PowerPoint) to the Solicitation module of the Procurement Integrated Enterprise 
Environment (PIEE) one week prior to the presentation date.  The Offeror will have a maximum of 45 minutes to provide 
its technical presentation.  The Offeror’s presentation must include a description of the proposed autonomy technology, 
how it supports Government objectives, and a draft work statement detailing how it will be developed, integrated (to 
include description of external dependencies), tested, and delivered (including labor hours, labor categories, 
subcontractors, materials required to complete the proposed work, and projected per unit cost ).  A maximum 30 minute 
question and answer (Q&A) session will follow the oral presentation with the Government team asking questions first 
for up to 20 minutes and the Offeror team asking questions for the final 10 minutes.  The presentations and Q&A will be 
recorded.  The recording will be kept as a part of the official contract file.  The Government will evaluate the information 
provided and select offers of interest. Offerors determined of interest will be invited to submit a cost proposal and if 
needed, a revised statement of work to address Government feedback provided during the TEAMS presentation. 
 
Step Three: Cost Proposal 
 
The Government will perform a final review of the full cost proposal and final statement of work.  If agreeable, the 
Government will enter negotiations and make an award to the Offeror.

Government is searching for technologies that are beyond the fundamental development stage .

Preferred Areas of Focus by Topic: 
 
Autonomous Mission Planning and Execution 
 
The Government seeks mission-specific planning functions to perform threat-informed, pre-mission team configuration and 
composition, and multi-aircraft mission planning and sequencing of tasks based on commander’s intent, orders, rules of 
engagement, airspace control measures, available situational knowledge, etc.  Also of interest are task level planning and 
execution functions for command and coordination of aircraft actions and payload actions capable of dynamically reacting to 
changes in situational awareness (SA) information or commander’s intent and issuing alerts when execution anomalies arise.  
 
Knowledge Representation and Sensemaking 
 
The Government seeks solutions that implement advanced perception algorithms capable of correlation and fusion of 
multimodal, multi-aircraft situational awareness data for high confidence automated object/target detection, recognition, 
identification, and operational state assessment.  Also of interest are algorithms for higher order abstractions and 
representations of four-dimensional SA, terrain data and mission data to include all relevant entities of interest and higher 
order knowledge abstractions for scene situational understanding, sense-making, and predictions that inform mission 
planning and mission oversight functions as well as commander’s decision making, with the ability to seek out additional 
data when current information is inadequate.

Secure Mobile Device Communications (SMDC) 
Prototype Other Transaction (OT) 
 
 
 
*Any submissions that are received by the Agreements Officer after the suspense date/time listed above will be 
deemed late and not evaluated. It is the sole responsibility of the company to ensure that its submission is received 
in the inbox listed above before the deadline specified. 
 
 
This AOI may result in the Government awarding a prototype OT in accordance with  
10 U.S.C. § 4022. This AOI, and any OT awarded from this AOI, is not subject to the Federal Acquisition 
Regulations (FAR) or its supplements. 
  
Project Number DISA-OTA-26-R-SMDC 
Commercial Solutions 
Opening Number HC108425S0001  
AOI Title Secure Mobile Device Communications Prototype OT 
Issued By Defense Information Systems Agency (DISA) | www.disa.mil 
Defense Information Technology Contracting Office (DITCO) 
Submission Instructions 
To respond to this AOI, please refer to paragraph 4 of the AOI 
and the Commercial Solutions Opening, section 3.1, General 
Guidelines and section 3.2, Phase 1 Solution Briefs. 
*Solution Briefs Due  
Date/Time (Suspense) 22 April 2026, 5:00 p.m., CDT 
Submit Solution Brief To 
DITCO OTA Team: 
disa.scott.ditco.mbx.ps84-other-transaction-authority@mail.mil  
Agreements Officer: Joe Santel 
Agreements Specialist: Ashley Fleming 


Version 1.0  Page 2 of 7 
1. BACKGROUND  
 
DISA currently manages mobile device services for the Department of Defense (DoD) and 
approved non-DoD users and is required to maintain compliance with evolving Commercial 
Solutions for Classified (CSfC) standards. The continuous evolution of CSfC Mobile Access 
Capability Package (MACP) requirements is essential for meeting growing security demands 
while improving functionality, usability, and compliance in a rapidly changing technological 
landscape. Earlier mobility solutions consisted of an End User Device (EUD), such as a phone, 
tablet, or laptop, paired with a Retransmission Device (RD) that functioned as a commercial 
mobile hotspot.  
 
2. PROBLEM STATEMENT  
 
The latest published CSfC MACP (version 2.7) requires the RD to be connected to the mobile 
device through a hardwired connection. In earlier versions of MACP, this requirement could be 
met by using a cellular hotspot device that connects to the mobile device via Wi-Fi connection. 
While a cable connection meets the new MACP technical standard, it is operationally untenable. 
The use of a visible cable between the EUD and the RD creates two critical issues: 
 
a. Degraded User Experience & Risk: Physical cables introduce significant user experience 
challenges and operational risks. From a user perspective, the cable is an encumbrance that 
can snag on other gear, get caught on the environment, and physically tether the user, 
restricting their mobility and creating a potential point of failure if disconnected. The 
physical cable makes the phone conspicuous and draws unwanted attention. This visibility 
creates a significant operational security risk. In environments where stealth and operational 
discretion are critical, such exposure could compromise the security of the mission and the 
individual, making it easier for adversaries to target or disrupt operations. The presence of a 
physical cable can serve as an indicator of the operator’s location, role, and equipment type, 
increasing the likelihood of detection and compromising the security of sensitive activities. 
 
b. Reduced Tactical Mobility: Forcing users to carry and physically connect separate devices 
is cumbersome, creates a logistical burden, and hinders the tactical mobility required for 
accessing networks like the Secret Internet Protocol Router (SIPR) Network in operational 
environments. 
 
This prototype OT seeks to develop an innovative and user-friendly Retransmission Device (RD) 
to bridge the gap between CSfC standards and operational needs. The ideal solution, likely a 
sleeve or integrated case, will satisfy the new CSfC hardwired connection requirement internally 
while appearing as a normal case to the outside observer. The goal is to eliminate conspicuous 
external cables, remove the logistical burden of separate devices, and restore full tactical 
mobility for users. 
 
3. DESIRED SOLUTION ATTRIBUTES  
 
A fully functional prototype must include the following unique or innovative capabilities, 
functions, and/or features:  

Version 1.0  Page 3 of 7 
 
3.1. Core Compliance & Physical Design 
 
a. The solution must meet or exceed all requirements of the CSfC MACP version 2.7, and all 
subsequent versions released during the period of performance. 
 
b. The solution’s physical footprint shall be minimized to reduce its visual signature. While a 
form factor similar in size to a commercial smartphone case is the desired baseline, 
companies are encouraged to propose innovative solutions that achieve the core requirement 
of being inconspicuous. 
 
c. The solution must be an all-in-one form factor that eliminates the need for a separate device 
and connecting cable. 
 
d. The solution must be modular to enable rapid, cost-effective portability of capabilities across 
current and future EUD form factors.  
 
e. The solution or physical design (e.g., smartphone case) must support both current and future 
approved DoD mobile devices/form factors (e.g., Samsung Galaxy S25 or S26). The ability 
to support additional form factors (e.g., tablets, laptops, etc.) is a desired feature; however, 
support for additional form factors would only be required in a follow-on production OT or 
contract.   
 
3.2. Component & Supply Chain Security 
 
a. The solution must be compliant with CSfC and National Information Assurance Partnership 
(NIAP) requirements. All components used in the solution must be on the CSfC Components 
List and NIAP validated. The Government will not consider solutions that rely on achieving 
NIAP validation during the prototype period of performance.  
 
b. The solution must adhere to Supply Chain Risk Management principles throughout its 
lifecycle. 
 
c. The solution must adhere to the Trade Agreements Act statutes throughout its lifecycle. All 
manufacturing and assembly, throughout the prototype and any potential follow-on 
production, must be performed domestically in compliance with International Traffic in Arms 
Regulations (ITAR). 
 
d. All modem chips must be compliant throughout the period of performance with Section 
889(a)(1)(A)&(B) of the FY19 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA). 
 
e. The Company must describe their process for adapting the proposed solution to new 
Government-approved moblie devices and form factors. In their solution brief, the Company 
must commit to completing any future form factor change requests within 90 days of 
receiving a formal request from the Government. This capability is considered a required 
performance standard for the successful awardee. 

Version 1.0  Page 4 of 7 
 
f. The company must demonstrate the ability to produce at scale and meet demand via an ITAR 
regulated facility. 
 
3.3. Connectivity & Transport 
 
a. The solution must provide unlocked, Fourth-Generation (4G)/Long-Term Evolution wireless 
network transport that can provide service in Continental United States (CONUS) and 
Outside Continental United States (OCONUS) for the prototype OT. If a follow-on 
production OT or contract is awarded, the Company must be capable of further developing 
the solution to support both 4G and Fifth-Generation cellular transport. “Unlocked" is 
defined as not being bound to a specific carrier, supporting both embedded Subscriber 
Identity Module (SIM) and physical SIM cards.  
 
b. The proposed solution must have the ability to utilize CONUS cellular modems for the 
prototype. If a production OT is awarded, the solution must support both CONUS and 
OCONUS cellular connectivity. 
 
c. The solution must provide 802.11 a/b/g/ac (Wi-Fi 6E/7) transport options. 
 
d. The connectivity chip responsible for external communication must be physically distinct 
from the main processor and not integrated within the same chip. 
 
e. It is desired, but not required, that the capability be designed to support emerging transport 
options, such as Direct-to-Device satellite communications, where applicable.  
 
f. The prototype must demonstrate Wi-Fi connectivity only. If a follow-on production OT or 
contract is awarded, the Company must be capable of futher developing the solution to 
support both Wi-Fi and Cellular connectivity.  
 
g. The Company must demonstrate the ability to obatin Federal Communications Commission 
(FCC) Certification for any components requiring U.S. celleuar network access. Applicable 
FCC certifications would only be required for a follow-on production OT or contract.   
 
3.4. Security Features 
 
a. The ability to create an outer VPN on the RD is a desired feature. If the outer VPN 
capability is included, it must utilize a cryptographic key store that is physically and 
logically independent of the EUD. 
 
b. If the RD is used to create a VPN, it must be able to support the CNSA Suite 2.0 Profile for 
IPSEC in accordance with the draft CSfC Post Quantum Cryptography Guidance 
Addendum. 
 
3.5. Lifecycle, Service & Management 
 

Version 1.0  Page 5 of 7 
a. The solution must include full lifecycle support, if the prototype is successful and moved into 
production, to include planning, procurement, deployment, sustainment, and secure disposal. 
 
b. The solution must offer a framework to control lifecycle costs and provide comprehensive 
support. This framework must account for future hardware and software evolution, allowing 
for cost-effective scalability and ongoing upgrades throughout the lifecycle of the 
solution.The solution must support automated inventory and asset tracking. 
 
c. The solution must be administered via a centralized, cloud-based platform that is authorized 
at Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program (FedRAMP) High and/or DISA 
Impact Level 6. 
 
d. The platform must support secure, over-the-air firmware updates. 
 
e. The platform must provide tools for remote monitoring and reporting. 
 
4. AWARDING INSTRUMENT  
 
This AOI solicitation will be awarded in accordance with the Commercial Solutions Opening 
(CSO) procedures detailed within the DISA CSO HC108425S0001, posted to SAM.gov on 8 
January 2025. The CSO outlines the guidelines for submitting solution briefs, pitches, and 
proposals and how the Government will evaluate responses to this AOI. The CSO can be found 
at: https://sam.gov/opp/98c4a509d78f4f95ae21586d7004fd0e/view 
 
As identified in paragraph 3.2 of the CSO, the Affirmation of Business Status Certification is 
attached to this AOI.  
 
5. SOLICITATION NOTES 
 
In addition to the general guidelines included in the CSO, the following guidelines apply to this 
AOI. 
 
 The Government will give preference to submissions that demonstrate an existing, reference-
verifiable commercial ability to accomplish the desired solution attributes listed above.  
 
 If the Government does not receive any solution briefs that demonstrate an innovative, 
existing, and reference-verifiable commercial ability to accomplish the desired solution 
attributes listed above, preference will be given to submissions demonstrating existing and 
recent products that can be adapted for the solicited purpose with the least amount of non-
recurrent-engineering effort. 
 
 To align with the target schedule, proposals with a performance period of six months or less 
are ideal. This timeframe is preferred to ensure rapid development and deployment of the 
proposed solution, allowing for a timely transition from the prototype phase to full 
implementation if the prototype has been determined successful by the Government.  
 

Version 1.0  Page 6 of 7 
 The anticipated total cost for this prototype project is between $500,000 to $850,000 to 
deliver 20 devices over a 6-month project period, including all associated costs for 
development, implementation, and necessary support.  
 
The primary goal is to identify and select the best possible solution for the Government's needs. 
As such, all submissions are strongly encouraged for consideration, regardless of the proposed 
performance period or target cost. The Government will evaluate each proposal based on its 
merits, innovation, feasibility,

Combined Synopsis/Solicitation W912C326RA007                                                                             
Architect-Engineer (A-E) Services for Structural and Mechanical (HVAC) Assessment of a 
Clinic Facility in Puerto Rico.  
NAICS Code: 541330 – Engineering Services 
PSC Code: C219; Architect and Engineering - General: other 
Set-Aside: Total Small Business 
Questions Due Date: 03 APR 2026, 5:00 PM Eastern Standard Time 
Response Date: 17 APR 2026, 8:00 AM Eastern Standard Time 
 
This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for Architect-Engineer (A-E) services prepared in accordance 
with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 36.2, Brooks Act. The Government intends to award a 
firm-fixed-price contract for the services described herein. 
1. PROJECT DESCRIPTION 
The Contractor shall provide all necessary professional engineering services to conduct a 
comprehensive assessment of a single-story, approximately 12,000 square foot clinic facility located in 
Puerto Rico. The work consists of a Base requirement and one (1) Optional requirement. 
• Base Requirement: A complete non-invasive structural assessment to evaluate the building’s 
structural integrity, identify deficiencies, and provide a report with a prioritized list of 
recommended repairs and an estimated magnitude of cost. 
• Optional Requirement: A complete mechanical (HVAC) assessment to evaluate the condition and 
performance of the HVAC system and its components. This includes performing an engineering 
analysis based on ACCA Manuals N, S, and D to determine if the equipment and ductwork are 
correctly sized and configured for the facility. If exercised, this option will require a separate 
report with prioritized recommendations and cost estimates. 
The Government may exercise the Option at its sole discretion after a review of the Structural 
Assessment Report. A detailed Statement of Work is provided in the attachments. 
 
2. SELECTION PROCESS 
Firms will be selected for negotiation based on demonstrated competence and qualifications in 
accordance with the Brooks Act (FAR 36.2). The Government will evaluate firms based on the selection 
criteria detailed in the attached solicitation package. These criteria include but are not limited to: (1) 
Specialized Experience and Technical Competence in both structural and HVAC assessments; (2) 
Professional Qualifications of Key Personnel; (3) Past Performance; and (4) Capacity to Accomplish the 
Work. 
Mandatory Prerequisite: All firms must provide evidence of a current, active license to practice 
engineering in Puerto Rico to be considered for this requirement. 
Interviews: The Government intends to make a selection based solely on the initial SF 330 submissions. 
However, the government reserves the right to conduct interviews with the most highly qualified firms if 
deemed necessary to make a final selection. 
3. SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS 
• Official Solicitation Package: All information required for this solicitation, including the complete 
Statement of Work, applicable clauses, and detailed evaluation criteria, is contained in the 
solicitation package attached to this notice. Offerors are responsible for downloading and 
reviewing all attachments. 
• Submission Method: This is a 100% paperless solicitation. All submissions (SF-330) shall be 
made electronically through the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) 
Solicitation Module, accessible at https://piee.eb.mil/. Submissions made by any other means will 
not be considered. 
• Questions: All questions regarding this solicitation shall be submitted through the PIEE 
Solicitation Module's question and answer feature by the date specified.

(Primary) Aheisha M Crooks, 
aheisha.m.crooks.civ@army.mil; and  
(Alternate) Harvey Odom 
harvey.odom.civ@army.mil

This is a solicitation for Architect-Engineer (A-E) services prepared in accordance with Federal

Synopsis of Proposed Contract 
Architect-Engineer (A-E) Services for Structural and Mechanical Assessment at Fort Buchanan, PR 
Solicitation Number: W91278-26-R-A007 
Issuing Office: Mission and Installation Contracting Command Ft. Buchanan (MICC-FB) 
Date Issued: March 24, 2026

1. General Information 
• Contract Information: This is a Combined Synopsis / Solicitation for a forthcoming requirement for 
Architect-Engineer (A-E) services. The Mission and Installation Contracting Command; Fort Buchanan, 
PR.  intends to award a single Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contract for the services described herein. 
• Procurement Method: The selection of an A-E firm will be conducted in accordance with the Brooks 
Act (Public Law 92-582), as implemented in Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Subpart 36.202.  
• NAICS Code 541330 (Engineering Services), with a small business size standard of $12.5 million and 
PSC Code C219; Architect and Engineering - General: other.  
• Set-Aside: This procurement is designated as Total Small Business Set-aside.  
 
2. Project Information 
• Project Title: Structural and Mechanical Assessment of Rodriguez Army Health Clinic, Fort Buchanan, 
PR. 
• Project Location: Rodriguez Army Health Clinic, Building 21, 21 Patriot Blvd., Fort Buchanan, PR 
00934.  
  
• General Description: the selected A-E firm will provide all necessary professional services to conduct a 
structural and mechanical assessment of the Rodriguez Army Health Clinic as described in section 3 
“Scope of Work (SOW). The facility is a single-story building of approximately 12,000 square feet (SF). 
The goal is to identify current conditions, deficiencies, and provide detailed recommendations for repair, 
replacement, or modernization to ensure the facility's long-term viability and compliance with current 
codes and standards. 
 
3. Scope of Work (SOW) 
The selected A-E firm shall be required to perform, but not be limited to, the following tasks: 
• Base Task: Structural Assessment 
• Conduct a non-invasive on-site inspection of all structural components, including foundation, 
load-bearing walls, columns, beams, floor and roof structures. 

 
Combined Synopsis/Solicitation W912C326RA007                                                                             
Architect-Engineer (A-E) Services for Structural and Mechanical (HVAC) Assessment of a Clinic 
Facility in Puerto Rico.  
• Evaluate the structural integrity and identify any signs of stress, deterioration, or failure that 
represent a risk to the facility occupants. 
• Review available construction documents and modification records. 
• Deliver a comprehensive final report documenting observed structural findings. For each finding, 
the report must provide photographic documentation and a clear explanation of the suspected 
cause. 
• Develop a prioritized list of recommended repairs or retrofits with estimated magnitude of cost. 
• Optional Task: Mechanical (HVAC) Assessment. This entire task is a separately priced option. The 
Government may exercise this option at its sole discretion after reviewing the findings of the Structural 
Assessment Report. 
• Conduct a non-invasive on-site inspection of the HVAC system, including all accessible 
ductwork, and integrated system components. 
• Evaluate the overall performance and condition of the HVAC system, with a primary focus on 
identifying ductwork deficiencies. 
• Perform an engineering analysis based on ACCA Manual N (Load Calculation), Manual S 
(Equipment Selection), and Manual D (Duct Design) to determine if existing equipment and 
ductwork are correctly sized and configured for the facility's current use as a clinic. 
• Deliver a comprehensive final report documenting mechanical findings. For each finding, the 
report must provide photographic documentation and a clear explanation of the suspected 
cause. 
• Develop a prioritized list of recommended repairs or replacements, including an estimated 
magnitude of cost for each recommendation. 
• Task 3: Deliverables 
• Draft Reports: Submit the following as separate documents for Government review: 
• Base task: Draft Structural Assessment Report 
• Optional Task: Draft Mechanical (HVAC) Assessment Report 
• Final Reports: After incorporating Government feedback, deliver the following as separate documents: 
• Final Structural Assessment Report: Include a prioritized list of recommended structural repairs 
and a corresponding estimated magnitude of cost for each repair. 
• Final Mechanical (HVAC) Assessment Report: Include a prioritized list of recommended 
mechanical repairs/replacements and a corresponding estimated magnitude of cost for each 
repair or replacement. 
• Stakeholder Briefing: Upon delivery of the final reports, provide a single presentation to government 
stakeholders summarizing the key findings and prioritized recommendations from both assessments. 
4. Instructions to Offerors 
Submission Method and Location: This is a 100% paperless solicitation. All submissions shall be made 
electronically through the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) Solicitation Module, 
accessible at https://piee.eb.mil/. Submissions made by any other means (e.g., via email or the SAM.gov 
portal) will not be considered. Offerors are responsible for registering in PIEE and ensuring their

Facility in Puerto Rico.  
submission is successfully uploaded by the required deadline. 
 
Submission Requirements: Offerors shall submit their complete Standard Form (SF) 330, "Architect-
Engineer Qualifications," Part I and Part II, in accordance with the instructions within the PIEE Solicitation 
Module. All submissions must be received by the date and time specified in the solicitation. 
Responsiveness: Submissions that fail to address any mandatory prerequisite or include required 
documentation as specified herein may be deemed non-responsive and removed from consideration. 
 
Evaluation Process and Interviews:  
1. The Government intends to make a selection based solely on the initial SF 330 submissions. However, 
the Contracting Officer reserves the right to conduct interviews with one or more of the most highly 
qualified firms if deemed necessary to make a final selection. Offerors are advised to submit their most 
advantageous qualifications in their initial SF 330 submission. 
 
2. Proposal Validity: Offerors shall state the period for which their SF 330 submission will remain valid. 
 
2.Submission Requirements 
• Interested firms are required to submit their qualifications package using the Standard Form 330 
(SF330), Architect-Engineer Qualifications.  
• Submissions must be sent electronically via the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) 
website. 
• The submission must include: 
• SF330 Part I: Provide contract-specific qualifications. Detail the proposed team, including key 
personnel and any subcontractors. 
• SF330 Part II: Provide general qualifications for the prime firm and each proposed subcontractor. 
• Your SF330 submission should address all evaluation criteria listed below. Pay close attention to 
demonstrating experience on projects of similar scope and complexity. 
 
5. Selection Criteria  
Mandatory Prerequisite: Licensure 
This is a "go/no-go" gateway. A firm must meet this requirement to even be considered for evaluation. 
Licensure in Puerto Rico: Firms must provide evidence of a current, active license to practice engineering 
in Puerto Rico, issued by the Colegio de Ingenieros y Agrimensores de Puerto Rico (CIAPR). Firms failing 
to provide this evidence will be considered non-responsive and will not be evaluated further. 
Scored Evaluation Criteria 
 
After meeting the mandatory prerequisite, firms will be evaluated based on the following criteria. (Criteria 
are listed in descending order of importance.) 
Factor 1: Specialized Experience and Technical Competence of the Firm 
This is the most important factor. It evaluates the firm's direct experience with the specific types of work 
required. 

 
Combined Synopsis/Solicitation W912C326RA007                                                                             
Architect-Engineer (A-E) Services for Structural and Mechanical (HVAC) Assessment of a Clinic 
Facility in Puerto Rico.  
Sub-Factor A: HVAC Assessment Experience: Demonstrated experience in performing HVAC 
assessments, including system diagnostics, deficiency analysis, and the development of ACCA Manual N, 
S, and D based calculations for commercial or institutional facilities. 
Sub-Factor B: Structural Assessment Experience: Demonstrated experience in conducting non-invasive 
structural condition assessments of existing buildings, including identifying deterioration, evaluating risks, 
and developing repair recommendations for facilities of similar size and construction. 
(Evaluation of this factor will focus on the relevance, complexity, and recency of the projects submitted in 
SF-330, Part I, Section F.) 
Factor 2: Professional Qualifications of Key Personnel 
This factor evaluates the specific expertise and qualifications of the individuals who will be assigned to the 
project. 
Structural Engineer: A licensed Professional Engineer with demonstrated experience in structural condition 
assessments and forensic analysis of existing buildings  
Mechanical Engineer (Project Lead): A licensed Professional Engineer with demonstrated experience 
leading HVAC assessment projects, specifically with expertise in ASHRAE standards for healthcare (if 
applicable) and ACCA design methodologies. 
(Evaluation of this factor will focus on the qualifications and tailored experience presented in the SF-330, 
Part I, Section E.)  
Factor 3: Past Performance 
In SF-330, Part I, Section F, submit a maximum of three (3) projects completed within the last five (5) 
years that you consider most relevant to the scope of this requirement. Relevance will be weighted more 
heavily than recency. For each project, ensure the SF-330 includes a complete project description and a 
current point of contact. 
The Government will evaluate the submitted projects on the demonstrated quality of work, cost control, 
timeliness

Performance Work Statement (PWS)

A-123 Internal Controls

4/14/2026

Version 3.0

Performance Work Statement (PWS)

A-123 Internal Controls

Vision Statement 

To strengthen the effectiveness and efficiency of internal controls over financial reporting and financial management systems to ensure compliance with applicable laws and regulations in accordance with the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) Circular A-123, Management's Responsibility for Internal Control.

1 General Information

1.1 Scope of Work 

The U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD), Government National Mortgage Association (Ginnie Mae) Office of Enterprise Risk (OER) requires contractor support to strengthen internal controls over financial reporting and financial management systems. Services shall include documenting, testing, accessing, and reporting on Ginnie Mae’s internal controls over financial reporting and financial management systems in accordance with OMB Circular A-123, including Appendix A, Management of Reporting and Data Integrity Risk Assessment of Ginnie Mae’s internal controls over financial reporting. 

The Contractor shall provide Risk Management and Internal Controls services to perform Ginnie Mae’s annual OMB Circular A-123 including Appendix A to document, test, access and report on Ginnie Mae’s internal controls over financial reporting and financial management systems. 

The support services shall include: 

Program Management

Assessments

OMB A-123 Entity Level Controls Assessment

Conclusion and Recommended Assurance Statement

Policy and Procedure Update

Training Services

Additional Special Assessments

Transition Services (if applicable)

Detailed descriptions of specific tasks are provided in Section 5 - Specific Tasks and Deliverables.

1.2 Background 

Ginnie Mae is responsible for its own financial statements and financial reporting and produces a "Report to Congress" and an Annual Report. HUD also receives Ginnie Mae financial information for inclusion in HUD's consolidated financial statements. Ginnie Mae is unique in that it does not use budgetary accounting, and it prepares standard financial statements in compliance with generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP).

Ginnie Mae’s management is responsible for establishing and maintaining effective internal controls and financial management systems that meet the objectives of the Federal Managers Financial Integrity Act of 1982 (FMFIA). Ginnie Mae currently conducts its annual assessment of internal control over the effectiveness and efficiency of operations and compliance with applicable laws and regulations in accordance with OMB Circular A-123. Ginnie Mae also conducts its annual assessment of the effectiveness of internal controls over financial reporting, which includes safeguarding of assets and compliance with applicable laws and regulations, in accordance with the requirements of Appendix A of OMB Circular A-123.

1.3 Constraints 

The services identified in this PWS will adhere to the rules, regulations, laws, standards, and conventions identified by HUD as well as within the Federal Government. Constraints include the following: 

Federal Managers Financial Integrity Act of 1982

https://www.whitehouse.gov/sites/whitehouse.gov/files/omb/financial/fmfia1982.html 

September 8, 1982  

OMB Circular A-123, Managements Responsibility for Internal Control https://www.whitehouse.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/OMB-Circular-No.-A-123-2026.pdf)

OMB A-123, Appendix A of OMB Circular A-123 Revised 

https://www.whitehouse.gov/wp-content/uploads/2018/06/M-18-16.pdf 

June 6, 2018

OMB A-11, Preparation, Submission and Execution of the Budget 

https://www.whitehouse.gov/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/a11.pdf

August 2025

The Green Book, Standards for Internal Controls in the Federal Government 

https://www.gao.gov/assets/gao-25-107721.pdf

May 2025

The Yellow Book, Government Auditing Standards 2024 Revised 

https://www.gao.gov/assets/d24106786.pdf

February 2024 Revision

Government Performance and Results Modernization Act of 2010 (GPRA) 

https://www.congress.gov/111/plaws/publ352/PLAW-111publ352.pdf 

January 4, 2011

Federal Information Security Modernization Act of 2014 (FISMA) 

https://www.cisa.gov/federal-information-security-modernization-act 

December 18, 2014

Federal Information Systems Controls Audit Manual (FISCAM) 

https://www.gao.gov/assets/80/77142.pdf 

February 2009

Improper Payments Information Act of 2002 (IPIA) and Improper Payments Elimination and Recovery Act 2012 

https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/PLAW-112publ248/pdf/PLAW-112publ248.pdf

January 10, 2013

Implementation Guide for OMB Circular A-123, Managements Responsibility for Internal Control Appendix A, Internal Control over Financial Reporting

https://www.whitehouse.gov/sites/whitehouse.gov/files/omb/circulars/A123/a123_appx_a_implementation_guide.pdf 

July 2005

Clinger-Cohen Act of 1996

https://www.fismacenter.com/Clinger%20Cohen.pdf 

February 10, 1996

Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP)

http://www.accountingtools.com/definition-gaap 

Federal Travel Regulations (FTR)

http://www.gsa.gov/portal/content/104790 

November 15, 2019

1.4 Non-Personal Services

The Government will neither supervise Contractor employees nor control the method by which the Contractor performs the required tasks. Under no circumstances shall the Government assign tasks to, or prepare work schedules for, individual Contractor employees. It shall be the responsibility of the Contractor to manage its employees and to guard against any actions that are of the nature of personal services or give the perception of personal services.

If the Contractor believes that any actions constitute, or are perceived to constitute personal services, it shall be the Contractor's responsibility to notify the Contracting Officer (CO) immediately. These services shall not be used to perform work of a policy, decision making or management nature, i.e., inherently Government functions. All decisions relative to programs supported by the Contactor shall be the sole responsibility of the Government. 

1.5 Period of Performance 

The period of performance shall be a 12-month base with four (4) 12-month option periods.

1.6 Place of Performance 

The services to be performed under this contract shall be performed at the contractor facilities. 

1.7 Hours of Operation

The Contractor is responsible for providing services between hours of 8:00am to 5:00pm, Monday thru Friday except for Federal holidays or when the Government facility is closed due to local or national emergencies, administrative closing, or similar Government directed facility closings. The Government reserves the right to change hours of operation or restrict contractor access. Government agencies will not be available during scheduled holidays, inclement weather, weekends, and after duty hours. 

The Contractor shall maintain an adequate workforce for the uninterrupted performance of all tasks defined within the contract when the Government facility is not closed for the above reasons. When hiring personnel, the Contractor shall keep in mind that the stability and continuity of the workforce is essential. 

1.8 Special Qualifications 

The Contractor shall have the following risk and compliance industry certifications: 

Certified Public Accountant (CPA)

Certified Information Systems Auditor (CISA)

Certified Internal Auditor (CIA)

Certified Fraud Examiner (CFE)

Certified Government Financial Manager (CGFM)

1.9 Post Award/Kickoff Conference

The Contractor shall attend any post award conference convened by the contracting activity or contract administration office in accordance with HUD Acquisition Regulation (HUDAR) clause 2452.237-79 - Post Award Conference.                    

1.10 Status Meetings

The Contracting Officer, Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR), and other Government personnel, as appropriate, may meet periodically with the Contractor to also review Contractor performance, requirement status, etc. At these meetings, the Contracting Officer will appraise the Contractor of how the Government views the Contractor's performance or progress of the requirement. The Contractor will apprise the Government of problems, if any, being experienced. Appropriate action shall be taken to resolve outstanding issues. These meetings shall be at no additional cost to the Government. Post Award Conference and subsequent meetings may be held via teleconference at the Contracting Officer's discretion.

1.11 Contractor Travel

Prior to travel, the Contractor shall coordinate with and receive Government authorization from the COR for all travel. Reimbursement of travel costs will be in accordance with the Federal Travel Regulation and in accordance with FAR 31.205-46.  

1.12 Transition-In

The Contractor shall, upon the Contracting Officer's written notice, furnish transition-in services as required. As a successor, the Contractor shall have sufficient personnel on board during the  30-day transition-in period to ensure a smooth transition with the incumbent Contractor. The Contractor shall provide an orderly transition of work acceptance and accomplishment such that any impact to the program is minimized. During the transition-in period, the Contractor shall become familiar with the requirements in order to commence full performance of services by the end of the contract transition-in period. Transition-in is not required if the successor Contractor is the incumbent Contractor.

1.13 Transition-Out 

To minimize any decrease in productivity and to prevent possible negative impacts on additional services, the Contractor shall have sufficient personnel on board during the 30-day transition-out period. The incumbent Contractor shall ensure a smooth transition with the successor Contractor during the transition-out period, prior to completion of contractual performance. The incumbent Contractor shall aid the successor in the development of plans, procedures, and methods for the assumption of all on going work. The Contractor shall provide an orderly transition of work acceptance and accomplishment, such that full control by the successor contractor is achieved by the end of the new contract transition-in period. 

2 Definitions and Acronyms

2.1 Definitions 

Business Day – Every official day of the week which are days between and including Monday to Friday. This does not include federal holidays and weekends.

Complementary User Entity Controls – Controls that management of the service organization assumes, in the design of the service organization’s system, will be implemented by user entities and are necessary to achieve the control objectives stated in management's description of the service organization’s system. 

Contractor  – A supplier or vendor awarded a contract to provide specific supplies or service to the Government. The term used in this contract refers to the prime.

Contracting Officer (CO) – A person with authority to enter into, administer, and/or terminate contracts and make related determinations and findings on behalf of the Government. Note: the only individual who can legally bind the Government.

Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR) – An employee of the U.S. Government appointed by the Contracting Officer to perform contract administration activities regarding technical issues. This individual has authority to provide technical directions to the Contractor if direction is within the scope of the contract, does not constitute a change, and has no funding implications. This individual does NOT have the authority to change the terms and conditions of the contract. 

Defective Service – A service output that does not meet the standard of performance associated with the Performance Work Statement.

Deliverable – Anything that can be physically delivered but may include non-manufactured things such as meeting minutes or reports.

Enterprise Risk Management – An effective agency-wide approach to addressing the full spectrum of the organization’s significant risks by understanding the combined impact of risks as an interrelated portfolio, rather than addressing risks only within silos.  

Government Furnished Property (GFP) - Government-furnished property is property in the possession of, or directly acquired by, the Government and subsequently furnished to the Contractor for performance of a contract. Government-furnished property includes, but is not limited to, spares and property furnished for repair, maintenance, overhaul, or modification.  Government-furnished property also includes contractor-acquired property if the contractor-acquired property is deliverable under a cost contract when accepted by the Government for continued use under the contract.

Independent Validation and Verification – A comprehensive review, analysis and testing performed by an objective third-party to confirm (i.e., verify) that the requirements are correctly defined, and to confirm (i.e., validate) that the systems correctly implement the required functionality and security requirements. 

Performance Standard - The Contractor’s performance level required by the Government.   

Performance Work Statement (PWS) – A statement of work for performance-based acquisitions that describe the required results in clear, specific, and objective terms with measurable outcomes.

Quality Assurance (QA) – Policies and procedures adopted by the Government to ensure that supplies and services acquired under Government contracts conform to the contracts quality requirements.  

Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan (QASP) – A plan describing how the agency will survey, observe, test, sample, evaluate and document the Contractor's performance in meeting critical performance standards identified in the contract.  

Quality Control (QC) – All necessary measures taken by the Contractor to assure that the quality of an end product of service shall meet contract requirements.

Subcontractor – Any person, other than the prime Contractor, who offers to furnish or furnishes any supplies, material, equipment, or services of any kind under a prime contract or a subcontract entered into in connection with such prime contract, and any person who offers to furnish or furnishes general supplies to the prime contractor or a higher tier subcontractor.  The Government does not have privity of contract with a subcontractor. 

2.2 Acronyms 

AICPA - American Institute of Certified Public Accountants

AQL - Acceptable Quality Level  

CCMB - Configuration Change Management Board   

CFO or OCFO - Office of the Chief Financial Officer of HUD   

CFPB - Consumer Financial Protection Bureau

CFR - Code of Federal Regulations   

CIO or OCIO - Office of the Chief Information Officer of HUD   

CO - Contracting Officer   

COR - Contracting Officer's Representative

CPO - Office of the Chief Procurement Officer o
