GENERAL INFORMATION

PLACE OF PERFORMANCE

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

DESCRIPTION

The Central Texas VA Health Care System (CTVAHCS) in Temple, Texas is seeking Service Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business (SDVOSB), Veteran Owned Small Business (VOSB), or Small Business sources capable of meeting the requirement listed below.  The acquisition will be accomplished using commercial item procedures in accordance with FAR Part 12.

NOTE: TO QUALIFY SDVOSB AND VOSB VENDORS MUST BE CERTIFIED IN THE SMALL BUSINESS SEARCH (SBS) DATABASE.

The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) is 541519.  Any SDVOSB, VOSB, or Small Business firms who wish to identify their interests and capability to provide this product must provide product specifications, performance and delivery information by notifying the Contract Specialist no later than TEN PM Central Time, April 24, 2026.  Notification shall be e-mailed to Akisha Woods, at Akisha.Woods@va.gov.

Any vendor who responds to this Notice must provide credentials to perform the requirement as outlined in the below scope. 

DISCLAIMER

This Sources Sought Notice is issued solely for information and planning purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation.  All information received in response to this Notice that is marked as proprietary will be handled accordingly.  In accordance with the Federal Acquisition Regulation, responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract.  Responders are solely responsible for all expenses associated with responding to this Notice.

SCOPE:

Introduction:  Central Texas Veterans Health Care System (CTVHCS) clinicians use Theradoc to provide medical technology that interprets records, alerts clinicians, and recommends patient-specific treatment options that are based on current medical guidelines and evidence, resulting in better healthcare decisions.  This favorably affects patients’ healthcare experiences and outcomes, while reducing costs.  VHA has purchased a license for TheraDoc, a Document Storage Systems (DSS) product, which requires an annual maintenance and telephone support services contract for those health care systems that use TheraDoc.      

		(1)	Background:  CTVHCS has a continuing need to use TheraDoc in support of safe, efficient and effective patient care, and must have a maintenance and telephone services contract in place to do so.  Use of TheraDoc is essential to patient care activities performed by many clinical staff, and it is imperative the maintenance service contract is established to make this possible.  Theradoc provides clinicians with patient information and medical knowledge to promote better patient care decisions.  It enables providers to make therapeutic interventions more quickly, improve appropriate use of antimicrobials, reduce adverse reactions, reduce the length of hospital stays, and more efficient, better and safer patient care.  Theradoc interprets records, provides alerts to clinicians, recommends evidence-based treatment options based on current medical guidelines, which results in better health care decision that improve patient outcomes while reducing costs.  It is imperative this medical surveillance capability for CTVHCS be maintained in fully operational status at all times in order to promote better patient care.

Scope of Work:  The Contractor to provide service and support to an existing TheraDoc for VistA Large Hospital-TESA Platform, that will include the following services, in addition to software upgrades as needed:

1) DSS-TDOC-VistA-LVL1: TheraDoc for VistA - TESA Platform, Pharmacy Assistant, Infection Control Assistant. Includes interfaces for ADT, Lab, Micro, Surgery, Inpatient Pharmacy, Radiology, BCMA, Vital Signs, Problem List. Annual Limited License. Includes Support and Maintenance and 24x7 monitoring support. Level 1 facility

2) DSS-TDOC-DBUSER: DSS TheraDoc EMR Embedded DB and ColdFusion Software.

3) DSS-OUTPT-PHARM-LL: DSS Outpatient Pharmacy Interface for TheraDoc, Annual Limited License per hospital. Includes support and maintenance for a period of one year 

4) DSS-MDI-VA-LL: DSS Medical Devices Interface (MDI) for TheraDoc, Annual Limited License per facility.  Includes support and maintenance for a period of one year.

5) DSS-PREMAPPSUPPORT-VAAF: DSS ADHOC Premium Application Workflow Support - Remote, per facility annual fee.

6) DSS-INST-R: DSS Remote Installation Services Per Day

7) DSS-TDOC-EMR: DSS TheraDoc EMR Project Management, Technical and Training Services Per Hour.

8) TRAVEL-Z: Travel Per Diem Expenses, per person, per week.

2.	REQUIREMENTS:

Type of Contract: Firm-Fixed-Price for the Base Year, followed by option years one through four. 

General Requirements:  To provide CTVHCS with continued support services performed by staff that are comprehensively trained in TheraDoc processes and procedures.

Period of Performance:  The maintenance and telephone support services contract to run for the Base Year from start of contract through the option years.  

3.	REFERENCES:  

Federal Standards and Guidance:	

		(1)	The Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) of 1996

Computer Security Act of 1987, Public Law 10-235

	(2)	OMB Circular A-123, Management’s Responsibility for Internal Control – Revised (03/10/2026) (35 pages, 528KB)

	(3)	5 U.S.C. 552a, Privacy Act of 1974, 5 United States Code 552a, Public Law 99-08.

	(4)	5 U.S.C. 552, Freedom of Information Act, 5 United States Code 552, Public Law

	(5)	18 U.S.C. 1030 (a) (3), Fraud and related activity in connection with computers.

	(6)	Electronic Communications Privacy Act of 1986, Public Law 99-08, 100 Stat. 1848.

	b.	Agency Policy and Guidelines:

(1) VA Directive 6008, Acquisition and Management of VA Information Technology Resources

	(2) VA Directive 6102, Internet and Intranet Services

	(3) VA Handbook 6340, Enterprise Mail Management Procedures

	(4) VA Directive 6403, Software Asset Management

	(5) VA Directive 6500, VA Cybersecurity Program 

		(6) VA Handbook 6500, Risk Management Framework for VA Information Systems, VA Information Security Program

		(7) VA Handbook 6500.6, Contract Security

		(8) VA Handbook 6513, Secure External Connections

		(9) VA Directive 6515, Use of Web Based Collaboration Technologies

		(10) VA Directive 6517 Risk Management Framework for Cloud Computing Services

c. Local Policies:

VHA Field VAMC Policy MCP 674-ISO-024, Management of Information Security and Privacy Incidents 

VHA Field VAMC Policy MCP 00-25, Facility Information System Contingency Plan (ISCP) Business Impact Analysis (BIA) and Business Continuity Plan-Continuity of Operations Plan (BCP-COOP)

VHA Field VAMC Policy MCP 003-001, Internet and Intranet-SharePoint Content Development

(4) VHA Field VAMC Policy MCP 674-ISO-003 – Use of Electronic Mail and Internet Usage Guidelines

(5) VHA Field VAMC Policy MCP 674-008-003, Records Management Program 

4.	DELIVERABLES:  

Contractor to provide the following services as needed:

Work directly with users to address any issues with TheraDoc products.

Respond to issues within required response times.

Advise local OI&T and/or Biomedical Engineering staff regarding configurations for products, new installations of products, and end-user activities.

Assist local OI&T and/or Biomedical Engineering staff regarding issues with infrastructure requirements for products, including hardware, bandwidth, best practices, etc.

Advise local OI&T/Biomedical Engineering staff and/or other local points of contact regarding any issues which may impact usage of licensed products.

Provide software upgrades as required to resolve TheraDoc server vulnerabilities reported by the VA, as well as other application enhancements. This will include “release notes” for all versions included the upgrades, for Pharmacy and IP&C.

Provide reports upon request to local OI&T and/or Biomedical Engineering staff for:

Summary of tickets currently open, and those closed with the past 7 days

Summary of known issues impacting site use of products with current status, expected release date, and workaround if available

Requesting Support and Assigning Priority: Contractor staff will be considered second level support for local OI&T staff, and as such support can only be initiated by local OI&T staff.  Priority of response is based on the following:

0-Urgent:  Initial response within 1 hour, with follow-up response within 2 hours.  For catastrophic incidents such as server crash, one or more product applications being inaccessible to all users, etc.

1-High:  Initial response within 2 hours, with follow-up within 22 hours (2 business days).  For instances in which the system is functioning, but in a severely reduced capacity significantly impacting portions of business operations

2-Medium:  Initial response within 4 hours, with follow-up within 33 hours (3 business days).  For instances of non-critical functionality loss in which some operations are impaired, but users and/or applications are able to continue to function

3-Low:  Initial response with 8 hours, with follow-up within 44 hours (4 business days).  For instances in which there is minimal impact to business operations.

5.	QUALITY ASSURANCE SURVEILLANCE PROGRAM (QASP):  The Contractor will ensure support services staff and actions are in compliance with the terms of the contract. 

6.	SECURITY CONSIDERATIONS:  Safeguarding patient health information (PHI) is a primary concern for VA staff and for contractor personnel working in VA facilities and/or working with PHI or other confidential/sensitive information.  DSS will adhere to all VA Information Security, Privacy and HIPAA requirements when obtaining and reviewing diagnostic information.  This includes as log files, error traps, screen capture images and database query results used to aid in providing support services required by the contract.

	a.	The Computer Security Act requires federal agencies to provide for mandatory periodic training in computer security awareness and accepted computer security practices for all employees who are involved with the management, use, or operation of a federal computer system within or under the supervision of the federal agency.  This includes contractors as well as employees of the agency. OMB Circular A-130, Appendix III, revised in 1996, enforces such mandatory training by requiring its completion prior to granting access to the system and through periodic refresher training for continued access.  Therefore, each user must be versed in acceptable rules of behavior for the application before being allowed access to the system.  VA and VHA policies specify mandatory orientation training prior to access and annual refresher training for all employees.  The training program also informs users on procedures for reporting security incidents.  Contractor staff must comply with training and security requirements to the same extent as VA staff.

      b.  Information made available to the contractor or subcontractor by VA for the performance or administration of this contract or information developed by the contractor/subcontractor in performance or administration of the contract shall be used only for those purposes and shall not be used in any other way without the prior written agreement of the VA. F-35 JOINT PROGRAM OFFICE  
DIRECTORATE OF ENTERPRISE SERVICES ACQUISITION 
 
 
 
 
SECURITY SUPPORT SERVICES 
PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT 
 
 
1. INTRODUCTION. 
The F-35 Lightning II Joint Program Office (JPO) leads the life-cycle program management of 
the F-35A, F-35B, and F-35C: the fifth-generation joint strike fighter air system of choice for the 
U.S. Air Force, U.S. Navy, U.S. Marine Corps (the US Services), Cooperative Program Partners 
(CPP), and foreign military sales (FMS) customers. The mandate of the JPO is to deliver a 
capable, available, and affordable air system to the warfighter - outpacing key competitors to win 
tomorrow's high-end fight as we develop, deliver, and sustain war-winning fifth-generation 
capabilities at high-end fourth-generation costs. 
• The JPO ensures that the F-35 is lethal, scalable, adaptable, and capable of competing and 
keeping the warfighter one step ahead of aggressors. 
• The JPO ensures that the F-35 is operative, and parts are available when needed. The long-
term goal is an environment of comprehensive sustainment excellence that includes 
initiatives to keep parts on wing longer, maintain appropriate spares, and enhance repair 
capability and velocity. 
• The JPO ensures that the F-35 is affordable for the U.S. services, international partners, and 
customers through cost reduction across the acquisition life cycle. 
 
1.1. Scope. 
The JPO, which is comprised of the US Services, CPP, and FMS customers, requires knowledge-
based security services in support of F-35 acquisition and sustainment activities. The F-35 JPO 
Security Directorate (herein referred to as F-35 JPO Security) has the critical mission of 
providing full spectrum multi-disciplined security support to protect F-35 technology and 
information across its enterprise and throughout the acquisition and sustainment lifecycle. F-35 
JPO Security efforts include providing advice and services regarding programmatic security 
measures that deny unauthorized access to F-35 facilities, equipment, and resources, and protect 
personnel, information, and property from damage and/or loss of technology. 
 


 
2 
 
Security support services encompass the management and control of controlled unclassified 
information (CUI), collateral/general service (GENSER) information, Special Access Program 
(SAP) information, North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) information, Critical Nuclear 
Weapons Design Information (CNWDI), Restricted Data (RD) and Formal Restricted Data 
(FRD), and Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI) across multiple security disciplines. 
Security support disciplines consist of, but are not limited to, General Security (GENSEC), 
Industrial Security (INDUSEC), Information Security (INFOSEC), Personnel Security 
(PERSEC), and Physical Security (PHYSEC). This contract will be used as a means of providing 
security services to the JPO globally.

UNITED STATES CAPITOL POLICE 
OFFICE OF ACQUISITION MANAGEMENT 
 
 
 
 
April 10, 2026
 
 
 
Subject: Request for Quotes (RFQ) for Comprehensive Wellness Application for the 
United States Capitol Police 
 
 
To Whom It May Concern, 
 
The United States Capitol Police (USCP), Office of Liebengood Center for Wellness 
(LCW) has a requirement for a comprehensive wellness application. You are hereby 
requested to submit a technical quote for a comprehensive wellness application in 
accordance with the enclosed Statement of Work. USCP intends to procure services 
under a Firm Fixed-Price contract type. 
 
 
Factors for Award 
 
Award will be made in accordance with the procedures of FAR Part 13 – Simplified 
Acquisition Procedures. The basis for award will be best value. In so doing, the 
Government may award to other than the lowest priced quote or other than the highest 
technically rated quote. This acquisition will be conducted using a phased approach. Phase I 
will consist of potential proposers submitting a document that addresses how it will address 
all elements under Factor 1. The next phase, a Pre-Award Demonstration will be scheduled at 
the conclusion of initial evaluation of quoters from Phase I. This demonstration will be 
considered Phase II of the RFQ. The purpose of the demonstration is to allow up to three (3) 
of the highest rated quoters to showcase the Wellness Application and present the 
functionality of the final product to USCP stakeholders.  All three Parts of the quote (listed 
below) will be considered when making the determination of the highest rated Quoters. 
Quoters that are selected to present for Phase II shall be required to prepare a virtual 
presentation (MS Teams) that shall not exceed one hour. Evaluation criteria for the 
Demonstration will be provided at the conclusion of Phase I evaluation.  
 
Phase I. The following technical evaluation factors are in order of importance:  
 
Factor 1 – Technical Capability and Understanding of the Requirements 
  
For Factor 1, the contractor shall demonstrate comprehensive understanding of the tasks 
outlined in Section C3-C7 of the SOW to include the following sub factors: 
  
1.1. Approach to accomplish scope elements in C3-C7 of the SOW 


1.2. Expertise accomplishing the elements in C3-C7 of the SOW 
1.3. Strategy for accomplishing the elements in C3-C7 of the SOW 
 
Factor 2 – Past Performance 
 
Past Performance: The Related Corporate Experience section shall briefly describe 
the experience of the vendor performing work similar to this one from the past three 
(3) years. Provide a demonstration of the contractor's knowledge and understanding 
of the SOW and stated requirements in general. Short abstracts of related work shall 
include the name, current affiliation and phone number of the sponsor's project officer 
(or equivalent), and dates the work was performed. Additionally, quoters shall provide 
at least three (3) references that have received services from the contractor, which are 
comparable to those described in this solicitation. Projects must have been completed 
within the last two (2) years or shall be currently in progress. 
 
The vendors past performance will be evaluated under existing and prior contracts for 
similar products and services over the last three years. The USCP will focus on 
information that demonstrates quality of performance relative to the complexity of the 
procurement under consideration. Please submit no more than three (3) Past 
Performance references for similar efforts as described in the SOW. For each contract 
or task order provided as a reference, the vendor shall send the Past Performance

Quote Submission Information 
 
Cover Letter: The cover letter shall include the quotation number, contractor name, 
address and phone number, a statement specifying the extent of agreement with all terms 
and conditions, and agreement to furnish any or all items upon which prices are offered at 
the price set opposite each item in Section B of the RFQ. The letter shall include the

documents. All documents associated with the written technical quote must not include 
any price information.

For your quotation to be considered responsive, it must be submitted no later than 2:00 
P.M., Eastern Daylight Savings Time on April 21, 2026, via email to 
Jennell.joyner@uscp.gov.

resulting contract. Any exceptions or deviations to these terms and conditions must be 
clearly indicated in the Contractor's quote. Cover letters shall indicate whether any 
exceptions or deviations are contained in the quote, the RFQ or specification requirements 
to which exception or deviation is taken, the page number(s) of the quote affected, and the 

price impact if any, and reason for the exception/deviation unless the rationale is reflected 
in the quote itself. 
 
In the event that your company declines to submit a quotation, please communicate this 
fact to the Contract Specialist as soon as possible. 
 
Please be advised that the USCP is under no obligation to pay for any costs incurred in the 
preparation of this quotation or to procure any of the supplies or services identified herein.  
 
 
The Government reserves the right to award without discussions. 
 
 
If you need additional information, please contact Jennell Joyner at Jennell. joyner@uscp.gov. 
 
 
 
Sincerely, 
 
 
 
 
Michael Iszard

technologies.

RFI: NAVAIR Weaponeering and Stores Planning (WASP) Systems Engineering (0147)

Agency: Department of the Navy

Office: Naval Air Systems Command (PMA-281)

Location: Naval Air Warfare Center Patuxent River, MD

SAM.GOV DESCRIPTION

DISCLAIMER
THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT ANNOUNCEMENT ONLY.  THIS ANNOUNCEMENT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. ALL INFORMATION SUBMITTED IN RESPONSE TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT IS VOLUNTARY AND THE GOVERNMENT WILL NOT PAY FOR INFORMATION REQUESTED NOR WILL IT COMPENSATE ANY RESPONDENT FOR ANY COST INCURRED IN DEVELOPMENT INFORMATION PROVIDED TO THE GOVERNMENT. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL; IT IS A MARKET RESEARCH TOOL TO DETERMINE POTENTIAL FIRMS CAPABLE OF PROVIDING THE SOLUTIONS DESCRIBED HEREIN PRIOR TO AN ISSUANCE OF A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. THE GOVERNMENT IS NOT OBLIGATED TO AND WILL NOT PAY FOR ANY INFORMATION RECEIVED FROM POTENTIAL SOURCES AS A RESULT OF THIS NOTICE. THIS DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT OF ANY KIND. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT OR NON-FAR BASED AGREEMENT (E.G. OTHER TRANSACTION) AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS TO THIS TECHNICAL DESCRIPTION IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY. FAILURE TO SUBMIT A RESPONSE WILL NOT PREVENT A COMPANY FROM PARTICIPATION IN ANY FUTURE COMPETITION RELATED TO THE WEAPONEERING AND STORES PLANNING (WASP) SOFTWARE DEVELOPMENT PROGRAM.

INTRODUCTION

This sources sought announcement is being posted to satisfy the requirement of Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) Policy, Guidance, and Instruction (PGI) 206.103-170(d). The Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR), Program Executive Office for Unmanned Aviation and Strike Weapons (PEO (U&W)), Strike Planning and Execution Systems Program Office (PMA-281) at Patuxent River, MD is conducting market research to determine the amount of responsible sources that have the capability, experience, facilities, and capacity to provide Integrated Product Office support services for the Weaponeering and Stores Planning (WASP) program. The Government is seeking industry input for support to the WASP Integrated Product Office to define the technical content of each WASP version and improve the delivery of flight clearance information to Fleet users through systems engineering, test and evaluation products and services, configuration management, and WASP laboratory/infrastructure management. The work includes support in a classified environment up to SECRET. 

NAVAIR intends to issue a sole source Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract to KBR Wyle Services, LLC for the continued software development of WASP Integrated Product Office if no other responsible and capable sources are identified. This acquisition is being pursued on a sole source basis under the statutory authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), as implemented by Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 6.103-1, only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. This Request for Information (RFI)/sources sought will assist NAVAIR in developing an acquisition strategy for any potential future sourcing methods for supplies and services outlined in this document. No Request for Quote (RFQ) exists; therefore, do not request a copy of the RFQ.

BACKGROUND

The WASP software application provides automated weapons and store loading, and delivery planning, and is certified as a permanent flight clearance application. The WASP software application provides authorized stores and configurations, validation of loading, carriage, jettison and release limits, authorized release parameters, fuze arming, safe escape limits, drag, weights and moment arms, Launch Acceptable Region (LAR) planning, sensor footprints, employment planning, Weaponeering reports and kneeboard cards for the F/A-18A-F and EA-18G. The WASP software is a Federated Application and is hosted on the JMPS-M hardware and the F/A-18, EA-18G MPE. The WASP software application operates independently of the JMPS-M Framework (FW), common components, Unique Planning Components (UPC) and other Federated Applications.

Due to highly specialized and unique engineering and test requirements of the WASP Integrated Product Office, only the incumbent has the necessary domain knowledge on WASP architecture, WASP software requirements. KBR Wyle Services’ highly specialized system engineering support efforts include the decomposition of requirements from the F/A-18 and EA-18G family of Naval Aviation Technical Information Product (NATIP) manual as well as the design and execution of all automated testing of the WASP application.  In addition, they are responsible for the design and development of the internal WASP nomenclature used to support all authorized weapons and stores that are published in each update of the NATIP manuals. The release cycle of current WASP is tied to the release cycle of the F/A-18 and EA-18G family of NATIP manuals with updates occurring multiple times per year for each Type/Model/Series aircraft in the F/A-18 and EA-18G family of aircraft. As such, this vendor is the only source that can provide the highly specialized services without unacceptable delays in fulfilling the Navy’s requirement to deliver the unique the continued development, delivery, and sustainment of WASP systems. 

ANTICIPATED PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE

Q1 FY27 to Q1 FY32

REQUIREMENTS

NAVAIR is seeking to identify the market (U.S. wholly owned companies only) capable of providing WASP Integrated Product Office services. The Government owns and will retain ownership and unlimited data rights to deliverables developed under the contract, including source code and related data. Planned work includes system engineering support, Non-Recurring Engineering (NRE) and testing in support of WASP software engineering analyses, requirement analyses and functional testing on multiple versions of the WASP software. The WASP software is certified as a permanent flight clearance application that is necessary for USN/USMC aircraft to maintain parity with their technical and safety-of-flight publications.

NAVAIR is seeking a potential contractor with the ability to provide research and development (R&D) to enhance the aircrew’s ability to plan safe stores loading and delivery of weapons onto targets. The contractor shall provide systems engineering products to PMA-281 WASP Integrated Product Office necessary to define the technical content of each WASP version with the goals of providing rapid delivery of essential data, providing test and evaluation products for WASP versions, providing configuration management of WASP technical source data and accessibility to data from off-site locations, and providing WASP lab facilities management and systems administration of WASP information technology resources.

NAVAIR is seeking a potential contractor with the ability to ingest and execute highly complex military requirements, interface documents and specifications, as well as experience in participating in the engineering change proposal construct. The potential contractor should have experience in the full scope of systems engineering to include requirements analysis and traceability, modeling and simulation, test and evaluation, complex integration, and risk management. The potential contractor should describe systems engineering experience with common systems engineering tools such as Azure DevOps Server (Microsoft), Confluence (Atlassian), and Jira (Atlassian) or other comparable tools through Model-based systems engineering practices.

STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW) 
 
Title: HiCAM Technology Assessment Support 
 
 
1. Objective/Requirements 
This contract shall provide composite aircraft manufacturing technology assessment and 
commercial production modeling SME support to the HiCAM Project Leadership Team. 
This support includes, but is not limited to, representing NASA as a Task Lead or key 
contributor in ACC work activities.  
 
It is anticipated that the Contractor will need to work in collaboration with NASA and 
other ACC partners to execute the work defined throughout this requirements document.  
However, the Contractor is expected to perform independent work, engage with internal 
and external stakeholders at the working and leadership levels, and be proactive 
throughout performance of these requirements. 
 
Background: 
The primary goal of the Hi-Rate Composite Aircraft Manufacturing (HiCAM) project is 
to demonstrate manufacturing approaches and associated technologies for large 
composite airframe structures that enable high-rate production (up to 80 aircraft per 
month) with reduced cost and no weight penalty versus 2020 technologies. The Project 
will develop mature, affordable, high-rate composite manufacturing and assembly 
technologies, with reduced equipment and tooling costs, enabling a faster, more cost-
effective production cycle for lightweight airframe structures. The Project will also 
develop model-based engineering tools needed to rapidly mature and optimize both 
component design and the manufacturing processes. Achieving the overall project goal 
will require improvements across the seven major areas that drive high-rate composite 
aircraft manufacturing: materials, architectures, laydown, cure, assembly, inspection, and 
paint. HiCAM has a finite duration and does not anticipate the need for support beyond 
fiscal year 2029. 
 
HiCAM technical work is performed by Cooperative Research Teams (CRT) whose 
members are part of the Advanced Composites Consortium (ACC). The ACC is 
comprised of government, industry, and academic institutions who partner in their 
pursuit of advancing high rate composite aircraft manufacturing techniques that align 
with Project objectives. CRTs collaboratively define and execute content outlined in 
work activity Project Work Plans (PWPs) that focus on manufacturing-specific 
technologies, or cross cutting model-based engineering tools, inspection and advanced 
assembly technologies, and capstone demonstration articles. However, these CRTs often 
focus only on specific technology development and do not consider how technologies 
developed by several CRTs might integrate to affect the overall performance of an 
advanced production system. Because of this, NASA established a Technology 
Assessment Process where commercial aircraft manufacturing production model subject 
matter experts (SME) developed simulations of future production systems to estimate the 
relative impact of proposed high-rate manufacturing technologies on system level key 

performance parameters, and to assess progress toward meeting Project goals.  NASA 
does not have the requisite in-house subject matter expertise in commercial aircraft 
production systems to effectively contribute to work activities defining the Technology 
Assessment Process, or to provide related insights and recommendations to the HiCAM 
Project Leadership Team regarding these topics. 
 
2. Characteristics, Scope, and Specs 
The contractor shall perform the following duties: 
 
 The Contractor shall provide an employee with the following skillsets and 
experience: 
o Knowledge of composite aircraft wing and fuselage structures and the specific 
high-rate manufacturing and assembly processes being developed within the 
NASA HiCAM Project. 
o Subject matter expertise and demonstrated experience performing composite 
manufacturing trade studies for commercial wing box and fuselage 
assemblies. This includes developing manufacturing models that define the 
people, processes, tooling, equipment, Takt time, and materials required to 
meet a specified production rate. 
o Demonstrated experience running Simulia discrete event simulations that 
estimate the required factory work area and recurring and non-recurring costs. 
 
 The Contractor shall: 
o Provide recurring briefings to the HiCAM Project Leadership Team that 
include, but are not limited to, assessments of technical progress, evidence of 
milestone completion and accomplishments, and updates on technology 
assessments performed by the HiCAM Technology Assessment Process 
(TAP) and manufacturing technology Cooperative Research Teams (CRTs).  
o Review and update HiCAM Activity-Level Models (ALMs) and discrete 
event simulations to generate updated Key Performance Parameters (KPPs). 
o Generate and recommend to the HiCAM Project Leadership Team innovative 
technical approaches to assess and/or improve production system 
performance.  
o Collaborate with HiCAM TAP CRT members to define and execute project 
work plan (PWP) tasks, and contribute to deliverables, milestones, risks, 
objectives, and schedule updates. 
o Actively collaborate with Members of Manufacturing Technology CRTs to 
provide written KPP and TRL/MRL assessment guidance consistent with 
HiCAM guidelines. 
o Review and update HiCAM wing and fuselage assembly baseline models 
consistent with HiCAM assessment processes and structural sizing guidelines.   
o Review and update system-level technology assessments performed by others 
to ensure consistency across the HiCAM manufacturing technologies. 
o Incorporate manufacturing process improvements from one manufacturing 
model to all other HiCAM manufacturing models as applicable (e.g., 

thermoplastic CRT process improvements applicable to resin infused and next 
generation thermoset models). 
o Develop and update hybrid production systems (components fabricated with 
more than one manufacturing approach) for the HiCAM wing and fuselage 
vision systems. 
o Perform SPACE RT Validation Testing of four (4) remote terminals in the 
Main Engine Controller at the John Doe facility in Canoga Park, CA, starting 
November 30, 2017.   
o Perform test to the " RT Validation Test Plan," Appendix A to SPACE using 
the Test Systems RT Validation Test Procedure dated June 1, 1985. 
o Provide test connector capability using Planet 1 type connectors. 
o Validate that the SPACE hardware meets the design requirements for rocket 
communication.   
o Perform electrical, noise rejection and protocol testing as called out in the 
SPACE design. 
 
 
3. Place of Performance 
Remote 
 
4. Period of Performance 
The period of performance of this contract is 12 months from the award date. 
 
5. Government Furnished Equipment and/or Information 
Laptop and software to perform PWS requirements. 
 
6. Travel 
The period of performance of this contract is 12 months from the award date. 
 Attend the annual HiCAM Spring and Fall Reviews in-person at NASA Langley 
Research Center. 
 Plan for one trip, 5-day duration, per WYE providing support, to attend a face-to-face 
technical exchange at an ACC Member’s facility. Assumed location of the face-to-
face is Seattle, WA.

MARKET SURVEY CAPABILITY ASSESSMENT FOR THE OFFICE OF

SECURITY AND HAZARDOUS MATERIALS SAFETY (ASH)

This is a market survey for a Tactical Intelligence Platform for International Travel. This is not a screening information request or request for a proposal of any kind. The FAA is not seeking or accepting unsolicited proposals. Vendors will not be notified of the results of this market survey or the results of the information submitted.

The purpose of this market survey is to solicit statements of interest and capabilities from all businesses capable of providing ASH with a Tactical Intelligence Platform for International Travel as described in this market survey.

The Office of Investigations & Professional Responsibility (AXI-1) International Travel Security Program (ITSP)’s mission is to protect the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) and the National Airspace System by preparing FAA employees who travel internationally with timely and pertinent information concerning the dangers and risks they may encounter while abroad, and countermeasures to protect themselves from becoming victims of terrorism and crime or targets of foreign intelligence entities. Furthermore, the ITSP ensures the FAA’s Duty of Care by monitoring safety and security concerns that could impact employees traveling internationally on official FAA business and advises them appropriately before departure and while on travel.

The FAA requires a submittal demonstrating your organization’s strategy, capability, and methodology of performance by responding to the inquiries below and completing them as they would relate to the FAA. Your response must not exceed a maximum of ten (10) pages. Use font size Times New Roman 11.    

Respondents must address all information requested in this Market Survey – Identified as items 1, 2, and 3 below - as these shall be considered Baseline Requirements. 

Response Requirements:

1. Cover Sheet: Complete the Cover Sheet and attach it to your submission (below).

2. Capability Questions and Statements: Answer every question thoroughly.

Does your company have experience providing current location-based intelligence reports and risk ratings (e.g., security, political, environment, health, etc.)? What location-based intelligence reports, trend reporting, and risk ratings does your company’s platform provide?

Does your company’s product track the location of international travelers, and does it provide real-time location-based alerts and risk analysis?

Does your company’s product offer the ability to run metrics reports (e.g., people at locations, alerts affecting locations where people are located, people affected and emailed by alerts, mobile app usage, days in country, communications sent by the platform, etc.)?

What experience does the company have in operating a 24/7 emergency hotline, and what is the process for assisting callers or addressing critical alerts?  

Does your company’s platform have a hierarchy of end users with the ability to restrict account creation, and what is the turnaround time for help tickets?

3. Documented Experience: Provide at least one example of past performance of a comparable size and scope (i.e. 10,000-12,000 trips annually, 1 administrator license, 5 user licenses, 3,000-4,000 international travelers). This example must be current within three (3) years. The Offeror must describe how the services they offered were similar in nature to servicing an organization like the FAA and provide a detailed explanation regarding their approach to the delivery of services and what obstacles, if any, they faced. 

Information applicable to all respondents:

Respondents must identify a representative to support further FAA inquiries and requests to clarify the information provided.

The principal North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this effort is 541990, “All Other Professional, Scientific and Technical Services”, size standard - $19.5M, or 513210, “Software Publishers”, size standard - $19.5M.

Any comment(s) the respondent wishes to provide shall be marked with the word “COMMENTS” and fully segregated from the requirements responses listed above. It is important to note that the government is not obligated to consider any comments received.

At this time, the nature of the competition has not been determined. The responses to this Market Survey will help determine the procurement strategy. The FAA may decide to do an unrestricted competition, a single source or a tiered competition or to set aside all or part of the procurement for certified small businesses or Small Disadvantaged Business (SDB), Socially Economically Disadvantage Business (SEDB) (8a), Small Disadvantage Veteran Owned Small Business (SDVOSB), Historically Underutilized Business Zone (HUBZone), Women Owned Small Business (WOSB), or Economically Disadvantage Women Owned Small Business (EDWOSB), or a Large Business. 

Only respondents to this market survey will receive the resultant Screening Information Request (SIR) if issued.

All responses to this market survey must be received by 5:00pm EST on May 15, 2026.  

All responses should be submitted via email to:

Stephania Ivory, FAA Contracting Officer – stephania.l.ivory@faa.gov

The FAA is not seeking or accepting unsolicited proposals. The FAA will not pay for any information received or costs incurred in preparing the response to this market survey. Therefore, any cost associated with the market survey submission is solely at the interested vendor’s expense.

Respondents seeking to protect intellectual property and/or confidential/proprietary information submitted in response to this announcement must clearly mark such intellectual property and or confidential and proprietary information. If such information is not so marked, the FAA will not accept liability for failure to safeguard it against open disclosure and may release the information at its sole discretion. 

If a Respondent wishes to restrict the response information, the Respondent must mark each sheet with the following legend:

“This data must not be disclosed outside the FAA and must not be duplicated, used, or disclosed in whole or in part for any purpose other than to assess the response. This restriction does not limit the FAA’s right to use information contained in the response if obtained from another source without restriction.”

U.S. GEOLOGICAL SURVEY 
PACIFIC COASTAL & MARINE SCIENCE CENTER 
STATEMENT OF WORK 
I. GENERAL INFORMATION
A. Introduction
The Coastal and Marine Geohazards of the U.S. West Coast and Alaska project at the
U.S. Geological Survey (USGS), Pacific Coastal & Marine Science Center (PCMSC)
in Santa Cruz, CA has a need for radiocarbon subsampling and geotechnical
measurements to be conducted on sediment cores that have been collected by USGS
researchers and are stored at the USGS PCMSC Sediment Core facility.
B. B
ackground
The USGS Coastal and Marine Geohazards of the U.S. West Coast and Alaska project
is engaged in ongoing research into the earthquake, tsunami and landslide hazards in
the coastal and marine environments of California, Oregon, Washington and Alaska.
As such, USGS researchers have collected hundreds of marine and lacustrine sediment
cores from these locations to develop stratigraphic records of earthquake triggered
sediment gravity flows, landslides or other event deposits that record the geologic
history of the region. The goal of these sediment archives is to develop a record of
earthquake recurrence and landslide susceptibility that will allow us to assess the
potential hazards to coastal populations and local infrastructure. Analysis of these
sediment cores requires precise radiocarbon dating of intervals above and below the
event deposit to develop detailed age models of geologic events. Geotechnical analyses
of sediment properties is required to characterize the physical properties of the seafloor
as a measure of susceptibility to slope failure.
C. D
efinitions
A “sediment core” or “core” as used in this work statement refers to the group of one
or more core segments collected from a single site. Therefore, the length of a single
core can vary greatly. A “subsample” refers to a unit of sediment extracted from a
particular depth interval in a sediment core.
D.
Scope
Services will include subsampling sediment cores, sieving samples, selecting material
for radiocarbon dating, identifying and logging dominant species or plant types,
preparing samples for submission to AMS facilities for radiocarbon analyses, making
measurements of sediment strength properties, assisting with sediment core splitting
and archival curation, and keeping detailed sampling and measurement notes.
II. WORK REQUIREMENTS
A. Technical Requirements.
1. W
ork requirements/products
• Analysis of marine and lacustrine sediment cores not to exceed a quantity of 400
samples collected by USGS researchers from sites onshore and offshore of
California, Oregon, Washington and Alaska. The vendor shall select appropriate
USGS, RFQ 140G0326Q0098 Sediment Core Subsampling, Processing, & Preparation
Page 4 of 35

material for radiocarbon analysis, (e.g. calcareous foraminifera from marine 
sediments; plant material from lacustrine sediments) from sediment cores 
subsample within intervals defined by USGS researchers.  The selected detrital 
material must be in good condition with no signs of reworking, entrainment, or 
long-distance sediment transport. Material should be appropriately cleaned and 
prepared for radiocarbon analyses. An attempt should be made to select sufficient 
material from each subsampled interval to provide enough carbon for Accelerator 
Mass Spectrometer (AMS) radiocarbon dating. To provide quality assurance, the 
vendor shall consult with the USGS technical liaison for material screening prior to 
preparing the samples for radiocarbon analyses. The USGS will determine the 
appropriate amount of material required for each sample as this varies among 
different projects and sample types. 
• Vendor shall provide shear strength measurements of up to 10 marine sediment 
cores and 10 lacustrine sediment cores conducted using both a handheld shear vane 
and benchtop fall cone penetrometer. Measurements of each instrument type should 
be conducted at 2cm intervals on pre-identified sediment cores unless otherwise 
requested by USGS personnel. 
• Vendor shall assist with core curation tasks including sectioning and splitting of 
unsplit sediment core samples and preparing core sections for storage and archival, 
(e.g., wrapping, labeling, packaging and placing in cold storage). 
• The vendor shall prepare and submit samples to an AMS dating facility designated 
by the USGS technical liaison with USGS personnel approval. Sample submission 
should be done monthly in batches of ~10 or more samples.  
 
2. Criteria for acceptance  
• The vendor shall confer with the USGS technical liaison in bi-monthly meetings to 
ensure dating material quality prior to preparing for radiocarbon analyses. 
• The vendor is expected to analyze up to 400 subsamples for radiocarbon dating 
over the period of performance (i.e. approximately 12-16 samples per month). 
• At least 80% of the subsamples analyzed should be able to yield viable radiocarbon 
results. To meet these criteria, some intervals may be combined with approval from 
USGS personnel. 
• Shear strength measurements should be completed on a minimum of 12 cores as 
outlined above. 
• All work will comply with guidelines outlined by the USGS Quality Management 
System (QMS) Instructional Memorandum and supporting manual, linked here: 
https://www.usgs.gov/office-of-science-quality-and-integrity/quality-management-
system-usgs-laboratories.  
• The vendor shall complete standardized QA/QC forms for QMS provided by the 
USGS technical liaison. 
 
B. Deliverables.  
 
• The vendor shall complete sample analyses within 60 days of receiving samples 
from the USGS.  
• For radiocarbon samples, the vendor shall provide a report to include a digital 
spreadsheet (MS Excel/.xlsx format) tracking subsampled intervals with sample 
identification numbers, sampling dates, sample thickness, floral and/or faunal 
assemblages and subsample weights and data report (MS Word document/.docx) 
USGS, RFQ 140G0326Q0098 Sediment Core Subsampling, Processing, & Preparation
Page 5 of 35

describing the number and type of samples processed, date of sample submission 
for radiocarbon dating (or reason sample was unable to be dated) and photographs 
of cleaned material from each subsample prepared for radiocarbon analyses. 
• For shear strength measurements, the vendor shall provide a digital spreadsheet 
(MS Excel/.xlsx) of all measurements collected.  
 
Delivery dates: The full scope of work is expected to be completed by September 30, 
2027. Quarterly progress updates will be provided to the USGS technical liaison. 
 
III. SUPPORTING INFORMATION 
 
A. Place of Performance. 
The sediment cores to be analyzed are stored in the refrigerated space at the USGS 
PCMSC in Santa Cruz, CA. In order to minimize disturbance to the cores, the 
contractor may use USGS facilities and equipment to perform non-personal services 
that are described above. The contractor must coordinate with core lab managers on a 
monthly basis to schedule lab access. 
 
C. Period of Performance  
Date of Award to September 30, 2027 
 
D. Government Furnished Property (GFP):  
 A government furnished laptop computer will be provided to allow for access to 
shared documents on OneDrive 
 
D. Special Considerations. 
 
1. Key personnel qualifications  
The contractor must have documented experience working with marine and lacustrine 
sediment cores, particularly experience with sieving samples and using a microscope to 
pick calcareous microfossils and organic material for radiocarbon dating. The 
contractor also must have knowledge of common foraminiferal species and detrital 
plant assemblages commonly found in coastal and marine regions of California, 
Oregon, Washington and Alaska. Experience should include working with both a 
benchtop fall cone penetrometer and a handheld shear vane.  
 
2.   Data Rights, Safety, Environment. 
All data produced will be the property of the USGS. Personal protective equipment 
(PPE; e.g., hearing protection, safety glasses, gloves, etc.) will be provided as needed. 
 
3. Security/Privacy issues  
Work may be performed at the USGS Pacific Coastal and Marine Science Center. The 
contractor is responsible for all costs of transportation to and from the USGS. A door 
entry access fob will be provided upon completion of a background check. 
Additionally, the contractor will need to complete basic IT security clearance to be

Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services

Supplemental Medical Review Contractor (SMRC) Statement of Work

Revised:

March 18, 2025

SCOPE

The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) is seeking a Supplemental Medical Review Contractor (SMRC) to perform medical reviews (MR) and medical review related activities in support of three initiatives within the Center for Program Integrity (CPI) to include the following:

The Provider Compliance Group (PCG) ‘Specialty Reviews’ for issues identified by Federal agencies, such as the Office of Inspector General (OIG), Government Accountability Office (GAO)1, and other CMS groups. In addition to support CMS’ internal data analysis programs to include the Comprehensive Error Rate Testing (CERT)2 program; the First-look Analysis Tool for Hospital Outlier Monitoring (FATHOM),3 and the Program for Evaluating Payment Patterns Electronic Reports (PEPPER)4 reports (Task 1);

Program Integrity Reviews (Task 2).

The work shall be performed as outlined in this Task Order Statement of Work (SOW), awarded under the Unified Program Integrity Contract (UPIC) Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract vehicle, in accordance with Sections 5.6; 5.8.1; and Section 8 of the UPIC Umbrella SOW (USOW).

PURPOSE

The purpose of the SMRC known as the “Contractor” for this SOW is to perform and/or provide support for a variety of tasks aimed at lowering the improper payment rates and increasing efficiencies of the MR functions primarily for Medicare Fee-for-Service (FFS); other product line analysis are limited and may include Medicaid FFS, private and group health insurance lines of business and Prescription Drug Plan (Part D). One of the primary tasks will be conducting large volumes of nationwide MR as directed by CMS. The MR will be performed on Medicare FFS claims for Part A, Part B, and durable medical equipment, prosthetics, orthotics and supplies (DMEPOS) programs. The Contractor is expected to perform MR on a large volume of claims. For example, some projects may require MR for up to 300,000 claims per project/task assignment. These medical review activities will assess compliance with Medicare’s coding, coverage, billing, and payment requirements and

1 For more information, see http://www.oig.hhs.gov/and http://www.gao.gov/.

2 The CERT program evaluates a statistically valid random sample of claims to determine if they were paid properly under Medicare coverage, coding, and billing rules.

3 FATHOM is a Microsoft Access application that allows CMS to provide each State with hospital-specific Medicare claims data statistics, which identify areas having high payment errors.

4 PEPPER is a comparative data report that provides hospital-specific Medicare data statistics for discharges vulnerable to improper payments.

identify claims improperly paid. The Contractor will recommend recoupment and/or adjustment for claims identified as improperly paid. Having a centralized MR resource that can perform large volume of MR nationally shall allow for a timely and consistent execution of MR review, activities, and decisions. The Contractor shall conduct the reviews and submit completed reports to CMS as described in this Statement of Work (SOW). The Contractor shall select subject claims, perform research and/or data analysis, and conduct reviews in a manner that will minimize provider and supplier burden. The Contractor must have in place adequate facilities, personnel, and equipment to perform medical reviews.

BACKGROUND

The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) is the Federal agency that administers the Medicare and Medicaid programs. A top priority for CMS is reducing improper payments in the Medicare Fee-for-Service (FFS) program. To protect the Medicare Trust Fund, CMS must prevent improper payments that result in a loss of taxpayer dollars. Preventing improper payments requires the active involvement of multiple components in CMS and effective coordination with its partners, including various Medicare Contractors and providers/suppliers. CMS evaluates medical records and related documents to determine whether Medicare claims were billed in compliance with statutory, regulatory and sub- regulatory coverage, coding, payment, and billing rules. Paid claims that do not comply with Medicare’s coverage, coding, payment and billing rules are considered improper payments. Analyses of Medicare Parts A/B/DMEPOS claims data is one way to identify that Medicare may have paid claims improperly. Providers and suppliers may submit claims to various Medicare contractors under multiple provider numbers. In addition, some potential improper payments can only be identified when a provider’s Medicare claims data is compared to what that provider billed to a Medicaid agency or other public or private payer. These improperly paid claims could result in significant losses to the Medicare Trust Fund.

The Contractor claim reviews require, at a minimum, the clinical evaluation of medical records and related documents to determine whether Medicare claims were billed and paid in compliance with Medicare’s coding, coverage, billing and payment requirements. Statutory authority for the MR programs is found in Sections 1833(e) and 1862(a) of the Social Security Act (the Act).

GENERAL REQUIREMENTS

The Contractor shall perform in accordance with applicable laws, regulations, Medicare manuals, and CMS requirements to ensure the financial integrity of the Medicare program. The Medicare program’s legal, policy, and operating environment is complex, and the Contractor shall utilize or interact with certain CMS guidelines, systems, equipment, and operational capabilities in the performance of its functions.

COLLABORATION WITH OTHER INTERNAL AND EXTERNAL ENTITIES

CMS depends on a close and coordinated working relationship between its internal components and external organizations. The Contractor shall work with and coordinate with, as necessary, external entities including, but not limited to, the following:

State Agencies

Investigative agencies (such as, but not limited to, OIG, GAO, Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), Department of Justice (DOJ), and CMS Regional Offices

Healthcare Fraud Prevention Partnership (HFPP) Trusted Third Party Contractor (TTP)

Program Integrity Contractors (UPIC/ National Benefit Integrity Medicare Drug Integrity Contract (NBI MEDIC))

Professional Organizations

Infrastructure Service providers, other CMS Contractors, including but not limited to the Medicare Administrative Contractors (MAC). The SMRC specifically will collaborate with the MAC for activities such as completion and maintenance of a Joint Operating Agreement (JOA) and/or Service Level Agreement (SLA).

Medical Review Accuracy Contractor (MRAC)

INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY (IT) AND SECURITY REQUIREMENTS

CMS requires that its business partners implement IT systems security controls in order to maintain the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of Medicare system operations in the event of computer incidents or physical disasters. The Contractor shall comply with the security requirements defined in the Business Partner System Security Manual (BPSSM), the CMS Information Security (IS) Acceptable Risk Safeguards (ARS), including CMS Minimum Security Requirements (CMSRs) (also known as IOM Pub. 100-25), and the Program Integrity Manual (IOM Pub. 100-8) all found at http://www.cms.gov/Regulationsand-Guidance/Guidance/Manuals/Internet-Only-Manuals- IOMs.html.

The Contractor’s information system/applications shall have a valid Authority to Operate (ATO) (conveyed through the CMS Chief Information Officer authorization decision process) before going into operation and processing CMS information. The implementation of a Federal Government information system requires a formal Government ATO for infrastructure systems and/or all application systems developed, hosted and/or maintained on behalf of CMS. NIST Special Publication (SP) 800-37, Guide for Applying the Risk Management Framework to Federal Information Systems: A Security Life Cycle Approach, and CMS procedures (located on the CMS Information Security website at http://www.cms.gov/Research-Statistics-Data-and-Systems/CMS- InformationTechnology/InformationSecurity) give guidelines for performing the system ATO process. The Contractor shall begin the process to obtain an ATO within 60 days of

contract award.

Additionally, the Contractor shall incorporate and utilize the following information technology requirements:

The Contractor staff shall be trained on security procedures as well as relevant aspects of the Privacy Act, Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA), and the Freedom of Information Act. The Contractor shall adhere to the 508 Accessibility clause (HHSAR 352.239-73).

The Contractor shall record completion of Information Security Awareness and RoleBased Security Training and retain the results in accordance with CMS procedures available at http://www.cms.gov/InformationSecurity. Training shall be consistent with the requirements contained in C.F.R. Part 5 Subpart C (5 C.F.R. 930.301) and conducted at least annually.

The Contractor shall have in place a request management and prioritization system. This system shall allow for workflow management, prioritization of activities, identity management, user provisioning requests and activity reports. This system shall ensure that MR projects are appropriately triaged and managed in a timely manner.

The Contractor shall protect all CMS information from unauthorized access, use, disclosure, duplication, modification, diversion, or destruction, whether accidental or intentional, in order to maintain the security, confidentiality, integrity, and availability of such information. The Contractor shall become and remain compliant with the requirements set forth at the CMS Information Security website at https://www.cms.gov/Research-Statistics-Data-and-Systems/CMS- InformationTechnology/InformationSecurity/Info-Security-Library-Items/CMS- InformationSecurity-Contract-Clause-Provision.html

The Contractor shall meet all FISMA/FedRAMP compliance requirements set forth at the CMS Information Security website at https://www.cms.gov/Research-Statistics-Dataand- Systems/CMS-Information-Technology/InformationSecurity/Info-Security- LibraryItems/CMS-Information-Security-Contract-Clause-Provision.html )

The Contractor shall access the IOM Pub.100-08 and Business Partners Systems Security Manual (BPSSM) at http://cms.hhs.gov/manuals/downloads/117_systems_security.pdf for guidance on both physical and operational security. Physical and operational security is essential for all CMS contracts.

The Contractor shall comply with FAR 52.239-1 Privacy and Security Safeguards, HHSAR 352.239-72 Security Requirements for Federal Information Technology Resources, and HHSAR 352.239-71 Standard for Encryption Language.

CMS’ Core Security Requirements, as defined in the CMS BPSSM, including security standards adopted under the Health Insurance Reform regulations published pursuant to the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) (FR Volume 68, Number 34 of February 20, 2003), are applicable to this contract and to all subcontracts (see https://cms.hhs.gov/manuals/downloads/117_systems_security.pdf for BPSSM).

The Contractor shall check the following web site frequently for updates to the manuals and tools: https://www.cms.gov/Research-Statistics-Data-and-Systems/CMSInformation- Technology/InformationSecurity/Information-Security-Library This page contains links to all of the security references needed for this SOW.

The Contractor shall allow CMS to observe SMRC-conducted audits, reviews, evaluations, tests and assessments of the SMRC’s security program and facilities upon request. The results of any SMRC-conducted annual audits, reviews, evaluations, tests and assessments shall be made available to the Government for review.

The Contractor shall utilize Electronic Submission of Medical Documentation (esMD) or applicable system for claims, prior authorization / pre-claim request review (esMD or other electronic medical system approved by CMS). The esMD system is operational at one of CMS Virtual Data Center (VDC) and allows providers and/or their represented agents known as Health Information Handlers (HIHs) to electronically submit medical documentation via a secure means to medical review Contractors. The esMD system is being reviewed to allow medical review Contractors to send claim review documents and data to providers via secure means. Any future updates to the system will be communicated to the Contractor by CMS.

The Contractor will provide all program management support functions, to include the participation of the medical director on the contract with the esMD recommendation and evaluation workgroup (esMD workgroup participation as required) to support the medical review conducted by the Contractor. In the initial implementation of the system, user requests will be made through a Contractor-furnished interface and a completed report of each medical review project/task will be passed directly back to CMS.

CMS has specific requirements when interfacing with other entities. Example entities that may interface with the Contractor include but are not limited to Medicare Administrative Contractors (MACs), Unified Program

Integrity Contractor (UPIC), National Benefit Integrity Medicare Drug Integrity Contract (NBI MEDIC), the HFPP Trusted Third Party (TTP) and analytics contractors, Medical Review Accuracy Contractor (MRAC), and the other related entities as directed by CMS.

The SMRC and entities interfacing with the SMRC shall develop a Joint Operating Agreements (JOA) or Service-Level Agreements (SLA). These agreements ensure that all parties understand their respective roles and responsibilities. The Contractors shall execute, update, and perform associated duties in accordance with a JOA and/or SLA. A JOA and/or SLA defines

mutually agreed upon and cost-effective methods of CMS contractors working together. Examples of activities that the JOA and/or SLA may cover are: adjustment of SMRC claims review, handling and reporting identified as well as collected underpayments and overpayments, reopenings, appeals of SMRC adjusted claims, reporting for SMRC support operations, and other SMRC support activities.

A JOA and/or SLA describes the work that needs to be accomplished, and the roles and responsibilities of each signatory to the success of the task or project. It includes specifics about who will do what, when, and for whom. The JOA and/or SLA also spells out the process the parties will follow if either believes that the other is not following the agreement, including any alternative dispute resolution procedures.

Each JOA and/or SLA should include, but not be limited to, the following topics:

Confidentiality

Definitions

Workload

Intent to Award Language: 
The USGS is seeking the procurement of the operation of NADP/NTN wet atmospheric 
monitoring station designated site NY01. Contractor is to operate a field located precipitation 
collection station, on a weekly basis, as part of the USGS National Trends Network (NTN).  
Period of Performance will be for a 12-month base period, plus four (4) 12-month option periods. 
The entire NADP network contracts with the Wisconsin State Laboratory of Hygiene (WSLH), 
and site operators deal directly with key personnel at WSLH regarding site specifications and 
maintenance, their performance, site operations, checking of data contained in the Reports Form, 
arranging for provision of needed replacement parts and when necessary, guidance and training. 
As appropriate, a WSLH employee or the site operator can contact the USGS directly for 
assistance or guidance. 
The USGS is aware of no other source that can provide the above. Therefore, it intends to make 
an award to Alfred University, unless it is contacted by any who believes they can provide the 
same service. Vendors are invited to contact the Contracting Officer, Brian Baker via email at 
brian_baker@ios.doi.gov no later than 12:00PM EST, Wednesday, April 29, 2026, with an 
affirmative answer. 
 
 
Sole Source Justification States the Following Part: 
The USGS, Water Mission Area, Observing Systems Division, Hydrologic Networks Branch 
requests award of a Firm-Fixed-Price sole source purchase order to Alfred University (Alfred). 
The anticipated period of performance is one year from date of award with four one-year option 
periods thereafter. 
 
The acquisition is to provide atmospheric deposition station operation services for a cooperatively 
supported station between the USGS, the site owner, and operator in support of the interagency 
National Atmospheric Deposition Program, National Trends Network (NADP-NTN). Operation of a 
NADP/NTN wet atmospheric monitoring station. Operation requires weekly site visits to the 
site to collect, process, and ship the precipitation sample, collect, process and transmit 
associated data with the site including the precipitation gage record and perform routine 
instrument checks, maintenance and repairs as needed. 
 
The Chemistry Department of Alfred University is the only source reasonably available to 
complete the requirement due to current involvement in the NADP/NTN Program and in 
atmospheric deposition and air quality monitoring and research. The analytical laboratory is 
located in a University building, the field and analytical equipment is owned by the 
University and is not open to the public for use by other contractors.

2. GENERAL INFORMATION 
 
2.1. Background: 
The DOI is the cabinet-level federal agency responsible for the stewardship and 
sustainable management of the nation’s public lands, natural resources, and cultural 
heritage. Through its bureaus—including the Bureau of Land Management (BLM), 
National Park Service (NPS), U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (USFWS), Bureau of 
Reclamation (BOR), and Bureau of Indian Affairs (BIA)—DOI manages over 500 
million acres of public lands and associated resources, supporting conservation, 
recreation, energy and mineral development, water projects, and tribal programs. 
 
To fulfill its mission, DOI relies on valuation services to provide independent, credible, 
and legally defensible valuations of federal lands, property rights, and natural resources. 
In general DOI valuation service needs include appraisals, feasibility studies, market 
studies, alternative valuation method work products, and data sourcing. The vast 
majority of valuation services are for appraisals, which are essential for: fee and less 
than fee land acquisitions, procurement of leased space, out leasing of Government 
property, issuance of right-of-way permits or other partial interests, disposals, and land 
exchanges.  Valuation services are for resources such as but not limited to; undeveloped, 
recreational and agricultural land, residential, commercial, industrial, special use 
properties, timber, minerals, and water rights; and calculation of damages or restitution 
in cases of trespass or unauthorized use.  
 
Through these services, DOI ensures fair compensation, responsible fiscal stewardship, 
and informed decision-making in the management of public lands and resources. By 
integrating technical appraisal expertise with federal policy and program objectives, DOI 
can effectively balance resource development, environmental protection, and public 
benefit. 
 
2.2. Purpose & Objective: 
Purpose 
The purpose of this effort is to acquire integrator program management and valuation support 
services through qualified industry partners to assist the DOI in delivering consistent, defensible, 
and timely valuation products. The integrator , henceforth referred to as contractor, will 
coordinate with industry experts, DOI program offices, and other stakeholders to ensure a 
centralized, streamlined, and efficient approach to the valuation activities required across the 
Department. 
The contractor is expected to subcontract most valuation services to qualified local valuation 
companies. 
Objective
 
The objective is to provide DOI with accurate, timely, and actionable valuation information that 
supports informed decision making for land and asset-related activities. Contractors shall deliver 
independent, professional valuation services that comply with all federal laws, regulations, 
policies, and applicable appraisal standards, including the Uniform Standards of Professional 

Page 4 of 38 
 
Appraisal Practice (USPAP) and the Uniform Appraisal Standards for Federal Land 
Acquisitions (UASFLA, Yellow Book). The integrator s will support the Government by 
coordinating program activities, coordinating workflow, ensuring quality assurance, and 
maintaining consistency in valuation processes across designated geographic regions. 
The contractor is also required to design, develop, and continuously maintain a functional live 
dashboard throughout the period of performance. 
Contract Awards  
Up to three Firm Fixed Price per unit a nd T&M contracts may be awarded, one for each 
geographic region (East, Central, West). A single award may be issued if one contractor is 
determined capable of fulfilling all regional requirements. 
 
 
2.3. Scope: 
This scope of this requirement includes the coordination by the contractor(s) of all 
requirements associated with federal appraisal and appraisal related service delivery. 
Valuation services include but are not limited to appraisals; feasibility studies; market 
studies; data sourcing; and consultation services (e.g., comparable sales/rental data, 
reviews of landowner’s appraisal, landowner conferences, and field review assistance), 
and the procurement of other real estate appraisal related services etc.

Statement of Work 

 Voicebrook VoiceOver PRO 

 VA Long Beach Health Care System 

Background: 

The VA Long Beach Health Care System Laboratory Anatomic Department, is seeking to procure speech recognition software that will allow pathology staff to dictate reports using speech recognition and templating features. The Voicebrook VoiceOver PRO Speech Recognition System is designed to be integrated with the VistA anatomic pathology information system. The Anatomic Pathology department at the VA Long Beach Health Care System currently has 8 Pathologists and 3 out of 16 Residents a month who are responsible for dictating gross and microscopic descriptions into a dictation system. Voicebrook VoiceOver PRO will allow for pathology staff to dictate on multiple workstations using speech recognition. 

In addition, it will provide the department with the ability to improve turnaround times of reports, reduce mistakes, and improve patient safety by implementing speech recognition-based reporting system. With this speech recognition system, users can navigate VistA using voice commands with custom Macros. VoiceOver PRO will also allow for hands-free command and control of VistA in the cutting room and at the microscope. Current workflow and other VistA processes will be unchanged with the use of Voicebrook. Voicebrook will work with each user, to ensure each attains maximum value from VoiceOver PRO in conjunction with Vista. 

Period of Performance

Base Year:          06/19/2026-6/18/2026

Option Year 1:  06/19/2027-6/18/2028

Option Year 2:  06/19/2028-6/18/2029

Option Year 3:  06/19/2029-6/18/2030

Option Year 4:  06/19/2030-6/18/2031

Scope of Service: 

The contractor, Voicebrook, shall provide supplies, accessories, equipment, initial training, and other resources required to deliver the requirements stated herein. Voicebrook will handle and segment the project implementation into five stages. These five stages will include Analysis and Planning, Workflow Integration and Customization, Preparation for Productive use, Go-Live, and Transition to support. During the workflow integration and customization phase, Voicebrook will integrate their software with the facilities underlying systems and hardware. This will require access to the test system and a network computer that is connected to VistA. This phase is required to successfully document the reporting process workflow and map out associated voice commands and integration points. 

Statement of Work for Voicebrook VoiceOver PRO at VA Long Beach Health Care System 

Voicebrook will: 

• Adhere to all of the security and privacy clauses listed in this statement of work 

• Provide the VA Long Beach Health Care System the necessary software for installation on their VA network. 

• Build the new workflow to match the VA Long Beach Health Care System pathology department’s reporting goals 

• Test the new pathology department’s workflow 

• Have access to a VA owned computer with the VistA test account only. Patient information is scrambled within the VistA test account. 

• Present the new workflow to the client team leaders for approval before training and Go- Live 

• Aid staff in developing non-eCC template content 

• Gather existing templates from users and transcriptionists. These templates will be converted into VoiceOver PRO templates 

• Provide sample set of templates which may be reviewed and modified to the department’s standards, except as may otherwise be specified in this statement of work. 

VA Long Beach Health Care System will: 

• Provide Voicebrook with access to equipment and only appropriate network rights to install their software. 

• Allow a credentialed Voicebrook resource access to the VA network and VistA test account via Voicebrook’s owned computer device for testing and implementation purposes. 

• Provide a network file share where VA Long Beach Health Care System users may store and access their speech profiles 

• Provide Voicebrook with access to the central file share for support purposes only 

• Provide dictation workstation with the following requirements: 

The following links provide access to the latest technical specifications associated to the proposed solution. 

VoiceOver PRO Desktop Requirements 

VoiceOver PRO Desktop Requirements 

VoiceOver PRO Server Requirements (DMNE) 

VoiceOver PRO Server Requirements - DMNE 

During the preparation for production use, all software and hardware is installed and tested on site production machines. During the Go-Live stage training will be provided in the user environment while working on live cases in a production environment.
