Page 4 of 14 
 
enabling Veterans and family members to submit nominations directly 
through the interface. 
8. Ask configurable questions related to a Veteran’s experience with 
specific staff members and provide individualized Veteran experience 
insights to employees and leadership. 
9. Enable real-time notifications to staff and leaders when recognition is 
received.  
10. Provide resources to support awareness and adoption of the 
healthcare patient driven recognition program.  
11. Ensure healthcare workers receive meaningful and frequent 
recognition by incorporating the voice of leaders, peers, Veterans, and 
their families. 
12. Reinforce Integrity, Commitment, Advocacy, Respect, and Excellence 
(ICARE) values by incentivizing and promoting mission-aligned 
behaviors across staff. 
13. Provide Veteran-to-staff, peer-to-peer, leader-to-staff, and leader-to-
team recognition capabilities. 
14. Enhance employee engagement by highlighting the impact of staff 
contributions through Healthcare patient driven recognition.  
15. Support employee celebrations including service anniversaries, new 
hires, milestones, and other culture-building events. 
16. Provide an internal social engagement environment that allows patient-
driven stories, positive experiences, and communication to be shared 
between individuals, teams, groups, departments, and across the 
organization.  
17. Enable leadership to communicate organizational priorities through 
digital communication tools within the platform. 
18. Provide opportunities to highlight positive care experiences across 
departments and service lines. 
19. Provide interactive challenges that promote teamwork, patient 
experience, quality, safety, and positive workplace behaviors. 
20. Provide platform user interface design with branding customization and 
data insights to drive organization improvements 
21. Provide real-time reporting and analytics to identify trends related to 
Veteran experience, staff engagement, and recognition activity. 
22. Deliver platform insights directly to leaders to surface areas of strength 
and share opportunities on how to make the biggest impact on your 
team  
23. Support data access and reporting capabilities to inform leadership 
decision making. 
24. Provide Software-as-a-Service based interactive software hosted in a 
secure cloud environment. 
25. Support access across Android and iOS devices. 
26. Include a companion mobile application. 
27. Provide Single Sign-On integration with existing authentication and HR 
systems.

28. Support at least 6,648 users and provide technical support. 
29. Provide ongoing technical support and system administration 
assistance. 
30. The Contractor shall implement an Information Security Management 
System (ISMS), that adheres to ISO27001 and HIPAA. 
31. The Contractor shall be SOC 2 Type II certified. 
32. Maintain an information security policy that complies with applicable 
regulatory and business requirements. This policy must protect all 
sensitive and confidential data stored, accessed, or transmitted by the 
software platform, including applications, components, infrastructure, 
and underlying code. 
33. The Contractor shall have a risk assessment program to assess the 
organization’s enterprise-level risk at least annually, or upon significant 
changes to the environment. 
34. Require employees with access to sensitive information to sign

system data 
35. The Contractor shall have a comprehensive security awareness

annual review of core security training; and team-specific training, as 
defined by security team. 
36. Strict control access to restrict private information to privileged users. 
These users are required to abide by their assigned responsibilities 
related to their elevated access. 
37. Data handling, retention, and disposal program to manage information 
in accordance with applicable laws, regulations, policies, and 
standards. This program establishes a formal data retention schedule 
and implements a data classification standard to ensure the 
confidential data is secured. 
38. Retains sensitive and confidential data only for as long as necessary to 
fulfill its purposes unless otherwise required by law or to meet legal 
and client contractual obligations. 
39. Network segmentation to prevent direct or unauthorized connections 
between an external network and its information systems, in particular 
confidential data in cloud environments. 
40. A vulnerability management program to ensure the confidentiality, 
integrity, and availability (CIA) of the organization’s information 
systems landscape, which includes all critical system resources. The 
program includes internal and external scans, penetration testing, and 
issue remediation for the purposes of identifying, detecting, classifying, 
prioritizing, remediating, validating, and continuously monitoring 
vulnerabilities.

Performance Work Statement 
AFLCMC Engineering Directorate (EN-EZ) 
Collateral Conference Room 162 
 
1.0 Background 
The U.S. Government requires a technology upgrade for the conference room located at 
conference room 162 located in Building 28, Area B, WPAFB, OH The purpose is to integrate 
a modern Uniﬁed Communications (UC) capability using Microsoft Teams into a Collateral 
Secret SIPRNET environment. The room contains existing VTC equipment that is outdated 
and scheduled for decommissioning but will remain in place temporarily. The new solution 
must be integrated with certain remaining components while replacing those that are 
incompatible. 
2.0 Scope 
The contractor shall provide and install a complete, turn-key solution to enable MS Teams 
functionality within the designated conference room. The work includes providing and 
installing a new camera, microphone system, and control system processor, and 
integrating these components with the existing displays and control interface. The ﬁnal 
system must be capable of dual operation, allowing users to select either the new MS 
Teams capability or the legacy VTC system until it is decommissioned. The solution must 
be engineered to function independently after the legacy system is removed without 
requiring rework. 
3.0 Speciﬁc Tasks 
The contractor shall: 
• 3.1 Install New Camera System: Provide and install one (1) 4K-capable web camera. 
The camera shall be mounted on the front wall, centered between the two existing 
wall displays. 
• 3.2 Install New Microphone System: Provide and install a microphone solution 
optimized for MS Teams. The preferred solution is a single tabletop device capable 
of capturing audio from all participants in the room. The device must feature a 
readily accessible physical mute/unmute control. Ceiling-mounted microphone 
solutions are not desired. 
• 3.3 Integrate Audio: Conﬁgure the audio output from the new MS Teams system to 
be routed through the two (2) existing 75-inch wall-mounted displays. 

• 3.4 Replace Control System Processor: Replace the outdated, end-of-life Crestron 
rack-mounted controller with a modern processor unit that is capable of supporting 
both the new MS Teams integration and the legacy VTC system. 
• 3.5 Reprogram Control Interface: Reprogram the existing Crestron touch panel to 
provide a single, intuitive user interface. The control panel must allow users to easily 
select and operate one of the following modes: 
• Microsoft Teams Session 
• Legacy GVS VTC System 
• PC-based Presentation (local display) 
• 3.6 System Integration and Dual-Use Functionality: Integrate the new MS Teams 
equipment with the legacy VTC system to allow for seamless switching between the 
two. The technical solution must be designed so that the future removal of the 
legacy VTC hardware does not disable or negatively impact the functionality of the 
newly installed MS Teams solution. 
4.0 Security and Compliance Requirements 
All equipment, software, and conﬁgurations provided under this contract must comply with 
all applicable security requirements for operation on SECRET networks. This includes, but 
is not limited to: 
• 4.1 DISA STIGs: The system and its components must be conﬁgured in compliance 
with all relevant Defense Information Systems Agency (DISA) Security Technical 
Implementation Guides (STIGs). 
• 4.2 IA Accreditation: All hardware and software components must be listed on the

1 
 
United States Transportation Command (USTRANSCOM) 
Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) 
Solicitation Number: HTC71126SCSO1 
 
1. GENERAL INFORMATION 
1.1. Solicitation Request: USTRANSCOM is soliciting Solution Briefs for efforts identified 
as Area(s) of Interest (AoIs) to this CSO. 
1.2. USTRANSCOM Overview: USTRANSCOM is the Department of War's (DoW) 
provider of full-spectrum global mobility solutions and capabilities in both peace and 
war. Partnering with industry and DoW customers, USTRANSCOM develops and 
executes innovative acquisition solutions for the Command's full-spectrum deployment 
and distribution mission.  
1.3. Contract Types: Based on submissions in response to AoIs under this CSO, 
USTRANSCOM may award a Firm-Fixed Price contract in accordance with the Federal 
Acquisition Regulation (FAR). Offerors are encouraged to review FAR 12.205 to 
familiarize themselves with the standard terms and conditions applicable to FAR Part 12 
contracts. In addition, USTRANSCOM reserves the right to award an Other Transaction 
(OT) Agreement for Prototype Project(s) in accordance with 10 U.S.C. 4022. 
1.4. Estimated Program Cost: General AoIs (see Attachment 1) do not have an estimated 
cost. Specific AoIs may designate an estimated cost at the AoI level.   
1.5. Non-Government Advisors: Non-government advisors may be used in evaluations and 
will have signed Non-Disclosure Agreements (NDAs). The Government will protect 
trade secret or commercial or financial information from unauthorized disclosure to the 
maximum extent permitted and as required by law. 
1.6. Authority and Competition: Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Subpart 212.70 
provides Contracting Officers authority to acquire commercial items, technologies, or 
services through CSOs. The CSO framework is recognized as a competitive procedure 
under 10 U.S.C. chapter 221 and FAR 6.102, treating acquired items as commercial with 
streamlined processes and fixed-price requirements. This CSO is issued on a full and 
open competitive basis. AoIs issued under this CSO may specify individual competitive 
environments. 
 
2. PROCEDURES 
2.1. Open Period: This CSO is continuously open until 1 February 2036 and may be 
updated periodically. The Government may extend this period by amendment.  
 

2 
 
2.2. AoIs: This CSO seeks Solution Briefs, Presentations/Pitches, and/or Written Proposals 
for commercial products, technologies, and services for USTRANSCOM's mission. Two 
types of AoIs will be utilized under this CSO: 
 
General AoIs: Includes general submissions against the AoIs stated in Attachment 
1. Submissions are accepted at any time during the open period of this CSO and will 
not have a separate AoI posting. General AoIs do not have dedicated funding. 
Responses will only be provided to submissions in accordance with Section 4. 
 
Specific AoIs: In instances where USTRANSCOM seeks more specific capability, 
Specific AoIs following the procedures in this CSO will be posted to 
www.SAM.gov with defined problems and limited submission windows. Specific 
AoIs may have dedicated funding. Responses will only be provided to submissions 
in accordance with Section 4. New AoIs may be introduced at any time during the 
solicitation period, and companies are encouraged to regularly check 
www.SAM.gov for updates. 
 
2.3. CSO Process: This process is designed to accommodate a multiple-phased approach as 
outlined in Sections 3 and 4. Awards may be made using either FAR Part 12, 
Acquisition of Commercial Products or Commercial Services, or OT authority. The 
Government may make no awards, one award, or multiple awards against the AoI. The 
Government reserves the right to determine that a combination of solutions is necessary 
to address the problem or meet mission requirements. CSO submission costs will not be 
reimbursed by the Government unless specifically stated in an AoI.  
 
2.4. Additional Guidelines: Use FAR Part 12 as a guide for contract provisions and clauses, 
recognizing they are applicable to resultant FAR-based awards. Multiple Solution Briefs 
are allowed for an AoI if representing distinct concepts. To receive an award, offerors 
must be a registered entity in www.SAM.gov.  
 
3. PHASE REQUIREMENTS  
 
3.1. Phase 1 – Solution Brief  
 
The purpose of the Phase 1 Solution Brief is to identify innovative contract solutions 
related to each AoI that effectively address capability gaps. Solutions Briefs must be 
submitted in response to either a General AoI or Specific AoI as outlined below.  
General AoIs (Format Requirements): All Phase 1 Solution Briefs shall use the Scout 
Card within the Vulcan platform and include a video submission.  
• Scout Card Submission: The Scout Card must be submitted through the Vulcan 
platform. Organizational information (e.g., company name, phone number, and 
address) must be current prior to submission. Each Scout Card submission must 
represent one unique response to the AoI of interest, with a descriptive title 
provided for each submission.  

3 
 
 
• Video Submission: The video must be no longer than five (5) minutes and 
address the Required Elements outlined in the paragraphs below. In doing so, the 
video presentation must demonstrate the actual working capability of the solution, 
not simply display a slideshow or PowerPoint-style presentation. 
Any submissions sent via email, missing a video, or submitted by other means will not be 
considered for evaluation. The Government will not evaluate a submission that does not 
adhere to these standards. 
Specific AoIs (Format Requirements): Submission requirements for Specific AoIs will 
be detailed in the individual AoI posting on www.SAM.gov and may include:  
• Scout Card and Video Submission: A Scout Card and video submission via the 
Vulcan platform as described above for General AoIs, or 
• Written White Paper Submission: Offerors must follow the submission 
instructions provided in the Specific AoI posting. When a written White Paper is 
required, the following format requirements apply unless otherwise stated in the 
Specific AoI posting. The written White Paper shall be digitally formatted to 8.5 x 
11 inches with one-inch margins, no longer than six (6) pages, single-spaced, with 
legible text, and no smaller than 12-point font. The Government will not evaluate 
a submission that does not adhere to these standards. 
General and Specific AoIs (Required Elements): The following required elements 
apply to all Phase 1 Solution Briefs.  
 
• Cover Letter: For Scout Card submissions through Vulcan, organizational and 
identifying information is captured through the platform profile. For written 
White Papers, a Cover Sheet must be included as one of the six pages and 
contain the following information: 
o AoI name and number 
o Descriptive title of submission (each submission should represent one 
unique solution) 
o Full company name and address  
o Point(s) of contact name, email, and phone number 
o If available/known, CAGE code, Unique Entity ID number, and Business 
Size Classification (i.e., large, small, or other socioeconomic category) 
• Executive Summary: Provide an executive summary of the technology or 
solution.  
 
• Solution Concept: Demonstrate and explain how the proposed technology or 
solution addresses capability gaps, delivers advancements, or otherwise provides 
unique value or utility in support of USTRANSCOM’s mission. Describe the 
unique aspects of your solution and the proposed work as it relates to the AoI. 
Identify whether the effort includes a prototype or new technology/capability, an 

4 
 
existing commercial technology/capability, or the further development of 
commercial technology for potential application to USTRANSCOM’s mission. 
 
• Offeror Responsibility & Solution Viability: Provide a brief overview of the 
offeror. Submit a summary of prior and current experience (Government and 
non-Government), qualifications, and resources or ability to obtain them. Use 
FAR Subpart 9.4 as a guide for demonstrating responsibility, recognizing these 
standards may not apply to OT awards. Additionally, provide a summary of 
product development, manufacturing (if relevant), and logistics strategy.  
 
• Estimated Price and Delivery Schedule. Provide a specific and logical 
estimated pricing breakdown, to include annual or monthly cost/price, for the 
solution proposed. Denote prices for optional components, features, or services. 
Pricing estimates must be representative of the viable solution. 
3.2. Phase 2 – Presentation/Pitch  
 
Format Requirements: The Presentation/Pitch shall be no more than 90 minutes unless 
otherwise specified. The Government reserves the right to record these presentations. 
 
Required Elements: The offeror’s Presentation/Pitch shall demonstrate the technical and 
business viability of the proposed solution in their Phase 1 Solution Brief in greater 
detail. The offeror is expected to expand on technical, price, and delivery schedule 
details, as well as provide additional information in response to questions from 
Government representatives.  
3.3. Phase 3 – Request for Proposal (RFP) 
 
Format Requirements: The Written Proposal shall include two volumes: Volume I – 
Technical (see page limits below) and Volume II – Price (no page limit). Additional 
volumes, attachments, or other items may be identified in the RFP. The Government may 
not evaluate a Written Proposal that violates these standards. The Government may also 
provide a list of provisions, clauses, or other terms and conditions. Offerors may include 
commercial terms and conditions, such as Service or User License Agreements, for 
consolidation with Government terms, but such terms should not conflict with the 
Government’s terms.  
 
Volume I – Technical – Required Elements:  
 
Cover Sheet (must be its own page): Provide the following information: 
• AoI name and number 
• Full company name and address  
• Point(s) of contact name, email, and phone number 
• CAGE code  
• Unique Entity ID number  
• Business Size Classification (i.e., large or small)  
• Socioeconomic Status (if applicable)  

5 
 
• Non-Traditional Contractor Self-Certification Statement (if applicable)  
 
Technical Proposal (No more than 10 pages): Describe the background and objectives 
of the proposed work, including the technical approach, deliverables, and resources 
needed to execute the proposed solution. Include the nature and extent of anticipated 
results, ancillary and operational issues such as certifications and algorithms, and any 
engineering or software development methodologies to be used.  
 
Statement of Work (SOW) (Page Limit will be specified in the RFP): Provide a SOW 
formally stating the work to be accomplished under a resultant contract or agreement.  
The SOW must be a separate document suitable for incorporation into the contract or 
agreement. Proprietary information must not be included. Pages shall be numbered with a 
document date under the title. The SOW must accurately describe the work to be 
performed and contain a summary description of the technical methodology, task 
descriptions (without excessive detail), contract deliverables, and timelines for contract 
deliverables within the proposed period of performance.  
 
Volume II – Price – Required Elements:  
 
MS Excel Spreadsheet: Provide a pricing model in Microsoft Excel editable format with 
active formulas containing the mathematical calculations of the proposed price. 
 
Price Proposal: Provide sufficient information to allow the Government to determine the 
fair and reasonableness of the proposed price. If additional information is necessary to 
support this determination, the Government may request other than certified cost and 
pricing data (e.g., commercial price catalogs, previous commercial sales receipts). The 
Government may request further content in the RFP. 
 
4. PHASE EV ALUATIONS 
 
4.1. Phase 1 – Solution Brief  
 
The Solution Brief evaluation criteria listed below are of equal importance. Additional 
technical evaluation criteria in Specific AoIs may be used. In these instances, the 
additional criteria will be posted with the Specific AoI on the www.SAM.gov website. 
 
Alignment to USTRANSCOM Mission: The proposed solution will be evaluated for its 
alignment with USTRANSCOM’s mission requirements and operational priorities. 
 
Technical Merit: The proposed solution will be evaluated based on the following 
subfactors: 
• Technical Feasibility: The soundness of the technical approach and likelihood of 
successful implementation. 
• Innovation: The uniqueness of the proposed solution in delivering new capabilities 
or approaches that are not currently implemented or available within existing 
Government systems or processes. 

6 
 
• Milestone Schedule: The reasonableness and clarity of the proposed schedule for 
achieving milestones and deliverables. 
• Prior Experience: The Government’s confidence in the offeror’s ability to deliver 
commercial products and services that meet the proposed technical performance 
requirements based on Government and non-Government experience with similar 
efforts. 
 
Funds Availability and Potential Return on Investment: The proposed solution will 
be assessed for its affordability and the value it provides relative to its cost, including its 
potential impact on USTRANSCOM’s operations. 
Evaluation Outcomes: For Solution Briefs submitted against a General AoI at 
Attachment 1, the Government may elect not to evaluate, provide no response, retain the 
solution in the USTRANSCOM library for future consideration, proceed to Phase 2, or 
proceed directly to Phase 3. For Solution Briefs submitted against a Specific AoI, 
USTRANSCOM will notify the offeror of one of the following outcomes:  
• The offeror may submit a Presentation/Pitch for evaluation in Phase 2. 
• The offeror may submit a Written Proposal for evaluation in Phase 3 (if the 
Government elects to forego Phase 2). 
• The proposed solution is not of continued interest. 
• The proposed solution is of interest but is not currently eligible for further 
consideration due to lack of Government resources and/or funding. 
 
Solution Briefs will be evaluated solely against the specified criteria and will not 
compared to other offeror submissions. 
Any ratings or feedback provided through the Vulcan platform are informational only and 
will have no bearing on the evaluation of Solution Briefs submitted under this CSO. The 
Government may use Vulcan to provide general feedback, but such input will not be 
considered as part of the evaluation process. 
 
4.2. Phase 2 – Presentation/Pitch 
Each Presentation/Pitch will be assessed based on the same evaluation criteria in Phase 1. 
Answers to the Government’s questions will also be considered.   
 
Evaluation Outcomes: After evaluating Presentation/Pitch submissions,

Sources Sought Notice 
 
Title:   IHS-JVN Teleophthalmology Program Support Contract  
Agency:  Indian Health Service  
Issue Date:  Monday April 6, 2026 
Due Date:  Monday April 20, 2026, no later than 5:00pm EST 
POCs:  Responses must be submitted via email to cynthia.cason@ihs.gov and 
hillary.marshall@ihs.gov and. Include “Teleophthalmology – Your Company Name” 
in the Subject of the email. 
 
This Sources Sought Notice (SSN) is for market research and planning purposes only and shall not be 
construed as a solicitation or an obligation or commitment to issue a solicitation by the Indian Health 
Service (IHS). This SSN is seeking information from the specific types of entities listed below to assess 
their capabilities in fulfilling the requirements set forth in this SSN. The information from this SSN will be 
used to determine the appropriate set-aside, if any, in accordance with the applicable regulations listed. The 
Government encourages the identified to respond to this Notice and will be assessed of their capabilities in 
the following priority: 
 
1. Indian Small Business Economic Enterprises (ISBEE) 
2. Indian Economic Enterprises (IEE) in accordance with HHSAR 326.603-1 
3. Small business concerns in accordance with FAR 19.502-2 (b)(1) & (2) 
 
Responses to the information requested will assist the Government in determining the appropriate 
acquisition method, including whether any ISBEE/IEE or small business set-aside is possible based on the 
Contracting Officer’s reasonable expectation of obtaining offers from two or more relevant concerns that 
will be competitive in terms of market price, product quality, and delivery capability. An organization that 
is not considered an ISBEE/IEE firm OR small business under the applicable NAICS code should 
NOT submit a response to this notice. The applicable primary NAICS code for this requirement is 
541690 - Other Scientific and Technical Consulting Services. The anticipated period of performance for 
this effort will be one year from the date of award, with up to four additional one-year option periods. 
Generic capability statements are not sufficient and may not be considered when assessing entity 
capabilities. 
 
Background 
The Indian Health Service (IHS) is the principal federal health care provider and health advocate for Indian 
people, and its goal is to raise their health status to the highest possible level. IHS provides a comprehensive 
health service delivery system for approximately 2.3 million American Indians and Alaska Natives (AI/AN) 
who belong to 573 federally recognized Tribes in 37 states. IHS has 12 Area Offices and 10 Accounting 
Offices across the United States. These offices support the extensive health care delivery network and 
provide managerial, financial and administrative support to the hospitals, clinics and health centers. All 
work under this contract shall be performed in direct support of the IHS Office of Finance, and Accounting 
(OFA) and Area Offices (including their respective facilities) within the IHS.  
 
The Indian Health Service Teleophthalmology Program uses the Joslin Vision Network (JVN) system, 
which is a specialized teleophthalmology modality for the remote diagnosis and management of diabetic 
retinopathy (DR). The Joslin Vision Network operates within the Comprehensive Diabetes Management 
Program (CDMP), a suite of software applications residing on the IHS JVN/CDMP server that provides 
multiple functions critical to the clinical operation of the JVN including patient clinical record management, 
database maintenance, clinical and administrative reporting, quality assurance (QA), Resource and Patient 
Management System/Electronic Health Record (RPMS/EHR) interoperability, and Digital Imaging and 

  
Sources Sought Notice 
IHS-JVN Teleophthalmology Program Support Contract 
2 
 
Communications in Medicine (DICOM) image management. As such, the CDMP serves as the platform 
for clinical operation of the JVN in the Indian Health Service (IHS). 
 
Deployment and use of the JVN system in the IHS allows participating facilities to image the retina of 
patients with diabetes for the purpose of remote diagnosis and recommendations for referral and 
management of diabetic retinopathy (DR). This allows timely diagnosis and treatment, thereby reducing 
avoidable vision loss among AI/AN’s. This is a critically important program from both clinical and 
regulatory vantage points. 
Diabetic Retinopathy is the leading cause of blindness amongst working age adults. Serious vision loss 
from diabetes can be nearly eliminated by timely diagnosis and treatment of high-risk disease. Before the 
IHS-JVN Teleophthalmology program was implemented, the sustained annual Diabetic Retinopathy 
examination rate in NA/AI patients was ~50%. In FY 2024, the IHS-JVN Teleophthalmology program 
alone captured 26,284 studies of American Indians/Alaska Native (AI/AN) patients, with ~25% identified 
with high risk findings. Those patients with high risk findings are at risk for progressing to blindness if not 
identified by imaging or dilated examination. In that same fiscal year, the IHS-JVN program deployed 18 
new cameras, totaling 113 active sites in 27 states. Continued growth of the program is anticipated based 
on historical data and ongoing interest from clinics across the country. 
 
The first clinical deployments of the IHS-JVN Teleophthalmology program began in the year 2000 and 
have continued incrementally. Currently there are 123 sites in 25 states (113 active in 2025). The majority 
of cameras deployed are stationary, while portable cameras provide services with additional outreach to 
small or remote locations. The IHS-JVN Teleophthalmology program uses the JVN technology to acquire, 
transmit, store/retrieve, interpret, and report retinal images from AI/AN’s with diabetes. These images are 
maintained on servers that operate on the IHS wide area network (WAN), and are routinely visible only by 
IHS reader staff to ensure the privacy of AI/AN patients. Evaluation of these images by IHS readers occurs 
at the National Reading Center using specialized reading and reporting software. This allows the remote 
diagnosis of level of Diabetic Retinopathy with development of a referral and treatment recommendations 
consistent with established standards of care. As a contingency of its use in the IHS, the system has been 
validated and operates at the American Telemedicine Association (ATA) Category 3 level, providing a DR 
diagnostic accuracy equal or better than a conventional dilated retinal examination. More importantly, this 
allows the majority of patients to be diagnosed and followed or referred remotely. If they progress to 
specific levels of DR, appropriate referrals and recommendations are made, thereby minimizing 
inconvenience and expense for the patient and increasing efficiencies for the hosting site. 
 
Purpose and Objectives 
The general purpose of this contract is to maintain ongoing development, implementation, and support of 
the IHS-JVN Teleophthalmology activities in Urban Indian Health Care clinics, Tribal Health Clinics and 
Indian Health Service hospitals and clinics with software, services and equipment. These software, services 
and equipment are provided by the vendor. 
Capability Statement/Submission Information 
A response to this SSN will be in the form of a capability statement to demonstrate capability and experience 
in the task areas identified further below. Specifically, please provide the following information below to 
demonstrate capabilities: 
 
Cover Page 
Please provide a cover page to include: 
1. Company Name 
2. Company Designation (ISBEE/IEE/SB)

Technical Areas

expertise and technical capabilities in the areas outlined further below in this SSN. 
 
Past Performance

relevant technical areas and magnitude of work. 
 
Other Information (Optional) 
You may include any other information that may be helpful in developing or finalizing the requirements of 
the potential acquisition.  
 
Submission Format 
To assist the Government in an expeditious review of your capabilities, the capability statement should be 
organized as follows: 
 Cover page 
 Executive Summary 
 Technical Areas in the order listed 
 Past Performance 
 Other Information, as applicable 
 
The tailored capability statement should not exceed 10 pages excluding Past Performance 
information. Font must not be less than 10 point (for readability) and may be submitted in either in either 
Microsoft Word or Adobe Portable Document Format (PDF) but must be a standard 8-1/2 by 11 inch in 
paper size. All proprietary information should be marked as such.  
 
Generic capability statements are not sufficient and will not be considered compliant with the 
requirements of this notice. 
 
Disclaimer and Important Notes  
This notice does not obligate the Government to award contract. Any information provided by industry to 
the Government as a result of this SSN is strictly voluntary. Responses will not be returned. No entitlements 
to payment of direct or indirect costs or charges to the Government will arise as a result of contractor 
submission of responses or the Government's use of such information. The Government reserves the right 
to use information provided by respondents for any purpose deemed necessary and legally appropriate. Any 
organization responding to this notice should ensure that its response is complete and sufficiently detailed 
to allow the Government to determine the organization’s capabilities to perform the work. Respondents are 
advised that the Government is under no obligation to acknowledge receipt of the information received or

provide feedback to respondents with respect to any information submitted. After a review of the responses 
received, a pre-solicitation synopsis and solicitation may be published on a government GPE. However, 
responses to this Notice will not be considered adequate responses to any resultant solicitation. 
 
Confidentiality. No classified, confidential, or sensitive information should be included in your response. 
The Government reserves the right to use any non-proprietary technical information in any resultant 
solicitation(s).  
 
Thank you for your interest in IHS programs.  
 
Task 1: OPERATIONS (SERVICE) 
Description of Work

 Support end-to-end Quality Assurance (QA) of the IHS-Teleretinal (IHS-TR) program at the 
National Operations & Reading Center and assist with data for peer review, efficiency and other 
analysis. 
 Assist in maintaining an externally pointing Web site for the IHS-JVN Teleophthalmology program

ihs.gov/Teleophthalmology website 
 Develop and maintain an internally pointing Web site for the IHS-TR Teleophthalmology program

I. Notice of Intent.

(a) Security Risk Review. The Security Risk Review is applied to federally funded research designed to help protect Department of the Air Force Science and Technology (S&T) by identifying possible vectors of undue foreign influence. AFRL will follow all policy and procedures outlined in Air Force Research Laboratory (AFRL) Instruction AFRLI 61-113, Science and Technology Protection for the Air Force Research Laboratory and Department of the Air Force Instruction DAFI 63-101/20-101, Integrated Lifecycle Management.

(b)  Security risk review for proposals will be developed for all proposed Senior/Key personnel and “Covered Individuals”. These risk reviews will be based on information disclosed in a Research and Related Senior and Key Person Profile and Security Questionnaire. In addition, any accompanying or referenced documents, publicly available information, and information contained in internal U.S. Government databases will be utilized in risk reviews. Nationality or citizenship is not a factor in the security risk reviews.

(c) When considering all external engagements, AFRL incorporates a holistic decision-making process that encompasses technical and security factors. The security review method implemented by AFRL measures risk factors to identify the appropriate Risk Acceptance Level (RAL) within the organization. The objective analysis of the security risk factors is conducted to empower AFRL’s S&T leaders to make risk-informed decisions. The review process generally looks at five factors, or risk areas, but with authority for expanded review as noted in OSD R&E Memorandum dated 6 Jun 2023. Q&A for N6523626R3007

1. Question: Does this opportunity require an accounting system that has been formally approved or audited by DCAA or DCMA?

Our accounting system has been independently audited by a third-party CPA firm and deemed DCAA-compliant/compatible. However, it has not undergone a formal DCAA or DCMA audit.

Could you please confirm whether this level of certification would be considered sufficient, or if a formal DCAA/DCMA-approved system is mandatory for eligibility?

Answer: An offeror may submit a proposal without a formal DCAA or DCMA accounting system audit; however, the audit would be required prior to contract award. Refer to DFARS 242.7502.

2. Question: Could you please clarify whether a Facility Clearance (FCL) is required for this opportunity? If so, what level of clearance is required?

Answer: As stated in the Section C PWS paragraph 8.1.1, “At time of task order award the contractor shall have a TOP SECRET (TS) facility clearance (FCL) with Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI) access (TS/SCI).” PWS paragraph 8.1.1.2 outlines the highest (up to) required security clearance level by PWS task paragraph and PWS paragraph 8.2.1.1 outlines the required minimum personnel security clearance level by labor category.

252.204-7025 NOTICE OF CYBERSECURITY MATURITY MODEL CERTIFICATION LEVEL REQUIREMENTS (NOV 2025)

(a) Definitions. As used in this provision, “controlled unclassified information (CUI),” “current,” “Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) status,” “Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification unique identifier (CMMC UID),” “Federal contract information (FCI)”, and “plan of action and milestones” have the meaning given in the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement 252.204-7021, Contractor Compliance With the Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Level Requirements, clause of this solicitation.

(b)(1) Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) level. The CMMC level required by this solicitation is: CMMC Level 2 (Self) (at time of award) and CMMC Level 2 (C3PAO) assessment (prior to the exercise of any options). This CMMC level, or higher (see 32 CFR part 170), is required prior to award for each contractor information system that will process, store, or transmit Federal contract information (FCI) or controlled unclassified information (CUI) during performance of the contract.

(2) The Offeror will not be eligible for award of a contract, task order, or delivery order resulting from this solicitation if the Offeror does not have, for each of the contractor information systems that will process, store, or transmit FCI or CUI and that will be used in performance of a contract resulting from this solicitation—

(i) The current CMMC status entered in the Supplier Performance Risk System (SPRS) (https://piee.eb.mil) at the CMMC level required by paragraph (b)(1) of this provision; and

(ii) A current affirmation of continuous compliance with the security requirements identified at 32 CFR part 170 in SPRS.

(c) Plan of action and milestones. If the Offeror has a CMMC Status of Conditional, the Offeror shall successfully close out a valid plan of action and milestones (32 CFR 170.21) to achieve a CMMC Status of Final.

(d) CMMC unique identifiers. The Offeror shall provide, in the proposal, the CMMC unique identifier(s) (CMMC UIDs) issued by SPRS for each contractor information system that will process, store, or transmit FCI or CUI during performance of a contract, task order, or delivery order resulting from this solicitation. The Offeror also shall update the list when new CMMC UIDs are generated in SPRS. The CMMC UIDs are provided in SPRS after the Offeror enters the results of self-assessment(s) for each such information system.

(End of provision)





252.237-7024	Notice of Continuation of Essential Contractor Services (Oct 2010)

(a)	Definitions.“Essential contractor service” and “mission-essential functions” have the meanings given in the clause at 252.237-7023 , Continuation of Essential Contractor Services, in this solicitation.

(b)	The offeror shall provide with its offer a written plan describing how it will continue to perform the essential contractor services within the PWS in Section C of the task order, Mission Essential Contractor Services, during periods of crisis. The offeror shall–

(1)	Identify provisions made for the acquisition of essential personnel and resources, if necessary, for continuity of operations for up to 30 days or until normal operations can be resumed;

(2)	Address in the plan, at a minimum—

(i)	Challenges associated with maintaining essential contractor services during an extended event, such as a pandemic that occurs in repeated waves;

(ii)	The time lapse associated with the initiation of the acquisition of essential personnel and resources and their actual availability on site;

(iii)	The components, processes, and requirements for the identification, training, and preparedness of personnel who are capable of relocating to alternate facilities or performing work from home;

(iv)	Any established alert and notification procedures for mobilizing identified “essential contractor service” personnel; and

(v)	The approach for communicating expectations to contractor employees regarding their roles and responsibilities during a crisis.

*To be completed with proposal submission.

(End of provision)

SOURCES SOUGHT: MSO Support Services for the Office of Naval Research  
1.1 Description  
This announcement constitutes a Sources Sought for the purpose of determining market 
capabilities. It does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), a Request for Quote 
(RFQ), or an indication that the Government will contract any of the items and/or services 
discussed in this notice. DO NOT send a proposal in response to this request for 
information. Responses should provide only the information requested in this notice. The 
Government reserves the right to issue the solicitation under any part of the Federal 
Acquisition Regulation deemed to best meet the needs of the Government. Neither ONR 
nor any other part of the federal government will be responsible for any cost incurred by 
responders in furnishing this information. 
1.2 Submission instructions for Capabilities Statements  
Interested parties shall read and review the below information and furnish the following 
information: 
• Name of Organization, Cage Code and DUNS Number; 
• Address of Organization; 
• Telephone Number, Address, and Email address for the primary point of contact for 
Capability Statement; 
• Business standing (i.e. large or small business) for NAICS 541611; 
• If a Small Business, indicate all Small Business Type(s) that you qualify for (e.g., 
Small Business, Woman-Owned Small Business, Economically Disadvantaged 
Woman-Owned Small Business, Small Disadvantaged Business, 8(a) Certiﬁed, 
HUBZone Certiﬁed, Veteran Owned Small Business, and/or Service-Disabled 
Veteran-Owned Small Business); 
• If 8(a), provide your 8(a) SBA Office POC/details, 8(a) entry and exit date 
• Brief summary of your organization’s capability to meet the requirements in the 
Performance Work Statement; 
• Brief summary of your organization’s capability to meet requirements for the 
required Personnel; 
• What type of work has your organization performed in the past in support of the 
same or similar requirements; 
• Brief summary of your organization’s experience in managing tasks of this nature; 

• Brief summary of your organization’s experience in managing a team of 
subcontractors, and if so how many; 
• Brief summary of the technical skills your organization possesses that ensures your 
capability in performing the requirements as stated above; 
• Brief summary of potential areas in the requirement in which small business 
participation may be possible; 
• Listing of any Government-Wide contracts held by the business that may be an 
appropriate vehicle for this acquisition. Please include contract numbers. 
 
All capability statements shall be nonproprietary and shall not contain classiﬁed 
information. Capability statements shall not exceed ﬁve (5) pages in length (excluding a 
cover page) and must be submitted by email no later than 12:00 pm Eastern Time, on 24 
February 2026 to Ellen Reed, Contracting Officer at ellen.c.reed.civ@us.navy.mil . Any 
responses received after the requested due date may not be considered for market 
research and acquisition planning purposes. 
 
2.0 Labor  Requirements  
The Office of Naval Research (ONR) seeks administrative support services. The contractor 
will provide a comprehensive solution to accomplish the tasks listed in the Draft 
Performance Work Statement. This includes, but is not limited to: 
• Asset Management  
• Classiﬁed Document Control  
• Common Access Card Issuing Official (IO)  
• Driver/Courier  
• Engineering Technician 
• Financial Analyst Support  
• Human Capital  
• Information Security (INFOSEC) 
• Mailroom Support  

• Policy Analyst  
• Program Manage ment  
• S&T Intelligence Liaison  
• Security  
• Supply Room Support  
• FOIA/PA  
• Records Management  
• Supplemental Labor (Electrical/Carpentry)  
• Supplemental Labor (General Labor)  
• Supplemental Labor (LAN Cabling)  
• Supplemental Labor (Office Relocation)  
 
(Note¿ .The.full.list.of.technical.tasks.for.all.positions.can.be.found.in.the.Draft.Performance.
Work.Statement) 
 
3.0 Incumbent Contractor s 
This effort is a consolidation of several current contracts. The incumbent contractors are:  
Aktarius LLC (Building Management support) 
Gemini Industries Inc. (Human Capital Analytical Support) 
 Thunder Ridge Solutions (Financial Support Services) 
 Crowned Grace Inc. (Conference and Event Planning Services) 
Next Intelligence Solutions, LLC (PAO Communication Support) 
 American Technology Solutions International (Front Office Support)  
GPI Enterprises (FOIA Support Services). 
4.0 NAICS Code and Small Business Size Standard  
The North American Industry Classiﬁcation System (NAICS) code applicable to this 
potential award will be 541611.  

5.0 Organizational Conﬂict of Interest  
ONR has determined that an actual or potential organizational conﬂict of interest (OCI) 
exists when a contractor performs both systems engineering and technical assistance 
(SETA) and Research and Development (R&D) work. Further details can be found at 
https://www.onr.navy.mil/About-ONR/compliance-protections/Organizational-Conﬂicts-
Interest. 
8.0 Contract Type  
ONR anticipates awarding a Firm Fixed Price contract. 
9.0 Security Requirements  
ONR anticipates some work will require a DD 254. Some positions will require personnel 
with a security clearance. 
10.0 Period of Performance  
The contract is anticipated to be 60 months/5 years in duration.

Performance Work Statement

National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA)

National Marine Fisheries Service (NOAA Fisheries)

Alaska Region

Professional Services for Restricted Access Management (RAM) Division Permitting Support

Background and Objectives

The National Marine Fisheries Service (NOAA Fisheries), a bureau of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration under the Department of Commerce, is a pioneer in quota-based fisheries management programs, which allocate total allowable catch to vessels, groups of cooperating vessels, or catch privileges to individuals. The Alaska Region (AKR) is one of five regional offices that together support marine resource management in all Federal waters. 

The Restricted Access Management Division (RAM) in the Alaska Region supports sustainable fisheries and promotes fishing communities by issuing Federal fishing permits and other fishery authorizations to fishery participants. Throughout the calendar year, RAM reviews and issues licenses for the American Fisheries Act (AFA) Program, the Amendment 80 Program, Individual Fishing Quota (IFQ) halibut and sablefish, the Rockfish Program, subsistence halibut, charter halibut, groundfish and crab License Limitation Program (LLP) and processes over a thousand IFQ halibut/sablefish, IFQ crab, Guided Angler Fish (GAF), and LLP license transfers, among others. RAM is regularly providing advice and notifications to fishermen and the public on the interpretation of Federal fishing regulations.

This contract is for professional services to support RAM in performing intake of permitting applications, providing first line customer service to the industry inquiries regarding applications and systems/application troubleshooting, and providing training and outreach.

Tasks and Deliverables

Fishery Application Intake and Processing (50%)– Contractor personnel will support the Restricted Access Management Division by performing intake of fishery applications and permits and inputting the necessary information in the required Alaska Region system for processing. RAM historically processes over 5,000 applications, received both by electronic and hard mail. Contractor personnel are expected to initially intake and enter the majority of these applications into AKR systems for further review. This includes reviewing the applications and submitting the information in the Integrated Fisheries Application (IFA) or legacy system, which involves generating cases and uploading intake documentation to each case.

Customer Service/Troubleshooting (30%) – Contractor personnel will provide first-line customer service to the industry through RAM’s public-facing email. This task is similar to a help-desk function. RAM will provide an answer base with standard responses and contractor personnel will respond to routine inquiries and escalate more complex questions to RAM staff for resolution. Inquiries commonly regard eFish or permitting systems, permitting actions, and user authorizations.


Outreach and Training (15%) – The contractor will provide outreach and training with external and internal users. This includes developing user guides, documenting process steps, and creating training materials. Contractor personnel may provide informal or formal training on the permitting process.


Document Management (5%) – Contractor personnel will support RAM with document management or programmatic records, to include filing. 

General Contract Deliverables:

The following is a list of deliverables under the basic contract, including administrative deliverables, required during the period of performance of this contract:  

Labor Categories

This will be a Time-and-Materials contract. The contractor will provide one or more personnel that meet the following description:

Data Technician 5: Collects, reviews, and inputs data into a computer processing system; audits output data. May be expected to code data and input data for computer processing.  Identifies and resolves production related errors. Maintains and revises procedural lists, control records and coding schemes to process source data. Must be familiar with a variety of the field's concepts, practices, and procedures. Relies on experience and judgment to plan and accomplish goals. Performs a variety of complicated tasks.  A wide degree of creativity and latitude is expected. 

Performance Requirements Summary

This contract includes a Performance Requirements Summary (PRS). The PRS plays an integral role in the administration of the contract. In addition to any applicable inspection clauses or other related terms and conditions contained in the contract, the PRS shall serve as a primary tool for inspection and acceptance of services as facilitated by the Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR), with support from the Technical Monitor (TM). Evaluation of the Contractor’s overall performance shall be in accordance with the performance standards set forth in the PRS, and will be conducted by the COR. The PRS constitutes a material aspect of the contract and will not be changed or otherwise modified without prior written approval of the Contracting Officer.

The PRS establishes key elements of Contractor performance that represent “mission essential” service requirements or “Deliverables”, which are identified in the table below. The “Performance Objective” column represents the standard against which Contractor performance will be measured in relation to accomplishment of the corresponding service output. The performance objective or “standard” describes the minimum acceptable level of service by the Contractor for satisfactory performance. The “Acceptable Quality Level (AQL)” column displays the maximum allowable deviation from the performance objective, which, if exceeded, evokes the negative incentive specified in the table below.  

Period of Performance 

Base Period: September 30, 2026 – September 29, 2027

Option Year 1: September 30, 2027 – September 29, 2028

Option Year 2: September 30, 2028 – September 29, 2029

Option Year 3: September 30, 2029 – September 29, 2030

Place of Performance 

Contractor work will be performed either at the NOAA Fisheries, Alaska Region office at 709 West 9th Street in Juneau, AK, or at a location of the Contractor’s discretion and agreed to by the government.  

Operational Hours 

The Contractor is responsible for conducting business, between the hours of 0800-1700 AKST Monday through Friday, except Federal holidays. 

Removing Contractors for Misconduct or Security Reasons

The Government may, at its sole discretion (in coordination with the Contracting Officer where practical), direct the Contractor to remove any Contractor employee from NOAA facilities for misconduct or security reasons.  Removal does not relieve the Contractor of the responsibility to continue providing the services required under the contract. The Contracting Officer will provide the Contractor with a written explanation to support any request to remove a Contractor.

Post-Award Conference 

The Contractor shall attend a post-award conference with the Contracting Officer, COR, and Project Lead/Technical Monitor no later than 10 business days after the date of award.  The purpose of the purchase order conference is to set the standards of performance, clarify details, place of performance, building access time, communication channels, required training, and progress report and invoicing details.  The Post-award conference will be held at the Government’s facility or via teleconference.

Government-Furnished Resources 

If contractor personnel choose to work onsite, the Government will provide the facilities, equipment, utilities, and/or services listed below:  

 

NOAA Fisheries Alaska Region will furnish access to computer equipment, telephone and work space for contractor personnel working on-site, as required and under the latest set of security regulations. All utilities, printing and standard office use of the facility will be available for the Contractor’s in performance of duties outlined in this PWS. The Contractor shall be responsible for operating under conditions that preclude any undue waste.

The Government will provide required software, software licenses, and replacement components for IT equipment as necessary.  

The Government will provide access to relevant systems, allowing Contractor personnel to view, edit, and add documentation to site and projects as needed.  

The Government will provide to the Contractor the following equipment, supplies, and similar, necessary to conduct these services and anticipates facility and security access as follows:

Travel, and Training 

Training: 

Training is authorized for NMFS/NOAA/DOC specific systems and requirements.  Completion certificates must be submitted to the COR. The following training is currently required to be completed under this Contract.  

NOAA IT security 

Records Management 101 

Contractor-provided Sexual Assault/Sexual Harassment Prevention and Response Training IAW NAM 1330-52.222-70(b)(6) 

In general, all training for Contractor resources shall be provided by the Contractor.  The only exception will be for NOAA specific training that is not available on the open market.  If a Contractor needs training on NOAA specific software, the training shall be approved and coordinated in advance with the COR and Technical Monitor. 

Travel: 

Travel is not anticipated under this contract.

Security Requirements

The suitability or risk level for this work has been determined to be Low. As such, the Contractor shall pre-screen their employees to disqualify anyone who does not meet the following criteria: Individuals on this contract must be eligible for approval of a Common Access Card (CAC) credential and be able to comply with the security requirement set forth in CAR 1352.237-70. Each Contractor employee that is devoted to this task will be required to provide fingerprints and a background investigation. 

Contractor personnel will be required to obtain a Common Access Card (CAC) and maintain a NOAA.gov email account. The security process can take from two to eight weeks to complete before a CAC can be issued, and therefore it is imperative to respond to government requests quickly and completely. New resources to the contract shall provide the requested information within 5 days of notification.

The Contractor must meet the Department of Commerce Enterprise Cybersecurity Policy (found at https://connection.commerce.gov/collection/it-security-policy-and-fisma-reporting-program)

Special Requirements

Confidentiality and Data Privacy

This contract may require that services contractors have access to Privacy Information. Service contractors are responsible for maintaining confidentiality of all subjects and materials and may be required to sign and adhere to a Non-disclosure Agreement (NDA).

Intellectual Property Rights

The Government has unlimited rights to all documents/material produced under this contract.  All documents and materials, to include the source codes of any software, produced under this contract shall be Government owned and are the property of the Government with all rights and privileges of ownership/copyright belonging exclusively to the Government. These documents and materials may not be used or sold by the Contractor without written permission from the Contracting Officer. Knowledge and experience with Alaska commercial fisheries and operations, including a minimum of three years experience working in Alaska fisheries permitting

Advanced Research Announcement (ARA), Call 05 
Overview Information 
 
NAICS Code: The NAICS code for this acquisition is 541715 and the small business 
size is 1,000 employees. 
Federal Agency Name: Air Force Research Laboratory, Sensors Directorate, 
AFRL/RYD 
ARA Title: Microelectronics Innovation for Next-generation System Advancement 
and Validation (MINSAV) 
ARA Number: FA8650-19-S-1932 
Call Title: TALOS 
Call Type: Call 05 Announcement 
 
THIS IS A ONE-STEP SOLICITATION FOR CALL 05 ISSUED UNDER MINSAV 
ARA. Unless otherwise stated in this call, all requirements listed within the 
basic ARA announcement are considered applicable. Offerors should monitor 
the SAM.gov website at http://www.sam.gov in the event this announcement is 
amended or calls are issued. 
 
Proposal Due Date and Time: 1 June 2026, 5:00PM EST. 
 
NOTE: Proposal receipt after the due date and time shall be governed by 
the provisions of FAR 52.215-1(c)(3). Any proposal received at the 
Government office designated in this ARA after the exact time specified is “late” and 
will not be considered except at the Contracting Point of Contact’s discretion. Early 
proposal submission is encouraged. 
 
Submission: UNCLASSIFIED proposals must be submitted electronically via email 
to Adam J Wentworth, Contracting Officer, AFRL/RYKSM at 
adam.wentworth@us.af.mil and Daniel Kelly, Contract Specialist, AFRL/RYKSM at 
daniel.kelly.29@us.af.mil or through secure file exchange at 
(https://safe.apps.mil/).  
 
Type of Contract/Instrument: The Air Force reserves the right to award 
contract(s) pursuant to 10 U.S.C. 4023 based on the instrument deemed most 
appropriate. It is anticipated that contract(s) awarded under this call will be a Cost 
Plus Fixed Fee C-type contract. Cost reimbursement contracts require successful 
offerors to have an accounting system considered adequate by the Defense 
Contract Management Agency (DCMA) for tracking costs applicable to the contract. 
 

Estimated Call Value: The total estimated call value is $34M (the AF reserves the 
right to exceed this amount if determined to be in the best interest of the 
Government). 
 
Anticipated Number of Awards: The Air Force anticipates awarding one (1) 
contract as a result of this call. However, the AF reserves the right to award zero, 
or multiple contracts, for all, some or none of the solicited effort(s) based on the 
offeror’s ability to perform desired work and funding fluctuations or availability.  
 
Notice to Offeror(s)/Supplier(s): IAW DAFFARS MP 5332.7(a), funds are not 
presently available for this effort. No award will be made under this solicitation until 
funds are available. The Government reserves the right to cancel this solicitation, 
either before or after the closing date. In the event the Government cancels this 
solicitation, the Government has no obligation to reimburse an offeror for any costs. 
 
Brief Call Summary: See Attachment 1.  
 
Address technical questions to the Technical POC: 
Peter Buxa, Program Manager, AFRL/RYDR 
2241 Avionics Circle, WPAFB OH 45433 
(937) 713-8725 or peter.buxa@us.af.mil 
 
Address contracting questions to the Contracting POC: 
Adam J Wentworth, Contracting Officer, AFRL/RYKSM 
2130 Eighth Street, Area B, Bldg. 45, WPAFB OH 45433-7541  
(312) 713-9982 or adam.wentworth@us.af.mil and  
Daniel Kelly, Contract Specialist, AFRL/RYKSM at daniel.kelly.29@us.af.mil. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

Full Text Announcement 
I. Program Description: Air Force Research Laboratory, Sensors Directorate 
(AFRL/RYD) is soliciting proposals as detailed below. Unless otherwise stated in 
this call, all requirements listed within the basic ARA solicitation are considered 
applicable. See basic ARA for further detailed descriptions of items listed below. 
 
1. Statement of Objectives (SOO)/Description of Technical Areas: See 
Attachment 1.  
2. Deliverable Items: 
a. Data Items: Reference Attachment 1 and Attachment 2.  
 
b. Software: Shall be submitted as required (generated) during performance 
and as outlined in Attachment 2.  
c. Hardware: Shall be submitted as required (generated) during 
performance and as outlined in Attachment 3.  
3. Period of Performance (PoP): 39 months (36 months technical effort, 3 
months final report)   
4. Other Requirements: 
a. Program Security Classification: This call is at the Controlled 
Unclassified Information (CUI) level. The SOO will be at the Secret 
Collateral level. Proposal submissions will have incorporated Secret 
Collateral Addendums and the contractor will be required to have the 
ability to obtain/submit such information. See Section VII below for 
additional information. 
b. Export Control: Information involved in this effort is subject to Export 
Control (International Traffic in Arms Regulation (ITAR)). 
c. Contractor Performance Assessment Reporting System (CPARS):  
CPARS is applicable IAW AFFARS 5342.1503.  
d. Unique/Special Clauses: In accordance with DFARS 252.204-7021 and 
DFARS 252.204-7025, the contractor shall have a current CMMC Level 2 
assessment posted in SPRS at the time of contract award and for the 
duration of the contract.  
 
e. Associate Contractor Agreement: Not anticipated on this call. 
f. Options: Options are not anticipated on this call. 
g. Organizational Conflict of Interest (OCI): In order to mitigate any 
potential OCI, DAFFARS provisional clause 5352.209-9001 is incorporated 
in Section L of the Model Contract (Attachment 4) and DAFFARS clause 
5352.209-9000 will be added to any resultant contract(s). If an OCI is 

anticipated, the contractor should provide the appropriate mitigation plan 
for Government review as part of their Business Proposal. 
5. Other Information: 
a. Government Furnished Property (GFP) Availability: GFP is 
anticipated on this call.   
b. Government Furnished Information (GFI) Software: GFI is not 
anticipated on this call.   
c. Base Support/Network Access: Access to DoD Supercomputing 
Resource Center hardware/software emulation tools is anticipated. 
d. Data Rights: Unlimited data rights are desired for this call. See detailed 
information contained within the basic ARA.  Data Rights desired by the 
contractor should be included with submission as part of the Section K 
(Certs and Reps), as attached to the ARA.  
II. Award Information:   
1. Anticipated Award Date: August 2026 
2. Anticipated Funding Profile:   
FY 25 FY 26 FY 27 FY 28 FY 29 Total 
9M 8M 13M 3.5M 0.5M 34M 
 
* This funding profile is an estimate only and not a contractual obligation for 
funding. All funding is subject to change due to Government discretion and 
availability. Potential offerors should be aware that due to unanticipated budget 
fluctuations funding in any or all areas may change with little or no notice.    
III. Eligibility Information: 
1. Eligible Offeror: This is an unrestricted solicitation. 
 
2. Other:  
a. Foreign Participation: Foreign Participation is not authorized on this call 
due to the sensitive nature of the technology and its level of classification.  
b. Export Control: This acquisition involves data that is subject to export 
control laws and regulations.  
NOTE: You may be ineligible for award if all requirements of this 
solicitation are not met on the proposal date, as identified in each call.  
IV. Proposal and Submission Information: 
1. Overview: Proposals submitted under this call shall be in accordance with 
the instructions provided both herein and within the basic ARA 
announcement. The Government intends to review resulting proposals and 
award all, some, or none of the proposal received without 

negotiations/discussions.  However, the Government does reserve the right 
to negotiate with those offerors whose proposals have been selected for 
funding. Offerors should be alert for any call amendments that may change 
proposal requirements or permit extensions to proposal submission dates.  
2. Proposal Instructions:  
a. See information provided in basic ARA announcement (Section IV.3.). 
b. Technical/Management Proposals under this call shall be submitted 
Unclassified. In addition, a Classified Proposal Addendum shall be 
separately submitted. Please contact the POCs listed in the Overview 
Section for delivery instructions. Please note, any appendices submitted 
will count against page limits. No classified cost volumes will be allowed. 
If proposal page count exceeds the requirement limit(s) below, only the 
first required page count(s) will be examined; the remainder will be 
discarded and not considered. 
c. Technical/Management Unclassified Proposal shall be limited to: Forty 
(40) pages 
d. Statement of Work ((SOW) Unclassified ONLY) shall be limited to: Ten 
(10) pages 
e. Classified Proposal Addendum shall be limited to: Five (5) pages 
f. Offerors must provide all of the following to be considered for award: 
1) Technical/Management Proposal 
2) SOW 
3) Business Proposal 
4) Subcontracting plans (if applicable) 
5) Classified Proposal Addendum 
V. Proposal Review Information: 
• Proposal - Peer or Scientific Review Criteria: Proposals will be reviewed 
through Peer or Scientific Review using the criteria below. The technical 
aspect, which is ranked, as the first order of priority, shall be reviewed based 
on the following criteria that are of equal order of importance.  
a. Technical Merit:  
1) The offeror’s understanding of the scope of the technical effort. 
2) Soundness of the offeror’s technical approach including whether the 
proposal demonstrates related experience and qualifications of 
technical personnel. 
3) Proposal’s potential to advance technology and the state of the art. 
4) The potential to transition the research and development 
deliverables to future Government needs.  Any proposed restriction 
on technical data or computer software will be considered. 

b. Cost/Price: The cost/price criterion includes the realism of the proposed 
cost. Cost/Price is a substantial factor but ranked as the second order of 
priority (If an offeror proposes the use of GFP and that proposed GFP 
provides the offeror an unfair competitive advantage, then FAR 45.202 
requires rental equivalent be applied to the Cost Factor for evaluation 
purposes only).   
2. Proposal – Review and Selection Process: 
a. Categories: Based on the Peer or Scientific Review, proposals will be 
categorized as Selectable or Not Selectable (see definitions below). The 
selection of one or more sources for award will be based on the Peer or 
Scientific Review, as well as importance to agency programs and funding 
availability.  
1) Selectable: Proposals are recommended for acceptance if sufficient 
funding is available.  
2) Not Selectable: Even if sufficient funding existed, the proposal should 
not be funded.  
b. No other criteria will be used. 
c. Prior to award of a potentially successful offer, the Contracting Officer will 
make a determination regarding price reasonableness. 
NOTE: The Government reserves the right to award some, all, or none of 
the proposals. When the Government elects to award only a part of a 
proposal, the selected part may be categorized as Selectable, though the 
proposal as a whole may not merit such a categorization. 
VI. Award Administration Information: 
Award Notices: Offerors will be notified whether their proposal(s) is 
recommended for award on or about 30 days after receipt. The notification is 
not to be construed to mean that any contract award is assured, as availability 
of funds and successful negotiations are prerequisites to any award.   
VII. Other Information:  
Proposal Content Checklist: See basic ARA. 
Revolutionary FAR Overhaul: Any award made will contain the appropriate 
FAR, DFARS, and DAFFARS clause updates to be consistent with the RFO, R-
DFARS, and DAF Contracting Compass. If any legacy clauses are used, they will 
be included in full text within the contract award.   
Within Scope Modifications: Potential offerors are advised that due to the 
inherent uncertainty of research and development efforts, awards resulting from 
this announcement may be modified during performance to make within scope 
changes, to include but not limited to, modifications that may increase overall 
contract ceiling amount. 

Nontraditional Defense Contractors: 
If a proposal will contain an assertion of a nontraditional defense contractor 
status, the proposal shall contain pricing information including a commercial 
pricing list or a proof-of-sale document such as an invoice showing commercial 
prices.  
This pricing information shall be submitted to AFRL as part of the proposal. If a 
subcontractor asserting nontraditional defense contractor status does not wish 
to submit proprietary pricing information to a prime for inclusion in the proposal, 
the subcontractor may separately submit to the Government team, whereupon 
the Government team will evaluate and provide a distilled analysis to the prime 
contractor.  
See DFARS 212.102(a)(iv) for explanation of contracting officers’ permissive 
authority on nontraditional defense contractors. 
Instructions to request Secret Collateral SOO: 
Please note for the Proposal submittal process, AFRL/RYDR will provide a Secret 
Collateral SOO. The process to request the document is delineated below. Please 
note, the document shall be requested from the Contract Specialist and shall be 
requested no later than (NLT) 1 May 2026.  
Daniel Kelly 
Contract Specialist, AFRL/RYKSM 
Daniel.kelly.29@us.af.mil 
 
Potential bidders shall include the following information in their email request. If 
any information is missing, AFRL/RYDR will be unable to provide the Secret 
Collateral SOO.  
 
a. Contractor Cage code. 
b. Contractor POC who can receive classified material. 
c. Classified Mailing Address or preferred secure electronic network. 
 
Upon receipt of the Secret Collateral SOO, vendors shall return the signed AF310 to 
the return mailing address, fax number, or secure electronic network point of 
access provided within 14 business days of receipt, at the attention of the Technical 
POC. 
 
Any potential offeror questions relating to the information provided within the 
Secret Collateral SOO shall be submitted to the Technical POC listed above, NLT 8 
May 2026 through the method at which the vendor received the SOO.  
 
Peter Buxa 
Program Manager, AFRL/RYDR 
peter.buxa@us.af.mil 
 
NO CLASSIFIED QUESTIONS SHALL BE SUBMITTED VIA EMAIL. 
 

Upon receipt of any questions, AFRL/RYDR will provide responses through the same 
delivery method. Due to the nature of classified information, no questions and 
answers will be posted on SAM.gov. 
 
If you have any questions relating to the request process for the Secret Collateral 
SOO, please contact the Technical POC. Additionally, please include a courtesy copy 
to the Contracting POCs listed within this call.  
 
NO CLASSIFIED QUESTIONS SHALL BE SUBMITTED VIA EMAIL.

the MC-CBRN program as it relates to medical emergency management in accordance with DAFI 
41-106, Medical Readiness Program Management and AF Tactics, Techniques, and Procedures

hours needed to accomplish the project.

correspond with Government personnel duty hours. Occasional change of work hours may be 
required to accommodate extraordinary requirements. Extended or compressed schedules that 
are mutually beneficial and do not exceed 80 work hours in the span of two weeks shall be 
coordinated through the COR. Government furnished resources shall be available during the 
hours of duty. 
 
4.2.  Place of Performance.  The work under this contract shall be performed at HQ Air 
Education and Training Command, JBSA- Randolph, Texas.  The contractor shall on occasion 
be required to attend training, briefings, mission events, and site visits within the San Antonio 
area, AETC base locations, and HQ AFMEDCOM.

be performed via telework by mutual agreement between AETC/SGX and the candidate, in 
accordance with AF and AETC telework policies. The government reserves the right to authorize 
situational telework on a case-by-case basis. Examples include but are not limited to the 
following: 1) an employee has a short-term need for uninterrupted time to complete work on a 
complex project or report. 2) an employee is recovering from illness or an injury and is 
temporarily unable to report to the traditional office physically. 3) an employee receives word of 
inclement weather and notifies her/his supervisor that s/he would like to opt for unscheduled 
telework that day.

Public Law 116-283, National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021; 5 U.S.C. 9101, Access to 
Criminal History for National Security and Other Purposes 5 CFR §1320.8, Agency collection of

relevant to Federal Grants, Cooperative Agreements, Contracts, Other Transaction Agreements or other 
research related agreements awarded by the Department of the Air Force. Records in these systems will 
be used to ensure Department of the Air Force sponsored and/or awarded federal grants, cooperative 
agreements, contracts, Other Transaction Agreements and/or benefits are awarded to responsible parties, 
entities, and individuals.  
 
Routine Uses: To contractors, grantees, experts, consultants, students, and others performing or working 
on a contract, grant, cooperative agreement, other transaction or other assignment for the Federal

To the appropriate Federal, State, local, territorial, tribal, foreign, or international law enforcement

indicates a violation or potential violation of law, whether criminal, civil, or regulatory in nature.

voluntary. However, 42 U.S. Code § 6605, which imposes certain disclosure requirements in connection 
with Federal research and development awards, provides various enforcement mechanisms for non-
compliance to include civil or criminal remedies. One such mechanism, which the Department of the Air

This notice is a synopsis for Geostationary Littoral Imaging and Monitoring Radiometer (GLIMR) Access 
to Space (ATS) “GLIMR ATS.” The purpose of this notice is to provide potential Offerors information 
regarding the procurement strategy, identify key upcoming milestones, and allow for comments on the 
draft requirement document(s).  
THIS INFORMATION IS FOR PLANNING PURPOSES ONLY AND IS SUBJECT TO CHANGE. 
The GLIMR investigation was selected in August 2019, under Earth Venture Instrument-5 (EVI-5) 
Announcement of Opportunity (AO) NNH17ZDA004O-EVI5, which solicited proposals for complete 
Principal Investigator (PI)-led spaceflight instruments to conduct innovative, integrated, hypothesis or 
scientific question-driven approaches to pressing Earth system science issues. GLIMR will operate from 
geostationary orbit and use a hyperspectral ocean color radiometer to observe coastal waters that provide 
critical economic and ecosystem services. GLIMR is a Category 3 mission (per NPR 7120.5) with a Class 
D payload (per NPR 8705.4). The Appendix to this document provides a high-level mission architecture 
and key payload parameters. 
The following is a summary of key procurement strategy elements: 
1. T
he GLIMR ATS scope includes the procurement of commercial services for the following:
a. Spacecraft and Launch Vehicle;
b. Integration Planning;
c. Ground System Integration, Testing, and Readiness;
d. Instrument -Spacecraft Integration, Test, and Pre-Launch Processing;
e. Spectrum Licensing and orbital slot authorization;
f. Launch and GLIMR In-orbit Checkout;
g. On-Orbit Spacecraft and Instrument Operations*; and
h. Programmatic and technical support.
*I
nstrument operations were not previously part of the ATS scope described under the
R
equest for Information or other publicly provided Market Research documents; however, it
i
s being added to the scope of this procurement.
2. T
he procurement will be conducted as a full and open competition under NAICS code 541715,
Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (Except
Nanotechnology and Biotechnology), 1,000 employee size standard, and as a commercial service
u
tilizing Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 12 terms and conditions with FAR Part 15
evaluation procedures. Selection will be based on the overall Best Value to the Government
considering price and non-price (experience/past performance, technical approach) factors. The
t
echnical approach will be proposed via oral presentations.
3. T
he expected period of performance (POP) will be five (5) years, consisting of a three (3) year
base period and two 1-year options for extended operations. The exact POP will be dependent on
Offeror solutions.
a. For the base period, this estimated POP assumes 7 months of integration planning from
contract award to instrument delivery, 11 months of integration and test from instrument
delivery to launch, 6 months for in-orbit checkout, and 1 year of baseline operations
.
b. T
he estimated instrument delivery readiness is no later than January 2027.
4. Th
e contract will be Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) with milestone payments.

Page 2 of 5 
5. There is no assumption or requirement that the GLIMR Instrument be a dedicated (single) 
spacecraft payload or one of several spacecraft payloads (e.g., hosting; rideshare). Rather, the 
Government is looking to industry to provide an effective solution that will meet the GLIMR ATS 
requirements.  
 
6. The following are ESTIMATED key milestone dates (NOTE: These are estimated dates only 
and may change at any time.):

comments and feedback to the documentation attached to this synopsis. As applicable, this notice 
will be updated based on continued industry engagement and feedback.

Please check www.SAM.gov regularly for updates. We look forward to your comments and feedback.
