This Statement of Work (SOW) details the work to be performed by the Geostationary Littoral Imaging 
and Monitory Radiometer (GLIMR) Access to Space (ATS) Contractor (Contractor) and its team 
members for the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) Life Cycle Implementation 
Phases D through F. 
GLIMR is a hyperspectral ocean color sensor which targets the Gulf of America and other coastal and 
ocean waters of North and South America. With its vantage point from geostationary orbit, GLIMR will 
be the first hyperspectral ocean color sensor in the Western Hemisphere to study ocean processes at 
the diurnal timescales required to observe the dynamic ecological, biogeochemical, and physical 
processes typical of coastal and ocean waters. GLIMR is uniquely designed to capture the 
spatiotemporal evolution of phytoplankton blooms, which grow and dissipate on scales of hours to 
days, monitor phytoplankton physiology, growth rates and shifts in community composition, resolve 
coastal features, fronts, eddies, and upwelling features, and monitor biogeochemical fluxes and land-
ocean exchanges at sub-diurnal to multi-day scales. GLIMR will improve quantification of primary 
productivity, biomass, and carbon fluxes within coastal aquatic ecosystems and across the land-sea 
interface and contribute observations that will aid development and evaluation of models that project 
future changes in carbon cycling and marine ecosystems for use in ecological forecasting and as 
inputs for improved climate change predictions. The two main science goals of GLIMR are (1) to 
understand the processes contributing to rapid changes in phytoplankton growth rate and community 
composition, and (2) quantify how high frequency fluxes of sediments, organic matter, and other 
materials between and within coastal ecosystems regulate the productivity and health of coastal 
ecosystems. The science application objectives aim to study the formation, magnitude, and trajectories 
of harmful algal blooms, oil spills, and Sargassum accumulation events.

AIR FORCE                                                                       
 INITIAL PROVISIONING PERFORMANCE SPECIFICATION (IPPS) 
22 May 2025 
          
 
1.  Initial Provisioning Performance Specification (IPPS).  This document provides specifications for 
contractor’s use in submitting Provisioning Technical Documentation (PTD) compatible with the AFMC 
D220 Provisioning System and participating in the provisioning process with the Government. 
 
1.1.  Initiator and Prime Provisioning Activity (PPA):     
 
          406 SCMS/GULAB-HILL 
          6038 ASPEN AVENUE 
          BLDG 1289 SW 
          HILL AFB UT 84056 
 
1.2.  Date of Initiation:   ______________                Revision # and Date:   ______________                 
 
2.  Correspondence: 
 
2.1.  Address all correspondence pertaining to spare/repair parts provisioning and related data items to 
the PPA. 
 
2.2.  The PPA, via delegated authority from the program office contracting office, shall be the sole 
Government activity with which the contractor interfaces on initial provisioning matters, unless 
specifically authorized by the PPA.  Pursuant to paragraph 2.1 and this paragraph, correspondence from 
the PPA shall be accepted and all provisioning actions therein accomplished unless otherwise directed 
by the Procuring Contracting Officer (PCO). 
 
3.  Conferences. 
 
3.1.  A Provisioning Guidance Conference (PGC) shall be scheduled by the PPA and should be held no 
later than 45 calendar days from receipt of contract by the PPA.  The PGC is normally held at Hill AFB, 
UT for approximately two days to ensure both the contractor and the government understand the 
provisioning requirements on contract.  If a PGC is not desired, the Contractor shall submit a written 
request for waiver of the PGC to the PPA.  In the event a waiver is approved, a mutual understanding of 
the Provisioning requirements must be communicated in some forum in which the AFMC Form 718 
(Provisioning Performance Schedule (PPS)) must be documented/completed, signed by government and 
contractor, and later mod’ed to the contract.   
 
3.2.  A Spares Provisioning Conference (SPC) is /is not  required.  If required, the SPC will be 
held at the contractor/vendor facility or the PPA.  The dates and time of the SPC along with specific 
requirements will be discussed at the PGC or during the completion of the AFMC Form 718 (PPS) if 
PGC is waived.  
 
3.3.  A sample article of the component/end item is /is not  required at the SPC.  If required, 
sample article will be viewed /disassembled  at the conference.  
 
 
4.  Manufacturers or Commercial Manuals are /are not  required.   When required furnish a 
manufacturer’s or commercial manual to supplement the Short Form Provisioning Parts Lists (SFPPL) or 
Provisioning Parts Lists (PPL) that have embedded Commercial Off-the-Shelf (COTS) equipment.  All 

 
publications prepared and printed without regard to Government format and outline, but which include a 
parts list will be acceptable as a manufacturer or commercial manual for the purpose of this requirement.  
This requirement applies only to available manuals for the end item or components thereof. No manuals 
will be developed to satisfy this requirement. 
 
5.  Interim Release (IR) is /is not  authorized. 
 
6.  Statement of Prior Submission (SPS) is required where applicable.    The SPS is submitted to 
certify that the contractor/subcontractor has/has not previously furnished to the Government PTD for the 
end item or any component thereof which may satisfy the PTD requirements of this contract.  The SPS 
will include identifying information (current procurement or previous submission) such as contract 
number, contract/exhibit line item number, end item/component type or model number/reference number, 
item name, manufacturer’s name and Commercial and Government Entity Code, PPA receiving the PTD 
and date prepared, NSN (if available) and other information as required by the PPA.  If the Government 
determines that the previously submitted data is adequate, the SPS may result in reduction or elimination 
of PTD and Engineering Data for Provisioning requirements specified on DD Form 1423 and conference 
requirements.   
 
7.  Provisioning Performance Schedule (PPS), AFMC Form 718.  PPS (Atch 1) will be developed by 
PPA and Contractor at the PGC or in other agreed upon format. 
 
8. Engineering Data for Provisioning (EDFP), SESS DI 81874: A drawing shall be provided for each 
first appearance (less drawings for MIL-SPEC CAGE Codes and Part Numbers) non-stock listed item 
appearing on the PTD. However, if the end item being provisioned was stock listed on a Support 
Equipment Recommendation Data (SERD) document, and the type Logistics Product Data is a PPL, an 
end item drawing with parts list is required to be able to have visibility of the PPL indenture breakdown. 
For provisioning purposes, EDFP order of precedence shall be: 
-Data equivalent to approved product engineering drawings. 
-Commercial drawings 
-Commercial manuals, when required to provide information on a commercial assembly. 
-Catalogs or catalog descriptions. 
-Sketches or photographs with brief descriptions of dimensional, materiel, mechanical, electrical, 
or other descriptive characteristics. When sketches or photographs are provided for an assembly, 
a bill of material shall also be provided. 
During the SPC, in the event an action requires linkage within D043A, it’s possible a drawing would be 
required for stock-numbered items for the purposes of linking a National Stock Number (NSN) with a Part 
Number. 
 
 
8.1.  Engineering Data for Provisioning (EDFP):  For provisioning purposes, EDFP shall be an integral 
part of the electronic 3D Model using Adobe® Acrobat® PDF format.  The EDFP will be annotated within 
the model to provide definitive identification of dimensional, material, mechanical, electrical, or other 
characteristics adequate to describe the end article(s) on contract.  The data known as geometry, 
dimension, and tolerance (GDT) is included in this definition of EDFP as is the data often referred to as 
form, fit, and function which indicates the physical characteristics, location, and functions of the item. 
 
If the EDFP is not retrievable from the 3D Model, then it must be provided with approved product 
engineering drawings that meets government requirements to fully describe each item of supply in its 
entirety. 
 
 
8.2.  Acceptable electronic media is Adobe
® Acrobat® PDF format. 
 

 
8.3.  Federal Supply Class (FSC) and Name assignment will be IAW DLA Logistics Information Services’ 
(DLA-LIS) Cataloging Handbooks H2 and H6. 
 
9.  Design Change Notices (DCN).  DCNs will include all changes required to an item previously 
presented by all types of PTDs to align spares support with actual production items.  Unless specifically 
instructed otherwise by the PPA, the contractor shall notify the PPA of any and all changes whether of a 
production or modification type which are approved for incorporation into the system/equipment 
furnished under the contract. DCNs are to be accompanied by applicable EDFP (3D Models).   
 
9.1.   Changes resulting from omission or correction of data previously submitted are considered 
administrative changes.  This type of change may be submitted in non-standard PTD formats to include 
business letter, computer lists, etc., as directed by the PPA at the PGC.    
 
9.2.  Reference Number Changes.  Reference numbers are not to be rolled or changed unless 
specifically allowed by applicable specifications.  New design numbers are not to be assigned strictly for 
administrative or manufacturing purposes, or to facilitate the production control process. 
 
9.3.  Reference Items.  Submit DCNs against only the first appearance items, unless specifically 
instructed otherwise by the PPA. 
 
9.4.  DCNs to document changes made during the provisioning process by the Government to previously 
submitted PTD shall not be submitted. 
 
9.5.  Procurable Type Items.  DCNs for procurable type items are required to be submitted within twenty-
one (21) days after release for fabrication or procurement for prime contractor design items and forty-two 
(42) days after release for fabrication and procurement of subcontractor supplied items.  
 
9.5.1.  DCNs Requiring Revision to Provisioned Item Orders (PIO).  When a design change affects any 
part ordered by the government, the contractor shall take immediate action to affect the following 
revisions and incorporate the results on DCNs for approval: 
 
9.5.1.1.  Deletions.  When a design change reduces or eliminates spare/repair parts requirements for the 
end item/component, the contractor shall delete or reduce such requirements originally ordered by PIO in 
the ratio authorized by the program data applicable to the end items on order that are affected by the 
DCN. 
 
9.5.1.2.  Adjustments.  When a spare/repair part previously ordered by the Government is replaced by 
another item, and the replacing part is not stocklisted, the contractor shall fabricate or procure the new 
item in the same ratio as the number of end items/components affected by the change not to exceed the 
amount funded for affected items.  When the adjustment requires an increase in the total quantity 
recommended or additional items of support, the increase will be recommended by the contractor in 
accordance with program data provided by the PPA. 
 
9.6.  Non-procurable Type Items.  When required by the PPA, design change data for non-procurable 
type items (items not coded as spares) (Source, Maintenance, Recoverability (SMR) Code first position 
X, A, M, K) will be prepared in accordance with instructions from the PPA.  Submittals will be within sixty 
(60) days after release for fabrication or purchase. 
 
10.  PTD Submittal Specifications.  The following paragraphs provide specifications for submission of  
PTD by multiple card image to be compatible with the AFMC Automated Provisioning System  
(hereafter referred to as the D220 System or its replacement system).  Strict adherence to these instructions must be 
 applied to ensure PTD is accepted by the D220 System.  Data elements to be included in the PTD are reflected  
in paragraph 12, Logistics Product Data Selection Table.  
           

 
10.1. Media/Software.  Acceptable electronic media files will be submitted via DoDSafe, Government program 
Specific electronic site or e-mail attachment. Submit e-mails with electronic PTD to gbmsp.Provisioning@us.af.mil. 
The subject line on the e-mail or DoDSafe as a minimum will cite the Contract number, PCCN, and SCC.  
 
10.1.1. Data may be input using Microsoft WORD and with the paragraph marker on, this will enable the 
spaces to be seen at all times.  
 
10.1.2.  Ensure margins are such that each line is exactly 80 characters as outlined in IPPS para 10.3.1. 
through 10.5.4.5 of the IPPS.  NOTE:  Do Not use the Tab key.   
 
10.1.3. First line of data will be the actual PTD header card as called out in IPPS para 10.3.1.   
 
10.1.4.  Blank lines between entries are not acceptable.  Do not put header, footer or page number in the 
page setup for the document.  Data must be saved as a Text file (.txt) file. 
 
10.1.4. Do not submit encrypted data.  D220 Provisioning system is for unclassified data only and D220 
does not have encryption capabilities. 
 
10.2.  Security Classification of Data.  Classified data (programs or line item data) cannot be entered 
into the D220 System.  Classified data is processed outside the D220 System using contingency  
operating procedures as program directed. 
 
10.3.  PTD Format and Summary Layout.  Government provided.  Refer to Attachment 2 for D220 
record format layout.  
             
10.3.1.  Header Card.  Required for all types and submissions of PTD. 
 
10.3.1.1.  CC 1-6, enter PCCN which will be provided at PGC. 
 
10.3.1.2.  CC 7-25, enter Procurement Instrument Identification Number (PIIN).  Do not use dashes.  
Alpha characters must be upper case. 
 
10.3.1.3.  CC 26-46, enter Model or Type No. 
 
10.3.1.4.  CC 47-56, Control Data: 
 
10.3.1.4.1.  CC 47, enter appropriate type PTD Code.  Mandatory entry.  This code, peculiar to the Air 
Force, identifies the type of PTD being submitted.  PTD code must be one of the codes defined below:

NATIONAL AERONAUTICS AND SPACE ADMINISTRATION 
John F. Kennedy Space Center  
Justification for an Exception to Fair Opportunity 
for 
Engineering Services During Construction 
of Repair Culverts, Various Locations, Phase 2, 
 KSC, FL, Project Control Number: 99588.1 
 
Description of the action being approved: This justification documents the basis for issuing an 
order under the Southeast Regional Architect and Engineer (SERAE) contract 
80KSC022DA119, Jones Edmunds, using an exception to the Fair Opportunity process. 
 
Description of the supplies or services required to meet the agency’s needs: This action is a 
firm-fixed price order, for architect and engineering (A&E) services during the Engineering 
Services During Construction (ESDC) of Repair Culverts, Various Locations, Phase 2, PCN 
99588.1 The total estimated price of the proposed order is $ and the estimated period of 
performance is 224 calendar days from date of award. 
 
Identification of Exception to Fair Opportunity: 
 
 FAR 16.505(b)(2)(i)(A), The agency need for the supplies or services is so urgent that providing 
a fair opportunity would result in unacceptable delays. 
 
 FAR 16.505(b)(2)(i)(B), Only one awardee is capable of providing the supplies or services 
required at the level of quality required because the supplies or services ordered are unique or 
highly specialized. 
 
 FAR 16.505(b)(2)(i)(C), The order must be issued on a sole-source basis in the interest of 
economy and efficiency because it is a logical follow-on to an order already issued under the 
contract, provided that all awardees were given a fair opportunity to be considered for the 
original order. 
 
 FAR 16.505(b)(2)(i)(D), It is necessary to place an order to satisfy a minimum guarantee. 
 
 FAR 16.505(b)(2)(i)(E), For orders exceeding the simplified acquisition threshold a statute 
expressly authorizes or requires that the purchase be made from a specified source.  
 
 FAR 16.505(b)(2)(i)(F), In accordance with section 1331 of Public Law 111-240 (15 U.S.C. 
644(r)), contracting officers may, at their discretion, set aside orders for any of the small 
business concerns identified in 19.000(a)(3). When setting aside orders for small business 
concerns, the specific small business program eligibility requirements identified in part 19 apply.  
 
 FAR 16.505(b)(2)(i)(G), The order satisfies one of the exceptions permitting the use of other 
than full and open competition listed in 6.302 (10 U.S.C. 3406(c)(5). The public interest 
exception shall not be used unless Congress is notified in accordance with 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(7). 


2 
Rev.:3/2025 
 
Supporting Rationale:  
 
The requirement for the design of the Repair Culverts, Various Locations, Phase 2, was issued through a 
Request for Technical Qualifications Narrative (TQN) to the nine A&E firms under the multiple-award 
SERAE contract: 
 
x 80KSC022DA114 – BRPH Architects Engineers, Inc. (BRPH),  
x 80KSC022DA115 – Merrick,  
x 80KSC022DA116 – RS&H, Inc. (RS&H),  
x 80KSC022DA117 – AECOM Technical Services, Inc. (AECOM),  
x 80KSC022DA118 – TSGHD AF JV1(TSGHD),  
x 80KSC022DA119 – Jones, Edmunds & Associates, Inc (JE),  
x 80KSC022DA120 – Johnson-McAdams Firm, P.A., THE (JMA),  
x 80KSC022DA121 – Nelson Engineering Company (Nelson),  
x 80KSC022DA122 – Jacobs Engineering Group Inc. (Jacobs).  
 
Five firms of the nine submitted TQN narratives; AECOM, Jacobs, Jones Edmunds, Nelson, and 
TSGHD AF JV1. Each TQN was evaluated, and Jones Edmunds was selected to provide a fee 
proposal on July 19, 2023. 
 
Jones Edmunds has been involved in the design of this project from the beginning, their expertise and 
knowledge in this area has increased since that selection. Jones Edmunds is the only A&E firm with the 
specialized expertise and knowledge of the engineering requirements and location specifics of Repair 
Culverts, Various Locations, Phase 2 at KSC. This previous experience provides necessary information 
that Jones Edmunds has the necessary tools to effectively perform the ESDC engineering services in 
support of the construction activities associated with this project. 
 
Jones Edmunds is the Engineer of Record (EOR) for the design and possesses unique, site-specific 
knowledge of the design intent, permitting constraints, and environmental considerations. Their 
continued involvement is essential for efficient and accurate ESDC, including: 
 
x Technical review and disposition of submittals, RFIs, and deviation/waiver requests 
x Site visits and engineering analysis 
x Clarification of design documents and specifications. 
 
Engaging a different firm would require significant time and cost for the new contractor to review and 
assume responsibility for the design, which could delay construction and increase risk. Therefore, this 
action qualifies under FAR 16.505(b)(2)(i)(C) as a logical follow-on to a previously issued order under 
the SERAE contract, where all awardees were given a fair opportunity to compete. 

3 
Rev.:3/2025 
 
Determination that the anticipated cost to the Government will be fair and reasonable: 
 
The Government will ensure a fair and reasonable price through the following steps: 
 
x Use of Pre-Negotiated Rates: The contractor will utilize labor hour rates established under the 
SERAE Advanced Pricing Rate Agreement (APRA), which were previously determined to be 
fair and reasonable and are part of Jones Edmunds base award, 80KSC022D0A119, awarded 
on September 10, 2021. 
x Technical Evaluation: The Government will conduct a technical evaluation of the proposed 
hours and labor categories. This includes math verification, comparison to the Independent 
Government Cost Estimate (IGCE), and review of historical labor hours for similar efforts. 
x Negotiation (if necessary): The Government reserves the right to negotiate proposed hours to 
ensure alignment with the scope and value of the effort. 
 
These steps are consistent with FAR 15.404-1 and will ensure the Government receives best value. 
 
Other Facts:  
 
Jones Edmunds previously performed the design of this project under Task Order 80KSC024FA091, 
valued at , and demonstrated successful  performance as reflected on their CPARS 
evaluation. Their specialized knowledge as the EOR will result in labor cost savings and reduce the 
risk of design misinterpretation. If another firm were selected, it would require approximately 30% 
more labor cost to the ESDC contract to review and assume responsibility for the design. This would 
also introduce delays and increase the risk of errors during construction. 
 
A statement of the actions, if any, the agency may take to remove or overcome any barriers 
that led to the restricted consideration before any subsequent acquisition for the supplies or 
services is made:  
 
The CO will continue to examine the market in the future for alternative solutions or new sources 
before executing any subsequent acquisitions for the same requirements.

2019.

knowledge in this area has increased since that selection. Nelson is the only A&E firm with the 
specialized expertise and knowledge of the engineering requirements and location specifics of the 
Electrical Substation USS-833A/B (13.8kV/480V) at the Vehicle Assembly Building Repeater

necessary tools to effectively perform the ESDC engineering services in support of the

construction for the S&RU Power Phase 6 project. Additionally, Nelson is the engineering firm of

specialized, making it challenging for another firm to replicate without a thorough understanding 
of the context in which it was designed. A new award and effort to review the design as a new 
EOR would impact the schedule by 4 months or more before the project can proceed.

SPECIAL NOTICE DARPA-SN-26-60 
Disruption through Intelligent Strategies, Counter Options, and Resilient Defenses 
(DISCORD) Proposers Day 
EVENT DATE: 7 May 2026, 9:30 AM – 5:00 PM Eastern Time (ET)
REGISTRATION DEADLINE: 28 APRIL 2026, 3:00 PM ET
REGISTRATION WEBSITE: https://creative.spa.com/darpa/sto/discord/pd/
TECHNICAL POC: Dr. Eric Davis, STO Program Manager
E-MAIL: DARPA‐SN‐26-60@darpa.mil
PROPOSERS DAY:
DARPA will host a Proposers Day in support of DARPA-PS-26-27, the DISCORD program on 
7 May 2026 at the SPA Arlington Research Collaboration Center (SPARCC), 4075 Wilson 
Blvd., Arlington, Virginia 22203 from 9:30 AM to 5:00 PM ET. The purpose of this conference 
is to provide information on the DISCORD program; promote additional discussion on this topic; 
address questions from potential proposers; and provide a forum for potential proposers to 
present their capabilities for teaming opportunities.  
PROGRAM OBJECTIVE AND DESCRIPTION: The objective of the DISCORD program is 
to develop an Artificial Intelligence (AI)-native1 tactics engine that can incorporate live sensor 
data and high-fidelity simulation to rapidly generate tactics that continuously adapt to changes in 
the operational environment. The goal is to provide commanders with a portfolio of diverse 
strategies that can pivot dynamically in response to evolving conditions.    
The DARPA DISCORD effort implements Ender’s Foundry, one of several warfighting Pace-
Setting Projects (PSPs) established by the Department of War. Ender’s Foundry’s intent is to 
accelerate AI-enabled simulation capabilities to ensure we stay ahead of AI-enabled adversaries.
REGISTRATION INFORMATION: DARPA hosts Proposers Days to promote teaming 
arrangements between researchers; provide potential performers with information on whether 
and how they might respond to the Government’s research and development solicitations; and to 
increase efficiency in proposal preparation and evaluation. Therefore, Proposers Days are open 
only to registered potential proposers.
Participants must register NLT 3:00 PM ET on 28 April 2026 at the following website: 
https://creative.spa.com/darpa/sto/discord/pd/. Due to space limitations of the conference facility, 
attendance will be limited to the first 80 registrants, and no more than 2 representatives per 
organization. Directions to the facility and other materials are also available on the website. 
There is no registration fee for attending this conference.
The DISCORD Proposers Day will include Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) and all 
attendees must be either U.S. Citizens or U.S. Persons. It is important to understand that a non-
U.S. citizen can either be a foreign person or a U.S. person.
1 AI-native refers to shifting workflows the same way computer-native workflows did in the 1980s, and internet-
native workflows did in the 2000s.  The new technologies must be developed and incorporated into workflows as a 
first principle, fully enabling the warfighter in the 21st century to fight with AI tools custom built for DoW 
purposes.

- A foreign person is any person who is not a lawful permanent resident of the United 
States, e.g., students or employees legally in the U.S. with a valid student or work visa.
- A U.S. person, which includes those known as “Green Card holders”, is a person who is a 
lawful permanent resident of the United States or who is a protected individual as defined 
by 8 U.S.C.1101(a)(20) or 8 U.S.C.1324b(a)(3).
CUI managed by DARPA, to include CUI that is NOFORN or EXPORT CONTROLLED, may 
be disclosed to U.S. Persons if they are a performer on a DARPA S&T proposal team or, if they 
are a performer who has been awarded a DARPA S&T project and their sponsoring institution 
has agreed to comply with DoD CUI policies and procedures as detailed in either DoD 5200.48, 
DFARS 252.204-7012, 7019, and 7020, or similarly acceptable guidance and direction.
All non-U.S. Citizen registrants must complete and submit a DARPA Form 60. All DARPA 
Form 60s must be submitted no later than 3:00 PM on 28 April 2026. 
Upon entry to a physical meeting, all attendees will be required to present valid, Government-
issued photo identification. Examples of approved forms of ID are available at the DARPA 
Visitor Information page.
Attendees who would like to present company overviews, discuss their technology expertise, 
and/or discuss teaming opportunities in scheduled presentations at the meeting should contact 
DISCORD@darpa.mil as soon as possible, but no later than the registration cutoff date for the 
Proposer Day. Presentations are limited to three (3) minutes each (including logistical issues) and 
only one (1) Microsoft PowerPoint slide (no build, no animation). Please include your contact 
information on your slide in a legible font. 
All material to be displayed at Proposers Day must be approved in advance by both the 
organization that funded the research and the DARPA Program Manager. The DARPA Program 
Manager will screen the proposed material for sensitive but unclassified material and approve in 
advance any presentations. It is the presenter’s responsibility to ensure that all material they plan 
to present at the Proposers Day has been approved by the funding organization in advance. An 
electronic copy of all material to be presented must be provided to DISCORD@darpa.mil no 
later than 3:00 PM ET on 30 April 2026. There will be no exceptions to this requirement. 
Companies are free to present, but DARPA does not sponsor that information on the Agency 
website.
DARPACONNECT: For those new to DARPA or national security, DARPA makes available a 
free, comprehensive resource via DARPAConnect on how to do business with the agency. In 
addition to DARPA 101 materials, relevant preparatory modules include “Making the Most of a 
Proposers Day” and “Understanding DARPA Broad Agency Announcements.” Registration and 
access are free at http://www.darpaconnect.us/.

This is a sources sought synopsis to determine the availability of potential sources capable of providing 
support services for Department of the Navy Chief Information Officer (DON CIO) – Information 
Technology Division (ITD).  The contractor shall provide support in the following areas: database 
administration, software development, data center operational support, data center migration, advanced 
system and network administration, information assurance, portfolio management, customer services and 
helpdesk, Video Teleconferencing (VTC), telecommunications, NMCI tech refreshes, mobility and 
wireless equipment upgrades, inventory logs, maintenance of SharePoint server farms and sites, portal 
upgrades, and engineering/development/integration of DON CIO Claimancy/SECNAV Headquarters’ 
hardware, software, and related systems. The contractor shall provide IT and IT-related support services 
in classified and unclassified areas, in accordance with this Performance Work Statement (PWS).  The 
effort includes recurring system support to new and legacy equipment and associated subsystems for 
failure analysis; configuration management; preparation, installation, testing of field change kits; system 
mission related support; and system management support.  This effort also includes over-the-horizon 
radar (OTHR) research, development, test, and evaluation (RDT&E) activities. 
The primary places of performance for work under this contract deployed either directly or indirectly to 
support DUSN(M) customers across the Navy Headquarters within the National Capital Region (NCR) including 
sites located at the Pentagon, Washington Navy Yard. This requirement is currently under contract 
N0018920F3058, through Booz Allen Hamilton (BAH) who is currently one of the companies with the 
knowledge and expertise to support this very unique system in accordance with the requirements 
described above.  
The anticipated ordering period for this Cost-Plus-Fixed Fee procurement is from Jul 5, 2026, through Jul 
4, 2027, with four (4) one (1) year options pursuant to FAR 52.217-9, including the 6-month option 
period pursuant to FAR 52.217-8. If all options are exercised in accordance with FAR 52.217-9, the 
contract ends Jan 4,2032. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code 
is 541330 - Engineering Services. It is expected that the award will be made no later than Jun 8, 2026, to 
allow services to begin on Jul 5, 2026. Interested offerors with a SeaPort NxG contract and possess the 
requisite experience, skills, resources, and capabilities necessary to perform the stated requirement are 
invited to respond to this market research survey/source sought synopsis by providing their capability 
information via the submission of an executive summary, no more than two (2) pages in length. The 
submission shall include the following information: (1) company name, address, point of contact with 
corresponding phone number and email address; and business size; and (2) relevant corporate experience 
information. Relevant corporate experience information is defined as experience that is of the same or 
similar scope, magnitude, and complexity to that which is described herein. This relevant corporate 
experience information should identify a customer point of contact with corresponding telephone number 
and email address. All submissions are required to be submitted via email to Tara Baker at 
tara.y.baker.civ@us.navy.mil no later than 12:00PM, EST on 22 April 2026. Please direct any questions 
concerning this sources sought synopsis to Tara Baker at tara.y.baker.civ@us.navy.mil.

DEFENSE LOGISTICS AGENCY (DLA) TRANSPORTATION PROCESS SUPPORT ADDENDUM TO FAR 52.212-2 EVALUATION- COMMERCIAL ITEMS ATTACHMENT 2  

Selection Process

The Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) Transportation Process Support requirement will utilize the Trade-off evaluation process where technical approach, key personnel, management and staffing plan, and past performance when combined are significantly more important than total price. The tradeoff process is appropriate when it is in the best interest of the government to consider award(s) to other than the lowest priced quoter or other than the highest technically rated quoter.  This process permits trade-offs among cost or price and non-cost/price factors and allows the government to accept other than the lowest priced offer.  The perceived benefits of the higher priced offer must merit the additional cost/price, and the rationale for trade-offs must be documented in the contract file. The government’s objective is to obtain the highest quality services considered necessary to achieve the required objectives. When using the trade-off process, all of the evaluation factors that will affect the task order issuance and their relative importance must be clearly stated in the solicitation.

Evaluation Factors

Evaluation factors represent those specific characteristics that are tied to the request for quote (RFQ) requirements and are expected to be discriminators or are required by statute/regulation.  They are the uniform baseline against which each contractor’s quote is evaluated allowing the government to make a best value determination.  The evaluation factors, their relative order of importance, and the importance of non-price to price factors must be set forth in the solicitation in enough depth to communicate what will be evaluated.  The evaluation factors will be the primary determinant of the detailed information requested in the solicitation’s instructions to contractors.  

Relative importance.  All non-price evaluation factors when combined are significantly more important than price.  The non-price evaluation factors are of equal importance.  As the non-price evaluation factors become more equal among quotes, the evaluated price becomes more important.

Basis for award(s).  Quotes will first be evaluated on the basis of the non-price evaluation factors as defined below.  The non-price evaluation factors include the following: Technical Approach, Key Personnel, Management and Staffing Plan, and Past Performance. Key Personnel will be evaluated as Acceptable or Unacceptable. Past Performance will be evaluated by the Contracting Officer as Acceptable or Unacceptable. Pricing will be evaluated for accuracy, fairness, reasonableness, and completeness.  The task order will be issued to the contractor whose quote offers the best value to the government based on the PWS requirements and the established evaluation factors. Each non-price factor (Technical Approach, Key Personnel, Management and Staffing Plan, and Past Performance) will be rated independently, and the non-price factor ratings for Technical Approach and Management and Staffing Plan will be rolled up into an overall rating.  A quote determined to be Unacceptable in either Key Personnel or Past Performance will not be eligible for award.

Factor 1 Technical Approach

Quoters must provide a capability statement detailing their technical abilities in performing the work outlined in the performance work statement. Ratings will be in accordance with Table 1 below and based on the technical proficiency that the contractor provides in their response.

Factor 2 Key Personnel

Key Personnel will be evaluated on an Acceptable/Unacceptable basis.  In order to be found Acceptable, quotes must include resumes and letters of intent (LOI) for all key personnel provided within its quote; but at minimum for each of the two Key Personnel positions listed in the PWS. Key personnel must meet all of the key personnel education and experience requirements that are listed in the performance work statement (PWS). Ratings will be in accordance with Table 2 below.

Factor 3 Management and Staffing Plan

Ratings will be in accordance with Table 1 below and the management plan will be evaluated to ensure that, at a minimum, the management plan explains how the contractor will successfully perform the following: 

The task order management and issue resolution.

The ability to recruit qualified personnel that will be able to fulfill the solicitation and PWS requirement. This includes the ability to address turn-over rate and rapidly hire and train personnel in a dynamic environment with changing workloads. 

The ability to retain qualified personnel. 

Please provide a personnel replacement plan that aligns with section V Personnel Issues of the PWS.

The contractor understands the work as evidenced by the proposed plan for overall implementation and execution.

Evidence of a process for ensuring quality and timeliness of deliverables.

A draft Quality Control Plan (QCP) must be submitted as well. This draft qualify control plan must outline the processes that the contractor will implement to ensure that the staffing and procedures for self-inspecting the quality, timeliness, responsiveness, and other performance requirements in the PWS are met.

Factor 4 Past Performance

The past performance evaluation will determine whether the government has a reasonable expectation that the quoter will successfully perform on this contract base on its prior contracts in accordance with Table 3, below. Past performance information will be based on the quote submittal, Contractor Performance Assessment Reporting System (CPARS) reports, and other government data systems. If a contractor does not have past performance data in these systems, the Contracting Officer may request government points of contact for references. The government will consider the following in determining past performance acceptability:

a. Relevancy. Past performance data will be reviewed for relevancy to the current solicitation. Relevant past performance data is a stronger predictor of future success. Past performance relevancy will be rated as either relevant or not relevant.

b. Recency. Past performance data will be reviewed for recency, which is defined as within the past three (3) years. Past performance recency will be rated as either recent or not recent.

c. Quality. Evaluation of past performance data will be based on actual ratings received in CPARS for technical/quality, schedule, cost, and management. If CPARS ratings are not available, the Contracting Officer may request two to five government points of contact (POCs) to provide past performance information. Past performance quality will be rated as either acceptable or unacceptable.

In order for a quote to be determined as acceptable in past performance, each offered past performance effort is required to be relevant, recent, and its quality acceptable.

Please provide contract number, POC, and a brief description of the most relevant, recent, and quality contract(s). 

NOTE: In the case of a quoter without a record of past performance or for whom information on past performance is not available or is so sparse that no meaningful past performance rating can be reasonably assigned, the quoter may not be evaluated favorably or unfavorably on past performance. Therefore, the quoter must be determined to have unknown (or “neutral”) past performance. In the context of acceptability/unacceptability, a neutral rating must be considered “acceptable.”

Unacceptable Rating: If a quoter receives a rating of unacceptable in either key personnel or past performance, then the quote is determined unacceptable. 

Total Price

Contractors must submit pricing using Attachment 4 DLA Transportation Process Support Schedule B spreadsheet that was provided. Please ensure all Excel calculations, equations, etc. are viewable, in-tact, and unprotected, limit dollar amounts to two decimal places.

J3 TRANSPORTATION PROCESS SUPPORT

Performance Work Statement

INTRODUCTION

BACKGROUND

The Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) is working with Department of Defense (DoD) and non-DoD stakeholders, various audit organizations (e.g., the General Services Administration (GSA), the Government Accountability Office (GAO), the DoD Inspector General (DoD IG), and the DLA Accountability Office), and commercial partners (e.g., U.S. Bank) to enhance and improve transportation financial management (TFM) processes and their associated automated tools and controls.  The primary goal of this effort is to improve stewardship of transportation expenditures.

DLA’s financial statements are audited annually by an independent public accountant (IPA).  During the audit, the IPA may request meetings with DLA to gain a full understanding of DLA processes and may also request that DLA provide information, documents, or answers to specific questions.  These requests are called provided by client (PBC).  As a result of the audit, the IPA may provide findings called notice of findings and recommendations (NFRs).  In response to NFRs, DLA defines corrective actions and schedules for implementation.

Organizations and contractors may perform work on behalf of DLA that impacts DLA’s financial statements.  When this occurs, the organizations and contractors are service organizations in relation to DLA, and DLA must obtain assurance that they have effective controls over their respective processes.  Organizations and contractors may provide this assurance by engaging an IPA to perform an examination in accordance with the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants (AICPA) Statement on Standards for Attestation Engagements No. 18 (SSAE No. 18) AT-C section 320, Reporting on an Examination of Controls at a Service Organization Relevant to User Entities’ Internal Control Over Financial Reporting.  That examination results in a System and Organization Controls (SOC) 1 Type 2 Report that is provided to their user entities.  A SOC 1 Type 2 Report is a report on controls at the service organization that are relevant to a user entity’s (such as DLA) internal control over financial reporting. Department of Homeland Security Customs & Border Protection (CBP) Statement of Work 
(SOW) for Illegal Transshipment Pilot 
1.0 BACKGROUND  
 
U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) plays a critical role in the enforcement of trade 
regulations and the collection of customs revenue, positioning itself as the nation’s second 
largest revenue collection agency. In Fiscal Year 2025, CBP successfully collected $216.7 
billion in duties, taxes, and fees, continuing a legacy of robust enforcement that has led to the 
collection of 99.5% of all customs tariff revenue owed to the U.S. since 1992.  
 
Despite this high collection rate, unscrupulous importers continue to engage in deceptive 
practices to evade antidumping and countervailing duties, tariffs, and other trade regulations, 
harming compliant business and eroding the revenue base. Chief among these deceptive 
practices are illegal transshipment schemes, or the act of routing of goods through a third country 
to obscure their true country of origin and avoid higher tariffs.  
 
To combat illegal transshipment, CBP has intensified its enforcement efforts by leveraging 
advanced technology, data analytics, and partnerships with other federal agencies 
and industry partners. These measures aim to detect and prevent illegal transshipment and other 
illicit schemes, ensuring compliance with trade laws and protecting U.S. economic interests.  
 
Under the Illegal Transshipment Pilot, CBP will explore whether Artificial Intelligence (AI) 
technology solutions offered by the private sector can help uncover illegal transshipment 
schemes at scale and with a high degree of accuracy. This technology demonstration presents 
opportunities for the private sector and CBP to identify enforcement efficiencies and maximize 
revenue collection.   
 
 
2.0 SCOPE   
CBP will assess the value of Artificial Intelligence (AI) driven commercial solutions that identify 
imports which pose a high risk for illegal transshipment. The development and implementation of 
these private sector solutions will enable CBP to explore how cutting -edge technologies may be 
leveraged to inform enforcement actions that prevent high- risk imports from entering the U.S. 
and/or lead to the identification of additional duties owed. 
 
Vendors will deliver insights about illegal transshipment risk via  referral packages  to CBP. 
Referral packages shall articulate specific risk factors that vendors believe are indicative of illegal 
transshipment. Referral packages must also identify or be easily traced to imports that are in transit 
and have not yet arrived in the U.S . To support this requirement, vendors may choose to receive 
the below manifest information for imports originating from countries that CBP identifies as being 
higher risk for illegal transshipment. CBP will make manifest information available to vendors no 
later than 72 hours before imports are expected to arrive in the U.S.   
 
• Port of Unlading 
• Port of Lading 
• Arrival Date 
• Bill Number 

5 
 
• HTS Code 
• Shipper 
• Consignee 
• Cargo Description 
• Declared Country of Origin 
 
Vendors will be given an opportunity to prove out the scalability and accuracy of their illegal 
transshipment solutions over the course of a no-cost, 180-day base period of performance. 
Scalability will be measured by the number of actionable referral packages vendors submit to 
CBP. Accuracy will be measured by the percentage of referral packages that lead to the 
prevention of high-risk imports from entering the U.S. and/or the identification of additional 
duties owed. CBP will have full discretion over which referral packages to investigate based on 
confidence levels, potential revenue impact, ongoing or previous enforcement actions, and 
resource availability. Only referral packages that CBP chooses to investigate and act upon will 
be factored into its assessment of accuracy.  
 
Vendors who achieve the performance milestones defined in Section 6.0 may have their option 
periods exercised by CBP.  
 
The solutions delivered under the Illegal Transshipment Pilot as outlined in this SOW must drive 
enhancements and efficiencies around targeting for illegal transshipment, maximizing the 
collection of revenue owed to the U.S., and allocation of CBP resources towards areas of highest 
revenue risk. The desired end state for this SOW is to identify AI-driven solutions that 
demonstrate the ability to accurately detect illegal transshipment at a rate of 90 percent or 
higher—all without exposure to law enforcement sensitive algorithms , CBP’s targeting models, 
and other sensitive data sets.  
 
 
3.0 PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE   
The contract base period of performance is intended to be 180 days and may contain up to two 
options.  
 
 
4.0 TYPE OF CONTRACT 
This award will establish a Non-FAR Contract through the DHS Commercial Solution Opening 
Pilot Program (CSOP). 
 
5.0  POINTS OF CONTACT 
Contracting Officer: Peter Giambone 
Email: PETER.A.GIAMBONE@CBP.DHS.GOV  
  Contract Specialist: Aristide Horugayve 
   Email: aristide.horugavye@cbp.dhs.gov

Based Period Deliverables 
Vendors shall submit illegal transshipment referral packages to CBP via email in accordance

they:

and,  
• Must contain substantive supporting evidence (minimum of five pages) with which to 
make high-confidence decisions about illegal transshipment risk.  
During the base period of performance, vendors will be asked to progressively demonstrate the 
scalability and accuracy of their solutions in 60-day increments. CBP will provide regularly 
scheduled feedback on whether referral packages:  
• Meet the above criteria for being considered actionable; and,  
• Lead to the prevention of high-risk imports being released into the U.S. and/or the 
identification of additional duties owed.  
CBP may at any time issue a stop work order to vendors who are unable to meet or exceed the 
scalability and accuracy thresholds for each 60-day increment.

7.1 Information Technology Security Compliance Requirements 
The contractor shall adhere to all DHS and CBP IT security policies and the basic requirements, 
security authorization, encryption compliance, and pass security review. 
 
7.1.1 DHS Security Policy Compliance Requirements  
All hardware, software, and services provided under this CSOP contract must be compliant with 
DHS 4300A, the DHS Management Directive 140-01, and Information Security Program and 
CBP Information Systems Security Policies and Procedures Directive, HB 1400-05D.  
7.1.2 Basic Requirements 
The contractor shall adhere to all DHS and CBP IT security policies listed in the applicable 
documents section, including the guidelines and policies stated in the DHS Sensitive Systems 
Policy Directive 4300A or any subsequent, replacement or revised publication. This policy 
mandates DHS organizational elements, including contractors, follow guidelines outlined in the 
DHS MD 4300A, DHS Sensitive Systems Directive, Information Technology Security Program, 
Version 13, with attachments or any subsequent, replacement or revised publication. 
DHS Directive 4300A, Basic Requirements outlines the management, operational and 
technical baseline security requirements (BLSR) for DHS Components to ensure 
confidentiality, integrity, availability, authenticity, and non-repudiation of sensitive 
information systems. The 4300A Directive provides greater detail of the BLSRs, including

Health Information System and Technology Architecture (VistA) Chemotherapy 
Manager (VCM) term software licenses with maintenance and support for all eight 
Veterans Integrated Service Network (VISN) 23 facilities. 
 
3. Description of the Supplies or Services : The VA, Veterans Health Administration 
(VHA) VISN 23 has a requirement for the renewal of eight brand name DSS VCM term 
software licenses with maintenance and support. The software shall interface with the 
VA legacy electronic health record, VistA/Computerized Patient Record System 
(CPRS). The licenses are required for the following facilities within VISN 23: 
Minneapolis VA Health Care System, VA Nebraska-Western Iowa Health Care 
System (includes Omaha VA Medical Center, Lincoln, and Grand Island), Iowa City 
VA Health Care System, Des Moines VA Central Iowa Health Care System, Fargo VA 
Health Care System, Sioux Falls VA Health Care System, VA Black Hills Health Care 
System (includes Hot Springs and Fort Meade), and St. Cloud VA Health Care 
System. 
 
VCM is a VA specific windows-based software decision support and ordering system 
that is fully integrated with VistA and provides seamless electronic interaction between 
the ordering oncologist and pharmacist. The VCM software must constantly 
communicate with VistA to pull up a patient’s latest vitals, lab results, pharmacy orders 
to allow the physicians to make informed treatment decisions at any given time during 
the patient’s treatment. The system must also be able to send data back to VistA for 
populating progress notes, lab information, pharmacy orders, and nursing orders in 
the patient’s chart in the electronic health record (EHR). This integration allows the 
oncologist to have an extremely efficient method for preventing medication errors due 
to misinterpretation of hand-written orders. This software is focused on patient safety 
and ensures that prescription order sets are integrated and complete and that dosing 
is appropriate. With VCM, the clinical practice of oncology in VA becomes automated 
from the assignment of therapy to the calculation of chemotherapy doses and to the 
documentation of care. Patient safety is maximized, clinical efficiency is increased, 
patient information is secure, and documentation of patient care is streamlined due to 
existing interfaces with VistA/CPRS. VA requires brand name DSS VCM term 
software licenses with maintenance and support as it aligns with the existing VA VCM 
infrastructure, protocol, and functionality and will allow VISN 23 to maintain 

DSS VISTA Chemotherapy Manager Control VA-26-00043056 
2 
operational availability. The required DSS VCM software with maintenance and 
support provides VHA staff with the resources necessary to provide safe and accurate 
care to the Veterans. The contractor-provided software maintenance ensures the 
software functions as intended and includes all new fixes, patches, corrections, 
releases, updates, versions, and upgrades to the software. Technical support consists 
of the contractor providing a range of services and assistance for the software via 
telephone, e-mail, and/or website, available Monday through Friday from 8am to 5pm 
Central time zone. The period of performance is June 6, 2026, through June 5, 2027. 
The total estimated price of the proposed action is . 
4. Statutory Authority Cited: Pursuant to  Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR)
Revolutionary Overhaul VA Deviation 16.507-7(b) the following brand name
requirement is being justified and approved as an exception to fair opportunity under
the statutory authority of Section 41 U.S.C. 4106(c)(2) as implemented by FAR
Revolutionary Overhaul VA Deviation 16.507-6(b)(2) titled “Only one awardee is
capable of providing the supplies or services required at the level of quality required
because the supplies or services ordered are unique or highly specialized”.
5. Rationale Supporting Use of Authority Cited: Based on the market research described
in Section 8 of this justification, it has been determined that limited competition is
available for the brand name DSS term software licenses with maintenance and
support among authorized resellers. The software licenses are required to ensure
VHA VISN 23 can use chemotherapy software that interfaces with VistA and that the
chemotherapy software system remains operational and has the required
maintenance and support to provide software updates and patches. VISN 23 facilities
are currently scheduled to transition to VA’s new EHR in June 2027. Based upon
previous acquisition history, any other solution would require extensive development,
time for a transition, and time for implementation and training on the new system. The
costs due to VistA’s programming language and interfacing requirements are
estimated to be approximately $1,750,000.00. In addition, the timeline is estimated to
be a minimum of 3 years to develop an enterprise-grade solution. Some of the work to
transition to a new VCM solution includes specifications receiving for hardware, server
approval including authority to operate with VA Office of Information Technology and
VA Healthcare Technology Management approval, server setup, interface
development with possible code modification for system mapping to HL7 industry
standard requirements, interface testing and regression testing for baseline validity,
development of drug library in replacement system, transcribing existing hematology
and oncology regimen templates, testing of each transcribed template (441 templates
estimated per site), importing legacy patient treatment care plans to replacement
system, and pharmacy/oncology/nursing user training on replacement system. In
addition to identifying programmers able to program in Massachusetts General
Hospital Utility Multi-Programming Systems (MUMPS), there are data elements that
are transmitted between DSS, VistA, and the analytics platform that must be
developed to match the systems and transmitted between the platforms when called
upon by each application. DSS VCM is unique in being able to seamlessly integrate
with VistA. The VA is currently not accepting new service requests for interface


DSS VISTA Chemotherapy Manager Control VA-26-00043056 
3 
development for VistA due to the impending migration to the new VA EHR. Even if 
another solution could be introduced there would be major delays and gaps in 
treatment to Veteran patients while the interfaces are developed and templates re-
built, costing the VA significant amounts of time and money to ensure those patients 
are treated timely and safely with minimum equivalent treatment plans. The DSS VCM 
software and maintenance are required for one year, at which time VISN 23 will 
transition to VA’s new EHR. 
Additionally, software maintenance and support ensure the software functions as 
intended and address program errors in prior software versions and provide security 
enhancements. Only DSS and its authorized resellers are capable of providing the 
necessary software maintenance and support as it requires access to the propriety 
source code to develop and implement software updates. Since the software is 
proprietary, a legal restriction is placed on access to the software code that is required 
to develop upgrades and patches to the software. Without this access, it is impossible 
for another source to modify the software code to provide the required maintenance 
and support. No source other than a DSS and its authorized resellers can provide the 
required maintenance and support described herein. In addition to the aforementioned 
costs, if the brand name DSS software maintenance is not procured, VISN 23 will lose 
access to the software and will be unable to maintain compliance with Pharmacy 
Benefits Management guidance of at least 90% of all chemotherapy used in the VA 
facilities having power plans/order sets to prescribe chemotherapy/hazardous 
medications. Not having the VCM software implemented across the VISN would have 
adverse effects on the oncology treatment plan selection, development, and utilization 
which puts the most critically ill Veteran patients at risk of receiving inappropriate care, 
inaccurate hazardous/antineoplastic medication dosing, illness, or possible death. 
Efforts to Obtain Competition: Market research was conducted, the details of which
are in Section 8 of this document. This effort did not yield any additional sources that
are able to meet the Government’s requirements. It was determined that limited
competition is viable among authorized resellers from the required brand name DSS
VCM term software with maintenance and support. In accordance with FAR Overhaul
VA Deviation 16.507-7(c)(1), this justification will be provided with the solicitation to all
Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business NASA SEWP V GWAC holders.
Furthermore, in accordance with FAR Overhaul VA Deviation 5.301(a), the award
notice for this action will be synopsized on the Contract Opportunities website.
Actions to Increase Competition: The Government will continue to conduct market
research to ascertain whether there are changes in the marketplace that would enable
future actions to be competed. Specifically, VHA will continue to monitor VA’s new
EHR, market trends, new/emerging products, looking for compatible and more
advanced technologies to meet VA needs.
Market Research: The Government’s subject matter experts conducted market
research on similar systems in September 2025. The following  alternativeoncology 
software solutions were reviewed:

DSS VISTA Chemotherapy Manager Control VA-26-00043056 
4

x MediTouch

x Eon Systems
Although these similar oncology solutions have EHR compatibility, they would require 
significant customization, as detailed above, for compatibility within VA’s current 
infrastructure (i.e., interfacing with VA VistA) and not work as a provided solution 
according to Presidential Executive Order 14271, “Ensuring Commercial, Cost-
Effective Solution in Federal Contracts.” Due to the propriety data and code of the 
brand name DSS VCM, maintenance and support cannot be administered by a third 
party. 
The Contract Specialist (CS) conducted market research in February 2026, using the 
NASA SEWP V GWAC market research and provider lookup tools to determine what 
vendors are capable of providing the full requirement. Based on this market research, 
the CS identified two Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses that are 
DSS authorized resellers and able to provide all required brand name products to 
meet the Government’s functional requirements. 
9. Other Facts: None.

HSAM 3016.507-6 
JUSTIFICATION FOR EXCEPTION TO FAIR OPPORTUNITY 
EXCEEDING THE SIMPLIFIED ACQUISITION THRESHOLD 
JEFO No.  FY26-00026  - 1 - 
 
 
JEFO No.: FY26-0049 
PR Number: PCCS-26-40001 
  
 
1. Agency and Contracting Activity.   
 
The Department of Homeland Security (DHS), Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency 
(CISA), Chief of Contracting Office (COCO) prepared this justification for an exception to fair 
opportunity. 
 
2. Nature and/or description of the action being approved. 
 
This Justification for an Exception to Fair Opportunity is prepared in accordance with Federal 
Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 16.507-6(d)(2), FAR Class Deviation 26-04, Revision 1 for FAR 
Part 16.
1  
 
3. A description of the supplies or services required to meet the agency’s need (including the 
estimated value). 
 
The CISA Cybersecurity Division, Vulnerability Management sub-division requires continued 
Cyber Hygiene (CyHy) services that aid in strengthening the cybersecurity posture, limiting 
exposure, and reducing exploitation rates for over 12,500 customers across the Federal Civilian 
Executive Branch, State, Local, Tribal, and Territorial Governments, and Critical Infrastructure 
entities, and which provide multiple types of vulnerability scanning. 
 
These services are highly specialized cybersecurity services aligned to modernized and 
automated scanning services and assessments, which enable CISA to defend the nation against 
rapidly evolving threats.  Scanning services are scalable products where the Government delivers 
proactive products that evaluate an organization’s cybersecurity posture as well as provide 
support on improving exposed vulnerabilities.  The first type of scanning service includes 
Vulnerability Scanning (VS) which is where CyHy Services scans for and reports on 
vulnerabilities that are detectable from outside an organization's network (IP-based).  The second 
kind of scanning service provided is Web Application Scanning (WAS).  This scanning service 
assesses the “health” of publicly available accessible web applications by checking for known 
vulnerabilities and weak configurations.  Finally, Posture and Exposure services are provided.  
Posture and Exposure services use open-source data from both freely available and/or vendor 
supplied data feeds to provide actionable reports to CyHy stakeholders. 
 
 
 
 
1 FAR Class Deviation 26-04, Revision 1 for FAR Part 16 was issued as part of the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul 
(RFO), which was implemented in response to Executive Order 14275, Restoring Common Sense to Federal 
Procurement, signed April 15, 2025. Any subsequent citations to FAR Part 16 in this document will be cited as 
“RFO FAR” for brevity, and are referring specifically to FAR Class Deviation 26-04, Revision 1 for FAR Part 16.  

 
HSAM 3016.507-6 
JUSTIFICATION FOR EXCEPTION TO FAIR OPPORTUNITY 
EXCEEDING THE SIMPLIFIED ACQUISITION THRESHOLD 
JEFO No.  FY26-00026  - 2 - 
 
 
The period of performance will be March 30, 2026 through March 29, 2027. The total estimated 
value is . 
 
4. Identify the exception to fair opportunity and supporting rationale, including a demonstration 
that the proposed contractor’s unique qualifications or the nature of the acquisition requires use 
of the exception cited. 
 
Pursuant to RFO FAR 16.507-6(b)(3), The order must be issued on a sole-source basis in the 
interest of economy and efficiency because it is a logical follow-on to an order already issued 
under the contract, where all awardees were given a fair opportunity to be considered for the 
original order. 
 
Rationale: 
 
The incumbent Contractor, NTT Data Services Federal Government, LLC (NTT Data) is 
currently performing services under task order 70RCSA20FR0000133, which is scheduled to end 
on March 29, 2026. The task order was competitively awarded to the incumbent on September 
30, 2020 against the General Services Administration (GSA) Alliant 2 Unrestricted procurement 
vehicle.  
 
NTT Data is the only vendor that can ensure continued critical services to prevent disruption of 
services to CISA and its customers until the competitive award in FY27 and transition of 
services to a new Contractor
2. NTT Data currently: (1) provides monitoring and response 
capabilities to the nation’s most critical entities; (2) delivers services to the ~12,500 CISA 
customers enrolled in Vulnerability Scanning, Web Application Scanning, and Posture & 
Exposure; (3) onboards new customers into these services and supports modernization and 
efficiency efforts; and (4) supports CISA’s ability to support the following direction: National 
Vulnerability Incident Response; National Cybersecurity Strategy’s Strategic Objective 1.5; 
Supporting the Federal Civilian Executive Branch’s compliance with mission Binding 
Operational Directives, including: 22-01 (replaced 18-01) - Reducing the Significant Risk of 
Known Exploited Vulnerabilities, 23-01--- Improving Asset Visibility and Vulnerability 
Detection on Federal Networks, and 23-02--- Mitigating the Risk from Internet-Exposed 
Management Interface. 
 
Continued support is essential. To solicit other sources at this time would result in schedule 
delays, performance disruption of critical security services, and unnecessary cost inefficiencies 
to the Government. A new competitive procurement could take up to 12 months before an award 
is made. This would delay performance, disrupt mission critical services and increase 
administrative costs to the Government. If a new vendor is awarded this effort there could be 
further disruption of services up to 4 months long while CISA clears the new contractor staff to  
 
2 Market research is being conducted in anticipation of a competitive award in FY27. Early findings demonstrate 
that there are multiple companies on the GSA Alliant 2 Unrestricted Government Wide Acquisition Contract that 
can support the requirement. GSA Alliant 2 is a mandatory strategic sourcing vehicle (SSV).  
 


 
HSAM 3016.507-6 
JUSTIFICATION FOR EXCEPTION TO FAIR OPPORTUNITY 
EXCEEDING THE SIMPLIFIED ACQUISITION THRESHOLD 
JEFO No.  FY26-00026  - 3 - 
 
 
on-board. For example, the average security entry on duty (EOD) timelines for CISA are 
between 69 and 120 days for the types of support needed on the current task order.  The follow-
on work must be performed immediately upon completion of the current task order to ensure 
continuity of operations and avoid a disruption of critical security services. NTT Data has unique 
knowledge and expertise with the current phase of the program that no other vendor possesses. A 
different vendor would have to work to catch up in order to become familiar with the services 
and perform the follow-on which would result in a substantial increase to program costs. The 
added administrative and performance cost as well as performance risk at this time dimmish 
economy and efficiency to the Government, making the short-term logical follow-on necessary.  
 
5. Determination by the Contracting Officer that  the anticipated cost to the Government  
will be fair and reasonable.  
 
Pursuant to RFO FAR 16.506(f), if the service prices were not established at the IDIQ level, then 
the Contracting Officer must establish prices for the order using the policies and methods in 
RFO FAR subpart 15.4. The Contracting Officer anticipates a fair and reasonable price will be 
achieved based on using the rates established by the GSA Alliant 2 GWAC, consideration of 
historical pricing, and comparison of the labor mix and level of effort to the Independent 
Government Cost Estimate (IGCE).  
 
6.  Any other facts supporting the justification. 
 
None at this time.  
 
7.  A statement of the actions, if any, the agency may take to remove or overcome any barriers 
that led to the exception to fair opportunity before any subsequent acquisition for the supplies or 
services is made.  
 
CISA continues to monitor the commercial marketplace and conduct market research. Award of 
a short-term task order to NTT Data will allow continued CyHy support while a competitive 
procurement is underway and will prevent the cessation of these highly specialized services in 
support of mission critical activities. The estimated award date is in Q2 Fiscal Year 2027. CISA 
intends to post the approved justification on www.sam.gov pursuant to RFO FAR 16.507-6(f)(1).   
 
8. Technical/Requirements Personnel Certification. 
 
Pursuant to RFO FAR 16.507-6(d)(2)(ix), I certify that this requirement meets the Government’s 
minimum need and that the supporting data, which form a basis for the justification, are accurate 
and complete. 
   
Contracting Officer’s Representative

Q1. The Statement of Work describes project management and facilitation functions. 
Could you clarify how many distinct labor categories or roles the Government anticipates 
will be required to successfully perform this contract? 
A1.  Labor categories and roles will be determined by the proposing organization as part of 
the proposal process in responding to the statement of work (SOW). 
 
 
Q2. Does the Government have a minimum key personnel requirement (e.g., must the 
Project Manager be named and committed in the proposal)? 
A2.  Per the instructions:  As part of Step 2, oƯerors shall submit resume(s) of key 
personnel to be assigned to the project, along with statement of relevance to our project (if 
not apparent from the resume) and a commitment statement to the project for the person 
identiﬁed. 
 
 
Q3. Is there a current incumbent contractor performing this or a similar scope of work? If 
so, could you please identify the incumbent? 
A3.  There is no current incumbent contractor. 
 
 
Q4. Is there a Government estimate or budget ceiling for this contract that can be 
disclosed? 
A4. This is not disclosed.  
 
 
 
Q5. Are labor rates expected to be based on a speciﬁc wage determination or GSA 
schedule, or may oƯerors propose independent commercial rates? 

A5.   This is not a GSA contract. Please use the speciﬁc wage determination or your own 
labor category if higher.  
 
 
 
Q6. Will the Government accept blended labor rates, or are fully burdened rates required 
by labor category? 
A6.   Please submit the labor rates on how you would invoice/charge per requirements of 
the SOW. Fully burdened is ﬁne if that’s part of how you would charge for a speciﬁc part.    
 
 
Q7. The SOW references a near-ﬁnal draft due approximately 45 days prior to the ﬁnal 
deadline, which would be June 17, 2027, while Section 6.0 also references August 1, 2027 
as the ﬁnal product due date. Could the Government conﬁrm the complete and 
authoritative milestone schedule to ensure accurate proposal planning? 
A7.  The ﬁnal product is due August 1, 2027.  A near-ﬁnal draft is due 45 days prior, on June 
17, 2027. 
 
 
Q8. Will the contractor be expected to host or manage the document repository for 
interview materials and draft documents, or will USGS provide a platform and storage 
solution? 
A8.  USGS will provide a platform and storage solution for interview materials and draft 
documents. 
 
 
Q9. Will the contractor have access to the existing West Coast and Alaska WBS 
dictionaries prior to contract award to inform proposal pricing and performance planning? 
A9.  Yes. 

 
 
 
Q10. The SOW states that all services can be provided remotely with no need for travel. 
Can the Government conﬁrm that all stakeholder interviews and meetings will be 
conducted virtually for the full duration of the contract? 
A10.  The Government conﬁrms that the contractor’s participation in all stakeholder 
interviews and meetings can be conducted virtually for the full duration of the contract.  No 
contractor travel will be needed. 
 
 
Q11. Approximately how many oƯerors does the Government anticipate inviting to Step 2 
oral presentations following the Step 1 advisory review? 
A11.  The Government anticipates inviting as many as are best suited to advance to Step 2, 
based on the Step 1 evaluations. 
 
 
Q12. What is the Government's anticipated award date and expected contract start date? 
A12.   Please refer to page 3 of the RFQ which has a date of 06/01/2026.  Contract award is 
before 05/31/2026.  
 
 
Q13. Will oral presentation instructions be provided to all oƯerors prior to Step 1 advisory 
notices, or only to those selected to continue to Step 2? 
A13.  Per the instructions:  Further instructions for the vendor presentations will be 
provided following the Step 1 Advisory notices, and presentation schedule commitments. 
 
 

Q14. Will the Government consider non-federal past performance references equally to 
federal past performance references in the evaluation?  
A.14.  Past performance references will be considered based on the amount of experience 
of relevant work as related to the statement of work.

The following pertains to this Amendment: 
Request for Information (RFI) QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS 
_______________________________________________________________________ 
QUESTION 1:  
Please confirm whether additional 11×17 pages, beyond the already permitted 11×17 organizational 
chart, may be included within the 75‑page limit for data presentation. Additionally, please clarify 
whether each 11×17 page will be counted as one page or two pages for the purposes of the page 
limit. 
ANSWER 1: 
Confirming the 11 by 17 page is only allowed for the organizational chart and is only counted as 
one page.  Additional 11 by 17 pages should not be included. 
 
QUESTION 2: 
Criterion 2 identifies both Project Managers and Task Order Managers as Key Personnel. Does 
NA VFAC Atlantic differentiate the responsibilities of Project Managers and Task Order Managers 
with respect to this IDIQ? If so, please explain. 
ANSWER 2: 
Task order managers and project managers are the same person (different titles) and therefore are 
treated synonymously or interchangeable.

Department of Veterans Affairs 
Enterprise Data Center and Telecommunications Modernization 
Request for Information 36C10B26Q0218 
1. Introduction 
 
This Request for Information (RFI) is issued for conducting market research and planning 
purposes only. Accordingly, this RFI constitutes neither a Request for Quote, Request for 
Proposal, nor a guarantee that one will be issued by the Government in the future; 
furthermore, it does not commit the Government to contract for any services described 
herein. Additionally, this RFI does not restrict the Government as to the ultimate 
acquisition approach. In accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 15.101(c), 
responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to 
form a binding contract. 
 
The purpose of this RFI is to identify qualified vendors who can meet Department of 
Veterans Affairs (VA) requirements for the Enterprise Data Center and 
Telecommunications Modernization (EDCTM) initiative, and to obtain industry input on the 
best approach for structuring and executing this requirement. Any contract or order that 
might be awarded based on information received or derived from this market research will 
be the outcome of the competitive process. Your response to this RFI will be treated only 
as information for the Government to consider. 
 
The Government is not responsible for any cost incurred by industry in furnishing this 
information. All costs associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the interested 
vendor’s expense. Not responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future 
solicitation if any is issued. Any information submitted by respondents to this RFI is strictly 
voluntary. All submissions will become Government property and will not be returned. 
Interested vendors are responsible for adequately marking proprietary, restricted, or 
competition sensitive information contained in their response. VA is under no obligation to 
provide feedback to the company, or to contact the company for clarification of any 
information submitted in response to this RFI. 
 
Be advised that set-aside decisions may be made based on the information provided in 
response to this RFI. Responses should be as complete and informative as possible. 
2. Background 
 
The VA, Office of Information and Technology, Infrastructure Operations, Data Center 
and Infrastructure Engineering division manages a large, geographically distributed 
portfolio of data centers, computer rooms, and telecommunications spaces. These 
environments support clinical, administrative, and mission-critical systems across the 
Veterans Health Administration, Veterans Benefits Administration, and National Cemetery 
Administration. 
 

Page 2 of 6 
 
There is no single standard configuration across VA data center facilities. Infrastructure 
varies significantly from site to site, including differences in equipment racks, cabling 
standards, power distribution, cooling systems, and facility layouts.

There is a page limitation for this RFI of 10 pages. The Government will not review any 
information or attachments in excess of the page limit.

Be advised that set-aside decisions may be made based on the information provided in

b. Brief Summary (not to exceed 10 pages), describing your company’s technical 
approach to meeting the requirements, outlined below. 
 
VA anticipates award of a firm fixed price Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) or an 
alternative ordering-based strategy to establish a pre-priced listing of discrete, hardware-
led deliverables for data center and telecommunications modernization work. The primary 
objectives for the procurement are: 
1) Standardize legacy and non-standard telecommunications and data center 
physical infrastructure; 
2) Identify and replace end-of-life or obsolete infrastructure components;  
3) Standardize inconsistent or site-unique installation practices across facilities;  
4) Update or complete design documentation and specifications; and  
5) Eliminate infrastructure designs that increase operational risk, cost, or 
complexity. 
 
The Government is seeking industry feedback to determine vendor capabilities, 
socio-economic categories, to identify industry best practices, and identify any 
alternate contract vehicles well-suited for this requirement.  
 
Hardware-Led Deliverables with Bundled Services. The Government envisions 
ordering data center modernization work as hardware-led line items. Each line item would 
represent a major infrastructure activity (e.g., Computer Room Air Conditioner (CRAC) 
unit replacement, structured cabling refresh, rack and enclosure installation) priced on a 
firm-fixed-price basis. The price would include all ancillary services necessary to produce 
a complete, installed, and operational outcome—including but not limited to site survey, 
engineering design, procurement, installation, testing, and documentation.  
 
Standardization Across Facilities. A key objective is to move VA data centers toward 
repeatable, standards-compliant configurations. The Government recognizes that site-
specific conditions will vary and that contractors will need to account for that variability.

vendors price work at facilities they have not previously been surveyed.
