DARPA-SN-26-33
1
Request for Information
DARPA-SN-26-33
Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency
Tactical Technology Office
Responses due 15 May2026, by 4:00 PM Eastern Time (ET).  
This Request for Information (RFI) from the Defense Advanced Research Projects 
Agency (DARPA)’s Tactical Technology Office (TTO) seeks information regarding 
capabilities for the following two categories.  
1) Unmanned aerial vehicle (herein referred to as “drones”) in the Group 1-3 space 
with capabilities for fully autonomous launch, recovery, storage, organization, 
recharging/refueling, organization, internal logistics management, and pre/post-
flight checkout.  Proposed drone designs must form a mission-focused, 
collaborative constellation.  Responses must be cognizant of long endurance 
drone constellations with high operational availability and constellation 
management.  
When responding to this category, use Attachment 1 and follow instructions 
provided in the Requested Information section below. 
2) Storage containers (herein referred to as “containers”) that provide fully 
autonomous drone storage, logistics management, launch, recovery, and 
recharge/refuel, while conforming to the intention of a standardized military 
container (e.g. Conex, 463L pallets, Tricon, ISU container, etc.).  Innovative ideas 
and non-standard containers (e.g. suitcase-based distributed systems, box-based 
systems) will also be considered within the context of the presented approach, but 
solutions should be compatible with current military transport capabilities. It is 
envisioned that these containers shall be self-sufficient with consideration of 
energy storage, communication equipment, and compute capability. 
When responding to this category use Attachment 2 and follow instructions 
provided in the Requested Information section below. 
Participants may respond to either one or both categories described above using separate 
Attachments (provided).
RFI Responses may be used as a market analysis tool informing DARPA about potential 
vendors for a new program seeking to advance fully autonomous and containerized, 
deployment, sustainment, and operational support of unmanned autonomous platforms in 
the Group 1-3 space.  
BACKGROUND:
Existing commercial, airborne Group 1-3 platforms are limited in endurance, payload 
capacity, and onboard electrical auxiliary power.  When operated as constellations, they 

DARPA-SN-26-33
2
typically require substantial infrastructure and basing area for deployment and recovery. 
These constellations typically require human involvement to recover, recharge/refuel, and 
launch again, lacking full autonomy necessary to achieve sustained operations spanning 
days or longer. The landscape of current platform technologies has broad limitations that 
require evolution to achieve high-endurance constellations consisting of drones with 
meaningful payload Size Weight, Power, and Cost (SWaP-C) staged from fully 
autonomous containers capable of complete mission-cycle management inclusive of 
launch, sustainment/swap-out, and recovery.  
Example limitations include, but are not limited to:
- Drones
oElectric-based platforms have limited battery discharge depth and recharge 
cycle limits that restrict flight time and sortie numbers before substantial 
performance degradation manifests or battery-changes are required. 
oHybrid-electric solutions add weight and the complexity of onboard fuel-
storage, combustion, electric-machines, and high-voltage power transfer.
oBuoyant solutions often lack fine six degrees of freedom (6DOF) control 
and typically have lower onboard auxiliary electrical power available 
without the use of heavy batteries or large solar panels.  
oFixed wing platforms typically prohibit compact, autonomous 
launch/recovery solutions without requiring human intervention at some 
step and lack the ability to hold fixed spatial positions (not required but is 
a limitation of fixed wing).
- Containers
oExisting containers often rely upon a Differential Global Positioning 
System (DGPS) and cannot position themselves in GPS-denied 
environments.
oDeployable containers often lack internal volume allocations for 
communication equipment and fuel-storage necessary to sustain a 
constellation for multi-day continuous missions.
oWhile some constellation delivery solutions can unleash hundreds of 
drones in under a minute, these platforms often lack the ability to integrate 
external payloads, with their additional SWaP, that enable meaningful 
effects/surveillance. 
oSome container solutions provide internal volume sufficient for drones 
with meaningful payload-size but may lack the deployment and recovery 
tempo required to rapidly establish a persistent drone constellation of 
adequate density for the desired effect. 
oModern containers optimize designs around battery-powered drones 
(typically low range, low endurance) without payloads and are incapable 

DARPA-SN-26-33
3
of supporting alternative fuel-sourced platforms providing extended flight 
times necessary to achieve mission relevance. 
While sufficient for preplanned lightshows and commercial activities, further 
advancements are required to exploit constellation technologies in a high platform 
density and rapid deployment scenario. Full autonomy in launch, mission, recovery, 
post/pre-flight and re-launch in a continuous operational cycle for extended hours/days is 
desired. 
DARPA has identified an exigent need for highly deployable, versatile-SWaP Group 1-3 
platforms, operating in autonomous constellations that are stored within, deployed from, 
recovered in, and managed by a fully autonomous container, to support a variety of 
payloads and missions in GPS-denied environments.  Advancements in low-SWaP 
technologies enable constellations comprising a variety of novel payloads, each requiring 
dedicated power and weight, but capable of operating in synchrony across the 
constellation.  Constellation populations may comprise up to 500 platforms (number may 
vary as a function of payload type). Each platform will be equipped with a subsystem or 
independent payload system with the potential to achieve high operational availability for 
the combined system over multiple-day periods.
DARPA is looking for responses for U.S. manufactured and assembled drones in the 
Group 1-3 space and containers spanning current and future technologies to chart the 
mosaic of possibility in advancing autonomous constellation dynamics for the military.  
Novel configurations that enable multi-day continuous operations with their corollary 
constellation management software (ideally with path optimization and collision 
deconfliction) and innovative configurations of autonomous container-based deployment 
solutions are of particular interest to DARPA.  
Forthcoming technology development programs may leverage these RFI results to inform 
a new program. 
A mission-adjacent use-case involves a transportable container deployed to an austere, 
GPS-denied environment in suboptimal terrain or onboard a host platform that, upon 
remote operator inputs, activates and autonomously deploys a series of platforms 
launching from a single area (possibly serially). The platforms traverse some radius 
away, loiter on-station with an active payload (not all necessarily in the same location nor 
same payloads), and execute a mission before returning back to the launch area, 
autonomously recovering, recharging/refueling, and launching again to repeat the mission 
(without human intervention).  The platform quantity is determined by the particular 
effect, target, and mission. Thus, “constellation” may comprise any number above 2. 

DARPA-SN-26-33
4
Container size is limited by transportability, endurance, storage, and operability 
objectives. 
DESCRIPTION:
This RFI is looking for information on novel, U.S. manufactured and assembled, aerial 
platforms and containers, and performers that fundamentally enable:
- Autonomy Level 4 (no human participation required except for mission 
definition) for the system’s operation: 
oE.g., the operator issues a command, then the drones/constellation 
maintain level 4 autonomy 
- Long-constellation endurance (on the order of multiple days)
- Drones with continuous electrical power available to payloads, low-cost 
Commercial-Off-the-Shelf (COTS) construction, and sized for containerized 
storage
- Constellation management software (path optimization, collision avoidance 
planning, constellation reshaping/reorientation, formation flying)
- Autonomous container operation (inclusive but not limited to storage, launch, 
recovery, recharge/refuel, constellation communications, compute capability, 
multi-day fuel/energy storage, and constellation management software)
Responders are requested to provide tabular information on either existing or notional 
platforms that may satisfy this RFI in the attachments provided. 
REQUESTED INFORMATION: 
DARPA is interested in responses that provide information and insights related to core 
capability metrics. Response instructions are below.  
If responding ONLY to the “Drone” portion of the RFI, see RFI Attachment #1 and 
complete the Cover Page, Required Data Table, enter any optional Graphics, and use the 
Technical Description sections as required, entering any References on the last page.  Use 
Attachment #1 to capture all information for your response, keeping all responses to 5 
pages maximum (including references).  Do not modify Attachment #1’s layout or add 
pages to Attachment #1. Keep all responses to the maximum 5-page limit of Attachment 
#1.

140FS126Q0050 - RFI 
Questions & Responses 
 
RFI 1.Please confirm an acceptable alternative for the lead commissioning agent qualifications 
(experience, education, commissioning background). ANSWER:  
A. 25+ years HV AC/BAS background: YES. 
B. Hands-on maintenance/repair experience: DOCUMENT AT LEAST 5 YEARS OF 
EXPERIENCE. 
C. BS/MS in Mechanical Engineering: YES, IN ADDITION TO AT LEAST 5 YEARS 
EXPERIENCE. 
D. Significant commissioning experience: "SIGNIFICANT" SHALL MEAN AT LEAST 5 
YEARS EXPERIENCE. 
RFI 2. Will a controls technician be available onsite, and does the O&M staff have a login for 
Metasys configuration and trending? ANSWER: 
There is no controls technician available at the project site. Staff has a log-in that allows 
configuration of alarms and trend logs. 
RFI 3. Clarify the RFP requirement for 2-point calibration and whether slope/intercept is 
applicable for thermistors.  ANSWER: 
Thermistors use non-linear lookup tables, so slope/intercept calibration is not meaningful; verify 
readings fall within acceptable error band and adjust offset if needed. Rtds or linear transmitters 
may use slope/intercept where applicable (e.g., heating water or outside air). 
RFI 4. Clarify whether the contractor is required to perform maintenance tasks in addition to 
retro-commissioning checklists. ANSWER: 
Item 8.2 refers to necessary site visits for contract completion. It is NOT intended to require 
general maintenance. Retro-commissioning checklists are expected; performing maintenance 
tasks is NOT.

SERDP and ESTCP Support
1     OBJECTIVE
The Strategic Environmental Research and Development Program (SERDP) and the 
Environmental Security Technology Certification Program (ESTCP) require program support to 
execute their missions of developing and demonstrating technologies that meet the Department of 
Defense (DoD) environmental and energy requirements. SERDP and ESTCP are separate 
programs that are managed through a joint program office. Support is needed at the program level 
and in each of the technical areas in which these programs invest. 
2     BACKGROUND
SERDP is a multi-agency research and development program that was established by Congress in 
1991. As described in Title 10, U.S.C. Sections 2901-2904, the major focus of SERDP is to 
"address environmental matters of concern to the Department of Defense and the Department of 
Energy through support for basic and applied research and development of technologies that can 
enhance the capabilities of the departments to meet their environmental obligations." SERDP 
supports environmental research and development activities in government, industry, and 
academic laboratories in the areas of Environmental Restoration, Munitions Response, Resource 
Conservation and Resilience, and Weapons Systems and Platforms.
ESTCP is a DoD demonstration and validation program for environmental, energy, and installation 
resilience technologies. The DoD established ESTCP in fiscal year 1995. ESTCP demonstrates 
and validates innovative technologies that target DoD's most urgent environmental, energy, and 
installation resilience needs and are projected to pay back the investment through cost savings, 
increased efficiency, and improved mission outcomes. The program provides funding to 
government, industry, and academic institutions to conduct demonstrations in the following six 
areas: Environmental Restoration, Installation Energy and Water, Munitions Response, Natural 
Hazards Adaptation, Resource Conservation and Resilience, and Weapons Systems and 
Platforms.
Details about the SERDP and ESTCP program structure, current projects, examples of solicitation 
documents, project requirements, and examples of program outreach can be found on the joint 
SERDP and ESTCP web site, https://serdp-estcp.mil/.
W912HQ26RA0010002

3     TYPE OF SUPPORT
The required services are expected to break out as roughly:
1.     Technical Review of Proposals and Documents: 35%
2.     Direct Support to Program Areas: 30%
3.     Administrative and Financial: 15%
4.     Meeting Planning, Logistics and Support: 10%
5.     Outreach: 10%
 
All personnel shall be qualified by education and experience appropriate to perform their assigned 
tasks. The following key personnel are essential to management and oversight, and shall meet the 
minimum specific qualifications outlined.
 
Project Manager: The project manager shall have a minimum of 10 years' experience in project 
management, including 5 years' experience managing a team of the size and diversity of skills 
needed to perform the work described. The project manager shall have experience with 
government management of research and development, as well as familiarity with the structure 
and management of the DoD. The project manager must have sufficient technical training so as to 
be capable of managing and assuring the technical quality of the support provided, including 
technical reviews.
W912HQ26RA0010002
Page 8 of 111

 
Information Technology Specialist: Three essential elements of the work described below are 
the online project management system, the online proposal management and evaluation system, 
and the SERDP and ESTCP joint web site. To manage these elements, the contractor must 
demonstrate that the individual in the role of providing oversight for the information technology 
enterprise has expertise in state-of-the-art hardware and software, including experience in web site 
management, database management, on-line reporting and management systems, acceptance 
and management of electronic proposals, and the appropriate security protections.
 
4     GENERAL REQUIREMENTS
This section describes the general requirements for this effort. The following sub-sections provide 
details of various considerations on this effort.
 
4.1    Non-Personal Services
The Government shall neither supervise contractor employees nor control the method by which the 
contractor performs the required tasks. Under no circumstances shall the Government assign 
tasks to, or prepare work schedules for, individual contractor employees. It shall be the 
responsibility of the contractor to manage its employees and to guard against any actions that are 
of the nature of personal services or give the perception of personal services. If the contractor 
believes that any actions constitute, or are perceived to constitute personal services, it shall be the 
contractor's responsibility to notify the Procuring Contracting Officer (PCO) immediately.

DEPARTMENT OF THE NAVY 
NAVAL INFORMATION WARFARE CENTER PACIFIC 
53560 HULL STREET 
SAN DIEGO, CALIFORNIA 92152-5001 
J&A No. 26-225 
 
JUSTIFICATION AND APPROVAL 
 FOR USE OF OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION 
 
1. Contracting Activity.  
 
Department of the Navy, Naval Information Warfare Center Pacific (NIWC PAC). 
 
2. Description of the Action Being Approved.  
 
The proposed action is to increase the ceiling for contract N00039-19-D-0006 awarded to 
Lockheed Martin (LM) by $30,000,000 from $104,242,344 to $134,242,344 in support of 
Radiant Mercury (RADMERC). The cost-plus-fixed-fee (CPFF), Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite 
Quantity (IDIQ) contract was awarded on a sole source basis on 01 September 2019 with a five-
year base period and one five-year option period. Based on the higher than expected burn rate, 
the option period was exercised on 27 October 2021, roughly three years earlier than initially 
planned. While the current contract’s ordering period ends on 30 September 2029, the remaining 
contract ceiling has been allocated and is expected to be obligated by Third Quarter, Fiscal Year 
2026. The ceiling increase is necessary to avoid a gap in services critical to the Department of 
War (DoW).  
 
3. Description of Supplies/Services.  
 
The ceiling increase to contract N00039-19-D-0006 will provide continued support for the 
Department of the Navy and other Agencies’ RADMERC operations  
The current contract provides for 
installation, program management, maintenance, modernization, and sustainment of RADMERC 
systems and will provide system security authorization support, and logistics and training 
services. The work scope also includes sustainment of existing  
 
 
 
 
Due to a software baseline compromise identified around March 2022, the National Cross 
Domain Strategy and Management office and NCDSMO and DoW Chief Information Office 
(CIO) directed the CDS developer, Lockheed Martin (LM), to ramp up efforts to deliver a new 
version. This directive,  
 have resulted in an increase in demand on 
current requirements, unplanned costs, and a higher demand for RADMERC services. To 
support the substantial unanticipated demand on the current contract’s requirements, a ceiling 
increase of $12,028,735 was awarded on 13 February 2025, to avoid a gap in capability while the 
follow-on contract was pending.  


 
 
 
 
   
 
Despite the February 2025 ceiling increase, the ceiling on N00039-19-D-0006 contract was 
nearly exhausted within seven (7) months, as NIWC Pacific  
Customers not being prepared, changing/increasing their 
RADMERC order allocation, and updating their baseline, also resulted in a significant increase 
in changes to the RADMERC schedule, which further caused LM to bid for more support hours.   
 
Contractually, multiple customers (new and existing), have asked for additional support with the 
current baseline, from upgrading existing systems, to requiring additional CDS installations. 
Since the transition of the RADMERC contract to NIWC Pacific, seventy-six (76) task orders 
have been awarded and the customer base has grown from  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
  
 
 
 
 
 
  
 
4. Identification of Statutory Authority:  
 
The statutory authority is 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), as implemented by Federal Acquisition 
Regulation (FAR) Subpart 6.302-1: Only one responsible source and no other supplies or 
services will satisfy agency requirements. 
 
5. Rationale Justifying Use of Cited Statutory Authority. 
 
 


 
  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
   
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 




 
6. Description of Efforts Made to Solicit Offers from as Many Offerors as Practicable.   
 
The proposed contract requirement will be synopsized on SAM.gov and any responses received 
will be considered prior to award. No additional market research was conducted because it is not 
practical, for the reasons discussed in paragraph 5 above, for any company other than LM to 
provide the required supplies and services. The USG did synopsize the previous procurement on 
the FEDBIZOPS via the NIWC PAC E-Commerce Central website on 03 December 2018. This 
announcement was posted for fifteen (15) days and resulted in only one question requesting the 
name of the incumbent contractor.  No other questions were received before the end date of 18 
December 2018. To date, no other potential sources have expressed interest in this requirement.  
 
7. Determination of Fair and Reasonable Cost.   
 
The Contracting Officer has determined that the anticipated cost to the Government for the 
supplies/services covered by this J&A will be fair and reasonable.   
 
8. Actions to Remove Barriers to Future Competition. 
 
Market research will be conducted for future contract requirements of this nature to determine 
the most advantageous method of fulfilling the Government’s need. As part of any future market 
research, the Government will monitor the NSA certification activity to determine if any other 
CDS can meet the Navy’s CDS certification requirements. 
 
The Government has established a CDS Working Group specifically to identify a viable long-
term solution that meets the requirements of all customers. The future solution is anticipated to 
be implemented incrementally over the next ten (10) years due to the complexity of the 
capability and the cost and time it takes to obtain NSA accreditation.

REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) 
 
MADE IN AMERICA MARKET RESEARCH HUB 
 
THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) NOTICE ONLY.  THIS IS NOT A 
REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS (RFP). NO SOLICITATION IS AVAILABLE AT THIS TIME. 
1. AUTHORITY 
This initiative supports statutor y domestic preference requiremen ts including the Buy American 
Act (41 U.S.C. § § 8301-8305) and E.O. 14005 Ensuring the Future is Made in All of America by 
All of America’s Workers. 
The objective is to strengthen co mpliance, transparency, and anal ytic capability across Federal 
procurement and Federal financial assistance programs. 
2. DESCRIPTION 
The Office of Management and Budget’s Made in America Office (MIAO) is exploring options to 
establish a centralized, scalable  capability to support domestic sourcing de terminations across 
Federal procurement and Federal financial assistance programs.  
Federal agency procurement officials and recipients of Federal financial assistance grants perform 
market research for two (2) main  reasons: (a) to identify a domestically manufactured product in 
compliance with Made in America laws, or (b) to verify that a domestic product is not available to 
justify a waiver from Made in America laws. Agencies and grantees currently utilize a wide range 
of market research methods, such as time-co nsuming phone calls to manufacturers, costly 
commercial market research platform licenses, and broad web searches that often result in out-of-
date or incomplete results.  
There is a clear need to provide Federal procurem ent officers and grantees a single, trusted, and 
continuously updated data source to help identify  domestic products effici ently and effectively. 
This effort seeks to improve th e consistency, defensib ility and efficiency of market research 
processes.  
3. VISION  
Federal procurement officials and grant recipients should be able to: 
 Reduce duplicative and burdensome market research 
 Quickly and accurately identify domestic manufacturers by product category 
As a result, desired outcomes are: 
 Increased Federal spending on American rather than foreign products 
 Increased Federal agency compliance with Made in America laws  

The long-term vision is to integrate this capa bility into the broader Federal acquisition and 
financial assistance ecosystem. 
4. OBJECTIVE 
The desired solution is a standardized, continuou sly updated dataset and an alytic capability that 
enables agencies to: 
a) Identify domestic manufacturers and suppliers by category; 
b) Support waiver review determinations with traceable documentation; and 
c) Reduce compliance burden while increasing the accuracy and defensibility of domestic 
sourcing determinations. 
d) The objective is not merely data  aggregation, but to create sust ainable infrastructure that 
improves compliance government-wide. 
A core objective of this effort is to reduce duplicative market research and compliance burden 
across agencies while improving consistency of domestic sourcing determinations.  
5. SCOPE OF EFFORT 
The anticipated scope of effort is laid out below. These phases are subject to change based on the 
path forward for development as a result of this RFI. 
Phase 1: Data Identification and Gathering. Identify and gather structured and unstructured market 
data sources from outside the Federal government. Integrate these with structured and unstructured 
data from within the Federal government (i.e., historical procurement, agency-submitted waivers) 
into a central data lake. 
Phase 2: Data Governance and Contextualiza tion. Develop governance po licies to regulate and 
manage data. Apply ontologies to accurately characterize data relationships between suppliers and 
across specific statutory domestic content requirements. 
Phase 3: Artificial Intelligence (AI) Layer. Utilize generative and/or agentic AI to easily interface 
between data and users. 
Phase 4: Reporting and Analytics. Extract insights from market research data, such as a report that 
identifies American-made products with probabili ties and suggestions for verification. Ability to 
integrate and scale advanced analytics capabilities in future phases. 
Any potential solution should be modular and scalable, capable of expansion across procurement 
and financial assistance contexts as policy requirements evolve.  
6. SYSTEM INTEROPERABILITY 

Solutions of interest should be capable of integration with existing Federal procurement and grants 
systems, including but  not limited to the Federal Pr ocurement Data System (FPDS), 
www.SAM.gov, and agency contract writing or grants management systems. 
Application Programming Interface (API) based or structured data exchange capabilities are 
strongly preferred to enable scalability and long-term sustainability.  
7. DATA GOVERNANCE AND SECURITY 
Solutions should enable: 
a) Traceability and auditability sufficient to s upport waiver review and Inspector General 
oversight; 
b) Clear documentation of data sources and validation methodologies; 
c) Secure handling of confidential, proprietary, or national security-sensitive information; and 
d) Mechanisms for continuous updating to reflect evolving manufacturing landscapes. 
Respondents are encouraged to describe proposed data ownership structures, licensing terms, and 
any restrictions on Government use of aggregated data. 
8. USER STORIES 
Illustrative use cases include:  
a) An agency procurement official can qui ckly and easily identify a domestically 
manufactured product, or verify that no domestic suppliers exist. 
b) A state or local recipient of Federal grant funding can quickly and easily identify a 
domestically manufactured product, or verify that no domestic suppliers exist. 
c) A MIAO staff member can quickly and easily verify an agency’s market research submitted 
through a waiver. 
 
9.  QUESTIONS FOR INDUSTRY 
MIAO seeks input on the following: 
Technology Architecture 
 What technical approaches are recommended for aggregating and maintaining large, 
disparate manufacturing datasets? 
 What methodologies are most effective for ensuri ng data quality, verification, and 
validation? 
 What level of effort and resources would be required to achieve these technical solutions? 
Data Sources 
 What commercially available data sources could enhance existing Federal data? 
 How should structured and unstructured data be harmonized? 

Security 
 In addition to government security requi rements, what additional safeguards are 
recommended for protecting business confidential or sensitive data? 
Updates and Sustainability 
 What approaches ensure continuous updating and scalability over time, given the rapidly-
evolving nature of manufacturing data? 
Licensing and Access 
 What licensing models are typical for soluti ons of this nature within the Federal 
Government or in the private sector? 
 
10. CONSIDERATIONS 
To the extent possible, the MIAO is seeking to leverage existing technology solutions that could 
be leveraged by the Federal government rather than developing a custom solution. 
The success of any solution will depend on the quality, relevance, and sustainability of underlying 
data sources, as well as the ability to integrate with existing Federal systems. 
This initiative is not intended to duplicate, replace, or conflict with existing Federal procurement, 
grants management, or market re search platforms. Rather, it is intended to complement existing 
systems by enhancing visibility  into domestic manufacturing cap acity and supply chain data 
relevant to statutory Made in America requirements.  
The Government has not made a determination regarding the appr opriate technical approach or 
acquisition strategy, if any. Responses will inform future planning decisions. 
The Government welcomes respons es from interested parties to include small businesses and 
innovative commercial providers with relevant capabilities.  
11. RESPONSES 
Interested parties are directed to respond to this RFI with a written response. Response shall be in 
Microsoft Word for Office or compatible format and shall not exceed 10 pages. A page is defined 
as each face of an 8½”  x 11” sheet with information contai ned within a one-inch margin on all 
sides. Font type shall be Times Roman 12 point. Responses are due no later than 11:00 pm ET on 
Wednesday, April 01, 2026  and should be sent via email to Salman.Shahid@oa.eop.gov (cc: 
Franky.M.Awuvey@oa.eop.gov)  with “Response to MIA Market Research Hub RFI” in the subject 
line. 
 
12. QUESTIONS: 

Questions regarding this announcement shall be submitted in writing by e-mail to 
Salman.Shahid@oa.eop.gov (cc: Franky.M.Awuvey@oa.eop.gov) with “Questions to MIA 
Market Research Hub RFI” in the subject line.  Verbal questions will NOT be accepted. Answers 
to questions will be posted to www.SAM.gov. The Government does not guarantee that questions 
received after March 18, 2026 at 11:00pm ET will be answered. The Government will not 
reimburse companies for any costs associated with the submissions of their responses. 
 
13. EVAULATION OF RESPONSES 
Responses will be reviewed for relevance, scalability, data quality methodology, security posture, 
and demonstrated experience supporting large-scale data aggregation efforts. After evaluation of 
responses, MIAO may conduct a virtual industry engagement session. If scheduled, details will be 
posted via SAM.gov and/or shared with respondents. 
14. DISCLAIMER 
This RFI is issued solely for Market Resear ch purposes in accordance with FAR Part 10. This 
notice does not constitute a solicitation and does not commit the Fe deral Government to contract 
for any supplies or services. Responses are voluntary, will not be formally evaluated and will be 
used for planning purposes only.  
Participation in this RFI does not confer any competitive advantage in any future potential 
procurement.  
 
All information contained in the RFI is preliminary as well as subject to modification and is in no 
way binding on the Government. FAR clause 52. 215-3, “Request for Information or Solicitation 
for Planning Purposes”, is incorporated by reference in this RFI. The Government does not intend 
to pay for information received in response to this RFI. Responders to this invitation are solely 
responsible for all expenses associated with responding to this RFI. This RFI will be the basis for 
collecting information on capabilities available. This RFI is issued solely for information and 
planning purposes. Proprietary information and trade secrets, if any, must be clearly marked on all 
materials. All information received in this RFI that is marked “Proprie tary” will be handled 
accordingly.  Please be advised that all submissions become Government property and will not be 
returned nor will receipt be c onfirmed. In accordance with FAR 15.201(e), responses to this RFI 
are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract.

continuously updated data source to help identify domestic products efficiently and effectively. 
This effort seeks to improve the consistency, defensibility and efficiency of market research 
processes.  
3. VISION  
Federal procurement officials and grant recipients should be able to: 
• Reduce duplicative and burdensome market research 
• Quickly and accurately identify domestic manufacturers by product category 
As a result, desired outcomes are: 
• Increased Federal spending on American rather than foreign products 
• Increased Federal agency compliance with Made in America laws  

The long- term vision is to integrate this capability into the broader Federal acquisition and 
financial assistance ecosystem. 
4. OBJECTIVE 
The desired solution is a standardized, continuously updated dataset and analytic capability that 
enables agencies to: 
a) Identify domestic manufacturers and suppliers by category; 
b) Support waiver review determinations with traceable documentation; and 
c) Reduce compliance burden while increasing the accuracy and defensibility of domestic 
sourcing determinations. 
d) The objective is not merely data aggregation, but to create sustainable infrastructure that 
improves compliance government-wide. 
A core objective of this effort is to reduce duplicative market research and compliance burden 
across agencies while improving consistency of domestic sourcing determinations.  
5. SCOPE OF EFFORT 
The anticipated scope of effort is laid out below. These phases are subject to change based on the 
path forward for development as a result of this RFI. 
Phase 1: Data Identification and Gathering. Identify and gather structured and unstructured market 
data sources from outside the Federal government. Integrate these with structured and unstructured 
data from within the Federal government (i.e., historical procurement, agency-submitted waivers) 
into a central data lake. 
Phase 2: Data Governance and Conte x tualization. Develop governance policies to regulate and 
manage data. Apply ontologies to accurately characterize data relationships between suppliers and 
across specific statutory domestic content requirements. 
Phase 3: Artifi cial Intelligence (AI) Layer. Utilize generative and/or agentic AI to easily interface 
between data and users.

MDA transferred sponsorship of the USU/SDL UARC to United States Space Force (USSF) on 
April 30, 2025.  As part of the coordinated turnover, USSF requested that MDA increase the 
ceiling and extend the ordering period for the contract while USSF develops and executes their

continued access utilizing this contract including non-MDA organizations comprised of the 
USAF, US Army, DARPA, DHS, NASA, SDA, and USN as well as multiple programs across 
MDA. 
 
Current utilization of the J&A ceiling is at 80%.  Upon consultation with stakeholders, MDA/DE 
determined that the ordering period extension and ceiling increase is in the best interest of the 
Government, reduces the risk of a break in service, and ensures continual technical and analytical 
support to provide a highly integrated and effective Missile Defense System.  Additionally, the 
increase in ceiling and ordering period extension of the MDA contract will reduce the risk of a 
lapse of contract support to all MDA and external agency stakeholders. 
4. Statutory Authority Permitting Other than Full and Open Competition, (FAR 6.303- 
2(b)(4)).  
The statutory authority permitting other than full and open competition for this effort is 10 U.S.C. 
3204(a)(3) as implemented in FAR 6.302-3(a)(2)(ii), Industrial mobilization; engineering, 
developmental, or research capability; or expert services, to establish or maintain an essential 
engineering, research or development capability to be provided by an educational or other 
nonprofit institution or a federally funded research and development center. 
5. Demonstration of Contractor's Unique Qualifications or the Nature of the Acquisition 
Requires Use of the Authority Cited (FAR 6.303-2(b)(5)).  
It is necessary to award this contract to USU/SDL in order to maintain the essential research and 
development capability provided by this research institution.  Since 1992, USU/SDL has 
provided the Government and MDA cost effective and responsive support in certain mission 
areas to include scientific and technological investigations in a broad range of disciplines such 
as:  electro-optical sensor systems; instrument and payload development, test, evaluation, 
integration, validation, and operations; data analysis; modeling and simulation; satellite sensor 
systems and components; manned and unmanned aircraft sensor suites; in-theater concept of 
command, control, communications, computers, intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance 
hardware and software; ground stations; active and passive sensor systems; and high-speed data 
transmission and network analytics.  USU/SDL has achieved significant advancement for its 
sponsors in all these areas through its substantial progress in system development, signal 
processing, modeling and analysis, phenomenology, test and evaluation, and weapon system 
engineering, investigations, and assessments of emerging science and communication 
techniques.  SDL's state-of-the art facilities and equipment consist of electro-optical sensor 
calibration/characterization equipment and facilities; integration and testing clean rooms and 
high bays with full contamination control services; space qualification and environmental

testing; nano satellite test and qualification facilities; machine shop; and electronics design and 
assembly labs.  USU/SDL is a multi-disciplined; defense oriented, scientific and technical 
research and development institution.  These capabilities cannot be replicated within the 
Government or external to the Government without considerable investment in time and 
resources, which would significantly delay critical support for missile defense.  USU/SDL has 
provided critically needed scientific and technological research in sensor, electronic, and 
software systems not otherwise available from any existing Government agency or private firm. 
The proposed effort has been reviewed to assure that it falls within the special core capabilities 
of the proposed institution, and it maintains essential engineering capability to be provided by the 
research institution.  USU/SDL meets MDA's scientific and engineering needs and has a proven 
strategic relationship by virtue of its broad knowledge of MDA's missile defense sensors, 
communications and weapons research requirements; past significant ballistic defense 
technology development and engineering efforts; expertise in sensor technology; broad access to 
information including proprietary data; and corporate knowledge and responsiveness based upon 
past performance of MDA's research and engineering requirements.  As a non-profit ins titution 
coupled with its non-interest in competing for mass production of sensors, communication or 
weapons systems, it is independent and objective, and free from real or perceived conflicts of 
interest.  It is a vital part of MDA's sensor technology program, and the continuation of its 
support through a contract is essential to maintain critical engineering, research, and 
development capabilities for the successful development and fielding of an integrated MDS. 
6. Efforts to Obtain Competition (FAR 6.303-2(b)(6)).   
In accordance with FAR 6.303-2(b)(6), efforts to obtain competition for this requirement were 
limited due to the unique nature of UARCs.  As permitted by FAR 6.302-3(a)(2)(ii), full and 
open competition need not be provided when it is necessary to establish or maintain an essential 
engineering, research, or development capability to be provided by an educational or other 
nonprofit institution, such as a UARC.  Consequently, this requirement was not synopsized in 
accordance with FAR 5.2, as UARC acquisitions are exempt from publicizing requirements 
under this authority.  Market research confirmed that only the designated UARC possesses the 
requisite capabilities and institutional knowledge to meet the Government’s needs.  No other 
sources were solicited, as no other organization could fulfill the specific requirements outlined 
for this effort.  This approach ensures the Government maintains critical research and 
development capabilities that are essential to its mission. 
To ensure the UARC obtains as much competition as possible in its subcontracting efforts, the 
Government will require the UARC to select subcontractors on a competitive basis to the 
maximum practical extent consistent with the objectives and requirements of the contract, as 
mandated by FAR 52.244-5.  The Government will monitor the UARC’s subcontracting process 
to confirm compliance with this requirement, including review of documentation supporting 
subcontractor selections.  This approach helps maximize competition at the subcontract level, 
even when the prime contract is awarded on a sole-source basis.

U.S. Customs and Border Protection 
Justification for Exception to Fair Opportunity (JEFO) 
 
_______________ 
1 In this document, citations to RFO Part 16 are citations specifically to Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Class Deviation 26-04 
R1 for FAR Part 16, which was issued as part of the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO), which was implemented in response to 
Executive Order 14275, Restoring Common Sense to Federal Procurement, signed April 15, 2025. 
Date: March 31, 2026 PR Number: 20157631 
1. Agency and Contracting Activity.
The Department of Homeland Security (DHS), U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP), Office of 
Acquisition (OA), Information Technology Contracting Division (ITCD), on behalf of  CBP’s Office of 
Enterprise Services (ES), Office of Information and Technology (OIT), Management and Governance 
Directorate (MGD), prepared this justification for an exception to fair opportunity1. 
2. Nature and/or description of  the action being approved.
CBP intends to issue a modification to firm, fixed-price (FFP) Task Order (TO) 70B04C25F00001307  in 
accordance with (IAW) the terms and conditions of the TO authorized by the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul 
(RFO) 52.217-8, Option to Extend Services, pursuant to RFO 16.507-6(b)(2). This modification action will 
exercise the Option appearing at Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 52.217-8, extending the period of 
performance of this TO up to six (6) months by adding an additional three (3) month option and three (3), one 
(1) month option periods.
A JEFO was previously approved to sole source TO 70B04C25F00001307 as an interim task order with a total 
period of performance of six (6) months, pursuant to FAR 16.505(b)(2)(i)(A) under the One Acquisition 
Solution for Integrated Services  Plus Unrestricted (OASIS+ UR), a General Services Administration (GSA) 
Multi-Agency Contract (MAC) for Enterprise Solutions support services.  
The modification to extend services under TO 70B04C25F00001307 will effectively increase the potential 
task order value and extend the period of performance, inclusive of all options, from 6 months to 12 months to 
provide for the continuity of MGD services, time to adequately recompete this requirement amongst the 
OASIS+ contract awardees, and sufficient time transitions services from the incumbent to the successor 
contractor (time to complete background investigations (BI)s in particular).  
3. A description of the supplies or services required to  meet the agency’s need (including the estimated
value and the period of performance).
The required services outline the need for comprehensive strategy implementation, financial planning, and 
investment management support services to include the delivery of leading commercial off-the-shelf 
technology solutions for automation and decision support.  This includes expert assistance with investment 
management, specifically for Capital Planning and Investment Control (CPIC) coordination, Office of 
Management and Budget (OMB) Business Cases, Standard Investment Reports, and Information Technology 
(IT) Portfolio formulation, along with technical development support for review and submission processes.  
The requirement is to enhance OIT’s budget formulation, planning, and reporting by bringing in best 
practices, increasing visibility and transparency into how IT funds are utilized to provide CBP mission 
outcomes and improve the transparency of strategic planning and governance.

Justification for Exception to Fair Opportunity (JEFO) 
Exceeding the SAT – RFO 16.507-6 
Rationale (for all exceptions):  
The statutory authority permitting other than full and open competition is implemented by RFO 16.507-
6(b)(2)entitled, “ Only one awardee is capable of providing the supplies or services required at the level of 
quality required because the supplies or services ordered are unique or highly specialized.” 
CBP competed the Enterprise Business Management Support Services 2 (EBMSS2) Blanket Purchase 
Agreement (BPA) under full and open competition against the GSA Multiple Award Schedule (MAS). In 
September 2025, CBP awarded a multiple-award BPA established with both large and small business GSA 
contact holders. Thereafter, multiple timely protests were filed against the EBMSS2 BPA. As of the date of this 
JEFO, the EBMSS2 BPA is undergoing protests effectively nullifying the acquisition plan to re-compete the 
MGD requirement against the EBMSS2 BPA and make a timely task order award prior to the expiration of the 
original period of performance of TO 70B04C25F00001307. 
The Contractor support for this requirement must begin April 1, 2026, without a break in service. This 
requirement involves investment management and budget support to ensure compliance with CBP, DHS, and 
OMB policies and guidance. The unique nature of the work being performed under this requirement necessitates 
that, to be successful, the contractor must possess comprehensive knowledge of the DHS Investment 
Evaluation, Submission, and Tracking (INVEST) system, collaboration/coordination with the DHS Office of 
the Chief Information Officer on the DHS Capital Planning and Investment Control (CPIC) process, custom-
designed Dashboards and CBP OIT leadership requirements, IT financial management, planning, and analysis 
services key to cloud migration, tech refresh planning, and cyber security investments for funding requirements 
and justifications. In addition, the contractor must possess full background investigations prior to 
commencement of work. Deloitte Consulting currently works extensively in the INVEST system, thoroughly 
understands the CPIC process, designed the Dashboards used by CBP leadership for budget and investment 
planning purposes, and provides subject matter experts to assist in financial planning, forecasting, and cloud 
migration modernization efforts. 
In addition to CPIC support, the incumbents provide IT financial management, planning, and analysis services 
supporting analytical platforms to inform in-year execution. This support is critical to key ongoing 
modernization efforts, i.e., cloud migration, tech refresh planning, and cyber security investments to inform 
funding requirements and justifications. Due to the planned retirement of the CBP National Data Center, this 
on-going support is critical in financial management and monitoring of CBP’s cloud environments and assisting 
funding decisions for cloud migration. The incumbent supports the initial financial planning process and cost 
estimation for the migration and has retained the personnel and expertise that would be costly to replace.  
Additionally, the size and scope of the incumbent has delivered modernization specific Subject Matter Experts 
(SMEs), as needed throughout the life of the contract within the framework of the firm fixed prices contract. 
Failure to award this as a sole source would result in increased risk and delays in compliance in the following 
areas:  
1) Inability to meet DHS’ due dates for investment reporting in INVEST for 74 IT investments;
2) Insufficient knowledge to effectively maintain Investment Dashboard reporting used by CBP OIT
leadership for 74 investments;
3) Inadequate preparation for monthly Financial Review Board meetings with CBP OIT Leadership on

Justification for Exception to Fair Opportunity (JEFO) 
Exceeding the SAT – RFO 16.507-6 
budget planning and formulation; 
4) Insufficient knowledge critical to the financial planning, forecasting, and monitoring of CBP IT
modernization efforts, i.e., cloud migration, tech refresh, and mission critical programs; and
5) Insufficient knowledge and planning for CBP's cloud hosting costs, putting CBP at risk of
overspending in cloud and physical data center usage and potentially data or application deletion from
having insufficient funds.
Deloitte, with their small business subcontractor Gray Rock, maintains current and active CBP background 
investigations and specialized knowledge and experience necessary to perform the required services without 
disruption until the recompete action can be duly executed by CBP. 
This task order modification will be issued in accordance with the existing terms and conditions of the base 
award and GSA OASIS+UR contract. 
5. Determination by the contracting officer that the an ticipated cost to the Government will be fair and
reasonable.
The Contracting Officer (CO) will determine the price fair and reasonable using one or all of the price 
analysis techniques detailed below, in accordance with RFO 15.404-1(b)(2), which include: (i) comparison 
of proposed prices to historical prices paid, whether by the Government or other than the Government, for 
the same or similar items; RFO 15.404-1(b)(4) comparison with competitive published price lists; and/or 
RFO 15.404-1(b)(5) comparison with the Independent Government Cost Estimate (IGCE). Furthermore, the 
inclusion of RFO 52.217-8, Option to Extend Services, in the task order base award permits the extension of 
services within limits and at the rates specified at the task order award, therefore, the CO can mitigate 
escalation costs by using previously negotiated rates deemed to be fair and reasonable. 
6. Any other facts supporting the justification.
Funding variances, including lapse in annual appropriations, have affected this requirement; however, CBP OIT 
fully intends to compete the next iteration of this contract action to award a task order to include a 12-month 
base period and the inclusion of RFO 52.217-8, Option to Extend Services . CBP must maintain the incumbent 
of the interim task order as it continues to refine and define the requirements for the next competition. 
7. A statement of the actions, if any, the agency may take to remove or overcome any barriers that led to
the exception to fair opportunity before any subsequent acquisition for the supplies or services is made.
CBP is unequivocally committed to achieving competition, to the maximum extent practicable, for this 
requirement. To actively address and overcome the barriers that necessitated this current exception to fair 
opportunity, and to ensure a robust competitive environment for the subsequent acquisition, CBP OIT and 
ITCD have undertaken and will continue to execute proactive measures.  
CBP OIT and ITCD are currently revising the acquisition plan to assess contract vehicles outside the EBMSS2 
BPA.  On March 20,2026, CBP posted a Request for Information (RFI1801914) along with a draft Statement of 
Work (SOW) on GSA OASIS+.

### Sheet: Q&A
TRIDENT_Industry Day Questions |  |  | 
Question ID | Question | Government Response | 
Q1 | Can the Government clarify whether the contractor will be expected to provide and maintain JWICS connectivity at contractor-provided SCIF facilities, or will the Government facilitate JWICS provisioning? Additionally, will the contractor be expected to maintain separate SIPRNET and JWICS enclaves, or will a single multi-level security architecture be acceptable? | If the requirement remains for JWICs connectivity at contractor-provided SCIF facilities, the Government will coordinate JWICS provisioning with the contractor as necessary.  Multi- level security architecture is not currently required, and such architecture will have to be further evaluated. | 
Q2 | Can the Government clarify whether a formal transition period with incumbent contractor knowledge transfer will be provided? If so, what is the anticipated duration of the transition period, and will the Government facilitate access to incumbent personnel, documentation, and systems during transition? | Yes. Transition-in period will be provided with coordination between incumbent and follow-on contractor.  Transition-out requirements are specified in the current DA contract with communication/coordination as necessary to ensure a seamless transition-out.  Currently the draft PWS specifies FOC for transition-in  NLT 60 days. | 
Q3 | Is there a requirement to  bring in an established technology integration ecosystem — including partnerships with defense technology OEMs, national laboratories, and academic institutions — to accelerate the identification, evaluation, and fielding of CWMD-relevant technologies? | This is not a requirement at this time. | 
Q4 | Is the contractor expected to propose a structured assessment methodology for COTS/GOTS and prototype technologies? | This is not a requirement. | 
Q5 | Will DTRA facilitate and coordinate SCI and SAP clearance read-ons? | Yes, DTRA will coordinate reading on individuals to special access and compartmented programs. | 
Q6 | Will the Contractor be expected to maintain a COMSEC Material Control System (CMCS) compliant with CNSSI 4005 or a successor directive? | COMSEC Material Control System  will be coordinated in conjunction with DTRA;  CO is on a subaccount within DTRA and will be maintained locally | 
Q7 | Is there a desire for this capability and an ability to host wargames? | Wargame hosting is not under this effort.  However, the contractor will be responsible to capture lessons learned from wargames and exercises. | 
Q8 | Can the government confirm if the award will not be Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA)? | Correct; Best Value is the current plan. | 
Q9 | Is the government considering oral presentations? | Use of Oral Presentations is under consideration. | 
Q10 | Please confirm classification of SOW. | RFP will be unclassified. PWS will include a classified addendum. Mechanics and instructions on submission and handling of proposal will be provided | 
Q11 | Is SCIF going to be a requirement at the contractor facility? | We are currently looking at the feasibility of SCIF space at the contractor’s site. | 
Q12 | Is effort less than $100 million? | No, this effort is in excess of $100 million. | 
Q13 | Is the Government looking at prioritized tasks over time? | DTRA has undergone budget cuts over time and this may or may not continue in the future.  While this effort is not intended to be an LOE contract, we need the ability to continue to meet mission demands under an ever-changing budget environment. | 
Q14 | Does the government see any specific challenges to accomplish this effort? | Inability to predict global crises and maintain the ability to mobilize and surge when needed to meet those challenges | 
Q15 | Please elaborate on the Research, Development Test and Evaluation (RDT&E) of technologies in the CWMD area. | This effort does not encompass RDT&E of CWMD solutions.  Rather, SMEs will be expected to understand and work with available technologies and provide recommendations and assistance to government.  SMEs will act as advisors, enablers incorporating solutions that are already developed. | 
Q16 | What Key Positions have you required in the past? | Key positions have not yet been determined for this effort, but In the past, the government has required Key positions for the PM and potentially the Task Lead. | 
Q17 | Can you say how many FTEs? | Not at this time. | 
Q18 | How much SCIF space is anticipated? | The government is evaluating the feasibility and amount of SCIF space needed. | 
Q19 | Can you specify where OCONUS requirements are? | Germany, Korea and Australia. | 
Q20 | Will names of companies excluded from competing on this effort be provided? | Yes. | 
Q21 | Is there a prohibition on exclusive teaming? | No. | 
Q22 | Please expand upon the nature of support to CCMDs. | Embedded Teams with CCMDs.  We help integrate DTRA capabilities into CCMDs and we support Teams that support CCMDs. | 
Q23 | Please expand upon the nature of Interagency Support. | We work with Communities of Interest (COI)s, we host LNOs which provide a rapid means to reach back to coordinate rapid response when needed. | 
Q24 | What are challenges to communication? | Coms networks are not always compatible.  We try to work those incompatibilities out with periodic exercises to identify and correct the issues.  Particularly we have seen problems in communication from the battlefield to the JOC and it is helpful to have people forward. |

    - Breaks in communication
    - Loss of government oversight
    - Negative Impact Operations
    - Misunderstanding of People who are forward
    - Loss of knowledge transfer
    - Loss of Geographical moving parts
    - Loss of turnaround response times |

Q33 | What combat support SURGE and in what durations? | If needed, the duration is short term, 60-90 days but not exceeding 180 days. |

Q40 | Does DTRA need operation management, technical support, readiness? | Yes. | 
Q41 | What Intelligence requirements does DTRA have? | None.  DTRA does not have intel authorities. Requests are coordinated with DIA and/or through COCOMs. | 
Q42 | How large is DTRA’s fleet? | DTRA Fleet (spread across 4 locations world wide): 10 x SUVs, 12 x trucks, 11 x vans, 3 x sedans, 7 x forklifts, 8 x trailers. |

THREAT REDUTION THROUGH INTEGRATED DEFENSE & EXPERT NETWORK TACTICS (TRIDENT)

PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT (PWS)

DEFENSE THREAT REDUCTION AGANCY (DTRA)

COMBAT SUPPORT DIRECTORATE (CZ)

INTRODUCTION

DTRA requires support services to provide a wide range of professional analytical services to assist with its mission of countering and deterring Weapons of Mass Destruction (WMD) and emerging threats in the Continental United States (CONUS) and Outside the Continental United States (OCONUS).

The DTRA Combat Support (CZ) Directorate provides advisory and operational support to Combatant Commands (CCMDs), Interagency partners, and Special Operations Forces (SOF) to enhance Countering Weapons of Mass Destruction (CWMD) capabilities. This support includes campaign management, operational planning, irregular warfare support, and WMD defeat advisory services.

These efforts will enhance DTRA’s situational understanding of Combatant Commands (CCMDs) with the integration of analysis, capabilities, technologies, and lessons learned to defeat the enemy networks that employ emerging threat weapons and WMD for strategic effect.

To accomplish this mission, DTRA CZ requires highly specialized contracted support with expertise in WMD, CWMD operations, special access planning, irregular warfare, military deception (MILDEC), and advisory services. 

SCOPE

The scope of this requirement will provide effective support for globally integrated operations, timely responses to WMD threats and activities, and enhanced collaboration with interagency and international partners. The requirements of this effort will provide Professional Services to DTRA CZ across multiple tasks to include classified and compartmented support, operational and strategic planning, data-driven decision support, and campaign management.

PLACE OF PERFORMANCE

The primary place of performance for this effort will be Ft Belvoir, VA with additional customer sites, both CONUS and OCONUS.

TASK 1: PROGRAM MANAGEMENT

1.1 OBJECTIVE

The contractor shall ensure all contract requirements are met, provide cost tracking and financial transparency, and facilitate coordination with Government stakeholders. The contractor shall designate a Program Manager (PM) to serve as the primary interface with the Contracting Officer (KO), Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR), Alternate Contracting Officer’s Representative (ACOR), or Technical Point of Contact (TPOC).  Contractor shall fully empower its PM to manage resources and make program decisions that are within the scope of the TRIDENT contract. Contractor’s PM shall provide management oversight of all program activities, inclusive of the processes, procedures, reports, checks, audits, and systems put in place to ensure the quality of work effort and deliverables. 

The contractor’s PM shall be responsible for: 

Managing contract personnel, including subcontractors. 

Overseeing contract execution, ensuring compliance with contract objectives. 

Identifying and mitigating schedule, performance, technical, and financial risks. 

Conducting cost monitoring and variance analysis. 

Implementing quality assurance measures to maintain performance standards, including timely and accurate submission of all contract deliverables.

1.2 SUBTASKS

1.2.1 PROGRAM MANAGEMENT PLAN (PMP)

The contractor shall develop and submit a Program Management Plan (PMP) in accordance with (IAW) CDRL A001 for government approval that achieves performance outcomes in accordance with the Acceptable Quality Levels (AQLs) described in performance requirements summary (PRS).  

The contractor shall address, at a minimum, the following in their PMP: 

Organizational structure. 

Staffing plan. 

Communications plan. 

Business processes and procedures.  

Task area management. 

Describe how contractor support services will be matrixed across task areas. 

Functional area management. 

Describe how contractor will integrate functional areas  

Subcontractor(s) management. 

Scheduling and monitoring of global mission support operations. 

Prioritizing Requests. 

Problem solving. 

Travel. 

Procurement function. 

Property management. 

Contract management. 

Financial management. 

Reporting. 

Deliverable management. 

After government approval and acceptance of the PMP, the contractor shall receive the COR’s acceptance in writing of the proposed change to the PMP. Contractor shall provide to the government any revisions to PMP within five business days of when changes are agreed.  

1.2.2 MEETINGS, CONFERENCES, REVIEWS, AND EVALUATIONS 

The contractor shall support recurring status meetings, Technical Interchange Meetings (TIMs), conferences, In-Progress Reviews (IPRs), and other performance evaluations with the government to discuss program progress, identify potential obstacles or risks to continued progress, and proactively apply resources to mitigate risk or resolve identified problems (realized risks).  

The contractor shall prepare agendas, meeting minutes, action item lists, and presentation materials for meetings, conferences, reviews, and evaluations. Contractor shall notify the government of its readiness prior to the start of any meeting, review, conference, or evaluation.

DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH & HUMAN SERVICES 
Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services 
7500 Security Boulevard, Mail Stop 00-00-00 
Baltimore, Maryland 21244-1850 
 
Office of Acquisition and Grants Management 
 
 
FEDERAL SUPPLY SCHEDULE SOLE SOURCE JUSTIFICATION 
 
Per Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation Overhaul (RFO) 8.401  
and General Services Administration Acquisition Regulation (GSAR) 538.7104-3(b) 
 
Acquisition Title:  Payment Standardization Calculation, Application and Code Conversion 
Agency:  Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) 
Contracting Officer:  Bridget Rineker 
 
1. Description of Action: 
• Task Order Number: 47QRAA25D002Q/75FCMC26F0064 
• Task Order Award Date: April 8, 2026 
• Total Price: $2,500,000, including options 
• Period of Performance: April 8, 2026, through February 7, 2027, with one 4-month option 
period (transition out) February 8, 2027, through June 7, 2027 
• Name of Contractor: Acumen, LLC  
 
2. Description of Services: 
CMS requires contractor support to (1) maintain and operate its Medicare payment standardization 
programs, providing payment standardization data for use by various CMS, Department of Health & 
Human Services (HHS) and other federal stakeholders for quality measure development, data 
analytics, to support program integrity, fraud prevention, and to support law enforcement; (2) 
convert the existing Statistical Analysis System (SAS) payment standardization codebase into a 
CMS-approved target language; and, (3) where applicable, transition the new, documented codebase 
and all associated payment standardization work to a successor contractor.  
 
3. Sole Source Authority: 
Pursuant to GSAR 538.7104-3(b), only one source is capable of providing the highly specialized 
services and solution required at the level of quality and timeliness demanded by this requirement.   
 
4. Sole Source Rationale: 
Acumen is uniquely qualified to convert the existing SAS payment standardization code into a CMS-
approved target language, as Acumen is the original developer of the SAS-based Medicare payment 
standardization programs currently in production at CMS. This gives Acumen unmatched knowledge 
of the codebase's architecture, logic, analytic transformations, and calculations, knowledge no other 
contractor can replicate with the same accuracy, efficiency, and accountability. 
 
Acumen has also accumulated deep expertise in CMS's payment standardization methodology, 
including specialized payment systems for unique provider types such as Critical Access Hospitals 
(CAHs), Federally Qualified Health Centers (FQHCs), Rural Health Clinics (RHCs), and Indian 
Health Service facilities. Transitioning to an unfamiliar contractor at this stage would introduce 
unacceptable risk of delay, data errors, and failure to meet CMS-specified tolerance thresholds. 
 
  

Page 2 of 2 
 
5. Other Facts and Statements of Action: 
 
• Publication: Pursuant to GSAR 538.7104-3(b)(3), this justification will be made publicly 
available within 14 days after task order award at the Government-Wide Point of Entry for a 
minimum of 30 days. 
 
• Price: This task order represents a fair and reasonable price consistent with GSAR 538.7102-
2(d)(2). 
 
• Follow-On Procurement:  CMS anticipates conducting a competitive procurement for any 
follow-on payment standardization data support. Requiring the contractor to fully document the 
converted codebase and transfer all work to a successor contractor is specifically designed to 
position CMS to compete future work among qualified offerors. 
 
 
This justification is accurate and complete to the best of the Contracting Officer’s knowledge and belief.   
 
 
 April 14, 2026

1. Background & Purpose 
The [Organization/Directorate] will convene one or more workshops to support strategic 
planning, technical exchange, stakeholder engagement, and decision-making. A Workshop 
Planning Committee (WPC) has been established to define objectives, participants, agenda, 
and outcomes. This SOW defines contractor support to provide professional facilitation and 
logistical coordination that ensures the committee’s planning activities and the workshop 
events are efficient, inclusive, compliant, and outcome-driven. 
 
2. Objectives 
The contractor shall: 
1. Provide expert, neutral facilitation for WPC meetings and the workshop(s). 
2. Plan and execute all logistics to support in-person, hybrid, or virtual formats. 
3. Develop artifacts (agendas, minutes, action-item trackers, run-of-show) and maintain 
authoritative records. 
4. Support stakeholder communications, registration, and post-event reporting. 
 
3. Scope of Work 
The scope includes end-to-end support for WPC planning and workshop execution, including: 
● Facilitation services for WPC sessions, working groups, and the workshop(s). 
● Scheduling, coordination, and logistics (venue, A/V, hybrid platforms, and on-site 
support). 
● Participant management (invites, registration, badging/entry coordination, help desk). 
● Agenda design and run-of-show orchestration. 
● Stakeholder communications (save-the-date, email campaigns, participant instructions, 
FAQs). 
● Post-event analysis and recommendations.  
 
4. Tasks & Deliverables 
Task 1: Project Initiation & Planning 
● T1.1 Kickoff & Discovery: Conduct a kickoff within [10] business days of award; 
confirm objectives, constraints, and workshop format(s). 

● T1.2 Project Management Plan (PMP): Deliver a PMP including schedule, milestones, 
roles/responsibilities (RACI), risk management approach, communications plan, and 
quality assurance. 
○ Deliverable D1: PMP (PDF + editable source), due within [15] business days of 
award. 
● T1.3 Facilitation Plan: Develop facilitation approach, participation methods (e.g., 
divergent/convergent techniques), decision frameworks, and escalation paths. 
○ Deliverable D2: Facilitation Plan, due within [20] business days of award. 
Task 2: Committee Support (WPC) 
● T2.1 Meeting Facilitation: Facilitate WPC meetings (cadence: [biweekly/monthly]), 
maintaining neutrality and ensuring agenda discipline, time management, and inclusive 
participation. 
● T2.2 Artifacts & Tracking: Prepare agendas, minutes, action logs, decision logs, 
risk/issues tracker, and attendance records within [3] business days post-meeting. 
○ Deliverables D3: WPC Meeting Pack (agenda + materials) 
○ Deliverables D4: WPC Minutes & Logs (action/decision/risk), delivered within [3] 
business days post-meeting. 
Task 3: Workshop Design 
● T3.1 Agenda & Run-of-Show: Co-develop workshop agenda, session objectives, 
timeboxing, speakers/facilitators, and buffer contingencies. 
○ Deliverable D5: Draft Agenda & Run-of-Show (v1), due [30] days before 
workshop; final due [7] days before. 
● T3.2 Session Materials: Create templates (slide decks, breakout worksheets, polling 
questions, evaluation forms). 
○ Deliverable D6: Session Materials Package, due [10] days before workshop. 
● T3.3 Hybrid/Virtual Design: Recommend platforms (e.g., Teams, ZoomGov), settings, 
engagement tools (Q&A, polls, whiteboarding), and remote participation standards. 
Task 4: Logistics & Operations 
● T4.1 Venue & A/V: Coordinate venue procurement (government-furnished or contractor-
arranged per COR guidance), room layouts, A/V, recording (if authorized), signage, 
wayfinding, and accessibility accommodations. 
● T4.2 Registration & Participant Management: Build/manage registration site or list, 
handle invitations, confirmations, pre-event comms, and on-site check-in/badging 
coordination per facility policies. 
○ Deliverable D7: Logistics Plan & Checklist (venue/A‑V, floor plan, seating, 
catering, badges, accessibility, sustainability), due [21] days before workshop. 
● T4.3 On-Site/Live Support: Provide staff for check-in desk, A/V liaison, session 
timekeeping, materials distribution, and speaker support. 

● T4.4 Contingency & Risk: Maintain contingency procedures (backup rooms, A/V 
redundancy, remote failover). 
Task 5: Communications & Stakeholder Engagement 
● T5.1 Messaging & Branding: Develop save-the-date, formal invites, joining 
instructions, FAQ, and house rules; align with [Agency/Center] brand guidance. 
○ Deliverable D8: Communications Pack (templates + schedule), due [30] days 
before workshop. 
● T5.2 Pre-Event Briefings: Provide speaker/host briefings and technical checks. 
● T5.3 Accessibility & Section 508: Ensure materials and platforms meet accessibility 
standards; provide alternative formats upon request. 
Task 6: Post-Event Reporting & Closeout 
● T6.1 Outcomes & Recommendations: Consolidate decisions, actions 
(owners/deadlines), risks/issues, and recommendations. 
○ Deliverable D9: Post-Event Report (executive summary; outcomes; metrics; 
lessons learned; recommendations), due within [10] business days after 
workshop. 
● T6.2 Data & Records: Provide finalized artifacts and transfer authoritative records per 
records management requirements. 
○ Deliverable D10: Records Package (minutes, logs, materials, registration 
metrics), due within [10] business days after workshop.

United States Transportation Command, Directorate of Acquisition, IT Programs & Support Services 
Division (USTRANSCOM/TCAQ-D), 508 Scott Drive, Scott AFB, IL 62225. 
 
2. NATURE AND/OR DESCRIPTION OF THE ACTION BEING APPROVED: 
 
The proposed action is award of a sole-source Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract to 
UNCOMN, LLC to provide mission-essential enterprise architecture, enterprise data, and enterprise 
engineering (EADE) technical support services to USTRANSCOM, Air Force Life Cycle Management 
Center (AFLCMC), and the U.S. Army Transportation Command (ARTRANS). The IDIQ will include 
Firm Fixed Price (FFP), Labor Hour (LH), and Time & Material (T&M) contract line items (CLINs). 
Funding will be applied at the task order level. 
 
These services were competed in CY2025, and a contract (HTC71126DE116) was awarded; however, a 
small business size protest is currently pending with the Small Business Administration (SBA). This 
action will support critical EADE services until the protest is resolved and the Government is able to 
acquire support under the follow-on contract.  
 
3. DESCRIPTION OF SERVICES REQUIRED TO MEET THE AGENCY’S NEEDS: 
 
The EADE contract will provide professional services, enterprise-wide support, and technical guidance 
related to mission needs and issues concerning the above commands and the Joint Deployment and 
Distribution Enterprise (JDDE). These services include operational and system perspectives of 
Command and Control (C2), planning, transportation, logistics, and business support system domains. 
Additionally, this requirement will continue support for prototyping, information support plan 
development, software development, and system administration allowing enterprise architecture data to 
reside in integrated architecture tool suites. These services allow USTRANSCOM and its component 
commands to share information and data across the enterprise, maintaining a true enterprise view.  
 
Since 2020, the EADE contract has been supported by the incumbent contractor, UNCOMN, LLC under 
HTC71120DD002. This was a competitive, small-business set-aside, single award IDIQ. 11 task orders 
were issued against this IDIQ. The awarded period of performance under all task orders ended on 30 
September 2025. After utilizing the full six months of FAR 52.217-8, Option to Extend Services, for 
each task order, the periods of performance (PoPs) are now set to expire on 31 March 2026.
  
 
 
Controlled by: USTRANSCOM  
Controlled by: Directorate of Acquisition 
CUI Category/ies: PROCURE 
Limited Dissemination Control: FED ONLY

CUI

6. DESCRIPTION OF EFFORTS MADE TO ENSURE THAT OFFERS ARE SOLICITED 
FROM AS MANY POTENTIAL SOURCES AS POSSIBLE. 
 
The market research report determined the level of collaboration required to continue services performed 
under the current EADE contract could pose a challenge to non-incumbents. To address this, a transition 
period was required for the follow-on acquisition. In accordance with FAR Part 5, the Government has 
determined a notice for the bridge requirement will not be publicized, as this action falls under the 
exception outlined in FAR 5.101(b)(2). The unusual and compelling urgency of the requirement does not 
allow the Government to comply with the publicizing timelines outlined in FAR Part 5. Publicizing this 
action would delay the award of the bridge contract, resulting in unacceptable interruptions to mission-
critical services.  
 
7. DETERMINATION BY THE CONTRACTING OFFICER THAT THE ANTICIPATED 
COST TO THE GOVERNMENT WILL BE FAIR AND REASONABLE. 
 
The Government will ensure the final price is fair and reasonable by conducting a detailed price analysis 
using one or more techniques outlined in FAR 15.404-1(b)(2). The Government has historical pricing 
from the predecessor contract (HTC71120DD002) and will also compare the proposed pricing to the 
pricing evaluated for HTC71126DE116, the protested action, which was determined fair and reasonable 
on 19 September 2025.  
  
8. THE REASON MARKET RESEARCH WAS NOT CONDUCTED. 
 
Due to the unusual and compelling urgency, market research was not conducted. As detailed above, the 
agency reviewed and adopted the market research report from Fiscal Year 2024 for EADE solicitation 
HTC71125RD002, which provided the basis for the Government’s decision to award a bridge contract to 
UNCOMN LLC.  The circumstances surrounding this requirement necessitate immediate action to 
ensure continuity of critical services and prevent unacceptable delays that would jeopardize mission 
success. The urgency of this acquisition leaves no time to conduct meaningful stand-alone market 
research without compromising the Government’s ability to have mission support. This action will 
support critical EADE services until the protest is resolved and the Government is able to acquire 
support under the follow-on contract. 
 
9. ANY OTHER FACTS SUPPORTING THE USE OF OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN 
COMPETITION. 
 
Transition to a new contractor at this critical juncture would introduce substantial risks to operational 
continuity, jeopardizing the coverage required to continued support. In addition, the time required to 
conduct a new competitive procurement, resolve potential post-award protests, and transition would 
drastically exceed the available timeframe, making it impossible to award a competitive interim contract 
before 1 April 2026.  
 
10. LISTING OF THE SOURCES, IF ANY, THAT EXPRESSED AN INTEREST IN THE 
ACQUISITION. 
 
Offers from other sources were not solicited for this bridge extension; however, the follow-on 
competition remains active. The follow-on acquisition has been impacted by a protest

BARRIERS TO COMPETITION BEFORE ANY SUBSEQUENT ACQUISITION FOR

STATEMENT OF WORK 
 
1. Objective/Requirements 
The development of the Quantitative Elemental Reconnaissance Instrument (QuERI) 
requires the design of electronics for a two-channel SDD system for spectroscopy 
and timing. Working the from the NICER heritage design, the electronics will 
integrate an FPGA in place of the microcontroller. Additionally, the electronic 
architecture will be designed to interface and/or control other system components 
(e.g., mechanical shutter, S-ray source electronics). 
 
2. Characteristics, Scope, and Specs 
The contractor shall perform the following duties:  
• Translation of science requirements to engineering requirements 
• Participate in the preparation of interface control documents 
• Develop electronic architecture and detailed schematics 
• Provide netlists and bill of materials for layout and fabrication and consult on 
these activities 
• Test and characterize the fabricated electronics 
• Make revisions to the design as required by the test results 
• Prepare detailed engineering documentation 
• Prepare reports and participate in team meetings 
 
 
3. Place of Performance 
Noqsi Aerospace, Ltd, Billerica MA 
 
4. Period of Performance 
Activities shall be performed March 15, 2026 through September 30, 2026.
