STATEMENT OF WORK

Lone Worker Devices and Monitoring Services

GENERAL: Central Arkansas Veterans Health Care System has a requirement for 140 lone worker safety monitoring devices for home care and community worker programs with 24/7/365 monitoring. This procurement is necessary to address the increase in safety events which include assaults, battery and aggressive animal attacks on home care staff. In addition, the lone worker safety monitoring device will improve timely notification of police and other emergency services while staff are out in the community and experience a disruptive event that increases the risk of harm to staff. 

BACKGROUND: Home Care and Community Workers are required to travel frequently throughout the community which increases the risk of encountering situations that places them at risk for harm (Bussing & Hoge, 2004). Civil unrest, violence in a home environment or entering environments where other VA staff or police are not present increases the likelihood of delayed awareness when a staff member is harmed or in danger. Staff are dependent on the ability to grab a VA issued smart phone, unlock the phone and then dial 911 while trying to flee from an unsafe situation. The lone worker safety monitoring device allows staff to push a button on device which is located on lanyard or on a badge holder on the outside of their shirt. The silent alarm does not emit an audible signal which prevents others from being aware that help was activated and does not further escalate the situation. The monitoring company will listen in and call for help when signs of struggles, distress or silence are detected.

With expanding demand for increased in-home care, little research and evidence is available that demonstrates proven techniques to increase personal safety.  Central Arkansas Veterans Health Care System Community Worker programs currently report to various service lines and information on safety events is not well known outside of individual programs. Community based programs are comprised of front-line staff and leadership representation. This facility is working towards standardization of processes, policies and safety precautions.

SCOPE: Central Arkansas Veterans Health Care system is requesting contractors provide specific equipment due to the listed salient characteristics in this section that meets the safety requirements of home care and community worker program needs. 

A Base plus 4-Year Option. 

      Base Year: POP  06/15/2026 – 06/14/2027

Option Year 1: POP 06/15/2027 – 06/14/2028

Option Year 2: POP 06/15/2028 – 06/14/2029

Option Year 3: POP 06/15/2029 – 06/14/2030

Option Year 4: POP 06/15/2030 – 06/14/2031

PHYSICAL CHARACTERISTICS: Equipment must have the physical characteristics needed for utilization with lone worker monitoring devices. The implementation of safety devices for lone workers in the community will have far reaching implications for direct care staff. This project impacts multiple services that will experience increased staff satisfaction related to enhanced personal safety. There may be an opportunity to use data to better understand the number of safety events occurring on an on-going basis.    

FUNCTIONAL AND PERFORMANCE CHARACTERISTICS: Equipment must provide the following functional and performance capability based on evidenced based research on personal safety standards, using recommendations from home care and emergency management experts, and endorsed by local end-users.  Additional function, performance and salient characteristics include:

Must come with 24/7/365 monitoring.

Check-in/Check-out feature.

Incapacitation/Man-Down detection.

Silent notification signal.

Global Positioning System/Global Navigation Satellite System (GPS/GNSS) dual signal detection and reporting.

Badge holder appearance to the public.

Immediate notification to emergency services.

Escalation notification to Veteran Health Administration when safety alert sent or man-down detected.

Ongoing customer support.

SPECIFIC NEED/SALIENT CHARACTERISTIC’S:  

Design:   Badge holder design

Panic alarm

Incapacitation/Man-Down detection

Immediate notification to emergency services.

Check-in/Check-out feature

GPS/GNSS dual signal detection and reporting

Waterproof and dust proof

24/7/365 monitoring

PERFORMANCE MONITORING: Employee safety device will operate on charge and allow for GPS/GNSS location detection when powered on. 

POTENTIAL REQUIREMENT GROWTH: The Government may require additional effort in order to successfully accomplish the Government’s scope of this requirement. The Government reserves the right to include additional staff and Service Lines within Central Arkansas Veterans Healthcare System as required and funding becomes available.  In accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation 52.212-4, any changes in the terms and conditions of this contract may be made only by written agreement of the Contractor and Contracting Officer.  The price for services for additional Service Lines are to be determined upon agreement between the Contractor and the Contracting Officer via bi-lateral modification at the Government’s request.

PLACE OF DELIVERY AND PERFORMANCE:

DELIVERY SCHEDULE: All items to be delivered within 30 days of purchase order processing and order placement.  

WARRANTY OF EQUIPMENT: Contractor must provide any manufacturer(s) warranty on devices.

SECURITY: The C&A requirements do not apply, and the Security Accreditation Pages is not required.

INFORMATION SECURITY: The contractors, their personnel, and their subcontractors shall be subject to the Federal laws, regulations, standards and VA Directives and Handbooks regarding information and information system security as delineated in this contract.

ACCESS TO VA INFORMATION AND VA INFORMATION SYSTEMS:  Custom software development and outsourced operations must be located in the U.S. to the maximum extent practical.  If such services are proposed to be performed abroad and are not disallowed by other VA policy or mandates, the contractor/subcontractor must state where all non-U.S. services are provided and detail a security plan, deemed to be acceptable by VA, specifically to address mitigation of the resulting problems of communication, control, data protection and so forth.  Location within the U.S. may be an evaluation factor.  

The contractor will not have access to VA Desktop computers, nor will they have access to online resources belonging to the government while conducting services. If removal of equipment from the VA is required, any memory storage devices, such as hard drives, solid state drives and non-volatile memory units will remain in VA control and will not be removed from VA custody.

This justification was prepared in accordance with FAR 16.505 by the Federal Communications
Commission {FCC), Headquarters {HQ), Office of the Managing Director {OMD), Enterprise
Acquisition Center {EAC) located at 45 L Street NE, Washington, DC 20554. The managing
program is the Public Safety and Homeland Security Bureau {PSHSB).
2. Nature and/or description of the action being approved.
To effectively manage risks to the U.S. communications sector and all dependent critical
infrastructure sectors and resources, the FCC requires an integrated solution enabling FCC staff
to analyze data from disparate sources and identify entities, equipment, and services that are
potentially owned, controlled, or influenced by foreign adversarial countries.
The Secure and Trusted Communications Networks Act of 2021 directed the Federal 
Communications Commission {FCC) to publish and update on its website a list of any 
communications equipment or service that poses an unacceptable risk to the national security 
of the United States or the security and safety of United States persons. These determinations 
are made by executive branch interagency bodies with appropriate national security expertise, 
including the Federal Acquisition Security Council {FASC); by the Department of Commerce 
pursuant to Executive Order No. 13873; by an appropriate national security agency; or for any 
communications equipment or services defined as covered telecommunications equipment or 
services under section 889{f){3) of the John S. McCain National Defense Authorization Act of 
2019. Updating this list-particularly identifying subsidiaries and affiliates of entities on the 
covered list-requires the ability to access and analyze official company filings and other public 
data available across hundreds of thousands of sources in multiple formats. 
Further, PSHSB is responsible for responding to requests for information from the determining 
bodies mentioned in the STCNA, the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States 
{CFIUS), and the Committee for the Assessment of Foreign Participation in the U.S. 
Telecommunications Services Sector {Team Telecom) which may solicit FCC feedback on 
investigations and cases which assess the national security risks of certain communications 
companies, equipment, and services. These requests for support require a rapid response in 
order to meet statutory deadlines. For these purposes, the FCC is in need of one or more 
solutions enabling the expedited analysis of aggregated data from multiple data streams and 
sources. Data sources would provide insights into company ownership; investment and investor 
stakeholders and percentages; consumers; tariff or sanction data. 

3. A description of the supplies or services required to meet the agency's needs (i ncluding the
estimated value).
Product: Quantifind GraphyteSearch Licenses
Description: Quantifind is a readily-available, Artificial Intelligence-enabled research database
that persistently inventories publicly available information relating to business ownership,
investment, trade, tariff, sanction data, and media information relating to specific businesses,
people, research entities, and academic institutions. Quantifind automatically scans across a
broad range of public and online data including on line news sources, company registration data,
and leaks databases; seeds queries with minimally available information as a name or email
address to cultivate analyses leading to the discovery of supply chain risk factors on transaction
counterparties and other non-customers; assesses risk relationships by revealing the entities
related to a known individual or business that are surfaced from across the external data and
rank-ordered for risk and relevancy; verification of Ultimate Beneficial Ownership {UBO) when
risk exposure is high; automated report generation; and the ability to integrate FCC-specific data
and enable case management. Further, Quantifind offers the ability to integrate external data
sources through Application Programmable Interface {API) management.

 SUPPORT TO DATA MANAGEMENT SERVICE – TRANSFER 
(DMS-T)

NCIA/ACQ/2026/06991 
Thursday, 09 April 2026 
 
NCIA Request for Information (RFI) 
 
To: Industry Partners 
Distribution List 
 
  
1. The NATO Communications and Information Agency (NCIA) is conducting market 
research to identify qualified vendors and gather input on potential solutions to support the 
ability of transfer data on the unclassified network, classified network and cross-domain.  
We hereby issue the attached Request for Information (RFI) RFI-187018-DMS_T to solicit 
feedback from capable and interested industry partners. 
2. This RFI is issued for planning purposes only and is not a request for bids . It is part of 
NCIA’s effort to ensure it has a clear understanding of the marketplace, available 
capabilities, and potential acquisition strategies to deliver ACO capabilities under the Intel 
and ISR Functional Services Data Management Project.  
3. We value your insight and invite you to: 
a. Provide a response to the information requested at Annex A. 
b. Share relevant corporate capabilities and experience; 
c. Review and comment on our draft requirements (Annex B) with a view to 
providing recommendations for improving performance outcomes, competition, 
effectiveness and efficiency; and identifying any risks or concerns that should be 
considered during planning. 
d. Provide your responses to the RFI questions in Annex C. 
4. Submission instructions and additional details can be found in the enclosure to this RFI. 
5. Only companies from a NATO member country can participate in or respond to this RFI 
(https://www.nato.int/cps/en/natohq/nato_countries.htm). 
6. Should you have any questions or need clarification, please contact Adrian Lita, Senior 
Contracting Officer (Consultant), at Adrian.Lita@ncia.nato.int  
7. We thank you in advance for your time and input, and we look forward to engaging with 
you as we shape this potential acquisition. 
 
8. Annexes: 
 
• Request for Information at Annex A 
• High-Level Summary of Requirements at Annex B 
• RFI Questions at Annex C 
• Distribution List at Annex D    
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 
NCIA/ACQ/2026/06991 
 
  
 Page 3

REQUEST FOR INFORMATION  
A. Introduction 
 
1. The NATO Communications and Information Agency (NC IA) is conducting market 
research to identify potential sources  and gather information regarding industry 
capabilities, through eliciting industry views on the envisioned services for transfer of 
ISR data outlined at Annex B - to inform the project requirements . This Request for 
Information (RFI) is issued solely for informational purposes and does not constitute a 
Request for Proposal (RFP), Request for Quotation (RFQ), or invitation for bid.  
B. Purpose 
 
1. The purpose of this RFI is to obtain input from industry to help inform the NCIA’s 
acquisition planning. Responses to this RFI will assist in refining requirements, 
identifying capabilities, and shaping the strategy for any future solicitation. 
C. Background 
 
1. ISR Functional Services programme represents NATO's commitment to establish a 
common digital data platform to manage multi-source/domain data from ingest through 
to dissemination from an unclassified to a classified environment and the provision of 
reusable core services to manage linkages and dependencies for both the Intelligence 
community and other Communities of Interests (CoIs). 
2. DMS-T will provide a data transfer capability to transfer collected ISR data on the 
unclassified network, classified network and cross-domain.  
3. The Service is envisaged to support Data Management Service capabilities already 
established within Alliance Persistence Surveillance from Space (APSS) programme, 
adopt and enhance them accordingly if needed.  
4. A High-Level Summary of the DMS-T requirements are contained within Annex B. 
5. The RFI seeks to elicit the view of industry partners on the scope of the envisioned 
services and facilitate the Agency’s insight into best -in-class industry solutions , 
including current market capabilities, and pricing models of Services offered. 
6. A full list of questions that the Agency would like to canvass industry views on are 
contained within Annex C 
D. Submission Instructions 
 
1. Interested parties are invited to respond in accordance with the instructions below: 
 
a. Submit responses via the email address in section H no later than 12:00 hours 
Central European Time (CET) on 07 May 2026. 
b. Responses should be submitted in PDF or Word format and must not exceed 10 
pages, including: 
i. Responses to Annex A, comments on Annex B 
ii. Responses to the questions in Annex C 
 
excluding: 
i. Cover page 
ii. Company brochures or product literature (if included) 
iii. Attachments such as past performance references 
 
c. Use the following subject line for submission 
i. “Response to RFI [RFI-187018-DMS_T] – [Company Name]” 

 
NCIA/ACQ/2026/06991 
 
  
 Page 5 
 
NCIA-ACQ-1.017(07.25)    
 
E. Industry Engagement 
 
1. The NCIA does not envisage conducting further industry engagement following the 
receipt of RFI responses.  
2. However, should this approach change, further information on additional RFIs and/or 
Industry Day events will be published through the NCIA ‘ Current Opportunities’ page 
and distributed via the National Delegations, NATEXs, and Embassies.  
F. Disclaimer

1. INTRODUCTION 
Headquarters Supreme Allied Commander Transformation (HQ SACT) is issuing this 
Request for Information (RFI) to engage with industry to conduct a current state of abilities 
for commercial industry to provide solutions to NATO capability requirements. The intention 
is to evaluate what could be immediately available, the art-of-the-possible, and current 
state-of-the-art capabilities with respect to eTacC capability, products, services, 
technologies, and methodologies. 
 
This Request for Information (RFI) does not constitute a commitment to issue a future 
request for proposal (RFP). The purpose of this request is to involve industry through 
collaboration, in an examination of future capabilities and an analysis of potential 
alternatives related to the implementation of the eTacC Capability Program Plan (CPP). 
 
Further, respondents are advised that HQ SACT will not pay for any information or 
administrative costs incurred in responding to this RFI. The costs for responding to this RFI 
shall be borne solely by the responding party. Not responding to this RFI does not preclude 
participation in any subsequent RFP if issued in the future. All information shared with ACT 
might be shared with contracted third parties to support the capability development process 
as needed. Provision of data, or lack of, will not prejudice any respondent if there is a 
competitive bidding process later as part of NATO Common-Funded Capability 
Development. 
2. BACKGROUND 
2.1. The North Atlantic Treaty Organization is exploring communication, networking, and data 
transformation solutions that will enable increased connectivity at the tactical edge across 
a multitude of legacy and emergent bearers, waveforms, and protocols.   
2.2. NATO's Enhanced Tactical Connectivity (eTacC) capability is envisioned to be a node 
which acts as a relay, gateway, and translator enabling the realization of Multi-Domain 
Operations through the bridging of heterogenous tactical networks based on operational 
demands. 
 
This is not a formal request for submissions as part of a procurement; but rather a 
general request intended to determine whether any possible solutions exist that 
should be included in one or many alternatives during the development. 
 
3. PROJECT DESCRIPTION 
3.1. Vision 
3.1.1. The North Atlantic Treaty Organization is exploring communication, networking, 
and data transformation solutions that will enable increased connectivity at the 
tactical edge across a multitude of legacy and emergent bearers, waveforms, 
and protocols.  NATO's Enhanced Tactical Connectivity (eTacC) capability is 
envisioned to be a node which acts as a relay, gateway, and translator enabling 
the realization of Multi-Domain Operations through the bridging of heterogenous 
tactical networks based on operational demands. The intent of this RFI is to 
solicit feedback from industry to help shape NATO's ambition. 

NATO UNCLASSIFIED 
HQ Supreme Allied Commander Transformation 
RFI-ACT-SACT-04-2026 
 
Page 4 of 9  
3.1.2. The eTacC capability seeks to enhance NATO’s ability to execute duties across 
the SACEUR AOR to provide the capability to communicate beyond line of sight 
during multidomain operations.  The eTacC capability will use a meshed 
communications capability enabling operations in a contested environment and 
bring spaced based information to the tactical level. 
 
3.1.3. The implementation of eTacC requires coherent alignment with other related 
and interconnected work strands. Therefore, based on eTacC operational and 
associated Capability Requirements (CRs), NATO is issuing this RFI to gain a 
better understanding of the national capabilities (GOTS/MOTS solutions) and of 
the commercial market and that is to provide this capability that NATO could 
potentially use to acquire eTacC solutions that meet the CRs. 
 
3.2. Objectives 
3.2.1. NATO has started developing the capabilities required for eTacC to align with 
the ORs which were stated in the ORS. 
 
3.2.2. With the development of capabilities, eTacC implementation efforts will neither 
supersede any existing NATO processes, nor impact initiatives that are not the 
responsibility of NATO AFSC. NATO eTacC efforts will support these processes 
and initiatives where applicable, thus avoiding any duplication of efforts. 
 
3.2.3. The eTacC capability seeks to identify broad areas of connectivity and 
communications gaps and lead to their rapid closure. This RFI will provide the 
ability to leverage assets and resources coming from related NATO 
Programmes capabilities, assets, and resources coming from Nations, their 
Industry, and their Academia, and finally filling the gaps of missing capabilities, 
assets, resources needed to achieve tactical level interoperability and 
connectivity.

NATO UNCLASSIFIED 
HQ Supreme Allied Commander Transformation 
RFI-ACT-SACT-04-2026 
 
Page 5 of 9  
 
3.2.4. Allied Command Transformation (ACT) is surveying Industry and Academia to 
understand what solutions may be able to support eTacC requirements. 
 
3.2.5. This survey seeks to gather information from Industry and Academia on existing 
eTacC solutions, as well as those in development that could potentially be 
procured by NATO. 
 
3.3. Expected Benefits to Respondents 
3.3.1. Market research to increase services provided that could broaden future 
markets and client base. 
3.3.2. Potential to broaden into military sector and international market. 
 
3.4. Expected Benefits to NATO 
3.4.1. Resilient and persistent eTacC capability solutions that meet current NATO 
Operational and Capability Requirements. 
3.4.2. Increased operational and tactical advantages over potential threats. 
 
4. REQUESTED INFORMATION 
4.1. The response(s) to this RFI shall be submitted by e-mail. 
Submissions must include both the Contracting and Technical POCs 
listed on page 2. The responses shall not contain proprietary and/or classified 
information. HQ SACT reserves the right to seek clarification on submissions. 
 
4.2. Eligibility to Respond: 
Only NATO Nations, Industry, and Academia that originate or are chartered/incorporated 
within NATO Nations are eligible to respond to this RFI. Companies from Partner Nations 
who want to participate should collaborate with a primary company headquartered within 
a NATO Nation. 
 
4.3. Response Template:

4.3.8. Responses shall not be classified above NATO UNCLASSIFIED.

of, will not prejudice any respondent if there is a competitive bidding process later as 
part of NATO Common Funded Capability Development.

4.5. Response Due Date 
Responses to this RFI must be received by 0900 am ET on 29 May 2026. The

5. CLARIFICATIONS AND QUESTIONS 
 
Technical inquiries about this RFI shall be submitted by e-mail solely to the POCs by 0900

All questions should be submitted by 11 May 2026 to allow for appropriate response time

6. ADDITIONAL INFORMATION 
 
6.1. Non-disclosure Principles and/or Non-disclosure Agreement (NDA) with Third

Analysis of Alternatives (AoA) investigation in support of this project. HQ SACT will 
follow nondisclosure principles and possibly conclude an NDA with that company to 
protect submitted information from further disclosure. As the third-party beneficiary of

JUSTIFICATION FOR AN EXCEPTION TO FAIR OPPORTUNITY 
1. Contracting Activity: Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) 
     Office of Procurement, Acquisition, and Logistics 
      Technology Acquisition Center 
      2 3 Christopher Way 
      Eatontown, NJ 07724 
       
2. Description of Action: 
 
The proposed action is for a firm-fixed price (FFP) order to be issued under National 
Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) Solutions for Enterprise-Wide 
Procurement (SEWP) V Government-Wide Acquisition Contract (GWAC) for brand 
name Laurel Bridge enterprise products supporting VA Office of Information & 
Technology (OIT) Health, Clinical Imaging, Digital Imaging and Communication in 
Medicine (DICOM) facility operations teams by supporting routing of image data, 
streamlining workflow processes through automation, enables robust DICOM message 
handling in VistA, and ensures historical and new imaging studies remain accessible at 
the point of care throughout VA’s nationside modernization efforts. 
 
Facility Operations: 
1. Lighthouse Licenses 
2. Compass Store DICOM Router Licenses 
 
3. Description of the Supplies or Services: 
 
The VA, OIT, Health, Clinical Imaging, has a requirement for renewal of existing 
maintenance license subscriptions for compass routers, Lighthouse licenses, and 
support services current fielded brand name Laurel Bridge products that supports 
imaging facility operations and technical development/implementation.  The base period 
will include the Laurel Bridge operational DICOM compass routers and Lighthouse 
perpetual licenses maintenance supporting enterprise-wide image data activities among 
VA facilities, community providers, and Department of War (DOW). Required software 
maintenance and support includes periodic updates, enhancements, and corrections to 
the software as well as technical/help desk support.  The period of performance for this 
action will include a 12-month base, and the total estimated price of the proposed action 
is  
   
4. Statutory Authority:  
 
Pursuant to Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 16.505(a)(4), the following brand 
name requirement is being justified and approved as an exception to fair opportunity 
under the statutory authority of Section 41 U.S.C. 4106(c)(2) as implemented by FAR 
16.505(b)(2)(i)(B), entitled “Only one awardee is capable of providing the supplies or 
services required at the level of quality required because the supplies or services 
ordered are unique or highly specialized”. 
 


  CONTROL NUMBER VA-26-00047245 
Page 2 of 5 
JA Template_FAR 16.5_(08-AUG-2024) 
5. Rationale Supporting Use of Authority Cited Above:  
 
Based on the market research, as described in Section 8 of this justification, it has been 
determined that limited competition is available among resellers of the required annual 
maintenance for the existing VA owned Laurel Bridge DICOM DCF local server runtime 
licenses, compass routers, Run-time licenses, PowerTool Suite, developer toolkits, 
Lighthouse licenses, and support services. VA utilizes Laurel Bridge DCF software to 
develop VistA Imaging applications for all VHA facilities. VA anticipates the need to 
utilize these Laurel Bridge products for for at least the next six (6) years. The required 
annual maintenance for products supports the Government daily imaging activites 
required to support critical health care services to Veterans timely and efficiently 
ensuring the VistA Imaging applications are operational and accessible with minimal 
interruption for patient care services. 
 
To maintain the existing Laurel Bridge products, a source must have access to its 
proprietary source code to provide the required support, configuration, and software 
updates.  No other source has the capability of developing/issuing software updates for 
the Laurel Bridge software due to the proprietary nature of the source code.  In addition, 
any other source would need access to this code to ensure all services provided are 
properly configured.  Therefore, only Laurel Bridge, or its authorized resellers, can 
provide the required maintenance support services for the currently fielded software and 
the annual maintenance of the Laurel Bridge DCF products and services required for 
VistA Imaging.  
 
If Laurel Bridge DCF is not procured, reengineering VistA Imaging to use an alternate 
toolkit is currently estimated to cost approximately $7M for the first year and take a 
minimum of 12 months to complete, in addition to the cost of the alternate toolkit 
estimated at $660,000 per year. This estimate is based on previous acquisition history, 
and it is not expected these duplicative costs would be recovered through competition. 
 
Failure to procure the required annual maintenance of the existing Government owned 
Laurel Bridge products and services would result in VA’s inability to evoke existing VistA 
Imaging applications to acquire, store and provide DICOM medical images among 150+ 
VA Medical Centers, the Department of War (DOW) medical care system and 
community providers resulting in negative outcomes from delays of health care services 
to Veterans. 
 
6. Efforts to Obtain Competition:  
 
Market research was conducted, details of which are in section 8 of this justification. 
This effort did not yield any additional sources that can meet the Government’s 
requirements. However, the undersigned VA technical representative determined 
that limited competition is available among authorized resellers for brand name 
Laurel Bridge, as well as software maintenance and support. In accordance with 
FAR 16.505(a)(4)(iii)(A)(1), this justification will be provided with the solicitation to all 
appropriate NASA SEWP V GWAC holders.  Furthermore, in accordance with FAR 
5.301, 16.505(b)(2)(ii)(D), and 16.505(a)(4)(iii), the award notice for this action will 

  CONTROL NUMBER VA-26-00047245 
Page 3 of 5 
JA Template_FAR 16.5_(08-AUG-2024) 
be synopsized on the Contract Opportunities website and this justification will be 
made publicly available within 14 days of award. 
 
7. Actions to Increase Competition:  
 
The Government will continue to conduct market research to ascertain if there are 
changes in the market place that would enable future actions to be competed. 
 
8. Mar
ket Research:  
 
The Government’s technical experts conducted market research from February to 
March 2026 by reviewing maintenance support services available from resellers of 
Laurel Bridge software.  Specifically, the Government’s technical experts reviewed 
products/services available from resellers (Minburn, V3 Gate) and Laurel Bridge to 
determine which sources can provide software maintenance licenses and support on 
the existing Laurel Bridge software.  Based on this review, it was determined that no 
other source could provide required licenses and maintenance support for Laurel 
Bridge software other than Laurel Bridge or one of its resellers because they lacked 
access to the proprietary source code necessary to provide the required support, 
configuration, and software updates.  Only Laurel Bridge or its resellers can access 
the proprietary source code to maintain the current fielded Laurel Bridge licenses. As 
described in Section 5 above, use of any other brand of software is not tenable due 
to the embedded code in the current infrastructure that is currently used at VA sites. 
 
The Government’s technical experts also reviewed public data to determine if 
applications developed by other vendors utilizing the Laurel Bridge products could 
be evoked either without using Laurel Bridge products or using an alternate 
manufacturer’s (Medical Connections, Ltd, MicroDicom, LeadTools, Merge 
Healthcare by IBM, Intelerad, DICOM Systems, AGFA, Sectra and Fujifilm Medical 
Systems, etc.) products, to which the results were inconclusive. As described above 
in section 5, the VistA Imaging software components that leverage the Laurel Bridge 
DICOM toolkit would need significant redesign to use another toolkit.  VistA Imaging 
neither has the funding, nor the development flexibility to support this redesign at 
this time. 
 
Given the VA legacy version of the Laurel Bridge software is proprietary or closed 
sourced, meaning the code is not made available to the general public for use, 
market research confirms that only Laurel Bridge (or its authorized resellers) can 
provide the annual maintenance requirements for the usage of the fielded Laurel 
Bridge products.  VA currently has government-owned copies of Laurel Bridge 
products, but these copies still rely on Laurel Bridge’s proprietary DCF SDK, which is 
embedded inside VistA Imaging. Even though the VA owns the deployed software 
version, the intellectual property inside it still belongs to Laurel Bridge.

IDIQ AE Multi-Discipline Architect & Engineering Services      N4008525R2591 
NAVFAC Mid-Atlantic Marine Corps AOR  Synopsis 
 
Page 1 of 13 
 
N40085-25-R-2591 INDEFINITE DELIVERY/INDEFINITE QUANTITY CONTRACT FOR MULTI-
DISCIPLINE ARCHITECT-ENGINEER (A-E) SERVICES IN SUPPORT OF PROJECTS 
PRIMARILY IN THE NAVFAC MID-ATLANTIC MARINE CORPS AREA OF RESPONSIBILITY 
(AOR) 
 
DESCRIPTION: ALL INFORMATION NEEDED FOR INTERESTED PARTIES TO SUBMIT A 
STANDARD FORM SF330, ARCHITECT ENGINEER QUALIFICATIONS IS CONTAINED 
HEREIN. THERE IS NO SEPARATE REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS (RFP) PACKAGE TO 
DOWNLOAD.  
 
This procurement will result in one Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity Architect-Engineer (A-E) 
Multi-Discipline Engineering Services contract as required for construction work.  Work under the 
contract is anticipated to occur primarily at NAVFAC Mid-Atlantic (MIDLANT), Marine Corps Area of 
Responsibility (AOR) including Marine Corps Air Station (MCAS) Cherry Point, Marine Corps Base 
(MCB) Camp Lejeune, Marine Corps Air Station (MCAS) Beaufort, Marine Recruit Depot (MCRD) 
Parris Island, and Marine Corps Air Station (MCAS) New River. However, work may be ordered 
throughout the NAVFAC MIDLANT AOR. These services will be procured in accordance with 40 
U.S.C. Chapter 11, Selection of Architects and Engineers, as implemented by FAR Subpart 36.6. The 
IDIQ contract will be for a five-year term. The total fee for the contract term shall not exceed 
$249,000,000. The guaranteed minimum for the contract term is $5,000. Firm-fixed price task orders 
will be negotiated for this contract. There will be no dollar limit per task order and no dollar limit per 
year. The estimated start date is September 2026. 
 
This proposed contract is being solicited on an UNRESTRICTED basis. The Small Business size 
standard classification is North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) Code 541330, 
Engineering Services, and the Small Business size standard is $25,500,000. The Government seeks the 
most highly qualified firm to perform the required services, based on the demonstrated competence and 
qualifications, in accordance with the selection criteria. 
 
The market research study N4008525R2591 conducted by NAVFAC MIDLANT included an 
assessment of relevant qualifications and capabilities of potentially qualified firms.  As a result of the 
market research analysis, a determination was made to solicit this procurement on an unrestricted basis 
inviting full and open competition. The NAVFAC MIDLANT small business office concurs with this 
decision.   
 
Typical task orders under this contract will be for military construction or major maintenance projects 
with construction costs ranging from $10M to $300M, however, some projects may be larger or smaller 
than this range. Facility types may include, but are not limited to, personnel housing facilities (Bachelor 
Enlisted Quarters (BEQ) and Bachelor Officers Quarters (BOQ)); office facilities; training facilities 
(operational, maintenance and classroom); and industrial maintenance facilities (Vehicle Maintenance 
Shops, Shore Intermediate Maintenance Activities, Aircraft Maintenance Hangars, Public Works Shops, 
Warehouses). Facility types may also include substantial work associated with ordnance 
production/storage facilities including electrical hazard classifications required to be designed to Naval 
Sea Systems Command Explosives Safety Management Policy (NAVSEA OP 5) requirements.  

IDIQ AE Multi-Discipline Architect & Engineering Services      N4008525R2591 
NAVFAC Mid-Atlantic Marine Corps AOR  Synopsis 
 
Page 2 of 13 
The general type of services expected include, but are not limited to, developing Design-Bid-Build 
packages, developing Design-Build Request for Proposal (RFP) packages, conducting Life Safety Code 
Studies, Interior space planning/design studies, Engineering site investigations and Preliminary 
Design. Facility Planning services include preparing Form DD1391 utilizing the Navy’s Programming 
Administration and Execution System (PAX) to develop requirements and project scope to include: 
Engineering evaluations; unit guidance costs or parametric cost estimating; development of alternatives 
and economic analysis; analysis of proposed project sites to address foundation, site utilities, issues 
related to site access constraints and project construction phasing and sequencing recommendations; 
identification of environmental, sustainable design and anti-terrorism/force protection issues; procedures 
for handling government collateral equipment lists; sustainable checklists, commissioning requirements, 
project preliminary hazard analysis; procedures for obtaining permits and regulatory approvals including 
work plan development; processes for review of contractor submittals, field consultations and 
inspections during construction; Title II Inspections, Electronic Operation and Maintenance Support 
Information (eOMSI), and Record document preparation. 
Comprehensive A-E services are required for planning, design, and construction services in support of 
new construction, renovations, repairs, replacements, demolition, alteration, and/or improvement of 
military and other governmental facilities to include base utility systems.  A-E services may include 
multiple design disciplines or single design disciplines, including but not limited to project management, 
architecture, landscape architecture, structural, mechanical, electrical, civil, geotechnical, fire protection, 
cost engineering, and interior designer.  Specialized services for telecommunications, physical security, 
audio-visual and collateral equipment may also be required.  
Specific types of A-E services that may be required under this contract include: 
 
1. Planning Services, including the development of project programming document (DD 1391), 
evaluations, site investigations, and cost estimates such as: 
 
a. Facility planning services, including: 
i. Project programming and requirements development  
ii. Conceptual pricing development 
iii. Development of Alternatives including Economic Analysis 
b. Interior Space Planning Design and Collateral Equipment Inventories 
c. Facility analysis, including: 
i. General condition assessment including code compliance 
ii. Energy utilization studies 
iii. Facility life safety code analysis 
iv. Exterior and interior hazardous material surveys and analysis 
d. Field investigation services, including: 
i. Geotechnical investigation in support of foundation design and site pavement 
recommendations  
ii. Utility location/identification  
iii. Site access studies including wayfinding and pedestrian corridors 
iv. Site topographic and property boundary studies, including flood zones and 
wetlands 
v. Environmental soil and ground water sampling and analysis 
vi. Fire Protection Investigations and Surveys  

IDIQ AE Multi-Discipline Architect & Engineering Services      N4008525R2591 
NAVFAC Mid-Atlantic Marine Corps AOR  Synopsis 
 
Page 3 of 13 
vii. Traffic analysis 
viii. Storm Drainage analysis/studies 
 
2. Design Services, including all supporting activities such as site/field investigation, surveys (to 
include hazardous material testing), design charrettes, cost estimates, etc.: 
 
a. Development of design-build RFP packages including schematic concept drawings and 
environmental studies 
b. Development of comprehensive design-bid-build packages that include full plans and 
specifications  
c. Construction Cost Estimates 
 
3. Construction Services such as the following services: 
a. Design Build design submittal reviews  
b. Contractor submittal reviews  
c. Field consultation and special inspections 
d. Electronic Operation and Maintenance Support Information (eOMSI)  
e. Obtaining environmental permits and regulatory approvals 
f. Commissioning Services 
g. As-built and Record Document preparation 
 
All engineering and design services shall comply with the most current edition of FC 1-300-09N Navy 
& Marine Corps Design Procedures, and other requirements as indicated on the Whole Building Design 
Guide Web Site (www.wbdg.org).  Selected A-E firm is required to have online access to web-based 
support programs and email via the internet for routine exchange of correspondence/information.  A-E 
firm is required to submit and maintain an A-E Accident Prevention Plan (APP) in accordance with 
USACE EM 385-1-1 for each project on this contract and Activity Hazard Analysis (AHA) for each in-
field action.  Key personnel, including sub-consultants, MUST be U.S. CITIZENS and able to obtain 
security clearances as required. 
 
A-E firms are required to prepare cost estimates utilizing the MCACES MII estimating system, 
specifications in the SPECSINTACT program, design-build RFPs utilizing NAVFAC Design-Build 
Masters, and drawings in AutoCAD DWG format (2020 or higher) or Revit (2021 or higher) utilizing 
the National CADD Standards format with NAVFAC specified modifications.  3D renderings and BIM 
modeling may also be required.  A-E firms or others under contract or providing services to NAVFAC 
may request software installation packages from NAVFAC Atlantic CI Cost.  The A-E is to send an 
email to NAVFAC-CI-Cost@navy.mil with the following in the Subject Section "MII License Request".   
Software is generally distributed to A-Es free of charge; however, accompanying database licenses must 
be purchased and licensed as appropriate by the user. 
 
Asbestos and or lead-based paint assessments may be required on this contract to determine the presence 
of hazardous material in existing facilities or at utility points of connections.  When asbestos or lead is 
found, comprehensive asbestos or lead surveys, to include sampling and testing, and the preparation of 
plans and specifications showing the location of asbestos and lead, and specifying the procedure to be 
followed during construction and/or demolition for removal or abatement, will be required.   
 

IDIQ AE Multi-Discipline Architect & Engineering Services      N4008525R2591 
NAVFAC Mid-Atlantic Marine Corps AOR  Synopsis 
 
Page 4 of 13 
Work in confined spaces may be required on this contract.  A-E firms must be able to accept work that 
involves asbestos, lead paint, PCBs, contaminated ground-water/soil and other hazardous materials, 
work on and under waterfront structures, on active airfields, and in confined spaces.   
 
Registered Communications Distribution Designer (RCDD) may be required for telecommunication 
systems.  Audio-visual systems may be required on this contract with services of Certified Technology 
Specialist-Designer (CTS-D).  CTS-D whose certification is ANSI accredited under the International 
Organization of Standardization (ISO) and the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) 
ISO/IEC 17024 certification of personnel.    
 
As defined by paragraph 1-5 of UFC 3-600-01, Fire Protection Engineering for Facilities, this contract 
will require the services of a licensed Fire Protection Engineer or sub-consultant. 
 
All contractors are advised that a Unique Entity Identifier is required prior to award. Contractors must 
complete the registration in System for Award Management (SAM) Database by selecting “Entity 
Information”. Failure to register in the SAM Database may render your firm ineligible for award. For 
more information, check the SAM Web site (https://www.sam.gov) Entity Information section. 
 
The awarded contract will be subject to specific provisions addressing the avoidance of organizational 
conflicts of interest, including NFAS 5252.209-9300, Organizational Conflicts of Interest. The prime 
firm for this contract will be required to perform throughout the contract term. A-E firms are advised 
that the selected firm, its subsidiaries or affiliates, and its subconsultants which design, prepare, or 
provide engineering services in support of construction contract documents cannot provide construction 
services for the same contract. This includes concept design, preparation of project programming 
documents (DD Form 1391), facility siting studies, environmental assessments, geotechnical services, 
engineering studies and services, design-build Requests for Proposals (RFPs), or other activities that 
result in identification of project scope and cost. The awarded contract will be subject to specific 
provisions addressing the avoidance of organizational conflicts of interest. The prime firm for this 
contract will be required to perform throughout the contract term. 
 
Interviews may be scheduled with firms slated as the most highly qualified. Firms slated for interviews 
may be asked to clarify information contained in the SF330 submittal. Elaborate presentations are not 
desired. 
 
SELECTION CRITERIA: 
 
Firms responding to this synopsis will be evaluated to determine the most highly qualified firms to 
perform the required services in accordance with the published selection criteria. Failure to comply with 
instructions or provide complete information may affect the firm’s evaluation or disqualify the firm from 
further consideration. The Selection of Architects and Engineers Statute and FAR Part 36.6 selection 
procedures apply. 
 
The A-E must demonstrate the team’s qualifications with respect to the published evaluation criteria. 
Failure to provide complete submission information defined in the evaluation criteria below may affect a 
firm’s qualification ratings. Evaluation Criteria (1) through (3) are considered most important and are 
equal among themselves; Criteria (4) through (6) are of slightly less importance and are equal among 

IDIQ AE Multi-Discipline Architect & Engineering Services      N4008525R2591 
NAVFAC Mid-Atlantic Marine Corps AOR  Synopsis 
 
Page 5 of 13 
themselves; Criterion (7) is of the least importance and will be used only as a tiebreaker among 
technically equal firms. Specific evaluation criteria include: 
 
1. Specialized Experience  
2. Professional Qualifications 
3. Past Performance  
4. Quality Control  
5. Program Management, Capacity, and Firm Location  
6. Commitment to Small Business 
7. Volume of Work 
 
Criterion 1 - Specialized Experience (SF330, Part I, Section F):  
 
Firms will be evaluated on specialized experience in performance of services similar to those anticipated

BACKGROUND

The purpose of this Performance Work Statement (PWS) is to define system functional support services for Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) Energy Business Process Support Directorate (BPSD), DLA Energy Procurement Process Support Directorate (PPSD), and DLA Finance Energy. As the Integrated Materiel Manager for petroleum products and services for the Department of Defense (DOD), DLA Energy is responsible for providing innovative logistical support in relation to Energy products to its customers. The focus of this PWS is to provide support for Energy related Supply Chain Management involving products and services to Global customers on 24-hour basis 365 days a year. DLA personnel interface with CONUS and OCONUS offices and personnel daily.

SCOPE

The DLA Energy Business Process Support Directorate (BPSD), Procurement Process Support Directorate (PPSD), and the DLA Finance Energy Process Lead have been established to provide process support to all aspects of the DLA Energy supply chain and enabling systems. This specifically supports the DLA Energy system architecture in a single environment with ancillary integrated system components (e.g. Fuels Manager Defense and Energy Procurement System Tools) known as “Digital Business Transformation”. This system architecture consists of the following:

Systems, Applications and Products (SAP) -S4 HANA (High Analytics Application)

Integrated Business Planning (IBP)

Supplier Relationship Management (SRM)

Industry Solution for Oil and Gas (IS-Oil)

Bulk Fuel Management (BFM)

Procurement for Public Sector (PPS) 

System knowledge beyond the scope of organic Business Process Analysts in these areas of the organization is required to execute aspects of this mission.

Ongoing analytics and troubleshooting services are required in all operational areas of mission, to include performance and impacts of Digital Business Transformation in use for DLA Energy.

Supplemental expertise to support development of new system-based processes is also required as part of this effort. Examples include ongoing definition and implementation of Audit Readiness protocols and data reconciliation strategy, or adaptation of existing system capability to support new commodities/business lines.

Provide technical insight, assistance, Course of Actions (COAs) to resolve issues, testing, research, and training to support the activities required for the integration and management of system functionality and business functions pre, during and post migration to the Enterprise Resource Planning Software package: SAP Business Suite 4 SAP HANA.

The Contractor will be provided access to Enterprise Business System (EBS), the system the contractor will be operating in.

Task Order and IDIQ Task:	There are three categories of EBS support required: Project Plan Development; Strategic Project Support and Subject Matter Expertise.

This Task Order falls under IDIQ RFP: SP4701-15-R-0030 Task Areas:

This task order is: unrestricted (i.e. open to other-than-small businesses, Group A contractors).

This task order is to be evaluated in accordance with Tradeoff source selection procedures. Award of this task order shall be made on a competitive best value basis, using “tradeoff” procedures between non-price and price. In evaluating task order proposals, the non-price factor is considered significantly more important than price. The Government may consider award to other than the lowest priced offeror or other than the highest technically rated offeror.

Current Incumbent Information: Energy Functional Support

ACCENTURE FEDERAL SERVICES LLC DBA ACCENTURE NATIONAL SECURITY 800 NORTH GLEBE RD #300

ARLINGTON VA 22203-1807 USA

Firm Fixed Price

TASK REQUIREMENTS

The vendor will be required to perform the following tasks:

TASK 1 - Project Plan Development (Reference IDIQ RFP SP4701-15-R-0030 Task Area 10)

The Contractor shall develop a project plan to accomplish the requirements of this PWS to include, but not limited to, the deployment phases: Initiation, Site Survey, Implementation, Post-Installation and Sustainment. Project plans will also be developed for specific tasks assigned by the Government within the scope of this PWS.

The contractor shall conduct In-Process Reviews (IPRs) as needed and provide information regarding task order status. IPRs shall provide for an interchange between the Government and contractor during the execution of the task order (e.g., review of the system design, reviewing the results of functional testing).

Sixty (60) calendar days prior to the end of this contract (base or option period), the Contractor shall deliver a written Transition Plan to the COR for the tasks to be performed.

Deliverable 1: Initial Overarching Project Plan and Schedule identifying initial scope of requirements identified in Tasks 2 through 3. Due within 4 weeks of task order award.

Deliverable 2: Updates to Overarching Project Plan identifying changes in timelines, expectations, or requirements. Due by 5th working day of each month.

Deliverable 3: IPR briefing and Review of Project Plan with DLA Energy Leadership. Due Monthly by 5th working day of each month.

Deliverable 4: Transition Plan- 60 calendar days prior to the end of this contract (base or option period). Plan shall include all aspects of transition cost analysis, propose schedules and document risks associated with such transition.

TASK 2 - Strategic Project Support (Reference IDIQ RFP SP4701-15-R-0030 Task Area 4) Strategic Project Support is required to achieve DLA Energy mission objectives. Each objective is concurrent with the Process Area’s operations. The contractor shall collaborate with the Process Area Leads to achieve objectives. A review of mission tasks will be conducted by the Process Area Leads, and reviewed with the contractor to establish project requirements, (i.e. outline of the issue, the value proposition, scope, approach, timeline, total cost and associated costs, mission impacts, potential shortfalls, actions for remedy, and results).

Work complexity will vary based on task, workload, and root cause analysis. The more complex an issue the longer the Government will allow for resolution. The Government Process Area Leads will manage the determination and application of complexity in concert with the contract resource assigned to each project. The Contractor will provide a recommended complexity level within one (1) business day of task identification. In the event the task is later determined to be more or less difficult, the Contractor will request in writing an authorization from the process area lead to modify the level of difficulty categorization. Task Delivery Timelines are identified in Table 3 at Section 2.5.

Provide technical expertise regarding the required and optimal use of SAP systems to meet DLA objectives, which includes the purchase, receipt, sales, storage, issue, transfer and transport of: bulk, packaged, containerized petroleum and other DLA products transportable by land, sea, air, pipeline, barrel, rail, or other as well as advising on emerging functionality available in EBS upgrades.

Provide Subject Matter Expertise (SME) and assist DLA in developing and supporting processes related to Audit Readiness, e.g., inventory reconciliation across system components within the Digital Business Transformation architecture.

Provide Subject Matter Expertise (SME) and assist DLA in identifying the value proposition of proposed projects during project planning or identification. This encompasses providing project and individual task planning to ensure the best value is delivered, communicated, and acknowledged to the customer base or services organization.

Provide recommendations and assist in the creation and execution of standard project lifecycle processes and templates across all projects. This process and template need to be identified and used for all projects in the planning phase of the project(s).

Provide current project status and subject matter expertise (SME) support during command level briefings for each project, to include, scope, and approach, timeline, results, and recommendations.

Project Documentation Minimum Requirements:

Executive Summary of the issue

Outline of the issue, value proposition, scope, approach, timeline, resolution, and results.

Project plan for the completion of the project

Deliverable 1: Weekly Executive Summary outlining all meetings attended during the previous week related to the project(s). Due 3 p.m. on the first working day of each week.

Deliverable 2: Monthly Executive Summary Status Report to review with Business Process Support Directorate (BPSD), Procurement Process Support Directorate (PPSD) and DLA Finance Energy Directorate Leadership. Due by the 5th working day of each month.

Deliverable 3: Task coordination, categorization, and documentation in accordance with table 3.

TASK 3 - Subject Matter Expertise (Reference IDIQ RFP SP4701-15-R-0030 Task Area 4)

Work complexity will vary based on project assignment, workload, and root cause analysis. The more complex an issue the longer the Government will allow for resolution. The Government Process Area Leads will manage the determination and application of complexity in concert with the contract resource assigned to the task. For each project the vendor will provide a recommended complexity level within one (1) business day of project identification. In the event the project is later determined to be more or less difficult, the vendor will request in writing an authorization from the process area lead to modify the level of difficulty categorization. Project Delivery Timelines are identified in table 3.

The vendor must have the capability to perform the same elements as Task 3 at other DLA Energy Regional Offices. In the event support is needed at another DLA Regional Office, the Contractor shall provide resources local to the applicable Regional Office Performance will be coordinated with the COR; contractor personnel shall interface with BPSD, PPSD, and DLA Finance Energy Process Leads in Ft. Belvoir and local leadership/personnel at the office assigned. A modification to the Task Order will be issued if resources are deemed necessary at other locations. Deliverables will be the same as Task 3.

The Contractor is required to provide Subject Matter Expertise (SME) to the Government, based on an comprehensive understanding of the SAP functionality as well as the functional and design specifications associated with the Reports, Interfaces, Conversions, Extensions, Forms and Workflows (RICE- FW) utilized within these EBS and other System modules:

Support reconciliation of inventory and other financial postings across multiple systems (EBS, Fuels Manager Defense (FMD), Fuels Depot System (FDS), Electronic Point of Sale (EPoS), Wide Area Work Flow (WAWF), Treasury Department’s G Invoicing, Salesforce) including accounting for variations and parity checks between external systems and EBS which is key to meeting Audit Readiness requirements and objectives. Additionally, this support will provide DLA Energy with the expertise and resources needed to quickly identify and address audit inquiries and concerns in a timely manner. Supplemental expertise to support development of new system-based processes is also part of this effort. Examples include EBS modifications in support of the implementation of the Treasury Department’s G-Invoicing system and DLA’s business management to Salesforce, ongoing definition and implementation of Audit Readiness protocols and data reconciliation strategy, or adaptation of existing system capability to support new commodities/business lines.

SAP Industry Solution for Oil and Gas (IS-Oil) and Public Sector

Supplier Relationship Management (SRM)

SAP Ariba Procurement for Public Sector (PPS)

Integrated Business Planning (IBP)

DLA Internet Bid Board System (DIBBS)

Electronic Document Access (EDA)

Fuel Manager Defense (FMD)

Fuels Depot Systems (FDS)

FDS - Asset Visibility (AV)

FDS - Inventory Management (IM)

Electronic Point of Sale (EPOS)

Federal Procurement Data System (FPDS)

Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) / Wide Area Workflow (WAWF).

External Interfaces with Vendor Systems (FLEET, AIRCARD, and SEA Card Vendors)

Enterprise Data Warehouse (EDW)

Customer Relationship Module (CRM)

Real Property (RP)

Additional Systems Integrated or Interfaced with SAP to support DLA activities

SAP High Performance Analytic Appliance

Business Objects

SAP Business Warehouse

Business Intelligence

Microsoft SQL Data Warehouse

Microsoft SQL Analysis Services

Microsoft SQL Reporting Services

QLIK Application

Treasury Department G-Invoicing System

Salesforce

ADVANA (Data Analytics)

SAP Business Suite (s) SAP HANA

Power BI

Bulk Fuel Management (BFM)

This Day-to-Day operational support includes the following:

Generalized Support for all process areas

Issue research and resolution identification.

Recommendations for optimizing processes and system utilization to support Audit Readiness or operational objectives, including utilization of Digital Business Transformation architecture components.

Creation of operational reports/metrics as they pertain directly to Digital Business Transformation, and as identified by BPSD, PPSD, or the DLA Finance Energy Directorates.

Assist in tracking projected savings and performance metrics against actual outcomes over the duration of a project. This does not involve oversight of other contractors.

Gather, review and submit changes to the Workbench documentation to support DLA Energy’s efforts.

Provide analysis of SAP solutions, data, and interfacing tools.

Provide analysis of interfaces between supported systems.

Providing detailed explanations of system functionality for Business Process Analyst in the assigned process area.

Draft and assist in implementation strategy development for system modifications.

Answering approximately 2 or 3 questions per week from each of the 90+ Business Process Analysts pertaining to EBS functionality and design.

Assist Government in identifying the functionality and implementation strategy to fully leverage existing EBS capabilities for Aerospace commodity support by learning Aerospace current business model and advising proper EBS tenets for maximum efficiency.

Assist in collecting data by providing explanations when there are data variances from what is expected in support of Audit Requests submitted by Financial Auditors and Independent Public Accountants.

Ongoing audit reconciliation, audit readiness, and general audit support.

Provide technical expertise, support, and analysis for ERP Transformation – Procurement for Public Sector and Bulk Fuels Management deployment. Provide support for Business Process Reengineering taskings.

Perform complex queries.

Provide DLA SAP solution implementation expertise.

Proved EBS product

SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE 

622673622


The Defense Information Systems Agency (DISA) is seeking sources for Defense Enterprise Office Solution (DEOS) Department of Defense (DoD) Office 365 Operations and Maintenance. This requirement will support DISA Portfolio Acquisition Executive Services (PAE Services) (SD), Enterprise Collaboration Services Division (SD3). 

CONTRACTING OFFICE ADDRESS:  

DISA/DITCO-NCR 

6910 COOPER AVE, 

FT. MEADE, MD 20755

INTRODUCTION:

This is a SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE to determine the availability and technical capability of large and small businesses (including the following subsets: Small Disadvantaged Businesses, Certified 8(a), Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses, HUBZone Small Businesses and Woman-Owned Small Businesses) to provide the required products and/or services. 

DISA SD / SD3 is seeking information from potential sources for: providing engineering, operations and cybersecurity support for the sustainment of and engineering of the DEOS DoD Office 365 Non-classified Internet Protocol Router Network (NIPRNet) and Secret Internet Protocol Router Network (SIPRNet) Tenants and potentially a Top-Secret Office-365 Tenant. 

DoD selected Microsoft Office 365 (M365) as the solution to provide common communication, collaboration, and productivity capabilities that are mission-effective, efficient, widely accessible, and facilitate DoD operations worldwide. DISA, in support of the Deputy Secretary of Defense’s direction to accelerate DoD’s adoption of cloud computing technology, plans to continue to build on its seamlessly integrated enterprise M365 as a replacement for disparate DoD legacy enterprise information technology services, such as individual voice, video, collaboration, email, content management, information management, and productivity suites. 

DEOS PMO operates the DoD365-Joint tenant (IL5) with approximately 137k users across Defense Agencies and Field Activities (DAFA) and Combatant Commands (CCMD) organizations; and the DoD365-Sec tenant (IL6) with approximately 350k users across the Department’s DAFAs, CCMDs, and MILDEPs. Additionally, at IL6, DEOS PMO operates two Five Eyes (FVEY) tenants for United Kingdom and Australia with the potential to add additional FVEY partner nations. Planning estimates for an IL7 environment are at approximately 150k users across DoD. DEOS PMO continuously evolves DoD365 capabilities as Microsoft 365 service offerings are enhanced and mission requirements emerge.  

The anticipated period of performance is a one-year base period and four one-year optional periods.

The anticipated period of performance is:

Base Year		April 3, 2027 – April 2, 2028 

Option Year 1		April 3, 2028 – April 2, 2029 

Option Year 2		April 3, 2029 – April 2, 2030 

Option Year 3		April 3, 2030 – April 2, 2031 

Option Year 4		April 3, 2031 – April 2, 2032

The anticipated place of performance is at DISA Headquarters (6910 Cooper Ave, Fort Meade, MD, 20755), DISA Columbus, Ohio (3990 E. Broad St., Bldg. 23 Columbus, OH 43218-1152), and any DISA-approved contractor Secure Facility at the convenience of the contractor.

DISCLAIMER: 

THIS SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS NOTICE. NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS NOTICE. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY.

CONTRACT/PROGRAM BACKGROUND: 

The DEOS DoD365 Operations and Maintenance requirement is a recurring requirement currently being executed under the following contract:

Contract Number: 47QTCA21A0001 / 47QFSA21F0023

Contract Vehicle: General Services Administration (GSA) Single-Award Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA)

Incumbent: General Dynamics Information Technology, Large Business

Method of previous acquisition: Task Order under Single Award Blanket Purchase Agreement 

Period of performance: 05 Mar 2021 - 4 May 2026 

The DISA DEOS also requires optional tasks to be incorporated into the follow-on contract for an IL7 (Top-Secret) solution. Therefore, in addition to the recurring requirements being performed in the existing Task Order above, the IL7 optional task requirements will also be included.

Additionally, the DISA anticipates awarding an additional one-year task order under the above single-award BPA, Contract Number 47QTCA21A0001, for a period of performance of 05 May 2026 - 04 May 2027.

REQUIRED CAPABILITIES: 

The DISA DEOS DoD 365 team requires a contractor to sustain, operate, engineer, and provide common communication, collaboration, and productivity capabilities to facilitate DoD operations worldwide. The Government is seeking contractors capable of providing subject matter expertise in support of this effort. 

Microsoft 365 (M365) Engineering and Operational Expertise (IL5, IL6, & IL7): Responses shall demonstrate experience and technical expertise in providing engineering, operations, and cybersecurity support for M365 environments at Impact Level 5 (IL5 – NIPRNet), Impact Level 6 (IL6 - SIPRNet), and Impact Level 7 (IL7 – Top-Secret) including integrated third-party products.  Describe and provide an example of your company’s experience, successful M365 deployments, troubleshooting complex issues, and optimizing configurations for large-scale DoD environments. Specific experience with Azure Government Unclass (IL5) and Secret (IL6) infrastructure is highly desirable. 


Cybersecurity and Risk Management: Responses shall demonstrate experience providing comprehensive cybersecurity services within DoD cloud environments (Azure preferred), including experience with Risk Management Framework (RMF) implementation, security control assessments, incident response, cyber threat hunting, and compliance with DISA Security Technical Implementation Guides, Information Assurance Vulnerability Management, and other DoD security policies and procedures. The ability to contribute to and maintain an Authority to Operate is critical. Describe and provide an example of your company’s experience providing comprehensive Cybersecurity and RMF Compliance in Cloud Environments (specifically M365, IL5 at a minimum) and DoD cloud environments.  


Knowledge Management and Training Capabilities: Given the need to create and maintain knowledge repositories and potentially develop training materials, responses shall demonstrate capabilities in knowledge management best practices, content creation, and online and virtual instructor-led training development. Describe and provide an example of improving user adoption and satisfaction through effective knowledge sharing and user engagement.

Staffing and Transition Management: Requires a smooth transition-in demanding rapid staffing. Responses shall showcase the ability to rapidly mobilize qualified personnel, manage staffing plans effectively, and execute seamless transitions. Describe and provide an example of your company’s experience managing staffing and transition for large-scale efforts (75-100 people) within 15-30 days of period of performance start date.

SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS: 

Facility Clearance Level. The work to be performed under this contract is up to the Top-Secret level. Therefore, responses shall demonstrate an interim or final Top Secret Facility Clearance from the Defense Security Service Facility Clearance Branch, which will be required at time of proposal submission.  Please include your company’s current facility clearance level in your reply to this notice.

Personnel Security. The work to be performed under this contract is up to the Top-Secret level.  All contractor staff are required to have a minimum of a Secret clearance and a Top Secret clearance will be required as needed to support specific DEOS projects. Describe and provide an example of your company’s experience managing security clearance requirements.    

Key contractor personnel shall be Microsoft 365 Administrator Expert Certified and the vendor shall be authorized to provide Enterprise Cloud Service Offering certified staff support.

Capability Maturity Model Integration (CMMI) Certification: Because of the complexity of the integration and operational management of the DEOS effort and ongoing requirements to develop and integrate new collaboration capabilities, prime contractors shall be at least CMMI Services V3.0 Maturity Level 5 for all contract work and supporting subcontractors shall be at least CMMI Services V3.0 Maturity Level 3 for the life of the contract. Please include your company’s current CMMI level in your reply to this notice and demonstrate the ability to have this certification at time of proposal submission.  

SOURCES SOUGHT:  

The North American Industry Classification System Code (NAICS) for this requirement is 541511 (https://www.census.gov/naics/), with the corresponding size standard of $34 million. In order to make a determination for a small business set-aside, two or more qualified and capable small businesses shall submit responses that demonstrate their qualifications. Responses shall demonstrate the company’s ability to perform in accordance with FAR clause 52.219-14, Limitations on Subcontracting.

To assist DISA in determining the level of participation by small business in any subsequent procurement that may result from this Sources Sought Notice, provide information regarding any plans to use joint ventures (JV) or partnering. Please outline the company's areas of expertise and those of any proposed JV/partner who combined can meet the specific requirements contained in this notice.

SUBMISSION DETAILS:

Responses should include:

Responses to the Required Capabilities and Special Requirements above;

Business name and address; 

Name of company representative and their business title; 

Small Business Socio-economic status (if small); 

Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) Code;

Prime contract vehicles; to include ENCORE III, SETI, NIH CIO-SP4, NASA SEWP V, GSA: OASIS, ALLIANT II, VETS II, STARS III, MAS (including applicable SIN(s), groups or pools), or any other Government Agency contract vehicle that allows for decentralized ordering. (This information is for market research only and businesses with a valid CAGE code that lack prime contract vehicles are still encouraged to respond to this notice.) 

Businesses who wish to respond shall send a response via email no later than 4:00 PM Eastern Standard Time on  to elizabeth.a.bono.civ@mail.mil and michelle.l.rand.civ@mail.mil . Interested businesses should submit a brief capabilities statement package addressing the specific questions above (no more than seven pages), demonstrating the ability to perform the services listed under Required Capabilities.

Proprietary information and trade secrets, if any, shall be clearly marked on all materials. All information received that is marked Proprietary will be handled accordingly. All submissions become Government property and will not be returned. All Government and contractor personnel reviewing submitted responses will have signed non-disclosure agreements and understand their responsibility for proper use and protection from unauthorized disclosure of proprietary information as pursuant to 41 USC 423. The Government shall not be held liable for any damages incurred if proprietary information is not properly identified.

For information on DISA’s requirements, you can find current information on our home page: www.disa.mil – that includes current forecast and the current acquisition strategies. If there is no information regarding the requirement you may be inquiring about, then there is no additional publicly available information. Please continue to review www.disa.mil.
