PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT (PWS) 
 
ARMY COMMUNITY SERVICES (ACS) Consolidated Services  
 
 
Part 1 
 
General Information 
 
1.  General: This is a non-personal service(s) contract under which the personnel rendering 
the service(s) are not subject, either by the contract’s terms or by the manner of its 
administration, to the supervision and control usually prevailing in relationships between the 
Government and its employees. 
 
1.1  Description of Services/Introduction: This is a non-personal service(s) contract to 
provide support to the USAG Italy Army Community Services which include, but are not limited 
to:  
 
1) ACS Lending closet:  
2) Front Desk:  
3) Bilingual Support services:  
4) Orientation Tour Operator:  
5) Italian Language Instructor:  
6) English as a second language instruction 
 
1.2  Background: This is to procure support services for the U.S. Army Garrison (USAG) Italy 
military community and Army Community Service (ACS) throughout the year. The purpose of 
this requirement is to facilitate ACS ability to provide comprehensive, coordinated, and 
responsive services that enhance mission readiness, improve quality of life, and support 
Soldiers, Department of the Army (DA) Civilians, and Families—particularly during transitions 
such as Permanent Change of Station (PCS) moves. These services include the ACS Lending 
Closet, which provides essential household items for temporary use; front desk support to 
assist with general inquiries and administrative coordination; bilingual assistance to bridge 
language gaps within the community; orientation tour operations that promote understanding of 
Italian history, customs, and culture; Italian language instruction to foster integration into the 
host nation environment; and English as a Second Language instruction to support non-native 
speakers. By consolidating these functions into a single contract, the government aims to 
maximize efficiency, eliminate duplication of services, and improve effectiveness through 
standardized service delivery in alignment with ACS and garrison goals. 
 
1.3  Scope: The Contractor shall provide   non-personal service(s) in support of ACS. The 
contractor services shall be made available in support of those who fall under the Status of 
Forces Agreement (SOFA) (Contractors that fall under SOFA, on a space-available basis). The 
Contractor shall perform to the standards and acceptable quality levels identified in this PWS 
and associated contract documents. 
 

   
 
Version – September 2024 Page 2 of 41 
1.4  Objectives:  
Orientation Tour Operator Services - objective is to reduce stress of relocated individuals to 
support integration and to familiarize Vicenza military community (VMC) members with the 
Italian culture, history and language. In order to facilitate the commander’s ability to provide 
comprehensive, standardized, coordinated, and responsive services that support Soldiers, 
Department of Defense (DoD) civilians, and Families regardless of geographical location to 
maximize both technology and resources, eliminate duplication in service delivery, and 
measure service effectiveness.  
 
Front Desk Services – Deliver high-quality customer service by assisting walk-in and 
telephonic inquiries, maintaining administrative records, and managing facility scheduling.  
 
Relocation/Lending Closet Administrative Services – Support military families by managing 
relocation resources, maintaining household lending inventory, and coordinating integration 
programs.  
 
Bilingual Support Assistant Services – Offer linguistic and administrative assistance in English 
and Italian to ease transitions into the local environment and provide necessary translations for 
daily life.  
 
Italian Language Instruction Services – Conduct structured language courses and cultural 
immersion activities to facilitate the acquisition of Italian language skills for spouses, service 
members, and civilian personnel.  
 
English as a Second Language Instruction - Provide English as a Second Language instruction 
to active duty, retired military, DoD civilians, and their family members, and Local National (LN) 
civilians. 
 
1.5  General Information: 
 
1.5.1  Quality Control Plan (QCP): The Contractor shall develop and maintain a QCP to 
ensure services are performed in accordance with (IAW) this PWS. The Contractor shall 
develop and implement procedures to identify, prevent, and ensure non-recurrence of 
defective services. The Contractor's QCP is the means by which it assures that the work 
provided complies with the requirements of the contract. 
 
The Contractor’s Proposed QCP shall be submitted to the Contracting Officer (KO) through the 
Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR) for review within ten (10) days after date of 
contract award  
 
The Government (KO, COR, and Quality Assurance Specialist) has three (3) days to review 
the Contractors submitted QCP. The Contractor will either receive an acceptance notice from 
the KO or the QCP with comments. The Contractor has an additional five (5) days to provide 
an updated copy of the QCP.  After acceptance of the QCP, the Contractor shall receive the 
Contracting Officer’s acceptance in writing.  Any proposed changes to the accepted QCP are 
required to be resubmitted for acceptance by the KO (through the COR) no later than thirty 

   
 
Version – September 2024 Page 3 of 41 
(30) days before implementation. At a minimum, the QCP shall include and answer the 
following to be acceptable:  
 
   a. How the Contractor will monitor work to ensure that performance complies with all 
deliverables (etc. timelines, deadlines, and goals). 
   b. How the Contractor will monitor work to ensure that performance complies with all 
specifications and requirements of the contract, including clauses. 
   c. How the Contractor will identify, investigate, and correct any non-conforming performance 
and prevent similar deficiencies in the future. 
   d. How the Contractor will file and save all Quality Control related documents for the life of 
the contract plus 5 years. 
 
1.5.1.1  Optional addendum to the QCP: RESERVED 
 
1.5.1.2  Quality Issues: The Contractor shall inform the COR of issues or potential issues that 
might affect the performance within 24 hours of identifying those issues. 
 
1.5.1.3  Quality Assurance: The Government will evaluate the Contractor’s performance 
under this contract in accordance with the Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan (QASP). This 
plan is primarily focused on what the Government must do to ensure that the Contractor has 
performed in accordance with the performance standards. It defines how the performance 
standards will be applied, the frequency of surveillance, and the acceptable quality levels 
(performance thresholds).

purpose of the PWS. If submittal of any documentation (e.g. deliverables, submittals, etc.)

Contractor support hour requirements often coincide, however, they may differ. Please refer to 
the following. 
 
1.7.1  Government Facility Office Hours: The Government facility office hours are 0800 to 
1700, Monday through Wednesday and Friday and 1300 to 1700 Thursday except U.S. 
holidays identified in paragraph 1.6.1 above or when the Government facility is closed due to 
local or national emergencies, administrative closings, or similar Government directed facility 
closings. 
 
1.7.2  Government Facility Operating Hours: The Government facility operating hours occur 
between the hours of 0800 to 1700, Monday through Wednesday and Friday and 1300 to 1700 
Thursday The Government facility is open for operations during the recognized U.S. Holidays 
identified in paragraph 1.5.3.1 above.  The Government facility may close due to local or 
national emergencies, administrative closings, or similar Government directed facility closings 
and will be communicated by the Contracting Officer to the Contractor. 
 
1.7.3  Contractor Support Hours: The Contractor shall provide in-person support during 
designated operating hours for each of the six functional areas: Orientation Tour Operations, 
Front Desk Services, Relocation and Lending Closet Administrative Services, Bilingual Support 
Assistance, Italian Language Instruction, and English as a Second Language Instruction. 
These positions are not authorized for overtime; all duties shall be performed within regular 
duty hours. Furthermore, Contractor Support Hours: As operational needs evolve, ACS 
reserves the right to adjust service schedules, including workdays and times).  The Contractor 
will receive a written notice from the KO through the COR with a minimum of two weeks' notice 
prior to any schedule changes.   The   Contractor shall at all times maintain an adequate 
workforce for the uninterrupted performance of all tasks defined within this PWS when the 
Government facility is not closed for the above reasons. When hiring personnel, the Contractor 
shall keep in mind that the stability and continuity of the workforce are essential. 
 
1) ACS Lending closet:  
 
Normal office hours at ACS are 0800 - 1700, Monday through Friday, with the exception of 
Thursday when ACS opens at 1300; the contractor shall provide coverage 20-25 hours per 
week. This coverage excludes the U.S. Federal holidays and installation closure days listed in 
PWS Paragraphs 1.6.1 and 1.6.2, respectively. 
 
2) Front Desk:

Normal office hours at ACS are 0800 – 1700, Monday through Friday, excluding U.S. Federal 
Holidays.  The workload is 35 hours per week. This coverage excludes the U.S. Federal 
holidays and installation closure days listed in PWS Paragraphs 1.6.1 and 1.6.2, respectively. 
 
3) Bilingual Support services:  
 
Normal office hours at ACS are 0800 - 1700, Monday through Friday, The contractor shall 
work no more than 30 hours per week. This coverage excludes the U.S. Federal holidays and 
installation closure days listed in PWS Paragraphs 1.6.1 and 1.6.2, respectively. 
 
 
4) Orientation Tour Operator:  
 
Between the hours of 0830-1530, Monday through Friday This coverage excludes the U.S. 
Federal holidays and installation closure days listed in PWS Paragraphs 1.6.1 and 1.6.2, 
respectively. Specifically for the tour operator function, duty will take place on every Tuesday

periods (July and August), double tours shall be conducted during the 1st and 3rd weeks of 
these months, if necessary, this is to accommodate the volume of personnel turnover in the 
region. This approach to scheduling ensures that we effectively manage the influx of personnel 
and maintain operational readiness during peak periods. 
 
5) Italian Language Instructor:  
 
The Contractor shall provide support between the hours of 0830-1700, Monday through Friday. 
This coverage excludes the U.S. Federal holidays and installation closure days listed in PWS 
Paragraphs 1.6.1 and 1.6.2, respectively. 
 
6) English as a second language instruction 
 
The Contractor shall provide instructional support between the hours of 1330-1530 on 
Tuesdays and 0900-1200 on Fridays. The contractor will have one hour per week for additional 
services which may include annual trainings, course preparation, and scoring exams. In the 
event the contractor is unable to fulfill their obligation, they shall provide an alternate within 48 
hours and shall inform the COR of the changes in writing. The number of students varies but 
will not exceed 20 people. 
 
1.8  Contractor Work Plan:  
 
For each of the following sections - ACS Lending closet, Front Desk, Bilingual Services, 
Orientation Tour Operator, Italian Language Instructor, ESL Instructor :  
 
The Contractor shall develop and maintain a comprehensive Work Plan, which must, at a 
minimum, outline regularly scheduled tasks, including location, scope of work, and timeline. 
The initial Work Plan shall be submitted to the Contracting Officer via the COR for review 
within seven (7) calendar days following the contract award. Upon submission, the

the Work Plan. Any proposed modifications to the approved Final Work Plan must be 
resubmitted via the COR for Government review and approval no later than thirty (30) days 
prior to implementation. The same review and approval timeline applies to all proposed

1.9  Military Work Schedule: The military work schedule may affect access to military 
operated facilities. If scheduled work or access to facilities is required, coordination with 
occupants (through the COR) will be necessary or the work in affected facilities shall be

1.10  Place of Performance: The work to be performed under this contract shall occur 
throughout the United States Army Garrison (USAG) Vicenza installations and including but 
not limited to the cities of Vicenza, as well as other surrounding municipalities and locations in 
the region as determined by mission requirements.

DEPARTMENT OF VETERANS AFFAIRS 
 
Justification and Approval (J&A) 
For 
Other Than Full and Open Competition 
 
Acquisition Plan Action ID: 36C241-26-AP-2692 
 
1. Contracting Activity: Department of Veterans Affairs, VISN 01, Jamaica Plain VA 
Medical Center, 150 S Huntington Ave, Boston, MA 02130 
 
2. Nature and/or Description of the Action Being Approved: This justification supports 
awarding a sole-source contract from one responsible source, WBRC, Inc. for a logical 
follow-on continuation of the previously completed feasibility study and will advance the 
project at Jamaica Plain VA Medical Center from concept-level validation into full a 
construction-ready design for the Neuroscience Research Renovation requirement. WBRC is 
the most qualified and the most knowledgeable firm for this requirement as they have already 
been on site and have provided the VA with a detailed analysis. 
 
3. Description of Supplies/Services Required to Meet the Agency’s Needs: The architectural 
and engineering A(/E) shall prepare design, construction documents, and provide 
construction period services to install a new freezer farm on the second floor of Building 10 
at the Jamaica Plain VA Medical Center and incorporate the basis of designs and findings of 
the VA JP Neuroscience Freezer Farm Feasibility Study Concept Design prepared by WBRC 
on 02-27-2026. This project will install a minimum of thirty 80-degree freezers, a small 
office and a laboratory space in approximately 3,855 square feet on the second floor of 
Building 10. The VA has selected to move forward with Concept Plan displaying a layout of 
60 to 65 freezers in the space.  
 
In addition to designing the space for the proposed freezers, the A/E will be responsible for 
reviewing all existing applicable codes and guidelines necessary to design a complete system 
with all operational functionality and required equipment, such as temperature recorders, 
remote alarms, storage baskets, auxiliary water cooling, etc. The A/E is responsible for all 
elements of design and engineering. This includes, but not limited to, physical security, 
resiliency, civil, structural, architectural, plumbing, electrical, mechanical, communication 
systems, and fire suppression/protection. 
 
4. Statutory Authority Permitting Other than Full and Open Competition: This acquisition 
is conducted under the authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), 41 U.S.C. 3304(a)(1), and FAR 
6.103-1, Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy 
Agency Requirements. 
 
5. Demonstration that the Contractor’s Unique Qualifications or Nature of the 
Acquisition Requires the Use of the Authority Cited Above (applicability of authority): 
WBRC is uniquely qualified, having already completed a thorough feasibility study under 
contract 36C24126P0160. Their work included infrastructure capacity evaluation, 

 
   Page 2 of 4 
 
development of concept-level architectural layouts, and preparation of multidisciplinary 
feasibility narratives confirming the viability of the proposed freezer farm installation. 
WBRC’s on-site assessments and direct coordination with VA end users have provided them 
with a detailed understanding of the project’s complexities, existing site conditions, and 
stakeholder-approved layout direction—elements critical to the engineering design effort. 
 
Key tasks performed by WBRC under the previous contract include: 
 Documentation of existing conditions 
 Site verification 
 Development of conceptual layout alternatives 
 Coordination with VA stakeholders 
 Production of accepted concept-level architectural layouts 
 Creation of a multidisciplinary feasibility narrative 
 
As the originator of the technical basis-of-design, WBRC possesses unique insight into space 
constraints, infrastructure assumptions, utility limitations, and feasibility-phase decisions 
validated in collaboration with VA end users. Awarding this contract to another firm would 
necessitate repeating feasibility-level evaluations and redeveloping concept documentation, 
resulting in substantial additional costs and unacceptable delays to implementing the freezer 
storage infrastructure that supports neuroscience research operations. 
 
Adherence to the Brooks Act is a foundational element of this justification. The Brooks Act 
mandates qualifications-based selection for all A/E services contracts, requiring agencies to 
select the most qualified firm rather than make a selection based solely on cost. Throughout 
its prior engagements, WBRC has been selected because of demonstrated competence, 
technical expertise, and consistent delivery of high-quality results at VA Medical Centers, 
including Boston. This qualifications-based procurement process ensures compliance with 
federal procurement standards and reinforces the VA’s commitment to securing the best 
possible expertise and continuity for complex A/E requirements such as these. Selection of 
WBRC through a sole-source contract not only upholds the Brooks Act, but also preserves 
the integrity and efficiency of the project, ensuring optimal outcomes for the Government. 
 
Awarding a Firm Fixed Price contract to WBRC will retain essential project knowledge, 
prevent unnecessary duplication of effort, and deliver cost savings, ultimately serving the 
best interest of the Government and aligning with statutory requirements for architectural and 
engineering services acquisition. 
 
6. Description of Efforts Made to ensure that offers are solicited from as many 
potential sources as possible (including whether a notice was or will be publicized as 
required by RFO Part 5 and, if not, which exception under RFO Part 5 applies): 
Market Research was performed to assess the availability of SDVOSB/VOSB A/E Firms 
and determined that, while other qualified firms exist, none possess the project-specific 
knowledge and experience of the existing conditions needed to perform without 
significant learning curve costs and delays. Competing this requirement at this stage 
would result in substantial duplication of effort and is not in the Government’s best 
interest. 

 
   Page 3 of 4 
 
 
In addition, a Notice of Intent to Sole Source will be posted to Contract Opportunities on 
SAM.gov to satisfy FAR 5 posting requirements. 
 
7. Determination by the CO that the Anticipated Cost to the Government will be Fair and 
Reasonable: The Contracting Officer will evaluate WBRC’s proposal to ensure pricing is 
fair and reasonable based on an independent government estimate (IGE), comparison to 
historical pricing under previously awarded contracts of similar scope as well as previously 
awarded contracts with WBRC. 
 
8. Description of the Market Research Conducted and the Results, or a Statement of the 
Reasons Market Research Was Not Conducted: Comprehensive market research was 
conducted; however, this requirement is uniquely tied to an assessment previously performed 
by WBRC. The specialized knowledge, experience, and familiarity that WBRC possesses 
regarding the project’s existing conditions cannot be easily replicated or transferred to 
another A/E firm without incurring a significant learning curve. Retaining WBRC ensures 
continuity of expertise across all phases of the project, which directly benefits the 
Government by minimizing the risk of future delays, errors, or omissions. WBRC’s retained 
historical project information and familiarity with site-specific conditions are critical to the 
successful completion of the required Engineering Services. Accordingly, it is in the 
Government’s best interest to engage the same A/E firm that performed the initial 
assessment, thereby avoiding unnecessary additional costs and inefficiencies.  
 
9. Any Other Facts Supporting the Use of Other than Full and Open Competition: Failure 
to maintain continuity of this follow-on requirement directly jeopardizes the timely 
completion of the Neuroscience Research Renovation project and could impact delivery of 
care to Veterans. Sole sourcing this requirement ensures seamless support to the logical 
follow-on requirement and avoids substantial additional expenditures. 
 
10. A Statement of the Actions, if any, the Agency May Take to Remove or Overcome any 
Barriers to Competition before Making subsequent acquisitions for the supplies or 
services required: Future A/E requirements for upcoming projects will be competed to the 
maximum extent practicable. This sole-source action is a logical follow on specific to the 
unique circumstances of the Neuroscience Research Renovation project and the prior 
involvement of WBRC.

I. 	INTRODUCTION:

The U.S. Army Combat Capabilities Development Command Chemical Biological Center (DEVCOM CBC) mission is to provide innovative chemical, biological, radiological, nuclear and explosive (CBRNE) defense capabilities to enable the Joint Warfighters’ dominance on the battlefield and interagency defense of the homeland. Mission areas and technical points of contact for within DEVCOM CBC are shown in Section VII of this Broad Agency Announcement (BAA). Proposals are sought from all eligible sources as specified herein, including educational institutions, nonprofit organizations, and private industry. This BAA provides general information, proposal preparation instructions, evaluation and selection criteria, and award administration.

	This BAA is intended to solicit preproposals for DEVCOM CBC for:

		A.  Procurement Contracts: Awarded Procurement Contracts shall apply to those parts of development not related to the development of a specific system or hardware procurement based on the Technical Readiness Level limitations described herein (see also “Technology Readiness Levels in the Department of Defense” at Section IX of this document). As to any resultant procurement contracts, this BAA is issued under the provisions of the Competition in Contracting Act of 1984 (Public Law 98-369), as implemented in the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 6.102 (d)(2) and in accordance with FAR 35.016. The purpose of procurement contracts placed under this BAA is to identify the best available science, and as such, there are no set-asides associated with any awards resulting from this BAA. In accordance with FAR 35.003, Contracts shall be used only when the principal purpose is the acquisition of supplies or services for the direct benefit or use of the Federal Government. Grants or cooperative agreements should be used when the principal purpose of the transaction is to stimulate or support research and development for another public purpose. Cooperative Agreements are discussed below at C.

	B.  Other Transaction Authority, the Prototype OT (pOTA): Following 10 U.S.C. §4022, Prototype OT projects must include a prototype per the statute and the transaction will “carry out prototype projects that are directly relevant to enhancing the mission effectiveness of personnel of the Department of Defense or improving platforms, systems, components, or materials proposed to be acquired or developed by the Department of Defense, or to improvement of platforms, systems, components, or materials in use by the armed forces.” Participation in Prototype OTs is directed toward non-traditional defense contractors (NDCs) and Small Businesses. Businesses that are neither NDCs nor Small Businesses may still be awarded a Prototype OT, but a third of the award costs in such cases must come from non-Government sources. The pOTA is unlike other Government Contracts such as Procurement Contracts (referenced above) in that Prototype OTs are not subject to the Competition in Contracting Act (CICA), FAR Part 6 or any other FAR based regulation. However, by statute, Prototype OTs require, to the maximum extent practicable, competitive procedures. Consequently, the mechanics of the competitive BAA process detailed in this BAA otherwise not applicable to OTs are, as supplemented herein, adopted as the competitive procedure for entering into OTs.

		1.  Section VII contains areas of interest to be competed hereunder for Prototype OT awards. Section VIII contains instructions specific to the development of, and evaluation of proposals, for prototypes. 

		2.  In general, OT Offerors may submit a preproposal (1) qualifying under Section VII.A of this BAA for one or more of the Mission Areas or (2) for prototype requirements identified in Section VIII or in a separate Request for Project Proposals (RPP) issued under this BAA. If two or more Prototype OT Offerors submit for the same requirement, the field of competition will be narrowed by the evaluations called for under this BAA for preproposals used to conduct phased evaluations using one or more of the evaluation factors.

		3.  If warranted, a Research OT under 10 U.S.C. §4021 may be the most appropriate agreement mechanism. Generally, Research OTs under §4021 differ from pOTA under §4022 in that Research OTs are used for basic, applied, and advanced research projects that are focused on validating research results and advancements, rather than for the delivery or acquisition of the resultant technologies. Delivery or acquisition of resultant technologies is the focus of the Prototype OT and the Production OTs that stem from the Prototype OT. Consequently, this BAA serves the additional purpose of solicitation for efforts that may result in a Research OT under 10 U.S.C. §4021.

		C.  Cooperative Agreements:  Under authority of 41 U.S.C. §6305, a legal instrument used to enter into a relationship, the principal purpose of which is to transfer a thing of value to the recipient to carry out a public purpose of support or stimulation authorized by a law of the United States, rather than to acquire property or services for the DoD’s direct benefit or use. With Cooperative Agreements, substantial involvement is expected between the DoD and the recipient when carrying out the activity contemplated by the cooperative agreement. The term does not include cooperative research and development agreements as defined in 15 U.S.C. § 3710a. Essentially, Cooperative Agreements are assistance instruments, not acquisition instruments. Acquisition instruments such as Procurement Contracts, Prototype OTs, and Production OTs are intended for provide specific deliverables for DoD’s direct benefit or use. By contrast, assistance instruments are meant to carry out or stimulate an authorized public purpose.  

	

D. Generally with respect to all instruments:

		1.  Generally, this announcement is continuously open. Preliminary proposals (preproposals) may be submitted and will be evaluated for the general requirements of this BAA at any time for the potential time up to the next five (5) years. The availability of funds may limit the ability of the U.S. Government to make awards in specific areas, nevertheless preproposals are sought under this BAA announcement for areas consistent with the mission areas identified in Section VII of this announcement. DEVCOM CBC is interested in proposals that seek new and innovative concepts for basic and applied research and for development efforts not related to the development of specific systems or hardware (in accordance with FAR 35.016). Offers for research efforts related to specific systems or hardware development will not be considered, except to demonstrate a concept.

		2.  This announcement of DEVCOM CBC’s current interests will also be posted on the System for Award Management (SAM) website (http://www.sam.gov) and the DEVCOM CBC website (http://www.cbc.devcom.army.mil). This announcement will also be available on the Grants.gov web portal (http://www.grants.gov/).

		3.  From time to time, special announcements or calls for proposals referencing this BAA may be issued for specific requirements in addition to any requirements announced in Sections VII and VIII. Additionally, the application process may be amended as other electronic application processes are implemented. All amendments to this BAA will be announced on the websites shown above. To facilitate communication on both scientific and administrative matters relating to this BAA, a single email address may be used for all communication with DEVCOM CBC. Please send all technical and administrative questions and inquiries to usarmy.apg.devcom-cbc.mbx.technical-outreach@army.mil. 

		4.  Administrative questions concerning the preparation of preproposals or proposals should be addressed to U.S. Army Contracting Command Edgewood Contracting Division Officer. They should be emailed to usarmy.apg.acc.mbx.devcom-cbc-baa@army.mil

 ATTN: DEVCOM CBC BAA.

II.  ACRONYMS / DEFINITIONS:

AGENCY: Agency means any of the military departments or defense agencies with authority to award OTAs for prototype projects.

AGREEMENTS OFFICER: An Agreements Officer has authority to enter into, administer, or terminate OTAs for prototype projects and make related determinations and findings.

DEVELOPMENT: The systematic use of scientific and technical knowledge in the design, development, testing, or evaluation of potential new products, or service (or of an improvement in an existing product or service) to meet specific performance requirements or objectives. It includes the functions of design engineering, prototyping, and engineering testing; it excludes subcontracted technical effort that is for the sole purpose of developing an additional source for an existing product. 

ENABLING TECHNOLOGIES: Technologies that are not countermeasure products or systems themselves but facilitate or accelerate the development of countermeasure products or systems. Examples of enabling technologies include combinatorial chemistry, high-throughput screening, microarrays, bioinformatics and computational biology, nanotechnologies, imaging (including biosensors and biomarkers), animal models, assays, and other product development tools.

BIOMANUFACTURING: Type of manufacturing that utilizes biological systems (e.g., living microorganisms, resting cells, animal cells, plant cells, tissues, enzymes, or in vitro synthetic (enzymatic) systems) to produce commercially important biomolecules for use in the agricultural, food, material, energy, and pharmaceutical industries.

Human Research Protection Official (HRPO): A federal employee designated by a DoD Component or institution to conduct administrative review of DoD-supported research in accordance with the requirements of the DFARS, or comparable requirement, and whose review of DoD-supported research is intended to ensure compliance with DoD Human Subjects Research (HSR) requirements. 

HRPO Review: Review by a delegated individual after an initial non-DOD Human Research Protection Program determination of not HSR or exempt HSR or IRB approval (for non-exempt HSR). The purpose of the HRPO review is to ensure compliance of a DOD-supported activity with the requirements identified at DODI 3216.02, Enclosure 3, paragraph 4c, prior to initiation of the DOD-supported portion of the human subject’s research conducted by the non-DOD institution.

Human Subject: A living individual about whom an investigator conducting research obtains data through intervention or interaction with the individual or obtains identifiable private information as defined in section 219.102(f) of Reference (c). (FDA regulations include a different definition of human subject. With respect to research subject to FDA regulations, the FDA definition in section 50.3(g) of Reference (d) also applies.)

OTHER TRANSACTIONS FOR PROTOTYPES (pOTA): The Department has authority under 10 U.S.C. §4022 to award “other transactions” in certain circumstances for prototype projects that are directly relevant to enhancing the mission effectiveness of military personnel and the supporting platforms, systems, components, or materials proposed to be acquired or developed by the Department of Defense, or to improvement of platforms, systems, components, or materials in use by the Armed Forces. The pOTA is an acquisition instrument that generally is not subject to the federal laws and regulations governing procurement contracts.  

OTHER TRANSACTIONS FOR RESEARCH: (Research OT):  Research OTs are authorized under 10 U.S.C. §4021 and are used for basic, applied, and advanced research projects. Research OTs are used for basic, applied, and advanced research projects that are focused on validating research results and advancements, rather than for the delivery or acquisition of the resultant technologies. The goal of these awards is to foster the best technologies for future defense needs with the most capable performers. The DoD Financial Management Regulation, vol 2B, chapter 5 contains a detailed description of basic vs applied vs advanced research (https://comptroller.defense.gov/Portals/45/documents/fmr/Volume_02b.pdf). See also 2 CFR 1108 definitions of basic, applied, and advanced research (https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/subtitle-B/chapter-XI/subchapter-A/part-1108).

NATIONAL AERONAUTICS AND SPACE ADMINISTRATION 
Information Technology Procurement Office (ITPO) 
Justification for an Exception to Fair Opportunity 
Agency-Wide Hexagon MSC Software Renewal 
 
Description of the action being approved: This justification documents the basis for issuing a 
Delivery Order (DO) under the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) Solutions 
for Enterprise-Wide Procurement (SEWP), Government Wide Acquisition Contract (GWAC), 
using an exception to the Fair Opportunity process.   
 
Description of the supplies or services required to meet the agency’s needs: This competitive 
action establishes a Firm-Fixed-Price delivery order issued under the NASA SEWP GWAC for the 
Agency-Wide Hexagon MSC-software renewal. MSC’s software products include integrated (such 
as Actran, Adams), modeling (such as Patran) and solver (such as Dytran, Nastran, Sinda) 
solutions and many other applications, the majority of which are in two token delivery system 
environments, the legacy MasterKey Plus perpetual licensed application environment and MSC 
One, a subscription-based system with core applications bundled into the system. The total 
estimated price of the proposed order is  and the period of performance is a one-year 
base period with one one-year option period commencing on April 1, 2026 with a potential end 
date of March 31, 2028. 
 
Identification of Exception to Fair Opportunity: 
 
 FAR 16.505(b)(2)(i)(A), The agency need for the supplies or services is so urgent that 
providing a fair opportunity would result in unacceptable delays. 
 
 FAR 16.505(b)(2)(i)(B), Only one awardee is capable of providing the supplies or 
services required at the level of quality required because the supplies or services 
ordered are unique or highly specialized. 
 
 FAR 16.505(b)(2)(i)(C), The order must be issued on a sole-source basis in the interest 
of economy and efficiency because it is a logical follow-on to an order already issued 
under the contract, provided that all awardees were given a fair opportunity to be 
considered for the original order. 
 
 FAR 16.505(b)(2)(i)(D), It is necessary to place an order to satisfy a minimum 
guarantee. 
 
 FAR 16.505(b)(2)(i)(E), For orders exceeding the simplified acquisition threshold a 
statute expressly authorizes or requires that the purchase be made from a specified 
source.  
 
 FAR 16.505(b)(2)(i)(F), In accordance with section 1331 of Public Law 111-240 (15 
U.S.C. 644(r)), contracting officers may, at their discretion, set aside orders for any of 
the small business concerns identified in 19.000(a)(3). When setting aside orders for 


2 
Rev.:3/2025 
small business concerns, the specific small business program eligibility requirements 
identified in part 19 apply.  
 
 FAR 16.505(b)(2)(i)(G), The order satisfies one of the exceptions permitting the use 
of other than full and open competition listed in 6.302 (10 U.S.C. 3406(c)(5). The 
public interest exception shall not be used unless Congress is notified in accordance 
with 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(7). 
 
Supporting Rationale:  
 
ImmixTechnology is the only responsible source capable of providing the agency-wide 
Hexagon MSC software. MSC’s software products are acquired from ImmixTechnology 
through the original equipment manufacturer (OEM) Hexagon. The OEM letter verified that 
no other vendor could provide MSC software licenses, updates, or support due to Hexagon’s 
exclusive reseller structure.  MSC’s software (MSC) provides multidisciplinary simulation, 
modeling, and solver environment required to support NASA’s mission-critical engineering 
programs, due to proprietary model compatibility, unique solver capabilities, and the agency’s 
extensive legacy model base. 
 
Market research of current simulation software shows that several major vendors—such as 
ANSYS, Siemens, and Dassault Systèmes—offer advanced virtual‑analysis tools, yet none 
fully match the integrated capabilities provided by Hexagon’s MSC Software. While these 
competing platforms focus primarily on traditional structural, thermal, and multi‑physics 
simulation, they do not incorporate the tightly connected ecosystem that sets MSC apart. 
 
MSC Software uniquely blends its decades‑proven solvers with Hexagon’s precision 
metrology, digital‑twin technologies, and real‑world sensor integration. This combination 
creates a closed‑loop environment in which models are continuously calibrated and validated 
against sub‑millimeter physical measurement data and high‑accuracy digital‑reality 
representations. As a result, MSC enables engineering teams—such as those at NASA—to 
verify spacecraft structures, materials, and mission scenarios with a level of real‑world 
fidelity that simulation‑only platforms cannot achieve. 
 
Competitor tools provide powerful virtual analyses, but they lack MSC’s ability to seamlessly 
integrate physical measurement and sensor data into simulations, maintain continuously 
updated digital twins grounded in real‑world conditions, deliver real‑time engineering insight 
through automated validation workflows, and reduce uncertainty through persistent 
model‑to‑measurement correlation. These attributes make MSC Software the only solution in 
its class that bridges the gap between virtual simulation and physical truth. This not only 
enhances reliability and mission readiness but also significantly reduces risk in environments 
where accuracy is critical. 
 
MSC’s simulation and CAE software technology has been used to support NASA for several 
years. NASA owns and maintains a variety of MSC software products including Nastran, 
Patran, Adams, Marc, Easy5, CAEfatigue, Actran, and Apex. These MSC software products 
are Commercial-Off-the-Shelf (COTS) software tools which allow users the ability to create 
multidisciplinary simulation models and perform structural, nonlinear, composite, dynamic, 

3 
Rev.:3/2025 
load, thermal, aeroelastic, fatigue, and acoustic analyses. These products include multi-bodied 
dynamics modeling, aeroelastic simulation, 2D-3D modeling, and solver analytical solution 
software among other tools sets, including a unified CAE environment for virtual product 
development. 
 
MSC is unique among simulation platforms because it combines decades‑proven structural, 
thermal, and multi‑physics solvers with  a broader ecosystem of precision metrology, 
digital‑twin technology, and real‑world sensor integration. While competitors such as 
ANSYS, Siemens, and Dassault focus primarily on virtual simulation, MSC stands out by 
tightly linking its analysis tools to physical measurement data and high‑accuracy 
digital‑reality models. This enables NASA to validate spacecraft structures, materials, and 
mission scenarios with a level of fidelity that bridges the gap between simulation and 
real‑world performance. MSC’s sub‑millimeter metrology, real‑time engineering insight, and 
automation capabilities provides a uniquely closed‑loop environment where models can be 
continuously calibrated, verified, and improved. As a result, MSC reduces uncertainty, 
improves reliability, and strengthens mission readiness in ways that traditional 
simulation‑only platforms cannot match. 
 
The Aerostructures Branch at AFRC relies on MSC software to perform the full range of 
structural analyses needed to support research activities and verify the airworthiness of new or 
modified flight hardware. These analyses—linear and nonlinear static, dynamic, vibration, 
and thermal, it is critical for predicting stress, deformation, buckling, and fatigue, and for 
establishing margins of safety required for mission success. At Glenn Research Center, the 
Materials and Structures and Propulsion Divisions also use MSC tools as primary FEA 
resources for major efforts such as Artemis, Hypersonics, Lunar Gateway, and future Mars 
missions. Engineers at GRC use products like Nastran, Patran, Easy5, and Adams to validate 
and optimize designs through virtual prototypes, supported by flexible Masterkey and MSC 
One licensing. LaRC similarly depends on MSC Nastran and Patran for coupled loads 
analysis on programs such as SLS and Commercial Crew, as well as for multi-year research 
efforts including SCALPSS, NGUS, ARC-LSI, SVTT, HSF, and HiCAM. LaRC also uses 
MSC Adams, Nastran, and Actran for multi-body dynamics, nonlinear simulations, and 
independent verification and validation of contractor analyses. Together, these centers 
demonstrate NASA’s broad and sustained reliance on MSC software for high-fidelity 
structural modeling, mission-critical analysis, and long-term program support. 
 
Determination that the anticipated cost to the Government will be fair and reasonable:  
 
Pricing will be assessed against the Independent Government Cost Estimate (IGCE), historical 
data, previous orders, and the current commercial price list to enable the Contracting Officer to 
determine fair and reasonable pricing. Based on this approach, the Contracting Officer believes 
this approach will ensure a fair and reasonable price.

None.

1.  Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR

2.  Contract Title 

GLAVA Radio Communications System Expansion with Additional Motorola APX NEXT & Lifecycle Support Services.

3.  Background  

The VA Police Service at the Greater Los Angeles Healthcare System operates one of the largest federal law enforcement agencies within the Veterans Health Administration, providing law enforcement and emergency response services across multiple VA medical centers, outpatient clinics, and veteran housing facilities throughout the Greater Los Angeles region. Current operations require the expansion of radio communications infrastructure and dispatch capabilities to support growing mission requirements, officer safety, and interoperability with local, state, and federal law enforcement partners including the Los Angeles Police Department (LAPD), Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department (LASD), Los Angeles Fire Department (LAFD), Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), and Department of Homeland Security (DHS).

This procurement effort is also in support of the Executive Order on the National Center for Warrior Independence (NCWI), which necessitates enhanced communication capabilities to ensure efficient coordination and secure communications. The procurement includes adding 100 new Motorola APX NEXT portable radios to the existing fleet to meet the demands of increased personnel and expanded operational requirements.

The expansion aligns with the goals of the National Emergency Communications Plan (NECP) to ensure effective interoperability, coordination, lifecycle management, and strengthening the cybersecurity posture of public safety communications as a whole.

4.Objective

The objective of this procurement is to expand the existing radio communications system and dispatch capability with modern, secure, fully interoperable equipment that meets federal law enforcement standards and supports VA Police operational requirements for the next five years. The system expansion shall provide:

Secure, encrypted voice communications for additional VA Police personnel

Seamless integration with existing ASTRO 25 infrastructure

Advanced digital features including voice control, smart programming, and connectivity management

Lifecycle support ensuring system reliability, security patching, and operational readiness

Compliance with federal information security standards and VA policy requirements

5. Scope

This Statement of Work / Performance Work Statement (SOW/PWS) defines the requirements for the procurement, implementation, and lifecycle support of 100 additional Motorola APX NEXT portable radio communications equipment. The Contractor shall provide all equipment, software, licensing, installation support, training, maintenance, and technical support necessary to establish and sustain a fully operational, secure, interoperable radio communications system supporting VA Police operations at the Greater Los Angeles Healthcare System (GLA).

LTE and Wi-Fi connectivity enabled

AES-256 encryption capability

P25 Phase II trunking capability

Integrated GPS

Bluetooth connectivity

Voice control (ViQi) capability

Smart Programming and Smart Connect features

Mission Critical Push-to-Talk (MCPTT) ready

Statement of Work (SOW) 

PURPOSE:


The purpose of this contract is to acquire updated two-way communications equipment, which in-turn shall enhance and improve the existing equipment and system used by the Northern Arizona Veterans Affairs Health Care System (NAVAHCS) Police Department.  The Contractor shall provide all necessary labor, supervision, equipment supplies, materials, materials, and travel to provide the equipment at NAVAHCS.  Furthermore, the NAVAHCS Police Department is seeking a portable radio, created specifically for mission-critical first responders who need to communicate across all frequency bands using the same device.  In order to maintain 100% complete compatibility with other VAPD stations within District 2, the Motorola model APX 8500 compatible with Programming over Project 25 (POP-25) that currently is in use within the district should be used.

BACKGROUND:


The United States Department of Veterans Affairs Police (VA Police) is the uniformed law enforcement service of the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, responsible for the protection of the VA Medical Centers (VAMC) and other facilities such as Outpatient Clinics (OPC) and Community Based Outpatient Clinics (CBOC) operated by United States Department of Veterans Affairs and its subsidiary components of the Veterans Health Administration (VHA), as well as the National Cemetery Administration (NCA) and the Veterans Benefits Administration (VBA) respectively. 

The Department of Veterans (VA) requires VA Police Officers to carry communications equipment.  Effective physical security requires the planning and protection of persons, resources, and property; prevention of loss and theft of supplies and property, and practical and economical application of technical security aids to augment police staff for the protection of VA facilities.  

Per VA Handbook 0730, The Radio Policy for requirements on communications throughout the Police service on VA campuses as well as the surrounding CBOCs states that  

VA Police officers will be always provided portable two-way radio units for use while on duty. 

Such radios will include a frequency dedicated exclusively for Police use to facilitate instant communication and direction during emergencies.  

The radio system is designed to prevent “dead spots’ from interrupting communications and will ensure that voice transmission is easily heard.

(AFRL/RY) is announcing its intent to solicit proposals under this “ARA with Calls”. 
Solicitations for white papers/proposals will be accomplished via calls. The calls will 
encompass the following effort: 
 
1. Statement of Objective/Description of Technical Area(s): 
The TEMPEST program will investigate, develop, mature, prototype and 
demonstrate methodologies, tools, techniques, and capabilities to identify 
susceptibilities and mitigate vulnerabilities in avionics systems, protect those 
systems against cyber-attack, provide simulation capabilities required to develop, 
mature and transition advanced avionics and sensor technologies, develop 
platform architecture technologies that enable revolutionary and agile capabilities, 
and expand emerging open system architecture (OSA) standards and approaches 
for existing and next-generation Air Force and Department of Defense (DoD) 
weapon systems in multi-domain environments. 
 
Calls issued against this ARA will: 
• Develop experimental programs that prototype, integrate and demonstrate 
promising cyber security and cognitive avionics technologies to increase our 
platforms’ and weapon systems’ survivability and resiliency in the face of multi- 
domain threats and attacks. 
• Develop, experiment, prototype and integrate, in a laboratory environment, 
new cognitive, cyber hardened and high speed, flexible system architectures. 
• Cooperate across the Air Force, DoD, and the Intelligence Community, to 
develop experimental programs that integrate advanced cyber security and 
cognitive sensor technologies, techniques, systems and developmental 
algorithms, new cyber hardened and high speed, flexible system architectures, 
and advanced avionics, sensors, processing, and exploitation capabilities 
focused on Command, Control, Communications, Computers, Intelligence, 
Surveillance and Reconnaissance (C4ISR) onto various weapon systems to 
create revolutionary capabilities. 
• Develop experimental programs that implement OSA-based reference

architectures to demonstrate the cost and time benefits of applying OSA 
techniques and align multiple open architecture (OA) standards to prove the 
interoperability of various standards. Apply and demonstrate tools, 
technologies, and techniques to more rapidly document, model, simulate, and 
analyze new OSA-based system capabilities to determine the benefits for 
individual platforms and the warfighter. 
Calls to be issued against the TEMPEST ARA must a) fall under at least one of the 
Technical Areas of Interest detailed in paragraph I.1.a. below, and b) involve at 
least one of the types of work detailed in paragraph I.1.b. below. 
 
a. Technical Areas of Interest: 
 
1) Technologies for Assessing Platform Cyber Security: 
Focuses on the design and development of technologies that provide tools 
to test and experimentation (T&E) units and Cyber units (such as Mission 
Defense Teams or Red Teams) to assess cyber vulnerabilities in weapon 
systems with embedded computers. 
2) Technologies for Cyber-Hardened Platforms: 
Focuses on the design and development of technologies that reduce 
weapon system vulnerability to cyber-attack. 
3) Technologies for Cyber-Resilient Platforms: 
Focuses on the design and development of technologies that counter both 
known and unknown attack vectors that occur during mission operations to 
maintain mission capability in cyber contested environments. 
4) Agile System Architecture Development and Integration: 
Focuses on the design/procurement, development and demonstration of 
tools, technologies, and advanced component prototypes to enable 
affordable, rapid development and integration of new and emerging 
warfighting capability. Characteristics of these systems include, but are not 
limited to: capable of performing multiple functions (e.g., radar, 
communications, and electronic warfare), capable of fusing different types 
of data collections (i.e., multiple intelligence (multi-INT)), inherently cyber 
secure and/or resilient to cyber-attack, and compliant with open system 
architecture standards and approaches. 
5) Open System Architectures for Trusted and Agile Platforms: 
Focuses on investigation, through analysis, demonstration and advanced 
component prototyping, the viability and relevance of current and emerging 
open system architecture standards and approaches to enable new 
capability for cyber trusted and agile platforms. This technology area seeks 
to determine the viability of an OSA implementation prior to system design 
and development. This technical area shall identify technological advances 
in open system architecture standards, software, processing, and hardware 
to demonstrate the viability of modular open system architectures.

Focuses on the discovery, design and implementation of novel technologies 
to advance the state-of-the-art in modeling/simulation to faithfully 
represent transmitters, receivers, electronic systems, hostile and friendly 
radars, and radio frequency propagation algorithms for use with advanced 
models and simulations. 
7) Technologies to Advance RF Simulation: 
Focuses on defining simulation requirements for accurately demonstrating 
and evaluating sensor technologies. This technology area includes the 
design and implementation of prototype hardware (commercial or custom) 
and corresponding operating software tools to conduct demonstrations of 
radio frequency receiving or transmitting systems. 
8) Techniques, methods and technologies for measuring sensor 
system performance: 
Focuses on developing simulation techniques and methods to rapidly evolve 
and evaluate advanced sensors and electronic warfare (EW) technologies 
demonstrated in laboratory environments. Work under this technical area 
of interest will develop and employ M&S methods to specify requirements, 
define architectures, conduct design trades, and report assessment and 
demonstration results. 
b. Development, Experimentation, Test, Evaluation, Assessment,

Draft Statement of Work (SOW) 
Cloud Center of Excellence (CCoE) Implementation 
Indian Health Service (IHS) 
Division of Information Technology (DIT) 
 
1. INTRODUCTION 
The Indian Health Service (IHS), an agency within the U.S. Department of Health and Human 
Services (HHS), is initiating a strategic modernization program to establish a Cloud Center of 
Excellence (CCoE). The CCoE will utilize Cloud (GovCloud - FedRAMP) to centralize, secure, 
and automate cloud operations while supporting mission-critical health IT objectives. 
This Statement of Work (SOW) outlines the tasks, deliverables, roles, and performance 
expectations for designing, implementing, and sustaining the CCoE in alignment with federal 
compliance frameworks including: 
• FedRAMP (High Baseline) 
• NIST 800-53 Rev 5 
• Executive Order 14028 
• OMB M-22-09, M-24-04 
• CISA’s Zero Trust Maturity Model (ZTMM) 
• Post Quantum Computing (PQC) Readiness meeting PQC Mandate Enablement   
• Secure AI ready platform  
 
2. BACKGROUND 
IHS currently operates in a decentralized IT environment that contributes to fragmented 
infrastructure, inconsistent security enforcement, and risk exposure. GAO Report GAO-21-20 
identified several deficiencies in cloud governance, visibility, and cybersecurity readiness. 
To address these gaps, IHS will implement a secure Cloud GovCloud-based environment that 
consolidates infrastructure, automates security workflows, and incorporates role-based AI tools. 
The CCoE will enable continuous compliance, reduce operational overhead, and support 
innovation across IHS facilities. 
 
3. SCOPE OF WORK 
The Contractor shall provide a comprehensive solution that includes, but is not limited to, the 
following capabilities: 

• Cloud Landing Zone Design & Deployment 
o Multi-account Cloud architecture with governance controls 
o Use of Cloud Control Tower, Service Catalog, and Cloud Organizations 
o Identity and access management aligned with Zero Trust principles 
• Secure Enclave Provisioning 
o Configured enclaves for development, staging, and production workloads 
o FedRAMP-compliant storage, compute, and networking (e.g., EC2, S3, VPC, 
PrivateLink) 
o Hardened environments using CIS benchmarks and Cloud best practices 
• Automation and Orchestration 
o Automated workflows for ATO lifecycle management 
o Continuous POA&M generation, patch validation, and compliance reporting 
o Integration with SIEM (e.g., Splunk), SOAR tools, and Cloud Security Hub 
• Data Engineering and ETL 
o Extract-Transform-Load (ETL) pipelines for ingesting and transforming log and 
event data 
o Integration with Cloud   native telemetry (e.g., CloudTrail, GuardDuty) and third-
party tools 
o Masking and classification of PHI/PII in compliance with HIPAA and FISMA 
• Large Language Model (LLM) Enablement 
o On-premise or enclave-deployed LLMs for secure, role-based inference 
o AI-assisted document generation (e.g., SSP, SAR, RAR, POA&M) 
o Local semantic search and summarization of compliance materials 
o Use of containerized, GPU-accelerated inference in isolated VPCs 
• Compliance Dashboards and Risk Analytics 
o Real-time compliance status dashboards for executive reporting 
o Dashboards showing ATO progress, open vulnerabilities, audit readiness 
o Integration with natural language interfaces for querying compliance data 
• Zero Trust Architecture Implementation 
o Aligned with CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model (ZTMM) 
o Support for microsegmentation, encrypted remote access, and continuous 
validation 
o Maturity benchmarking and optimization across all ZTA pillars 
• Security Operations and Monitoring 
o Centralized log aggregation and threat detection via SIEM 
o Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR), vulnerability management 
o Continuous diagnostics and mitigation (CDM) support 
• Secure Data Vault and Metadata Governance 
o Encrypted storage with tagging and classification aligned with NIST 800-60 
o Role-based tagging, automated metadata parsing, and retention policies 
o AI-assisted classification and redaction for secure document handling 
• Stakeholder Support and Role-Based Toolkits 
o Interfaces and workflows tailored to ISSOs, POA&M Analysts, Auditors, System 
Owners 
o Embedded help systems and LLM-based support assistants 
o Training materials and job aids customized per role 

 
4. OBJECTIVES 
The objectives of the Cloud Center of Excellence (CCoE) initiative are to modernize, secure, and 
automate IHS cloud operations across the enterprise, in alignment with federal mandates, audit 
recommendations, and the agency’s mission to improve healthcare delivery through digital 
transformation. This section outlines the business, technical, security, and strategic outcomes the 
initiative is expected to achieve. 
4.1 Business Objectives 
• Establish a centralized cloud governance model to address findings in GAO Report 
GAO-21-20 and reduce operational fragmentation. 
• Enable secure, compliant testing and deployment of mission-critical applications through 
standardized Cloud environments. 
• Implement a cost accountability framework via a chargeback model supported by Cloud 
Budgets and Cost Explorer. 
• Reduce total cost of ownership through tool rationalization, license consolidation, and 
automation of manual compliance functions. 
• Improve leadership visibility into risk posture, operational performance, and compliance 
status through real-time executive dashboards. 
4.2 Technical Objectives 
• Design and deploy a secure Cloud Landing Zone architecture with multi-account 
governance, VPC segmentation, and centralized identity and access management. 
• Automate core compliance and operational workflows including: 
o ATO package generation 
o POA&M lifecycle tracking 
o Patch deployment validation 
o Security incident ticketing and audit response 
• Integrate telemetry, logs, and vulnerability scan results into a unified SIEM and 
dashboarding platform. 
• Establish secure ETL pipelines from Cloud  and third-party telemetry sources into 
centralized compliance dashboards and data lakes. 
• Deploy GPU-enabled container environments for operating fine-tuned, enclave-hosted 
LLMs in support of documentation generation, compliance analytics, and secure 
information retrieval. 
4.3 Security and Compliance Objectives 
• Achieve continuous compliance monitoring and FedRAMP alignment across deployed 
systems and workflows. 
• Implement Zero Trust Architecture (ZTA) principles throughout the environment in 
accordance with CISA’s ZTMM framework. 

• Provide role-specific support tools for ISSOs, Security Control Assessors, POA&M 
Analysts, and System Owners, enhancing their efficiency and audit-readiness. 
• Enable enclave-based LLMs to support automated generation of SSPs, SARs, SAPs, and 
other required documentation with no data egress. 
• Monitor compliance posture in real-time through dashboards that provide insights into 
ATO progression, vulnerability resolution, patch coverage, and audit gaps. 
4.4 Strategic Outcomes 
• Empower IHS leadership with defensible, data-driven insights into cybersecurity, 
operations, and cloud utilization. 
• Institutionalize a scalable, repeatable cloud operations model that supports future IHS 
initiatives, including EHR modernization and AI-driven analytics. 
• Reduce the burden on IHS security and compliance staff by automating routine 
workflows and documentation tasks using enclave-secured LLMs. 
• Increase IHS agility in adopting and securing commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) tools by 
establishing pre-authorization environments. 
• Create a foundation for continual innovation by deploying cloud-native and AI-native 
technologies in a secure and governed manner. 
 
5. PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE 
One Year. All core implementation phases (enclave setup, automations, training) are to be 
completed within the Base Year. 
 
6. PLACE OF PERFORMANCE 
All work shall be performed remotely unless otherwise directed by the Contracting Officer. The 
Contractor shall use IHS-approved virtual collaboration platforms for meetings, training, and 
reviews. 
 
7. PHASED IMPLEMENTATION PLAN & DELIVERABLES 
The CCoE shall be delivered in three integrated phases. Each phase builds on the previous to 
ensure secure design, operational automation, and sustainable cloud governance. All activities 
will comply with IHS, HHS, and federal cybersecurity mandates. 
7.1 Phase 1: Foundation — Secure Enclave and Cloud  Infrastructure 
Deployment 

Objective: 
Establish the secure Cloud GovCloud infrastructure, deploy baseline logging, identity, and ETL 
capabilities, and prepare for authorization under FedRAMP and IHS-specific requirements. 
Key Activities: 
• Deploy Cloud Landing Zone using Cloud Control Tower and multi-account best practices 
• Configure core services: EC2, S3 (Standard, Glacier IR, Deep Archive), IAM, VPC, and 
PrivateLink 
• Enable centralized logging, auditing, and threat detection with Cloud CloudTrail, 
GuardDuty, and Config 
• Provision ETL servers and data pipelines to Splunk/Data Lake 
• Deploy GPU-enabled container environments for local LLMs in isolated VPCs 
• Draft core ATO documentation including SSP, SAP, RAR, and ConMon strategy 
• Establish compliance governance alignment with NIST, ZTMM, and FedRAMP High 
Deliverables: 
• Cloud Landing Zone Architecture and Configuration Artifacts 
• IAM and VPC Security Configuration Documentation 
• Hardened ETL Server Deployment Package and Logging Setup 
• Baseline Data Classification and Masking Policy 
• Initial LLM Hosting Blueprint with Secure Container Deployment 
• Draft ATO Documents: SSP, SAP, RAR, Continuous Monitoring Strategy 
• Cloud Governance and Risk Register (Initial Baseline) 
7.2 Phase 2: Automation — Compliance, Risk Visibility, and ATO Enablement 
Objective: 
Automate security workflows, compliance operations, and risk analytics; integrate dashboarding, 
vulnerability scanning, and AI-powered documentation assistance. 
Key Activities: 
• Configure automation engines for POA&M tracking, ATO artifact generation, and patch 
lifecycle management 
• Integrate Cloud Security Hub, SIEM, SOAR, and ticketing systems (e.g., ServiceNow) 
• Deploy real-time dashboards for ATO progression, risk indicators, and vulnerability 
metrics 
• Train enclave-hosted LLMs on redacted historical data for audit RFI generation, 
SSP/POA&M summarization, and classification 
• Conduct full UAT with compliance and security teams across workflows and dashboards 
• Finalize all ATO documentation for formal submission 
• Document governance procedures for automation use and LLM assistance 
Deliverables: 

• Validated Automation Playbooks for ATO, POA&M, Patch, and IR workflows 
• Deployed Compliance Dashboards with Export/Reporting Capabilities 
• Integrated SIEM/EDR/Vulnerability Dashboard and Alerting Interfaces 
• Enclave-Based LLM Toolkits: Prompt Libraries, Summary Engines, Audit RFI Generator 
• Peer-Reviewed Codebase and QA Documentation for Security Automations 
• Completed ATO Package: SSP, SAP, SAR, POA&M Workbook 
• UAT Report, Change Logs, and Final QA Sign-off 
7.3 Phase 3: Transition — Training, Knowledge Transfer, and Operational 
Readiness 
Objective: 
Ensure IHS personnel are fully equipped to operate, sustain, and enhance the CCoE platform 
through structured training, documentation, and role-specific toolkits. 
Key Activities: 
• Deliver role-specific training for ISSOs, System Owners, Engineers, Analysts, and 
Auditors 
• Provide instructional resources: slide decks, recordings, quick-reference guides 
• Conduct operational exercises in staging environments to validate training 
comprehension 
• Finalize SOPs for Cloud, ETL, automation workflows, and LLM-based compliance 
tooling 
• Complete knowledge transfer and governance handoff with defined ownership and 
escalation paths 
• Deliver final project documentation package and operational readiness checklist 
Deliverables: 
• Training Curriculum by Role (ISSOs, DevSecOps, Security Analysts, etc.) 
• Admin Manuals, Reference Guides, and Recorded Training Sessions 
• SOPs for Enclave Management, ETL, Compliance Automation, and LLM Use 
• Knowledge Transfer Package with Architecture, Workflows, a

Special Notice DARPA-SN-26-57 
Strategic Technology Office (STO) Office-wide Industry Day 
Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) 
 
Posting Date: April 9, 2026 
Event Date: June 8-9, 2026 
Registration Deadline: May 15, 2026, at 1:00 p.m. Eastern Time (ET) 
Registration Website: https://cvent.me/e9mAMw  
Technical POC: Dr. John Paschkewitz, Office Director 
E-mail: DARPA-SN-26-57@darpa.mil  
 
DESCRIPTION: 
The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) Strategic Technology Office (STO) 
will host a STO Office-wide Industry Day event on June 8-9, 2026. The event will be held at the 
DARPA Conference Center (DCC) located at 675 N. Randolph St., Arlington, VA 22203. 
Advance registration is required. There will be no on-site registration. This event will be 
hosted in-person only. The event will include presentations by the STO Director and Program 
Managers (PM), panel discussions, and an opportunity for one-on-one engagement with STO 
PMs via sidebar meetings.  
The purpose of the event is to (1) familiarize attendees with STO’s vision, problem spaces, PMs, 
and technology interests; and (2) facilitate technical discussion between STO PMs and attendees 
that explore innovative and impactful solution ideas for strategic national security challenges. 
This meeting will be held at the SECRET collateral level.  
 
STO MISSION AND FOCUS AREAS: 
STO is DARPA’s systems warfare office pursuing innovative and disruptive technologies for 
existing and future battlespaces. With peer competitors able to develop and field new capabilities 
at speeds unmatched by prior U.S. adversaries, STO focuses on the ability to provide warfighters 
with systems that enable superior adaptation at speed and scale and that create new opportunities 
for deterrence and overmatch.  
STO’s technical focus areas include: 
• Multi-Domain Mission Systems – new systems and resilient architectures with the ability 
to sense and sense-make; includes AI-native planning & execution systems to provide 
orchestrating effects  
• Maritime – maritime capabilities that leverage U.S. asymmetric advantages and create 
novel operational dilemmas for competitors and adversaries 
• Space – space systems that leverage scaling provided by America’s rapidly growing 
commercial space industry  
• Industry, Infrastructure, and Information – strengthening U.S. assets and ecosystems, 
creating complexity to stymie potential adversaries, and accelerating our own ability to 
field new capabilities 

DARPA-SN-26-57 
Page 2 of 4 
 
 
REGISTRATION INFORMATION: 
The STO Office-wide Industry Day will be held on June 8-9, 2026, at the DARPA Conference 
Center (DCC) located at 675 N. Randolph St., Arlington, VA 22203. Advance registration is 
required and there will be no on-site registration. 
Attendance is open to registrants with at least a SECRET clearance, on a first-come, first-served 
basis with no more than two representatives per business unit of an organization until venue 
capacity is reached. The determination of what constitutes a business unit will be made by 
DARPA. Interested parties are encouraged to coordinate attendance internally within their 
organizations prior to registration. 
Registration closes at 1:00 pm ET on May 15, 2026. Visit requests, security clearances, and 
other applicable documents must be sent to DARPA by this time. 
Participants must register prior to registration close at https://cvent.me/e9mAMw. 
 
SIDEBAR MEETINGS: 
Registered attendees will have the option to request 15-minute sidebar meetings with STO PMs 
to further elaborate their specific technical fields. Only a limited number of meeting times are 
available and there is no guarantee all attendees will be scheduled for sidebar meetings. 
To best align the research interests of participants with those of STO PMs, interested 
parties must submit the request form provided at the end of this Special Notice prior to 
registration close. 
Attendees will be notified of their meeting time and on-site instructions. No additional sidebar 
meetings will be scheduled during the event. No more than 2 representatives may join in a single 
sidebar meeting. 
Please note that no competition-sensitive information will be shared or discussed in the sidebar 
meetings. 
Sidebar meetings may require additional clearances to be sent to DARPA. DARPA will notify 
the participants of their meeting time and classification of discussion. At that time, participants 
will have 5 business days to submit any additional clearance visit request. For those requesting 
an SCI-level sidebar discussion, SCI-level visit request can be sent proactively, prior to being 
notified of sidebar selection. 
 
SECURITY INFORMATION:  
All attendees must transmit their security clearances to DARPA. Clearances must be received 
prior to the registration close. Failure to complete and submit the required forms prior to the 
registration deadline may result in the cancellation of existing registration.  
• For collateral-level visits to DARPA, please have the Facilities Security Officer (FSO) 
send a visit request via Defense Information System for Security (DISS) using the SMO 
Code: DDAAUS4. You may also fax your clearance/visit request to DARPA at (703) 

DARPA-SN-26-57 
Page 3 of 4 
 
528-3655 or send it via encrypted e-mail to SID-CPC@darpa.mil. The Technical POC is 
John Paschkewitz at (571) 218-4322 and the Security POC is Jamie Bugett. The purpose 
is to attend the STO Office-wide Industry Day 2026 DARPA-SN-26-57.   
For additional instructions on sending visit requests and security clearances to DARPA, please 
visit http://www.darpa.mil/policy/visitor-information.  
The optional sidebar meetings will be held at DARPA and may be offered up to the TOP 
SECRET/SCI-level classification. Attendees invited to sidebar meetings will be notified prior to 
the event, anticipated by 26th of May 2026. Based on highest classification requested by 
participants, classified meetings may require additional security clearance transmittal.  
In anticipation of an SCI-level visits: Please fax your clearance/visit request to the SSO at 703-
528-3655 (unclassified). You may also send your SCI visit requests as follows: 
o Via JWICS, the requesting SSO may send a message with the visit information to 
SSO DARPA. 
o Via DISS, the requesting SSO may send a visit request using the SMO Code 
DDAAUS2. 
 
TEAMING: 
To assist those wanting to establish collaborative teaming efforts and business relationships, 
participants may indicate on the registration website that they authorize their contact information 
to be shared among meeting participants. For organizations new to DARPA, this may be of use 
in connecting with potential partners. Team formation, communications, and networking are the 
sole responsibility of the participants.  
 
DISCLAIMERS: 
This Special Notice is issued solely for information and program planning purposes and does not 
constitute a formal solicitation for proposals or proposal abstracts; any so sent will be 
disregarded. In accordance with FAR 15.201(e), responses to this Special Notice are not offers 
and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. Attendance is strictly 
voluntary and is not required to propose to subsequent Announcements (if any) or Solicitations 
(if any) on this topic. DARPA will not provide reimbursement for costs incurred in responding to 
this Special Notice. Respondents are advised that DARPA is under no obligation to acknowledge 
receipt of any information received or provide feedback to respondents with respect to any 
information submitted under this Special Notice.

Strategic Technology Office (STO) Office-wide Industry Day 
Request for Program Manager Sidebar Form 
 
Responses are expected to be UNCLASSIFIED and should be submitted via email attachment to 
DARPA-SN-26-57@darpa.mil. No classified submissions should be emailed to this inbox.  
To submit a classified response, interested participants must pre-coordinate via UNCLASSIFIED 
email request to DARPA-SN-26-57@darpa.mil. Email subject should read: “Request to submit 
classified sidebar materials.” Email request should also include the intended classification of the 
content. At least one week prior to deadline for pre-coordination is recommended, for material to 
be received at DARPA prior to registration close.
