Hull Plating (Side Scan), Ultrasonic Testing 
1. SCOPE 
1.1 Intent. This work item describes the requirements for the Contractor to perform thickness 
measurements of the underwater (u/w) body and freeboard by ultrasonic side scan method. 
1.2 Government-furnished property.  
None. 
2. REFERENCES 
COAST GUARD DRAWINGS 
Coast Guard Drawing 87 WPB 085-013, Rev B, Docking Plan 
Coast Guard Drawing 87 WPB 111-001, Rev H, Shell Expansion 
Coast Guard Drawing 87 WPB 111-050, Rev A, Updates to DWG 87-WPB-111-001 Exhaust 
Port Insert Plate Installation and Details 
COAST GUARD PUBLICATIONS 
Surface Forces Logistics Center Standard Specification 0000 (SFLC Std Spec 0000), 2022, 
General Requirements 
OTHER REFERENCES 
American Society for Nondestructive Testing (ASNT) SNT-TC-1A, 2016, Recommended 
Practice for Personal Qualification and Certification in Nondestructive Testing 
3. REQUIREMENTS 
3.1 General. 
3.1.1 CIR.  
None. 
3.1.2 Tech Rep.  
Not applicable. 
3.1.3 Protective measures. The Contractor must furnish and install all protective measures in accordance 
with SFLC Std Spec 0000, paragraph 3.3.3 (Vessel component, space, and equipment protection). 

3.1.4 Interferences. The Contractor must handle all interferences in accordance with SFLC Std Spec 0000, 
paragraph 3.3.5 (Interferences). Known interferences include, but are not limited to the following: 
 Hull zinc anode system 
 Docking blocks 
3.2 Work coordination and preparation. The coast guard will complete specified vessel work detailed in 
this specification package to ensure the side scan survey does not necessitate a work stoppage. The 
goverment will abide by the following guidance, to facilitate the ultrasonic survey: 
 Ensure that all freeboard and u/w body surface preparation and primer coat application tasks 
are completed prior to the survey. 
 Prior to side-scan survey, inspect interior and bilge plating for the presence of bubbles of 
rusted metal. Break up and remove all rust bubbles to ensure accurate survey results. 
 Provide a continuous supply of fresh water at .50 gpm within 50 feet of the vessel with 
standard hose bib fitting. 
 Provide 110 VAC electrical power, and scaffolding or other suitable means of access to bring 
inspection personnel within one foot of all the hull surface inspection areas that are five feet 
above ground level. 
3.3 Side scan requirements and procedures. The Contractor must ensure the following referring to Coast 
Guard Drawings 87 WPB 085-13, 87 WPB 111-001, and 87 WPB 111-050 as guidance during the 
performance of the tasks specified below. 
3.3.1 Testing company and personnel. Provide the services of a qualified ultrasonic testing company, with 
suitable side scan equipment, to conduct a “Scanning Crawler Automated Test” of the vessel’s freeboard 
and u/w hull plating for the presence of metal corrosion and deterioration. Ensure the following: 
 All scanning operations are completed by personnel meeting the personnel qualification and 
certification, as required by contractor process. This contractor-developed personnel 
qualification and certification process must meet, at a minimum, ASNT Recommended 
Practice No. SNT-TC-1A.  
 An ASNT Level III Analyst is on site, to oversee the project and evaluate the collected data. 
 An ASNT Level III or II Analyst is on site, to verify with a hand held gauge all areas on the 
hull identified as thinner than the specified criteria, in order to expedite all repair procedures. 
 Qualified personnel are provided to complete all on-site inspections. 
3.3.2 Coast Guard notification.  
3.3.2.1 Provide a daily update to the COR on all areas inspected and potential issues or schedule changes. 
3.3.2.2 Notify the COR at least 3 days prior to completion for an onsite review of readings and repair 
areas. 
3.3.3 Scanning parameters. Use the following parameters during the course of this inspection: 
 Automated scanning resolution must be set to 0.5” x 0.5” 
 Plates where scan data indicating wastage greater than or equal to 25% nominal plate 
thickness must be highlighted in “RED” and designated “repair areas”.  
 Plates where scan data indicating wastage greater than or equal to 15% to 24% of nominal 
plate thickness must be highlighted in “YELLOW”. 

 Plates where scan data indicating wastage greater than or equal to 10% to 14% of nominal 
plate thickness must be highlighted in DARK GREEN.  
 Hand held UT readings must be taken to verify bad metal areas found with the side scan 
equipment. All readings must be provided to the COR and the lowest reading marked on the 
hull at the bad metal location. 
 Areas that are accessible but cannot be reached by the automated scanner must be scanned 
with a hand-held meter at a resolution of 2” x 2”. Any repair areas found during the hand scan 
must be marked on the ships hull and their approximate positions recorded on the plate 
drawings and report summary. 
3.3.3.1 Any scanning parameter or scope of work changes must be approved by the KO. 
3.3.3.2 The echo to echo transducer is not authorized due to inconsistent readings and technical 
difficulties. 
3.3.3.3 There must be no deviation from the color scheme specified above. 
3.3.4 Ensure that the side scan inspection area includes the Port, Starboard, and Transom exterior shell 
plating, but must exclude the following list. 
 Areas under and within 6-inches of blocks and side blocks (areas that are accessible 6 inches 
from blocks and side blocks must be hand scanned.) 
 Areas up to 6-inches around any obstacle on the hull including sea suctions, discharges, 
rudderposts, anodes, stern tubes, and docking blocks. 
 Any areas blocked by immovable scaffolding or shipyard activity. 
3.4 Side scan reports. The Contractor must submit a CFR containing the final report within three working 
days after the side scan inspection is completed. A copy of all repair areas must be clearly marked, in 
yellow or white, on the provided shell plate drawing(s), and provide a summary document of same areas. 
Submit two hard copies of the report with two CD’s containing the electronic (raw) data prior to departing 
the job site. Ensure the reports include: 
 Inspection overview. 
 Data sheets for each plate with designated repair areas outlined in blue. 
 Mosaic of scanned data overlaid on Coast Guard Drawing 87 WPB 111-001. 
NOTE 
Where hull repairs are required in the vicinity of the exhaust teardrops, use 
Coast Guard Drawing 87 WPB 111-050 for guidance on location of stainless 
steel hull inserts and when planning for plating renewal. 
3.4.1 Photos. Provide digital photos of all designated repair areas. 
3.4.2 Electronic files. Ensure CD’s contain a complete copy of the report, interactive data files, and digital 
pictures. All electronic files must be compatible with standard USCG workstation operating software. 
Electronic files format must be such that the CG has the capability to change the percent of wastage 
(format conditioning) per plate. Electronic files must be capable of being opened using MS Word, MS 
Excel, or PDF software. Digital pictures must be recorded in JPEG format. 

3.5 Touch-up preservation. The Contractor must prepare and coat all disturbed interior bilge surfaces to 
match existing adjacent surfaces in accordance with SFLC Std Spec 6310, paragraph 3.1.13 (Touch-ups 
and minor coating repairs.) 
4. NOTES 
This section is not applicable to this work item

Sources Sought: Security Cameras and Lenel HSPD-12/FIPS 201-3 Compliant Door Access Control 
Systems - Installation, Service, and Maintenance for the Great Plains Area Indian Health Service 
(GPAIHS), Office of Information Technology (OIT) Department, Aberdeen, South Dakota. 
Sources Sought Notice Number: SS-26-IHS-1520131.  
This is a Sources Sought notice. This notice DOES NOT constitute a request for proposal, request for 
quote or invitation for bid. This Sources Sought is a market research tool being utilized to determine the 
availability of qualified Indian Small Businesses Economic Enterprises (ISBEEs) and Indian 
Economic Enterprises. (IEEs) capable of performing the requirement prior to issuing a Request for 
Quote. This is not a solicitation for proposals and no contract will be awarded from this announcement. 
No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to this 
announcement. All responses will be provided by an e-mail response. No presentations will be scheduled. 
Your responses to the information requested will assist the Government in determining the appropriate 
acquisition method, including whether a set-aside is possible. The applicable NAICS code for this 
acquisition is 541519 (Other Computer Related Services). 
1.0
 BACKGROUND 
T
he Indian Health Service (IHS) an agency within the Department of Health & Human Services is 
responsible for providing federal health services to American Indians and Alaska Natives.  The Indian 
Health Service provides a comprehensive health service delivery system for approximately 1.9 million 
American Indians and Alaska Natives who belong to 567 federally recognized tribes, in 35 states.  The 
Indian Health Service Headquarters is located in Rockville, MD and then divided into twelve physical 
areas:  Alaska, Albuquerque, Bemidji, Billings, California, Great Plains, Nashville, Navajo, Oklahoma, 
Phoenix, Portland and Tucson.  
The Great Plains Area Office (GPAO) works in conjunction with its 19 Indian Health Service Units and 
Tribal Managed Service Units to provide health care to approximately 122,000 Native American located 
in North Dakota, South Dakota, Nebraska, and Iowa.  The Area Office’s service units include seven 
hospitals, eight health centers, and several smaller health stations and satellite clinics.  
2.0 OBJECTIVE 
T
he mission of the Indian Health Service (IHS) is to raise the physical, mental, social, and spiritual health 
of American Indians and Alaska Natives to the highest level. As part of this mission, the IHS is 
committed to ensuring the safety and security of its patients, staff, and facilities while providing high-
quality healthcare services across its regions. 
To support this mission, the purpose of this contract is to design, furnish, install, and maintain Homeland 
Security Presidential Directive 12 (HSPD-12) compliant Physical Access Control Systems (PACS) and 
video surveillance systems and alarms in Indian Health Service facilities located throughout the Great 
Plains and Billings Area, including North Dakota and South Dakota. These systems will enhance the 
protection of federal facilities, patients, staff, and property through compliance with HSPD-12, Federal 
Information Processing Standard (FIPS) 201-3, and all applicable federal security and privacy regulations. 
The implementation of these systems will ensure standardized, secure, and efficient access control for all 
I
HS facilities, promote accountability, and safeguard critical federal healthcare infrastructure. By 
integrating advanced physical security technologies, the IHS will continue to uphold its mission of 

providing safe and secure environments where quality healthcare can be delivered to the Native 
communities it serves. 
• All systems must comply with HSPD-12 and FIPS 201-3 Personal Identity Verification (PIV) 
standards.  
• Physical Access Control (PACS) must come from the GSA Approved Products List under the 
13.01 Topology 
• Maintain fully functional, continuously operating door access and video surveillance systems. 
• Provide secure, auditable, and centrally managed access to protected facilities. 
• Integrate panic devices and intrusion detection systems 
• Minimize system downtime and security vulnerabilities through proactive service and 
maintenance. 
 
3.0 SCOPE OF WORK 
 
This Performance Work Statement (PWS) defines the requirements for the installation, configuration, 
integration, service, and ongoing maintenance of security camera systems, intrusion alarms and Lenel 
door access control systems in accordance with Homeland Security Presidential Directive 12 (HSPD-12) 
and Federal Information Processing Standard (FIPS) 201-3. The contractor shall provide all personnel, 
equipment, tools, materials, supervision, and services necessary to ensure continuous operation and 
compliance of physical security systems. The contractor that is awarded this contract must be 
certified or have a certified sub-contractor in the LenelS2 OnGuard™ software applications and 
hardware installation/maintenance. The Government must retain rights to all associated   data, 
hardware and software and have full access to all elements of the video surveillance and physical access 
systems. At no point can the Government be locked out of the system. The contractor will be required to 
provide a full plan for annual licensing, repairs and annual service/maintenance.   
The existing security infrastructure before this IDIQ award includes Recording Servers, Access Panels, 
Lock Power Supply, Cameras, Card Readers, Electrical Strikes, Exit Door Push Buttons, Panic Buttons, 
integration with alarm systems, and Door Monitor Switches at the Service Unit Pharmacy Locations.  
The current software utilized for Surveillance management is Milestone Systems XProtect Corporate. The 
current software utilized for Access Control is OnGuard and Lenel. 
Existing Hardware Estimates (these are minimums): Brand Name or Equal 
Door Readers – 535 ea 
Door Reader Modules – 225 ea 
Lenel Controllers – 56 ea 
HSPD12 PAM Modules – 80 ea 
Interior IP Cameras appx – 800 ea 
Exterior IP Cameras appx - 120 ea 
Virtual Servers – 30 ea 
Panic Buttons - 80 ea 
Intercom master door stations – 15 with 36 Doors 
The Recording Servers currently in place are virtual servers with Windows 2022. During the base +4 
option years of this contract, there will be a Windows OS Server upgrade that the vendor will be expected 
to perform.  In addition, the vendor will be responsible for ensuring that the servers remain up and fully 

patched/maintained throughout the life of this contract.  This includes (but is not limited to) adequate 
partitions configured for system growth, system updates and maintenance.  
This performance-based methodology requires the contractor, as part of its proposal, to furnish the 
government with a Performance Work Statement (PWS) that defines how the contractor proposes to 
accomplish the work. The contractor shall also furnish standards that demonstrate the accomplishment of 
the work as proposed. 
4.0 TYPE OF ORDER 
 
The anticipated contract type is Firm-Fixed-Price, Indefinite-Delivery/Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) with an 
estimated five-year ordering period. This will be a Non-Personal Service Type, Commercial Item, 
Purchase Order to design, furnish, install, and maintain Homeland Security Presidential Directive 12 
(HSPD-12) compliant Physical Access Control Systems (PACS) and video surveillance systems and 
alarms in Indian Health Service facilities located throughout the Great Plains and Billings Area, including 
North Dakota and South Dakota. 
 
5.0 ANTICIPATED PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE 
 
Period of Performance: 5-year ordering period (IDIQ) 
 
6.0 PLACE OF PERFORMANCE 
 
All work shall be performed at the designated federal facilities, as listed in the contract. A table of 
currently supported facilities is included in the PWS. The list is subject to change upon mutual agreement 
of the Government and the Vendor.  Some remote diagnostics and updates may be conducted offsite.

8.0 PAYMENT 
I
nvoices submitted under any award will be required to utilize the Invoice Processing Platform (IPP) in 
accordance with HHSAR 352.232-71, Electronic Submission and Processing of Payment Requests”.  
P
ayment will be made upon receipt of a complete and accurate invoice, and successful completion of an 
acceptance inspection in accordance with the Prompt Payment Act. Invoices shall be submitted with all 
information and supporting documentation. A complete and accurate invoice is substantially correct in 
that all aspects of the required information are clearly evident on the invoice and submitted through the

Important notice: 
It should be clearly understood that this Sources Sought notice is not an award or commitment by the

1. Purpose and Objective

The US Government (Caspian Team at UP) is seeking innovative commercial solutions to manage, standardize, and validate high-volume data streams. The primary objective is to maintain the integrity of the SchemaOne data standard while leveraging automation and dedicated 24/7/365 on-call technical expertise to accelerate the ingestion of time-series logs and cyber threat intelligence (CTI).

2. The Problem

Currently, the Government faces challenges in maintaining consistency across diverse, voluminous datasets that flow at all hours. As data sources evolve, the manual effort required to map and validate data creates bottlenecks. Furthermore, out-of-cycle data breaks and schema drifts occur outside of standard business hours, leading to data loss or corruption. We require a partner who can eliminate configuration drift and data acquisition irregularities via a solution that includes 24/7/365 operational monitoring and immediate on-call remediation to ensure the reliability of mission-critical data.

3. Desired Outcomes & Technical Requirements

The Government is looking for vendors to demonstrate capabilities in the following four pillars:

Lifecycle Leadership & Governance: Provide end-to-end management of the SchemaOne standard. This includes maintaining the framework and facilitating stakeholder alignment through the CCB. Vendors must provide a 24/7/365 on-call support structure capable of addressing critical schema failures or ingestion blockers in real-time.

Intelligent Data Mapping: Deliver a scalable solution to map ingested datasets to the SchemaOne specification. The solution must ensure absolute consistency in field names and formats across disparate sources.

High-Fidelity Transformation: Provide a robust mechanism to transform raw source data into SchemaOne-compliant formats with minimal latency and high-availability (HA) failover.

Continuous Validation & 24/7 Health Monitoring: Implement a solution to continuously validate ingested data. This system must proactively detect irregularities and trigger automated alerts to on-call personnel, ensuring that configuration drift is corrected immediately, regardless of the hour or day.

4. AI Enhancement & Efficiency Criteria

A key differentiator for proposed solutions will be the integration of AI to drive operational efficiencies and support on-call responders. The Government expects the vendor to demonstrate how AI/ML will:

Augment On-Call Responsiveness: Use AI-driven diagnostics to provide on-call engineers with instant root-cause analysis for data failures.

Reduce Time-to-Field: Accelerate the transition of new datasets into production.

Minimize Error & Fatigue: Use automated reasoning to reduce the volume of "false positive" alerts, ensuring that 24/7 on-call resources are focused on genuine mission-critical issues.

Rev.: 10/2025 
NATIONAL AERONAUTICS AND SPACE ADMINISTRATION 
MARSHALL SPACE FLIGHT CENTER 
JUSTIFICATION FOR OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION 
(JOFOC) 
For SCALABLE SCIENCE DATA EXPLORATION 
80MSFC23CA017 
 
1. Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 6.104-1(a)(1) – Identification of the agency and 
the contracting activity, and specific identification of the document as a “Justification 
for other than full and open competition.” 
 
 This document is a justification for other than full and open competition prepared by 
National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) /George C. Marshall Space Flight 
Center (MSFC). 
  
The procuring agency is NASA, and the contracting activity is MSFC. 
 
2. FAR 6.104-1(a)(2) – The nature and/or description of the action being approved: 
 
This justification supports the award of a sole-source extension to Contract 
80MSFC23CA017 with Element 84 to continue performance under the Scalable Science 
Data Exploration effort. The extension will add three months to the current period of 
performance, establishing a new end date of June 30, 2026, with an additional one-month 
option period through July 31, 2026, if required. 
 
3. FAR 6.104-1(a)(3) – A description of the supplies or services required, to meet the 
Agency’s needs (including the estimated value): 
 
NASA/MSFC requires continued development of tools, services, and platforms for scalable 
visualization, exploration, and analysis of Earth science data in a commercial cloud 
environment. The effort focuses on evolving current capabilities to enable interactive 
visualization and exploration of large datasets through innovative, cloud-native solutions. 
The contractor shall: 
 
x Develop open-source tools for ingesting and cataloging selected science datasets into the 
cloud. 
x Develop cloud-native services for indexing and dynamic scaling based on demand. 
x Develop cloud-native search, discovery, and distribution services to deliver Earth 
observation data for visualization and geospatial analysis. 
 
These capabilities directly support NASA’s Earth Science Division within the Science 
Mission Directorate and are essential for meeting mission objectives 
 
The estimated period of performance associated with this action is April 1, 2026 through July 
31, 2026 for the 3-month extension plus the 1-month option period. The overall contract 

2 
Rev.:10/2025 
period of performance will be extended, and the total estimated dollar value is $430,000.00 
for the 3-month extension and option period. The current contract value would increase from 
$2,381,703 to $2,811,703 for the 3-month extension and option.  The overall period of 
performance is from July 29, 2023 through July 31, 2026.   
 
4. FAR 6.104-1(a)(4) – An identification of the statutory authority permitting other than 
full and open competition: 
 
The statutory authority permitting other than full and open competition is 10 U.S.C. 
3204(a)(1), as implemented by FAR 6.302-1, Only one responsible source and no other 
supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. 
 
5. FAR 6.104-1(a)(5) – A demonstration that the proposed contractor’s unique 
qualifications or the nature of the acquisition requires use of the authority cited:  
 
The rationale supporting the use of 10 U.S.C 3204(a)1, which is only one responsible source, 
and no other supplies and services will satisfy agency requirements, as described below. 
The primary justification for this sole-source extension is the alignment with NASA’s 
acquisition strategy and the imminent transition to the Next Generation Scalable Data 
Engineering, Operations, and Informatics Support for Open Science (Next Gen) contract. The 
Next Gen acquisition, which is being conducted under full and open competition, is 
scheduled to begin its phase-in on April 30, 2026. Attempting to award a new, standalone 
contract at this time would be impractical and contrary to the Government’s best interest for 
the following reasons: 
x Ensuring Continuity of Operations During Transition 
The current effort directly supports mission-critical Earth Science data visualization and 
exploration capabilities. Disrupting this work by introducing a new contractor would 
jeopardize continuity during the transition period, creating operational risk and potential 
delays in meeting stakeholder requirements. 
x Time Constraints and Integration Risks 
The extension period is limited to three months, with an optional one-month contingency. 
Any new contractor would require significant time to gain sufficient understanding of the 
existing infrastructure and deliverables. This timeline is incompatible with the short-term 
nature of the extension and the scheduled phase-in of Next Gen. 
While Element 84’s unique technical expertise and familiarity with the existing system 
reinforce this determination, the overriding factor is that the Government has already 
committed to a competitive follow-on acquisition. Maintaining Element 84 for this brief 
extension ensures a seamless transition, minimizes risk, and upholds the Government’s 
acquisition strategy. 
 
6. FAR 6.104-1(a)(6) – A description of the efforts made to ensure that offers are solicited 
from as many potential sources as practicable, including whether a notice was or will be 
publicized as required by part 5 and, if not, which exception under part 5 applies: 

3 
Rev.:10/2025 
A notice to the Government Point of Entry (GPE) website (Sam.gov) was published January 
13, 2026 through January 28, 2026, in accordance with FAR part 5. This posting informed 
potential sources of NASA’s intent to award this sole-source contract extension to Element 
84. The results of this synopsis are summarized in Section 10 below. 
 
7.  FAR 6.104-1(a)(7) – A determination by the contracting officer that the anticipated cost 
to the Government will be fair and reasonable: 
 
The Contracting Officer’s signatu re on this document indicates that the Contracting Officer 
has determined that the anticipated cost to th e Government will be fair and reasonable. The 
Contractor shall be required to submit a proposal to be evaluated and negotiated by the 
Government. Prior to execution of the contract ual instrument, a proposal analysis will be 
performed. The proposal analysis will ensure that  the final agreed-to pr ice for the contract 
action is fair and reasonable. 
 
The Contracting Officer will assess the Contractor’s proposal utilizing cost and price analysis 
techniques in accordance with the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 15.404-1 to 
determine a fair and reasonable price. 
 
8. FAR 6.104-1(a)(8) – Description of the market research conducted, and the results, or a 
statement of the reason market research was not conducted (e.g., urgent, and 
compelling requirement): 
 
A SAM.gov market survey was not conducted for the proposed acquisition due to the 
complex nature of the requirements and the urgent need to execute the action in a very short 
timeframe. The requirements of the current Element 84 contract for this extension are 
presently under full and open competition with the Next Gen activity. Due to the anticipated 
phase-in of the follow-on Next Gen competitive acquisition beginning April 30, 2026, an 
attempt to award another new, standalone contract at this time is not practical nor in the best 
interest of the government.  
 
However, in addition to the synopsis notice posted on January 13, 2026, and in accordance 
with FAR 8.002(a)(2), market research was performed by the mandatory source 
AbilityOne.gov Procurement List with no availability. A review of the Office of Procurement 
Strategic Sourcing Website was performed yielding no solutions. Other sources were 
reviewed such as geospatial data science contracts via GSA eLibrary, and other Government 
contracts. Additional review of existing NASA contracts, per NFS 1808.004, that provide the 
required services has been conducted and none were suitable for this requirement. 
 
9. FAR 6.104-1(a)(9) – Any other facts supporting the use of other than full and open 
 competition: 
 
None. 
 
10. FAR 6.104-1(a)(10) – A listing of the sources, if any, that expressed an interest in 
writing in the acquisition: 

4 
Rev.:10/2025 
 
A notice of NASA’s intent to award this sole-source action was synopsized on the GPE 
website (Sam.gov) from January 13, 2026 through January 28, 2026, per FAR part 5 (See 
Section 6 above).  This posting informed potential sources of NASA’s intent to award this 
sole-source extension to Element 84.  One interested company responded to the posting and 
requested consideration. 
 
11. FAR 6.104-1(a)(11) – A statement of actions, if any, the agency may take to remove or 
overcome any barriers to competition before any subsequent acquisition for the 
supplies or services required: 
 
We are actively removing barriers to competition by having a full and open competition for 
the Next Gen follow-on contract, and this requirement will continue to be competed into the 
future.  The Agency will continue to examine the market in the future for alternative 
solutions or new sources before executing any subsequent acquisitions for the same 
requirements.

Responses due 22 April 2026, by 4:00 PM Eastern Time (ET).
This Request for Information (RFI) from the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency 
(DARPA)’s Tactical Technology Office (TTO) seeks to gain understanding of the U.S. 
industry and supplier base that could support rapid manufacturing of less expensive counter-
air capabilities at greater scale.
Responses to this RFI will be used to inform DARPA TTO programs on emerging 
technologies and suppliers that could aid in developing producible weapons at notably higher 
volumes and speeds much more affordably.
Intellectual or other privileged or proprietary information contained in responses to this RFI 
will not be distributed outside of the U.S. Government. In the event that a new DARPA 
program is developed in response to this RFI and a solicitation is issued, no intellectual or 
other proprietary information received in response to this RFI will be divulged to agencies 
outside the U.S. Government.
BACKGROUND:
To accelerate current weapons development timelines, DARPA is considering an 
alternative development paradigm to increase the nation’s magazine depth and breadth. 
Rather than starting with complex, high-end systems that are typically large, expensive, 
exquisite, and few, a new approach prioritizes design for manufacturing at speed and 
scale. The goal is to produce large quantities of capabilities that are smaller, smarter, and 
significantly more affordable—designed for high-volume manufacturing. 
DESCRIPTION:
This RFI seeks information on counter-air weapon system integrators with the capability 
to conduct state-of-the-art design iteration, rapid prototyping, and manufacturing of missiles, 
leveraging readily available parts and various subsystems. The weapon may be carried by 
airborne platforms or may be delivered across domains, as is the case with some existing 
counter-air capabilities. This RFI will also be used to identify industry partner capability for 
fully developing, integrating, and testing a counter-air prototype weapon that can be 
manufactured rapidly at scale.

 Responses must address all of the following technical areas:
1. Capability to conduct integrated effector design, manufacturing, and test as well 
as effector performance and engagement analysis.  The integrator will be 
responsible for overall weapon prototype development through rapid design and 
test iteration and must substantiate the traceability of the design to rapid weapons 
manufacturing approaches.
2. Capability to conduct cost and manufacturing planning and analysis for a 
productionized version of a designed-for-manufacturing prototype weapon.
3. Capability to develop missile models to be provided to third parties for 
operational analysis.

submissions become Government property and will not be returned. Marketing brochures and/or generic 
company literature will not be considered and shall not be sent in response to this RFI. 
Purpose of RFI 
IBC’s Human Resources Directorate seeks information from industry on AI tools and applications capable of 
securely supporting a mainframe-centric, payroll-focused, PII-regulated environment across the full systems 
software development lifecycle and operational landscape. HRD maintains and enhances an integrated 
personnel and payroll system, along with multiple supporting subsystems, that interface with numerous 
Federal systems and serve more than 300,000 employees across multiple agencies and commissions. 
HRD is seeking solutions that can automate testing (script, unit, regression, load, performance), strengthen 
batch processing and JCL scripting/job-run comparisons, and support comprehensive database management 
(configuration, capacity and space utilization, security recognition, forecasting and drift detection, patching, 
migrations, conversions, and integrity). HRD also requires capabilities tailored to payroll operations, 
including payroll calculations, retroactive processing, W-2 and ACA processing, annual pay adjustments, and 
file generation and transmission. 
Additional areas of interest include AI-enabled code and infrastructure analysis and refactoring (mainframe 
module assessment, call-routine mapping, bug identification, historical change analysis, and LLM-based 
scanning), automated generation of system documentation, training materials, and analytical reports, and 
customer service workflow automation (ticket creation and routing, self-service tools, legal and payroll 
guidance). Solutions must support cross-platform integration with Federal partners such as OPM, IRS, and 
shared service providers; operate in a non-multi-tenant environment; align with FedRAMP controls; meet 

 
 
 
2 
 
 
Section 508 requirements; and provide governance, auditability, scalability, and deployment options suitable 
for IBC HRD. 
Responses to this RFI will help HRD identify viable industry solutions and vendors capable of meeting these 
mission needs and will inform the development of future procurement strategies. 
Background: IBC as a Shared Services Provider 
IBC is an Office of Personnel Management (OPM) authorized Shared Service Provider (SSP) that provides 
systems and services to its parent, DOI, and 54 other federal agencies (customers). HRD fully maintains and 
enhances its integrated personnel/payroll system and its supporting sub systems. HRD’s integrated personnel 
and payroll system and sub systems interface with several Government computer systems which service more 
than 300,000 employees (customers) from numerous Federal agencies and commissions.  
 
The operational environment includes: 
 
• Large-scale mainframe and batch processing ecosystems 
• Mission-critical payroll and personnel systems containing Personally Identifiable Information (PII) 
• Extensive JCL, ADBAS, batch scheduling, and interface dependencies 
 
These sub systems complement HRD’s integrated mainframe personnel/payroll system in various ways to 
include: 
• Payroll/personnel data warehousing 
• Service management ticketing  
• Timekeeping and attendance 
• Workforce tracking 
• Learning, development, and performance management 
• Planning, hiring, tracking 
 
Our systems provide thorough support throughout the entire development and maintenance life cycle. This 
includes the creation and implementation of methodologies and standards, in-depth requirements analysis, and 
comprehensive business process evaluation. Additionally, we conduct extensive technology research, manage 
communications effectively, and design robust system architecture. Our expertise extends to system 
development and maintenance, software development, application re-hosting, and the conversion of legacy 
systems. By integrating these diverse elements, we ensure that our solutions are both innovative and reliable, 
while meeting the highest standards of quality and performance. 
 
Objectives 
  
IBC-HRD is seeking a Vendor who provides an AI-Tool or Application which will compliment HRD systems 
in their ability to:  
 
• Automate and Produce 
o Script test software 
o Unit test software 
o Regression test 
o Load test 
o Performance test 
o Batch processing capabilities 
o Database configuration – preserving integrity and infrastructures

o Database space utilization 
o Database security recognition 
o Patch upgrades 
o New client migrations   
 
• Online/Production – Automated job run and compares 
o QA (Quality Assurance) processing and testing 
o Production script case – data input 
o W2s 
o Annual pay raise implementation 
o ACA (Affordable Care Act) processing 
o Software version release cadence 
o File creation, generation. Transmission (internal and external) 
o Payroll calculation and retroactive processing  
o Workflow generation 
 
• Assess Production and Test Databases  
o Conversions of software 
o Data transfer and conversion 
o Integration 
o Database performance 
o Capacity 
o Usage logs 
o Security 
o JCL scripting  
 
• Analyze code and infrastructures 
o Ability to scan various LLMs (large language models) in its entirety 
o Mainframe 
o Refactoring code 
o Module assessment 
o Call routines  
o Bug fixes 
o Historical pinpoints of software modifications 
o Mapping 
 
• Create system documentation and training materials 
 
• Generate data analysis reports among systems 
 
• Customer Service Ticket Generation 
o Situational customer ticket creation  
o Assigning of ticket to corresponding branch or working group 
o Associated and relevant resources applicable for usage with ticket generation 
 Legal documents 
 Payroll or personnel guides 
o Job aids 
o Bots 
 
• Self Help Feature 
o Situational customer inquiry for payroll or personnel processing 

 
 
 
4 
 
 
o Associated and relevant resources applicable for payroll or personnel processing 
o Bots  
 
• Cross platform compatibility 
o Assess HRD’s systems and ability to work in partnership supporting HRD functions 
o Integrate with non HRD systems and Federal Agency partnering

STATEMENT OF WORK

1. INTRODUCTION: Architect-Engineer (A-E) services are required to provide project planning, site investigation; complete detailed designs for maintenance, repair, alteration, and new construction projects; and construction management, including submittal reviews. These projects will require multi-disciplinary planning, designing and engineering service for institutional, commercial and industrial type facilities, including architectural, structural, civil, mechanical, electrical, environmental, and real property services.

2. SCOPE: The Architect-Engineer (A-E) shall provide to the Government Title I (A & B) and/or Title II (C) Services.

a. Work shall include field survey; site and facility investigation; preparation of special technical studies; analyses of structural systems; feasibility and concept studies; material investigation and color studies; preparation of architectural engineering studies and/or investigation and preparation of architectural and engineering documents and reports for architectural projects with associated structural, civil, landscaping, mechanical, electrical, environmental, real property, subsurface soil investigations and incidental work; preparation of design documents to include building and ground alteration, maintenance, repair and minor construction; cost and schedule estimates; and monitoring and evaluating the construction progress for conformance to plans and specifications including review of required submittals by the contractor. This indefinite delivery indefinite quantity (ID/IQ) contract will be for one basic period with four option periods, at the discretion of the Government. The cumulative amount of all delivery orders will not exceed $10,000,000 per year and individual delivery orders will not exceed $1,500,000. Delivery Orders over $1,000,000 require Congressional Notification.

b. Applicable Standards, Manuals, and Pamphlets: The A-E shall design this project in accordance with Local, State, National, and DOD standards which apply, including but not limited to: UFC, NFPA, NFC, ANSI, OSHA, ASTM, NEC, ICC, etc.

c. Construction Time: The A-E shall provide a recommended construction performance period for the complete project. Recommendations will be based on the designer’s experience, knowledge of the industry, local market forces, weather conditions and availability of resources. Specific references shall be made to equipment/material items that may have a long lead time, and could pose a problem to the performance period.

3. STATEMENT OF SERVICES: The A-E shall perform all or part of the following services as more specifically identified in each delivery order.

a. Title I (Type “A” Services). These services involve field investigations and surveys (topographic, geotechnical, etc.); similar fact finding surveys of the site essential to proper design; prepare reports and similar services not involved in the preparation of designs, plans, drawings, and specifications. These services may also include environmental compliance documentation (e.g., NEPA), endangered species surveys, wetland delineations, hazardous material surveys, real property record searches, and land use analyses.

b. Title I (Type “B” Services). These services include those items normally furnished by an A-E in the actual preparation of the design documents (plans, drawings, estimates, specifications, submittal register etc.) and include visual inspection of the site or facility for familiarization with scope, general conditions, and coordination with using activities. This can also include environmental mitigation design and real property asset integration.

c. Title II (Type “C” Services). Those items involving inspecting, monitoring, and evaluating construction activities to validate conformance to plans and specifications, including reviewing, evaluating and testing product submittals and shop drawing; and preparation of construction contract modifications.

4. ARCHITECT-ENGINEERING SERVICES:

a. Title I (Type “A” Services). The A-E shall perform all work required to investigate existing conditions. This work include field investigations and surveys (topographic, geotechnical, chemical, site utilities, existing mechanical etc.) and similar fact finding surveys of the site in order to provide reports of existing conditions on which to base proper design; and similar services not involved in the preparation of designs, plans, drawings, and specifications. This may also include the preparation of environmental assessments (EAs), environmental impact statements (EISs), cultural and natural resource surveys, real property inventories, and site selection studies.

b. Title I (Type “B”) Services: The A-E Title I Type “B” services include those items normally furnished by an A-E in the actual preparation of the design documents (plans, drawings, estimates, specifications, submittal register, Comprehensive Interior Design, etc.) The A-E shall perform all work required to produce documents describing the work required to accomplish the intent of the project as specifically identified in each Delivery Order. Unless otherwise specifically provided therein, the A-E shall perform these services as follows.
1) Field Survey and Investigation: The A-E shall visually inspect the site and/or facility for familiarization with the scope of work and general conditions of the facility; coordinate with the using activities to obtain their operational activities for the development of functional relationships and detailed requirements. The A-E shall visit the project site for investigation of the existing physical conditions and to ensure the accuracy of the drawings, as available, furnished to the A-E by the Government.
2) Cost Estimates: The A-E shall design each project to provide a complete and usable facility within a given target construction cost provided by the Government. The target construction cost will be provided to the contractor in our requests for proposal and on the executed contractual document, the Standard Form 252.  The A-E’s cost estimates shall be based on labor and material prices prevailing in the project’s locality.  Cost estimate shall be descriptive, detailed, and includes all operations of work required including quantities and unit costs.  Additionally, the construction cost estimate shall include Government Furnished Equipment (GFE) and contractor furnished equipment when applicable.  The A-E cost estimate shall summarize all cost by material, labor, other direct costs, overhead, profit, and bonding costs. Cost estimates shall be prepared on an electronic version of the AF Form 3052 provided by the Government or pre-approved A-E’s equivalent electronic spreadsheet that provides the information specified above.
3) Project Costs: The A-E shall be required to conduct the field survey and investigations, prepare the preliminary drawings, data, reports, etc., and design the full scope of the work as outlined above and as agreed upon during review of study data and recommendations. If the estimated costs exceeds the amount indicated on the project description sheets for each project (based on current anticipated scope and subject to adjustment to approved scope), sufficient alternates to the construction contract should be determined at the time of the preliminary review conference to reduce the cost below this amount, if deemed necessary by the Government.

c. Title II (Type “C” Services): Those items involving inspecting, monitoring, and evaluating construction activities to validate conformance to plans and specifications. These services include reviewing, evaluating and testing product submittals and shop drawing and preparation of construction contract modifications.

d. Applicable Standards, Manuals, and Pamphlets: The A-E shall prepare all design documents in conformance with the applicable portions of the following:
1) Unified Facilities Criteria (UFC).
2) Applicable Air Force Policy Directives, Instructions, Pamphlets, Manuals, Technical Data Bulletins, Engineering Technical Letters and other documents.
3) Current state and national codes, regulations, and specifications involving architectural, civil, electrical, environmental, real property, and mechanical disciplines associated with the design and construction of each project as referenced by UFC.
Reference sources are available upon request by either websites or government furnished.

e. Guide Specification: The A-E shall use U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Unified Facilities Guide Specifications (UFGS), Construction Specification Institute (CSI) or American Institute of Architects (AIA) guide specifications (edited) as the basis for producing specifications under this contract.  The specifications shall be tailored to suit the specific work requirements of the individual items contained in the Delivery Order.  Extraneous material that does not apply shall be deleted.  While the A-E should cover relevant items in full scope to assure quality construction and compliance, the use of notes on the drawings either to accentuate important items in the specifications, or to take the place of lengthy written specifications for routine or simple items is encouraged.  Entire specifications for simple projects of low monetary value may be by notes on the drawings.  The A-E is permitted to use specific manufacturer’s part or model numbers to describe a specified item, however, in all such cases, at least two other approved manufacturer’s part or model numbers shall be specified or an “or equal” statement shall be included unless the government wishes to sole source an item. If sole source is required the government will provide the appropriate justification for that specific sole source.


f. Economic Studies: In preparing designs the A-E shall make a comparative cost analysis to justify the selection of type and source of utilities, major items of equipment, building components, materials, method of construction, siting, plumbing, lighting, heating, air conditioning, building configuration, electrical systems, column spacing, roads, story heights, structural system, and selection of interior and exterior finishes.  The analysis will include cost of operation and maintenance over the expected life of the project.  This cost analysis shall include consideration of the life cycle cost of the facility.  Major decisions shall be documented in the design analysis.

g. Simplified Design: The use of simplified design techniques is encouraged in routine, simple projects and/or those of low monetary values.

5. PHASES OF COMPLETION: Unless specifically defined otherwise in the Delivery Order, the A-E shall accomplish the design of a project in phases which consist of the following:

a. Phase I

1)  Survey of existing facilities.

2)  Study of requirements.

3)  Conceptual Floor Plans and Elevations

During Phase I, the A-E shall conduct a survey investigation and study based on broad guidance furnished herein, and as may be supplemented by other Government-furnished material, will determine the recommended scope, materials, quantities, etc., and proceed to Phase II.  Conferences or site visits will be conducted (if required).

b. Phase II for accomplishing design work:

1)  35% Drawings (half size)

2)  35% Specifications

3)  35% Cost Estimate

4)  Design Analysis

5)  Conference at the Contracting Office (unless specifically omitted)

and/or

6)  65% Drawings (half size)

7)  65% Specifications

8)  65% Cost Estimate

9) Design Analysis

10) Conference at the Contracting Office (unless specifically omitted):

c. Phase III Completion of design (unless specifically omitted) shall include all review comments from Phase II:

1)  First Final Drawings (95%) (half size & full size)

2)  First Final Specifications (95%)

3)  First Final Cost Estimate (95%)

4)  First Final Design Analysis (95%)

5) Conference at the Contracting Office (unless specifically omitted)

6) Final documents (100%) as listed below shall be delivered to the office of the Contracting Officer incorporating all review comments from the 95% review.

			(a) Final Drawings (half size &full size)

			(b) Final Specifications

			(c) Final Cost Estimate

			(d) Final Design Analysis

6. GOVERNMENT FURNISHED INFORMATION: The Government, through the office of the Contracting Officer, will furnish within five days after issuance of a contract, applicable data and information (as available) for the execution of the described work.  Data shall be returned to the Contracting Officer upon completion of the individual project.  This data is on file in the Base Civil Engineering (BCE) and may be obtained for review by the A-E during negotiations.  All data from the Government shall be treated with care and is classified as “Controlled Unclassified Information”, unless told otherwise. All data cannot be distributed, retransmitted or reproduced without written permission from the Government.   The data will include where applicable and available:

a. General Site Plan.

b. Small scale layout drawing or sketch showing possible arrangement of space (to serve as a guide).

c. Basic floor plan showing location of project (unless specifically omitted).

d. Existing record drawings as available.

e. Design criteria applicable to required Delivery Order.

f. Special requirements for preparation of drawings, reports, specifications, cost estimates, and design analysis.

g. Government-furnished equipment list, if applicable.

7. CHANNELS FOR OBTAINING INFORMATION: 

a. Except as specified herein, all requests for information necessary for the execution of this work shall be made to the Contracting Officer.

b. The A-E shall, at all times, maintain close liaison with the Contracting Officer and the Base Civil Engineer to assure maximum coordination in accomplishing the work.

c. The A-E shall appoint a Project Engineer or Project Manager for each project to serve as the single point of contact and liaison between the A-E and the Government.  Upon execution of the contract, the A-E shall advise the Contracting Officer in writing of the name of the individual so designated.  The A-E’s Project Manager shall be responsible for the complete coordination of all work required for the project.  (The Project Manager shall be able to respond to government inquires on any project within 24 hours).

d. The A-E shall advise the Contracting Officer of any discrepancies, ambiguities and lack of clarity noted in plans and specifications furnished for use in connection with the project.

e. During the execution of the work under this contract, the A-E shall maintain close liaison with the Contracting Officer and the BCE, or his designated representative.  The BCE will coordinate the work with the users and other agencies.

f. Cost estimates, and computation sheets prepared by the A-E shall be marked “FOR OFFICIAL USE ONLY’.

This recommendation is for the acquisition of supplies or services determined to be reasonably available 
from only one source/only one manufacturer. Competition is impractical for the following reasons (please 
answer the questions below): 
 
1. What are the reasons for soliciting only the suggested source/suggested brand name? Please provide 
the unique characteristics of the items or services along with the supporting rationale and the market 
research performed to substantiate your reason for the suggested source/brand name. 
    
This procurement is to renew licenses that are being used currently by the Advanced Measurements and 
Flow Physics Branch to perform research in support of numerous NASA missions. PowerFLOW 
software is used to simulate unsteady flows over complicated geometries without the requirement for 
extensive and costly grid generation. This software suite includes the capability to rapidly generate 
embedded Cartesian grids with varying resolution. Proprietary technology for near-wall treatment allows 
the use of wall functions instead of resolving the flow all the way to the wall, reducing the grid 
requirement. Furthermore, the unique algorithm is very efficient on modern CPUs and parallelizes 
efficiently to many cores. The PowerFLOW suite also includes complete flow analysis and noise 
prediction codes that are required to fully analyze a configuration. Researchers in the Research 
Directorate (RD) have been running PowerFLOW simulation studies to investigate the aeroacoustic 
performance of the high-lift configuration of the Common Research Model (CRM). PowerFLOW has 
algorithmic advantages that allow meshes to be quickly generated around complicated geometries and 
can perform unsteady simulations with acoustic predictions in a relatively efficient manner. These 
advantages result in a better turnaround of simulations than our other tools, which will allow more 
configurations to be evaluated before the wind tunnel test.  
 
2. What is the impact to the government if another vendor/brand is used? Include any dollar, schedule, 
or compatibility impacts if possible. 
 
Our branch members have developed a level of proficiency using the PowerFLOW software suite which 
results in an efficient workflow. Switching to another brand would result in delays and inefficiencies in 
production. No other product is compatible with PowerFLOW datasets, and Dassault Systems is the only 
entity authorized to sell the software in the United States. The introduction of a new brand of software to 
meet this functional requirement would have repercussions on project timelines, budgets, and staff.

NATIONAL AERONAUTICS AND SPACE ADMINISTRATION 
MARSHALL SPACE FLIGHT CENTER (MSFC) 
JUSTIFICATION FOR OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION 
(JOFOC) 
For NOVEL TECHNOLOGIES TO SUPPORT SCIENCE DATA SYSTEM 
80MSFC22CA004 
 
1. Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 6.104-1(a)(1) – Identification of the agency and the 
contracting activity, and specific identification of the document as a “Justification for 
other than full and open competition.” 
 
 This document is a justification for other than full and open competition prepared by National 
Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) / George C. Marshall Space Flight Center 
(MSFC). 
  
The procuring agency is NASA, and the contracting activity is MSFC. 
 
2. FAR 6.104-1(a)(2) – The nature and/or description of the action being approved: 
 
This justification provides the rationale for contracting by other than full and open competition 
to award an extension to contract number 80MSFC22CA004 with New Rights Group, Inc. dba 
Development Seed (herein referred to as Development Seed). The extension will add three 
months to the current period of performance, establishing a new end date of June 30, 2026, 
with an additional one-month option period through July 31, 2026, if required. 
 
3. FAR 6.104-1(a)(3) – A description of the supplies or services required, to meet the 
Agency’s needs (including the estimated value): 
 
The NASA Interagency Implementation and Advanced Concepts Team (IMPACT) requires 
continued integration of NASA’s specialized Earth science data, services, and tools into 
custom research applications and workflows. These capabilities enable the infusion of 
emerging trends in informatics, data science, and information technology to develop innovative 
solutions for science data management, dissemination, and rapid prototyping of advanced 
concepts in scientific data systems. The work includes addressing challenges related to data 
search, access, and usability. Specifically, the contractor will develop systematic approaches to 
data management and stewardship supporting distributed archive centers, provide system 
architecture analysis for IMPACT, and perform data curation for collaborations within NASA 
and with external partners, including other government agencies, industry, and academia.  
 
Although the present contract includes a 12-month Option Period 4 (October 1, 2025 – 
September 30, 2026), exercising that option is not in the Government’s best interest. Option 
Period 4 contains tasks outside the current scope and does not align with the anticipated 
transition to the Next Gen contract. Therefore, extending Option Period 3 is the most efficient 
and cost-effective solution to maintain uninterrupted support. Pursuant to FAR 6.104-1(a)(3), 
this extension is justified to ensure continuity of services critical to NASA’s Earth science data 

2 
Rev.:10/2025 
integration and advanced concept development. A lapse in performance would result in 
disruption of ongoing system architecture analysis and data stewardship activities, delays in 
collaborative efforts with interagency and international partners, and increased risk to NASA’s 
ability to meet mission objectives for scientific data management and open science initiatives. 
Development Seed is uniquely positioned to provide these services without additional phase-in 
time or risk to schedule. Engaging a new contractor for this short-term extension would 
introduce significant inefficiencies and jeopardize milestone completion. 
 
NASA/MSFC seeks to modify Development Seed’s existing contract, 80MSFC22CA004, to 
extend the period of performance for short-term continuity of service. The estimated period of 
performance associated with this action is from April 1, 2026 through July 31, 2026 for the 3-
month extension plus the 1-month option period. The overall contract period of performance 
will be extended, and the total estimated dollar value is $1,956,000.00 for the 3-month 
extension and option period. The current contract value would increase from $30,755,494.00 to 
$32,711,494.00 for the proposed action. The overall period of performance is from January 1, 
2022 through July 31, 2026. 
 
4. FAR 6.104-1(a)(4) – An identification of the statutory authority permitting other than full 
and open competition: 
 
The statutory authority permitting other than full and open competition is 10 U.S.C. 
3204(a)(1), as implemented by FAR 6.302-1 Only one responsible source and no other 
supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. 
 
5. FAR 6.104-1(a)(5) – A demonstration that the proposed contractor’s unique 
qualifications or the nature of the acquisition requires use of the authority cited:  
 
The rationale supporting the use of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), which is only one responsible source, 
and no other supplies and services will satisfy agency requirements, as described below. 
 
The primary justification for this sole-source extension is the alignment with NASA’s 
acquisition strategy and the imminent transition to the Next Generation Scalable Data 
Engineering, Operations, and Informatics Support for Open Science (Next Gen) contract. 
The Next Gen acquisition, which is being conducted under full and open competition, is 
scheduled to begin its phase-in on April 30, 2026. Attempting to award a new, standalone 
contract at this time would be impractical and contrary to the Government’s best interest for 
the following reasons: 
 
• Ensuring Continuity of Operations During Transition 
Development Seed’s demonstrated capabilities and familiarity with the existing 
cyberinfrastructure enable them to maintain and support the current system without 
interruption, ensuring that IMPACT deliverables and milestones remain on schedule. 
Disrupting this work by introducing a new contractor would jeopardize continuity during the 
transition period, creating operational risk and potential delays in meeting stakeholder 
requirements. 
 

3 
Rev.:10/2025 
 
• Time Constraints and Integration Risks 
The extension period is limited to three months, with an optional one-month contingency. Any 
new contractor would require time to gain an understanding of the existing infrastructure and 
deliverables. This timeline is incompatible with the short-term nature of the extension and the 
scheduled phase-in of Next Gen.  
 
While Development Seed’s technical expertise and knowledge of the existing system reinforce 
this determination, the overriding factor is that the Government has already committed to a 
competitive follow-on acquisition. Maintaining Development Seed for this brief extension 
ensures a seamless transition, minimizes risk, and upholds the Government’s acquisition 
strategy. 
 
6. FAR 6.104-1(a)(6) – A description of the efforts made to ensure that offers are solicited 
from as many potential sources as practicable, including whether a notice was or will be 
publicized as required by part 5 and, if not, which exception under part 5 applies: 
A notice to the Government Point of Entry (GPE) website (Sam.gov) was published January 
13, 2026, through January 28, 2026, in accordance with FAR Part 5. This posting informed 
potential sources of NASA’s intent to award this sole-source extension to Development Seed. 
The results of this synopsis are summarized in Section 10 below. 
 
7.  FAR 6.104-1(a)(7) – A determination by the contracting officer that the anticipated cost to 
the Government will be fair and reasonable: 
 
The contracting officer’s signature on this document indicates that the contracting officer has 
determined that the anticipated cost to the government will be fair and reasonable. The 
contractor shall be required to submit a proposal to be evaluated and negotiated by the 
Government. Prior to execution of the contractual instrument, a proposal analysis will be 
performed. The proposal analysis will ensure that the final agreed-to price for the contract 
action is fair and reasonable. 
 
The Contracting Officer will assess the Contractor’s proposal utilizing cost and price analysis 
techniques in accordance with the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 15.404-1 to 
determine a fair and reasonable price.  
 
8. FAR 6.104-1(a)(8) – Description of the market research conducted, and the results, or a 
statement of the reason market research was not conducted (e.g., urgent, and compelling 
requirement): 
 
A SAM.gov market survey was not conducted for the proposed acquisition. The requirements 
of the current contract are being competed in the currently underway Next Gen acquisition. 
Due to the anticipated phase-in of the follow-on Next Gen competitive acquisition award 
beginning April 30, 2026, an attempt to award another new, standalone contract to bridge the 
gap at this time is neither practical nor in the best interest of the government. 
 

4 
Rev.:10/2025 
However, in accordance with FAR 8.002(a)(2), market research was performed by the 
mandatory source AbilityOne.gov Procurement List with no availability. A review of the 
Office of Procurement Strategic Sourcing Website was performed yielding no solutions. Other 
sources were reviewed such as geospatial data science contracts via GSA eLibrary, and other 
Government contracts. Additional review of existing NASA contracts, per NFS 1808.004, that 
provide the required services has been conducted and none were suitable for this requirement.
 
 
9. FAR 6.104-1(a)(9) – Any other facts supporting the use of other than full and open 
 competition: 
 
None. 
 
10. FAR 6.104-1(a)(10) – A listing of the sources, if any, that expressed an interest in writing 
in the acquisition: 
 
A notice of NASA’s intent to award this sole-source action was synopsized on the GPE 
website (Sam.gov) from January 13, 2026 through January 28, 2026, per FAR part 5 (See 
Section 6 above). This posting informed potential sources of NASA’s intent to award this sole-
source extension to Development Seed. One interested company responded to the posting and 
requested consideration. The response was not deemed credible. 
 
11. FAR 6.104-1(a)(11) – A statement of actions, if any, the agency may take to remove or 
overcome any barriers to competition before any subsequent acquisition for the supplies 
or services required: 
 
The Agency is actively removing barriers to competition by having a full and open competition 
for the Next Gen follow-on contract, and this requirement will continue to be competed into 
the future. We will continue to examine the market in the future for alternative solutions or 
new sources before executing any subsequent acquisitions for the same requirements.

2. Nature and/or description of the action being approved, including a description of 
the supplies or services required to meet the agency’s needs and the estimated 
value. 
a. Acquisition purpose and objectives.  
On August 15, 2025, the NIH Director’s Priorities 
https://www.nih.gov/aboutnih/nih-director/statements/advancing-nihs-mission-
through-unified-strategy were published with specific reference to a Real-World 
Data Platform. The priority states “Real-World Data Platform: NIH is 
establishing a robust and secure national infrastructure to integrate and link 
data from various real-world sources consistent with a deep respect for 
individual privacy rights. This new Real-World Data Platform will provide 
advanced computational analysis resources for investigators across numerous 
research areas, including neurodevelopmental disorders and chronic 
diseases.” Rather than creating a new system, it has been determined to be in 
the best interest of the government to utilize and enhance existing 
infrastructure that exists within N3C and Data COUNTS. 
During this transition phase, the Palantir platform that hosts the N3C was 
abruptly taken offline while HHS determined its acquisitions strategy for 
Palantir software. HHS recently executed a contract with Palantir allowing N3C 
to come back online publicly, reopening March 2, 2026. Based on these 
negotiations, N3C is now hosted within a different cloud provider with a 
different set of features. These changes required NCATS to pivot its focus 
away from the original objectives of integrating N3C and Data COUNTS.  
Federal Supply Schedule (FSS) Sole 
Source Justification (SSJ) 

Page 2 of 13  
The purpose of this acquisition is to provide NCATS and the community of N3C 
contributors and researchers continuity. The abrupt shutdown of the N3C 
platform was highly disruptive to researchers utilizing the N3C to fulfill 
commitments on grants, write their dissertations, and continue working on 
projects built over the past six years.  
The overarching objective of this work has been reduced from fifteen objectives 
to nine. These core objectives of integrating N3C and Data COUNTS, while 
transitioning N3C to a Dynamic Workspaces architecture, ensuring operational 
continuity, enhancing data utility for the research community, and achieving full 
compliance with all CADR requirements. To accomplish this, NCATS has 
identified objectives across nine workstreams that will need to be run by the 
Awardee. Therefore, objectives are written in alignment with the workstreams: 
Program Strategy, Governance, and Leadership: This objective provides for 
expert leadership and strategic consultation to NCATS during the bridge 
period. The work will focus on supporting NCATS in ideation, strategy, and 
planning for the future-state platform and the successful transition to a new 
vendor. This includes developing strategic roadmaps, advising on the technical 
and governance requirements for the platform recompete, and leading 
community and stakeholder engagement to manage expectations and ensure 
alignment with the new program direction. 
Modular Application Development: This objective involves the design, 
development, testing, and documentation of a set of modular, platform-agnostic 
web applications. This work is focused on creating standalone user-facing tools 
for core N3C services, including applications for registration and data access 
management, a concept set explorer, and a phenotype builder. These 
components will be built as portable, flexible applications, designed to be 
deployed on any future platform and to address CADR security and access 
control requirements. 
Platform-Agnostic Data Infrastructure: This objective focuses on the 
operations and maintenance of platform-agnostic data infrastructure. This work 
represents the comprehensive oversite of the data lifecycle, intended to be a 
portable, efficient, and well-documented service. This includes engineering 
data acquisition, data quality, linkage, and OMOP harmonization pipelines. 
Scientific and Technical Research and Support: To showcase the power of 
the N3C model, a team of Real World Evidence (RWE) Subject Matter Experts 
(SMEs) is needed to create high-caliber studies, tools, and resources. This 
objective includes providing these scientific services and supporting other high-
impact special projects that leverage the unique capabilities of the N3C 
platform. 
N3C Education and Training: Rebuilding and advancing N3C Education to 
support the evolving needs of the research community as the program 
transitions to a new platform and Dynamic Workspace model. It includes 
providing pedagogical leadership, recovering and redesigning legacy training 
materials, and developing a scalable, platform-agnostic education 
infrastructure. Core activities involve creating new registration processes, 
training tools, and a synthetic dataset; integrating updated resources such as 

Page 3 of 13  
data visualization and phenotype tools; and implementing modern content and 
learning management systems. The effort ensures that educational materials 
and training programs remain aligned with NCATS priorities, are easily 
accessible, and effectively equip users to leverage the new N3C environment.  
Enhance Capabilities of the Data COUNTS Initiative: In partnership with 
data contributing healthcare organizations, enhance the current capabilities of 
the Data COUNTS initiative to facilitate delivery of EHR data to NIH.  
Enhance Coordination of the Data COUNTS Ecosystem: Provide 
coordination and engagement of the Data COUNTS partner health institutions 
with NIH. 
Facilitate Prize Competitions: Facilitating prize competitions require a group 
of SMEs to be able to manage, evaluate, and give recommendations on 
targeted public health questions that require a high level of methodological 
rigor to answer. 
 
b. Project background.  
The National Institutes of Health (NIH) is the Nation's leading Medical Research 
Agency and the primary Federal Agency whose mission is to seek fundamental 
knowledge about the nature and behavior of living systems and apply that 
knowledge to enhance health, lengthen life, and reduce illness and disability by 
supporting and making medical discoveries. The National Center for Advancing 
Translational Science (NCATS) at the NIH focuses on all aspects of the translation 
of research with an innovative pipeline of treatment discoveries for all diseases. 
NCATS' mission is to improve health through smarter science that results in more 
treatments for all people more quickly.  
 
The National Clinical Cohort Collaborative (N3C) began as a collaborative vision 
for a national data resource that turned real-world evidence into the knowledge 
urgently needed to address the pandemic. It systematically collected data derived 
from electronic health records (EHRs) and other important repositories from 
different institutions and harmonized these data in a centralized resource available 
for collaborative research. The program has since expanded beyond its initial 
narrow focus to be a resource ready to leverage real world evidence based data to 
answer questions about any disease. 
 
Building upon this successful foundation, N3C has transitioned to be composed of 
a set of robust, scalable, and secure platform-agnostic components and data 
infrastructure. These include portable data pipelines, reusable knowledge objects 
(such as phenotypes and concept sets), and modular web applications (such as for 
data access management). This approach ensures all components are designed 
for compliance with stringent government requirements for Controlled-Access Data 
Repositories (CADR). This work also focuses on preserving the core principles of 
centralized data harmonization and a secure analytical environment while 
supporting capabilities that grant institutions granular control over the use of their 
data. 
 
The Data COUNTS initiative serves as a foundational EHR data collection engine 
that ensures full provenance, traceability, and minimal data loss from health 

Page 4 of 13  
systems. Data COUNTS provides federated collection of EHR and other clinical 
data, as well as data and transmission architecture based on open-industry data 
and interoperability standards. It supports a broad array of use cases across HHS 
with appropriate adherence to data privacy, security, and data access policies. 
Together with the Data Collect Once Use Numerous TimeS (COUNTS) Initiative, 
N3C forms the foundational infrastructure of the NIH wide real-world evidence-
based research. The infrastructure will integrate vast amounts of real-world data 
from EHRs, insurance claims, pharmacies, and other sources. Building on prior 
NIH-funded efforts, the combined N3C and Data COUNTS efforts will eliminate 
redundancies from data collection, linkage, and analysis infrastructures, and will 
dramatically reduce administrative overhead by relying on a unified set of data use 
and governance agreements. It will provide direct access to advanced 
computational resources to support cutting-edge artificial intelligence/machine 
learning (AI/ML) modeling, petabyte-scale storage/compute, and high-throughput 
analytics. 
In FY 2024 the scientific and technical support services for the N3C and Data 
COUNTS were procured together on GS35F023GA-75N95023A00001 BO 14 
National Clinical Data Collaborative COUNTS (NacDacC). Procuring these 
services through one vendor on one task order has allowed the NCATS and 
ODSS to begin working together and creating efficiencies across N3C and Data 
COUNTS. In FY 2025 a 6-month sole source logical follow-on contract (GS-35F-
023GA/75N95025F00079) was awarded under FAR Subpart 8.405-6(a)(1)(i)(C). 
By continuing under one unified task, NCATS and ODSS could economically and 
efficiently make changes to the N3C and Data COUNTS programs to allow them 
to fulfil the vision of the NIH Director’s Real- World Data Platform priority.  
During this transition phase, the Palantir platform that hosts the N3C was 
abruptly taken offline while HHS determined its acquisitions strategy for Palantir 
software. HHS recently executed a contract with Palantir allowing N3C to come 
back online publicly, reopening March 2, 2026. Based on these negotiations, 
N3C is now hosted within a different cloud provider with a different set of 
features. These changes required NCATS to pivot its focus away from the 
original objectives of integrating N3C and Data COUNTS. A sole-source award to 
the existing vendor through the same GSA contract is needed to allow time to 
accomplish the initial integration objectives while also rebuilding N3C based on 
HHS’s new requirements for Palantir environments. Competing the requirement 
now would add unacceptable additional cost, delay, complexity, or uncertainty of 
execution.

b. Project description.
