SBU - CONTRACTING AND ACQUISITIONS 
U.S. DEPARTMENT OF STATE 
Enterprise Physical Security Information Management (PSIM) Platform 
Global Integration, Engineering, and Operations Support 
REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) / SOURCES SOUGHT (SS) 
19AQMM26N0033 
 
 
1. Purpose 
The Government is seeking industry capability information from firms with demonstrated 
experience integrating and sustaining enterprise Physical Security Information 
Management (PSIM) systems within secure government or similarly controlled 
environments. The requirement involves engineering, integration, sustainment, and operational 
support of a globally deployed PSIM platform integrating multiple physical security subsystems 
including enterprise video management systems, access control systems, intrusion detection 
systems, GIS-based facility mapping, 3-D modeling environments, and advanced video analytics 
capabilities including facial recognition and license plate recognition technologies. 
The system operates within segmented network environments supporting mission-critical 
operations, requiring high-availability architecture, controlled software release management, 
and integration of multiple security technologies into a unified operational platform. The 
Government is particularly interested in vendors with demonstrated experience supporting 
large-scale integrated security systems operating within secure or regulated environments 
and capable of providing continuous operational support for mission-critical platforms. 
This notice is for market research purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation. 
2. Unique System Architecture 
The environment supported under this requirement is not a conventional enterprise IT system. 
The PSIM platform operates within a distributed, multi-tier security architecture integrating 
multiple security technologies and data environments into a unified operational platform. 
The architecture integrates: 
• Enterprise Video Management Systems (VMS) 
• Access Control Systems (ACS) 
• Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) 
• Geographic Information Systems (GIS) 
• 3-D facility modeling and visualization platforms 

 
SBU - CONTRACTING AND ACQUISITIONS 
• Enterprise relational databases and data warehousing environments 
• Event correlation and alarm management engines 
• Secure API integration with external security platforms 
The environment supports global deployments across secure facilities and operates within 
network environments that include: 
• Segmented network enclaves 
• Virtualized server infrastructure 
• High-availability production environments 
• Configuration-controlled software release pipelines 
• Secure enclave cybersecurity requirements 
• Strict configuration baselines and system authorization controls 
The system must maintain the following operational standards: 
• Greater than 99.9% uptime for production server environments 
• Greater than 99% uptime for client environments 
• Real-time alarm ingestion and correlation across integrated security systems 
• Continuous centralized system health monitoring and reporting 
The architecture requires experience integrating physical security subsystems with enterprise 
software platforms operating in controlled security environments. 
3. Advanced Video Analytics Integration 
The PSIM environment incorporates advanced video analytics capabilities used to enhance 
situational awareness and automated security detection functions. 
The architecture integrates both camera-edge analytics and centralized server-based video 
analytic processing platforms supporting technologies including: 
• Facial Recognition (FR) 
• License Plate Recognition (LPR) 
• Object detection and classification 
• Motion-based event analytics 
• Behavioral detection analytics 
The system must support ingestion and correlation of analytic outputs generated from: 
• Edge analytics embedded within IP cameras 
• Server-based analytic engines 
• Video management system analytic modules 
• Third-party analytic platforms 

 
SBU - CONTRACTING AND ACQUISITIONS 
Analytic events are correlated with other security system events and presented within the PSIM 
environment to support operational decision making. 
The architecture must support high-volume analytic event processing while maintaining system 
performance and operational availability. 
4. Required Industry Experience 
The Government seeks vendors with direct and verifiable experience supporting complex 
security system environments with the following technical capabilities. 
Enterprise PSIM Integration 
• Configuration and customization of enterprise PSIM platforms 
• Integration of multiple vendor security systems into unified command environments 
• Alarm/event normalization and correlation 
• Integration of VMS, ACS, IDS, and perimeter detection systems 
• Development and maintenance of PSIM interfaces and integration services 
Mission-Critical System Engineering 
• Secure enterprise application architecture 
• High-availability system engineering 
• Enterprise database architecture and administration 
• DevSecOps practices in controlled environments 
• Enterprise configuration, release, and patch management 
Physical Security System Integration 
• Integration of physical security subsystems with enterprise software platforms 
• Video management system integration 
• Security command center technology and monitoring platforms 
• Alarm monitoring and operational dashboards 
Advanced Video Analytics Integration 
• Camera-edge analytics platforms 
• Server-based video analytic processing engines 
• Facial recognition system integration 
• License plate recognition system integration 
• Analytic event ingestion and alarm correlation 
• Integration of analytic outputs into PSIM operational environments 
• Optimization of analytic processing pipelines for real-time security operations 
 
 

 
SBU - CONTRACTING AND ACQUISITIONS 
 
GIS and Spatial Data Integration 
• GIS-based facility mapping and spatial data management 
• Spatial database architecture 
• Integration of GIS data into operational security systems 
• 3-D facility modeling and visualization platforms 
Cybersecurity and Compliance 
• Support of systems operating within FISMA-aligned environments 
• Information Assurance documentation and compliance support 
• System configuration baselining and security hardening 
• Security authorization and accreditation support 
• Coordination with Information System Security Officers (ISSO) 
Tiered Operational Support Model 
The PSIM system operates under a structured support model including: 
Tier 1 operational support 
Tier 2 technical troubleshooting and escalation 
Tier 3 engineering support and system development 
The environment includes 24/7 Integrated Operations Center (IOC) support, requiring: 
• Continuous system monitoring 
• Rapid response to operational incidents 
• Tiered escalation of system issues 
• Structured incident management and tracking processes 
5. Specialized Government Processes 
The requirement includes operational governance processes that may differ from commercial IT 
environments. 
These processes include: 
• Government-controlled Configuration Control Boards (CCB) 
• Formal change approval and release governance processes 
• Operational Readiness Reviews (ORR) 
• Government Acceptance Reviews prior to global deployment 
• Alpha and Beta testing cycles conducted within designated government facilities 
• Configuration-controlled release pipelines 
• Quality Assurance and Compliance Reporting requirements 
• Formal Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) development and maintenance 

 
SBU - CONTRACTING AND ACQUISITIONS 
V endors unfamiliar with these processes may not be suitable for this requirement. 
 
6. Capability Indicators 
The Government is specifically interested in vendors demonstrating experience supporting 
environments involving: 
PSIM integration 
Enterprise Video Management Systems 
Physical security system integration 
Advanced video analytics integration 
Facial recognition technologies 
License plate recognition systems 
Edge analytics platforms 
Server-based analytic processing engines 
GIS-enabled security systems 
3-D facility modeling environments 
DevSecOps pipelines in controlled environments 
Configuration control governance 
FISMA-aligned operational environments 
Enterprise alarm monitoring platforms 
Mission-critical uptime requirements 
7. Anticipated Contract Characteristics 
The anticipated contract may include: 
• Base period with option years 
• Labor-based service Contract Line Item Numbers (CLINs) 
• Engineering and integration services 
• Global sustainment and support services 
• Software integration milestones 
The final contract structure will be informed by responses received through this market research 
effort. 
8. Response Requirements 
Interested vendors should provide: 
1. Company information and business size classification 
2. Relevant past performance within the past five years 

 
SBU - CONTRACTING AND ACQUISITIONS 
3. Description of experience supporting enterprise PSIM or comparable integrated security 
platforms 
4. Demonstration of experience supporting mission-critical security systems 
5. Description of capability to support 24/7 operational environments 
Responses should focus on direct technical capability and experience supporting complex 
integrated security systems. 
7. Submission Instructions 
All written responses should be submitted in Microsoft-compatible formats (e.g., Word) or PDF.  
Responses must use 12-point font and 1-inch margins, including all text, tables, and graphics.  
Page size shall be 8 ½ X 11-inch.  Page limit is twenty-five (20) single sided.   
Additional attachments such as data sheets providing additional technical details for proposed 
solutions may also be provided, if necessary, in addition to the 20-page limit. General brochures 
or other marketing materials not directly relevant to the Department requirements are not 
requested and will not be considered as part of the response. 
Please submit all responses to Jennifer C. Willis at WillisJC2@state.gov May 7
th, 2026, by 3:00 
PM ET.

Vendor Questions and VA’s answers in red. 

Question #1: Is the Contractor responsible for removing insulation from medium and high-pressure steam lines and hot water piping to facilitate bolt survey?

Answer #1: Yes, insulation must be removed and replaced.  However, if the bolts need to be replaced, insulation does not need to be replaced.

Question #2: Following completion of the survey, is the Contractor responsible for replacing and/or restoring any insulation that was removed or disturbed during the course of the work?

Answer #2: Yes.  However, if the bolts need to be replaced, insulation does not have to be installed.

Question #3: If asbestos-containing materials (ACM) are present in an area that impedes surveying the bolts, should the contractor exclude that area? Or will identified ACM be handled through a modification for abatement?  

Answer #3: If asbestos is encountered during the survey, a modification to the contract will need to be done. 

Question #4: How does the VA anticipate surveying concealed pipe behind walls or chases? Should bolts that require wall demo be excluded from the survey? 

Answer #4: When the beginning of the pipe is exposed and has been surveyed and requires replacement, it is assumed that all bolts on the pipe run will be the same type of bolt.

Question #5: Access to piping systems throughout the facility will be time consuming and require continued coordination. Some areas will need access to ceilings, chases, or in confined spaces. We ask that the period of performance be modified to 180 calendar days for the full survey, reporting, and reviews. 

Answer #5: The performance period will be adjusted due to the complexity of this requirement to 180 days.

Question #6: Does the VA anticipate the contractor providing any level of infection control during this survey? Often investigative work does not require ICRA measures, however, we need to be certain for bidding purposes.  

Answer #6: Infection control measures that create dust in public areas will require ICRA measures.  However, 1 removing ceiling tile within a 50 sq ft area is permitted without ICRA barriers.  Mechanical spaces will not require ICRA.

Question #7: Can the VA provide a mechanical as-built or utility drawing of all lines that are to be included in the survey?   

Answer #7: The VA does have drawings of the utility lines, but not 100% updated/correct.  Drawings/plans provided.

A.3  STATEMENT OF WORK

Oklahoma City Veterans Affairs Health Care System 

Statement of Work

ASTM307 Bolt Replacement Survey

GENERAL:

This project is to survey and identify locations of ASTM 307 bolts and develop a replacement plan to replace the bolts with the required ASTM A193 at the OKC VA HCS at Oklahoma City, Oklahoma.  

The contractor is fully responsible for verifying and validating all information contained within this statement of work. Contractor must fully evaluate the condition of the existing structures and verify the current condition of the project site. 

All measurements/quantities provided in this document are approximate and are to be used for reference only. The contractor will be responsible for taking on-site measurements and verifying all quantities and distances.

All materials/fasteners/etc. must be new and provided by the contractor unless otherwise specified.

The contractor shall abide by all Safety, Security and Infection Control Policies and Procedures of the Oklahoma City VA HCS. 

VA facilities are tobacco free.  No smoking is permitted on VA property. The contractor is responsible for their subcontractor’s compliance with this policy.

All work must conform to, and comply with, the latest edition/version of ALL applicable VA, federal, state, and local laws, rules, regulations, codes, and standards.

JUSTIFICATION: 

 

Per VHA directive, All VAMCs must complete a survey of their existing steam and hot water piping systems and develop a replacement plan, prioritizing high and medium pressure steam and hot water piping systems operating at over 50 pounds per square inch. If ASTM A307 bolts (all grades) are identified, an Interim Safety Measure must be developed to ensure the safety of staff and the facility until replacement is complete.

STATEMENT OF WORK:

The contractor shall provide supervision, manpower, and materials to provide a replacement plan to replace ASTM A307 bolts currently installed in the facility to the required ASATM A193 bolts as the appropriate fastener for steam and hot water piping.

Contractor shall locate and document all ASTM 307 bolts that are installed on high and medium pressure steam and hot water piping

Contractor shall prioritize replacement plan from high and medium pressure steam and hot water piping systems operating over 50 pounds per square inch. 

Contractor shall provide report consisting of locations of ASTM 307 bolts with quantities at each equipment

Contractor shall dispose of any trash or debris they generate during the duration of the performance period and completion of project

Clean up area after project completion and contact COR for final inspection

Performance Period: 30 days after Notice to Proceed

SITE VISIT: Parking is limited. To get to the Engineering Trailers, walk south past boiler plant, turn left, and up the ramp. Engineers/CCRs trailer is on left (See map to engineering trailers).

Normal working hours are from 7:00 AM to 3:30 PM (local time), Monday through Friday except for weekends and established Federal Holidays.

REQUEST FOR INFORMATION 
OPERATIONAL TEST AND TRAINING INFRASTRUCTURE (OTTI) 
SPACE DATA MANAGEMENT DIVISION 
1.0 Description 
 
1.1 The United States Space Force (USSF) is seeking information on how an interested 
contractor could provide the user interface and automation layer of a military Human Resources 
Information Technology (HRIT) system that is easy to use for both Guardians and Human 
Resource (HR) Practitioners. In  support of this effort, USSF is interested in gathering industry 
feedback on a phased approach to incrementally deliver military HR and Talent Management 
capabilities in accordance with the Personnel Management Act. 
 
1.2 THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) ONLY. This Request for Information 
(RFI) is issued solely for information and planning purposes (market research), in accordance with 
Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation Overhaul (RFO) 15.101(c) . This RFI does not 
constitute a solicitation (Request for Proposal (RFP) or Request for Quotation (RFQ)) or a 
promise to issue a solicitation in the future. This RFI does not commit the Government to 
contract for any supply or service whatsoever. Responses to this RFI are not offers and cannot be 
accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. Furthermore, the Government is not, at 
this time, seeking proposals and will not accept any unsolicited proposals. Respondents are 
advised that the Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in 
response to this RFI. All costs associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the 
responding party’s expense. Not responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in any 
future solicitation, if any is issued. Any information submitted by respondents to this RFI is 
strictly voluntary. All submissions become Government property and will not be returned. 
Proprietary information will be safeguarded in accordance with the applicable Government 
regulations. Proprietary information or trade secrets shall be clearly identified. 
 
2.0 Background 
 
The USSF is at a pivotal moment in its evolution as it works to implement the Space Force 
Personnel Management Act (PMA) by the end of Fiscal Year (FY) 2028, as defined in the FY24 
National Defense Authorization Act. This legislation introduces a groundbreaking approach to 
military personnel management, creating a service model without traditional components and 
offering both full -time and part -time service options instead of a reserve or guard component. 
This shift is designed to enhance flexibility, efficiency, and readiness, ensuring the Space Force 
can attract, recruit, and retain the top talent necessary to maintain superiority in the space domain. 
However, the current military HR systems in use by the USSF are highly fragmented, with over 
300 disparate systems in operation. The goal for this effort is to incrementally deploy capabilities 
that bring together Sustained (full -time) and Non- Sustained (part -time) Guardians  

2 
Distribution Statement A. Approved for public release: distribution is unlimited. 
 
into a single cohesive application, eliminating the need to transition between systems, an action 
that often creates gaps in pay and benefits throughout a member’s career. 
 
The Space Force’s mission to bring together Sustained and Non-sustained Guardians into a single 
system is driven by the need to align its workforce management practices with its unique 
operational demands. As the newest branch of the DOW, the USSF faces distinct challenges in 
managing a growing and diverse force while maintaining compliance with evolving policies and 
regulations. Current systems have created inefficiencies, such as repetitive manual tasks and 
fragmented data management, which negatively impact morale, retention, and operational 
effectiveness. To address these challenges, the USSF is committed to deploying capabilities that 
integrate modern technology, simplify processes, streamline workflows, and enhance the overall 
user experience for both Guardians and HR practitioners. 
 
This modernization effort is critical to ensuring the Space Force can meet Congressional timelines 
outlined in the Personnel Management Act (PMA), improve operational effectiveness, and support 
its mission to prevail in the space domain. By presenting USSF HR and Talent Management 
functions in a unified system, the USSF aims to eliminate inefficiencies, improve data 
transparency, and create a seamless experience for its workforce. This initiative represents a 
significant step forward in aligning the Space Force capabilities with its strategic goals and setting 
a new standard for personnel management within the DOW. 
 
The USSF seeks an incremental, phased approach to deploy military HR capabilities to align with 
PMA and the larger “Federal HR 2.0” modernization effort. This approach seeks to deploy small 
capabilities quickly that provide demonstrated value to the Space Force. 
3.0 Requirements 
The USSF needs the capability to identify, track, and manage Guardians in a single system without 
component. The system must be modern, secure, and adaptable to evolving business processes and 
the unique workforce management needs of a growing force. As the USSF moves forward as a 
service without component, the system must be capable of providing Guardians with flexible 
workflows and processes to manage Active Guardians in both Sustained (full -time) and Non-
Sustained (part-time) duty status which sets the USSF apart from other DOW services branches. 
One potential solution the Space Force is considering for improving the user experience for 
Guardians is the deployment of a COTS/SaaS Guardian Automation Layer (GAL) and Guardian 
Data Layer (GDL). By decoupling front end software experience (GAL) from the back-end system 
interfaces (GDL), the future military HRIT system will be  able to remain flexible and scalable as 
the USSF grows. These capabilities will enable the USSF to respond rapidly to emerging 
requirements, integrate with existing and future platforms, maintain vendor competition, and 
remain sustainable through changes in policy, organization, and scale. 
3.1 Guardian Automation Layer (GAL): The GAL will serve as the Single User Interface for 
Guardians and HR Practitioners to interact with military HR Data. Historically, Guardian data has 
been stored within disparate systems, making process improvements and automation cumbersome. 
With no single source of truth for Guardian records or port-of-call for completing military HR 

3

actions, practitioners and end users rely on manual workarounds to reach data needed for decision 
making. 
The primary purpose of the Space Force GAL is to track and manage Guardians in a service 
without component structure throughout the military HR lifecycle. The desired solution will allow 
the Guardian a continuous experience within the GAL throughout the entirety of the HR lifecycle, 
from onboarding and career development to retirement and beyond. The GAL will be flexible, 
with a positive user experience based in human- centered design practices that are reflective of 
modern commercial capabilities. 
The USSF is pursuing a solution that leverages role-based authorities within a unified interface to 
analyze data and create interactive dashboards. Low code/no code configurability will allow 
practitioners to adapt to the evolving policy and process requirements, such as PMA. 
Automation and AI capabilities are a highly desired function of the GAL. The USSF aims to 
greatly reduce administrative burden by freeing Guardians from routine and repetitive tasks and 
will allow for increased focus on higher level work to deliver results for the USSF. It will also 
improve data quality, timeliness of service delivery, Guardian self -service, and HR data 
transparency to Guardians. 
The available dashboards should provide Guardians with a view of open HR actions and track the 
stage of these actions in the workflows. This will reduce the administrative burden on Guardians, 
Supervisors, Commanders, and HR practitioners by providing transparency and reducing the need 
for follow-up correspondence. 
In line with current USSF and DOW policies, the Government is seeking to minimize custom 
software development and maximize the use of commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS), software-as-a-
service (SaaS), and configurable solutions for the GAL. 
3.2 Guardian Data Layer (GDL): The GDL will be the primary integration point and data 
repository for Guardian Data between the GAL and applicable Department of the Air Force (DAF), 
DOW, and other US Government systems. The GDL will be comprised of tools designed to collect, 
store, process, disseminate, and analyze military HR data including, but not limited to, database 
services, data warehousing, big data, data integration tools, data visualization, business 
intelligence, data lake, extract, transformation, application programming interfaces (APIs), and 
data governance. The Guardian Data Layer will also be capable of hosting other commercial 
applications that may need access to Guardian Data. Any solution chosen for the GAL will need 
to integrate with the GDL. 

4 
Distribution Statement A. Approved for public release: distribution is unlimited. 
 
4.0 Requested Information 
 
Before answering the questions below, please review the Attachment to this RFI, “System 
Requirements Document (SRD) - Space Force Guardian Personnel Management System.” 
 
4.1 : Compliance, Security & Data Sovereignty 
 
4.1.1 Does your product have a current Authority to Operate (ATO)? Specify the Impact 
Level (IL) and whether you have FedRAMP or DISA certification. If not, what is your 
roadmap to achieve certification? 
4.1.2 Is your organization owned or operated, in whole or in part, by a foreign entity? 
Describe the relationship and confirm if your platform ensures full data segregation 
between U.S. and foreign operations. 
4.1.3 Can your solution deploy on a Government Cloud (GovCloud) or provide its own 
equivalent? What is your platform's data storage architecture, preferred deployment 
model, and why? 
4.1.4 How does your product manage secure, role -based access for external users (e.g., 
civilian employees, support contractors) who manage military personnel but may not be 
managed in the HR system? Address licensing implications for these users. 
 
4.2 : Core Platform Capabilities & SRD Compliance 
 
4.2.1 Review the attached System Requirements Document (SRD). For each requirement, 
complete the SRD Spreadsheet by stating if the requirement can be met "Out of the 
Box," "With Configuration," or "With Customization." Provide SKU numbers for all 
"Out of the Box" or "With Configuration" solutions. 
Out of the Box: Capability exists in the system without any changes required to 
implement 
Configuration: Changes are required in the system but the ability to make the changes is 
a part of the system design and capabilities. 
Customization: Changes are required in the system and require coding or development 
against the product line. 
 

5 
Distribution Statement A. Approved for public release: distribution is unlimited. 
 
 
4.2.2 How does your platform manage military -specific constructs, including: rank as a 
dynamic attribute, multiple service dates, and unique personnel cases (e.g., Exceptional 
Family Member Program, Joint Spouse)? 
4.2.3 Does your product support a mixed workforce (full-time military, part-time military, 
civilian) within a single environment, accommodating unique data fields, rules, and 
processes for each population? Are the data fields fixed and require development 
against a product line or are they customizable? 
4.2.4 Describe your product's ability to integrate personnel and financial data to support 
complex "change of station" events. Highlight any native data visualization capabilities 
(e.g., map-based tracking). 
4.2.5 Describe how your system supports multi -step onboarding workflows, from initial 
recruitment and pre-assignment (training) to the first duty assignment, ensuring data 
accuracy and dashboard visibility. 
4.2.6 Does your product have native capabilities for generating standardized forms with 
electronic signatures? Does your product store documents attached to a personnel 
record? Detail any associated costs and recommended approaches for mobile or 
workflow optimization. 
4.2.7 Does your product have native capabilities to perform data analytics and data 
visualization? 
 
 
4.3 : Implementation, Sustainment & Scalability 
 
4.3.1 Provide a sample implementation plan, including recommended sequencing, testing 
approach, and deployment schedule against the capabilities identified in the draft 
capabilities roadmap. Include a reasonable timeline for a vendor to ramp up to full 
operational capacity. 
4.3.2 Based on the information provided, what is a reasonable cost estimate for 
implementation? What key factors or risks could affect the timeline and cost? 

6

4.3.3 Describe your sustainment strategy, particularly how unique configurations are 
preserved during update cycles. 
4.3.4 To support a force of 10,000 Guardians by 2028 and 40,000 by 2040, what is the 
recommended size for the technical support/sustainment team and the corporate HR 
team? 
4.3.5 What training do you recommend for end-users, and what is the typical time required for 
a user to become proficient? 
 
4.4 : Past Performance & Market Position 
 
4.4.1 Describe your past experience providing Enterprise HR platforms to military and/or 
U.S. Government organizations, highlighting your approach to navigating complex 
policy and compliance environments.

providers to deliver a unified solution.

SUBJECT: 
The Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR) Line-up Assessment for Upcoming 
Navigation Challenges to Help Ease Risk (LAUNCHER) project (STMD-GCD funded) 
requires a handheld mobile LiDAR mapping instrument to provide a commercial-off-the-
shelf comparison and ground-truth comparison to data collected by Kinematic Navigation 
and Cartography Knapsack (KNaCK) mobile LiDAR instrument data. Requirements for 
the requested instruments are: a handheld, LiDAR-based mapping sensor that includes 
GPS/GNSS capability, includes integrated cameras, has a sensor with ~100 m ranging 
and 0.5 cm range resolution, utilizes a sophisticated simultaneous localization and 
mapping (SLAM) processing solution, and a local-machine (i.e. NASA computer) 
processing software with a perpetual license that does not require cloud-computing 
resources or purchase of processing credits, data processing software compatible with 
plug-ins for Esri ArcPro and Agisoft Metashape software.  The identified instrument that 
meets requirements is the GeoCue TrueView GO 132S mapping system. This is a 
handheld scanning LiDAR sensor and associated compute, power supply, and processing 
software to allow for comparable mobile 3D mapping to the existing MSFC capability 
KNaCK system, and which will allow appropriate comparison. 
No existing mobile LiDAR Mapping capability exists within the agency that can provide 
the same required ground truth and comparison

PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT (PWS) 
 
C01SM/Security Management Program Mission and Readiness Support Services 
In Support of 
Commander, Littoral Combat Ship Squadron One 
Naval Base, San Diego, CA 
 
Part 1 
General Information 
 
1.  GENERAL: This is a non-personal services contract to provide Security Management 
Program Mission Readiness to Commander, Littoral Combat Ship Squadron One N00SM 
Department Staff. The Government will not exercise any supervision or control over the contract 
service providers performing services herein. Such contract service providers shall be 
accountable solely to the Contractor who, in turn, is responsible to the Government. 
 
1.1  Description of Services/introduction: Contractor support is required to provide Security 
Management Program Mission Readiness to enhance warfighting readiness and increase the 
Security proficiency of Littoral Combat Ship Squadron One, to include afloat and ashore 
claimants and staff.  The contractor shall provide support for in-port services. 
 
1.2  Background: Security governed by the DoD and SECNAV requirements.  The mission of 
COMLCSRON ONE Security is to provide support services for the overall operational and 
administrative objectives of Commander, Littoral Combat Ship Squadron One.  This supports 
our ability to man, train, and equip COMLCSRON ONE in security management. LCSRON One 
security assets provide LCS Afloat Commanding Officers with credible security support and 
protection of information across the LCS platform.  
 
1.3.  Objectives:  The Contractor shall provide Security Management Support and Services to 
include: Conducting training events, Subject Matter Expertise (SME) Support, Readiness 
Support, Meeting Support, Compliance Support, Curriculum Development, Instruction and 
Processes Development, Trends Analysis, Command and LCS Ship Security Support, Asset 
Support, Compliance Evaluation Support, Command Security Equipment Support, 

 
Modernization Support, Risk Management Support, Content Development and Communication 
Strategy Development.   
 
1.4.  Scope:  In addition to contract Program Management functions, the following Mission 
Readiness Security Support Roles shall be included in the Scope of this contract: 
 
1.4.1  SECURITY MANAGER SUPPORT.  Providing administration support across a wide 
range of security disciplines to protect physical and information command assets.  
   
1.4.2  LITTORAL COMBAT SHIP SQUADRON ONE SECURITY SUPPORT.  Providing 
administration support across a wide range of security disciplines to protect physical and 
information support for LCS Ship assets. 
 
1.5.  Period of Performance: The base period of performance is one year with one option year. 
 
1.6.  General Information: 
 
1.6.1.  Quality Control:  The Contractor shall develop and maintain an effective quality control 
program to ensure services are performed in accordance with this PWS.  The contractor shall 
develop and implement procedures to identify, prevent, and ensure non-recurrence of defective 
services.  The contractor’s quality control program is the means by which they assure themselves 
that work complies with the requirement of the contract.  The contractor’s Quality Control Plan 
(QCP) will be part of the proposal submission and evaluation (see Section L).  The contractor 
shall receive the Contracting Officer’s acceptance, in writing, of any proposed change to the 
submitted QCP. 
 
1.6.2.  Quality Assurance:  The Government shall evaluate the contractor’s performance under 
this contract in accordance with the Quality Assurance Surveillance Program (QASP).  This plan 
is primarily focused on what the Government must do to ensure that the contractor has 
performed in accordance with the performance standards.  It defines how the performance 
standards will be applied, the frequency of surveillance, and the minimum acceptable quality 
levels and defect rate(s). 
 

 
1.6.3.  Recognized Holidays:  The contractor is not required to perform services on the following 
Holidays: 
New Year’s Day Labor Day 
Martin Luther King Jr.’s Birthday Columbus Day 
President’s Day Veteran’s Day 
Memorial Day Thanksgiving Day 
Juneteenth 
Independence Day 
Christmas Day 
 
1.6.4.  Hours of Operation:  The contractor is responsible for conducting the majority of work 
between the business hours of 0700 to 1630, referred to as “Core Hours,” Monday thru Friday, 
except for Federal Holidays, or when the Government facility is closed due to local or National 
emergencies, administrative closings, or similar Government-directed facility closings.  
Adjustments to the working hours to meet mission requirements shall be coordinated through the 
TPOC and the supported Government personnel, and shall range from 0500 to 1800, as needed.  
The contractor must, at all times, maintain an adequate workforce for the uninterrupted 
performance of all task defined within this PWS when the Government facility is not close for 
the above reasons.  When hiring personnel, the Contractor shall keep in mind that the stability 
and continuity of the workforce are essential. 
 
1.6.5.  Places of Performance: The work to be performed under this contract will be performed at 
the following locations: 
 
Location 1:  Commander, Littoral Combat Ship Squadron One, 2680 Woden St., Bldg. 3304B, 
Suite 2, San Diego, CA 92136 
 
Location 2:  Onboard various COMLCSRON ONE afloat platforms, Naval Base San Diego, San 
Diego, CA 92136 
 
Location 3:  Government may consider approving situational telework to support the contract 
during unforeseen health, security, natural events
 or other scenarios that may influence 

 
attendance.  These periods will be approved in writing by the TPOC as required to meet the 
command mission as necessary.   
 
1.6.6.   Type of contract: Firm Fixed Price. 
 
1.6.7.  Security Requirements:  The Contractor shall meet all requirements contained in the DD 
Form 254.  Highest level of classification of the work to be performed is at the SECRET level. 
 
1.6.7.1  Common Access Card (CAC) Issuance:  The Government Contractor CAC  serves as the 
primary method of identification for the Contractor employees, as well as providing the basis of 
Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) access to the Navy/Marine Corps Intranet (NMCI), and 
numerous Navy web sites, which may also require PKI access.  The TPOC shall assist in 
providing the Contractor the appropriate documentation for obtaining a CAC . 
Both physical and logical access is the requirement to qualify for CAC issuance for Contractors 
who need access to, or are stationed on, bases/facilities that use Navy Access Control System 
(NCACS).  If both physical and logical access is deemed warranted, then the Government will 
sponsor the Contractor for the issuance of a CAC.  Within 30 days of task order award, the 
Contractor shall identify those personnel to the Technical Point of Contact (TPOC) whom the 
Contractor can justify requiring physical and logical access.   A CAC cannot be issued to 
personnel who do not have a favorably adjudicated National Agency Check with fingerprints or 
higher.  The Contractor shall effectively manage their workforce to avoid delays resulting from 
personnel who do not have the necessary eligibility. 
The Contractor shall be responsible for obtaining any government issued identification cards 
from the former employee and to turning those items over to the TPOC within five (5) days of 
the termination of the employment. 
 
1.6.7.2.  The nature of this task requires access up to SECRET information. The work performed 
by the contractor could include access up to SECRET, information, and spaces. The contractor 
could be required to attend meetings classified up to the SECRET level. Sufficient contractor 
personnel assigned to this effort shall possess a current Tier 3 or Tier 3 Re-investigation 
(T3/T3R), as delineated within Section 1.6.17.  Personnel supporting the roles within this effort 
shall require security clearances and billets up to the SECRET level and shall require access to 
government offices and SECRET areas, data, and facilities to successfully accomplish the 
tasking identified within the PWS.  Contractor personnel assigned to this effort who require 
access to SECRET data and spaces shall possess a current T3/T3R with Secret eligibility and 
Access reflected in Defense Information System for Security (DISS). 

 
 
1.6.7.3.  Communication Security (COMSEC): There are no COMSEC requirements anticipated 
in this contract. 
 
1.6.7.4.  Operations Security (OPSEC) Requirements: The Contractor shall apply Operations 
Security (OPSEC) to enhance protection for classified and unclassified critical information, 
pursuant to the National Security Decision Directive Number 298, DoDM 5205.2, OPNAV, and 
supplementary instructions.  Service OPSEC guidance shall also apply if the contracted activity 
is performed in a Service-level operational environment.  If a conflict is identified between 
Service and higher-level guidance, the Contractor shall contact the TPOC for clarification.  The 
Contractor shall develop, implement and maintain an OPSEC program to enhance protection of 
classified and unclassified critical information that will be used at the Contractor’s location 
during the performance of this task order in accordance with this PWS and DD-254 Contract 
Security Classification Specification.  The Contractor shall be in compliance with security 
requirements imposed by documents generated in response to DoDI 5200.39, Critical Program 
Information (CPI) Protection within the Department of Defense, May 28, 2015 Incorporating 
Change 3, Effective October 1, 2020. The Contractor shall be in compliance with OPSEC 
measures if imposed by programs supported or by documents generated by NAB Coronado.  The 
Contractor shall be in compliance with DFARS 252.204-7012 Safeguarding Covered Defense 
Information and Cyber Incident Reporting.  OPSEC Awareness Education and Training shall be 
provided or coordinated through Government channels as a cost management process. The 
TPOC can assist with this training coordination option.  All personnel supporting the contract 
shall receive initial OPSEC awareness training and Annual OPSEC Refresher training.  If the 
contractor has existing OPSEC awareness education, training, and planning processes in place to 
protect corporate information, these should be applied pending Government acceptance rather 
than creating a new program. The contractor shall have an OPSEC plan for this task order.  The 
OPSEC plan shall be provided with and approved by COMLCSRON ONE TPOC after contract 
award and shall be imposed on subcontractors as appropriate.  Program protection measures shall 
be applied and approved by COMLCSRON ONE at all locations where Critical Information is 
developed, produced, analyzed, maintained, transported, stored, tested, or used in training.  The 
Contractor shall request guidance from the TPOC on any specific predetermined OPSEC critical 
information associated with the task order or any associated OPSEC plans that directly relate to 
the information provided by the Government.  OPSEC protective measures shall be applied as 
directed by the Government.  While performing on a Government site, the Contractor shall 
comply with the OPSEC guidance or plans specific to that location or program supported. 
 
1.6.7.5. SECRET Justification:  Due to the sensitive nature of operational information, which 
will be required to successfully execute the tasking identified in this PWS in support of 
COMLCSRON ONE, the contractor supporting this role shall require access to SECRET as 

 
directed by the government.  The access must include SECRET spaces, documentation, and data 
which are relevant to the development of the deliverables and which satisfy the technical 
requirements of this task.   
 
1.6.7.6.  Physical Security:  The contractor shall be responsible for the safeguarding of all 
Government equipment, (classified/unclassified) information, and property provided for 
contractor use.  At the close of each work period, government facilities, equipment, and materials 
shall be secured. 
 
1.6.8.  Contractor Personnel.  Contractor employees’ conduct shall be IAW 5 CFR Parts 2600-
2641 and DOD-5500 7-R (Joint Ethics Regulations).  If a Contract employee is removed from 
the job site or dismissed from the premises by the Government for violations, the Contractor is 
not relieved of the requirement to provide sufficient personnel to perform the services as required 
by this PWS.  IAW 18 USC 1382, the authority of the Government to control and deny a 
Contractor employee entry to all or part of Government facilities is absolute.  The individual 
concerned has no right to appeal.  The Contractor shall minimize delays in starting work because 
of issues with having insufficient cleared personnel.  Contractor personnel accessing 
Government networks in the performance of contract work require a favorably adjudicated 
personnel security investigation, whether or not an actual security clearance is required.  
Personnel whose duties meet the criteria for an Automated Information System (AIS) Level 1 
designation require a favorably adjudicated Tier 5 (T5) or Tier 5 Reinvestigation (T5R).  This 
applies to all IA and Cybersecurity tasks.  The T5 or T5R must be updated every 5 years. A 
favorably adjudicated Tier 3 (T3) or Tier 3 Reinvestigation (T3R) for civilian personnel is 
required for AIS Levels 2 and 3.  Additionally, Telecommunications Directive (NTD) 02-06, 
Information Assurance (IA) Training Requirement, DoDD 8570.01-M, Information Assurance 
Training, Certification, and Workforce Management Policy, and DoDI 8500.2 E3.3.7 require that 
all authorized users of DoD Information Systems receive initial IA awareness orientation as a 
condition of access and thereafter must complete annual IA refresher awareness training to 
maintain an active user account.  Access requests to DoD IT systems shall utilize OPNAV 
5239/14 (REV 9/2011) SAAR-N form. SECNAVMAN 5239.2 IA Workforce Management 
Manual provides additional amplifying policy and requirements. 
 
1.6.9.  When performing the tasks specified in this PWS whether in public or otherwise, through 
e-mail, phone calls, or meeting attendance, Contractor personnel shall make clear to all 
individuals they deal with that they are Contractor employees and not DoD employees.  When 
participating and introducing themselves during official events wherein DoD, non-DoD or 
foreign officials are present, Contractor personnel shall identify themselves as employees of the 

 
Contractor.  Contractor personnel must clearly identify who their employer is in a visible area 
(i.e. clothing, company shirt/logo, pin, company ID, etc.).

USA Storage 3.0  
Statement of Objectives (SOO) 
 
 
 
 
 
Executive Office for United States Attorneys (EOUSA) 
Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) 
  


1.0 INTRODUCTION  AND PURPOSE  
The United States Attorneys organization is comprised of ninety-four (94) Districts with 
roughly two-hundred fifty (250) offices in geographically dispersed sites throughout the 
continental United States, Alaska, Guam, the Marianas Islands, Puerto Rico, Hawaii, and 
the U.S. Virgin Islands.  The Executive Office for United States Attorneys (EOUSA) is 
responsible for providing administrative, technical, and legal support to all United States 
Attorneys’ offices (USAOs). 
The Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) of the Executive Office for United 
States Attorneys (EOUSA) delivers technology solutions that enable United States 
Attorney’s Office (USAO) employees to effectively carry out their complex operational 
duties. OCIO works collaboratively with USAOs and other stakeholders to translate their 
business needs into effective IT solutions, providing essential tools that support the 
DOJ’s mission.  OCIO designs, develops, and implements enterprise-scale solutions 
across a range of areas, including custom application development, server and virtual 
infrastructure, voice and unified communications, video services, cloud storage, and 
wide and local area networking. Additionally, EOUSA operates the Network Operations 
Center (NOC), which houses the core hardware infrastructure for each OCIO staff. The 
NOC also serves as the location for TechOne, EOUSA’s nationwide IT help desk. TechOne 
provides Tier 2 technical support to all USAOs.  
This Statement of Objectives (SOO) is provided in support of a Request for Information 
(RFI) issued by the Executive Office for United States Attorneys (EOUSA). The purpose of 
this RFI is to conduct market research to identify commercial capabilities and solution 
approaches that may support a future acquisition for enterprise Storage as a Service, 
referred to as USAStorage 3.0. The RFI is for information gathering and planning 
purposes only and does not constitute solicitation. 
2.0 BACKGROUND  
EOUSA supporting United States Attorneys’ Offices (USAOs) nationwide requires a 
modernized, scalable, and secure enterprise storage solution to support evidentiary and 
mission data. Existing storage capabilities must evolve to address continued data 
growth, multi-location access requirements, continuity of operations, and enhanced 
governance, auditability, and security. EOUSA is seeking to understand how industry 
solutions deployed in FedRAMP-approved Government Cloud environments can meet 
these needs. 
3.0 SCOPE 

The scope of this SOO encompasses enterprise-wide storage capabilities supporting 
approximately 15,000 users across roughly 250 office locations. The solution must 
support an initial data footprint of nearly 20 petabytes, with the ability to scale 
indefinitely for usable capacity and support the ongoing growth of the USAOs at 
approximately two percent month over month, historically. The solution must support 
access to data from multiple geographic locations, at the nearest logical location to the 
user, and enable continuity of operations (COOP) for remote users and COOP processes. 
4.0 OBJECTIVES  
The following objectives define the desired outcomes for the USAStorage 3.0 capability. 
Respondents are encouraged to describe how their solutions meet or exceed these 
objectives. Respondents are required to describe and detail, with specificity, their 
reliance on third parties and/or subcontractors to meet these requirements. 
Respondents must include transparency information regarding any intended use of large 
language models (LLMs) (e.g., AI-assisted technologies) supplied by the contractor 
including its acceptable use policy, model/system/data card information, end user 
resources for the LLM, details regarding the mechanisms for end user feedback (see 
attached Department Local Clause DOJ-09 Large Language Models (MAR 2026). 
Respondents are further required to clearly state any and all assumptions they may 
make in their response to each of the objectives and sections herein. 
4.1 A
RCHITECTURE AND ACCESS OBJECTIVES  
The solution shall provide centralized, authoritative storage hosted in a Geo-dispersed 
FedRAMP-approved Government Cloud environment. Users must be able to access all 
authorized files from multiple locations, including office, remote, virtual private network 
(VPN), and Contingency of Operations (COOP) environments, through Server Message 
Block (SMB) functionality and interface. If on-site cache or edge components are 
utilized, the solution must ensure that all files remain directly accessible from the cloud-
based service without dependency on local infrastructure. Any proposed solutions must 
comply with Local Clauses DOJ-02, DOJ-05, DOJ-07 regarding contractor privacy 
requirements, security protocols, and auditing controls. The solution will include and 
support deduplication and compression to reduce the overall cost. The primary user 
access method shall be SMB-based file shares compatible with Windows operating 
systems and existing user workflows. The solution shall provide LAN speed access to 
data regardless of geo-location of user in relation to the data when the accessing system 
is within the USAO network.  The solution shall integrate with and be accessible to 
cloud-based Virtual Machines (VMs) for processing case data, hosted in the same Gov-
cloud instance.  

4.2 IDENTITY AND ACCESS CONTROL OBJECTIVES  
The solution shall integrate with EOUSA enterprise identity services through OKTA. User 
authentication shall be performed at the Windows workstation level using PIV-based 
credentials. File and folder access permissions shall be enforced based on the 
authenticated user’s enterprise Active Directory management and group memberships. 
The solution shall support enterprise-scale authorization and role-based access controls 
without requiring separate storage-specific credentials. 
4.3 SECURITY AND COMPLIANCE OBJECTIVES  
The solution shall operate entirely within U.S.-based Government Cloud regions. All 
system data, backups, replicas, and metadata shall remain within the United States. All 
contractor personnel who are directly accessing, administering and/or otherwise 
manipulating the system on behalf of the vendor in performance of this contract, shall 
be U.S Citizens based in the continental United States. The solution shall support FIPS 
140-2 encryption of data at rest and in transit and comply with applicable DOJ security 
and privacy requirements. 
4.4 AVAILABILITY , CONTINUITY , AND RESILIENCE OBJECTIVES  
The solution shall provide high availability and resilience suitable for enterprise 
operations. The system shall support continued access to data during localized site 
outages and enable continuity of operations for remote users and COOP processes. The 
solution shall support a target service availability of 99.8 percent and recovery time 
objectives within 12 hours for district-level or backend infrastructure failures. 
4.5 DATA MANAGEMENT AND LIFECYCLE OBJECTIVES  
The solution shall support full data lifecycle management, including commonly used 
industry classifications for tiered storage options. The tiered storage shall align with hot, 
warm, cold, and archive with each tier defined by clear performance and access 
characteristics. For example, the hot tier shall provide near real-time access to data with 
sub-second latency and support high-throughput, frequent access workloads. The warm 
tier shall support regularly accessed data with moderate latency (typically within 
seconds) and balanced performance and cost. The cold tier shall be optimized for 
infrequently accessed data, with retrieval times ranging from minutes to hours and 
lower storage costs. The archive tier shall support long-term retention of rarely accessed 
data at the lowest cost, with retrieval times that may extend to several hours or longer. 
The solution shall support retention enforcement, write-once-read-many (WORM) 
capabilities, litigation hold, and long-term evidentiary preservation. These capabilities 

shall be manageable through centralized administrative controls with attendant and 
commensurate reporting methods. 
The proposed solution shall provide a scalable, high-performance storage capability 
designed to support future AI integrations, including preparedness for vectorization and 
large language model (LLM) workloads, across an initial dataset of approximately 20 
petabytes, with the flexibility to expand as data volumes and mission needs grow, while 
ensuring compliance with Increasing Public Trust in Artificial Intelligence Through 
Unbiased AI Principles OMB M-26-04.. The solution must enable efficient ingestion, 
cataloging, and indexing of structured and unstructured data to facilitate advanced 
search, containerization, and vectorization use cases. The architecture should be 
extensible to incorporate advanced content analysis capabilities, including metadata 
extraction, classification, and enrichment, allowing future enhancements without 
significant reengineering.  
4.6 M
IGRATION OBJECTIVES  
The solution shall support the migration of existing data from current enterprise storage 
platforms, including approximately 18 billion files and 20 petabytes of data, with 
continued growth during migration. Production migration activities shall be completed 
within a 24-month period. The migration approach shall minimize disruption to end

Sources Sought Notice for U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development 
Technology Transformation Next Generation  
Notice No. NFNC-2026 -0310 
 
THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE (NOTICE) FOR LARGE AND SMALL SCHEDULE 
CONTRACTORS.  THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS AND THIS NOTICE DOES 
NOT REPRESENT A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT TO ISSUE A SOLICITATION OR 
TO ESTABLISH A MULTIPLE AWARD VEHICLE. 
 
1. The US Department of Housing and Urban Development is issuing this notice as a 
means of conducting market research to identify parties having an interest and the 
resources to support our requirement for Technology Transformation Next Generation 
(H2TNG). Additional information about the requirement is available in the Appendix 
accompanying this notice. Results of this market research will contribute to 
determining the method of acquisition.  
 
2. The contractor(s) must deliver comprehensive IT Support Services and Technology 
Transformation Next Generation (ITSS and 2TNG) solutions across HUD 
Headquarters (HQ), regional and ﬁeld offices, data centers, and other designated 
locations.  Support shall span the functional areas of the Office of Chief Information 
Officer (OCIO), including but not limited to: 
 
 OCIO front office  
 Assistance Chief Information Officer Business IT Resource Management (ACIO 
BIRM)  
 Office of Chief Technology Officer (OCTO)  
 ACIO Customer Relationship & Performance Management (ACIO CRPM) 
 Office of Chief Information Security Office (OCISO)  
 ACIO Office of Infrastructure & Operations (ACIO OIO)  
 Office of the Artiﬁcial Intelligence Officer (OAIO)  
 Office of Digital Business Officer (ODBO)  
 
3. The applicable North American Industry Classiﬁcation System (NAICS) code 
assigned to this acquisition are 541512 - Computer Systems Design Services – PSC 
codes: D300 (IT and Telecom) category, particularly D301 (Facility Operation and 

Maintenance), D306 (Systems Analysis), D307 (IT Strategy and Architecture), and 
D399 (Other IT and Telecom Services). 
 
4. There is no solicitation currently, and this request for capability information does not 
constitute a request for proposals. Submission of any information in response to this 
market survey is purely voluntary, and we assume no ﬁnancial responsibility for any 
costs you incur to respond.     
 
5. Responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the government to 
form a binding contract.  We will treat all submissions as business conﬁdential 
materials, which will become government property, and will not return the 
submissions. 
 
6. We are considering establishing multiple Blanket Purchase Agreements (BPAs) 
against Federal Supply Schedule (FSS) contracts. Learn more about the FSS program 
at http://www.gsa.gov/schedules. U.S. General Services Administration (GSA) has a 
FASt Lane vendor onboarding program. FASt Lane: Making it easier | GSA 
 
7. If your organization has the potential capacity to perform H2TNG services, please 
provide the following information:  
 
a. Organization name, address, email address, website address, telephone number, 
and size and type of ownership for the organization. 
 
b. If you have a GSA contract: GSA contract number(s), applicable Serial Identiﬁcation 
Number(s) (SIN). 
 
c. Tailored capability statements addressing the particulars of this effort, with 
appropriate documentation supporting claims of organizational and staff capability.  
 
d. If you anticipate signiﬁcant subcontracting or anticipate teaming to deliver technical 
capability, address the administrative and management structure of such 
arrangements.  
 
 
 

8. We will evaluate market information to ascertain potential market capacity to:  
 
a) Provide services consistent in scope and scale with those described in this notice 
and otherwise anticipated. 
b) Secure and apply the full range of corporate ﬁnancial, human capital, and 
technical resources required to successfully perform similar requirements. 
c) Implement a successful project management plan that includes compliance with 
program schedules, cost containment, meeting/tracking performance, 
hiring/retention of key personnel, and risk mitigation. 
d) Provide services under a performance-based service acquisition contract. 
 
9. Based on the responses to the sources sought notice/market research, we may set 
aside this procurement for small businesses or procure through full and open 
competition, and we will make multiple awards. We will not provide feedback or 
evaluations to companies regarding their submissions in response to this notice. 
 
Submission Instructions : We are inviting interested parties who consider themselves 
qualiﬁed to perform the above-listed services to submit a response to this notice by April 30, 
2026. You must email your responses to this notice to travis.l.sutton@hud.gov and 
Gene.H.Jackson@HUD.gov.    
Please contact Travis Sutton or Gene Hamilton Jackson if you have any questions concerning 
this opportunity.   
When emailing your questions, responses, etc., the subject line of the email should read 
“FOUO\\INFO: Sources Sought Notice NFNC-2026-0310 H2TNG– ( Insert Your Company 
Name)” .

management, project lifecycle management, governance, risk & compliance, enterprise

Quarterly/Annual Data Calls, plans of action and milestones (POA&Ms) tracking, security

Section M- N68335-26-R-1036 EVALUATION FACTORS FOR AWARD (SERVICES)

PART A: GENERAL INFORMATION

Basis for Award

 The Government intends to make a fair opportunity selection and award one (1) TO to the Contractor representing the “best value” to the Government, price and other factors considered. “Best Value” means the expected outcome of an acquisition that, in the Government’s estimation, provides the greatest overall benefit in response to the requirement (see FAR 2.101 Definitions). The best value evaluation is, in and of itself, a subjective assessment by the Government of the proposed solution that provides the optimal or most advantageous results to the Government. A comparative analysis of TO proposals considering all evaluation factors will be made to determine the best suited TO proposal offering the best value to the Government. The Government intends to award a TO to the responsible Contractor whose TO proposal conforms to the RFTOP’s requirements and is the most advantageous to the Government based upon an assessment of the evaluation factors described further below.

The Government does not evaluate every requirement of the RFTOP under Section M of the RFTOP. The awarded Contractor: however, is required to comply with all requirements of the awarded TO.

Although the Government may waive informalities and minor irregularities in TO proposals received, the failure to comply with terms and conditions of the RFTOP may adversely impact the Contractor’s evaluation results and could result in the Contractor being removed from consideration for award. Informalities and minor irregularities may be defined as clerical errors, minor template or format errors, or administrative clarifications.

 If a fail rating is found under key personnel within the technical volume of the Contractor’s proposal, this will render their proposal unawardable.

2.0 Contractor Responsibility to Submit an Unambiguous Convincing Task Order Proposal

2.1 It is the Contractor’s responsibility to draft a logical, unambiguous proposal that contains all pertinent information in sufficient detail so that Government evaluators are able to meaningfully evaluate the Contractor’s proposed approach and cost/price.

2.2 Failure to follow the instructions detailed in Section L, Part A, Paragraph 2.0 TO Proposal Format and its subparagraphs may result in the TO proposal being deemed non-compliant, not evaluated, and considered ineligible for TO award.

 Fair Opportunity

This RFTOP is conducted under the fair opportunity guidelines of FAR Subpart 16.507, which outlines the ordering procedures for orders issued under Indefinite-Delivery/Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contracts. This method does not use any aspects of FAR Subpart 15.2.

 The use of this fair opportunity process does not obligate the Government to determine a competitive range, conduct discussions with any contractors, solicit responses or revisions thereto, or use any other source selection techniques associated with FAR Subpart 15.2. The identification of terminology similar to use in FAR Subpart 15.2, such as the Government’s questions and comments, and the Contractor’s answers and responses do not constitute discussions, clarifications, communications, or exchanges as used in FAR Subpart 15.2.

 Under FAR 16.507, the Government is required to afford all Contractors under the multiple-award contract a fair opportunity to submit an offer and have that offer fairly considered. Accordingly, the Government will evaluate each Contractor’s TO proposal fairly, similarly, and in accordance with the RFTOP’s evaluation criteria. If the Government does not award on initial TO proposals, the Government will not establish a competitive range comprised of all of the most highly rated proposals. Accordingly, the Contractor’s initial TO proposal must contain the Contractor’s best terms, conditions, and prices. Pre-award debriefings and pre-award notifications of exclusion prior to award are not required under FAR Subpart 16.5, and the Government will not provide them.

After the Government has afforded all eligible Contractors under the Seaport NxG multiple-award contract a fair opportunity to submit a TO proposal and have that TO proposal fairly considered, the Government’s selection official may take or direct one or more of the following actions:

Award to the Contractor whose TO proposal submission conforms to the RFTOP’s requirements and offers the best value to the Government based upon the evaluation methodology defined in Section M of the RFTOP;

Obtain written resolutions or response revisions from the Contractor whose initial TO proposal 

Submission may or may not conform to the RFTOP’s requirements and offers the best value to the Government based upon the evaluation methodology defined in Section M of the RFTOP and may be awardable under the RFTOP’s evaluation criteria. Written resolutions or response revisions may include but not be limited to easily-resolvable informalities, minor irregularities, or negative findings, the resolution of which do not remove evaluated positive findings or increase the Contractor’s total evaluated price of the TO;

Obtain cost/price supporting information, without obtaining an increase in proposed cost/price, from the Contractor whose initial TO proposal submission conforms to the RFTOP’s requirements and offers the best value to the Government based upon the evaluation methodology defined in Section M of the RFTOP;

Further consider only those Contractors who are most likely to provide the most advantageous revised 

responses to participate in one-on-one negotiations via interchanges and submit proposed fixes and/or revised responses. Interchanges are defined as, “fluid interaction(s) between the contracting officer and the Contractors that may address any aspect of the response/TO proposal and may or may not be documented in real time.” Interchanges may be conducted with one, some, none, or all of the Contractors who submitted TO proposals;

Further consider only the Contractor determined to offer the best value to the Government based upon the evaluation methodology defined in Section M of the RFTOP, despite any negative findings that may exist with that response, where other Contractors do not have a reasonable prospect for award; and/or

Not award to any Contractor.

Interchanges with a Contractor do not constitute “discussions” as defined in FAR Subpart 15.2, because FAR Subpart 15.2 does not apply to this TO competition, which will be conducted under FAR Subpart 16.507.

CAUTION: The Government anticipates selecting the successful Contractor from initial TO proposal submissions without requesting revised responses; however, nothing herein shall preclude interchanges with Contractors, and interchanges with one Contractor does not entitle other Contractors to interchanges as well. Contractors are strongly encouraged to submit their best technical, past performance, and cost/price in response to this RFTOP.

A Contractor’s Proposed Features as Performance Requirements

The Government may decide to write specific features of a Contractor’s proposed approach that provides benefit to the Government directly into the Statement of Work, Specification, or other section of the TO at any time prior to award.

If the Government’s selection official has selected an apparent successful Contractor, and the apparent 

successful Contractor does not agree to include any of the Contractor’s proposed features directly into the Statement of Work, Specification, or other section of the TO prior to award, the Government will revise the selection official’s decision record. This may or may not change the TO selection decision, depending upon the proposed feature’s benefit(s) that will no longer be reflected in the selection official’s decision record.

5.0 Evaluation Factors and Methodology for Award

The Government will evaluate TO proposals using the following factors:

Technical Sub factors:

Past Performance

The evaluation will consider Technical, Past Performance, and Cost/Price factors listed above in descending order of importance. Understanding of the Work/SOW Approach and Key Personnel Resumes, are sub factors of the Technical Factor; they are of equal importance. In evaluating the technical response, the two sub factors are separately rated. 

Technical is more important than Past Performance. Past Performance is more important than Cost/Price. Technical and Past Performance factors, when combined, are significantly more important than Cost/Price.

Small Business is not part of the tradeoff and TO proposals must receive an “acceptable” rating to be eligible for award.  Additionally, CMMC is not a part of the tradeoff, and the apparently successful offeror must possess the required CMMC Level 1 Self-Assessment prior to award.  Compliance is a material condition of award. 

The Government will perform a Technical/Past Performance/Cost/Price tradeoff analysis to select the TO proposal that provides the “best value” as defined in Section M, Part A, Paragraph 1.1 above. The Contractor is advised that the lowest priced TO proposal meeting the RFTOP requirements may not be selected for a TO award if award to a higher priced Contractor is determined to be more advantageous and/or beneficial to the Government provided that the perceived advantages and/or benefits merit the additional cost/price.

The Government intends to strictly enforce all of the RFTOP submission requirements outlined in Section L. Any information submitted shall be in accordance with the instructions in Section L of this RFTOP.

NOAA GNSS Radio Occultation Commercial Data Buy

SBEM IDIQ Task Order 1 (TO-1)

Statement of Work

Introduction

In this Task Order, NOAA intends to acquire near-real-time global navigation satellite system (GNSS) radio occultation (RO) satellite data satisfying the requirements set forth in the NOAA Commercial Data Program Space Based Environmental Monitoring (SBEM) IDIQ contract Statement of Work (SOW). NOAA intends to use these data in operational numerical weather prediction models, space weather models, and other systems. NOAA reserves the right to issue subsequent, simultaneous, and additional Task Orders for RO data during this period of performance. 

Scope

NOAA is soliciting commercial near-real-time satellite-based GNSS RO and ionospheric measurements that will be processed into neutral atmosphere and space weather products. These derived products will be fed into NOAA’s operational data systems, including weather and space weather analysis and prediction systems, and used for weather, climate, and atmospheric research purposes. All data and products will be archived by NOAA. NOAA seeks the following requirements:

Requirements

Part I - Data Preparation

Requirements for New GNSS-RO Data Providers

For Contractors who have not previously delivered GNSS-RO data to NOAA, the Contractor shall provide all necessary information needed to support NOAA implementation and testing of the Contractor’s data. The Contractor shall provide technical documentation (SBEM IDIQ SOW Section C.4.5.3: Data Delivery and Documentation), including but not limited to data format specifications, sample data, and other information required for data ingestion and processing (SBEM IDIQ SOW Sections C.3.1: Test Data, C.3.1.1: Limited Test Data Deliveries, C.4.5.4: GNSS-RO Test Data). Delivery mechanisms and data handling procedures will be communicated to the Contractor.

The Contractor shall provide engineering support as needed to enable Government acquisition and processing of the supplied datasets to include supporting technical exchanges. The Contractor shall deliver sample data for secure ingest, configuration and testing. Additionally, the Contractor shall deliver up to 48 hours of contiguous near-real-time data for testing of delivery and data flow processes (SBEM IDIQ SOW Sections C.3.1: Test Data, C.3.1.1: Limited Test Data Deliveries, C.4.5.4: GNSS-RO Test Data).

The Period of Performance for Data Preparation shall be for 35 days from December 1, 2026 through January 5, 2027 and shall start and end at 11:00 am Eastern Time. 

Part II - Data Delivery

General Requirements for All Data

Period of Performance for Data Delivery.

For Contractors who have previously provided data to NOAA, the period of performance shall be for 731 days estimated from December 1, 2026 through December 1, 2028 and shall start and end at 11:00 am Eastern Time. 

For Contractors who have not previously provided data to NOAA, the Data Delivery Period of Performance shall immediately follow the Data Preparation Period of Performance and shall be for 696 days estimated from January 5, 2027 through December 1, 2028 and shall start and end at 11:00 am Eastern Time. 

The Offeror shall deliver Level 0 and Level 1a data (SBEM IDIQ SOW Section C.4.5: Delivery Requirements).

Data delivered shall be subject to the terms and conditions specified in SBEM IDIQ SOW Section C.3.7. of the IDIQ contract. NOAA has no additional obligations under the IDIQ contract or this Delivery Order related to data use by third parties. In no event is NOAA liable to the contractor for third party use or release of contractor data. Delivery of the data will utilize one or more of the following Data Rights options:

Option 1:  Right to distribute all Contractor-provided data to any entity immediately after receipt at NOAA with no restrictions on their use or further distribution, under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International license (CC BY 4.0). 

Option 2:  Right to distribute all Contractor-provided data to U.S. Government agencies, International Partners, including but not limited to those responsible for national meteorological, space weather, or hydrological services, and National Meteorological and Hydrological Services, WMO-designated Regional Specialized Meteorological Centers, members of the Coordination Group for Meteorological Satellites, and non-profit entities and academic entities, immediately after receipt at NOAA, for non-commercial use but not for further distribution. 

Option 2A:  In addition to the rights under Option 2, Option 1 rights will apply to all Contractor-provided data beginning at 24 hours after collection. 

Option 3:  Right to distribute all Contractor-provided data to U.S. Government agencies, International Partners, including but not limited to those responsible for national meteorological, space weather, or hydrological services, and National Meteorological and Hydrological Services, WMO-designated Regional Specialized Meteorological Centers, and members of the Coordination Group for Meteorological Satellites, immediately after receipt at NOAA, for non-commercial use but not for further distribution. 

Option 3A:  In addition to the rights under Option 3, Option 1 rights will apply to all Contractor-provided data beginning at 24 hours after collection. 

Spatial distribution is an important aspect of the data delivery requirements. The Government seeks delivery of all global data (all latitudes and longitudes) to meet or exceed the requirements specified in SBEM IDIQ SOW Section C.4.3.2: Specific Geospatial Distributions, paragraphs 1 and 2 only (paragraph 3 will not apply to this task order). 

This SOW includes Desired Capabilities.  Desired Capabilities are features of Offeror provided data that are requested by the Government but are not mandatory.  Desired Capabilities are requested in order to improve the utility of delivered data and are considered to add value to the Offeror proposals.  

Requirement - Neutral Atmosphere Data

The Government seeks a total of 10,000 to 20,000 compliant radio occultation (RO) profiles per day as specified in SBEM IDIQ SOW Sections C.4.3.3: Neutral Atmosphere Data Requirements (Category 1), and C.4.5: Delivery Requirements. 

Desired Capability - Total Electron Content (TEC) Data 

The Government seeks a total of 500 to 1,000 compliant Total Electron Content (TEC) ionospheric tracks per day as specified in SBEM IDIQ SOW Sections C.4.3.5.: Space Weather Data Requirements, C.4.3.5.1.: Requirements for Total Electron Content (TEC), and C.4.5: Delivery Requirements. 

Desired Capability - Temporal Resolution Enhancements

To increase temporal resolution of the Government’s GNSS-RO data collections, the Government seeks RO observations from Sun-Synchronous Orbits (SSO) other than only within the 0800-1200 and 2000-2400 equatorial crossing time ranges and/or from lower-inclination orbits (non-SSO).  The equatorial crossing time is defined as when the space vehicle crosses the Earth’s equatorial plane.  This Temporal Resolution Enhancement data will be included as part of the total number of profiles in Part II, Section II of this SOW. The Contractor is requested to provide the number of compliant temporal resolution enhancement RO profiles they can deliver within each proposed local time window and/or from each lower-inclined orbit (for satellites not in SSO).

While currently a desired capability, NOAA views the diversification of equatorial orbital crossings and increased temporal sampling over the tropics and subtropics as a high-priority strategic objective. The Government intends to use this data to validate requirements for anticipated mandatory coverage in future Task Orders.

Requirement Deliverables - Operational Status Reporting

The Contractor shall deliver information reports as specified in the SBEM IDIQ SOW Section C.3.3. Notifications. Additionally,

The Contractor shall deliver these information reports no later than the 7 calendar days after the end of each 3-month reporting period (e.g., Mar 1st, Jun 1st, Sep 1st, Dec 1st).

The Contractor shall inform the Government within 24 hours of any anomalies that adversely affect contractual data delivery requirements and provide an estimated time of repair.

On January 18, 2017, the Access Board issued a final rule that updated accessibility 
requirements covered by Section 508 and refreshed guidelines for telecommunications

effect on January 18, 2018.  The revisions and updates to the Section 508-based 
standards and Section 255-based guidelines are intended to ensure that information 
and communication technology (ICT) covered by the respective statutes is accessible to 
and usable by individuals with disabilities. 
 
2.1 SECTION 508 – INFORMATION AND COMMUNICATION TECHNOLOGY (ICT) 
STANDARDS 
 
The Section 508 standards established by the Access Board are incorporated into, and 
made part of all VA orders, solicitations and purchase orders developed to procure ICT.  
These standards are found in their entirety at: Revised 508 Standards and 255 
Guidelines (access-board.gov).  A single PDF file version of the Revised Section 508 
Standards and 255 Guidelines will be supplied upon request, or can be obtained from 
the Access Board website.  Federal agencies must comply with the Rehabilitation Act of 
1973, as amended.
