STATEMENT OF WORK 
 
 1.0 Scope 
This Statement of Work (SOW) sets forth the requirements of non-personal professional 
support services in the areas of: security program support and compliance for the protection of 
personnel, information, and assets in addition to providing customer service consisting of 
project management, continuous improvement, and Security Education Training Awareness 
(SETA) activities in support of Naval Surface Warfare Center, Crane Division (NSWC Crane).   
In addition support shall include the performance of the following tasking: Security Functional 
& Compliance Support, Information Security (Infosec) Support, Personnel Security (Persec) 
Support, Security Education, Training, And Awareness (Seta) Support, Industrial Security 
(Indusec) Support, Insider Threat Support, Physical Security (Physec) Support, Emergency 
Management Support, Communications Security (Comsec) Support, Special Security Office (Sso) 
Support, Sensitive Activity & Intelligence-Related Contracting Support, Operations Security 
(Opsec) Support, Visitor And Access Control Support, Security Coordinator, and Security 
Respose Team Support Service. This Task Order (TO) supports organizations and projects base-
wide and is pertinent to the Corporate Operations Security Division, and their customers at 
NSWC Crane. 
The Contractor may be required to perform work at the Top Secret (TS)/Sensitive 
Compartmented Information (SCI) level.  The Contract shall have the ability to receive clearance 
for unescorted access to Government Owned Controlled Spaces.  Access to TS/SCI will be for 
the purpose of site survey, installation, maintenance, and repairs of security and infrastructure 
protection equipment in support of the mission critically systems at Government facilities. 
1.1 Background 
NSWC Crane is a world class Naval Installation providing technical solutions to the Department 
of Defense. The secured installation is located in southwest Indiana and covers approximately 
100 square miles. NSWC Crane provides comprehensive leadership and support for complex 
military systems spanning development, deployment and sustainment in three mission areas: 
Electronic Warfare/Information Operations, Strategic Missions, and Special Missions. NSWC 
Crane leverages its unique technical capabilities and those of industry partners to provide rapid 
response technical solutions to meet the mission of the warfighter.   
NSWC Crane Security Division provides security policy and program management to all focus 
areas within NSWC Crane.

The Contractor shall provide qualified personnel that will support NSWC Crane in the 
execution of their overall organizational functions and the specific missions of the 
individual activities as listed herein of this SOW.   
The Contractor shall execute the scope of work in a manner that provides for high 
quality, timely, and well-integrated support services while incorporating the proper mix

represent the Government nor appear to represent the Government in performance of 
these contract services.  All analyses, reports, data, and deliverable produced under this 
contract shall be property of the United States (U.S.) Government. 
The Contractor shall provide support for a variety of Security programs.  Services may be 
provided on site at NSWC Crane or at the Contractor’s facility.  This SOW has been 
organized by Task Areas which supports the scope of work under 1.0 and the Corporate 
Operations Security Division.  
Estimated on-site/off-site labor hours are delineated in the Level-Of-Effort attached 
hereto.  Distance support and place of performance is described in paragraph 6.1 of this 
SOW. 
3.1 Functional Performance Requirements 
3.1.1 Security Division Functional & Compliance Support (TASK AREA 1) 
3.1.1.1 The Contractor shall provide management and operational support including office 
management, meeting and event coordination, preparation of documents and 
presentations, distribution of information, metrics management, and logistics support. 
The Contractor shall perform scheduling and organizing of meetings, events and 
conferences including conference rooms and other spaces required to implement the 
activity.  The Contractor shall support the visitor request process to ensure authorized 
and appropriate personnel are allowed access to buildings and spaces.  The Contractor 
shall provide support for personnel moves by completing required paperwork and 
monitoring progress. The Contractor shall maintain the inventory and track the office 
supplies and shall initiate replenishment efforts with the appropriate Government 
entity. 
3.1.1.2 The Contractor shall support the planning for and organization of events, ceremonies, 
trade shows and meetings, which will typically include coordination with and support to 
the Security Division as the lead for event management at NSWC Crane. 
3.1.1.3 The Contractor shall develop, deliver, and maintain records of correspondence including 
memos, letters, announcements, and other types of communiques.  The Contractor 
shall prepare and analyze various types of documents including property passes, visit

requests, naval messages, passports, Crane internal memos, and off station letters.  The 
Contractor shall assign sequential numbers for various documents and correspondence 
using an established number tracking system.  The Contractor shall perform document 
and form preparation, review, submission, and tracking.  The Contractor shall develop,

perform distribution of information across organizations via paper documents, email,

data.  This data consists of items such as business records, management type 
information; and engineering drawings, manuals, and other technical documents for 
which hard copy or magnetic media masters are to be retained.  The Contractor shall 
receive documents, maintain an automated logging system, copy each document on the 
media available for protection on a sequential number system, remove and release 
documents as requested, maintain a record or master of copy holders, provide 
reproduction and distribution, and perform other librarian type tasks.  Distribution tasks 
require packaging, labeling, and mailing or otherwise shipping single or multiple 
documents to single or multiple locations within or outside the Government. 
3.1.1.5 The Contractor shall support the records management programs performing as the 
formal and appointed Records Liaison or alternate as requested.  The Contractor shall 
perform document and records management support by maintaining document lists 
and inventories, evaluating document format and content, updating and editing 
documents and information, and developing new documents as requested.  The 
Contractor shall develop and execute policies, practices, and processes to assist in 
managing the full data lifecycle of data, records, and information.  The Contractor shall 
support the formatting, controlling, and tracking of records in the formal records 
management template, format, and tools including the Corporate Document 
Management System.  The Contractor shall perform accounting of documents and 
assessing the status and retention and disposition requirements and take actions to 
accomplish goals and actions. 
3.1.1.6 The Contractor shall, as requested, provide facility and safety support to include 
entering, tracking, and identifying, and reporting information.  The Contractor shall 
perform as the point of contact for Public Works and the Naval Facilities Command

PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT   
 
Protective Intelligence Practical Exercise Interview Training 
 
Part 1 
 
GENERAL INFORMATION 
 
 
1. INTRODUCTION: 
The United States Secret Service (USSS) James J. Rowley Training Center (RTC) 
provides all specialized training for USSS Special Agents and Secret Service Police 
Officers.  The mission is to prepare USSS Special Agents and Police Officers to deal 
with subjects who directly have an interest or nexus to the people we protect.  These 
individuals typically live with mental illness requiring our Special Agents and Police 
Officers to understand the fundamentals of various mental illnesses, how these affect a 
person’s perception of reality and how to communicate with these persons effectively. 
 
These Protective Intelligence (PI) skills require that Special Agents and Police 
Officers understand and be able to employ a variety of specialized investigative tools 
and techniques.  Among these is the ability to interview PI subjects, the individuals 
whose threats, unusual direction of interest and inappropriate behaviors place them at 
the center of PI investigations.     
 
Special Agents and Uniformed Division officers must possess specialized interviewing 
skills that are highlighted by two important facts. First, the primary objective of U.S. 
Secret Service protective intelligence investigations is to render a sound evaluation of 
a subject’s risk of unwanted outcome. This requires that Special Agents and 
Uniformed Division officers execute protective intelligence interviews in a manner 
that differs in key aspects from traditional criminal interrogations. Second, most U.S. 
Secret Service protective intelligence subjects live with mental illness. This requires 
that Special Agents and Uniformed Division officers understand the fundamentals of 
various mental illnesses, how these affect a person’s perception of reality, and how to 
communicate with these people effectively. 
                     
  
1.1 Scope:  
This is a non-personal services contract/order to provide contractor services to instruct 
protective intelligence practical exercise interview training as part of the USSS protective 
intelligence basic and advance training program. This procurement is for a primary 
instructor (psychologist) and a secondary instructor (psycho dramatist).  
 
The contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, 
tools, materials, supervision, and other items of non-personal services necessary to 
perform lectures, demonstrations, and psycho dramatic roles at RTC facilities as defined 
in this Performance Work Statement except for those items specified as Government 

2 
 
Furnished Property (GFP) and services.  The contractor shall accomplish all lectures, 
demonstrations, and psycho dramatic roles on the dates scheduled, within the times 
allotted 
 
1.2.  Specific Tasks: 
The contracted psychologist and psycho dramatist will provide all academic knowledge, 
skills and experiences along with goods or services produced such as research reports, 
curriculum development, lecture notes, or educational data sets, demonstrations of 
potential interviews or encounters with subjects displaying various mental illnesses and 
practical exercises or lectures on how to handle such encounters, to USSS Special Agents 
and Police Officers.     
 
1.2.1.  Basic Services:  
Contractors shall provide their own transportation to and from RTC at their expense 
along with lecture notes, Power Point handouts, and any lecture material.  Contractors 
will also provide their own costumes, make up, appearance modification disguises, props, 
or any item carried or worn specifically to develop their character(s).  
 
1) Protective Intelligence Simulations – Special Agent Training Course (SATC)   
• Duration: 2-DAY Course (A & B Sessions, 8 hours each) Total of 16 hours = 1 
Class 
• Number of Students in attendance per session/class: Maximum of 24 Students 
Total 
    
The objective of this course of instruction is to provide SATC recruits an opportunity to 
deepen their understanding of the protective intelligence threat assessment process and 
cultivate their skills at interviewing and assessing protective intelligence subjects. This 
will be accomplished through brief classroom instruction at the start of class, and through 
several distinct simulated protective intelligence interview scenarios. The primary 
instructor will facilitate instruction, including instruction at the start of class, and 
coach/guide recruits during the simulated protective intelligence interviews. The 
secondary instructor (Psycho dramatist) will portray the protective intelligence subjects 
during the simulated interviews and provide feedback at the conclusion of the training 
class. The primary instructor must have conducted numerous mental health evaluations 
and treatment of mentally ill patients suffering from various disorders to include 
Schizophrenia, Bipolar Mood Disorder, and Antisocial Disorder. The secondary 
instructor or psycho-dramatist will portray the roles in the simulated protective 
intelligence interviews. He or she must be trained to the standards of the American Board 
of Examiners in Psychodrama and Sociometry and must have experience working in a 
law enforcement environment, portraying persons who live with a variety of mental 
illnesses. 
 
A ‘stop-action’ coaching methodology will be employed by the primary and secondary 
instructor during the simulated protective intelligence interviews. This will give the 
primary instructor the opportunity to provide Special Agent recruits with real-time 
feedback during the practical exercises. It will also allow the primary instructor to replace 

3 
 
the recruits conducting the interview, thereby allowing all recruits the chance to 
participate in the simulated protective intelligence interviews.  
 
All simulated protective intelligence interviews will be observed by the entire class. The 
recruits’ participation in the simulated interviews will serve as the catalyst for the 
primary instructor to speak with recruits about the information learned during the 
interviews, strategies for case management, and related considerations. The recruits’ 
participation in the simulated interviews will also serve as the catalyst for RTC PI Section 
staff to provide recruits operational guidance regarding how the simulated PI interview 
scenarios would be managed in the real world.   
  
This class will be delivered to a maximum of 24 total Special Agent recruits over the 
course of two days. One group of 12 recruits will receive instruction on the first day, and 
the second group of 12 recruits will receive instruction on the second day. This two-day 
format will allow all 24 students to participate in the simulated interviews and associated 
discussions regarding case management. 
 
Each simulated interview will be designed by the primary and/or secondary instructor 
with input from RTC PI program staff. 
 
The primary and secondary instructors must possess sufficient versatility in the 
facilitation of instruction and portrayal of the roles to allow for adjustments to meet the 
individual learning needs of the recruits.  To this end, the primary and secondary 
instructors must have a thorough understanding of the concept of protective intelligence, 
coupled with an in-depth appreciation of the behavioral analysis approach to protective 
intelligence investigations. 
 
As a caveat to the above requirements, the primary instructor shall be responsible for 
providing the RTC PI Section with suitable replacements if the primary and/or secondary 
instructor are not available to instruct an SATC class as scheduled.  The replacements are 
expected to possess credentials and a level of experience suitable for a law enforcement 
training environment.  The replacements will be compensated by the primary instructor 
as subcontractors, and no additional payment for this service will be provided by the U.S. 
Secret Service. The replacement instructors must be able to pass a background 
investigation to gain access to U.S. Secret Service facilities and information.  RTC PI 
Section management reserves the right to vet the academic credentials presented by the 
replacement primary and/or secondary instructors, including their psycho-dramatist 
credentials, prior to a scheduled class.  The primary instructor will provide the RTC PI 
Section staff sufficient notice of his or her intention to use a replacement or replacements 
to allow the RTC PI Section staff an opportunity to complete the vetting process and 
arrange for proper security clearances for the individual. 
    
The primary and/or secondary instructor shall work with RTC PI Section staff to create 
and/or update and/or modify the interview scenarios periodically to ensure their 
timeliness and relevance.

SECTION B - CONTINUATION OF SF 1449 BLOCKS

B.1  IDIQ CONTRACT ADMINISTRATION DATA

B.1.1 Contract Administration: 

All contract administration matters will be handled by the following individuals:

a.  CONTRACTOR:  	TBD

b.  GOVERNMENT:		Contracting Officer 36C10X

Strategic Acquisition Center – Frederick

Department of Veterans Affairs

5202 Presidents Court, Suite 103

Frederick MD 21703

Roles and Responsibilities

The IDIQ CO is responsible for providing overall scope oversight, maintaining communication between Contractors and VA, ensuring contract compliance, administering base contract and modifications, and ensuring that annual performance evaluations are completed at the base contract level. Each task order (TO) will have an identified COR who will be responsible for ensuring that task orders are within the scope of the IDIQ base contracts, administering all task order awards, overseeing payment or rejection of invoices, and ensuring that annual performance evaluations are completed at the TO level.

CO and COR Authority

The CO reserves the right to designate a Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR) at the IDIQ contract or individual task order level. The CO will issue a designation letter to the COR and the Contractor to ensure that all parties understand the limited authority of the COR. The COR will also be responsible for overseeing payment of invoices after acceptance of work. Only a warranted CO is authorized to make changes to the terms and conditions, scope, price, or period of performance of the contract or any TO. The COR and any other Government representative are not authorized to obligate the Government or modify the contract or any TO.

Task Order and Delivery-Order Ombudsman

In accordance with VAAR 816.505(b)(8), the task-order and delivery-order ombudsman for VA is the Associate Executive Director for Procurement Policy, Systems and Oversight, Office of Acquisition and Logistics. The VA Ombudsman shall review and resolve complaints from Contractors concerning all task and delivery order actions and, if corrective action is needed, will provide a written determination of such action to the CO. Contractors are encouraged to first address any concerns with the CO before contacting the Ombudsman. COs will be notified of any complaints submitted to the VA Ombudsman.

B.1.2 Task Order Procedures

General

Contractors under the IDIQ shall provide services as requirements are identified throughout the ordering period. The ordering period of the contract is a 5-year period from date of award, inclusive of a base period and four (4) one-year option periods. This ordering period coincides directly with the stated period of performance in the IDIQ Performance Work Statement. When the term or services are extended under FAR 52.217-8 or 52.217-9 respectively, the ordering period is considered to be extended as well.

Each requirement will specify details as they relate to deliverables, performance, and other technical items. Contractors may be required to use the Acquisition Task Order Management System (ATOMS), an automated system that facilitates pre‑award and post‑award communications and oversight for VA enterprise multi‑award IDIQ contracts, for all task orders. Specific instructions for use of ATOMS, if required, will be provided by the CO in the Task Order Proposal Request (TOPR) or separate guidance.

This Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract will utilize a decentralized ordering approach. Task orders may be issued from both the Veterans Health Administration (VHA) Office of Healthcare Technology Management (HTM) ordering officials and Strategic Acquisition Center (SAC) contracting officers, provided they are acting within the scope of their authority and this contract. The Government will determine the appropriate ordering activity for each task order. Activities authorized to place orders against this IDIQ contract include all Strategic Acquisition Center (SAC) COs. The Government reserves the right to expand this ordering authority to other activities when appropriate and beneficial.

Ordering and fair opportunity

(1) The IDIQ will follow ordering procedures as outlined in Revolutionary FAR Overhauled (RFO) FAR 16.507. The CO will provide all awardees a fair opportunity to be considered for all awards under the IDIQ which exceed the micro‑purchase threshold, unless one of the exceptions in RFO FAR 16.507-6 applies. If such an exception applies, the CO will execute the task order as a sole‑source task order and prepare the required justification in accordance with FAR and agency procedures.

Under this multiple award IDIQ contract, one or more blanket purchase agreements (BPAs) may be established to fill repetitive needs for services using the procedures at RFO FAR 16.507-3 through 16.507-5. When established, BPA recipients will be provided fair opportunity to compete for orders (calls) against the BPAs. 

TOPR issuance and competition

(1) For each requirement, the CO will provide all awardees a fair opportunity to be considered by issuing a brief request for quote (RFQ). The RFQ will typically include the Performance Work Statement (PWS), period of performance, place of performance, and any other necessary information. A formal solicitation document or detailed evaluation criteria will not be required for task order issuance. As requirements for the TOPR are defined, the CO will determine the evaluation factors and issue a solicitation. Contractors will be given the fair opportunity to compete for task order awards, assuming one of the exceptions noted above does not exist. Contractors unable to perform the requirements as stated in a TOPR must submit a “no‑bid” to the CO with a brief, yet specific, explanation. Repeated failure to provide a response will be reflected in past performance evaluations at the IDIQ level and may be taken into consideration when deciding whether or not to exercise options.

(2) Contractors shall submit a price quote in response to the RFQ. Quotes may include labor categories, labor hours, and corresponding rates as necessary to support the proposed price. Each TOPR will include, at a minimum:

The due date and instructions for proposal submission,

A Statement of Work (SOW), Statement of Objectives (SOO), or Performance Work Statement (PWS) with a description of the requirements, including deliverables, minimum qualifications, and applicable information,

The place and period of performance, and

Any additional information deemed necessary by the CO.

(3) The Government will evaluate price only for each RFQ. Task orders will be awarded to the Contractor whose quote represents the lowest‑priced, technically acceptable solution based on the requirements described in the PWS. The CO may determine technical acceptability based solely on confirmation that the quoted services meet the requirements stated in the PWS. No adjectival ratings, formal evaluation plans, or narrative technical evaluations will be used. Each TOPR will have a unique evaluation plan that will be developed by the CO. Factors, with the exception of Price, will be assigned an adjectival rating. In general, TOPRs may be evaluated by analysis of the following factors:

Technical Capability: The Contractor will be asked to discuss their plan for accomplishing the work of the requirement. This factor may include subfactors such as a management plan, staffing plan, or key personnel.

Past Performance: The Contractor will be asked to provide narratives of recent and relevant references and past performance questionnaires which confirm the level of quality. The CO may consider relevant performance on task order awards under this IDIQ and any other information available from Government sources.

Price: The Government will evaluate price reasonableness using price analysis techniques as prescribed in RFO FAR 15.404-1(b). When competing for Labor Hour type TO awards, Contractors are permitted to propose labor rates that are equal to or lower than those as listed in their contract. The Government will ensure that rates are not reduced to a level that risks nonperformance by requiring justification for the reduced rate at the time of proposal. Contractors may be requested to identify labor categories, number of hours, and labor rates in their price proposal for performance of each task.  

Any other factors as determined appropriate by the CO.

Resumes for Key Personnel are required at the task order level to verify that proposed personnel meet the minimum qualification requirements. Although task orders will be evaluated on an LPTA, price‑only basis, the Government must still confirm that personnel meet the required qualifications to perform the work described in the PWS. Resumes will be reviewed solely to confirm that personnel meet the requirements on a pass/fail basis and will not be scored.

The CO is not required to prepare formal evaluation plans, evaluate offers, post notice on the System for Award Management (SAM) webpage or hold discussions or negotiations with each offeror. The CO will, however, maintain an internal record of the award decision and supporting information, including the rationale for placement and price of each order, consistent with RFO FAR 16.507 documentation requirements.

In accordance with RFO FAR 16.507-2(a)(2), the CO has broad discretion in determining which Contractor should be awarded a task order. The CO will issue a task order to the Contractor whose proposal is most advantageous to the Government considering the evaluation factors specified in the TOPR. The CO reserves the right to withdraw or cancel the TOPR. In such event, the Contractor will be notified, via email, of the CO’s decision. This decision shall be final and conclusive and shall not be subject to the Disputes Clause or the Contract Disputes Act.

Upon TO award, the TO will be sent via email to the Contractor. The Contractor is not authorized at any time to commence TO performance prior to issuance of a signed TO or other written approval provided by a CO. The Contractor’s failure to begin performance within the time frame required may result in termination of the task order and reconsideration of the other task order proposals received in response to the TOPR.

Task orders may only be modified by written modification, executed by a warranted CO.  The Contractor shall not perform or provide services that are not expressly stated in the contract or TO. Each work order issued will always be within scope of the awarded task order it falls under. A work order is a written direction issued by the Local COR (L‑COR) that provides additional detail, clarification, or instructions for specific services already covered under an awarded task order. A work order does not add new scope, change pricing, or modify the terms of the task order. Instead, it breaks down the TO-level requirements into more discrete, actionable assignments so the contractor can perform the services when the specific need arises. Work orders are administrative instruments used to manage and execute the requirements within the task order--they are not separate contracts, task orders, or modifications, and they cannot be used to add new work. All work orders must remain fully within the scope of the parent task order.

(2) Upon completion of work order services, a review and/or examination and a determination of acceptance will be made by the TO COR. Acceptance at the work‑order level will be documented in accordance with ordering‑office procedures and retained in the TO file.

B.1.4 Minimum Guaranteed Amount and Maximum Value

Orders beyond the minimum will be determined by department needs and the results of fair opportunity competitions, other than exceptions referenced in RFO FAR 16.507-6. The Government has no obligation to award TOs beyond the minimum guaranteed amount. 

Maximum Aggregate Value

The maximum aggregate value of all contract awards and task orders under this IDIQ contract is $175,000,000.00. This ceiling is neither divided nor multiplied by the number of awardees.

The Government has entered into other contractual relationships in order to provide technical services throughout VA. These services are separate from this IDIQ contract, but may be related to or in close proximity to those provided under this IDIQ contract. Contractors are advised that such access or support may create an Organizational Conflict of Interest (OCI) under FAR Subpart 9.5. Failure to appropriately address an OCI may result in remedies consistent with FAR 9.5, including disqualification from related procurements or termination of this contract.

B.1.7 Options

Any options will be clearly identified in the TOPR, and FAR 52.217‑9 will be incorporated into task orders that contain options. Exercise of options will be effected by unilateral modification issued by a warranted CO and is at the sole discretion of the Government.

U.S. Bureau of Reclamation

Request for MRG – River Eyes Monitoring

Performance Based Work Statement

Background and Introduction

The Bureau of Reclamation (Reclamation), Upper Colorado Basin Region, Albuquerque Area Office, is seeking contractor assistance with up to daily River Eyes monitoring activities in the Middle Rio Grande during periods of potential river intermittency.  The River Eyes program (https://webapps.usgs.gov/MRGESCP/data/river-eyes) is a cooperative interagency monitoring effort established to assist federal and state agencies in complying with 2016 U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (USFWS) Biological Opinion (https://www.fws.gov/southwest/es/NewMexico/BO_MRG.cfm) requirements.  The program provides field observations of conditions that lead to river intermittency and drying.  These field reports, together with U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) stream gauge data and weather conditions, are used to assist USFWS with daily planning of rescue and relocation of stranded Rio Grande Silvery Minnow (RGSM).  The information is also used to assist federal and state water operations and resource managers with managing river flows to reduce the amount and rate of river drying that may occur daily, and coordinating RGSM egg collection efforts for transport to authorized facilities.

Scope

The primary objective of this contract is to provide up to daily monitoring of river conditions to support river managers in their operations when there is the potential for river intermittency, generally from April to October each year.  Monitoring may occur between Cochiti Dam and Elephant Butte Reservoir in the Cochiti, Angostura, Isleta, and San Acacia reaches (see attached map; these areas correspond to the Middle Rio Grande Conservancy District’s Cochiti, Albuquerque, Belen, and Socorro Divisions) when gauged flows indicate that river drying is imminent or has already occurred.  The majority of the work is anticipated to occur in the Isleta and San Acacia reaches.

Key River Eyes activities to be performed by the contractor will include observations of flow intermittency and pool formation, stage readings at established staff gauges, discharge measurements to confirm gauged flows or to determine flows in ungauged portions of the river, photo documentation and GPS surveying of river drying, and other pertinent observations as detailed by task in Section 3.  Following data collection, data shall be compiled and presented in tabular, graphical, and map formats, as appropriate.  Text messages on river conditions and extent of drying will be sent daily, verbal summaries will be provided during operations conference calls, and written notes shall be prepared for every day that field observations are made and distributed via email as soon as possible.  A draft and final summary annual report shall be prepared to compile the data collected.

The Contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, tools, materials, vehicles, supervision, and other items and services necessary to safely complete the tasks defined in this Performance Work Statement.  The Contractor shall perform to the standards in the contract.

Scientific integrity is vital to Department of Interior (DOI) activities under which scientific research, data, summaries, syntheses, interpretations, presentations, and/or publications are developed and used.  Failure to uphold the highest degree of scientific integrity will result not only in potentially flawed scientific results, interpretations, and applications but will damage DOI’s reputation and ability to uphold the public's trust.  All work performed shall comply with the DOI Scientific Integrity Policy posted to https://www.doi.gov/scientificintegrity, or its equivalent as provided by the Contractor's organization or State law.

General Requirements and Information

Contract Administration

The Government will neither supervise Contractor employees nor control the method by which the Contractor performs the required tasks.  Under no circumstances will the Government assign tasks to, or prepare work schedules for, individual Contractor employees.  The Contractor shall manage the timeliness, completeness, and quality of all work performed.  The Contractor shall ensure customer satisfaction and professional and ethical behavior of all Contractor personnel.

The Contractor shall assign work effort and maintain proper and accurate timekeeping records of personnel assigned to work on the project.  The Contractor shall provide administrative support to employees in a timely fashion (e.g., timekeeping, leave processing, pay, emergency needs).

Personnel Qualifications

The Contractor shall provide a contract manager who will be responsible for the performance of the work.  The Contractor shall not employ any person for work on this contract if such employee is considered by the Contracting Officer (CO) to be a potential threat to the health, safety, security, general well-being, or operational mission of Reclamation and its employees.  The Contractor shall not employ any person who is an employee of the U.S. government, if employing that person would create a conflict of interest or the impression of such.

The Contractor shall provide sufficient field staff capable of safely performing the required tasks and the field transportation, data collection, and monitoring equipment needed for monitoring tasks.  The contract manager and field staff, together, must have the following qualifications:

Ability to clearly communicate the results of requested data collection in written and oral formats sufficient for daily texts, emails, operations conference calls, and annual reporting.

Ability to understand, interpret, and present scientific data.

Ability to meet deadlines, stay within budget, and communicate well with others.

Close coordination will be required with other activities on the river including the USFWS-led RGSM fish rescue, egg collection, and interagency water operations.  Depending on river conditions, the Contractor shall participate in water operations calls, which will occur at least weekly but may be daily.  Details pertaining to discrete tasks are outlined below.

Travel

The Contractor shall use the appropriate government rates as posted on www.gsa.gov for mileage costs to perform monitoring work.  No other travel is expected.

Access

The Contractor shall be responsible for obtaining access permissions and keys from various landowners, tribes, and government agencies as appropriate to perform work under this contract.

Training

The Contractor is responsible for all training for its employees.

Performance Period, Schedule, and Locations

The performance period for River Eyes support extends from February 1 for a duration of 12 months, though the work should be complete by January 31 of the following calendar year.  In addition to the Base Period (Year), this contract will include four Option Periods (Years).  Scheduled activities for each period are as follows:

The field season may start as early as March 1 and extend through October 31.  The Contractor may be required to provide services on holidays and weekends.  However, the Contractor may not be allowed access to Pueblo lands on holidays, Pueblo cultural days, or when the tribe declares their lands to be closed.  In these cases, observations above and below Pueblo lands may suffice.

Work may occur in the Cochiti and Angostura reaches, but will most likely only occur in the Isleta and San Acacia reaches of the Rio Grande, with occasional monitoring of the Angostura Reach.  Locations may be difficult to access and muddy.  Use of uncrewed aircraft (drones) is acceptable as long as the Contractor follows U.S. Department of Interior policy (see links in Government Furnished Materials, below) and the drone is capable of providing data collection meeting specifications.

Government Furnished Materials

Reclamation will provide all relevant Reclamation policy and guidance in electronic format within 5 days of contract award, to include the following:

DOI Scientific Integrity Policy (https://www.doi.gov/scientificintegrity)

Reclamation's Safety Handbook and Standards (https://www.usbr.gov/safety/rshs/index.html)

DOI Uncrewed Aircraft Systems Policy Information (https://www.doi.gov/aviation/uas/policy), specifically DOI OPM-11 DOI Use of Uncrewed Aircraft Systems (UAS) (https://www.doi.gov/sites/default/files/documents/2025-01/opm-11_0.pdf)

Contact information for River Eyes participants

GIS data showing field locations and Reclamation’s river miles (RMs)

A template for the draft and final reports for the Contractor to use that will assist Reclamation in making the reports accessible in accordance with Section 508 of the Rehabilitation Act.

Performance Requirements

Although field observations could begin as early as March 1, a more typical start date for field work is mid-April to early May, and in some years, work may not begin until September.  In most years, field work will continue until October 31, but if the river reconnects late in the irrigation season and is expected to remain connected, field observations may be stopped prior to October 31. The meeting may be held virtually, or the Contractor may provide a meeting facility in or near the project area (or it may be held at AAO).  Contractor shall prepare an agenda, have appropriate staff attend, and provide meeting minutes. The acquisition of the supplies/services particular to one manufacturer or company because the 
supplies/services are unique or highly specialized under a Sole Source Justification. 
3. Description of Supplies/Services and Estimated Value 
SWFPAC currently supports a mission-critical 2003 Microsoft Access database which is in need of 
immediate migration to Nintex Automation (a.k.a. K2). Microsoft products no longer support 
2003 Microsoft Access without a separate extended support subscription for Windows 11. 
SSP/SWFPAC’s extended support subscription ends in July 2026, and no further subscriptions 
are authorized, which is driving the requirement for immediate migration of all SWFPAC 
legacy 2003 Microsoft Access databases to Nintex Automation.   SWFPAC requires 
professional assistance to accelerate the migration in order to meet the deadline while 
ensuring required data integrity, database access, and solution operability. 
 
Due to both the critical nature of the data to be transferred and the compressed timeline in 
which the migration must occur, SWFPAC requires professional assistance for the migration 
of its Microsoft Access legacy database to the Nintex Automation product. The knowledge 
and skill required to perform this crucial data migration under a compressed timeframe far 
exceeds that of SWFPAC’s personnel.

FORT PECK SERVICE UNIT INDIAN HEALTH SERVICE                                                                                                                                STATEMENT OF WORK FOR HEALTH INSURANCE VERIFICATION AND CLAIMS MANAGEMENT SERVICES

PROJECT TITLE: Medicare and Private Insurance Claims Management and Insurance Eligibility Services

BACKGROUND/PURPOSE: 

The Mission of the Fort Peck Service Unit is to provide the best possible healthcare services to the Fort Peck Service Unit community members and all other eligible Native Americans.  The purpose of this contract is to enhance and to maximize third party revenue and collection activities for the business aspect of health care and its revenue generation activities. 

The Fort Peck Service Unit aims to create an efficient, streamlined process for claims management and insurance eligibility verification services through the vendor, Inovalon Provider Inc. To meet this mission, the Fort Peck Indian Health Service has identified a need for an online claims management and eligibility verification software to provide a centralized service for billing services and to track revenue generation. 

The vendor will provide technology that identified third party eligibility information and workflow plus Medicare AR reporting and workflow for the Fort Peck Service Unit. The need to verify eligibility for the various health insurance programs in real time will enhance operations for the business aspect of health care. Effective services for both Medicare and Private Insurance claims will keep the hospital on top of capturing reimbursement dollars from the patient’s initial point of service. These services make an impact on the reduction of staff overtime costs and will drastically reduce the need for follow-up of the claims denied.

The Fort Peck Service Unit requires an application that will provide daily Medicare AR report for efficient account management. These services shall follow HIPAA, IHS OIT mandates, and the Privacy Act. 

  

SCOPE: 

The contract shall:

Attain comprehensive eligibility information– make eligibility requests to Medicare and commercial (Private Insurance) payors.

Perform batch eligibility checks – determine eligibility status for multiple patients at one time.

Better manage workflow with a customizable dashboard that prioritizes and assigns patients, payers and daily task lists. The application allows user to set up reminders and notes to staff at multiple locations. 

Experience integration between eligibility and claims functions. 

Eliminate repetitive tasks with the ability to run multiple payers and patients in one session.

Increase efficiency when checking eligibility – verify a patient’s eligibility status with multiple payers.

Save significant time using batch imports of eligibility data files. 

Enhance record-keeping with access to all eligibility transaction history.

The contractor shall provide a secure exchange data software solution that provides technology for:

Connectivity to the Medicare DDE (Direct Data Entry/FISS (Fiscal Intermediary Standard System) and automated claims status reporting, payment floor details and other reports

Eligibility verification for third party payers to include Medicare

Eligibility results must include start and end dates of coverage

Capability to search eligibility for third party coverage for patients

Third party insurance medical claims validation, approval and processing services via a clearinghouse for Medicare, Medicaid, VA and Commercial Payers for the Fort Belknap Service Unit

Processes all claim types: Emergency, Inpatient, Outpatient and Specialty Clinics; and provide both solicited and unsolicited claims status

The software must provide rigorous and thorough claims rules and business custom rules

Capability for self-monitoring usage of services for thresholds

Training and support related to scope of work-training provided either on-site or via teleconference

The software services shall comply with the following constraints:

The software service shall not require the Fort Peck Service Unit to install contractor software within the Fort Peck Service Unit or Indian Health Service network.

The service shall enable the Fort Peck Service Unit to exchange data utilizing a Secure File Transfer Protocol (SFTP) as approved by the Indian Health Service Office of Information Technology.

The service shall support Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) transactions and interactive Telnet application protocol sessions.

The service shall support unlimited users and access shall be workstation independent.

The service shall not entail development of Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) transaction set translation or mapping processes, non-CMS or non-IHS generated data or messages, or data reformatting. 

APPLICABLE DOCUMENTS:  

Secure internet-based connectivity to all current fiscal intermediaries.

Ability to send medical emergency, Inpatient, Outpatient, and Specialty claims to Medicare Contractor and other Payers using secure date exchange technology.

Unlimited Direct Data Entry (DDE) online Medicare claims status/corrections for Medicare Part A.

All electronic transactions and DDE/FISS shall provide confidentiality, authentication, integrity and non-repudiation.

Automated batch 837/835 file transfers.

Automated batch 276/277 claims status capability.

Accept electronic claims from Resource Patient Management System (RPMS).

Reports and acknowledgements on all claims sent.

TASKS:  

Simple user-friendly interface with a single sign-on login and ID. Eligibility verification for hundreds of payers, with information that includes co-pays, termination dates, deductibles and coinsurance 

Consistent data displays of response results by payer class 

Quick batch entry – check eligibility status for multiple patients with a single payer 

Multiple insurance eligibility verification – check a patient’s eligibility status at multiple insurance plans simultaneously 

Alerts to indicate other coverage for Medicare patients – instances of HMO enrollment, dual eligibility, Medicare as a Secondary Payer, and many more admissions scenarios are brought to the attention of designated personnel 

Ability to filter Service Type Code (STC) queries and responses and save your favorites, organized by payer 

All-payer eligibility access 24/7 – easily verify data after hours and on weekends 

Storage of all validation transactions for historical proof of eligibility status when eligibility is challenged retroactively 

Flexible revalidation option for either an individual patient or batch without having to rekey demographic data 

Option to run recurring batches for your patient census to regularly monitor insurance coverage 

Easy implementation, with minimal IT involvement – ABILITY web-based services are compatible with current versions of industry-leading browsers

DELIVERABLES AND DELIVERY SCHEDULE: 

Provide a single secure electronic location to manage all electronic claims, including VA claims.  

Verify Medicare and Commercial Payer eligibility in real time and batches.

Provide knowledgeable support personnel to assist with any issues regarding the processing of the medical claims.

The Contractor shall provide toll free telephone/technical support during normal business hours, 7 AM to 7 PM, Monday thru Friday, except Government holidays.

The Contractor shall provide a two (2) hour minimum response time from notification by IHS at no additional cost to the Fort Belknap Service Unit.

The medical claim processing services shall meet the following standards:

Third party insurance medical claims shall be submitted to the appropriate carrier/payer via the Contractor provided clearinghouse by the close of the next business day after receipt from IHS.

Third Party Insurance medical shall be transmitted electronically to the appropriate carrier/payer.

The Contractor shall use routine editing procedures to detect defects in medical claims information supplied by the government.  The Contractor shall reject and not process all medical claims with defects.  The Contractor shall provide the service location with edit status reports listing the defect to aid the service location in the correction of the detected defects.  

The Contractor shall provide for correction all claims rejected by all the carriers/payers for any reason other than the inappropriate format to the claims.

The Contractor shall provide the capability for medical claim errors to be corrected and resubmitted electronically and provide a report of rejected medical claims within 4 hours of batch submission.

The Contractor shall make available productivity and submission reports within 24 hours of batch transmission.

GOVERNMENT-FURNISHED EQUIPMENT AND INFORMATION:  

Secure internet-based connectivity to all current fiscal intermediaries.

Ability to send medical emergency, Inpatient, Outpatient, and Specialty claims to Medicare Contractor using secure date exchange technology.

Unlimited Direct Data Entry (DDE) online Medicare claims status/corrections for Medicare Part A.

All electronic transactions and DDE/FISS shall provide confidentiality, authentication, integrity and non-repudiation.

Automated batch 837/835 file transfers.

Automated batch 276/277 claims status capability.

Accept electronic claims from Resource Patient Management System (RPMS).

Reports and acknowledgements on all claims sent.

PLACE OF PERFORMANCE:  

Fort Peck Service Unit 107 H. Street, Poplar MT.   59255 via online insurance verification software access

PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE:  Base Year  04/01/2026 to 03/31/2027 

Plus 4 option years

SECURITY:  

Secure internet-based connectivity to all current fiscal intermediaries.

Solicitations for supplies and services shall require the submission of a Section 5085 Product Assessment Template. The template can be found at https://www.itic/org/policy/accessibility/vpat.

1.0.  SCOPE OF WORK: The contractor shall provide all management, transportation, tools, 
supplies, , and labor necessary to provide the Joint Enabling Capabilities Command (JECC) with 
one (1) Manpower and Personnel Staff Representative to perform expert analysis, strategic 
guidance, and direct execution of human relations (HR) tasks by integrating best practice from 
military and civilian human capital programs to support the JECC J1 mission.  The contractor 
shall provide one (1) qualified Special Security Representative (SSR) to assist the J2 Special 
Security Officer (SSO) and security team in the administration of all related security functions.  
The contractor shall provide two (2) Assessments Support Analysts for the JECC J3 to 
effectively direct mid and long-term capability allocation; improve the quality of, and accelerate, 
staff and commander decision cycles; and reduce overall risk for the organization through 
rigorous, focused assessments support services.  The contractor shall provide one (1) qualified 
Safety and Airborne Operations Program Manager to ensure the implementation of a 
comprehensive Safety and Occupational Health (SOH) program that protects military and 
civilian personnel, prevents accidental loss of resources, and ensures compliance with all 
applicable regulations.  All labor necessary is to be performed from the JECC at Norfolk Naval 
Base, Norfolk, VA while supporting subordinate commands: Joint Planning Support Element 
(JPSE) located at Norfolk Naval Base, Norfolk, VA and Joint Communications Support Element 
(JCSE) located at MacDill Air Force Base, Tampa, Florida.    
 
2.0. DESCRIPTION OF SERVICES: The contractor shall perform the tasks and furnish the 
services articulated herein, ensuring that all actions align with the highest standards of 
professional conduct and the specific requirements of this statement.

2.1 Manpower and Personnel Staff Representative:  The contractor shall provide one (1) full-
time qualified contractor to perform the following tasks to support the strategic human 
resources needs of JECC J1: 
2.1.1. Strategic Workforce Planning & Management 
• Provide analysis and recommendations to support the alignment of manpower and 
personnel programs with organizational goals and future mission requirements. The 
contractor shall conduct research on best practices and propose strategic frameworks for 
leadership consideration.

branding, and outreach. 
o Developing data-driven recommendations and conceptual frameworks to enhance 
personnel retention.

in hiring, position management, or any other inherently governmental functions.

organizational structures to identify opportunities for enhanced operational effectiveness 
and resource optimization 
2.1.2.    Policy Analysis and Joint Compliance 
• Analyze joint and service-specific personnel policies, instructions, and regulations. Based 
on this analysis, the contractor shall develop and propose recommendations for 
command-level policy modifications. The purpose of these recommendations is to 
provide government leadership with options for improving organizational efficiency and 
effectiveness. 
• Provide subject matter expertise and advisory support regarding Department of War 
(DoW), U.S. Transportation Command (USTRANSCOM), Joint Staff, and Service 
Component regulations. The contractor shall: 
• Review proposed or existing command HR initiatives and provide an analysis of their 
alignment with higher headquarters policy and regulations. 
• Serve as an expert resource to government personnel by interpreting complex regulatory 
language and providing comparative analysis of compliance practices across different 
organizations. 
• Note: The ultimate responsibility for ensuring regulatory compliance and the direction of 
all HR activities remains an inherently governmental function. 
2.1.3.   Joint Manpower and Billet Management 
• Joint Manning Document (JMD) Management: Actively manage the command's JMD, 
including validating, creating, and modifying billet requirements. Process Joint Table of 
Distribution (JTD) change requests and coordinates with higher headquarters to ensure 
100% billet accuracy. 
• Manning Analysis and Forecasting: Conduct comprehensive manning analysis across all 
assigned and attached units, identifying critical vacancies, personnel gaps, and skill 
imbalances. Provide data-driven recommendations and predictive analysis to leadership 
to mitigate manning shortfalls and support future operations.

• Multi-Service Evaluation Systems: Serve as the command's subject matter expert on the 
various service-specific evaluation systems (e.g., Army Officer Evaluation 
Report/Noncommissioned Officer Evaluation Report (OER/NCOER), Navy Fitness 
Report/Evaluation (FITREP/EVAL), Air Force Officer Performance Report/Enlisted 
Performance Report (OPR/EPR). Provide authoritative guidance and quality control for 
all reports to ensure accuracy and compliance with each service's standards. 
• Awards and Decorations Program: Manage the command’s Joint awards program. This 
includes processing recommendations for Joint Service awards (e.g., Defense Meritorious 
Service Medal (DMSM), Joint Service Commendation Medal (JSCM), Joint Service 
Achievement Medal (JSAM), reviewing submissions for accuracy, managing award 
quotas, and ensuring compliance with DoW and command policies. 
2.1.5.  Data Analysis and Reporting 
• Conduct advanced statistical analysis of workforce trends, readiness metrics, and 
demographic data to provide actionable, predictive insights to senior leadership. 
• Prepare and present comprehensive, senior-level reports and briefings on manpower 
status, personnel program performance, and strategic human capital initiatives. 
2.1.6.  HR Systems and Liaison Duties 
• Force Management and Tracking System (FMTS) Support: The contractor shall possess 
subject matter expertise in FMTS to provide data analysis and advisory support to 
government leadership. Responsibilities include: 
• Extracting and analyzing data to develop reports on personnel status, mobilization trends, 
and the alignment of personnel with operational requirements. 
• Identifying and documenting potential data discrepancies for government review and 
resolution. 
• Providing technical and functional expertise to government users to assist their 
management of the system. 
• Joint HR Systems Analysis: The contractor shall maintain proficiency in authorized joint 
and military personnel systems (e.g., DIHRS, service-specific databases) to extract data 
and perform analysis. The contractor will not be granted access to the Defense Civilian 
Personnel Data System (DCPDS) or any other system used for managing civilian 
personnel actions. Support includes: 
• Aggregating and synthesizing data from various sources to create comprehensive 
personnel reports. 
• Providing analysis on personnel trends and metrics to inform government decision-
making. 
• Liaison Support to Service Components: The contractor shall serve as a technical 
facilitator to assist in the resolution of complex, service-specific personnel, pay, and 
entitlement issues. The contractor shall:

General Information 
 
Document Type: Sources Sought Notice

DESCRIPTION OF SOURCES SOUGHT 
 
The purpose of this notice is to identify potential sources for addition to the general pool of Blanket 
Purchase Agreements (BPAs) of Board approved entities with expertise as actuaries or in underwriting 
of insurance policies to serve as reviewers of policies; In accordance with 7 USC CHAPTER 36, 
SUBCHAPTER I: FEDERAL CROP INSURANCE and 7 USC 1508: Crop insurance. 
 
The Risk Management Agency (RMA) of the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) is 
responsible for supervision of the Federal Crop Insurance Corporation (FCIC), administration and 
oversight of programs authorized under the Federal Crop Insurance Act (7 U.S.C. 1501 et. seq.), any 
pilot or other program involving revenue insurance, risk management education, risk management 
savings accounts; the uses of the futures market to manage risk and support farm income that may be 
established under the Federal Crop Insurance Act or other law; and, other programs the Secretary of 
Agriculture considers appropriate. The Agricultural Risk Protection Act of 2000 modified the Federal 
Crop Insurance Act to: 
 
1) Require the Board of Directors of the Federal Crop Insurance Corporation to “establish 
procedures under which any policy or plan of insurance, as well as any related material or 
modification of such policy or plan of insurance, to be offered under this title shall be subject to 
independent reviews by persons experienced as actuaries and in underwriting, as determined by the 
Board;” and 
 
2) Direct the Board, to the maximum extent possible, to “contract with private insurance 
companies, private rating bureaus, and other organizations as appropriate for actuarial services, 
services relating to the loss adjustment and rating plan of insurance, and other services to avoid 
duplication by the Federal Government of services that are or may be readily available in the private 
sector.” 
 
FCIC is attempting to determine the availability of sources within the private sector to conduct these 
actuarial and underwriting activities required by the Federal Crop Insurance Act. 
 
For companies interested in this Sources Sought notice, please ensure responses provide the requested 
information outlined below. 

2  
The following is requested from interested sources. 
 
The Contractor Response must include the following Basic and Contractor Capability 
Information: 
Basic Required Information: 
1. The Sources Sought number; 
2. Contractor company name, address, telephone number, CAGE Code, NAICS, and SAM 
UEI number; 
3. Confirmation that vendor is active in SAM and/or is actively taking steps to be active in 
SAM; 
4. Company point of contact name, email address, and telephone number; 
5. Identification of size, large or small, and if small identify the socioeconomic category (ie. 
small business, veteran-owned small business, service-disabled veteran-owned small 
business, Historically Underutilized Business Zone (HUBZone) small business, small 
disadvantaged business, and women-owned small business concern). 
6. Within your response, provide a statement describing how you specifically qualify as an 
actuary, an underwriter, or both. State all the specific items under which you qualify. 
Please refer to the definitions and qualification requirements of actuary and underwriter 
below. 
 
Actuary - A person having technical competence relating to the current financial implications of future 
contingent events, especially as this affects the establishment of premium rates for insurance, as 
evidenced by: 1) membership, as either a fellow or associate, in the Casualty Actuarial Society; 2) at 
least 10 years of professional level work experience as an actuary setting rates for crop insurance or 
related lines such as hail, livestock, or farm insurance; or 3) at least 15 years of professional level 
insurance premium rate setting experience in, or equivalent to, the GS-1510 (Actuary) job series. 
 
Underwriter - A person having technical competence and experience with the design of insurance 
policies, the classification and acceptance or rejection of risks, or the class of asset or activity (e.g. - 
the production risks or economics of specific crops) proposed to be insured, and who applies such 
knowledge to assure the proper functioning of insurance programs, as evidenced by: 1) at least 10 
years of professional level work experience as a crop insurance underwriter; 2) at least 15 years of 
professional level work experience as a property and casualty underwriter in fields related to crop 
insurance, such as hail, livestock, or farm insurance; 3) at least 15 years of experience as an 
agricultural risk management consultant; 4) a Ph.D. in agricultural economics with at least 5 years of 
post-doctoral work in crop insurance or agricultural risk management; or 5) a Ph.D. with at least 5 
years of post-doctoral work in a field of agriculture, risk management, etc., directly related to the 
agricultural commodity or activity proposed to be insured.

STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW) 
Eastern Oklahoma VA Health Care System 
Elopement Alarm System 
At the new Tulsa VA Medical Center 
GENERAL 
PURPOSE / OBJECTIVE: Eastern Oklahoma VA Health Care System (EOVAHCS) requires a 
contractor to supply and install an Elopement Alarm System to notify nursing staﬀ of 
monitored patients leaving that are identiﬁed at elevated risk for elopement at the Tulsa VA 
Medical Center.  The contractor will be required to supply and install all components and to 
monitor 8 doors on 4 ﬂoors and 16 annunciating stations including wiring between all devices 
in accordance with this statement of work in a cost eﬀective, eﬃcient, and safe manner, while 
in accordance with the VA Mission.  
BACKGROUND: A facility in Tulsa, Oklahoma, is currently being renovated for the purpose of 
being used as the new Tulsa VA Medical Center (VAMC) in June 2026.  The facility will need an 
Elopement Alarm System between May 2026 and August 2026.  The facility is currently under 
control of VHiT and the construction contractor remodeling the facility.  The Elopement Alarm 
System is required to be installed during the hospital activation period so that it is functional 
before ﬁrst patient is seen. 
LOCATION: The new Tulsa VA Medical Center will be located at 440 S. Houston Ave, Tulsa, 
Oklahoma 74127. 
PERFORMANCE PERIOD/DELIVERY TIMES: The VA requires delivery and installation of product 
between May 2026 and August 2026 as required by the construction contractor.  After award 
delivery times will be coordinated through the COR. 
The Contractor shall furnish all contract oversight, management, Technically Trained Personnel, 
OEM authorizations to support provision and installation of OEM products, applicable licenses, 
uniforms, equipment, tools, materials, supplies, storage, insurances, shipping and delivery costs, 
and transportations necessary to provide the products, and associated installation, for EOVAHCS 
in accordance with this SOW. Any services associated with this product are considered non-
personal services. The Contractor, its employees, agents, and subcontractors shall not be 
considered VA employees for any purpose of fulﬁlling the SOW and shall be considered 
employees of the Contractor.  
 
Qualiﬁcations of Contractor : For a contract of this size, scope and complexity, the successful 
Contractor must provide products and perform in a professional manner and quality as 
recognized by commercial industry standards as good to excellent.  Contractor must provide to 

 
the COR and CO, and maintain for the life of the contract, written certiﬁcation from the Original 
Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) that authorizes the Contractor to provide and install the 
products and software, as detailed in the Contractor’s quote and identiﬁed in this SOW. 
 
SCOPE: EOVAHCS requires a contractor to provide  equipment and installation that meets or 
exceeds the physical, functional, and performance of the listed salient characteristics in the 
following sections. The equipment features are essential to the technical requirements to meet 
the department's needs and account for retroﬁtting an existing structure.  
 
SALIENT CHARACTERISTICS  
Contractor is required to provide the following products, brand name or equal, including 
installation at the location outlined in this SOW.  Elopement system must be compatible with 
and integrated with the Jeron Provider 790 nurse call system. 
 
Equipment: 
8 Each  Wanderguard Blue  Door Alarms Controller 
 
• Wirelessly identiﬁes bracelets within range and issues alert 
• Capable of upgrade to provide the following: 
o Proximity Awareness 
o Auto-door locking mags 
o Access Keypads/Badge Readers 
 
16 Each Wanderguard Blue  Nurse Station Annunciators 
 
• Provides audible indication of door alert at 4 locations on 4 ﬂoors 
 
50 Each Wanderguard Blue Bracelets 
   
• Durable/Cut-Resistant Bands 
• IP67 or better water ingress protection 
• Smooth surface for easy sterilization 
 
INSTALLATION AND TRAINING: Installation and staﬀ training are to be provided as part of this 
procurement. Delivery and installation must be coordinated with the local COR. See the 
Performance section below.  
 

 
Manuals: Contractor shall provide electronic copies of the user manuals and repair 
manuals for each diﬀerent model of product and software installed under this order or 
contract at no additional cost to the government. 
Installation, in addition to the time required for setup of the individual cells and 
cabinets.  The contractor will provide a senior technical expert for server setup and 
testing 
 
QUALITY 
 
Conformance Standards 
Refer to section on Safety and Compliance in this SOW. 
 
Rework or Remedy 
Rework or Remedy is deﬁned as performing the Service again until the Purpose of this 
SOW is achieved in full.  This involves less than Satisfactory Service by the Contractor 
and as noted by the COR. Rework or Remedy occurs at no additional cost to the 
Government. Payment will be withheld until all services are performed to the 
Satisfactory level in accordance with this SOW and as documented by the COR. 
INSPECTION:  Will be performed a representative from OIT and Engineering.  Each 
resultant inspection shall be documented and provided to the COR within 7 days of 
installation along with any inspection documentation or checklists required by the 
manufacturer.  Any changes in inspection requirements during the period of installation 
will be communicated to the Contractor immediately.  
Inspection and Acceptance of Products and Services: The Government reserves the 
right to inspect and test services in accordance with this SOW and the Contract. The only 
individual authorized to oﬃcially accept services is the COR. While inspection of services 
may be delegated by the COR and a shared responsibility with departmental 
management staﬀ, the COR is ultimately the only authorized individual to approve and 
accept services on behalf of the VA. 
 
WARRANTY OF EQUIPMENT: Government requirement for standard manufacturer industry 
warranty term. The government does not accept an extended warranty, which requires 
advance payment. 
PERFORMANCE PERIOD AND DELIVERY:  

 
• All items to be delivered and installed after receipt of purchase order starting on or 
around May 2026 through August 2026. 
• Delivery and receipt of the proposed items are anticipated to be directed to the location 
identiﬁed below. Conﬁrmation of delivery location will be provided by the VA COR post-
award. Delivery must be coordinated with VA COR before any delivery attempts. Any 
item that has not been coordinated will be turned away and any additional charges will 
be the responsibility of the sender/transportation company.  
• Contractor`s responsibility will include oﬄoading the equipment from the truck, moving 
the equipment to the correct delivery location in the space, uncrating or unboxing the 
equipment, removing all trash, and setting up the equipment according to the 
manufacturer`s speciﬁcations, followed by testing the equipment to verify that it is 
operational. Equipment installation paperwork & warranty information must be handed 
to the approved government contact onsite.   
• VA STANDARD BUSINESS HOURS AND FEDERAL HOLIDAYS 
• Hours: Normal duty hours are 8:00 a.m. through 4:00 p.m. for the VA and 7:00 a.m. 
through 5:00 p.m. for the construction site, Monday through Friday, not including 
federal holidays. Whenever contact with a facility is required outside of normal duty 
hours, the Contractor shall coordinate these times with the designated COR. 
• In accordance with 5 U.S.C. 6103, Executive Order 11582, and Public Law 94-97, the 
following national holidays are observed and for the purpose of this contract are deﬁned 
as “Legal Federal oﬃcial holidays.”  
New Year’s Day  January 1st  
Martin Luther King’s Birthday  Third Monday in January  
President’s Day  Last Monday in February  
Memorial Day  Last Monday in May  
Juneteenth  June 19th  
Independence Day  July 4th  
Labor Day  First Monday in September  
Columbus Day  Second Monday in October  
Veteran’s Day  November 11th  
Thanksgiving Day  Fourth Thursday in November  

 
Christmas Day  December 25th  
 
In addition to the days designated as holidays, the Government observes the following days: 
• Any other day designated by Federal Statute 
• Any other day designated by Executive Order 
• Any other day designated by the President of the United States to be a Federal holiday 
 
• Noncontract Charges: The contractor shall not perform any service that will result in 
additional charges without prior approval from the Contracting Oﬃcer.  
• Payment: Payment will be made upon receipt of a properly prepared invoice, which 
references the period for which payment is due, the contract number, and/or assigned 
purchase order number. The invoice must include the correct payment address.  
• Waste Removal: The contractor is responsible for removing and properly disposing of all 
waste related to the services provided on-site at all VA facilities.  
 
SAFETY AND COMPLIANCE 
The Contractor must perform services and ensure equipment functions in accordance with: 
a) local, state, and federal Occupational Safety and Health guidelines and legislation, to 
include Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), the American National 
Standards Institute (ANSI) safety guidelines; 
b) local, state, and federal Fire and Safety legislation and guidelines, to include VA Health 
Care System directives and legislation on Fire and Safety, as well as the latest published 
edition of NFPA-99 (Health Care Facilities Code) 
 
REGULATORY REQUIRMENTS: 
a. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) Quality System Regulation as stated in 21 CFR Part 
820 
b. Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) 
 
Medical Center Policies 
Each VA Medical Center has policies that are updated from time to time. The COR can 
provide more detailed information to the contractor of these upon commencement of 
the contract and throughout the term of the contract, as needed, especially policies 
regarding, parking, possession of weapons, cell phone use and photography as well as 

 
smoking on VA property. Violations of such policies may result in individual ﬁnes or 
citation answerable in the United States (Federal) District Court. 
 
Contractor Point of Contact (POC) 
The Contractor shall specify an individual who shall serve as a single point of contact for 
all contract issues (POC). Contractor must provide the COR and Contracting Oﬃce with 
the POC contact details, to include business phone number or cell phone number and 
email, as a minimum: 
a) Within 5 business days of contract award, 
b) Within 5 business days after renewal or extension of services in accordance with, and 
if permitted by applicable FAR clause, and 
c) Within 5 business days prior to a change in the POC by the Contractor. 
The POC must be easily accessible by phone and return COR calls within 48 hours of a 
voice message left by the COR. 
 
Contracting Oﬃcer’s Representative (COR) 
Upon contract commencement, the Contracting Oﬃcer will notify the Contractor in 
writing as to the COR assigned to this contract, and upon reassignment of a new COR, as 
applicable. Contractor shall only respond to requests for changes, new products or 
service, from the COR or the CO. If any product or services is requested from any source, 
other than the COR or the CO, the Contractor is to advise the individual of this 
requirement and refuse to respond. Any billing resulting from unauthorized service will 
not be paid by the government.  
 
Authority of the COR 
The Contracting Oﬃcer is the only person authorized to approve changes in any of the 
requirements of this contract. In the event the Contractor aﬀects any changes at the 
direction of any person other than the Contracting Oﬃcer, the changes will be 
considered to have been made without authority and no adjustment will be made in the 
contract price or schedule to cover any increase in costs incurred as a result thereof. The 
Contracting Oﬃcer shall be the only individual authorized to accept nonconforming 
work, waive any requirement of the contract, and/or modify any term or condition of 
the contract. The Contracting Oﬃcer is the only individual who can legally obligate 
Government funds. No costs chargeable to the proposed contract can be incurred before 
receipt of a fully executed contract or speciﬁc authorization from the Contracting Oﬃcer. 
Any invoicing or charges resulting from unauthorized service will not be paid by the 
government. 
 

 
LIABILITIES AND INSURANCES 
Protection from Damage 
Contractor shall provide all labor, materials, and equipment necessary for protection of 
VAMC personnel, furnishings, equipment and buildings from damage, and shall replace 
or repair any damage due to work performed under this contract equal to its original 
construction and ﬁnish. 
 
Liability Insurance 
Contractor must provide the COR and the CO with written conﬁrmation that Contractor 
has adequate insurance protection against negligent work and other forms of liability.

Version 2.0

Background:    Institute for Learning, Education and Development (ILEAD), Production and Delivery (PD)Service Line in St. Louis, MO maintains a live broadcast facility and contracts support services for closed captioning on both “live” and “offline” captioning for all ILEAD video deliverables.  ILEAD automates its captioning services with the use of closed captioning appliances that automatically convert speech to text captioning.

ILEAD owns EnCaption closed captioning automatic speed recognition (ASR) appliances requires support and software upgrades.  

The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) is currently undergoing a reorganization that may result in future changes to its organizational structure, processes, responsibilities, and priorities. Such changes could affect the customers, services, or support described in this Product Description. Accordingly, the Contractor shall remain adaptable and responsive to evolving VA requirements and work in close coordination with the Government to assess and implement necessary adjustments, as needed. Any resulting changes will be completed by bilateral contract modification.

Records Management Language for Contracts

When Federal agencies acquire goods or services, they need to determine what Federal records management requirements should be included in the contract. Federal contractors often create, send, or receive Federal records. Federal contracts should provide clear legal obligations describing how the contract employees must handle Federal records. 

Agency records officers, procurement counsel, and acquisitions officers must discuss how to integrate records management obligations into their existing procurement processes. NARA has developed the following language to be included as an agency-specific term and condition in Federal contracts for a variety of services and products. The majority of contracts should include language on records management obligations, but each contract should be evaluated individually. For example, the data-rights paragraph (Paragraph 10 below) may not be appropriate for all contracts. Instead, agencies may be better served by one of the established data-rights clauses in the Federal Acquisition Regulations. 

This language should not replace specific records management requirements included within Federal information system contracts. 

RECORDS MANAGEMENT OBLIGATIONS

A.  Applicability

This clause applies to all Contractors whose employees create, work with, or otherwise handle Federal records, as defined in Section B, regardless of the medium in which the record exists.  

B.  Definitions

“Federal record” as defined in 44 U.S.C. § 3301, includes all recorded information, regardless of form or characteristics, made or received by a Federal agency under Federal law or in connection with the transaction of public business and preserved or appropriate for preservation by that agency or its legitimate successor as evidence of the organization, functions, policies, decisions, procedures, operations, or other activities of the United States Government or because of the informational value of data in them.  

The term Federal record:

includes Institute for Learning, Education and Development (ILEAD) records. 

does not include personal materials.

applies to records created, received, or maintained by Contractors pursuant to their ILEAD contract.

may include deliverables and documentation associated with deliverables.
