STATEMENT OF WORK

BACKGROUND

VA Long Beach Healthcare System (VALBHS) is requested services for the implementation of an RTLS/RFID Asset Tracking solution to support the needs of the healthcare system. The Department of Veterans Affairs’ Real Time Location System (RTLS) Program affects areas of clinical and administrative workflows by providing process improvement and automation efficiency. Significant potential uses and benefits of this technology throughout VA are numerous and include improved quality of patient care and satisfaction, reduced health care asset management costs, improved capacity/resource planning, improved employee, and patient safety, and improved general asset management and inventory. The RTLS solution is comprised of multiple applications impacting the logistics supply chain, inventory accountability, Biomedical Engineering, Office of Information and Technology (OIT), Sterile Processing, Dental and Surgical Services, Cardiac Catheterization Labs, and a host of other clinical departments. RTLS applications are deployed to more than 225 VA medical centers. Current installations use proprietary CenTrak and Infor Location-Based Intelligence (LBI) software for tagging, tracking, and integration into a single database.  CenTrak® proprietary active Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) hardware and software provide zonal, room-level, and within-room level accuracy regarding asset location, staff location, patient location, as well as environmental variables.

SCOPE

This Statement of Work establishes the requirements for Information Technology (IT) services, hardware, and software to implement CenTrak and Infor LBI-based Asset Tracking (AT) at the VA Long Beach Healthcare System. The Contractor shall provide RTLS hardware, software, documentation, and services to authorized users in VHA. Services include installation, end user acceptance testing, training, warranty services, engineering, and professional services.  The scope of this order shall include completion of implementation already started and expansion of current inactive system at VA Long Beach Healthcare System. 

GENERAL REQUIREMENT

The Contractor shall provide all necessary labor, materials, supplies, parts, batteries, software (needed for the general operation of the system), tools, equipment, testing equipment, travel, transportation expenses and other related costs to provide the completion of implementation of the current inactive system at VA Long Beach Healthcare System.

The contractor will provide the additional necessary hardware that will work with the currently installed RTLS equipment in all buildings within the main campus and update any necessary outdated hardware to enable functional asset tracking. Any parts before being replaced must be approved by Biomedical Engineering.

Throughout this process the vendor will ensure communication with Biomedical Engineering. This will include but not limited to working with Biomedical Engineering to schedule the installation, confirm installation is complete and have it inspected and provide proper documentation of installation in a timely manner when requested.

PERFORMANCE DETAILS

PERFORMANCE PERIOD

The period of performance will be 12 months from date of award.

This is for a full-service contract to include all necessary scheduled service during normal working hours five (5) days per week, Monday through Friday 7:30AM-4PM unless otherwise stated and approved ahead of time by Biomedical Engineering. This excludes any national holidays. There are eleven (11) Federal holidays set by law (USC Title 5 Section 6103) that VA follows. Under current definitions, five (5) are set by dates:

If any of the above falls on a Saturday, then Friday shall be observed as a holiday. Similarly, if one falls on a Sunday, then Monday shall be observed as a holiday. 

The other six (6) are set by a day of the week and month:

PLACE OF PERFORMANCE

Facility implementation shall be limited to all buildings within the VA Long Beach Healthcare System main campus at 5901 E 7th St. Long Beach, CA 90822. Tasks under this PWS shall be performed at the VA facility listed above (primarily for hardware installation, tagging, and system administration). Project management tasks can be performed remotely.

TRAVEL

The Government anticipates travel under this effort to perform the tasks associate with the effort, as well as to attend program-related meetings and conferences throughout the Period of Performance. All travel costs shall be the responsibility of the vendor and included in the firm-fixed price line items. These costs will not be directly reimbursed by the Government.

CONTRACTOR DETAILS

5.1 CONTRACTOR QUALIFICATIONS

Personnel performing installation and other services for this requirement must be fully qualified Field Service Engineer (FSE) who has been trained on the specific equipment in accordance with the original manufacturer’s installation, maintenance, and repair procedures. The personnel shall be fully certified by the Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) Centrak and Infor LBI before performing work at VA Long Beach Healthcare System. “Fully certified” is defined as factory-trained or equivalent and experienced to work on the equipment assigned. The contractor shall provide a narrative that describes its specialized experience providing installation and maintenance on Centrak and Infor LBI hardware and software. 

5.2 CONTRACTOR BADGING

Compliance with VA Handbook 0735 – HSPD-12 Program

To comply with Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Handbook 0735, Homeland Security Presidential Directive 12 (HSPD-12) requirements, the Prime Contractor shall coordinate with the Point of Contact (POC) regarding all site visits to the VA Long Beach Healthcare System. Badges are mandatory for all contractors and subcontractors entering the facility.

The Prime Contractor is responsible for ensuring that all required information and documentation are submitted to the POC with sufficient lead time to allow for proper processing of badge requests. No contractor or subcontractor may begin work onsite without an approved badge, except under emergency conditions as outlined below.

Processing Time

Badge issuance may take up to 30 calendar days due to required background checks. The Prime Contractor must begin coordination with the POC immediately upon contract award to avoid repair, service, or project delays.

Onsite Visits for Badging

Contractors should anticipate at least two separate onsite visits:

One visit for fingerprinting.

One visit to pick up the issued badge.

Mandatory Training

All contractors and subcontractors must complete mandatory training assigned through the VA’s electronic Training Management System (TMS) before badges are issued. This training typically requires approximately two (2) hours to complete. Badge issuance and retention are contingent upon successful completion of this training.

5.3 CONTRACTOR ONSITE REPORTING PROCEDURES

The Contractor must report to the Biomedical Engineering Department (Building 5, Room 138) to sign the visitor logbook. In addition to signing-in, the Contractor personnel shall wear their VA issued badge and identify him/herself to the Using Service before proceeding to the job site. 

For services to be performed outside normal working hours, the Contractor must obtain approval from the Biomedical Engineering POC prior to performing any after-hour work. If the afterhours request is approved, the Contractor must report to the Biomedical Engineering Department (Building 5, Room 138) to sign the visitor logbook and pick up a visitor badge. In addition to signing-in, the Contractor personnel shall identify him/herself to the Using Service before proceeding to the job site.

Prior to leaving the facility, the Contractor shall communicate status of equipment to the Using Service and sign out of the logbook in the Biomedical Engineering Department

PROJECT MANAGEMENT

STAFFING REQUIREMENTS

The Contractor shall provide a single Contract Implementation Manager, and one standby Backup Manager, as the sole points of contact to coordinate and manage all interactions, engagement, and services provided to the Government under this contract. The Contract Implementation Manager and Backup Managers shall be separate from the System Administrator.

REPORTING REQUIREMENTS

The Contractor shall provide the POC with Monthly Progress Reports in electronic form in Microsoft (MS) Word, MS PowerPoint, or MS Project formats for this contract. The report shall include detailed instructions/explanations for each required data element to ensure that data is accurate and consistent. These reports shall reflect data as of the last day of the preceding month.

The Monthly Progress Reports shall cover all work completed during the reporting period and work planned for the subsequent reporting period.  The report should also identify any problems that arose, and a description of how the problems were resolved. The Department of Veterans Affairs’ Real Time Location System (RTLS) Program affects areas of clinical and administrative workflows by providing process improvement and automation efficiency. Significant potential uses and benefits of this technology throughout VA are numerous and include improved quality of patient care and satisfaction, reduced health care asset management costs, improved capacity/resource planning, improved employee, and patient safety, and improved general asset management and inventory. The RTLS solution is comprised of multiple applications impacting the logistics supply chain, inventory accountability, Biomedical Engineering, Office of Information and Technology (OIT), Sterile Processing, Dental and Surgical Services, Cardiac Catheterization Labs, and a host of other clinical departments. RTLS applications are deployed to more than 225 VA medical centers. Current installations use proprietary CenTrak and Infor Location-Based Intelligence (LBI) software for tagging, tracking, and integration into a single database.  CenTrak® proprietary active Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) hardware and software provide zonal, room-level, and within-room level accuracy regarding asset location, staff location, patient location, as well as environmental variables.

SCOPE

This Statement of Work establishes the requirements for Information Technology (IT) services, hardware, and software to implement CenTrak and Infor LBI-based Asset Tracking (AT) at the VA Long Beach Healthcare System. The Contractor shall provide RTLS hardware, software, documentation, and services to authorized users in VHA. Services include installation, end user acceptance testing, training, warranty services, engineering, and professional services.  The scope of this order shall include completion of implementation already started and expansion of current inactive system at VA Long Beach Healthcare System. 

GENERAL REQUIREMENT

The Contractor shall provide all necessary labor, materials, supplies, parts, batteries, software (needed for the general operation of the system), tools, equipment, testing equipment, travel, transportation expenses and other related costs to provide the completion of implementation of the current inactive system at VA Long Beach Healthcare System.

The contractor will provide the additional necessary hardware that will work with the currently installed RTLS equipment in all buildings within the main campus and update any necessary outdated hardware to enable functional asset tracking. Any parts before being replaced must be approved by Biomedical Engineering.

Throughout this process the vendor will ensure communication with Biomedical Engineering. This will include but not limited to working with Biomedical Engineering to schedule the installation, confirm installation is complete and have it inspected and provide proper documentation of installation in a timely manner when requested.

PERFORMANCE DETAILS

PERFORMANCE PERIOD

The period of performance will be 12 months from date of award.

This is for a full-service contract to include all necessary scheduled service during normal working hours five (5) days per week, Monday through Friday 7:30AM-4PM unless otherwise stated and approved ahead of time by Biomedical Engineering. This excludes any national holidays. There are eleven (11) Federal holidays set by law (USC Title 5 Section 6103) that VA follows. Under current definitions, five (5) are set by dates:

If any of the above falls on a Saturday, then Friday shall be observed as a holiday. Similarly, if one falls on a Sunday, then Monday shall be observed as a holiday. 

The other six (6) are set by a day of the week and month:

PLACE OF PERFORMANCE

Facility implementation shall be limited to all buildings within the VA Long Beach Healthcare System main campus at 5901 E 7th St. Long Beach, CA 90822. Tasks under this PWS shall be performed at the VA facility listed above (primarily for hardware installation, tagging, and system administration). Project management tasks can be performed remotely.

TRAVEL

The Government anticipates travel under this effort to perform the tasks associate with the effort, as well as to attend program-related meetings and conferences throughout the Period of Performance. All travel costs shall be the responsibility of the vendor and included in the firm-fixed price line items. These costs will not be directly reimbursed by the Government.

CONTRACTOR DETAILS

5.1 CONTRACTOR QUALIFICATIONS

Personnel performing installation and other services for this requirement must be fully qualified Field Service Engineer (FSE) who has been trained on the specific equipment in accordance with the original manufacturer’s installation, maintenance, and repair procedures. The personnel shall be fully certified by the Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) Centrak and Infor LBI before performing work at VA Long Beach Healthcare System. “Fully certified” is defined as factory-trained or equivalent and experienced to work on the equipment assigned. The contractor shall provide a narrative that describes its specialized experience providing installation and maintenance on Centrak and Infor LBI hardware and software. 

5.2 CONTRACTOR BADGING

Compliance with VA Handbook 0735 – HSPD-12 Program

To comply with Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Handbook 0735, Homeland Security Presidential Directive 12 (HSPD-12) requirements, the Prime Contractor shall coordinate with the Point of Contact (POC) regarding all site visits to the VA Long Beach Healthcare System. Badges are mandatory for all contractors and subcontractors entering the facility.

The Prime Contractor is responsible for ensuring that all required information and documentation are submitted to the POC with sufficient lead time to allow for proper processing of badge requests. No contractor or subcontractor may begin work onsite without an approved badge, except under emergency conditions as outlined below.

Processing Time

Badge issuance may take up to 30 calendar days due to required background checks. The Prime Contractor must begin coordination with the POC immediately upon contract award to avoid repair, service, or project delays.

Onsite Visits for Badging

Contractors should anticipate at least two separate onsite visits:

One visit for fingerprinting.

One visit to pick up the issued badge.

Mandatory Training

All contractors and subcontractors must complete mandatory training assigned through the VA’s electronic Training Management System (TMS) before badges are issued. This training typically requires approximately two (2) hours to complete. Badge issuance and retention are contingent upon successful completion of this training.

5.3 CONTRACTOR ONSITE REPORTING PROCEDURES

The Contractor must report to the Biomedical Engineering Department (Building 5, Room 138) to sign the visitor logbook. In addition to signing-in, the Contractor personnel shall wear their VA issued badge and identify him/herself to the Using Service before proceeding to the job site. 

For services to be performed outside normal working hours, the Contractor must obtain approval from the Biomedical Engineering POC prior to performing any after-hour work. If the afterhours request is approved, the Contractor must report to the Biomedical Engineering Department (Building 5, Room 138) to sign the visitor logbook and pick up a visitor badge. In addition to signing-in, the Contractor personnel shall identify him/herself to the Using Service before proceeding to the job site.

Prior to leaving the facility, the Contractor shall communicate status of equipment to the Using Service and sign out of the logbook in the Biomedical Engineering Department

PROJECT MANAGEMENT

STAFFING REQUIREMENTS

The Contractor shall provide a single Contract Implementation Manager, and one standby Backup Manager, as the sole points of contact to coordinate and manage all interactions, engagement, and services provided to the Government under this contract. The Contract Implementation Manager and Backup Managers shall be separate from the System Administrator.

REPORTING REQUIREMENTS

The Contractor shall provide the POC with Monthly Progress Reports in electronic form in Microsoft (MS) Word, MS PowerPoint, or MS Project formats for this contract. The report shall include detailed instructions/explanations for each required data element to ensure that data is accurate and consistent. These reports shall reflect data as of the last day of the preceding month.

The Monthly Progress Reports shall cover all work completed during the reporting period and work planned for the subsequent reporting period.  The report should also identify any problems that arose, and a description of how the problems were resolved.  If problems have not been completely resolved, the Contractor shall provide an explanation including a plan and timeframe for resolving the issue. BACKGROUND

The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Veterans Health Administration (VHA), is one of the world’s largest health care delivery organizations. The Revenue Operations (RO) team is seeking ongoing healthcare revenue industry modeled best practice management consulting services and healthcare revenue operations business information technology tools to sustain, transform and continuously improve revenue cycle activities within the Office of Finance (OF). Revenue Operations (RO) and the seven (7) regionally aligned Consolidated Patient Account Centers (CPACs) support a vast healthcare enterprise in the service of our Nation’s Veterans. The goal of RO is to support the field in the management of the revenue cycle. As part of that effort, RO provides a variety of program services including the following: payer relations, metric-based quality / policy operational analyses, rate development, eBusiness EDI solutions and best practice modeling with a focus on process standardization to enhance revenues.

The Consolidated Patient Account Center (CPAC) uses standardized methods, tools, and processes to improve efficiency, effectiveness, and accountability in revenue operations. CPAC’s state-of-the-art business processes ensure that VA collects revenue from private health insurance carriers for nonservice-connected care provided to insured Veterans. These funds go back to the VA Medical Centers (VAMCs) to provide health care services to our Veterans. There are seven regional CPACs located around the country that provide revenue cycle management to all the  Veterans Integrated Service Network (VISNs) and their associated VAMCs. CPACs perform back-end revenue cycle processes while the VAMCs maintain ownership of key Veteran-facing revenue functions.


Transformation from the VA current state legacy system to the Oracle Health Electronic Health Record (OH EHRM) and its related health and revenue information technology tools is a critical endeavor for Revenue Operations. The RO team requires support to maintain and improve its best practice private sector revenue cycle performance while it transforms, as necessary, to the Oracle Health revenue technology tools. During preparation, deployment and stabilization of OH EHRM, RO seeks to continue its utilization of healthcare revenue business best practices and healthcare revenue business tools which provide work drivers to track and prioritize key revenue cycle activities, provide improved revenue collection services that focus on integral cash generation, improved payer management, standardization of processes, training and development of staff, along with extensive use of metrics and analytics to measure and validate performance.

These efforts are in response to Public Law 110-387, Section 406, which requires Revenue Operations and the CPACs to carry out the following functions: (1) Reengineer and integrate all business processes of the revenue cycle of the Department; (2) Standardize and coordinate all activities of the Department related to the revenue cycle for all health care services furnished to Veterans for nonservice-connected medical conditions; (3) Apply commercial industry standards for measures of access, timeliness, and performance metrics with respect to revenue enhancement of the Department; and (4) Apply other requirements with respect to such revenue cycle improvement as the Secretary may specify.  In meeting these goals, VA VHA strives to provide high quality, effective, and efficient Information Technology (IT) services to those responsible for providing care to the Veterans at the point-of-care as well as throughout all the points of the Veterans’ health care in an effective, timely and compassionate manner.  VA depends on Information Management/Information Technology (IM/IT) systems to meet mission goals.

This will be based upon your estimate of how long the Replacement of IBM COBOL Mainframe System for Veteran Benefit Debt Management will take to complete.

Replacement of IBM COBOL Mainframe System for Veteran Benefit Debt Management

Scope


The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) requires contractor support to modernize a legacy Veteran Benefit Debt Management system that is running on an IBM COBOL mainframe system. The Contractor shall provide the technical expertise necessary to design, develop, implement, test, and transition to a modernized solution that fully replaces the legacy mainframe capabilities while ensuring continuity of operations.

2.0 Background


The current Veteran Benefit Debt Management system supports agency-wide Veteran Benefit and Debt operations. It performs debt aging, generates demand letters, and conducts file-based integrations with approximately ten external systems. Each external system integration utilizes a unique file-based interface. Approximately two million debt records are maintained in Virtual Storage Access Method (VSAM) and sequential file structures.

The legacy environment consists of:

257 COBOL modules totaling approximately 258,000 lines of code

540 JCL files totaling approximately 43,000 lines of code

87 PROCS totaling approximately 8,000 lines of code

18 COPYBOOKS totaling approximately 14,000 lines of code
These programs are executed daily or on demand via the CA7 scheduler.

Additionally, the system includes approximately 300 Java programs (126,000 lines of code) executed on Microsoft Windows servers, also via Computer Associates Workload Manager 7 (CA7) or on demand.

The legacy mainframe serves as a backend system and transmits updates to a Microsoft SQL Server database that supports APIs running on the MuleSoft AnyPoint Platform. These downstream systems are expected to remain in operation and must be fully supported by the contractor’s solution.

Requirements

Solution Development and Modernization


The Contractor shall provide a replacement solution that:

Replicates or enhances all existing functional capabilities of the Veteran Benefit Debt Management system.

Supports all debt management operations including, but not limited to, debt aging, demand letter generation, and batch processing.

Accommodates the migration and processing of approximately two million debt records currently stored in VSAM and sequential files.

Integration Requirements


The Contractor shall:

Provide interfaces that support all current file-based integrations with approximately ten external systems.

Maintain compatibility with each system’s unique integration format and operational requirements.

Ensure continued interoperability with the existing Microsoft SQL Server environment and MuleSoft Anypoint Platform APIs that depend on mainframe-generated updates.

Operational Requirements


The Contractor shall ensure the modernized solution:

Supports scheduled and on-demand execution of batch processes analogous to those performed using CA7.

Provides equivalent or improved performance, reliability, and auditability compared to the legacy environment.

Supports secure, reliable data transfer between all interfacing systems.

3.4 Data Migration


The Contractor shall:

Migrate all legacy VSAM and sequential file data without loss or corruption.

Conduct validation of migrated datasets to ensure data integrity and functional continuity.

3.5 Transition and Implementation


The Contractor shall:

Provide a detailed transition plan that ensures uninterrupted operations during system cutover.

Deliver training materials and training sessions to VA personnel as required.

Provide post-implementation support during stabilization.

4.0 Constraints and Considerations

All existing downstream systems (SQL Server, MuleSoft APIs) must remain operational throughout.

The Contractor shall ensure compliance with VA security, privacy, and data-protection requirements.

All modernization efforts must minimize disruptions to current business operations.

COMBINED SYNOPSIS / SOLICITATION-COMPETITIVE 
 
 
Title: Maintenance Contract for Tape Backup and Disk Storage Systems 
 
1. This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with 
the format in Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Subpart 12.6 as supplemented with 
additional information included in this notice.  This announcement constitutes the only 
solicitation; quotes are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be 
issued. 
 
The solicitation number is PCA-NIMH-01870 and the solicitation is issued as request for 
quotation (RFQ). 
 
This acquisition is for a commercial item or service and is conducted under the authority of 
the FAR Part 13 —Simplified Acquisition Procedures; and FAR Part 12 —Acquisition of 
Commercial Items and is not expected to exceed the simplified acquisition threshold. A 
fixed-price type of purchase order is contemplated for this requirement. 
 
A maintenance contract is required to provide the necessary maintenance for a tape backup 
system that is used to back up the data stored on the disk storage system to tape.  This ensures 
that no data will be lost in case of disk storage failure.  The maintenance contract also includes 
maintenance for the disk storage system that will provide necessary updates to firmware and 
immediate service in the event of failure of individual disks or other components within the 
system. 
 
The NIMH, Human Genetics Branch, Section on Developmental Neurogenomics conducts 
studies of developmental neuropsychiatric diseases.  These studies involve the collection of 
very large genetic, neuroimaging, and behavioral datasets.  The data are stored on large 
capacity disk storage arrays and backed up onto tape for storage at a remote site in case of a 
catastrophic event.  The objective is to ensure that the data will be available with a minimum of 
downtime in case of disk or tape drive failure.  The maintenance contract also provides support 
in terms of firmware and software upgrades especially with regards to data security.    
 
See Attachment 1 – Purchase Description or Statement of Work, for additional details. 
 
2. The solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect 
through Federal Acquisition Circular 2025-05, dated 08-07-2025.  
 
3. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code for this procurement is 
518210 – Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related 
Services, and the small business size standard $40,000,000. 
 
Line Items: Through this procurement NIMH anticipates a single award, firm fixed price 
purchase order for Maintenance Contract for Tape Backup and Disk Storage Systems  
(Lowest Price Technically Acceptable) as described in Attachment 1 – Purchase Description 
or Statement of Work. 

Page 2 of 6 
 
 
 
Project Requirements: Independently and not as an agent of the Government, the Contractor 
shall furnish all the necessary services, qualified personnel, material, equipment, and facilities, 
not otherwise provided by the Government as needed to perform the Statement of Work below: 
 
The maintenance contract requires in-depth knowledge and expertise of the hardware and 
software components of the disk storage and tape backup systems. Technical assistance will be 
available on a 24/7 basis in order to minimize downtime for the researchers that depend on 
these systems.  
 
The Government requirement is to avoid interruptions in research activities causing loss of 
productivity.  Repairs will be performed under the direction of technical experts. 
 
LEVEL OF EFFORT: 
The amount of labor hours by the technical experts will vary according to disk storage and tape 
backup system needs.  The systems are known to be robust and reliable so the effort will be a 
function of unforeseen hardware failure or software upgrades.   
 
GOVERNMENT RESPONSIBILITIES: 
The Government will ensure the specific equipment is available for onsite maintenance or repair 
by the contractor, if needed. 
 
DELIVERY OR DELIVERABLES 
The contractor will provide technical phone support on a 24/7 basis and will provide next 
business day access to upgrades, onsite support and assistance, and repair, maintenance, and 
replacement of parts. 
 
REPORTING REQUIREMENTS  
4. Not applicable.

Technical Evaluation Criteria 
 
As part of the Technical Quote, the Offeror shall include the following:  
 
Maintenance Contract for Tape Backup and Disk Storage Systems 
ATTACHMENT 2: Technical Evaluation Criteria 
 
The Government will award a contract or purchase order resulting from this requirement on the 
basis of best value, technical factors and price considered. 
 
Factor 1: Technical Approach  
 
The Contractor’s proposal shall address each area of the statement of work in sufficient 
detail to demonstrate a clear understanding of the specific characteristics needed to 
fulfill these requirements. The proposed technical approach shall be evaluated for the 
capability of the contractor to provide exceptional service and support for backing up 
data stored on the disk storage system to tape. This encompasses requiring technical 
phone support on a 24/7 basis and next business day access to upgrades, onsite 
support and assistance, and repair, maintenance, and replacement of parts in the event 
of failure of individual disks or other components within the system.  Capability in these 
areas shall be viewed favorably.  
 
 
Factor 2: Past Performance 
The Contractor shall provide at least two (2) past performance references completed 
during the past five (5) years with knowledge of the contractor’s relevant skills and 
experience related to the requirements outlined in this Statement of Work. 
 
References shall include the following information: 
 
a. Name of Organization 
b. Description of Requirement and Specific Responsibilities of the Offeror 
as they relate to the SOW 
c. Contact Name and Title 
d. Total Contract Value 
e. Contract Period of Performance

Technical proposals will be evaluated using a summary adjectival rating in accordance with the 
following scale: 
 
Excellent

the superior attainment of all requirements and objectives. The risk of unsuccessful 
performance is very low as the proposal provides a clear understanding of the requirements and 
demonstrates the offerors’ ability to meet the requirement. Risk Level: Very Low 
 
Good

objectives. This approach includes advantageous characteristics of substance, and few 
relatively minor disadvantages, which collectively can be expected to result in satisfactory 
performance. The risk of unsuccessful performance is low as the proposal contains alternative 
solutions which are considered feasible and practical. These solutions are further considered to 
reflect low risk in that they are clear and precise, supported, and demonstrate an understanding 
of the requirements. Risk Level: Low 
 
Acceptable 
The proposal demonstrates an approach which is capable of meeting all requirements and 
objectives. The approach includes both advantageous and disadvantageous characteristics of 
substance, where the advantages are not outweighed by the disadvantages. Collectively, the 
advantages and disadvantages are likely to result in acceptable performance. The risk of 
unsuccessful performance is moderate, as the proposal solutions are generally feasible and 
practical. These solutions may also be considered to reflect moderate risk in that they may be 
somewhat clear and precise, partially supported, and/or demonstrate a general understanding 
of the requirements. Risk Level: Neutral 
 
Marginal

and objectives. The approach has disadvantages of substance and advantages, which if they

1. Contracting Activity:  Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Veterans Integrated Service Network

2. Nature and/or Description of the Action Being Approved:  This justification is in support of a new, 
single award, Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contract for an Architectural-Engineering (AE). 
 
3. Description of Supplies/Services Required to Meet the Agency’s Needs:  Iowa City VA Health Care  
System (ICVAHCS) has a need for Construction Period Services (CPS) for Project Number: 636A8-22-
001 Renovate 6th Floor Clinical Support Construction Period Services (CPS). These services are in 
support of construction phase of this project. CPS includes bidding support services, construction 
support services, and record drawings of the completed project. The approximate estimated value 
of these services is  
 
4. Statutory Authority Permitting Other than Full and Open Competition:  41 USC §3304(a)(5), 38 U.S. 
Code § 8127(c), as implemented by RFO 6.103-5 (Authorized or Required by Statute).  COs may use 
the non-competitive (sole source) procedures authorized in VAAR 819.7008 (DEVIATION) or VAAR 
819.7009 (DEVIATION)- up to $5,000,000.  Check the specific VAAR clause used below:   
(X) 819.7008 Sole source awards to a certified service-disabled veteran-owned small business 
 
5. Demonstration that the Contractor’s Unique Qualifications and/or Nature of the Acquisition 
Requires the Use of the Authority Cited Above (applicability of authority):  38 U.S. Code § 8127(c) 
allows sole source awards to a SDVOSB concern if the concern has been determined to be a 
responsible source with respect to performance. Geo Bancroft Engineering LLC, Inc. has had no 
known issues with performance that would not allow a sole source contract under this authority. 
Geo Bancroft Engineering LLC, Inc. has met the requirements under VAAR 819.7003 (DEVIATION) 
and has been determined to be an eligible SDVOSB.  
 
The following narrative demonstrates that it is in the government’s best interest to sole source this 
requirement under the authority VAAR 819-7008. The original design and construction documents 
(drawing and specifications) of this project were completed under Contract Number: 
36C26319D0044; Task Order Number: 36C26322N0625. The task order included CPS as options, but 
the option was never exercised due to the lack of funding for the construction project. The task 
order was closed out on April 10, 2025. This project is currently approved on the Strategic Capital 
Investment Plan (SCIP) so there is now a need for CPS.  
 
The services requested for this acquisition would allow the original design firm, Stone Group 
Architects, Inc., to provide and perform CPS without going through additional costly design reviews. 
 
It is expected that no duplication of costs would be passed on to the government, whereas if

another AE firm was expected to conduct these services; there would be additional costs associated  
with the liability and time needed for reviewing another firm’s design and construction documents.  
There would also be costs associated with providing construction support services (answering RFI,  
issuing ITC’s, etc.) on a project that was not their own. It is also assumed that there would be some  
additional costs to CPS to mitigate the risk of providing support to another firm’s design.  
 
The factor to sole source the CPS back to the AE record of design is due to no added liability costs for  
services performed during construction. During construction, many questions and requests for  
opinions or instructions on the design, specifications, and drawings are posed to the AE to provide a  
clear direction or understanding of the intent back to the construction contractor. Most of these  
responses and/or instructions can be provided easily by the AE of record as they provided the plans  
and design based upon their own independent studies and reviews of the project needs.  
 
Even if assuming a sole source contract added a premium to the procurement price due to lack of  
competition, it would not equal the cost and time savings that the government would receive by  
sole sourcing this requirement to Geo Bancroft Engineering LLC.  
 
Due to the projected cost and time savings, a sole source procurement is being pursued. Continuing  
to have Geo Bancroft Engineering LLC as the AE of record during construction will save the  
government money and allow for a basis of efficiency. It would be costly to have another AE firm  
duplicate the efforts already paid for and pay a higher price to offset any liabilities that another firm  
would be held to for a project that another AE has designed. 
 
6. Description of Efforts Made to ensure that offers are solicited from as many potential sources as 
deemed practicable, including whether a notice was or will be publicized as required by RFO 6.301 
and, if not, which exemption under RFO 5.101(b)(1)  applies:   Market research was conducted; 
however, seeking a competitive solution for CPS would likely result in additional costs and time to 
the government so a sole source contract is being sought.  
Market research techniques used to identify potential sources for this requirement include 
contacting knowledgeable individuals in this industry regarding market capabilities to meet the 
requirement without duplication of costs or additional time. An email was sent to AE firms inquiring 
about the willingness to perform additional design services, including CPS, and what if any, impact 
there would be on cost and time.  
A Notice of Intent to sole source was posted on April 7, 2026, to SAM.gov/Contract Opportunities; 
Notice Number: 36C26326R0055. The notice indicated that the intent was to sole source a contract 
with Stone Group Architects, Inc. utilizing FAR 6.302-1 authority; however, it was decided to change 
the authority to VAAR 819.7008. It provided a brief synopsis of history of this project which 
supported the rationale of why it was the government’s intent to sole source to Geo Bancroft 
Engineering LLC. An opportunity for firms to respond to the notice was provided until April 22, 2026, 
and no responses were received. Although the purpose and content of the Notice of Intent did not 
change, an amended notice referencing the revised authority was published. 
 
7. Determination by the CO that the Anticipated Cost to the Government will be Fair and 
Reasonable:  It is anticipated that the cost will be considered fair and reasonable. A separate price 
fair and reasonableness determination will be conducted using the techniques described in FAR

15.404-1(b), including but not limited to a technical/price evaluation of the AE’s proposal in 
comparison to the IGCE that has been provided by the Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR). 
 
8. Description of the Market Research Conducted and the Results, or a Statement of the Reasons 
Market Research Was Not Conducted: Limited market research was conducted specifically for this 
project; however, due to the uniqueness of this project and under the VAAR 819.7008 authority, a 
sole source is being conducted. Market research techniques used to identify potential sources for 
requirements like this, such as adding CPS for a project that has already been designed included 
contacting knowledgeable individuals in this industry regarding market capabilities to meet the 
requirement without duplication of costs or additional time. Current and previous discussions with 
several AE firms were held to determine what, if any, impacts could be had on an AE firm when 
executing additional design efforts and/or CPS on another AE’s design. In response to the email sent 
out to AE firms about the willingness to perform additional design services, including CPS, and what 
if any, impact there would be on cost and time, all AE firms responded that while yes, they could 
take on the responsibility of another firm’s design, it would not be ideal and would not come 
without additional costs and time. In reviewing the responses received, much of the additional costs 
and effort of time would be duplicated due to the need for additional reviews and having to learn 
the design and project. In addition, there would be cost and time risk involved for both the 
government and the AE firm. The risk to the AE firm is having to be liable for another firm’s design. 
This would create the need for higher costs to ensure that the risks are mitigated. Ultimately, the 
government would need to pay a premium for these services if another AE firm performed them.  
 
AE firms, other vendors, or the public were provided an opportunity to respond to the Notice of 
Intent to sole source that was posted on April 7, 2026, to SAM.gov/Contract Opportunities. There 
were no responses received on the posted notice.  
 
Other market research efforts included querying Small Business Administration (SBA) Small Business 
Search for SDVOSB vendors. A strict search for SDVOSB vendors in South Dakota and states within 
VISN 23 under NAICS 541330—Engineering Services was conducted and resulted in 71 vendors; 
however, the results showed many of the vendors listed were not AE firms. An additional separate 
search was conducted for Stone Group Architects, Inc. and resulted in an active SDVOSB 
certification.  
 
The results of the market research efforts indicate that soliciting from additional sources would not 
be practicable, i.e., better use of taxpayer money. Soliciting to other sources would likely create 
unwarranted and unnecessary added costs, time delays, and risks; therefore, a sole source award is 
being pursued.  
 
There are no exceptions to the Buy American Act or Trade Agreement Act for this requirement.  
 
As described in Section 6 above, market research, in accordance with FAR Part 10, was advising 
industry of the pending acquisition and soliciting inquiries from interested parties. 
 
 
9. Any Other Facts Supporting the Use of Other than Full and Open Competition:  AE firm for this

kitchen equipment, to fit the footprint of the proposed space. The vendor has also specified the

Statement of Work (SOW) 
Trelew Meteor Radar (TreMoR) Node in Global Network 
Period of Performance: Through September 30, 2026 
 
1. Background 
 
The Trelew Meteor Radar (TreMoR) is the newest node within the global meteor radar network. 
The system plays a critical role in upper-atmosphere research, space weather monitoring, and 
measuring mesospheric winds in northern Patagonia.  
This Statement of Work covers the administration, operation, and maintenance of TreMoR.  
 
2. Scope of Work 
The Contractor shall provide comprehensive operational management, technical oversight, and 
sustainment of TreMoR. The scope includes, but is not limited to, the following: 
 
2.1 System Operations and Administration 
·        Overall technical and operational management of the TreMoR system. 
·        Ensuring continuous and reliable data acquisition. 
·        Coordination with international collaborators and network partners. 
·        Oversight of data integrity, archiving, formatting, and transmission to network repositories. 
·        Scheduling and coordination of maintenance windows. 
·        Supporting operational data delivery requirements. 
 
2.2 Maintenance and Technical Support 
·        Routine preventive maintenance of the central radar system. 
·        Maintenance and monitoring of all remote autonomous receiving stations. 
·        Troubleshooting hardware, software, and communications issues. 
·        Replacement or repair coordination of malfunctioning components. 
·        System performance optimization and calibration oversight. 
 
2.3 Operational Expenses 
The SOW includes coverage and administration of operational costs necessary to maintain 
system functionality, including: 
·        Electricity and power-related expenses 
·        Internet and communications services 
·        Site security and basic physical infrastructure protection 
·        Routine local operational support costs required to ensure uninterrupted system 
performance 
 
3. Deliverables 
The Contractor shall: 
·        Maintain operational uptime consistent with standard practices for distributed scientific 
radar networks. 
·        Provide periodic operational status updates (quarterly or as requested). 
·        Immediately notify relevant stakeholders of any major system interruptions. 
·        Ensure continuity of scientific and operational data production and network integration. 

 
4. Period of Performance 
The Period of Performance shall extend from the effective date of award through September 30, 
2026.

I. PROGRAM DESCRIPTION 
 
1. STATEMENT OF OBJECTIVES 
a. This is a BAA of the Air Force Research Laboratory, Munitions Directorate 
(AFRL/RW) under the provisions of Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 
paragraph 6.102(d)(2), which provides for competitive selection of research 
proposals. Proposals submitted in response to the BAA that are selected for award are 
considered to be the results of full and open competition and in full compliance with 
the provisions of PL 98-369, the Competition in Contracting Act of 1984. This 
acquisition is unrestricted. Small businesses are encouraged to propose on all or any 
part of this solicitation. The NAICS Code for this acquisition is 541715, Research and 
Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except 
Nanotechnology and Biotechnology), and the small business size standard is 1,000 
employees. For purposes of this announcement, research is defined to be scientific 
study and experimentation directed at increasing knowledge and understanding in 
relation to long term national security needs. It is an enhancement to related 
exploratory and advanced development programs. A program should be designed to 
demonstrate well-defined and substantive research results, should not be overly 
ambitious or open-ended, and should not be a paper study that inherently requires a 
substantial testing effort. Any significant testing is unlikely; however, there is a 
possibility of experimental testing to support battle lab experiments proposed under 
this BAA. Programs to support Team Eglin Technology Demonstration Programs 
may also be considered under this BAA. 
 
b. AFRL/RW awards to educational institutions, non-profit organizations, and private 
industry for research in Air Delivered Effects. This BAA is intended to cover, in 
general nature, all research areas of interest under this Directorate. Offerors 
contemplating a submission to AFRL/RW are strongly encouraged to contact the 
AFRL/RW technical POC for the research area to ascertain the extent of interest 
AFRL/RW may have in a specific research project. 
 
c. AFRL/RW is the primary Department of the Air Force (DAF) organization concerned 
with conventional munitions technology development. AFRL/RW plans and executes 
research, development, and test of conventional munitions, and supports conventional 
munitions Weapons Program Offices. There are three product divisions within the 
Munitions Directorate that conduct research and development (R&D). They are the 
Ordnance Division (RWM), Weapon Engagement Sciences Division (RWW), and 
Strategic Planning and Integration Division (RWP).

Description  - The U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) Federal Crop Insurance Corporation 
(FCIC)/Risk Management Agency (RMA) requests services in an advisory capacity for the Nursery 
Value Select Pilot Crop Insurance Program for subtropical and temperate plants. This is a combined

This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotes are being requested, and a separate

on nursery issues related to subtropical and temperate plants in areas covered by the 10 RMA 
Regional Offices. The Contractor shall perform the following tasks as detailed below: 
(i) A
dvise, assist, and coordinate with RMA personnel and other interested parties on questions
and issues related to nursery plant production practices, plant classification and taxonomy, hardiness
zone limitations, storage and plant protection procedures and requirements, risk assessment,
wholesale marketing, and nursery crop insurance procedures.
(ii) Attend RMA and nursery industry meetings, as necessary.
(iii) Aid and participate with RMA personnel in large claims, as necessary.
(iv) Possess knowledge of the NVS pilot crop insurance program to advise and assist RMA in
modifications to the nursery program.

ATTACHMENT A

Red Hat Professional Services

Ansible Automation Platform Integration

for: 

Abacus Visual Playbook Builder and Automation Orchestrator

Department of Veterans Affairs

Veterans Health Administration (VHA)

Veterans Integrated Service Network 23 (VISN 23)

Healthcare Technology Management / Biomedical Engineering

Document Purpose

This document serves as Attachment A to the Performance Work Statement (PWS) for the Abacus Visual Playbook Builder and Automation Orchestrator acquisition. It defines the scope and requirements for Red Hat Professional Services engagement.

This document covers the interconnected technical areas requiring Red Hat expertise:

VM Provisioning and VLAN Management — API-driven infrastructure automation across multiple Nutanix sites

Windows Certificate Authentication — Secure, scalable authentication for managing Windows hosts

Certificate Management Workflows — Git-based certificate lifecycle management with four (4) distinct workflows

Presigned URL Workflow — S3 asset retrieval for playbook execution without direct AWS credentials

Real-Time Job Output Streaming — WebSocket integration for live job status in external UI

AAP Infrastructure and Self-Management — Operational best practices for running AAP

Abacus: The Orchestration Application

Abacus is the external application that orchestrates all user interaction and workflow coordination. Understanding Abacus's role is essential context for the AAP integration design.

Abacus Responsibilities

User interface for all VM provisioning and configuration requests

Determines which AAP job templates to invoke based on user actions and site context

Specifies which playbooks to execute (via Git commit reference)

Manages S3 asset references and coordinates presigned URL workflow

Handles user authentication and authorization before calling AAP APIs

Displays real-time job execution output streamed from AAP

Retrieves workstation onboarding script from Git

AAP's Role

AAP serves as the automation backend — it does not provide user-facing interfaces for end users. All user interaction happens in Abacus; Abacus calls AAP APIs; AAP runs playbooks against target infrastructure.

VM Provisioning and VLAN Management

This section describes the requirements for automating Windows VM provisioning and network management across multiple Nutanix sites.

Multi-Site Architecture

The Government has eight (8) geographically distributed sites, each with its own Nutanix Prism Element cluster. A single AAP installation serves all sites with strict security boundaries between them.

Multi-Site Security Model

The primary security requirement is strict site isolation. Users at Site A shall not have access to, view, or modify resources at Site B — even through misconfiguration.

Implementation approach:

One (1) AAP Organization per site (e.g., Minneapolis, Omaha, Fargo)

Organization-scoped Nutanix credentials (each credential can only access its site's cluster)

AD group to AAP Team mapping for RBAC

Site-specific VLAN configuration files in Git (vars/sites/{site}_vlans.yml)

Physical Sites:

Fort Meade, Fargo, Sioux Falls, Saint Cloud, Minneapolis, Omaha, Iowa City, Central Iowa

Logical Site:

VISN23 (administrative; no dedicated cluster; staff can work across all physical sites)

Each physical site has its own Prism Element cluster and AD security groups. VISN23 staff are granted cross-site access via AD group membership.

VLAN/Network Configuration Support

VLAN and network configuration management requirements are specified in Category LV [LV1-LV22]. The implementation mechanism (Abacus-native functionality, AAP workflows, dedicated service, or equivalent) is at Contractor discretion.

Red Hat Scope for VLAN-Related Work:

Red Hat's involvement in VLAN management is limited to technical guidance and integration support if the Contractor selects an AAP-based implementation approach:

API-Driven VM Provisioning

VM creation is triggered by Abacus via AAP's REST API — not through AAP's self-service portal. Abacus specifies the site, and the appropriate job template is invoked.

API Design:

One (1) Job Template per site (eight (8) total): minneapolis-vm-create, omaha-vm-create, etc.

Abacus determines which endpoint to call based on user's site

Site identifier implicit in endpoint (not passed as parameter)

VM Creation Parameters:

VM Creation Workflow Steps

The VM creation workflow shall execute the following steps:

Load VLAN configuration from Git for the target site

Perform "subnet math" to determine which VLAN the IP address belongs to

Validate IP is within usable range (not gateway, broadcast, etc.)

Check for IP conflicts (query existing VMs in Nutanix)

Create VM in Nutanix using specified template

Configure disks and CD-ROMs

Configure Windows hostname and network settings (mechanism at Contractor discretion per [L25])

Power on VM

Onboard VM for Windows authentication (see Section 3.6)

Add host to AAP inventory based on site, project, and group

Return result to Abacus

Automated VM Onboarding

After a VM is created and powered on, it must be onboarded into the Windows certificate authentication system before it can be managed by Ansible. This onboarding is an extension of the VM creation workflow.

Workflow continuation after VM power-on:

Wait for VM to complete initial Windows setup (sysprep completion)

Execute onboarding configuration (either via sysprep or initial connection)

Validate WinRM connectivity using certificate authentication

Add host to AAP inventory with correct Organization, Inventory, environment group, and component group memberships

Tag host with appropriate metadata (creation date, template used, etc.)

DRY Architecture Requirement

All eight (8) sites shall use identical playbook code — a single Git repository with no per-site playbook copies. Site-specific differences shall be handled via:

Organization-scoped credentials

Job Template extra variables (site_name, nutanix_cluster)

Site-specific variable files in Git (vars/sites/{site}_vlans.yml)

Benefit: Update playbook logic once; all eight (8) sites automatically receive the update.

VM Template Registry (Admin-Only)

Infrastructure administrators need the ability to register new Windows VM templates so they become available for VM provisioning. This shall be restricted to admin AD groups only.

Windows Certificate Authentication

This section describes the certificate-based authentication design for managing Windows hosts with Ansible.

Problem Statement

The Government needs to manage a mixed environment of Windows machines where some are domain-joined and others exist in workgroups. Several critical constraints eliminate traditional authentication methods.

Why Traditional Methods Do Not Work:

Solution: Two-Certificate Architecture

The solution is a certificate-based authentication system where Ansible uses WinRM over HTTPS with client certificate authentication. This approach uses two (2) separate certificates with distinct purposes.

Certificate 1: Windows Host Server Certificate

Purpose: Encrypts the WinRM communication channel (like HTTPS for a website)

Location: Each Windows host generates its own self-signed certificate

Private key: Never leaves the Windows host; never shared with Ansible

Validation: Ansible ignores validation (ansible_winrm_server_cert_validation: ignore)

Certificate 2: Ansible Client Certificate

Purpose: Proves Ansible's identity; replaces username/password authentication

Location: Single CA-signed certificate from Venafi on Ansible controller

Private key: Stored on Ansible controller only

Public key: Distributed to all Windows hosts (Trusted People store)

Mapping: Windows hosts map this certificate to local ansible_admin user

Git Repository for Platform Configuration

All certificate materials, root CAs, and generated scripts are stored in a dedicated Git repository. This design provides several benefits:

No TLS trust dependency: Git access via SSH requires no TLS certificate validation

Version history: All changes are tracked with full audit trail

Single source of truth: One authoritative location for all certificate-related materials

Resilience: If S3 or other infrastructure becomes untrusted due to CA rotation, Git remains accessible

Certificate Management Workflows Overview

Certificate management is divided into four (4) distinct workflows, each with a specific purpose and scope:

Initial Host Onboarding Workflow

When adding a new Windows host to Ansible management, an administrator performs an initial RDP session to execute a PowerShell setup script. This is the "moment of physical presence" to establish trust relationships.

The onboarding script performs these steps:

Generate self-signed certificate and configure WinRM HTTPS listener on port 5986

Import the root CA certificate that signed the Ansible controller certificate into Trusted Root store

Read Ansible controller certificate thumbprint

Create local ansible_admin user account with strong random password (generated locally, never transmitted)

Create certificate mapping: "when this certificate is presented, authenticate as ansible_admin"

After onboarding, Ansible can connect using certificate authentication without passwords transmitted over the network.

Workflow 1: Certificate Preparation and Staging

This workflow extracts certificate materials from a Venafi export, stages them in Git, and generates the onboarding script. It is a "safe" operation that does not touch any Windows hosts.

Trigger:

Admin uploads venafi-export.pfx (or ZIP containing PFX) to controller-certificate/ folder in Git, then runs the job template with the decryption password.

Steps:

Pull latest from Git repository

Detect file format (PFX directly, or ZIP containing PEM files, etc.)

Decrypt/extract using provided password: Private key → Store in AAP credential storage; Public certificate → Write to controller-certificate/public-cert.pem; Thumbprint → Extract and write to controller-certificate/thumbprint.txt; Signing root CA → If not already in root-ca/ folder, add it

Render onboarding-workstation.ps1 from Jinja2 template, embedding the root CA, thumbprint, public certificate, and logic for local user creation and certificate mapping

Write rendered script to generated/onboarding-workstation.ps1

Commit and push all changes to Git

Job completes successfully

Workflow 2: Certificate Rotation to Existing Hosts

This workflow pushes the new certificate to all managed Windows hosts. It requires careful design for reliability and rollback safety.

Pre-Conditions:

Workflow 1 has completed — all materials staged in Git

The old certificate is still valid (running 45-60 days before expiration)

AAP currently authenticates to Windows hosts using the old certificate

Both old and new credentials are available to AAP

Safety Mechanism: Scheduled Task Rollback

Before changing anything on a host:

Create a Windows scheduled task that will restore the old certificate mapping

Task triggers either on system reboot OR after a timeout (e.g., 10-15 minutes)

Then make the change:

Apply new certificate mapping (new thumbprint → ansible_admin)

Validate immediately:

Attempt to connect using the NEW certificate

Based on result:

Success: Delete the scheduled task (disarm the rollback), mark host as rotated

Failure: Leave scheduled task in place, mark host as failed — the host will auto-recover when the task fires or on next reboot

Workflow 3: Root CA Distribution to Windows Hosts

This workflow pushes all root CA certificates from the Git repository to all managed Windows hosts. It is idempotent — Windows handles "already present" gracefully.

Purpose:

Ensure Windows hosts trust all internal root CAs. This is needed for presigned URL downloads from Nutanix Objects S3 endpoint and any other internal HTTPS services Windows hosts may need to access.

Trigger:

Admin runs job template after adding new CA to root-ca/ folder in Git.

Steps:

Pull latest from Git repository

Read all .crt files from root-ca/ folder

For each managed Windows host: Push all CA certificates to Trusted Root Certification Authorities store (Windows handles idempotency natively)

Track per-host status: success, failed, unreachable

Persist state so re-runs can target only incomplete hosts

Report summary

Workflow 4: Execution Environment CA Trust Update

This workflow updates the AAP Execution Environment's CA trust store without requiring a container image rebuild.

Purpose:

Ensure the Execution Environment trusts all internal root CAs. This is required for amazon.aws.aws_s3 collection connecting to Nutanix Objects (presigned URL generation) and any other collections/modules that connect to internal TLS endpoints.

Desired Outcome:

Pull latest from Git repository

Read all .crt files from root-ca/ folder

Transform to format required by EE (Red Hat to recommend appropriate format)

Update the EE's CA trust source via the recommended mechanism

Result: Collections use system CA trust, which now includes new CAs — without rebuilding the EE image

Administrator Certificate Renewal Workflow

The annual certificate renewal should be as simple as possible for the administrator.

Desired admin experience:

Admin requests new certificate from Venafi portal, downloads the export (typically a ZIP containing an encrypted PFX)

Admin uploads the raw Venafi export (unmodified) to the Git repository (controller-certificate/ folder) via the Git web interface

Admin triggers Workflow 1 through AAP

Admin provides the PFX decryption password when prompted (this password shall be treated as sensitive data and not persisted after the workflow completes)

Admin reviews the generated onboarding script and staged materials

Admin triggers Workflow 2 to rotate existing hosts

If a new root CA was added, admin triggers Workflow 3 and Workflow 4 (or these may be automatically chained)

Key requirement:

The administrator should not need access to Linux command-line tools, OpenSSL, or manual file manipulation. The goal is that an administrator can complete annual certificate renewal by performing two (2) primary actions: uploading a file and providing a password.

CA Certificate Updates

When a new internal root CA is issued (for example, when the certificate authority used to sign the Nutanix Objects TLS certificate rotates), the administrator commits the new CA certificate file to root-ca/ in the Git repository.

Required propagation:

Workflow 3: Push new CA to all existing managed Windows workstations

Workflow 4: Update Execution Environment CA trust via ConfigMap/Secret

Workflow 1 (if re-run): Regenerate onboarding script (though new hosts only need the controller certificate's signing CA)

Operational Visibility and Recovery

All certificate management workflows involve changes across hundreds of hosts or critical infrastructure. Red Hat shall design these workflows with

Synopsis/Notice of Intent to Sole Source 
 
The F-35 Joint Program Office (JPO) of Arlington, V A, intends to solicit, negotiate, and award a 
sole source contract under the authority of Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) Federal 
Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 6.103-1, “Only One Responsible Source And No Other Supplies 
or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements”, to Lockheed Martin Aeronautics (LM Aero). 
The proposed North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this acquisition 
is 541512, Computer Systems Design Services, with a small business size standard of $34.0 
million. One or more of the items under this acquisition is subject to Free Trade Agreements. 
 
All responsible sources may submit a capability statement in response to this notice of intent to 
sole source. The F-35 JPO will consider all capability statements received within fifteen (15) 
days after the date of publication of this pre-solicitation notice. 
 
Potential offerors must have a Top-Secret security clearance to be eligible for award. If the 
Government chooses to release a solicitation for the requirements described herein, the 
Government will provide a DD-254 form. 
 
The F-35 JPO has a requirement to support the Foreign Military Sales (FMS) customers by (1) 
establishing connectivity between a Mission Data (MD) development site at Eglin AFB, FL, and 
a MD Validation & Verification (V&V) site at Lockheed Martin Aeronautics in Fort Worth, TX, 
and (2) providing the required hardware and software for said development and test. This effort 
is referred to XRL Integration and supports the creation of FMS Mission Data Files (MDF). The 
contractor shall be responsible for procuring, delivering, and installing the necessary hardware, 
software, and network infrastructure that supports MDF efforts and for interconnectivity.   
 
LM Aero is the sole designer, developer, and integrator of the F-35 aircraft, and the only entity 
with the experience, proprietary software, and technical expertise needed to equip the 
reprogramming laboratory and integrate it with a complimentary reprogramming facility. As a 
result, LM Aero is the only known qualified source able to fulfill the requirements specified 
herein. 
 
Points of contact are Jonathan Chen, Contract Specialist, at Jonathan.Chen@jsf.mil, and Colin 
McCarthy, Contracting Officer, at Colin.McCarthy@jsf.mil.

Takata Airbag Recall Data Compilation and 
Visualization Support 
  
Draft Statement of Work 
693JJ926RQ000286 
 
U.S. Department of Transportation (US DOT) 
 National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) 
 
 
 
 
 
 
  


 
SECTION C – DESCRIPTION, SPECIFICATION, WORK STATEMENT 
1.0 Background 
The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) is an agency of the U.S. 
Department of Transportation (DOT).  NHTSA’s mission is to save lives, prevent injuries, and 
reduce traffic-related health care and other economic costs. The agency develops, promotes, and 
implements effective educational, engineering, and enforcement programs with the goal of 
ending preventable tragedies and reducing economic costs associated with vehicle use and 
highway travel.  NHTSA’s Office of Defects Investigation (ODI) is responsible for identifying 
vehicle safety defects.  This is done by analyzing data received from numerous sources, 
including consumer complaints, tips and referrals, and manufacturer-submitted data such as 
warranty claims, death and injury reports, and manufacturer communications and technical 
service bulletins.  ODI also administers, on average, over 1,000 safety recalls each year, which 
include millions of motor vehicles, child seats, tires, and other automotive equipment.   
 
The Takata air bag inflator recalls are the largest and most complex automotive recalls in U.S. 
history.  These recalls involve over 60 million Takata air bag inflators in tens of millions of 
vehicles in the United States.  The recalls are due to a design defect whereby the phased-
stabilized ammonium-nitrate (PSAN) propellant used in the air bag inflator degrades, causing it 
to burn too quickly when ignited.  This defect can result in the inflator rupturing during 
deployment, essentially exploding and shooting sharp metal fragments (like shrapnel) at vehicle 
occupants.  Rupturing Takata inflators have resulted in 18 deaths in the United States and 
hundreds of injuries, including a significant number of serious injuries involving lacerations and 
other serious consequences to the occupants’ face, neck, and chest area. 
 
To address the unprecedented and varied challenges presented by the Takata recalls, NHTSA 
established a Coordinated Remedy Program in November 2015 to accelerate and coordinate the 
recalls, NHTSA appointed an Independent Monitor in December 2015 to assist NHTSA in the 
ongoing oversight of Takata and the vehicle manufacturers’ repair programs.  The Independent 
Monitor and his team have been heavily involved in the recalls for the past five years, and 
accordingly have developed a unique and nuanced understanding of the multitude of issues and 
challenges that the recalls pose. 
 
 
2.0 Scope 
The objective of this Statement of Work (SOW) is to enter into an agreement to acquire expert 
consulting services for the management of a Tableau-based data-reporting and data-visualization 
platform specifically tailored to the Takata recalls. 
  

 
3.0 Purpose 
This SOW supports NHTSA’s mission to save lives, prevent injuries, and reduce traffic-related 
health care and economic costs, as the rupturing of Takata inflators has resulted in 18 deaths in 
the United States and hundreds of injuries, including a significant number of serious injuries 
involving lacerations and other serious consequences to the occupants’ face, neck, and chest 
area. 
 
4.0 Specific Tasks 
Task 1:  Takata Recall Data Analysis 
The contractor shall support the intake and analysis of Takata recall data by providing: 
• Management of data intake and visualization output derived from vehicle manufacturer 
data submissions in the Takata recalls (containing recall-related information such as 
completion percentages, repair activity by dealer, and unrepaired air bag inflators by ZIP 
code). 
 
• Quality-control processes and data analyses, with reports accessible to registered users 
through a web-based portal for general reference as well as use in conjunction with 
owner-outreach and earned-media campaigns. 
 
 
• Utilization of the Tableau platform for the management of data intake and visualization 
output from vehicle manufacturer submissions as described above, using this platform for 
analysis and to facilitate segmentation analysis of vehicle owner populations 
(demographic and geographic), which in turn can be used to inform potential outreach 
strategies. 
 
The contractor shall: 
• Deliverable 01:  Provide NHTSA with access to data from vehicle manufacturer 
dashboard data submissions as incorporated into contractor’s data environment (SQL and 
Tableau) each month. 
  
• Deliverable 02:  Provide NHTSA with monthly quality-control reviews of vehicle 
manufacturer dashboard data submissions.  
 
• Deliverable 03:  Coordinated monthly conference calls and make available its data 
science experts to provide support to NHTSA throughout the duration of the contract. 
 
Task 2:  Project Meetings 
The contractor shall participate in regular on-site or virtual project meetings to discuss status 
specifications, work plans, schedule and related topics.  A bi-monthly status meeting shall be 
held with the task order COR. 

 
The contractor shall conduct presentations and briefings directly related to the project as 
requested by the government. 
• Deliverable 04: Status meetings held every other month with the COR and other NHTSA 
personnel. 
 
Task 3 – Kick-Off Meeting 
Resources:  Program Manager 
Within fifteen days (15) of award, the contractor shall meet with NHTSA program personnel via 
video conference to discuss the objective and performance of the contract.  During this time, the 
contractor shall present a briefing that discusses the detailed scope of the project: 
• Deliverable 05:  Kick-Off meeting notes and point of contact information. This report 
shall include: 
o Points of contact on this project 
o Background/Experience of staff who will be active on this project 
o Review and agree on status meetings 
o Schedule 
o Method (face-to-face, telephone, etc.) 
Any questions or other issues regarding the technical approach and staffing plan will be 
addressed at this time.  In addition, the administration of the contract will be discussed to ensure 
all parties understand their contractual duties and responsibilities. 
 
Task 4:  Project Management and Work Plan 
The contractor shall provide a Project Manager (PM) to provide overall management of the task 
order, and prepare meeting notes, deliverable schedule, and biweekly activity reports. 
The PM role includes, but is not limited to, the following major work streams: Project 
Management, Communications, Stakeholder Management, and Requirements Elicitation. The 
PM shall maintain daily communication and coordination with the COR when communicating 
with system stakeholders. The Contractor shall establish a solution that complies with Federal 
and DOT security requirements. 
 
• Deliverable 06:  Within two (2) weeks of task order award, the contractor shall prepare a 
Work Plan, based on the contractor’s proposal, task order negotiations with NHTSA, and 
information discussed at the kick-off meeting.  The work plan shall include: 
 
o Description of how the contractor will record information 
o Description of how the contractor will present/communicate findings to NHTSA 
 
The Work Plan shall be in written/electronic format and provided to the COR two (2) weeks after 
task order award. 
  

 
 
Task 5:  Bi-Monthly Progress Report and Teleconference 
 
Beginning thirty (30) days after Contract award, the Contractor shall provide twelve (12) bi-
monthly project status reports to the COR of the Contract by the 15
th calendar day of the month, 
following the month being reported.  The purpose of this report is to: 
 
o Describe the status of the technical tasks. 
o Update NHTSA on costs and schedule.   
 
• Deliverable 07:  The bi-monthly report shall include the following information: 
 
General Information: 
 
• Contractor name 
• NHTSA contract number 
• Contract number 
• Project title 
• Period of performance 
• Reporting period 
• Name and phone number for the NHTSA COR 
• Name and phone number for Project Manager 
 
Project Status 
 
• Accomplishments made during the reporting period; 
• Preliminary or interim results, conclusions, trends or other items of information that are 
of interest to NHTSA; 
• Plans for accomplishments in the next reporting period; 
• Problems that the contractor has experienced in conducting their services; and specific 
action that NHTSA should undertake to alleviate a problem; 
• Remaining milestones and deliverables, and their status; 
• An updated risk register; 
• Projected costs for the duration of the project; and 
• A comparison of actual versus projected costs 
 
• Deliverable 08: Pull Option -  The contractor shall provide secured (FIPS 140-2) 
compliant, read only connection accessible to authorized NHTSA personnel for the 
entirety of the period of performance (PoP).  The connection will access the data via:   
 
o Direct database connection to all relevant database objects (e.g. tables, views) 
o Database view as defined by NHTSA, or 
o Repository contain raw data file in the format of, but not limited to: 
o CSV file with a format defined by NHTSA 
o XML file with a schema defined by NHTSA 

 
• Deliverable 09:  Push Option – The contractor will email a password protected data file 
to selected NHTSA personnel every month and when requested by NHTSA during the 
period of performance (PoP).  The data file will be in the format of, but not limited to: 
 
o CSV file with a format defined by NHTSA
