STATEMENT OF WORK (SERVICES) 
(SOW) 
 
GENERAL INFORMATION 
Title of Project: 
Support for XNAT instance for FMRIF. 
 
Statement of Need and Purpose: 
The Functional MRI Facility (FMRIF) in the National Inst itute of Mental Health (NIMH) is seeking support 
for its data and workflow management platform, XNAT, which currently aggregates data from multiple  MRI 
scanners in the NMR Center (where FMRIF’s and other  IC’s scanners are located), provides access to 
these data to the users of these scanners, and also serves as platforms for managing, sharing, and 
processing these data. 
 
Background Information and Objective: 
Since its inception, FMRIF has operated a series of web-based platforms that serve to both aggregate 
image data from the MRI scanners ow ned and operated by the FMRIF, and to share these data out to its 
users, so they could securely retrieve their data using a web browser, or other web-based tools.  The first 
such service used by FMRIF was a commercial PACS system from Intelerad.  However, as both the number 
of scans conducted on FMRIF scanners rose, along with the volume of Functional MRI data generated, 
FMRIF encountered significant performance issues that could not be resolved by the vendor of that system.  
FMRIF then investigated multiple options to replace the Intelerad system, exploring both commercial and 
open source software (including, but not limited to, dcm4chee, XNAT, COINS, and  NiDB).  In all cases, 
there were either significant deficiencies, and / or la ck of flexibility, that prec luded use of any of these 
packages by FMRIF.  Ultimately , a custom database and web application was created in-house, by a 
FMRIF-employed programmer, and that platform served FMRIF for almost a decade.  However, in 2020, 
because of a loss of staff and expertise with FMRIF’s in-house data management systems, FMRIF sought 
a commercial option, with support, to replace its in-house data management solution.  That contract 
(75N95020P00651) was awarded to Radiologics to help FMRIF deploy, migrate data to, and support a 
single instance of XNAT.  This was successfully rolled out to FMRIF’s and other Facilities’ users, and now 
FMRIF seeks an agreement to continue supporting it s XNAT instance for its data warehousing, 
management, and processing needs. 
 
Period of Performance: 
Support for 1 year is required, starting on ASAP in FY 26, with 4 additional opti on years of support also 
being requested. 
 
SCOPE OF WORK 
General Requirements: 
Independently and not as an agent of the Government, the Contractor shall furnish all the necessary 
services, qualified personnel, material, equipment, and facilities, not otherwise provided by the Government 
as needed to perform the Statement of Work below: 
 

Version 11-30-2016-1 
FAR Part 11—Describing Agency Needs 
Page 2 of 4 
 
Specific Requirements: 
 
Support of FMRIF’s XNAT platform includes: 
• Updating XNAT software on supported instances to provide new capabilities, and address any 
emergent performance and security issues. 
• Updating integration with institutional authentic ation system (LDAP and Active Directory) to 
facilitate user authentication and system access. 
• Maintaining and updating interfaces with multiple MR scanner vendors to allow automatic capture 
and aggregation both raw (k-space) and DICOM data generated by these vendors’ platforms. 
• Supporting transport of acquire d and computed DICOM data between (i.e. send to and receive 
from) the platform and commercial PACS systems, and MR scanners 
• Continue to provide training and training materi als for FMRIF staff and users to administer and use 
the system. 
• Continue to develop and provide tools for versi on tracking and maintaining provenance of data and 
analysis pipelines. 
• Support scaling of compute and storage needs as the number of scanners, aggregated studies, 
and data processing compute loads increase.  
• Develop and support interfaces for visualizi ng and analyzing data, including, but not limited to, 
derivation of basic quality assurance metrics. 
• Continue supporting tools and / or interfaces for metadata search and management.  
• Supporting and developing tools to leverage OCI-compliant containers for data processing, 
including, but not limited to, containers providing tools such as AFNI, FreeSurfer, and FSL. 
• Support interfacing with large- scale batch processing system such as slurm and PBS on local HPC 
and commercial cloud compute resources. 
• Support exporting image and study data into BIDS  (Brain Imaging Data Structure) compliant data 
sets. 
• Support providing automated and customizable dat a anonymization / de-identification for exported 
datasets. 
• Support open REST-based APIs to all services  and data, and support for external language SDKs 
(e.g. MATLAB, Python, and R). 
• Provide mechanisms and interfaces for validat ion of data uploads into the system, and detection 
and logging of errors or omissions with such uploads. 
• Support command line integration access to API to facilitate scripting, data import and export, job 
scheduling and status, and building analysis pipelines. 
• Provide guaranteed response times to customer qu eries about issues, acknowledging of receipt of 
report of issues within 24 hours, with a 4 week window to resolving any issues raised. 
• Develop and provide options to consolidate dat a storted by XNAT on disk into fewer objects, 
allowing backup of XNAT to tape, and providing a more streamlined path for XNAT sites to migrate 
their instnaces to cloud services. 
• Keeping software deployed at, developed for, NIH open source, and available to the wider research 
community. 
• Provide at least 3 references wh o can attest to ability and experience supporting XNAT instances. 
 

Version 11-30-2016-1 
FAR Part 11—Describing Agency Needs 
Page 3 of 4 
 
LEVEL OF EFFORT: 
The contractor is expected to employ staff fa miliar with DICOM communication protocols, understand 
various computer network communication protocols and security standards, and also familiar with medical 
imaging data processing requirements.  Staff should be intimately familia r with the XNAT application, its 
operation, and should have extensive experience developing software and features that work both within, 
and interact with, the XNAT application. 
 
GOVERNMENT RESPONSIBILITIES: 
The government will supply all information necessary for contractor to complete their efforts. The 
government will also provide either physical or virtual computer systems on which the software platform will 
be deployed.  Under a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) between the contractor and government, the 
government will also provide remote access to vendor to system(s) on which the platform is deployed, to 
facilitate trouble-shooting, and performance and feature enhancements. 
 
DELIVERY OR DELIVERABLES: 
The contractor must deploy the scientific imaging data management system to a FMRIF-operated physical 
or virtual computers, and demonstrate how its operations meets and conforms to the above-listed “Specific 
Requirements.”  The contractor must also help ma intain the performance of the system, as well its 
adherence to all security policies and requirements. 
 
REPORTING REQUIREMENTS: 
The contractor should report general performance me trics of the platform (relative compute load, and 
storage usage).  The contractor should also report  when systems are access ed, and for what purposes 
was access made.  The contractor should also notify when system patches and updates become available, 
to enhance performance of the platform, as well as satisfy security and policy requirements. 
 
OTHER CONSIDERATIONS: 
Travel: 
No travel costs are anticipated to execute tis contract.  Any and all travel costs are expected to be covered 
by the costs of this contract. 
 
Key Personnel: 
The relevant key personnel have been specified under the “Level of Effort” section. 
 
Information System Security Plan: 
This statement of work requires the contractor to (1) develop, (2) have the ability to access, and (3) maintain 
a federal information system.  All work on this pla tform, and access to the machines on it will be under a 
Memorandum of Understanding betw een the contract and NIH’s Center  for Information Technology.  
Contractor will maintain systems to provide best perf ormance, and also maintain compliance with current 
NIH policies and requirements. 
 
Data Rights: 
Any data generated by this procurement or system will belong to the Government.  The Government will 
retain all rights over any generated data.

Section 508—Electronic and Information Technology Standards: 
The contractor shall comply with Section 508 of the Rehabilitation Act (29 U.S.C. § 794d), as amended by 
the Workforce Investment Act of 1998 (P.L. 105-220), August 7, 1998.  This system will not be accessible 
to the general public – it will only be accessible NIH employees with the relevant training. 
 
Publications and Publicity: 
This SOW is not expected to generate any publications. 
Confidentiality of Information: 
This SOW is not expected to utilize or generate any confidential information.

1. Independent Government’s Cost Estimate  
2. Evaluation / Selection Criteria

REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) FOR CAD MODEL CONVERSION AND COMMENT 
ADJUDICATION SERVICES 
THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) ONLY . This RFI is issued solely for 
information and planning purposes – it does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or 
a promise to issue an RFP in the future. This request for information does not commit the 
Government to contract for any supply or service whatsoever. Further, the Government is 
not at this time seeking proposals and will not accept unsolicited proposals. Responders 
are advised that the U.S. Government will not pay for any information or administrative 
costs incurred in response to this RFI; all costs associated with responding to this RFI will 
be solely at the interested party’s expense. Not responding to this RFI does not preclude 
participation in any future RFP , if any is issued. 
 
1.0 Description & Background 
Naval Surface Warfare Center Panama City Division (NSWC PCD) is seeking information on 
industry capabilities to perform a large-scale Computer-Aided Design (CAD) model 
conversion and engineering comment adjudication project. 
We currently maintain a system model consisting of approximately 8,000 individual part 
and assembly files. These files were developed in a variety of CAD software packages. The 
primary goal is to consolidate all of these files into a single, native SolidWorks format within 
a compressed timeframe. Additionally, a significant number of engineering comments 
associated with these models need to be professionally adjudicated. 
This RFI will be used to identify potential sources with the technical expertise, capacity, 
and project management skills to meet these requirements. 
2.0 Scope of Requirements 
The overall goal of this effort is to enable a robust, model-based configuration management 
environment for the system model within a SolidWorks PDM (Product Data Management) 
system. To achieve this, all system models must be converted to a uniform, native 
SolidWorks format. 
The work is divided into a primary, time-sensitive task and secondary tasks with a more 
flexible timeline. Interested parties are encouraged to propose timelines and approaches 
that reflect this prioritization. 
 
2.1 Primary Task: High-Priority Model Conversion 

This is the main effort and is on an accelerated schedule. 
• Requirement: Convert approximately 8,000 CAD models from their source formats 
into native SolidWorks files. The primary goal is a rapid turnaround to deliver a 
complete, uniform set of model files. 
• Source Files: 
• 40% Siemens NX 
• 40% SolidWorks 
• 10% CREO (formerly Pro/ENGINEER) 
• 10% Other (Vendors should specify which "Other" formats they have 
experience converting). 
• Key Deliverables: 
• Converted models must be native SolidWorks parts (.sldprt) and assemblies 
(.sldasm) with full feature tree history and design intent preserved. 
• All assembly mate and part constraints must be fully functional. 
• The conversion process must ensure no loss of data, geometry, or metadata. 
• A final, verified, and organized data package of all native SolidWorks models. 
• Project Timeline: All work under this Primary Task must be completed 
within approximately two (2) months from the start of work. 
 
2.2 Secondary Tasks: Drawing & Comment Resolution 
These tasks are secondary to the model conversion and are not bound by the same 
aggressive timeline. Responders may propose completing these tasks concurrently with 
the primary task if feasible, or as a subsequent phase of work. 
2.2.1 Sub-Task: Drawing Update and Re-formatting 
• Requirement: Convert all engineering drawings associated with the models from 
Task 2.1 and update them to a new Government-provided standard. 
• Key Deliverables: 
• All drawings converted to native SolidWorks Drawing files (.slddrw). 

• Drawings must remain fully associated and correctly linked to their 
respective 3D models. 
• All drawings must be updated to incorporate a new Government-provided 
SolidWorks drawing template and adhere to all specified formatting 
guidance. 
2.2.2 Sub-Task: Implementation of Approved Engineering Changes 
• Requirement: Implement approximately 5,000 comments into the newly converted 
SolidWorks models and drawings. 
• Government-Furnished Information: A Comment Resolution Matrix (CRM) will be 
provided. This matrix details all comments and their corresponding Government-
approved corrective actions. All GFI will be CUI (Controlled Unclassified 
Information). 
• Key Deliverables: 
• Execution and implementation of the approved corrective actions directly 
into the native SolidWorks files (both models and drawings). 
• A final disposition report or an updated CRM, verifying the completion of 
each required change. 
• A version-controlled set of the final, modified SolidWorks files. 
3.0 Requested Information 
Interested parties are requested to provide a capability statement that addresses the 
following areas: 
• Corporate Information: 
• Company Name, Address, and Website. 
• Point of Contact (Name, Title, Email, and Phone Number). 
• CAGE Code and/or UEI Number. 
• Business Size and Socio-Economic Status (e.g., Small Business, 8(a), 
Woman-Owned, etc.). The applicable North American Industry Classification 
System (NAICS) code for this effort is anticipated to be 541330 (Engineering 
Services). 
• Technical Approach & Capabilities: 

• A detailed description of your proposed methodology for the CAD conversion 
task, including software tools, quality assurance checks, and processes to 
ensure model integrity. 
• A detailed description of your proposed process for the comment 
adjudication task, including how you would track, report, and resolve the 
comments. 
• An outline of your project management plan. This plan should specifically 
address the two-month timeline for the Primary Task and provide a separate, 
proposed timeline for the Secondary Tasks. Please include proposed 
milestones and your communication strategy. 
 
• Innovative Solutions & Artificial Intelligence (AI): NSWC PCD is interested in 
understanding and potentially leveraging innovative solutions to increase the 
efficiency and accuracy of this project. Responders are encouraged to 
describe any proposed use of Artificial Intelligence (AI), machine learning, or 
other advanced automation techniques in their approach to either the CAD 
conversion or the comment adjudication tasks. Please detail the expected 
benefits (e.g., reduced timeline, improved quality, cost savings) and any 
associated risks of using such technologies. 
• A description of your data handling and security protocols to protect 
sensitive information. 
• Past Performance & Experience: 
• Provide brief summaries of at least two (2) and no more than four (4) projects 
of similar size and scope completed within the last five years. Include the 
client, a description of the work, and the project outcome. 
• Cost Information: 
• Provide a Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) cost estimate. This ROM should 
be broken down to clearly distinguish between the cost for the Primary Task 
(2.1) and the costs for each of the Secondary Tasks (2.2.1 and 2.2.2). 
4.0 Submission Instructions 
• Responses are requested no later than 1500 CST 29 April, 2026. 
• Submissions should be sent electronically in Portable Document Format (PDF) 
to: garrett.j.calhoun.civ@us.navy.mil. 

• The subject line of the email should read: "Response to RFI for CAD Conversion 
Services" . 
• Proprietary information, if any, MUST BE CLEARLY MARKED. All submissions 
become Government property and will not be returned. 
5.0 Questions 
• All questions regarding this RFI shall be submitted in writing by email 
to: garrett.j.calhoun.civ@us.navy.mil. Phone inquiries will not be accepted.

1. The NATO Communications and Information Agency (NCIA) is conducting market 
research to identify qualified vendors and gather input on  a service to support the NATO 
Intelligence Surveillance Reconnaissance Force (NISRF) and provide them with a 
Geographic Information System (GIS)  data management service.  We hereby issue the 
attached Request for Information (RFI)  RFI-186975-GIS_DMS to solicit feedback from 
capable and interested industry partners. 
 
2. This RFI is issued for planning purposes only and is not a request for bids . It is part of 
NCIA’s effort to ensure it has a clear understanding of the marketplace, available 
capabilities, and potential acquisition strategies to deliver NISRF the data management 
service in support of their Intelligence Production Capacity Alignment. 
 
3. We value your insight and invite you to: 
a. Provide a response to the information requested at Annex A. 
b. Share relevant corporate capabilities and experience; 
c. Review and comment on our draft requirements (Annex B) with a view to providing 
recommendations for improving performance outcomes,  competition, 
effectiveness and efficiency; and i dentifying any risks or concerns that should be 
considered during planning. 
d. Provide your responses to the RFI questions in Annex C. 
 
4. Submission instructions and additional details can be found in the enclosure to this RFI. 
 
5. Only companies from a NATO member country can participate in or respond to this RFI 
(https://www.nato.int/cps/en/natohq/nato_countries.htm). 
 
6. Should you have any questions or need clarification, please contact Adrian Lita, Senior 
Contracting Officer, at Adrian.Lita@ncia.nato.int  
 
7. We thank you in advance for your time and input, and we look forward to engaging with 
you as we shape this potential acquisition. 
 
8. Annexes: 
 
• Request for Information at Annex A 
• High-Level Summary of Requirements at Annex B 
• RFI Questions at Annex C 
• Distribution List at Annex D

REQUEST FOR INFORMATION  
 
A. Introduction 
 
1. The NATO Communications and Information Agency (NC IA) is conducting market 
research to identify potential sources  and gather information regarding industry 
capabilities, through eliciting industry views on the envisioned services for the NISRF 
GIS data management service outlined at Annex B - to inform the project requirements. 
This Request for Information (RFI) is issued solely for informational purposes and does 
not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), Request for Quotation (RFQ), or invitation 
for bid.  
 
B. Purpose 
 
1. The purpose of this RFI is to obtain input from industry to help inform the NCIA’s 
acquisition planning. Responses to this RFI will assist in refining requirements, 
identifying capabilities, and shaping the strategy for any future solicitation. 
 
C. Background 
 
1. NCIA seeks to provide a NISRF GIS data management service  to NISRF to support 
their Processing, Exploitation and Dissemination (PED) process, both for federated 
and organic PED.  
2. This NISRF GIS data management service  will support, maintain, manage, develop, 
and advise the NISRF with various GIS applications, workflows, scripts and services. 
3. The Service is envisaged to contain several key capabilities, including : development 
of dedicated tools, manage data synchronization with external entities, and maintain 
NISRF GIS dashboards, portals and applications. 
4. A High -Level Summary of the GIS data management service requirements are 
contained within Annex B. 
5. The RFI seeks to elicit the view of industry partners on the scope of the envisioned 
services and facilitate the Agency’s insight into best -in-class industry solutions , 
including current market capabilities, and pricing models of Services offered. 
6. A full list of questions that the Agency would like to canvass industry views on are 
contained within Annex C 
 
D. Submission Instructions 
 
1. Interested parties are invited to respond in accordance with the instructions below: 
 
a. Submit responses via the email address in section H no later than 12:00 hours 
Central European Time (CET) on 30 April 2026. 
 
b. Responses should be submitted in PDF or Word format and must not exceed 10 
pages, including: 
i. Responses to Annex A, comments on Annex B 
ii. Responses to the questions in Annex C 
 
excluding: 
 
i. Cover page

iii. Attachments such as past performance references

i. “Response to RFI-186975-GIS_DMS – [Company Name]” 
 
E. Industry Engagement 
 
1. The NCIA does not envisage conducting further industry engagement following the 
receipt of RFI responses.  
2. However, should this approach change, further information on additional RFIs and/or

and distributed via the National Delegations, NATEXs, and Embassies.

Note: The NCIA is seeking industry feedback. 
 
1. Background 
 
The NATO Communications and Information Agency (NCIA) aims to support the NISRF with 
their GIS data management requirements.   
 
NCIA requires a contractual mechanism that comprises of best-in-class industry solutions to 
provide this type of data management services for NISRF.  
 
2. Scope 
 
The overall scope of the NISRF GIS data management service is to provide support with the 
development, management, and sustainment of the NCIA provided geospatial solutions for 
the NISRF.  
The service provider is invited to propose a service that includes, but is not limited to, the 
requests below.  
 
 
a. Develop ArcGIS ModelBuilder models, services, tools, python utilities 
and scripts. 
b. Manage and maintain ARCGIS databases, services and data access 
permissions 
c. Manage and maintain ARCGIS operational data, layers, (map) services, 
workflows, templates, dashboard, portals, service and user accounts 
d. Create and maintain Topographic-, hydrographic-, aeronautical-, 
intelligence-, and imagery base maps at NISRF  
e. Advise NISRF staff on Geospatial Data Management and (Arc) GIS 
technology matters. 
 
 
3. Envisaged Contractual Relationship 
 
As stated in the Objectives section, the Agency envisages the NISRF GIS data 
management service capability to be provided by the successful Contractor in any 
subsequent NATO Competitive Procurement procedure.  
 
 
4. Performance Requirements/ Service Level Agreements 
 
The service should encompass, but is not limited to, the following type of service 
provisions. The service provider is invited to propose a comprehensive service that 
complies with the objectives for NISRF.  
 
a. Working hours: office hours 
b. Reporting: weekly 
c. Service Progress Meeting: quarterly

QUALITY ASSURANCE SURVEILLANCE PLAN (QASP)

Foundation Sustainment Support, Software and Integration (FS3i)

Software COTS Procurement and Common Services Task Order

31July 2025

TABLE OF CONTENTS

QUALITY ASSURANCE SURVEILLANCE PLAN (QASP)

INTRODUCTION

This Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan (QASP) is pursuant to the requirements listed in the Foundation Sustainment Support, Software and Integration (FS3i) IDIQ Performance Work Statement (PWS) and the “Software COTS Procurement and Common Services” Task Order (TO) Performance Work Statement (PWS). This plan sets forth the procedures, guidelines and surveillance measure for the FS3i Government Program Management Office (GPMO) will use to ensure the required performance standards or service levels are achieved by the contractor.

Purpose

This QASP is a government-developed document used to determine if the contractor’s performance meets the performance standards contained in the contract. The QASP defines the roles and responsibilities of all members of the GPMO, identifies the performance objectives, defines the methodologies used to monitor and evaluate the contractor’s performance, describes quality assurance documentation requirements, and describes the analysis of quality assurance monitoring results.

The contractor is responsible for implementing and delivering performance that meets contract standards using its Quality Control Plan (QCP). The QASP provides the structure for the government’s surveillance of the contractor’s performance to assure that it meets contract standards.

The government has provided the contractor an informational copy of the QASP as an Attachment to the solicitation to support the contractor’s efforts in developing a QCP.

The QASP is part of the contract in that the CO and/or COR will report the results of the surveilled Acceptable Performance Levels (APLs) to the Award Fee Board for consideration in the Award Fee determination. 

Performance Management Approach

The PWS structures the acquisition around “what” service or quality level is required, as opposed to “how” the contractor should perform the work (i.e. results, not compliance). This QASP will define the performance management approach taken by the GPMO to monitor and manage the contractor’s performance to ensure the expected outcomes or performance objectives communicated in the PWS are achieved. Performance management rests on developing a capability to review and analyze information generated through performance assessment. The ability to make decisions based on the analysis of performance data is the cornerstone of performance management; this analysis yields information that indicates whether expected outcomes for the project are being achieved by the contractor.

Performance management represents a significant shift from the more traditional quality assurance (QA) concepts in several ways. Performance management focuses on assessing whether outcomes are being achieved and to what extent. This approach migrates away from scrutiny of compliance with the processes and practices used to achieve the outcome. A performance-based approach enables the contractor to play a large role in how the work is performed, as long as the proposed processes are within the stated constraints. The only exceptions to process reviews are those required by law (federal, state, and local) and compelling business situations, such as safety and health. A “results” focus provides the contractor flexibility to continuously improve and innovate over the course of the contract as long as the critical outcomes expected are being achieved and/or the desired performance levels are being met.

Performance Management Strategy

The contractor is responsible for the quality of all work performed. The contractor measures that quality through the contractor’s own quality control (QC) program. QC is work output, not workers, and therefore includes all work performed under this contract regardless of whether the work is performed by contractor employees or by subcontractors. The contractor’s QCP will set forth the staffing and procedures for self-inspecting the quality, timeliness, responsiveness, customer satisfaction, and other performance requirements in the PWS. The contractor will develop and implement a performance management system with processes to assess and report its performance to the designated government representative. This QASP enables the government to take advantage of the contractor’s QC program.

The government representative(s) will monitor performance and review performance reports furnished by the contractor to determine how the contractor is performing against communicated performance objectives. The government will make determination regarding incentives based on performance measurement metric data and notify the contractor of those decisions. The contractor will be responsible for making required changes in processes and practices to ensure performance is managed effectively.

ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Program Manager

The PM has the ultimate authority for the success or failure of the program and represents the Agency to the awarded vendor. The PM’s authorized representatives assist in administering the program contract. The PM is responsible for general/technical and financial administration of the program and to ensure proper government surveillance of the contractor’s performance. The PM is not empowered to make any contractual commitments or authorize any contractual changes on the government’s behalf. Any changes the contractor deems may affect contract price, terms, or conditions shall be referred to the CO for action. The PM and additional representatives will have the responsibility for completing QA monitoring forms used to document the inspection and evaluation of the contractor’s work performance. Government surveillance may occur under the inspection of services clause for any service relating to the contract.

Contracting Officer

The contracting officer (CO) is responsible for monitoring contract compliance, contract administration, and cost control and for resolving any differences between the observations documented by the Program Manager (PM) and/or Contracting Officer's Representative (COR), and the contractor. The CO will designate one full-time COR as the government authority for performance management. The number of additional representatives serving as technical inspectors/monitors depends on the complexity of the services measured, as well as the contractor’s performance, and must be identified and designated by the CO.

2.1 The Contracting Officer’s Representative

The Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR) is designated in writing by the CO to act as his or her authorized representative to assist in administering a contract. COR limitations are contained in the written appointment letter. The COR is responsible for general/technical administration of the project and ensures proper government surveillance of the contractor’s performance. The COR is not empowered to make any

contractual commitments or to authorize any contractual changes on the government’s behalf. Any changes that the contractor deems may affect contract price, terms, or conditions shall be referred to the CO for action. The COR will have the responsibility for completing QA monitoring forms used to document the inspection and evaluation of the contractor’s work performance. Government surveillance may occur under the inspection of services clauses (Reference Part I, Section E of the contract) for any service relating to the contract.

METHODOLOGIES TO MONITOR PERFORMANCE

Surveillance Techniques

In an effort to minimize the performance management burden, simplified surveillance methods shall be used by the government to evaluate contractor performance when appropriate. These are the primary methods of surveillance:

100% Inspection – Each month, within 5 business days following contractor delivery, the COR will review the generated documentation to ensure compliance to quality performance

While it is the Government’s intent to conduct inspections 100% of the time, the volume of inspections may exceed the capacity of the GPMO. Should that happen the GPMO will conduct inspections in accordance with the priorities established by the Government Program Manager (GPM)

Periodic Inspection – The COR typically performs periodic inspections on a monthly basis

Random Sampling – At the CO/COR’s discretion, the government may review inspect documents generated by the contractor, without notice.

Validation – manual or automated testing demonstrates that the software baseline is behaving as expected by the users

Customer Feedback – described in 3.1.1

Customer Feedback

The contractor is expected to establish and maintain professional communication between its employees and customers. The primary objective of this communication is customer satisfaction. Customer Satisfaction is the most significant external indicator of the success and effectiveness of all services provided and can be measured through customer surveys.

Performance management drives the contractor to be customer focused through initially and internally addressing customer feedback and investigating the issues and/or complaints but the customer always has the option to communicate feedback/complaints to the CO and COR, as opposed to the contractor.

Customer feedback/complaints may also be obtained either from the results of formal customer satisfaction surveys or from random customer surveys.

QUALITY ASSURANCE DOCUMENTATION

The Performance Management Feedback Loop

The performance management feedback loop begins with the communication of expected outcomes. Performance standards are expressed in the PWS and assessed using the performance monitoring techniques shown in Attachment 1 – Performance Requirements Summary.

Monitoring Forms

The government’s QA surveillance, accomplished by the COR, will be reported using the monitoring form in Attachment 2 – Sample Quality Assurance Monitoring Form. This form, when completed, will document

the government’s assessment of the contractor’s performance under the contract to ensure that the required results are being achieved. The COR and CO will retain a copy of all completed QA surveillance forms.

ANALYSIS OF QUALITY ASSURANCE ASSESSMENT

Determining Performance

The Government will use the monitoring methods cited in Attachment 1 to determine whether the performance standards/service levels/AQLs have been met. If the contractor has not met the minimum requirements, it may be asked to develop a corrective action plan to show how and by what date it intends to bring performance up to the required levels.

Reporting

At the end of each month, the COR will prepare a written report for the CO and GPM, summarizing the overall results of the quality assurance surveillance of the contractor’s performance. This written report, will include the contractor’s submitted report and the completed quality assurance monitoring forms (Attachment 2 – Sample Quality Assurance Monitoring Form), will become part of the QA documentation. It will enable the government to evaluate whether the contractor is meeting the stated objectives and/or performance standards, including cost/technical/scheduling objectives. This report will be provided to the Award Fee board as input for final Award Fee determination and used for purposes of the contractor’s annual Performance Assessment Report (PAR). 

Reviews and Resolution

The CO or PM may require the contractor’s project manager, or a designated alternate, to meet with the CO and/or PM and other government personnel as deemed necessary to discuss performance evaluation. The PM will define a frequency of in-depth reviews with the contractor, including appropriate self-assessments by the contractor; however, if the need arises, the contractor will meet with the PM and/or COR as often as required or per the contractor’s request. The agenda of the reviews may include the following:

Monthly performance assessment data and trend analysis

Issues and concerns of both parties

Projected outlook for upcoming months and progress against expected trends, including a corrective action plan analysis

Recommendations for improved efficiency and/or effectiveness

Issues arising from the performance monitoring processes

The COR will coordinate and communicate with the contractor to resolve issues and concerns regarding marginal or unacceptable performance.

The COR, CO and GPM along with the contractor will jointly formulate tactical and long- term courses of action. Decisions regarding changes to metrics, thresholds, or service levels will be clearly documented. Changes to service levels, procedures, and metrics will be incorporated as a contract modification at the convenience of the CO.

DESCRIPTION

Notice of Intent to Sole Source Requirement

The Department of Veterans Affairs, VA Healthcare System, Network Contracting Office 1, Regional Procurement Office East intends to negotiate a sole source contract for 6515 - Medical and Surgical Instruments, Equipment, and Supplies in accordance with FAR13.106-1(b). Competition is restricted on this procurement due to Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements. The associated NAICS code for this is 541715. The vendor will be Stumptown Research and Development, LLC. PO Box 1110, Black Mountain, NC 28711.

Description of Supplies:

SUPPLY: The Contracting Activity is looking to acquire the design and fabrication of an Advanced Blast Simulator with a 24in x 24in internal cross section for testing biomedical targets. This system will include a dual mode driver, expanding transition section, test section and end wave eliminator. The test section will be made with two observation ports and multiple sensor locations. One test specimen holder, a data acquisition computer, a pitot-static probe, and three piezoresistive wall mounted pressure sensors. Installation and operational training shall be included. The location of the service will be at the White River Junction Veterans Affairs Medical Center 215 North Main Street, White River Junction, VT 05009.

It is the Government's belief that only the proposed candidate possesses the required capabilities to successfully meet this requirement.  It is the Government's intention to solicit and negotiate with only this source. This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals.  It is not a solicitation or request for offers.

DESCRIPTION

As permitted by FAR Part 10, this Sources Sought Notice (SSN) is being utilized for informational and planning purposes for Veteran Decedent Memorial Data/Information Analysis & Visualization. Your response will assist the Government in the development of its acquisition strategy for a possible Request for Quote (RFQ), to be issued on a later date. 

This SSN shall not be construed as an RFQ or as any commitment or obligation on the part of the Government to issue a solicitation. No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to this SSN or any follow-up information requests. 

Response is strictly voluntary - it is not mandatory to submit a response to this notice to participate in any formal RFQ process that may take place in the future however, it should be noted that information gathered through this notice may significantly influence VA’s acquisition strategy.

BACKGROUND

The work outlined in this PWS shall be performed by a Small Business Innovation Research Program (SBIR) Phase II Contract holder by further developing, integrating, and applying the SBIR-derived approach to a new mission area and use case(s) supporting U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA)/National Cemetery Administration (NCA). 

NCA is one of three Administrations within VA responsible for delivering services and benefits to Veterans. Pursuant to the National Cemeteries Act of 1973 and other statutory authorities and regulations (38 U.S.C. 2306, 38 U.S.C. Chapter 24, 38 CFR Parts 38-39), NCA is responsible for providing cemetery services to Veterans and other eligible persons. NCA’s responsibilities include the operation and maintenance of 153 national cemeteries and the construction of new national cemeteries.

NCA’s mission is to honor Veterans with final resting places in national shrines and with lasting tributes that commemorate their service to our Nation. NCA provides burial space for eligible Veterans and family members; maintains graves and their environs as national shrines in perpetuity; supports state and tribal organizations through the Veterans Cemetery Grants Program; and furnishes headstones, markers, medallions, and Presidential Memorial Certificates in recognition of service to a grateful nation. NCA also administers grants for establishing or expanding state and tribal government Veterans cemeteries.

A key aspect of this project is to support NCA in the operational programming of the Riverside Education and Interpretive Center (REIC). As a natural extension of NCA’s mission, NCA is enhancing and transforming its approach to memorialization beyond foundational elements (headstones/markers/medallions and Presidential Memorial Certificates) to enable more interactive and engaging experiences with the communities in which national cemeteries are located. Beginning in 2016, NCA established the Veterans Legacy Program (VLP) to commemorate Veterans and service members through discovery and sharing of their stories, including education outreach to K-12 schools and students. In 2019, NCA launched the Veterans Legacy Memorial (VLM), an online memorial platform allowing users to interact with the memories of Veterans interred in NCA cemeteries. Establishing an education and interpretive center at Riverside National Cemetery is a logical next step in this transformational effort, and the REIC will be the first of its kind for NCA.

This effort will leverage an iterative, SBIR-informed delivery approach to produce implementation-ready products that optimize REIC stand-up and can be adapted for future NCA education and interpretive centers.

PTAG: Seeking Contractor for USPTO Asset Management Program Support Services  
 
THIS IS A PTAG SOURCES SOUGHT REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) ONLY.  
 
This PTAG 6.1.1 Sources Sought (request for information) Notice (RFI) is strictly for market research 
ONLY.  It is for informational and planning purposes and shall NOT be construed as a solicitation or 
as an obligation or commitment by the Government at this time. 
 
PTAG 
The Government contemplates utilizing the Alternative Competition Method in accordance with the 
Patent and Trademark Office Acquisition Guidelines (PTAG) and the Patent and Trademark Office 
Efficiency Act 35 U.S.C. 2(b)(4)(A). This Sources sought notice is intended as preliminary market 
information gathering which the USPTO will use to determine which contractor(s) is/are the most 
likely to successfully meet the agency’s needs and are thereby eligible to participate in an alternative 
competition. As a result of this market research, the solicitation will only be issued to those qualified 
contractor(s) that are deemed most likely to successfully meet the agency’s requirement as stated 
below. 
• This RFI is being made available under NAICS 541519 – Other Computer Related Services and 
PSC R799 Support— Management: Other 
 
1. Purpose of this Sources Sought / Request for Information (RFI) 
The purpose of the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office’s (USPTO) Request for Information (RFI) is to 
educate USPTO about the capabilities and offerings of commercial sources to offer comprehensive 
Asset Manager Support Services which includes extensive use of the ServiceNow platform.  
 
The responses to this RFI should provide USPTO management with an understanding of each firms   
experience and the range of services provided.  This will allow USPTO management to conduct 
thorough market research, identify suitable providers, and make informed decisions. 
 
 
#### ABRIDGED STATEMENT OF WORK #### 
 
A. Disclaimer:   
This is an abridged version of the SOW specific to this source sought notice (RFI).  It is intended to 
provide enough information to allow contractors the ability to determine whether they would be 
able to fulfill these requirements.   
 
B. Background 
 
Under the Office of the Chief Administrative Officer (OCAO), the Office of Administrative 
Services (OAS) is responsible for managing the agency’s Asset Management Program. The Asset 
Management Program provides personal property management inventory services for the 
agency’s accountable property. The program also manages the surplus and property disposal 
efforts and oversees and tracks the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office’s (USPTO) assets through 

RFI Number: ACQ-26-0906     Page 2 of 9 
 
receipt at the agency’s warehouses through deployment and final surplus/excess.  The Asset 
Management Program supports approximately 15,000 users on campus, regional offices, 
teleworkers and in contractor facilities  on and offsite.  
 
The Inventory Support Team (IST) is the  central support for the program’s asset management 
oversight work. The IST oversees a multitude of services, and all processes related to support  
asset management including Product Category Maintenance; Property Custodian 
Administration; Surplus/Excess Maintenance; Data Quality; Financial Reconciliation; System  
Testing; Standard Development; Asset Verification; Quality Assurance; and Asset Reporting. 
The IST also provides all asset management related Training and Documentation; and 
management of the Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) hardware.  
 
The IST supports the development and implementation of asset management policies, 
guidance, and procedures to ensure  that USPTO is positioned to maintain accountability for its  
acquired assets. The contractor researches and applies new concepts, practices, and develops 
solutions to resolve problems for which established policies are not fully applicable. The 
contractor collaborates with OAS, Office of  the Chief Information Officer (OCIO), and other 
USPTO Business Unit (BU) staff to identify issues, problems, and concerns with asset 
management policies, practices, systems, and procedures.  The IST proposes modifications to 
streamline and eliminate redundancies and improve management, accountability, and 
reporting of USPTO property.  
 
This initiative is part of the Mission Support Goal: Deliver Organizational Excellence in the 
Strategic Plan. Objective 1: Enhance Human Capital Management and Foster Employee 
Engagement – A. Optimize performance culture.  
 
C. Objective 
 
The objective of the contract is to provide OAS with support for the oversight and 
management of USPTO’s Asset Management Program for the next five years and ensure 
no interruption in services.  
 
To assist OAS in leveraging automation and technology – to include ServiceNow , IBM 
Tririga, Tableau, and Business Analytics – in the overall management of the Asset 
Management Program, the SOW will include conducting a site survey as part of the 
continuous improvement process.  
 
D. Scope  
(The requirements/deliverables include but are not limited to those listed below – a  
complete and final  SOW will be provided when an RFQ is released)   
 
The Contractor shall be responsible for the project management, oversight coordination, 
process and inventory support for the following activities:  
 
D.1 Inventory Support: 

RFI Number: ACQ-26-0906     Page 3 of 9 
 
 
D.1.1 Contractor shall be responsible for the execution of the Fiscal Year Asset 
Management guidelines and schedules of activities for all organizations within the 
U. S. Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO). The guidelines and schedules of 
activities will be determined by the USPTO’s Asset Management Team and will be 
provided to the contractor via the Asset Management page located on the 
PTOWeb homepage. As changes are required, updated documents will be posted 
to the Asset Management page.  
 
D.1.2 Contractor shall be responsible for collaborating with the Office of the Chief 
Information Officer’s (OCIO) ServiceNow team as it relates to the scheduling and 
distribution of USPTO Asset Attestation notifications using the ServiceNow  
automated attestation system based on the determined distribution schedule.  
 
D.1.3 Contractor will be responsible for monitoring the completion of asset attestation 
verification for both end users and remaining Property Custodians with NFN NONE 
assigned assets through a ServiceNow created dashboard. The Contractor will be 
responsible for working with the ServiceNow team to identify a solution for asset 
attestation noncompliance and assist in the contact of end user supervisors and 
remaining Property Custodians for NFN NONE and Shared assigned assets. 
 
D.1.4 Contractor will responsible for perform inventory scan on Shared and NFN None 
assets. 
 
D.1.5 Contractor shall maintain 95% to 98% inventory accuracy of all active/achieved 
property/assets. 
 
D.1.6 Contractor shall perform audit and provide update on all unverified/false assets within 
30 days.

Statement of Work (SOW) for

Engineering and Technical Support for Division 42 Propulsion Program 

1.0 INTRODUCTION

1.0.1  The Naval Surface Warfare Center Philadelphia Division (NSWCPD) is a Department of Defense entity responsible for research and development, test and evaluation, engineering and fleet support organization for the Navy’s ships, submarines, military watercraft and unmanned vehicles.  This requirement is for NSWCPD Division 42, which is responsible for engineering and technical support services, program management, and logistics support services for propulsion systems onboard US Navy Vessels.

1.0.2  This contract is for non-personal services.  It does not create employment rights with the U.S. Government whether actual, inherent, or implied

1.0.3  Government/Contractor Relationship

1.0.3.1  The services to be delivered under this Contract are non-personal services and the parties recognize and agree that no employer-employee relationship exists or will exist under the Contract between the Government and the Contractor's personnel.  Therefore, it is in the best interest of the Government to provide both parties a full understanding of their respective obligations. 

1.0.3.2  The Contractor employees shall identify themselves as Contractor personnel by introducing themselves or being introduced as Contractor personnel and displaying distinguishable badges or other visible identification for meetings with Government personnel. In addition, Contractor personnel shall appropriately identify themselves as Contractor employees in telephone conversations and in formal and informal written correspondence.

1.0.3.3   Contractor personnel under this Contract shall not engage in any of the inherently Governmental functions listed at FAR Subpart 7.5 or DFARS Subpart 207.5. 

1.0.4  Employee Relationship: 

1.0.4.1  The services to be performed under this Contract do not require the Contractor or its personnel to exercise personal judgment and discretion on behalf of the Government.  Rather the Contractor's personnel will act and exercise personal judgment and discretion on behalf of the Contractor.  

1.0.4.2  Rules, regulations, directives, and requirements that are issued by the U. S. Navy and NSWCPD under its responsibility for good order, administration, and security are applicable to all personnel who enter a Government installation or who travel on Government transportation.  This is not to be construed or interpreted to establish any degree of Government control that is inconsistent with a non-personal services contract. 

1.0.4.3  Inapplicability of Employee Benefits: This Contract does not create an employer-employee relationship.  Accordingly, entitlements and benefits applicable to such relationships do not apply.   

1.0.4.4  It is the Contractor's, as well as the Government's, responsibility to monitor Contract activities and notify the Contracting Officer if the Contractor believes that the intent of this Section has been or may be violated.  

1.0.4.4.1  The Contractor shall notify the Contracting Officer in writing via letter or email within three (3) calendar days from the date of any incident that the Contractor considers to constitute a violation of this Section.  The notice should include the date, nature, and circumstances of the conduct; the name, function, and activity of each Government employee or Contractor official or employee involved or knowledgeable about such conduct; identify any documents or substance of any oral communication involved in the conduct; and the Contractor's estimated date when, absent a response, cost, schedule or performance will be impacted.

1.0.4.4.2  The Contracting Officer will, within five (5) calendar days after receipt of notice, respond to the notice in writing.  In responding, the Contracting Officer will either:

(i)	Confirm the conduct is in violation and when necessary direct the mode of further performance,

(ii)	Countermand any communication regarded as a violation,

(iii)	Deny that the conduct constitutes a violation and when necessary direct the mode of further performance, or

(iv)	In the event the notice is inadequate to make a decision, advise the Contractor what additional information is required, and establish the date by which it should be furnished by the Contractor.  

BACKGROUND

The NSWCPD Propulsion Division 42 is responsible for engineering and technical support services, program management, and life cycle engineering for Hull, Mechanical and Electrical (HM&E) systems on U.S. Navy Vessels. The systems and support include Diesel Engines, Gas Turbine Engines, Combustion Air Systems, Machinery Arrangements, Main Reduction Gear (MRG), Propulsors, Propellors, Shafting, Waterjets, Rudders, Bow Thrusters, Dehumidifiers, and Vent Fog Systems. 

SCOPE OF WORK 

The contractor shall provide engineering, technical support, and program management services that include Ship Design and Acquisition Support, In-Service engineering support, Modeling and Simulation Support, Machinery Systems Engineering Support, Ashore and Afloat Test Engineering Support, Field Engineering Support, Logistics and Training Support

The Navy engineering and business knowledge areas covered by this scope are:

Combustion air systems in-service engineering and life cycle management covering all surface ship (non-nuclear) diesel and gas turbine ship classes and craft

Small gas turbine engine systems in-service and life cycle engineering for the Navy’s assault craft and mine hunter platforms

New acquisition and in-service gas turbine engineering and integration support

Machinery system arrangements design and integration development for early concept explorations, Programs of Record (POR), in-service modernization projects, and new capabilities assessments for all Surface ship (non-nuclear) classes

Afloat workshop arrangements design and integration development for early concept explorations, Programs of Record (POR), in-service modernization projects, and new capabilities assessments

New acquisition program Systems Engineering Management and design support, 2S COG Program Engineering Support, including Gas Turbine Engines, Combustion Air Systems, Machinery Arrangements, Main Reduction Gear (MRG), Propulsors, Propellors, Shafting, Waterjets, Rudders, Bow Thrusters, Dehumidifiers, and Vent Fog Systems. 

Land-Based Test Site and Engineering Site Systems Engineering and Technical Management during site concept development, production, and operation.

Electric Drive Test Facility (EDTF), Energy Programs, Compatibility Test Facility (CTF), Electric Ships Office, Science & Technology (S&T), Research & Development (R&D and Hybrid Electric Drive (HED).

Support for the Propulsion Executive Steering Committee

Condition Based Maintenance (CBM)/Condition Assessment

Compatibility Test Facility (CTF) Systems Engineering and Technical Management during site concept development, production, and operation

2.0 APPLICABLE DOCUMENTS 

2.1 The Contractor shall reference and utilize the latest version available of applicable documents when performing tasks within this SOW.

2.2 These documents will be provided upon request.

Risk Management Framework Process Guide , Version 3.1 dated 3 Feb 2020 (available at https://portal.secnav.navy.mil/NAVWAR/Pages/default.aspx)

DoD 8570.01-M Information Assurance Workforce Improvement Program, Change 4 dated 10 Nov 2015

MIL-STD-3045, Design Criteria Standard, U.S. Navy Surface Ship Machinery Arrangements

S9311-A3-MMA-A10 (Rev 11) Auxiliary Power Unit (APU) System, Landing Craft Air Cushion (LCAC) Technical Manual

S9234-FG-MMM-010 (Rev 4) Model T-1302S-28AA Saturn Gas Turbine Power Plant Assembly Technical Manual

S9234-NH-MMO-010 LANDING CRAFT, AIR CUSHION (LCAC) MAIN PROPULSION ENGINE ORGANIZATIONAL LEVEL 4 MAINTENANCE

S9234-NJ-MMO-010 MAIN PROPULSION ENGINE MODEL NUMBER ETF40B FOR LANDING, AIR CUSHION (LCAC) ORGANIZATIONAL LEVEL 6 MAINTENANCE

COMUSFLTFORCOMINST 4790.3 JOINT FLEET MAINTENANCE MANUAL (JFMM), VOLUME IV, REV D

MIL-STD-1472G, DEPARTMENT OF DEFENSE DESIGN CRITERIA STANDARD: HUMAN ENGINEERING

S9234-HE-MMA -010 thru -040, MT7 O/I/D-Level Technical Manuals and Illustrated Part Catalog

S9502-AA-TMM-100, MT7 Auxiliary Systems

The Contractor shall reference and utilize the latest version available when performing tasks within this PWS.

3.0.  REQUIREMENTS

The Contractor shall provide engineering, technical, project management, programmatic, logistics, training, and graphics/modeling support for Hull, Mechanical and Engineering (HM&E) and Propulsion systems onboard U.S. Navy ships. Ship classes include: LCAC, SSC, LCS 1, LCS 2, DDG 1000, MCM, DDG 51, CG 47, LCC, LPD 17, LHD 8, LHA 6, LHA 8, LXR, LSD 41, MSC, USV and CVN, SSN, SSBN, SSGN, Columbia Class, and other future U.S. Navy ship classes, U.S. Coast Guard, U.S. Army, and foreign Naval vessels via the Foreign Military Sales (FMS) Program.

The Contractor shall be required to provide support to the Propulsion Division, the Program Office and the Program Field Offices. Continental United States (CONUS) and Out of Continental United States (OCONUS) locations such as, Philadelphia, PA ; Norfolk, VA; Williamsburg, VA; Mayport, FL; Kings Bay, GA; Pascagoula, MS; Ingleside, TX; Bath, ME; Bangor, WA; Everett, WA; San Diego, CA; Bremerton, WA; Portsmouth, NH; Groton, CT; Pearl Harbor, HI; Key West, FL; Camp Pendleton, CA; Virginia Beach, VA; Cincinnati, OH; and Panama City, FL. The following outlines Contractor requirements and will be supplemented by specific work statements

in individual Technical Instructions (TI’s). TI’s will vary in the level and complexity of requirements, from the full scope of the technical services of this Statement of Work (SOW) to portions of the SOW only.

DIVISION 42 PROPULSION SYSTEMS SUPPORT

SHIP DESIGN AND ACQUISITION SUPPORT

The Contractor shall provide engineering support for new acquisition and modernization programs that includes developing, reviewing, and updating performance specifications, program and technical requirements, drawings, contract deliverables, deviation requests and other technical artifacts. 

The Contractor shall review ship and craft program contract deliverables, formulate responses, and coordinate comment workflow.  Responses may be issued as replies to Requests for Clarifications, Justifications for Technical Determinations (JTD's), or Proposed Changes (PC's).

The contractor shall perform afloat workshop capability assessments that validate maintenance requirements, identify lifting and transportation methods tooling/equipment/material, and confirm compliance with maintainability standards.

The Contractor shall perform human factors assessments that verify machinery systems designs conform to MIL-STD-1472G and are compatible with the capabilities of operators and maintainers.  

The Contractor shall review contract deliverables, formulate responses to clarification and deviation requests, and assist with compiling and coordinating integrated responses.

MODELING AND SIMULATION SUPPORT

The Contractor shall provide computational engineering analysis capability that includes finite element modeling and analysis, control systems assessments, rotor dynamics analysis, thermal analysis of machinery systems, material assessments, and computational fluid dynamics.  Software application access/expertise must include Ansys, Inc.’s Ansys, Dybobes’ Dyrobes, Fluent Inc.’s Fluent, and Matworks’ MATLAB, software packages.

The Contractor shall perform 2D and 3D modeling and simulation of machinery systems.   2D and 3D modeling and simulation shall be used to support engineering analyses, design feasibility assessments, instruction and training, information briefs, visual displays, and to create signage and placards. Software application access/expertise must include AutoDesk’s AutoCAD and Navisworks, Dassault Systems’ SOLIDWORKS, Robert McNeel & Associates’ RHINOceros, and PTC’s Creo software packages.

MACHINERY SYSTEMS ENGINEERING SUPPORT

The Contractor shall provide engineering support for the design, installation, testing, operation and maintenance of propulsion and power generation systems that include gas turbine engine systems, diesel engine systems, combustion air systems, active emissions control systems, prime mover cooling systems, bleed air systems, shafting, propellers, rudders, appendages, waterjets, controllable pitch propeller systems, auxiliary propulsion systems, and main reduction gear equipment including clutches, couplings, bearings, seals and all associated control systems and interfaces.

Request for Information (RFI)  
Pursuant to FAR 15.101 “Early exchanges with industry” this announcement constitutes a request for 
information for information and planning purposes for qualified and experienced sources to provide 
engineering, technical, programmatic, and analytical support and services to the United States Navy’s 
Forward Deployed Regional Maintenance Center (FDRMC) located in Naples, Italy, with detachments in 
Manama, Bahrain and Rota, Spain. This is not a solicitation announcement for proposals and no contract 
will be awarded from this announcement. It is not to be construed in any way as a commitment by the 
Government for any purpose other than to gain the information requested, nor will the Government pay 
for the information submitted in response. Interested parties are encouraged to respond to this RFI.  
Scope 
FDRMC requires personnel support in the following areas and/or disciplines:  
• Engineering Technicians (for example, but not limited to Mechanical Auxiliary, Mechanical 
Hydraulics, Marine Gas Turbine Inspector, Combat Systems-CANES/Afloat Network, Combat 
Systems-SPY, and METCAL Program)  
• Naval Architect 
• Additive Manufacturing Technician 
• Depot and Intermediate Maintenance Support/Production Controllers (for example, but not 
limited to D Level Planner, IMA Planner, Dive Planner, Fleet Technical Assistance Integrator, 
Planner)  
A DRAFT Performance Work Statement is provided containing further details.  
The Government may consider issuing one or more solicitations for this requirement. The Government 
may consider the award of either a single or multiple-award contract(s) as a result of the solicitation(s). 
This is a follow on requirement of contract N0018920F3045, which currently in place providing the 
services described in the performance work statement.  
Place of Performance (Site Locations)  
• Primary: FDRMC Manama, Bahrain; FDRMC Naples, Italy; FDRMC Rota, Spain. 
• Other miscellaneous outside of the continental United States (OCONUS) geographical locations 
in the operational area of FDRMC and the 5th and 6th Fleets, to include Romania and Poland. 
• Global deployment (and TDY) as necessary to support ship maintenance operations. 
• Work may be performed in office settings, as well as in industrial/shipyard environments, and on 
naval vessels. 
• In Bahrain, work may take place at contractor and Government sites. In Italy and Spain, work 
takes place primarily at the Government sites. 
NAICS Code  
The NAICS code for this requirement is anticipated to be 541330, Engineering Services, with a size 
standard of $41.5 million. The product service code (PSC) is R425, Engineering and Technical Services.  
Period of Performance  
Performance is estimated to commence around 01 JAN 2027. The period of performance is anticipated to 
consist of up to five years of performance, potentially through a five-year ordering period or a one-year 

base and option periods, and may include FAR clause 52.217-8, Option to Extend Services, to provide for 
an additional six months of performance.  
Capabilities Statement  
This is a market research tool. The input provided will help the Navy ascertain the interest, capability, and 
capacity of potential businesses. If you are an interested business, NAVSUP FLC Sigonella, Naples Shore 
Office appreciates your assistance in providing a capabilities statement addressing all the items below. 
Please limit your responses to the requested information only. Standard company brochures will not be 
reviewed. Submissions must not to exceed ten standard typewritten pages. Submit any technical questions 
and inquiries within the response.  
1. Full business name, address, point of contact, telephone number, and e-mail address  
2. Contractor and Government Entity (CAGE) code and Data Universal Numbering System 
(DUNS) number  
3. Size of business: Large Business, Small Business, Small Disadvantaged, 8(a), HUBZone, 
Woman-owned, Service Disabled Veteran-Owned, or other category  
4. If the services can be obtained from an existing Government contract vehicle, to include the 
General Services Administration (GSA) or Seaport Next Generation (NxG), provide the 
applicable contract number.  
5. Indicate if your company can be a prime contractor for this effort or, if not, whether your 
company can be a subcontractor. If subcontractors are to be used, provide the anticipated 
percentage of effort to be subcontracted and if a small or large business subcontractor(s) will be 
used.  
6. The Government is determining the acquisition strategy for this potential acquisition. If any 
potential acquisition will be a small business set-aside, then FAR clause 52.219-14, Limitations 
on Subcontracting, applies. If there is sufficient demonstrated interest and capability among small

assessment, troubleshooting, repair, testing, training, and logistics support related to the specific system or equipment type.

Request for Information: 
Engineering Support Services of the H-1 Helicopter Platforms 
 
This market survey is being conducted to identify potential sources that may be able to provide 
engineering and logistical support for the United States Air Force (USAF) TH-1H and UH-1N 
helicopter platforms hereby referred to collectively as H-1. This support will provide the USAF 
H-1 Helicopter Program Office (HPO) technical expertise, access to Original Equipment 
Manufacturer (OEM) proprietary data including but not limited to structural/component data, 
drawings, qualification data, and analysis techniques as required to adequately maintain 
operational, safety, suitability, and effectiveness (OSS&E) for the H-1 platform. Sole source to 
Bell Helicopter is anticipated due to the lack of proprietary data and engineering expertise 
needed to perform this support effort. 
The Contractor will be required to furnish all material, support equipment, tools, test equipment, 
and services. The Contractor will be responsible for providing, maintaining, and calibrating all 
support equipment required at their facility or a subcontractor’s facility. Contractor furnished 
material or parts used for replacement shall equal or exceed the quality of the original material or 
parts. 
Contractors/Institutions responding to this market research are placed on notice that participation 
in this survey does not ensure participation in future solicitations or contract awards. The 
Government will not reimburse participants for any expenses associated with their participation 
in this survey. 
In accordance with FAR 52.215-3: 
a. The Government does not intend to award a contract on the basis of this solicitation or to 
otherwise pay for the information solicited except as an allowable cost under other 
contracts as provided in subsection 31.205-18, Bid and proposal costs, of the Federal 
Acquisition Regulation. 
 
b. Although “proposal” and “offeror” are used in this Request for Information, your 
response will be treated as information only. It shall not be used as a proposal. 
 
c. This Request for Information is issued for the purpose of market research.

requirement and a Contractor Capability Survey, which allows you to provide your 
company’s capability.

should provide documentation that supports your company’s capability in meeting these 
requirements. Failure to provide documentation may result in the Government being 
unable to adequately assess your capabilities. If you lack sufficient experience in a 

particular area, please provide details explaining how you would overcome the lack of 
experience/capabilities in order to perform that portion of the requirement (i.e., teaming, 
subcontracting, etc.) 
 
a. Identify any areas of work that your organization believes should be broken out 
exclusively for Small Business. 
 
3. Both large and small businesses are encouraged to participate in this Market Research. 
Joint ventures or teaming arrangements are encouraged.

Request for Information: 
Engineering Support Services of the H-1 Helicopter Platforms 
PURPOSE/DESCRIPTION 
 
The USAF currently has 85 H-1 helicopters, distributed throughout a number of USAF units 
within the United States. UH-1N helicopters are specially equipped to operate in search and 
rescue, missile support, training, Very Important Person (VIP) transport, and special operation 
force missions. The TH-1H helicopters are the sole Helicopter Division aircraft used by the 
USAF for undergraduate pilot production. 
 
At least a portion of the H-1fleet is expected to remain in service until 2042. While the 
Government had a full data package delivered with the aircraft in the 1960’s, the data has not 
been maintained over the years to a level that adequately captures all design changes since 
aircraft delivery. A multi-disciplined engineering team with expert knowledge is needed to 
provide repair instructions which may require modification support, accident investigation 
support, re-qualification data, and technical order changes. Life cycle sustainability for the H-1 
necessitates engineering support available through a contractual agreement. 
 
Occasionally, the UH-1N Depot locations require engineering assistance to resolve Programmed 
Depot Maintenance (PDM) issues beyond the published technical orders. The US Government 
engineers require access to engineering data to effectively resolve any PDM issues and manage 
requirements. 
 
A logistics team is needed to provide and facilitate responses to questions and possible issues 
from the USG and provide technical support and resolve discrepancies for H-1 and Bell Logistics 
products. As issues arise, the Contractor shall investigate the root cause and provide 
recommendations, review drawings and applicable data, and coordinate with USG, Engineering, 
and other H-1 technical experts to respond to fleet issues.  
 
We are conducting market research to identify potential sources of expert knowledge, drawings, 
technical data specifications, proprietary data, analysis and reports pertaining to H-1 helicopters 
as requested by the Government. The Contractor will be required to provide engineering 
assistance for repair questions and modification of the H-1 for which the Government does not 
have the expertise necessary to take such actions independently. 
 
In addition, the Contractor will be required to support mishap investigations and provide 
solutions to grounding issues. Aircraft on Ground (AOG) situations dictate timely responses. 
Field technical assistance requests immediately impacting mission requirements must be 
resolved within five (5) days of receipt. The USAF may require immediate assistance with expert 
technical knowledge in these instances.

Part II. Capability Survey Questions 
1) General Capability Questions: 
 
1) Describe briefly the capabilities of your company and the nature of the goods and/or

2) Describe your company's past experience on previous projects similar in complexity to 
this requirement. Include contract numbers, a brief description of the work performed,

and manuals. Identify what software programs are utilized to generate these data products

4) Are there specific requirements in the documentation that we provide that would

5) What engineering support experience do you have with the TH-1H and UH-1N helicopter

2) Engineering Services Questions: 
 
1) Describe your experience working mishap investigations and other Aircraft on Ground 
(AOG) issues relating to the H-1 helicopter. 
 
2) Describe your capabilities and experience providing field technical assistance for the H-1 
helicopter. 
 
3) Describe your in-house expert knowledge, drawings, technical data, specifications, data 
and reports pertaining to the H-1 helicopter. 
 
4) Describe an instance where engineering assistance was provided to the government to 
resolve a Programmed Depot Maintenance (PDM) issue beyond the published technical 
orders for the H-1 helicopter. 
 
5) Describe an example of when your capabilities and sustaining engineering expertise 
resulted in cost savings for the H-1 helicopter. 
 
6) How will your organization address the absence of proprietary drawings, specifications, 
technical data, test procedures, etc. pertaining to the H-1 helicopter? 
 
 
 

3) Logistics Reachback Support Question: 
 
1) What is your company's experience in accessing and utilizing government and OEM 
(Original Equipment Manufacturer) technical data, including engineering drawings, to 
resolve logistics and supply discrepancies? 
 
2) Describe your proposed approach to investigating and diagnosing the root cause of 
logistics issues for H-1 products. Please include the methodologies and tools you would 
employ.
