Co-located Hosting Services for Department of Veterans Affairs

This Request for Information (RFI) is issued for information and planning purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation nor does it restrict the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) as to the ultimate acquisition approach.

This notice is issued solely for information and planning purposes - it does not constitute a Request for Quote (RFQ)/Invitation for Bid (IFB)/Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFQ, IFB, or RFP in the future. This notice does not commit the VA to contract for any supply or service. Further, the VA is not seeking quotes, bids, or proposals at this time and will not accept unsolicited proposals in response to this source sought notice. The VA will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this notice. Submittals will not be returned to the responder. Not responding to this notice does not preclude participation in any future RFQ or IFB or RFP, if any is issued. If a solicitation is released, it will be synopsized on the Governmentwide Point of Entry, as appropriate. It is the responsibility of potential offerors to monitor the Governmentwide Point of Entry for additional information pertaining to this requirement. 

VA’s Office of Information & Technology (OIT), Connectivity & Collaboration Services (CCS) has a requirement to provide a like-for-like transition of existing contracted Co-located Hosting Services (CHS) for VA’s Gateway North and East locations.  The like-for-like transition means that where a technology exists today, it will transition to a like technology provided by the contractor.  For example, if a fiber cross connect is currently contracted, a fiber cross connect will be procured on the new contract. 

VA intends to upgrade services if the existing contracted services have reached end of life and require an upgrade.  The upgrade will be a like-for-similar upgrade.  For example, if Battery Distribution Fuse Bays (BDFBs) are currently being used and they are at end of life, the replacement model will be procured as part of the Contractor’s Transition Project.

VA envisions maintaining current legacy services in the initial transition to a new contract vehicle (like-for-like) leveraging existing equipment with a roadmap to an end state of a fully developed and modern CHS solution.

Technical Description

The contractor shall provide facilities for data centers that will be populated by Government Furnished Equipment (GFE), such as servers, routers and load balancers.

VA may, at its discretion, acquire support services and equipment (i.e. related Labor and Equipment). The contractor shall provide all personnel, transportation, equipment, tools, materials, supplies, installation, management, supervision, engineering, maintenance, testing, and services necessary to make all housed equipment fully operational. The contractor shall provide qualified staff proficient in central office/data center engineering, construction, and maintenance to enable continuous operation of telecommunications systems as appropriate, to include Project Management and Transition Support. These services shall be fully defined if an RFP is issued.

Description of Current Environment

VA’s four (4) data centers are co-located in carrier facilities in Gateway North (Chicago, IL), Gateway East (Sterling, VA), Gateway South (Dallas, TX), and Gateway West (Santa Clara, CA).  There are two (2) providers currently, each providing CHS at geographically separated locations.  A dual-carrier approach is currently being taken with diverse path access provided for redundancy at each location. This RFI is only seeking information regarding potential new sites for Gateways North and East.

Each VA Gateway is a Tier 3 data center, with direct connection to Tier 1 Internet Service Providers (ISPs) from both data carriers via geographically redundant fiber points of presence.  All four (4) data centers are manned 24x7x365 by contractor staff, and upon notification by VA, access is provided to VA’s leased space to VA authorized personnel, at all times.  Each data center provides Smarthands to enable data center personnel to provide hands-on access to GFE, with VA direction.

Location Requirements

The Contractor shall adhere to TIA-942-B Rated 3 Site Selection criteria.  In addition, the Contractor shall ensure the following data center facility requirements are met:

One of the data center locations shall be within 30 miles of Sterling, VA.

One of the data center locations shall be within 30 miles of Chicago, IL.

The contractor's data center shall be at least 2 miles from any airport, to reduce risk, but within a 15-mile radius of an International Airport for ease of commute.

The contractor's data center shall be at least 300 yards from major railway / train tracks.

The contractor's data center shall be located in at least a 100-year flood zone or better.

The contractor's data center shall be located outside hurricane zone.

The contractor's data center shall be located outside tornado zone.

Functional Definition

CHS shall include a secure location with cage and racks and include site surveillance.  This service also provides external traffic access as required such as; internet and other dedicated connection speeds, space requirements, maintenance support and operational support, as specified.

Standards

The CHS contractor shall comply with the following standards:

TIA-942 Telecommunications Infrastructure Standard for Data Centers (as updated)

Statement on Standards for Attestation Engagements no. 16 (SSAE 16)

International Organization of Standardizatation standard 27001 Information Security (ISO27001)

Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI-DSS)

Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 (HIPAA)

Power (Electrical)

The Contractor facilities shall meet or exceed the TIA-942-B Rated-3 standard for electrical systems.  In addition, the Contractor shall meet the following electrical requirements at each location:

Delivery of the following types of power to the VA’s racks shall be made available: 

20Amp, 100/120V, Single Phase,

30Amp, 100/120V, Single Phase,

30Amp, 200/208V, Single Phase,

20Amp, 208V, Three Phase,

30Amp, 208V, Three Phase,

50Amp, 208V, Three Phase,

60Amp, 208V, Three Phase.

20Amp, 220V, Three Phase

National Electrical Manufacturers Association (NEMA) L5-20R and L6-30R or L21-30R receptacles are required depending on the Power Distribution Unit (PDU) power type in each rack. No current power requirements exceed basic power requirements (110V/208V/220V | 20A/30A | Single-Phase/Three-Phase). Some cabinets require four total power feeds (2 x A-side and 2 x B-side basic power). 

Utility and power distribution feeds shall be redundant and ensure 99.999% power availability.

Utility power shall be fed by independent sources on the electrical grid.

Utility fees shall enter the property via diverse routes.

Utility feeds shall be dedicated to each data center facility.

One utility feed shall be underground and concrete-encased end-to-end.

Maintenance bypasses shall be uninterruptable power supply (UPS) protected.

Circuitry for electrical feeds shall have no single point of failure from grid to cabinet:

N + 1 redundant power distribution unit (PDUs) shall feed VA’s CHS space,

PDUs shall have redundant, diverse feeds from separate UPS modules,

Power distribution systems shall be designed to meet electrical power draw necessary for VA’s CHS environment; and,

The facility shall support a power density up to 200 Watts per sq. ft.

Cooling and Environment (Mechanical)

The Contractor facilities shall meet or exceed the TIA-942-B Rated-3 standard for mechanical systems or local building codes, or whichever is more stringent.  In addition, the Contractor shall ensure the following environment requirements are met at each location:

Dry-bulb temperature and non-condensing humidity range within the CHS environment shall follow recommended ASHRAE standards for Class A environmental envelopes.

Real-time monitoring of all battery(s) and branch circuit(s) to the cooling systems.

The environment shall include non-corrosive, pre-action sprinkler system and/or gaseous fire suppression systems.

Fire detection and pre-action sprinkler systems shall be zoned and shall not affect VA equipment if fire is localized to a non-VA zone; and,

Allows VA to measure temperature and humidity at approximately 48 inches above the raised floor surface on the front intake of each supported equipment cabinet.

Connectivity (Telecom)

The Contractor shall meet or exceed TIA-942-B Rated-3 standard for telecommunications.  In addition, the Contractor shall ensure the following telecommunications connectivity requirements are met at each location:

The data center shall have dedicated Tier 1 IP backbone connectivity.  A Tier 1 network is defined as a network that can reach every other network on the Internet without purchasing IP transit or paying for peering;

The data center shall be carrier-neutral, allowing access and cross-connect to any VA-approved carrier.

The data center shall meet cross-connect requirements:

Copper and fiber connections shall be available, and infrastructure supports a minimum of 100Gbps bandwidth,

Connections shall span VA cages and non-VA cages serving VA, to include VA’s Trusted Internet Connections (TIC),

Data center (inter-VA cage) fiber buildouts shall allow for multi-mode fiber (MMF), 50-micron, OM3/4 grade or single-mode fiber (SMF) 8-micron,

Provide TIC connections at each location, using fiber interconnection services, consisting of four (4) additional point-to-point single mode fiber connections with LC connector types capable of supporting 100GBASE-LR4 connectivity per location,

POP connections, from data center’s point of presence into the building to VA’s cage(s), shall allow for MMF, 50-micron, OM3/4 grade or SMF 8-micron,

MMF or SMF selection will depend on cage distances and transport of circuit,

The data center shall continue support for T1 and T3 access in current inventory. There are currently no plans to upgrade interfaces in place on the network equipment,

The data center shall continue to support VA’s enhanced Plain Old Telephone System (ePOTS) lines to and within VA’s environment.

Pathway and cable conduits / risers in support of connectivity between cages, floors, and related resources as required.

The data center shall include diverse internal and external fiber routes with diverse network entry points.

An internal meet-me-room or telecom exchange point shall be part of the environment.

The data center shall protect the core network from customer access, both physically and logically.

The data center shall provide private data transport interconnectivity between data centers (non-adjacent cages or various buildings); and,

The Contractor’s network shall be monitored from a Contractor-controlled Network Operations Center (NOC).

Security

The Contractor shall provide physical security at the CHS facilities that meet or exceed TIA-942-B Rated-3 standards.  In addition, the Contractor shall ensure the following physical security requirements are met at each location:

The data center shall be staffed 24x7x365.

Mantraps shall be installed to segregate access at the main entrance to the facility.

Dual factor authentication, including biometric screening, is required for entry to secure areas.

Onsite digital video camera surveillance shall be available and monitored 24x7x365, internal and external to the facility, including loading docks and entry points.

Digital video recordings shall be archived for a minimum of five calendar days and include all personnel entering, working within, and exiting VA’s assigned spaces and the Contractor’s data center hallways.  A copy of the archived data shall be available to VA upon request by the next business day. 

All cabinets shall be lockable, and cages built with 6 sides including top and under raised floor (all sides may be secure mesh).

The Contractor shall allow for VA-owned private access control systems and digital video systems for VA’s cages and cabinets.  Alternatively, equipment may be provided for VA use for this purpose.

Smart hands staff shall be direct hires of the prime Contractor or the data center provider.

Visitors shall be tracked with logs maintained and available to VA upon request by the next business day.

A VA-defined list of personnel shall be maintained for authorized access to VA’s co-location space and referenced by the Contractor when access is requested.  For instances when access is required by personnel not on the access list, VA authorized personnel will initiate a ticket with the Contractor to allow authorized access on an individual case basis.

Security badges shall be provided and available to VA authorized personnel as needed, not separately priced, and not to exceed 30 per facility; and,

Electronic key card access shall be provided to all VA managed cage(s), in accordance with the inventory list.

Support and Services

The Contractor shall provide support services to the CHS facilities troubleshooting and repair support within the VA CHS environment.  For each location, the Contractor shall:

Provide on-site staff at the facility 24x7, capable of performing smart hands work.  In addition, provide skilled, certified (CompTIA Network+, Security+, or equivalent) network engineers for such support.  Historically, VA requires an average of 24 hours of smart hands work per month per data center.  Smart hands support in this SOW is defined as:

Onsite / offsite troubleshooting assistance

Interface card removal, installation and configuration 

Pre-wiring of patch panels and in-rack equipment

Assisting with RMAs / break-fix incident response

Testing cabling or other media for continuity

Providing visual verifications to assist in remote troubleshooting 

Inventorying/labeling of equipment and cables

Power cycling equipment and soft booting a server

Bootstrapping server or network equipment

Moving equipment within VA space

Moving or securing cables

Equipment installations and configurations

Replacement of failed equipment using VA-provided hardware.

Replacement of failed network cabling using Contractor-provided replacements of an identical length, grade, connector type, and color (including replacement of existing labels with new labels containing the same information).

Replacement of failed power cabling, receptacles, and power distribution units (PDUs) using Contractor-provided replacements of an identical make and model.  If an identical make and model are not commercially available, the Contractor shall substitute a replacement of an equivalent quality, gauge, length, connector type, and metering and remote access functionality.

Special Notice N0001426SN003 
Special Program Announcement for Office of Naval Research 
Research Opportunity: 
ONR Innovation Industry Day (I2D): Power & Energy 
 
I. INTRODUCTION 
 
This announcement describes a technology area, entitled ONR Innovation Industry Day (I2D): 
Power & Energy under the N0001425SB001, Long Range Broad Agency Announcement for 
Navy and Marine Corps Science and Technology which can be found at 
https://www.onr.navy.mil/work-with-us/funding-opportunities/announcements. The submission 
of proposals, their evaluation and the placement of research contracts or agreements will be 
carried out as described in the above Long Range Broad Agency Announcement. 
 
The primary goal of the I2D is to solicit direct feedback from industry. Insights gathered will 
directly inform future S&T opportunities, with the aim of encouraging subsequent white paper 
submissions for FY27 consideration. 
 
II. TOPIC DESCRIPTION 
This event is a unique forum where the ONR Power & Energy Focus Area Lead will present 
science and technology (S&T) challenges projected over the next 15 years. ONR seeks to engage 
non-traditional, commercial, and innovative partners interested in addressing the Navy's future 
power and energy needs, particularly within Technology Readiness Levels (TRL) 1-6. 
Discussions will center on key research areas, including: Energy Storage, Power Generation, 
Thermal Management, and Power Distribution, Control & Resilience. 
 
Objective: 
 
The Office of Naval Research (ONR) is interested in encouraging subsequent white paper 
submissions for FY27 consideration. 
 
III. INUDSTRY DAYS 
 
ONR will host its inaugural Innovative Industry Day (I2D) on Thursday, May 14, 2026, focused 
on their Power & Energy portfolio. 
 
The Industry Day will take place at the Bobby Junker Executive Conference Center (BJECC) at 
ONR. 
 
 

Approved, DCN# 2026-4-1-2149 04/02/2026

VISITOR ACCESS & SECURITY 
 
All visitors attending the Innovation Industry Day at the ONR facility must be pre-registered 
through the Pentagon Force Protection Agency (PFPA) Visitor Management System (VMS). 
Please note, ONR partners with PFPA to manage building access, and walk-in registrations are 
not permitted. To ensure a smooth arrival, please follow this three-step process:

INTRODUCTION  
This SOURCES SOUGHT is a market research tool to determine the availability and technical 
capability of interested businesses who have an interest in and the resources to support a follow 
on contract for Engineering, Prototyping and Fabrication.  
 
DISCLAIMER  
THIS SOURCES SOUGHT IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A 
REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL, INVITATION FOR BID, OR REQUEST FOR OFFER. IT 
DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A 
COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT 
OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A 
CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE 
TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. ANY 
INFORMATIONSUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS TO THIS TECHNICAL DESCRIPTION 
IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY.  
 
DESCRIPTION  
As the organic Lead Systems Integrator
® (oLSI®) for the Naval Air Warfare Center Aircraft 
Division (NAWCAD), Webster Outlying Field (WOLF) operates under a product-based business 
model whereby NAWCAD WOLF civilians lead and manage the execution of the 
requirements for defense weapon systems programs with combined Government-Industry teams. 
Using this oLSI® approach, the Government maintains control of intellectual property and data 
rights, enabling WOLF to rapidly adapt solutions to the dynamic needs of the warfighter.  
The NAWCAD WOLF Engineering & Prototyping (EP) Operations provides rapid organic 
engineering, prototyping, reverse-engineering, environmental testing, antenna repairs/life cycle 
extensions, and production capabilities in support of NAWCAD, Naval Air Systems Command 
(NAVAIR), and the NAWCAD WOLF Divisions. The EP Operations, operating under 
the oLSI® model, has requirements to provide engineering support, systems engineering 
support, fabrication support, and compliance support to include product and part design 
engineering; production engineering; drafting; Computer Aided Design (CAD); Computer Aided 
Manufacturing (CAM); Modeling and Simulation (M&S); machining; sheet-metal design, 
layout, and fabrication; welding; assembly; composite repairs and fabrication of composite 
components and structures; woodworking; painting, including preparation and application of 
corrosion control coatings and powder coating; management of a stockroom  (e.g., tooling, hand 
tools, and fasteners), facilities and personnel safety management and preparedness to include 
Hazardous Materials (HAZMAT).   
This procurement is a follow-on to task order N0042124F0690, under the Single Award IDIQ 
Contract N00421D0014, competitively awarded to Altus Technical Solutions, LLC.  The 

existing task order has Cost-Plus-Fixed-Fee (CPFF) Contract Line Item Numbers (CLINs) for 
Labor, cost reimbursable CLINs for Other Direct Costs (e.g. Travel, Material, and Field 
Services) and Not Separately Priced (NSP) CLINs for Data and Contractor Acquired Property 
and has a period of performance from 08 July 2024 to 07 July 2029.   
The attached draft SOW/PWS provides additional information about the required tasking. If your 
company has any questions about the structure of the SOW/PWS, or areas that may need further 
definition, please also identify those in the response.  
Place of Performance: Contractor Site (22%), Government Site (78% Webster Field, St. 
Inigoes, MD, NAS Patuxent River, MD and selected travel sites listed in SOW/PWS Paragraph 
3.1.5.1). 
 
ADDITIONAL INFORMATION 
A DD Form 254 Contract Security Classification Specification shall apply to this requirement, 
and the prime contractor shall have or demonstrate ability to obtain a “Secret” Facility Clearance 
under this contract.   
The follow-on procurement is anticipated to be a competitively awarded Seaport MAC Task 
Order (TO) under FAR 16.505 with a combination of Performance Based work and LOE hours 
with a base year and four (4) option years. 
The proposed contract is anticipated to include tasking that would be accomplished by labor 
categories that are subject to the Service Contract Act.   
 
ELIGIBILITY  
The applicable NAICS Code for this requirement is 541330 with a Small Business Size standard 
of $47 Million. The Product/Service Code (PSC) for this effort is L099, Technical 
Representative - Miscellaneous. This Sources Sought Synopsis is requesting responses to the 
following criteria from any or all businesses that can provide the required services under the 
NAICS Code.  
Offerors MUST have an adequate accounting system in accordance with FAR 16.301-3(a)(3) in 
order to be eligible for award of this cost-type contract. 
 
SUBMISSION DETAILS  
Interested businesses are requested to submit a capabilities statement of no more than ten (10) 
pages in length in Times New Roman font of not less than 12 pitch.  
Interested businesses should submit a brief capabilities statement package that shall address, at a 
minimum, the following items:  

1) What type of work has your company performed in the past in support of the same or similar 
requirement? This should include the contract number, organization supported, indication of 
whether as a prime or subcontractor, contract value, Government point of contact, and a brief 
description of how the referenced contract relates to the services described in the draft 
SOW/PWS.  
2) Can or has your company managed a task of this nature? If so, please provide details.  
3) Can or has your company managed a team of subcontractors before? If so, provide details.  
4) What specific technical skills does your company possess which ensure capability to perform 
the tasks outlined in the draft SOW/PWS? 
5) Please note that under a Small-Business Set-Aside, in accordance with FAR 52.219-14, the 
small business prime must perform at least 50% of the work themselves in terms of the cost of 
performance. Provide an explanation of your company's ability to perform at least 50% of the 
tasking described in this SOW/PWS for the base period as well as the option periods.  
6) Provide a statement including current small/large business status and company profile to 
include number of employees, annual revenue history, office locations, DUNS number, CAGE 
code, etc.

Engineering, Prototyping, and Fabrication Support Services 
Statement of Work/Performance Work Statement 
 Scope.  
As the organic Lead Systems Integrator® (oLSI®) for the Naval Air Warfare Center Aircraft 
Division (NAWCAD), Webster Outlying Field (WOLF) operates under a product-based business 
model whereby NAWCAD WOLF civilians lead and manage the execution of the requirements 
for defense weapon systems programs with combined Government-Industry teams. Using this 
oLSI® approach, the Government maintains control of intellectual property and data rights, 
enabling WOLF to rapidly adapt solutions to the dynamic needs of the warfighter. 
The NAWCAD WOLF Engineering & Prototyping (EP) Operations provides rapid organic 
engineering, prototyping, reverse-engineering, environmental testing, antenna repairs/life cycle 
extensions, and production capabilities in support of NAWCAD, Naval Air Systems Command 
(NAVAIR), and the NAWCAD WOLF Divisions. The EP Operations, operating under the 
oLSI® model, has requirements to provide engineering support, systems engineering support, 
fabrication support, and compliance support to include product and part design engineering; 
production engineering; drafting; Computer Aided Design (CAD); Computer Aided 
Manufacturing (CAM); Modeling and Simulation (M&S); machining; sheet-metal design, 
layout, and fabrication; welding; assembly; composite repairs and fabrication of composite 
components and structures; woodworking; painting, including preparation and application of 
corrosion control coatings and powder coating; management of a stockroom  (e.g., tooling, hand 
tools, and fasteners), facilities and personnel safety management and preparedness to include 
Hazardous Materials (HAZMAT).  
This Statement of Work (SOW)/Performance Work Statement (PWS) is in direct support of 
projects related to multiple major defense acquisition programs, other acquisition category 
designations, and/or other defense weapons systems to include, but not be limited to, SPN 
Antenna Systems, AEGIS hardware, OE-120 system hardware, Family of Special Operations 
Vehicles (FOSOV) FOSOV and other tactical vehicle hardware, and fabrication and 
refurbishment of various other shipboard, vehicle, and aircraft components with an agile 
management approach to ensure that solutions are delivered efficiently and effectively.

IV. DESCRIPTION 
                   
The Federal Aviation Administration’s (FAA’s) continuing mission is to provide the safest, most 
efficient aerospace system in the world. This mission is a continuing one, and the FAA is 
prioritizing the modernization of the national airspace system to enhance safety, increase 
capacity and efficiency, improve air traffic management and give controllers the updated tools 
they need.  The agency is focused on replacing the current air traffic control system to enhance 
safety in the sky, reduce delays, and unlock the future of air travel. 
 
This draft Statement of Work (SOW) sets forth a broad set of needs and requirements for the 
NSEMS Contract(s), to assist the FAA in accomplishing its mission and to support bringing the 
FAA vision to realization.  The goal of NSEMS is to support the FAA’s strategic vision and 
priorities: 
 
• To make aviation safer, smarter, more secure, and efficient; and 
• To deliver benefits to the NAS through enhancements, improvements, innovations, and 
upgrades to its technology and infrastructure. 
 
The acquisition strategy for the procurement has not been determined at this time ; However, 
either an unrestricted competition or a set -aside will be chosen depending on the responses to 
this RFI/Market Survey. 
                                                                                                                                           
a) This is not a Screening Information Request or Request for Proposals of any kind; 

NSEMS REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) / MARKET SURVEY 
Page | 2 
 
b) The FAA is not seeking or accepting unsolicited proposals; 
c) The FAA will not pay for any information received or costs incurred in preparing the 
response to the market survey; and 
d) Any costs associated with the market survey submittal are solely at the interested 
vendor’s expense. 
 
The purpose of this RFI is to solicit statements of interest and capabilities statements from large 
and small businesses ((a) Socially and economically disadvantaged business (SEDB) expressly 
certified by the Small Business Administration (SBA) for participation in SBA’s 8(a) program; 
(b) Service-disabled veteran-owned small business (SDVOSB); (c) Women-Owned Small 
Business (WOSB); (d) Historically Underutilized Business Zone (HUBZone) small business; and 
(e) Small business (SB)), capable of providing the services outlined in this document, in the 
timeframe stated in this document.  The responses to this RFI will help determine the acquisition 
strategy and whether adequate competition exists to set aside the competition.  This notice is for 
informational and planning purposes only.  This notice does not restrict the FAA from the 
ultimate acquisition approach it may take in connection with this requirement, nor does it restrict 
changes to the SOW.

Universal Numbering Systems (DUNS) Number, and Unique Entity ID (UEI) . 
 
2. Point of contact to include an e-mail address and telephone number.

• Ability to provide services in support of Mission Management pillar and its requirements 
• Ability to identify, offer, and provide additional services that enhance the FAA’s NSEMS 
program

Page | 3 
 
 
2.  Industry feedback is requested on the draft SOW for this requirement.  Please list any 
challenges or potential performance roadblocks related to fulfilling the draft SOW requirements 
and any suggestions for improving the draft SOW language.  Feedback is also requested 
regarding the proposed PSC and NAICS codes.  Comments on PSC/NAICS and suggestions for 
alternative codes must include supporting rationale.

Review and complete the Matrix found on the “Capability by Region” tab.  Refer to

113 Holland Avenue, Albany, NY 12208

1. Introduction

The Albany Stratton VA Medical Center (VAMC) requires enhancements to its Physical Access Control System (PACS) to improve facility security, access accountability, and compliance with VA Handbook 0730, VA Physical Security Design Manual, Federal Interagency Security Committee Risk Management Process Standards, Office of Security and Law Enforcement (OS&LE) and Joint Commission standards.

2. Background and Objective

This project will install PIV-enabled access control hardware on four (4) doors and integrate all components into the existing Lenel OnGuard PACS environment to enhance controlled access, alarm monitoring, and life-safety compliance. 

The Albany Stratton VA Medical Center currently operates a Lenel OnGuard ADV SUSP access control license capped at 256 readers. This threshold has been reached across the medical center and CBOCs, limiting the VA’s ability to expand PIV-enabled access control in compliance with Executive Order 14111 and the Interagency Security Committee (ISC) Physical Security Criteria.

This limitation poses a compliance risk as VA-controlled facilities are scheduled for Federal Protective Service (FPS) reinspection using the Modified Infrastructure Survey Tool (MIST). Vendor confirmation verifies that the ADV SUSP license cannot exceed 256 readers. An upgrade to Lenel OnGuard PRO is required.

3. Place of Performance

All work shall be performed at Albany Stratton VA Medical Center, 113 Holland Avenue, Albany, NY 12208. Work locations include:
• Room C51-1 – Medical Gas Storage
• Room C52 – Bio-Med
• Emergency Department Circle Entrance
• VIP Ramp Entrance

4. Period of Performance

All work shall be completed within ninety (90) calendar days from the Notice of Award.

5. Scope of Work

The contractor shall furnish all labor, materials, equipment, wiring, programming, testing, documentation, and coordination necessary to deliver a fully functional PACS installation integrated into the existing Lenel OnGuard system.

The contractor shall furnish all labor, licensing, and coordination necessary to upgrade the existing Lenel OnGuard ADV SUSP license to the PRO license tier.

6. Deliverables

The contractor shall provide and install the following:
Lenel Software Upgrade deliverables:

CLIN 0001 – Base Requirement

• Upgrade Lenel OnGuard software license from ADV SUSP to PRO

• Includes activation of 64 additional reader licenses

• Increases total system capacity from 256 to 320 readers

Activated Lenel OnGuard PRO license

• Documentation verifying updated reader capacity

• Vendor confirmation of successful implementation

PACS Installation Deliverables:

CLIN 0002 – Equipment and Installation

• Four (4) HID PIV-class dual-frequency readers (SIGNO 40K)
• Four (4) door position sensors (magnetic contacts)
• Two (2) cylindrical electrified locksets with integrated Request-to-Exit (RQE)
• Two (2) electric door strikes
• Two (2) electrified retracting panic exit devices
• Four (4) ADA-compliant wave-to-open push buttons
• Drill-out of one (1) solid wood door
• Drill-out of one (1) hollow metal fire-rated door
• Four (4) armored door loops
• Four (4) surface-mounted wire mold raceways with fittings for concrete walls
• Two (2) Lenel LNL-1320 Dual Reader Interface Modules
• Two (2) wall-mounted access control cabinets
• One (1) 24VDC power supply
• Two (2) 24VDC backup batteries
• Two (2) Altronix ACM4 Access Power Controllers, four (4) fused outputs each, Fire Alarm Interface (FAI) capable
• Two (2) amber door-open indicator lights

All equipment shall be new, UL-listed where applicable, and fully compatible with the existing Lenel OnGuard PACS.

7. Door-by-Door Technical Requirements

7.1 Door C51-1 – Medical Gas Storage (Basement)
Dual hollow metal, fire-rated door. Install reader, cylindrical electrified lockset with RQE, DPS, armored loop, and two amber indicators. Door shall be drilled without recertification. Cabling shall terminate in Room C66. Power provided by Altronix ACM4 #1 serving Doors C51-1 and C52. Alarms shall report to Lenel OnGuard.

7.2 Door C52 – Bio-Med Room (Basement)
Solid wood door. Install reader, cylindrical electrified lockset with RQE, DPS, and armored loop. Door shall be drilled and cabled to Room C66. Power shared from Altronix ACM4 #1. Lenel LNL-1320 module installed in shared cabinet.

7.3 Emergency Department Circle Entrance (1st Floor – D Wing)
Glass door with operator. Install reader, electric strike or electrified panic device, DPS, and ADA wave button. Wire to Room D101. Lenel 1320 and power available in room D101. Alarms programmed in Lenel OnGuard.

7.4 VIP Ramp Entrance (1st Floor – C Wing)
Metal door with panic hardware. Install reader, electrified panic device or strike, DPS, and ADA wave button. Install Lenel LNL-1320 in Room C124c with dedicated cabinet. Power provided by Altronix ACM4 #2. Integrate with existing Lenel LNL-3300 controller.

8. Government-Furnished Property

The Government will provide the existing Lenel OnGuard PACS, available controller capacity, network connectivity, existing cable pathways, facility power, and access to work areas.

9. Inspection and Acceptance

The VA Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR) shall inspect all work upon completion. No invoice shall be processed until all systems are verified operational and formally accepted. 

System verification confirming a capacity of 320 readers with no disruption to operations.

10. Exclusions

Any work not explicitly stated in this Statement of Work is not authorized without written modification from the Contracting Officer.

STATEMENT OF WORK
I. GENERAL INFORMATION
A. Introduction
The USGS Geology, Minerals, Energy, and Geophysics (GMEG) Science Center requires 
whole-rock samarium-neodymium, uranium-lead, and rubidium strontium isotope analyses of 
samples collected from mafic-ultramafic igneous (cumulates) and evolved intrusive igneous 
(porphyries) rocks. These isotope analyses will support ongoing research for critical mineral 
studies of rocks associated with arc magmatism, copper porphyry formation, and the mission 
of Earth MRI. 
B. Background
In igneous rocks, isotopes systems are used to determine melt sources (e.g., mantle plume 
or sub-continental mantle lithosphere) and extent of contamination of those melts. The 
combination of Rb-Sr, U-Pb, and Sm-Nd isotope system has been widely used to study 
porphyry copper deposits as well as the origin of ultramafic cumulates. These data will help to 
understand the petrogenesis of porphyry deposits USGS Earth MRI focus areas, including the 
Wikieup and the Greyback plutons, AZ, as well as ultramafic xenoliths associated with 
mineralization in central AZ. The Rb-Sr, U-Pb,  Sm-Nd isotopes will help to elucidate the 
sources setting(s) of these magmatic events and their degree of contribution. 
C. Definitions/Applicable Documents
Briefly, the methods for separation and isotopic measurement of the parent and daughter 
nuclides involve first dissolving whole-rock sample powders with concentrated acid in 
pressurized (Parr) vessels. For the U-Pb and Sm-Nd systems the dissolutions are then spiked 
with a tracer solution. Parent and daughter nuclides are then isolated by cation exchange 
chromatography. Once purified, parent and daughter isotopic compositions are measured by 
multi-collector inductively coupled plasma mass-spectrometry (MC-ICP-MS).
Literature that provides an overview of the methods:
•Cheng, H., King, R. L., Nakamura, E. (2008). Coupled Lu–Hf and Sm–Nd 
geochronology constrains garnet growth in ultra-high-pressure eclogites from the Dabie 
orogen. J. Metamorphic Geol., v. 26, p. 741–758.
•White, William M., Francis Albarède, and Philippe Télouk. “High-Precision Analysis of Pb Isotope 
Ratios by Multi-Collector ICP-MS.” Chemical Geology 167, no. 3 (2000): 257–70. 
https://doi.org/10.1016/S0009-2541(99)00182-5.
•Gaschnig, Richard M., Jeffrey D. Vervoort, Reed S. Lewis, and Basil Tikoff. “Isotopic Evolution of 
the Idaho Batholith and Challis Intrusive Province, Northern US Cordillera.” Journal of Petrology 
52, no. 12 (2011): 2397–429. https://doi.org/10.1093/petrology/egr050.
•Johnson, T. A., Vervoort, J. D., Ramsey, M. J., Aleinikoff, J. N., Southworth, S. (2018). 
Constraints on the timing and duration of orogenic events by combined Lu–Hf and Sm–
Nd geochronology: An example from the Grenville orogeny. Earth Planet. Sci. Letters, v. 
501, p. 152–164.

140G0326Q0079 4 of 16
Literature that provides examples of the application of Sm-Nd isotope, Pb-Pb, and Rb-Sr 
geochemistry to ultramafic cumulates and magmas associated with copper porphyry deposits:
•Bouse, Robin M., Joaquin Ruiz, Spencer R. Titley, Richard M. Tosdal, and Joseph L. Wooden. 
“Lead Isotope Compositions of Late Cretaceous and Early Tertiary Igneous Rocks and Sulfide 
Minerals in Arizona; Implications for the Sources of Plutons and Metals in Porphyry Copper 
Deposits.” Economic Geology 94, no. 2 (1999): 211–44. 
https://doi.org/10.2113/gsecongeo.94.2.211.
•Lang, James R., and Spencer R. Titley. “Isotopic and Geochemical Characteristics of Laramide 
Magmatic Systems in Arizona and Implications for the Genesis of Porphyry Copper Deposits.” 
Economic Geology 93, no. 2 (1998): 138–70. https://doi.org/10.2113/gsecongeo.93.2.138.
D. Scope 
We have collected samples from a variety of Laramide igneous rocks and ultramafic xenoliths 
for Sm-Nd isotopic analysis. In combination with major and trace element geochemistry, the 
Sm-Nd data will be used constrain magmatic source(s) and petrogenetic models.
II. WORK REQUIREMENTS
A. Technical Requirements
1. Work Requirements/Products
The USGS will provide 25 surface whole rock samples for the Sm-Nd, U-Pb, and Rb-Sr 
analyses. The samples have been pulverized in agate or alumina corundum (avoiding 
metal) and at least 1 g of powder per sample is available to submit to the lab along with 
garnet separates for the few samples that contain the mineral. The submitted samples will 
be analyzed using recognized spikes, separation methods, standards, and instrumental 
techniques to meet the typical precision for analyses reported throughout the literature (2σ 
< ± ~0.00001).
2. Criteria for acceptance of Product 
Analyses will be accepted if they meet the requirements of the lab’s quality control and 
quality assurance specialists.
B. Deliverables
1. Characteristics for work product described in II.A.1.
Deliverables will include Sm-Nd, Rb-Sr, and U-Pb elemental and isotopic compositions 
of the 25 samples submitted. A report will be submitted to the USGS upon completion of 
the work. This report will contain all relevant isotopic data that would routinely be 
included in scientific papers. This includes:
• A description of analytical techniques and methods of data reduction
• Table of the isotopic data, including elemental and isotopic concentrations of Sm, 
Nd, U, Pb, Rb, and Sr along with their uncertainties.
The contractor will communicate with the USGS on a regular basis and in case of any 
unforeseen complications with the rock samples submitted.

140G0326Q0079 5 of 16
2. Delivery dates
Depending on lab schedules, the work for 25 samples should be completed within 12 
months from the award of the contract. Digital data can be transferred to the USGS by 
email or other means of data delivery. Excess powdered sample should be returned to the 
USGS.
III. SUPPORTING INFORMATION
A. Place of Performance
At the contractor's lab. 
B. Period of Performance
The work will require ~30 days of lab time, performed within 12 months from the award of 
the contract.
C. Government Furnished Property (GFP): None.
D. Special Considerations
1. Key personnel qualifications: 
The lead isotope geochemistry expert of the lab should have a Ph.D degree and have 5 or 
more additional years of experience. They should have authorship on several peer-
reviewed publications that report Sm-Nd, Rb-Sr, and U-Pb analyses for igneous rocks. 
The lab must be an internationally recognized and reputable isotope geochemistry lab. 
2. Data Rights, Safety, Environment: None
3. Security/Privacy: None

OVERVIEW 
 
1. CSO Sponsor: Office of the Secretary of War, Golden Dome for America (GDA) 
 
2. Authority: DFARS 212.70 – Defense Commercial Solutions Opening; Other Transaction 
Authority (10 USC 4022); Authority to acquire innovative commercial products and 
commercial services using general solicitation competitive procedures (10 USC 3458, as 
amended by P.L. 119-60); OSW Memo, “Direct Reporting Program Manager Appointment 
for Golden Dome for America” dated 20 August 2025. 
 
3. Objective: GDA seeks innovative solutions or potential capabilities that fulfill requirements, 
close capability gaps, or provide potential innovative technological advancements that 
accelerate GDA's ability to achieve its mission using Streamlined Acquisition Procedures. 
 
4. Period of Availability: From date of CSO posting through 30 September 2035. 
 
5. Opportunity Description: The Homeland is currently at risk and is relatively undefended 
from a new generation of advanced weapons being actively developed by adversaries.  
GDA’s core mission is to rapidly field a defense to protect Americans and critical 
infrastructure from this real, complex, and growing threat. The spectrum of dangers includes 
sophisticated ballistic missiles, hypersonics advanced cruise missiles, and other modern 
aerial systems. To achieve this unprecedented and realistic goal within a compressed 
timeframe, GDA will operate as an agile organization with a mandate to leverage commercial 
innovation. Rapid and flexible contracting will accelerate the adoption of critical 
technologies, unconstrainted by legacy policy and regulatory limitations. This CSO allows 
GDA to select vendors whose solutions show the greatest potential to achieve the GDA 
mission. Submissions will be evaluated using a merit-based peer-review, technical review, or 
operational review process consistent with 10 U.S.C. §3458. 
 
Under this CSO, GDA has OT authority to partner with nontraditional and traditional defense 
contractors and non-profit research institutions to carry out prototype projects that are 
directly relevant to enhancing the mission effectiveness of military personnel and the 
supporting platforms, systems, components, or materials proposed to be acquired or 
developed by the DoD, or the improvement of platforms, systems, components, or materials 
in use by the armed forces for GDA. Under this CSO, GDA may also use FAR-based 
methods for procuring services. This CSO is a mechanism for GDA to use competitive 
procedures to award OT agreements or contracts. Whether an award is an OT agreement for a 
Prototype Project, or follow on prototype/production agreement, or a FAR-based contract 
award is at the sole discretion of the government. 
 
 

HQ020226S0001 
Page 3 of 8 
6. Award Parameters 
 
a. There is no specific restriction on the number, type, value, or frequency of awards that 
may be made under this CSO. 
b. Multiple awards are anticipated and may vary widely in terms of scope, duration, 
and price, consistent with the objectives of this CSO. 
c. The Government reserves the right to select for award all, none, some, or selected 
portions thereof, of any submission that may be received in response to this CSO. 
d. Any white paper or proposal selected for funding may be incrementally funded at 
the discretion of the Government. 
e. The Government reserves the right to negotiate proposal scope of work, price, and 
other terms and conditions as may be required. 
f. Most efforts awarded under this CSO will be fixed-price milestone OT agreements 
or Firm, Fixed Price FAR contracts. 
g. To promote opportunity for maximum collaboration and rapid engagement between 
multiple respondents, and due to a fiscally constrained operating environment, 
respondents should note that the Government places a significantly higher value on 
ideas, concepts, and proposed solutions that promote quick testing of applications 
and/or proof-of-concept scenarios. 
h. This CSO may be used for OT agreements designed to enable collaboration at higher 
security levels when necessary for prototype concept development. 
i. The Government may either rely on the scope description and price cited in a white 
paper, without having to request a separate proposal (i.e., a “one-step” process), or the 
Government may issue an RFP after receipt of a white paper, requesting a proposal and 
more detailed price be submitted based on the white paper (i.e. the “two-step” process). 
In instances where the Government elects to make an award based solely on a white 
paper submission, the white paper must contain sufficient detail regarding the technical 
approach, scope of work, deliverables, and price to enable evaluation in accordance with 
the stated criteria and to support an award decision. The Government may request 
additional information as necessary to ensure that submissions are evaluated on a 
comparable basis. 
 
PARTICIPANT ELIGI BILITY REQUIREMENTS 
 
1. Eligible Participants: All sources capable of addressing the objectives of this CSO, 
consistent with statute and regulation, including the security requirements of this effort, are 
encouraged to respond. 
 
2. Procurement Integrity, Standards of Conduct, Ethical Considerations, and Conflicts of 
Interest: With respect to submissions in response to this CSO, submitting parties are notified 
that that the Government will assess all submissions for the existence or appearance of any 

HQ020226S0001 
Page 4 of 8 
potential conflicts of interest. Notwithstanding any Government assessment to be conducted 
as a result of submissions to this CSO, it is principally incumbent upon the submitting party 
to assess all facts relevant to the existence or potential existence of a conflict of interest to 
disclose such information to the Government for appropriate consideration. Conflicts may be 
either organizational or personal. With respect to any party that may already be doing 
business with GDA in a capacity to provide scientific, engineering, technical assistance 
(SETA), or similar support, such parties are hereby notified that without prior written agency 
approval and authorization, such entity will not be authorized to simultaneously provide 
SETA, or similar support, and also be a technical performer in any capacity under this CSO. 
 
EV ALUATION CRITERIA 
 
1. White Papers: White paper submissions will be reviewed for interest in accordance with the 
stated objectives of this CSO, which is to specifically seek innovative commercial items, 
technologies, and services that support GDA. If the Government seeks to award directly from 
a white paper, it will be evaluated in terms of Technical and Price, as detailed in the 
evaluation of proposals section. Calls, if issued, may contain separate and unique white paper 
review guidelines specific to the objectives of the Call in question.  
 
2. Proposals: Proposal submissions will be evaluated based on Technical and Price. When 
evaluating submissions, the Government will weigh the relative value of the proposed effort 
in relation to its anticipated cost and the overall portfolio of efforts under consideration, in 
order to maximize mission impact within available resources.  
  
a. Technical: This CSO seeks various innovative commercial items, technologies, 
and services intended to address existing gaps, revolutionize operations and/or 
capability, and/or significantly strengthen past, current, planned, or unforeseen 
operational paradigms. Technical applications that demonstrate breakthrough 
promise, as determined by the Government, will be given higher priority 
consideration than commercial innovation applications that merely introduce 
incremental improvements in existing operations. Commercial innovation 
applications that support urgent pressing needs, as determined by the Government, 
will be given higher priority consideration than those that address lower priority 
focus areas.
 
 
b. Price: A contract/agreement will only be awarded if the Contracting 
Officer/Agreements Officer negotiating and awarding the contract/agreement 
determines the price to be fair and reasonable. 
 
3. Individual Requests for Proposals (RFPs): RFPs, if issued, may clarify or further define 
these criteria; add criteria where necessary to support specific program objectives; and/or 
adjust their relative order of importance. In all cases, the Government will clearly identify the 

HQ020226S0001 
Page 5 of 8 
evaluation criteria and their relative importance in the applicable RFP and will evaluate 
proposals solely in accordance with those stated criteria. 
 
WHITE PAPER CONTENT AND FORMAT REQUIREMENTS 
 
Parties interested in engaging GDA under this CSO with innovative commercial items, 
technologies, and/or services of interest that would advance GDA’s mission, may submit a 
white paper to the Government at any time after the CSO opens and before the end of the 
CSO period of availability. The Government may also issue Calls requesting white papers 
that address specific challenges faced by GDA.  
 
1. Due Dates: Due dates will be specified in Calls. White papers provided not in response to a 
specific Call may be provided at any time during the CSO period of availability. However, 
interested parties should consider that white papers issued within one month or less of the 
end of the Period of Availability may not be submitted in time for the Government to review 
and make an award decision. 
 
2. White Paper Restrictions: There is no limit on the number of white papers that may be 
submitted in response to this CSO. White Papers, consistent with the objectives of this CSO, 
are highly encouraged. There is no restriction on the number of white papers that may be 
submitted from any single party, subject to the following conditions: 
 
a. The Government desires commercial innovation consistent with the objectives of this 
CSO. 
 
b. The Government intends to focus its review resources on submissions that are responsive 
to the objectives of the CSO. Submissions that are determined to be non-responsive, 
duplicative, or not aligned with the stated objectives may receive limited or no further 
consideration. 
 
3. Format Requirements: The content included in a white paper submission is anticipated to 
vary widely by submitting party, with response to the CSO intended to be uncomplicated, 
subject to the following format instructions: 
 
a. NOT TO EXCEED 10 PAGES IN TOTAL LENGTH (Including price information) 
b. 8 ½ by 11-inch paper format, with at least one-inch margins on all sides 
c. Font Type should not be smaller than 12 pt, although smaller font type may be used for 
figures, tables, and charts. 
d. Must be written in the English language. 
e. Must comply with appropriate security requirements. 
f. Proprietary information, if included in a white paper submission, must be marked for 
proper identification. On first page, mark as follows: "PROPRIETARY INFORMATION: 

HQ020226S0001 
Page 6 of 8 
This white paper includes data that shall not be disclosed outside the Government and 
shall not be duplicated, used, or disclosed-in whole or in part-for any purpose other than 
to review the contents of this submission. This restriction does not limit the Government's 
right to information if such information is obtained from another source without 
restriction.". On any other page that contains proprietary information, mark as follows: 
"PROPRIETARY INFORMATION: Use or disclosure of data contained on this page is 
subject to the restriction on the first page of this white paper submission.". 
 
4. Minimum Content Requirements:  
On Page 1, include the following: 
 
a. CSO number. 
b. Name of company, address, business size, and socioeconomic category, if applicable. 
c. Identify as traditional or non-traditional defense contractor, and whether a for-profit or 
non-profit business entity. 
d. Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) code. 
e. Unique Entity Identifier (UEID). 
f. Business, technical, and security POCs with unclassified/secure telephone numbers and 
email addresses. 
g. Classified level at which respondent is cleared to receive/store classified material. 
h. Period of performance and task objectives. 
i. Technical summary and proposed deliverable(s). The technical portion shall include a 
discussion of the nature and scope of the effort and the respondent's proposed 
approach/solution, and any proposed deliverable(s). 
j. Price for accomplishing the work.  
 
5. Point of Contact: 
All questions related to this CSO and Calls issued under this CSO shall be sent via e-mail to: 
osd.pentagon.ousd-r-e.mbx.gda-contracting@mail.mil

1. Due Dates: Due dates will be specified in the RFPs.  
 
2. Format Requirements: At a minimum, RFPs must conform to the following content and 
format requirements. At its sole discretion, the Government may modify these requirements

1.0. Introduction 
The Naval Research Laboratory (NRL) Radar Division is seeking contractor assistance in the 
design, development, and integration of radio frequency (RF) and high frequency (HF) systems. 
The task areas of interest include: mobile over-the-horizon (OTH) radar, HF surface wave radar, 
arctic HF OTH radar, homeland defense radar, high power HF transmitter, and multifunctional 
RF.   
 
1.1 Scope  
This statement of work (SOW) describes the research and development, engineering, and 
integration support the contractor is required to provide the Advance Radar Systems Branch of 
the Radar Division at NRL, Washington DC. NRL Radar Division requires the contractor to 
work alongside the Government research team in the following areas: HF and RF systems, signal 
processing hardware, mechanical analysis, and system integration on mobile platforms. 
Additionally, this SOW requires the contractor to support technology advancements, system 
requirements definition, architecture maturation, system and unit design, and the development 
and transition to an operational system to support the effort. The contractor will be required to 
support unclassified and classified tasks up to the Secret level.  
2.0. General Requirements  
 
2.1 Non-Personal Services 
The Government will neither supervise contractor employees nor control the method by which 
the contractor performs the required tasks. The Government will not assign tasks to, nor prepare 
work schedules for individual contractor employees. The contractor shall be responsible for 
managing its employees and guarding against any actions that are of the nature of personal 
services, or give the perception of personal services as defined in FAR 37.104, Personal Services 
Contracts. 
 
The contractor shall notify the Contracting Officer if any Government requested actions 
constitute, or are perceived to constitute, personal services. 
 
2.2 Overview 
The following subsections specify requirements for contract management and contractor 
personnel administration. 
 
2.2.1 Management 
The contractor shall establish clear organizational lines of authority and responsibility to ensure 
effective management of the resources assigned to this contract. 
 
2.2.2 Personnel Administration 
The contractor shall assign a single point of contact, also known the Program Manager (PM), 
who must work closely with the Contracting Officer and the Contractor Officer’s Representative 
(COR), as applicable. 
 

N0017326RTS07 
Page 3 of 10 
The contractor PM is ultimately responsible for ensuring that the contractor’s performance meets 
all Government contracting requirements within cost and schedule. The PM must have the 
requisite authority for full control over all company resources necessary for contract 
performance. As appropriate, the role of PM is a full-time management position. 
 
The contractor shall maintain the adequacy of its employees by providing initial and refresher 
training to meet the SOW requirements. 
 
The contractor shall make all necessary travel arrangements for contractor employees only after 
the travel has been reviewed and approved by the COR at least three weeks prior to the actual 
trip. Exceptions may be made for unexpected travel requirements. 
 
2.2.3 Administration 
The contractor shall establish processes and assign appropriate resources to effectively 
communicate with the Government during contract administration. 
 
The contractor shall respond to Government requests for contractual actions within five business 
days. 
 
The contractor shall assign work effort and maintain proper and accurate time keeping records of 
personnel assigned to work on this contract. 
 
2.2.4 Subcontractor Management 
 
The contractor shall be responsible for any subcontract management necessary to integrate work 
performed on this contract and shall be responsible and accountable for subcontractor 
performance on this contract. The prime contractor will manage work distribution to ensure there 
are no Organizational Conflict of Interest (OCI). Consent to subcontract shall be in accordance 
with procedures established under FAR clause 52.244-2, Subcontracts. 
 
2.3 Contractor Furnished Equipment, Materials, Subcontracts and Supplies  
Equipment and unexpended materials and supplies purchased by the contractor under this 
contract become the property of the Government at the end of the performance period, including 
all options. 
 
The contractor shall provide any other equipment, material, and supplies, not furnished by the 
Government, but required to perform the work detailed herein. 
 
2.4 Contractor Personnel, Disciplines, and Specialties 
The required and/or desired minimum education, certifications, clearance, and experience 
requirements for contractor personnel to perform the support tasks identified in this SOW are 
defined in the contracts “Personnel Qualifications” attachment. 
 
2.5 Use of Government Property at Government Facilities 
If determined to be in the Government’s best interest, the Government will make available the 
materials, office space, communications capability, and information for use by the contractor in 

N0017326RTS07 
Page 4 of 10 
the performance of this contract at Government facilities. Government property used by the 
contractor at the Government’s facilities will be on a rent-free basis and all such property shall 
be considered to remain in the possession and control of the NRL for property responsibility and 
accountability purposes. 
 
2.6 Requirement for On-site Contractors 
 
The contractor shall comply with requirements for On-Site Contractor performance at 
Government facilities. The full text of the requirements for On-Site contractors is set forth as an 
attachment to the contract. Pursuant to DFARS 211.106 contractor employees shall identify 
themselves as contractor personnel by introducing themselves or being introduced as contractor 
personnel and displaying distinguishing badges or other visible identification for meetings with 
Government personnel. In addition, contractor personnel shall appropriately identify themselves 
as contractor employees in telephone conversations and in formal and informal written 
correspondence. 
 
2.7 Place of Performance 
It is anticipated that work will be performed at the following locations: 
 
• NRL – Washington, D.C. 
• NRL Chesapeake Bay Detachment (CBD) – Chesapeake, MD 
• Tilghman Island, MD 
• Naval Air Station Patuxent River – Patuxent River, MD 
• NASA Flight Facility – Wallops Island, VA 
• Other Government facilities as needed 
• Contractor facilities 
 
The contractor shall perform work at Government facilities within the normal work hours unless 
differing hours are specified by the COR. The contractor is not required to maintain the same 
hours as Government employees; however, contractor employees performing working at NRL 
must work during the normal workweek. Contractor personnel working off-site must remain 
reachable (e.g. phone, email, Microsoft Teams, etc.) by Government personnel. In the event of 
severe weather conditions, the contractor should refer to the top banner of the NRL website for 
the NRL-DC operating status or refer to the Office of Personnel Management website for the 
operating status of the U.S. Government offices in Washington, D.C. area and for additional 
information. 
 
2.8 Travel / Temporary Duty (TDY) 
Travel may be required to conduct experimental research, and/or attend Government reviews or 
scientific meetings and seminars.
 The contractor shall submit all travel requirements (e.g. plans, 
agenda, itinerary, and dates) in writing for pre-approval to the Government COR. Travel is on a 
strictly cost-reimbursable basis. The contractor shall bill costs for travel in accordance with FAR 
31.205-46 Travel Costs (subject to local policy & procedures) and DoD’s Joint Travel 
Regulations.  
 

N0017326RTS07 
Page 5 of 10 
The contractor shall be able to provide two persons within one day of travel notification for 
deployment to support work described in this SOW at any location within the United States. The 
persons are to deploy with tooling for mechanical or electrical work necessary to maintain or 
repair EMWRF related equipment. 
 
2.9 Patents – Reporting of Subject Inventions 
 
All subject inventions must be properly reported through the iEdison system at 
https://www.nist.gov/iedison. Additionally, the contractor shall provide interim reports and a 
final report in accordance with DFARS 252.227-7039 Patents - Reporting of Subject Inventions, 
utilizing DD Form 882. If there are no subject inventions to report, the contractor is still required 
to submit the DD Form 882. Reports shall be delivered via email to the points of contact 
identified in Block 14 of CDRL A006. 
 
3.0. Technical Requirements   
 
3.1 Mobile Over-the-Horizon Radar R&D (Task 1) 
The objective of this task is to develop, design, install, and maintain a long-range surveillance 
and targeting system to demonstrate and mature HF radar and communications on mobile 
platforms. Under this contract, the contractor shall provide support in the following areas: 
• High Frequency (HF) radar system design (CDRL A002) (CDRL A005) 
o Perform system analysis, design, development, and laboratory and/or field test of 
HF systems (i.e. radar, communications, electronic warfare) 
o Conduct trade studies that lead to optimal system performance for a defined set of 
conditions and applications 
o Perform technical analysis and computer modeling and simulations to evaluate 
component and subsystem level performance for the radar system 
• Design and development of signal processing radar hardware and software (CDRL A002) 
(CDRL A005) 
o Develop, design, and build new signal processing hardware for the system 
o Perform laboratory and field experiments of radar sub-systems to support RF 
development 
o Setup and perform component and system measurements such as S-parameters, 
linearity (i.e. P1dB, OIP3) noise figure and others 
o Develop software blocks to integrate and mature various signal processing blocks 
(i.e. beamforming, peak detection, tracking, and coordinate registration) 
• Carry out system integration of transmit and receive HF systems on land, maritime, 
and/or air platforms (CDRL A002) 
o Develop a schedule to plan out system integration and installation timeline 
o Develop a procurement plan in support of equipment acquisition 
o Develop test plans, reports, user manuals, and other documentation 
• Participate in technical meetings and design reviews, provide critiques, review 
documentation, and monitor

1.0  BACKGROUND 
The mission of the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Veterans Health Administration 
(VHA) is to provide superior healthcare services to Veterans of the United States. As 
the largest integrated healthcare system in the country, VA is uniquely positioned to 
develop and provide advanced healthcare capabilities to over 9 million Veterans. One 
significant challenge facing the VA and its ability to deliver high quality and reliable 
patient care to our Nation’s Veterans is the increase in demand for veteran patients to 
be seen within the VA healthcare system. In the short window of time allocated for each 
patient appointment, providers have a multitude of clinical and administrative tasks to be 
completed. This increases risk of important information being omitted due to rushed 
interviews and contributes to provider burn out. The myriad of tasks expected of 
providers beyond caring for patients puts significant cognitive burden and increased 
strain on them professionally. This strain has the potential to negatively impact patient 
care. It can also contribute to provider attrition, causing additional impact to Veterans 
and clinical staff.  
 
One method to reduce the risk of missing vital clinical information that impacts patient 
care planning and reducing cognitive burden for our providers is the use of ambient 
scribe technology. Artificial Intelligence (AI) ambient scribes utilize a microphone on a 
secure device. The ambient AI scribe transcribes patient encounters. It then uses 
machine learning and natural-language processing to summarize the conversation's 
clinical content and produce a transcribed note documenting the visit. Such transcribed 
conversations between patients and providers automatically leverage AI technologies to 
create notes in the appropriate format (generate clinical documentation) and summarize 
a patient’s visit. Automating these tasks increases accuracy of information, saves the 
providers time, and reduces their mental strain. Visit notes that include a patient’s care 
plan is a critical component of treatment and care delivery. The software functions as a 
medical and clinical system, equipment, device, or software (MCSEDS) as defined in 
VA Directive 6008. 
 
Ambient scribe technology also enables other labor-saving capabilities to include but 
not limited to: pre and post visit charting to summarize important information prior to visit 
by either completing the task with AI or integrating with provider pre-charted note, 
coding support, order capture, after-visit summaries, drafting care plans and other 
capabilities.  
 
The ambient scribing solution required is unique to the operational environment and 
specific challenges faced by the Veterans Health Administration (VHA). In January 
2024, VHA undertook an AI Technical Sprint challenge to ensure that potential solutions 
were rigorously tested through a competitive and impartial evaluation process under 
H.R. 4521-Bioeconomy Research and Development Act Of 2021 [America COMPETES 
Act of 2022]. The goal of the competition was to identify the top AI solutions identified 
through the VHA AI Tech Sprint Track 1: Ambient Dictation of Clinical Encounters.  
 
Throughout the Technical Sprint, many solutions demonstrated superior technical 
maturity and clinical performance. Their development was closely aligned with the 
urgent needs of the VHA, specifically targeting enhancements in provider burnout and 
clinical documentation efficiencies. IT professionals and healthcare providers assessed

Moreover, the effectiveness and safety of these solutions were evaluated through a

DESCRIPTION

Sources Sought Notice / Request for Information

Office of Construction and Facilities Management (CFM) – 

Reduce Inefficiencies & Costs in VA Design and Construction (RICVDC)

This notice is issued by the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Office of Construction and Facilities Management (CFM) as specified below for the review and optimization of VA standards and requirements found on the Technical Library (TIL) for use across the Department to ultimately improve cost, quality, and operation. The purpose of this Sources Sought Notice is to gather information from the contractor community at large for the purpose of acquisition planning and market research to identify potential sources capable of performing the scope of services contained herein. Additionally, the notice is to solicit feedback regarding the intended tasks to be completed to meet the VA Secretary’s direction. Further consideration outside of these stated purposes is not authorized and will not be further discussed. 

This notice does not constitute a Request for Proposal, Invitation for Bid, or Request for Quotation, and is not to be construed as a commitment by the Government to enter into a contract. Furthermore, responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. Responders are solely responsible for all expenses associated with preparation of a response to the notice. While encouraged, industry is not required to respond to this notice.

Objective of RICVDC

To obtain professional support to conduct a thorough and comprehensive review of current standards and requirements and implement modifications to respond to the VA Secretary’s direction. Therefore, by engaging a qualified consultant, VA will optimize VA Requirements to improve cost, schedule, quality, safety, and resiliency of VA owned facilities and leases while ensuring compliance with Federal and State requirements and safeguarding Veteran-centric care environments. Specific objectives are:

Improve design and construction efficiency by adopting applicable private healthcare industry practices and standards while preserving VA mission-critical, statutory, and Fourth Mission requirements.

Assist CFM in identifying opportunities to reduce inefficiencies, validate and standardize space criteria, eliminate unnecessary variability, and clarify technical and programmatic requirements.

Establish and support engagements with private sector partners to identify and inform actionable solutions and leverage commercial best practices that will improve cost effectiveness, delivery timelines, and constructability outcomes.

Assist CFM in creating and promoting clear, consistent VA requirements, and the application of commercially proven delivery approaches to enhance predictability, affordability, and performance in healthcare facility development.

Please submit your response to Contracting Officer, Jason Hardy at jason.hardy@va.gov by 3:00pm CST, Friday, April 17, 2026. If your firm requires additional time for a response, please contact the Contracting Officer. Thank you for taking the opportunity to provide your professional input in an effort for the VA to improve its project delivery for Veterans!

Specific objectives are:

Assist CFM in creating and promoting clear, consistent VA requirements, and the application of commercially proven delivery approaches to enhance predictability, affordability, and performance in healthcare facility development.

Background

The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) constructs, leases, renovates and maintains healthcare facilities dedicated to providing healthcare to our Veterans. Delivering appropriately planned and designed facilities is critical for the mission of VA. The VA Office of Construction and Facilities Management (CFM) is charged with setting the standards and guidelines that all healthcare facilities follow to accomplish the VA mission: 

“To fulfill President Lincoln's promise to care for those who have served in our nation's military and for their families, caregivers, and survivors.”

The VA Technical Information Library (TIL) contains the VA Planning, Design and Construction documents that establish and illustrate the requirements to be implemented on VA facility design and construction projects. These documents, hereinafter referred to as ‘TIL Documents’, establish the framework of requirements within which functional spaces of a healthcare facility are planned and designed to facilitate safe, effective and efficient healthcare delivery for Veterans, staff and visitors. These requirements, hereinafter referred to as “VA Requirements,” provide guidance to VA personnel and design professionals in the tasks of planning, designing, and constructing VA healthcare facilities. They are closely interrelated with, and incorporate, as appropriate, current VA/VHA Directives, standards, Handbooks and Policies. 

In December 2025, the VA Secretary issued a memo entitled “Reduce Inefficiencies and Costs in VA Facilities Design and Construction”, which reiterated VA’s need to deliver first-class health care facilities to our Veterans and noted VA’s Fourth Mission: “to improve the Nation’s preparedness for response to war, terrorism, national emergencies, and natural disasters”. The Secretary directed CFM and VHA to identify opportunities for improvements in VA healthcare design and construction standards, adopt private healthcare industry practices and standards where applicable, while maintaining VA mission critical requirements. 

Therefore, CFM is looking to evaluate, clarify, and optimize planning, design, and construction requirements contained in the VA TIL, including but not limited to VA/VHA Directives, and applicable Federal Laws such as VA’s Fourth Mission that governs VA healthcare facilities. The effort seeks to compare VA requirements with applicable federal regulations, healthcare codes, and private-sector standards such as those from the Facilities Guidelines Institute (FGI), International Code Council (ICC), Joint Commission, and other governing bodies – to identify redundancies, conflicts, inefficiencies, and areas where multiple compliance options exist. 

EXPERTISE AND PROFESSIONAL CAPABILITIES

The consultant team for this project shall have the following expertise and professional capabilities to successfully complete the scope of services:  

Architecture and Engineering:

Mechanical Engineering (including HVAC, building automation, plumbing, medical gas, boiler operation, water safety, and infection control) 

Electrical Engineering (including normal power, emergency and backup power, lighting, low voltage power systems)

Infection Prevention Practitioner (CIC) for ICRA/ILSM implications

Information Technology

Historic Preservation

DETAILED SCOPE OF SERVICES 

The consultant shall provide services for the following tasks conducting industry engagement sessions, researching and analyses of documentation leading to the development of recommendations / deliverables for potential VA implementation for improvement. 

TASK #1: DATA SOURCE IDENTIFICATION, COLLECTION, ANALYZATION AND ORGANIZATION 

Analyze current model building codes and industry design requirements and the federal regulatory requirements for the design, construction and operation of healthcare facilities, including any codes or other requirements used by industry leaders within the healthcare design community identified by reference. The resources and identified documents include, but not limited to, requirements defined in the latest release of the Federal Guidelines Institute (FGI) guidelines appropriate for VA facilities, the International Code Commission (ICC) and the Joint Commission Standards, which define the certification requirements of VA healthcare facilities, etc. Consultant shall complete the following:

Identify and document with a crosswalk analysis and provide recommendations, based on life cycle cost analysis, the differences between current model building codes and industry design requirements and VA design requirements for VA owned properties and lease properties. 

Using identified documents, where multiple options for compliance exist in the code or requirements, provide analysis of private industry versus VA application. 

In particular, assess the Facility Guidelines Institute (FGI) guidelines itemizing specific references where VA Requirements differ from the requirements stated in the FGI guidelines and other requirements noted above.  Consultant shall develop justifications and cost impact models for those select criteria that exceed FGI and code minimums and are determined to be essential to VA mission and compliance with Federal requirements. Where conflicts exist between TIL Documents and FGI, applicable codes, standards, and federal law, the consultant will document those conflicts and provide pathways for resolution and document risk trade-offs for VA governance decisions. Consultant shall provide an assessment of the process and procedure for identifying use of space during design related to operational efficiency and elements that are included related to occupant and patient welfare (i.e. - large interior open spaces, methods for providing natural light, function over form). 

Deliverable: Develop a decision package based on identified differences between model building codes and industry design requirements and VA design requirements, including recommendations on which requirements to preserve, which to remove, with justification of why. The package shall include documentation to support the analysis, justification and conclusion. Additionally, prepare life cycle cost valuations as supporting documentation in analysis and on which recommendations are based. Lastly, the decision package shall include:
