Advanced Uncooled Thermal Integration Efforts

Request for Information (RFI)

Background:

The United States Army Combat Capabilities Development Command (DEVCOM), Command, Control, Computers, Communications, Cyber, Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance (C5ISR) Center is performing market research to inform future system level requirements and/or prototype development/build efforts which integrate next generation uncooled thermal sensors. The desired systems shall incorporate Government Furnished Equipment (GFE) thermal sensors. These thermal sensors will be compliant with a TBD Interface Control Document and will be lens-less.  The system integrators will need to design an appropriate lens for the application that will interface with the sensors to demonstrate the advanced capability and prove out Technology Readiness Level (TRL) 6+ by being assessed in a relevant environment. Responses including complete systems and/or individual capabilities/expertise listed below are welcome.  Proposed systems should focus on showcasing these advanced sensors in systems that are optimized for low Size, Weight, and Power and Cost (SWaP-C).

Requested Information: 

The C5ISR Center requests the following information:

Company Information

Company Name

Business designation (Traditional, Nontraditional).

Company Address

RFI Technical POC Name, Email Address, and Phone number

RFI Business/Contract POC Name, Email Address, and Phone number

CAGE Code 

Facility Clearance Level

Joint Certification Program (JCP) DD Form 2345 (JCP Home (dla.mil))

Technical Information

The technical information is contained in a CUI attachment.  See directions below on how to request access.

Submission Requirements: 

Submission of vendor capabilities and technologies which relate to the RFI. 

Existing technology and how it addresses the requirements or how it can be modified to address the requirements.

Relevant experience in integrating EO/IR sensors into Prototype Systems, especially in the areas defined above.  Detail any relevant expertise with EO/IR integration related to any Program of Record or fielded systems and how it relates to the areas defined above or offers risk reduction.  

Innovative/novel solutions for addressing requirements or planned research in the technology areas along with timelines to expected deliverables.  

Assessment of the Technical Maturity/Technology Readiness Level of technology.

Submission of a Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) cost to meet the desired integration timelines and prototype quantities or to provide the specific capabilities detailed below.

Any comments, questions, or concerns regarding the requested sensor integration and prototype build or on the other capabilities requested.

Submission Instructions: 

All documents shall be portion marked IAW DoDM 5200.01-V2. Submission of proprietary and other sensitive information shall be marked and identified with disposition instructions (submitted material will not be returned).

Subject line should be: Advanced Uncooled Thermal Integration Efforts.

The RFI response shall be limited to 5 pages.

Unclassified responses must be to: usarmy.apg.devcom-c5isr.mbx.rti-industry-engagement@army.mil.

Responses with CUI must be sent encrypted via DoD SAFE submitted via DoD SAFE (https://safe.apps.mil/).  If you require a DoD SAFE drop link, please contact usarmy.apg.devcom-c5isr.mbx.rti-industry-engagement@army.mil.	

For submission of SECRET or higher classification material to C5ISR Center, please contact usarmy.apg.devcom-c5-isr.mbx.rti-industry-engagement@mail.smil.mil.

Responses submitted by contractors that contain U.S. classified military information (CMI) generated in conjunction with a DOD program should be classified in accordance with the applicable Security Classification Guide (SCG). Please include a copy of the SCG with the submission. Only U.S. citizens are authorized to respond to this RFI.

Access to additional technical details (If applicable):

 

This RFI provides general public release requirements ONLY. Additional technical detail is available in Attachment 01 to this RFI, entitled Attachment 01 Technical Information. Attachment 01 is controlled, containing Control Unclassified Information (CUI), therefore, is not available for general release. To gain access to the controlled document, your company/entity must be certified by the Joint Certification Program (JCP).  To request download of the controlled attachment, you must click on the document title to request access. Please enter the reason for requesting access and with your JCP certification number and CAGE code. Once approved, you will be granted permission to access the controlled document. You may request access to the controlled document until the RFI submission response window has closed.

 

Note: Please contact the U.S./Canada Joint Certification Office for any inquiries regarding the Joint Certification Program. The web link for JCP is JCP Home (dla.mil).

Questions and Requests for Clarification:

 

Questions and requests for clarification of information must be submitted to: usarmy.apg.devcom-c5isr.mbx.rti-industry-engagement@army.mil (UNCLASSIFIED) or usarmy.apg.devcom-c5-isr.mbx.rti-industry-engagement@mail.smil.mil (CLASSIFIED) no later than 5 calendar days following RFI posting. NOTE: If you are sending a CLASSIFIED question, please send a courtesy email to the UNCLASSIFIED mailbox to notify of the request on the Classified side. 

Questions with CUI shall be submitted via DOD SAFE. If you require a drop link, please contact usarmy.apg.devcom-c5isr.mbx.rti-industry-engagement@army.mil. Questions and requests will only be accepted in writing; phone calls will not be accepted. 

Requests shall be submitted only to the email address specified above. Any other forms of request for additional information will not be honored.

Response Due Date: 30 Calendar Days after release

Data Rights:

It is desirable that data be received with unlimited rights to the Government. If a proposed solution to this RFI shall include any data rights restrictions, responses should clearly denote anticipated assertions. It is also recognized that proprietary data may be included with the information provided. If so, it is the responsibility of the interested party submitting data to clearly mark such proprietary information and clearly separate it from the unrestricted information as an addendum. No Classified data shall be provided via email.

Disclaimer:

This RFI is issued solely for information and planning purposes and does not constitute a solicitation. In accordance with FAR 15.202 (e), responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. No award is intended as a result of this notice. The Government will not reimburse costs incurred by respondents in response to this RFI, or for participating in information exchange regarding details of the RFI.  

Any information submitted by respondents to this sources sought synopsis is voluntary. The Army does not intend to award a contract on the basis of this notice or to otherwise pay for the information solicited. Respondents should not construe this synopsis as a commitment for any purpose. Respondents will not individually be notified of the results of any government assessments. The Government's evaluation of the capability statements received will factor into whether any forthcoming solicitation will be conducted as a full and open competition or as a set-aside for small businesses, or any particular small business designation (e.g. SDVOSB, HUBZone, 8(a), WOSB, EDWOSB.).

II. APPENDIX B: Rules of Behavior for VA Contractors 
CONTRACTOR RULES OF BEHAVIOR 
This User Agreement contains rights and authorizations regarding my access to and 
use of any information assets or resources associated with my performance of services 
under the contract terms with the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA). This User 
Agreement covers my access to all VA data whether electronic or hard copy (“Data”), 
VA information systems and resources (“Systems”), and VA sites (“Sites”). This User 
Agreement incorporates Rules of Behavior for using VA, and other information systems 
and resources under the contract.  
1. GENERAL TERMS AND CONDITIONS FOR ALL ACTIONS and ACTIVITIES 
UNDER THE CONTRACT: 
a. I understand and agree that I have no reasonable expectation of privacy in 
accessing or using any VA, or other Federal Government information systems.  
b. I consent to reviews and actions by the Office of Information & Technology (OI&T) 
staff designated and authorized by the VA Chief Information Officer (CIO) and to the 
VA OIG regarding my access to and use of any information assets or resources 
associated with my performance of services under the contract terms with the VA. 
These actions may include monitoring, recording, copying, inspecting, restricting 
access, blocking, tracking, and disclosing to all authorized OI&T, VA, and law 
enforcement personnel as directed by the VA CIO without my prior consent or 
notification. 
c. I consent to reviews and actions by authorized VA systems administrators and 
Information Security Officers solely for protection of the VA infrastructure, including, 
but not limited to monitoring, recording, auditing, inspecting, investigating, restricting 
access, blocking, tracking, disclosing to authorized personnel, or any other 
authorized actions by all authorized OI&T, VA, and law enforcement personnel.

d. I understand and accept that unauthorized attempts or acts to access, upload, 
change, or delete information on Federal Government systems; modify Federal 
government systems; deny access to Federal government systems; accrue 
resources for unauthorized use on Federal government systems; or otherwise 
misuse Federal government systems or resources are prohibited. 
e. I understand that such unauthorized attempts or acts are subject to action that 
may result in criminal, civil, or administrative penalties. This includes penalties for 
violations of Federal laws including, but not limited to, 18 U.S.C. §1030 (fraud and 
related activity in connection with computers) and 18 U.S.C. §2701 (unlawful access 
to stored communications). 
f. I agree that OI&T staff, in the course of obtaining access to information or systems 
on my behalf for performance under the contract, may provide information about me 
including, but not limited to, appropriate unique personal identifiers such as date of 
birth and social security number to other system administrators, Information Security 
Officers (ISOs), or other authorized staff without further notifying me or obtaining 
additional written or verbal permission from me. 
g. I understand I must comply with VA’s security and data privacy directives and

obtained from the Contracting Officer’s Technical Representative (COTR). If the 
contractor believes the policies and guidance provided by the COTR is a material 
unilateral change to the contract, the contractor must elevate such concerns to the 
Contracting Officer for resolution. 
h. I will report suspected or identified information security/privacy incidents to the 
COTR and to the local ISO or Privacy Officer as appropriate. 
2. GENERAL RULES OF BEHAVIOR  
a. Rules of Behavior are part of a comprehensive program to provide complete 
information security. These rules establish standards of behavior in recognition of 
the fact that knowledgeable users are the foundation of a successful security 
program. Users must understand that taking personal responsibility for the security 
of their computer and the information it contains is an essential part of their job.

(1) Follow established procedures for requesting, accessing, and closing user 
accounts and access. I will not request or obtain access beyond what is normally 
granted to users or by what is outlined in the contract. 
(2) Use only systems, software, databases, and data which I am authorized to 
use, including any copyright restrictions. 
(3) I will not use other equipment (OE) (non-contractor owned) for the storage, 
transfer, or processing of VA sensitive information without a VA CIO approved 
waiver, unless it has been reviewed and approved by local management and is 
included in the language of the contract. If authorized to use OE IT equipment, I 
must ensure that the system meets all applicable 6500 Handbook requirements 
for OE. 
(4) Not use my position of trust and access rights to exploit system controls or

(5) Not attempt to override or disable security, technical, or management controls 
unless expressly permitted to do so as an explicit requirement under the contract 
or at the direction of the COTR or ISO. If I am allowed or required to have a local 
administrator account on a government-owned computer, that local 
administrative account does not confer me unrestricted access or use, nor the 
authority to bypass security or other controls except as expressly permitted by 
the VA CIO or CIO’s designee. 
(6) Contractors’ use of systems, information, or sites is strictly limited to fulfill the

criminal law still apply. 
(7) Grant access to systems and information only to those who have an official 
need to know.

DESCRIPTION/SPECIFICATIONS/STATEMENT OF 
WORK INTRODUCTION 
The Bureau of Ocean Energy Management (BOEM) through the Marine Minerals Program has 
worked to identify sand resources across the Gulf of America (GOA). These resources are 
economically valuable because they are used in beach replenishment and other coastal 
protection and restoration projects. Recent studies have shown strong evidence that the offshore 
sand may contain concentrations of heavy and critical minerals, adding to its economic value. 
Locating sources of critical minerals in sediment resources in the GOA region and determining 
their concentrations could provide a secure and reliable supply of critical minerals related to our 
national security and economic prosperity. 
The BOEM’s intent with the request for information (RFI) is to find a vendor that can identify 
critical mineral deposits along the Texas Coast by analyzing 318 samples from 159 cores collected 
and are stored in Boca Raton, FL and Austin, TX.  The goal of the project is to support BOEM’s 
National Offshore Critical Mineral Inventory (NOCMI) to characterize critical mineral resources 
on the OCS.  This proposed work aligns with President Trump's Executive Orders 14285, 
Unleashing America's Offshore Critical Minerals and Resources, and 14154, Unleashing American 
Energy, which prioritize unleashing America’s potential to explore and develop OCS critical 
mineral resources. Furthermore, the work is in support of 30 CFR PART 581—Leasing of Marine 
Minerals other than oil, gas, or Sulphur in the Outer Continental Shelf. 
 

SOURCES SOUGHT INFORMATION 
BOEM/BSEE is issuing this RFI as part of market research in accordance with federal 
acquisition regulation (FAR) Part 10 to determine the availability and technical capability of 
sources proposing to identify critical mineral deposits along the Texas Coast by sampling these 
cores for critical minerals.  
This Request for Information / Sources Sought Synopsis does not constitute an Invitation for 
Bids (IFB), a Request for Quote (RFQ), or a Request for Proposal (RFP) and it should not be 
construed as a commitment of any kind by the Government to issue a formal solicitation or 
ultimately award a contract. The U.S. Government is in no way liable to pay for or reimburse 
any companies or entities that respond to this announcement. Any costs incurred by interested 
vendors in response to this announcement or incurred for participation in this market survey 
will NOT be reimbursed. All information marked as proprietary information will be safeguarded 
to prevent disclosures to non-Government personnel and entities. There is no bid package or 
solicitation document associated with this announcement. Response to this RFI is strictly 
voluntary. NO SOLICITATION DOCUMENTS EXIST AT THIS TIME. 
Restricted or proprietary components, interfaces and equipment, or proprietary data 
provided should be clearly marked and presented as an addendum to the non-restricted/non-
proprietary information. In the absence of such identification BOEM will assume to have 
unlimited rights to all the technical data in the information paper. 
BOEM is seeking information from vendors that have the capability of performing the work 
described below in the Objective and Scope. Responses must be identified by RFI No. 
DOIMFBO260003 and the following information should be included in a cover letter to your 
response: 
1. Company name 
2. SAM.gov UEI number 
3. Mailing address 
4. E-mail address 
5. Telephone number 
6. Web site address (if available) 
7. Business Size and Eligibility under U.S. Government socio-economic programs 
(i.e., type of business - large, small, small-disadvantaged, Woman-owned, veteran-
owned, or 8(a)) under North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code 
associated with the project. 
8. Confirm if your company is registered in the System for Award Management 
(SAM). 
9. Any established pricing catalogs, rough of magnitudes or additional pricing 
information an interested party is willing to share regarding their products. This 
information would be for market research information only. 
10. NAICS code recommendations for this scope (if any) 
 
There is a ten (10) page limit to this response. Responses should be submitted to: 
bradford_kelly@ios.doi.gov  
 
Based upon responses received, BOEM representatives may choose to meet (virtually) with 

potential vendors and hold one-on-one exchanges. Such exchanges will be considered further 
Market Research intended to obtain clarifications of potential capability and/or experience to 
assist BOEM in defining and developing its requirements. While a response to this RFI is not 
mandatory, the likelihood of engaging in one-on-one exchanges may increase the likelihood of 
engaging these market research efforts with interested parties. Any participation in these 
efforts will not be reimbursed. 
OBJECTIVE 
The objective of this RFI is to identify vendors that have the capabilities to identify critical 
mineral deposits along the Texas OCS by conducting elemental/mineralogical analyses on 318 
samples from 159 cores (Map and Core Locations in Appendices 1 below). The cores are in 
storage in Austin, TX and Boca Raton, FL. Elemental/mineralogical analyses should include 
basic testing to determine the elements found in the samples. Based on these results, select 
samples should be further processed through more specialized equipment to separate out the 
heavy minerals, calculate their distribution and mass, and determine their provenance, 
composition, and recoverability. 
SCOPE 
The vendor must have the ability to travel to Austin, TX and Boca Raton, FL where the cores are 
being stored, collecting samples from those cores, and conducting elemental / mineralogical 
analyses on those samples. Based on initial core descriptions, a minimum of 2 samples from 
each core should be identified prior to collection and discussed with BOEM geologists .  
Samples should be collected by an experienced geologist and shipped to the testing facility. 
Cores will remain in storage. All collected samples are to be run through grain size analysis 
using a Laser Particle Size Analysis (LPSA). All samples should be analyzed with an exploration 
style analysis to determine the elements in each sample. The analysis should be conducted on the 
relevant critical minerals in the Gulf of America from the final 2025 List of Critical Minerals, 
published to the Federal Register. After elemental analysis is completed, the need for additional 
testing will be discussed with BOEM. Specified samples should be analyzed to separate out the 
heavy minerals, calculate their distribution and mass, and determine their provenance, 
composition, and recoverability.

1 
 
 
Department of State 2026 A/E IDIQ for  
Worldwide Environmental Engineering Services  
 
Sources Sought - Market Research 
  
This is a Sources Sought notice Only. This Sources Sought Notice is issued for information and 
planning purposes as part of U.S. Department of State market research and does not constitute an 
RFP or a promise to issue an RFP in the future. The purpose of this notice is to obtain 
information regarding the availability and capability of qualified Small Business (SB), Women 
Owned Small Business (WOSB), HUBZone (HUBZ), 8(a), and Service-Disabled Veteran-
Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) - (SDVOSM) under NAICS code 541330. All interested 
firms must have an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM) at the time 
of submission and must not be listed on the Excluded Parties List. Acquisition strategy and set-
aside decisions may be made based on the information provided in response to this Sources 
Sought notice. Information submitted in response to this notice will be used solely for acquisition 
planning and will not be shared outside the government acquisition team. 
Responders are advised that the government will not pay for information submitted in response 
to this sources sought notice, nor will it compensate responders for any costs incurred in the 
development/furnishing of a response.  
Please note that a decision not to submit a response to this sources sought notice will not 
preclude a vendor from participating in any future solicitation. 
Description:  Engineering services may include, but are not limited to, conducting asbestos 
inspection surveys/sampling of DOS properties worldwide in accordance with U.S. 
Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Asbestos Hazard Emergency Response Act (AHERA) 
standards; produce Post Asbestos Management Plans utilizing the DOS asbestos inspection 
database; perform Asbestos Industrial Hygiene oversight of DOS asbestos remediation projects; 
conduct lead inspection surveys/sampling of DOS properties; perform toxic and hazardous 
material assessments at DOS properties; perform air quality analyses to address potential 
environmental contaminants (examples such as radon, mold, heavy metals, etc) in occupied 
work/residential locations; and provide EPA AHERA Asbestos Inspector training and 
certifications for DOS personnel.  
Scope: The environmental engineering services scope may include the following professional 
services: architecture, environmental field staff Certified Industrial Hygiene (CIH), Certified 
Hazardous Materials Management (CHMM), Certified Safety Professional (CSP) data analytics, 
facility management, project management, and construction management. 
 
The firm shall coordinate U.S. Government’s requirements and the applicable laws, codes and 
standards at the overseas project sites.  
  
We are seeking Companies in the following Socio-Economic Categories under NAICS code: 
Small Business (SB), Women Owned Small Business (WOSB), HUBZone (HUBZ), 8(a), and 
Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSB). All interested companies must 
have an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM) and not be on the 
Excluded Party List. 

 
2 
 
 
 
1. Technical Requirements 
 
2A.  Submission Requirements and Format:   
2A.1 Organization.  Organize submittals by factor according to the list in Section 2.C below.  
Tab and clearly identify each factor in the submittal. 
2A.2 Language.  Use only the English language.  Submit an English translation for all 
information originally provided in another language.  If an English translation is not 
provided, DOS will not review or consider the information submitted only in another 
language.  Non-English language pages are not included in any page counts. 
2A.3 Page Limits.  Maximum page limits for each factor are identified in Section 2.C.  If a 
submission exceeds the allowable page limits, DOS may consider only the designated 
number of pages, starting with the first page of each factor.   
2A.4 Page Size.  Pages are based on a single-sided 8 ½” x 11” (or A4) sheet.   Page 
equivalencies are:  one double-sided page = two single-sided pages; 11”x17” fold-outs = 
two pages per side.  Except where otherwise specified, the maximum paper size 
permitted is 11” x 17” (or A3).   
2A.5 Font.  Submit offers in size 12 font minimum.  Only the Standard Form (SF) 330, 
required for use by the design subcontractors, may be prepared in size 10 font.   SF 330 is 
available through:  https://www.gsa.gov/forms-library/architect-engineer-qualifications 
2A.6 Color.  Submit text as black writing on a white background.  Text that is difficult to read 
due to the use of colored text, colored background, and/or font selection may result in a 
failure of one or more factors. 
2A.7 Format and Copies.   Provide one electronic copy via email; see submission instructions 
at the end of this sources sought notice. 
2A.8 Missing Information.  A proposal submission discovered to be incomplete or missing the 
required information may be eliminated from further consideration.   
2A.9 Additional Information.  Offerors are cautioned that DOS will consider only the 
information in the submission and that obtained by DOS from additional sources 
concerning past performance.   
 
2B.  Definitions: 
2B.1 Where the term “Offeror” is used, it is intended that requirements for the Offeror apply 
equally to either a single Contractor or to all parties of a Joint Venture (JV), where 
applicable. 
2B.2 The contract(s) included in this sources sought are referenced as “the Contract” in 
Section 2.C. 
 
 
2C.  CONTENT OF SUBMISSIONS AND FACTORS FOR EVALUATION: 
 
 
FACTOR 1: Joint Venture Agreement/Signed Statement of JV Intent & Description of 
Partnership.   
1.1 Page limit:   Three.  The JV agreement or Statement of Intent to form a JV does not count 
against the page limit for this factor. 
1.2 If the planned organizational structure for the Offeror is a JV, provide a Statement of 
Intent to form a JV, signed by all parties to the JV.  If a formal JV has already been 

 
3 
 
formed, the JV agreement may be submitted in lieu of the Statement of Intent.  If the 
Offeror is not submitting as a JV, include a statement in the submission in response to 
this factor. 
1.3 Organizations that wish to rely upon the experience or financial resources of any other 
legally related entity or organization, including parent companies, subsidiaries, or other 
related firms, must do so by way of a JV. 
1.4 Describe the relationship of the JV parties. 
1.5 Identify each JV party’s role. 
1.6 Identify the type and percentage of work assigned to each JV party.   
 
If the offeror is organized as a Joint Venture, DOS will evaluate whether the roles and 
responsibilities of the JV parties have been adequately described.  This factor is not 
applicable if there is no JV. 
 
 
FACTOR 2: A/E Firm Past Performance on Management/ Planning (12 pages maximum) 
2.1 Page limit:   Four per project.   
2.2 Submit a portfolio of at least three projects that have been managed/ planned and 
completed or accepted by the client as a viable solution in the last ten years.  Project 
values shall range from $250,000 to $1,000,000 USD. A maximum of one example may 
be an OBO project. 
 
2.2.1 Each project example shall include the following information: 
2.2.1.1 Project Name 
2.2.1.2 Identify A/E Firm role and area(s) of responsibility on each project 
2.2.1.3 Project program and function 
2.2.1.4 Project budget, final contract amount, schedule, and completion date 
2.2.1.5 The projects presented shall display the Offeror’s unique approach to solving 
complex and overlapping owner’s requirements.  
2.2.1.6 The material shall address the management/ planning approach with salient 
features for each project and explain how the client’s multi-functional and 
complex program, image, mission, economic, schedule, maintenance, 
functional and operational objectives were satisfied by the overall 
management/ planning solution.   
2.2.1.7 Describe the relevance of submitted projects to the specific IDIQ scope or 
description under which the offeror is submitting.  
       2.2.18 Cite any certificates, awards, peer recognition, etc. demonstrating high                   
performance management/ planning solutions.   
 
FACTOR 3: Core Team Key Personnel Profiles (8 pages maximum) 
3.1 Page limit:   1 per profile.   
3.2       Identify Key Personnel in the leadership roles identified below: 
A. Program Manager  
B. Project Manager  
C. Certified Industrial Hygienist (CIH)  
D. Certified Hazardous Material Manager (CHMM)  
E. Certified Safety Professional (CSP)  
 
3.2.1 Profile shall include the following information: 

 
4 
 
3.2.1.1 Name 
3.2.1.2 Education and professional experience including licenses and qualifications. 
3.2.1.3 Area of responsibility and leadership on the project examples of Factor 2. 
      3.2.1.4 Cite any professional awards, peer recognition, etc. for achievements                    
in the field and notable accomplishments. 
 
 
ALL SUBMISSIONS MUST BE RECEIVED BY 12:00 P.M. Eastern Time on April 14, 2026. 
 
We are seeking Companies in the following Socio-Economic Categories under NAICS code 
541330– Engineering Services: Small Business (SB), Women Owned Small Business (WOSB), 
HubZone (HUBZ), 8(a), and Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSB).  
 
 
Offeror must state the following on the cover of the submission: 
 
• Worldwide Environmental Engineering Services Market Research 
• Identify the offeror’s business size status/social-economic category (Small Business (SB), Women 
Owned Small Business (WOSB), HubZone (HUBZ), 8(a), and Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned 
Small Businesses (SDVOSB) under NAICS code 541330 
 
Offeror’s SAM.gov registration Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) number 
Email submissions are authorized to be sent to the following FAN addresses: 
Primary: PakuwalS1@FAN.gov 
Alternate: BotkinLL@FAN.gov  
 
Please UPLOAD the submission (PDF files) to your Google Drive (FAN – Foreign Affairs 
Network or personal) AND share/send the submission from Google to the FAN.gov email 
addresses above and please give the CO’s EDIT permission for these files. The files will just be 
downloaded.  
  
In order to upload your proposals onto Google Drive and share, perform the following steps:   
1. Go to drive.google.com, log into your Google account with your username and password. 
If you do not have a Google account, you will need to create one.  
2. At the top left, click New then select File Upload or Folder Upload, and choose your file 
or folder you want to upload.   
3. Right click the file or folder you want to share and select SHARE.  
4. Enter these email address PakuwalS1@fan.gov and BotkinLL@fan.gov.  Make sure the 
EDITOR option selected.  
5. Click Send.  
  
Note: If you have a FAN (Foreign Affairs Network) account upload the proposals to the FAN 
Google Drive. If you do not have a FAN account, you can upload the proposals to a personal 
Google Drive then share. Sharing from your personal Google Drive account is acceptable. 
 
REQUESTS FOR CLARIFICATIONS must be submitted in writing to Samantha Pakuwal at 
PakuwalS1@fan.gov.

DRAFT STATEMENT OF WORK 
WEAPONS EFFECTS 
 
1.0 BACKGROUND 
The Naval Surface Warfare Center, Carderock Division (NSWCCD), Survivability and Weapons Effects Division 
(Code 66) is responsible for theoretical and applied research efforts to extend the understanding of the response of US 
Navy platforms to threat weapon engagements.  These engagements includ e underwater explosions (UNDEX) , air 
explosions (AIREX), and penetrating weapons  with modeling & simulation (M&S) of UNDEX and AIREX events 
being a major part of this mission that requires unique software applications and expertise. 
2.0 OBJECTIVE 
The contractor shall provide scientific and technical services with experts in UNDEX and AIREX analysis of undersea 
and surface vessels to develop and utilize  specialized software codes  that: 1) Aid in the selection of live fire  events 
and provide support to live fire test and evaluation programs ; 2) Simulate an underwater shock environment from a 
far field or near miss location; 3) Simulate the response of Navy platforms to UNDEX and AIREX for far field, near 
miss, contact, and internally detonating weapon attacks; 4) Check the integrity of a computational models; 5) Solve 
finite element model’s elastic-plastic response and reduced order engineering tools to UNDEX and AIREX events; 
and 6) Simulate a nuclear underwater shock environment or nuclear air blast environment from a far field location. 
The technical areas in this Task Order (TO) shall include comprehensive software engineering, development, and 
enhancement, finite element and reduced order model construction to include deactivation diagrams and quality 
assurance, numerical model  and algorithm  review and verification , software application training , design yard 
qualifications submittal review , data analysis, data science, and artificial intelligence / machine learning in order to 
support the vulnerability design processes for multiple Navy platforms. 
3.0 APPLICABLE DOCUMENTS 
• MIL-S-901D, MILITARY SPECIFICATION: SHOCK TESTS. H.I. (HIGH -IMPACT) SHIPBOARD 
MACHINERY, EQUIPMENT, AND SYSTEMS, REQUIREMENTS FOR (17 -MAR-1989) 
4.0 SCOPE OF WORK 
The contractor shall provide specialized scientific, engineering, and technical services in the field s of UNDEX shock 
qualification, UNDEX damage assessment, AIREX damage assessment , and ship survivability directed towards 
research, development, test , and evaluation (RDT&E) for various submarine and surface ship programs. The 
contractor shall provide all services, materials, facilities and equipment necessary to perform specific tasks within the 
following general tasking areas: 
4.1 Support the development, implementation, and transition of new technologies involving: testing 
strategies, transient shock analysis , and analytical methods that improve the ability of ship, 
components, systems, and personnel to resist the damaging effects of threat weapon attacks. Follow 
rigorous software development practices, including strict version control, continuous integration,  
use of code documentation generators to be specified in each Technical Instruction (TI) , unit and 
regression testing, code c overage assessments, and agile management for all tools developed or 
modified and share code repositories with Government personnel . Support developing, 
documenting, and execution strategies for verification and validation (V&V) of numerical 
simulations. Contractor support will range from limited assistance to government engineers on a 

 
task to autonomous execution of tasking with all results reported to the government as required by 
the TO and associated Contract Data Requirements List (CDRL) deliverables. Guidance and criteria 
for contractor support will be defined in each individual TI. (CDRL A001, A002, A003) 
4.2 Develop Software: 
4.2.1 Support in the development of software applications, code, modules, and plugins that will 
aide in the fields of UNDEX shock qualification, UNDEX damage assessment, AIREX 
weapons effects evaluation, and ship survivability analysis. 
4.3 Develop Training and Documentation Manuals for Software: 
4.3.1 Develop detailed software theory manuals, user’s manuals , and verification manuals 
including example problems. (CDRL A003) 
4.3.2 Develop and conduct software application training courses for any tools developed in Task 
Area 4.2 for Government personnel at NSWCCD and/or the contractor’s facility. (CDRL 
A003) 
4.3.3 Develop and conduct training related to shock qualification of shock test machines, 
platforms and vehicles including training on UNDEX theory and methods of analyzing 
ship and equipment responses to underwater explosion shock. (CDRL A002) 
4.4 Software Support: 
4.4.1 Provide technical support to users to fix issues that arise post software deployments. 
Software is to be defined in the individual TI and may include but not be limited to specific 
weapons effects software such as  but not limited to  ASAP, NESM, INSiTE, TDC, 
UERDTools, and SUBVALUE. Maintain logs of technical issues and resolutions and 
provide quarterly reports tracking resolutions. (CDRL A001, A003, A004) 
4.5 Develop Analytical Methods and Various types of Models: 
4.5.1 Develop defined finite element and reduced order representations of test articles, platforms, 
and vehicles including systems and systems deactivation diagrams that appropriately 
represent and capture their responses to a damaging event due to UNDEX, AIREX, and 
penetration mechanics, documenting all efforts. (CDRL A001, A002) 
4.5.2 Develop or support the creation of or modification to finite element and reduced order 
models of naval maritime platforms to include structure, components, systems, and system 
deactivation logic. 
4.5.3 Develop defined finite element models and reduced order representations of shock test 
machines, platforms and vehicles that appropriately represent and capture their responses 
to a shock event documenting all efforts. (CDRL A002) 
4.5.4 Develop and execute strategies for analyses and qualification of external volumes subjected 
to weapons loads. (CDRL A002) 
4.6 Execute Computer Model Simulations and Analyses: 
4.6.1 Conduct computational UNDEX analyses of Shock test machines, platforms and vehicles, 
documenting all efforts. (CDRL A002) 
4.6.2 Conduct computational UNDEX, AIREX, and penetration mechanics analyses of test 
articles, platforms, and vehicles, documenting all efforts. (CDRL A001, A002) 
4.6.3 Conduct and document data analyses and research available data and documentation on 
both physical measurements obtained from Shock Testing and computational data. (CDRL 
A002) 
4.6.4 Support the e valuation of  numerical models, reduced order models, and finite element 
models developed by other contract activities  or Government personnel, for accuracy and 
applicability to s hock design and qualification processes , hull integrity evaluations, and 
live fire test and evaluation assessment s including recoverability, documenting all efforts  
in technical reports . Applicable agreement and use rights to be provided in individual TI 
defining subject tasking. (CDRL A002) 

 
4.6.5 Conduct or support computational weapons effects assessments of threat weapons against 
naval maritime platforms in all aspects of platform vulnerability and recoverability 
documenting all efforts. (CDRL Item A002) 
4.7 Provide support to shock qualification efforts for shipboard equipment in accordance with ship 
specifications including generation of ship and equipment finite element models, review of technical 
analyses and reports, and performing finite element and reduced order model analyses. Finite 
element and reduced order models may be provided by the government or developed by the 
contractor. Status of finite element and reduced models will be defined in the individual TI(s). 
(CDRL A002) 
4.8 Support Testing and Material Procurement: 
4.8.1 Provide support to conduct weapons effects  testing or other Navy shock qualification 
testing and measurement efforts including test design, planning, and execution efforts. This 
includes both physical, on-site support, in addition to support from the contractor’s primary 
place of performance. 
4.8.2 Provide support and technical guidance to shock test and trials planning, documenting all 
efforts. (CDRL A002) 
4.8.3 Procure equipment, materials, and information as necessary  with consent from 
Government to provide technical support as defined in the TI(s). 
5.0 GOVERNMENT FURNISHED EQUIPMENT/PROPERTY/INFORMATION 
The Government shall furnish all necessary Government -Furnished Equipment (GFE) and/or Government -
Furnished Property (GFP). Specific GFE/GFP items will be detailed within each corresponding Task Instruction (TI). 
All requisite information pertaining to the GFE/GFP will be included in the associated TI. 
6.0 DATA REQUIREMENTS AND DELIVERABLES 
Data to be provided shall be prepared as specified in individual TIs and shall be distributed to the designated 
Technical Advisor (TA). In addition, a copy of the Monthly Status Report shall be provided to the Contracting 
Officer’s Representative (COR). Below is a table of CRLS for each Task Area.
  
CDRL Title Task Areas 
A001 Computer Software Product 4.1 – 4.5 
A002 Technical Report – Study Services 4.1 – 4.5 
A003 Software User Manual and Support 4.1 – 4.5 
A004 Presentation Materials 4.1 – 4.5 
A005 Meeting Minutes 4.1 – 4.5 
A006 Contracting Officer’s Management Report 4.1 – 4.5 
A007 Software License Requirements List 4.1 – 4.5 
 
7.0 SECURITY REQUIREMENTS 

 
Security will be in accordance with the terms and conditions cited in the DD Form 254, in Section J, of the TO.  The 
maximum level of security classification required for the work under this contract is SECRET; the classification of 
work under this contract will be specified in the individual TI. When tasking is at the CUI level, un-cleared US 
persons may work on the tasking in accordance with relevant security requirements  of the specific TI. 
7.1 Contractor shall be able to send and retrieve classified information  and electronic files to/from the 
government upon request using the Secret Internet Protocol Router Network (SIPRNET), or via 
FEDEX, or by contractor courier. The maximum duration from the time of request to time of 
classified information receipt or retrieval shall be no more than 48 hours. 
7.2 Non-Disclosure   
The Contractor shall not disclose any information provided by the Government or developed or 
relating to the items to be delivered and services to be performed without the PCO’s prior approval.  
All data provided to the Contractor shall be protected from t he public.  Dissemination or public 
disclosure includes permitting access to such information by foreign nationals or by any other person 
or entity, publication of technical or scientific papers, advertising, or any other proposed public 
release.  The Cont ractor shall physically protect such information to prevent access by any 
unauthorized person or entity. 
7.3 Performance in Government Facilities   
The Contractor shall comply with the requirements of local instructions regarding performance in 
Government facilities.  All persons engaged in work while on Government property shall be subject 
to search of their persons (no bodily search) and vehicles at  any time by the Government, and shall 
report any known or suspected security violations to the appropriate Security Department.  
Assignment, transfer, and reassignment of Contractor personnel shall be at the discretion of the 
Contractor.  However, when the Government directs, the Contractor shall remove from contract 
performance any person who endangers life, property, or national security through improper 
conduct.  All Contractor personnel engaged in work while on Government property shall be subject 
to the DoD Standards of Conduct. 
7.4 Information Security and Computer System Usage 
Computer Usage: In accordance with U.S. Navy policy, any personnel, including the Contractor, 
who utilizes DoD-owned systems, shall assume responsibility for adherence to restrictions regarding 
internet and e-mail usage. Navy policy prohibits racist, sexis t, threatening, pornographic, personal 
business, subversive or politically partisan communications.  All personnel, including the 
Contractor, are accountable and must act accordingly.  
7.5 System Monitoring: DoD computer systems are monitored to ensure that the use is authorized, to 
facilitate protection against unauthorized access, and to verify security procedures, survivability and 
operational security.  During monitoring, information may be examined, recorded, copied, and used 
for authorized purposes.  All information, including personal information, placed on or sent over a 
DoD system may be monitored.  Use of a DoD system constitutes consent to monitoring.  
Unauthorized use may result in criminal prosecution.  Evidence of unauthorized use collected during 
monitoring may be used as a basis for recommended administrative, criminal or adverse action.  
7.6 Electronic Spillages 
7.6.1 General: Electronic spillages (ES) are unacceptable and pose a risk to national security.  
An ES is defined as classified data placed on an information system (IS), media or hardcopy 
document possessing insufficient security controls to protect the data at  the required 
classification level, thus posing a risk to national security (e.g., Sensitive Compartmented 
Information (SCI) onto collateral, Secret onto Unclassified).  The Contractor's performance 
as it relates to ES will be evaluated by the Government.  Electronic spillage reflects on the 
overall security posture of the Government and a lack of attention to detail with regard to 
the handling of classified information of IS security discipline.  If a Contractor is 

 
determined to be responsible for an ES, all direct and indirect costs incurred by the 
Government for ES remediation will be charged to the Contractor. The incident will be 
reflected in the Contractor’s performance rating. 
7.6.2 Spillage Responsibilities: Local command security will continue to be responsible for the 
corrective action plan in accordance with the security guidance reflected on the DD Form 
254. Command security will identify the Contractor facility and contract number associated 
with all ES during the investigation indicating Contractor support. Command security will 
notify the contracts division with the Contractor facility name and contract number, 
incident specifics and associated costs for cleanup.  The PCO will be responsible for 
working with the Contractor to capture the costs incurred during the spillage clean up.  The 
Contractor is also responsible for taking Cybersecurity Awareness training annually via its 
Facility Security Officer (FSO) as part of the mandatory training requirements.  If an ES

FA300226R0015 
Request for Information (RFI)/Sources Sought (SS) 
 
Strategic Talent & Assessment Research (STAR) Support  
 
1.0 DISCLAIMER 
 
This Request for Information (RFI)/Sources Sought (SS) seeks information regarding availability and 
capability of all qualiﬁed small business ﬁrms to perform a potential requirement. Responses received 
will be used for acquisition strategic decision-making purposes only and will not be disclosed outside this 
agency. This announcement is for informational purposes only. The information obtained may be used 
for acquisition planning purposes. This announcement does not constitute an Invitation for Bids, 
Request for Proposals, or a Request for Quotations, and is not to be construed as a commitment by the 
Government to issue a contract or otherwise pay for the information solicited. The Government does 
not intend to award a contract on the basis of this notice. Companies responding to this RFI/SS notice 
are advised that participation does not ensure involvement in any future solicitation or contract award. 
No proposals are being requested or accepted under this notice, and this announcement shall not be 
construed as a commitment by the Government to issue a solicitation or to ultimately award a contract, 
nor does this synopsis restrict the Government to a particular acquisition approach. Contact with 
Government personnel, other than those speciﬁed in this RFI/SS, by interested ﬁrms or their employees 
regarding this requirement is not permitted. The Government will not pay for any information submitted 
in response to this announcement. Any costs associated with providing information to either this notice 
or any follow-up information requests shall not be reimbursed. Costs incurred as a result of this 
announcement shall be borne solely by the respondent and shall not be payable by the Government.  
 
2.0 DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENT 
 
2.1. The 338th Enterprise Sourcing Squadron (ESS), at Joint Base San Antonio (JBSA) – Randolph, Texas 
(TX), is seeking information concerning the availability of technically capable small business ﬁrms to 
provide non-personal services for the Air Force Personnel Center (AFPC)/ Strategic Research & 
Assessment Branch (DSYX), located at JBSA-Randolph TX. The Headquarters, United States Air Force, 
Director of Air Force Military Force Management Policy, AF/A1P, Accession and Training Division (A1PT) 
is responsible for the Air Force Examining Activities Program, which supports the STAR Program 
established in DAFMAN 36-2664. The STAR mission is to develop assessments and screening processes 
to assess recruit and Airmen knowledge, skills, abilities, and potential, and then optimally match 
personnel to jobs that optimize their abilities and potential to support optimal warﬁghting mission 
capability. The purpose of the program is to apply scientiﬁc evidence-based practices to optimize human 
capital management, mission capability, readiness, reduce attrition, and increase retention by improved 
selection, classiﬁcation, and utilization assessment. The Service Provider (SP) shall provide a broad set of 
technical skills critical to the eﬀectiveness of STAR, including psychometric expertise, programming, 
database management, research design, data analysis, assessment development, aviation psychology, 
and direct software and system engineering. The SP shall be expected to provide technically qualiﬁed 
employees and meet all the requirements and responsibilities listed in the attached draft Performance 
Work Statement (PWS) (Attachment 1). 
 
2.2. For purposes of this RFI/SS Notice, the main North American Industry Classiﬁcation System (NAICS) 
code for the requirement will be 541715 Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and 
Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology), Size Standard: 1,000 employees.  
 

FA300226R0015 
3.0 SMALL BUSINESS INFORMATION  
 
3.1 The Government reserves the right to determine whether a Small Business (SB) set-aside is 
appropriate for this acquisition based on responses to this notice. In order to support a Government SB 
set-aside determination, interested SB concerns must provide suﬃcient written information to indicate 
their capability to successfully perform and manage all the requirements listed in the attached draft 
PWS (Attachment 1). 
 
3.2 Identify business type (Small Business (SB), Small Disadvantaged Business (SDB), 8(A)-Certified Small 
Disadvantaged Business (8a), Hubzone Small Business (HUBZone), Woman-Owned Small Business 
(WOSB), Veteran-Owned Small Business (VOSB), Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business 
(SDVOSB)) based upon NAICS Code 541715, Size Standard 1,000 employees. 
 
4.0 ACQUISITION INFORMATION 
 
4.1 The Government is contemplating an Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract with a 5-
year ordering period. Information contained in this RFI/SS is subject to change. The attached draft PWS 
document is subject to change in any resultant solicitation. 
 
5.0 RESPONSE SUBMISSION  
 
5.1 All interested parties who believe they can meet all aspects of the requirements are invited to 
complete the attached Contractor Capability Survey (see Attachment 2) describing their capability and 
qualiﬁcations to provide the required support services. The purpose of using the survey format, in lieu of 
a free format, is to obtain pertinent and uniformed information from all interested ﬁrms. Interested 
ﬁrms must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) to be eligible for payment from 
any Department of Defense activity. Information on registration and annual conﬁrmation requirements 
may be obtained at www.SAM.gov.   
 
5.2. To be considered by the Government, interested parties must email their response and completed 
Contractor Capability Survey (Attachment 2) to the Point of Contact identified below no later than 4:00 
PM, Central Daylight Time (CDT) on 10 Apr 2026.  
 
5.3. Information contained in this RFI/Sources Sought is subject to change. It is the responsibility of 
interested parties to check SAM.gov regularly for any changes or updates. The Government is under no 
obligation to consider information received after the due date as part of the formal market research for 
this acquisition.  
 
5.4. Responses to this notice and/or questions shall be submitted via email to Contract Specialist: 
Melissa Gonzalez at melissa.gonzalez.6@us.af.mil.

running, and fixing systems, directly responsible for operational output. Services include 
providing a broad set of technical skills critical to the effectiveness of STAR, including 
psychometric expertise, programming/database management, research design, data analysis, 
assessment development, aviation psychology, and direct software and system engineering. The 
Contractor shall provide technically qualified employees to meet the stated objectives and 
accomplish the work required under this PWS. Specific requirements will be identified by the 
issuance of individual Task Orders (TOs). 
 
1.2 Background. The Headquarters, United States Air Force, Director of Air Force Military 
Force Management Policy, AF/A1P, Accession and Training Division (A1PT) is responsible for 
the Air Force Examining Activities Program, which supports the STAR established in DAFMAN 
36-2664. The STAR mission is to develop assessments and screening processes to assess recruit 
and Airmen knowledge, skills, abilities, and potential, and then optimally match personnel to 
jobs that optimize their abilities and potential to support optimal warfighting mission capability. 
The program is supported by personnel at Air Staff, the Air Force Personnel Center (AFPC), and 
Air Education and Training Command (AETC). The purpose of the program is to apply scientific

assessment. The program, which includes a staff of technically qualified researchers and 
analysts, requires direct technical execution via contract for a series of specialized technical 
skills either not possessed by the staff or deemed inefficient for the staff to support with their 
skillsets. This contract supports the DoW's emphasis on direct technical execution from 
contractors.

documents that the contractor and contractor subs shall comply with and reference in the

will require written Government approval from the CO prior to use. This list will be confirmed

This is a Sources Sought notice is being issued for market research purposes to

requirement 
 
NO SOLICITATION IS AVAILABLE 
 
Requests for a solicitation will go unanswered. No award will be made from this Notice. 
Responses will be used to determine potential acquisition strategies, understand current 
market capabilities, and to gain knowledge of potential sources. 
 
GENERAL SCOPE 
 
The United States Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Southwestern Middle East 
District (SWM) anticipates a potential requirement for a seven-year Single Award Task 
Order Contract (SATOC) to support the pre-design activities and 100% design solution 
supporting the development of a secure compound that is ICD-705 compliant at Al 
Udeid Air Base, Qatar.  These requirements stem from the Space Forces Central 
Command (SPACECENT) and the Al Udeid Air Base 2040 Strategic Master Plan. 
 
This project is anticipated to include the following:  
 
1. Produce a Planning Charrette Report II (PCR II), including a DD Form 1391. 
 
2. Geotechnical survey. 
 
3. Plan and design a Secure Administrative Headquarters building (CATCODE 141446, 
Combat Center Building). 
 
4. Ancillary supporting facilities to include, but not limited to, secure warehouse facility, 
general purpose storage, access control and guard house complex, antennae yard 
and shelter building, multiple unit buildings, secure perimeter fencing, Intrusion 
Detection System (IDS) and Closed Circuit Television surveillance of the perimeter 
and compound. 
 
5. All site and building utility services to include, but not limited to, services for potable 
water, non-potable water/fire water, electrical distribution, surface water 
management, sanitary sewer, lift stations, pump systems, secure and unclassified 
communication network, substations, generators, fueling operations, and chilled 
water. 
 
6. All site work to include, but not limited to, any applicable demolition, site preparation 
and grading, vehicle circulation network (paved and gravel), military and personal 

vehicle parking (paved and gravel), sunshades, concrete pads, pedestrian 
circulation, coordinated shelter for base circulation services, curb, gutter, sidewalks, 
ancillary hardscapes and xeriscaping.   
 
7. It is anticipated any other supporting work necessary to make a complete and usable 
facility to include any necessary element not listed herein will also be included. 
 
The potential requirement may result in a SATOC solicitation in approximately October 
2027. If solicited the Government intends to award the anticipated requirement by 
approximately June 2028. 
 
The North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code for the potential 
requirement is anticipated to be 541330 Engineering Services. 
 
Companies with the professional qualifications, specialized expertise, technical 
competence, and workload capacity to complete the work described above are invited 
to provide capability statements. 
 
CAPABILITY STATEMENT 
 
Please complete the questionnaire at https://forms.osi.apps.mil/r/kmR3vNMHup by 8 
April 2026 11:59 Eastern Time. 
 
Responses will not be considered an offer, proposal, or bid for any solicitation that may 
result from this Notice. Moreover, responses will not restrict the Government to an 
acquisition approach. This Notice is for information and planning purposes only. 
Respondents will not be notified of the results of any review conducted of the capability 
statements received. 
 
Questions may be sent by e-mail to the Contract Specialist, Tracy Gusukuma at 
tracy.m.gusukuma@usace.army.mil. 
 
Please include, ‘MARKET RESEARCH Space Campus’ in the e-mail subject line.

P
erformance Work Statement  
Dynamic Frequency Comb Applications Support 
Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) 
Re
questing Laboratory / Division / Group: 
C
ommunications Technology Laboratory 
Spectrum Research and Technology Division 
Fiber Sources and Applications, (675.02) 
I.
BACKGROUND:
T
he Fiber Sources and Applications Group (675.02), at the National Institute of Standards and Technology
(NIST) Boulder Colorado campus, develops novel applications of frequency combs for optical time transfer,
spectroscopy and ranging.  Of particular relevance here, this group has developed frequency comb-based
optical two-way time-frequency transfer (O-TWTFT) that can allow frequency comparisons and time
synchronization across a distributed network of clocks.  They have also developed dual-comb spectroscopy
for open-path atmospheric sensing. This work requires tight collaboration between laser science and digital
control communities.
II.
PURPOSE:
F
requency comb-based applications of time-transfer and dual-comb spectroscopy require advanced control
algorithms and real-time processing. The objective of this Performance Work Statement (PWS) is to continue
advancement of both systems by exploring the use of real-time phase/timing control of the frequency comb
pulse train output. The work will develop the necessary digital-control of the phase/timing of the frequency
comb output, contribute to the algorithm modifications and system modifications for both time-transfer and
dual-comb spectroscopy to exploit this new capability, and then implement the new algorithms by modifying
the existing NIST real-time digital signal processing systems accordingly.
T
his work will require the tight integration of FPGA based digital control systems with a number of laser
frequency comb platforms. The goal is to build upon existing infrastructure in comb control including phase
locking algorithms and FPGA platforms. Algorithm development by the contract will be performed with high
level guidance only and the contractor will need to provide technical solutions to a range of scientific
problems. Strong understanding of femtosecond laser operation, free-space optical time transfer and phase
locking will be required.
T
he current state-of-the-art for this work can be found in the following publications
https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-022-05225-8 and
https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-023-06032-5
Draft

 
 
 
Figure 1:  Existing real-time digital signal processor hardware for the optical time transfer.   
The digital signal processor for the dual-comb spectroscopy is similar to this design but uses a 
different FPGA. The digital control system for the frequency combs is located at 
https://www.nist.gov/services-resources/software/fpga-based-digital-control-box-phase-
stabilization-frequency-comb.   
 
Place of Performance:  
 
The development work shall be completed at the Contractor’s facility. Any required onsite testing and 
meetings will be conducted at the NIST, Boulder, CO campus, specifically Bldg. 1 (i.e., the Radio bldg.) and 
Bldg. 81 (i.e., the Precision Measurement’s Lab). Specific travel requirements based on required tasks will 
be identified under the respective task order. The Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR) and/or Subject 
Matter Expert (SME) may direct the flow of technical matters while on the Boulder campus. 
 
Regular Business Hours: 
 
Regular business hours are Monday through Friday, 8:00 am to 5:00 pm Local Time, excluding Federal 
holidays and NIST closures. 
 
Period of Performance/Delivery Date: 
 
Base Period 1 Year 
Option Period 1 1 Year  
Option Period 2 1 Year 
Draft

 
 
Option Period 3 1 Year 
Option Period 4 1 Year 
 
III. SPECIFIC REQUIREMENTS: 
 
1. The following are the types of services that may be procured via Task Orders: 
 
a. Task 1 - Algorithms and digital implementation for dynamic, arbitrary real-time control of the comb 
phase/time output 
 
NIST frequency combs are controlled by a field-programmable gate array (FPGA) controller. 
Through real-time analysis and feedback to the comb, the controller is able to adjust the absolute 
timing of the comb pulses in an arbitrary fashion, limited only by the comb actuator. While the basic 
comb control has been shown, the Contractor shall build on existing technology to develop advanced 
algorithms to generate the maximum dynamic flexibility in the comb phase/timing control. The 
Contractor shall develop and implement algorithms necessary in VHDL/Verilog code for the FPGA. 
The Contractor shall modify this comb control to implement the applications. 
 
Task 1.1 - Develop next generation firmware for maximum dynamic control of the frequency 
comb pulse train phase/timing to accommodate platform motion 
 
The contractor will refine existing control firmware and algorithms to support new frequency 
comb platforms and actuator designs as well as scan patterns that will be required to 
accommodate platform motion and atmospheric induced timing noise in optical time transfer 
applications as well as novel scan petters for spectroscopy. The firmware on the existing NIST 
FPGA comb controller shall be updated, tested and optimized for maximum dynamic control 
allowing the slewing of control signals to compensate doppler shifts. 
 
Task 1.2 - Dynamic and coherent CW laser scanning 
 
The contractor will propose and develop algorithms to maintain tight phase lock between a 
frequency comb and a CW laser while that laser is swept to match the expected Doppler shift 
profile associated with a reflection off of a LEO satellite. Sweep will match both the expected 
frequency shift range and slew rate while maintaining less than 0.1 rad of residual phase noise on 
the CW laser even in the presence of comb crossings.  
 
Task 1.3 - Variable logging and system start up 
 
Contractor will facilitate software and firmware development to ensure that critical measurement 
variables such a repetition rate are implemented in the control software. Additionally, the 
contractor will contribute to the development of algorithms to simplify cold start operations. 
Contractor should propose a list of logged frequency comb parameters that will be necessary to 
recover all required time shifts. Logging and cold start algorithms will be updated with each 
iteration of the systems design on one year cadence. 
 
b. Task 2 - Long-range Optical Time Transfer through phase-controlled combs 
 
Research has shown that Optical Time Transfer could operate at much lower received powers, and 
therefore longer range, if it were possible to dynamically control the phase of the frequency combs 
(see Task 1). The Contractor shall work with NIST to advance current algorithms to fully develop this 
Draft

 
 
phase-control approach of the combs for a long-range mode of operation in the presence of platform 
motion. This task shall include contributions to overall system design, algorithm development, 
implementation in the existing NIST real-time digital signal processor through firmware 
modifications to both the FPGA and digital signal processor, field tests, and data analysis, as well as 
porting existing code bases to new FPGA platforms as old equipment becomes unavailable. This 
process shall involve the Contractor participating in at least two field tests of the system for a total 
duration of two months. 
 
Task 2.1 - System design and algorithm development for platform motion 
 
The Contractor shall develop tracking oscillator algorithms that can deal with the substantial 
platform motion expected when transferring femtosecond timing from ground to a LEO satellite. 
Work will mix algorithms for steering the frequency combs to ensure the pulses reflected off the 
satellite are always within 10 fs of the pulse center of the pulses from the local tracking oscillator 
comb. Additionally, the contractor should develop algorithms to ensure that the heterodyne beat 
between the Doppler-shifted return frequency comb and the tracking oscillator comb is well 
controlled enough to allow narrow filtering of return signals for improved signal in the presence 
of high link loss. Contractor should propose viable solutions for measuring and compensating for 
these Doppler shifts.   
 
Task 2.2 - Implementation of Long-range Optical Time Transfer 
 
The Contractor shall implement the algorithms by making modifications to the VHDL and C++ 
code in the existing real-time digital signal processor hardware for the optical time transfer. The 
Contractor shall also develop the Python code for the associated modifications to the GUI 
interfaces. The Contractor will also provide for the porting of existing capabilities to newer 
hardware platforms. 
 
Task 2.3 - SLR station field tests and data analysis  
 
The Contractor shall participate in three rounds of field tests of the optical time transfer system at 
an SLR station. Field tests are still being scheduled but will occur on a roughly 18-month 
cadence starting in September 2026. The Contractor shall perform data analysis and 
documentation of the results of the field tests and will work with the team to iterate on the 
control and Doppler correction algorithms to maintain femtosecond level time-transfer 
performance. The data analysis shall generate level 2 processed data directly from the raw data 
files saved by the real-time digital signal processor. The data analysis shall be completed in 
Matlab and the Matlab code library supplied to NIST with sufficient documentation to reproduce 
the analysis in another language such as Python.   
 
Task 2.4 - SLR Optical Communication channel  
 
The Contractor shall specify hardware, presumably an FPGA or RFSoC, and build a digital 
backbone for an optical communication channel on this platform. In the first iteration the digital 
backbone will generate a data stream at least 10 MB/s that will be written onto a cw laser with an 
EOM or used to directly amplitude modulate a diode laser. The second iteration will incorporate 
PRBS streams (or similar) that can be used for course ganging and timing measurements 
between nodes. A third iteration will push data rates up to 1 GB/s 
 
Task 2.5 - Optical Terminal Tracking Control  
Draft

 
 
 
The Contractor shall develop robust software solutions to interface with existing optical terminal 
hardware and will enable active tip tilt correction for the free space link at >100 Hz feedback 
bandwidths. Error readout in this is done with a SUI 320CSX camera and which will record the 
center of mass of the incoming beam and will feed a +/-2V control signal for X and Y degrees of 
freedom to either a fast-steering mirror or a galvo mirror pair. Camera readout and center of 
mass processing as well as the generation of the control signal should be done on a 
microcontroller or the contractor’s choosing. 
 
c.  Task 3 - Phase-stepped dual-comb  
 
Dual-comb and related measurement techniques can operate with a much higher signal-to-noise ratio 
by dynamically controlling the phase of the frequency combs (see Task 1). The Contractor shall work 
with NIST to exploit this new capability by consulting on advanced algorithms and system design. 
The algorithms shall be capable of real-time operation on existing NIST digital processors. The 
system design shall be documented to the component level with a preference for standard components 
already in use by NIST. The Contractor shall modify the NIST FPGA comb controller system to 
interface with the dual-comb system both for control and data acquisition. The Contractor shall 
facilitate the testing of the system and testing with a focal plane array through algorithm development 
and firmware/software modifications. This process shall involve the Contractor participating in at 
least one lab experiment. 
 
 Task 3.1 Algorithms and system design for phase- stepped dual-comb spectroscopy 
 
The Contractor shall develop the system design and algorithms for phase-stepped dual-comb 
spectroscopy based on the results of Task 1. 
  
 Task 3.2 Implementation and testing 
 
The Contractor shall assist with the implementation of the necessary software/firmware changes 
in the existing NIST FPGA comb controller and dual-comb acquisition system for phase-stepped 
dual-comb spectroscopy. 
   
For code developed under Tasks 1 through 3, the following specifications shall be met:  
 
1. All code shall be covered with unit tests to at least 95% to verify functionality and to guard against 
regressions from future refactoring, extension, and/or bug fixes. 
 
2. All code shall be supplemented by software test benches that enable simulation and unit testing 
without the need for hardware. Testing code may be written in Matlab or Python. 
 
3. All code shall be documented by appropriate comments and naming conventions (in addition to Task 2 
above.) 
 
4. Proprietary or closed-source software, including FPGA IP cores, shall not be used unless the 
Contractor has previously verified NIST already owns such IP cores.   
 
5. Code shall be organized to be reviewed by the Government on a regular basis, as specified in the 
deliverable table (Section IV).  The results of the reviews are to be integrated into successive 
development steps. 
Draft

 
 
 
6. This code shall be compatible with the existing firmware and custom NIST real-time processor for 
optical two-way time transfer. 
 
7. All project software being developed shall be maintained in a suitable repository (e.g., GitHub) to 
allow Government to monitor development progress and provide rapid feedback when changes are 
needed. 
 
8. The documentation shall include a description of the basic algorithms and their implementation in the 
DSP or FPGA. The documentation shall also include a basic mathematical description of the algorithm 
appropriate for publication in a scientific journal. 
 
The code shall be implemented on the custom NIST real-time processor shown in Figure 1.  
 
III. GENERAL REQUIREMENTS 
 
1. Government Responsibilities: 
 
Government will provide access to the time transfer systems during development cycles. Because of the 
cost of this access, access time will be limited to 2 weeks per year. Early-stage development should be 
done on a vendor owned test system and implemented on the government system only after significant 
testing has been done. 
 
2. Government Furnished Property  
 
All property, data and information provided by the Government in the performance of this task remains

termination of this requirement. Likewise, all deliverables generated under this requirement remain the 
property of the Government.

31 March 2026 
 
Note: This questionnaire/survey is for obtaining information only. Companies are 
encouraged to provide responses to this questionnaire but are advised that their 
participation is voluntary only.  Contractors responding to this Request for Information 
(RFI) are placed on notice that participation in this survey does not ensure participation in 
future solicitations or contract awards.  The government will not reimburse participants 
for any expenses associated with their participation in this survey. 
 
INSTRUCTIONS: 
 
1. Attached is the draft PWS for the F-15 Engineering Services effort requirement and a 
contractor capability survey, which allows you to provide your company’s capability. 
2. If, after reviewing these documents, you desire to participate in the market research, you 
should provide documentation that supports your company’s capability in meeting these

4. Questions relative to this market survey should be addressed to Tyler Law, 
tyler.law.4@us.af.mil.  
  

 
 
 
 
Requirements Description 
Silver Bullets (SB) 
 
 
PURPOSE/DESCRIPTION 
 
       The Government is conducting market research to identify potential sources that possess the 
expertise, capabilities, and experience to meet qualification requirements for the sustainment of 
all F-15 engineering services areas.  All engineering tasks issued within the period of performance 
are intended to be short-term projects, estimated at typically less than 1000 hours. 
The projected period of performance for this engineering service is five-years (basic plus 4 
option years) and will continue through FY32.   
These services have been performed sole source by Boeing for roughly 25 years, at which 
point it was with McDonnell Douglas which merged with Boeing in 1997. Over the past several 
years, F-15 Engineering has used a FFP pricing arrangement, with a most recent 12 month period 
of performance. Reports are delivered as tasks are completed via e m a i l  a n d  Boeing’s BPN 
website. Thorough technical, price and/or cost analyses have been and will be performed as 
necessary by the F-15 System Program Office (SPO), Defense Contract Audit Agency (DCAA) 
and/or the Defense Contract Management Agency (DCMA). 
 
A complete description of work is provided in the attached draft Performance-Work-
Statement (PWS): Silver Bullet (SB) Requirements.

support for the following F-15 aircraft fleets:  United States Air Force (USAF), Air National

(RSAF), and Israeli Air Force (IAF), Republic of Korea Air Force, Republic of Singapore Air 
Force, and Japan Air Self Defense Force. These services include testing, simulation, problem 
analysis, training, parts substitution analysis, risk assessments, inspection advisories and 
corrective actions to resolve field operational problems and improvement requirements.

the Contractor which exceeds the technical capabilities of the F-15 System Program Office 
(SPO). The studies performed under this program prevent potential mishaps thus preserving the 
F-15 fleet.

unpredictable work environment. Requirements for various unique scenarios arise which require 
testing, simulation, problem analysis, training, parts substitution, analysis, risk assessment,

requirements.
