REQUEST FOR INFORMATION 
Product Support Business Case Analysis (BCA) for USAF E-7A Aircraft 
10 March 2026 
1.0 Description 
1.1 The United States Air Force E-7A Program Office (AFLCMC/WIW), is seeking information 
from interested companies with the ability to perform a comprehensive Product Support Business 
Case Analysis (BCA) for the E-7A aircraft fleet.  
• Notice Type: Request for Information (RFI) 
• Reference Number: RFI-E7A-BCA-2026 
• Posting Date: 10 March 2026 
• Response Due Date: 11 May 2026, 5:00 PM (EST) 
• Agency: Department of the Air Force (DAF) 
• Office: E-7A System Program Office (SPO) 
• NAICS Codes: 
541611 - Administrative Management and General Management Consulting Services 
541330 - Engineering Services 
1.2 THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) ONLY . This RFI is issued solely for 
information and planning purposes; it does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or a 
promise to issue an RFP in the future. This RFI does not commit the Government to contract for 
any supply or service whatsoever. Further, the Air Force is not at this time seeking proposals and 
will not accept unsolicited proposals. The U.S. Government will not pay for any information or 
administrative costs incurred in response to this RFI. Not responding to this RFI does not 
preclude participation in any future RFP, if any is issued. 
2.0 Background 
The Department of the Air Force is acquiring the E-7A aircraft to replace a portion of the E-3 
Sentry Airborne Warning and Control System (AWACS) fleet. The E-7A will provide critical 
airborne early warning, surveillance, and battle management capabilities. To ensure optimal fleet 
readiness and long-term affordability, the E-3/E-7A SPO is seeking to identify sources capable of 
performing a comprehensive Product Support Business Case Analysis (BCA). 
The objective of this BCA is to identify the most effective and efficient product support strategy 
for the E-7A fleet throughout its planned life cycle. The PS-BCA will need to accommodate a 

fleet size of at least two but possibly up to twenty-six aircraft. The analysis will inform the Air 
Force’s decision-making process for structuring the E-7A’s sustainment enterprise. 
3.0 Scope of the Business Case Analysis (BCA) 
The Government is seeking a comprehensive BCA that analyzes the costs, benefits, and risks of 
different product support strategies for the E-7A aircraft. The analysis must address sustainment 
at both the field level (organizational and intermediate maintenance) and depot level. 
The BCA must, at a minimum, analyze the following three product support alternatives: 
Alternative Field-Level 
Sustainment 
Depot-Level 
Maintenance 
Description 
Alternative 1 Organic Organic All maintenance, supply, and 
support functions performed by 
Government personnel and 
facilities.  
Alternative 2 Hybrid Contractor A single prime contractor is 
responsible for supporting 
Active-Duty technicians with all 
aspects of field 
and the single prime 
contractor is responsible for all 
aspects of depot sustainment 
(i.e., Contractor Logistics 
Support - CLS).  
Alternative 3 Hybrid-to-Organic Hybrid-to-Organic Public-Private Partnership. A 
single prime contractor is 
responsible for supporting 
Active-Duty technicians with all 
aspects of field and the single 
prime contractor is responsible 
for all aspects of depot 
sustainment utilizing 
only government buildings and 
government 
employees (i.e. providing ~50% 
of manpower, ~75% of tools and 
test equipment, supply and 
logistics support). Additionally, 
recommend timeline for support 
to be phased out and transitioned 
to alternative 1 full-organic.  
 

The final BCA report shall be developed in accordance with the latest version of the DoD 
Product Support BCA Guidebook and DoDI 5000.91, Product Support Management for the 
Adaptive Acquisition Framework, DAFI63-101/20-101 - Integrated Life Cycle Management. 
Additionally, information and/or recommendations that utilize government equipment must 
comply with DAFMAN 23-119 - Government Furnished Property guidance. 
The analysis for each alternative must include a detailed Life-Cycle Cost (LCC) estimate, a 
qualitative and quantitative benefit analysis against Key Performance Parameters (KPPs) like 
Materiel Availability, and a thorough risk and sensitivity analysis.   
4.0 Requested Information 
4.1 Interested parties are requested to submit a capabilities statement that addresses the following 
areas. Please limit your response to no more than 15 pages. 
4.1.1 Corporate Experience:  
• Provide a brief company overview, including CAGE code, business size, and 
socioeconomic status under the referenced NAICS codes.  
• Describe your company's experience in conducting Product Support BCAs for 
major DoD weapon systems, particularly for large airframes or complex 
Command, Control, Communications, Computers, Intelligence, Surveillance and 
Reconnaissance (C4ISR) systems. Please provide at least two specific examples 
from the past five years.  
• Detail your experience with analyzing and modeling different sustainment 
strategies, including organic, CLS, and hybrid/PBL constructs.  
4.1.2 Technical Approach & Capabilities:  
• Outline your proposed methodology for developing the E-7A BCA, specifically 
addressing how you would structure the analysis of the three required 
alternatives.  
• Describe the analytical tools, cost models, and data sources you would employ to 
conduct the LCC, risk, and benefit analyses.  
• Describe your corporate capabilities for accessing and analyzing technical data, 
maintenance records, and supply chain information for a military weapon system.  
• Respondents should be able to provide information for fleet size ranging from two 
to twenty-six aircraft. 
4.1.3 Personnel Qualifications:  
• Describe the qualifications, certifications, and experience of the key personnel 
who would be assigned to this project (e.g., Program Manager, Lead Analyst). Do 
not provide resumes.  

4.1.4 Cost and Schedule:  
• Provide a Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) cost estimate to complete the BCA 
as described in Section 3.  
• Provide an estimated timeline for completion of the BCA from the date of 
contract award.  
4.1.5 Government Requirements:  
• Identify any information required from the government to complete BCA such 
as phased inspection requirements, calendar date and/or flight hour-based 
maintenance requirements, facilities, tools, test equipment, 
and/or trained personnel.  
 
5.0 Submission Instructions 
5.1 Submissions are due no later than the response date and time specified in Section 1.0.  
5.2 Submissions shall be in Microsoft Word or Adobe PDF format and sent 
electronically. Submissions are due no later than 11 May 2026, 5:00 PM EST and submitted 
via e-mail only to richard.axtell.2@us.af.mil gregory.mackessy.1@us.af.mil  
5.3 The subject line of the email shall read: "Response to RFI-E7A-BCA-2026 - [Your Company 
Name]". 
5.4 Proprietary information, if any, should be clearly marked. To aid the Government, please 
segregate proprietary information. 
6.0 Industry Discussions  
E-7A Wedgetail representatives may or may not choose to meet with potential offerors. Such 
discussions would only be intended to get further clarification of a respondent’s ability to 
perform the Product Support BCA.  
7.0 Questions  
Questions regarding this announcement shall be submitted in writing by email to the Contracting 
POCs (richard.axtell.2@us.af.mil and gregory.mackessy.1@us.af.mil). Verbal questions will 
NOT be accepted. Questions will be answered by email; accordingly, questions shall NOT 
contain proprietary or classified information. The Government does not guarantee that questions 
received after 11 May 2026 will be answered. 
 
 
 
 

8.0 Summary  
This RFI is issued solely to identify sources and information that can aid in the completion of a 
Product Support BCA. The information provided in the RFI is subject to change and is not 
binding on the Government. The Air Force has not made a commitment to procure any of the 
items discussed, and release of this RFI should not be construed as such a commitment or as 
authorization to incur cost for which reimbursement would be required or sought. All 
submissions become Government property and will not be returned.

Remaining Items – Technical Assistance and Coordination Outcomes Database

PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT (PWS)

BACKGROUND

The three programs within the existing Remaining Items (RI) Technical Assistance and Coordination Outcomes (TACO) database (RI-TACOd) are the National Flood Risk Management Program (NFRMP), Floodplain Management Services (FPMS), and the Planning Assistance to States (PAS) programs. The RI-TACOd was developed in 2022 and directly supports these three programs.  The tool serves as the primary mechanism to gather and record project/study proposals for the NFRMP, FPMS, and PAS programs. This includes collecting proposals, ranking/prioritizing for eligibility, selecting for funding, tracking and reporting progress, and project closeout.  The database resides within the Amazon Web Services (AWS) GOV cloud, which is managed by USACE’s Civil Works Business Intelligence (CWBI) program.  RI-TACOd uses AWS cloud-native tools and open-source technical solutions.  The AWS tools and scripts provide users with the means to submit their information, and program managers with the ability to manage and evaluate the process throughout its lifecycle.  With RI-TACOd already deployed, USACE has identified operation and maintenance (O&M) tasks that are necessary for the database to continue to thrive, as well as new development tasks to help advance the tool to its next phase of existence. 

SCOPE

This task order is designed to provide Contractor support to the Government for maintenance and modernization of RI-TACOd. Activities within major task areas will be evaluated and prioritized by the NFRMP/FPMS/PAS program managers (referenced as the Project Delivery Team [PDT] within this PWS) in consultation with the Contractor. Activities will reflect program requirements, user issues, and available resource levels. Several major task areas are to be managed through this delivery order. The task areas are described in Section 4. 

A description of general tasks includes the following:

General database development, assistance, and maintenance for DynamoDB and/or PostgreSQL databases.  

Make changes to database schema as needed to match any changes to the fields (name changes or additions).

Keep changelog of fields that renamed or added over time.

General assistance, and maintenance with web-based data entry interfaces and report generation.  The current interface uses ReactJS. 

General assistance in interfacing with customers and ensuring the Data Entry and Reporting system remains operational.  

Data must be made easily accessible to USACE for use in reporting tools such as Power BI,   A Representational State Transfer (REST) web service should be developed or a direct connection to the data accessible in Power BI should be made available.   Full instructions should be provided for end users to create a connection. General assistance with development of data services to ensure program data can be used within existing USACE tools (ex. Microsoft PowerBI). 

Develop a REST web service endpoint that provides geographic data in a GeoJSON format for use in ArcGIS Portal web maps.

General assistance to program managers in multiple business areas; this may include compiling reports for the managers, attending meetings, and presenting at meetings. 

Delivering training to users, database administrators, program managers, and others on how to enter data and pull reports once the new tool is operational.

Maintaining and enhancing system documentation.

Coordinate with CWBI PMO to maintain cybersecurity compliance, risk management framework documentation, and remediating vulnerabilities.

USACE access approvals and associated paperwork must be completed by Contractor personnel within 10-business days from notice to proceed and/or within 10 business days of notification and instructions from the Government.  As new staff join the team the development of new AWS capability to support RI-TACOd will be performed using Contractor assets.  More specifically, the Contractor will utilize the GovDEV environment for development of code. Any code or application passed to the Government will be hosted on the test/demonstration server for USACE Program Manger review and approval prior to being deployed by USACE resources with virtual technical assistance of deploying the components from the Contractor.  Ideally the Contractor will use continuous integration / continuous delivery pipeline with full infrastructure as code model to allow frequent automated deployments using Agile processes. The Government will host the testing and production cloud-based servers on the CWBI cloud environment. The Contractor will provide draft deliverables to the Government at the prescribed milestones and be available to the Government for any technical assistance needed to complete the loading of code in the test and production environments.  All code and deliverables developed are the property of USACE. All code must be maintained in CWBI's GitHub repository to ensure it can be scanned by CWBI's Information System Security Office. This team would also be responsible for responding to any findings from those scans.

The Contractor shall provide appropriate oversight and Project Management for every task in this PWS to ensure consistent oversight and coordination. Activities will reflect program requirements, user issues, and available resource levels. For the duration of this contract every month and when a need arises, the PDT in consultation with the Contractor, will evaluate and prioritize specific activities to be accomplished within each of the major task areas. Additional requests for updates and enhancements will be provided to the Contractor from the USACE Program Managers (PgMs)/Contracting Office Representative (COR) (both will be included on each request for situational awareness). These new requests will be addressed by the Contractor in the normally scheduled meetings or as necessary. 

The Contractor will work with the PDT to ensure technical accuracy, clarity and appropriateness of key software and documentations while balancing project tasks, deadlines, and on-time deliverables. 

The Contractor’s personnel must demonstrate the capability and appropriate experience to successfully perform a project of this scope and magnitude. The Contractor’s personnel should be familiar with the USACE Civil Works (CW) Program, and knowledge of the CW NFRMP, FPMS, and PAS missions or similar missions is beneficial but not required. The Contractor shall have extensive technical knowledge of programming in database and web-based data entry and reporting solutions to make the necessary revisions to the relevant systems. In addition to these general skills and experience, the Contractor should also possess the following:

Knowledge and experience in developing, maintaining and documenting changes to a relational database operated from a Government data center on Amazon Web Services (AWS cloud). 

Knowledge and experience of data entry and options to increase automation and efficiency.

Knowledge and experience with documenting data systems and processes and creating reports for increased efficiency.

Knowledge and experience in optimizing the performance of existing relational database applications, including procedures, functions, etc.

Knowledge and experience with creating Representational State Transfer (RESTful) services utilizing common data dissemination formats.

Knowledge and experience with making websites 508 compliant.

Knowledge of database design with respect to user experience to enable a design that maximizes efficient data entry and minimizes user data entry errors.

Maintain a clean, intuitive, and logical layout that is easy for users to navigate.

Use a consistent and accessible design for all text, colors, and interactive elements.

Knowledge and experience preparing geospatial services.

Knowledge and experience delivering solutions that align with Agile methodology.

As the Contractor updates their staffing plan an update will be provided to the PDT to ensure the requirements of this PWS are continuing to be met. An updated QA/QC plan with the updated staffing plan may be requested. 

In compliance with DoDI 8500.01 (2014) section 3.c.2, DoDI 8510.01 (2016) section 3.d, and USACE ER 25-1-112 (2014) section 7.1.3; all information systems (IS) and platform information technology (PIT) systems developed and/or supported under this contract shall comply with all Department of War (DoW), DISA, Army, and USACE cybersecurity and information technology (IT) requirements. This includes IS/PIT compliance with DISA security technical implementation guides (STIG) and being categorized IAW CNSSI 1253 using security controls developed IAW the risk management framework (NIST SP 800-53). STIG compliance shall include but is not limited to most current version of the DISA published Application Security and Development STIG and the internet access point (IAP) demilitarized zone (DMZ) STIG. Further, the Contractor shall comply with DFARS clause 252.204-7012 (Safeguarding Covered Defense Information and Cyber Incident Reporting) and implement NIST SP 800-171 requirements to protect covered defense information / controlled unclassified information.

General REQUIREMENTs

The following sub-sections provide details of various general requirements for this effort.

Non-Personal Services

The Contractor shall provide strictly non-personal services and contractor employees are not subject to direct supervision and control by the Government.  The Contractor shall advise and assist the Government but shall not make final decisions or certifications on behalf of the Government nor perform any inherently governmental functions.  The Contractor and its employees shall not represent the Government nor appear to represent the Government in performance of these contract services.  Contractor personnel shall clearly identify themselves as contractor employees in all interactions during contract performance.

Data Storage, Rights, and Ownership

The CSP has no rights to the DoW’s information/data. For more information on data storage, data rights, and data ownership requirements refer to Section 5.2, Legal Considerations, in the DoW Cloud Computing Security Reference Guide (SRG).

This would not include code, processes, or automation that USACE might subscribe to that are commercially available under Commercial Use Rights and/or Government Purpose Rights.

NOTICE OF INTENT to Sole Source 
 
1. SOLICITATION NUMBER: NIMH26000869 
 
TITLE: LMP744 in Recurrent Glioblastomas 
 
2. CLASSIFICATION CODE:R499 – SCIENTIFIC CONSULTING SERVICES 
 
NAICS CODE: 541715 – Research and Development in Physical, Engineering, and 
Life Sciences. 
 
3. RESPONSE DATE: April 15, 2026, at 12:00 PM EST 
 
4. PRIMARY POINT OF CONTACT: 
Joe Kennedy 
Joseph.kennedy@nih.gov 
Phone: 262-391-7630 
 
5. DESCRIPTION: 
 
INTRODUCTION 
 
This is a notice of intent, not a request for a quotation. 
 
THIS IS A PRE-SOLICITATION NON-COMPETITIVE (NOTICE OF INTENT) 
SYNOPSIS TO AWARD A CONTRACT WITHOUT PROVIDING FOR FULL OR 
OPEN COMPETITION (INCLUDING BRAND-NAME).  
 
The National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke (NINDS) intends to 
negotiate on a sole source basis with Emmes, for a base and five (5) option 
years. 
 
NORTH AMERICAN INDUSTRY CLASSIFICATION SYSTEM (NAICS) CODE 
and SET ASIDE STATUS 
 
The intended procurement is classified under NAICS code 541715 – Research 
and Development in Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences with a Size Standard 
of 1000 employees.  
 
This intended procurement will be a small business set-aside requirement.  
 
REGULATORY AUTHORITY  
This acquisition is conducted under the authority of the Federal Acquisition 
Regulation (FAR) Part 13—Simplified Acquisition Procedures. Contracts 
awarded using FAR Part 13—Simplified Acquisition Procedures are exempt from 
the requirements of FAR Part 6—Competition Requirements. FAR Subpart 
13.106-1 (b) Soliciting from a single source provides that: For purchases not 
exceeding the simplified acquisition threshold, Contracting Officers may solicit 
from one source IF the contracting officer determines that the circumstances of 
the contract action deem only one source reasonably available (e.g., urgency, 

exclusive licensing agreements, brand-name OR industrial mobilization). 
 
The resultant contract will include all applicable provisions and clauses in effect 
through the Federal Acquisition Circular (FAC) Number 2026-01, dated March 
13, 2026.  
 
DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENT 
 
Purchase Description 
 
Independently and not as an agent of the Government, the Contractor shall 
furnish all the necessary services, qualified personnel, material, equipment, and 
facilities, not otherwise provided by the Government as needed to perform 
the Statement of Work below: data collection, data abstraction, data 
identification, data validation, communication among clinical team, and 
understanding of clinical research protocol. 
 
Specific Requirements 
 
Clinical monitoring services will be responsible for overseeing clinical research 
efforts away from direct patient care. Detailed clinical monitoring will ensure 
accurate data abstraction, validation, and reporting. The place of performance will 
be a combination of onsite at the National Institutes of Health campus in 
Bethesda, Maryland and remote work 
  Salient Characteristics: 
 
The goal of this clinical trial is to evaluate progression-free and overall survival in 
participants with recurrent glioblastoma receiving LMP744 compared to historic 
controls. We will also directly compare molecular and metabolic profiles of 
tissue, CSF, and plasma pre- and postexposure to LMP744 to determine 
pharmacologic responses to the drug in this patient population. We will also 
correlate pre- and post-exposure molecular and metabolic profiles with clinical 
response and outcome, to determine which molecular and metabolic features are 
predictive of drug response. The latter information will be critical for the design 
of phase III clinical trials involving LMP744. Finally, we will evaluate the safety 
of LMP744 in patients with recurrent glioblastoma through continuous, objective 
monitoring. This is the first clinical trial to investigate the role of the novel 
indenoisoquinolone, CMYC/TOPOISOMERASE 1 inhibitor LMP744 in 
participants diagnosed with recurrent glioblastoma. Results from this study will 
provide objective assessment of the pharmacologic response to the drug and 
provide an initial assessment of efficacy when compared to historical controls. 
Our goal is to address the urgent need for effective therapies for patients with 
recurrent glioblastoma. Clinical trial monitoring of each enrolled patient (40 total) 
will be required for accutae assessment of safety for enrolled patients and future 
patients on study.  

 
Period of Performance 
 
The proposed period of performance shall be base plus 4 option years. 
 
Base: 5/1/26 – 4/30/27 
 
Level of Effort 
 
Clinical monitoring – 1634 hours total estimate over 5 years 
  
Government Responsibilities 
 
Clinical monitoring services will require access to government CTDB database 
reports. No requirement to access government facilities or equipment. No 
restrictions noted for holidays or other times.  
 
Reporting Requirements 
 
N/A 
 
OTHER CONSIDERARTIONS: 
 
Data Rights 
 
Data abstraction will be required for these requested services. Data will be abstracted 
from patient database reports. Collaboration with the clinical team as well as 
attendance of clinical research team meetings and individual meetings with PIs 
will be required for data review and protocol compliance. Clinical monitoring 
services will also require identification of missing source documents and requests 
of these from the research team 
 
Section 508—Electronic and Information Technology Standards 
 
Contracting services will be not required to procure, maintain and use electronic and 
information technology 
  
Confidentiality of Information: 
 
Contracting services will have access to clinical database reports for 
assessments. Data generated is not confidential - reporting to the public will 
include deidentified data. The contracting services will handle data/information 
prior to publication with discretion. 
 
(INCLUDING BRAND-NAME) DETERMINATION 
 
The determination by the Government to award a contract without providing for 
full and open competition is based upon the market research conducted. 
Specifically, Emmes, is the only vendor in the marketplace that can provide the 

services required by the National Institute of Health. 
 
The intended source is: 
 
 
Emmes Company, LLC 
401 N. Washington Street, Suite 700 
Rockville, MD 20850 
 
The essential characteristics of the clinical data management services that limit 
the availability to a sole source are sensitive clinical data abstraction, contracting 
service options and uniqueness of clinical trial discretion. Only this suggested 
source can furnish the requirements, to the exclusion of other sources, because 
current clinical trial approvals with readiness for patient enrollment of deadly 
brain cancer treatment.  
 
CLOSING STATEMENT 
 
THIS SYNOPSIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS. However, 
interested parties may identify their interest and capability to respond to this notice.  
 
A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon 
responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. All responsible 
sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation which shall be 
considered by the agency. The information received will normally be considered solely 
for the purpose of determining whether to proceed on a non-competitive basis or to 
conduct competitive procurement.  
 
Responses to this notice shall contain sufficient information to establish the interested 
parties' bona-fide capabilities for fulfilling the requirement and include: unit price, list 
price, shipping and handling costs, the delivery period after contract award, the prompt 
payment discount terms, the F.O.B. Point (Destination or Origin), the Unique Entity ID 
UEI), the Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN), and the certification of business size. 
 
Responses must include the place of manufacturing (i.e. address if supply/equipment is 
a domestic end product and includes country of manufacture).  All offerors must have an 
active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM) www.sam.gov. 
 
All responses must be received by the closing date and time of this announcement and 
must reference the solicitation number, NIMH26000869.  
 
Responses must be submitted electronically to Joe Kennedy, Contract Specialist, at 
joseph.kennedy@nih.gov   
 
U.S. Mail and fax responses will not be accepted.

Request for Information
DARPA-SN-26-51
Low Cost, Manufacturable Counter-Air Missile Propulsion
Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency
Tactical Technology Office
Responses due 22 April 2026, by 4:00 PM Eastern Time (ET).
This Request for Information (RFI) from the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency 
(DARPA)’s Tactical Technology Office (TTO) seeks to improve its understanding of the 
U.S. industry and supplier base for rocket propulsion technologies that can enable the 
development and production of low-cost missiles at speed and scale.
Responses to this RFI will be used to inform DARPA programs on emerging weapons 
technologies and suppliers that could play a role in the development of low cost, highly 
manufacturable missiles.
Intellectual or other privileged or proprietary information contained in responses to this RFI 
will not be distributed outside of the U.S. Government. In the event that a new DARPA 
program is developed in response to this RFI and a solicitation is issued, no intellectual or 
other proprietary information received in response to this RFI will be divulged to agencies 
outside the U.S. Government.
BACKGROUND:
DARPA is seeking to revolutionize weapons development by dramatically shrinking the 
time it takes to produce today’s systems. One proposed strategy inverts the traditional 
process by prioritizing manufacturability from the outset, allowing the weapon’s ultimate 
capabilities to be determined by what can be produced quickly and efficiently at mass 
scale. An important area of focus for this initiative is the production of propulsion 
systems, which are a notorious bottleneck in missile manufacturing. DARPA is actively 
scouting breakthrough technologies capable of compressing this production timeline from 
months to days and potentially hours.
DESCRIPTION:
This RFI seeks information on state-of-the-art development and manufacturing processes 
for missile propulsion systems, leveraging advanced propulsion prototyping, manufacturing, 
and testing. This RFI will also be used to identify industry partners that can assist in rapid 
prototyping, specifically as it applies to missile propulsion development. 

DARPA-SN-26-51
2
REQUESTED INFORMATION: 
DARPA is interested in responses that must address all of the following technical areas:
1. Advanced, high performance missile propulsion technologies and rapid 
manufacturing and production approaches.
2. Rapid propulsion system prototyping technologies and approaches for rapid 
design iteration. 
3. Anticipated propulsion system performance based on proposed rapid production 
approaches.
SUBMISSION FORMAT:
Attachment 2 contains a format template for responses to this RFI.
General Guidelines: 
Respondents to this special notice are encouraged to be as succinct as possible, 
while also providing actionable insight.
All submissions must be written in English.
White papers shall not exceed seven (7) single-sided written pages using 11-point 
font with 1” margins all around. Font no smaller than 10-point may be used for 
figures, tables, and charts. 
Electronic submittal shall be in Microsoft Word or PDF format. 
All documents submitted must be clearly labeled with the DARPA special notice 
number (DARPA-SN-26-51), respondent organization, and white paper title.
To the maximum extent possible, respondents are encouraged to send non-
proprietary information. 
oRespondents are responsible for clearly identifying proprietary 
information. Submissions containing proprietary information must have 
the cover page and each page containing such information clearly marked 
with a label such as “Proprietary” or “Company Proprietary.” NOTE: 
“Confidential” is a classification marking used to control the 
dissemination of U.S. Government National Security Information as 
dictated in Executive Order 13526 and should not be used to identify 
proprietary business information.
Do not include elaborate brochures or marketing materials; only include 
information relevant to the areas identified above.
Use of a diagram(s) or figure(s) to depict the essence of the response is permitted 
and counted towards page count.
Send unclassified submissions to DARPA-SN-26-51@darpa.mil. DO NOT 
SUBMIT CLASSIFIED INFORMATION TO THIS ADDRESS. Please see 
Attachment 1 - Security to this notice for instructions on submitting classified 
information.

DARPA-SN-26-51
3
Submissions must be received no later than 4:00 PM ET, 22 April, 2026. 
Submissions sent through other mediums, channels, or after the prescribed 
deadline will not be considered. Early responses are encouraged.
All white papers shall contain the following sections which are included in the page 
count:
A. Cover Sheet. Provide the following information:
a. Response Title
b. Technical point of contact name, organization, telephone number and 
email address (The contact information should include the respondent’s 
technical and/or administrative points of contact (names, addresses, phone 
numbers, fax numbers, and e-mail addresses) to enable potential 
clarification discussions. Identify your primary work location as 
appropriate.
c. Indicate classification level of response (e.g., Unclassified, 
Unclassified/Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI), Secret 
Collateral).
d. Submissions must include company Commercial and Government entity 
(CAGE) Code, Facility Clearance status/level, and document safeguarding 
level.   Technical Description. Graphics within the technical descriptions 
are encouraged to the extent that they aid in succinctly describing the 
concepts.
B. Graphic Overview Slide. If desired, include a single PowerPoint slide that 
graphically depicts the main ideas of the response.
C. Bibliography/References 
All technical and administrative correspondence and questions regarding this 
announcement and how to respond to this RFI should be sent to DARPA-SN-26-
51@darpa.mil. E-mails pertaining to this RFI that are sent directly to individual DARPA 
Program Managers will not receive a response. No telephone inquiries will be accepted.
NOTE: DARPA may conduct individual discussions with respondents as necessary to 
gain a full understanding of the technical and partnership models submitted. DARPA will 
contact respondents individually via e-mail. 

DARPA-SN-26-51
4
ELIGIBILITY
DARPA invites white paper submissions from all those engaged in related research 
activities and appreciates responses from all capable and qualified sources, including, but 
not limited to, universities, University-Affiliated Research Centers (UARCs) and 
Federally Funded Research and Development Centers (FFRDCs), private or public 
companies, and Government research laboratories. 
DISCLAIMERS AND IMPORTANT NOTES:
This is an RFI issued solely for information and new program planning purposes; 
it does not constitute a formal solicitation for proposals. In accordance with 
Federal Acquisition Regulation 15.201(e), responses to this RFI are not offers and 
cannot be accepted by the Government as such. 
Responses do not bind DARPA to any further actions related to this topic, 
including requesting follow-on proposals from respondents to this RFI. 
Submission is voluntary and is not required to propose to a subsequent solicitation 
(if any) on this topic. 
DARPA will not provide reimbursement for costs incurred in responding to this 
RFI. 
Respondents are advised that DARPA is under no obligation to acknowledge 
receipt of the information received or provide feedback to respondents with 
respect to any information submitted under this RFI.
DARPA will disclose submission contents only for the purpose of review. 
Submissions may be reviewed by the Government (DARPA and other 
Government partners), FFRDCs, and Scientific, Engineering and Technical 
Assistance (SETA) support contractors bound by appropriate non-disclosure 
agreements.

DARPA/TTO
DARPA-SN-26-51@darpa.mil

PROGRAM SECURITY

Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) and Controlled Technical Information (CTI) on Non-DoD Information Systems

For unclassified white papers containing Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI), applicants will ensure personnel and information systems processing CUI security requirements are in place.

If an unclassified submission contains CUI or the suspicion of such, as defined by Executive Order 13556 and 32 CFR Part 2002, the information must be appropriately and conspicuously marked CUI in accordance with DoDI 5200.48. Identification of what is CUI or higher in reference to air-to-air missile concepts should be clearly detailed within your source security classification guide (SCG) or Controlled Unclassified Information Guide (CUIG).

Those submitting white papers involving the pursuit and protection of DARPA information designated as CUI must have an information system authorized to process CUI information IAW NIST SP 800-171 and DoDI 8582.01.

Further information on CUI identification, marking, protecting and control, to include processing on Non-DoD Information Systems, is incorporated herein and can be found at https://www.darpa.mil/about/offices/contracts-management/proposer-general-terms#cui.

Classified Submissions

Additional information on these subjects can be found at https://www.dcsa.mil/.

	(a)	Classified Markings

At this time, DARPA anticipates that white papers submitted in response to this SN may involve access to classified information. Classified submissions shall be transmitted and marked in accordance with the security classification guidance referenced and sourced from your governing Security Classification Guide (SCG).  This SCG must be provided to the DARPA Program Security Representative for review along with written authorization for the use of classified information in response to this Request for Information from the Office of Primary Responsibility.

If a submission contains Classified National Security Information or the suspicion of such, as defined by Executive Order 13526, the information must be appropriately and conspicuously marked with the classification level and declassification date. 1.0  GENERAL STATEMENT OF SERVICES 
 
1.1 Introduction and Purpose. NASA has tasked the US Army Corps of Engineers Engineering 
and Support Center, Huntsville, to initiate a Facility Reduction requirement at the AMES 
research center in San Francisco, CA. Buildings are considered excess and will be demolished. 
The purpose of this contract is to procure Pre-demolition surveys according to the requirements 
set forth in this Performance Work Statement (PWS) 
1.2 Site Description and Location. AMES Research Center, 64 Facilities at Moffett Blvd, 
Mountain View, CA 94035. 
1.3 Security Requirements .  The Contractor shall be required to comply with all Installation 
entrance and security requirements.  The Contractor shall be responsible for assuring that all 
employees meet the access requirements of the Installation prior to the execution of work action 
on the Installation.   The Contractor will be required to present identification for base access 
installation requirements. 
1.3.1.1 AT Level I Training.  All contractor employees, including subcontractor employees, 
requiring access to Federally controlled facility or Military I nstallations, facilities, controlled 
access areas, or require network access, shall complete AT Level I awareness training within 30 
calendar days after contract start date or effective date of incorporation of this requirement into the 
contract, whichever  is applicable. Upon request, the contractor shall submit certificates of 
completion for each affected contractor employee and subcontractor employee, to the COR or to 
the contracting officer (if a COR is not assigned), within 5 calendar days after completion of 
training by all employees and subcontractor personnel. AT Level I awareness training is available 
at the following website: http://jko.jten.mil/courses/atl1/launch.html; or it can be provided by the 
RA ATO in presentation form which will be documented via memorandum. 
1.3.1.2 Access and General Protection/Security Policy and Procedures.  All contractors and all 
associated sub-contractors employees shall comply with applicable installation, facility and area 
commander installation/facility access and local security policies and procedures (provided by 
government representative). The contractor shall also provide all information required for 
background checks to meet installation/facility access requirements to be accomplished by 
installation Provost Marshal Office, Director of Emergency Services or Security Office. Contractor 
workforce must comply with all personal identity verification requirements (FAR clause 52.204 -

Page 2 of 45 
 
 
9, Personal Identity Verification of Contractor Personnel) as directed by DOD, HQDA and/or local 
policy. In addition to the changes otherwise authorized by the changes clause of this contract, 
should the Force Protection Condition (FPCON) or Health Protection Condition (HPCON) at any 
installation or facility change, the Government may require changes in contractor security matters 
or processes. 
1.3.1.2b For contractors who do not require a CAC but  do require access to a DoD facility or 
installation. Contractor and all associated sub -contractors employees shall comply with 
adjudication standards and procedures using the National Crime Information Center Interstate 
Identification Index (NCIC-III) and Terrorist Screening Database (TSDB) (Army Directive 2014-
05 / AR 190 -13), applicable installation, facility and area commander installation/facility access 
and local security policies and procedures (pr ovided by government representative, as NCIC and 
TSDB are available), or, at OCONUS locations, in accordance with status of forces agreements 
and other theater regulations. 
1.3.1.3 Suspicious Activity Reporting Training (e.g. iWATCH, CorpsWatch, or See Something, 
Say Something) . Military Instillations have suspicious activity reporting requirement. Report 
suspicious activities to appropriate law enforcement agencies. Infringement of the base policy may 
result in a fine or incarceration. 
1.3.1.5 Contractors w ill be escorted in areas where they may be exposed to classified and/or 
sensitive materials and/or sensitive or restricted areas.  All contract employees, including 
subcontractor employees who are not in possession of the appropriate security clearance or access 
privileges, will be escorted in areas where they may be exposed to classified and/or sensitive 
materials and/or sensitive or restricted areas. 
1.3.1.6 Pre-screen candidates using E-Verify Program. The Contractor must pre-screen Candidates 
using the E -verify Program (http://www.uscis.gov/e -verify) website to meet the established 
employment eligibility requirements. The Vendor must ensure that the Candidate has two valid 
forms of Government issued identification prior to enrollment to ensure the correct information is 
entered into the E-verify system. An initial list of verified/eligible Candidates must be provided to 
the COR no later than 3 business days after the initial contract award. 
1.4 Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) Requirements . The scope of this effort 
requires the contractor and/or subcontractor information system to process, store, or transmit FCI 
or CUI, and requires the contractor and/or subcontractor to comply with CMMC requirements. The 
Contractor shall have and maintain for the duration of this contract, order, or agreement a current 
CMMC status at the following CMMC level, or higher:  CMMC Level 2 (Self) for all information 
systems used in performance of th e contract, task order, or delivery order that process, store, or 
transmit FCI or CUI.  See DFARS 252.204-7021 “Contractor Compliance With the Cybersecurity 
Maturity Model Certification Level Requirements”, for the definitions, requirements, reporting, 
and subcontract information for this contract/order/agreement” 
 
2.0 OBJECTIVE - The objective of this Performance Work Statement is to plan and complete 
the environmental sampling of facilities at the installation.  The structures of concern are listed in 
Table I.  The sampling will determine ACM and ORM materials and complete a Waste Stream 

Page 3 of 45 
 
 
Analysis for RCRA 8 metals, lead-based paint (LBP) and PCB’s-in-paint for those parts of the 
structure currently identified as potentially having any painted components.  Following 
sampling, the Contractor shall be able to completely quantify the environmental contamination 
present and the methods required to remove and dispose of said contamination in a safe manner.  
All sampling shall be planned and performed in accordance with Federal, State, and local 
regulations for the installation.  All recommendations for follow-on actions shall also be in 
accordance with Federal, State, and local regulations.  Laboratory testing and analysis shall be 
completed within the workdays identified in table two following the respective site sampling 
field activity completion. The results of the site investigation and sampling effort will be 
provided in an individual Pre-Demolition Assessment Report for the installation that will be 
submitted within the workdays identified in table two following the receipt of sample results.  
The intent of this contract effort is to provide comprehensive sampling for all ACM/ORM 
materials to include the facility exterior, roof, basement/crawl spaces, etc. The Contractor shall 
make every reasonable effort to access these areas when present in each facility. The Report will 
specifically address any areas within given structures that were not accessible during the survey 
and state the size of the area not accessed, and current or immediate previous use of the area not 
sampled.  
 
3.0  DETAILED  DESCRIPTION  OF  SERVICES 
3.1 General Requirements.  All work performed by the Contractor shall be designed and 
implemented in a manner which conforms to this PWS and all applicable Federal, State, and 
local requirements. The Contractor shall present a complete description of the planning and 
assessment process as applied to the subject facilities. 
 
3.2 (Task 1) Pre-Demolition Assessments. 
3.2.1 (Task 1.1) Accident Prevention Plan and Sampling Plan. No more than the workdays 
identified in table two after award, the Contractor shall prepare and submit an Accident 
Prevention Plan (APP), including the Sampling Plan.  No Site Investigation shall be performed 
until the APP has been reviewed and approved by the Government.  The APP must include 
recommendations for utilization of Personnel Protective Equipment (PPE) as required to ensure 
worker protection to the extent required by law or recommended as prudent and appropriate by 
the contractor.  The types and numbers of samples per material type shall be generally described, 
as well as the process for collecting and securing the samples.  The laboratory used for analysis 
shall be identified.  Any special conditions required by State or Commonwealth regulations shall 
also be noted in the plan. 
 
When the work plan is submitted, please provide a separate submittal consisting of the 
Abbreviated Accident Prevention Plan, Activity Hazard Analysis, and SSHO Qualifications.  
Specific requirements for these safety submittals can be found in Appendix D Safety 
Requirements. 
 
The Site-Safety Health Officer (SSHO) and the Quality Control Manager (QCM) shall always be 
present on- site while field activities are occurring. The SSHO shall comply with all applicable 
safety criteria and shall use their discretion to determine which activities require the SSHO to be 
present, and where the SSHO will be for day-to-day operations. 

Page 4 of 45 
 
 
Government Designated Authority (GDA) for reviewing and accepting all required safety 
submittals is the HNC Safety Office. 
 
The APP and all Activity Hazard Analysis’ (AHAs) shall be reviewed and accepted by the 
Government Safety Office prior to the notice to proceed. The installation or additional stake 
holders may require reviews of the Contractor’s AHAs which shall be accommodated by the 
Contractor.

STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW) 
Technical Surveillance Countermeasures (TSCM) and Technical Development Support Services

1.0 INTRODUCTION 

UNCLASSIFIED 
 
 
UNCLASSIFIED 
The Contractor shall provide all personnel, supervision, and other items necessary to perform services to 
support the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency (NGA), Office of Counterintelligence (SIC) as defined 
in this Task Order (TO) Statement of Work (SOW), except for those items specified as government 
furnished property and services. This SOW describes the non-personal services contract required to 
support the mission of NGA for the Office of Counterintelligence. The Government shall not exercise any 
supervision or control over the contract service providers performing the services herein. Such contract 
service providers shall be accountable solely to the Contractor, who is responsible to the Government 
for accountability of Contractor and subcontractor personnel. 
1.1 BACKGROUND 
The Department of War is responsible for providing the most advanced technical security and 
countermeasures capabilities to protect sensitive facilities, information, and communications from 
unauthorized access or exploitation. The DOW Technical Security program is responsible for detecting, 
deterring, and neutralizing technical surveillance threats directed against DOW facilities and personnel. 
The Technical Security program implements DOW and Intelligence Community (IC) direction to 
integrate, enhance, and optimize technical security and signals countermeasures programs in support of 
the protection of national intelligence, sources, and methods, including sensitive compartmented 
information, and the facilities, systems, and networks that house them. 
1.2 SCOPE 
Except for those items specified as government furnished property and services, the contractor shall 
provide technical security support services to the Office of Counterintelligence necessary to complete 
associated tasks and responsibilities in the following functional areas outlined below and defined in this 
SOW: 
• Technical Surveillance Countermeasures (TSCM): Pre-Construction Surveys, Emergency Surveys, 
Routine Surveys, In-Place Monitoring 
• Data Engineering: Database design, implementation, and management 
• Software Development: Application design, coding, testing, and maintenance 
• Front-End Development: User interface design and implementation 
• Back-End Development: Server-side logic and API development 
• Technical Security and Signals Countermeasures (TSSC) Analysis: Technical security assessments 
and analysis 
1.3 Organizational Conflict of Interest (OCI) 
Prime Contractors are hereby informed that an actual and/or perceived OCI may arise in the 
performance of this requirement. This support, as fully described in Section 3.0, Appendix A and 
Appendix B, provides technical security support to DOW. These efforts may include access to existing 
technical security performance contract information and will include supporting all technical security 
areas, including but not limited to analyzing and documenting the following: requirements, existing and 
proposed technical solutions, financial data and estimates as well as any supporting documentation for 

UNCLASSIFIED 
 
 
UNCLASSIFIED 
future technical security services. All personnel assigned to this task order will be required to sign the 
standard Non-Disclosure Agreement. 
Should an OCI arise under this contract, the contractor will be required to notify the Contracting Officer 
immediately and then provide an OCI Mitigation Plan for the Contracting Officer's review and approval 
within 48 hours from time of notification to the CO. 
2.0 APPLICABLE DOCUMENTS 
In addition to the documents listed in this SOW, a list of applicable reference documents is provided for 
reference. See Appendix C. 
3.0 DESCRIPTION OF WORK 
3.1 Security Support Service Requirements 
The contractor shall provide services necessary to complete associated tasks and responsibilities of the 
SOW in the functional areas listed and described below, which is inclusive of Appendix A: Anticipated 
Support Requirements that identify Labor Categories (LCAT) and Skill Levels, and Appendix B: Position 
Descriptions that identify government-defined labor. 
3.1.1 Technical Surveillance Countermeasures (TSCM) 
Functional Description: The TSCM functional area refers to the procedures and techniques implemented 
to detect, identify, and neutralize electronic eavesdropping devices or other technical threats that 
compromise the security and confidentiality of sensitive information. This includes: 
• Pre-Construction Surveys: Evaluating plans and designs for new facilities to identify and mitigate 
potential technical security vulnerabilities 
• Emergency Surveys: Responding to suspected technical security breaches or incidents 
• Routine Surveys: Conducting scheduled examinations of facilities to detect unauthorized 
surveillance devices 
• In-Place Monitoring: Continuous monitoring of sensitive areas for unauthorized signals or 
activities 
• The TSCM functional area refers to the procedures and techniques implemented to detect, 
identify, and neutralize electronic eavesdropping devices or other technical threats that 
compromise the security and confidentiality of sensitive information. This area is led by a Senior 
TSCM Lead who ensures team compliance with all TSCM activities and standards. 
Expected Outcomes: 
• Successful detection and neutralization of all unauthorized surveillance devices in NGA facilities 
• Comprehensive documentation of technical vulnerabilities in pre-construction designs with 
specific mitigation recommendations 
• Emergency response to suspected technical security breaches within 24 hours of notification 

UNCLASSIFIED 
 
 
UNCLASSIFIED 
• Complete and thorough routine surveys conducted according to established periodicity 
• Effective continuous monitoring of sensitive areas with prompt alert response within 
established timeframes 
• Detailed survey reports documenting findings and recommendations delivered within 10 
business days of completion 
• Implementation of effective countermeasures that successfully mitigate identified threats 
• Compliance with ICD 705 and NGA standards for all TSCM activities 
3.1.2 Data Engineering 
Functional Description: The Data Engineering functional area encompasses the design, implementation, 
and management of databases and data pipelines to support TSSC operations and analysis. This 
includes: 
• Database design and optimization for TSSC data collection and analysis 
• Development of data pipelines for processing TSSC data 
• Implementation of data storage solutions for long-term analysis 
• Creation of data models to support analytical requirements 
Expected Outcomes: 
• Optimized database schemas that enhance TSSC data collection and analysis capabilities 
• Secure, efficient data pipelines with robust validation procedures that ensure data integrity 
• Properly implemented data storage solutions compliant with classified environment 
requirements 
• Comprehensive data models that effectively support analytical requirements 
• Documented database architecture that meets security and performance standards 
• Weekly data engineering status reports that track progress and identify issues 
• Data quality reports that demonstrate the effectiveness of data validation procedures 
• Secure integration with existing government systems and databases 
3.1.3 Software Development 
Functional Description: The Software Development functional area covers the design, coding, testing, 
and maintenance of custom software applications to support TSSC operations. This includes: 
• Development of TSSC analysis tools 
• Creation of reporting and visualization applications 
• Implementation of signal processing algorithms 

UNCLASSIFIED 
 
 
UNCLASSIFIED 
• Integration with existing government systems 
Expected Outcomes: 
• Functional, secure software tools for analyzing TSSC data that meet user requirements 
• Effective algorithms for signal processing and analysis that enhance threat detection capabilities 
• Intuitive visualization tools that enhance understanding of TSSC data 
• Customized reporting interfaces that meet user requirements and streamline workflows 
• Secure integration with existing government systems with proper documentation 
• Weekly software development status reports that track progress and identify issues 
• Thoroughly documented code and technical specifications that facilitate maintenance 
• Applications that successfully pass security testing before deployment 
3.1.4 Front-End Development 
Functional Description: The Front-End Development functional area focuses on creating user interfaces 
for TSSC applications that are intuitive, responsive, and effective. This includes: 
• Design and implementation of user interfaces for TSSC applications 
• Development of interactive data visualization components 
• Creation of responsive web applications for field use 
• Implementation of user authentication and authorization interfaces 
Expected Outcomes: 
• Intuitive user interfaces for TSSC applications that enhance productivity and user satisfaction 
• Interactive data visualization components that effectively display technical security data 
• Responsive web applications optimized for field use by technical security personnel 
• Secure login interfaces with appropriate role-based access controls 
• User interfaces that comply with government accessibility standards 
• Weekly front-end development status reports that track progress and identify issues 
• User interface style guides that ensure consistency across applications 
• Usability testing reports that document user feedback and implemented improvements 
3.1.5 Back-End Development 
Functional Description: The Back-End Development functional area encompasses server-side logic, API 
development, and system integration for TSSC applications. This includes: 

UNCLASSIFIED 
 
 
UNCLASSIFIED 
• Development of RESTful APIs for TSSC data access 
• Implementation of server-side business logic 
• Integration with government authentication systems 
• Development of automated data processing workflows 
Expected Outcomes: 
• Secure, well-documented APIs for TSSC data access with appropriate authentication controls 
• Robust server-side components with appropriate error handling and logging capabilities 
• Successful integration with government authentication systems 
• Efficient automated data processing workflows that enhance analytical capabilities 
• Server architecture that meets security and performance requirements 
• Weekly back-end development status reports that track progress and identify issues 
• API documentation that facilitates integration with other systems 
• Performance testing reports that demonstrate system efficiency and scalability 
3.1.6 TSSC Analysis 
Functional Description: The TSSC Analysis functional area covers the technical assessment and analysis 
of potential security vulnerabilities and countermeasures. This includes: 
• Analysis of RF signals and electromagnetic emissions 
• Assessment of physical security measures 
• Evaluation of technical security controls 
• Development of countermeasures recommendations 
Expected Outcomes: 
• Accurate identification and characterization of potential threat signals from RF analysis within 
48 hours of signal collection 
• Comprehensive evaluation of physical security controls with documented vulnerabilities 
delivered in standardized assessment reports 
• Thorough assessment of technical security control effectiveness with specific recommendations 
for improvement 
• Identification of gaps in technical security coverage with prioritized remediation 
recommendations 
• Tailored countermeasures recommendations with detailed implementation plans and resource 
requirements 

UNCLASSIFIED 
 
 
UNCLASSIFIED 
• Cost-benefit analysis for recommended countermeasure options to support decision-making 
• Detailed signal analysis reports delivered within 10 business days of analysis completion 
• Physical security assessment reports with actionable recommendations that comply with ICD 
705 standards 
• Technical security evaluation reports identifying specific vulnerabilities with mitigation 
strategies 
• Quarterly summary reports that track trends and emerging threats to inform proactive security 
planning 
• Annual technical security threat assessments that inform strategic planning and resource 
allocation

ARCHITECT-ENGINEER QUALIFICATIONS OMB Control Number:  9000-0157 
Expiration Date:  1/31/2027
STANDARD FORM 330 (REV. 7/2021) PAGE 1 OF INSTRUCTIONS 
Prescribed by GSA - FAR (48 CFR) 53.236-2(b)
PURPOSE  
 
Federal agencies use this form to obtain information from 
architect-engineer (A-E) firms about their professional 
qualifications.  Federal agencies select firms for A-E contracts on 
the basis of professional qualifications as required by 40 U.S.C. 
chapter 11, Selection of Architects Engineers, and Part 36 of the 
Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR).  
 
The Selection of Architects and Engineers statute requires the 
public announcement of requirements for A-E services (with 
some exceptions provided by other statutes), and the selection of 
at least three of the most highly qualified firms based on 
demonstrated competence and professional qualifications 
according to specific criteria published in the announcement.  
The Act then requires the negotiation of a contract at a fair and 
reasonable price starting first with the most highly qualified firm.  
 
The information used to evaluate firms is from this form and other 
sources, including performance evaluations, any additional data 
requested by the agency, and interviews with the most highly 
qualified firms and their references.
GENERAL INSTRUCTIONS  
 
Part I presents the qualifications for a specific contract.  
 
Part II presents the general qualifications of a firm or a specific 
branch office of a firm.  Part II has two uses:  
 
1.  An A-E firm may submit Part II to the appropriate central, 
regional or local office of each Federal agency to be kept on file.  
A public announcement is not required for certain contracts, and 
agencies may use Part II as a basis for selecting at least three of 
the most highly qualified firms for discussions prior to requesting 
submission of Part I.  Firms are encouraged to update Part II on 
file with agency offices, as appropriate, according to FAR Part 
36.  If a firm has branch offices, submit a separate Part II for 
each branch office seeking work.  
 
2.  Prepare a separate Part II for each firm that will be part of 
the team proposed for a specific contract and submitted with Part 
I.  If a firm has branch offices, submit a separate Part II for each 
branch office that has a key role on the team.
INDIVIDUAL AGENCY INSTRUCTIONS 
 
Individual agencies may supplement these instructions.  For 
example, they may limit the number of projects or number of 
pages submitted in Part I in response to a public announcement 
for a particular project.  Carefully comply with any agency 
instructions when preparing and submitting this form.  Be as 
concise as possible and provide only the information requested 
by the agency.
DEFINITIONS 
 
Architect-Engineer Services:  Defined in FAR 2.101.  
 
Branch Office:  A geographically distinct place of business or 
subsidiary office of a firm that has a key role on the team.  
 
Discipline:  Primary technical capabilities of key personnel, as 
evidenced by academic degree, professional registration, 
certification, and/or extensive experience.  
 
Firm:  Defined in FAR 36.102.  
 
Key Personnel:  Individuals who will have major contract 
responsibilities and/or provide unusual or unique expertise.
SPECIFIC INSTRUCTIONS 
 
Part I - Contract-Specific Qualifications  
 
Section A. Contract Information.  
 
1. Title and Location.  Enter the title and location of the 
contract for which this form is being submitted, exactly as shown 
in the public announcement or agency request.  
 
2. Public Notice Date.  Enter the posted date of the agency's 
notice on the Federal Business Opportunity website 
(FedBizOpps), other form of public announcement or agency 
request for this contract.  
 
3. Solicitation or Project Number.  Enter the agency's 
solicitation  number  and/or  project  number,  if  applicable, 
exactly as shown in the public announcement or agency request 
for this contract. 
 
Section B.  Architect-Engineer Point of Contact.  
 
4-8.  Name, Title, Name of Firm, Telephone Number, Fax 
(Facsimile) Number and E-mail (Electronic Mail) Address. 
Provide information for a representative of the prime contractor 
or joint venture that the agency can contact for additional 
information.
AUTHORIZED FOR LOCAL REPRODUCTION
Paperwork Reduction Act Statement - This information collection meets the requirements of 44 USC § 3507, as amended by section 2 of the Paperwork 
Reduction Act of 1995.  You do not need to answer these questions unless we display a valid Office of Management and Budget (OMB) control number.  
The OMB control number for this collection is 9000-0157.  We estimate that it will take 29 hours (25 hours for part 1 and 4 hours for Part 2) to read the 
instructions, gather the facts, and answer the questions.  Send only comments relating to our time estimate, including suggestions for reducing this 
burden, or any other aspects of this collection of information to:  U.S. General Services Administration, Regulatory Secretariat Division (M1V1CB), 1800 F 
Street, NW, Washington, DC  20405.

Section C.  Proposed Team.  
 
9-11.  Firm Name, Address, and Role in This Contract. 
Provide the contractual relationship, name, full mailing address, 
and a brief description of the role of each firm that will be 
involved in performance of this contract.  List the prime 
contractor or joint venture partners first.  If a firm has branch 
offices, indicate each individual branch office that will have a key 
role on the team.  The named subcontractors and outside 
associates or consultants must be used, and any change must 
be approved by the contracting officer. (See FAR Part 52 Clause 
"Subcontractors and Outside Associates and Consultants 
(Architect-Engineer Services)").  Attach an additional sheet in the 
same format as Section C if needed.  
 
Section D.  Organizational Chart of Proposed Team.  
 
As an attachment after Section C, present an organizational 
chart of the proposed team showing the names and roles of all 
key personnel listed in Section E and the firm they are 
associated with as listed in Section C.  
 
Section E.  Resumes of Key Personnel Proposed for this 
Contract.  
 
Complete this section for each key person who will 
participate in this contract.  Group by firm, with personnel of the 
prime contractor or joint venture partner firms first.  The following 
blocks must be completed for each resume:  
 
12.  Name.  Self-explanatory.  
 
13.  Role in this contract.  Self-explanatory.  
 
14.  Years Experience.  Total years of relevant experience 
(block 14a), and years of relevant experience with current firm, 
but not necessarily the same branch office (block 14b).  
 
15.  Firm Name and Location.  Name, city and state of the 
firm where the person currently works, which must correspond 
with one of the firms (or branch office of a firm, if appropriate)  
listed in Section C.  
 
16.  Education.  Provide  information  on  the highest relevant 
academic degree(s) received.  Indicate the area(s) of 
specialization for each degree.  
 
17.  Current Professional Registration.  Provide information 
on current relevant professional registration(s) in a State or 
possession of the United States, Puerto Rico, or the District of  
Columbia according to FAR Part 36.  
 
18.  Other Professional Qualifications.  Provide information 
on any other professional qualifications relating to this contract, 
such as education, professional registration, publications, 
organizational memberships, certifications, training, awards, and 
foreign language capabilities.
19.  Relevant Projects.  Provide information on up to five 
projects in which the person had a significant role that 
demonstrates the person's capability relevant to her/his proposed 
role in this contract.  These projects do not necessarily have to 
be any of the projects presented in Section F for the project team 
if the person was not involved in any of those projects or the 
person worked on other projects that were more relevant than 
the team projects in Section F.  Use the check box provided to 
indicate if the project was performed with any office of the current 
firm.  If any of the professional services or construction projects 
are not complete, leave Year Completed blank and indicate the 
status in Brief Description and Specific Role (block (3)).  
 
Section F.  Example Projects Which Best Illustrate Proposed 
Team's Qualifications for this Contract.  
 
Select projects where multiple team members worked 
together, if possible, that demonstrate the team's capability to 
perform work similar to that required for this contract.  Complete 
one Section F for each project.  Present ten projects, unless 
otherwise specified by the agency.  Complete the following 
blocks for each project:  
 
20.  Example Project Key Number.  Start with "1" for the first 
project and number consecutively.  
 
21.  Title and Location.  Title and location of project or 
contract.  For an indefinite delivery contract, the location is the 
geographic scope of the contract.  
 
22.  Year Completed.  Enter the year completed of the 
professional services (such as planning, engineering study, 
design, or surveying), and/or the year completed of construction,  
if applicable.  If any of the professional services or the 
construction projects are not complete, leave Year Completed 
blank and indicate the status in Brief Description of Project and 
Relevance to this Contract (block 24).  
 
23a.  Project Owner.  Project owner or user, such as a 
government agency or installation, an institution, a corporation or 
private individual.  
 
23b.  Point of Contact Name.  Provide name of a person 
associated with the project owner or the organization which 
contracted for the professional services, who is very familiar with 
the project and the firm's (or firms') performance.  
 
23c.  Point of Contact Telephone Number.  Self-explanatory.  
 
24.  Brief Description of Project and Relevance to this 
Contract.  Indicate scope, size, cost, principal elements and 
special features of the project.  Discuss the relevance of the 
example project to this contract.  Enter any other information 
requested by the agency for each example project.

Section H.  Additional Information.  
 
30.  Use this section to provide additional information

Sections A-G.  
 
Section I.  Authorized Representative.  
 
31. and 32.  Signature of Authorized Representative and 
Date.  An authorized representative of a joint venture or the 
prime contractor must sign and date the completed form.  
Signing attests that the information provided is current and 
factual, and that all firms on the proposed team agree to work on 
the project.  Joint ventures selected for negotiations must make 
available a statement of participation by a principal of each 
member of the joint venture.

Cost Estimate by Development Assistance Type and By Task Performer:  Provide an estimate of the cost of the Engineering and Technical Assistance (Technology Transfer) and General Business Development Assistance.  Include a cost breakdown of the seperate developmental assistance types by cost categories.  Indicate the percentage of each cost category for the total effort.

The required minimum amount of Engineering and Technical Assistance is 50% of the total effort.

Section D:	Mentor Firm Eligibility

Provide a statement (be sure to include the date of approval) that the Mentor Firm has been previously approved under the DoW Mentor-Protégé Program (provide a copy of approval letter, if available) and is still eligible to participate as a Mentor Firm per the requirements set by DFARS Appendix I-102 or identify anticipated schedule to submit a Mentor Application.

Section E:	Mentor Firm Information

Section F:	Mentor Firm Background

Provide a brief summary about the Mentor Firm including a company profile, volume of DoW/Service or Agency contracts, and accomplishments under their Small Business programs.  Indicate whether the Mentor Firm has one or more DoW contracts with an active small business subcontracting plan.

Section G:	Mentor Firm Capacity and Capability

Identify and describe the Mentor Firm's qualifications, capabilities, experience with small business assistance, expertice in related technical areas, proposed facilities and equipment, and capacity for achieving the proposed agreement objectives.

Section H:	Mentor Firm Past Performance

Identify and describe the Mentor Firm’s past performance, if any, in the DoW and Service/Agency Mentor-Protégé program.  Include all past and active Mentor Protégé Agreements and proposed agreements currently being considered (indicate agency).  Identify any past Nunn-Perry awards and/or any significant mentoring accomplishments.

Section I:	Protégé Firm Eligibility

Provide a statement that the Protégé Firm is currently eligible to participate in the DoW Mentor Protégé Program as a “disadvantaged small business concern” (DSB) as defined in Public Law 101-510, Section 831, as amended, pursuant to all of the following criteria below:

(1)  A small business concern as defined in the Small Business Act, 15 U.S.C. 631 et seq., and implementing SBA regulations in Title 13 of the Code of Federal Regulations;

 

(2)  Eligible for the award of Federal contracts;

 

(3)  Not more than the Small Business Administration (SBA) size standard for its primary North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code;

 

(4)  Not owned or managed by individuals or entities that directly or indirectly have stock options or convertible securities in the Mentor Firm;

(5) 	Is not currently a party to another Mentor Protégé agreement under the DoW Mentor-Protégé Program authority, 10 U.S.C. 2302 note;

(6) 	Has not had another Mentor Protégé agreement under the DoW Mentor-Protégé Program authority, 10 U.S.C. 2302 note; and

 

(7)  At least one of the following:

A small business concern owned and controlled by socially and economically disadvantaged individuals as defined in section 8(d)(3)(C) of the Small Business Act (15 U.S.C. 637(d)(3)(C)).

(B) 	A business entity owned and controlled by an Indian tribe as defined by section 8(a)(13) of the Small Business Act (15 U.S.C. 637(a)(13));

(C) 	A business entity owned and controlled by a Native Hawaiian Organization as defined by section 8(a)(15) of the Small Business Act (15 U.S.C. 637(a)(15));

(D) A qualified organization employing severely disabled individuals operating on a for-profit or nonprofit basis that -

Uses rehabilitative engineering to provide employment opportunities for severely disabled individuals and integrates severely disabled individuals into its workforce;

Employs severely disabled individuals at a rate that averages not less than 20 percent of its total workforce;

Employs each severely disabled individual in its workforce generally on the basis of 40 hours per week; and

Pays not less than the minimum wage prescribed pursuant to section 6 of the Fair Labor Standards Act (29 U.S.C. 206) to those employees who are severely disabled individuals (as defined in section 8501 of title 41, United States Code) or a severely disabled individual (as defined in such section).

(E) A small business concern owned and controlled by women, as defined in section 8(d)(3)(D) of the Small Business Act (15 U.S.C. 637(d)(3)(D));

(F)	A small business concern owned and controlled by service-disabled veterans (SDVOSB) as defined in Section 8(d)(3) of the Small Business Act (15 U.S.C. 637(d)(3));

(G) A qualified HUBZone small business concern (as defined in section 31(b) of the Small Business Act [15 U.S.C. 657a(b)]);

(H)	A small business concern that –

Is a non-traditional defense contractor, as such term is defined in 10 U.S.C. 2302; or

Currently provides goods or services in the private sector that are critical to enhancing the capabilities of the defense supplier base and fulfilling key Department of War needs.

Protégé Firm DoW Subcontract Awards to Other than the Mentor Firm.  Provide the number and total dollar amount of DoW subcontract awards made to other firms than the proposed Mentor by the Protégé Firm during the two preceding fiscal years (if any).  Please note fiscal year here represent the government’s fiscal year which runs October 1 through September 30.

Section M:	Mentor Firm – Protégé Firm Relationship

Provide a statement on the current and/or past relationship of the Mentor Firm's with the Protégé Firm.

Mentor Firm DoW Subcontract Awards to Protégé Firm.  Provide the number and total dollar amount of DoW subcontract awards made to the Protégé Firm by the Mentor Firm during the two preceding fiscal years (if any). Provide the following information if the Protégé Firm has previously participated in the DoW Mentor-Protégé Program during the last five (5) years.  Provide a statement (separate enclosure to this template) that there will be no duplication of effort (i.e., developmental assistance provided by the Mentor Firm) previously provided to the Protégé Firm under prior agreements.  This must be agreed upon and presented on letterhead from both the Mentor Firm and Protégé Firm.

Please note fiscal year here represent the government’s fiscal year which runs October 1 through September 30.

Describe the anticipated developmental assistance approach for the Protégé Firm specifying the type of assistance plann.  Provide how this approach will address the Protégé Firm’s nes to enhance their ability to perform successfully under contracts or subcontracts within DoW and other Federal agencies.

Information shall include identification and description of major tasks anticipated to be accomplished.  Technology transfer to the Protégé Firm must equate to at least 50% of the total proposed effort.

Identify and describe the anticipated work effort(s) by all authorized subcontractor(s) such as a Historically Black College & University (HBCU), Minority Institution (MI), Procurement Technical Assistance Center (PTAC), Small Business Development Center (SBDC), Women’s Business Center (WBC) or Manufacturing Extension Partnership (MEP) in the anticipated Protege Firm development efforts. If applicable, provide the current Technical Readiness Level (TRL) and/or Manufacturing Readiness Level (MRL) of the Protégé in the mentoring areas (including engineering and technical assistance and general business developmental assistance) and indicate the anticipated TRL and/or MRL at completion of the agreement.
