GENERAL INFORMATION

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

DESCRIPTION

VISN MUSE NX Performance PCS

PRESOLICITATION NOTICE 

Notice of Intent to Sole Source

-NONCOMPETITIVE-

Veterans Integrated Service Network 19 (VISN 19)

VISN MUSE™ NX Performance PCS Sustainment and Support

The Department of Veterans Affairs, Network Contracting Office (NCO) 19, intends to award a non-competitive sole source firm fixed price (FFP) contract to GE MEDICAL SYSTEMS INFORMATION TECHNOLOGIES, INC. to provide continued sustainment, support and service of MUSE™ NX Performance PCS cardiology software (MUSE) for existing systems at VISN 19 facilities. The requirement includes ensuring that the equipment operates as the original equipment manufacturer (OEM) intended, uninterrupted (95% uptime), in a cost-effective, efficient manner, contributing to the Veterans Administration’s (VA)’s Mission.

MUSE is proprietary and highly specialized and is cardiology’s data management system.  There are no other authorized resellers or distributors of this product/service.   MUSE reads electrocardiograms (ECG)s prior to exams, identifies, analyzes readouts, and predicts emerging heart issues.  This system assists providers to manage cardiac disease and automates orders and billing which eliminates paper processes. 

A maintenance, sustainment and support contract is needed for MUSE. The services required include but are not limited to: technical phone support, corrective and preventative maintenance, bug fixes, and upgrades/patches. These services are used to keep the system working to avoid possible delays in patient care. Technical phone support aids in troubleshooting problems, corrective and preventative maintenance maintain workflow for clinicians, and upgrades prevent the system from becoming vulnerable while on the network. 

The FFP service contract anticipated will have a base period of one (1) year and four (4) 1-year ordering periods of performance.

The estimated period of performance is 9/1/2026 - 8/31/2031.

Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements per 41 USC §3304(a)(1) as implemented by RFO 6.103-1(b).

The applicable NAICS Code is 541519 and the size standard is $34 Million.  

This notice of intent is not a request for competitive quotes.  Responses received will be evaluated; however, a determination by the Government not-to-compete the proposed procurement based upon responses received to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government.

*Supporting evidence must be furnished in sufficient detail to demonstrate the ability to meet the government’s needs.  

Responses to this Notice of Intent to Sole Source shall be received by 10:00AM (Mountain Time) 4/22/2026. to the Contract Specialist, Christine Jarvis, christine.jarvis@va.gov 

Responses received will be evaluated; however, a determination by the Government not-to-compete the proposed procurement based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. If no responses are received, the Contracting Officer will proceed with the sole source requirement to proprietary GE MEDICAL SYSTEMS INFORMATION TECHNOLOGIES, INC.

Introduction: 
 
This is a Request for Information (RFI) only issued for conducting market 
research.  Accordingly, this RFI constitutes neither a Request for Quote (RFQ), 
Request for Proposal (RFP), nor a guarantee that one will be issued by the 
Government in the future; furthermore, it does not commit the Government to 
contract for any services described herein.  The Department of Veterans Affairs 
(VA) is not, at this time, seeking proposals or quotes, and therefore, will not 
accept, review, or evaluate unsolicited proposals or quotes received in response 
hereto. This notice is not to be construed as a commitment on the part of the 
Government to award a contract, nor does the Government intend to pay for any 
information submitted because of this request.  The Government does not 
reimburse respondents for any costs associated with submission of the 
information being requested or reimburse expenses incurred for responses to 
this RFI.   
 
The information provided may be used by VA in developing its acquisition strategy and 
Performance Work Statement (PWS) or Product Description (PD).  Any information 
submitted by respondents to this RFI is strictly voluntary; however, any information 
received shall become the property of the Government and will not be returned to the 
respondent.  Interested parties are responsible for adequately marking proprietary, 
restricted, or competition sensitive information contained in their response. This is a 
request for information and does not obligate the Government in any way, nor does it 
commit the Government to any specific course of action. Product information, 
brochures, part numbers, and/or other description information may be included with the 
submission.

Efficiency” Cost Efficiency Initiative, dated February 26, 2025, commences a 
transformation in Federal spending on contracts, grants, and loans to ensure 
Government spending is transparent and Government employees are accountable to 
the American public. To comply with this EO, RFIs will now require a response to 
possible strategies and direction on how the VA can lower spending on future 
acquisitions. See question #3 below. 
President Trump issued two directives to transform the way our industry partners do 
business with the government. EO 14240 directs us to centralize federal procurement to 
eliminate duplication and waste. EO 14275 calls out long-standing concerns about the 
efficiency of the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) framework. Together, these 
charge us with building a more agile, effective, and accountable procurement system.  
As such, bundled pricing will not be accepted. Itemized pricing is required.

This intent to sole source announcement is posted for 15 days in accordance with FAR 5.2 - Synopses of Proposed Contract Actions. 

The Department of Veterans Affairs, The War Related Illness and Injury Study Center, Washington DC Office has an acquisition need for continued services and seeks a sole source acquisition strategy. The War Related Illness and Injury Study Center, Washington DC Office intends to modify Contract No. 36C24525P0477 to add an additional position and increase the contract value in accordance with FAR 6.302-1 Only one responsible source will satisfy the agency requirements. 

Background Information/Purpose. 

The War Related Illness and Injury Study Center (hereafter “DC WRIISC”) in Washington, DC is a national post-deployment health resource for the Veterans Health Administration (VHA). The WRIISC develops and provides post-deployment health expertise to Veterans and their health care providers through clinical programs, education and risk communication, and research.

HOME serves Veterans and their families as the leader and authority on health outcomes of military exposures through science, policy, education, and communication. HOME is a trusted team that Veterans and stakeholders rely on as a definitive source of information on military exposures. 

HOME consists of four interrelated programs, one of which is the WRIISC. The WRIISC thus requires the service expertise of a not-for-profit organization that provides scientific support related to military medicine and veteran health in support of this reorganization to leverage expertise acquired in the prior contract and apply it towards the new duties of these new workforce demands. In addition, WRIISC requires that the organization provides support and administrative capabilities to allow WRIISC staff to maintain their scientific and clinical focus to achieve their goals for Veteran healthcare. 

The organization must have extensive experience managing clinical research in the military/veteran community with expertise in recruiting and hiring research personnel and knowledge of the Washington DC VA Medical Center. Specifically, the WRIISC is interested in maintaining capabilities in the form of staffing of a Health Coach to assist Veterans with making better health choices through lifestyle changes; an Associate Scientific Director, who will support the Research Director and Director at the WRIISC in scientific planning and research portfolio management; and an Epidemiologist with expertise study design and statistical methods.  A Senior Education and Risk Communication Advisor (SERA), a doctorate level medical professional, will contribute strategic expertise in risk communication to enhance HOME outreach. 

Unique Qualifications — 

The War Related Illness and Injury Study Center (WRIISC) in Washington, DC is a national program dedicated to Veterans’ post‑deployment health concerns and unique health care needs. To meet increasing demands associated with the application of the PACT Act (H.R.3967 — 117th Congress) and to support leadership reorganization under the VA’s Health Outcomes Military Exposures (HOME), WRIISC seeks to modify its existing support arrangement. 

This modification adds one Epidemiologist position to serve as the lead for VMOAT operations, providing epidemiological oversight of survey instrument design and validation, exposure data governance, multi‑modal data integration (survey, clinical, biomarker, and administrative), analytic rigor (e.g., allostatic load and exposure mixtures), and regulatory coordination (IRB/HRPP) necessary for national scale.

The Epidemiologist will establish a rapid‑response operational infrastructure for VMOAT, manage QA/UAT cycles to ensure reliable downstream reporting, and translate findings into actionable risk communication and educational outputs for Veterans and providers.

This role preserves continuity with prior work under HJF, enables timely execution of VMOAT within WRIISC’s clinical and research mission, and directly advances HOME’s goals by providing trusted, science‑based evidence on military exposures and health outcomes. No inherently governmental functions are assigned; work will be performed as non‑personal scientific and technical support under Government direction.

Opening this contract to full competition or breaking up work among new vendors would introduce substantial delays, increase total costs, and create redundancies that impede progress on active tasks. Given the contract’s current momentum and the integrated nature of the SOW, HJF remains the only practical and qualified choice to continue execution without interruption. Awarding to HJF under FAR 13.5 preserves cost, schedule, and mission continuity, allowing VHA to meet essential directives under the PACT Act and HOME while advancing research and operational goals efficiently and on time.

Modification information – 

The Government awarded contract no. 36C24525P0477 and determined fair and reasonable pricing prior to award date of April 30,2025. The Government will modify the contract with the current pricing established in the base contract, and the pricing will be subject to no adjustments. The period of performance shall be for the remaining option year 1 through option 4.  Option periods are exercised as needed and are not guaranteed.  The Period of Performance reads as follows:

•	Option Year Period 3:			4/30/2028 – 3/29/2029		

•	Option Year Period 4:			4/30/2029 – 3/29/2030

Justification for Other than Full and Open Competition Bureau of Land Management

FAR 13.106-1(b)(1) Simplified Acquisitions

PR # 0044040825

Identification of the agency and the contracting office. 

Bureau of Land Management – Department of the Interior -US Wildland Fire Service 4955 Canyon Crest Dr.

Riverside CA, 92507

Description of supply or service required to meet the agency’s needs. 

Tablet Command is an approved app that can be downloaded on our mobile devices through the DOI company portal. In order to use the app we need to purchase 25 licenses for users. We also need them to establish a portal for our organization that has maps of our specific Direct Protection Areas, Mutual Threat Zones, as well as the real-time satellite location data for all of our fire resources. We also need “view only” access to our cooperator’s Computer Aided Dispatch logs for fires, and vehicle location data for those same cooperators who we have data sharing agreements with. We also need the functionality to use tablet command for our Incident Commander’s to manage our Incidents.

The rationale or circumstances for limiting competition. We need to be able to receive and share data with our cooperators in real time, in the field, on mobile devices. This is important so we can have a common operating picture and make timely decisions on wildland fires that don’t conflict with our cooperator’s decisions. There is no other platform that can share the types of information that we need to share. We need to see the real time GIS locations of our cooperator’s fire equipment, and they need to be able to see our equipment locations in GIS. We need to be able to view Computer Aided Dispatch notes for our cooperators with data sharing agreements.

A description of the Market Research (MR) conducted and the results or a statement of the reason MR was not conducted. 

The Government has conducted research for a platform that could have the features and integration of tablet command. The data sharing ability with cooperators is the most important aspect. So many of our cooperators already use Tablet Command including San Bernardino County, Cal Fire SDU, Cal Fire RRU, Cal Fire BDU, San Diego County, Riverside County, Kern County, Imperial County, Los Angeles County, Redlands City, Highland City, Apple Valley City, Victorville City, and Palm Spring City. Since these cooperators are already using this platform, it is really easy to share locations, intelligence, and other data to maintain a common operating picture. There are many times on incidents that we are in unified command with 3 or 4 of these cooperators and the timely information sharing is critical. Tablet Command will remove several barriers to much of the information.

The Government was unable to locate a competitor with the ability to view interagency shared AVL (automatic vehicle locations or view shared interagency CAD (computer aided dispatch) incident data across

jurisdictional boundaries. These two items are the most critical components that we need to carry out our mission.

PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT (PWS) 
M5 RACER Heavy Platform Maintenance Support 
26 FEB 2026 
Part 1 
General Information 
1. G eneral:  This is a non-personal service(s) contract under which the personnel rendering
the service(s) are not subject, either by the contract’s terms or by the manner of its
administration, to the supervision and control usually prevailing in relationships between the
Government and its employees.
1.1  Description of Services/Introduction:  This is a non-personal service(s) contract to 
provide maintenance support for four (4) M5 Robotic Autonomy in Complex Enviornments for 
Resiliency (RACER) Heavy Platforms.   
1.2  Background:  The 36th Engineer Brigade has received four (4) RACER Heavy Platforms 
(RHP) with full autonomy sensors and compute capability, permanently transferred from the 
DARPA RACER program. These platforms are unique and not part of an established Army 
program of record, thus lacking institutional sustainment support. This contract is required to 
provide the necessary maintenance and support to ensure the RHPs are operational for use in 
training events, experimentation, and to support the 1st Cavalry Division’s Transformation in 
Contact (TiC) 2.0 efforts, culminating in a validating National Training Center (NTC) rotation 
(27-05).  
1.3  Scope:  The Contractor shall provide non-personal service(s). The Contractor shall 
provide maintenance, sustainment, and training support for four RHPs. This includes, but is not 
limited to: on-site Field Service Representative (FSR) support during training events; 
preventive and corrective maintenance; management of a budget for replacement parts, 
sensors, and consumables; subcontracted support  
, ; remote and on- site autonomy software support, including updates and 
patches; and management of network and data subscriptions for the platforms. 
1.4  Objectives:  The objective is to provide a comprehensive maintenance and sustainment 
package that ensures the 4x RHPs are fully mission-capable, safe, and reliable for use by the 
36th Engineer Brigade. This support will reduce the risk of system failure during major training 
events and allow Soldiers to operate, maintain, and troubleshoot the platform effectively.  
1.5  General Information:

ontrol Plan (QCP): The Contractor shall develop and maintain a QCP to 
ensure services are performed in accordance with (IAW) this PWS. The Contractor shall 
develop and implement procedures to identify, prevent, and ensure non-recurrence of

GENERAL INFORMATION

DESCRIPTION

INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE

The Department of Veterans Affairs Network Contracting Office (NCO) 6, on behalf of VISN 6  intends to enter into a sole source procurement with CareFusions Solutions LLC, 3750 Torrey View Court, San Diego, CA 92130. 

NAICS code 541519-Other Computer Related Services. The proposed contract action is to provide software management services to Alaris Infusion System. The Contractor is to provide  software management services to include; internet, webinar and on-site training and clinical education, support ranging from remote monitoring of the Alaris Systems Manager to technical support for the Alaris Infusion System and includes collection of data and providing analytic tools and services to VISN 6 VA Medical facilities. The Government intends to solicit and negotiate with only one source under the authority of FAR 6.103-1(b) using the procedures under FAR 12.102 (a), Restricting Competition. Contract will be for a period of performance of a base plus four option years. This notice of intent is not a request for quotation. Interested parties may identify their interest in the requirement and capabilities to monique.cordero@va.gov no later than 10:00 AM EST, Aug.7, 2024. Telephone inquirers will not be accepted.  All information shall be furnished at no cost or obligation to the Government.

Gray market items are Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEM) goods sold through unauthorized channels in direct competition with authorized distributors.  This procurement is for software management services for OEM medical supplies, medical equipment and/or services contracts for maintenance of medical equipment (i.e., replacement parts) for Wilmington VA Health Care Clinic. No remanufacture or gray market items will be acceptable.

Vendor shall be an OEM, authorized dealer, authorized distributor or authorized reseller for the proposed medical supplies, medical equipment and/or services contracts for maintenance of medical equipment (i.e., replacement parts), verified by an authorization letter or other documents from the OEM, such that the OEM’s warranty and service are provided and maintained by the OEM. All software licensing, warranty and service associated with the medical supplies, medical equipment and/or services contracts for maintenance of medical equipment shall be in accordance with the OEM terms and conditions.

The delivery of gray market items to the VA in the fulfillment of an order/award constitutes a breach of contract. Accordingly, the VA reserves  the right to enforce any of its contractual remedies. This includes termination of contract or, solely at the VA’s election, allowing the Vendor to replace, at no cost to the Government, any remanufactured or gray market item(s) delivered to the VA medical facility upon discovery of such items.

No solicitation will be made. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. A determination by the Government not to complete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government.

Statement of Work 
NeuroX-Fusion: LLM-Foundation Model Alignment 
 
Period of Performance: 
Twenty-four (24) months from subcontract start date. 
1. Background and Purpose 
The DOE ASCR–funded NeuroX-Fusion project aims to construct a unified, multimodal foundation 
model of the human brain— integrating MRI, electrophysiology, video, and language— using a Large 
Language Model (LLM) as a shared semantic space. The roadmap culminates in NeuroX-Fusion, a 
130B-parameter “digital twin” that unifies NeuroX-MRI and NeuroX-Ephys via LLM-based alignment. 
 
The Subcontractor shall be a leader in: 
• Naturalistic fMRI and intracranial recordings 
• Brain–language mapping and LLM–brain encoding 
• Neural coupling during storytelling and real-world communication 
 
The Subcontractor will help refine LLM–brain alignment, validate cross-modal fusion between fMRI 
and electrophysiology, and co-develop protocols to use the digital twin for in-silico experiments.  
 
This Statement of Work (SOW) formalizes a focused, two-year subcontract to: 
• Design and validate LLM–Foundation Model (FM) alignment strategies and 
benchmarks for NeuroX-MRI, NeuroX-Ephys, and NeuroX-Fusion. 
• Co-design neuroscience-aligned pretraining and auxiliary objectives that embed 
neurocognitive constraints directly into NeuroX foundation model training. 
• Deliver datasets, benchmarks, and prototype pipelines that integrate early NeuroX 
checkpoints and drive rapid iteration. 
• Academic dissemination (conference and journal publications) is encouraged, consistent with 
DOE and institutional requirements. 
2. Scope of Work and Major Task Areas 
Work under this SOW is organized into three major task areas: 
• Task Area 1 – LLM–Foundation Model Alignment 
• Task Area 2 – Neuroscience-Aligned Pretraining Objectives 
• Task Area 3 – Prototyping, Datasets, Benchmarks, and Hackathon 
 
Each task area includes specific subtasks and deliverables.

3. Detailed Tasks and Deliverables 
Task Area 1 – LLM–Foundation Model Alignment 
Objective: 
Ensure that NeuroX foundation models (NeuroX-MRI, NeuroX-Ephys, and ultimately NeuroX-Fusion) 
learn latent representations that are neurally and cognitively plausible when aligned to an LLM, 
especially under naturalistic narrative and communication stimuli. 
Task 1.1 – Alignment Design for Naturalistic Language and Narratives 
The Subcontractor shall: 
• Specify alignment strategies between: 
o Token- and layer-level representations from an LLM applied to continuous language 
(stories, conversations, movie dialogue); and 
o Brain representations from MRI and electrophysiology for the same stimuli. 
• Provide guidance on: 
o Which LLM layers and NeuroX feature levels should correspond to different 
cortical hierarchies and timescales of processing. 
o How to handle speaker–listener coupling, inter-subject shared versus idiosyncratic 
variance, and narrative/event structure in the alignment design. 
Deliverable T1.1: 
“LLM–Foundation Model Alignment Design Note” (approximately 2–4 pages, PDF), explicitly 
tailored to NeuroX-MRI, NeuroX-Ephys, and NeuroX-Fusion. 
 
Task 1.2 – Alignment Benchmarks and Evaluation Metrics 
The Subcontractor shall: 
• Define quantitative benchmarks to test whether NeuroX models, when projected into the 
LLM latent space, capture: 
o Semantic structure of continuous narratives (event boundaries, topic shifts, 
suspense points). 
o Known hierarchical processing patterns in cortex during naturalistic stimuli. 
• Propose metrics including, but not limited to: 
o Encoding/decoding performance (correlation/R²) for fMRI and Ephys. 
o Inter-subject correlation (ISC) and shared-variance measures. 
o Region- and layer-resolved alignment curves. 
 
Deliverable T1.2: 
Benchmark specification document (PDF) plus example evaluation scripts (e.g., Jupyter notebooks) 
runnable on modest-scale models and subsets of NeuroX data. 
 

 
  March 9, 2026

does not constitute “development” or “production” technology under applicable export control 
regulations. 
 
Task 1.3 – Cross-Modal Validation for NeuroX-Fusion 
The Subcontractor shall: 
• Define tests to evaluate whether MRI and Ephys branches, when aligned through the shared 
LLM space, produce consistent semantic trajectories for the same stimuli. 
• Identify canonical paradigms (e.g., story listening, movie-viewing tasks) and expected cross-
modal patterns (spatial vs temporal signatures, hierarchical processing) that serve as validation 
targets for NeuroX-Fusion. 
Deliverable T1.3: 
“NeuroX-Fusion Cross-Modal Validation Playbook” (PDF), with specific contrasts, ROIs, and example 
analyses. 
 
Task Area 2 – Neuroscience-Aligned Pretraining Objectives 
Objective: 
Design, prototype, and specify neuroscience- and cognition-aligned pretraining/auxiliary 
objectives that encode realistic constraints from human communication and brain dynamics directly 
into NeuroX-MRI, NeuroX-Ephys, and NeuroX-Fusion training. These objectives will complement 
other neuro-informed loss functions and fusion layers developed by NeuroX collaborators. 
 
Task 2.1 – Objective Design: Naturalistic Narrative and Communication Priors 
The Subcontractor shall: 
• Co-design with BNL and collaborators a set of pretraining or auxiliary objectives that 
encourage NeuroX models to: 
o Predict/encode brain responses to continuous narratives given text, video, and/or 
internal NeuroX representations. 
o Capture speaker–listener coupling and shared semantic spaces across individuals. 
o Respect multi-timescale structure (fast lexical/phonetic vs slow narrative/event-
level dynamics). 
• Express each objective as a well-defined loss term compatible with NeuroX training (e.g., 
contrastive objectives, prediction heads, regularizers). 
Deliverable T2.1: 
“Neuroscience-Aligned Objective Specification” (PDF) describing each objective, required inputs, 
pseudo-code for loss computation, and its role in MRI, Ephys, and Fusion training. 
 
Task 2.2 – Prototype Implementations on Small-Scale Models 
The Subcontractor shall: 
• Implement reference versions of at least two to three core neuroscience-aligned objectives using:

o Lab and/or publicly available brain datasets. 
• Demonstrate that: 
o The objectives are numerically stable; and 
o They improve alignment metrics defined in Task 1 (e.g., encoding correlation, ISC) 
compared with simple baselines. 
Deliverable T2.2: 
Prototype code modules (e.g., PyTorch / HuggingFace style) implementing selected objectives, with

Task 2.3 – Integration Requirements for NeuroX Training 
The Subcontractor shall: 
• Translate objective designs into clear API and data requirements for the NeuroX training 
stack, specifying: 
o Necessary internal activations (e.g., layer-wise embeddings, temporal pooling outputs). 
o Annotation formats and batching schemes for aligned brain–text–video windows. 
• Coordinate with BNL and external collaborators (e.g., Cha/Moon labs) so these objectives 
are compatible with other knowledge-constrained loss functions and multi-modal fusion 
layers planned for NeuroX. 
Deliverable T2.3: 
“NeuroX Training Integration Requirements” (PDF), optionally co-signed with BNL, for engineering 
implementation. 
 
Task Area 3 – Prototyping, Datasets, Benchmarks, and Hackathon 
Objective: 
Provide concrete datasets, benchmarks, pipelines, and a focused hackathon that operationalize Task 
Areas 1 and 2 and accelerate integration with early NeuroX checkpoints. 
 
Task 3.1 – Dataset Curation for Pretraining and Evaluation 
The Subcontractor shall: 
• Curate one or more naturalistic neuroimaging datasets (subject to IRB and data-use 
agreements) suitable for: 
o Neuroscience-aligned pretraining objectives (Task 2). 
o Alignment and evaluation benchmarks (Task 1). 
• For each dataset, provide: 
o Preprocessed fMRI or electrophysiology signals, or standardized preprocessing instructions.

o Time-aligned transcripts and/or annotations (e.g., words, sentences, events, scenes). 
• Recommended splits for model training, validation, and evaluation-only usage. 
 
Deliverable T3.1: 
Dataset package(s) or secure access instructions, plus accompanying documentation targeted to

Task 3.2 – Benchmark Definitions and Leaderboard Templates 
The Subcontractor shall: 
• Define benchmark tasks that NeuroX models should be evaluated on, such as: 
o Predicting brain activity from text/video embeddings. 
o Inferring semantic/event labels from NeuroX brain latents. 
o Capturing shared vs idiosyncratic components across subjects.

o LLM + prototype brain model → 
o Neuroscience-aligned losses and alignment metrics → 
o Evaluation and visualization outputs. 
• Ensure these pipelines are structured to allow NeuroX-MRI/Ephys/Fusion checkpoints to be 
inserted later with minimal code changes. 
Deliverable T3.3: 
Example notebooks/scripts plus a brief summary of findings on current (non-NeuroX) models. 
 
Task 3.4 – NeuroX-Fusion Hackathon 
Objective: 
Conduct an intensive joint hackathon to integrate early NeuroX checkpoints into pipelines and 
stress-test neuroscience-aligned objectives and benchmarks.

is a SET ASIDE. No other offers will be considered. SeaPort MAC 
holders will need to register for PIEE accounts in order to 
receive solicitations and submit proposals/offers.***. 
 
Naval Sea Logistics Center (NAVSEALOGCEN) intends to solicit a 
SeaPort-NxG task order to provide engineering and technical 
services to support the Miniature Microminiature Module Test and 
Repair Program In-Service Engineering Agent’s responsibilities 
of progressive repair capability for Government electronic and 
electrical systems. The solicitation for this requirement will 
be posted in the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment 
(PIEE) Solicitation Module and publicized via SAM.gov. 
 
A SeaPort-NxG Sources Sought notice was issued in the SeaPort 
portal on 26 January 2026 for this requirement entitled, “2MMTR 
FOLLOW ON.” Based on the responses received, NAVSEALOGCEN 
intends to issue this solicitation as a SeaPort NxG Small 
Business set-aside.   
 
NOTE:  To be eligible as a SeaPort-NxG Small Business during the 
competitive ordering process, the Prime’s basic SeaPort NxG 
contract must reflect a Small Business within the System for 
Award Management (SAM) at the time of proposal submission. 
 
This notice also provides a draft Performance Work Statement 
(PWS) for the upcoming task order solicitation. The draft PWS is 
being released to solicit comments and questions from interested 
parties.   
 
Interested parties/potential offerors are encouraged to respond 
to this Advance Notice with questions and comments as soon as 
possible in order to allow for review prior to release of the 
solicitation.  Questions and answers shall be submitted by email 
to marisa.n.wirfel.civ@us.navy.mil and 
cody.d.hutchinson.civ@us.navy.mil.  Note that questions/comments 
submitted in response to this draft PWS may not receive a 
response; however, all questions and comments will be reviewed 
by the Government to assist in identifying revisions that may be 
incorporated in the PWS. 
 

The resulting task order is anticipated to be a level of effort 
task order issued on a Cost-Plus-Fixed-Fee (CPFF) basis.  It is 
anticipated that award of the task order will be made on a best 
value basis to the Government, and a trade-off analysis will be 
performed taking into consideration technical capability, past 
performance, and evaluated cost / price.  The solicitation is 
anticipated to include a one-year Base Period and four (4) one-
year Option Periods. 
 
The incumbent contractor currently providing the support 
services for this requirement is Engineering Services Network 
under SeaPort-NxG task order N00178-19-D-7599/N6660422F3006. 
 
NAVSEALOGCEN anticipates procurement milestones to occur on or 
around the following dates: 
 
Solicitation Issued: April 2026 
Proposals Due: May 2026 
Task Order Award: August 2026 
Task Order Start: October 2026

3RD PARTY VESSEL INSPECTION SERVICES 
STATEMENT OF WORK 
1. BACKGROUND
The U.S. Maritime Administration (MARAD) is an agency of the United States Department of 
Transportation. MARAD requires the services of a third-party Ship Inspection Service provider 
(Contractor) to provide class-style inspections of MARAD Ships, outside of the Ship Inspection 
requirements of US LAW (American Bureau of Shipping (ABS) (Class) and the United States 
Coast Guard (USCG)). MARAD requires a comprehensive analysis of each vessel’s condition, 
including its documentation, machinery, hull, and coatings. The material condition assessment 
will include a thorough structural and machinery inspection of the vessels and a comprehensive 
report on the conditions of the vessels.  The Contractor shall assess deficiencies that have 
resulted in a USCG 835 or ABS Condition of Class or Finding. MARAD is seeking a third-party 
ship inspection, in addition to the official ABS and USCG inspections required by law, to obtain 
another professional opinion on the condition of its Ready Reserve Fleet vessels. Therefore, any 
entity, other than ABS, meeting the qualifications set forth herein may be considered for award. 
2. CONTRACT INFORMATION

The Contractor shall conduct vessel inspections in two phases. The first phase of the vessel 
inspection that will be conducted will be the preparation phase; the second portion of the 
inspection will be the on-site inspection phase.   
2.1 Preparation Phase  
The following information will be provided at the award of a task order to kick off the inspection 
of a vessel. All documentation shall be reviewed before the start of the on-site inspection. The 
following information will be provided to determine the scope of the on-site inspection.  
2.1.1. Vessel Information: 
o Number of Vessels: Six (6) vessels may be selected for inspection from 
the three classes listed below. 
o Vessel Class and Locations:  
• Watson Class (6ea): Baltimore, MD, Norfolk, V A, New Orleans, 
LA, Vancouver, WA 
• Bob Hope Class (5ea): Newport News, V A, Portland, OR 
• Cape S class (5ea): Norfolk, V A, San Francisco, CA 
o Inspection Scope: All areas of the ship to be inspected.   
o Past Reports: Obtain and review any prior class inspection and service 
reports 
2.1.2. Required Documentation: 
o Class Certificates: Verify all relevant class certificates and regulatory 
compliance documents. 
o Vessel Maintenance Records: Review records on the last dry docking, 
previous inspections, and maintenance conducted on each vessel. 
o Operational Logs: Ensure the operational logs for the vessel's 
machinery and equipment are current. 
2.2. On-Site Inspection Phase 
The Contractor shall apply its own professional maritime inspection methodology consistent 
with classification-society practices. The procedures listed in Sections 2.2.1 through 2.2.7 
represent minimum expectations for inspection scope and reporting and do not prescribe the 
Contractor’s proprietary methods. 
For each vessel, the inspections are to be scheduled during a monthly Dock Trial to allow 
machinery to be observed while in operation.    

2.2.1.  Hull Inspection: 
o Visual Inspection: Thoroughly examine the vessel’s hull for any signs 
of damage, cracks, corrosion, or other structural weaknesses. 
o Thickness Measurement: Review the most recent ultrasonic thickness 
gauges. 
o Condition of Coatings: Inspect the condition of anti-corrosion coatings 
and protective paints. Check for peeling, blistering, or any signs of wear.  
o Bilge Areas and Sea Chests: Ensure that these areas are free of debris, 
corrosion, and that the coatings are in intact. 
o Tanks and Tank Coatings: Inspect the condition of anti-corrosion 
coatings and protective paints. Check for peeling, blistering, or any signs 
of wear. Material condition of the steel structure to be noted. 
2.2.2. Machinery and Engine Room: 
o Main Engine and Auxiliary Equipment: Inspect the condition of the 
main engine, auxiliary engines, and generators for any signs of excessive 
wear, oil leaks, or vibrations. All equipment to be observed while in 
operation as practicable. 
o Piping and Valves: Check the condition of piping systems, including 
steam, fuel, lube oil, cooling water, and ballast systems, for leaks, 
corrosion, and proper insulation.  
o Electrical Systems: Inspect the main electrical panels, circuit breakers, 
and safety systems to ensure they are in good order.   
o HV AC Systems: Verify the air conditioning, ventilation, and heating 
systems in the engine room and house for proper functioning. 
2.2.3. Cargo Equipment: 
• Ramps, Cranes, Elevators, and Material Handling Equipment: 
Observe operational test. Identify and record any anomalies in 
machine performance. Inspect for material condition including 
hydraulic hoses and condition of wires. 
• Cargo Hold Ventilation: Verify all cargo hold fans are operational.  
2.2.4. Coatings and Paints: 

o Deck Coatings: Assess the condition of the deck paint and non-slip 
surfaces. Verify if there are any areas that need resurfacing or 
maintenance.  
o Interior Coatings: Review the condition of coatings in spaces like the 
cargo holds, ballast tanks, stair towers, and other interior sections prone 
to wear. 
2.2.5. Safety Equipment: 
o Lifesaving Equipment: Ensure all lifeboats, life rafts, life vests, and 
other required lifesaving equipment are in place, operational, and 
compliant with regulatory requirements.  
o Fire Safety Equipment: Inspect fire extinguishers, sprinklers, and 
alarms for operational readiness. 
o Navigational Equipment: Verify the functionality and calibration of 
navigational systems (radars, GPS, AIS, etc.) as per regulatory 
requirements. 
2.2.6.  Structural Integrity and Stability: 
o Ballast and Stability System: Inspect the vessel's ballast system and 
stability equipment. Verify that they are operating correctly. This is to 
include Ballast Treatment Systems.  
o Strength of Hull Supports: Assess areas that are critical to structural 
integrity, such as bulkheads, frames, and support beams. 
o Load Line Markings: Verify that the load line markings are intact and 
readable. 
2.2.7.  Pollution Prevention: 
o Bilge Water Treatment: Inspect the system for treating and discharging 
bilge water. Ensure it complies with MARPOL regulations. 
o Sewage Treatment: Inspect the sewage treatment system for material 
condition, functionality and regulatory compliance.  
o Garbage Management: Confirm the presence and condition of waste 
management systems. 
3. DELIVERABLES 
3.1. Post-Inspection Report 

After completing the inspection of each vessel, the Contractor shall compile a detailed report for 
each vessel that includes: 
3.1.1. Executive Summary: 
o Overview of the vessel’s overall condition and any immediate concerns. 
o Summary of key areas requiring attention or repairs. 
3.1.2. Inspection Findings and Deficiencies 
o List all deficiencies 
o Submit a plan for dates of inspections to the Ships Operations 
and Maintenance Officers (SOMOs) to be coordinated via 
area division COR. MARAD will reply within 3 business 
days confirmation of schedule or provide alternate date(s) of 
inspection. 
o Provide the location and immediate impact of each 
deficiency 
o Provide a prioritization for each deficiency - Critical, High 
Priority, Medium Priority, and Low Priority to guide 
prioritization of repairs or maintenance. 
o All Deficiencies shall be provided with an assessment of risk 
based on the ship’s ability to be activated within a 5-day 
window and complete 180 days of traditional cargo vessel 
operations.  
o Hull Condition: Specific areas that show signs of damage, corrosion, or 
wear. 
o Machinery Condition: Any issues found with the engine room equipment 
including pumps, electrical systems, or other mechanical components. 
o Coating Conditions: Any issues found with paint or coatings on the 
vessel, including deterioration or necessary touch-ups. 
o Safety Systems: Whether or not safety equipment is up-to-date and in 
good working order.

Audio Visual/Information Technology (AV/IT) Support 
Maneuver Support Center of Excellence (MSCoE) G6 Contract 
Performance Work Statement (PWS) DRAFT v5 
Fort Leonard Wood, Missouri 
Part 1: Service Provision and Scope 
C.1. GENERAL:
The contractor shall provide all personnel, materials, supervision, other items, and non-
personal services to deliver Audio Visual/Information Technology (AV/IT) services for 
facilities maintained by the contractor. This includes ensuring the seamless operation, 
maintenance, and support of AV/IT systems, infrastructure, and integrated technologies, 
as well as compliance with all applicable Department of War (DoW), Army, and 
installation-specific regulations, standards, and directives. The contractor shall ensure 
that all AV/IT systems remain operationally ready, secure, and aligned with the mission 
requirements of the  
Maneuver Support Center of Excellence (MSCoE) G6 at Fort Leonard Wood, 
Missouri. 
The scope of AV/IT services encompasses, but is not limited to, the following technology 
domains: 
• Audio Visual (AV): Projectors, display panels, video walls, audio systems,
microphones, speakers, amplifiers, and associated control systems
• Information Technology (IT): Network infrastructure, workstations, laptops,
peripherals, software applications, cybersecurity compliance, and IT service
management
• Unified Communications & Collaboration (UC&C): Video Teleconferencing
(VTC) systems, collaboration platforms (e.g., Microsoft Teams, Zoom), and
integrated communication systems
• Control Systems: Crestron, Extron, AMX, and other AV/IT control and
automation platforms
• AV Network Infrastructure: Switches, routers, and cabling infrastructure
supporting AV/IT systems
C.1.1. Description of Services / Introduction:
The contractor shall maintain government-owned and operated AV/IT systems at Fort 
Leonard Wood, Missouri to ensure continuity of service and provide upgrades as 
DRAFT

required to ensure system integrity, interoperability, and compliance with applicable 
standards. The contractor shall perform to the standards specified in the Performance 
Work Statement (PWS). Support includes, but is not limited to, the following roles and 
responsibilities: 
1. AV/IT Classroom and Facility Support:
AV/IT Helpdesk Troubleshooting and Ticketing System:
The contractor shall manage and resolve AV/IT-related helpdesk tickets, providing first 
line troubleshooting for all AV/IT systems across MSCoE G6 supported facilities at Fort 
Leonard Wood, Missouri. This includes: 
• Diagnosing hardware, software, and network-related issues affecting AV/IT
systems
• Coordinating repairs with vendors, manufacturers, and internal technical staff
• Ensuring timely resolution of user-reported problems within established contract
timeframes as defined in this contract
• Maintaining accurate and up-to-date records within the designated ticketing
system
• Generating trend analysis reports to identify recurring issues and recommend
systemic solutions
AV/IT Event Setups: 
The contractor shall coordinate and execute AV/IT setups for events, conferences, 
training sessions, and command briefings at MSCoE G6 supported facilities, ensuring 
proper functionality of all AV/IT equipment and IT infrastructure. This includes: 
• Conducting pre-event site surveys to assess technical requirements for both AV
and IT systems
• Testing all equipment prior to events, including audio systems, display systems,
video teleconferencing (VTC) platforms, network connectivity, and collaboration
software
• Providing on-site technical support during events and addressing any AV/IT
technical issues in real time
• Coordinating with event organizers, facility managers, and the Contracting
Officer's Representative (COR) to ensure mission success
• Conducting post-event equipment checks and documenting any issues or
lessons learned
DRAFT

• Ensuring network bandwidth and IT resources are adequate to support event
requirements
AV/IT Tier 1 & Tier 2 Support: 
The contractor shall perform installation, troubleshooting, and maintenance of AV/IT 
systems, providing Tier 1 and Tier 2 support for all AV/IT-related issues across  
MSCoE G6 supported facilities at Fort Leonard Wood, Missouri. This includes: 
• Installing new AV/IT equipment and infrastructure components, including network
hardware, workstations, and AV systems
• Configuring systems to meet user and mission requirements, including AV
network configurations and AV system programming
• Conducting scheduled and unscheduled preventive maintenance to ensure
optimal performance and system longevity
• Maintaining an inventory of all AV/IT equipment, components, software licenses,
and spare parts
• Coordinating with the MSCoE G6 IT staff to ensure AV/IT systems remain
compliant with network security policies, Army Cybersecurity requirements,
and DoW Information Assurance standards
• Supporting IT/AV lifecycle management, including equipment refresh planning
and technology upgrades
C.1.4. Hours of Operation:
The contractor shall conduct business between the hours of 0630 to 1700 Local Time, 
Monday through Friday, excluding Federal holidays, unless otherwise directed by the 
Government. The contractor shall support up to thirty (30) special events requiring 
AV/IT support on evenings or weekends, coordinating a minimum of seven (7) calendar 
days in advance. 
The Government reserves the right to adjust work schedules as mission dictates, 
providing a 7-calendar-day notice beforehand. In case of urgent mission requirements, 
the contractor shall make reasonable efforts to accommodate short-notice requests in 
coordination with the COR. 
Special Event Support: For special events requiring AV/IT support outside regular 
business hours at Fort Leonard Wood, Missouri, the contractor shall: 
• Coordinate with the COR to ensure adequate staffing and resources are
available for both AV and IT support requirements
DRAFT

• Provide a detailed written plan for event support, including personnel
assignments, AV/IT equipment requirements, network resource allocations, setup
timelines, and contingency measures
• Ensure all AV/IT equipment and IT systems are tested and operational no later
than two (2) hours prior to event start time
• Designate a lead AV/IT technician as the primary point of contact for each special
event
• Ensure network connectivity, VTC systems, and collaboration platforms are fully
operational and tested prior to each event
• Document all special events, support activities and submit a post-event summary
report to the COR within three (3) business days following the event
Part 2: Specific Deliverables 
C.2. Period of Performance:
The Period of Performance (PoP) for this contract shall be as follows:
• Base Period: Twelve (12) months from the date of contract award
• Option Period 1: Twelve (12) months
• Option Period 2: Twelve (12) months
• Option Period 3: Twelve (12) months
• Option Period 4: Twelve (12) months
• Total Potential Contract Duration: Sixty (60) months (five years)
All services shall be performed at Fort Leonard Wood, Missouri, unless otherwise 
directed by the Contracting Officer (CO) or COR. 
C.3. Specific Deliverables:
The contractor shall perform the following tasks to administer, maintain, operate, and 
repair Government AV/IT systems and peripheral equipment across all MSCoE G6 
supported facilities at Fort Leonard Wood, Missouri: 
AV/IT Classroom and Facility Support: 
• Manage AV/IT-related helpdesk tickets and provide troubleshooting, including
diagnosing hardware, software, network, and cybersecurity-related issues and
coordinating repairs
DRAFT

• Coordinate AV/IT setups for events and training sessions, including pre-event site
surveys, equipment testing, network readiness checks, and on-site support
• Perform installation, troubleshooting, and maintenance of AV/IT systems,
including installing new equipment, configuring systems, and conducting
preventive maintenance
• Maintain a comprehensive inventory of all AV/IT equipment, software licenses,
and components
• Ensure all AV/IT systems remain compliant with applicable DoW and Army
cybersecurity, IT, and information assurance standards
• Support AV/IT lifecycle management activities, including equipment refresh,
software updates, and technology upgrades
C.3.1. Tier 1 Support
Definition:
Tier 1 support serves as the first point of contact for users experiencing AV/IT issues 
across MSCoE G6 supported facilities at Fort Leonard Wood, Missouri. This level of 
support focuses on basic troubleshooting, phone-based assistance, remote support, 
and hands-on support for straightforward AV and IT problems. Tier 1 technicians shall 
be knowledgeable in common AV/IT systems, software platforms, network 
fundamentals, and user-facing technologies deployed across MSCoE G6 support 
facilities. 
Responsibilities: 
Phone and Remote Support: 
• Answer user calls and provide immediate assistance for common AV/IT issues
such as display problems, audio issues, network connectivity, software
application errors, and basic equipment troubleshooting
• Guide users through step-by-step solutions over the phone or via remote desktop
tools, ensuring clear communication and user understanding
• Utilize approved remote support tools to diagnose and resolve AV/IT issues
without requiring an on-site visit when possible
• Support users with IT-related issues including account access, software
functionality, and peripheral device connectivity
• Document all remote support interactions in the ticketing system
Ticket Management: 
DRAFT

• Log all user issues in the designated ticketing system, categorizing them based 
on priority, complexity, and impact to mission 
• Assign tickets to appropriate AV/IT technicians based on skill set and workload 
• Escalate unresolved or complex AV/IT issues to Tier 2 support, providing detailed 
notes, diagnostic findings, and context for efficient resolution 
• Monitor open tickets to ensure resolution within established contract timeframes 
and provide status updates to users 
• Identify and flag recurring AV/IT issues for problem management review 
Basic Hands-On Support: 
• Perform simple hardware checks, such as verifying cable connections, restarting 
devices, checking power supplies, and inspecting AV signal paths and IT network 
connections 
• Assist users with basic AV/IT setups, such as connecting projectors, adjusting 
audio levels, configuring display settings, establishing VTC connections, and 
connecting to network resources 
• Replace consumable items such as batteries, cables, remote controls, and basic 
IT peripherals as needed 
• Conduct basic software troubleshooting, including application restarts, driver 
updates, settings adjustments, and basic network connectivity diagnostics 
• Support user account management tasks in coordination with MSCoE G6 IT staff 
Examples of Tier 1 Tasks: 
• Resolving projector connectivity issues 
• Adjusting audio levels for classroom presentations 
• Assisting with basic AV/IT equipment setup for classroom presentations 
• Troubleshooting VTC connection issues for routine meetings 
• Replacing faulty cables, remote controls, or IT peripherals 
• Restarting unresponsive AV/IT control systems 
• Assisting users with network connectivity issues 
• Supporting basic software application troubleshooting 
C.3.2. Tier 2 Support 
DRAFT

Definition: 
Tier 2 support handles more complex and technical AV/IT issues that require 
advanced expertise, specialized tools, and in-depth system knowledge across MSCoE 
G6 supported facilities at Fort Leonard Wood, Missouri. This level of support focuses 
on equipment repair, replacement, programming, system integration, network 
configuration, and advanced troubleshooting. Tier 2 technicians shall possess advanced 
knowledge of AV/IT systems, control systems, network infrastructure, cybersecurity 
compliance, and integration technologies. 
Responsibilities: 
Equipment Repair and Replacement: 
• Diagnose and repair faulty AV/IT hardware, including projectors, audio systems, 
display panels, control processors, network switches, servers, and workstations 
• Replace damaged or outdated AV/IT equipment, ensuring compatibility with 
existing systems and compliance with Government-approved equipment lists 
• Coordinate warranty repairs and vendor support for both AV and IT equipment as 
needed 
• Maintain a spare parts inventory for AV/IT equipment to minimize system 
downtime 
• Support IT hardware lifecycle management, including equipment imaging, 
configuration, and deployment 
Programming and Configuration: 
• Configure AV/IT systems to meet specific user and mission requirements, 
including custom audio settings, display resolutions, control system 
programming, network configurations, and integration with IT infrastructure 
• Program AV control systems (e.g., Crestron, Extron, AMX) to support new or 
modified AV/IT configurations 
• Integrate AV/IT systems with IT infrastructure, including AV network switches and 
collaboration platforms (e.g., Microsoft Teams, Zoom) 
• Configure and maintain IT systems including workstations and AV network 
devices in coordination with MSCoE G6 IT staff 
• Ensure all AV/IT configurations are documented and maintained in the AV/IT 
system documentation library 
DRAFT

• Support software deployment, patch management, and system updates for AV/IT 
systems 
Advanced Troubleshooting: 
• Investigate and resolve complex AV/IT issues, such as system failures, software

combination of sources), what is your methodology to create real world representations of specific 
features? What combinations of data types are used in your process (e.g. vector-to-vector, image-to-

would you ensure critical processes/outputs are prioritized for review?  What are your defined threshold 
metrics for minor, major and critical for AFE outputs for topographic, maritime and aeronautical 
features? How would you achieve an objective threshold accuracy of 80% with a goal for objective 
accuracy of 99% for topographic, maritime and aeronautical features? How does your solution interface 
with GIS systems for viewing, evaluating and editing results? Describe any AI/ML models that are used

AFE products.  What are the nominal/baseline operating benchmarks and infrastructure specifications for 
your system?

1.0 Summary and Background 
To overcome a historically fragmented data landscape where critical information is trapped in 
disconnected, stove-piped systems, the Foundation Digital Twin (FDT) program requires an Automated 
Feature Extraction (AFE) capability. This automated engine is essential for autonomously scanning vast, 
disparate datasets to identify and catalog the critical infrastructure and objects of interest that form the 
core of its living, authoritative digital replica of the globe. By pivoting from an outdated, product-focused 
model to this unified, data-centric architecture, the AFE process is an essential component for achieving 
true data harmonization and maintaining a temporally relevant and spatially accurate version of 
Foundation GEOINT for users. 
The overall purpose of this Statement of Objectives is to acquire a contractor who can provide robust 
Automated Feature Extraction (AFE) solutions. To respond, vendors are required to select features from 
the list in Appendix A and, for each selected feature, provide a detailed explanation of how their solution 
meets the requirements of the specific use cases described in Section 3.0. These solutions will modernize 
NGA's geospatial intelligence production by leveraging AI/ML to automate manual processes, improve 
data accuracy, and ensure seamless integration with critical NGA production systems. The successful 
implementation of AFE capabilities will significantly enhance timeliness, relevance, and accuracy of 
geospatial intelligence, directly supporting national security missions. 
The National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency (NGA) is a Department of War (DoW) combat support 
agency and a member of the National Intelligence Community (IC). NGA develops imagery and map-
based intelligence solutions for U.S. national defense, homeland security, and safety of navigation. 
NGA’s mission is to “provide timely, relevant, and accurate geospatial intelligence in support of national 
security.” 
The current Foundation GEOINT environment faces significant operational challenges that impede 
efficiency and effectiveness. Foundation GEOINT (FG) Analysts spend extensive time on repetitive 
manual feature extraction, conflation, and validation, which are time-consuming activities that could be 
automated. To address these challenges and support NGA's 2035 GEOINT Concept of Operations, NGA 
seeks to implement AFE capabilities. These solutions should leverage artificial intelligence and machine 
learning (AI/ML) to transform geospatial intelligence production, significantly reducing manual 
processing time, increasing data accuracy, and enabling the rapid delivery of intelligence to decision-
makers. 
2.0 Scope of Work 
The scope of this effort is to acquire services or capabilities for AFE capabilities focused on features 
identified by FG as important but challenging. This includes the provisioning, configuration, deployment, 
and sustainment of a commercial/out-of-the-box AFE capability to automate the identification and 
extraction of geospatial features from imagery and other source materials. AFE capabilities will be a 
critical enabler for modernizing Foundation GEOINT processes and will be integrated with key NGA 
systems. The work will support NGA's maritime, aeronautical, topographic, geographic, and geomatics 
mission domains and will be integrated into NGA’s FG production environments on all required security 
domains.

4 
UNCLASSIFIED 
3.0 Objectives 
The contractor shall achieve the following four high-level objectives to successfully deliver a 
comprehensive Automated Feature Extraction (AFE) solution: 
Objective 1 
Provide and Deploy a High-Performing Automated Feature Extraction (AFE) Capability as a 
Service 
The primary goal is to provide, deliver, and sustain a robust AFE capability that automatically detects and 
extracts geospatial features from various sources including imagery (EO, SAR, HS, MS) and raster maps. 
This system must be capable of monoscopic and/or stereoscopic extraction and handle individual and 
batch processing. The capability shall automatically attribute extracted features based on observable 
characteristics in accordance with NGA domain standards and preserve feature geometry, spatial 
relationships, and metadata from the source data. 
Objective 2  
Ensure High-Quality Data and Enable Analyst-in-the-Loop Validation 
The contractor shall implement a system that ensures the accuracy and reliability of all extracted data. 
This includes achieving a threshold accuracy of 80% for topographic and maritime features and 90% for 
aeronautical features, with an objective accuracy of 99%. The system must feature automated quality 
assessment processes with confidence scores and provide an intuitive interface for analysts to review, 
validate, and correct extracted features. All analyst feedback shall be used to continuously improve the 
performance of the AI/ML models. 
Objective 3  
Enable Seamless Utilization by NGA's GEOINT Ecosystem via Open APIs  
FG desires that AFE capabilities be exposed as a service that is callable and accessible from NGA 
Architecture via open APIs. This requires seamless interoperability with the systems and data repositories 
responsible for geospatial AFE data generation and AFE repository management. The contractor’s 
solution shall provide a documented set of open APIs and utilize NGA standardized formats (e.g., GDB, 
Shapefile) for all extracted features to ensure seamless interoperability with current enterprise systems 
and adaptability for any future integrations. 
Objective 4  
Meet and Maintain Stringent Performance and Security Standards 
The solution must be scalable, reliable, and secure. The system shall be capable of processing a standard 
1GB source file in less than 10 minutes and achieve 99% availability in the production environment. The 
contractor must ensure the system is deployable to both Unclassified and Classified domains and 
complies with all applicable security directives, including DNI ICD 503 and all requirements outlined in 
DD Form 254.

PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT (PWS)

1. Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR).  

a. Primary COR.  See DITCO Additional Text G1 - Points of Contact

b. Alternate COR.  See DITCO Additional Text G1 - Points of Contact

c. Property Administrator See DITCO Additional Text G1 - Points of Contact 

2. Contract or Task Order Title.  International Acquisition and Engagements

3. Background.   International Acquisition includes the cross-border procurement of defense articles and services, as well as cooperative research, development, production, and sustainment programs with allied and partner nations. These activities are critical for enhancing interoperability, sharing technology and cost burdens, and strengthening the defense industrial base of the U.S. and its partners. The Defense Information Systems Agency (DISA) plays a crucial role in these programs by providing vital IT articles and services to partner nations via various International Programs, thereby improving communication, information sharing, and operational effectiveness. Agency International Acquisition governance is codified by the Foreign Assistance Act (22 U.S.C. §2151), Arms Export Control Act (22 U.S.C. §2778), Defense Security Cooperation Agency (DSCA) Manual 5105.38-M, Security Assistance Management Manual (SAMM), Department of Defense (DoD) 7000.14-R, and DoD Financial Management Regulation (FMR).

4. Objectives: The objective of this contract is to provide non-personal services to DISA supporting International Acquisition to include Foreign Military Sales (FMS), Engagements, and Business Process Engineering activities, to include international agreements and technology release. The contractor will support the International Acquisition and Engagement office, Program Acquisition Executive (PAE) Offices, Program Management Offices (PMOs), and Resource Managers to fulfill partner nations' acquisition requirements. This requires highly integrated expertise in international acquisition protocols, including FMS, as well as knowledge of DISA and DoD specific systems and DSCA policies and processes.

5. Scope. The contractor shall provide international acquisition, programmatic, general portfolio management, and FMS financial services to meet international obligations. This includes support for FMS and Building Partnership Capacity (BPC) case development, execution, system acquisition and delivery, asset tracking, sustainment, and case closure, strategic international engagement activities and business process engineering. All tasks must be compliant with applicable Department of Defense (DoD) governance and guidelines.

 

The contractor shall execute the following task areas:

Task Area 1: International Acquisition Professional Services - Foreign Military Sales

Task Area 2: International Acquisition Professional Services – Engagements and Business Process Engineering

Surge Support: The Government may require surge support during any performance period. Surge modifications will be within the scope of this PWS and shall not exceed 20% of the contractor’s total proposed cost/price for the base and all option periods, excluding any extension of services pursuant to FAR 52.217-8.

Government Rights: The Government will have unlimited rights and exclusive ownership of all deliverables (e.g., briefs, reports, manuals, plans, research) created under this contract. These deliverables may not be used or sold by the contractor without written permission from the Contracting Officer.

Technology: Non-developmental items (NDI) and commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) products and processes shall be used to the maximum extent practicable.

6. Performance Requirements. The following tasks establish the foundation of services and products for Agency International Acquisition and Engagements. The contractor shall provide operational, process, and financial management for the development, execution, reconciliation, and closure of FMS cases.

6.1 Task 1 – International Acquisition Professional Services - Foreign Military Sales

6.1.1 Subtask 1- FMS Program Management.

The contractor shall:

Provide operational, process, and financial management for the development, execution, reconciliation, and closure of up to 60 FMS/BPC cases.

Conduct a kick-off meeting within ten (10) business days after award to discuss programmatic requirements, schedules, roles, and responsibilities.

Provide a draft Contract Management Plan at the kickoff meeting and a final version within 15 business days after the meeting.

Submit a Monthly Status Report (MSR) detailing actions performed on all tasks.

Meet with the COR and program manager monthly to discuss the status of each case.

6.1.2 Subtask 2- FMS Case Management. 

The contractor shall:

Develop and coordinate products, create documentation, and participate in reviews related to DISA’s FMS/BPC actions.

Manage and track customer requests, official cases and lifecycle status within the Defense Security Assistance Management System (DSAMS), and applicable DISA and DSCA dashboards and tracking systems.

Deliver coordinated FMS/BPC agency packages for Government review and submission for Letter of Offer and Acceptance (LOA) development.

Develop recommendations to ensure case requirements are clearly planned, acquired, and delivered.

With Government approval, implement process improvement measures.

Develop FMS training resources and provide recommendations for Agency FMS strategic level planning.

Coordinate FMS program portfolio reviews. 

Maintain electronic case and funding document files via SharePoint/shared drive.

6.1.3 Subtask 3 - FMS Financial Management. 

The contractor shall:

Prepare funding documents and load financial information into FMS/BPC-related financial systems, including but not limited to DISA accounting systems, Telecom Services Enterprise Acquisition Services (TSEAS) Inventory and Billing Information (TIBI), Defense Integrated Financial System (DIFS), Centralized Information System for International Logistics (CISIL) and various Security Cooperation systems.

Maintain electronic case and funding document files via SharePoint/shared drive.

Collect, analyze, and file vouchers for FMS/BPC contracts.

Review financial plans and coordinate with the DISA Comptroller’s Office, Defense Finance and Accounting Service (DFAS) and other DoD agencies to identify discrepancies and validate transactions. 

6.1.4 Subtask 4 - FMS Reconciliation and Financial Process. 

The contractor shall:

Retrieve and analyze reports from DoD financial and logistical systems to ensure full reconciliation of all FMS/BPC case transactions.

The contractor shall retrieve FMS case-related funding documentation and financial reports from the accounting system(s), the Defense Integrated Financial System (DIFS), and the Centralized Integrated System-International Logistics (CISIL). This information must be reviewed and analyzed to ensure transactions are reconciled across all systems and that both the performance and cash sides of DIFS are aligned.

Reconcile and clear financial discrepancies to align systems as required.

Obtain voucher copies, enter information into the required system, and prepare funding packages for submission in accordance with DoD and Office of the Chief Financial Officer requirements.

Prepare and coordinate voucher correction packages with DISA and Defense Finance and Accounting Service (DFAS) to ensure correct billing.

6.1.5 Subtask 5 – FMS Case Closure. 

The contractor shall:

Review the inventory of FMS/BPC cases in supply/service complete (SSC) status and provide recommendations on case closure actions.

Research contract and funding discrepancies and draft follow-up letters for document finalization.

                 	         

6.1.6 Subtask 6 - Operating Procedures and Internal Processes. 

The contractor shall:

Provide input and recommendations on business process development for Financial Improvement and Audit Readiness (FIAR) compliance efforts for approximately 60 cases monthly.

Maintain a complete library of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for all FMS/BPC tasks.

Ensure a comprehensive and compliant records management system is in place.

Develop and update business process flow charts and narratives.

compliance efforts for approximately 60 cases.

Deliverables:

6.2 Task 2 – International Acquisition Professional Services – Engagements and Business Process Engineer Activity

 The contractor shall provide analytical, operational, and technical services for the planning and execution of the Government's international acquisition activities.

6.2.1 Subtask 1 – International Engagements

The contractor shall:

Coordinate pre-engagement, dayof logistics, and post-engagement activity DISA international partner forums and foreign official visits to DISA HQ.

Adhere to all applicable DoD and DISA policies, including International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) and Foreign Disclosure approval.

Monitor and analyze activities of international organizations to identify strategic engagement opportunities for DISA.

Record meeting minutes, noting all decisions and action items for Agency International Engagements, International Acquisition review and planning meetings. 

Track the progress of all action items and report any delays to the appropriate government personnel.

Maintain and update agency database of international visits information and relevant international affairs information via designated portal. Maintain an organized record of all meeting materials (agendas, presentations, minutes, etc.) within designated site.

Prepare quarterly and annual reports on the Agency's international activities internal and external to DISA HQ activities.

Conduct monthly audits to recommend compliance improvements for DISA's international acquisition activities. Archive materials in accordance with DISA's records management policies.

6.2.2 Subtask 2 – Business Process Engineer Activity

The Business Process Engineer shall provide the necessary expertise to analyze, document, re-engineer business processes related to International Acquisition activity. This includes, but is not limited to, the following tasks:

6.2.2.1 Process Analysis and Documentation:

Conduct comprehensive analyses of existing international acquisition processes, including but not limited to FMS, Technology Release and Foreign Disclosure (TRFD), International Engagements, International Agreements, Program International Acquisition and training coordination.

Document current "as-is" business processes, workflows, and systems using industry-standard methodologies and tools.

Identify bottlenecks, redundancies, and inefficiencies in current processes.

6.2.2.2 Process Re-engineering and Improvement:

Design and propose "to-be" business processes that are more efficient, effective, and aligned with strategic objectives.

Develop and present business case analyses for proposed process changes, including cost-benefit analysis and risk assessment.

Collaborate with stakeholders to develop and implement new and improved business processes.

ADEQUATE ACCOUNTING SYSTEM 
FA8051-24-S-0001 Attachment 1 
 
  
In order to avoid potential contracting delays, it is suggested that companies interested in 
pursuing cost reimbursement type contracts under the subject BAAs have an adequate 
accounting system in place per Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP), Generally 
Accepted Government Auditing Standards (GAGAS), the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 
and Cost Accounting Standards (CAS).  Therefore if you have not already had a Defense 
Contract Audit Agency (DCAA) review of your accounting system, it is necessary for DCAA to 
perform an audit to confirm that an adequate system is in place. 
 
DCAA’s requirements and standards are available on their Website at: https://www.dcaa.mil/.  
Select “Customers” from the drop down menu and then click on “Guidance” and “Audit Process 
Overview – Information for Contractors”. The Preaward Accounting System Adequacy 
Checklist is available by selecting “Customers” from the drop down menu and then “Checklists 
and Tools” and “Pre-award Accounting System Adequacy Checklist”.   
 
For Offerors without a DCAA-approved cost accounting system, DCAA will require a SF 
Form 1408.  Please complete the SF 1408 found at https://www.gsa.gov/system/files/2024-
08/SF1408-14f.pdf and submit the completed form with your proposal.  
 
Proposals requesting a cost-reimbursement type contract without including the completed 
SF1408 may be deemed non-conforming to the solicitation.  
 
The Government recognizes that this form is intended for an auditor to use when evaluating a 
contractor's cost accounting system. However, your preliminary responses to the questions will 
expedite the DCAA accounting system review. To complete the form, check the boxes on the 
second page (Section II), then provide a narrative explanation of your accounting system on page 
one (Section I) to supplement the checklist in Section II. It is expected that the answers to the 

questions on the SF 1408 will be “Yes” and will have adequate narrative remarks for each 
question to demonstrate to DCAA that an appropriate accounting system is in place prior to their 
initiation of a review of that system.  The Government will forward a copy of the form to the 
cognizant DCAA Field Office with the request for audit.   
Note that the cost of any audit activity is not considered an allowable direct charge to the 
contract currently contemplated or any other contract. 
 
Adequate Accounting System and Cost Accounting Standards (CAS) Notices and 
Certification.  Per FAR 52.230-2, any procurement contract in excess of $2M resulting from 
this solicitation will be subject to the requirements of the Cost Accounting Standards Board (48 
CFR 99), except those contracts which are exempt as specified in 48 CFR 9903.201-1. Any 
offeror submitting a proposal which, if accepted, will result in a CAS compliant contract, must 
submit representations and a Disclosure Statement as required by 48 CFR 9903.202 detailed in 
FAR 52.230-2. The disclosure forms may be found at 
https://www.whitehouse.gov/omb/management/office-federal-procurement-
policy/#_Office_of_Federal_5  
 
 
Agencies and Resources available to assist you: 
 
DCAA SMALL BUSINESS SEMINARS – To schedule contact your local DCCA Audit Office.  
 
DCAA Locator:  https://www.dcaa.mil/Locator/  
 
DCAA Audit Process Overview:  https://www.dcaa.mil/Guidance/Audit-Process-Overview/  
 
DCAA Small Business Focal Point: (571) 448-3478  
 
Defense Contract Management Agency (DCMA):  http://www.dcma.mil/ 
 
Small Business Administration:  https://www.sba.gov/about-sba/sba-locations/headquarters-
offices  
 
SF 1408 Pre-award Survey of Prospective Contractor Accounting System Checklist:  
https://www.dcaa.mil/Checklists-Tools/Pre-award-Accounting-System-Adequacy-Checklist/

1 INTRODUCTION 
1.1 EXECUTIVE SUMMARY 
The Defense Security Cooperation Agency (DSCA) Office of Business Operations (OBO) 
Information Management and Technology (IM&T) Directorate manages the Agency’s IT 
systems across several portfolios that align to the DSCA lines of business. Historically, a 
program-centric model of IT management was employed, providing programs with broad 
latitude to use and seek funding for technologies and solutions they deemed best fit their 
requirements. While this approach served individual programs well, it contributed to a high 
degree of technical variance and the creation of technology/data silos, leading to: 
• High Total Cost of Portfolio Ownership – Duplicative capabilities have been 
established at DSCA and across the IAs with no economies of scale or standardization 
able to be realized. This includes areas such as licensing negotiations with vendors, high 
acquisition overhead to maintain contracts and renewals, and a highly specialized 
workforce being required to maintain the many disparate technologies in the portfolio. 
• Large Cyber Security Attack Surface – Many different Commercial Off The Shelf 
(COTS) software stacks in use, all with unique cyber-attack surfaces, vendor support 
timelines, and vulnerability remediation procedures. 
• Siloed Workforce – Difficult to move IT personnel across programs due to high degree 
of specialized technology and knowledge required on a program-by-program basis. 
• Talent Management Challenges – Challenging to attract and retain highly skilled labor 
due to diverse and aged technologies in use across the portfolio. 
• High Acquisition Overhead – Industry engagement is unique for each program in the IT 
portfolio. 
More recently, DSCA has migrated to a portfolio and enterprise approach to IT management to 
address the challenges above.  In 2023, IM&T established the Engineering and Architecture 
Review Board (E&ARB) to augment the existing IT governance process. Chaired by the DSCA 
Deputy CIO for Data, Security, and Technology (DST), the E&ARB was instituted to provide a 
technical review of incoming IT demands and develop recommended Courses Of Action (COAs) 
prior to review by the CIO, Portfolio Investment Review Board (PIRB) and/or Strategic 
Investment Board (SIB). By developing technical COAs that align with enterprise IT direction 
prior to funding alignment, variance (and the associated challenges) will be reduced over time, 
leading to a more manageable portfolio of IT systems, and more responsive IT workforce. 
The E&ARB requires a baseline set of IT standards to provide consistent, achievable, and 
practical technical recommendations to investment boards in order to ensure sound Agency 
technology investments. This document captures DSCA’s enterprise IT Standards, as 
incorporated into the Security Cooperation Enterprise Architecture to track technical compliance 
of DSCA software solutions across multiple dimensions (See Table 1).
