1.2 GUIDING PRINCIPLES 
DSCA’s mission is to advance U.S. defense and foreign policy interests by building the capacity 
of foreign partners to encourage and enable allies and partners to respond to shared challenges. 
Information Technology (IT), notably, is not part of the core DSCA mission space. Rather, IT is 
a force multiplier enabling DSCA to better execute the Security Cooperation mission. As IT is 
not a core competency, DSCA endeavors to leverage fully-managed DoD and appropriately 
accredited industry solutions wherever possible to minimize the amount of in-house IT resources 
devoted to the operations and sustainment of commodity IT and maximize the use of in-house IT 
resources dedicated to delivering technology solutions that provide direct value to the Agency’s 
mission. In this vein, when considering new solutions and standards, if an approved Software as 
a Service (SaaS) solution can be used to meet a requirement, it should be. If SaaS is not practical, 
capability built on top of an enterprise Platform as a Service (PaaS) is preferred. If no fully-
managed SaaS or PaaS can be utilized, custom software development and/or self-managed 
Commercial Off The Shelf (COTS) software approaches can be considered. The IT standards 
outlined in this document provide direction across all architectural patterns outlined above to 
DSCA-internal program offices and industry partners to use during the IT project planning cycle 
to ensure alignment with overall Agency enterprise IT direction and minimize the amount of 
variance found in the IT portfolio.  
1.3 GUIDANCE TO INDUSTRY 
The guidance provided in this document is designed to provide broad technical guidance to 
ensure consistency in approach to IT programs across the Agency and enable a smooth transition 
from active system development to sustainment - it is not intended to limit technical innovation 
proposed by industry by requiring compliance with fine-grained technical requirements.  DSCA 
has strong preference for solutions proposed by industry that fall within the technical guardrails 
outlined in this document, comply with DOD directives, and are capable of fulfilling the 
intended mission needs. However, no proposals will be disqualified from consideration if they 
suggest an alternative approach. If a proposed solution does not align with standards herein, 
proposals should clearly document why the approach deviates from baseline standards and 
represents better total value to DSCA. 
1.4 POLICIES AND PROCEDURES 
This document is intended to be updated periodically. IM&T will perform review of the 
standards outlined above at least bi-annually to ensure they best align with our mission, allow for 
consideration of new and innovative technologies, and remain consistent with industry best 
practices. Following its initial release, changes to this document will be briefed to the E&ARB 
for concurrence and to IT program managers for the identification of any necessary actions 
required to bring systems into compliance. The standards may also require ad-hoc updates per 
Federal / DoD guidance, cybersecurity issues, etc. In these cases, an ad-hoc review will be 
conducted to redefine and implement the affected standards. 

 IT STANDARDS 
Page 8 
1.5 EXCEPTIONS TO POLICY 
The E&ARB is the governing body responsible for defining and maintaining DSCA IT 
standards. New IT demands and proposals will be evaluated for compliance with IT standards 
during the Solutions Analysis phase of the IM&T Intake to Prioritization (I2P) process. Requests 
for exception to policy are adjudicated by the E&ARB exception process. The E&ARB 
coordinator will provide guidance on preparation of your request to the E&ARB for 
consideration, and coordinate logistics to ensure a timely review of request.  E&ARB 
recommendations are provided to the DSCA CIO, who holds the decision authority to approve or 
deny exception to policy requests, for final determination.

DESCRIPTION

Pre-solicitation/Sources Sought Notice – HEYEX Software

 

Department of Veterans Affairs, Veterans Health Administration, Network Contracting Office 16 (NCO16) 

This SSN is for market research and planning purposes only and shall not be considered an 

Invitation for Bid (IFB), Request for Task Execution Plan, Request for Quotation (RFQ), or a 

Request for Proposal (RFP). Additionally, there is no obligation on the part of the Government to acquire any products or services described in this SSN. Your response to this SSN will be treated only as information for the Government to consider. You will not be entitled to payment for direct or indirect costs that you incur in responding to this SSN. This request does not constitute a solicitation for proposals or the authority to enter negotiations to award a contract. No funds have been authorized, appropriated, or received for this effort. Interested parties are responsible for adequately marking proprietary, restricted, or competition-sensitive information contained in their response. The Government does not intend to pay for the information submitted in response to this SSN. 

The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) for this requirement is 541519 – Other Computer Related Services with a size standard of 150 employees and a Product Service Code (PSC) of 7B20. 

HEYEX SOFTWARE

PURPOSE: The Network Contracting Office (NCO) 16, located at the Galleria Financial Center, 5075 Westheimer Rd, Ste 750, Houston, TX 77030, hereby issues the following Sources Sought to Request for Information (RFI) with the intent of determining the contractor interest, capabilities, and qualifications of potential business to upgrade the SPECTRALIS Software (HEYEX2).  HEYEX2 is equipment that captures high-resolution, cross-sectional images of the retina and optic nerve, which allows providers to diagnose and treat retina and glaucoma-related diseases and conditions for the Central Arkansas Veterans Healthcare System’s (CAVHS) Little Rock/North Little Rock, AR location. 

The Contractor shall upgrade the existing SPECTRALIS Software at CAVHS, provided by Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) trained and certified technician(s) with expertise in the SPECTRALIS Software (HEYEX2).  The Sources Sought will be used to determine if a set-aside for any small business program is appropriate.  The Government anticipates awarding a competitive, firm fixed price contract.  Please review this announcement and respond to the questions below, as well as provide OEM authorization.

The Government is in no way obligated to do business with or enter any form of contract with any person, firm, or other entity that receives or responds to this announcement.

OBJECTIVE: The objective of this SSN/RI is to find qualified contractors with the ability to upgrade the SPECRALIS Software (HEYEX2).

PLACE OF DELIVERY: 2200 Fort Roots Drive, Bldg 182, North Little Rock, AR 72214

RESPONSES REQUESTED: NCO 16 requires all the following information and questions answered in this RFI/SSN: Questions and information that are not provided shall be considered nonresponsive to the SSN/RI, and the contractor may not be considered as part of this market research.

Contractors shall provide their points of contact's name(s), address(es), telephone number(s), and email address(es), and the company's business size, SAM Unique Entity Identification Number.

Is your company a small business, SDBs, HUBZone, or 8A concern?  Please provide proof of qualifications.

Is your company considered small under the NAICS code: 541519?

Are you an authorized distributor/seller for the software listed in the draft SOW?  Please provide evidence/authorization/agreement from OEM.

Include in your capability statement a list of active contracts for commercial, federal, state, and local governments, like this requirement.  List contracts shall provide communication on the government requirement, illustrating the capability for comparison.

For this requirement, is your company available under any of the following:

Government Wide Agency Contract (GWAC)

General Services Administration Services (GSA)

Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ)

Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA)

If so, please list the contract number and SIN.

OPPORTUNITY: NCO 16 is seeking information from potential contractors on their ability to meet this requirement.  THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT FOR INFORMATION (RFI) ONLY.  Small business concerns are encouraged to respond to this Sources Sought to assist NCO 16 in determining potential levels of competition available in the industry.  Contractors shall possess the capability to provide all requirements and objectives.

INSTRUCTIONS AND RESPONSE GUIDELINES: Sources Sought responses are due by Friday, 10 April 2026 at 10:00 AM CST via email to Carmyn.williams@va.gov.

Telephone requests or inquiries will be accepted.

 

Public Information will not be provided and shall be utilized to the full extent possible.

This is a New Requirement.

Please provide the information you deem relevant to respond to the specific inquiries of the Sources Sought. Information provided will be used solely by NCO 16 as "market research" and will not be released outside of the NCO 16 Purchasing and Contract Team.

Draft Statement of Work (SOW)

BACKGROUND: Central Arkansas Veterans Healthcare System (CAVHS) has a requirement to upgrade the SPECTRALIS Software (HEYEX2). 

SCOPE: HEYEX 2 is equipment that captures high-resolution, cross-sectional images of the retina and optic nerve, which allows providers to diagnose and treat retina and glaucoma-related diseases and conditions.

SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS: 

Scalability: HEYEX 2 can scale from a small practice with a single device to a large enterprise with hundreds of imaging devices across multiple sites. 

Database: It supports an SAP® SQL database for stability and scalability, which is essential for managing large volumes of data. 

User Interface: HEYEX 2 features a robust clinical tool set that allows efficient data pre-processing and simultaneous access to patient records by multiple users. 

Integration: The platform interfaces with Electronic Health Records (EHR) systems, eliminating duplicate entries and streamlining workflow. 

Security: HEYEX 2 is designed with cybersecurity features to ensure the security of patient data and images. 

SPECIFICATIONS: Must have the capability to support the following:

• Up to eight (8) imaging modes: Spectral domain Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT), infrared reflectance (IR), MultiColor (MC), 

BluePeak blue laser autofluorescence (BAF), blue reflectance (BR) (sometimes referred to as “red-free”), 

OCT angiography (OCTA), fluorescein angiography (FA), and ICG angiography (ICGA).

• Up to ten (10) simultaneous imaging options: OCT+IR, OCT+BAF, OCT+BR, OCT+MC, OCT+FA, 

OCT+ICGA, BAF+IR, FA+IR, ICGA+IR, FA+ICGA. 

• Up to five (5) separate light sources at the following wavelengths: 880 nanometers SLD, 815 nanometers diode laser, 

786 nanometers diode laser, 518 nanometers diode laser, 486 nanometers diode laser. 

• Fundus image field of view ranges from 8° up to 102° with exchangeable optical lenses.

MAINTENANCE: The maintenance for the HEYEX 2 system will be done annually by our BioMed Team.

TRAINING: The eye clinic already has this system at the stations; they just need to update the software and firmware.

PART II: FULL TEXT OF ANNOUNCEMENT 
 
 
PART IIA: OPPORTUNITY DESCRIPTION 
SAF/CDM is interested in the full range and full scope of innovative commercial items, 
technologies, and services to support various activities . This Commercial Solutions Opening 
(CSO) is intended to  represent a streamlined mechanism for  engaging interested sources, in 
a manner consistent with  the security classification  requirements of this effort, and  utilize 
flexible acquisition procedures consistent with statutue and regulation.  Government 
interest in major program topic areas is  as identified below. 
Respondents to this CSO will reference the particular major program topic area that is the 
subject of their submission to aid in timely government review.  
 
MAJOR PROGRAM THRUST AREAS 
 
 
Innovative approaches technologies, and methodologies that support Concept 
Development by  SAF/CDM to  enable mission partners in the following general 
categories: 
a. Counter strategic competitors' malign influence 
b. Big Data, Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning (Al/ML), technologies and 
processes 
c. Emerging cyber technologies and methodologies 
 
 
PART IIB: INFORMATION CONCERNING POTENTIAL AWARDS 
1. AWARD TYPES: Limited to fixed-price, or fixed-price variant, commercial 
contracts and other transaction agreements (OTA) . See Glossary for specific 
definitions. 
 
NOTE: In accordance with 10 U.S.C. 2371b(f), participants are  hereby notified that 
the government may award a follow-on production contract or  Other Transaction 
Agreement (OTA) for  Prototype Project, for any OTA for  Prototype Project awarded 
under this CSO if: (1) that participant  in the OTA for Prototype Project, or a 
recognized successor in interest to the OTA for Prototype Project, successfully 
completed the entire prototype project provided for in the OTA for Prototype Project, 
as modified; and (2) the OTA for Prototype Project provides for  the award of a follow- 
on production contract or OTA for Prototype Project to  the participant, or a 
recognized successor in interest to the OTA for Prototype Project.  

Page 5 of 22  
 
2. AWARD PARAMETERS: 
a. There is no specific restriction on the number, type, value, or frequency of 
awards that may be made under this CSO 
b. Multiple awards are anticipated and may vary widely in terms of scope, 
duration, and price, consistent with the objectives of this CSO. 
c. The government reserves the right to select for award all, none, some, or 
selected portions thereof, of any proposal that may be received in response to 
this CSO. 
d. Any proposal selected for funding may be incrementally funded at the 
discretion of the government. 
e. The government reserves the right to negotiate proposal scope of work, 
price, and other terms and conditions as may be required. 
f. To promote opportunity for maximum collaboration and rapid engagement 
between multiple respondents, and due to a fiscally constrained operating 
environment, respondents should note that the government places a 
significantly higher value on ideas, concepts, and proposed solutions that 
promote quick testing of applications and/or proof-of-concept scenarios. 
g. White Papers must be submited prior to receipt of Proposals, and 
Proposals may be submitted only as specifically requested by the 
government. See Appendix A and Appendix B for specific instructions. 
 
3. ESTIMATED CSO BUDGET: $100 Million for all awards to be made under this CSO. 
This value is for planning purposes only, as funding at this level is currently not 
available. The government contemplates funding to be made available under• this 
CSO from time-to-time to fund effort consistent with the objectives of this CSO but no 
promises or guarantees are provided. Any award made under this CSO will comply 
with the stated objectives and instructions of this CSO. 
 
PART IIC: PARTICIPANT ELIGIBILITY REQUIREMENTS 
1. ELIGIBILE PARTICIPANTS: All sources capable of addressing the objectives of this 
CSO, consistent with statute and regulation, including the security requirements of 
this effort, are encouraged to respond. 
 
2. PROCUREMENT INT�GRITY, STANDARDS OF CONDUCT, ETHICAL 
CONSIDERATIONS, AND CONFLICTS OF INTEREST: With respect to 
submissions in response to this CSO, submitting parties are notified that that the 
government will assess all submissions for the existence or appearance of any potential 
conflicts of interest. Notwithstanding any government assessment to be conducted as a 
result of submissions to this CSO, it is principally incumbent upon 

Page 6 of 22  
the submitting party to assess all  facts relevant to the existence or potential 
existence of a conflict of interest to disclose such information  to the government for 
appropriate consideration.  Conflicts may be either organizational  or personal. With 
respect to any party that may already be  doing business with SAF/CDM in a capacity 
to provide scientific, engineering, technical assistance (SETA), or similar support,  
such parties are hereby notified that without prior written agency approval and 
authorization, such entity will not be authorized to simultaneously provide SETA , or 
similar support, and  also be a technical performer  in any capacity under this CSO.  
 
 
PART IID: SECURITY REQUIREMENTS 
1. SECURE COMMUNICATIONS: A classified version of this CSO is avalable on the 
NRO ARC. Questions of a security nature should be referred to the security point of 
contact listed in this CSO as applicable . See Part IIF for Government Point of 
Contact information. 
 
2. DD FORM 254 DEPARTMENT OF DEFENSE SECURITY CLASSIFICATION 
SPECIFICATION: This CSO contains security guidance will be included in the DD 
Form 254 Department of Defense Security Classification  Specification Guidance . All 
parties interested in responding to this CSO, will  comply with the security guidance 
included in this CSO at Appendix C, and/or any specific security guidance that  may be 
included in any Call that may be issued under this CSO. As a wide variety of 
responses, as well as potential awards of diverse scope and value and associated 
classification levels under this CSO are possible, the government will  provide award 
specific security details  for individual award actions as required . 
 
3. SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS BASED ON CLASSIFICATION LEVEL: 
 
a. All responses to this CSO must be submitted to: 
Kevin Adams at kevin.adams.20@us.af.mil 
 
b. Follow the guidance below based on particular classification  level, contact 
kevin.adams.20@us.af.mil 
 
PART IIE: REVIEW/EVALUATION CRITERIA 

Page 7 of 22  
1. WHITE PAPERS: White Paper submissions will  be reviewed for interest in 
accordance with the stated objectives of this CSO, which is  to specifically seek 
innovative commercial items,  technologies, and services that support a multitude of 
DoD activities. See Appendix A for White Paper submission requirements.  
 
2. PROPOSALS: Proposal submissions will be evaluated in accordance with the 
following four (4) mandatory stated evaluation criteria, listed in descending order of 
importance: Technical, Importance to Agency Programs, Funds Availability, and Price. 
See Appendix B for Proposal submission requirements.  
 
a. Technical: This CSO seeks various innovative commercial items, 
technologies, and services intended to address existing gaps, revolutionize 
operations and/or capability, and/or significantly strengthen past, current, 
planned, or unforseen operational paradigms.  Technical applications that 
demonstrate break through promise, as determined by the government, will 
be given higher priority consideration than commercial innovation 
applications that merely introduce incremental improvements in  existing 
operations. 
 
b. Importance to Agency Programs: This CSO seeks various innovative 
commercial items, technologies, and services in direct support of a variety of 
Department of Defense (DoD) activities.  Commercial innovation 
applications that support urgent pressing needs, as determined by the 
government, will be given higher priority consideration than those that 
address lower priority focus areas.
 
 
c. Funds Availability: This CSO contemplates multiple awards that represent 
a multitude of different work scopes and dollar values for the most promising 
commercial innovation concepts of interest to  the government, as determined 
by the government for all  awards made under this CSO, including any Call  that 
may be issued, however, only a limited pool of funds may currently be 
available to fund a variety of commercial innovation subjects of interest.  All 
funding is subject to availability and it is within the sole discretion of the 
Government to incrementally fund  any such awards. 
 
 

Page 8 of 22  
d. Price: Price shall be considered to determine that the price is fair and 
reasonable. 
 
PART IIF: GOVERNMENT POINTS OF CONTACT 
1. BUSINESS AND TECHNICAL: Questions of a business and/or technical nature should 
be addressed to the following:  
 
Kevin Adams, contracting officer at Kevin.adams.20@us.af.mi l or 301-203-4766

COMMERCIAL CONTRACT - means a mutually binding legal relationship for commercial 
items, technologies, and/or services obligating the seller to furnish the commercial items, 
technologies, and/or services and the buyer to pay for them. Commercial contracts awarded 
under this CSO are intended to be streamlined award instruments and will follow the 
procedures of FAR Part 12 Acquisition of Commercial Items, FAR Part 13 Simplified 
Acquisition Procedures, and implementing DFARS and AFFARS regulations as required. 
Interested parties to this CSO are encouraged to review FAR 52.212-4 and FAR 52.212-5 for 
standard terms and conditions of a FAR Part 12 commercial contract. [NOTE: FAR Part 15

Commercial contracts awarded under this CSO are limited to fixed price, or fixed-price 
variant, as described in FAR Part 16 Types of Contracts, and implementing DFARS and 
AFFARS regulations.

award instrument that is not subject to the FAR, DFARS, and AFFARS regulations, unless

(OUSD(A&S)) Other Transactions Guide dated November 2018. These award instruments 
represent another potential means to engage interested parties as circumstances may 
warrant. 
See https:llwww.acq.osd.milldpap/cpic/cp/10USC2371bOTs.html for additional information.

a review of submissions by scientific, technological,  or other subject-matter experts. The 
CSO is intended to obtain solutions or new capabilities that fulfill  requirements, close 
capability gaps, or provide potential technological advancements.  Various responses, 
including price, that represent widely different approaches for addressing the  
governments targeted areas of  interest, are anticipated

II. DETAILED INFORMATION ABOUT THE FUNDING OPPORTUNITY 
A.  Program Description  
The Naval Research Laboratory (NRL ) is the Navy's corporate laboratory.  NRL conducts basic 
and applied research for the Navy in a variety of scientific and technical disciplines.  The research 
conducted at NRL is a broadly based multidisciplinary program of scientific research and 
advanced technological development directed toward maritime applications of new and improved 
materials, techniques, equipment, systems and ocean, atmospheric, and space sciences and related 
technologies.  Although NRL conducts most of its research programs within NRL facilities and 
associated warfare centers, NRL intends to fund research conducted with educational facilities 
and industry partners which are related to specific topics included in this BAA announcement. 
NRL announcements may be accessed at https://www.nrl.navy.mil/Doing-Business/Contracts/Broad-
Agency-Announcements/. 
 
NRL requests white papers for long-range Science and Technology (S&T) projects which may 
offer advancement and improvement potential for Navy and Marine Corps operations.  This                                          
announcement emphasizes NRL’s broad role in the competitive funding of meritorious research 
across a spectrum of science and engineering disciplines.  NRL Program Code descriptions and 
NRL science and technology pursuits are provided at 
https://www.nrl.navy.mil/research/directorates -divisions/.  
 
Please note that this BAA announcement is an expression of interest and does not commit the 
Government to make any award or to pay for any proposal preparation costs.  The costs 
associated with proposal preparation in  response to this BAA are not considered allowable 
direct charges under any resultant contract; however, proposal preparation may be an allowable 
expense to the normal bid and proposal indirect cost s specified in FAR 31.205- 18. 
 
 
B.  Federal Award Information   
 
1.  Eligibility for Competition - Proposals for renewals or supplementing existing projects are 
eligible to compete with applications for new Federal awards under this BAA.   
 
2.  Contracted Fundamental Research  - With regard to any restrictions on the conduct or 
outcome of work funded under this BAA . NRL will follow the guidance on and definition of 
“contracted fundamental research” as provided in the Under Secretary of Defense (Acquisition, 
Technology and Logistics) Memorandum of 24 May 2010.  
 
“Contracted fundamental research” in this DoD contractual context includes research performed 
under grants and contracts that are: 
a. funded by Research, Development, Test and Evaluation (RDT&E) Budget Activity 1 
(Basic Research) and conducted by universities or industry or;  
b. funded by RDT&E Budget Activity 2 (Applied Research) and performed on 
university campuses.  The research shall not be considered fundamental in those rare 
and exceptional circumstances where the applied research effort presents a high 

 
 
Cleared for Public Release   Page 7 
likelihood of disclosing performance characteristics of military systems or 
manufacturing technologies that are unique and critical to defense, and where 
agreement on restrictions have been recorded in the contract or grant.  
Pursuant to DoD policy, research performed under grants and contract s that are a) funded by 
Budget Activity 2 (Applied Research) and NOT performed on -campus at a university or b) 
funded by Budget Activity 3 (Advanced Technology Development) or Budget Activity 4 
(Advanced Component Development and Prototypes) does not meet the definition of “contracted 
fundamental research.”   
 
In conformance with the USD (AT&L) guidance and National Security Decision Directive 189, 
NRL will place no restriction on the conduct or reporting of unclassified “contracted 
fundamental research,” except as otherwise required by statute, regulation or executive order.  
For certain research projects, it may be possible that the research being perf ormed by the prime 
contractor is restricted research, while a subcontractor may be conducting “contracted 
fundamental research.”  In those cases, it is the prime contractor’s responsibility in the proposal 
to identify and describe the subcontracted unclass ified research and include a statement 
confirming that the work has been scoped, negotiated, and determined to be fundamental 
research according to the prime contractor and research performer.  
 
As a general practice, fundamental research is awarded by grants to universities and with 
contracts to industry.  Non-fundamental research is normally awarded under contracts and may 
require restrictions during the conduct of research and a DoD pre-publication review of such 
research results due to subject matter sen sitivity.  Potential offerors should consult with the 
appropriate NRL Technical POCs to determine whether the proposed effort would constitute 
fundamental or non-fundamental research . 
FAR Part 35 restricts the use of Broad Agency Announcements (BAAs)  to the acquisition of 
basic and applied research, and that portion of advanced technology development not related to 
the development of a specific system or hardware procurement.  Contracts , grants, and other 
assistance agreements made through BAAs are for scientific study and experimentation directed 
towards advancing state of the art and increasing knowledge or understanding.

the technical approach to be pursued by the offeror selected.

Request for Information (RFI) 
REQUEST FOR INFORMATION 
Air Force Life Cycle Management Center (AFLCMC) 
SOF C-130 Program Office
 Fixed Wing Lightweight Hardware Recovery System (LARS) Hardware Refresh 
CAUTION: 
This Request for Information is published for Market Research purposes only.   The Government is 
conducting market research to identify potential sources that possess the capabilities and experience 
to meet qualification requirements to provide engineering services fo r AFLCMC SOF C-130 Program 
Office system and subsystems.  THIS I S A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI)  ONLY.  In 
accordance with FAR 52.215-3, this RFI is issued solely for information and planning purposes. It 
does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an  RFP in the future.  This 
request for information does not commit the Government to contract for any supply or service 
whatsoever.

incurred in response to this RFI; all costs associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the 
interested party’s expense.  Not responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future RFP 
nor does it ensure participation, if any is issued.  If a solicitation is released, it will be synopsized on the 
Federal Business Opportunities (SAM.gov) website.  It is the responsibility of the potential offerers to

Potential sources must possess the means to provide a design for a refreshed hardware system for the 
Lightweight Airborne Recovery System (LARS) on the HC-130J and MC-130J.  The design for the 
LARS hardware refresh shall be a Form-Fit-Function (FFF) replacement of the current hardware 
components. The hardware components to be analyzed for a FFF replacement shall be the following:

The government is conducting market research to identify potential sources possesing the means to 
design a hardware system for the Lightweight Airborne Recovery System (LARS). Potential sources 
must possess the means to design a refreshed hardware system for the Lightweight Airborne Recovery 
System (LARS) on the HC-130J and MC-130J.  The design for the LARS hardware refresh shall be a

SECTION E - SOLICITATION PROVISIONS

E.1 52.212-1 INSTRUCTIONS TO OFFERORS—COMMERCIAL ITEMS (JAN 2017)

  (a) North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code and small business size standard. The NAICS code and small business size standard for this acquisition appear in Block 10 of the solicitation cover sheet (SF 1449). However, the small business size standard for a concern which submits an offer in its own name, but which proposes to furnish an item which it did not itself manufacture, is 500 employees.

  (b) Submission of offers. Submit signed and dated offers to the office specified in this solicitation at or before the exact time specified in this solicitation. Offers may be submitted on the SF 1449, letterhead stationery, or as otherwise specified in the solicitation. As a minimum, offers must show—

    (1) The solicitation number;

    (2) The time specified in the solicitation for receipt of offers;

    (3) The name, address, and telephone number of the offeror;

    (4) A technical description of the items being offered in sufficient detail to evaluate compliance with the requirements in the solicitation. This may include product literature, or other documents, if necessary;

    (5) Terms of any express warranty;

    (6) Price and any discount terms;

    (7) "Remit to" address, if different than mailing address;

    (8) A completed copy of the representations and certifications at FAR 52.212-3 (see FAR 52.212-3(b) for those representations and certifications that the offeror shall complete electronically);

    (9) Acknowledgment of Solicitation Amendments;

    (10) Past performance information, when included as an evaluation factor, to include recent and relevant contracts for the same or similar items and other references (including contract numbers, points of contact with telephone numbers and other relevant information); and

    (11) If the offer is not submitted on the SF 1449, include a statement specifying the extent of agreement with all terms, conditions, and provisions included in the solicitation. Offers that fail to furnish required representations or information, or reject the terms and conditions of the solicitation may be excluded from consideration.

  (c) Period for acceptance of offers. The offeror agrees to hold the prices in its offer firm for 30 calendar days from the date specified for receipt of offers, unless another time period is specified in an addendum to the solicitation.

  (d) Product samples. When required by the solicitation, product samples shall be submitted at or prior to the time specified for receipt of offers. Unless otherwise specified in this solicitation, these samples shall be submitted at no expense to the Government, and returned at the sender's request and expense, unless they are destroyed during preaward testing.

  (e) Multiple offers. Offerors are encouraged to submit multiple offers presenting alternative terms and conditions, including alternative line items (provided that the alternative line items are consistent with subpart 4.10 of the Federal Acquisition Regulation), or alternative commercial items for satisfying the requirements of this solicitation. Each offer submitted will be evaluated separately.

  (f) Late submissions, modifications, revisions, and withdrawals of offers.

    (1) Offerors are responsible for submitting offers, and any modifications, revisions, or withdrawals, so as to reach the Government office designated in the solicitation by the time specified in the solicitation. If no time is specified in the solicitation, the time for receipt is 4:30 p.m., local time, for the designated Government office on the date that offers or revisions are due.

    (2)(i) Any offer, modification, revision, or withdrawal of an offer received at the Government office designated in the solicitation after the exact time specified for receipt of offers is "late" and will not be considered unless it is received before award is made, the Contracting Officer determines that accepting the late offer would not unduly delay the acquisition; and—

        (A) If it was transmitted through an electronic commerce method authorized by the solicitation, it was received at the initial point of entry to the Government infrastructure not later than 5:00 p.m. one working day prior to the date specified for receipt of offers; or

        (B) There is acceptable evidence to establish that it was received at the Government installation designated for receipt of offers and was under the Government's control prior to the time set for receipt of offers; or

        (C) If this solicitation is a request for proposals, it was the only proposal received.

      (ii) However, a late modification of an otherwise successful offer, that makes its terms more favorable to the Government, will be considered at any time it is received and may be accepted.

    (3) Acceptable evidence to establish the time of receipt at the Government installation includes the time/date stamp of that installation on the offer wrapper, other documentary evidence of receipt maintained by the installation, or oral testimony or statements of Government personnel.

    (4) If an emergency or unanticipated event interrupts normal Government processes so that offers cannot be received at the Government office designated for receipt of offers by the exact time specified in the solicitation, and urgent Government requirements preclude amendment of the solicitation or other notice of an extension of the closing date, the time specified for receipt of offers will be deemed to be extended to the same time of day specified in the solicitation on the first work day on which normal Government processes resume.

    (5) Offers may be withdrawn by written notice received at any time before the exact time set for receipt of offers. Oral offers in response to oral solicitations may be withdrawn orally. If the solicitation authorizes facsimile offers, offers may be withdrawn via facsimile received at any time before the exact time set for receipt of offers, subject to the conditions specified in the solicitation concerning facsimile offers. An offer may be withdrawn in person by an offeror or its authorized representative if, before the exact time set for receipt of offers, the identity of the person requesting withdrawal is established and the person signs a receipt for the offer.

  (g) Contract award (not applicable to Invitation for Bids). The Government intends to evaluate offers and award a contract without discussions with offerors. Therefore, the offeror's initial offer should contain the offeror's best terms from a price and technical standpoint. However, the Government reserves the right to conduct discussions if later determined by the Contracting Officer to be necessary. The Government may reject any or all offers if such action is in the public interest; accept other than the lowest offer; and waive informalities and minor irregularities in offers received.

  (h) Multiple awards. The Government may accept any item or group of items of an offer, unless the offeror qualifies the offer by specific limitations. Unless otherwise provided in the Schedule, offers may not be submitted for quantities less than those specified. The Government reserves the right to make an award on any item for a quantity less than the quantity offered, at the unit prices offered, unless the offeror specifies otherwise in the offer.

  (i) Availability of requirements documents cited in the solicitation.

    (1)(i) The GSA Index of Federal Specifications, Standards and Commercial Item Descriptions, FPMR Part 101-29, and copies of specifications, standards, and commercial item descriptions cited in this solicitation may be obtained for a fee by submitting a request to—

GSA Federal Supply Service Specifications Section 

Suite 8100 470 East L'Enfant Plaza, SW

Washington, DC 20407

Telephone (202) 619-8925 

Facsimile  (202) 619-8978.

    

  (ii) If the General Services Administration, Department of Agriculture, or Department of Veterans Affairs issued this solicitation, a single copy of specifications, standards, and commercial item descriptions cited in this solicitation may be obtained free of charge by submitting a request to the addressee in paragraph (i)(1)(i) of this provision. Additional copies will be issued for a fee.

    (2) Most unclassified Defense specifications and standards may be downloaded from the following ASSIST websites:

      (i) ASSIST (https://assist.dla.mil/online/start/);

      (ii) Quick Search (http://quicksearch.dla.mil/);

      (iii) ASSISTdocs.com (http://assistdocs.com).

    (3) Documents not available from ASSIST may be ordered from the Department of Defense Single Stock Point (DoDSSP) by?

      (i) Using the ASSIST Shopping Wizard (https://assist.dla.mil/wizard/index.cfm);

      (ii) Phoning the DoDSSP Customer Service Desk (215) 697-2179, Mon-Fri, 0730 to 1600 EST; or

      (iii) Ordering from DoDSSP, Building 4, Section D, 700 Robbins Avenue, Philadelphia, PA 19111-5094, Telephone (215) 697-2667/2179, Facsimile (215) 697-1462.

    (4) Nongovernment (voluntary) standards must be obtained from the organization responsible for their preparation, publication, or maintenance.

  (j) Unique entity identifier. (Applies to all offers exceeding $10,000, and offers of $10,000 or less if the solicitation requires the Contractor to be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) database.) The Offeror shall enter, in the block with its name and address on the cover page of its offer, the annotation ‘‘Unique Entity Identifier’’ followed by the unique entity identifier that identifies the Offeror’s name and address. The Offeror also shall enter its Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT) indicator, if applicable. The EFT indicator is a four-character suffix to the unique entity identifier. The suffix is assigned at the discretion of the Offeror to establish additional SAM records for identifying alternative EFT accounts (see subpart 32.11) for the same entity. If the Offeror does not have a unique entity identifier, it should contact the entity designated at www.sam.gov for unique entity identifier establishment directly to obtain one. The Offeror should indicate that it is an offeror for a Government contract when contacting the entity designated at www.sam.gov for establishing the unique entity identifier.

  (k) System for Award Management. Unless exempted by an addendum to this solicitation, by submission of an offer, the offeror acknowledges the requirement that a prospective awardee shall be registered in the SAM database prior to award, during performance and through final payment of any contract resulting from this solicitation. If the Offeror does not become registered in the SAM database in the time prescribed by the Contracting Officer, the Contracting Officer will proceed to award to the next otherwise successful registered Offeror. Offerors may obtain information on registration and annual confirmation requirements via the SAM database accessed through https://www.acquisition.gov.

  (l) Debriefing. If a post-award debriefing is given to requesting offerors, the Government shall disclose the following information, if applicable:

    (1) The agency's evaluation of the significant weak or deficient factors in the debriefed offeror's offer.

    (2) The overall evaluated cost or price and technical rating of the successful and the debriefed offeror and past performance information on the debriefed offeror.

    (3) The overall ranking of all offerors, when any ranking was developed by the agency during source selection.

    (4) A summary of the rationale for award;

    (5) For acquisitions of commercial items, the make and model of the item to be delivered by the successful offeror.

Statement of Work (SOW)

Application Development and Support Services (ADSS)
FMCS

1.0 BACKGROUND

The Federal Mediation and Conciliation Service (FMCS) is an independent federal agency established under the Labor Management Relations Act of 1947 (Taft-Hartley). FMCS provides mediation, conflict resolution, and training services nationwide and internationally.

FMCS operates a cloud-based digital environment built primarily on Microsoft 365 (M365), including SharePoint Online, Microsoft Teams & Integrations, Power Platform components, and integrated third-party systems such as Collabware Collabspace for Electronic Records Management (ERM) and LMS365 for learning management. The environment supports enterprise-wide collaboration, records management, training systems, and operational applications 

FMCS requires contractor support to provide Application Development and Support Services (ADSS) across its enterprise Microsoft 365 environment and all related systems. The Contractor shall deliver comprehensive, full lifecycle IT services, to include application development, modernization, system integration, operations and maintenance (O&M), system assessments, cloud migration support, and security and compliance services. These services will ensure FMCS systems remain secure, reliable, scalable, and aligned with agency mission needs.

1.1 PURPOSE

To obtain comprehensive Application Development and Support Services (ADSS) to support FMCS’s enterprise application ecosystem, cloud platforms, and digital services.

1.2 OBJECTIVE

To provide full lifecycle support for application development, modernization, integration, and operations and maintenance (O&M) across FMCS’s Microsoft 365 environment and all related systems.

1.3 CONTRACT OVERSIGHT

All work shall be performed under the direction of the FMCS Chief Information Officer (CIO) and the Contracting Officer Representative (COR). The contractor’s program management activities shall also provide support for change management, risk management, and performance management in alignment with the CIO’s strategic goals.

1.4 MONTHLY STATUS REPORT (MSR)

The Contractor shall provide a Monthly Status Report (MSR) summarizing project activities, progress, risks, and performance. The MSR shall be submitted no later than the 5th of each month via email to the COR and CIO.

1.4.1 Contents

Executive Summary

Status of all current projects, including: 

Risks and issues

Planned and actual completion dates

Current phase

Disposition (red/yellow/green)

Key milestones

Upcoming activities

Staffing updates

Operations Performance Matrix

1.4.2 Format

One-page coversheet

No more than 3 pages per project

Moderate margins

12-point Times New Roman

1.4.3 Final MSR

A final MSR shall be submitted on the last business day of the final period of performance.

1.4.4 Monthly Financial Dashboard

Delivered monthly to the COR, including:

Planned

Actuals

Variance

2.0 SCOPE OF WORK

The Contractor shall provide full lifecycle Application Development and System Support (ADSS) services across FMCS’s Microsoft 365 ecosystem and associated application environments. The Contractor shall deliver secure, compliant, and modernized solutions that support FMCS mission needs, ensure operational continuity, and enable ongoing modernization.

2.1 Required Services

The Contractor shall provide, at a minimum, the following services:

• Application Development, Modernization, Enhancement, and Integration

Design, develop, enhance, and integrate applications across FMCS environments.

Modernize legacy applications and support cloud-ready architectures.

• Microsoft 365 Platform Support

Provide support for SharePoint Online, Microsoft Teams, Power Apps, Power Pages, and Power Automate.

Maintain and enhance workflows, forms, portals, and collaboration solutions.

• Enterprise Systems Support

Provide operational and enhancement support for FMCS’s Enterprise Records Management (ERM) and Learning Management System (LMS) platforms.

• Operations and Maintenance (O&M)

Deliver ongoing O&M and support for all supported systems, including troubleshooting, patching, monitoring, and performance optimization.

Maintain system documentation, run books, and configuration records.

• System Assessments and Modernization Recommendations

Conduct assessments of existing systems and provide modernization roadmaps aligned with industry standards and best practices.

• Security and Compliance

Ensure compliance with FISMA, NIST, and OMB A-130 requirements.

Ensure Section 508 accessibility compliance for applicable ICT.

Support governance, data management, and security documentation.

• Cloud Migration and Legacy Modernization

Provide planning, analysis, and execution support for cloud migration initiatives.

Modernize legacy systems to align with FMCS’s cloud strategy.

• Enhancement of Systems and Processes

Improve systems, applications, and business processes to align with industry best practices and evolving FMCS needs.

2.2 Contract Line-Item Numbers (CLINs)

CLIN 1 – Operations & Maintenance (O&M), Minor Enhancements, and Support Activities

The Contractor shall:

Provide O&M & support for all Microsoft 365 systems, CCMS, Arbitration systems, and FMCS web.

Perform minor development or enhancement tasks requiring less than 40 hours per issue or task.

Provide security compliance support (Agency/Federal) and transition completed work into O&M.

Provide planning, coordination, and support for new initiatives.

Maintain system documentation, run books, and technical artifacts.

CLIN 2 – Major Enhancements and New Initiatives

The Contractor shall:

Perform major enhancements requiring greater than 40 hours per issue or task.

Support development activities for new initiatives.

Provide security compliance support (Agency/Federal) and transition completed work into O&M.

Develop and maintain documentation, run books, and technical artifacts.

3.0 CONTRACTOR REQUIREMENTS

3.1 Technical Qualifications

The Contractor shall possess:

Demonstrated expertise in Microsoft 365 development and administration

Experience with Power Platform (Power Apps, Power Automate, Power Pages, Power BI), Microsoft Teams Integrations, Azure Services

Experience supporting enterprise content management and LMS systems

Familiarity with federal IT security, compliance, and governance requirements

Experience ensuring achieving ATO and establishing continuous monitoring for compliance with FISMA (High and Moderate), NIST 800-53, OMB A-130, FMCS IT security policies, and Section 508 accessibility requirements for all applicable Information and Communication Technology (ICT).

Experience with cloud migration planning and modern application architecture

Expertise in modern, OpenSource platform capabilities, including application development, data modeling, integration, and migration planning

Ability to document and analyze legacy systems (Dynamics, Power Apps, Dataverse, C#, .NET, SQL Server)

CMMI Level 3 Dev and services

Experience with relational Databases: SQLServer, Postgres, Oracle

Experience design and implement enterprise reports and dashboards

Experience implementing forms and workflows

Experience with regulatory agencies, and distributed userbase across the country and the world.

Experience with environments in Azure cloud

3.2 Experience

Minimum five (5) years providing ADSS in cloud environments

Experience supporting small to medium federal agencies and sub agencies

Experience supporting modernization or migration initiatives

Minimum ten (10) years implementing, modernizing and maintaining enterprise, mission-critical systems

3.3 Personnel Security

Tier 2 (Moderate Risk) background investigation with favorable adjudication

4.0 TASKS

4.1 INVESTIGATION PHASE – 3 Months

The Contractor shall conduct a comprehensive investigation of the FMCS Microsoft 365 environment during the initial three-month period. This phase runs concurrently with the O&M Phase.

4.1.1 Investigation Activities

Kickoff meeting within one (1) week of award.

Evaluate the current M365 environment (SharePoint, Teams, Power Apps, Power Pages, Power BI, LMS365, Collabspace, Dataverse, SQL, Azure Services).

Evaluate incomplete tasks from previous vendor.

Conduct interviews and review processes to identify issues and errors.

Collect requirements for new features and applications.

Submit documentation and present findings.

Provide modernization and mitigation recommendations, including data storage recommendations (SharePoint lists, Dataverse, SQL).

4.2 OPERATIONS AND MAINTENANCE PHASE – 12 Months (Concurrent)

4.2.1 O&M Activities

Redevelop under-functioning Power Apps.

Develop new sites, Power Apps, and Power Pages.

Update recordkeeping strategies to meet NARA/OMB requirements.

Implement new LMS365 features and support separation of LMS and Intranet home sites.

Conduct ongoing O&M for SharePoint, Collabspace, LMS365, Power Apps, Power Pages, and Dataverse.

Provide collaboration and training for FMCS IT staff and the eLearning Training Specialist.

Procure and manage licensing for Collabspace, LMS365, and approved add-ons.

Provide full documentation and training for applications and customizations.

Continuously evaluate FMCS systems against industry standards and recommend enhancements to improve performance, usability, accessibility, maintainability, and security.

4.2.2 Active Applications Currently Maintained Under This Contract

4.3 OPTION PERIODS – Two (2) Option Years, 12 Months Each

Development and modernization

Operations and maintenance

Continued licensing of Collabspace and Collabmail

4.4 COMPLIANCE, GOVERNANCE, AND RECORD MANAGEMENT

The Contractor shall:

Support NARA/OMB compliance

Maintain ERM tools and processes

Ensure adherence to FMCS governance, accessibility, and data-management standards

Ensure all systems comply with FISMA, NIST 800-53, OMB A-130, FMCS IT security policies, and Section 508 accessibility requirements, including conformance with the Revised 508 Standards and WCAG 2.0 Level AA for all applicable Information and Communication Technology (ICT).

Support ATO documentation, POA&Ms, and continuous monitoring

Implement secure development practices

Ensure enhancements align with industry standards for security, accessibility, data governance, and digital service delivery

4.5 LICENSING AND PLATFORM SUPPORT

Assist with license management

Provide optimization recommendations

4.6 OPTIONAL TASK – Legacy Systems, Web, and Cloud Migration Roadmaps

All optional task deliverables shall include:

Cost estimates for recommended modernization activities

Cost-benefit analysis

Industry-standards alignment analysis

Security modernization recommendations

Future-state architecture

Implementation prerequisites and sequencing

4.6.1 CCMS Documentation, Modernization Assessment, Migration Roadmap & Migration Implementation

Current System Overview

Platform: Microsoft Dynamics / Power Apps

Hosting: Azure GCC Medium

Criticality: Medium

Known Issues: Aging architecture, limited extensibility

A. CCMS Documentation

Document architecture, data model, workflows, integrations, security roles, hosting configuration, and compliance posture.

B. CCMS Modernization Assessment

Identify modernization opportunities, technical debt, data strategy improvements, and alignment with industry standards.

C. Migration Roadmap (Planning Only)

Includes feasibility analysis, migration approach, data mapping, integration requirements, security requirements, cost estimates, cost-benefit analysis, future-state architecture, and sequencing.

D. CCMS Migration Implementation (Optional Execution Task)

If exercised, includes configuration, development, data migration, integration, testing, deployment, training, and post-migration support.

E. Deliverables

CCMS Documentation Package

Modernization Findings Report

Migration Roadmap

Optional: Migration Implementation Plan

Optional: Completed Migration

4.6.2 Arbitration System Documentation, Modernization Assessment, Migration Roadmap & Migration Implementation

Current System Overview

Tech Stack: Custom .NET application on Azure VMs with SQL Server backend

Users: Public-facing; ~661 arbitrators; 12,000+ external users

Criticality: High/Medium

Known Issues: Legacy architecture, security vulnerabilities

A. Arbitration System Documentation

Document architecture, SQL schema, workflows, integrations, hosting configuration, and compliance posture.

B. Modernization Assessment

Identify modernization opportunities, data strategy improvements, and alignment with industry standards.

C. Migration Roadmap (Planning Only)

Includes feasibility analysis, SQL mapping, integration requirements, security requirements, cost estimates, cost-benefit analysis, future-state architecture, and sequencing.

D. Arbitration Migration Implementation (Optional Execution Task)

If exercised, includes configuration, development, data migration, integration, testing, deployment, training, and post-migration support.

E. Deliverables

Arbitration Documentation Package

Modernization Findings Report

Migration Roadmap

Optional: Migration Implementation Plan

Optional: Completed Migration

4.6.3 FMCS Web Environment Documentation 

Current System Overview

Tech Stack: WordPress, Apache, AWS

Users: 118,000+ annually

Criticality: High

Known Issues: OMB compliance risks, accessibility issues

Document WordPress configuration, Apache and AWS architecture, DNS/DNSSEC, integrations, security posture, modernization opportunities, and cost estimates.

4.6.4 AWS to Azure Migration Roadmap & Migration Implementation

A. AWS Environment Assessment

The Contractor shall assess the current AWS hosting environment, including workloads, architecture, DNS/DNSSEC, integrations, performance, and security posture.

B. Azure Migration Roadmap (Planning Only)

The Contractor shall develop a detailed migration roadmap including:

Migration strategy

Future-state Azure architecture

Data and application migration plan

Security and compliance mapping

DNS/DNSSEC transition plan

Cost estimates for migration, hosting, re-architecture, and decommissioning

Implementation sequencing and dependencies

C. AWS to Azure Migration Implementation (Optional Execution Task)

If exercised, the Contractor shall:

Prepare Azure environment

Migrate applications, data, and services

Re-platform or re-architect components as required

Transition DNS/DNSSEC

Conduct testing and deployment

Provide post-migration stabilization

Decommission AWS resources

D. Deliverables

AWS Environment Assessment Report

Azure Migration Roadmap

Optional: Migration Implementation Plan

Optional: Completed AWS→Azure Migration

Optional: AWS Decommissioning Report

5.1 Project Plan for Investigation Phase
5.2 Investigation schedule and stakeholder list
5.3 Investigation report
5.4 Monthly Status Reports (MSR)

Inmate Tablet Initiative 
Statement of Objectives 
Page 2 of 32 
 
Executive Summary 
The FBOP Enterprise Tablet Initiative seeks to design, deploy, and sustain a secure, scalable, and 
compliant digital services platform that will provide approximately 150,000 users across 120 facilities 
nationwide with equitable access to education, healthcare, legal, religious, and communication 
resources. The program’s purpose is to enhance service delivery while maintaining strict adherence to 
federal IT security and accessibility standards. 
The initiative encompasses the full lifecycle of planning, procurement, installation, configuration, and 
sustainment of tablet devices and supporting infrastructure. This includes extending wired and wireless 
network access to the housing unit bed level and designated service areas (visitation, education, 
medical, psychology, religious, and recreational spaces) with explicit prohibitions on wireless bridging. 
All tablet devices will support modern Wi-Fi standards (IEEE 802.11a/b/g/n/ac, Wi-Fi 5, Wi-Fi 6, Wi-Fi 6E, 
and forward compatibility with Wi-Fi 7). All other equipment will support wired Ethernet connectivity 
(IEEE 802.3 over Cat6 cabling). Hosting will reside exclusively in GovCloud environments, with 
mandatory FedRAMP High certification and full FISMA compliance. 
The solution must enable secure subscription-based access to streaming, downloadable content, and 
learning modules, while enforcing restrictions such as single-player gaming only. Additional services 
include AM/FM radio - television, mail scanning, and secure international and local calling capabilities. 
Telehealth (psychology and medical visits), religious programming, legal, and educational visits will be 
proctored or confined to approved designated locations. To ensure adherence to FBOP IT Standards the 
vendor must enable FBOP administrative oversight through role-based access controls with nested 
group management up to five layers deep, ensuring granular control across devices, groups, locations, 
and content. 
A seven-day Service Level Agreement (SLA) for device repair or replacement is required to minimize 
downtime, ensure service continuity, and minimize user volatility due to device failure. All software and 
firmware updates must be applied within 14 days of release, with vendors required to provide 
documentation, testing certifications, and ongoing interoperability validation. Accessibility remains a 
cornerstone of the program, with Section 508 compliance and features such as closed captioning, TTY 
integration, and note-taking functionality required to support users with disabilities.

PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT (PWS)

Enterprise Technical Documentation, Modernization Strategy, and Roadmap Development Services.

BACKGROUND

The Federal Mediation and Conciliation Service (FMCS) operates a cloud‑based enterprise digital environment centered on Microsoft 365 (M365) services and integrated commercial and custom applications. The current ecosystem includes SharePoint Online, Microsoft Teams, Power Platform components, Dataverse, SQL Server, Collabspace (ERM), LMS365, Azure cloud services, a .NET C# application, an AWS‑hosted WordPress public website, and multiple legacy custom-developed systems.

FMCS requires performance‑based contractor support to develop authoritative enterprise technical documentation, including system overviews, architecture descriptions, and functional designs that define how FMCS business processes, user interactions, data flows, and system capabilities will operate within the future‑state enterprise environment. The Contractor shall also develop modernization strategies, migration roadmaps, and future‑state architecture recommendations. All services must align with federal IT, cybersecurity, and records management requirements and support the Agency’s long‑term goals for modernization, interoperability, and operational resilience.

2.0 PURPOSE

To obtain performance-based services for enterprise technical documentation,

modernization strategy development, and future-state roadmap generation across the

Agency’s digital ecosystem.

3.0 OBJECTIVE

The Contractor shall deliver comprehensive system documentation packages,

modernization assessments, cloud migration roadmaps, Migration feasibility studies and

analysis of alternatives (Salesforce, Power Platform, Opensource, others), enterprise future-state architecture blueprints, governance and compliance alignment frameworks, and technology strategy plans supporting executive decision-making and digital

transformation.

4.0 PERFORMANCE-BASED SCOPE

The Contractor shall perform work based on measurable outcomes including

documentation completeness, modernization recommendations, compliance traceability,

and roadmap sequencing.

4.1 ENTERPRISE TECHNICAL DOCUMENTATION

Deliver complete documentation packages including architecture diagrams, data

models, workflow documentation, integration maps, security models, hosting

configurations, compliance posture mapping (FISMA, NIST 800-53, OMB A-130,

Section 508), dependency mapping, risk identification, and licensing inventories.

4.2 MODERNIZATION ASSESSMENTS

Provide structured modernization analysis including technical debt assessment, security

posture evaluation, accessibility review, governance assessment, scalability analysis,

prioritized recommendations, and modernization sequencing.

4.3 FUTURE-STATE ARCHITECTURE & STRATEGY

Develop a 1–3 year enterprise modernization strategy including future-state

architecture, application rationalization, cloud optimization roadmap, data strategy,

governance enhancements, security modernization plan, DevSecOps framework,

reporting and analytics strategy, and budgetary planning framework.

4.4 SYSTEM-SPECIFIC DOCUMENTATION & ROADMAPS

Produce documentation and strategy deliverables for:

• Microsoft 365 ecosystem

• CCMS (Dynamics / Power Apps – Azure GCC)

• Arbitration System (.NET / SQL / Azure)

• WordPress Public Web Environment (AWS)

• WordPress AWS to Azure Migration

Each shall include current-state documentation, modernization assessment, cost-benefit

analysis, future-state architecture, and migration sequencing plan.

4.5 COMPLIANCE & GOVERNANCE ALIGNMENT

All deliverables shall align with FISMA , NIST 800-53, OMB A-130, Section 508 (WCAG

2.0 AA), NARA requirements, secure development practices, ATO documentation,

POA&M tracking, and continuous monitoring frameworks.

4.6 INVESTIGATION PHASE (FIRST 90 DAYS)

Deliver Investigation Project Plan, stakeholder interview summaries, system inventory,

architecture baseline report, technical debt register, risk register, and modernization

opportunity matrix within 90 days of award.

4.7 REPORTING REQUIREMENTS

Provide Monthly Status Reports including executive summary, documentation progress,

roadmap development status, risks/issues, milestones, and financial dashboard

(planned vs actual vs variance).

5.0 DELIVERABLE SCHEDULE

• Investigation Project Plan – 20 Days; Day 20

• Baseline Documentation – 45 Days; Day 45

• System Documentation Packages – Rolling Delivery

• Modernization Reports – Within 45 Days after Baseline; Day 90

• Enterprise Strategy Report – 60 Days; Day 60

• Migration Roadmaps – 90 Days; Day 90

• Final Consolidated Strategy & Roadmap – 120 Days; Day 120

6.0 PERFORMANCE METRICS

• Documentation Accuracy ≥90%

• Cost Estimate Reliability ±20%

• Compliance Coverage 100%

• On-Time Delivery ≥90%

7.0 PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE

Base Period: 4 months

8.0 ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

Deliverables will be accepted when documentation is complete and accurate, roadmaps

include sequencing and cost models, compliance traceability is validated, and executive

stakeholders approve.

SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE 
Enterprise Technical Documentation, Modernization 
Strategy, and Roadmap Development Services 
Federal Mediation and Conciliation Service (FMCS) 
NAICS Codes Under Consideration: 541512, 541519 
_________________________________________________________________________________________________________ 
GENERAL INFORMATION 
THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT ANNOUNCEMENT ONLY. This notice is issued for market 
research purposes in accordance with FAR Part 10. This announcement does not constitute 
a solicitation or a promise to issue a solicitation in the future. The Government will not pay 
for any information submitted or for any costs associated with providing a response to this 
notice. 
 
The Federal Mediation and Conciliation Service (FMCS) is conducting market research to 
identify qualified and interested firms capable of providing enterprise technical 
documentation, modernization strategy development, and roadmap development services. 
 
The Government intends to use responses to this Sources Sought notice to support market 
research, refine the draft scope, develop an Independent Government Cost Estimate (IGCE), 
and determine the appropriate acquisition strategy, including potential small business set-
aside decisions. 
BACKGROUND 
FMCS operates a cloud-based enterprise digital environment centered on Microsoft 365 
(M365) and integrated systems including SharePoint Online, Microsoft Teams, Power 
Platform, Dataverse, SQL Server, Collabspace (ERM), LMS365, Azure cloud services, custom 
.NET applications, AWS-hosted WordPress environments, and legacy systems. 
REQUIREMENT OVERVIEW 
FMCS seeks contractor support to develop enterprise technical documentation, 
modernization strategies, migration roadmaps, future-state architecture, and 
governance/compliance frameworks supporting agency modernization and executive 
decision-making. 
SCOPE SUMMARY 
• Enterprise technical documentation (architecture diagrams, workflows, data 
models, integration maps) 

• Modernization assessments (technical debt, security posture, scalability, 
governance) 
• Future-state architecture and strategy (1–3 year roadmap, cloud optimization, 
DevSecOps) 
• System-specific documentation and roadmaps (M365, CCMS, Arbitration system, 
WordPress, migration planning) 
INVESTIGATION PHASE 
• System inventory and stakeholder interviews 
• Architecture baseline assessment 
• Risk and technical debt identification 
• Modernization opportunity analysis 
• This phase is anticipated to occur within the first 90 days of performance. 
DELIVERABLES (REPRESENTATIVE) 
• Investigation Project Plan 
• Baseline Documentation 
• System Documentation Packages 
• Modernization Reports 
• Enterprise Strategy Report 
• Migration Roadmaps 
• Final Consolidated Strategy 
PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE 
Base Period: Approximately 4 months 
The Government requests feedback from industry on whether the proposed period of 
performance is appropriate for the scope of work described. 
REQUESTED INFORMATION FROM INDUSTRY 
A. Company Information 
• Company name 
• UEI 
• CAGE Code 
• Business size 
• Socioeconomic status 
• Point of contact 
B. Capability Statement 
• Experience with enterprise documentation 

• Experience with modernization strategy 
• Experience with cloud migration planning 
• Experience supporting federal IT environments 
C. Relevant Experience 
• Similar contracts 
• Scope and complexity 
• Contract value 
• Period of performance 
D. Pricing / IGCE SUPPORT (IMPORTANT) 
• Provide a Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) 
• Include labor categories, hours, and rates if available 
• Break out assumptions for investigation phase, documentation, and strategy work 
E. Acquisition Strategy Input 
• Recommended contract type 
• Recommended pricing structure 
• The Government anticipates a performance-based contract structure with defined 
deliverables and requests industry feedback on the most appropriate contract type 
for this requirement, including whether a Firm Fixed Price (FFP) or hybrid approach 
is most suitable. 
• Recommended approach (deliverable vs labor based) 
F. NAICS Recommendation 
Recommend the most appropriate NAICS code and provide rationale. 
G. Feedback on Draft Requirement 
• Identify unclear requirements 
• Suggest improvements 
• Identify restrictive elements 
H. Labor Categories 
Provide typical staffing mix for this type of work. 
I. Contract Vehicles 
Identify relevant contract vehicles (GSA MAS, GWACs, etc.). 
RESPONSE INSTRUCTIONS 

Responses shall include the subject line: 'Sources Sought Response – FMCS Enterprise 
Documentation & Strategy' 
 
Responses are due by: April 10, 2026 at 5:00 PM EST 
 
Submit responses to: 
Bronson Madero 
bmadero@fmcs.gov 
 
Telephone inquiries will not be accepted. 
IMPORTANT NOTICE 
This notice is issued solely for market research purposes and does not constitute a 
solicitation. The Government does not intend to award a contract based solely on responses.

Attachment H: Intellectual Property/Data Rights Assertions

Cyber Physical Systems Executing in Real Time (CyPhER) Forge

INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY/DATA RIGHTS SUBMISSIONS

Proposers shall submit the Intellectual Property (IP)/Data Rights Assertions as part of the Oral Proposal Package (OPP) to be considered for an award under this Program Solicitation (PS). Guidance on compiling the OPP can be found in Attachment C – Oral Proposal Package Instructions and Templates. 

Proposers must complete this form in a manner consistent with CyPhER Forge’s Intellectual Property and Data Rights strategy outlined in Section 6.4. of the PS. All assertions must be clearly justified.

IP/Data Rights Assertion submissions shall address both the Phase 1 Base and Phase 2 Option. Do not submit separate IP/Data Rights Assertion materials for each phase. 

Reference the template included in this Attachment for guidance on content requirements. 

Intellectual Property (IP) and Data Rights

Describe the proposed IP and data assertion rights for DTs, AI Test Agents, CyPhERs, related artifacts generated during program performance, and automated pipelines for generating DTs and AI Test Agents, as described in Section 6.4 of the PS. The Proposer shall provide a plan to transition DTs, AI Test Agents, CyPhERs, and automated pipelines for creating DTs, AI Test Agents, and CyPhERs at the end of the program.

Provide the following information, as applicable. Note: DARPA will assume unlimited rights to all IP not explicitly identified as restricted in the proposal.

For each data or software item for which restrictions are asserted (i.e., anything less than Unlimited Rights), Proposers must:

Identify the specific tasks within the PS, Work Breakdown Structure (WBS), or Task Description Document (TDD) to which the item applies and explain its relevance.

Specify the data or software to be delivered (not just the title). If the item is not a standalone deliverable, describe its connection to or integration with other OT for Prototype Project award deliverables.

For items developed wholly or partially at private expense, provide a development timeline with key milestones and supporting documentation, such as private funding records, evidence of development history, and all proprietary information to confirm no Government funds were used.

Certify the item will not be developed, modified, or altered using Government funds during OT for Prototype Project award performance. 

Technical Data and Computer Software

In Table 1, the Proposer shall identify all assertions for any IP restrictions on technical data or any non-commercial computer software to be provided to DARPA during the period of performance for the CyPhER Forge program.

Identify all proprietary claims to results, prototypes, deliverables or systems supporting and/or necessary for the use of the proposed research, results, prototypes and/or deliverables. Provide a short summary for each item asserted with less than unlimited rights that describes the nature of the restriction and the intended use of the IP in the conduct of the proposed research. 

“Data” is more than computer-related items. It includes, for example, DTs, AI Test Agents, Integrated CyPhERs, artifacts generated by these, and processing data. Reference Section 7, Definitions within the PS. 

Note: Open-source software is considered “commercial” software under relevant Government regulations and should be included in Table 2.  

Table 1 - Non-Commercial Software or Data

*The “Asserted Rights Category” column must use the definitions in Section 7, Definitions of the PS (e.g., Unlimited rights, Government purpose rights, limited rights).

In Table 2, the Proposer shall identify any commercial software (including open-source) or data that shall be used during the period of performance of the CyPhER Forge program or be incorporated into deliverables that will be provided with any restrictions on its use or distribution. The Proposer shall include libraries, runtime systems, and operating systems in Table 2. If there are no such items, the required response in Table 2 is “None.”

Table 2 – Commercial Software or Data

Patent Dependencies

The Proposer shall identify all patented inventions owned by or assigned to the Proposer, subcontractor/teaming partners, and individuals of those entities.  

In Table 3, the Proposer shall provide documentation proving ownership or possession of appropriate licensing rights to all patented inventions to be used for the CyPhER Forge program. Attachment B: Abstract Instructions and Template

Cyber Physical Systems Executing in Real Time (CyPhER) Forge

ABSTRACT SUBMISSON

Proposers must submit both an Abstract Summary Slide and a written Abstract to be considered to receive an invitation to submit an OPP under this Program Solicitation (PS).

Submissions must comply with the formatting and content requirements specified in:  

Attachment A – Abstract Summary Slide Template 

Attachment B – Abstract Instructions and Template 

Abstract Summary Slide and written Abstract submissions shall use file name conventions: 

“Attachment A – Company Name – CyPhER Forge”

“Attachment B – Company Name – CyPhER Forge”

Abstract submissions shall address both the Phase 1 Base, and Phase 2 Option. Do not submit a separate Abstract Summary Slide or written Abstract for each phase. 

Abstract Summary Slide Instructions

Use of Attachment A – Abstract Summary Slide Template is mandatory. Proposers shall submit the Abstract Summary Slide in Microsoft PowerPoint and PDF format. Font size no smaller than 10-point Tahoma shall be used; 8-point may be used for figures, tables, and charts. Reference  the template for content requirements. Content requirements on the template should be deleted prior to submitting.  

Abstract Submission Instructions

Font size no smaller than 12-point Times New Roman shall be used; 8- or 10-point may be used for figures, tables, and charts. 

The written Abstract shall not exceed the maximum page limits defined below:

Abstract Cover Sheet (mandatory, one (1) page maximum)

Executive Summary, Technical Understanding and Approach, and Technical Ability (mandatory, 10 pages maximum including text, figures, tables, charts, etc.)

Compute Approach (mandatory, one (1) page maximum)

Management Approach (mandatory, one (1) page maximum)

Estimated Cost (mandatory, two (2) pages maximum)

References (mandatory, four (4) pages maximum)

Executive Summary 

Provide a summary of the technical problems the program seeks to solve. This summary shall be stated in the Proposer’s own words without any “copy and paste” from this PS. The goal is for the Proposer to demonstrate a clear understanding of the program’s purpose and goals.

Provide a clear and compelling summary of the proposed technical understanding and approach to achieve the program’s goals and metrics. For each technical pillar, the Proposer shall describe the unique approach, its novelty compared to the current state-of-the-art, challenges associated with this proposed approach, and an explanation as to why it will succeed. Clearly articulate the connections between the technical pillars and how advancements in one (1) area will enable capabilities in others.

Detail the proposed method for creating real-time, multi-physics Surrogate Models (SMs) from High-Fidelity Models (HFMs). 

Explain how the proposed approach will couple the five (5) core physics domains (aerodynamics, structures, propulsion, servodynamics, and controls).

Describe how the Proposer will achieve the real-time prediction speeds required by the program, moving beyond the days/weeks cycle time of traditional methods.

Justify why the chosen modeling technique is superior to alternatives for this specific application.

Provide rationale for why the proposed UQ approach is robust, scalable to a complex multi-physics system, and will be successful where others have struggled.

Technical Pillar 3: Continuous Data Assimilation

Articulate how the proposed approach creates a single, Government-owned truth source that is more valuable than the raw data itself and enables the confidence-driven test paradigm.

Describe the proposed approach to creating Artificial Intelligence (AI) test agents that can adaptively plan, execute, and analyze flight sciences test sorties to improve the accuracy and quantified uncertainty of the DT safely and efficiently while respecting user-defined risk tolerance, user-defined test objectives, and user-defined constraints.

Address how the proposed approach will also work to detect and avoid unknown or undefined risks (i.e., extreme events), not just proximity to known safety boundaries.

Address how the proposed approach will work in off-line training as well as in real-time safety assurance.
