REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) - Consumer-Reported 
Veriﬁcation Data Sources for State Medicaid Eligibility 
Determination 
NOTICE ID: 269998 
POSTED DATE: March 27, 2026 
RESPONSE DATE: April 17, 2026, 5:00 PM Eastern Time (Responses will be considered as 
received). 
THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) ONLY . THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION. This 
notice is issued solely for market research and information planning. This RFI does not 
constitute a solicitation for proposals, a request for quotations, or an invitation for bids. 
Responses to this RFI are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a 
binding contract. CMS is under no obligation to issue a solicitation or award a contract 
based on responses received. No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated 
with providing information in response to this RFI or any follow-on information requests. 
This RFI is issued for market research purposes only. Questions regarding this RFI will not 
be accepted or answered. Vendors should address any assumptions or clariﬁcations within 
their written response submission. 
SECTION 1 —  INTRODUCTION AND PURPOSE 
1.1 Purpose 
The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) is conducting market research to 
identify and assess industry capabilities for providing consumer-reported veriﬁcation data 
services to support state Medicaid agencies in meeting federal eligibility determination 
requirements. 
CMS is developing the EMMY (Eligibility Made Easy) platform, a centralized, API-based data 
exchange infrastructure designed to provide participating state Medicaid agencies with 
standardized access to trusted third-party data sources for eligibility veriﬁcation. This RFI 
supports CMS's broader market intelligence efforts to understand the landscape of 
available data sources, vendor capabilities, and potential approaches to meeting CMS's 
veriﬁcation data needs across multiple data domains. 
This RFI seeks information across two related but distinct areas of interest: 

Page 2 of 18 
 
1. Immediate Focus — Payroll and Employment Veriﬁcation Data: CMS has an 
operational need for authoritative payroll and employment veriﬁcation data to 
support Medicaid eligibility determinations and to prepare for community 
engagement veriﬁcation requirements established under the Working Families Tax 
Cut Act (WFTCA), which takes effect January 2027, subject to implementing 
guidance. This data domain represents the primary procurement focus of this 
market research effort. 
 
2. Broader Strategic Interest — Additional Veriﬁcation Data Domains: CMS is also 
gathering market intelligence on industry capabilities across other veriﬁcation data 
domains relevant to Medicaid eligibility and beneﬁts program compliance, including 
but not limited to educational enrollment veriﬁcation, asset and ﬁnancial 
veriﬁcation, and identity veriﬁcation. Responses addressing these additional 
domains will inform CMS's broader platform strategy and ongoing acquisition 
planning activities. Vendors should note that this RFI does not signal a single 
consolidated procurement across all data domains described. CMS's approach to 
acquiring services in these additional domains, including whether and how each 
domain is addressed, will be determined through ongoing acquisition planning. 
Vendors are encouraged to respond to the areas most relevant to their capabilities. 
Responses addressing only one data domain are equally welcome as responses 
addressing multiple domains. 
1.2 Background 
State Medicaid agencies are required to verify applicant-provided information related to 
employment status, earnings, and other eligibility factors when evaluating eligibility for 
Medicaid and other beneﬁts programs. The current veriﬁcation landscape presents 
signiﬁcant operational challenges: many states rely on manual veriﬁcation processes, 
maintain fragmented direct relationships with individual data providers, and face 
inconsistent access to authoritative data sources, resulting in administrative burden on 
beneﬁciaries, processing delays, and duplicative costs across states. These challenges are 
not limited to payroll and employment data; they extend across the full range of veriﬁcation 
data types that states rely upon to make accurate, timely eligibility determinations. 
CMS is developing the EMMY platform, through the Center for Medicaid and CHIP Services 
(CMCS), to address these challenges by enabling states to access trusted veriﬁcation data 
sources through a standardized, centralized federal service, reducing burden, improving 
consistency, and supporting cost-effective access at scale. An anticipated primary 
objective of the EMMY platform is to provide participating state Medicaid agencies with a 

Page 3 of 18 
 
standardized, centralized mechanism to veriﬁcation services across relevant data 
domains, reducing the need for states to independently negotiate and maintain separate 
vendor agreements and associated costs.  
CMS is pursuing veriﬁcation data integration across multiple domains as part of its broader 
eligibility modernization strategy, with individual data domains being addressed through a 
combination of acquisition efforts and workstreams. 
The urgency of this effort is reinforced by the Working Families Tax Cut Act (WFTCA), which 
establishes community engagement requirements for certain Medicaid beneﬁciaries 
effective January 2027, subject to implementing guidance. Under the WFTCA, certain 
beneﬁciaries must verify participation in qualifying activities, which may include 
employment, work activities, and educational enrollment, as a condition of eligibility. 
States will need reliable, scalable access to veriﬁcation data across multiple domains to 
implement these compliance workﬂows. CMS is focused on achieving integration 
readiness for payroll and employment veriﬁcation in advance of the statutory deadline, 
while simultaneously gathering market intelligence on the broader landscape of 
veriﬁcation data services to inform its ongoing platform strategy. 
Pending Legislation Note: H.R. 1 (Public Law 119-21), commonly referred to as the Working 
Families Tax Cut Act (WFTCA), has been enacted. The January 2027 effective date 
referenced in this RFI pertains speciﬁcally to the WFTCA's community engagement 
veriﬁcation requirements. References to those requirements in this RFI are subject to 
implementing guidance and federal rulemaking, which are still being developed. CMS is 
conducting this market research in advance of ﬁnal implementing guidance to ensure 
readiness, and vendor responses should be scoped accordingly. 
1.3 EMMY Platform Context 
CMS is developing EMMY as a platform to support Medicaid eligibility veriﬁcation and 
program compliance workﬂows through trusted third-party data sources. EMMY is being 
designed as an API-based service that will enable participating state Medicaid agencies to 
submit veriﬁcation requests and receive authoritative data responses through a 
standardized, secure interface, replacing fragmented state-level approaches with a shared 
federal capability. 
CMS intends for EMMY to serve as an extensible platform capable of integrating multiple 
veriﬁcation data domains over time. The payroll and employment veriﬁcation integration 
represents the immediate acquisition focus that this market research effort is designed to 
support. Other veriﬁcation data domains described in this RFI are areas of strategic interest 
that CMS is evaluating as part of its broader eligibility modernization strategy. This RFI is a 

Page 4 of 18 
 
market research instrument spanning all of those domains, gathering intelligence across 
the full veriﬁcation data landscape. 
EMMY is being developed as an open-source platform. CMS is committed to open, 
interoperable integration approaches that avoid proprietary vendor lock-in and preserve 
CMS's ability to adapt its platform architecture over time. Vendors are encouraged to 
describe their current API architecture and data exchange approach, and to identify any 
aspects of their technical architecture or licensing model that would present challenges in 
supporting integration with an open-source, interoperable federal platform, including how 
their data assets and API layer are structured to support open integration. 
SECTION 2 —  SCOPE OF MARKET RESEARCH 
CMS is seeking information on industry capabilities across multiple veriﬁcation data 
domains relevant to Medicaid eligibility determination and beneﬁts program compliance. 
This section describes the scope of CMS's market research interest and provides context to 
help vendors assess their potential ﬁt and respond meaningfully. 
This RFI gathers market research across multiple veriﬁcation data domains to inform CMS's 
broader eligibility veriﬁcation modernization strategy. Payroll and employment veriﬁcation 
(Section 2.1) is the immediate acquisition focus of this market research effort. Other data 
domains described in this RFI may be the subject of separate CMS acquisition activities; 
this RFI does not represent the full scope of CMS's eligibility veriﬁcation efforts and should 
not be interpreted as signaling a single consolidated procurement. Vendors should 
respond to the domains most relevant to their current capabilities. Responses addressing 
a single data domain are equally welcome as responses addressing multiple domains. 
2.1 Payroll and Employment Veriﬁcation (Immediate Acquisition Focus) 
CMS has a need for authoritative payroll and employment veriﬁcation data to support 
Medicaid income-based eligibility determinations and to prepare for community 
engagement veriﬁcation requirements established under the WFTCA, effective January 
2027, subject to implementing guidance. 
CMS is seeking to understand the market's capacity to provide services that support the 
following general outcomes: 
• Veriﬁcation of an individual's current or recent employment status, including full-
time, part-time, seasonal, and other employment classiﬁcations 
• Veriﬁcation of earnings and payroll data sufficient to support income-based 
eligibility determinations 

Page 5 of 18 
 
• Coverage across a broad range of employer types, industries, and geographies, 
including awareness of known coverage gaps for populations such as gig workers, 
self-employed individuals, and workers in informal or non-traditional employment 
arrangements 
• Data that is sufficiently current and frequently refreshed, including real-time or 
near-real-time availability where feasible, to support reliable eligibility 
determinations 
• Consent-based veriﬁcation workﬂows that respect applicable privacy and 
employment data protections, including the Fair Credit Reporting Act (FCRA) 
• Secure data exchange compatible with federal integration standards and the EMMY 
platform architecture 
CMS is interested in understanding both the current state of the market for these services 
and vendors' perspectives on what is technically and commercially feasible within the 
timeframes relevant to this requirement. 
2.2 Educational Enrollment Veriﬁcation (Strategic Market Intelligence) 
CMS is gathering market intelligence on industry capabilities for educational enrollment 
veriﬁcation data. Under the WFTCA, educational enrollment may constitute a qualifying 
community engagement activity, creating a potential future need for enrollment veriﬁcation 
at scale. 
CMS is seeking to understand the market's capacity to support the following general 
outcomes: 
• Veriﬁcation of an individual's current enrollment status at an educational institution, 
including degree or program information where available 
• Veriﬁcation of enrollment dates, academic terms, and enrollment intensity (full-
time versus part-time) 
• Coverage across institution types, including two-year colleges, four-year 
universities, vocational and trade programs, and other qualifying educational 
programs, with institution name and location included in veriﬁcation response 
where available 
• Consent-based veriﬁcation workﬂows consistent with applicable privacy 
requirements, including the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA) and 
other applicable laws 
• Secure data exchange compatible with federal integration standards 
CMS is interested in understanding the current landscape of educational enrollment data 
sources, the nature and breadth of available coverage, and any legal or regulatory 

Page 6 of 18 
 
considerations speciﬁc to this data domain that would affect its use for Medicaid eligibility 
purposes. 
2.3 Asset and Financial Veriﬁcation 
CMS is gathering market intelligence on industry capabilities for asset and ﬁnancial 
veriﬁcation data relevant to Medicaid eligibility determinations. Areas of general interest 
include: 
• Veriﬁcation of ﬁnancial account ownership and balances 
• Veriﬁcation of ﬁnancial asset holdings relevant to eligibility determinations 
• Coverage across ﬁnancial institution types and account categories 
• Consent-based veriﬁcation workﬂows consistent with applicable ﬁnancial privacy 
requirements, including the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act (GLBA) and other applicable 
law 
• Secure data exchange compatible with federal integration standards 
CMS is interested in understanding the nature and breadth of available data sources in this 
domain, as well as any legal or regulatory constraints that would affect the use of ﬁnancial 
veriﬁcation data for Medicaid eligibility purposes. 
2.4 Identity Veriﬁcation 
CMS is gathering market intelligence on industry capabilities for identity veriﬁcation and 
prooﬁng services relevant to Medicaid eligibility workﬂows. Areas of general interest 
include: 
• Identity prooﬁng and authentication services 
• Social Security Number (SSN) validation 
• Address and date of birth veriﬁcation 
• Fraud detection and prevention capabilities relevant to beneﬁts eligibility contexts 
• Integration approaches for identity veriﬁcation within eligibility determination 
workﬂows 
CMS is interested in understanding how identity veriﬁcation services are currently delivered 
in government beneﬁts contexts, including applicable compliance frameworks and 
integration approaches. 
2.5 Multi-Source and Integrated Veriﬁcation Platforms 
CMS is also interested in understanding whether vendors offer integrated platforms that 
provide access to multiple veriﬁcation data types through a uniﬁed interface or API. Areas 
of general interest include: 

Page 7 of 18 
 
• Single-API access to multiple veriﬁcation data domains (e.g., payroll, enrollment, 
identity) 
• Approaches to managing consent across multiple data domains through a single 
workﬂow 
• Uniﬁed reporting and case management capabilities 
• Commercial models for multi-domain platform access 
• Extensibility and the ability to add new data domains over time

THIS IS A NOTICE ONLY FOR SUBMISSION OF ARCHITECT-ENGINEERING QUALIFICATION PACKAGES, SF 330.

Network Contract Office 21 (NCO 21) is seeking Architectural/Engineering Firms to submit Standard Form (SF) 330s regarding the Statement of Work (SOW) attached to this request. The project is for The Veterans Affairs (VA) Palo Alto Health Care System located at 1080 Innovation Way, Sunnyvale California.

General Intent: Design requirement to facilitate a construction project to renovate approximately 21,000 GSF of existing shell space on the first floor of a 2-story building, for dry lab research and associated site improvements, to include surface parking.

The applicable North American Industry Classiﬁcation System (NAICS) Code is 541330, Engineering Services, and the small business size standard is $25.5 million U.S. dollars. The Product or Service Code is C1DA.

This procurement is a 100% Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) set aside under the Veterans First Contracting program as required by 38 U.S.C. Sections 8127-8128, as implemented under VA Acquisition Regulation (VAAR) 819.7. The term SDVOSB under the Veterans First Contracting program has the same meaning as service-disabled veteran-owned small business concern deﬁned in FAR subpart 2.101, except for acquisitions authorized by 38 U.S.C. 8127 and 8128 for the Veterans First Contracting Program. These businesses must be listed as veriﬁed in the Small Business Administration (SBA) Small Business Search (SBS) database at https://search.certiﬁcations.sba.gov/ in addition to meeting the NAICS code small business size standard to be eligible for award under the Veterans First Contracting Program.

All SDVOSB ﬁrms that submit SF 330s must be listed as veriﬁed in the Small Business Administration (SBA) Small Business Search (SBS) database to be considered for this procurement. Offers from unveriﬁed SDVOSBs are considered deﬁcient and will not be evaluated further. A ﬁrm’s status will be veriﬁed in SBS at time of receipt of the SF330, prior to conducting evaluations/interviews/discussions, and prior to award. This set aside process is in keeping with VA Implementation of the Veterans First Contracting Program, FAR Part 19, and the requirements of FAR 36.202 for acquiring Architect-Engineer Services.

This notice serves as the Governments call for Standard Form (SF) 330s from interested SDVOSB Architectural/Engineering (A/E) Firms concerns. Firms that meet the requirements described in this announcement are invited to submit one (1) electronic copy of their SF 330 package via e-mail to Jose A. Hernandez at jose.hernandez1@va.gov and Alison Weinstein at alison.weinstein@va.gov by April 24, 2026 at 8:00 AM PST. SF 330, Part I may include evidence of experience and capabilities the applicant considers relevant. Part II shall be submitted for each proposed consultant’s office involved.

The Government will evaluate SF 330’s received in response to this notice to identify at least three (3) of the most highly qualiﬁed SDVOSB ﬁrms to perform the required services. The Government will then hold discussions/interviews with the most highly qualiﬁed SDVOSB ﬁrms based on the evaluation factors listed in this notice (see below).

Evaluation Factors

The following evaluation criteria, listed in descending factor order of importance and weight, will be used for the SF330 evaluation. Sub-factors when combined represent the overall score for the factor.

Factor 1: Professional Qualiﬁcations

Professional qualiﬁcations necessary for satisfactory performance of A/E services necessary to complete the type of work required for this project.

Architects must be licensed in any state of the United States of America.

Mechanical, Electrical, and Fire Protection Engineer must be licensed engineers registered in any state of the United States of America.

Structural Engineer must be licensed in any state of the United States of America.

Factor 2: Specialized Experience and Technical Competence

Subfactor 2A - Specialized experience and technical competence in designing Air Handler Unit Projects. All lead Architects, Project Managers, Mechanical, Electrical and Fire Protection engineers must show 3 projects of similar size or scope.

Subfactor 2B - Speciﬁc experience and qualiﬁcations of personnel proposed for assignment to this project and their record of working together as a team. All lead Architects, Project Managers, Mechanical, Electrical and Fire Protection engineers must have 5+ years’ experience in a hospital setting.

Subfactor 2C – Experience in construction period services to include professional ﬁeld inspections during the construction period, review of construction submittals, support in answering requests for information during the construction period, and support construction contract changes including drafting statements of work and cost estimates.

Factor 3: Capacity to accomplish the work in the required time. Availability of all lead Architects, Project Managers, Mechanical, Electrical and Fire protection Engineer must be submitted as a percentage in the SF-330. Example: Mechanical Engineer is 40% available based on other concurrent projects (list projects).

Factor 4: Past Performance

Past performance on contracts with Government agencies and private industry in terms of cost control, quality of work, and compliance with performance schedules. Must submit completed Contractor Performance Assessment Report System (CPARS) evaluations for at least three (3) but no more than five (5) projects in similar scope, size, and complexity within the past five (5) years from the date of the posting of this solicitation to sam.gov. If a CPARS is available for at least three projects, it must be submitted.

Factor 5: Location

Location in the general geographical area of the project and knowledge of the locality of the project; provided, that application of this criterion leaves an appropriate number of qualiﬁed ﬁrms, given the nature and size of the project.

The Technical Evaluation Board (TEB) will prepare a report recommending three (3) ﬁrms, in order of preference, from the ﬁrms with which discussions have been conducted. The TEB shall select 3 ﬁrms, in order of preference, based on the combined SF 330 and discussion/interview score, that are considered to be the most highly qualiﬁed to perform the required services.

Selection shall be based on the evaluation factors. The selection authority shall review the recommendations of the evaluation board and shall, with the advice of appropriate technical and staff representatives, make the ﬁnal selection. This ﬁnal selection shall be a listing, in order of preference, of the ﬁrms considered most highly qualiﬁed to perform the work. If the ﬁrm listed as the most preferred is not the ﬁrm recommended as the most highly qualiﬁed by the evaluation board, the selection authority shall provide for the contract ﬁle a written explanation of the reason for the preference.

Negotiations shall be made with the top-rated ﬁrm. Where negotiations with the top-rated highly qualiﬁed ﬁrm are unsuccessful, the contracting officer shall terminate the negotiations and undertake negotiations with the ﬁrm next in order of preference.

If a mutually satisfactory contract cannot be negotiated, the contracting officer shall obtain a written ﬁnal proposal revision from the ﬁrm and notify the ﬁrm that negotiations have been terminated. The Contracting Officer will then initiate negotiations with the next ﬁrm on the ﬁnal selection list. This procedure shall be continued until a mutually satisfactory contract has been negotiated. If negotiations fail with all selected ﬁrms, the contracting officer shall refer the matter to the selection authority who, after consulting with the contracting officer as to why a contract cannot be negotiated, may direct the evaluation board to recommend additional ﬁrms.

Questions regarding this procurement should be directed, in writing, to the Contract officer via e-mail to Jose A. Hernandez at jose.hernandez1@va.gov, alternate POC:  Alison Weinstein at alison.weinstein@va.gov 

ARCHITECT-ENGINEER DESIGN STATEMENT OF WORK

PROJECT NO:  640-26-113

PROJECT NAME: Renovate Building 1002 at Sunnyvale

PROJECT LOCATION: 1080 Innovation Way, Sunnyvale CA 

PROJECT TYPE: NRM

ESTIMATED CONSTRUCTION COST: $25,000,000

PERFORMANCE PERIOD: 233 Calendar Days

1. GENERAL INTENT:

The Contractor (herein referred to as “AE”) shall provide professional Architect-Engineer (AE) services for preparation of schematics, design development and construction documents in accordance with VA Program Guide PG 18-15, Volume C, dated November 2008 for the project at the VA Palo Alto Health Care System in accordance with this design statement of work.

2. SCOPE OF WORK:

A-E Part One Services (also known as Design Phase Services) for this design project include and not limited to site visits, field investigations, studies, and user interviews to prepare drawings, specifications, and cost estimates for all facets of work and disciplines/trades to facilitate a construction project to renovate approximately 21,000 GSF of existing shell space on the first floor of a 2-story building, for dry lab research and associated site improvements, to include surface parking. Building 1002 is a two-story steel framed building construction in 1962. Projects to seismically upgrade, add elevator and lobby, building envelope improvements and roofing work were completed. The interior of the building presently exists as a shell space. 

The project includes, but is not limited to:

Dry lab research space on the first floor of a 2-story building.  The 2nd floor to remain as a shell space.

Development of a minimum of three (3) conceptual floor plans.

Complete utility infrastructure to support the entire building. 

Surface parking improvements for occupants of first floor only. 

Site improvements to address storm drainage issues. 

Site security. Replacement of property line fencing.

Removal of vehicle entrance gate. 

Security Surveillance TV system and Intrusion Detection System. 

Underground utilities investigation and verification. Identify and confirm locations and their conditions. 

Design of a roof access stairway from second floor for maintenance. 

Completion of existing unfinished Room A-104.

Buildings 1043 and 1018 are not included in this project.

A-E Part Two Services (also known as Construction Period Services) for this design project include responding to construction contractor Requests For Information (RFIs) during the solicitation (solicitation support) and construction phases of the construction project; attendance at pre-bid, post-award, and commissioning kick off construction project conferences; review of construction material submittals and shop drawings; approximately 1 site visit per month during construction (both scheduled and emergent) to ensure compliance with the design drawings and specifications; preparation of site visit reports; coordination with project commissioning requirements; review of any construction project modifications for cost and technical acceptability; attendance and participation during the final acceptance inspection; preparation of the punch list; and preparation of record drawings of the completed construction project based on the construction contractor’s as-built drawings. The A-E shall prepare a submittal log to be utilized by the VA during construction period services. 

The above paragraphs constitute a basic outline of the work to be accomplished, and in no way comprise all the details for design of this project. The A-E shall initiate detailed inspection of the project site to determine the needs and conditions for the design of this project. Copies of record drawings will be made available to the highest rated A-E firm. The A-E will verify the validity of the record drawings prior to the start of design work and conduct site investigations as necessary throughout the design. 

The A-E shall be solely responsible for the management, including all associated labor, equipment, materials, mailing costs, and inspection, to meet the requirements of the design project. The A-E shall further provide meeting minutes for all meetings held under this design project.

3. DESIGN WITHIN FUNDING LIMITATIONS:

The design shall be prepared by the A-E to permit the award of a construction contract, using Federal Acquisition Regulation procedures for the construction of the facilities, at a cost that does not exceed the project’s estimated construction contract price of $25,000,000. The design project must comply with VAAR 836.606-71, Application of 6 percent architect-engineer fee limitation.

4. DESIGN INDEPENDENCE, FURNITURE, AND EQUIPMENT: 

Designs for construction must produce a “complete and usable” facility or improvement when constructed. VA policy (VHA Office of Capital Assets Management, Engineering and Support memo Updated Construction Guidance and Expectations dated Sep 12, 2016) requires the A-E to certify that their design (including all bid alternates/bid deducts) is independent of any future construction project. In addition, the A-E must certify that it has produced a design that does not include furniture and equipment that will be procured separately. Equipment that can be part of the design includes those items to meet code requirements for building occupancy; items covered in the VA’s Master Construction Specifications (PG-18-1) Divisions 1 through 10, 13 through 26, or 28 through 48; non-IT equipment items covered by Division 27; and items covered by Division Numbers 12 31 00, 12 32 00, 12 34 00, and 12 36 00.

The A-E shall submit as part of the Final Bid Documents submittal a signed letter on company letterhead stating the design’s independence.

5. DESIGN CRITERIA:

The VA Technical Information Library (TIL) available at Technical Information Library (TIL) - Office of Construction & Facilities Management (va.gov) is managed by the VA Office of Construction & Facilities Management and is the master repository for all VA Numbered Standards for Construction to include design and construction specifications, procedures, standard details, BIM/CAD standards, equipment guides, space planning, and design guides. The documents of the TIL shall be the minimum design criteria for all VA projects performed in the construction of new facilities and the modernization, alteration, addition, or improvement of its real property. All design documents shall be developed in accordance with the VA TIL, including (but not limited to) the following listed Department of Veterans Affairs References:

Where conflicts exist between VA adopted codes and standards and the documents on the TIL, the A-E shall bring this to the attention of the VA. The resolution of the conflict shall be made by the authority having jurisdiction for VA to ensure consistency department-wide.

GENERAL INFORMATION

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

DESCRIPTION

INTRODUCTION: 

It is for information and planning purposes only and shall not be construed as a solicitation or as an obligation on the part of the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA).

The Veterans Health Administration (VHA) Program Contracting Activity (PCAC) intends to negotiate on a sole-source basis with BWBR, an other-than business concern, to provide a refresh of the existing documents, Solicitation Support Services (SSS), and Construction Period Services (CPS) during the construction of Project #607-24-112 Replace Building 1 Windows in Madison, WI 53705 

PROJECT BACKGROUND & DESCRIPTION:

Our intention is to procure a refresh of the existing drawings SSS and CPS in support of Project #607-24-112 Replace Building 1 Windows – Madison WI. The current design firm of record is BWBR, located at 1 S Pinckney St, St Ste 500. They are an other-than business concern and have been in the process of designing this project since September 09, 2022. The current design contract with BWBR no longer has solicitation support and construction period services as part of the scope. 

The design is now 100% complete but requires revisions. Additionally, this project requires SSS and CPS in order to support the construction portion of this requirement. Any prospective design firm will need to possess working knowledge of all issues that may arise and will assume the liabilities associated with any and all aspects of the design. 

Throughout the solicitation period, the A-E shall provide solicitation support services (SSS)  to include, but not limited to, attending the pre-bid site-visit meeting and project walk, answering any technical questions/requests for information (RFIs) received from contractors within five calendar days of the date the questions, and providing addenda as necessary if required to revise specs and drawings. 

The A-E shall provide CPS throughout the construction period to include, but not limited to, providing responses to any requests for information, reviewing submittals, creating a complete set of air emissions permit and land disturbance permit application forms, completing site visit reports, reviewing modification requests, completing a punch list, and delivering record drawings.  

PROCUREMENT INFORMATION:

The proposed project will be a sole source continuation design contract to the original designer of record, BWBR. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code 541330 (size standard $25.5 million) applies to this procurement. It is the intent of the Government to award this project as a sole source. However, if a firm feels like they can meet the requirements of this project, the Government will review the information provided (as specified in the Capabilities Statement below), in order to make a final determination.

CAPABILITY STATEMENT:

Respondents shall provide a general capabilities statement in the following information:  

Section 1: Provide company name, UEI number, company address, Point-of-Contact name, phone number and email.

Section 2: Provide company business size based on NAICS code 541330. Also, provide business type (i.e., Large Business, Small Business, Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business, Small Disadvantaged Business, Women-Owned Small Business, Hub Zone Small Business, etc.).

Section 3: Provide a Statement of Interest in the project. 

Section 4: Provide examples of similar work your company has performed where you have taken over the responsibilities, and liabilities associated with any and all aspects of the design, for Solicitation Support Services and Construction Period Services from a design that was completed by another firm. Provide no more than three examples of this within the past seven years. Include the project name, project owner and contact information as this person may be contacted for further information, project scope, project size (Example: square footage), building use (Example: Medical Facility, Office Building, etc.), project dollar value, start and completion dates. 

Any responsible source who believes it is capable of meeting this requirement may submit a capability statement to Lucretia.Maloney@va.gov  and William.Henkel@va.gov no later than April 10, 2025 at 1:00 PM (ET). It is requested that interested contractors submit a response (electronic submission) of no more than 4 single side pages that addresses the above information. This response must be submitted as a single application-generated (not scanned) PDF document that is less than or equal to 4MB in size. Please note that hard copies will not be accepted. 1. Qualifications. 
The personnel qualifications for support of this contract are listed below.  For all qualifications 
requiring experience, the years of experience must have been recent and relevant and in the 
capacity detailed in the labor categories listed below.  Required technical certifications and other 
relevant qualifications may be further defined in the individual task order. 
2. Job Groupings. 
The following labor categories will be grouped into 4 distinct areas: (1) Engineer/Scientist; (2) 
Technician; (3) Security; and (4) Management/Management Support Staff.   
3. Engineer/Scientist Group 
3.1. Information Systems Engineer Level 4 
Lead contractor related efforts and provides expert consultation in the translation of business 
requirements into IT requirements, designs, and acquisition packages. Provide in-depth 
engineering analysis of IT alternatives for the U.S. Army in support of strategic modernization 
efforts. Provide telecommunications enhancement designs for medium and large-scale 
telecommunication infrastructures.  Provide interface support to IT end users, DoD IT service 
provider personnel, USAISEC, and program management offices.  Apply knowledge of 
engineering and scientific principles, computer technologies, and human cognition to design, 
implement and manage information systems.  The information systems engineer may be called 
upon to design and develop databases, develop system architectures, establish system standards, 
integrate an information system with varied data sources and networks, and generally to plan, 
integrate, design, test or operate information systems.  Bachelor of Science degree in electrical, 
computer, or electronics engineering (or closely related curriculum) from an ABET accredited 
institution with a minimum of 15 years of information systems engineering experience in two or 
more information technologies as identified in paragraph 7.1 or as specified in the individual task 
order. 
3.2. Information Systems Engineer Level 3 
Lead contractor related efforts in the translation of business requirements into IT requirements, 
designs and acquisition packages.  Provide in-depth engineering analysis of IT alternatives for 
the U.S. Army in support of strategic modernization efforts. Provide telecommunications 
enhancement designs for medium and large-scale telecommunication infrastructures. Provide 
interface support to IT end users, DoD IT service provider personnel, USAISEC, and program 
management offices.  Apply knowledge of engineering and scientific principles, computer 
technologies, and human cognition to design, implement and manage information systems.  The 
information systems engineer may be called upon to design and develop databases, develop 
system architectures, establish system standards, integrate an information system with varied 
data sources and networks, and generally to plan, integrate, design, test or operate information 
systems.  Bachelor of Science degree in electrical, computer, or electronics engineering (or 
closely related curriculum) from an ABET accredited institution with a minimum of 10 years of 
information systems engineering experience in one or more information technologies as 
identified in paragraph 7.1 or as specified in the individual task order. 

3.3. Information Systems Engineer Level 2 
Support efforts in the translation of business requirements into telecommunications 
requirements, designs and acquisition packages.   Provide in-depth engineering analysis of IT 
alternatives for the U.S. Army in support of strategic modernization efforts. Provide IT 
enhancement designs for medium and large-scale IT infrastructures. Provide interface support to 
IT end users, DoD IT service provider personnel, USAISEC, and program management offices.  
Apply knowledge of engineering and scientific principles, computer technologies, and human 
cognition to design, implement and manage information systems.  The information systems 
engineer may be called upon to design and develop databases, develop system architectures, 
establish system standards, integrate an information system with varied data sources and 
networks, and generally to plan, integrate, design, test or operate information systems.  Bachelor 
of Science degree in electrical, computer, or electronics engineering (or closely related 
curriculum) from an ABET accredited institution with a minimum of 5 years of information 
systems engineering experience in one or more information technologies as identified in 
paragraph 7.1 or as specified in the individual task order. 
3.4. Information Systems Engineer Level 1 
Support efforts in the translation of business requirements into IT requirements, designs and 
acquisition packages. Provide engineering analysis of IT solutions for the U.S. Army in support 
of strategic modernization efforts.   Provide IT designs for segments of medium and large-scale 
infrastructures. Provide engineering support to Master, Senior and Journeyman level engineers, 
USAISEC, and program management offices.  Bachelor of Science degree in electrical, 
computer, or electronics engineering (or closely related curriculum) from an ABET accredited 
institution. 
3.5. Computer Scientist Level 4 
Possess thorough expert knowledge of current and developing technologies related to the 
interoperability of information systems, information technologies, software, corporate level 
databases, protocols, networking, information processing methods, information/computer 
security, and the use of simulation and modeling tools.  Bachelor of Science degree in Computer 
Science, Information Systems, or Software Engineering from an ABET accredited institution 
with 30 semester hours in a combination of mathematics, statistics, or computer science.  Must 
have a minimum of 15 years of experience in systems design of major information technology 
systems. 
3.6. Computer Scientist Level 3 
Possess thorough knowledge of current and developing technologies related to the 
interoperability of information systems, software, corporate level databases, protocols, 
networking, information processing methods, information/computer security, and the use of 
simulation and modeling tools.  Bachelor of Science degree in Computer Science, Information 
Systems, or Software Engineering from an ABET accredited institution with 30 semester hours 
in a combination of mathematics, statistics, or computer science.  Must have a minimum of 10 
years of experience in systems design of major information technology systems. 

3.7. Computer Scientist Level 2 
Possess a working knowledge of current and developing technologies related to the 
interoperability of information systems, software, corporate level databases, protocols, 
networking, information processing methods, information/computer security, and the use of 
simulation and modeling tools.  Bachelor of Science degree in Computer Science, Information 
Systems, or Software Engineering from an ABET accredited institution with 30 semester hours 
in a combination of mathematics, statistics, or computer science.  Must have a minimum of 5 
years of experience in systems design of major information technology systems. 
3.8. Computer Scientist Level 1 
Analyzes information requirements.  Evaluates analytically and systematically problems of 
workflow, organization, and planning and assists Senior Computer Scientists and Computer 
Scientists develop appropriate corrective action.  Help develop plans for automated information 
systems from project inception to conclusion.  Identify and define problems.  Develop system 
requirements and program specifications, from which programmers prepare detailed flow charts, 
programs, and tests.  Develop, in conjunction with functional users, system alternative solutions.  
Bachelor of Science degree from an ABET accredited institution with 30 semester hours in a 
combination of mathematics, statistics, or computer science. 
3.9. Senior Computer Programmer 
Must be capable of using third and fourth generation or current state-of-the-art information 
technology equipment and languages to analyze system requirements and devise program logic 
for business, management, communication, tactical, and technical problems.  Must be able to 
develop detailed flow charts and instructions for programs, develop general run diagrams and 
process flow charts.  Must be able to develop tape layouts and record formats and add additional 
data items necessary to accomplish work products.  Must be experienced in relational and object 
oriented languages, applications, and operating systems.  Must have a minimum of 10 years of 
programming experience in software development or maintenance with a Bachelor of Science 
degree from an ABET accredited institution, or equivalent.

TJC Mock Inspection Questions
1. Training materials / printed standards
The SOW references providing 25 sets of contractor-developed training materials and 
printed standards. Please confirm whether this requires 25 full printed copies of the cited 
standards/manuals for attendees, or whether contractor-developed training materials for 
25 attendees plus limited reference copies of the cited standards would satisfy the 
requirement.
Government Response: Contractor shall provide 25 sets (hard copies) of the 
referenced standards + 25 sets (hard copies) of contractor-developed training 
material. 
2. Virtual versus in-person training
May one or both required training sessions be delivered virtually or in a hybrid format, 
provided all required content is covered and attendee participation/documentation is 
maintained?
Government Response: All required training sessions shall be delivered in person 
at the El Paso VA Health Care System.
3. Electronic delivery versus hard-copy delivery
Where the SOW references cloud delivery, may final deliverables and training materials 
be submitted electronically through a secure shared platform instead of hard-copy 
binders, except where printed copies are expressly required?
Government Response: Yes, unless where required to be hard copy as per SOW.
4. Meaning of “cloud delivery”
Please clarify whether “cloud delivery” refers to contractor-hosted secure file sharing, a 
VA-approved collaboration environment, or another Government-designated platform.
Government Response: For purposes of this requirement, “cloud delivery” refers 
to a contractor‑hosted secure file‑sharing platform.
5. Updated life-safety plan source files
For updated life-safety plans and associated deficiency markups, will the Government 
provide editable source files such as AutoCAD, Bluebeam, or layered PDFs, or should 
offerors assume updates will be performed from static PDF plan sets only?
Government Response: The Government will provide the most current set of Life 
Safety drawings in AutoCAD format for contractor use.
6. Required deliverable format for markups and plan updates
Please confirm the expected final format for building-plan deficiency identification and 
updated life-safety plans, including whether annotated PDFs are acceptable or if native 
CAD revisions are required.
Government Response: Deficiency identification may be submitted in annotated 
PDF format; however, the Contractor shall provide the final revised Life Safety 
Plans in AutoCAD format.
7. Training attendee scope
Please confirm whether the 25-person training requirement applies to one audience 

Page 3 of 4
across two sessions, or to two separate audiences that would each require complete 
material sets.
Government Response: Training shall be delivered to two separate audiences. 
Audience A (approximately 13 staff) and Audience B (approximately 12 staff) will 
each receive the full set of required training sessions and documentation at 
separate times to ensure continuity of operations.
8. Document review / presentation period
Please confirm whether the referenced document review and presentation effort is 
expected to occur remotely, on site, or at the contractor’s discretion.
Government Response: Document review and the associated presentation/ 
briefing shall be conducted on site
9. Credential documentation
For required credentials, should offerors provide copies of active certifications with the 
quote, or is a resume and certification information sufficient?
Government Response: Offerors shall submit copies of all required active 
certifications in addition to resumes demonstrating relevant experience.
10. Relevant experience / past performance
Will the Government consider relevant healthcare safety, life-safety, EOC, infection 
control, and survey-readiness experience performed in VA, other federal healthcare 
settings, or comparable healthcare systems as acceptable experience for this 
requirement?
Government Response: Yes
11. Preferred report templates or formats
Does the Government have preferred templates or required formats for reports, 
deficiency logs, photo documentation, and Excel-based summaries, or may offerors use 
their own standard formats so long as all required elements are addressed?
Government Response: Offerors may utilize their own standard templates and 
formats, provided all required elements are included and the format reasonably 
simulates Joint Commission survey practices.
12. Distribution of responses
Will responses to vendor questions be issued to all interested offerors through an 
amendment or written Q&A?
Government Response: All responses will be provided through an amendment 
and will be posted to sam.gov.
13. Is it possible to get a detailed facility list, including square footage and occupancy count, 
as applicable for each space?
Government Response: Please see below information on buildings and square 
footage. No occupancy counts readily available. Main building (building 1) has 
around 1,700 active employees. 

Page 4 of 4
14. Are the EOC/IC and LS assessments required to be in parallel, consecutively, or can 
they be scheduled separately?
Government Response: Can be scheduled separately
15. Section 4.7 of the RFQ lists the following Contractor Provided Training requirements.  
Please confirm that El Paso VAHCS wants the training days focused as follows:
1 dedicated day for SOC specific topics (Reference RFQ Sections 4.7.1 to 4.7.1.4) 
1 dedicated day for EOC & IC specific topics (Reference RFQ Sections 4.7.2 to 4.7.2.3) 
Government Response: Confirmed. One (1) training day shall be dedicated to 
SOC‑specific content, and one (1) training day shall be dedicated to 
EOC/IC‑specific content. As noted previously, training will be delivered to two 
separate audiences.

Statement of Work (Revised) 
AFLCMC/ES VTC and A/V System Maintenance 
 
1.0 Purpose 
The purpose of this Statement of Work (SOW) is to secure a contractor to perform 
comprehensive maintenance and support for the Video Teleconferencing (VTC) and 
Audio/Visual (A/V) system located in building 1624, conference room 203, at 5 Eglin Street, 
Hanscom AFB, MA 01731. The contractor shall ensure the system remains fully functional 
through proactive maintenance, timely hardware replacement, on-call support, and user 
training. 
2.0 Scope of Work 
• Provide maintenance for a full audio visual and URL solution for one independent 
conference room that is capable of both classiﬁed and unclassiﬁed video 
teleconferencing (VTC) connectivity.  
• Classiﬁed and unclassiﬁed VTC utilizes a single CODEC, automated periods 
processing hardware, and has NIPR/SIPR Teams capabilities.  
• Replacement parts to the VTC AV system shall comply with the established Defense 
Information Systems Agency (DISA) policy, Video Services Policy Security Technical 
Implementation Guide (STIG).  
• The system will maintain GVS comparability and remain on the Defense Information 
Systems Agency (DISA) Approved Products List (APL) and be Joint Interoperability 
Test Command (JITC) approved.  
• Video Teleconference equipment must be searched as both terms; VTC and Uniﬁed 
Capabilities Conferencing Systems (UCCS) in the following DISA APL: 
https://aplits.disa.mil/processAPList.action.  
The contractor's responsibilities include: 
• Evaluating all existing A/V equipment against current security and compliance 
standards. 
• Replacing or upgrading components as required to meet the speciﬁcations outlined 
in this SOW. 
• Installing, integrating, programming, and testing all new equipment. 
• Providing comprehensive documentation and user training. 

• Delivering ongoing preventative maintenance and on-call support services. 
3.0 Technical Requirements 
3.1. System Security and Compliance 
Governing Standards: Cybersecurity requirements will be governed by the DISA Risk 
Management Executive (RME) Vendor Security Technical Implementation Guides (STIG) 
program. Interoperability requirements will be identiﬁed by the Uniﬁed Capabilities 
Requirements (UCR)-CORE document.  
(Please note: DISA APL has been sunset, so it is no longer the standard. Moving forward, 
cybersecurity requirements will transition to the DISA RME Vendor Security Technical 
Implementation Guides (STIG) program, while interoperability requirements will be 
identiﬁed by the Uniﬁed Capabilities Requirements (UCR)-CORE document and enforced 
through contractual provisions.) 
• Prohibited Technology: The system is non-radio. No components shall be enabled 
for Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, or any other wireless communication method. 
• Secure/Non-Secure Status: The existing secure/non-secure marquee indicators, 
both inside and outside the room, shall remain operational. 
• UPS Replacement: The rack UPS needs to be replaced to meet AF compliance. 
Smart Online UPS required to include Double Conversion feature, Utilizing current 
wall sockets and voltages in room 203.   
3.2. Hardware and Equipment Upgrades 
• Cameras: There are currently two cameras. A CISCO Precision 60 PTZ for SIPR & a 
recent QSC NC-20-60 PTZ for NIPR via Fiber.  
• The CISCO camera may need to be replaced with High deﬁnition PTZ camera 
that has two ports. One for SIPR GVS and one for adding SIPR TEAMS laptop 
app. Recommend QSC NC-20-60 so, matches current NIPR camera in looks, 
speciﬁcations and functionality.  
• Will consider alternate compatible business class PTZ camera’s that 
speciﬁcations are equivalent or better. 
• CODEC: The VTC CODEC for the classiﬁed and unclassiﬁed system shall be 
replaced with a modern, compliant equivalent that supports IP-based connections 
and unclassiﬁed Voice over IP (VoIP) audioconferencing. 

• All replacements must be a DISA approved product and compatible with the 
existing system. VTC unit can connect via Internet Protocol (IP) 
• In addition, it has the ability for Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP) 
connections for unclassiﬁed audioconferencing. The audioconferencing is 
programmed to be disabled for classiﬁed conferences. 
• Operator Display Upgrade:  
Note: Operator desk currently has one GFE furnished 32in ViewSonic computer 
display as that is the largest ﬁt for console.  It shall be replaced with two monitors of 
desktop standard viewing size or larger. 
• Upgrade operator area display hardware & program conﬁguration so, any 
display output can be shown on any room display independently and 
simultaneously.  
• Ability to see Main desktop display presentations or communication apps 
and extended display separately simultaneously on front screens, that will 
mirror operator desk monitors.  
• The ability for operators to work on local desktop displays will not be seen by 
attendees so the operator can research questions or check emails.  
 
• Credenza: If current AV cabinet cannot properly be reconﬁgured to house all 
required equipment and ensure that the temperature does not exceed the device's 
maximum MFR operating temperature limits then, the contractor’s proposal will 
provide estimate for a new locking credenza on casters with built in racks.  After 
Award of contract, the credenza design, material and color must be pre-approved by 
the Government ES POC prior to purchase. Shall have proper AC voltages and surge 
protection available where UPS is not utilized. Use existing AV racks for audio-visual 
equipment that can be locked in a rack system. 
 
3.3. Control System and User Interface 
• Touch Panels: 
• If touch panel replacement is required for compatibility, new screens no 
smaller than 10 inches shall be installed. The existing design, coloring, and 
icon style of the touch panel interface shall not be changed without 
Government consent (21.5 in at Operator desk & 10.1in at conference table.)  

• The ES logo on the touch panels must be updated, and the time display must 
be set to Eastern Standard Time. This feature should be user-friendly for 
future modiﬁcations. 
• SIPR Teams Integration: The newly introduced SIPR Teams audio/video signal data 
will come from DoD SIPR laptop connected at operator console and shall be wired 
and programmed into AV rack/touch panel system.  
• May require adding a (3rd Freeport SCC unit to current periods processing 
system.) 
• Camera Control: The control system must allow the SVTC camera to be turned 
on/off and have its presets utilized without interrupting active service. 
• White Noise System: One white noise system with a minimum of two white noise 
speakers mounted on the outside of each door, wired safely in/thru wall with the 
ability to turn on and off from inside the room. The volume level to the white noise is 
adjustable from inside the room, if able to automate into AV system. No Bluetooth, 
wireless, or Wi-Fi system/speaker exist or are allowed. 
3.4. Cabling and Installation 
• The contractor shall provide all cables, connectors, power strips, power supplies, 
and miscellaneous materials required for a complete installation. All wiring at the 
A/V desk must be professionally managed and bundled. 
4.0 Contractor Deliverables 
• System Documentation: The contractor shall produce and develop supporting 
documentation, diagrams, and artifacts for all system modiﬁcations and 
replacements. 
• Source Code: Uncompiled CRESTRON source code shall be delivered in a DISC to 
the Government. (It should be uncompiled so that it can be edited in the future if 
you ever need to get the system updated with new components or add a capability 
like secure VTC etc.) 
• Diagrams: Signal ﬂow diagrams (for Audio, Video, and Control) and wiring 
schematics shall be provided in both PDF and large-format prints. All equipment 
and wiring must be clearly labeled. (Signal ﬂow diagrams should include separate 
sheets for 1) AUDIO 2) VIDEO 3) CONTROL Coding (raw code). Wiring Schematics- 
Label equipment and wiring. 

• Equipment Disposal: The contractor is responsible for the removal and disposal of 
all broken, unserviceable, or replaced components.  
• Purchase and Install: All new equipment included as needed after receiving 
approval from the Government representative. The government will need to be 
informed if any equipment is backordered or will not arrive on time for installation. 
• Training: The contractor shall provide training and orientation for at least two 
Government individuals on the use of all new equipment and system functionalities. 
5.0 Service and Support Requirements 
• Service Calls: A one-hour remote response time is required for all service calls, 
Monday-Friday, 0800-1800 ET. 
• On-site Support: If requested, the contractor must provide on-site support for 
troubleshooting and maintenance within one business day. It is expected that the 
assigned technician will be local to meet this requirement. Additionally, the 
technician will ensure installation, integration, programming and testing of the new 
equipment is up to customer standards. 
• Preventative Maintenance: The contractor shall perform preventative maintenance 
twice annually on a mutually agreed upon schedule. 
• Service Hours: The estimated yearly service commitment is 16 hours. 
6.0 Period of Performance and Warranty 
• Period of Performance: The contract will consist of one (1) base year plus four (4) 
one-year option periods, commencing promptly after the contract is awarded, with 
no break in service between periods. 
• System Warranty: If replacement equipment or hardware is required, the contractor 
shall provide a one-year warranty on all equipment and systems installed, effective 
from the date of installation. This warranty applies to the base year and all exercised 
option years. 
  

Appendix A: Current Equipment Inventory 
The following is a non-exhaustive list of equipment currently installed in the VTC/AV system. 
The contractor is responsible for maintaining or replacing this equipment to meet the 
requirements of this SOW. Equipment is not required to be brand name, but must be equal 
in quality, function, compatibility with the overarching system, and meet the security 
standards set out in Section 2.0. 
Approximate room 203 speciﬁcations:19’10” by 23’8” .

REQUEST FOR INFORMATION 
NOTICE # 36C10X26Q0118 
This Request for Information (RFI) is released by the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), 
Strategic Acquisition Center-Frederick (SAC-F) in accordance with Revolutionary FAR Overhaul 
(RFO) 15.101(c). This RFI is issued for the purpose of conducting market research and learning 
about industry capabilities.  
 
THERE IS NO SOLICITATION AT THIS TIME. This notice does not constitute a request for 
quotes or proposals, and the Government does not intend to award a contract based on this RFI 
or otherwise pay for the information requested. Submission of any information in response to 
this notice is purely voluntary. The Government assumes no financial responsibility for any costs 
incurred. 
 
This RFI does not obligate the Government to any specific course of action or guarantee a 
future solicitation or contract for services described in this notice. Responses will be treated as 
information only and not as a proposal. Respondents are responsible for adequately marking 
proprietary, restricted or sensitive information contained in their response.  
 
The Government is seeking as much information as possible and a complete response from 
industry to this RFI during this market research activity may assist the Government in 
developing an acquisition strategy and requirements. 
 
BACKGROUND: 
 
Medical Disability Examination Office (MDEO) Program Overview 
 
The mission of the Medical Disability Examination Office (MDEO) is to support the Department 
of Veterans Affairs’ (VA) disability claims process by administering VA’s contract medical 
disability examination program worldwide to ensure Veterans and Service Members receive 
timely and high-quality examinations in support of their disability claims. MDEO strives to make 
a meaningful difference in the lives of those who served by increasing access to accurate and 
timely disability exams and shortening the claims process.  
 
The MDEO Quality Compliance Program is a critical component in VA’s examination process, 
particularly in the review and assessment of Disability Benefit Questionnaires (DBQs). The 
primary mission of the MDEO Quality Program is to ensure the accuracy and completeness of 
DBQs completed by contracted examiners. These questionnaires play a pivotal role in 
determining the eligibility and benefits for disability claims submitted by Veterans and Service 
Members. The quality of these examinations directly impacts the benefits that Veterans receive, 
which underscores the importance of a rigorous quality assurance program. 
 
MDEO Quality Compliance Program Goals 
 
Ensuring Accuracy and Completeness: 
 
The foremost goal of the MDEO Quality Compliance Program is to guarantee that every DBQ is 
accurate and complete. This ensures that Veterans' disability claims are processed correctly, 
allowing for proper benefits allocation. 
 
Quality Performance Assessment: 
 
VA assesses the quality performance of each vendor on a quarterly basis. This performance 
assessment is based on a review of a statistically valid random sample of completed DBQs. By 

REQUEST FOR INFORMATION 
NOTICE # 36C10X26Q0118 
sampling and reviewing these questionnaires, VA can maintain high standards of quality across 
all examinations. 
 
Quality Assessment Process 
 
Sample Identification: 
 
VA identifies a statistically valid random sample of completed DBQs. This approach ensures that 
the sample is representative of the total population of DBQs submitted, thereby providing a 
reliable basis for performance assessment. 
 
Data Upload and Management: 
 
The sampled DBQ data is uploaded into the Mandatory Contract Examination Quality (MCEQ) 
database, a custom-built application within Salesforce. MCEQ serves as the central repository 
for all quality assessment data, facilitating efficient management and analysis. 
 
Conducting Reviews: 
 
The MDEO team conducts detailed reviews of the sampled DBQs by applying predefined quality 
assessment criteria. These criteria are designed to meticulously evaluate each questionnaire for 
accuracy and completeness. 
 
Recording Findings: 
 
The accuracy findings from the reviews are recorded and stored in the MCEQ system. These 
findings are critical for assessing vendor performance on a quarterly basis and identifying error 
trends that require attention. 
 
Benefits of Automation 
 
MDEO is exploring the use of automation to enhance the quality assessment process.  
The primary objectives of incorporating automation are: 
 
Broader Compliance Checks - Automation would allow MDEO to perform compliance checks on 
a larger or total population of completed DBQs. This would significantly improve the breadth and 
depth of quality assessments. 
 
Improved Efficiency and Effectiveness - Automated systems can process more DBQs in less 
time compared to manual reviews. This efficiency would enable MDEO to provide more timely 
feedback to vendors and conduct deeper analyses of compliance quality. 
 
Trend Identification and Analysis - Automation can enhance the ability to identify and analyze 
trends within the data. This can lead to more insightful recommendations and targeted 
improvements in the examination process. 
 
By leveraging automation in the quality assessment process, MDEO aims to achieve more 
comprehensive compliance checks and improve the overall quality of DBQs. This will ultimately 
enhance the accuracy of disability claims determinations and better serve the needs of 
Veterans. 
 

REQUEST FOR INFORMATION 
NOTICE # 36C10X26Q0118 
SUMISSION INSTRUCTIONS: 
 
Interested contractors are to respond to this notice by e-mail to Lindi.Sylvester@va.gov and 
Vincent.Bender@va.gov no later than 9:00 AM EDT on April 13, 2026. Please reference Notice 
# 36C10X26Q0118 in e-mail subject line. 
 
Submissions must include the following: 
 
A. Cover Sheet - 1 page 
 
1. Company name, address, SAM UEI number, and CAGE code. 
2. Primary point of contact to include e-mail address and phone number. 
3. Type of business (as listed in SAM.gov). 
4. North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) that best fits these task areas. 
5. If applicable, GSA contract number, schedule, and SIN category; specific information of 
other GWAC or VA-wide Ordering Contracts. 
 
B. Index – 1 page 
 
Please provide an index to assist the Government in identifying where you have addressed 
each question below in your Capabilities Statement and Market Information. This index should 
provide question number and corresponding page and section heading and/or paragraph 
number. 
 
C. Capabilities Statement and Market Information - no more than 5 pages 
 
Please respond to the following questions by providing a capabilities statement and market 
information. 
 
DBQ Audit Capability: 
 
1. What automation tools or software do you have available that are capable conducting 
reviews and identifying whether a DBQ audit checklist is fully and accurately completed? 
 
2. What is your monthly volume capacity? 
 
Monthly Feedback Provision: 
 
3. Can you provide detailed monthly feedback on the DBQ reviews to assist with vendor 
communications and internal analysis? 
 
Report Generation and Analysis: 
 
4. Are you able to generate monthly and quarterly reports that identify trends and include 
recommendations for improvements? 
 
5. Are your reports customizable to suit our program needs? 
 
Other Information: 
 
6. Please provide any other feedback or suggestions that you deem appropriate.

2) Question: What is the purpose of this Program Announcement (PA), DARPA-PA-26-02-02?
Answer: The purpose of this QBIT is to encourage new entrants into Stage A of QBI, 
ensuring DARPA has visibility into all approaches and potential solutions.
3) Question: If our company participated in a prior QBI or Underexplored Systems for Utility-
Scale Quantum Computing (US2QC) effort but are not currently active participants, are we 
eligible to apply to this solicitation?
Answer:  While this QBIT is not intended to solicit proposals from performers selected under 
prior QBI or US2QC solicitations, those performers are not precluded from submitting new 
proposals under this PA if they believe their approach offers new or distinct contributions to 
the QBI. Performers who participated in a prior QBI or US2QC effort but did not move 
beyond Stage A should contact DARPA via QBI@darpa.mil prior to submission.
4) Question: If our company applied to a prior QBI or US2QC solicitation but was not selected, 
are we eligible?
Answer: Yes. If you believe that you can make a strong case that your organization is on a 
path to building a utility-scale quantum computer by 2033, you are invited to apply to QBI. 
Please clearly describe recent advances in your approach and technology.
5) Question: This solicitation has a different structure from previous US2QC and QBI 
solicitations. Why is that?

DARPA-PA-26-02-02 Stage A QBIT 
Frequently Asked Questions 
  2 
6) Answer: Unlike previous solicitations, this opportunity has a rolling admission process such 
that any abstracts submitted prior to the date and time stated in the QBIT PA will be 
considered. 
7) Question: Do we need to start with Stage A, or can we apply directly to Stage B? 
Answer: DARPA-PA-26-02-02 is soliciting abstracts for Stage A of QBI only.  Per the PA, while 
six months is the expected Stage A term, milestones may be completed early, allowing 
DARPA the opportunity to evaluate performers’ concepts ahead of the six-month timeline. 
8) Question: How many awards are anticipated?  
Answer: Multiple awards are anticipated. 
9) Question: Are you only interested in proposals to QBI for fault-tolerant, gate-based (or 
equivalent) machines, or are other quantum computing approaches, such as quantum 
annealing, acceptable? 
Answer: Yes, other quantum computing approaches, such as quantum annealing, are within 
scope.  DARPA is interested in revolutionary approaches from any entity who believes they 
can build an industrially useful quantum computer by 2033.  
10) Question: We are interested in developing applications and algorithms for fault-tolerant 
quantum computers.  Can we apply to QBI Stage A?  
Answer: Entities interested in working only on applications and algorithms should only 
apply to this QBI solicitation as part of a larger team that is developing a complete quantum 
computing solution.  Alternately, you may submit a abstract to the QBI Independent 
Verification and Validation (IV&V) Topic, to supply innovative infrastructure, equipment, 
and expertise for independent verification and validation (IV&V) support to QBI (QBIT Link: 
DARPA-PA-26-02-01.) 
11) Question: If we are selected for IV&V support, does that exclude us from submitting to QBI 
as a performer? 
Answer: An entity receiving an award for IV&V support under DARPA-PA-26-02-01 may be 
excluded from receiving an award under Stage A QBI (DARPA-PA-26-02-02) as a research 
performer due to potential organizational conflicts of interest (OCI). Additionally, DARPA 
may require IV&V performers to declare their participation in QBI to the relevant 
contracting activity when proposing to any other U.S. Government solicitation related to 
quantum computers. This ensures transparency and mitigates conflicts of interest. Any 

DARPA-PA-26-02-02 Stage A QBIT 
Frequently Asked Questions 
  3 
entity with specific concerns or questions about eligibility should contact the cognizant QBIT 
email address.  
12) Question: Will QBI have a parallel “seedling” or “SBIR adoption” track for transformational 
subcomponents like sub-4k cryofluids or cryo-thermal-electro-optic-system designs that 
would benefit all the QBI performer teams? 
Answer: Not at this time.  
13) Question: Can foreign companies participate in the program?  Would a foreign company be 
required to have U.S. citizen staff or hardware physically located in the U.S. to be eligible for 
any stage? 
Answer:  Non-U.S. organizations and/or individuals may participate to the extent that such 
participants comply with any necessary nondisclosure agreements, security regulations, 
export control laws, and other governing statutes applicable under the circumstances. 
14) Question: The solicitation uses the phrase “Computational Value” – how will this be 
evaluated and defined? 
Answer: In general, computational value will be measured in dollars.  It is anticipated 
proposers will describe their approach to quantify the value of their utility-scale concept. 
15) Question: If two companies propose similar system designs based on comparable 
technologies, does DARPA intend to contract both for Stage A if their approaches are 
deemed sound, or will only one company be selected per technical approach? 
Answer: There is no limitation on the number of performers per hardware paradigm.  
Multiple approaches using similar technology will be considered.  Proposals are evaluated 
against the criteria in the program announcement – not each other. 
16) Question: Given Intellectual Property protection requirements, how does DARPA plan to 
manage potential transitions of personnel between proposer institutions and T&E 
institutions over the course of the QBI program, while ensuring compliance with IP 
safeguards and avoiding conflicts of interest? 
Answer: DARPA has established robust procedures for evaluating and managing conflicts of 
interest to ensure the integrity of the program. Each agreement includes specific terms 
governing data and intellectual property (IP) rights, with additional provisions for entities 
performing Independent Verification and Validation (IV&V) to address their unique role in 
the program. Any potential conflicts of interest or IP concerns will be handled on a case-by-

DARPA-PA-26-02-02 Stage A QBIT 
Frequently Asked Questions 
  4 
case basis, in accordance with applicable laws, regulations, and DARPA policies, ensuring 
compliance and fairness throughout the program. 
17) Question: What information should an entity include in a submission if they have conducted 
serious due diligence and believe they can deliver an industrially useful quantum computer 
by 2036, but not by 2033? 
Answer: It is recommended that proposers include details about what will be built by 2036, 
what milestones will be achieved by 2033, and any potential strategies for accelerating the 
proposed timeline. 
18) Question: What if a company believes they can deliver a militarily useful but not an 
industrially useful quantum computer by 2033?  Is that acceptable, or does it have to be 
“industrially relevant?” 
Answer:  
DARPA is interested in advancing technologies with both commercial and defense-specific 
utility and has included both Research OTs and Prototype OTs as possible award 
instruments. This approach allows for the negotiation of awards that are intended to (1) 
spur dual-use research & development with a path to commercialization; and (2) acquire 
prototype capabilities for the Department, with the potential for follow-on production.   
19) Question: Can an organization submit multiple abstracts? 
Answer: The announcement does not limit the number of abstracts, either in total or from a 
given organization.  However, DARPA encourages each organization to present their 
strongest team capable of meeting the program’s objectives, ideally through a single 
abstract submission. 
20) Question: How can support technology firms participate in the QBI process? 
Answer: Support technology firms interested in participating in QBI can do so by directly 
contacting a performer to discuss opportunities for collaboration as a subperformer. This 
may involve providing components, subsystems, or other technical contributions to support 
the performer’s efforts in building a utility-scale quantum computer. 
21) Question: The program announcement states, “Specifically excluded is research that 
primarily results in evolutionary improvements to the existing state of practice.”  Could you 
describe what you mean by this?  

DARPA-PA-26-02-02 Stage A QBIT 
Frequently Asked Questions 
  5 
Answer: DARPA seeks revolutionary rather than evolutionary solutions given its mission is 
to drive transformative advancements in technology that can significantly impact national 
security and scientific progress. Evolutionary solutions typically involve incremental 
improvements to existing technologies, which may not be sufficient to address the complex 
challenges posed by emerging fields like quantum computing. Revolutionary solutions, on 
the other hand, aim to achieve breakthroughs that fundamentally change the state of the 
art, enabling capabilities that were previously unattainable. 
22) Question: What specific assurances can DARPA provide that performer proprietary 
information shared during the proposal process and the QBI program will be handled 
appropriately? 
Answer: DARPA takes proprietary information very seriously.  Any information submitted to 
DARPA as part of a proposal to DARPA-PA-26-02-02 is considered selection-sensitive 
information and is protected in accordance with DoD Instruction 5200.48 and established 
Agency policies.  Prior to the start of performance, DARPA will work with the performer to 
negotiate terms and conditions that include robust data and intellectual property 
protection measures.  All QBI Test and Evaluation and IV&V personnel employed during 
contract execution are required to adhere to strict conflict of interest and data protection 
agreements to ensure the confidentiality and security of proprietary information. 
23) Question: Can I propose my own Schedule of Milestones and Deliverables? 
Answer: It is anticipated that all QBI Stage A performers will use the same Schedule of 
Milestones and Payments, as shown in Table 2 of the Program Announcement; however, 
proposers may suggest an alternate schedule of milestones and payments as long as the 
total payments in Stage A do not exceed $1M. 
24) Question: Will there be any restrictions on the publication of scientific advances by a 
performer that come about due to QBI work? 
Answer: Publication restrictions will be negotiated prior to a Stage A award. Draft terms and 
conditions addressing items such as publication of scientific results, technology developed 
under the award, and content of technical feedback will be provided as a part of the full 
proposal invitation package. At this time, DARPA does not anticipate imposing restrictions 
on performers releasing their own company’s data. 
25) Question: What advice do you have for first-time applicants to a DARPA program? 

DARPA-PA-26-02-02 Stage A QBIT 
Frequently Asked Questions 
  6 
Answer: Potential proposers are encouraged to carefully read the Program Announcement 
(PA) in its entirety to fully understand the requirements and objectives. Proposers should 
utilize the required templates provided in the announcement and ensure their submissions 
adhere to the outlined instructions. Additionally, any questions should be submitted in 
accordance with the procedures specified in the PA. The DARPAConnect platform at 
DARPAConnect.us is a valuable resources for familiarizing oneself with DARPA, its 
processes, and insights into how programs and proposals are assessed.
