A. Topic Description
The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) is issuing a Quantum Benchmarking 
Initiative topic (QBIT) to solicit innovative approaches addressing challenges related to quantum 
computing. The QBIT will examine approaches to constructing a utility-scale fault-tolerant 
quantum computer and computational workflows that include quantum compute steps. Proposed 
research should investigate approaches that enable revolutionary advances in design, engineering, 
testing, and evaluation of such systems. Specifically excluded is research that primarily results in 
evolutionary improvements to the existing state of practice.  The purpose of this QBIT is to 
encourage new entrants to QBI, ensuring DARPA has visibility into all approaches and potential 
solutions. While this QBIT is not intended to solicit proposals from performers selected under 
prior QBI or US2QC solicitations, those performers are not precluded from submitting new 
proposals under this PA if they believe their approach offers new or distinct contributions to the 
QBI initiative.
This QBIT is issued under DARPA’s Quantum Benchmarking Initiative (QBI), described in the 
QBI 2026 Program Announcement (PA), DARPA-PA-26-02. To view the original DARPA PA 
for QBI 2026, visit SAM.gov under solicitation number DARPA-PA-26-02: 
https://sam.gov/workspace/contract/opp/c26b38bf041a4d70b00ed619bebb4773/view
If selected for negotiation of an award, proposers should anticipate either an Other Transaction for 
Research agreement (herein referred to as “Research OT”) under 10 U.S.C. §4021 or an Other 
Transaction for Prototype agreement (herein referred to as “Prototype OT”) under 10 U.S.C. 
§4022.  See Section E, Award Information, for additional details regarding award type.

Requirements 
The NGA Police based in Saint Louis, Missouri and Springfield, Virginia have a requirement for 
a Police Administration System (PAS). Which would allow the NGA Police to manage, store, 
and retrieve information related to incidents, arrests, evidence, personnel files, and other critical 
data, to improve efficiency.  
Comparable Commercial-off-the-Shelf (COTS) items are acceptable for consideration.  
 
• Police Administration System shall follow 34 U.S. Code 41303 – Uniform Federal Crime 
Reporting Act of 1988 (UCR Reporting) 
• Police Administration System shall follow Federal Code of Regulations Title 28 Chapter 
1 Part 20 to ensure criminal history record information wherever it appears is collected, 
stored, and disseminated in a manner to ensure the accuracy, completeness, currency 
integrity, and security of such information and to protect the individual privacy.  
• Currently FEDRAMP High 
• Impact Level IV (to process law enforcement sensitive information) 
• Police Administration System certified to the DoD 5015.02 standard. 
• Software maintenance agreement 
• Software warranty  
• Vendor shall have established UEI Number, CAGE Code, registered in SAM. 

UNCLASSIFIED 
 
 
 
 
  PAGE 2 OF 42 
 
 
 
UNCLASSIFIED 
• Vendor will serve as the Prime contractor.  
• Demonstrated experience working within TS/SCI environment(s) 
• Shall be in compliance with NARA. 
• PAS shall abide by all Federal regulations required of a PAS system for police 
departments. 
• Form repository for all NGA Police forms. To enable all forms to be accessible and 
identifiable 
• Server storage space requirements/capabilities for on premises PAS 
• Single entry (i.e., no duplicate data entry)  
• Maximum use of Federal charge code tables  
• Ability to enter and query narrative(s)/text fields.  
• Spell check and formatting capability on narrative(s)/ text fields.  
• Single database (i.e., virtual or physical) Validation on data entry (i.e., logical edits, edit 
checks for all fields)  
• Common Access Card login 
• Name and Password login (option)  
• Track and add/remove people. To remove or add permissions.  
• Ability to connect to Missouri Uniform Law Enforcement System (MULES), Virginia 
Criminal Information Database, and National Crime Information Center integrated into 
PAS. 
• Citrix integrated into PAS 
• Receipts for vehicle maintenance recorded per vehicle in PAS. 
• Access to ALERTS system for reports, tickets – Specifically for SIPE Police  
 
Vehicles 
 
• Automatic Maintenance scheduler 

UNCLASSIFIED 
 
 
 
 
  PAGE 3 OF 42 
 
 
 
UNCLASSIFIED 
• Lifecyle Management System – Lets department know when vehicle has reached its 
lifecycle and needs replaced. 
• Tracks vehicle through its lifecycle 
• Tracks all vehicle related costs and totals how much has been spent. 
 
Officer Clothing Records 
 
• Clothing and Equipment record for each officer 
• Ability to use CAC to digitally sign clothing record. 
• All officers shall have their own clothing record recorded in their personnel file within 
the PAS. 
Investigations 
 
• Ability to connect to Digital Data Exchange (DDEX) is integrated into PAS. 
• Ability to upload case information from a suspicious activity report/DDEX into report in 
PAS. 
• Search link for DDEX in PAS 
• Ability to connect to the National Data Exchange (N-DEX) in PAS 
Police Operations 
 
• Officer scheduling program (identify shifts, supervisor, officer)  
• General easily identifiable tile in PAS for reports to be written. 
• Report writing program/template with required fillable fields. 
• User interface identifies what user has been granted access to 
• An agency’s PAS should provide the capabilities for users to generate inquiries to 
internal data sources from within each module where such inquiries make sense. 
• System will offer the ability for two levels of review for each police report. 

UNCLASSIFIED 
 
 
 
 
  PAGE 4 OF 42 
 
 
 
UNCLASSIFIED 
• There will be a module for a central records section where various reporting documents 
of the agency can be managed. 
• At the administrative level, for administrators to keep informed and allocate manpower 
and resources. 
• Easy ability to obtain the disposition of reports. A report will be created and sent to the 
FBI. The report must accurately reflect the results of charges filed alleging violations of 
the law. 
• Provide a fingerprint card with case number.  This will allow for ease of reference after 
booking and record keeping. 
• The disposition page of an arrest should show the FBI number on the Final Disposition 
Report. If the FBI number is unknown, then the subject’s complete name should be 
reported as it was sent on the FBI fingerprint image.   
• The local arrest number as shown on the fingerprint image for which the disposition is 
being submitted should also be stated on the Final Disposition.  
• The Final Disposition should show any changes from the original charge as it appears on 
the arrest fingerprint image to the charge for which conviction was obtained. 
• Ability to access the Criminal History Record Information (CHRI) (Internal PeopleSoft 
Process) is not needed to connect to outside sources. 
• Ability to access NCIC.  
• Originating Agency Identified (ORI) file – will hold contact information (such as an 
agency’s address and telephone number.  
• Uniform Crime Reporting 
• Reporting module. Easily be able to obtain UCR report for each month or years of 
information. 
▪ The following is necessary for any agency which expects to generate 
Uniform Crime Reports from its records system: 
▪ A permanent record of each crime is made at once upon receipt of the 
complaint. All reports of thefts or attempted thefts are included regardless 
of the value of property involved. 

UNCLASSIFIED 
 
 
 
 
  PAGE 5 OF 42 
 
 
 
UNCLASSIFIED 
▪ Crime trends data module. Should show the crime trend from one period 
to the next are presented in the UCR Programs annual report.  The crime 
trend module should show the percentage change in crime based on data 
reported in a prior equivalent period. Trends can be computed for any time 
limit, such as month, quarters, or years.  
▪ The UCR reporting should compute the volume trend and the rate trends. 
• Easily identifiable tiles for each respective police division (Operations, Tactical Response 
Team, Investigations, Canine).  Each division should be able to store personnel records, 
operational plans, Standard Operating Procedures etc.…  
• Police Administration System shall be in compliance with Section 889(a)(1)(A) which 
prohibits the Federal Government from procuring or obtaining, or extending or renewing 
a contract to procure or obtain “any equipment, system, or service that uses covered 
telecommunications equipment or services as a substantial or essential component of any 
system, or as critical technology as part of any system,” on or after August 13, 2019, 
unless an exception applies or a waiver is granted. 
PAS System and Vendor Requirements 
 
• Vendors must be willing to sign a statement verifying no covered telecommunications 
equipment or service that uses covered telecommunications equipment or services as a 
substantial or essential component of any system, or as critical technology as part of any 
system that are in violation of Section 889(a)(1)(A) were used.  
• PAS should have basic master indices that correlate and aggregate information in the 
following areas: people, locations, property, conveyances (e.g., vehicles), and 
organizations.  
• This is to eliminate redundant data entry by allowing the reuse of previously stored 
information and the automatic update of the master indices upon the entry of report 
information. 
• Master indices information shall be captured in a variety of ways, including during the 
input of information from incident, traffic accident, and vehicle reports and citation, 
booking, arrest, juvenile, fingerprint, and mug shot subsystems. Prior to accepting an 
entry, PAS should automatically give the user the option of deciding whether there is a 
match based on existing data. 

UNCLASSIFIED 
 
 
 
 
  PAGE 6 OF 42 
 
 
 
UNCLASSIFIED 
• The system should support the validation and linking of addresses, commonplace names, 
and street intersections. Linkages among any information contained in the master indices 
(e.g., people to places or person to person) must be included in PAS. 
• Query and retrieval by name, vehicle, location, organization, and/or property to produce a 
comprehensive response displaying all related records in the system. 
• The PAS Master Name Index (MNI) function links an individual master name record to 
every event (e.g., incident-report, arrest report, field interview, accident report, and 
license and permits) in which the individual was involved or associated. Every person 
found within these events is given a master name record. Should that person become 
involved in another event, the single master-name record is linked to all the other events 
so that by querying that one name, the system can produce a synopsis of all the 
involvements associated with that one person. It also eases the linking of other names to 
an individual master name record (i.e., alias information and relationship data). In 
querying an individual MNI record, the user would also be able to view all related 
records, as well as those associated with that individual. When a record or report is added 
to PAS and a person is linked (i.e., indexed) to that event, the system should perform a 
particularly important matching function using a rule-based process. The purpose of this 
matching function is to either automatically link an existing MNI record or to present the 
user with a list of potential matches to the name so that the user can make the matching 
decision. PAS should provide a matching algorithm that will offer the ability to search 
the name file by a variety of criteria, such as sound-alike searching; phonetic 
replacement; diminutive first names (e.g., James/ Jim/Jimmy) and other static 
demographic information, such as age, sex, and race. Once a list of potential matches is 
provided, the user can decide whether the information should be linked to an existing 
master name record or whether a new master name entry should be added.  In addition to 
names, the MNI should, at a minimum, capture and support information on: Physical 
characteristics (e.g., current and past descriptors) Race and ethnicity Location history 
(e.g., current and past residences) Employer information.  Telephone numbers Known 
associates Alias names/monikers Available mug shot(s) and photographs Scars, marks, 
and tattoos Modus operandi (i.e., unique method of operation for a specific type of crime) 
Identification (e.g., social security, driver’s license, and local and county identification) 
NCIC fingerprint classification.  
• More information can be added, but older information should be maintained and 
viewable. 

UNCLASSIFIED 
 
 
 
 
  PAGE 7 OF 42 
 
 
 
UNCLASSIFIED 
• The PAS MNI should also provide maintenance functions that will allow a record or 
report to be unlinked from one MNI and linked to another. Since it is not always possible 
to ensure that the correct MNI record is linked to an event record, it must be possible to 
correct it. Functions also should be provided that will allow two or more MNI records to 
be merged into one record. 
 
Master Vehicle Index 
When a vehicle is linked to an incident in PAS, it should be added to the vehicle record in the 
Master Vehicle Index (MVI), which provides an agency with a detailed, searchable store of 
information about vehicles. PAS should offer the capability to search on:  
• Vehicle Identification Number (VIN)  
• License plate number  
• License plate state  
• License plate year 
•  Registered owner 
 Description (e.g., make, model, year, color, style, and attributes 
 
• Tied to M.U.L.E.S, V.C.I.N., and NCIC 
• Field Interview Report check box to vehicle report. 
 
Master Property Index (MPI) 
Each record is catalogued by using unique property characteristics: 
 
• Make  
• Model  
• Brand  
• Description  
• distinguishing characteristics  
• serial number 

UNCLASSIFIED 
 
 
 
 
  PAGE 8 OF 42 
 
 
 
UNCLASSIFIED 
•  Industry property coding standards should be used during the entry of property records 
into PAS.  
• Any property records entered throughout PAS should automatically cross-reference MPI 
to find potential matches based on the unique property characteristics. 
• Location identifier of evidence i.e.…locker or evidence room 
• System should show who entered the information into the MPI. 
• Track the chain of custody. 
• Auto generate time stamp of logged evidence 
• Internal audit report review 
• Other supervisors can review reports if another supervisor is out of the office – ability to 
assign a proxy. 
• Records retention determined by (day, month, and year)  
• Storage for completed FOIA requests. 
• All calls for service (CFS) are recorded in a structured records environment, offering the 
ability to run reports on this data, while also maintaining a historical record on all calls.  
• The data are either segmented or identifiable by the agency. 
Incident Reporting 
 
• CFS record in PAS should be linked to the incident and should be easily accessible from 
the incident report. 
• Certain types of incident reports must be available to the public. Witness information, as 
well as the names of juveniles who are subjects or victims, may need to be redacted for 
public consumption. PAS must be able to recognize the age of the majority in the 
jurisdiction by the date-of-birth information entered into the system that is available to 
the public. The system should support the redaction prior to printing a public copy or 
making the report available to the public. 
• The data captured in this module must support the preparation and submission of all 
required federal crime reporting and provide the capability to print a copy of both the 
completed department’s incident report and the redacted incident report. 

UNCLASSIFIED 
 
 
 
 
  PAGE 9 OF 42 
 
 
 
UNCLASSIFIED 
• Reports based on period of time. 
• Area 
• Incident type  
• Location code (e.g., geocode)  
• Initial call type Offense type  
• Summary of incidents by officer 
• Incident reports have free-text fields, to allow the collection of an unlimited amount of 
narrative information. 
• System should offer the capability to search the narratives for a specific word or phrase. 
• Check box to send report to Detectives.  PAS will automatic

Attachment 02 
Contract Surveillance Plan for 
Small Unmanned Air Systems Reusable Architecture 
1. Purpose
This Contract Surveillance Plan (CSP) is a Government developed and applied document used to 
ensure systematic Quality Assurance (QA) methods are used in the administration and 
surveillance of tasking under the Task Order (TO). The intent is to ensure the Contractor 
performs in accordance with (IAW) the Statement of Work (SOW) and the Government receives 
the quality of services called for in the SeaPort-Next Generation (NxG) Multiple Award Contract 
(MAC) TO. 
The Naval Air Warfare Center Aircraft Division (NAWCAD) Webster Outlying Field (WOLF) 
Ship & Air Integrated Warfare (SAIW) Division, operating under the organic Lead Systems 
Integrator® (oLSI®) model, has the requirement to provide systems engineering and evaluation, 
Small Unmanned Air Systems (SUAS) Reusable Architecture (SRA) cybersecurity, technical 
management support, and SRA life cycle support. 
This TO will have Cost-Plus-Fixed-Fee (CPFF) term Contract Line Item Numbers (CLINs) for 
labor and cost reimbursable CLINs for Other Direct Costs (ODCs). The TO will have a base and 
four option years. A properly executed CSP will assist the Government in achieving the 
objectives of this procurement. 
2. Authority
Authority for issuance of this CSP is provided under TO Section E – Inspection and Acceptance, 
which provides for inspections and acceptance of the services, products, and documentation 
called for in the TO that will be executed by the Contracting Officer (KO) or a duly authorized 
representative. 
3. Scope
To fully understand the roles and responsibilities of the parties, it is important to first define the 
distinction in terminology between Quality Control Plan (QCP) and the CSP. The Contractor, 
and not the Government, is responsible for the QCP, which defines the management and quality 
control actions necessary to meet the quality standards set forth in the TO. 
The CSP provides Government surveillance oversight of the Contractor’s efforts to assure they 
are timely, effective, and delivering the results specified in the TO. 
4. Government Resources
The following definitions for Government resources are applicable to this plan: 
KO: A person duly appointed with the authority to enter into a contract (Procuring Contracting 
Officer (PCO)), or a person with the authority to administer contracts (Administrative 

 
  2   
   
 
Contracting Officer (ACO)) and make related determinations and findings on behalf of the 
Government. The ACO will be designated in the resulting TO. KOs are designated via a written 
warrant that sets forth limitations of authority. 
 
Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR): An individual appointed in writing by the PCO 
to act as their authorized representative to assist in administering the TO. The COR will be 
appointed in the resulting TO. The limitations of authority are contained in the letter of 
appointment. 
 
Alternate Contracting Officer’s Representative (ACOR): An individual appointed in writing 
by the PCO to act as their authorized representative, in the absence of the COR, to assist in 
administering the TO. The ACOR will be appointed in the resulting TO. The limitations of 
authority are contained in a written letter of appointment. 
 
Government Project Lead (GPL): The COR designates individual GPLs to assist in 
administering specific efforts under the TO. 
 
5. Responsibilities 
 
The following Government resources will have responsibility for the implementation of this 
CSP: 
 
KO: The KO (PCO or ACO) ensures performance of all necessary actions for effective 
contracting, ensures compliance with the terms of the TO, and safeguards the interests of the 
United States in the contractual relationship. The KO assures that the Contractor receives 
impartial, fair, and equitable treatment under the TO. The KO is ultimately responsible for the 
final determination of the adequacy of the Contractor’s performance. 
 
COR: The COR is responsible for technical administration of the TO and assures proper 
Government surveillance of the Contractor’s performance. The COR is not empowered to make 
any contractual commitments or to authorize any changes on the Government’s behalf. Any 
changes that the Contractor deems may affect the TO price, terms, or conditions shall be referred 
to the KO for action. 
 
ACOR: The ACOR assists the COR for technical administration of the TO and assures proper 
Government surveillance of the Contractor’s performance. The ACOR is not empowered to 
make any contractual commitments or to authorize any changes on the Government’s behalf. 
Any changes that the Contractor deems may affect the TO price, terms, or conditions shall be 
referred to the KO for action. 
 
GPL: The GPL is responsible for assisting in administering specific efforts under the TO. A 
GPL cannot, in any manner, alter the scope of the TO, make commitments, or authorize any 
changes on the Government’s behalf. 
 

 
  3   
   
 
6. Methods of QA Surveillance 
a. Contractor Performance Assessment Reporting System (CPARS): The marketplace 
for this type of effort is very competitive. As such, the successful Offeror has a vested 
interest in the Government generated CPARS under this TO. Additionally, an evaluation 
using the CPARS format will be performed at the end of each base or option year. This 
evaluation will be one determinant in the award of future TOs or option exercises. The 
Government will address the quality of product or service, schedule, cost control, business 
relations, management, utilization of Small Business (SB), and other important areas for this 
procurement. Some of the monitoring methods to be used will be Government observation, 
review of reports, customer feedback, and review of Contract Data Requirements Lists 
(CDRLs). As this information may affect future source selections throughout the Department 
of Defense (DoD), as well as the continuation of this tasking, the annual Government 
assessment will be used appropriately as an additional performance oversight and 
communication tool within the policies of this CSP. 
 
b. CSP: This document will be used by the COR, ACOR, and GPLs in the technical 
administration of this TO. In addition to the below instructions, the form to be used for 
documentation of QA surveillance is the Surveillance Activity Checklist (SAC). 
 
7. Surveillance 
 
Enclosure (2) sets forth the performance standards, incentives, and surveillance methods for the 
Contractor, COR, ACOR, and GPLs while Enclosures (1) and (3) provide the checklist and 
means for the COR to document the results of the surveillance and will be provided to the KO. 
 
8. Documentation 
 
In addition to providing reports to the KO, the COR will maintain a complete QA file. The file 
will contain copies of all reports, evaluations, recommendations, and any actions related to the 
Government’s performance of the QA function, including the originals of the QA Checklists. All 
such records will be maintained for the life of the TO. The COR shall forward these records to 
the KO at termination or completion of the TO. 
 
9. Enclosures

SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE 

Tracking Number 612674211


The Defense Information Systems Agency (DISA) is seeking sources for Enterprise Integration and Innovation/Emerging Technology (EII/EM8) Office for Joint Interoperability of Tactical Command and Control Systems (JINTACCs) Software Development and Sustainment. 

CONTRACTING OFFICE ADDRESS:  DITCO-NCR, 6910 Cooper Ave, Fort Meade, MD 20755

INTRODUCTION:

This is a SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE to determine the availability and technical capability of small businesses (including the following subsets: Small Disadvantaged Businesses, Certified 8(a), Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses, HUBZone Small Businesses and Woman-Owned Small Businesses) to provide the required products and/or services. 

The DISA / Emerging Technologies organization is seeking information from potential sources for software development and sustainment of two systems summarized below. 

Tactical Data Link Configuration Management Tool (TCMT)

TCMT is a Configuration Management (CM) application that was developed under a previous contract and to date can generate two documents 1) MIL-STD-6017 Variable Message Format (VMF) and 2) Joint Multi-Tactical Data Link (TDL) Operating Procedures (JMTOP) CJCSM 6120.01.  It was developed to perform CM of TDL MIL-STDs using a systematic approach that ensures consistency of processing and tracks the impacts to previously released products. The TCMT is a replacement for the legacy software TDL Document System (TDS). TCMT is composed of both Commercial-Off-The-Shelf (COTS) products and custom code. 

 

United States Message Text Format (USMTF) – Web Application (WA)

The USMTF-WA is an application in sustainment that supports the CM of MIL-STD-6040.  Specifically, the USMTF-WA is used to update the Message Text Format (MTF) message catalog.  The catalog contains over 300 message formats.  The messages are the official source for DoD entities to convey information in a non-real time format.  USMTF messages are made of Sets and Fields. Sets and Fields may be used in any of the 300+ MTF messages. 

The anticipated Period of Performance is Sep 2026 – Sep 2030.

The anticipated Place of Performance is both Fort George G. Meade (FGGM) and the contractor’s location (within 50 miles of FGGM).

DISCLAIMER: 

 

THIS SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL.  IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT.  RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS NOTICE.  NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS NOTICE.  ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY.

CONTRACT/PROGRAM BACKGROUND: 

Contract Number: HC102818D0035  HC104724F6681 

Contract Vehicle: ENCORE III Small Business Suite

Incumbent and their size: AccelGov. / Small Business. 

Method of previous acquisition: Small Business set-aside. 

Period of performance: Sep 2024 – Sep 2025 

REQUIRED CAPABILITIES: 

JINTACCS SDS involves continuing development for the current TCMT and USMTF-WA.  Describe and provide an example of your company’s experience with developing custom built user interfaces and databases that integrate COTS products, e.g. JAMA, mySQL, Kubernetes, Angular, NodeJS and NGINX. 

JINTACCS SDS work involves using data from a legacy system.  The data needs to be provided into the new system without any loss or errors.  Describe and provide an example of your company’s experience with Extract, Transform, and Load (ETL) with databases and other data sources. 

JINTACCS SDS involves maintaining and sustaining current tools.  Describe and provide an example of your company’s experience with maintenance and sustainment of systems, especially those that involve Cloud based solutions (JWCC, Amazon Web Services (AWS) etc.), Red Hat Enterprise Linus (RHEL), Windows Server, mySQL, and MS SQL, ensuring the upkeep of development, pre-production, and production Impact Level 4 (IL4) environments.

The JINTACCS SDS tools have been developed using Agile sprint releases, and the Government team expects to continue this approach.  Describe and provide an example of your company’s experience in Agile development using scrum working with multiple teams.

The JINTACCS SDS tools make use of extensible markup language (XML).  USMTF is currently transitioning to using the National Information Exchange Model (NIEM).  Describe and provide an example of your company’s experience with XML and  NIEM.

SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS: 

N/A.

SOURCES SOUGHT:  

The North American Industry Classification System Code (NAICS) for this requirement is 541512, with the corresponding size standard of $34 million. 

The purpose of this Sources Sought notice is to identify vendors with the capability to perform the services listed under the 'Required Capabilities' section below. The Government is particularly interested in identifying vendors who currently hold government vehicles and have the immediate capacity to perform these services.

To assist DISA in determining the level of participation by small business in any subsequent procurement that may result from this Sources Sought Notice, provide information regarding any plans to use joint ventures (JVs) or partnering.  Please outline the company's areas of expertise and those of any proposed JV/partner who combined can meet the specific requirements contained in this notice.

In order to make a determination for a small business set-aside, two or more qualified and capable small businesses must submit responses that demonstrate their qualifications.  Responses must demonstrate the company’s ability to perform in accordance with FAR clause 52.219-14, Limitations on Subcontracting.

SUBMISSION DETAILS:

Responses should include:

Business name and address; 

Name of company representative and their business title; 

Small Business Socio-economic status (if small); 

CAGE Code;

Prime contract vehicles; to include ENCORE III, SETI, NIH CIO-SP4, NASA SEWP V, General Service Administration (GSA): OASIS, ALLIANT II, VETS II, STARS III, MAS (including applicable SIN(s), groups or pools), or any other Government Agency contract vehicle that allows for decentralized ordering.  (This information is for market research only and businesses with a valid cage that lack prime contract vehicles are still encouraged to respond to this notice.) 

Businesses who wish to respond must send a response via email NLT 4:00 PM Eastern Daylight Time (EDT) on  to Yajie “Amy” Kim at yajie.kim.civ@mail.mil.  Interested businesses should submit a brief capabilities statement package addressing the specific questions above (no more than five pages) demonstrating the ability to perform the services listed under Required Capabilities.      

Proprietary information and trade secrets, if any, must be clearly marked on all materials.  All information received that is marked Proprietary will be handled accordingly.  All submissions become Government property and will not be returned.  All government and contractor personnel reviewing submitted responses will have signed non-disclosure agreements and understand their responsibility for proper use and protection from unauthorized disclosure of proprietary information as pursuant to 41 USC 423.  The Government shall not be held liable for any damages incurred if proprietary information is not properly identified.

For information on DISA’s requirements, you can find current information on our home page: www.disa.mil – that includes current forecast and the current acquisition strategies. If there is no information regarding the requirement you may be inquiring about, then there is no additional publicly available information. Please continue to review www.disa.mil.

Industry Questions and Government Answers

Question 1: The first page of the SF33 states the following: "6 The Government has not designated key personnel for the labor category positions associated with this Solicitation / Task Order.” However, in section 3.1.3 Element C – Personnel Approach (It requests one resume for each position) and the requirements for each Key Personnel. Can the gov't clarify if Key personnel are required or not?

Answer 1: Refer to Personal Qualifications, Attachment 02, the Government did not identify key personnel. Additionally, see Solicitation, Section A, item #6 (page 2 of 52).

Question 2: Can you clarify on the 2.5 if the File Naming Convetion is to be used or the 3.0 Proposal Organization and Content naming convention?  See illustration below:

Answer 2: See Section L, Attachment 23, paragraph 2.5 File Naming Convention. Paragraph 3.0 does not conflict with paragraph 2.5, it provides additional proposal organization context, as applicable. 

----------------------------------------------As of 19 March 2026--------------------------------------------------------------------

Question 3: N6426726R3002, Section L, p. 7: Does the 12 point Times New Roman font requirement apply to document headers and footers, or may those be less than 12 point? 

Answer 3: See Solicitation N6426726R3002, Attachment 23, SeaPort Section L, Paragraph 2.0, font text shall be 12-point Times New Roman. Yes, this includes headers and footers. See “except for” for exceptions to the 12-point font size.

Question 4: N6426726R3002, Section L, p. 7: Are Call-Out boxes considered graphics, and therefore, allowed to be no smaller than 9 point font? 

Answer 4: Call-out boxes are considered graphics.

Question 5: N6426726R3002, Section L, p. 7: Are tables considered graphics, and therefore, allowed to be no smaller than 9 point font? 

Answer 5: Tables are considered graphics. 

Question 6: N6426726R3002, Section L, p. 7: Will the Government please confirm that the hyperlinks referenced in the proposal formatting instructions refer to external hyperlinks only?

Answer 6: See Solicitation N6426726R3002, Attachment 23, SeaPort Section L, Paragraph 2.0, no hyperlinks (internal or external).

Question 7: N6426726R3002, Section L, p. 7: Because PIEE does not faciliate direct association between the prime and its subcontractors, should subcontractors reference their company and RFP number in their file names?  For example, N6426726R3002_XYZcompany_sub-to-PrimeName_Volume_III_Cost Proposal Narrative.

Answer 7: See Solicitation N6426726R3002, Attachment 23, SeaPort Section L, Paragraph 2.5, “. . . and other useful identifying information.” Yes, the example is acceptable.

Question 8: N6426726R3002, Section L, p. 7: Format instructions state, "PDF Files shall be searchable when reviewed electronically." Are images included as supporting documentation (e.g. DCAA/DCMA letter) required to be fully searchable within PDF submisisons? 

Answer 8: See Solicitation N6426726R3002, Attachment 23, SeaPort Section L, Paragraph 2.0 “PDF files shall be searchable when reviewed electronically.” This searchable requirement applies to all content within the PDF submission.

Question 9: N6426726R3002, Section L, p. 8: Instructions for Element A Technical Approach indicate offerors are to address C.5.2.7.  However, 5.2.7 is only the heading "Transition." Will the Government confirm offerors are to respond to 5.2.1.7 instead?

Answer 9: See Solicitation N6426726R3002, Attachment 23, SeaPort Section L, Paragraph 3.1.1, Element A-Technical Approach, Section C, Paragraph 5.2.7, includes subparagraph 5.2.7.1.

Question 10: N6426726R3002, SF 33, p. 10 and Section L, pgs. 8 & 9: In the instructions for Element A Technical Approach, offerors are required to address C.5.2.7, which is Transition. Offerors are also instructed to address a "detailed plan of action .... to fully assume responsibilities within 30 days" within Element B Management.  To eliminate redundancy, is it permissible for offerors to fully address transition in Element A and refer back to this section in Element B?

Answer 10: See Solicitation N6426726R3002, Attachment 23, SeaPort Section L, Paragraph 3.0, “Offeror shall organize its proposal and include all proposal content exactly as described herein.”

Question 11: N6426726R3002, Attach. 9: Will the Government confirm that Program Manager on the Past Performance Reference Form is intended to the Government Program Manager?

Answer 11: Yes. 

Question 12: SF33_Solicitation_N6426726R3002; pg. 2 of 52; section A.6 states " The Government has not designated key personnel for the labor category positions associated with this Solicitation / Task Order." However, SF33_Solicitation_N6426726R3002; pg. 12 of 52; section C-237-H002 states, "Substitution of Key Personnel." Since Key Personnel are not required, will the Government please remove section C-237-H002 from the solicitation?

Answer 12: No.

Question 13: SF33_Solicitation_N6426726R3002; pg. 2 of 52; Section A.2 states, "2. The Government contemplates award of a Cost-Plus-Fixed-Fee (CPFF) Level-of-Effort (LOE) Task Order resulting from this Solicitation." However, Section L; pg. 1 of 15; Section L, states "52.216-1 TYPE OF CONTRACT (APR 1984) - The Government contemplates award of a cost-plus-fix-fee (CPFF) contract resulting from this solicitation." Will the Government please clarify if the awarded contract will be a CPFF or CPFF LOE?

Answer 13: Amendment 0001 is forthcoming. CPFF LOE.

Question 14: N6426726R3002, Section L; pg. 4 of 15; Section L-211-H001 states "L-211-H001 UPDATES TO PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE AND DELIVERY DATES (NAVSEA) (JUN 2022) For proposal purposes the estimated date of contract, task order, or delivery order award is 05/28/2026." Will the Government please clarify the delivery order award date of 05/28/2026, as the Base Year PoP also starts May 28, 2026. Are we to assume that transition begins on May 28, 2026, and concludes 30 calendar days later?

Answer 14: Per Section L-211-H001 and Section F-CLIN 6000, Period of Performance begins 05/28/2026; and Section C, Paragraph 5.2.7, “…phase-in support shall begin at award for 30 calendar days.”

Question 15: N6426726R3002, Section L; pg. 11 of 15; 3.3.3 Cost Proposal Narrative; Direct labor rates states "Offeror and cost reimbursement subcontractors shall describe the basis of estimate for each direct labor rate proposed and provide substantiating information that fully corroborates each direct labor rate proposed." Will the Government clarify if pointing to the Wage Determination for BOE of a direct labor rate for the SCA labor categories is providing enough substantiating information for the Government? If it does not, will the Government please elaborate on what additional information the Government is requesting/requiring to see?

Answer 15: The Government has outlined specific requirements for substantiating direct labor rates. While referencing the wage determination may provide as a partial basis for estimating direct labor rates, it is unlikely to fully meet the Government's requirements for substantiating information. The solicitation explicitly requires additional substantiating information to fully corroborate each proposed rate.

Question 16: Will the Government allow offerors to add minimum hours to capture Management Support costs within a labor category for Financial Analyst?

Answer 16: The labor categories and associated hours are defined in the Attachment 01-LOE

Question 17: Attachment_01_LOE_N6426726R3002 shows "SCA - Regular - Government Site; 01313 - Secretary III (Administrative Assistant) Orlando FL, with a total of 9,560 and 1,1912 hours per yr, and Non-SCA - Regular - Contractor Site; MANP2 - Program Manager II with total hours of 4,780 and 956 hrs. per yr. of this contract." However, Attachment_02_Personnel_Qualifications_N6425726R3002 shows "01313 - Secretary III (Administrative Assistant), Orlando, FL with 4,780 hrs. and MANP2 - Program Manager II (Non-SCA), Contractor Site, with a total of 9,760 hrs."It looks as though the hours for the Secretary III, Orlando, FL, location, and MANP2 - Program Manager II were transposed. Will the Government please provide clarity to the hour discrepancies and update the applicable solicitation documents

Answer 17: Amendment 0001 is forthcoming. Attachment 02-Personnel Qualification will be updated.

Question 18: Attachment_12_GFP_N6426726R3002 shows a total of 12 laptops the Government will provide. Will the Government also be providing laptops for the remaining staff?

Answer 18: The Government will provide laptops for filled positions.  

Question 19: N6426726R3002, Section L; pg. 9: Section L states, "Note: .... Nevertheless, in the Staffing Plan narrative, Offeror may describe actions it has taken to mitigate the impact of these risks to the Government." Will the Government confirm Offerors may provide the staffing Plan Narrative within Volume I Element C - Personnel Approach and there is no page limit?

Answer 19: See Solicitation N6426726R3002, Attachment 23, SeaPort Section L, Paragraph 3.0, Element C: Personnel Approach there is no page limit, which includes Staffing Plan.

Question 20: File Submission Format: One File Per Volume vs. Multiple Files

Reference: Solicitation N6426726R3002, Attachment 23 (Section L), Page 8 of 15, Paragraph 2.5 (File Naming Convention)

Section 2.5 provides file naming examples that appear to suggest individual files per document (e.g., separate files for Technical Approach and Key Personnel Resumes within Volume I). May an Offeror submit each proposal volume as a single consolidated PDF file (e.g.,CompanyName_Volume_I_Technical.pdf containing Element A, Element B, and all Element C content)? Or does the Government require each element and document within a volume to be uploaded as a separate file in the PIEE Solicitation Module?

Answer 20: See Solicitation N6426726R3002, Attachment 23, SeaPort Section L, Paragraph 3.0 “Offeror shall

organize its proposal into separate volumes …”  

Question 21: Reference: Solicitation N6426726R3002, Attachment 23 (Section L), Page 4 of 15, Paragraph 3.1.2 (Element B — Management Approach) and Proposal Organization Table (Page 3 of 15, Paragraph 3.0)

Question: Element B — Management Approach requires Offerors to address eight distinct areas including overall management approach, organizational chart, communications plan, quality control process, cost monitoring approach, risk management approach, subcontractor management, and a detailed 30-day transition plan with measurable milestones. The Proposal Organization Table allocates 10 pages to Element B. Element A — Technical Approach, which requires discussion of four specific SOW paragraphs, is allocated 20 pages.

Given the breadth and specificity of the eight requirements in Element B , particularly the requirement for a detailed transition plan with measurable milestones addressing hiring, onboarding, and training , does the 10-page limit for Element B apply to the Management Approach content only, with the transition plan excluded from that page count? Or does the 10-page limit encompass all Element B content including the transition plan?

Answer 21: See Solicitation N6426726R3002, Attachment 23, SeaPort Section L, Paragraph 3.0, “Offeror shall organize its proposal and include all proposal content exactly as described herein.” 

Question 22: Will the Government permit offerors to utilize the format in Attachment 09 and include all past performance references in Volume II?

Answer 22: See Solicitation N6426726R3002, Attachment 23, SeaPort Section L, Paragraph 3.2, “Offeror shall provide all past performance information in accordance with Attachment 09 – Past Performance Reference.”

Question 23: If offerors can confirm that no OCI exist, are they still required to submit an OCI Mitigation plan within Volume IV Contract Documentation?

Answer 23: See Solicitation N6426726R3002, Attachment 23, SeaPort Section L, Paragraph 3.4.1, “If an Offeror believes no organizational conflict(s) of interest exists, an affirmative statement that no such conflict exists shall be included in the cover letter.” … “If it is believed that no conflicts of interest exist, then the Offeror shall clearly state this, in addition to providing their corporate policy for resolving OCIs.”

Question 24: Attachments 01 and Attachment 02 hours vary for the Program Manager and the Secretary III in Orlando, FL. Will the Government please confirm the total hours offerors are to bid for the Program Manager and the Secretary III in Orlando, FL.

Answer 24: See answer for question #17. 

Question 25: In regards to the Technical Approach to SOW 5.2.7, will the Government please confirm if offerors are to write an approach as the incumbent contractor supporting a new contractor as a phase-in plan? OR, should the approach be written as the new contractor coming into and taking over the contract?

Answer 25: See Solicitation N6426726R3002, Section C, SOW, Paragraph 5.2.7 “… other than the incumbent Contractor, phase-in support shall begin at award for 30 calendar days,” “ ... Contractor shall provide a transition out plan IAW CDRL A008, for phase-out support,” and Attachment 23, SeaPort Section L, Paragraph 3.1.1, “Offeror shall describe its specific understanding, capability, experience, and technical approach.” 

Question 26: N6426726R3002, Section L; pgs. 8 and 9: In Section L, 3.0 Proposal Organization and Content, Offerors are allocated 10 pages for Element B Management Approach.  However, as indicated in Section L, 3.1.2, there are 8 bulleted items required for response. Will the Government consider allowing 15 pages for the Element B management section response?

Answer 26: No.

Question 27: N6426726R3002, Section L; pg. 10, Section 3.2 Volume II Past Performance (Factor 2): Will the Government allow offerors to provide a one-page introduction for their Volume II Past Performance responses?

Answer 27: See Solicitation N6426726R3002, Attachment 23, SeaPort Section L, Paragraph 3.0 “Page limitations will be treated as maximums.”

Question 28: N6426726R3002, Section L; pgs. 8 and 10, Section L instructions for Past Performance (L.3.2.2) state, "Offeror shall provide three past performance references, if available, which shall reflect recent experience performed within the last five (5) years of the solicitation release date and that demonstrates experience relevant to the solicitation’s PWS/SOW."  However, the Technical Volume instructions (L.3.1.1) specify four SOW paragraphs (5.2.1.1, 5.2.1.2, 5.2.7, 5.2.1.10) requiring response. Will the Government clarify if it's your intent for past performance responses to address all RFP SOW Performance Requirement areas or only the four specified for the Technical Approach?

FY27 COMMON MISSILE COMPARTMENT (CMC) 

1.0	Product Service Code (PSC)  

L014 – Technical Representative – Guided Missiles

2.0	North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code	

The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 541330 - Engineering Services.

3.0	Contracting Office Address

Strategic Systems Programs (SSP)

1250 10th Street, Suite 4600

Washington DC 20374

4.0	Synopsis

This is a SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE (SSN) announcement.  SSNs are issued to assist the Agency in performing market research to determine industry interest and capability.  THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION FOR PROPOSALS AND NO CONTRACT SHALL BE AWARDED FROM THIS SYNOPSIS. Therefore, no proposals are being requested or accepted in response to this SSN. 

5.0	Purpose

In accordance with (IAW) Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 10, SSP is conducting market research to determine if sources are capable of successfully performing the requirements identified in this SSN. Specifically, SSP is seeking capable firms to support Trident II (D5LE) Missile Reentry Subsystems supplies and services in support of the construction of the Common Missile Compartment for the Columbia Class Submarine as identified in the enclosure  (1) SSN Statement of Work (SOW) cited in paragraph 8.0 below. 

The contract type will include Cost Plus Fixed Fee, Level-of-Effort (LOE) and Completion Term Contract Line Item Numbers (CLINS).  The performance of the Contract will be from 1 March 2027 – 28 February 2032. 

NOTE: Given the highly technical nature of SSP’s mission set as a major weapons systems command and corresponding technical requirements, respondents must provide recent and relevant past performance data (as detailed below) to demonstrate and substantiate the respondents’ ability to successfully execute requirements detailed in this SSN. 

6.0	White Paper Capability Statement Credentials

a.  SSP is seeking detailed, complete, and thorough White Paper capability statements from interested firms who can demonstrate and document that they 1) possess the minimum qualifications and experience identified in paragraph 7.0 which are critical to the successful execution of the requirements, and 2) demonstrate recent and relevant experience, as the Prime contractor (or subcontractor) performing the same/similar efforts of the same/similar scope, size, and complexity to the enclosure (1) SSN SOW requirements identified in paragraph 8.0.  Interested firms must demonstrate their existing capability, or potential to acquire the capability, to meet the enclosure (1) SSN SOW requirements by the time of contract award, estimated to be 1 March 2027. 

6.1	Small Business Concerns

IAW FAR Subpart 19.101 Small business goals, SSP seeks to provide maximum practicable opportunities in its acquisitions to small business, veteran-owned small business, service-disabled veteran-owned small business, HUBZone small business, small disadvantaged business, and women-owned small business concerns.  Small Business Concerns who possess the minimum qualifications and experience identified in paragraph 7.0 and who can demonstrate the capability (or ability to obtain the capability by the contract award date) to execute the complete requirements identified in the enclosure (1) SSN SOW in paragraph 8.0, as well provide the requisite past performance experience detailed in Section 9.0, are encouraged to respond to this SSN.  

If a small business concern intends to partner with another entity, the small business concern must identify which specific enclosure (1) SOW efforts/tasks it intends to perform, as well as the specific efforts/tasks the partner will perform, with the substantiating data required in this SSN supporting the identified partnering roles and responsibilities.  NOTE: 100% of the enclosure (1) SOW and SSN requirements must be addressed in any submitted partnering submittal, if obtainable. 

NOTE:  In the event this contract is set aside for small business concerns, the small business concern agrees that it will be in strict compliance and conformance with the percentage payment limitations for services, supplies, or construction (as applicable) to subcontractors that are not similarly situated entities in accordance with FAR 52.219-14 Limitations on Subcontracting and state such in their response.  

7.0	Minimum Qualifications / Experience Requirements

Interested firms shall document and submit specific and evidenced / demonstrated possession of the minimum qualifications and experience requirements in the technical areas identified in enclosure (1) SSN SOW requirements in paragraph 8.0.  This experience shall be documented as specified in paragraph 9.0. SSP requires Engineering Services to support integration of existing Trident II (D5) Submarine Launched Ballistic Missiles, including Nuclear Reentry Bodies into new U.S. and U.K. submarine classes. The Engineering Services sought will support completion of the submarine designs, and the construction and test support for both classes. SSP requires Engineering Services to support the design and production of Submarine Launched Ballistic Missile servicing support equipment, and the development, production, and integration of specialized Submarine Launched Ballistic Missile simulator test equipment. The Period of Performance is estimated to be five (5) years.

NOTE:  This requirement will entail the development and delivery of Digital Engineering (DE) Contract Data Requirements List (CDRL) deliverables.  Firms must identify their present capability to develop and deliver DE CDRL deliverables.

8.0	Description of Requirements  

See enclosure (1) SSN SOW Requirements.  

8.1	Quantity of Personnel Required / Place of Performance

There will be no Full Time Equivalent (FTE) personnel who will provide on-site support at the Washington Navy Yard. 

9.0	Evidentiary Qualifications/Experience Documentation Requirements

Interested firms must possess the requisite minimum qualifications and experience identified in paragraph 7.0 and demonstrated relevant and recent experience as it relates to the enclosure (1) SOW requirements in paragraph 8.0. White Paper Capability statements must include all of the content and details identified below: 

9.1	Minimum Qualifications / Experience Requirements Validation

White Paper Capability statement submissions shall include a discrete section with the heading “Minimum Qualifications / Experience Requirements” and document, with specific information, each of the minimum qualifications identified in paragraph 7.0.  This section may cite contract reference efforts detailed in Table A of paragraph 9.2 below provided that respondents provide context and rationale as to how that contract reference effort(s) demonstrate possession of the applicable Minimum Qualifications / Experience requirements identified in paragraph 7.0 – or have capability of obtaining by contract award.

9.2	Relevant & Recent Experience / Supporting Narratives

In addition to demonstrating possession of the requisite Minimum Qualifications / Experience requirements identified in paragraph 7.0 above (or have capability of obtaining by contract award), interested firms shall demonstrate relevant and recent experience performing the same or similar efforts and or completion tasks (as applicable) to the enclosure (1) SSN SOW requirements in paragraph 8.0.  Relevant experience is defined as performing efforts/tasks similar in scope, size, and complexity as the enclosure (1) SSN SOW requirements with an annual incurred cost/expense of at least $3.5M.  Recent experience is defined as work performed within 5 years of the SSN posting date.  To substantiate the performance of relevant and recent efforts/tasks to the enclosure (1) SSN SOW requirements, White Paper Capability statements shall provide a list of current or previous contract references and the efforts/tasks performed thereunder detailing and evidencing a direct correlation of the contract reference efforts/tasks to the enclosure (1) SSN SOW using the specific outline provided in Table A below.  Submitter’s responses to the Table A SSN CLIN SOW outline shall include the following information per individual contract reference: 

Summary of relevant work performed and how that specific work demonstrates capability to perform the specific requirements identified in the enclosure (1) SSN SOW requirements;

Current / Prior Contract Number(s) and Customer/Agency Supported; 

Identification of your role as the Prime or Subcontractor; 

Contract Type; 

Period of performance of the specific contract reference effort performed;

Quantity of FTE personnel utilized on the specific contract reference effort, per annum, with distinction and FTE quantities identified between the respondents FTE employees and any subcontractor FTE employees; 

Net Dollar value (base and options) for each contract reference and the Annual Incurred costs for each contract reference provided which demonstrates the magnitude of those contract references in comparison to the annual estimated value cited in paragraph 9.2 above.  NOTE: solely citing an IDIQ ceiling amount or base and all options aggregate value without the annual incurred costs for the submitted contract reference(s) is NOT acceptable – amounts must be specific to the actual incurred costs for a Contract CLIN(s) or Individual Task Order(s), for the contract reference(s) cited in Table A below; and

Customer point of contact with valid phone number and email.

TABLE A – SUMMARY OF RELEVANT & RECENT WORK EXPERIENCE

10.0	Company Information and Deadline for Submittal

White Paper Capability statements shall be submitted in Microsoft Word for Office 2000 compatible format or PDF format and are due no later than 10 April 2026, 4:00pm EST.  The White Papers shall not exceed 5 pages in total, using 12-point Times New Roman and 1” margin and shall be submitted via e-mail to Elizabeth.Tamas@ssp.navy.mil and Angela.McKelvey@ssp.navy.mil. NOTE: The page count, font size, and margin requirements apply to the entire SSN response, to include any Cover Page, Attachments, Headers, Footers, etc. “excluding” the Company Administrative Information below.  

The Government is seeking detailed content and responses to the SSN requirements over any promotional details, pictures, etc. 

ALL White Paper Capability submittals shall include the following Company Administrative Data which is NOT counted in the aforementioned maximum 5-page limit:

 

Company Administrative Information

Company Name:

Company Point of Contact (email and phone) and Title:

Company Address:

Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) No:

Cage Code:

Size of business, including; total annual revenue, by year, for the past five years and number of employees; 

Ownership, including whether: small business, veteran-owned small business, service-disabled veteran-owned small business, HUBZone small business, small disadvantaged business, and women-owned small business concerns;

Number of years in business; 

Identification of the current security clearance held at your facility that will provide support to the enclosure (1) SOW requirements.  NOTE: Work to be performed under this contract shall require the contractor to have a facility clearance of SECRET and a computing facility that is cleared to process SECRET data. 

Respondents to this SSN shall indicate which portions of their response are proprietary/business sensitive and should mark them accordingly.  It is the responsibility of the SSN respondent to monitor the sam.gov website for additional information pertaining to any potential acquisition.

11.0	Government Assessment

The White Paper Capability statement responses to this SSN must meet the requirements stated in the SSN and will be reviewed to determine whether each respondent is capable of performing the requirements.  This review will be based solely on the specific data and supporting content provided by the respondents in their White Paper Capability statement submissions and responses to any follow on clarification inquires submitted by the Government.  Incomplete or generalized White Paper Capability statements, without specificity as it relates to the SSN content requirements, omitted content, or content which fails to address all of the requirements of this SSN, will have a direct effect upon the Government’s assessment of the White Paper submittal.   The Government’s assessment will include, but is not limited to, the following: 

(1) The respondent’s specific and evidenced / demonstrated possession of the Minimum Qualifications / Experience requirements identified in paragraph 7.0;

DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION 
FEDERAL HIGHWAY ADMINISTRATION 
JUSTIFICATION FOR OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION  
 
 
1. Identification of the agency and the contracting activity  
 
Federal Highway Administration Headquarters, Office of Acquisition and Grants 
Management, 1200 New Jersey Avenue, S.E., Washington, DC 20590. 
 
- for     - 
 
The Build America Bureau, U.S. DOT Office of the Secretary (the Bureau) 
1200 New Jersey Avenue, S.E., Washington, DC 20590 
 
 
2. Nature and/or description of the action being approved 
 
The Bureau has a requirement for specialized financial analysis and credit risk modeling 
support services to support components of its Credit Programs. Specifically, this 
requirement would be for unique and critical services that will support and maintain the 
Railroad Credit Assessment and Portfolio Management System (RCAPM) that supports 
the Bureau credit Office’s (OST-Z20) Railroad Rehabilitation and Improvement 
Financing (RRIF) Program, and assists OST-Z20 in generating loan level subsidy 
calculations, modification cost analyses, and annual re-estimates, as well as the annual 
budget formulation calculations in accordance with Federal Credit Reform Act (CRA) 
requirements. 
 
3. Description of the supplies or services required to meet the agency’s needs 
(including the estimated value) 
 
Task 1: Maintenance of Railroad Credit Assessment and Portfolio Management System 
x Maintain, test, and deploy two separate RCAPM production instances (external with 
2-factor auth; internal with PIV/OWIN/iCAM), plus two staging environments for each; 
follow Configuration Control Board (CCB) procedures for all code/data changes and 
facilitate internal/external testing prior to production rollout. 
x Ensure error-free operation of all RCAPM modules (CRA, Re-estimate, Budget 
Formulation, Modification, Loan Management), provide technical support and coding 
fixes, and manage security remediation per severity timelines (Critical: immediate; High: 
30 days; Medium: 60 days; Low: 90 days), including participation in monthly security 
briefings and ongoing control assessments. 
x Maintain comprehensive continuity and recovery procedures to minimize downtime, 
participate in tabletop and full contingency exercises (failovers, backups, restorations), 

2 
 
and ensure compliance of contractor processes with required security assessment 
controls. 
Task 2: Updates to the Railroad Credit Assessment and Portfolio Management System 
x Ensure RCAPM credit-subsidy modules (CRA, Re-estimate, Budget Formulation) stay 
consistent with OMB’s Credit Subsidy Calculator and update CRA inputs (discount rates, 
default/recovery rates, collateral haircuts, borrower rates) as required. 
x Support Loan Management System data import, management, and reporting—guarantee 
error-free data transfer to dependent modules, implement changes for new 
reporting/data/import requirements and external system interfaces (Delphi, iCAM, 
OMB), and manage users/user groups and access. 
x 3HUIRUP KLVWRULFDO GHIDXOW DQDO\VLV  UDWHG FRPSDQLHV  WRXSGDWH ORJLVWLF UHJUHVVLRQ
coefficients for the internal credit-rating model and RRIF portfolio adjustments, apply 
results to RCAPM, and update all supporting documentation. 
Task 3: Develop and Conduct Training for RCAPM system to Bureau Personnel 
x The Contractor shall develop and provide in-person training for RCAPM system to the 
Bureau staff on an as needed basis during the life of the contract. Training shall be 
provided at the Bureau site. 
Task 4: Provide Modeling Support 
x Consult with the Bureau on complex subsidy calculations, provide recommendations, and 
assist with audit responses related to the RCAPM system. 
x Run subsidy scenarios (including altering technical assumptions), perform modification 
analyses with supporting spreadsheets, and build Excel-based models for analyses outside 
the RCAPM framework when needed. 
x Participate in third-party meetings as requested (e.g., OMB, DOT leadership, OST, 
Treasury, ESC) to represent analyses and coordinate with stakeholders. 
Task 5: Provide Budget Formulation, FAIC / Reestimate, and Loan Management Support 
x Provide budget formulation and execution support: determine Budgetary Resources for 
Delphi’s Budget Execution Module, produce supporting spreadsheets and an annual 
methodology summary, prepare Credit Supplement input for the President’s Budget, and 
compute Financing Account Interest (FAIC) and year-end borrowings. 
x Perform interest and technical re-estimates and reconciliations: run Re-estimate Module 
calculations with memos for the Bureau/OMB, update R-Summary for OST/OMB 
approval, recalculate interest/principal and revise repayment schedules on prepayments, 
and reconcile loans monthly between ESC and LMS. 
x Support audits and portfolio actions: respond to borrower audit requests with LMS/ESC 
reconciliations, review requests to sell collateral for financing-agreement compliance, 
and implement required LMS updates. 

3 
 
Task 6: Ongoing RRIF Program Support 
x Provide information for the preparation of the apportionments (SF-132s) to OST for 
OMB signature. 
x Review the budget execution reports (SF-133s) on a monthly basis and reconcile against 
the RCAPM system. 
x Work with ESC to identify unobligated balances to be transferred to the Treasury’s 
general fund. 
x Support the preparation of MAX Data based on OMB Circular A-11. 
x Support of financial inquiries and payment/disbursement processing requests for the 
RRIF program from financial reporting team. 
The total estimated amount of this anticipated contract is  to be expended 
over an 23-month period of performance. 
 
 
4. Statutory authority permitting other than full and open competition 
 
The authority to enter into a contract for this effort without full and open competition is 
DOT Deviation No.2025-010 dated July 24,2025, which implements the Revolutionary 
FAR Overhaul (RFO) Part 6 competition requi rements per 6.103-1. Only one responsible 
source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements.  This justification 
is prepared under the authority of 41 U.S.C. 1901. BancLab designed the subject portfolio 
management tool, inclusive of coding, calcu lations, and updates to align with Bureau 
practices. Searches for contractors/vendors  with the requisite knowledge of the RRIF 
program in concert with an understanding of federal credit subsidy program reporting and 
having a readily available portfolio management tool for a seamless transition to the DOT 
and Bureau’s future state (Google) operating environment revealed that BancLab is the 
only knowledgeable contractor that can provi de this service as required and without 
substantive delay. 
 
5.  Demonstration that the proposed contractor’s unique qualifications or the nature of 
the acquisition requires use of the authority cited 
 
BancLab LLC built the RCAPM Application for the Bureau’s RRIF credit program.  This 
includes coding, subsidy calculations/inter polation, program modules, and reporting 
functionality that comports with the requirements of the Credit Reform Act. The Bureau 
relies on the functionality and unconstrained availability of RCAPM to manage its RRIF 
program.  Only Banclab has the required knowledge and experience to support and 
maintain this system in the short term while the Department of Transportation transitions 
to Google and aligns its requi rement with the OneGov initiative. This sole source award 
will allow time for the Government to transition this requirement to a competitive 
requirement in the future.   
 
Market Research performed resulted in no other commercially available solution or vendor 
that provides an application with this f unctionality readily available and without a 


4 
 
requirement for extensive customization to meet the needs of the RRIF program. The time 
and coordination efforts required to develop and customize a comparable application will 
hinder the Bureau’s ability to facilitate the close of RRIF projects currently in the credit 
review process that require financial information/parameters produced by RCAPM and/or 
unintentionally cause delays and inaccurate reporting of end of year calculations and audits.  
Due to the timeframe required and the unique qualifications of Banclab, only one source 
will satisfy the Government’s requirement.  
 
 
 
7. Determination by the Contracting Officer that the anticipated cost to the 
Government will be fair and reasonable 
 
The FHWA Contracting Officer will conduct a price analysis of the contractor’s proposal 
to  ensure that all costs associated with the proposed contract are fair and reasonable.   
8. Description of the market research conducted and the results or a statement of the 
reason market research was not conducted 
 
The GSAeLibrary Contractor Listing was searched for the presence of qualified contractors 
using NAICS Code 541511 (Custom Computer Programming Services) and key words 
indicative of the knowledge and experience requi red to perform the services required for 
successful performance under this contract.  No contractors were identified.  Additionally, 
online searched for vendors providing such services supporting federal programs did not 
identify any sources that could meet the Bureau’s immediate needs.  
 
9. Other facts supporting the use of other than full and open competition 
 
The Build America Bureau intends to recompete this requirementvia full and open 
competition in the future. To allow for full and open competition, the Government intends

ATTACHMENT 1: SOLICITATION TOPICS AREAS/AREAS OF INTEREST

Problem Statement 

DLA Aviation Engineering needs a way to develop Engineering Support Activities (ESA) approvable level 3 TDPs per MIL-STD-31000 and ASME Y14.100 for government use in order to enable competitive procurement for parts that are considered hard to procure and/or non-procurable. 

Background

As the nation’s logistics combat support agency, the Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) manages the end-to-end global defense supply chain – from raw material to end user disposition – for the five military services, 11 combatant commands, other federal, state and local agencies, and partner and allied nations. 

DLA’s mission is to “deliver readiness and lethality to the Warfighter Always and support our nation through quality, proactive global logistics.” To accomplish this mission, DLA has a staff of about 25,000 employees divided into multiple supply chains that contract for materiel and services across the military classes of supply: subsistence (food/water), clothing and textiles, bulk petroleum and other energy products, construction materiel and equipment, personal demand items, medical materiel and equipment, and repair parts for land, sea and air systems. (Defense Logistics Agency, 2024)

DLA Aviation engineering provides program management and technical expertise for engineering programs for the Aviation Supply Chain (ASC). DLA Aviation engineering mission is to improve the quality and lead time of DLA Aviation’s Products/Services through source development, product improvement, reverse engineering, organic manufacturing, sustainment and reliability initiatives and other technical services. DLA Aviation engineering is interested in filling a capability gap to develop technical data when limited item data is available, obsolete and/or no DLA stock on hand. As a result, the submission should address risk to mitigate contested logistics challenges and support demand surges during conflict.  Submissions should describe unique aspects of your solutions that fill capability needs as it related to the problem statement.  The level of detail provided for each desired solution feature or the order in which they appear is not intended to convey any information regarding relative priority.

Desired Solution Features

3.1	Phased approach to create and provide complete ESA approvable Level 3 TDPs that specifies method of manufacturing and technical requirements

3.2	Build and validate a proof-of-concept model for developing, coordinating and approving Technical Data Packages (TDPs), (i.e., manufacturing capability for enabling TDP creation) when existing engineering pathways are counterproductive

3.3	Clear and comprehensive framework for obtaining and managing intellectual property (IP) rights for the technical data packages, with a focus on government purpose rights. This is necessary to ensure that the government has the rights to use, modify, and distribute the technical data packages for government purposes, including procurement and sustainment activities while also ensuring that the rights of IP owners are respected and protected

Project Expectations 

4.1	Provide an initial proof-of-concept to rapidly develop and demonstrate a process to develop and deliver technical data for jointly selected candidate parts for specific weapon systems 16-26 weeks from award. 

4.2	Create and develop innovative tools, methodologies, and qualification frameworks that accelerate future efforts when limited item data is available, obsolete, and/or there is no stock on hand to support a reverse engineering effort.

4.3 	There is no specific Technology Readiness Level (TRL) requirement; however, proposed solutions should be approximately TRL 6 and above to enable assessment of the technical feasibility, responsiveness, viability, and desirability of the proposed solution and support a rapid transition into operation. We're seeking solutions that are developed and proven enough to be quickly adaptable for use in real-world situations. Ideally, your technology has already been successfully piloted or deployed in a commercial setting. This will allow us to effectively evaluate its potential for national security applications and ensure a smooth transition into active use.

4.4	Build and strengthen partnerships (traditional or non-traditional contractors) across the global defense industrial base and increase alignment with ESAs. Engage innovative non-traditional suppliers that do not work with the government. 

4.5	Assess and shape the risk: identify and mitigate supply chain vulnerabilities within the global Defense Industrial Base.  

Intellectual Property

At a minimum, DLA anticipates acquiring Intellectual Property:

5.1	Identify and describe any technical rights, including intellectual property rights, that are part of the proposed solution. This includes, but is not limited to, information, products, or services that are protected by law as intangible property, including data (e.g., technical data and computer software), technical know-how, inventions, creative works of expression, and trade names.   Minimum Rights in Technical Data and Computer Software including marking requirements will be outlined in the resultant Performance Work Statement. 

5.2 	Technical data for the solution: 

5.2.1	 Necessary for operation, maintenance, or training;  

5.2.2 	That describes the required overall physical, functional, and performance characteristics (along with the qualification requirements, if applicable) of an item, component, or process to the extent necessary to permit identification of physically and functionally interchangeable items. This is often called ‘form, fit, and function’ data (see 48 C.F.R. § 252.227-7015(a)(3)); and

5.2.3	The primary purpose of the resulting procurement is to develop Engineering Support Activities (ESA) approvable level 3 TDPs per MIL-STD-31000 and ASME Y14.100 for government use in order to enable release to the public for competitive procurement of parts that are considered hard to procure and/or non-procurable.  

5.2.4	The IP rights are fully negotiable; however, the project goal is to develop TDPs for competitive procurement, which includes Government Purpose Rights, Specially Negotiated License Rights, and Unlimited Rights for the U.S. Government partner.

Foreign Ownership and Control; Foreign Access to Technology

6.1	The Responder  shall provide details of any foreign ownership or control that may exist within their corporate structure. 

6.2	The Responder shall have the ability to create and store export-controlled data in accordance with export control regulations.

Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM)

Proposer solution brief must provide a ROM estimate for each desired solution feature in section 3 above.

Submission Instructions

Solutions Briefs are due no later than March 14, 2025, at 5:00PM EDT. Please submit the Solution Briefs via email to Thomas Walsh Thomas.Walsh@dla.mil.

Area of Interest 05- Decision Analytics, Operational Planning and Predictive and 
Probabilistic AI Modeling 
ATTACHMENT 1: SOLICITATION TOPICS AREAS/AREAS OF INTEREST 
 
1.0 Problem Statement  
DLA has an urgent demand for improved visibility of the supply chains to respond 
proactively.  DLA requires artificial intelligence (AI) capability to interact with critical 
operational data in a classified environment leveraging DLA's existing Gemini-AI based large 
language model (LLM).     
 
2.0 Background 
As the nation’s logistics combat support agency, the Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) manages 
the end-to-end global defense supply chain – from raw material to end user disposition – for the 
five military services, 11 combatant commands, other federal, state and local agencies, and 
partner and allied nations.  
 
DLA’s mission is to “deliver readiness and lethality to the Warfighter Always and support our 
nation through quality, proactive global logistics.” To accomplish this mission, DLA has a staff 
of about 25,000 employees divided into multiple supply chains that contract for materiel and 
services across the military classes of supply: subsistence (food/water), clothing and textiles, 
bulk petroleum and other energy products, construction materiel and equipment, personal 
demand items, medical materiel and equipment, and repair parts for land, sea and air systems. 
(Defense Logistics Agency, 2024) 
 
DLA J6 provides program management, information technology, and technical expertise to 
enable secure, scalable digital capabilities across the enterprise.  As operations become more 
complex and unpredictable, DLA requires enhanced capabilities to improve data visibility, 
integration, and decision making. 
 
The current analytical tools are insufficient and lack the necessary interaction with data to enable 
decision making based on probabilistic and predictive models.  Additionally, current processes 
and solutions do not provide timely access to logistics data sourced from enterprise resource 
planning (ERP) systems and other operational data repositories, causing delays in decision 
making, reducing operational efficiency. Current systems do not allow personnel to interact 
effectively with critical operational data in classified environments or leverage predictive and 
probabilistic insights.  To address these gaps, DLA is pursuing the rapid deployment of a 
Gemini-based prototype to provide the agency with improved access to and interaction with 
critical, operational data – including data derived from ERP systems and related logistics 
platforms, in both SIPR and NIPR environments.  This capability leverages DLA’s existing 
Gemini-AI LLM, which serves as the foundational user interface and reasoning engine, enabling 
personnel to interact with data using natural language queries to generate insights and support 
decision making.  This capability empowers personnel to anticipate and mitigate risk, respond 
proactively to disruptions, and maintain continuous support even in challenging or contested
