United States Geological Survey (USGS) 
Request for Information (RFI) and Sources Sought 
Economic Analysis of the Earth Mapping Resources Initiative (Earth MRI) 
 
General Information 
Tracking Number:    140G0126Q0082 (SAM.gov) 
      RFI1802859 (ebuy.gsa.gov) 
Release of RFI Date:    03/26/2026     
Response Submission Date:   04/14/2026 
NAICS Code:     541611 (Administrative Management and General 
Management Consulting Services) 
GSA MAS Schedule Category (SIN)  541611 (Professional Services/Business    
      Administrative Services) 
 
This is a Request for Information (RFI).  This is not a solicitation for a contract award.  This action is for 
market research (information) purposes only, is not a request for proposals or quotations, and does not 
obligate the Government in any way.  A solicitation may or may not result from this request.  The 
Government will not reimburse the respondents for any costs associated with the information submitted in 
response to this request.  The Government will treat each submission in confidence.  Responses will assist 
the USGS in understanding available analytical approaches and organizational capabilities relevant to 
conducting an economic analysis of the USGS Earth Mapping Resources Initiative (Earth MRI) within 
the Geology, Energy, and Minerals Mission Area (GEMMA). 
 
I. Introduction  
The Nation’s geologic framework is under-mapped relative to other developed nations. We lack the 
systematic, high-quality data needed to understand our nation’s geologic resources and address its 
changing mineral needs.  In 2019, the USGS launched the Earth MRI to answer this challenge by 
transforming and modernizing the Nation’s mapping of the surface and subsurface.  Furthermore, E.O. 
14154, Unleashing American Energy (January 20, 2025) directly calls on the USGS to “accelerate the 
ongoing, detailed geologic mapping of the United States, with a focus on locating previously unknown 
deposits of critical minerals” through the Earth MRI.   
 
In 2021, Earth MRI received $320 million in supplemental funding to spend over five years (FY22-FY26) 
from the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (IIJA).  IIJA funding dramatically accelerated the pace of 
the program and the scope of data collection.  The USGS partners with state geological surveys, private 
industry, federal agencies, tribes and others to prioritize work and to collect and disseminate data.  
Through these partnerships, Earth MRI leverages both national-scale coordination and local expertise to 
maximize the value and impact of data collection.   
 
Earth MRI is collecting an unprecedented volume of foundational geoscience data across the full extent of 
the nation that presently includes geophysical, geochemical, hyperspectral, topographic, geologic and 
mine waste data of the surface and subsurface.  The USGS is providing a crucial national perspective of 
the nation’s geology and mineral resources by making these data publicly available and ready for 
integration and analysis.  Earth MRI data collection is presently focused in areas with potential critical 
and industrial minerals, including in mine wastes.  Additionally, the same data provide essential 
information about groundwater and energy resources, potential natural hazards, and infrastructure needs 
in these areas, informing management of wide-ranging natural resources.  In some applications, Earth 
MRI datasets may also be used in combination with other publicly available federal datasets, including 
satellite-based Earth observation systems such as Landsat, to improve understanding of geologic features, 
surface conditions, and resource potential.   
 

2 
 
USGS is exploring approaches for conducting an economic analysis of the Earth MRI to better understand 
the economic value and estimated return on investment associated with Earth MRI activities and data 
products.  This RFI is intended to inform the USGS about vendor interest, capabilities, and experience in 
performing these services.   
 
II. Analytical Considerations 
USGS seeks information on analytical approaches and technical expertise relevant to evaluating the 
economic value and benefits associated with Earth MRI activities, data, maps, and other products, 
including both current program outputs and potential future benefits associated with expanded data 
collection.  The analysis may evaluate direct and indirect economic benefits associated with Earth MRI, 
including the value of Earth MRI data products used in science, operational applications, and decision-
making.  The study may examine how these data products support mineral resource assessments, resource 
exploration activities and investments, infrastructure planning, hazard understanding, and other 
applications supported by improved geologic information.  Improved geologic information reduces 
uncertainty and risk associated with mineral exploration and may motivate, direct, and accelerate 
investment and (or) resource development decisions.  In many cases, improved geologic information may 
create both direct and indirect economic value by reducing uncertainty and improving the quality of 
information available for decision-making, which may influence resource exploration and related 
investment decisions, capital allocation, and resource development planning.   
 
In addition to market impacts, the analysis may consider non-market benefits associated with publicly 
available Earth MRI data products.  Where feasible, these benefits should be quantified using appropriate 
economic approaches.  In cases where benefits cannot be readily monetized, qualitative assessment may 
be appropriate to describe the broader value of Earth MRI.  The analysis may also consider how Earth 
MRI data may be used, or may increasingly be used, in future applications, in combination with other 
publicly available datasets, including satellite-based Earth observation systems such as Landsat, and how 
integration of geologic and remotely sensed datasets may enhance interpretation of surface conditions, 
resource potential, and related decision-making. 
 
Multiple analytical approaches may be appropriate for evaluation of the value of publicly available 
geoscience data programs, and respondents may describe approaches that capture how current/future 
Earth MRI datasets influence exploration activities, investment decisions, resource management, and 
other applications supported by improved geologic information.  Economic approaches should be 
consistent with Office of Management and Budget (OMB) guidance for economic analysis, where 
possible.  Findings from the analysis will inform program planning, investment decisions, and evaluation 
of future Earth MRI activities. 
 
III. Data Collection Considerations 
Understanding how Earth MRI activities, data, maps, and other products are used and applied may 
involve collecting information from data users and subject matter experts.  Responses should place 
emphasis on applications related to mineral exploration and development, while also considering the 
broader range of users and use cases supported by Earth MRI.  The specific type of data collection would 
depend on the analytical methods and study design proposed, and not all activities described below would 
necessarily be required.  Potential options might include user engagement methods such as surveys, 
interviews, workshops, focus groups, etc. to inform the economic analysis and study design.  Some of 
these are subject to the Paperwork Reduction Act (PRA).  Contractor responsibilities would include 
development of data collection methodology, instrument design, sampling strategies, and related 
preparatory work supporting the economic analysis.  The contractor would also prepare technical 
materials supporting the PRA information collection request (ICR) package for OMB review, including 
descriptions of data collection design and methodology.  USGS would manage the PRA submission and

BACKGROUND

The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Office of Research & Development (ORD) has several units that function in various areas to advance basic science and clinical research into clinical practice and aims to improve the health and well-being of our nation’s Veterans. One of the current priority areas of VA ORD is to improve access for Veterans to participate in clinical research activities. The ORD Enterprise Optimization Unit (EO) is one of these functional groups and includes both the VA Cooperative Studies Program (CSP) and the Million Veteran Program (MVP). 

The CSP is a clinical research infrastructure embedded within the VA healthcare system. The program was established to execute multi-site clinical trials and epidemiological studies within the purview of VA.1,2 The program’s infrastructure has several Coordinating Centers responsible for the planning and conduct of large multi-site clinical trials in the VA. CSP also established a consortium of 20 VA Medical Centers (VAMCs) called the Network of Dedicated Enrollment Sites (NODES) with teams (Nodes) providing site-level expertise and innovative approaches to address challenges to clinical trial execution.3-7 CSP has extensive sponsor experience in working with sites across a variety of sizes, complexity levels, and geographic locations both within the VA healthcare system and internationally which has created a vast repository of institutional knowledge in the program as it relates to site-level study management.

The MVP is a national research program designed to advance precision health care by learning how genes, lifestyle, military experiences, and exposures affect health and wellness. MVP is the world’s largest biorepository of Veteran data linked to a healthcare system with more than 1,000,000 Veterans enrolled and has one of the world’s most diverse cohorts of any genetic research program. 

PURPOSE:

The Enterprise Optimization (EO) unit, through CSP and MVP, are issuing this Request for Information (“RFI”) to solicit information to further advance efforts to increase Veteran access to participate in clinical research opportunities. Information collected from this RFI will serve as continued market research for the development of a Collaborative Research and Development Agreement (CRADA) with a Community Partner(s) (CPs), e.g., retail pharmacy locations, community health centers, academic medical centers and facilities, clinical laboratory sites, etc., to accomplish this objective. Such an agreement will detail the resources to be provided by the VA and the CSP and describe the purpose and expected work to be accomplished between the CSP and MVP research teams and the identified CP. CPs with the infrastructure and capacity to operate in rural areas of the United States (or its territories) will be prioritized. 

The VA CSP would like to explore the feasibility of establishing community partnerships with community-based locations to serve as additional clinical research study locations for identified CSP clinical trials and/or epidemiological studies. The intent of this effort is to increase the number of research study sites that Veterans have access to for their participation in clinical research. It is anticipated that these CPs will have the necessary infrastructure in place (dedicated clinical research exam rooms, exam rooms, diagnostic tools (e.g., otoscopes, ophthalmoscopes), vital sign monitors, and medical carts, etc. to complete clinical research study visits (enrollment, follow-up) and all research activities associated with those visits (informed consent, data and blood/specimen collection and shipping, study procedures, etc.) and will supplement existing locations that have been traditionally employed as CSP research sites, e.g., VA Medical Centers (VAMCs), Community-Based Outpatient Clinics (CBOCs), etc. Additionally, the selected CP will have infrastructure and locations in United States geographic regions that align with the CSP Network of Dedicated Enrollment Sites (NODES) so that this clinical research network can support the coordination of start-up, operations, and logistics at these sites. CSP Node sites are currently at the following U.S. locations (Ann Arbor, MI; Atlanta, GA; Aurora, CO; Boston, MA, Bronx, NY; Cleveland, OH; Dallas, TX; Los Angeles, CA; Hines, IL; Houston, TX; Long Beach, CA; Madison, WI; Minneapolis, MN; Omaha, NE; Palo Alto, CA; Philadelphia, PA; Portland, OR; Salt Lake City, UT; San Diego, CA; & Seattle, WA). 

The MVP is interested in expanding blood collection capabilities to include rural and remote collection facilities not already covered by the MVP footprint. Activities would include 1) CP staff collecting and labeling blood from consented MVP participants (MVP would securely confirm consent has been obtained) and 2) secure shipment of blood specimens to approved VA/MVP facilities.

DESCRIPTION OF DATA:

CSP data includes electronic health record data, study self-reported surveys, genomic data, and data from other approved data sources on CSP participants. Access to individual level coded CSP data is limited to VA researchers and provided within the VA secure computing environment, in accordance with VA regulatory approvals. The developed CRADA will further outline the relevant regulatory requirements for transmission of appropriate data between the CP(s) and VA and establish data transmission efforts that align with VA data security and privacy regulations. 

No MVP data beyond what is needed to confirm consent will be available to the CP.

RESEARCH SCOPE:

The goal of this proposed collaboration between the CSP, MVP, and CP is to employ U.S. based Community Partners (CPs), e.g., retail pharmacy locations, community health centers, academic medical centers and facilities, clinical laboratory sites, etc., to serve as clinical research study sites and increase the catchment area of available research study locations that Veterans can access to participate in VA clinical research. The proposed partnership activities will include the following:

The identified CP will have locations that will function as clinical research study visit sites for CSP and MVP

Research activities include research study participant enrollment and follow-up visits and/or other research activities associated with those visits (informed consent, data and blood/specimen collection and shipping, study procedures, etc.)

REQUIREMENTS:

Community Partner and project staff must be located in the contiguous United States, or its territories (American Samoa, Guam, the Northern Mariana Islands, Puerto Rico, and the United States Virgin Islands)

Number 70RDA125R00000013 
 
August 6, 2025 
 
 


UNCLASSIFIED 
UNCLASSIFIED 
 
 
MARITIME CAPABILITIES AND INNOVATION  
COMMERCIAL SOLUTIONS OPENING PILOT 
PROGRAM (CSOP) 
General Solicitation 
 
Open for 12 Months Until August 5, 2026 
 
 
Background 
 
The National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) for Fiscal Year (FY) 2017, Title VIII, § 880 
(Pub. L. 114-328), Pilot Programs for Authority to Acquire Innovative Commercial Items 
Using General Solicitation Competitive Procedures (as amended), provided the statute for the 
Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to carry out a “Commercial Solutions Opening Pilot 
Program” (CSOP) to competitively procure innovative commercial products. 
 
The CSOP is a non-Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) merit-based solution selection 
strategy for DHS to acquire innovative commercial products and services through the award 
of a contract. The CSOP vests Contracting Officers with additional procedural discretion and 
flexibility so that innovative commercial products and services may be solicited, offered, 
evaluated, and awarded in a simplified manner that maximizes efficiency and economy and 
minimizes burden and administrative costs for both the Government and industry. DHS has 
determined that under this pilot program, a General Solicitation can be executed to solicit 
proposals from industry. Each proposal is evaluated on its individual merits rather than on a 
comparative basis, and the Government has considerable latitude in determining which of 
the submitted proposals it will fund.  As a result, DHS’s Office of Program Accountability and 
Risk Management (PARM) is issuing the subject General Solicitation for DHS and all its 
Components to rapidly procure innovative commercial maritime capabilities and solutions.  
The Department’s maritime responsibilities span a wide array of missions, including 
homeland defense readiness, law, border, and trade enforcement, disaster response, 
counter-illicit trafficking, humanitarian response, and critical infrastructure protection . 
These missions depend on a broad ecosystem of platforms, technologies, port systems, 
and operational capabilities that must be acquired, sustained, and modernized in a fiscally 
responsible, secure, and mission-driven manner. 
DHS Components— including the U.S. Coast Guard, U.S. Customs and Border Protection, 
the Federal Emergency Management Agency, the Transportation Security 
Administration, and others — operate in increasingly contested and complex maritime 
environments. These environments demand coordinated investment in both platforms 
and enabling systems, as well as a deliberate approach to oversight, digital modernization, 
industrial base health, and workforce readiness. 
 

UNCLASSIFIED 
UNCLASSIFIED 
 
 
The Under Secretary for Management, as the Department’s Chief Acquisition Officer, is 
responsible for ensuring that DHS’s maritime capabilities are delivered effectively, 
efficiently, and in support of national priorities. This includes not only acquisition of new 
vessels and craft, but also the transformation of how DHS approaches inspections, trade 
enforcement, sustainment, and maritime domain awareness. To this end, the Department 
is leveraging this General Solicitation to identify and invest in innovative, non-traditional, 
and cross-cutting solutions to improve outcomes across the maritime domain. 
 
What are the goals of the DHS General Solicitation? 
 
The Maritime Capabilities and Innovation General Solicitation aims to identify new ideas, 
approaches, tools, and partnerships that can help the Department address critical 
challenges and accelerate transformation across its maritime enterprise. This General 
Solicitation provides a flexible mechanism to solicit, evaluate, and fund exploratory and 
applied work that does not fit neatly into traditional acquisition frameworks, but that has 
the potential to improve DHS’s ability to acquire, oversee, and operate with their maritime 
enterprise. 
 
The goals of this General Solicitation are to: 
• Advance U.S. maritime dominance goals through increased resilience in 
shipbuilding, port infrastructure, supply chains, and workforce development.  
• Support mission- driven modernization of acquisition, sustainment, oversight, 
and operational execution across DHS’s maritime activities; 
• Expand collaboration with industry, academia, non -profits, and other non -
traditional entities working on maritime technology, security, and logistics; 
• Strengthen maritime acquisition outcomes by enhancing lifecycle planning, risk 
management, and component-level coordination; 
• Enable innovative solutions to complex and persistent maritime challenges 
through applied research, technical insight, policy frameworks, or prototype 
concepts; 
 
The procurement is limited to innovative commercial products or services . Within the 
meaning of the statute, innovative is defined as, “Any new technology, process, or method, 
including research and development, or any new application of an existing technology, 
process, or method.”   
 
This General Solicitation will stay open for a period of 12 months, until August 5, 2026.  
Industry is invited to respond to this open call for innovative solutions at any time during 
the stated period. Submissions will be accepted on a rolling basis, allowing for continuous 
engagement and the opportunity to present solutions as they are developed. The 
Government anticipates reviewing the Maritime Capabilities and Innovation CSOP  
mailbox approximately every (2) weeks to check for submissions.   
 
This General Solicitation is intended to be used by any of the Components within the 
Department. For more information regarding the diverse mission space of DHS , please 
visit our public website at: https://www.dhs.gov/ 
This General Solicitation does not have a ceiling, but each individual CSOP 
contract/agreement awarded may not exceed $25M.  The Government anticipates that all 

UNCLASSIFIED 
UNCLASSIFIED 
 
 
CSOP awards will be Firm Fixed Price (FFP) but reserves the right to award utilizing other 
contract types if needed. One of the advantage s of the CSOP authority is that  the 
Government and Vendor together develop negotiable award terms (including payment, 
intellectual property and data rights license terms, schedule, milestones, and pricing.) 
 
Who Can Participate? 
 
All US- based entities are eligible to participate, including established Government 
Contractors, commercial companies, and small businesses as defined by SBA standards. 
Foreign companies may participate through established US subsidiaries that are 
incorporated in the United States and registered to conduct business domestically.  Non-
traditional vendors, such as academic institutions, research organizations, and non-profit 
entities are also encouraged to participate . Contract employees will be required to 
undergo a favorable Suitability Assessment as determined by the D epartment. In 
addition, the Contractor may be required to comply with A gency Personal Identity 
Verification procedures identified in the contract that implement Homeland Security 
Presidential Directive-12 (HSPD-12). 
 
Submissions or proposals may be subject to Section 889, the Prohibition on Certain 
Telecommunications and Video Surveillance Services or Equipment, of the 2019 National 
Defense Authorization Act as applicable. 
    
To be eligible for award, companies must be registered in the System for Award Management 
(SAM.gov), prior to DHS making a CSOP award. 
 
Initial Strategic Focus Areas in the Maritime Domain 
DHS operates across a diverse and complex maritime environment, encompassing 
homeland defense readiness , law , border, and trade enforcement, disaster response, 
counter-illicit trafficking, humanitarian response, and critical infrastructure protection . 
This General Solicitation invites novel concepts, tools, frameworks, and partnerships to 
help DHS address persistent and emerging problem sets across this domain. Proposed 
efforts should aim to improve mission outcomes, increase operational efficiency, and 
strengthen acquisition and sustainment of maritime capabilities. 
DHS is seeking video solution  submissions which are relevant to one or more of the  
following Strategic Focus Areas:  
A. Maritime Technology Innovation and Digital Transformation 
• DHS seeks innovative approaches to accelerate the responsible adoption of digital 
tools and engineering innovation across maritime missions and acquisitions. This 
includes improving how platforms and systems are designed, tested, deployed, and 
supported using data-driven and modern software-based approaches. 
B. Program Oversight and Acquisition Risk Management 
• Delivering maritime capabilities at speed and scale requires better oversight tools 
and risk-based decision-making. DHS is seeking innovative approaches to increase 

UNCLASSIFIED 
UNCLASSIFIED 
 
 
transparency and reduce acquisition risk across programs and Contracting 
strategies. 
C. Lifecycle Sustainment and Operational Readiness 
• Reducing the cost and complexity of sustaining both legacy and new maritime 
platforms is essential to long -term mission success. DHS is seeking innovative 
approaches to maintain asset availability, manage obsolescence, and align 
sustainment models with operational needs. 
D. Supply Chain Resilience and Port Infrastructure Risk 
• Ensuring visibility and resilience across maritime supply chains and infrastructure 
is a growing priority. DHS is looking for innovative methods to manage physical 
and digital risks that impact port operations, vessel systems, and critical industrial 
partnerships. 
E. Trade Enforcement and Inspection Innovation 
• Improving the effectiveness and efficiency of maritime inspections is vital to 
securing the flow of lawful trade. DHS is interested in innovative concepts that 
enhance inspection capabilities, targeting tools, and data integration in support of 
trade enforcement.

Adrianna Menker, Contracting Officer, AFRL/RYKSW, adrianna.menker@us.af.mil 
 
*****************This announcement does not request any proposals at this time****************** 
The following program is an anticipated requirement for the Air Force Research Laboratory, Sensors 
Directorate, Spectrum Warfare Division (AFRL/RYW) located at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, OH. A 
two-step closed Advanced Research Announcement (ARA) for this requirement is anticipated to be 
published on SAM.gov around May 2026. 
The anticipated funding listed below reflects estimated funding only. This estimate is not a promise of funding. 
Funding is uncertain and is subject to change. Changes in funding availability may occur at the discretion of the 
Government. 
 
PROGRAM DESCRIPTION: The purpose of this notice is to provide information about a anticipated two-
step closed ARA for Precise Ensemble Network Communications Allowing PNT (PENCAP). 
 
This notice is not a solicitation. The Government will not reimburse costs associated with any 
communication submitted in response to this notice. No documentation is requested at this time. 
TECHNICAL DESCRIPTION: The objective for PENCAP is the development of a network clock ensemble 
and the implementation of it on a VPX card capable of running pntOS. Prototype cards, networking methods, 
and an ensemble algorithm will be delivered to the Government for further development and testing. 
 
The algorithm will be designed to be robust in dynamic environments, continuously evaluating both local and 
remote timing references for stability, trustworthiness, and source validity. It will incorporate a weighting 
system, allowing references to enter and exit the ensemble without disrupting it, and will feature outlier 
rejection to discard invalid or unstable measurements, ensuring a consistently accurate time. 
To support the algorithm, a resilient network method will be designed to disseminate timing and stability 
information. This network will utilize various existing communication links on aircraft and can be configured in 
multiple ways, such as point-to-point or hub-and-spoke. The system will be designed to authenticate new nodes 
that join the network, ensuring the traceability and integrity of all connections. 

Page 2 of 2  
The ensemble algorithm and network method will be implemented on a prototype card. This will involve 
modifying a Commercial-Off-The-Shelf (COTS) 3U VPX card to function with pntOS. The design will 
emphasize open standards for both data and physical interfaces to simplify future integration and upgrades. The 
project will culminate in a series of simulated, lab, and flight tests to demonstrate the card's full capabilities. 
ANTICIPATED FUNDING: A potential contract is anticipated with an estimated total contract value of 
$9,300,000.00. This funding profile is an estimate only and not a contractual obligation for funding. All 
funding is subject to change due to Government discretion and availability. Potential offerors should be aware 
that due to unanticipated budget fluctuations, funding in any or all areas may change with little or no notice. 
 
ANTICIPATED CONTRACT TYPE: A Definitive (c-type) Cost-Plus Fixed Fee (CPFF) contract is anticipated.

The contractor shall submit certificates of completion for each affected contractor and subcontractor employee to the contracting officer within 15 calendar days after completion of training by each employee or subcontractor personnel.  AT Level 1 awareness training is available at the following website: https://jko.jten.mil/courses/atl1/launch.html.

1.4.5.4 iWATCH Training: The contractor and all associated subcontractors with an area of performance within an Army-controlled installation, facilities or area shall brief all employees on the local iWATCH program (training standards provided by the requiring activity Antiterrorism Officer (ATO)). This local developed training shall be used to inform employees of the types of behavior to watch for and instruct employees to report suspicious activity to the COR or the KO. This training shall be completed within 30 calendar days of contract award and within 30 calendar days of new employees commencing performance.  The contractor shall report completion for each contractor employee and subcontractor employee to the contracting officer within 15 calendar days after completion of training. 

1.4.5.5 Communications Security/Information Technology (COMSEC/IT) Security.  All communications with DoD organizations are subject to COMSEC review.  All telephone communications networks are continually subject to intercept by unfriendly intelligence organizations.  DoD has authorized the military departments to conduct COMSEC monitoring and recording of telephone calls originating from, or terminating at, DoD organizations.  Therefore, the contractor is advised that any time contractor personnel place or receive a call they are subject to COMSEC procedures.  The contractor shall ensure wide and frequent dissemination of the above information to all employees dealing with DoD information.  The contractor shall abide by all Government regulations concerning the authorized use of the Government's computer network, including the restriction against using the network to recruit Government personnel or advertise job openings.  

1.4.6 Physical Security. The contractor shall safeguard all Government property provided for contractor use. At the close of each work period, Government facilities, equipment and materials shall be secured. 

1.4.7 Reserved

1.4.8 Post Award Conference/Periodic Progress Meetings: The contractor agrees to attend any post award conference convened by the KO in accordance with FAR 42.5. The KO, COR and other Government personnel, as appropriate, may meet periodically with the contractor to review the contactor’s performance. At these meetings, the KO will apprise the contractor of how the Government views the contractor’s performance and the contractor shall apprise the Government of problems, if any, being experienced. The contractor shall resolve outstanding issues raised by the Government. Contractor attendance at these meetings shall be at no additional cost to the Government. 

1.4.9 Contract Manager (CM): The contactor shall designate a CM who shall ensure performance under this contract CM shall be present during the course of the training day on 28-31 May 2026. The name of this person, and an alternate who shall act for the contractor when the CM is absent, shall be designated in writing to the KO. The CM or alternate shall have full authority to act for the contractor on all contract matters relating to daily operation of this contract.  The CM shall work through the Contracting Officer to resolve issues, receive technical instructions, and ensure adequate performance of services.  The CM shall ensure that contractor employees do not perform any services outside the scope of the contract without an official modification issued by the KO.  The CM shall ensure contractor employees understand that services performed outside the scope of the contract are performed wholly at the expense of the contractor.

1.4.10 Identification of Contractor Employees: All contractor personnel are required to identify themselves as such to avoid creating an impression that they are Government employees. Contractor personnel shall wear identification badges distinguishing themselves as such. The badges shall have the company name, employee name and the word “contractor” displayed.  

1.4.10.1 The contractor shall retrieve all identification media (including vehicle passes) from its employees who depart employment for any reason. The contractor shall return all identification media (i.e., badges and vehicles passes) to security gate upon the employee’s departure.

1.4.11. Combating Trafficking in Persons: The United States Government has adopted a zero-tolerance policy regarding trafficking in persons. Contractors and contractor employees shall not engage in severe forms of trafficking in persons during the period of performance of the contract; procure commercial sex acts during the period of performance of the contract; or use forced labor in the performance of the contract. The Contractor shall notify its employees of the United States Government’s zero tolerance policy, the actions that will be taken against employees for violations of this policy. The contractor shall take appropriate action, up to and including termination, against employees or subcontractors that violate the US Government policy as described at FAR 22.17.

1.4.12 Reserved

1.4.13 Data Rights: The Government has unlimited rights to all documents/materials produced under this contract. All documents and materials, to include the source codes of any software, produced under this contract shall be Government owned and are the property of the Government with all rights and privileges of ownership/copyright belonging exclusively to the Government. These documents and materials may not be used or sold by the contractor without written permission from the KO. All materials supplied to the Government shall be the sole property of the Government and may not be used for any other purpose. This right does not abrogate any other Government rights. 

1.4.14 Organizational Conflicts of Interest (OCI): The contractor and subcontractor personnel performing services under this contract may receive, have access to or participate in the development of proprietary or source selection information (e.g., cost or pricing information, budget information or analyses, specifications or work statements, etc.) or perform evaluation services which may create a current or subsequent OCIs, as defined in FAR Subpart 9.5. The contractor shall notify the KO immediately whenever it becomes aware that such access or participation may result in any actual or potential OCI and shall promptly submit a plan to the KO to avoid or mitigate any such OCI. The contractor’s mitigation plan will be determined to be acceptable solely at the discretion of the KO. In the event the KO unilaterally determines that any such OCI cannot be satisfactorily avoided or mitigated, the KO may impose other remedies as he or she deems necessary, including prohibiting the contractor from participation in subsequent contracted requirements which may be affected by the OCI.

1.4.15 Reserved

BACKGROUND

The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Office of Information & Technology (OIT), Office of Information Security (OIS) strives to provide high quality, effective, and efficient Information Technology (IT) services to those responsible for providing care to the Veterans at the point-of-care as well as throughout all the points of the Veterans’ health care in an effective, timely and compassionate manner. VA depends on Information Management (IM)/IT systems to meet mission goals.

OIS is one of six divisions within OIT. OIS’s mission, in collaboration with its business partners, is to provide an enterprise information security program that strengthens security strategy, risk management, engineering excellence, policy, budgeting, and operations services to over 25 million Veterans, families, and their caregivers.

Within OIS, the Information Security Programs and Logistics (ISPL) service line is responsible for coordinating activities across OIS to ensure operations and the use of resources are integrated, transparent, and efficient. ISPL develops the program’s strategic goals, objectives, and recommends necessary adjustments to improve the organization’s ability to meet those goals. Additionally, ISPL evaluates, develops, recommends, and implements management and administrative practices for efficiencies and to meet organizational goals and objectives. ISPL functions include the following: Cybersecurity Program Planning; Programming; Budgeting and Execution; Acquisition Management; Cybersecurity Program Integration; and OIS logistics functions, such as, Chief of Staff and Business/Program Administration.

A primary task within the lifecycle management of OIT Audit processes is ISPL’s support of multiple audit activities that involve Veterans Health Administration (VHA), Veterans Benefits Administration (VBA) and National Cemetery Administration component agencies and their respective applications. These activities include interviews of management personnel, inspection of information security policies and procedures, observation of operational controls, and technical control testing of VA general support systems and major applications. Additionally, corrective actions identified in prior audits are often evaluated for implementation.

ISPL supported audits currently include, but are not limited to, the following:

A.	Federal Information Security Management Act (FISMA) of 2002 (“FISMA”, 44 U.S.C. § 3541) is a United States Federal Law enacted in 2002 as Title III of the E-Government Act of 2002. The act requires each federal agency to develop, document, and implement an agency-wide information security program to ensure the adequacy and effectiveness of VA’s information security programs. FISMA requires agency program officials, Chief Information Officers, and Inspector Generals to conduct annual reviews of information security programs.

B.	Federal Information System Controls Audit Manual (FISCAM) provides auditors with specific guidance in order to evaluate the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information systems. FISCAM is consistent with the National Institute of Standards and Technology’s (NIST) guidelines for complying with FISMA. NIST Special Publication 800-53 provides recommended security controls for federal information systems and organizations. Appendix 3 of FISCAM provides a crosswalk to those controls. On a recurring basis, the VA conducts audits of IT systems, programs, and procedures to identify material weaknesses within VA IT systems.

C.	Internal Revenue Service (IRS) Publication 1075 requires the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to ensure that personal and financial information furnished to the Internal Revenue Service is protected against unauthorized use, access, or disclosure. The VA receives Federal Tax Information directly from the IRS and from secondary sources such as the Social Security Administration. Pursuant to Internal Revenue Code IRC 6103 or through an IRS-approved exchange agreement, the VA must have adequate programs in place to protect any data received.

The IRS conducts cyclic audits to evaluate the VA’s compliance with IRS data security requirements. The ISPL Division’s functions include identifying broad trends of non-compliance among all audit activities (FISMA/FISCAM, Government Accountability Office (GAO), IRS, etc.); identifying and involving stakeholders at all levels during all audit activities, facilitating root cause analysis on audit findings: coordinating remediation activities based on applicable laws and regulations and validating enterprise compliance implementation activities.

I. INTRODUCTION: 
The Joint Program Executive Office for Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear 
Defense (JPEO-CBRND) is organized into five Joint Project Management Offices (JPMO), 
each responsible for specific commodity areas. General information on the JPEO-CBRND and 
subordinate JPMOs can be obtained from the JPEO-CBD website at 
http://www.jpeocbd.osd.mil/. Mission areas and technical points of contact for the product 
management offices are shown in Section VII of this BAA. As the purpose of this BAA is to 
identify the best available science in the identified areas of research interest, proposals are 
sought from all eligible sources as specified herein, including educational institutions, nonprofit 
organizations, and private industry. This Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) provides general 
information, proposal preparation instructions, evaluation and selection criteria, and award 
administration. 
Offerors may submit unsolicited proposals (preproposals) for consideration under the general 
requirements of this BAA at any time, as long as the announcement is active, in support of 
research and development within the mission areas identified in Section VII of this 
announcement. Studies related to novel solutions and improved methods to develop medical 
countermeasures more rapidly and with increased efficiency through enabling technologies, life 
cycle bioinformatics, and improved logistics tracking are of specific interest to the Government. 
 
This announcement will also be available on the Grants.gov web portal (http://www.grants.gov/), 
the Contract Opportunities section of SAM.gov website (https://sam.gov) and the JPEO-CBD 
website (http://www.jpeocbd.osd.mil/). 
 
From time to time, special announcements or calls for proposals referencing this BAA may be 
issued for specific requirements in addition to any requirements announced in Sections VII and 
VIII. Additionally, the application process may be amended as other electronic application 
processes are implemented. All amendments to this BAA will be announced respectively. To 
facilitate communication on both scientific and administrative matters relating to this BAA, a 
single email address may be used for all communication with the Government. Please send all 
technical and administrative questions and inquiries to usarmy.detrick.dod-jpeo-
cbrnd.mbx.baa@army.mil. Potential Offerors are encouraged to discuss their proposal ideas 
with the JPMO technical contacts listed in Section VII (B). 
 
Administrative questions concerning the preparation of preproposals or proposals should be 
addressed to U.S. Army Contracting Command Edgewood Contracting Division/ Grants 
Officer. They should be emailed to usarmy.detrick.dod-jpeo-cbrnd.mbx.baa@army.mil, 
ATTN: CBRND BAA 22-01. 
 
This Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) will remain open in perpetuity until canceled by 
the U.S. Army. However, individual requests for white papers, requests for project 
proposals, and any other requirement specific solicitation will be open for a limited time as 
identified in each document. 
 
This BAA is intended to solicit pre-proposals for: 
1. Procurement Contracts,: Awarded Procurement Contracts shall apply to those parts of 

Page 4 of 46  
development not related to the development of a specific system or hardware procurement based 
on the Technical Readiness Level limitations described herein. As to any resultant procurement 
contracts, this BAA is issued under the provisions of the Competition in Contracting Act of 1984 
(P.L. 98-369), as implemented in the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 6.102 (d)(2) 
and in accordance with FAR 35.016(a). The purpose of Procurement Contracts for research

Page 5 of 46  
and/or development placed under this BAA is to identify the best available science, and as such, there 
are no set-asides associated with any awards resulting from this BAA 
 
2. Grants and Cooperative Agreements: Consistent with the regulatory authority in Code of Federal 
Regulation (CFR), Title 2.A, Chapter II, Part 200, funds may be awarded to stimulate or support 
a public purpose consistent with objectives to develop, approve, and field medical CBRN 
countermeasures and enabling biotechnologies, or, as defined in 31 U.S.C. 6305, to transfer a 
thing of value to a recipient to carry out a public purpose of support or stimulation authorized by 
a law of the United States instead of acquiring (by purchase, lease, or barter) property or services 
for the direct benefit or use of the United States Government. These efforts should be intended 
for scientific study and experimentation directed toward advancing the state-of-the- art or 
increasing knowledge or understanding, rather than focusing on a specific system, product, or 
medical countermeasure. The purpose of grants and cooperative agreements placed under this 
BAA is to identify the best available science, and as such, there are no set-asides associated with 
any awards resulting from this BAA. This BAA operates as a competitive procedure for the 
award of grants and cooperative agreements. 
 
3. Other Transactions (OTs) for Research: As prescribed in 10 U.S. Code 4021, OTs for 
Research are non-FAR based agreements for use in carrying out basic, applied and advanced 
research. The intent of an OT for Research is to spur dual-use research and development 
(R&D) between the Government and Industry. An OT for Research requires cost sharing 
between the awardee and the Government, and to the maximum extent practicable, OTs for 
Research should not duplicate research being undertaken under other agreements, grants, or 
procurement contracts. OTs for Research may only be used for a research project when the 
use of a standard contract, grant, or cooperative agreement for such project is not feasible or 
appropriate. 
 
4. Prototype Project Other Transactions (OTs): The award of Prototype OTAs shall be for the 
development of prototypes in accordance with 10 USC 4022 The resultant award of any 
OTA using the procedures of this BAA either announced in Section VII or for a requirement 
announced in section VIII are NOT made or issued under the provisions of the Competition 
in Contracting Act of 1984 (P.L. 98-369), FAR Part 6 or any other FAR based regulation. 
However, solely as a matter of convenience to meet the requirement for maximum 
practicable competition, the mechanics of the competitive BAA process detailed in this 
BAA otherwise not applicable to OTAs are, as supplemented herein, adopted as the 
competitive procedure for entering into OTAs.

defined as a special class of assistance instruments used to support or stimulate research. A TIA 
may be either a kind of cooperative agreement or a type of assistance transaction other than a 
grant or cooperative agreement. TIAs allow for involvement of commercial firms in defense 
research programs and for other purposes (described in 32 CFR 37 appendix A) related to 
integrating the commercial and defense sectors of the nation's technology and industrial base. 
A TIA may be a cooperative agreement with provisions tailored for involving commercial 
firms (as distinct from a cooperative agreement subject to all of the requirements in 32 CFR 
part 34), or another kind of assistance transaction described in 32 CFR 37 Appendix B. TIAs 
are more flexible than traditional Government funding instruments allowing for negotiation of

under a TIA are to provide at least half of the costs of the project in accordance with 32 CFR § 
37.215(b) to demonstrate its strong commitment to and self-interest in the project’s success.

1 INTRODUCTION AND OVERVIEW 
 
The Federal Highway Administration (FHWA) Office of Infrastructure Research and 
Development (HRDI) Bridge Engineering Research Team is announcing its intent to solicit 
white papers and proposals under this Broad Agency Announcement (BAA). This BAA is 
developed in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation
 (FAR) 6.101(b)(3)(ii) and FAR 
35.102. This BAA involves the use of a 5-year Open BAA to quickly and efficiently execute 
research and development to deliver practical solutions to high priority problems. This strategy 
will provide FHWA an acquisition tool with the flexibility to solicit white papers, proposals and 
make awards that meet present and compelling needs. 
 
White papers and proposals will only be solicited and accepted during individual calls. Calls for 
white papers and proposals will occur periodically throughout the life of the BAA. Each call will 
identify: (1) specific topic areas; (2) any changes to the standard evaluation criteria or white 
paper and/or proposal preparation instructions, and; (3) cutoff dates for submissions. 
This BAA is an expression of interest only and does not commit the Government to pay any 
proposal preparation costs. All responsible sources capable of satisfying the Government's needs 
may submit a proposal. The Government reserves the right to award contracts  that are 
determined to be of benefit to the Government in achieving the goals of this program. 
1.1  Background 
The FHWA HRDI Bridge Engineering Research Team conducts and directs research efforts in 
support of the development of testing standards, structural design and construction 
specifications, and acceptance criteria.  The FHWA HRDI Bridge Engineering Research Team 
leads the development and advancement of next generation structural materials and systems, and 
provides leadership in the development of standards, specifications, and acceptance criteria to 
enable their deployment.  The work conducted generally enables the advancement of state-of-
the-art solutions and positions HRDI as a leader in the deployment of such technologies to 
maintain or improve the safety, integrity, durability, and resilience of the Nation’s bridges and 
highway structures. 
 
1.2   Legislative Authority 
The legislative authority for this BAA is found under 23 U.S.C. 502(b)(3)(C), which states: “The 
Secretary may carry out research, development, and technology transfer activities related to 
transportation by making grants to, or entering into contracts and cooperative agreements with 
one or more of the following: National Academy of Sciences, the American Association of State 
Highway and Transportation Officials, any Federal laboratory, Federal agency, State agency, 
authority, association, institution, for-profit or nonprofit corporation, organization, foreign 
country, or any other person.” 
 
1.3  Purpose 
The purpose of this BAA is to solicit a variety of solutions that will support the FHWA Bridge 
Engineering Research Team’s research initiatives to develop next generation structural materials 
and systems in the following program areas:

• Structural Steel 
• Structural Concrete 
• Geotechnical Structures 
• Bridge Hydraulics 
 
Research topics are focused on developing technologies in support of FHWA strategic goals. The 
new strategic plan and associated goals are expected to be published in February 2026.

The Offeror shall propose and implement a delivery method consistent with this requirement. If 
it is determined that the Offeror’s performance under the contract is not progressing to the 
satisfaction of the Government, the Government retains the right to commence a process to

conjunction with FAR clause 52.242-15, Stop-Work Order.

The open period for BAA white papers and proposals will be defined in each issued call. The 
FHWA may modify the schedule or research topics. If such changes are made, the call will be 
amended. This BAA and calls issued thereto will be posted to the www.SAM.gov
 website. It is 
the responsibility of the Offeror and interested parties to be aware of BAA calls and amendments 
by regularly checking the website and registering to receive notifications and updates to this 
specific BAA. 
 
2.2 Communications Protocol 
Any exchanges of information must be consistent with procurement integrity requirements of 
section 27 of the Office of Federal Procurement Policy Act (41 U.S.C. 423, as amended) (see 
FAR 3.104). All information exchanges will be conducted through the Contract Specialist and/or 
Contracting Officer. Offerors are advised that any indication of interest, in the affirmative, is not 
meant to imply nor in any way impart an obligation on the part of the Government that an award 
will be forthcoming for the offered work or project. 
 
2.3 Points of Contact 
All white paper and proposal submissions shall be delivered in electronic format (PDF and 
Excel) to the Contract Specialist and Contracting Officer indicated in each BAA Call. 
 
2.4 Offeror Eligibility 
This is an unrestricted BAA. Any responsible source may submit a proposal for consideration, 
including, but not limited to, States or local governments, or organizations of State or local 
governments, universities or institutions of higher education, hospitals, non-profit organizations, 
private individuals, corporations, and businesses or commercial organizations. 
 
All Offerors must be registered in the Federal Government’s 
System for Award Management 
(SAM) system prior to formal Proposal submission.

DISTRIBUTION D. Distribution authorized to Department of Defense (DoD) and US DoD Contractors only. 
ADMINISTRATIVE OR OPERATIONAL USE, March 2026. Other requests for this document will be referred to

WARNING - This document contains technical data, directly or by reference, whose export is restricted by the Arms Export 
Control Act (Title 22, U.S.C., Sec 2751, et. seq.) or the Export Administration Act of 1979, as amended. Violations of these 
export laws are subject to severe criminal penalties. Mark and disseminate document in accordance with provisions of DoD 
Directive 5230.25 and E.O. 13559. 
DESTRUCTION NOTICE – Destroy by any method that will prevent disclosure of contents or reconstruction of the document. 
 
  
Controlled by: Information Protection 
CUI category: CUI Basic 
Distribution: DoDI 5230.24 marked herein 
    

 
1.0 Description of Services 
 
1.1. (CUI) This PWS describes the scope of services and materials required to complement 
the AN/ALR-69A organic engineering capability. While the scope of this PWS is extensive in 
nature, the expertise required is specific to the AN/ALR-69A RWR systems. The Contractor 
shall supply AN/ALR-69A RWR engineering services and materials as required to complement 
the Air Force Life Cycle Management Center, Electronic Warfare and Avionics Division 
(AFLCMC/ESY) organic engineering capability. These services and materials shall include: 
 
Requirement Description CUI 
A Engineering Support of software tasks for repair, perfection of the AN/ALR-69A 
Operational Flight Programs (OFPs) and Mission Data File (MDF) tables (to 
include block cycle build(s) prior to full inclusion into OFP) 
B Laboratory, ground, and flight test support for OFP effectiveness/certification and 
integration efforts 
C Engineering Support for AN/ALR-69A technical support/integration with; 
weapons system (i.e. aircraft), mission equipment avionics, flight line equipment, 
as well as Depot and field level support equipment 
D Studies, analyses, evaluation, and experiments utilizing hardware/software to 
define deficiencies, modifications, capabilities, and supportability issues for 
the 
system 
E Technical services for new or current aircraft integration efforts involving the 
RWR; for interoperability or compatibility with systems installed along with 
the AN/ALR-69A 
F Deliver Hardware and software items in support for the AN/ALR-69A Software 
Engineering Environment (SEE) and Test Tools (TTs) 
G Design and prototype AN/ALR-69A software/firmware modifications and 
integration efforts to/for the RWR system 
H Documentation support that includes updating AN/ALR-69A software 
documentation, source data for commodity technical orders, technical data 
package (system and parts specifications), and familiarization training materials 
I Engineering Services to support organic source of repair (SOR) capabilities, to 
define test program sets (TPS) requirements, to plan and update SEE and TTs 
associated with the AN/ALR-69A RWR system 
 
1.2. Benefit to United States Air Force (USAF):   
(CUI) This effort provides a significant benefit to the USAF by enabling aircrews and Mission 
Data (MD) programmers to maintain effectiveness in the Area of Responsibility (AOR). It 
allows them to effectively identify and provides situational awareness for emerging threats to 
meet their mission requirements.  The effort will make the system more sustainabe translating to 
an improved ability to identify/range/locate threats, increased integration with the aircraft

system, the AN/ALR-69A Program Office needs to direct a tasking alignment of the Contractor 
to maintain a common software/hardware engineering environment and the configuration 
tracking to understand functional changes in the software and hardware. The Government’s goal 
is to keep the software/hardware baselines similar which will make a single AN/ALR-69A

software and hardware across various aircraft platforms.

(CUI) The AN/ALR-69A System tasking and studies requires a specific skill-set and

Guidance for the Request for Information (RFI)

**As stated, all information within is for RFI purposes. No contract will be awarded pursuant to this RFI. Read all information within for additional information. ** 

As part of the RFI, the Government is seeking to obtain concerns or questions related to the PWS, the instructions to offerors (technical approach), and evaluation criteria. Following is an abbreviated section of the Instructions to Offerors. The instructions are related only to the Technical Approach, as related back to the PWS. Reminder that this is not a solicitation and proposals are not being accepted. 

As provided in the RFI, paragraph 5g., use the following Draft Instructions (technical approach), along with the draft PWS, to address any concerns or questions you have, as it pertains to creating a proposal. 

 

DRAFT INSTRUCTIONS TO OFFERORS (ABBR SECTION)

All sections of an Offeror’s proposal would need to make direct reference to the PWS specification paragraph numbers. A proposed technical approach (and methods) must be presented in a clear and logical order based on the offerors understanding of the instructions (technical approach). Statements such as “will comply”, “meets the intent of”, or “we intend to meet the requirements” and the like, would not suffice.

**TECHNICAL APPROACH**

Offerors shall submit a technical approach that demonstrates techniques, methods, and processes that would successfully accomplish the objective specified in the referenced PWS (specifically “how” the objectives will be accomplished), namely: 

Providing a contractor-owned, contractor-operated electronic system as evidenced by screenshots of existing capabilities.  (refer to PWS section 4.1)

Anticipated number of full research applications to FOAs: 5,000-10,000 (typically 50-1,500 per program) 

Anticipate one Vision Setting meeting and 1-2 Programmatic Review meetings per year per program

DRAFT Performance Work Statement

Programmatic and Administrative Support Services

Congressionally Directed Medical Research Programs

PART 1

1.0 GENERAL INFORMATION

1.1 This is a non-personal services contract to provide programmatic and administrative support services to the Congressionally Directed Medical Research Programs (CDMRP) and the Defense Health Agency Research and Development (DHA R&D).

1.2 Description of services/introduction: The contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and other items and non-personal services necessary to perform programmatic and administrative support services as defined in this Performance Work Statement (PWS) except for those items specified as government furnished property and services. The contractor shall perform to the standards in this PWS.

1.3 Background: 

The CDMRP is an office within the DHA R&D that manages biomedical research programs in response to the expressed needs of Congress and its stakeholders. Congress adds funding for the CDMRP into the annual defense appropriations bill.  The CDMRP is responsible for planning, coordinating, integrating, programming and budgeting program funding. 

The CDMRP’s hallmarks include:

investing in groundbreaking research 

targeting critical gaps 

reviewing applications using a two-tier formal review with no standing peer review panels and no “pay line” 

involving consumer advocates throughout the program cycle

supporting both the next generation of researchers and established scientists 

funding the full pipeline of research development from basic to clinical research; and

fostering collaboration and synergy  

The CDMRP uses the two-tier review process to develop funding recommendations that balance the most meritorious science across many disciplines and offer the highest promise to fulfill programmatic goals. 

The first tier of the two-tier review process is peer review. Peer review is a criteria-based process where individual applications are evaluated based on their scientific and technical merit. Applications are evaluated by scientific discipline, specialty area, or award mechanism by scientific, technical and consumer peer reviewers.

The second tier of review is programmatic review. Applications are programmatically reviewed by members of the programs’ Programmatic Panel. Programmatic review is a comparison-based process in which applications compete in a common pool and in some cases across multiple research areas. Programmatic review balances the potential outcomes and risks of scientifically meritorious applications to select those that have the highest potential to help achieve the vision and goals of the respective program. Support for the programmatic review is a major aspect of this contract. 

 

The CDMRP strives to transform health care for Service Members, Veterans, their Families, and the American public through innovative and impactful research. While individual programs are unique in their focus, all the programs managed by the CDMRP share the common goal of advancing paradigm shifting research, solutions that will lead to cures or improvements in patient care, or breakthrough technologies and resources for clinical benefit. 

For more information on the office of the CDMRP, go to https://cdmrp.health.mil and review materials provided on the website about the CDMRP program cycle. For more information on the two-tier review process, review the video overview on CDMRP’s YouTube channel here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ULqi-5V5ZGM

1.6.1.1 Provide an incoming transition plan for 90 days from contract to contract. The plan shall initially be submitted with the Offeror’s proposal and updated after award. Coordinate with the government in planning and implementing a complete transition. The Government will designate a transition period for the incoming Contractor to coordinate and work with the existing contractor. 

The Transition-In Plan shall describe in detail how the Offeror will transition in to the resultant contract to include being capable of providing full performance on the day after the end of the transition-in period. This includes the following tasks:

1.6.1.2 Transition-out period:  Provide an outgoing transition plan for the 60-day period prior to contract end when work is being transitioned from this active contract to a follow-on contract/order or Government entity. A draft plan shall be submitted within 90 calendar days prior to the end of the contract. The final plan will be approved by the Government within 75 calendar days prior to the end of the contract.

In accordance with the Government-approved Transition-Out plan, the Contractor shall assist the Government in planning and implementing a complete transition from this contractor to the follow-on contract. The plan shall include formal coordination with Government staff and successor staff and management. The transition plan shall also include delivery of copies of existing policies and procedures, delivery of required metrics and statistics, ensuring continuity of services, transition of historic data to new Contractor system including a list of current incumbent Contractor personnel, return/transfer of GFP, and coordination with the Government to account for government keys, ID/access cards, and any security codes (if applicable). 

1.7 Administrative specifications

1.7.1 Place of performance: The work shall be performed at the contractor’s location or remotely. In person meeting support will be required at Fort Detrick, Maryland and other meeting locations within the National Capitol Region.

1.7.2 Hours of operation: The contractor is responsible for conducting business Monday through Friday except Federal holidays, or when the Government facility is closed due to local or national emergencies, administrative closings, or similar Government-directed facility closings. 

The contractor must maintain an adequate workforce for the uninterrupted performance of all tasks defined within this PWS when the Government facility is not closed for the above reasons. Overtime is not permitted.

CDMRP’s normal business hours are 8:00 am to 5:00 pm (Eastern Standard Time). CDMRP core hours are from 9:00 am to 3:00 pm (EST).

1.7.3 Emergency Services: On occasion, services may be required to support an activation or exercise of contingency plans outside the normal duty hours. The contractor shall designate an Emergency point of contact (POC) in the event of a Continuing Operations (COOP) drill or emergency event requiring 100% accountability of all contractor staff with a DoD ID number. Once initiated, responses are required within one hour of being contacted by the COR or Chief of Acquisition.

1.8 Contractor travel: The Contractor shall be required to travel within the Continental United States (CONUS) and within the National Capitol Region (NCR) to attend meetings, conferences, and training. The contractor may be required to travel off-site to these locations in support of this PWS. Contractor shall be authorized travel expenses consistent with the cost principles and procedures in Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 31.2, Travel Costs and the limitations of funds specified in this contract. All travel requires Government approval/authorization and notification to the Contracting Officer Representative (COR).

The QCP shall identify the Contractor’s methods of quality surveillance, performance standards, roles and responsibilities, and ways of identifying potential risks along with a plan to address them if/when they arise. 1 REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) PURPOSE AND GOVERNMENTS 
DISCLAIMERS  
1.1 PURPOSE 
The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) to request 
detailed data, innovative approaches, and strategic insights from industry partners regarding their 
capabilities and readiness to (1) support the transition of the National Airspace System (NAS) and its 
supporting Air Traffic Control (ATC) infrastructure to Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) and (2) support 
the transition of FAA business systems to PQC. 
The NAS is undergoing a generational transformation to realize a modern, resilient, and globally leading 
ATC system capable of integrating new entrants ( e.g., drones, Advanced Air Mobility (AAM), and 
commercial space operations). Achieving this vision requires a secure foundation capable of withstanding 
emerging threats, including those posed by quantum computing. W ithout quantum‑resistant, crypto‑agile 
security, the NAS cannot achieve the reliability, performance, or international leadership required in th e 
decades ahead. FAA therefore views PQC not as a compliance exercise, but as a foundational enabler of 
modernization—one that must be embedded into every vendor solution, every system upgrade, and every 
step of the Brand New Air Traffic Control System (“BNATCS”)1. 
Specifically, th is RFI seeks industry input on the challenging and mandatory transition of both FAA 
enterprise IT and FAA NAS safety-critical ATC systems to quantum-resistant algorithms to meet federal 
mandates, while managing the high cost, complex recertification, and potential operational disruption of 
integrating new cryptography into FAA operations.  The Government is also seeking information regarding 
the most effective architecture for the enterprise-wide transition to PQC. As National Institute of Standard 
(NIS) standards continue to finalize, the Government is evaluating the feasibility of a "One -Stop Shop" 
(Integrated Suite) approach versus a "Best-of-Breed" (Modular Component) approach. The goal is to ensure 
FAA NAS and FAA non-NAS systems remain "crypto-agile" while minimizing implementation risks and 
interoperability gaps.  FAA recognizes that the PQC market is still maturing and that potential vendors may 
not currently possess the internal capability to execute a fully  integrated solution. Specifically, the FAA 
acknowledges that: 
• A single provider may not have validated all necessary cryptographic primitives across all hardware 
and software layers.   
 
1 https://www.faa.gov/new-atcs 

 
 
2 
 
• A provider’s offerings may not support both FAA Information Technology (IT) and FAA 
Operational Technology (OT) systems. 
• Integration of PQC into legacy National Airspace System (NAS) infrastructure or legacy FAA 
business infrastructure may require specialized expertise that exceeds the scope of a single product 
suite. 
1.2 REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) ONLY. 
This RFI is issued solely for information and planning purposes and does not constitute a Request for 
Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFP in the future. Your response will be treated as information 
only, and it shall not be used as a proposal. This RFI does not commit the Government to contract for any 
supply or service whatsoever. 
The Government is not, at this time, seeking proposals and will not accept unsolicited proposals. 
Respondents are advised that the Government will not reimburse any costs associated with preparing or 
submitting a response to this RFI. Submission of a response does not guarantee participation in any future 
solicitation or resulting contract award. Information obtained through this RFI may be used to inform the 
FAA’s acquisition strategy for PQC modernization. The FAA, at its sole discretion, may contact one, some, 
all, or none of the respondents to the RFI and ask for additional information.

The migration of Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) systems, encompassing both enterprise

Control (ATC) System improvements.  This RFI explicitly requests vendor analysis on the potential 
disruption or delay caused by PQC insertion into both NAS ATC as well as FAA Information Technology 
systems.

PART I – OVERVIEW INFORMATION

CONCISE SUMMARY OF TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENT:   Seeking innovative research in technologies and techniques to establish trusted foundations for hardware and software that enables secure, resilient and affordable Command, Control, Communications, Computers, and Intelligence (C4I) and Cyber technologies (C4I and Cyber Technologies) information processing systems. entitled Foundations of Trusted Systems.

However, the Air Force reserves the right to award zero, one, or more Procurement Contracts or Other Transactions, and assistance instruments for all, some, or none of the solicited effort based on the offeror’s ability to perform desired work and funding fluctuations. There is no limit on the number of OTs that may be awarded to an individual offeror.  

TYPE OF INSTRUMENTS THAT MAY BE AWARDED: FAR based Procurement contracts, CFR based grants and cooperative agreements or other transactions (OT) under 10 USC 4021, 10 USC 4022 (previously 10 USC 4002, 2371, 10 USC 4003, 2371b) depending upon the nature of the work proposed. 10 USC 4023 also allows for FAR based contracts, OTs for research, OTs for Prototype, and assistance instruments.
