BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT (BAA) TITLE: Foundations of Trusted Systems                                                                                             

BAA NUMBER: BAA FA8750-25-S-7001

Assistance Listing Number: 12.800 and 12.910 

Federal Acquisition Supply Chain Act (FASCSA) Orders: As of the date of this solicitation amendment, there are no applicable FASCSA orders. This requirement only applies to FAR based awards. 

I.  TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENTS:

The Air Force Research Laboratory is soliciting white papers under this Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) for research, development, integration, test and evaluation of technologies/techniques to establish trusted foundations for hardware and software that enables secure, resilient and affordable Command, Control, Communications, Computers, and Intelligence (C4I) and Cyber technologies (C4I and Cyber Technologies) information processing systems.

Trusted, Secure, and Resilient Computational Systems: The objective of this technical area is to research and develop the essential elements, tools, and methodologies for trusted, secure, and resilient computing environments, including both the underlying hardware and software, side by side with power, cost, performance, and reliability. Topics of interest include, but are not limited to:

Problems and challenges with current processor designs for trustworthiness and their solutions

Problems and challenges with current computer architectures for trustworthiness and solutions to them

Tools and methodologies for ensuring trustworthiness of integrated circuits (ICs) and systems targeting malicious inclusions such as hardware Trojans, side-channel timing attacks, etc.

New computer architectures for secure and reliable computing, including data integrity and code protection and verification.

Operating System level constructs, objects, functions, and distributions that must be provided to complement the hardware to enable a trustworthy computing base.

Tools and methodologies for ensuring trustworthiness and security of the software development process, including compilers, assemblers, linkers, binary checks, and source code analysis.

State-of-the-art software-based assurance designs, methodologies, or concepts which are better suited for implementation in hardware than software.

Hardware architecture techniques for self IC inspection, characterization, and testing/debug. The se techniques can be applied for automated post fabrication verification and/or adaptive system degradation.

(2) Trusted and Assured Software:

(a) Software Assurance: The objective of this area is to enhance and create foundations of Software Assurance (SwA).  Achieve SwA across the application space through a holistic approach, agilely addressing all layers of the supply chain and enterprise including governance, partnerships, process, standards, and education. Areas of interest include:

(i) SwA technology which advances the state of SwA by addressing technology gaps to improve SwA tools (e.g. precision and recall), and scalability (e.g. code size, expertise required, and execution time).

(ii) Tools Assessment and Categorization  

(iii) Evidence-based software assurance

(iv) Prototype Software Assurance Demonstration  

(b) Trusted and Resilient Software-intensive Systems Engineering: The objective of this technical area is to develop resilient techniques, methodologies and tools to guarantee trust (as measured by correctness, security, reliability, predictability, and survivability) and maintain this trust as self-healing/repair techniques fight through cyber-attacks, including zero-day attacks. This research area seeks to extend and advance software development tools that will enable the development and maintenance of trusted and resilient software systems for enterprise and tactical level embedded cyber physical platforms in DevSecOps. This area will focus on research and development to advance software (SW) development tools, to include formal tools, model based techniques and/or architectures based approaches to enable the development of SW systems that are both trusted and resilient. Research and development will also be focused on new approaches, methods and/or tools for continuous (runtime) Verification & Validation(V&V) and runtime environments that can monitor and maintain a trusted and resilient envelope of operation. Technical areas of interest include:

(i) Scalable techniques to enable trust in model-based software engineering, including correctness of machine learning

(ii) Model-based engineering for predictable software attributes  

(iii) Formal methods tools, including connecting proofs of the models to actual code and auditable proof production for tools and static analysis algorithms

(iv) Provably correct code generation and repair

(v) Evolutionary approaches, trusted software and systems composability  

(vi) Modeling, analysis, and verification of autonomous software  

(vii) Novel architectural approaches, strategic “roots of trust,” hardening and resiliency techniques such as artificial diversity, containment areas for execution of untrusted software, lightweight runtime monitoring techniques and utilization of hardware (HW) advances  

(viii) Trusted and resilient mechanisms to fight through software failures, cyber-attacks to include zero-day attack  

(ix) Human understanding and trust of automated software development, red teaming, metrics and measures of trustworthy systems, integration, validation and demonstration on a realistic mission critical embedded system exemplar  

(x) Autonomous resilience, self-healing software systems, and pliable computing.  

(c) Cyber Physical Systems (CPS): The objective of this technical area is to develop the tools, methodologies, and foundational science providing required scalability and interoperability to make integration and subsequent analysis of computational and physical components and the networks connecting them practical. Technical areas of interest include:

(i) Specification, modeling, and analysis such as heterogeneous models of computation and hybrid discrete and continuous systems;   

(ii) Modularity, composability, predictability, and synthesis addressing the issues of scalability and the integration of legacy systems; and   

(iii) Verification and validation techniques (assurance, simulation, formal methods, correct-and-secure-by-construction, etc.) applicable to these models.  

  

(d) AI in Trusted Systems: The objective of this research area is to leverage the potential of human-machine teaming to improve automation, raise human understanding, and thereby mitigate the potential risks of bad information or bad decisions from designers.  This area’s focus is therefore on raising abstraction levels, leveraging AI for aiding in correct-by-construction design and evaluation, and developing techniques for continual assurance of the learning-enabled components of those systems.  Technical areas of interest include:

(i) Capturing, learning, or annotating software intent and constraints separate from the concrete decisions required to create a specific instance of software

(ii) Using captured intent to drastically reduce the human-in-the-loop effort needed to adapt software to new requirements, platforms, and resources

(iii) Verifying that the newly adapted software provides the functional needs of the customer/end user and that the instance does not violate any requirements

(iv) Integrating a new intent-defined software development paradigm into existing Agile workflows to enable adoption and transition into the greater programmer community

(v) Cost-effective, reliable methods of predicting performance of system configurations using high-fidelity models

(vi) Automated decision-making processes that can rapidly converge on solutions concerning interdependent design constraints

(vii) Exploration techniques that scale to large state spaces

(viii) Means of curating evidence for the assurance of software

(ix) Technology for validation and assessment of confidence in an assurance case argument

(x) Automated construction of assurance cases

(xi) Continual assurance technology for learning-enabled components.

(xii) Establishing robust mechanisms to monitor, validate, and assess machine learning models

(xiii) Detecting and mitigating security vulnerabilities, including drift, bias, and adversarial attacks in AI systems.

(xiv) Integrating security-by-design principles into the development and deployment lifecycle of learning-enabled components

(xv) Assessing the correctness of AI-based decisions and behaviors through rigorous testing and validation processes, ensuring alignment with intended functionality and minimizing risk 

(xvi) Utilizing AI to streamline the adoption, automation, and scalability of formal methods and verification techniques in software development, enhancing usability, reducing expertise barriers, and facilitating more effective human-machine collaboration.

(e) Digital Engineering Model-based Analysis: In support of the Digital Engineering Strategy, it is required to develop techniques and methodologies to extract software models from code. Rapid and accurate generation of models is foundational to reducing errors and time required to develop and maintain complex software systems. Technical areas of interest include:

(i) Extraction of models from source code

	- Generated models should have formal semantics for analyzability

	- Support, but not need not be strictly limited to, extraction from C/C++ sources

	- Due to the complexities involved, it is anticipated that extraction from source code will come first

(ii) Models of the behavior of the source code as well as its structure

(iii) Annotation of the extracted models with requirements and other non-functional properties necessary for security analysis

(iv) extraction of models from binaries – these models should also have formally analyzable semant

B.4 STATEMENT OF WORK

1. Background. 

The Environmental Management Service (EMS) at the VA San Diego Healthcare System requires a customer feedback monitoring service to support restroom cleanliness monitoring and service response. The system will allow patients, visitors, and staff to provide real-time feedback regarding restroom conditions and notify EMS personnel when cleaning or supply services are required.

The objective is to improve restroom cleanliness, responsiveness to service issues, and overall patient experience through real-time data collection and reporting.

2. Scope. 

The contractor shall provide a software-based restroom feedback monitoring service that collects real-time customer feedback data and alerts EMS personnel of restroom service needs.

The contractor shall provide all software, system hosting, communications services, data processing, reporting capability, and technical support necessary to operate the restroom feedback monitoring system.

The service shall support approximately 58 restroom feedback terminals currently installed throughout the VA San Diego Medical Center. The Government will provide the existing feedback terminals. The contractor shall ensure system connectivity, monitoring capability, and data reporting functionality.

3. Salient Characteristics  

Real-Time Feedback Monitoring
3.1 Collect and process customer satisfaction feedback from restroom feedback terminals in real time.
3.2 Record timestamp and terminal location associated with each feedback response.
3.3 Allow EMS personnel to monitor restroom conditions through a centralized interface.

Alert Notification Capability
3.4 Provide automated alerts when restroom service issues are reported (e.g., dirty restroom, missing supplies).
3.5  Notifications shall be capable of delivery via email alerts, SMS text alerts, mobile application notifications, or web dashboard alerts.

Reporting and Analytics
3.6  Provide real-time dashboard capability.
3.7  Generate restroom cleanliness and performance reports.
3.8 Identify trends in restroom satisfaction and service response times.
3.9 Reports must be exportable in Excel, PDF, or CSV format.

System Access
3.10  Secure web-based administrative dashboard.
3.11 Multiple user accounts for EMS personnel.
3.12 Mobile access capability for authorized users.

Data Management
3.13 Provide system hosting and data storage.
3.14 Ensure data integrity and security.
• Allow export of raw data for VA analysis.

Technical Support
3.15 Provide system troubleshooting, maintenance, and updates.
3.16 Support availability Monday–Friday, 8:00 AM – 5:00 PM Eastern Time, excluding federal holidays.

4. Quality Assurance 

The contractor shall ensure the feedback monitoring system remains operational and capable of transmitting and reporting data from all active terminals.

The contractor shall perform periodic system checks to verify system connectivity and reporting functionality.

5. Period of Performance

The task order shall cover services for a base period of one (1) year with option to exercise up to (4) one-year option periods.

CHAPTER 1: INTRODUCTION

OVERVIEW

Broad Agency Announcements (BAAs) are solicitation methods for Research and Development (R&D) efforts based on synopses published in the Governmentwide Point of Entry (GPE) and/or Grants.gov that provide for full and open competition in accordance with (IAW) Federal Acquisition Regulations (FAR) 6.102(d)(2) and merit-based, competitive procedures IAW Office of Management and Budget (OMB) guidance, “Uniform Administrative Requirements, Cost Principles, and Audit Requirements for Federal Awards,” published in the Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) at 2 CFR part 200 and implemented by the DoD at 2 CFR part 1104, “Implementation of Governmentwide Guidance for Grants and Cooperative Agreements”.  Provisions of the DoD Grants and Agreements Regulations (DoDGARs) other than 32 CFR parts 32 and 33 continue to be in effect, with applicability as stated in those provisions. BAAs are established in FAR 35.016 and are authorized for the acquisition of basic and applied research and that part of development not related to the development of a specific system or hardware procurement. The objective of a BAA is to encourage participation by science and technology firms and educational institutions in meeting Air Force R&D goals for innovative ideas and approaches for research that is general in nature.

CRITERIA FOR USE

Use of a BAA to solicit for research and development is encouraged when:

The Government desires new and creative solutions to problem statements.

Using a conventional statement of work could result in unintentionally stifling ideas and concepts given many possible approaches.

Fulfilling requirements for scientific study and experimentation directed toward advancing the state-of-the-art or increasing knowledge or understanding rather than focusing on a specific system or hardware solution.

The Government must be able to state its objectives in terms of areas of need or interest rather than specific solutions or outcomes.

Meaningful proposals with varying technical/scientific approaches are reasonably anticipated.

CHAPTER 2: DEFINITIONS

Agreements Officer: Title given to a person with the authority to enter into, administer, and/or terminate non-FAR based acquisitions.

Assistance Instrument: Business arrangement that is appropriate when the goal of the program is to transfer a thing of value to accomplish a public purpose of support or stimulation as authorized by law. Assistance instruments include Grants, Cooperative Agreements (CAs), Technology Investment Agreements (TIAs), and Other Transactions (OTs). Assistance instruments are covered by Office of Management and Budget (OMB) guidance, “Uniform Administrative Requirements, Cost Principles, and Audit Requirements for Federal Awards,” published in the Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) at 2 CFR part 200 and implemented by the DoD at 2 CFR part 1103, “Interim Grants and Cooperative Agreements Implementation of Guidance in 2 CFR part 200” (79 FR 76047, December 19, 2014).  

Broad Agency Announcement (BAA): A general announcement of an agency’s research interest including criteria for selecting proposals and soliciting the participation of all offerors capable of satisfying the Government’s needs. (See FAR 6.102(d)(2) and FAR 35.016.).

BAA Amendment: Any change to the originally released Announcement. A BAA amendment may include a change to the time and date for receipt of proposals or white papers. A change to an individual Call issued under a BAA, will be classified as a Call Amendment. 

Contract Specialist: Term used interchangeably to include the Contract Negotiator or Buyer. Be advised only a Contracting Officer is warranted to obligate the Government. Regulations specify several other functions that must be performed by a Contracting Officer.

Contracting Officer: Title given to a person with the authority to enter into, administer, and/or terminate contracts and make related determinations and findings. Only a Contracting Officer or Grants Officer has the authority to obligate the Government.

Contractor Acquired Property: Property acquired, fabricated, or otherwise provided by the contractor for performing a contract and to which the Government has title.

Cooperative Agreement: An assistance instrument in which there will be substantial involvement between the Government and the recipient to perform basic research, applied research, and advanced technology development. A cost-sharing arrangement may be required. (See 2 CFR §200.24)

Funding Opportunity Announcement (FOA):  To avoid confusion between acquisition and assistance program solicitations, AFRL uses the term “FOA” for assistance only program solicitations.  In general, the terms BAA or FOA will be used interchangeably within this document.

Government Furnished Property (GFP): Property in the possession of, or directly acquired by, the Government and subsequently furnished to the contractor for performance of a contract. Government-furnished property includes, but is not limited to, spares and property furnished for repair, maintenance, overhaul, or modification. Government-furnished property also includes contractor-acquired property if the contractor-acquired property is a deliverable under a cost contract when accepted by the Government for continued use under the contract. (See FAR Part 45.)

Governmentwide Point of Entry (GPE): The single point where Government business opportunities greater than $25,000, including synopses of proposed contract actions, solicitations, and and associated information, can be accessed electronically by the public. BAA solicitations are published at the GPE. The GPE is located at https:// sam.gov/.

Grant: An instrument under which the Government provides assistance to a recipient (college/university/non-profit organization) for basic, applied or advanced research. There is no substantial Government involvement. (See 2 CFR §200.51)

Grants.gov: The public notification media used when a BAA will allow for the award of an assistance instrument (grant, cooperative agreement, technology investment agreement) as well as a contract.

Grants Officer: Title given to a person with the authority to enter into, administer, and/or terminate grants and cooperative agreements.

Independent Research and Development (IR&D) Cost: The cost of effort which is neither sponsored by a grant, nor required in performing a contract, and which falls within any of the following four areas: (a) Basic research, (b) Applied research, (c) Development, and (d) Systems and other concept formulation studies. (See FAR 31.001.)

Other Transactions for Prototype  10 U.S.C 4022 provides the Secretary of the Air Force authority to enter into transactions (other than contracts) for prototype projects that are directly relevant to enhancing the mission effectiveness of military personnel and the supporting platforms, systems, components, or materials proposed to be acquired or developed by the Department of Defense, or to improvement of platforms, systems, components, or materials in use by the armed forces. Agreements issued under this authority are commonly referred to as Other Transaction (OT) for Prototype agreements. 

Other Transactions for Research: An instrument under which the Government provides assistance to a recipient (can be a single recipient or a consortium) to transfer something of value to the public sector. Substantial Government involvement and 50/50 cost sharing are required. Used when it is not appropriate or feasible to use a contract, grant, or cooperative agreement. (See 10 U.S.C. 4021.)

Peer or Scientific Review: The process where each proposal is reviewed against the criteria called out in the BAA. It may also address the technical team’s assessment of applicable quantitative elements, to include number of labor hours proposed, skills mix, materials, subcontracting, etc.

Price Analyst: A contracting professional whose function is focused on analyzing and negotiating an offeror's cost proposal and documenting the results of the negotiation. 

Program Manager (PM): The individual responsible for overseeing/managing a Science & Technology (S&T) acquisition or assistance project. This individual may have a different job title in their primary position.

Statement of Work (SOW): The document that captures the technical content of the contractual effort. The contract may incorporate portions of the offeror’s technical proposal instead of a formal SOW. For BAAs, offerors are often required to submit a non-proprietary contractor statement of work (sometimes referred to as a C-SOW).

Technology Investment Agreements (TIA): An assistance instrument used to attract non-traditional DoD contractors and facilitate the integration of the defense and commercial industries. It requires a 50/50 cost share unless waived. (See 32 CFR §37.100.)

White Paper: A brief (usually 2-5 pages) summary of the proposed technical approach with an accompanying rough-order-of-magnitude (ROM) price.

CHAPTER 3: PROCESSES

BAA PROCESS: The first step usually involves an announcement on the Governmentwide Point of Entry (GPE) and, for assistance instruments, Grants.gov, that requests interested offerors to submit either a white paper or full proposal (depending on the BAA variation selected, see below). The BAA announcement on the GPE and, for assistance instruments, Grants.gov, will be the only solicitation. This may be a short announcement that links to further information or the full announcement. It is recommended interested offerors read the BAA very carefully. Typically, the following information will be included in the BAA announcements:

An identifying number and program name.

Points of contact for both contracting and technical matters. Offerors are encouraged to make contact with the listed individuals for any assistance required.

A description of the broadly stated areas of potential basic research or a description of the scientific or engineering problems needing new and creative solutions. A short summary of areas of program interest, expanded as appropriate, to include problems, objectives, and deliverable items (reports, software, prototypes, etc.).

Information on proposal or white paper format and number of copies of requested.

The address and/or method for submittal.

If a two-step BAA variation is used, a description of the full proposal invitation procedures.

Criteria for selecting white papers and proposals.

If an informational briefing is scheduled, details as to time, date, place, number of attendees permitted, clearances needed, etc.

Advice to foreign-owned firms that their participation is subject to foreign disclosure review procedures and that they should immediately contact the contracting focal point for information if they contemplate responding.

If export-controlled technical data is involved, a note advising that only firms holding certification under the US/Canada Joint Certification Program (JCP) https://www.public.dacs.dla.mil/jcp/ext/ are allowed access to such data.

The total dollar value or range of dollar values as well as anticipated period of performance may be stated in the announcement.

A statement that multiple white papers or proposals addressing different research areas, within the purview of the announcement, may be submitted by each offeror.

Notice to offerors that only Contracting/Grants/Agreements Officers are legally authorized to commit the Government.

Date and time when white papers or full proposals will be due. If an Open BAA variation has been selected white papers or proposals may be allowed over a specified extended period.

BAA VARIATIONS

Variations of the BAA process are available for use. The following types are commonly used but are not considered all inclusive.

One-Step: The one-step process is used to request full technical and cost proposals from each offeror. The proposals are reviewed in accordance with the solicitation criteria and typically all of a selected proposal, part of a selected proposal, or none of a proposal may be selected for award.

Two-Step: The two-step process is sometimes used when a large number of proposals are anticipated. Potential offerors are invited to submit brief descriptive white papers in lieu of full proposals. The BAA must state whether an unfavorable white paper review will bar the offeror from further consideration. Full proposals are requested from those offerors selected in the white paper review process. When proposals are received, they are reviewed consistent with the process for one-step BAAs.

Open BAA: This approach allows for white paper and/or proposal submittals at any time within a specified period. BAAs must be publicized no less frequently than annually. White papers/proposals are reviewed when received during the period that the BAA is open. One of the purposes of an Open BAA is consideration of Industry-Generated ideas. The open BAA concept gives the Government flexibility to accomplish some of the acquisition planning activities after white paper receipt when more details are known to the Gov’t. (Note: Under a Closed BAA, all acquisition planning activities are accomplished prior to solicitation release). 

Closed BAA: This approach allows for white paper and/or proposal submittals at a specified date and time as set forth in the BAA. Late bid and proposal provisions (IAW FAR 52.215-1(c)(3)) are usually included in the BAA. The closed BAA is used when the Government has a better understanding of the existing R&D requirement and more defined research objectives.

BAA with Calls: This technique allows for publication of a basic BAA solicitation that contains overarching information.  The basic BAA often functions as a framework identifying the technical areas and giving the basic terms and administrative information of the BAA, and it is usually open for at least 12 months. The requests for white papers and/or proposals are transmitted via Calls that are published separately from the basic BAA at various times during the open period of the basic BAA (Note: The first Call(s) may be published with the basic BAA). The Calls may further define the technology/government needs or just request white papers or full proposals. The Calls may also inclu

1.0 Background 
PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT (PWS) 
Electronic Warfare and Electromagnetic Special Programs 
 
 
Naval Undersea Warfare Center Division, Newport (NUWCDIVNPT) Office of Technical Project 
Management Code 349, Electromagnetic (EM) Special Programs and Advanced Electronic Warfare 
(EW), is tasked to perform a wide range of engineering and program management functions in 
support of special programs in the area of EW and Communication systems, which augment 
submarine tactical capabilities. Code 349 EM Special Programs functions as the Technical Design 
Agent (TDA), Acquisition Engineering Agent (AEA), In-service Engineering agent (ISEA), and 
Software Support Agent (SSA) for special mission EW and Communications systems, subsystems, 
sensors and networks. Code 349 EM Special Programs is responsible for the development and test 
of prospective systems, in-service engineering support for existing systems, and quick reaction 
support to the Fleet based upon new and emergent operational requirements. 
 
1.1 Places of Performance: Work will be performed at NUWCDIVNPT, contractor site, other 
Government sites, and other contractor sites as identified by and called out in the technical 
instructions. 
 
1.2. Authorized Users: NUWCDIVNPT, Electromagnetic Systems Department, Code 34. 
 
1.3 Sponsors: Current and prospective program sponsors to be supported under this task order 
include: 
- Fleet Forces Command (FFC) 
- OP NAV N2/N6 
- OP NAV N97 
- Strategic Capabilities Office (SCO) 
- Submarine Security Program (SSP) 
- NAVSEA PMS-435 
- PMW-770 
- Commander Submarine Atlantic Fleet (CSL) 
- Commander Submarine Pacific Fleet (CSP) 
- Navy Tactical Exploitation of National Capabilities (TENCAP) 
- Office of Naval Research (ONR) 
 
- Navy Cyber Warfare Development Group (NCWDG) 
- Office of Naval Intelligence (ONI) 
- Special Operations Command (SOCOM) 
- Naval Special Warfare Development Group (NSWDG) 
- National Reconnaissance Office (NRO) 
- National Security Agency (NSA) 
- Naval Information Warfare Center (NIWC) 
 
1.4 Types of Funding: The Government contemplates the following types of funds will be obligated 
under this task order: 
- Operation and Maintenance, Navy (O&MN) 
- Other Procurement, Navy (OPN) 
- Research, Development, Test & Evaluation, Navy (RDT&E,N) 
- Research, Development, Test & Evaluation, Defense Agencies (RDDA) 
 
2.0 Scope 

This tasking is for engineering services to develop and field special mission EW and special 
augmentation systems, subsystems, sensors, and associated networks onboard submarines and 
other platforms such as Unmanned Aerial and Undersea Vehicles (UAV/UUV). Engineering services 
include: In-service and Operational services, Engineering and Software Development, Assembly and 
Fabrication, Test and Evaluation, Configuration Management and Project Management services. 
Required services under this task order will be driven by operational, Fleet and Intelligence 
community requirements, which are often new and emergent in nature. 
 
 
2.1  Program or Systems Supported 
 
The following special augmentation systems are supported by this task order: 
- Mission Configurable Mast (MCM) and Payloads 
- Signals Research Target Development (SRTD) Mast and Payloads 
- Multifunction Modular Mast (MMM) Payloads 
- Special Operations Intelligence System (SOIS)

4.0 Technical Requirements 
 
The contractor shall perform technical services as detailed in the following tasks associated with EW 
and special augmentation systems specified in paragraph 2.0. 
 
The following tasks shall be accomplished in accordance with Applicable Documents (AD) identified 
in Section 3.0, and utilizing Government Furnished Information (GFI) listed in Section 6.0, and as 
specified in individual TIs. 
4.1 In-Service Maintenance and Operational Support 
 
In accordance with the Applicable Documents in Section 3.0, the contractor shall perform in-service 
maintenance and operational services related to the special augmentation systems identified in 
paragraph 2.0 which are installed on US submarines and other platforms. 
 
 
Applicable to Task 4.1, where the TIs or GFI indicate Maintenance and Operational Support is associated with 
Wartime Operations and represent a critical need for the Navy, the contractor shall: 
 
a. Assign the action within 72 hours. 
b. Begin performance on the wartime related effort immediately upon assignment. 
c. Create a schedule within 72 hours which demonstrates a plan to complete the action and provide any 
negative impacts on other non-Wartime Acquisition Response Plan (WARP) scheduled tasking. 
d. Provide daily status reports of percentage complete toward the proposed schedule and details of any issues 
impacting timely and accurate completion. 
The contractor shall: 
 
4.1.1 Maintain the operational readiness of special augmentation systems and return special 
augmentation systems to Ready for Issue (RFI) status. The contractor shall troubleshoot, repair, 
refurbish, upgrade, test and certify systems as RFI that are removed from platforms prior to the systems 

being cross-decked to another platform. For augmentation systems that include composite 
components, such as antenna radomes and radar absorbing structures, the contractor shall only 
perform cosmetic and non-structural repairs and restoration.. The contractor shall report structural 
damage of composite components to NUWCDIVNPT Code 349. 
 
NOTE: The contractor personnel performing  subtask 4.1.1 are required to possess a Category 3 (CAT-
3) crane certification per NUWCDIVNPTINST 5100.14G and Naval Facilities Engineering Command 
publication NAVFAC P-307. 
 
4.1.2 Conduct Pre-Installation Check-Out (PICO) to assess the condition of the ship’s outboard 
mast prior to either removal of the ships mast and installation of a special augmentation mast or verify it 
is functional and usable for integration with the ship’s inboard equipment. The contractor shall install 
special augmentation systems. The contractor shall  p erform engineering services to 
resolve technical issues encountered during the installation process and perform troubleshooting to 
identify functional issues with installed augmentation equipment, including radio frequency (RF) 
interfaces to the tactical periscope and imaging mast. The contractor shall d efine, develop, 
document, and submit updates to the TEMPALT TDP via the Departure from Specification (DFS) 
process to reflect the as-installed configuration when deviations from the GFI are required. In 
accordance with the ADs in 3.1, and using GFI 6.15, the contractor shall perform System Operational 
Verification Tests (SOVTs) on installed systems. 
 
4.1.3 Perform cyber security certifications up to SCI level on special augmentation systems installed 
on submarines and other naval vessels. NOTE: The contractor personnel performing this subtask are 
required, at a minimum, to be cyber security workforce certified at Information Assurance Technical 
(IAT) level II.

is required for end-to-end certification and training.

1 SECTION I 
 
1.0 DESCRIPTION OF SERVICES 
 
1.0.1 Background. 
The Checkmate division (AF/A35K), within Air Force Operations (AF/A3), requires contractor support to provide 
the Chief of Staff of the Air Force (CSAF) and other Department of the Air Force (DAF) leaders with informed 
advice, opinions, recommendations, and innovative ideas to better support the warfighter. The Checkmate division 
develops operational plans and concepts to address near-term, current global challenges as outlined in the National 
Security Strategy (NSS), National Military Strategy (NMS), and National Defense Strategy (NDS). To effectively 
support Checkmate, the Contractor shall demonstrate exceptional critical thinking and problem-solving skills, 
coupled with a deep understanding of airpower principles and their application across the operational spectrum. The 
Contractor shall provide expertise on the decision-making processes used by the Joint Chiefs of Staff (JCS) Tank 
and the National Security Council (NSC), as well as formal and crisis action planning methodologies. The 
Contractor will proactively anticipate and resolve complex problems, leveraging their airpower expertise to develop 
innovative and effective solutions for the warfighter. The Contractor will serve as a readily available "think tank" 
capability for the AF/A3 and its staff, providing cross-functional expertise and facilitating processes both within 
and outside of headquarters to advance the air, space, and cyberspace operational vision. 
 
1.0.2 Scope. 
To maintain a core of expertise within the AF/A3, the Contractor shall provide personnel with in-depth knowledge 
of current Air Force and joint issues, demonstrating a strong understanding of airpower principles and their 
application to strategic and operational challenges. The Contractor will apply critical thinking and problem-solving 
skills to assist Checkmate in anticipating future developments and planning requirements at the institutional, air 
component, and combatant command (CCMD) levels. This includes proactively identifying potential challenges 
and developing innovative solutions informed by airpower experience and expertise. The Contractor shall compile 
comprehensive briefing materials and actively participate in presentations, ensuring that DAF senior leaders receive 
sound military advice grounded in thorough analysis of airpower capabilities. In general, the Contractor shall 
provide advanced information gathering and strategic analysis to support Checkmate’s efforts to effectively employ 
warfighting capabilities, leveraging their expertise to optimize airpower's contribution to national security 
objectives. Subject matter experts (SMEs) will provide operational planning knowledge and advise service-level 
efforts in planning current and future contingency operations, applying their critical thinking skills to assess risks 
and opportunities within the six regional and functional aspects detailed below. 
 
1.1. REQUIREMENTS 
 
1.1.1 The Contractor shall provide Subject Matter Experts (SMEs) capable of delivering expert consultation and 
analysis on a wide range of national security matters, applying critical thinking and problem-solving skills to 
complex challenges. While individual SME positions will be regionally agnostic, individuals filling these positions 
will align to core National Security Strategy (NSS) and National Defense Strategy (NDS) priorities. The core 
responsibilities of these SMEs shall include: 
 
1.1.1.1 Operational Planning Team (OPT) Support: Planning, leading, and participating in OPTs and representing 
the Air Force as experts in the application of airpower and operational art. 
 
1.1.1.2 Strategic and Operational Concept Development: Assisting in the development of innovative strategic and 
operational concepts, with a specific focus on maximizing the effective integration of air, space, and cyberspace 
power to empower the warfighter at the forward edge. This includes applying critical thinking to evaluate existing 
concepts and identify opportunities for improvement. 
 
 

Page 4 of 20 
 
DRAFT PWS – A3 CHECKMATE SUPPORT FOLLOW-ON                                             Solicitation #: FA7014-26-R-PKHB06 
 
1.1.1.3 Effective Employment Expertise: Providing expert advice and informed opinions on the effective use and 
employment of air, space, and cyberspace capabilities by Combatant Commanders (CCDRs), the military services, 
Allies/partners, and the interagency community. This requires a deep understanding of airpower principles and their 
application across diverse operational environments. 
 
1.1.1.4 Wargaming and Modelling and Simulation (M&S): Utilizing wargaming and M&S techniques to drive 
transformation within the DAF by participating in, and at times directly hosting, wargames and M&S events that 
assess and analyze emergent Air Force operational plans, capabilities, and force employment concepts. This 
includes employing critical thinking to analyze wargame and/or M&S outputs to identify key insights for 
improving warfighting capabilities. 
 
1.1.1.5 Fact-Finding and Analysis: Conducting thorough fact-finding and analysis to support decision-making, 
leveraging their expertise to identify key trends, assess risks, and develop effective mitigation strategies. A 
secondary function of this is to provide advocacy for the warfighter at the HAF-level.  
 
1.2. WARFIGHTER SUPPORT SUBJECT MATTER EXPERT    
 
1.2.1 Six full-time equivalents (FTEs) shall be Warfighter Support SMEs, providing focused support to air 
operations planning, operational art and design, and CCMD contingency plans. This role will be distinct from, but 
conceptually analogous to, a uniformed services action officer. 
 
1.2.2 Key Duties. 
 
1.2.2.1 Contractors shall assist in developing, coordinating, and advising on the implementation of policies related 
to air, space, and cyberspace power to support the CSAF, Deputy Chief of Staff for Operations (AF/A3), and 
Numbered Air Force (NAF)/Air Component Commanders and their Staffs. Contractors shall be focused on the near-
term time horizon (0-36 months) and the current operational challenges associated with Checkmate division 
assigned priorities. 
 
1.2.2.2 Contractors shall participate in the operational planning and analysis process and advise the Joint Staff (JS) 
and CCMD staffs on how to optimize USAF capabilities in support of the warfighter when confronting the 
operational challenges outlined in NSS, NDS, and other policy guidance. 
 
 
1.2.2.3 Contractors shall lead and participate in OPTs and represent the Air Force as airpower SMEs. 
 
1.2.2.4 Contractors shall deliver high-level briefings and reports to senior USAF and Department of War (DoW) 
leaders, translating complex airpower concepts and operations into clear, actionable insights for General Officers 
and Senior Executive Service (SES) stakeholders. 
 
1.2.2.5 Contractors shall provide advice and assessments to validate that assigned planning inputs are strategically 
sound, operationally and logistically feasible, and resource informed/supportable according to the delineations of 
responsibilities as set forth in Title 10, Title 22, Title 32 and Title 50 of the United States Code (USC).
 
 
1.2.2.6 Contractors shall provide rapid and reach back support to CCMD staffs and the Joint Force Air Component 
Commanders (JFACCs) for operational planning activities, contingencies, and exercise events pertaining to 
supported CCMD Areas of Responsibility (AORs). 
 
1.2.2.7 Contractors shall maintain situational awareness of, and provide recommendations about, the current 
political-military (Pol-Mil) issues and operational challenges associated with threats and priority regions as outlined 
within strategic planning guidance, e.g., the NDS, and be able to articulate the impact these have on USAF equities 
to DAF senior leaders.

Call for Solutions for

Airspace Common Operating Picture

Note: Please advise the cognizant Procurement Contracting Officer and Contract Specialist as soon as possible via the email above if your organization intends to submit a Solution Brief in response to this Call for Solution.

Any submissions that are received by the Procurement Contracting Officer (PCO) after the suspense date/time listed above will be deemed late and not evaluated. It is the sole responsibility of the company to ensure that its submission is received in the inbox listed above before the deadline specified.

Description:

The U.S. Army Contracting Command - Orlando (ACC-Orlando) is issuing this Call for Solutions under the authority of 10 U.S.C. § 3458 and Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) Subpart 212.70. This Call for Solutions is intended to competitively acquire innovative commercial products or technologies to support the development and deployment of the: 

Airspace Common Operating Picture (A-COP) 

The U.S. Army requires an advanced airspace management capability to ensure safe, efficient, and compliant operations within Special Use Airspace (SUA) at Army installations. Current systems lack the ability to provide real-time surveillance, monitoring, and deconfliction of manned aircraft and Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS) Groups 1-5, as defined by AR 95-2, AR 350-52, AR 385-63, and TC 3-04.15. This capability gap poses significant risks to safety, operational effectiveness, and compliance with Army regulations.

The envisioned solution must integrate real-time data from manned and unmanned platforms, including Automatic Dependent Surveillance-Broadcast (ADS-B) equipped military and civilian aircraft, and provide situational awareness to Range Management Authorities (RMA). The system must operate continuously, with minimal latency, and deliver precise positional data to support safe operations in high-density environments. Additionally, the solution must align with the Modular Open Systems Approach (MOSA) to ensure compatibility with current and future tactical networks, such as the Tactical Awareness Kit (TAK) and Range Facility Management Support System (RFMSS). The solution must also be scalable, customizable, and capable of supporting operations across multiple installations listed in the Basis of Issue Plan. It must provide flexible data relay options, customizable alerts, and ensure secure operations within a limited-access network. 

1.1	The U.S. Army seeks innovative commercial solutions that address the following attributes: 

Real-Time Airspace Surveillance and Monitoring:

Systems capable of integrating data from multiple sources, including ADS-B, radar, and other sensors, to provide a comprehensive airspace picture.

Solutions that support continuous, low-latency operations in high-density environments.

Deconfliction of Manned and Unmanned Aircraft:

Tools for real-time deconfliction of UAS Groups 1-5 and manned aircraft operating within SUA.

Capabilities to provide automated alerts and recommendations to Range Management Authorities (RMA).

Integration with Tactical Networks:

Solutions that align with the Modular Open Systems Approach (MOSA) and are compatible with existing Army systems, such as the Tactical Awareness Kit (TAK) and Range Facility Management Support System (RFMSS).

Systems that support future scalability and interoperability with emerging technologies.

Scalability and Customizability:

Solutions that can be deployed across multiple Army installations and adapted to varying operational requirements.

Customizable alerting mechanisms, data relay options, and user interfaces to meet mission-specific needs.

Secure Operations:

Systems that ensure secure data transmission and operations within limited-access networks.

Compliance with Army cybersecurity standards and protocols.

Advanced Data Analytics and Visualization:

Tools for advanced data processing, visualization, and reporting to enhance situational awareness and decision-making.

Capabilities to provide predictive analytics for airspace management.

Awarding Instrument

This Call for Solution solicitation will be awarded in accordance with the Army Open Solicitation procedures detailed within Solicitation W9128Z-25-S-A002, posted to SAM.gov on 01 May 2025. This Call for Solution will utilize CSO procedures. Use of a CSO in accordance with DFARS Subpart 212.70 in conjunction with FAR 35 and DFARS 235 is considered to be a competitive procedure for the purposes of 10 U.S.C. chapter 221 and FAR 6.102.

Solicitation Notes

In addition to the general guidelines included in the Open Solicitation, the following guidelines apply to this Call for Solution.

Offerors are responsible for monitoring SAM.gov for any amendments to this solicitation that may have updated information.

The Government will give preference to submissions that demonstrate an innovative, existing, and reference-verifiable commercial ability to accomplish the desired solution attributes listed above.

Resellers and academic research proposals are not desired.

All solution briefs will be valid for 180 calendar days after the submission date.

The Solution Brief must identify any intellectual property involved in the effort and associated restrictions on the Government’s use of that intellectual property.

The Government reserves the right to go directly from Solution Brief to award.

General Information and Questions

Questions are to be sent only to the Procurement Contracting Officer and Contract Specialist (POCs) listed in this Call for Solution. The following shall be utilized in the email subject line: Call for Solution – CPE-STRI-ACOP (reference the section area). Material questions and answers will be published and updated on www.sam.gov.

Phase 0: Solicitation for Solution Briefs

Interested offerors must submit a concise solution brief (maximum 10-page white paper or 20 slides) addressing the following:

Executive Summary: Overview of the proposed solution and its relevance to the desired solution under this Call for Solutions.

Technology Concept: Description of the innovative aspects of the solution, including any required development or adaptation. Show and/or describe how your proposed solution or potential new capabilities represent an application of innovative commercial products, innovative commercial technologies or adaptations/modifications of existing commercial product technologies to the A-COP.

Company Viability: Overview of the company including relevant experience.

Intellectual Property (IP): Description of any proprietary technologies or data rights.

Submission Guidelines:

Interested offerors shall include Company Name, Title, Date, Point of Contact Name, E-Mail Address, Phone, and Address.

The title page does not count against page limit, however, the executive summary does.

The period of performance of the contract resulting from this Call for Solutions should generally be no greater than five (5) years.

Technical data with military application may require approval, authorization, or license for lawful exportation.

All solution briefs, presentations, and proposals must be Unclassified. Do NOT mark any documents as “CONFIDENTIAL”. Solution briefs, presentations, and proposals containing data that is not to be disclosed to the public for any purpose or use by the government except for evaluation purposes shall include the following general disclaimer on the cover page:

“This [select one: solution brief, Presentation, or Proposal] includes data that shall not be disclosed outside the government, except to non-government personnel for evaluation purposes, and shall not be duplicated, used, or disclosed - in whole or in part - for any purpose other than to evaluate this submission. If, however, an agreement is awarded to this company as a result of - or in connection with - the submission of this data, the government shall have the right to duplicate, use, or disclose the data to the extent agreed upon by both parties in the resulting agreement. This restriction does not limit the government's right to use information contained in this data if it is obtained from another source without restriction. The data subject to this restriction are contained in sheets [insert numbers or other identification of sheets]” 

Submissions must be submitted electronically.

Offerors that are not chosen for the presentation phase will be notified in writing as soon as practicable. Further verbal feedback may be provided, upon request, at the Contracting/Agreements Officer’s discretion.

Phase 1: Solution Brief Evaluation

The Government will conduct an initial down select based on solution briefs submitted in Phase 0. Upon review of a solution brief, the Government may elect to invite “all, some or none” of the proposed solutions into Phase 2, the presentation/pitch based on the merits of the solution brief. In Phase 2, companies are invited to pitch and further discuss their proposed concept/technology/solution in person or virtually. During Phase 2, the Government may request and/or provide additional information to the company.

Solution Briefs will be evaluated on the following criteria:

Technical merit of the proposed solution, including the extent to which the proposed solution is unique, and/or innovative to fulfill the requirement for the A-COP. Technical Merit is defined as having direct relevance to the stated requirement, addressing identified capability gaps, and providing innovative technological advancements. 

The government may elect to use external market research in the evaluation of a company’s viability.

Phase 2: Solution Presentation/Pitch

Down selected offerors will be invited to present their solutions to the Government and to participate in a live demonstration. The presentation shall include:

Detailed technical and business viability of the solution

Proposed schedule and milestones

Anticipated data rights assertions

Explanation of Data Rights

Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) pricing: Estimated cost and payment terms.

7.2.		Participation in the live demonstration in a relevant environment will be coordinated by the Government.

Phase 2: Presentation/Pitch Evaluation

Individual presentations/pitches will be evaluated against the evaluation criteria below and not against any other presentations/pitches. Presentation/pitch submissions will be valid for 120 days after pitch evaluation. The government will aim to complete evaluation of presentation/pitches within 30 calendar days of the presentation/pitch. After completing the evaluation of presentation/pitch submissions, the government will notify the company that: they may submit a Full Proposal for evaluation in Phase 3; or their proposed concept/technology/solution is not of continued interest to the Government, and they will not be required to submit a Full Proposal and advance to Phase 3. 

Presentation/Pitch evaluation criteria are listed in order of importance from top to bottom. Presentation/pitches shall be evaluated/scored on the following factors:

Level of relevancy of the solution in addressing the A-COP with a commercially available product and/or process;

The technical merit of the proposed solution adequately addressed the A-COP and demonstrated feasibility for the Government to pursue the proposed solution;

Level of uniqueness, and/or innovative approach to solve the Government’s need;

Level of technical risk/maturity;

Level of risk placed with the proposed ROM;

Level of risk in the proposed milestone schedule and its ability to meet the A-COP requirement within a relevant time period;

Level of risk in the company’s viability and business solution; and

Level of potential risk in anticipated IP and data rights assertions

 Phase 3: Full Proposal

Based upon the results of market research, Phase 1 and/or Phase 2 evaluation(s) above, the government may request a proposal. If that occurs, a company, or companies will be invited to develop and submit a written proposal as well as negotiate appropriate terms and conditions, as applicable, governing the requirement. At this stage, the selected companies may discuss proposal development details during the proposal writing process with their assigned government expert(s) or government teaming partner(s).

Additionally, companies are invited to provide their own internal terms and conditions that may be consolidated with those of the government. This includes, but is not limited to, Service License Agreements (SLA) and/or User License Agreements (ULA).

Companies should note that there are certain terms and conditions the government may be unable to accept. However, projects awarded through the CSO may provide flexibility to adopt customary industry standards where it is otherwise legal and meets the government’s general public responsibility.

Offerors advancing to this phase will submit a detailed proposal, including:

Technical Volume: The technical volume shall include a detailed work plan indicating how each aspect of the objectives is to be accomplished. The technical volume should be in as much detail as the offeror considers necessary to fully explain its proposed technical approach or method, including all assumptions utilized to develop its proposed solution and associated costs. The technical volume should reflect a clear understanding of the nature of the work being undertaken. The technical volume must include information on how the project will be organized, staffed, and managed. Information should be provided that demonstrates Offeror’s understanding and management of important events or tasks. The technical volume must include a list of suggested deliverables and deliverable dates.

NOTE: The government reserves the right to further define the required technical proposal content based upon the specific contract requirements for the A-COP.

Price Volume: Detailed cost breakdown and justification. The government reserves the right to request any other price data or supporting cost information the government deems necessary to determine the total overall price is fair and reasonable. This can include but is not limited to commercial price catalog(s), previous commercial sales receipts, and/or other proprietary information to help the government determine reasonableness and future budgetary cost estimates. The Government reserves the right to further define the required price proposal content based upon the relevant requirements of the proposed solution.

Payment Milestones: In-Depth timeline/schedule to include parts lead time, build phase, and fielding. 

Additional Proposal Submission Content:

Small Business Subcontracting Plan: Large business Offerors shall submit either an individual subcontracting plan and/or master subcontracting plan (if available) in accordance with FAR 52.219-9 Small Business Subcontracting Plan (Sep 2023), DFARS 252.

GENERAL INFORMATION

DESCRIPTION

Pre‑Solicitation Notice – Notice of Intent to Award a Sole Source Contract

This is not a solicitation.

The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) intends to negotiate a sole source, firm‑fixed‑price purchase order for a one‑year period with:

University of South Florida

4202 E Fowler Ave

Tampa, FL 33620

The purpose of this requirement is to obtain specialized research support for the VA Ann Arbor Health Care System Research Department. The University of South Florida will provide analysis of plasma samples for eicosanoid quantification, including prostaglandins, leukotrienes, and specialized pro‑resolving mediators (resolvins, protectins, and maresins). Services will also include:

Comprehensive lipidomic data reports with eicosanoid and SPM quantification, pathway analysis and interpretive summaries.

Expertise in data interpretation and integration of lipidomic findings with clinical and mechanistic outcomes.

Contributions to manuscripts, grant progress reports, and presentations requiring lipidomic expertise and data integration.

The University of South Florida is uniquely positioned to meet these needs due to its established collaboration with the Ann Arbor VA and its specialized expertise in lipidomic analysis. Awarding this requirement to another vendor would result in substantial duplication of cost and unacceptable delays to critical VA research efforts.

Due to the fact that the University of South Florida has the unique specialize expertise in the current on-going research studies and the advanced lipidomic analysis, the University of South Florida is the only center capable of this high-level lipidomic analysis. Since the intent is to procure this requirement on a sole source basis, no solicitation will be posted on SAM.gov Contract Opportunities.

The applicable NAICS code is 541715 (Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences, except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology), with a 1,000‑employee size standard. The Product Service Code (PSC) is AN41. The authority for this action is FAR 6.302‑1, Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements.

Interested parties may submit inquiries regarding this notice by email only to:

Ann Marie Stewart

Contracting Officer

Email: annmarie.stewart@va.gov

The VA will consider all responses received; however, the decision to conduct a competitive procurement based on responses to this notice is solely at the discretion of the Contracting Officer.

PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT (PWS) 

Program Analysis and Administrative Support Services

COMNAVSURFPAC INSPECTOR GENERAL

1.  General:  This is a non-personal services contract to provide Program Analysis, Administrative Support Services, and Logistic Support to Commander, Naval Surface Force, U.S. Pacific Fleet (COMNAVSURFPAC) Inspector General. The Government shall not exercise any supervision or control over the contract service providers performing the services herein.  Such contract service providers shall be accountable solely to the Contractor who, in turn is responsible to the Government. 

1.1  Description of Services/Introduction:  The contractor shall provide all personnel necessary to perform Program Analysis, Administrative Support Services, and Logistic Support to COMNAVSURFPAC Inspector General as defined in this Performance Work Statement except for those items specified as government furnished property and services.  The contractor shall perform to the standards in this contract.

1.2 Background:  COMNAVSURFPAC Inspector General Office is responsible for the  inspections, investigations, reviews, audits and inquiries into any and all matters of interest to COMNAVSURFPAC to include such matters as effectiveness, efficiency, economy; personnel discipline, morale and welfare; management practices, command relationships, Management Internal Controls, Command Evaluations, and organizational structures for Commander Naval Surface Forces, U.S. Pacific Fleet - Code N01IG, Naval Amphibious Base, Coronado, CA.  

1.3 Objectives:  The contractor shall provide services and functions described herein to assure effective and efficient operation of the CNSP Inspector General’s office.  

1.4 Scope:  COMNAVSURFPAC IG requires program Management, administrative support, and logistic support services.  Services include: 

The contractor shall provide program management support to the Inspector General’s Office related to investigations, audits/assessments/reviews, and command evaluations.

The contractor shall provide daily administrative support to the Inspector General’s Office including receiving and screening incoming correspondence/calls; and formatting and distributing correspondence.

The contractor shall provide daily logistic support to the Inspector General’s Office including contacting witnesses, arranging meetings, facilitating visits, scheduling inspections, and maintaining files

Period of Performance:  The period of performance shall be for one Base year and one Option year of 12 months each. The Period of Performance reads as follows:

Base Year:  9 June 2026 – 8 June 2027

Option Year 1:  9 June 2027 – 8 June 2028

1.6 General Information

1.6.1 Quality Control The contractor shall develop and maintain an effective Quality Control Program (QCP) to ensure services are performed in accordance with this PWS.  The contractor shall develop and implement procedures to identify, prevent, and ensure non-recurrence of defective services.  The contractor’s QCP is the means by which he assures himself that his work complies with the requirement of the contract. The QCP is to be delivered within 5 days after contract award. After acceptance of the QCP the contractor shall receive the contracting officer’s acceptance in writing of any proposed change to his Quality Control system.  

1.6.2 Quality Assurance:  The government shall evaluate the contractor’s performance under this contract in accordance with the Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan.  This plan is primarily focused on what the Government must do to ensure that the contractor has performed in accordance with the performance standards.  It defines how the performance standards will be applied, the frequency of surveillance, and the minimum acceptable defect rate(s).       

1.6.3  Hours of Operation:  The contractor is responsible for conducting business, between the hours of 0630-1630 Monday thru Friday except Federal holidays (mentioned below) or when the Government facility is closed due to local or national emergencies, administrative closings, or similar Government directed facility closings.  The exception to the hours of availability must be approved by the Inspector General. The Contractor must at all times maintain an adequate workforce for the uninterrupted performance of all tasks defined within this PWS when the Government facility is not closed for the above reasons.  When hiring personnel, the Contractor shall keep in mind that the stability and continuity of the workforce are essential.    

New Year’s Day					Labor Day

Martin Luther King Jr.’s Birthday			Columbus Day

President’s Day					Veteran’s Day

Memorial Day					Thanksgiving Day

Juneteenth					Christmas Day

Independence Day				

1.6.4 Place of Performance:  The work to be performed under this contract will be performed at COMNAVSURFPAC Bldg 11, Room 105, 2841 Rendova Road, Naval Base Coronado, San Diego, CA 92155.  

1.6.5   Type of Contract:  The government will award a Firm Fixed Price Order.  

1.6.6   Security Requirements:  Contractor personnel performing work under this contract must have a Secret Clearance and NIGHTS user ID at time of the proposal submission, and must maintain the level of security required for the life of the contract.  The security requirements are in accordance with the attached DD 254 

1.6.7 PHYSICAL Security:  The contractor shall be responsible for safeguarding all government equipment, information and property provided for contractor use. At the close of each work period, government facilities, equipment, and materials shall be secured.

1.6.8  Post Award Conference/Periodic Progress Meetings:  The Contractor agrees to attend any post award conference convened by the contracting activity or contract administration office in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation Subpart 42.5. The contracting officer, Contracting Officers Representative (COR), and other Government personnel, as appropriate, may meet periodically with the contractor to review the contractor's performance.  At these meetings the contracting officer will apprise the contractor of how the government views the contractor's performance and the contractor will apprise the Government of problems, if any, being experienced.  Appropriate action shall be taken to resolve outstanding issues.  These meetings shall be at no additional cost to the government.  

1.6.9  Contracting Officer Representative (COR):  The (COR) will be identified by separate letter.  The COR monitors all technical aspects of the contract and assists in contract administration The COR is authorized to perform the following functions: assure that the Contractor performs the technical requirements of the contract: perform inspections necessary in connection with contract performance: maintain written and oral communications with the Contractor concerning technical aspects of the contract: issue written interpretations of technical requirements, including Government drawings, designs, specifications: monitor Contractor's performance and notifies both the Contracting Officer and Contractor of any deficiencies; coordinate availability of government furnished property, and provide site entry of Contractor personnel.  A letter of designation issued to the COR, a copy of which is sent to the Contractor, states the responsibilities and limitations of the COR, especially with regard to changes in cost or price, estimates or changes in delivery dates.  The COR is not authorized to change any of the terms and conditions of the resulting order. 

1.6.10  Key Personnel:  The following personnel are considered key personnel by the government:  Navy Inspector General Hotline Tracking System Program (NIGHTS) Manager and Audit Assessment Coordinator. This person must be an expert on the use and procedures of the NIGHTS data base as well as the format and terminology from day one. 

  

1.6.11  Identification of Contractor Employees:   All contract personnel attending meetings, answering Government telephones, and working in other situations where their contractor status is not obvious to third parties are required to identify themselves as such to avoid creating an impression in the minds of members of the public that they are Government officials.  They must also ensure that all documents or reports produced by contractors are suitably marked as contractor products or that contractor participation is appropriately disclosed. 

1.6.12  Organizational Conflict of Interest:  Contractor and subcontractor personnel performing work under this contract shall sign a ‘Non-Disclosure Agreement’ in accordance with Organizational Conflict of Interest Clause. These personnel may be removed from the worksite if the Inspector General determines, in his sole discretion, that the contractor employee has compromised or otherwise exploited Personal Identifying Information (PII), or has released any investigation, audit, inspection, or related information without the express permission of the Inspector General.  

2.  Definitions and Acronyms:

2.1.  DEFINITIONS:  

2.1.1.  CONTRACTOR.  A supplier or vendor awarded a contract to provide specific supplies or service to the government.  The term used in this contract refers to the prime.

2.1.2.  CONTRACTING OFFICER.   A person with authority to enter into, administer, and or terminate contracts, and make related determinations and findings on behalf of the government.  Note: The only individual who can legally bind the government.

2.1.3.  CONTRACTING OFFICER'S REPRESENTATIVE (COR).   An employee of the U.S. Government appointed by the contracting officer to administer the contract.  Such appointment shall be in writing and shall state the scope of authority and limitations.  This individual has authority to provide technical direction to the Contractor as long as that direction is within the scope of the contract, does not constitute a change, and has no funding implications.  This individual does NOT have authority to change the terms and conditions of the contract. 

2.1.4.  DEFECTIVE SERVICE.  A service output that does not meet the standard of performance associated with the Performance Work Statement.

2.1.5.  DELIVERABLE.  Anything that can be physically delivered, but may include non-manufactured things such as meeting minutes or reports.

2.1.6.  KEY PERSONNEL.  Contractor personnel that are evaluated in a source selection process and that may be required to be used in the performance of a contract by the Key Personnel listed in the PWS.  When key personnel are used as an evaluation factor in best value procurement, an offer can be rejected if it does not have a firm commitment from the persons that are listed in the proposal.

2.1.7.  PHYSICAL SECURITY.  Actions that prevent the loss or damage of Government property.

2.1.8.  QUALITY ASSURANCE.  The government procedures to verify that services being performed by the Contractor are performed according to acceptable standards.

2.1.9.  QUALITY ASSURANCE Surveillance Plan (QASP).  An organized written document specifying the surveillance methodology to be used for surveillance of contractor performance.  

2.1.10.  QUALITY CONTROL.  All necessary measures taken by the Contractor to assure that the quality of an end product or service shall meet contract requirements.

2.1.11.  SUBCONTRACTOR.  One that enters into a contract with a prime contractor.  The Government does not have privity of contract with the subcontractor.

2.1.12.  WORK DAY.  The number of hours per day the Contractor provides services in accordance with the contract.

2.1.12.  WORK WEEK.  Monday through Friday, unless specified otherwise.

NOTICE OF INTENT – BRAND-NAME 
Solicitation Number: PR15893854 
 
 
This is not a solicitation; this is a NOTICE OF INTENT to award a brand-name procurement action as 
follows: 
 
The Bureau of International Narcotics and Law Enforcement (INL) at the U.S. Embassy in Bogotá -
Colombia intends to award a firm fixed-price purchase order for the supply of Financial Investigation 
Software Licenses. For this requirement, ALTIA SOFTWARE LICENSES is considered the only 
brand, and no other supplies or services will accomplish Embassy Bogota requirements. 
 
A brand name restriction is required for this software procurement due to integration and compatibility 
issues with the software currently in use by the Colombian National Police (CNP)  and to meet 
operational requirements. CNP investigators are trained exclusively with Altia software, and it is the 
only brand authorized for use by the CNP as part of their financial crime investigations. 
 
Product Service Code: 7A21, IT and Telecom - Business Application Software. 
NAICS code: 541511, Custom Computer Programming Services. 
 
This procurement action is being conducted in accordance with the statutory authority of FAR Part 
6.103-1, which states that only one brand-name and no other will satisfy Embassy Bogota requirements.  
 
Any interested party that believes it can meet the requirements described herein may identify 
themselves and must provide evidence of their capability to fulfill the requirement.  
 
Responses must be submitted in writing to contact Javier F. Lopez at LopezJF@state.gov and must 
be received no later than April 4, 2026, at 16:00 hours (Bogota, Colombia) time. 
 
 
Sincerely, 
 
Chantale Breton 
Contracting Officer, INL Bogota

TAX RELIEF PROCEDURES 
 
(a) General. This clause supplements FAR 52.229-6, Taxes – Foreign Fixed-Price Contracts (Reference 
29.402-1(a)). The prices set forth in this contract are exclusive of all taxes and duties from which the 
U.S. Government is exempt by virtue of agreement between the U.S. Government and the Government

(b)(1) Procedures. The Contractor shall follow the procedures in paragraph (c) of this clause regarding 
tax relief as provided in the agreement between the U. S. Government and Colombia. The diplomatic tax 
privilege belongs to the U.S. Government and applies to taxes and duties payable to Colombia that are 
directly attributable to contract costs identified in paragraph (c) as subject to exemption, e.g., taxes or 
duties levied by Colombia on labor and materials that are applied to or utilized in perfor mance of this 
contract. 
(2) The procedures in paragraph (c) are based on the current local tax relief agreement between the US 
Government and Colombia and are subject to change. 
 
(c) The following procedures are included in, or are derived from, the agreement negotiated with 
Colombia and are hereby incorporated into this clause: 
 
“Any quotation, invoice or bill to be submitted to the USG/INL Colombia for payment of cost incurred 
under this contract should reflect zero value concerning VAT or IVA (Impuesto a las Ventas). Upon 
contract award, the Office of INL Bogota will issue an ex emption letter (Exención de Impuesto) to the 
awardee to be presented to the Government of Colombia for any claim that may arise during the 
performance of this contract. The awardee, not the USG will coordinate directly with the Government 
of Colombia on any VAT or IVA matter under this contract”. 
 
(d) Remedies. The Government may impose the following remedies in the event the Contractor fails to 
follow the procedures outlined in paragraph (c) of this clause. These actions are in addition to any other 
remedies available to the Government: 
(1) The Contracting Officer may suspend contract payments in accordance with the procedures at FAR 
32.503-6(a)(1). 
(2) The Contracting Officer may terminate the contract for default in accordance with the procedures at 
FAR Subpart 49.4.
