Request for Information (RFI) 

Automated Pharmacy Prescription Dispensing Kiosks – Department of Veterans Affairs 

TAC RFI Number: 36C10B26Q0129

Purpose:

The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) is seeking industry feedback to inform planning, acquisition strategy, and solution design for a secure, automated, pharmacy prescription dispensing kiosk that enables Veterans to receive medications prescribed by a licensed provider through a pharmacist-verified dispensing workflow to improve timely access to medications while maintaining full regulatory compliance and patient safety. This Request for Information (RFI) seeks responses from Vendors interested in supporting an initial pilot implementation, with the potential to expand to a full-scale deployment, and demonstrating the ability to deliver a unified solution that supports ongoing operations, maintenance, and enterprise-wide adoption of the product.

This RFI is issued for information and planning purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation nor does it restrict the Government as to the ultimate acquisition approach. In accordance with (IAW) Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 15.101(c), responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. The purpose of this RFI is to obtain market information on capable sources of supply, industry practices, and input specific to the information provided. The Government is not responsible for any cost incurred by industry in furnishing this information. All costs associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the interested party’s expense. Not responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future Request for Proposals, if any is issued. Any information submitted by respondents to this RFI is strictly voluntary. All submissions become Government property and will not be returned. Any proprietary/sensitive information must be clearly marked by the vendor. 

Background:

VA pharmacies are a key resource for Veterans, family members, caregivers, and survivors, and are often required to support overall Veteran care. The VA currently delivers pharmacy services through a combination of medical center pharmacies, outpatient clinics, mail order fulfilment, and community partners (i.e. Community Care Networks).

To improve timely access to medications and enhance the Veteran experience, the VA plans to pilot and deploy automated pharmacy prescription dispensing kiosk(s) as part of a more unified and modernized pharmacy service delivery model. This effort seeks to expand secure, pharmacist-verified dispensing capabilities in strategic locations (to be determined), leveraging standardized technology workflows, and inventory management practices. The goal is to improve convenience and continuity of care through the automated system, reduce wait times and operational burden, support secure after-hours access in centralized locations including rural communities, and deliver safe, accurate, and consistent pharmacy services for Veterans. 

Performance Objectives:

Improve Veteran Access to Medications

Enable timely, convenient access to specific non-controlled, non-hazardous prescriptions that a patient may need to start right away, such as antibiotics or urgent short-term treatments, all available through a kiosk. 

Potential to support a feature that allows Veterans access to a pharmacist in real time.

Vendor must have a plan for potential positioning of their solution outdoors and potentially separate from the point of care provided (state laws do not prohibit such positioning) to enable 24/7 access by Veterans. 

Solution must have the capability to integrate (via Application Programming Interface) with VA’s Federal Electronic Health Record (Oracle Health) and existing Veterans Health Information Systems and Technology Architecture (VistA) electronic health record system.

Vendor must provide 24-hour support to resolve information technology issues.

Support Verified Provider Prescriptions

Accept and process prescriptions from any licensed and authorized prescriber for all Veterans verified within VA systems.

Ensure all prescriptions undergo appropriate pharmacist review and verification prior to dispensing.

Ensure Patient Safety, Accuracy, and Authentication

Maintain a high standard of dispensing accuracy.

Provide pharmacist oversight to ensure appropriate dosage of medications are stocked within the automated system. 

Ensure proper replenishment of medications is available and completed promptly. 

Verify patient identity using secure, reliable authentication methods to ensure medications are dispensed only to authorized recipients.

Maintain Regulatory and Policy Compliance 

Comply with all applicable federal, state, and local pharmacy laws, VA policies, and cybersecurity and privacy requirements, including Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act and VA information security standards.

Support Data Visibility and Reporting

Provide accurate and timely reporting on utilization, inventory, and system uptime.

Support Organizational Change Management

Assist with communication, training, and deployment planning across the VA network.

Help advertise the existence among local Veteran populations.

Requested Information:

Vendors are encouraged to provide the following:

A brief capability statement, including relevant experience. Please do not include generic marketing materials.

Footprint of the device.

Specific requirements for operation (power, connectivity, etc.).

Recommended approach to achieving full scalability VA-wide utilizing the above objectives, including:

Operational Plan detailing a unified enterprise-ready solution.

Proposed approach to adhere to varying state mandates and approach to obtain waivers, if necessary. 

Proposed approach to integrating solution with VA’s Federal Electronic Health Record (Oracle Health solution) and VistA electronic health record system.

Proposed approach for monitoring and maintenance to include software updates and mechanical repair.

Examples of automated pharmacy prescription or other medical dispensing kiosk deployment.

Proposed approach to providing remote pharmacist access.

Describe system operations and maintenance, to include:

Overall inventory capacity as well as inventory at the unit-dose and bottle level, including real time counts. 

Describe how the system manages lot numbers, expiration dates, and recalls.

Proposed approach to maintaining appropriate inventory.

Proposed approach to Veteran verification, to include:

Describe security controls to prevent unauthorized access, theft, or removal of medication without a verified prescription. 

Key risks and mitigations VA should consider

High-level cost and schedule considerations

Innovative ideas or technologies VA should explore 

Other considerations the VA should consider regarding implementation of a pilot program to full scale deployment.

Submittal Information:

This is a RFI only. It is requested that all companies interested in participating in this effort note their interest and provide an indication of their respective capabilities to perform the effort described above. Marketing material will not be accepted as an indication of capability. The vendor must display that their solution is tested and has been successfully implemented in a healthcare setting. Only responses related to the Government’s requirements as listed above will be considered. 

Provide the following information on the first page/slide of the submission:

Name of Company

Address

Point(s) of Contact

Company Business Size and Status

NAICS code(s) – If applicable, identify your company’s Small Business size status based upon the applicable NAICS code of 541512. For more information refer to http://www.sba.gov/.

Socioeconomic data

Data Universal Numbering System (DUNS) Number

The vendor shall submit their response no later than February 2, 2026 at 12 PM ET.  Submissions should not exceed 15 pages. Questions shall be submitted no later than January 21, 2026 5 PM ET. Responses and questions are to be sent via email to Andrea Caltabilota at Andrea.Caltabilota@va.gov, Nicole Bestreski at Nicole.Bestreski@va.gov, and Robert Kirzow at Robert.Kirzow@va.gov. Please include " Automated Pharmacy Prescription Dispensing Kiosks " in the subject line of your response. Mark your response as "Proprietary Information" if the information is considered business sensitive. 

NO MARKETING MATERIALS ARE ALLOWED AS PART OF THIS RFI.

The Government will only review what is being requested under the “Submittal Information” section of this RFI. The Government will not review any other information or attachments included that exceed this limit.

THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR 
PROPOSAL. THERE WILL NOT BE A SOLICITATION, SPECIFICATIONS, OR 
DRAWINGS AVAILABLE AT THIS TIME. 
The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Baltim ore District (NAB) seeks to determine the 
interest, availability, and capability of potential sources to satisfy an upcoming requirement . The 
requirement is for the operation and m aintenance (O&M) of HURREVAC managed by the 
FEMA/USACE National Hurricane Program. HURREVAC stands for Hurricane Evacuation and 
is a restricted -use computer program funded by FEMA and USACE for use by government 
emergency managers to track hurricanes, support evacuation decision making, and provide data 
and information to support hurricane emergency management planning and operations. In addition, 
the Real Time Evacuation Planning Model (RtePM) is hosted on the same cloud server used to 
host HURREVAC. RtePM is a restricted-use, web-based transportation model designed to capture 
the impacts of traffic flow along a regional roadway network and calculate hurricane evacuation 
clearance time. 
By way of this Market Survey/Sources Sought Notice, the NAB intends to determine the extent of 
capable firms that are engaged in providing the services described hereunder.  Responses to this 
Sources Sought announcement will be used by the Government to make appropriate acquisition 
decisions.  
Responses to this Notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the U.S. Government to form a 
binding contract. It is the responsibility of the interested vendors to monitor this site for 
additional information pertaining to this notice and any subsequent amendments. All submissions 
become government property and will not be returned. Any solicitation issued as a result of this 
notice will be in a separate announcement. 
PROJECT DESCRIPTION 
USACE-NAB has been tasked to solicit for and award the operation and maintenance of 
HURREVAC from date of award to 12 months from date of award. HURREVAC is a  real-time 
data analysis tool allows state and local emergency management officials to make prudent and 
informed decisions based on information developed during the FEMA Hurricane Evacuation 
Studies process and real -time forecast data distributed by the Na tional Weather Service (NWS) 
and the National Hurricane Center  (NHC)/Tropical Analysis and Forecast Branch  (TAFB). 
HURREVAC has over 36,000 registered users at all levels of government and serves as the primary 
evacuation decision assistance tool for emergency managers threatened by tropical systems. 
The proposed project will be a competitive, firm-fixed-price services contract. 
This primary purpose of this project consists of the following: 
• Maintain continual verification and monitoring of data sources and feeds. The nature of 
real-time data and the often rapidly changing dissemination techniques, formats and 
accessibility are such that the sources of specific data may need to be modified over 
time. Examples include, and are not limited to, real-time hurricane advisory files from 
the National Hurricane Center, the Central Pacific Hurricane Center, the Joint Typhoon 

Warning Center, Wind and Storm Surge Probability and Hindcast data from the 
National Hurricane Center, and rainfall/river flood data from the National Weather 
Service. Other pertinent and relevant publicly available data sources may be identified 
for future inclusion as they come available. 
• Monitor system performance through the contractor-built monitoring system. The 
system goal for uptime during hurricane season is 99% with a recovery buffer of five 
(5) minutes. When downtime occurs, the requirement is to document the issues, 
resolutions, and recovery buffer times and submit to USACE and FEMA. 
• Update database files, including hurricane tracking error values, hurricane evacuation 
study data, evacuation zones and clearance time data, forecast and storm surge products, 
and other National Hurricane Program products. 
• Operate and maintain user base and authentication and provide user technical support. 
This includes the following requirements: 
o Adding new user system access to HURREVAC and/or RtePM at 
specified authorization levels based on USACE and FEMA approval and 
guidance. 
o During active tropical systems that are a threat to the United States and its 
Territories (within 120 hours of a potential impact), staff a 24-hour 
technical support system that will respond to technical assistance requests 
submitted by users via email, phone, or through the system itself within 
one hour. 
• Maintain primary and secondary backup personnel during the contract period that have 
full working knowledge of the program coding, data feed coding, and overall system 
support and maintenance. The intent of this work item is to provide redundancy to 
ensure the program is always available and working correctly for users. 
• Maintain database hosting capabilities for the transportation model, RtePM, which is a 
tool that may be used in hurricane evacuation studies to determine evacuation clearance 
times. 
• Coordinate with USACE and FEMA to resolve all major problems, issues, concerns, or 
modifications and/or improvements, and document actions taken. 
 
The purpose of this notice is to gain knowledge of interest, capabilities, and qualifications of 
various members of industry, to include the Small Business Community: Small Business (SB), 
Section 8(a), Historically Underutilized Business Zones (HUBZone), S ervice-Disabled Veteran-
Owned Small Business (SDVOSB), and Women- Owned Small Business (WOSB). The 
Government must ensure there is adequate competition within any given socioeconomic category 
of responsible contractors. Large businesses are not prohibited from submitting a response to this 
notice; however, SB, Section 8(a), HUBZone, SDVOSB, and WOSB businesses are highly 
encouraged to participate. 
North American Industry Classification System code for this procurement is 541519
 Other 
Computer Related Services which has a small business size standard of $34,000,000.00. 
Vendors should address ALL of the following information in their submittal:  
1. Company name, address, point of contact, phone number, e-mail address, CAGE code, and UEI 
number. Indicate if your company is currently registered with the Systems for Award Management 
(SAM) database. If not, indicate if it has been registered in the past or intends to register.  

2. In consideration of NAICS code 541519, interested qualified Large Businesses (LB), Small 
Business (SB), Small Disadvantaged Business (SDB), Service-Disabled Veteran Owned SB 
(SDVOSB), Veteran-Owned Small Business (VOSB), Historically Underutilized Business Zones 
(HUBZones), or Qualified Section 8(a) certified firms. 
  
3. Indicate if your company is currently prohibited from doing business with the Federal 
Government. Yes/No. (If yes, explain).  
4. Indicate the primary nature of your business. Narratives shall be no longer than three (3) pages 
demonstrating experience in the type of work required. 
 
5. Provide a concise narrative with at least two (2) but no more than three (3) relevant projects 
with similar requirements described above within the past ten (10) years. The capabilities 
statement shall include the following: 
a. A brief description of the project  
b. Customer name  
c. Timeliness of performance  
d. Customer satisfaction  
e. Dollar value of the project 
 
Narratives shall be no longer than ten (10) pages in one .pdf file. Double sided pages will count as 
two (2) separate pages. Comments will be shared with the Government, but otherwise will be held 
in strict confidence. 
SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS: 
THIS NOTICE IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL, QUOTE OR BID. It is a market research 
tool being utilized to determine the availability of potential qualified contractors before 
determining the method of acquisition. In addition, this source sought is not to be considered as a 
commitment by the Government, nor will the Government pay for any information solicited or 
delivered. 
Interested parties who consider themselves qualified to perform the above-listed requirement are 
invited to submit a response to this Sources Sought Notice no later than (NLT) Wednesday, 28 
January 2026 at 11:00 A.M. Eastern Standard Time (EST). All responses under this Sources 
Sought Notice must be emailed referencing the sources sought notice number 
W912DR26X1B3C.  
Telephone inquiries will not be accepted or acknowledged, and no feedback or analysis will be 
provided to companies regarding their submissions. If you have any questions concerning this 
opportunity please contact, Sharon.Alexander@usace.army.mil
  or Angela Padua, email:  
Angela.S.Padua@usace.army.mil  
** Please note vendors not registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) database 
prior to award of contracts will not be eligible for award. Vendors must all be registered in SAM 
under the applicable NAICS code (541519) as indicated in the advertised RFP to be considered 
for award. Vendors may register for SAM online at www.sam.gov or by calling 1.866.606.8220.

Hyperlinks

The Offeror shall not use hyperlinks in proposal volumes. 

Virus Free Electronic Submission

The Offeror is responsible for ensuring that its electronic proposal is virus free. The Offeror shall certify, in its proposal cover letter, that all electronic proposal information delivered throughout the evaluation (e.g., original proposal submission, responses to evaluation notices, Final Proposal Revisions) are virus free. The Offeror shall specify the software, version, and virus definition used to check the data

Multimedia

In order to reduce file sizes, the Offeror shall not embed sound or video (e.g., MPEG) files within the proposal submission. The Offeror is encouraged to simplify the color palette used in creating figures; and minimize size of graphics files; and avoid scanned images. 

File Naming Conventions

Valid extensions for files using their associated applications follow: 

The Offeror shall follow the basic structure of the file naming convention in Table G-1 (Offeror Electronic File Naming Convention) for electronic file submissions (e.g., proposal volumes, attachments, appendices), where “#” represents the sequential numbering of files.  Offeror’s shall keep file names short (i.e., under 40 characters) so that the files are accessible on Government share drives.  Files with longer names often become corrupt or inaccessible.

The Offeror should provide one folder for each volume or annex, containing all electronic files requested within the volume or annex. Please submit each volume, or annex as one file if possible. Offerors should not provide each section/paragraph as separate files.

Contractor to reperform the services or redeliver the goods in conformity with the requirements of the Award, at no
additional increase in total contract amount.  When the services to be performed are of such a nature that the defect
cannot be corrected by reperformance of the services, the FDIC shall have the right to (1) require Contractor
immediately to take all necessary steps to ensure future performance of the services in conformity with the
requirements of the contract; and (2) reduce the contract price to reflect the reduced value of the services
performed.  In the event Contractor fails promptly to reperform the services or redeliver the goods, or to take
necessary steps to ensure future performance of the services or delivery of the goods in conformity with the
requirements of the Award, the FDIC shall have the right to either (1) by contract or otherwise, have the services
performed or the goods delivered in conformity with the contract requirements and charge to Contractor any cost
occasioned to the FDIC that is directly related to the performance of such services or the delivery of such goods; or
(2) terminate this Award for default as provided in 7.6.6-02, Termination for Default.
 
(c) Contractor shall provide and maintain an inspection system acceptable to the FDIC covering the goods or
services to be delivered or performed hereunder.  Records of all inspection work by Contractor shall be kept

agent, the FDIC would make payments by other than EFT.

TSA PRE-SOLICITATION NOTIFICATION

The Transportation Security Administration (TSA), a component of the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), is responsible for protecting our Nation’s transportation systems to ensure freedom of movement for people and commerce. These statutory responsibilities encompass providing the most effective transportation security in the most efficient way possible as a high-performing counterterrorism organization. To enhance mission performance and achieve its shared goals, TSA is committed to promoting a culture founded on integrity, innovation, and team spirit.

In support of TSA’s mission, the Information Technology (IT) office provides world-class information technology services. Field Operations & CUstomer Support (FOCUS) will establish a new Task Order to provide the TSA enterprise-wide Single Point of Contact Information Technology help desk and headquarters/field Information Technology Specialist support.

Purpose

TSA is announcing the intention to make available to interested GSA Multiple Award Schedule (GSA MAS) vendors a Virtual Reading Room (VRR), which will contain documents pertinent to the upcoming solicitation for FOCUS. The VRR will likely contain Sensitive Security Information (SSI). Therefore, access to the VRR will be restricted to vendors and individuals that have been approved by TSA. The purpose of this notice is to announce the VRR and rules regarding access to the VRR.

Requirements Background and Overview

TSA’s IT infrastructure and engineering are currently supported by the IMPACT II task order. The IMPACT II task order provides the skill sets necessary to operate and maintain the TSA IT Enterprise to include supporting engineering and development. TSA determines all development and engineering included in the enterprise to support its end-users. The TSA IT Enterprise supports approximately 85,000 employees and contractors at various locations, including TSA Headquarters (HQ) currently located in Springfield, VA; approximately 440 airports and Federal Security Director (FSD) offices; international support sites; and numerous other mission critical centers and locations. Approximately 85 percent of TSA users consist of a combination of Transportation Security Officers (TSOs) and Federal Law Enforcement Officers (LEOs), while other TSA staff includes TSA HQ employe

Performance Work Statement (PWS) 
Enterprise Network and Information Security Enhancement (ENISE) 
1.   Background 
The Internal Revenue Service (IRS) administers America’s tax laws and collects the revenues 
that fund most government operations and public services.  The IRS and its employees represent 
the face of government to more U.S. citizens than any other agency. 
 
IRS provides services to millions of taxpayers to help them understand and meet their tax 
obligations.  We also deter people inclined to evade their responsibilities and vigorously pursue 
those who violate tax laws.  Service and enforcement are equally important priorities for the IRS. 
We are committed both to providing excellent service to taxpayers and enforcing America’s tax 
laws in a balanced manner. 
 
Beginning in mid-2006, the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) released several 
memorandums to address protecting the vast quantities of information managed by the 
Government. OMB’s Memorandum 06-16 speaks directly to the ability to manage Sensitive but 
Unclassified (SBU)/Personally Identifiable Information (PII) extracts for legitimate use, and 
OMB M-07-16 which emphasizes protection and management of SBU/PII as a federal 
requirement. 
2.   Objective  
 
The IRS has identified cloud technology as a key support enabler: hosting and managing big data 
and enabling IT operational excellence through use of complex applications and programs. 
Cloud computing will allow the IRS to efficiently manage, operate and run a very large-scale 
computing infrastructure that delivers the capacity, availability and performance that will permit 
nearly 90,000 end users to focus on mission accomplishment while accessing more than 500 
applications and programs. 
This effort supports the Cybersecurity Information Protection Enhancement Controls (CIPEC) 
program’s mission to enhance and standardize data protection controls across the enterprise, 
safeguarding sensitive taxpayer data, and ensuring the integrity and security of the IRS systems. 
2.1   Purpose 
Given the services provided to the Taxpayers of the United States of America, the volume and 
sensitivity of Taxpayer data (e.g., IRS Employee data, IRS Affiliate Organizational Entities - 
Public, Private or Non-profit) has grown exponentially.  Associated with this reality is the 
mission-critical need to protect this PII and SBU Information and guard against the increased 
occurrence of Enterprise Data (or Privacy) breaches and identity theft. 
 

  
 
2 
 
Privacy breach1 and identity theft are among the most prevalent and publicized cyber-crimes in 
the news today. According to the Open Security Foundation, which hosts “DataLossDB” a 
database which records unauthorized Personally Identifiable Information (PII) incidents.  
 
Despite increased awareness, data privacy legislation, federal guidance, as well as the 
implementation of Agency-specific policies and security awareness training programs to help 
guard against the unauthorized disclosure of and access to Agency SBU information and PII, the 
inadvertent disclosure of this data continues day to day by well-meaning and dedicated 
employees. 
2.2   Agency Mission  
Considering these trends over the past quarter of a century, the U.S. Department of the Treasury 
and the IRS recognized the need for the implementation of a comprehensive system to: 
 
 Accurately discover or prevent SBU/PII data leakage. 
 Maintain the confidentiality of SBU/PII being stored and used by the IRS. 
 Ensure public trust in conducting business with the IRS electronically (e.g., IRS 
Modernized eFile (MEF)system). 
 Prevent unauthorized disclosure of SBU/PII being stored and used by the IRS. 
 
As an element of the Treasury Department’s ongoing efforts to improvement its Cybersecurity 
program, the Office of the Chief Information Officer (CIO) provided additional controls, in its 
memorandum “TCIO-M-09-04”, related to the management of Treasury’s Cybersecurity 
environment. These new controls focus particularly on the storage of data on removable media 
and the unauthorized transmission of information outside the Department.  
3.   Scope of Work 
The purpose of the ENISE Project is to augment the IRS CIPEC Program’s DLP Technical team 
with experienced Cloud Technical, Federal Information Security Management Act (FISMA) 
Compliance, and Program support Subject Matter Experts (SMEs), who have successfully 
supported the implementation/integration of an “on prem” Enterprise DLP Commercial-Off-The-
Shelf (COTS) Solution within an Enterprise Agency’s Hybrid Cloud Ecosystem – primarily 
utilizing the COTS Cloud product offerings of Microsoft, Skyhigh, Broadcom, Palo Alto etc.  
 
The primary goal of this acquisition is to ensure the continued provision of trained and certified 
Information Technology (IT) professionals with extensive experience in developing and 
implementing Cloud Migration projects. This effort supports the CIPEC program’s mission to 
enhance and standardize data protection controls across the enterprise, safeguarding sensitive 
taxpayer data, and ensuring the integrity and security of the IRS systems. Additionally, the 
government seeks to future-proof its technical environment by integrating emerging technologies 
and solutions. It also aims to explore innovative mechanisms to incorporate artificial intelligence 
 
1 The term “breach” is also defined by OMB memoranda M-07-16,: “Safeguarding Against and Responding to the Breach 
of Personally Identifiable Information”, May 22, 2007, as: “For the purposes of this policy, the term “breach” is 
used to include the loss of control, compromise, unauthorized disclosure, unauthorized acquisition, unauthorized 
access, or any similar term referring to situations where persons other than authorized users and for an other than authorized 
purpose have access or potential access to personally identifiable information, whether physical or electronic.” 

  
 
3 
 
and machine learning (AI/ML) technologies to further enhance operational capabilities and 
efficiencies. 
 
The ENISE Project will be implemented as a multi-year multiple-release effort. Although the “on 
prem” and “Cloud” solutions are intended to be functionally equivalent, the Architecture, 
Infrastructure, Configuration, Security Compliance model and Implementation approach required 
for the successful implementation of the IRS DLP in the Cloud solution is to be fundamentally 
different.   
 
The IRS Business Units and IT organizations rely on the CIPEC to provide Subject Matter 
Expertise relating to the implementation and operational support of Broadcom, Inc’s, Symantec 
DLP Suite COTS solution and Cloud Computing, related to the specific solutions the IRS has 
already acquired and have implemented.  This requisite expertise that the DCM ENISE Project 
must continue to provide, is associated with related competencies including: solution 
architecture/engineering, requirements elicitation, project management techniques and 
approaches, cloud solution FISMA security & privacy compliance, Cloud DLP systems and 
database administration, data leakage event troubleshooting, solution DLP detection rule 
development, detection rule triggers & configurable exceptions, systems upgrade work for 
solutions of various vendors, event management and triaging workflow development, role based 
access management and control.  In addition to protecting the IRS from data exfiltration the 
ENISE project will also be configuring Palo Alto Cloud Hosted Security Stack to enhance the 
organizational network secure posture. To support the DCM ENISE project needs, while 
maintaining a cost-effective price structure, the PWS will include Firm Fixed Price (FFP) tasks.

3.1   Current Information Technology (IT)/Network Environment  
In 2013, the SPIIDE Project was initiated and the IRS Cybersecurity A&I’s DLP Program 
Management Office (PMO) was stood-up to execute the implementation of a Commercial-Off-
The-Shelf DLP solution.   
 
The IRS DLP solution was implemented in two separate software releases: 
 Release 1.0 focused on implementing the first of three Functional Uses Case components: 
Data-In-Motion (DIM).  The Data-In-Motion (DIM) component, implemented in the IRS 
Production Operational environment, monitors the presence unencrypted PII or SBU data 
in outbound email messages and posted to public-facing IRS Web Sites.  Using this IRS 
DLP COTS component, certain instances of unencrypted PII and SBU data is detected, 
their transmission outside of the IRS Network perimeter is blocked and the responsible 
IRS employee is notified by an auto-generated email response.   
 Release 2.0 focused on implementing the final two of three Functional Uses Case 
components: Data-At-Rest (DAR) and Data-In-Use (DIU).  Data-At-Rest (DAR) 
component specifically scans fileshares, SAN/NAS storage, SharePoint, Websites, 
Databases, etc. for files containing sensitive content (such as PII, PCI, HIPAA, etc.) 
and/or other content/context including age of the file, file types, encrypted files, etc. The 
deployment scope of the DIU component, via use of endpoint agents locally installed on 
enterprise workstations (Laptops) and on servers, monitors and responds to the presence 
of PII & SBU Data (currently configured as DLP policies). 
4.   Tasks 
Outlined in this PWS is a detailed description of the professional services that the selected 
Contractor shall provide to the ENISE Project, to support the continued instantiation of the IRS 
enterprise DLP solution in the emerging IRS Cloud ecosystem. This effort also includes the 
deployment and configuration of Palo Alto Next Gen Firewall (NGFW) technologies, as well as 
related activities (e.g., authoring required OneSDLC documentation, participation in established 
Integrated Project Teams (IPTs) and/or establishing a new IPT for the DLP in the Cloud effort, 
support for IRS FISMA Annual Security Compliance Assessments (ASCA). 
 
The following tasks are the high-level summary of the scope for this Performance Work

Treasury Inspector General for Tax Administration (TIGTA), and Government Accountability

Notice of Intent to Award Sole Source 
This is a COMBINED SYNOPSIS/SOLICITATION for commercial services prepared in accordance with 
the guidelines established in the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 13, utilizing Simplified 
Acquisition Procedures. This announcement serves as the sole solicitation; no written solicitation will be 
issued. 
The Air Force intends to award a non-co mpetitive contract to Science Applications International 
Corporation (SAIC)  in acco rdance with FAR 13.106-1(b)(1), which permits procurement from a single 
responsible source when no other supp lies or services can fu lfill ag ency requiremen ts. The 
requirement is for Joint Range Extension (JRE). The contractor shall deliver help desk support and 
sustainment services for the following JRE systems: JRE-3081, JRE-3171, JRE-3172, and JRE-13240. 
The applicable North American Industry Classification System Code for this requirement is 541512. This 
synopsis is issued in compliance with FAR Part 5.203. The 633rd Contracting Squadron, located at 14 
Burrell St, building 67, Langley AFB, VA 23665, intends to award a sole source contract to acquire 
services in support of the Air Combat Command CSS/SCPI . 
This notice of intent does not constitute a request for competitive quotes; however, interested parties 
who believe they possess the capability to fulfill this requirement are invited to submit a capability 
statement to SSgt Tierra Brown at tierra.brown.1@us.af.mil for review no later than 4:00 PM 
Eastern Time on September 9, 2025. Late submissions will not be considered. Please ensure that your 
response includes clear and persuasive evidence that competitive procurement would be beneficial to the 
Air Force. The decision by the Government not to pursue competitive contracting based on responses to this 
notice rests solely with the Government. Information received will generally be evaluated solely for the 
purpose of determining whether to proceed with a competitive procurement. For any inquiries
regarding this notice, please contact SSgt Tierra Brown at tierra.brown.1@us.af.mil Note: Late 
responses will not be considered.

Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) - USTRANSCOM Information Technology (IT) 
Enterprise Modernization (ITEM) Solutions 
1. INTRODUCTION AND BACKGROUND 
1.1 The United States Transportation Command (USTRANSCOM) is issuing this CSO in 
accordance with Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) 212.70, Defense 
Commercial Solutions Opening. USTRANSCOM conducts global integrated mobility operations 
and relies on robust IT systems and technologies that meet stringent DoD security standards.  
2. PURPOSE 
2.1 This CSO, in accordance with DFARS 206.102-70(a), is a competitive solicitation focused on 
innovative information technologies and services to meet the mission of the USTRANSCOM 
Enterprise. The Government seeks to obtain innovative solutions or potential new capabilities to 
fulfill requirements, close capability gaps, or provide potential technological advancements. The 
Government’s areas of interest (AoIs) will appear in individual CSO Calls.  
3. CSO APPROACH 
3.1 This CSO seeks an innovative approach to meet various USTRANSCOM IT needs. The 
Government encourages proposals that span a wide spectrum of possible technical and business 
solutions in response to the specific AoIs. Each AoI will identify USTRANSCOM’s interest for 
an individual IT program requirement or solution, or a broadly defined interest covering the full 
range of IT program requirements or solutions. All submissions in response to any AoI will be 
governed by this CSO unless otherwise noted in the individual AoI or in the individual CSO 
Call.  
3.2 The Government anticipates awarding firm fixed-price type contracts. The Government 
reserves the right to award both Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR)-Based contracts and/or 
Other Transactions (OTs) for prototype projects under 10 U.S.C. § 4022, with potential follow-
on production contracts or agreements. 
3.2.1 FAR-Based Contracts: Upon favorable evaluation and subject to the availability of funds, 
the Government may choose to award a contract under the FAR and, where applicable, the 
DFARS. The Contracting Officer will negotiate directly with the Offeror on the terms and 
conditions of the contract, including pricing, delivery, and payment terms, and will execute the 
contract on behalf of the Government. Contracts awarded under this process will comply with all 
applicable FAR and DFARS requirements, including those related to competition, pricing, and 
contract administration. Any resultant contract will include terms and conditions appropriate to 
the scope and objectives of the acquisition. 
3.2.2 OTs for Prototype and Production: Upon favorable review and subject to the availability of 
funds, the Government may choose to award an OT for Prototype and Production as deemed 
appropriate for the transaction. The Agreements Officer will negotiate directly with the Offeror 

on the terms and conditions of the OT, including payments, and will execute the OT on behalf of 
the Government. Upon successful completion of a prototype project under an OT for Prototype 
agreement, the Government and Offeror may negotiate a follow-on production contract or 
agreement without further competition as authorized under 10 U.S.C. § 4022(f). Any 
concept/technology/solution successfully proven through an OT for Prototype can be transitioned 
to production. Any resultant OT for Prototype awarded under this CSO will include language 
providing for the potential award of a follow-on production contract or agreement. 
3.4 Awards will be based on a multi-phase evaluation process detailed in Section 5. The 
Government reserves the right to fund all, some, one, or none of the proposals, including partial 
or incremental funding. 
4. GENERAL INFORMATION 
4.1 POINT OF CONTACT: The Contracting Officer, Ms. Meggan DeBrobander, and the 
Contract Specialist, Mr. Jonathan Severin, are the sole points of contact for the overarching 
USTRANSCOM ITEM Solutions CSO.  However, other Contracting Officers and Contract 
Specialists may be identified as POCs for individual CSO Calls.  
4.1.1 CSO General Questions: General CSO Questions may be sent via email to the 
USTRANSCOM Contracting Team at transcom.scott.tcaq.mbx.tcaq-ds@mail.mil. The 
Government anticipates a large amount of interest in this CSO, and to maintain a written record 
of questions, this is the only email address that will be used for general question communication. 
Material questions and answers will be published and updated on SAM.gov. 
4.2 CLASSIFIED INFORMATION: All Phase I submissions shall be unclassified. However, 
offerors must possess the necessary clearances and facilities to handle classified information up 
to the SECRET level. Specific classification requirements will be addressed in subsequent 
contracting actions. 
Offerors must possess all required personnel security clearances, facility clearances, and other 
infrastructure requirements necessary to perform any proposed classified work in accordance 
with the draft Contract Security Classification Specification (DD Form 254) without reliance on 
Government resources. As a wide variety of responses, as well as potential awards of diverse 
scopes and associated classified classification levels under this CSO are possible, the 
Government will provide award-specific security details for individual award actions as required. 
A draft DD Form 254 will be provided with a Phase III request for proposal, as necessary.  
5. SUBMISSION INFORMATION  
5.1 SUBMISSION OVERVIEW: The USTRANSCOM ITEM CSO will remain open indefinitely 
on SAM.gov with updates as needed. The Government may post CSO Calls at any time to 
incorporate AoIs. Interested companies are encouraged to frequently check SAM.gov for new 
AoI postings.  

5.1.1 The Government will not reimburse companies for the costs associated with submissions 
for any phase.  
5.1.2 Submissions for all phases shall be sent to the Contracting Team’s POCs listed in the 
individual CSO Call. To ensure submissions have been received by the Government, Offerors 
shall send a separate email (not containing attachments) to the Contracting Team’s POCs listed in 
the individual CSO Call immediately after emailing a submission to confirm receipt. Hardcopies 
for any phase will not be accepted.  
5.1.3 Offerors shall appropriately mark each page of the Phase I, Phase II, and Phase III 
submissions that contain proprietary information.  
5.2 TWO OR THREE PHASED SUBMISSION PROCESS: This CSO may be conducted in two or 
three phases as follows:  
5.2.1 Phase I - PowerPoint and White Paper: Phase I solutions will be requested by individual 
CSO Call and will be evaluated for each AoI. Interested Offerors must submit a PowerPoint 
briefing and White Paper in accordance with the instructions provided in Attachments 1 and 2. 
The instructions may request multiple White Papers depending on the complexity and stage of 
the individual AoI. Acceptance dates for the Phase I PowerPoint and White Paper will be 
specified in the respective CSO Calls. Due to the broad requirements and financial scope of this 
CSO, Offerors must ensure that submissions are succinct yet descriptive.  
5.2.2 Phase II - Pitch Session (optional): Phase II submissions will only be requested from 
Offerors who are invited by the AoI Contracting Team to a pitch session after reviewing Phase I

Area of Interest (AOI) 1a and 1b 
HT0038-25-S-C001 
Data Product Management and Data Integration 
Dated 10 July 2025 
 
BACKGROUND 
 
The Enterprise Intelligence & Data Solutions (EIDS) Program Management Office (PMO) mission is to 
"deliver, connect, and curate data to facilitate informed decision-making across a diverse data 
ecosystem in support of Military Health, Readiness, and Federal Health data integration and 
innovation." This mission is achieved through the MHS Information Platform (MIP) and associated 
systems. The EIDS PMO is interested in awarding other transaction agreements under the authority of 
10 U.S.C. 4022 in the following Area of Interest: 
 
Area of Interest #1a: Data Product Management 
Data Product Management includes a comprehensive suite of services to support the entire lifecycle of 
data products. This includes, but is not limited to, documentation, engineering support, lifecycle 
sustainment, DevSecOps adoption, and product ownership/project management. This AOI includes 
Technical Data Governance and Technical Data Management, ensuring data quality, security, 
interoperability, and compliance through data stewardship, governance process automation, and data 
policy implementation.  Data Product Management also includes critical support in defining and 
managing comprehensive Cloud Services, to include the management and administration of the AWS 
GovCloud environment. This AOI may also include security control implementation, performance 
monitoring, incident management, deployment automation, data migration support, capacity planning, 
and cost optimization. 
  
Area of Interest #1b: Data Integration  
This AOI includes addressing challenges related to cloud-hosted and cloud-native data solutions, 
including database, data warehousing, data lake, and cognitive computing. This AOI encompasses 
design, architecture, content development, operational sustainment, and ongoing support for data 
solutions, with a focus on leveraging AI, ML, and NLP capabilities. This AOI may also include data 
integration processes (e.g., extract, transform and load (ETL) or extract, load, transform (ELT)), legacy 
systems, data dictionaries and catalogs, implementing automated monitoring, and coordinating with 
other service domains to build interoperable and secure data solutions. 
 
 
 
 

2 
CALL FOR CAPABILITY STATEMENTS 
 
Interested companies may submit Capability Statement(s) to address either AOI 1a or 1b or both 1a and 
1b.  The Government’s market intelligence indicates a significant overlap in this area of expertise.  The 
Government will review the Capability Statements for merit and may make one award for the combined 
1a and 1b or make multiple awards/treat these as separate AOIs. 
 
 General Guidelines 
1. Unnecessarily elaborate brochures or proposals are not desired.  Do not include resumes for any 
personnel.  
2. Use of a diagram(s) or figure(s) to depict the essence of the proposed solution is strongly 
encouraged. 
3. All Capability Statements shall be unclassified.  
4. Successful prototype projects may require companies to obtain a Secret clearance.  Successful 
prototype projects will be required to comply with all applicable Department of Defense 
cybersecurity initiatives and applicable laws, including but not limited to the Privacy Act and 
Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act.  While there is no requirement as part of 
the Capability Statements to show the ability to hold a clearance or to have experience in these 
other areas, companies should structure their approach and consider including partners who 
will be able to successfully perform in this environment.  
5. Companies are encouraged to familiarize themselves with 10 U.S.C. 4022(d).  
 
Capability Statements for AOI #1 
Capability Statements should not exceed four (4) written pages.  Alternatively, Capability Statements 
may take the form of briefing slides which should not exceed fifteen (15) slides.  The page limits are not 
requirements, but strong recommendations.  The Government is not providing detailed limitations on 
formatting (such as margins, font size, etc.), but companies are reminded that the Government may take 
into account whether the content is easily readable and provides a good user experience as part of their 
review.  Submissions should include at a minimum: 
 
• Title Page (does not count against page limit).  
• To the extent that the company considers the information exempt from FOIA, companies should 
mark information to be protected from Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) disclosure and a 
legend identifying the documents as being submitted on a confidential basis.  
• Entity Name, Date, Point of Contact Name, E-Mail Address, Phone, and Address. 
• Specifically identify the AOI (i.e., 1a, 1b, or both 1a and 1b) for which the Capability Statement is 
submitted. 
• Describe your capabilities for the AOI.  
 
 
 

3 
DUE DATE 
 
Submissions are due NLT 1500 ET on 14 July 2025 to the Agreement Officer points of contact via email 
at lacey.n.lockard.civ@health.mil and elizabeth.l.holten.civ@health.mil.  The Government is under no 
obligation to timely review submissions that arrive after this date and time.  
 
REVIEW PROCESS  
 
This AOI is leveraging a multi-phased review process.   
 
During the initial review phase, the Government will review Capability Statements to determine 
whether the submission has sufficient merit to invite the company to the next review step.  Depending 
on the quality and number of submissions for AOI 1, the Government intends to provide a use case and 
invite those companies who have been determined to possess sufficient merit based on the Capability 
Statement to respond with a 5-7 minute video.  The Government then plans to notify companies of their 
status with respect to the AOI.  
 
Once the initial multi-phased review process yields a group of companies determined to have merit, the 
Government intends to share one or more problem statements with some of all of those companies and 
elicit responses leading to the award of one or more prototype other transaction agreements.  The 
Government will provide more details with respect to the review process in connection with the 
issuance of the problem statements.    
 
AWARDING INSTRUMENT 
 
This Area of Interest solicitation will be awarded in accordance with the Commercial Solutions Opening 
(CSO) number HT0038-25-S-C001 (PEO DHMS) posted on SAM.GOV website.

SECTION 1 – INTRODUCTION 
 
1.1 Background and Authority 
 
The mission of the Program Executive Oﬃce, Defense Healthcare Management Systems (PEO DHMS), is 
to transform the delivery of healthcare and advance data sharing through a modernized electronic 
health record for service members, veterans, and their families. PEO DHMS is an acquisition organization 
that oversees three program management oﬃces: DOD Healthcare Management System Modernization, 
Joint Operational Medicine Information Systems, and Enterprise Intelligence and Data Solutions. These 
oﬃces acquire, deliver, and support information technology and services that enable data sharing and 
modernization of the electronic health record. 
 
DHMS is interested in awarding other transaction agreements under the authority of 10 U.S.C. 4022 to 
carry out prototype projects that are directly relevant to enhancing the mission eﬀectiveness of 
personnel of the Department of Defense or improving platforms, systems, components, or materials 
proposed to be acquired or developed by the Department of Defense, or to improvement of platforms, 
systems, components, or materials in use by the armed forces.   
 
A prototype project includes, but is not limited to, a project that addresses:  
(A) a proof of concept, model, or process, including a business process; 
(B) reverse engineering to address obsolescence; 
(C) a pilot or novel application of commercial technologies for defense purposes; 
(D) agile development activity; 
(E) the creation, design, development, or demonstration of operational utility; or 
(F) any combination of subparagraphs (A) through (E). 
 
This CSO is issued under the authority of 10 U.S.C. 4022 and is not subject to the Competition in 
Contracting Act, the Federal Acquisition Regulation, or the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation 
Supplement.  Any successful prototype project (or portion thereof) awarded under this CSO may be 
selected for a follow-on production agreement or contract pursuant to 10 U.S.C. 4022(f).  
 
1.2 CSO Procedures 
 
This CSO is a competitive solicitation that satisﬁes the requirement in 10 U.S.C. 4022(b)(2) that the 
Government, to the maximum extent practicable, use competitive procedures when entering into 
agreements to carry out the prototype projects.  Unless otherwise set forth in an Area of Interest (AOI), 
there are no restrictions on who may submit a response to this CSO.  Each AOI will identify the expected 

2 
 
review process, which will vary depending on the complexity of the area and the anticipated number of 
responses.  
 
The Government intends to leave this CSO open and continuously post updates to this CSO, if necessary.  
Although the Government may determine additional companies have merit with respect to an AOI at any 
time, interested companies are encouraged to meet the due dates set forth in this CSO or in connection 
with any AOI as the Government has set aside personnel to review submissions based on the dates 
shared with industry.  The Government is under no obligation to consider submissions made later than 
the posted due date.  
 
The Government, in its sole discretion, may add companies whose information was included as part of a 
submission that was determined to have merit for purposes of an AOI, but who was not the “prime” or

The Government will not pay for costs associated with the preparation of Capability Statements or any 
other materials used to determine whether the company has merit for purposes of an AOI or is 
awardable for purposes of a prototype other transaction agreement.  
 
1.3 Areas of Interest 
 
The Government will issue Areas of Interest (AOIs) seeking submissions under this CSO. The Government 
may post new or revise AOIs at any time.  
 
SECTION 2 – Agreement Oﬃcer; Support Contractors and Non-Government Advisors  
 
Be advised, only an Agreement Oﬃcer has the authority to enter into a binding agreement on behalf of 
the Government and has exclusive authority to change the terms of an agreement. Inquiries may be sent 
to the points of contact for this CSO announcement at lacey.n.lockard.civ@health.mil and 
elizabeth.l.holten.civ@health.mil.   
 
DHMS policy is to treat all submissions as conﬁdential information, and to disclose their contents only for 
the purpose of review. Restrictive notices notwithstanding, during the review process, submissions may 
be handled by support contractors for administrative purposes and/or to assist with review.  Submission 
under this CSO will constitute a grant of authority by the submitting company to the Government to 
allow the use of non-Government advisors to participate in review of all phases of the CSO process for all 
AOIs.  If your company has any concerns with support contractors accessing proprietary information, 
please contact the Agreement Oﬃcer points of contact listed above in advance of submission. 
Submissions will not be returned.

1 
 
Performance Work Statement (PWS) 
National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) 
NOAA Fisheries 
Alaska Fisheries Science Center (AFSC) 
Marine Mammal Laboratory (MML) 
Alaska Ecosystems Program (AEP) 
Steller Sea Lion Artificial Intelligence (AI) Image Processing and Counting Effort 
1.0 Background 
The Alaska Ecosystems Program (AEP) is charged with monitoring the protected Steller sea lion 
populations in Alaska. AEP conducts annual crewed and uncrewed (UAS) aircraft surveys of known sea 
lion terrestrial sites during the peak of the breeding season to collect counts. Aerial survey teams collect 
vertical (or near vertical; i.e., nadir) high-resolution overlapping imagery (to ensure complete coverage) 
of sea lions hauled out on land and swimming in the water nearshore. The level of overlap is not optimal 
for creating high accuracy mosaics, and AEP is seeking to work with experts in artificial intelligence (AI) 
to improve current image registration and detection/classification models used to generate Steller sea 
lion counts from the high-resolution imagery.  
 
AEP has conducted UAS surveys since 2014, employing various camera makes/models (i.e., images with 
different resolutions) mounted to a downward facing gimbal to collect vertical images. Typically, there 
are up to approximately 15 sites per year that are surveyed using the UAS. Flights are conducted 
manually (i.e., not standardized track lines and therefore varying overlap). These images are higher 
resolution than the crewed aircraft imagery and typically do not have any metadata associated (e.g., 
date, time, latitude, longitude, etc.).  
 
Since 2007, the crewed aircraft survey has implemented either a single-camera (only for the first few 
years) or three-camera array mounted in the belly port of the aircraft (Figure 1). The center camera is 
vertically oriented while the starboard and port cameras are tilted towards center at an approximate 21° 
angle (fixed) to provide approximately 10% horizontal overlap between the three-image sets. As the 
plane flies, there is approximately 60% vertical overlap between image sets. AEP has employed three (3) 
different camera make/models for these surveys since 2007 (i.e., varying resolution and scale of 
imagery). There are sites that require a single pass, however, many sites require multiple passes to fully 
cover a site (with overlap between passes to ensure complete counts). It is also common to have some 
passes repeated (i.e., high overlap of the same area). AEP attempts to conduct plane passes in a 
‘racetrack’ fashion, however, topography and weather can hinder the ability to do so, resulting in less 
organized plane passes. Over 100 sites can be surveyed with this method. 
 

 
2 
 
 
Figure 1—Schematic of the three-camera array mounted in the belly port of the crewed 
aircraft that collects 3-image sets with ~60% vertical overlap and fixed ~10% 
horizontal overlap as the plane flies. 
 
Currently, our traditional count workflow involves two (2), full-time biologists to process and count all 
imagery independently, and when complete, compare and reconcile counts. The traditional method 
involves first manually mosaicking imagery by puzzling images together and drawing lines to eliminate 
areas of overlap to prevent double counts of sea lion individuals. The counters then review each image, 
placing a color-coded dot on each sea lion. Each color represents an age and sex classification: adult 
male, sub-adult male, adult female, juvenile, pup, dead non-pup, and dead pup. Once counting is 
completed by the independent counters, counts are summed by site for live non-pups (adult male, sub-
adult male, adult female, and juvenile) and pups, and compared between counters. Any counts that are 
>5% different (or a difference of >20 for non-pups and >10 for pups) are revisited by counters, requiring 
them to evaluate images in order to correct their count. This traditional count method can take up to 
four (4) months for the two (2) full-time biologists.  
 
To streamline this process, AEP has been working on developing an artificial intelligence approach for 
image processing and counting. Specifically, to work with AI experts to develop an image registration 
method to account for overlapping portions of the images to eliminate double counts, as well as 
counting and classifying individual sea lions. AEP contracted with Kitware, Inc. from 2019 to 2022, who 
developed several detection and classification models and two (2) image registration models, along with 
several pipelines, utilities, scripts, and improvements to Kitware’s DIVE graphical user interface (GUI;  
the VIAME Toolkit and specific “Sea Lion Models”openly available on Github).  


 
3 
 
Websites for VIAME Toolkit and Sea Lion Models via Github 
Kitware’s VIAME Toolkit:  
https://www.viametoolkit.org/ 
Kitware’s Sea Lion Models via Github:  
https://github.com/VIAME/VIAME/wiki/Model-Zoo-and-Add-Ons#sea-lion-models 
2.0 Scope/Tasks 
AEP assessed the highest accuracy detection and classification models and both image registration 
models, identifying the most optimal for further development: the FUSION (all class) detection and 
classification model and the Suppression image registration model. During model assessment, AEP 
identified areas of improvement to guide future development of existing models, scripts, utilities, 
pipelines, and the DIVE desktop GUI. The Contractor shall further develop and improve the detection 
and classification model (FUSION) and image registration model (Suppression); further develop utilities, 
pipelines, and scripts required to improve and evaluate models’ performance; and finally, improve the 
DIVE (desktop, not the web) interface to support model implementation and improve user experience. 
Details are specified in Tasks below. Kitware developed several pipelines, utilities, and scripts to perform 
various tasks and support the FUSION and Suppression models; for example, suppress water detections, 
ignore regions, register frames, and generation of tile mosaics. Further development of these--or 
development of new--pipelines, utilities, and scripts may be required to support the Tasks below. The 
Contractor shall not develop any new detection and classification or image registration models. 
Additionally, there are existing scripts for model scoring and performance, and receiver operating 
characteristic (ROC) curve generation utilized for evaluating models to understand accuracy and 
performance. AEP and the Contractor shall work together to discuss and finalize objectives, project plan, 
and prioritization of and within each task.  
 
To summarize, the Contractor is required to perform the following objectives: 
1. Further develop FUSION (all class) detection and classification model 
2. Further develop Suppression image registration model 
3. Supporting scripts, pipelines, utilities, or similar to support models 1-2, above.  
4. Tile mosaic capabilities (for three-image sets) that can be used in the DIVE (desktop) GUI with 
objectives 1-3, listed above. 
5. Single frame (for single and three-image sets) capabilities that can be used in the DIVE (desktop) 
GUI with objectives 1-3, listed above. 
6. DIVE desktop GUI capabilities to view, edit, process, and evaluate (i.e., attribute fields) 
detections and annotations generated from models and products from objectives 1-3, listed 
above, for images configurations from objectives 4 and 5, listed above.  
7. Virtual training covering how to use products, how to train models, how to use DIVE with these 
products and for editing and evaluation of model outputs.  
Details pertaining to Task needs are described in paragraph form and bulleted lists, with specific Task 
Deliverables listed as letter bullets listed at the end of each Task. Timing and metrics of success can be 
found in the Schedule of Deliverables and Performance Requirements Summary sections below. Key 
tasks include the following: 

 
4 
 
2.1 Task 1: Project Communication 
A. Quarterly Virtual Meetings: The Contractor shall coordinate with AEP Technical Point of Contact 
(TPOC; will be assigned upon award), to schedule virtual quarterly meetings with AEP and the 
Contractor (i.e., technical project manager; at minimum, other teammates shall join when 
applicable) to discuss efforts to date (with demos/visuals, if applicable), goals for the following 
quarter, project priorities, timelines, data needs from AEP (e.g., training data, flight logs, survey 
data), and any other pertinent topics. This task includes a “kick-off” meeting at the start of the 
base and option year (if applicable) when priorities and timelines will be discussed for the year. 
At the end of the base and option (if applicable) year, there will be a “wrap up” meeting that 
counts towards the quarterly meeting requirement.  
B. Monthly Reports: The Contractor shall provide brief (approximately 1-2 pages) monthly reports 
from the technical project manager on progress, issues encountered, recommendations, efforts 
accomplished the month prior, and any plans for the following month. The technical project 
manager shall address any follow-up questions from AEP regarding the monthly summary 
reports. Monthly summary reports shall be submitted with the monthly invoices. 
C. Iterative Products: The Contractor shall share iterative versions of model, pipelines, utility, 
scripts, and/or other products (e.g., DIVE GUI updates) from Tasks 2-4 to AEP as available to 
allow AEP to conduct assessments with sample data. This will assist AEP in providing meaningful 
feedback on products to support and inform further development throughout the effort, and 
allow AEP to stay informed on progress. The Contractor shall only share iterative products that 
AEP will be able to implement on a test set of data, accompanied by instructions on how to 
implement and use the iterative products.  
2.2 Task 2: Tile Mosaic Capabilities 
Kitware developed a script to create “tile mosaics” from the image sets captured with the three-camera 
array (crewed aircraft survey; Figure 2A). AEP assessments discovered tile mosaics lacked functionality in 
several ways:  
● Scripts frequently failed, and regularly created inaccurate tile mosaics (i.e., distorted mosaics), 
especially for images with homogenous substrate (e.g., water and vegetation; Figure 2B). 
● The Suppression image registration model failed to create suppression zones on an average of 
50% (range: 0-95.2%) of tile mosaics.  
● Of sea lions that the detection and classification model missed (i.e., not annotated), 93% were 
due Suppression model errors. This is a higher percentage than instances with single-frame 
imagery, which resulted in 23% of missed animals.  
● Tile mosaics were not compatible with the desktop DIVE desktop GUI (only the web GUI). 

 
5 
 
 
Figure 2—Examples of tile mosaics of the image sets captured by the three-camera array 
that are acceptable (A) and poor (B) quality.  
A. Improved Tile Mosaic Capabilities: The Contractor shall improve the ability to create accurate 
tile mosaics from three-image sets consistently. 
B. DIVE Desktop GUI: The Contractor shall develop DIVE desktop GUI to be compatible with tile 
mosaics (e.g., ability to view, edit, and evaluate model detections with tile mosaics in DIVE) 
matching existing capabilities for single frames. 
2.3 Task 3: Suppression Image Registration Model 
The Suppression image registration model performed well in some instances with single-frame imagery 
and for sites that only required a single plane pass. In instances with single-frame imagery, where there 
were multiple, overlapping plane passes (or manual UAS flights), the model did not perform at 
identifying sea lions that have already been “seen” by the models in previous passes. Within a single 
pass, approximately 8.6% of sea lion annotations were duplicates (i.e., same sea lion annotated on 
multiple images). As stated above, of sea lions that the detection and classification model missed (i.e., 
not annotated), 93% were due Suppression model errors. With tile mosaic imagery, these percentages 
were even higher at 25% duplicates and 93% missed. An average of 50% (range: 0-95.2%) of the tile 
mosaics failed to have suppression zones written at all. 
To assist in the development of this feature, AEP will provide flight logs (.csv files) for imagery collected 
by the crewed aircraft with location, roll, pitch, yaw, heading, altitude, etc., information that can be 
linked to image frame numbers. This information is largely unavailable for UAS imagery. If relevant to 
this task, information on the camera makes/models can be found in image metadata (i.e., image 
resolution and scale information). 
A. Improved Suppression Image Registration Model: The Contractor shall further develop the 
Suppression image registration model to improve performance for single-frame imagery. The 
Contractor shall develop the model (or additional script) to include registration for multiple, 
overlapping plane passes (e.g., loop closure) and manual UAS flights for single-frame (single and 
three-image sets) and tile mosaic imagery options. Ensure the Suppression model is functional 
with single-frame and tile mosaic imagery inputs in the DIVE desktop GUI, allowing users to run 


 
6 
 
models, and view, edit, and evaluate (e.g., attributes) annotations. In order to improve and 
support this model, further development of, or development of new, scripts and/or pipelines 
may be required. 
2.4 Task 4: FUSION (All Class) Detection and Classification Model 
The FUSION (all class) detection and classification model detects individuals and classifies them by age 
and sex classes, including dead animals (adult male, sub-adult male, adult female, juvenile, pup, dead 
non-pup, and dead pup). In assessing the FUSION (all class) detection and classification model, AEP 
identified several areas where the model requires improvement: increase accuracy of detecting 
individuals in large, overlapping aggregations; detecting animals in the water (hereafter referred to as 
“water detections”); and reducing false positive detections in water (e.g., waves, seaweed, light 
reflections, etc.). To ameliorate the latter, the model should be developed to separate land detections 
from water detections.  
 
The model will also be improved by including scale information using the camera make and model 
sensor information, especially for UAS imagery. Five (5) different camera makes/models have been 
utilized to-date. Camera make/model upgrades are expected to occur in the future and require a way to 
account for changes in image resolution (i.e., scale). Finally, AEP will provide new and upgraded 
(previously used annotations now with higher resolution imagery) training data to retrain the model.
